column2: The Silk Road
column3: 丝绸之路

column2: Out of the Pass
column3: 出关

column2: Beyond the Jade Gate
column3: 玉门关外

column2: When the gate shut behind you, a sentry poured a bowl of wine on the ground: for those on the road, he said. Which ones, you asked; he did not answer, only lifted his lantern higher. On its paper, in ink long faded: "The Thousand Li, out through the pass in the seventh month, three hundred camels." Not one of that caravan came back, ten years ago. Now the court opens the road again, and the first to go out are you.
column3: 关门在身后合上时，守卒往地上泼了一碗酒，说是敬路上的人。你问敬哪些人，他不答，只把灯笼挑高了些。灯笼纸上有一行褪了色的墨字：「千里号，丁未年七月出关，计驼三百」。十年前出关的那支商队，没有一个人回来。如今朝廷重开商路，第一支出关的，是你们。

column2: Yumen Gate
column3: 玉门关口

column2: The gate of Yumen Pass stands open, yet a hitching post bars the archway. A few sand-bandit blades in a toll officer's stolen cap are charging everyone who leaves: a hundred coins a head, double for mules, extra if you cry. The old night watchman hides in an arrow slit and waves you away. Beyond the gate lies the frontier, and the wind smells of sand.
column3: 玉门关的城门洞开着，门洞里却横着一根拴马桩。几个沙匪刀手戴着从关吏头上扒下来的乌纱帽，挨个向出关的人收「出关钱」：一人一百文，骡马加倍，哭的另算。关楼上的老更夫缩在箭窗里冲你们直摆手。门外就是关外，风里一股沙子的味道。

column2: The cap rolls into the ditch and the post becomes firewood. The watchman climbs down and holds his lantern to a brick in the archway, where a knife has cut a line of small characters: 'Third month, Dingwei year. The Qianli caravan went out. Three hundred souls.' Plenty of people have left by this gate in ten years, he says, but you are the first to take this road west to trade since then.
column3: 乌纱帽滚进了沟里，拴马桩劈了当柴。老更夫爬下关楼，举着灯笼照门洞里的一块砖：一行刀刻的小字，「丁未年三月，千里号出关，三百人」。他说十年来出关的人不少，可走这条路去西边做大买卖的，你们是头一支。

column2: Willow Pavilion
column3: 折柳亭

column2: The first pavilion outside the pass has an old willow beside it, its branches heavy with faded strips of cloth: everyone who leaves ties one, hoping to know the place again on the way home. Today a gang of rogue soldiers is hacking at the trunk. 'Good firewood,' they say, 'hardly anyone comes back anyway.' An old woman who sells incense hugs the tree and will not let go.
column3: 关外第一座亭子叫折柳亭，亭边一棵老柳，枝上系满了褪色的布条：出关的人系一条布，盼着回来时还认得这里。今天一伙兵痞拎着斧头在砍树，说「烧火正好，反正没几个人回来」。一个卖香烛的老太太抱着树干，死活不撒手。

column2: The soldiers drop their axes and run. The old woman points to the highest branch: three hundred identical red strips, tied on the same day, not one ever untied. 'The Qianli caravan's,' she says. 'Whoever ties a cloth has to come back and untie it himself.' Then she presses a strip of blue cloth into your hands.
column3: 兵痞们丢下斧头跑了。老太太指给你们看最高的那根枝：上面密密麻麻系着三百条一样的红布，同一天系的，一条都没解下来过。「千里号的。」她说，「系布的人回来，要自己解。」她又塞给你们一条蓝布。

column2: Dice Slope
column3: 骰子坡

column2: A gang of gamblers who fled their debts inside the pass has joined the sand bandits. They're running a book, and the bet is you: 'Will the pioneers come back alive?' Odds: three hundred to one. Anyone who won't bet gets robbed. Their leader clutches a greasy betting ledger, and his eyes light up at your banner: 'The horse itself has arrived!'
column3: 坡上蹲着一伙从关里逃债出来的赌鬼，入了沙匪的伙。他们开了个赌局，赌的是你们：「开拓队能不能活着回来」，一赔三百。谁不肯下注就抢谁。领头的拿着一本油腻的赌簿，见了你们的旗子，眼睛一亮：「正主来了！」

column2: The loaded dice get stamped into the sand and the betting book is yours. On its first page is a bet from ten years ago: 'Will the Qianli caravan come back?' Only one person bet 'yes', and he signed with a little abacus. 'That fellow bet on himself,' the leader mutters, 'and he's never come to collect.'
column3: 灌了铅的骰子被一脚踩进沙里，赌簿归了你们。翻到最前面，是十年前开的一局：「千里号回不回」，押「回」的只有一个人，签名是一把小算盘。领头的嘟囔：「那人押了自己，到现在也没来收钱。」

column2: Bell Slope
column3: 响铃坡

column2: The old road climbs a gentle slope here, and on the crest a band of desert raiders has hung their stolen bells all over a dead tree. When the wind blows they clang so loudly you hear them from far off. Every caravan they rob gives up one bell as a trophy. There must be sixty or seventy on the tree; the oldest, rusted to half a shell, they say wasn't stolen but found in the sand.
column3: 古道在这里翻一道缓坡，坡顶一伙大漠响马把抢来的铃铛挂满了一棵枯树，风一吹叮当乱响，远远就能听见。他们每劫一队就摘一个铃铛当战利品。树上少说挂了六七十个，最老的一个锈得只剩半边，响马说那一个不是抢的，是在沙里捡的。

column2: The raiders scatter and you take the bells down for their owners to claim. The half-rusted one is cast with the character Qian. Its clapper is gone, and it makes no sound when shaken. An old porter passing by says the caravan that went out ten years ago had bells exactly like it.
column3: 响马散了，你们把铃铛一个个摘下来，等失主来认。那个锈了半边的铜铃上铸着一个「千」字，铃舌早没了，摇起来一声不响。一个过路的老脚夫说，十年前出关的那支商队，铃铛都是这样的。

column2: Wandering Milestone
column3: 挪步碑

column2: A milestone by the road reads 'Yangguan, 120 li west'. The locals say it moves one step west every night, chasing the caravan that left ten years ago. A mad Taoist and a dozen followers kowtow around it, calling themselves the Followers of the Stone, and collect 'offerings' from travellers. Anyone who won't pay is held down to knock his head on the stone a hundred times.
column3: 路边一块里程碑，「西去阳关一百二十里」。附近的人都说这碑每晚往西挪一步，是在追十年前那支商队。一个疯道士带着十几个信徒围着碑磕头，自称「随石教」，向过路人收「随喜钱」，不给的就被信徒们按在碑前磕满一百个头。

column2: The followers scatter. That night you watch the stone and catch the mad Taoist levering it a step west. But what the moved base reveals stops you short: three hundred fine notches, each with one small character beside it, the first character of a name. The Taoist says he only wanted to bring them a little closer to the west.
column3: 信徒们一哄而散，夜里你们守着碑，果然看见那疯道士偷偷撬着碑往西挪。可碑座底下露出来的东西让人愣住：三百道细细的刻痕，每道旁边一个小字，是名字的头一个字。疯道士说，他只是想让它们离西边近一点。

column2: Deserters' Camp
column3: 逃兵屯

column2: A sprawl of mud-brick huts holds more than a hundred deserters from the border army. They've seized the farmland, named themselves 'First Battalion Beyond the Pass', and still muster, drill and sound the horn every day; they just never fight, and collect 'army pay' from passing merchants. The notice on their gate has more wrong characters than right ones, and it is signed 'Qianli Caravan Escort Battalion'.
column3: 一大片土坯房，住着上百个从边军里逃出来的兵痞。他们占了屯田，自封「关外第一营」，每天照样点卯、操练、吹号，就是不打仗，只向过路的商人征「军饷」。营门口贴着一张告示，错字比字还多，落款写的却是「千里号护卫营」。

column2: The horn dies mid-call. An old soldier among the surrendered says, red-faced, that ten years ago this unit was assigned to escort the Qianli caravan. The night before they set out, an order came cancelling it, and the caravan left on its own. 'Then we heard not one came back, and we... couldn't face going back to camp.' The fields go back to the farmers. You keep the notice.
column3: 号角吹到一半就哑了。降兵里一个老卒红着脸说：十年前他们这营本是派去护送千里号的，出发前一夜一纸调令撤了，商队自己走了。「后来听说一个都没回来，我们就……没脸回营了。」屯田还给了庄户，那张告示你们留着。

column2: First Post Station
column3: 头道驿

column2: The first post station beyond the pass has been besieged by sand bandits for three days. The clerks have barricaded the door with tables and chairs and are guarding a wax-sealed dispatch tube: an urgent court message, they say, to be handed only to 'the pioneers'. The bandits think it's full of banknotes and keep battering the door, yelling 'hand it over and we'll let you go!' The door bristles with arrows.
column3: 出关后的头一座驿站被一伙沙匪围了三天。驿卒们用桌椅堵住大门，死守着一只封了火漆的公文筒，说是朝廷的急递，只交给「开拓队」。沙匪以为筒里是银票，一边撞门一边喊：「交出来就放你们走！」门板上已经插满了箭。

column2: The bandits are scattered and the clerks open up and hand you the tube. Inside is a court notice to every station on the road: 'The pioneers travel west. Stations are to assist them, and to seek news of the Qianli caravan.' The old clerk says a notice much like it came ten years ago, except that one said: 'Assist the Qianli caravan.'
column3: 沙匪被打散，驿卒们开门把公文筒交到你们手里。里面是朝廷发给沿路的告示：「开拓队西行，沿途驿站照应，并访千里号下落。」老驿卒说，十年前也来过一份差不多的，只是那份上写的是「照应千里号」。

column2: The bandit camp yields forty sacks of millet, two jars of salted meat, a bundle of new whips, a dozen sledgehammers bent from battering the door, and a sketch of the station marked 'silver here'.
column3: 沙匪营里抄出四十袋小米、两缸腌肉、一捆崭新的马鞭、十几把撞门撞弯了的铁锤，还有一张画着驿站的草图，标着「银子在此」。

column2: The clerks read you the latest bulletins every time, the clerk's wife slips fresh sesame flatbreads into your saddlebags, and someone always mends the frayed corner of your banner.
column3: 驿卒们每次都把最新的塘报念给你们听，驿卒老婆烤好芝麻馕塞进鞍袋，还替你们把磨破的旗角缝好。

column2: Six-Way Fork
column3: 六岔口

column2: Six tracks fan out here, and at the fork sits a fortune-teller called Master Six Roads. He freely admits he's a fraud who draws his sticks at random, yet strangely he's always right. A gang of sand bandits has tied him up at the fork and makes him predict which caravans are worth robbing. He's so accurate and they rob so well that merchants have nearly vanished from these parts.
column3: 六条小路在这里散开，路口坐着个摆摊算卦的「六路先生」。他自己承认是个骗子，卦签都是瞎抽的，可怪就怪在每回都准。一伙沙匪把他绑在路口，逼他算哪一路商队有钱，算得太准，沙匪抢得太顺，附近的商人都快绝迹了。

column2: Untied, Master Six Roads draws a stick for you out of habit, stares at it a long while, then says shakily: 'Out west, people will ask you for a ledger. Further west, a man with only one eye is waiting for you to ask him a question.' He won't take a coin for this one. It's too accurate. It frightens him.
column3: 绳子一松，六路先生顺手给你们抽了一签，看了半天，哆嗦着说：「往西有人跟你们要一本账，再往西，有个只剩一只眼的人在等你们问话。」他说这卦他不收钱，太准了，怕。

column2: Grey-Eyed Trader's Tent
column3: 灰眼胡商帐

column2: A big tent stitched with copper discs belongs to a grey-eyed foreign trader with a beard in three braids. He takes goods, never coins: 'beyond the pass, copper is scrap'. Nor does he deal with weaklings. To enter his tent you must first beat his hired blades, and he sits at the flap cracking melon seeds, enjoying the show.
column3: 一顶缀满铜片的大帐，主人是个灰眼睛的胡商，大胡子编成三股。他只收货，不收铜钱，说铜钱「到了关外就是废铁」。他也不跟软脚虾做生意：想进他的帐，得先赢过他雇的那几个刀手。他坐在帐门口嗑瓜子，看得津津有味。

column2: The last blade goes down. The trader roars with laughter and holds the flap open for you to trade. In a corner sits a dusty stack of felt hats. 'Ten years ago a man with an abacus ordered three hundred and paid half. He put one on there and then, and said he'd collect the rest on the way back.' He counts them for you: two hundred and ninety-nine. 'Trade for anything else you like. Not these.'
column3: 最后一个刀手躺倒，胡商哈哈大笑，掀帘请你们进去换货。帐角压着一摞落了灰的毡帽。「十年前一个拿算盘的人订了三百顶，付了一半。他自己当场戴走一顶，说剩下的回来再取。」胡商数给你们看：二百九十九顶。「别的货随便换，这些不行。」

column2: Singer's Mound
column3: 唱曲墩

column2: Under a mound of earth sits a blind old fiddler, singing a song nobody has heard: 'Three hundred went out past the gate, the bookkeeper lit a lamp and counted...' A gang of rogue soldiers kicks over his bowl and says the song is bad luck. He keeps singing. A string snaps; he sings on.
column3: 土墩下坐着一个瞎眼的老琴师，拉着一把蒙羊皮的胡琴，唱一支谁也没听过的曲子：「三百人出关去，账房先生点灯数……」一伙兵痞围着他踢翻了他的碗，说这曲子晦气，不许再唱。老琴师偏不停，弦断了一根，接着唱。

column2: The soldiers gone, the old man restrings and sings you the whole song. The last line: 'The lamp counted two hundred and ninety-nine, and the bookkeeper would not leave.' He learned it ten years ago from a caravan hand, he says, who told him someone on the road was keeping accounts, and he must sing it whole when they came back.
column3: 兵痞们跑了，老琴师换上新弦，把整支曲子唱给你们听。最后一句是「灯数到二百九十九，账房先生不肯走」。问他从哪儿学的，他说是十年前一个伙计教的，那伙计说，路上有人记账，回来时要听他唱全。

column2: Bridal Gully
column3: 喜轿沟

column2: A bridal sedan stands in the gully and the bride inside is crying. A bully's thugs have stopped the wedding party. They don't want money; they want one sheet of paper from the dowry chest, which they say is 'worth a camel'. The groom, a young falconer, is rolling up his sleeves to fight to the death, and the bride cries from the sedan: 'My father left me that!'
column3: 沟里停着一顶花轿，新娘子在里头哭。一个恶霸的家丁拦住了送亲的队伍，不要钱，要嫁妆箱子里的一张纸，说那张纸「值一头骆驼」。新郎官是个放鹰的小伙子，正撸起袖子准备拼命，新娘在轿子里喊：「那是我爹留给我的！」

column2: The thugs are driven off. The bride lifts the curtain and shows you the paper: an IOU, 'One camel borrowed, to be returned on our way back. Qianli caravan', stamped with a little abacus seal. Her father waited ten years and in the end made it part of her dowry. 'It says it'll be returned,' she says with a smile. 'I'm married now. It can wait with me.'
column3: 家丁被打跑了。新娘掀开轿帘，把那张纸给你们看：一张欠条，「借驼一头，归时奉还，千里号」，落款盖着一枚小算盘印。她爹等了十年没等到，就把它当了嫁妆。「上头说归时还，」她笑着说，「我嫁了，它也跟着我等。」

column2: Noon Slope
column3: 正午坡

column2: A sand bandit stands on the crest with a sword in his arms. Every noon he stops one traveller to duel; losers leave their weapons, and nobody has ever won. Ten years ago, he says, he lost here to a man, the guard captain of a great caravan, half a beat faster than him, who spared his life and said only, 'Again when I come back.' He has waited every noon since.
column3: 坡顶站着一个抱刀的沙匪，每天正午拦住一个过路人比刀，输了留下兵器，赢了……还没人赢过。他说十年前就在这里输给过一个人，那人是一支大商队的护卫头，刀法比他快半拍，赢了也不要他的命，只说「回来再比」。他从那天起每天正午都在等。

column2: The swordsman loses and sits on the slope a long time without a word. Then he hands you a broken sword tip: it chipped off the guard captain's blade in their duel, and it's engraved 'Qianli'. 'He never came back,' says the swordsman. 'So you come back in his place, and we'll duel again.'
column3: 刀客输了，坐在坡上半天没说话，然后把一截断刀尖递给你们：那是当年护卫头的刀，比刀时崩下来的，上面刻着「千里号」。「他没回来，」刀客说，「那就你们替他回来，下回我们再比。」

column2: Silver That Wasn't
column3: 错银车

column2: A gang of sand bandits has robbed an ox cart stacked with bright white bricks they took for silver ingots, and danced around it for joy. But chop or burn them as they will, the 'silver' won't melt, and one bandit who licked it spat for a full minute: salty. They refuse to admit it and insist the silver has turned into a demon, ordering the old carter to 'change it back'.
column3: 一伙沙匪抢了一辆牛车，车上码着一块块白亮亮的砖，以为是银锭，乐得在车边跳舞。可他们用刀砍、用火烧，「银子」就是不化，有个沙匪舔了一口，咸得直吐。他们不肯认，硬说是银子成了精，押着赶车的老汉要他「把银子变回来」。

column2: The bandits are driven off. The carter explains it's neither silver nor ordinary salt but his yearly load of 'homeward salt': ordered ten years ago by the Qianli caravan, one cartload a year, buried under cairns along the road for them to eat on their way home. Each brick bears a little abacus seal. 'They paid for ten years,' the old man says. 'This year's the last load.'
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。老汉说这车不是银也不是普通的盐，是他每年往西边送的「回程盐」：十年前千里号走时在他这儿订的，一年一车，埋在沿路的石堆底下，等他们回程时吃。砖上都压着一枚小算盘印。「钱付了十年的，」老汉说，「今年是最后一车。」

column2: Feast-Day Ridge
column3: 节日梁

column2: This band of desert raiders has an ancestral rule: they only rob on feast days, and farm the rest of the time. But this year there aren't enough feasts, so they've invented one: 'Pioneers Leave the Pass Day', which is today. The whole gang has put on New Year clothes, pasted red paper all over the ridge, and are banging a gong waiting for you.
column3: 这伙大漠响马有条祖传的规矩：只在过节的日子打劫，平时种地。可今年的节不够用了，他们自己发明了一个：「开拓队出关节」，今天就是。全伙人穿上了过年的新衣裳，在梁上贴了红纸，敲着锣等你们。

column2: The feast is over and the raiders sheepishly take off their best clothes. The old chief hands over a wooden box. Ten years ago, also on a feast day, they robbed this box from the Qianli caravan's rearguard and found only paper: three hundred names, neatly copied. 'The bookkeeper rode back asking for it. Said it was the copy, and losing it meant a whole night writing it out again,' the chief says. 'We never returned it. Always felt a bit bad.'
column3: 节过完了，响马们脱了新衣裳。老头领交出一只木匣：十年前也是过节，他们劫了千里号押尾的这只匣子，里面全是纸，三百个名字抄得工工整整。「那账房追回来要，说丢了副本要重抄一夜。我们没还，一直怪不好意思的。」

column2: Poem Wall Tower
column3: 题壁墩

column2: The wall has a gap here, and a gang of rogue soldiers prises out its bricks to sell inside the pass. Its surface is covered in poems left by travellers through the ages, and a poor poet thin as a bamboo pole keeps watch at the gap, copying every poem before its brick is taken. Today he spreads his arms to shield one brick: its two lines, he says, he's been copying for ten years and can't bear to finish.
column3: 长城在这里塌了一个豁口，一伙兵痞每天拆墙砖拉去关里卖。墙上写满了历代过客的题诗，一个瘦得像竹竿的穷诗人守在豁口，每拆一块砖，他就抢着把砖上的诗抄下来。今天兵痞们要拆的那块，他张开双臂护着，说那上面的两句他抄了十年也舍不得抄完。

column2: The soldiers flee and the brick is saved. On it are two lines in small, neat script, tidy as a ledger: 'Reckon it stroke by stroke; repay it step by step.' No name, only a little abacus drawn below. The poet says it's the least poetic poem he's ever seen, and his favourite.
column3: 兵痞们跑了，砖保住了。上面是两行小楷，字迹工整得像账簿：「一笔一笔算，一步一步还。」落款没有名字，只画了一把算盘。诗人说，这是他见过最不像诗的诗，也是他最喜欢的一首。

column2: Sand-Measuring Terrace
column3: 量沙台

column2: On an earth terrace, a scholar in a long gown measures the gobi length by length with a knotted rope. He means to draw a 'True Survey Map' from Yumen to Yangguan and has been at it four years. Yesterday sand bandits stole his rope to tie up loot and lined their cooking pot with his drafts. He sits crying like a child: the most important page burned too.
column3: 一座土台上，一个穿长衫的书生拿着一根打了结的长绳，一绳一绳地量戈壁，要画一张从玉门到阳关的「丈量真图」，已经量了四年。昨天一伙沙匪抢了他的绳子去捆货，还把他的草稿垫了锅底。书生坐在台上哭得像个孩子，说最要紧的那一页也烧了。

column2: You recover the rope, and the page has lost only a corner. It turns out it isn't his draft but an old sheet he found by the road: 'Yumen to Yangguan, 314,000 paces', counted day by day. Four years of measuring, the scholar says, and his figure differs from it by only a hundred paces. 'Whoever wrote this counted every single step.'
column3: 绳子抢回来了，那一页只烧掉一角。原来那不是他的稿子，是他在路边捡的一张旧纸，上面记着「玉门至阳关，三十一万四千步」，逐日记数，一步不差。书生说他量了四年，量出来的数跟这张纸只差一百步。「记这张纸的人，是一步一步数着走的。」

column2: Fake Gate
column3: 假关门

column2: A wooden archway straddles the old road, painted 'Yumen Pass'. But Yumen Pass is twenty li behind you. A gang of sand-bandit blades dressed as gate guards checks papers and collects duty with wooden swords, and beats anyone who says 'this isn't Yumen Pass'. Plenty of strangers have been fooled into paying twice.
column3: 古道正中竖着一座木头牌坊，刷着三个大字「玉门关」，可玉门关明明在身后二十里。一伙沙匪刀手扮成守关兵，拿着木头刀查验文牒、征收关税，谁说「这不是玉门关」就挨一顿揍。不少外地商人真被唬住了，老老实实交了两回钱。

column2: The archway comes down in a cloud of dust. On the back of the 'Yumen Pass' board is a line of old paint: 'Qianli caravan, cart no. 37'. The bandits say they found the planks by the road. It seems the caravan began breaking up its carts here, leaving the wood behind and switching to camels for the desert.
column3: 牌坊被推倒了，砸起好大一片土。翻过那块写着「玉门关」的木板，背面还有一行旧漆：「千里号第三十七车」。沙匪说木板是在路边捡的大车板子。原来商队过了这里就开始拆车，把木头留在路上，换成骆驼进沙漠。

column2: Cookpot Ridge
column3: 锅灶梁

column2: Cooking smoke curls over the ridge and the smell of meat carries for miles. A gang of sand bandits has kidnapped a head chef from a restaurant inside the pass and makes him cook for them daily; they're all shiny with grease. Chained to the stove, he sneaks extra salt into every dish to drive them off. They only like it more.
column3: 梁上炊烟袅袅，肉香飘出好几里。一伙沙匪绑了关里酒楼的一个大厨，逼他天天给他们做饭，吃得一个个油光满面。大厨被拴在灶台边，一边炒菜一边偷偷往锅里多撒盐，想把他们齁跑，可他们越吃越爱吃。

column2: The bandits have eaten too much to run and are hauled out one by one. The chef fries you a huge panful, talking as he cooks. Ten years ago he cooked the Qianli caravan's farewell banquet, three hundred portions. As it broke up, the bookkeeper asked for one more bowl: 'Save it for whoever comes after us.' He sets out the bowls. 'Today someone's finally come to eat it.'
column3: 沙匪吃撑了跑不动，被一个个拎了出来。大厨给你们炒了一大锅菜，边炒边说：十年前千里号出关，送行宴是他掌的勺，三百份。临散席，账房先生又要了一碗，说「给后头来的人留着」。他摆上碗筷：「今天总算有人来吃了。」

column2: Bone Post Station
column3: 白骨驿

column2: The courtyard walls are built of bleached bones, white from afar; hence the name. Only an old postmaster lives here, and every night at dusk he lights twelve lamps, never one fewer, and keeps them burning till dawn. Sand bandits have learned he stores jars of lamp oil and come to take them tonight. The old man stands before his lamps hugging an oil jar. The lamps, he says, must not go out.
column3: 驿站的院墙是用兽骨垒的，远看一片白，所以叫白骨驿。驿里只住着一个老驿丞，每天天一黑就点起十二盏灯，一盏不少，一夜不灭。一伙沙匪打听到他存着好几坛灯油，今晚来抢，老驿丞抱着油坛子站在灯前，说灯不能灭。

column2: The bandits are driven beyond the bone walls and not one lamp goes out. The postmaster opens a yellowed register. 'Ten years ago the Qianli caravan rested here. Their bookkeeper entered every name, stroke by stroke, and gave each a number.' He points at the lamps. 'Each lamp lights twenty-five names. Twelve lamps, three hundred people.' But when you count, the last lamp has only twenty-four. Number three hundred is blank except for one word: 'Bookkeeper'. 'He entered everyone else,' the old man says, 'but never himself.'
column3: 沙匪被赶出了骨墙，一盏灯也没灭。老驿丞翻开驿簿：「十年前千里号在这里歇过一夜，账房先生登了三百个名字，每人编了号。一盏灯照二十五个，十二盏，三百人。」可最后一盏灯下只有二十四个名字，第三百号空着，只写了「账房」。「他登了别人，就是不写自己。」

column2: Jujube Boundary
column3: 枣树界

column2: An old jujube tree stands exactly on the boundary between two villages. East says the tree is theirs; West says fruit that falls on their side is theirs. After ten years of quarrelling, both sides hired sand bandits this year to 'settle it'. The bandits tied up both villages, stripped the tree, and are sitting under it spitting out stones.
column3: 两个村子之间长着一棵老枣树，正好在界上。东村说树是东村的，西村说枣子落在西村就是西村的。吵了十年，今年两边都花钱雇了沙匪来「评理」，结果沙匪把两村的人都绑了，枣子也摘光了，正坐在树下吐枣核。

column2: The bandits flee. Each headman pulls half a sheet of paper from his coat, and the halves fit perfectly: a ruling written for them ten years ago by a passing bookkeeper, 'East picks in odd years, West in even; the shade is for all', torn in two in a later quarrel. Facing that little abacus seal, the headmen are too ashamed to speak.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。两个村长各从怀里掏出半张纸，一对，严丝合缝：是十年前路过的一位账房先生替他们写的公断，「单年东摘，双年西摘，树荫共用」，后来吵架撕成了两半。两个村长对着那把小算盘印，臊得说不出话。

column2: Marmot Burrows
column3: 獭子洞

column2: A barren slope riddled with marmot burrows. A rumour has spread across the frontier: the Qianli caravan's bookkeeper buried silver along the road and recorded it in his ledger. A gang of sand bandits is convinced it's under this slope, and spends every day on their bellies digging out hole after hole, hands covered in marmot bites, press-ganging passers-by to help.
column3: 一片满是旱獭洞的荒坡。关外传开了一个谣言：千里号的账房在沿路埋了银子，记在账本上。一伙沙匪认定银子就在这片坡底下，天天趴在地上一个洞一个洞地掏，被獭子咬得满手牙印，还把路过的人抓来帮着掏。

column2: The bandits are run off. You don't dig; you just plant a sign: 'No silver here, the marmots will testify.' But the rumour doesn't stop. Further west, more and more people are looking for that ledger.
column3: 沙匪被赶走了，你们没去掏洞，只在坡上插了块木牌：「此坡无银，獭子作证。」谣言却没停，往西去的路上，越来越多的人在找那本账本。

column2: Sand Fox Dens
column3: 沙狐窝

column2: In the rock crevices at the foot of the northern hills lives a clan of sand foxes. At night they come down to steal chickens and jerky, and anything shiny: brass buttons, earrings, the station's lamp glass. The herders say these foxes 'never run out': drive off one litter and another wriggles out, so every spring someone has to be hired to clear them.
column3: 北山脚下的乱石缝里住着一大窝沙狐，夜里成群下山偷鸡、叼肉干，还专偷亮晶晶的东西：铜扣、耳环、驿站的灯罩。牧民说这窝狐狸是「生不完的」：一窝刚赶走，石缝里又钻出一窝新的，每年开春都要请人来清一次。

column2: The foxes are driven back into the hills, and from the crevices you pull out a hoard of shiny trinkets, among them a brass abacus bead carved with Qian. Who knows where the foxes found it. But as you leave, new kits are already yipping in the rocks. You'll have to come back and clear them again.
column3: 狐群被赶回了深山，石缝里掏出一窝亮晶晶的小玩意，其中有一颗铜算盘珠，刻着「千」字，不知道狐狸从哪儿叼来的。可你们离开时，石缝里又传出了小狐狸的叫声，过一阵还得再来清。

column2: Garrison Granary
column3: 屯田仓

column2: This granary stores seed for the garrison farmers. Its steward, Hu, in league with a gang of rogue soldiers, has locked the doors and produced a 'Qianli caravan IOU': ten years ago the caravan borrowed grain and never repaid it, he says, so the farmers must pay the debt for them, with seed at triple price. They can't, and spring ploughing is slipping away.
column3: 这座粮仓本是给屯田庄户存种粮的。管事姓胡，勾结一伙兵痞锁了仓门，拿出一张「千里号欠条」，说十年前商队借了仓里的粮没还，这笔账要庄户们替他们还，种子三倍价钱。庄户们交不起，春耕眼看要误了。

column2: Steward Hu is hauled down and the soldiers scatter. The IOU is an obvious fake: no abacus seal. An old farmer snorts: 'My family has a real one. They borrowed one measure of wheat and left another as interest.' The doors are flung open and the farmers line up for seed.
column3: 胡管事被请了下来，兵痞四散。那张欠条一看就是假的：没有算盘印。一个老庄户冷笑：「真欠条我家有一张，人家借的是一斗麦，还多给了一斗当利钱。」仓门大开，庄户们排着队领种子。

column2: Under the floor: three hundred measures of wheat, a chest of coins, dozens of bolts of fine cloth, a stack of half-written fake IOUs, and a sword with a gilded hilt and a blade of rusty iron.
column3: 仓底抄出三百斗麦子、一箱铜钱、几十匹细布、一叠还没写完的假欠条，还有一把剑柄镶金、剑刃却是生锈铁片的佩剑。

column2: Every time you pass, a farmer runs over from the fields with a sack of freshly milled flour and a jar of home-pickled chive blossoms.
column3: 庄户们每次都从地头跑过来，塞给你们一口袋新磨的麦面，还有一罐自家腌的韭菜花。

column2: Han Crossbow Vault
column3: 汉弩库

column2: At the end of the old road, a sand-choked track leads to a half-buried stone vault, its lintel carved 'Hexi Crossbow Armoury'. A tough band of desert raiders dug it open, having heard the Qianli caravan hid its ledger here. Three days of searching found no ledger, only Han-dynasty repeating crossbows, which they're scrubbing and test-firing; the bolts go clean through a door plank.
column3: 古道尽头，一段被沙土封住的老路通向一座半埋的石库，门楣上刻着「河西弩库」。一伙精悍的大漠响马挖开了门，听说千里号把账本藏在了这里，进去翻了三天，账本没找到，倒翻出了汉朝的连弩，正擦着锈试射，箭能钉穿门板。

column2: The raiders are driven out. No ledger, of course; only a chalk mark inside the door: the character Qian, an arrow pointing west, and beside it, 'Checked. Nobody here.' As though the caravan had once searched this place for someone. You take what crossbows still work and seal the door again.
column3: 响马被打出了石库。账本果然不在，只在库门内侧找到一个粉笔画的记号：一个「千」字，一支箭头指向西边，旁边写着「已查，无人」。像是当年商队在这里找过什么人。你们带走能用的弩，把库门重新封上。

column2: Painted Cave
column3: 岩画洞

column2: A shallow cave at the foot of the hills is covered in ancient paintings: hunters, gazelles, horsemen. The local children swear the painted people move at night, and sometimes smoke. The adults don't believe it, but plenty has gone missing lately. You creep up at night, and sure enough, firelight flickers inside and the figures sway.
column3: 山脚有个浅洞，洞壁上满是古人画的岩画：猎人、黄羊、骑马的人。附近的孩子说，岩画里的人夜里会动，还会冒烟。大人们不信，可最近确实丢了不少东西。你们夜里摸过去，洞里果然有火光，岩画上的人影一晃一晃。

column2: It was a gang of sand bandits dividing loot, their fire making the paintings dance. They run. Looking closely by torchlight, you find a newer painting beside the ancient hunters: a long line of little figures, hand in hand, walking west. Exactly three hundred. The last one looks back, holding a book.
column3: 是一伙沙匪躲在洞里分赃，火光把岩画照得像在动。沙匪跑了，你们举着火把细看，古人的猎手旁边多了一长串新画的小人，一个牵一个往西走，数下来正好三百。最后一个小人回过头，手里拿着一本书。

column2: False Beacon
column3: 乱烽墩

column2: A beacon tower by the wall sends up wolf-smoke every few days. The garrison has rushed out several times, always to find nothing. A gang of rogue soldiers holds the tower, lighting false alarms to draw the garrison off while they loot the shops below. The garrison no longer trusts this beacon; they call it 'the boy who cried wolf'.
column3: 长城边的一座烽火台，三天两头冒狼烟，关里的守军跑来好几趟，每次都扑个空。原来是一伙兵痞占了烽台，点假烽火把守军引走，再去抢关下的商铺。守军已经不信这座烽台了，说它是「放羊的孩子」。

column2: The soldiers are driven off. The old beacon keeper says the last true fire here was ten years ago: when the Qianli caravan left, the court had every beacon light a fire of safe passage, relayed tower to tower all the way to Yangguan. 'Whoever was at Yangguan knew they were coming.' You light one honest fire, and it passes west.
column3: 兵痞被赶下了烽台。老烽卒说，这座烽台上一次点真火是十年前：千里号出关，朝廷让沿路烽燧一站站点平安火送他们，一直传到阳关。「阳关那头的人，那时候就知道他们要来了。」你们又点了一把真火，往西传去。

column2: Unfinished Game
column3: 残棋坡

column2: A chessboard is carved into a flat rock on the slope, pieces half set out. The bandit chief here is chess-mad: he doesn't rob captives, he makes them play. Win and pass; lose and leave your baggage. But this one game nobody may touch. Ten years ago a merchant with an abacus played him to this point and said, 'We'll finish when I'm back.' He polishes the board every day.
column3: 坡上一块平石刻着棋盘，棋子摆了一半。一伙沙匪的头领是个棋痴，抓了过路人不抢东西，只逼着下棋，赢了放行，输了留下行李。可这盘棋他不许人碰：十年前一个拿算盘的商人跟他下到这里，说「回来再下完」。他天天擦这盘棋。

column2: The chief loses and shows you the unfinished game with a sigh. 'That bookkeeper played beautifully, but this one move he miscalculated: gave up his chariot, and everything after was lost. I asked if he'd overlooked it. He said no. He'd got his sums wrong.' He bags the pieces and hands them to you. 'Ask him for me whether he's worked it out yet.'
column3: 头领输了，带你们看那盘残棋，叹口气：「那账房棋下得极好，偏偏这一步算错了，弃了车，后面全是死局。我问他是不是看走眼了，他说不是看走眼，是算错了账。」他把棋子收进袋子交给你们：「替我问问他，现在算明白没有。」

column2: Reed Bend Powder Cellar
column3: 芦湾火药窖

column2: In the reeds at a bend of the Shule River lies a cellar guarded by a bully's crack household troops; sparks are often seen at its mouth at night. Inside are twenty crates of fireworks, bought ten years ago by the merchants' guild inside the pass, to be set off by the river the day the Qianli caravan came home. The bully plans to strip out the powder and sell it to the bandits.
column3: 疏勒河拐弯处的芦苇荡里藏着一个地窖，一个恶霸养了一队精锐护院守着，夜里常有人看见窖口冒火星。窖里存着二十箱烟花，是十年前关里的商会凑钱买的，说好千里号回来那天在河边放。恶霸打算把烟花拆了，取火药去卖给沙匪。

column2: The guards are broken up. All twenty crates are intact, each pasted with red paper: 'To be lit on the day the Qianli caravan returns in triumph', faded now to pink. You reseal them and take one crate along. Someday you'll need it.
column3: 护院们被打散了。二十箱烟花一箱没少，箱上贴着红纸：「千里号凯旋之日燃放」，纸都褪成了粉色。你们把箱子重新封好，留了一箱带在身上。总有一天用得上。

column2: Stage Slope
column3: 戏台坡

column2: A makeshift stage stands at the foot of the slope, and a travelling opera troupe is caught between two gangs of sand bandits. The eastern gang demands 'The Qianli Caravan Leaves the Pass'; the western gang insists on 'The Qianli Caravan Meets a Ghost'. Sing the wrong one and your trunks get smashed. The troupe master, sweating, says they're really one play; it's just that nobody knows the ending.
column3: 坡下搭着一座草台，一个走江湖的戏班被两伙沙匪夹在中间：东边的要他们唱《千里号出关》，西边的偏要听《千里号遇鬼》，谁唱错了一出就砸谁的箱子。班主急得满头汗，说这两出戏其实是一出，只是没人知道结尾。

column2: Both gangs are driven off. The troupe master grabs your sleeve: 'You're going west to find them, aren't you? When you do, come back and tell us the ending.' The troupe will keep performing the first half, he says, until someone brings back the second.
column3: 两伙沙匪都被打跑了。班主拉着你们问：「你们是往西去找他们的吧？找到了，回来告诉我们结尾。」他说戏班会一直唱前半出，唱到有人把后半出带回来为止。

column2: Reed Flat
column3: 芦花滩

column2: Reeds line the Shule River here, plumes white as snow. The old ferryman has a daughter who poles a boat steadier than any man. For months someone has been cutting the tow rope from underwater at midstream, and passengers say a water ghost lives in the river. The daughter doesn't believe it and hides in the reeds at night to see one.
column3: 疏勒河边一片芦苇，芦花白得像雪。摆渡的老汉有个闺女，撑船比男人还稳。这几个月船过河心时总有人从水下割断缆绳，渡客都说河里有水鬼。闺女不信邪，夜里守在芦苇荡里，要看看水鬼长什么样。

column2: You drag out the 'ghosts': sand bandits breathing through reed straws. The daughter cracks the leader on the head with her pole. When she was eight, she says, she helped her father ferry the Qianli caravan across, and a bookkeeper gave her a sweet instead of the fare: 'I owe you. Two when I'm back.' 'I don't care about sweets any more,' she pouts. 'But he has to come back.'
column3: 水鬼被揪了出来：几个叼着芦管潜水的沙匪。闺女一篙子敲在为首那个的脑门上。她说她八岁那年，帮爹撑船送千里号过河，有个账房先生没给她船钱，给了她一颗糖，说「先欠着，回来给你两颗」。「我现在吃糖不稀罕了，」她撇撇嘴，「可他得回来。」

column2: Shule Ferry Market
column3: 疏勒官渡

column2: The only official ferry on the Shule River. The east bank has quarries, the west bank tamarisk woods, and the two used to trade across the water: stone going west, timber coming back. Now sand bandits hold the landing, the ferries are moored by their stockade and the official scale lies at the bottom of the river. For half a year the banks have shouted across the water without a single deal.
column3: 疏勒河上唯一的官渡，河东是采石场，河西是红柳林，从前两岸隔河做买卖：东岸的石料过河，西岸的木料回来。如今渡口被一伙沙匪霸着，渡船拴在他们的营寨边，官秤被扔进了河里。两岸的人隔着水喊了半年，一笔生意也做不成。

column2: The bandits are driven into the river and the ferries run again. The old ferryman fishes up the scale and trade resumes: stone west, timber back. He opens the ferry register at a line from ten years ago: 'Qianli caravan. 300 people. Fare owed, to be paid later.' All the way from Yumen to here, the bookkeeper's IOUs line the road, every one saying 'to be paid later'. 'He wrote down everything he owed,' says the ferryman. 'But where's his own ledger?'
column3: 沙匪被赶下了河，渡船重新开动。老渡工从河底捞起官秤，两岸的生意重新做了起来：石料过河，木料回来。他翻出渡簿，指着十年前的一行字：「千里号，三百人，渡资欠，后补。」那一路，账房先生留下的欠条从玉门一直排到了这里，每一张都写着「后补」。老渡工说：「他欠的都记着，可他自己的账本呢？」

column2: Buddha Head Hollow
column3: 佛首洼

column2: In a hollow lies a stone Buddha head taller than a man, flakes of gold leaf still on one cheek. A troop of fierce desert raiders dragged it out of a ruined temple to the north and is rolling it away inch by inch on logs to sell to a rich family inside the pass; they've stuffed their ration bags into its ears. A few old monks followed for thirty li, and are held off by arrows at the rim.
column3: 洼地里躺着一颗一人多高的石佛头，半边脸还贴着剥落的金箔。一队凶悍的大漠响马把它从北边的废寺里拖了出来，用木滚子一寸寸往外运，说是要卖给关里的富户，佛头的耳朵里塞着他们的干粮袋。几个老和尚追了三十里，被箭逼在洼外。

column2: The raiders scatter and the monks chant around the head. Set into a hollow at the back of it is a wooden tablet: 'The three hundred of the Qianli caravan vow: on our return, the Buddha shall be gilded anew.' The bookkeeper paid half the gold then, the monks say, and wrote an IOU for the rest: 'payable on return'. You help them carry the head home.
column3: 响马被打散了，老和尚们围着佛头念经。佛头后脑的凹槽里嵌着一块木牌：「千里号三百人许愿：归时重塑金身。」老和尚说，那账房先生当年先付了一半的金子，另一半写了欠条，「归时付」。你们帮着把佛头运回了寺里。

column2: Racing Flat
column3: 赛马滩

column2: On the gravel flat a band of raiders blocks the road and challenges you to a race. The stake is the road itself: win and you may pass; lose and you leave every last parcel. Their leader is a lean young man on a chestnut whose saddle is carved with a number: 117. It's his father's number, he says. He races for money so he can go west and find him.
column3: 砾石滩上，一伙响马拦着路要跟你们赛马，赌注是这条路：你们赢了，路归你们走；输了，留下全部货物。领头的是个精瘦的年轻人，骑一匹枣红马，马鞍上刻着一个数「一百一十七」。他说这是他爹的号，他赛马攒钱，是要往西去找爹。

column2: His men are scattered and the race never happens. The young man hangs his head: ten years ago the bookkeeper gave everyone in the caravan a number, and his father was 117, who carved it on this saddle before he left. 'Three hundred numbers in all,' he says. 'They say number three hundred was the bookkeeper himself.'
column3: 他的人被你们打散，比赛也就不了了之。年轻人垂着头说，十年前账房先生给商队里每个人编了号，他爹是第一百一十七号，走前把号刻在马鞍上留给他。「一共三百号，」他说，「听说第三百号是账房自己。」

column2: Wall Garrison Fort
column3: 长城戍堡

column2: A small fort at the foot of the wall whose real garrison was transferred long ago. A gang of rogue soldiers wears their old uniforms and poses as the garrison: drawing ghost pay by day, letting smugglers through by night. Not a grain goes to the families nearby, and they've even used the fort's old logbook to prop up a table leg.
column3: 长城脚下的一座小戍堡，真正的戍卒早就被调走了。一伙兵痞穿上他们留下的旧号衣，冒充守军，白天吃空饷，晚上开堡门放私货过关。堡里的粮仓一粒米都不给附近的人家，连堡里那本旧戍簿都被他们拿去垫了桌脚。

column2: The impostors are thrown out and the grain goes to the soldiers' widows. You pull the logbook out from under the table leg. An entry from ten years ago: 'Qianli caravan passed the wall. 299 mounted; one on foot at the rear, abacus in hand, counting aloud. Asked why, he said: I need to know how long this road is.'
column3: 冒牌守军被赶了出去，粮仓分给了戍卒遗孀。你们从桌脚下抽出那本戍簿，十年前的一条写着：「千里号过墙，二百九十九人骑驼，一人步行在后，手持算盘，口中数数。问之，答曰：我要知道这条路有多长。」

column2: Under the impostors' bedrolls: over two hundred catties of army grain, a jar of bootleg liquor, a dozen forged badges, and a list of every cartload of contraband they let through.
column3: 兵痞的铺盖下面翻出了二百多斤军粮、一坛私酒、十几块伪造的腰牌，还有一本私货清单，记着他们放过关的每一车货。

column2: The soldiers' widows bring out dried yoghurt and roasted barley flour whenever your column appears, and press hand-stitched cloth shoes on you: frontier stones are hard on shoes, they say.
column3: 戍卒的遗孀们一见你们的人马就端出酸奶疙瘩和炒面，还硬塞几双纳好的布鞋，说关外的石头费鞋。

column2: Forged IOU Shop
column3: 假欠条铺

column2: A mud hut by the old road hangs a sign: 'Documents Written'. Inside, a gang of sand-bandit blades keeps a scribe who deserted from the border army, forging 'Qianli caravan IOUs'. Since word spread that the court has sent pioneers out, everyone says the court will pay the caravan's debts, and a forged IOU sells for five taels. The buyers are queuing to cash them with you.
column3: 古道边一间土屋挂着「代写文书」的招牌。屋里一伙沙匪刀手养着一个从边军逃出来的书手，专门伪造「千里号欠条」：朝廷派了开拓队出关的消息一传开，人人都说朝廷要替千里号还债，一张欠条能卖五两银子。买了假条的人排着队等你们来兑。

column2: The blades run off and the trembling scribe hands over a botched abacus seal. He copied it from a real IOU, he says, but on the real seal the third rod of the abacus is missing a bead. He thought the seal was damaged and added it back. 'Adding it is what made mine fake.' The missing bead looks like a mark the bookkeeper left on purpose.
column3: 刀手们跑了，书手哆嗦着交出一枚刻坏了的算盘印。他说他照着一张真欠条刻的，可真的那枚印上，算盘第三档少了一颗珠子，他以为是印坏了，就给补上了。「补上了，反倒成了假的。」那颗少了的珠子，像是账房故意留的记号。

column2: Matchmaker's Tower
column3: 媒婆墩

column2: A fat matchmaker lives under a tower by the wall, running a nasty racket with a few rogue soldiers: she goes door to door to the wives of Qianli caravan men, saying 'they died in the sand long ago', pressing them to remarry, and pocketing a fee from the grooms. Those who refuse get their doors smashed. Today it's the wife of number fifty-eight, who blocks her doorway with a broom.
column3: 长城边的墩台下住着个胖媒婆，带着几个兵痞做一门缺德生意：挨家挨户找千里号伙计的老婆，说「人早死在沙里了」，逼她们改嫁，收男方的谢媒钱。不肯改嫁的，兵痞就去砸门。今天她们找上的是第五十八号的媳妇，那媳妇抄着扫帚堵在门口。

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the matchmaker is chased three li by a troop of wives with brooms. Number fifty-eight's wife, panting, says the bookkeeper visited every household back then and told each the same thing: 'If the men can't come back, the accounts will. Every coin of their wages.' 'He was a man of his word,' she says. 'So I'm waiting for his accounts.'
column3: 兵痞被打跑，媒婆被一群媳妇拿扫帚追出了三里地。五十八号的媳妇喘着气说，当年账房先生挨家挨户上门，跟每一家都说过同一句话：「人要是回不来，账也一定回来，工钱一文不少。」「他说话算数，」她说，「我就等他的账。」

column2: Old Tent Camp
column3: 旧帐营

column2: On the edge of the desert sprawls a great camp of fifty tents, the biggest sand-bandit lair around. Oddly, the tents are far finer than the bandits' clothes: thick camel-hair felt trimmed in blue, door flaps embroidered with a faded Qian. The bandits say they found them pitched and ready, with nobody in them.
column3: 沙漠边缘扎着一座大营，五十顶帐篷连成一片，是这一带最大的沙匪窝。奇怪的是，这些帐篷的料子比沙匪身上的衣服好得多：厚实的驼毛毡，镶着蓝边，门帘上绣着褪了色的「千」字。沙匪们说帐篷是捡来的，捡来时搭得好好的，一个人也没有。

column2: You overturn the camp. Each tent has six berths: fifty tents, three hundred exactly, each with a numbered tag. The Qianli caravan pitched this as a camp for the journey home before entering the desert. Two hundred and ninety-nine berths were slept in. Only number three hundred's bedroll is still neatly rolled, never opened, with a slip tucked under it: 'Accounts unsettled. No sleep.'
column3: 大营被掀翻了。你们细看，每顶帐篷六个铺位，五十顶正好三百，每个铺位上钉着一个号牌。这是千里号进沙漠前搭好留下的回程营地。二百九十九个铺位都睡过，只有第三百号的铺盖卷得整整齐齐，从没打开过，上面压着一张条子：「账未清，不睡。」

column2: Treasure Pits
column3: 掘宝坑

column2: The sand is pocked with pits, some big enough to bury an ox. A gang of sand bandits paid thirty taels for 'a torn page of the Qianli ledger', said to record where the caravan buried its silver, and has dug by it for two months, turning up only sand and a dead scorpion. Now they're press-ganging passers-by to dig, promising a tenth of the treasure.
column3: 沙地上到处是坑，大的能埋一头牛。一伙沙匪花三十两银子买了一张「千里号账本残页」，说上面记着商队埋银子的地方，照着挖了两个月，只挖出沙子和一只死蝎子。他们还把路过的人抓来帮着挖，说挖到了分一成。

column2: The captives are freed. You look over the 'ledger page': it plainly shows the city-god temple of some county town inside the pass. The bandits sit stunned at the bottom of their pit. Everyone beyond the pass is hunting that ledger now, their leader says: some say it records silver, some say debts, some say where the three hundred went.
column3: 被抓来的人放了，你们拿过那张残页一看，画的分明是关里某个县城的城隍庙。沙匪们坐在坑底愣了半天。领头的说，关外现在人人都在找那本账本：有人说里面记着银子，有人说记着欠债，有人说记着三百个人的下落。

column2: Buried Bell Gully
column3: 埋钟沟

column2: In a deep gully a gang of sand bandits is digging up a great bronze bell buried in the sand, convinced it's gold. The old folk of the nearby villages kneel at the edge begging them to stop: three hundred families pooled their copper to cast it ten years ago, to be rung the day the caravan came home, and buried it later for fear of thieves. Half of it is exposed already, covered in writing.
column3: 一条深沟里，一伙沙匪正挖着一口埋在沙下的大铜钟，以为是金子铸的。附近村子的老人们跪在沟边求他们住手：这口钟是十年前三百户人家凑铜铸的，说好商队回来那天敲，后来怕被抢，就埋了。钟已经露出半边，上面密密麻麻全是字。

column2: The bandits are driven off. The bell is cast with two hundred and ninety-nine names; the last space holds only the word 'Bookkeeper'. When the bell was cast, the old folk say, not one of the three hundred families knew the bookkeeper's name. He never told anyone. You help them bury it again.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。钟身上铸着二百九十九个名字，最后一格空着，只铸了「账房」两个字。老人们说，铸钟的时候，三百户人家谁也不知道账房先生叫什么，他从来没跟人说过。你们帮着把钟重新埋好。

column2: Ghost Tax Shoal
column3: 鬼税滩

column2: By the river a 'ghost tax collector' appears only at night, white-faced in a blue robe with a green lantern, stopping travellers to collect a 'homeward duty' and moaning: 'The Qianli caravan's homeward duty. You pay it for them.' Terrified travellers drop their coins and run. A large gang of rogue soldiers hides in the reeds, waiting to collect.
column3: 河边有个夜里才出现的「鬼税吏」，白脸、青袍，提着一盏绿灯笼，拦住夜行人收「回程税」，嘴里念叨：「千里号的回程税，你替他们交了吧。」过路人吓得丢下钱就跑。一大伙兵痞躲在芦苇里，等着收钱。

column2: The ghost's white face is flour, and the soldiers are routed. The real old tax collector is alive, living by the bend, and shows you a 'duty waiver' he wrote ten years ago: on the day the Qianli caravan returns, this ford charges no duty. 'I wrote it and waited for them,' he says. 'Never thought someone would play ghost with it.' And he mentions an old squad leader at a lonely beacon to the north, who escorted the caravan part of the way.
column3: 鬼税吏的白脸是抹的面粉。真正的老税吏住在河湾，拿出一张十年前写好的「免税帖」：千里号回程之日，此渡免税。「我写好了等他们，没想到有人拿它装鬼。」他说北边孤烽燧有个老伍长，当年押送过千里号一段路。

column2: Singing Dune
column3: 鸣沙丘

column2: When the wind blows, this dune 'sings', a fine clattering like someone flicking abacus beads. The locals say the Qianli ledger is buried beneath it, and the bookkeeper is still down there doing his sums. A gang of sand bandits believed it, has dug the dune full of holes, and when a hole collapses they grab passers-by to keep digging.
column3: 这座沙丘一刮风就会「唱歌」，声音细细碎碎，像有人在拨算盘珠子。附近的人说，千里号的账本就埋在这座沙丘底下，账房在下面还在算账。一伙沙匪信了，在沙丘上挖得千疮百孔，挖塌了就把路过的人抓来接着挖。

column2: You dig the bandits out of the sand. There's nothing under the dune. But when the wind blows, the sand still clicks and clatters. An old herder says the dune has always sung like this. It's just that before ten years ago people heard drums in it, and since then everyone hears an abacus.
column3: 沙匪被你们从沙子里刨了出来，沙丘下面什么都没有。可风一吹，沙子照样「噼啪噼啪」地响。一个老牧人说，这沙丘一直这么唱，只是十年前以前，大家听着像打鼓，十年后，听着都像算盘了。

column2: Twins' Shallows
column3: 双头滩

column2: A rope divides the riverbank in two: a gang of sand bandits on the east half, another on the west. Their chiefs are identical twins who hate each other to the bone. Their father was the Qianli caravan's guide, and before he left he told each son half a sentence. For ten years the brothers have fought over whose half matters more.
column3: 河滩被一条绳子从中间分成两半，东半边一伙沙匪，西半边一伙沙匪，两个头领是一对双胞胎，长得一模一样，恨对方恨得要命。他们的爹是千里号的向导，临走前跟两个儿子各说了半句话，两兄弟为了谁听的那半句更要紧，打了十年。

column2: Both gangs are flattened, and you sit the brothers down together and make each say his half. The elder: 'If the bookkeeper doesn't come back...' The younger: '...go to Yangguan and ask the one-eyed man.' The brothers stare at each other a long time, and for the first time in ten years, sit side by side.
column3: 两伙人都被打趴下了，你们把两兄弟按在一起，让他们各说半句。哥哥说：「账房先生要是没回来……」弟弟说：「……就去阳关问那个独眼的。」两兄弟愣了半天，十年来头一回坐到了一起。

column2: Sand Fox Ridge
column3: 沙狐岭

column2: The moment the ridge village sees your banner, every man, woman and child pours out with hoes and carrying poles, blocking the road and shouting: 'Hand over the ledger!' A gang of sand bandits got here first and spread word that the pioneers are carrying the Qianli ledger, whipping the villagers into a fight while they hide behind, waiting to pick over the leftovers.
column3: 岭上的村子一见你们的旗子，男女老少拿着锄头扁担全涌了出来，堵在路口喊：「账本拿来！」原来一伙沙匪提前放出风声，说开拓队身上带着千里号的账本，逼着村里人跟你们拼命，沙匪自己躲在后面等着捡便宜。

column2: The bandits are dragged out and the villagers lower their hoes. The headman explains, red-faced: ten years ago the bookkeeper borrowed forty sacks of grain here, wrote a receipt, and said, 'It's in the ledger. Someone will come to repay it.' The village wants the ledger not to collect a debt, but to see whether that entry was ever written. You promise: find the ledger, and you'll come back to check the accounts together.
column3: 沙匪被揪了出来，村里人放下了锄头。村长红着脸解释：十年前千里号路过，账房先生借了村里四十袋粮，写了借据，说「账本上记着，日后有人来还」。村里人要账本，不是要讨债，是想看看那一笔到底记上没有。你们答应他们，找到账本，一定回来对账。

column2: Water Clock Pavilion
column3: 漏刻亭

column2: In a small pavilion by the river stands a bronze water clock, dripping drop by drop; for ten years the old keeper has topped it up and logged the hours every day. A few days ago a gang of sand bandits smashed it and stole a sealed iron box he'd hidden in a pillar. He sits among the broken bronze saying over and over: 'It falls due this year. It falls due.'
column3: 河边一座小亭子里立着一架铜漏壶，水一滴一滴往下漏，守亭的老人十年来天天添水、天天记时辰。前几天一伙沙匪砸了漏壶，抢了老人藏在亭柱里的一只封口铁盒。老人坐在一地碎铜里，一遍遍地说：「今年就到期了，就到期了。」

column2: You recover the box, unopened. Ten years ago, the old man says, the bookkeeper asked him to keep this clock running and open the box when ten years were up. Inside is a single sheet: 'Number 300: name to be filled in by himself once the accounts are settled.' The bookkeeper wouldn't even write his own name until his sums came out right, the old man says. 'Ten years are up. He ought to come back and write it.'
column3: 铁盒抢回来了，沙匪没打开过。老人说，十年前账房先生托他守这架漏壶，满十年就开盒。盒里只有一张纸：「第三百号：姓名待账清后自填。」老人说，账房先生连自己的名字都要算清了才肯写，「十年满了，他也该回来填了。」

column2: Braying Hollow
column3: 驴鸣洼

column2: A hundred donkeys are tethered in the hollow, and when they bray together it hurts your ears. They belong to villagers who pooled their money to go west themselves and find the Qianli ledger, to check their own accounts against it. Barely out of the village they were waylaid by rogue soldiers, who led every donkey here to sell inside the pass.
column3: 洼地里拴着上百头驴，一齐叫起来震得人耳朵疼。驴的主人是附近村子的人，他们凑了钱，打算自己赶着驴去西边找千里号的账本，好对一对自家的账。刚出村就被一伙兵痞截了，驴全被牵到这里，要拉去关里卖。

column2: The soldiers are beaten off and the donkeys untied. The villagers thank you warmly but have lost heart: 'The west is too far. We'd never make it.' They press half their travel money on you and ask you to take one look at the ledger for them when you find it. The donkeys walk home in a line on their own.
column3: 兵痞被打跑了，驴一头头解了缰绳。村里人谢了又谢，却也泄了气：「西边太远了，我们走不到。」他们把凑的路费塞给你们一半，说找到账本，替他们看一眼。驴不用人赶，自己排着队往家走。

column2: Gourd-Mask Camp
column3: 葫芦营

column2: These figures wear hollowed gourds painted with green fangs and call themselves 'the ghosts of the Qianli caravan'. At night they visit the villages demanding offerings: the three hundred dead have come home hungry, they say. The villagers, frightened and heartbroken, actually set out offering tables. By daylight, a few gourds still say 'Wang Family Melon Patch'.
column3: 这伙人脸上扣着挖了洞的葫芦瓢，画着青面獠牙，自称「千里号的鬼」，夜里到附近村子里讨供品，说是三百个死鬼回来要吃的。村里人又怕又心疼，真的摆了供桌。白天一看，有几个葫芦上还写着「王家瓜田」。

column2: Shattered gourds everywhere, and under them, half-grown boys. Their leader sobs that his father was number eighty-eight, and he played ghost hoping his father might come back as one too, looking for him. You hand them over to the village elders, who don't beat them, but give them all the cakes from the offering tables.
column3: 葫芦瓢碎了一地，底下都是半大小子。领头的那个哭着说，他爹是第八十八号，他扮鬼是想看看，爹会不会也扮成鬼回来找他。你们把他们交给村里的长辈，长辈们没打他们，把供桌上的饼都给了他们。

column2: Kneeling Camel Flat
column3: 跪驼滩

column2: Rows of white camel skeletons lie on the sand, more than a hundred, every one kneeling, heads to the southwest, perfectly aligned, as if waiting for someone. A band of desert raiders has camped among them, burning bones for fuel and saying even ghosts won't come here. But they can't sleep at night, and keep hearing bells inside the bones.
column3: 沙滩上一排排白森森的骆驼骨，有一百多具，全是跪着的姿势，头朝西南，整整齐齐，像在等谁。一伙大漠响马在骨堆中间扎营，正拿骨头当柴烧，说这地方鬼都不敢来。可他们夜里睡不着，总说听见骨头里有铃响。

column2: The raiders leave faster than they came. Every saddle-bone is branded Qian and Yangguan, and they kneel facing the old Yangguan fort. The lead skeleton's saddle-bone also bears a line of tiny carving: 'The ledger stays on me. While I live, the ledger lives.' So the ledger never left the bookkeeper's side.
column3: 响马们跑得比来时还快。每具骨架的鞍骨上都烙着「千」字和「阳关」。它们跪着的方向，正是阳关故垒。领头那具骨架的鞍骨上还刻着一行小字：「账本随身，人在账在。」原来那本账，从来没离开过账房先生的身边。

column2: Answering Rock
column3: 答问石

column2: A cluster of wind-sculpted boulders stands in the sand, and legend says if you ask a question into the cracks, the rock answers, only always wrongly: ask east, it says west; ask about today, it answers tomorrow. A gang of sand bandits has set up an offering table and charges ledger-hunters a tael per question.
column3: 几块被风削得奇形怪状的大石头立在沙里，传说对着石缝问话，石头会回答，只是答得总不对：问东答西，问今天答明天。一伙沙匪在石头旁边摆了供桌，向找账本的人收「问石钱」，一问一两银子。

column2: The bandits are run off, and you drag a skinny man out of the cracks, the one who did the answering. Out of curiosity you ask the rock yourself: 'Where is the ledger?' Wind moans through the holes in reply, and it sounds like 'Yangguan'. 'That one,' whispers the skinny man, 'wasn't me.'
column3: 沙匪被打跑了，石缝里还揪出来一个负责回答的瘦子。你们不信邪，自己对着石缝问了一句：「账本在哪？」风从石洞里穿过去，呜呜地答了一声，听着像「阳关」。瘦子在旁边小声说：「这句不是我答的。」

column2: Uyghur Fur Tent
column3: 回鹘皮帐

column2: An old Uyghur fur buyer has a tent piled with fox and wolf pelts. He wraps them not with twine but with old pages covered in writing, found in an abandoned beacon tower. Lately some rogue soldiers ransack his tent daily, convinced the pages are the Qianli ledger, taking furs for free and grabbing the paper too. His tent is nearly torn apart.
column3: 一个收皮子的回鹘老汉，帐子里堆满了狐皮、狼皮。他包皮子不用麻绳，用一页页写满字的旧纸，是从一座废烽燧里捡来的。最近几个兵痞天天来翻他的帐子，咬定那些旧纸就是千里号的账本，皮子白拿，纸也抢，老汉的帐子快被拆光了。

column2: The soldiers are beaten so badly they'll never be back, and the old man pitches his tent again, glad to trade furs with you. The pages aren't the ledger at all, but a garrison soldier's diary in crooked writing: 'Alone on the tower again today.' The rest, he says, blew down to the river, where some sand bandits picked them up for kindling.
column3: 兵痞被打得再也不敢来了，老汉重新支起帐子，愿意跟你们换皮货。那几页旧纸根本不是账本，是一个戍卒的日记，字迹歪歪扭扭：「今日又是一个人守墩。」老汉说，剩下的纸被风刮到河边，让一伙沙匪捡去引火了。

column2: Numbered Tamarisks
column3: 号树坡

column2: A line of tamarisks once grew along this slope, one every li, each trunk hung with a small wooden tag bearing a number. A gang of rogue soldiers has been cutting them down for charcoal kilns and throwing the tags on the ground. The locals say the Qianli caravan's people planted them by hand, one each, to find their way home. Smoke pours from the kilns; they've cut past number two hundred.
column3: 坡上原本长着一行红柳，一里一株，每株的树干上都挂着一块小木牌，写着一个号。一伙兵痞砍了红柳垒窑烧炭，木牌扔了一地。附近的人说，这是千里号的人亲手种的，每人一株，回来时好认路。窑口浓烟滚滚，已经砍到第二百多号了。

column2: The kilns are knocked down and the soldiers sentenced to replant, hanging each tag back on its bush. At the very end, at number three hundred, you find only a dug hole where no tree was ever planted, and beside it a sharpened stick reading: 'To be planted on the way home.'
column3: 窑被推倒了，兵痞们被罚去补种，种一株挂回一块牌。补到最后，你们发现第三百号那里只有一个挖好的坑，从来没种过树，坑边插着一根削尖的树枝，上面写着：「回程时种。」

column2: Shrine Under the Wall
column3: 墙下庙

column2: At the foot of the wall stands a tiny shrine to Lord Guan, kept by a lame old monk, stubborn and stingy, who collects the temple's debts and will chase a debtor to the ends of the earth for unpaid incense money. A gang of rogue soldiers has turned the shrine into a stable, splattering Lord Guan's face with dung. The old monk chased them with his account book demanding 'stable fees' and got kicked to the ground.
column3: 长城根下有一座小小的关帝庙，庙祝是个瘸腿的老和尚，脾气又倔又抠，专替庙里讨债，谁欠了香火钱，追到天边也要讨回来。一伙兵痞把庙当了马棚，关公像脸上溅了马粪，老和尚拿着账簿追着他们要「马棚钱」，被一脚踹倒在地。

column2: The soldiers are thrown out and the old monk cleans the statue, then shows you his account book: 'Qianli caravan, 300 safe-passage charms, 299 collected.' The bookkeeper refused his own, saying, 'My safety I'll pray for once the accounts are settled.' The monk sniffs. 'He still owes me for one charm.'
column3: 兵痞被赶了出去，老和尚擦干净神像，翻开账簿给你们看：「千里号，平安符三百张，已取二百九十九张。」账房先生当年不肯要自己那一张，说「我的平安，等账清了再来求」。老和尚哼了一声：「欠着我一张符钱呢。」

column2: Red Lady's Camp
column3: 红娘子营

column2: In the desert a small caravan is surrounded by a large gang of sand bandits. Its leader is a woman in a red robe called the Red Lady, who rides up and down with her whip, ordering her men to circle the wagons. 'I'm after the ledger, not your lives!' she shouts. 'Out of my way!' The bandits jeer that a woman dares cross the frontier, and the arrows fly thicker.
column3: 沙漠里一支小商队被一大伙沙匪围住了。商队的头领是个穿红袍的女人，叫红娘子，骑着马挥着鞭子指挥伙计们把货车围成一圈。她冲沙匪喊：「我找的是账本，不是你们的命，让开！」沙匪笑她一个女人也敢走关外，箭越射越密。

column2: You break the bandits from outside. The Red Lady coils her whip and bows her thanks. Her father was the Qianli caravan's chief guide, she says, and for ten years everyone has said he led them astray. She means to find the ledger and see who really chose the route. 'See you in the Sand Sea,' she says, and rides west, in even more of a hurry than you.
column3: 沙匪被你们从外面冲散了。红娘子收起鞭子，抱拳道谢。她说她爹是千里号的头一号向导，十年来人人都说是她爹把商队领迷了路。她要找到账本，看看那一路的路线是谁定的。「沙海见。」她说完就往西去了，比你们还急。

column2: Wrestling Ground
column3: 摔跤场

column2: Five roads meet here, and every autumn the herders wrestle on this grassy flat. This year's prize is 'a page from the Qianli ledger', which a local bully claims he paid a fortune for. He has bet heavily against the champion Bater, and sent his thugs to seize Bater's mother to make him throw the match. Bater stands in the ring, fists clenched, motionless.
column3: 五条路在这里交汇，每年秋天牧民们在这片草滩上摔跤。今年的彩头是一页「千里号账本」，恶霸说是他花大价钱买来的。他押了大注赌头名巴特尔输，派家丁扣了巴特尔的老娘，逼他装输。巴特尔站在场中，攥着拳头一动不动。

column2: The thugs go down, the mother is freed, and Bater wins with a shoulder throw, then gives you the prize. It isn't the ledger, but a page from an old market register stamped 'Desert Border Market', recording a 'grain for timber' trade from ten years ago with an altered figure. That market lies in the desert to the southwest, Bater says, deserted these ten years.
column3: 家丁倒了，老娘救了出来，巴特尔一个过肩摔赢了头名，把那页纸送给你们。纸不是账本，是一页旧市簿，盖着「沙中互市」的印，记着十年前的一笔「以粮易木」，数目被涂改过。巴特尔说，那个互市就在西南的沙漠里，荒了十年。

column2: Wang Manor
column3: 王家庄

column2: A great walled manor belongs to Squire Wang, the district's biggest bully. When the Qianli caravan's men failed to return ten years ago, he went door to door with a stack of 'IOUs', claiming every one of the three hundred owed him money, and took their families' land piece by piece. Today he's taking the last plot from the family of number two hundred and six.
column3: 一座带围墙的大庄子，庄主王大户是这一带最大的恶霸。十年前千里号的人一去不回，他就拿着一摞「欠条」挨家上门，说那三百个伙计都欠他的钱，把他们家里的地一块块收进了自己名下。今天他又要收第二百零六号家的最后一块地。

column2: You breach the walls and burn Squire Wang's deeds along with his stack of fake IOUs, and the land of two hundred and ninety-nine families goes back to its owners. Did he ever take the bookkeeper's land, you ask? Squire Wang blinks. 'His? Nobody ever knew where his home was. It's as if he... never had one.'
column3: 庄墙被攻破了，王大户的地契和那摞假欠条一起烧了，二百九十九户人家的地都回了原主。你们问他有没有收过账房先生家的地，王大户愣了愣：「他家？谁也不知道他家在哪，他好像……就没有家。」

column2: Hawk Banner Hill
column3: 鹞旗岗

column2: A black banner flies on the dune crest, painted with a one-eyed hawk. Every bandit gang around pays tribute to 'the Hawk' at Yangguan, and this hill is where it's collected. A notice is posted below, and a few bandits are fretting over it: 'The Hawk commands: whoever obtains the Qianli ledger shall bring it to Yangguan as found, unread. Disobey and lose a hand.'
column3: 沙岗上插着一面黑旗，旗上画着一只独眼的鹞子。这一带的沙匪都向阳关的「鹞子」纳贡，这座岗子就是收贡的地方。岗下贴着一张告示，几个沙匪正对着它发愁：「鹞子令：凡得千里号之账者，原样送阳关，不许翻看，违者断手。」

column2: You tear down the banner and seize the tribute cart bound west. A captive says the Hawk issued this order as soon as talk of the ledger spread. People have brought him several fakes, and he throws each away after one glance at the cover: 'Not this one.' 'He's seen the real one,' the bandit says. 'He must have.'
column3: 黑旗被扯了下来，往西送的贡车截下了。被俘的沙匪说，自从关外传开了账本的事，鹞子就下了这道令。有人送去过好几本假的，鹞子只看一眼封皮就扔了：「不是这本。」「他见过真的，」那沙匪说，「他肯定见过。」

column2: Torn Page Ford
column3: 残页渡

column2: Following the old Uyghur's directions, you find a gang of sand bandits roasting fish by the river, and burning in their fire are the diary's pages. By the firelight you read one: 'The squad leader's token is still on me. Brothers, wait for me.' Another says 'escorted them to Yangguan', and a bandit is screwing it up to toss into the flames.
column3: 你们循着回鹘老汉的话找到河边，一伙沙匪正围着火堆烤鱼，火堆里烧的正是日记的纸页。你们隔着火光看见一页上写着：「伍长令还在我身上。兄弟们，等我。」另一页写着「送到阳关」四个字，一个沙匪正把它揉成团丢进火里。

column2: The bandits scatter and you snatch most of the diary from the fire. The last pages read: 'Ten years ago went west with the Qianli caravan. At Yangguan the one-eyed chief let the caravan into the Sand Sea but turned us five guards back. The bookkeeper said: I've done the sums, there's enough for the road ahead.' The final page is dated last month: 'The lone tower. Holding it alone. If anyone finds this, please come and see me.'
column3: 沙匪被打散，大半本日记抢了出来。最后几页写着：「随千里号至阳关，独眼的头领放商队入沙海，却把我们五个护卫赶了回来。账房说：我算过了，前头的路够走。」末一页是上个月的：「孤墩独守。拾得此书者，请来看看我。」

column2: Children's Toll
column3: 孩童关

column2: A gap in the wall has been taken over by a band of children who've built a 'checkpoint' of broken baskets: travellers must tell a story to pass, and a dull one won't do. But a few rogue soldiers stand behind them, using the children to stop people while they rifle through their bundles. The children have no idea; they think the uncles are helping them guard the gate.
column3: 长城的一个缺口被一群孩子占了，他们用破筐垒了个「关卡」，过路人得讲一个故事才放行，讲得不好听不许过。孩子们背后却站着几个兵痞，借着孩子们拦人，顺手翻人家的包袱。孩子们不知道，还以为那几个叔叔在帮他们守关。

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the furious children pelt them with clods. As thanks, the children tell you the best story they ever collected, from an old camel driver back from Yangguan: ten years ago, when the caravan reached Yangguan, the bookkeeper and a one-eyed chief shut themselves in and drank all night. Next day the caravan went into the Sand Sea, but the bookkeeper was still sitting in the doorway, doing his sums.
column3: 兵痞被赶走了，孩子们气得拿土块砸他们。作为谢礼，孩子们给你们讲了他们收过最好的故事：一个从阳关回来的老驼夫讲的，说十年前商队到了阳关，账房先生跟一个独眼的头领关起门喝了一夜酒，第二天，商队进了沙海，账房先生却还坐在门口算账。

column2: Horse Fair Flat
column3: 马市滩

column2: On the first of every month the herders hold a horse fair here. Today a large band of raiders has turned up, not to sell horses but to auction a locked sandalwood box which, they say, holds the Qianli ledger. Opening bid: a hundred horses. Several bandit gangs are bidding red-faced, the price is already at three hundred, and knives are about to come out.
column3: 每月初一，牧民们在这片滩上赶马市。今天马市上来了一大伙响马，不卖马，拍卖一只上了锁的檀木匣子，说里面就是千里号的账本，起价一百匹马。几伙沙匪争得面红耳赤，价钱已经叫到了三百匹，眼看就要动刀子。

column2: You scatter all the gangs at once and prise the box open: inside is an empty abacus frame, not a single bead. The seller says he bought it from an old underling at Yangguan. 'No ledger, but an abacus,' an old herder laughs. 'And where are the beads? Taken away one by one.'
column3: 你们把几伙人一起打散了，撬开匣子：里面是一把空算盘框子，珠子一颗都没有。卖家说这是从阳关一个老喽啰手里买来的。「账本没有，算盘倒有，」一个老牧民笑了，「算盘珠子呢？叫人一颗一颗拿走了。」

column2: Shadow Puppet Booth
column3: 皮影棚

column2: A shadow-puppet troupe has set up a booth beside the yurts to perform 'Three Hundred Leave the Pass', and the children watch without blinking. Halfway through, a gang of rogue soldiers bursts in: this play annoys the Hawk, they say, and word has come from Yangguan that whoever performs it again gets their trunks burned. The troupe master shields his chest of puppets from the brazier.
column3: 一个皮影戏班子在毡房边搭了个棚子，演《三百人出关》，娃娃们看得眼睛都不眨。演到一半，一伙兵痞冲进来，说这出戏惹鹞子不高兴，阳关那边传话来，谁再演就烧谁的箱子。班主抱着一箱皮影，挡在火盆前面。

column2: The soldiers are thrown out and the show goes on. Afterwards the master shows you one puppet: the bookkeeper, abacus in hand, his face left blank, no features carved. The man who made it had seen the bookkeeper, the master says, but couldn't remember his face for the life of him. 'Only that he always had his head down, counting.'
column3: 兵痞被打出了棚子，戏接着演。散场后班主拿出一个皮影：账房先生，手里一把算盘，脸却是空白的，没有刻五官。班主说刻这个皮影的人见过账房，可怎么也想不起他的脸，「只记得他一直低着头算。」

column2: Lizard Den
column3: 蜥蜴窝

column2: These sand bandits keep a great sand lizard as a guard dog, half as long as a man, with a tail that can knock you flat. They call it 'General'. It basks all day on a black hawk banner they stole from the Hawk: they were once his men, thrown out for secretly reading a 'ledger', and they got the lizard for fear he'd come after them.
column3: 这伙沙匪养了一条大沙蜥当看门狗，有半人长，尾巴一甩能把人抽倒，取名「将军」。它整天趴在一面黑色的鹞子旗上晒太阳，那面旗是沙匪们从鹞子那里偷出来的：他们原本是鹞子的手下，因为偷翻了一本「账本」被赶了出来，怕鹞子来找，才养了这条蜥蜴。

column2: The bandits run off, but General doesn't stir. A captive says the ledger they read was a fake, but the Hawk threw them out anyway: 'The ledger isn't for you to read. It's for its owner to bring back.' General eats a scrap of your meat and ambles off into the dunes.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了，「将军」却趴着没动。被俘的一个说，他们翻的那本是假的，可鹞子还是赶走了他们：「账本不是给你们看的，是给它的主人带回来的。」「将军」吃了你们一块肉，慢悠悠爬进了沙丘。

column2: Old Blade Noodle Shop
column3: 老刀面铺

column2: A noodle shop in the desert run by a retired executioner from inside the pass, whose knife cuts noodles finer than hair. A party of the Hawk's tribute collectors has taken it over, declaring this a tribute road and claiming three-tenths of every bowl. The old man says nothing and keeps sharpening his knife, brighter and brighter. It unnerves the collectors, but they still won't leave.
column3: 沙漠里一间面铺，掌柜是关里退下来的老刽子手，一手刀工切面切得比头发还细。一伙鹞子的收贡人占了面铺，说这里是贡道，每碗面抽三成。老掌柜不吭声，只是磨刀，越磨越亮，收贡人看着发毛，可还是不肯走。

column2: The collectors are driven off and the shop steams again. From under the stove the old man brings out a sheet: ten years ago the bookkeeper ate a bowl here, had no small change, and tore a page from his ledger as an IOU. It records a trade at the desert border market, stamped with the abacus seal missing one bead. 'Torn from the real ledger,' the old man says. 'The only one I'd trust.'
column3: 收贡人被打跑了。老掌柜从灶台底下摸出一张纸：十年前账房先生在这儿吃面没带碎钱，从账本上撕下一页当欠条。纸上记着沙中互市的一笔买卖，盖着少一颗珠子的算盘印。「真账本上撕的，」老掌柜说，「我只认这一张。」

column2: The collectors' chests yield thirty-odd sacks of flour, a dozen jars of vinegar, a cart of split firewood, and a tribute ledger noting the cut from every bowl, written in characters finer than the noodles.
column3: 收贡人的箱子里翻出三十多袋面粉、十几坛醋、一车劈好的柴，还有一本收贡账，记着每碗面抽的钱，字写得比面还细。

column2: The old man always boils you a big pot of noodles, cut hair-fine and drenched in sizzling chilli oil: 'Eat your fill before you go. A blade shouldn't work on an empty stomach.'
column3: 老掌柜每次都给你们下一大锅面，切得细细的，浇上滚油辣子，说：「吃饱了再走，刀不能空着肚子用。」

column2: Dry Well Platform
column3: 枯井台

column2: On an abandoned earth platform there's a dry well too deep to see the bottom, and at its mouth a wooden sign: 'The Hawk commands: nobody goes down this well.' A gang of sand bandits camps on the platform, but none dare go near: every night a moaning rises from below, like someone weeping, or calling out drill commands. They sleep with their hands over their ears.
column3: 一座废弃的土台上有一口枯井，深不见底，井口立着一块木牌：「鹞子令：此井不许下。」一伙沙匪在台上扎营，却没人敢靠近那口井：一到夜里，井底就传出呜呜的声音，像是有人在哭，又像是在喊口令。沙匪们捂着耳朵睡觉。

column2: The bandits are run off. You lie at the rim and listen all night: sometimes weeping, sometimes like a roll call, 'one, two, three'. A row of footholds is cut into the shaft, leading down into the dark. Why would the Hawk forbid anyone to go down? You decide to find out.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。你们趴在井口听了一夜，那声音一会儿像哭，一会儿又像「一、二、三」地点名。井壁上凿着一排脚窝，通到黑漆漆的井底。鹞子为什么不许人下去？你们决定下去看看。

column2: Kite Tower
column3: 风筝台

column2: On an earth platform in the sand, a gang of bandits is flying strings of black kites, cloth strips tied to their tails, drifting west on the wind. It's the Hawk's message tower: who's hunting the ledger, what banner they fly, how far they've come. A kite can carry it to Yangguan in a day. As you arrive, a new kite rises from the tower.
column3: 沙地上一座土台，台上一伙沙匪放着一串串黑风筝，风筝尾巴上拴着布条，顺风飘向西边。这是鹞子的传信台：谁家在找账本、谁带着什么旗子、走到了哪里，一只风筝一天就能报到阳关。你们刚到，台上就升起了一只新风筝。

column2: The kite flyers are scattered and you haul down the last kite. Its strip reads: 'The Qian banner has arrived, past Hawk Banner Hill.' Beside it lies another kite that drifted back from Yangguan with a one-line reply: 'Do not stop them. About the ledger, let them come and ask me.'
column3: 放风筝的沙匪被打散了，你们拽下了最后那只风筝。布条上写着：「千字旗到，已过鹞旗岗。」旁边是从阳关飘回来的另一只，回话只有一行：「不许拦。账的事，让他们来问我。」

column2: Cartwheel Fort
column3: 车轮寨

column2: A gang of sand bandits has broken up dozens of carts and stacked the wheels ring upon ring into a stockade, a hedgehog from afar. They used to be the Hawk's men, broke away recently and set up on their own. Inside they hold a lanky young underling called Xiao Chai, tied to a wheel in the sun for two days because he refused to join the revolt, his lips cracked.
column3: 一伙沙匪拆了几十辆大车，用车轮子一圈圈垒成寨墙，远看像一只刺猬。这伙人原是鹞子的手下，前些日子反了出来，自立山头。寨子里关着一个半大的小喽啰，叫小柴，因为不肯跟着反，被绑在车轮上晒了两天，嘴唇都裂了。

column2: The wheel wall comes down and Xiao Chai is untied. Only after half a skin of water can he speak. 'The Hawk's men have split in two. The old hands keep to his rules; the new lot want to take over while he's ill.' He knows the way to Yangguan and who stands where, he says, and offers to guide you.
column3: 车轮墙被推倒了，小柴解了绑，喝了半囊水才开口：「鹞子的人现在分成了两拨，老弟兄守着他的规矩，新来的想趁他病了翻天。」他说他知道阳关的路，也知道谁站哪一边，愿意给你们带路。

column2: Old Border Market
column3: 互市旧址

column2: A crumbling mud-walled town in the desert, once the border market where eastern timber and western grain changed hands. Deserted ten years, it's all roofless warehouses and a leaning flagpole. A large gang of sand bandits has taken it over, stabling horses in the warehouses, gambling in the clerk's office, and pasting the market register's pages over the windows one by one.
column3: 沙漠中一片残破的土城，从前是关内外互市的地方：东边的木料、西边的粮食在这里交易。互市荒了十年，只剩塌了顶的货栈和一根歪倒的市旗杆。一大伙沙匪占了这里，把货栈当马棚，把市令的衙门当赌场，市簿被撕得一页一页糊了窗户。

column2: The bandits are driven out, the market flag rises, timber and grain merchants trickle in, and the market reopens: timber for grain, twelve thousand catties a day. You peel the register pages off the windows and find an entry from ten years ago: 'Qianli caravan, grain for timber.' The torn ledger page from the noodle shop fits its missing corner exactly, and side by side they show it: the bookkeeper got this sum wrong, a whole cartload of grain short. The figure was corrected in darker ink, as if he noticed later. He went into the road ahead with too little grain.
column3: 沙匪被逐出土城，市旗重新升起，木商和粮商陆续赶来，互市重开：拿木料换粮食，一天一万二千斤。你们从窗纸上揭下市簿，找到十年前的一笔：「千里号，以粮易木。」老面铺那页账本残页正好补上缺的一角，两边一对：账房在这一笔上算错了，少算了一整车粮。旁边用深墨改了数，像是他后来才发觉。前头的路，他少带了粮。

column2: Lonely Beacon
column3: 孤烽燧

column2: The lone tower from the diary stands before you, a thin thread of smoke rising from its top. A gang of sand bandits surrounds it, yelling for whoever's up there to hand over what's inside: treasure left by the Qianli caravan's guards, they've heard. No answer comes, only one arrow, its force nearly spent, landing a foot in front of a bandit. The old squad leader is still alive.
column3: 日记里说的孤墩就在眼前，墩台上飘着一缕细细的烟。一伙沙匪围着墩台，喊着让上面的人把墩里的东西交出来，他们听说那是千里号的护卫留下的宝贝。墩上没人答话，只射下来一支箭，力气已经不大，扎在沙匪脚前一尺。老伍长还活着。

column2: The bandits scatter. The old squad leader sits slumped against the wall, nothing but bones, clutching a token. He and five men escorted the Qianli caravan to Yangguan, he says. The Hawk turned them back, and the bookkeeper wrote them an IOU for their wages: 'I've done the sums, there's enough for the road ahead.' 'He got them wrong.' He presses the Squad Leader's Token on you. 'My brothers are scattered across the frontier. Take this to the barracks and shout: old brothers! They'll come. Finish that road for us.' He closes his eyes, as if he's finally set something down. You bury him beneath the tower.
column3: 沙匪被打散了。老伍长靠在墙根，瘦得只剩骨头，手里攥着一块令牌。他说当年他带五个兄弟护送千里号到阳关，鹞子把他们赶了回来，账房给他们写了工钱欠条，说「我算过了，前头的路够走」。「他算错了。」老伍长把伍长令塞给你们：「兄弟们散在关外，拿去兵营，喊一声老兄弟们，他们就来。替我们把那段路走完。」他闭上眼睛，像是终于放下了什么。你们把他葬在墩下。

column2: Midriver Isle
column3: 河心洲

column2: On a tamarisk-covered sandbar in the middle of the Shule River, a large gang of sand bandits raids boats from rafts. Their chief is an old rider who fled Yangguan, a scar across his face. He doesn't rob for money; he captures people to ask them: 'Have you come looking for the three hundred?' Answer yes and you go free. Answer no and you go in the river.
column3: 疏勒河中间一片长满红柳的沙洲，一大伙沙匪扎着羊皮筏子在这里劫船。头领是个从阳关跑出来的老骑手，脸上一道刀疤。他不劫钱，只劫人问话：「你们是来找那三百个的？」答「是」的放走，答「不是」的扔进河里。

column2: You storm the isle and the bandits surrender. Ten years ago, the scarred old rider says, he kept the gate at Yangguan and watched the Hawk stand there counting the caravan one by one. Number three hundred was the bookkeeper. Next morning two hundred and ninety-nine went into the Sand Sea. The bookkeeper stayed behind and sat a whole night with the Hawk in his tent. 'That's all I saw,' he says. 'Then I got scared and ran.'
column3: 沙匪投降了。刀疤老骑手说，十年前他在阳关守门，看着鹞子一个一个数那支商队，数到第三百个，是账房。第二天一早，二百九十九个人进了沙海，账房留下来，跟鹞子在帐里坐了一夜。「我就看见这么多，后来怕了，就跑了。」

column2: Tea Mule Tower
column3: 茶骡墩

column2: Two dozen mules laden with brick tea are tethered under a wall tower. The tea merchant is locked inside by rogue soldiers who brew milk tea with his cargo every day. He shouts from the window: 'That's the Hawk's order! One load a year, never a year missed!' The soldiers laugh: 'The Hawk's on his way out. Who cares about his tea?'
column3: 长城边一座墩台下拴着二十几头骡子，驮着关里来的砖茶。赶骡子的茶商被一伙兵痞锁在墩台里，兵痞们天天用他的茶煮奶茶。茶商在窗口急得直喊：「那是鹞子订的！每年一驮，一年都不能少！」兵痞们笑他：「鹞子快不行了，谁还管他的茶。」

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the merchant let out. Every year, he says, the Hawk orders a load of fine tea and never drinks it, storing it untouched. Once he dared ask why, and the Hawk said: 'One year a man drank with me all night, then went into the Sand Sea alone the next day. He said he'd come back to drink tea with me and finish our accounts.' The merchant sighs. 'Ten loads now, and he's never come back to drink it.'
column3: 兵痞被赶走，茶商被放了出来。他说鹞子每年订一驮好茶，从来不喝，原封不动存着。有一年他忍不住问，鹞子说：「那年有个人跟我喝了一夜酒，第二天一个人进了沙海，说回来要跟我喝茶，把账算完。」茶商叹气：「十驮了，那人还没回来喝。」

column2: Wild Horse Valley
column3: 野马谷

column2: Deep in the gobi is a valley where wild herds come to foal. A tough troop of desert raiders has laid hobble ropes at its mouth to catch this year's foals. One old horse in the herd stands out: it still wears a half-rotted saddle with bulging saddlebags and lets no one near. The raiders say it's a runaway from the Qianli caravan, and the bags might hold the ledger.
column3: 戈壁深处一条山谷，是野马群产驹的地方。一队精悍的大漠响马在谷口下了绊马索，要抓今年的马驹。野马群里有一匹老马格外显眼：身上还套着一副烂了一半的鞍子，鞍袋鼓鼓囊囊，不让任何人靠近。响马说那是千里号跑丢的马，鞍袋里说不定就是账本。

column2: The raiders are beaten back, the ropes cut, and the herd bursts out of the valley. The old horse runs last, looks back at you once, and its loosened saddlebag drops a small cloth bundle. Not the ledger, but an old abacus missing one bead on the third rod, its frame carved 'spare'. The bookkeeper carried two abacuses, but only one ledger.
column3: 响马被打退，绊马索割断了，野马群冲出了谷口。那匹老马跑在最后，回头看了你们一眼，鞍袋松了，掉下来一个小布包。里面不是账本，是一把旧算盘，第三档少了一颗珠子，框上刻着：「备用」。账房连算盘都备了两把，账本却只有一本。

column2: Barber's Slope
column3: 剃头坡

column2: This gang wanted to join the Hawk, got turned down, and set up on their own in a huff. They kidnapped a barber to give them all 'the Hawk's haircut' for a fierce look. The nervous barber slipped and shaved the chief on one side only. The chief, having no mirror, found it nice and cool and ordered the whole gang to copy it. Now they're all half bald, and strut about very proudly.
column3: 这伙沙匪想投鹞子，被拒了，一气之下自立门户。他们绑了个剃头匠，要剃一个「鹞子头」显得威风。剃头匠胆子小，手一抖，给头领剃了个阴阳头。头领没镜子，觉得挺凉快，下令全寨照着剃。现在个个半边光头，见了人还挺神气。

column2: The half-bald bandits scatter, looking from afar like zebras. Xiao Chai laughs till he can't stand. 'The Hawk wouldn't take them because they'd robbed an old woman on the road. His rules: don't kill travellers, don't touch goods under the Qian banner.' The barber says he's seen the real Hawk: hair white all over, turned white in a single night ten years ago.
column3: 半边光头们四散而逃，远看像一群斑马。小柴笑得直不起腰：「鹞子不收他们，是因为他们劫过一个过路的老太太。鹞子的规矩是：不杀过路人，不碰千字旗的货。」剃头匠说，他见过真鹞子，一头白发，是十年前一夜白的。

column2: Crooked Brokers
column3: 黑牙行

column2: A 'broker's house' by the border market buys up 'torn pages of the Qianli ledger' and sells them on to people hoping to claim a reward at Yangguan. Its weights are sand-filled, its rulers an inch short, and anyone who calls the pages fakes meets the blades in the back yard. A long queue clutching scraps of paper waits outside, each hoping theirs is real.
column3: 互市边上开着一家「牙行」，专门收购「千里号账本残页」，转手卖给想去阳关讨赏的人。秤砣里灌了沙，量纸的尺子短一寸，谁敢说是假货，后院的刀手就出来。门口排着一长溜捧着破纸的人，都盼着自己那张是真的。

column2: The blades go down and the brokers' house is shut. The manager confesses that not one page they sold ever earned a reward: the Hawk doesn't even read them. He just feels the paper and says 'no'. 'The real ledger is on western mulberry paper,' the manager says. 'The Hawk knows by touch. He's held that ledger in his own hands.'
column3: 刀手被打倒，牙行被查封。掌柜招认，他们卖出去的残页没有一张拿到过赏钱：鹞子看都不看，只摸一摸纸，就说「不是」。「真账本用的是西边的桑皮纸，」掌柜说，「鹞子一摸就知道。他亲手摸过那本账。」

column2: Howling Flat
column3: 狼嚎滩

column2: This sandy flat is gobi wolf country, and at full moon the howling never stops. In past years the Hawk's riders patrolled here and the wolves kept their distance. This year the Hawk pulled every rider back to Yangguan, and the wolves grow bolder, attacking caravans by day and carrying off foals. The packs whelp twice a year: wipe out one, and another appears the next.
column3: 这片沙滩是戈壁狼的地盘，一到月圆，狼嚎声此起彼伏。往年鹞子的马队常在这一带巡逻，狼不敢近人；今年鹞子把人马都收回了阳关，狼群胆子越来越大，大白天就敢扑商队，叼走马驹。狼一年下两窝崽，打掉一群，第二年又冒出一群。

column2: The pack is broken and the lead wolf flees into the dunes. The road will be safe for a while, but when the cubs grow up next spring, you'll have to clear them again. The locals say the wolves multiplied from the day the Hawk withdrew, as if even they knew the man at Yangguan could no longer watch the world outside.
column3: 狼群被打散，头狼逃进了沙丘深处。这一阵商路能安生了，可等明年开春，狼崽子长大了，还得再来清一次。附近的人说，鹞子收兵那天起狼就多了，好像连狼都知道，阳关上的人顾不上外头了。

column2: Tunnel Under the Well
column3: 枯井地道

column2: Climbing down the footholds, you find a tunnel running sideways from the bottom of the well. A chill wind blows through it, and the moaning is air rushing along the passage. Deep inside, firelight: a few sand bandits are prising open an army chest carved with the character Shi, ten. They think it holds the Qianli ledger, and hearing footsteps, lunge with their blades.
column3: 顺着枯井壁上的脚窝爬下去，井底横着一条地道，阴风阵阵，那呜呜的声音就是风穿过地道发出来的。地道深处有火光，几个沙匪正撬着一只军箱，箱上刻着「什」字。他们以为里面是千里号的账本，听见脚步声，抄起刀扑了过来。

column2: The bandits flee. In the chest lies a Ten Leader's Token on top of a note: 'We ten were sent out nine years ago to search for the Qianli caravan. A sandstorm drove us into this tunnel; all of us lived. We searched a year. Nobody on the road, and no ledger on the road either. The Hawk said the ledger went with the bookkeeper. We've scattered across the frontier as herders. Brother who comes after: take this token to the barracks and call out. We're all still here.' The 'one, two, three' in the well was the wind carrying their old roll call. The Hawk forbade the well so no one would take this token.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。箱子里是一块什长令，压着一张纸条：「我们这一什十人，九年前奉命出关寻千里号，遇沙暴躲进此道，都活了下来。寻了一年，路上无人，账也不在路上。鹞子说，账跟着账房走了。我们散在关外放牧，后来的兄弟，拿这令去营里喊一声，我们都在。」井底的「一、二、三」，是风里留着他们当年点名的回响。鹞子不许人下井，是怕有人拿走这块令。

column2: Mirror Sands
column3: 照镜沙

column2: A troop of sand-bandit archers got hold of a chest of bronze mirrors and planted them on the dunes, flashing the noon sun into travellers' eyes and shooting while they're blinded. Lately, though, they hardly rob at all; the mirrors all flash westward. They're signalling for the Hawk, reporting the movements of ledger-hunters to Yangguan at a tael per flash.
column3: 一伙沙匪弓手得了一箱铜镜，插在沙丘上，正午把阳光反射进过路人的眼睛，趁人看不见就放箭。可他们最近不怎么劫道了，镜子都对着西边一闪一闪：原来他们替鹞子打镜语，把找账本的人一路的动静报给阳关，一闪一两银子。

column2: You attack on a cloudy day, the mirrors are useless, and the archers suddenly can't see a thing. Their leader says Yangguan's only reply this month has been the same question, over and over: 'Has the Qian banner arrived?' You pull up a whole chest of mirrors and give them to the girls of the district.
column3: 你们挑了个阴天去打，镜子没了用处，弓手们一下成了瞎子。领头的说，阳关那边回的镜语这个月只有一句，翻来覆去：「千字旗到了没有？」镜子你们拔了一箱，分给了附近的姑娘们。

column2: Holy Water Altar
column3: 仙水坛

column2: An earthen altar in the desert bears a clay idol of 'Mother Sand'. A gang of bandits calling themselves the Mother Sand sect preach everywhere that the Qianli ledger is a 'cursed book': it cursed the three hundred into the sand, and whoever seeks it will be next. They sell protective 'holy water' at a tael a bowl. It's well water stirred with soot.
column3: 沙漠里一座土坛，坛上供着泥塑的「沙母娘娘」。一伙自称「沙母教」的沙匪四处传道：千里号的账本是一本「咒书」，三百人就是被它咒进沙里的，谁找它谁就是下一个。他们卖「仙水」辟邪，一碗一两银子，其实是兑了锅灰的井水。

column2: The sect is scattered and the idol toppled; out of its belly tumble piles of swindled silver and a homemade 'cursed book' full of drawn ghosts. You return the silver to the faithful. An old woman spits. 'Curse my foot. That ledger records what people owe. If it curses anyone, it's the debtors.'
column3: 沙母教被打散，泥塑推倒，肚子里掉出一堆骗来的银子，还有一本他们自己做的「咒书」，里面画满了鬼。你们把银子分还给了信徒。一个老阿妈呸了一声：「哪有什么咒，那本账是记人家欠账的，最多咒的是欠债的人。」

column2: Press-Gang Slope
column3: 抓丁坡

column2: Only the old and the very young are left in the village below the slope. A gang of sand bandits flying the Hawk's banner is press-ganging the young men, roping them in a line 'to serve the Hawk'. Xiao Chai spits at the sight. 'The Hawk never press-gangs. He only takes volunteers. These are Bald Wolf's men.' Bald Wolf is the most ambitious of the Hawk's chiefs, recruiting everywhere.
column3: 坡下的村子里只剩老人和孩子。一伙沙匪打着鹞子的旗号抓丁，把村里的年轻后生拴成一串，说是给鹞子充军。小柴一看就啐了一口：「鹞子从来不抓丁，他只收自愿的。这是秃狼的人。」秃狼是鹞子手下最有野心的头目，正四处拉人。

column2: The ropes are cut and the young men run back to their mothers, and Bald Wolf's men end up roped together instead. Bald Wolf has promised, Xiao Chai says, that the Hawk is dying, and whoever follows him gets a share of the Hawk's storehouse once he takes Yangguan. 'But what's in that storehouse,' Xiao Chai lowers his voice, 'the Hawk has always said none of it is his.'
column3: 绳子割断了，后生们扑回了娘的怀里，秃狼的人反被拴成一串。小柴说，秃狼放话：鹞子快死了，谁跟着他，等他占了阳关，鹞子仓里的东西人人有份。「可那仓里的东西，」小柴压低声音，「鹞子说过，一样都不是他的。」

column2: Lost Sands Hollow
column3: 迷沙窝

column2: A great sandstorm has trapped a patrol of riders in this hollow. Their horses have bolted, the markers are buried, their water's nearly gone, yet they still stand in the road with blades raised, voices cracked like broken gongs. Black hawk pennants on their backs mark them as the Hawk's scouts, but they're patrolling the wrong way: they should be watching east, yet they've been heading west.
column3: 一场大沙暴把一队骑手困在了沙窝里。他们的马跑了，路标被埋了，水也快喝光了，却还端着刀拦在路上，嗓子哑得像破锣。他们背上插着黑色的鹞子小旗，是鹞子的巡哨，可巡的方向不对：他们本该巡东边，却一直往西走。

column2: The scouts throw down their blades almost at once and beg for water. Every year, their leader says, the Hawk sends a party west to the edge of the Sand Sea, to see if anyone has come out. From his shirt he takes an order he keeps close: 'If you see the bookkeeper, ask him to come back to Yangguan. The accounts are not finished.' 'Ten years,' he says. 'Not once.'
column3: 巡哨没打几下就扔了刀，跪下来求水。领头的说，鹞子每年派一队人往西走，走到沙海边上，看有没有人从里面走出来。他从怀里掏出一张贴身带着的令：「若见账房，请回阳关，账未算完。」「十年了，」他说，「一次也没见着。」

column2: Halfway Teahouse
column3: 半路茶馆

column2: A teahouse on the open plain where the Hawk's old hands stop to rest and drink, kept by a one-armed veteran. Bald Wolf's men have besieged it for three days to force the old hands inside to join him. The old hands have taken the doors off for shields and sit inside drinking and cursing. They're on their eighth pot and still won't come out.
column3: 荒原上一间茶馆，是鹞子手下老弟兄们歇脚喝茶的地方，掌柜是个独臂的老兵。秃狼的人把茶馆围了三天，要逼里面的老弟兄投他。老弟兄们把门板拆下来当盾，在里面一边喝茶一边骂，茶都续到第八壶了，就是不出来。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are scattered and the old hands come out with their teacups and nod to you. The Hawk hasn't slept a full night in ten years, an old rider says. Every midnight he gets up and stands outside his tent looking west. 'We keep his rules not because we fear him,' he says, 'but because there's an account weighing on his heart, and someone has to help him settle it.'
column3: 秃狼的人被打散了，老弟兄们端着茶碗出来，冲你们点点头。一个老骑手说，鹞子十年没睡过一个整觉，每到半夜就起来，站在帐外看西边。「我们守着他的规矩，不是怕他，」他说，「是觉得他心里压着一笔账，得有人来帮他算。」

column2: The besiegers left behind twenty-odd sacks of fried rice, a cart of firewood, a dozen jars of stolen wine, and a big banner they never got to fly, crookedly embroidered with the words 'Bald Wolf'.
column3: 围茶馆的人留下二十几袋炒米、一车干柴、十几坛抢来的酒，还有一面没来得及打出去的大旗，上头绣着「秃狼」两个大字，绣得歪歪扭扭。
