column2: The one-armed keeper always brews you his best brick tea, pouring one-handed without spilling a drop, and wraps up a packet of tea and some rock sugar for the road: you need something sweet in your mouth out there.
column3: 独臂掌柜每次都沏一壶最好的砖茶，单手倒得一滴不洒，再给你们包上一包茶叶和几块冰糖，说路上嘴里要有点甜。

column2: Falcon Thieves' Nest
column3: 鹰贼窝

column2: These sand bandits have trained falcons to stoop from the sky and snatch travellers' bundles. Lately they don't go for purses, but paper: anyone carrying a 'ledger page' gets struck. The paper in their nest is piled into a small hill, and they plan to take it to Yangguan sheet by sheet and try their luck.
column3: 这伙沙匪训了几只鹰，专从天上俯冲下来抓过路人的包袱。最近他们抓的不是钱袋，是纸：谁身上带着「账本残页」，鹰就扑谁。窝里的纸已经堆成了小山，他们打算一张一张送去阳关碰运气。

column2: The bandits flee, the falcons perch on your flagpole, and you release them into the sky. You go through the pile of paper: not one sheet is mulberry paper, not one bears the abacus seal with the missing bead. The real ledger was never scattered along the road.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了，鹰落在你们的旗杆上不肯走，你们把它们放回了天上。那一堆纸你们翻了一遍，没有一张是桑皮纸，没有一张盖着少一颗珠子的算盘印。真的账本，从来就没散落在路上。

column2: Road-Closed Sands
column3: 封路沙

column2: A barricade of stakes and camel thorn blocks the sandy road, guarded by the Hawk's riders, who turn back everyone heading west: 'By the Hawk's order, the western road is closed this month.' Merchants sent back curse by the roadside. Seeing your banner, the riders glance at each other, then raise their blades anyway.
column3: 沙道上横着一道用木桩和骆驼刺扎成的路障，一伙鹞子的骑手守着，所有往西去的人一律赶回去，说是鹞子的令：「西去之路，本月封闭。」被赶回来的商人在路边骂骂咧咧。骑手们看见你们的旗子，互相看了一眼，还是举起了刀。

column2: The riders are scattered and the barricade torn down. The road was closed to keep out the ledger-hunters, a captured rider says, but the order goes on: 'If the Qian banner comes, let it pass; but test them first.' 'We've tested you,' he says, rubbing his shoulder. 'That'll do.'
column3: 骑手被打散，路障拆了。被俘的骑手说，封路是为了挡住那些找账本的人，可令的后半句是：「千字旗来，可放；放之前，试一试他们。」「我们试过了，」他揉着肩膀说，「够了。」

column2: Captive's Slope
column3: 压寨坡

column2: In the fort on this slope Bald Wolf is holding a high official's daughter for a thousand-tael ransom. Yet all the shouting from the fort is hers: 'The food's too salty!' 'Your blades are blunt!' 'You lot think you can take Yangguan?' The bandits hunch their necks like scolded schoolboys.
column3: 坡上的寨子里关着一位关里大官的千金，秃狼要她家拿一千两银子来赎。可寨子里传出来的骂声全是那位小姐的：「饭做得太咸！」「刀磨得太钝！」「就你们这样还想占阳关？」沙匪们个个缩着脖子，像挨骂的学童。

column2: You storm the fort and find the young lady in the chief's chair with a riding crop. The bandits bolt like hares. She overheard Bald Wolf's plan, she says: the moment the Hawk falls, raid his storehouse and sell everything inside. 'From what I heard, those things belong to someone else, left in his keeping,' she says. 'Robbing a deposit is the lowest thing there is.'
column3: 你们攻进寨子，小姐正坐在头领的椅子上，手里拿着一根马鞭。沙匪们跑得比兔子还快。小姐说她偷听到了秃狼的打算：等鹞子一倒，就抢鹞子仓，把里面的东西全卖了。「我看那里头的东西，」她说，「是别人寄存的。抢寄存的东西，最没出息。」

column2: Whistling Arrow Slope
column3: 鸣镝坡

column2: The Hawk's scouts crouch on the crest, each with whistling arrows. Spot travellers and they loose one: one whistle means 'cargo', two 'soldiers', three 'run'. Seeing your banner, they loose three in a row, but instead of running, they draw blades and charge.
column3: 坡顶上蹲着鹞子手下的哨探，人手一把带哨子的响箭。远远看见有人过来，就放一支，一声是「有货」，两声是「有兵」，三声是「快跑」。他们看见你们的旗子，一口气放了三支，自己却没跑，拔刀冲了下来。

column2: The scouts are routed. A young one, questioned, says three whistles is the Hawk's rule, but the Hawk also said that when they see 'that banner', nobody runs. He can't say which banner; only that the Hawk said it ought to bear the character Qian. The ledger order, the road-closing order, the 'test them' order: all along the way, they were waiting for you.
column3: 哨探被打散了。审问一个年轻的，他说放三支响箭是鹞子的规矩，可鹞子又说过，见了「那面旗子」不许跑。他说不清是哪面旗子，只记得鹞子说那面旗子上该有一个「千」字。一路上收账本的令、封路的令、试一试的令，原来都在等你们。

column2: Two-Headed Camp
column3: 两头营

column2: Some of Bald Wolf's men have merged with another bandit gang, but the two chiefs won't bow to each other: one wants to attack Yangguan now while the Hawk is ill, the other wants to wait until he dies and pick up the pieces. Three days of arguing, separate cooking pots. When you arrive they're screaming over who leads the charge.
column3: 秃狼的一伙人和另一伙沙匪合了营，可营里两个头领谁也不服谁：一个说趁鹞子病了马上打阳关，一个说等鹞子死了再去捡现成的。两边吵了三天，连吃饭都分锅。你们来的时候，他们正为谁当先锋吵得不可开交。

column2: When you charge, both chiefs shout 'you first!' and neither goes. The camp falls apart. Bald Wolf doesn't fear the Hawk himself, Xiao Chai says, so much as the Hawk's old hands, who say that while the Hawk stands, nobody makes trouble at Yangguan.
column3: 你们一冲，两个头领同时喊「你先上」，结果谁也没上。营散了。小柴说，秃狼最怕的不是鹞子，是鹞子手下那些老弟兄，他们说鹞子不倒，阳关就不许乱。

column2: Foothill Tavern
column3: 山脚酒肆

column2: At the foot of the northern hills stands a tavern whose landlady, Mistress Qin, brews famous highland barley wine. Half a month ago some of Bald Wolf's men moved in, drinking without paying and smashing tables: 'once we take Yangguan, this tavern's ours too'. Mistress Qin buried her best jars out back and has sat at the door with a rolling pin, cursing them for three days.
column3: 北山脚下一间酒肆，老板娘姓秦，酿的青稞酒远近闻名。半个月前秃狼的一伙人住了进来，天天喝酒不给钱，喝醉了还砸桌子，说「等我们占了阳关，这酒肆也是我们的」。秦老板娘把剩下的好酒埋进后院，拿着擀面杖坐在门口骂了三天。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off. Mistress Qin digs up her jars, the smell fills the hillside, and the tavern reopens with her best wine and meat to trade. Every third month, she says, the Hawk comes alone, sits all night, pours three hundred cups onto the ground, and drinks the last himself. 'That one,' she says, 'he says he drinks for a man who got his sums wrong.'
column3: 秃狼的人被赶跑了，秦老板娘刨出酒坛，酒香飘了满山，酒肆重新开张，好酒好肉拿出来跟你们换。她说鹞子每年三月来一次，一个人坐一夜，倒三百杯酒洒在地上，最后一杯自己喝。「那杯，」她说，「他说是替一个算错账的人喝的。」

column2: Watching Dune
column3: 望人沙

column2: A lone mud house stands on a dune, and every evening a middle-aged woman stands before it gazing west for two hours. Her husband was a camel driver with the Qianli caravan, gone ten years. Every midnight her old camel breaks its halter and walks toward Yangguan, and comes back on its own the next day. A gang of sand bandits wants this 'camel that knows the way', and has surrounded the house.
column3: 沙丘上一间孤零零的土屋，屋前站着一个中年妇人，每天傍晚往西边看，一看就是一个时辰。她的男人是千里号的驼夫，走了十年。她家那峰老骆驼每到半夜就挣开缰绳往阳关走，第二天又自己回来。一伙沙匪看上了这峰「认路的骆驼」，把屋子围了起来。

column2: The bandits are driven off. From her coat the woman takes a small cloth bundle holding a bronze bell clapper. 'When he left he gave me this. He said if the bell doesn't ring, he's only stopped on the road, and when he comes back we'll put it in again.' All the animals around here walk to Yangguan at night, she says, kneel outside the old fort, and come home at dawn. 'Whatever they're waiting for,' she says, 'I'm waiting too.'
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。妇人掏出一枚铜铃舌：「他走时留给我，说铃铛不响，就是他在路上停下了，回来再装上。」她说这一带的牲口夜里都往阳关走，到故垒外头跪下，天亮才回来。「它们在等什么，我也在等。」

column2: Sand Sled Camp
column3: 沙橇营

column2: A big crew of Bald Wolf's men has a new trick: riding wooden sleds down from high dune crests, fast as arrows, crashing into caravans and scrambling back up with the loot. The dunes are scored with long grooves like the strings of a giant harp. Xiao Chai curls his lip. 'If the Hawk's old hands saw this, they'd laugh their teeth out.'
column3: 秃狼手下的一大伙人想出了新花样：坐着木头沙橇从高高的沙丘顶上冲下来，快得像箭，一眨眼冲进商队，抢了东西再爬回去。沙丘上满是沙橇划出的长槽，像一张巨大的竖琴。小柴看了直撇嘴：「鹞子的老弟兄要是看见这种打法，能笑掉牙。」

column2: You wait at the foot of the dunes and overturn the sleds one by one. The captives say they use sleds because Bald Wolf hasn't enough horses: the Hawk's horses only accept the Hawk's old hands and throw Bald Wolf's men the moment they mount. You give the sleds to the local children, who scream down the dunes all day.
column3: 你们守在沙丘底下，沙橇一个个冲下来，一个个被掀翻。被俘的人说，他们用沙橇是因为秃狼的马不够：鹞子的马只认鹞子的老弟兄，秃狼的人一上马就被掀下来。沙橇你们给了附近的孩子们，他们一整天都在沙丘上尖叫。

column2: Night Kneeling Flat
column3: 夜跪滩

column2: On the sands east of Yangguan, a gang of sand bandits has opened a 'wonder of the frontier' business: every midnight the animals of the district walk across this flat toward Yangguan, and the bandits charge passing merchants ten coins a head to watch 'the Kneeling of Ten Thousand Camels'. Watch without paying and they keep your camel so it can go kneel too.
column3: 阳关东边的沙滩上，一伙沙匪做起了「看奇景」的生意：每到半夜，附近的牲口都会从这片滩上走过，往阳关去，沙匪就向过路的商人收钱，一人十文，管看一场「万驼夜跪」。谁看了不给钱，就扣下他的骆驼，让它也去跪。

column2: The bandits flee. At midnight you see it for yourselves: lines of animals crossing the flat, camels, horses, donkeys, silent, not one bellowing. Where the old Yangguan fort comes into view, they kneel all together, heads to the west. Near dawn they rise and go home. Nobody drives them, and nobody can stop them.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了。半夜里，你们果然看见一串串牲口从滩上走过，骆驼、马、驴，安安静静，一头都不叫，走到能望见阳关故垒的地方，齐刷刷跪下，头朝西。天快亮时，它们又站起来，各自回家。没有人赶，也没有人能拦。

column2: Empty-Stable Inn
column3: 夜空栈

column2: An inn in the middle of the desert has a strange reputation: guests who wake at midnight always find their animals gone, and back again at dawn with sand caked on their knees. A gang of sand bandits has seized the inn to sell 'camel ropes' at a tael each, guaranteed to stop them wandering. They wander anyway, snapping the ropes. The owner's family has been thrown out to a lean-to.
column3: 沙漠中间一座客栈，有个怪名声：住店的客人半夜起来，总发现自家的牲口不见了，天亮又回来了，满膝盖都是沙。一伙沙匪趁机占了客栈，卖「拴驼绳」，一根一两银子，说拴了就不跑。可拴了照跑，绳子还被挣断。店主一家被赶到门外搭窝棚。

column2: The bandits are thrown out and the family moves back in. Their own animals wander too, the owner says. It started ten years ago, after the Qianli caravan stayed a night here. 'I've given up tying them,' he says. 'They go to Yangguan and they're back by dawn. More reliable than people.' A sign goes up by the gate: 'For the pioneers, free of charge.'
column3: 沙匪被赶出了客栈，店主一家搬了回去。店主说他家的牲口也跑，十年了，从千里号在这里住过一夜之后就开始了。「我不拴了，」他说，「它们去阳关，天亮就回来，比人守信用。」门口挂上了一块牌子：「开拓队来，分文不取。」

column2: The bandits hid over sixty bundles of alfalfa, twenty sacks of beans, a heap of unsold 'camel ropes', and a clay jar of silver, all rope money they swindled.
column3: 沙匪在店里藏了六十多捆苜蓿草料、二十袋豆子、一大堆没卖出去的「拴驼绳」，还有一口装满碎银的陶罐，都是骗来的绳子钱。

column2: The family has the beds heated early and the landlady cooks mutton soup, while the children take your banner, beat the dust out of it, and plant it back by the gate, so travellers in the night will know the pioneers are staying here.
column3: 店主一家早早烧好炕，老板娘煮一锅羊肉汤，孩子们把你们的旗子拿去掸了灰，再插回门口，说这样夜里过路的人都知道开拓队住在这儿。

column2: Silk Cellar
column3: 丝绸窖

column2: Beneath a collapsed Han-dynasty post station on the gobi lies a cellar. An elite troop of riders guards its mouth, not Bald Wolf's men but the Hawk's oldest companions, taking shifts for ten years and letting no one near. Bald Wolf's men tried to raid it the day before yesterday and left several dead. At night, a few camels always come to kneel on the sand above it.
column3: 戈壁上一座塌了的汉代驿站，地下有一个窖。一队精锐的骑手守着窖口，不是秃狼的人，是鹞子最老的弟兄，十年来轮班看守，谁也不让靠近。秃狼的人前天来抢过一回，死了好几个。窖口上方的沙地里，夜里总有几峰骆驼来跪着。

column2: The old companions fight hard, but in the end stand aside. 'If you can beat us,' says their leader, 'you've earned a look.' Inside lie hundreds of bolts of silk, each sealed 'Qianli caravan': before entering the Sand Sea, the caravan left what it couldn't carry here. The deposit slip in the bookkeeper's hand is nailed to the wall: 'To be collected on return. Held in the Hawk's keeping.' Ten years in his keeping, and not one bolt missing.
column3: 老弟兄们打得很硬，最后让开了路：「打得过我们，就配看。」窖里码着几百匹丝绸，都贴着千里号的封条，墙上钉着账房写的寄存单：「回程取，鹞子代管。」代管十年，一匹没少。

column2: Empty Temple
column3: 无人寺

column2: A small temple stands on the gobi. The monks left long ago, yet every dawn the bell rings three times by itself. Bald Wolf's men don't believe in such things and want to melt the bell down for blades. As soon as they climb the tower, it rings again and they nearly fall, but they still won't leave: 'There's going to be a fight at Yangguan. We need bronze.'
column3: 戈壁上一座小寺，和尚早就走光了，可寺里的钟每天清晨都会自己响三下。秃狼的人不信邪，想把铜钟拆下来熔了换刀，刚爬上钟楼，钟又响了，吓得差点摔下来，可他们还是不肯走，说「阳关要打仗，缺铜」。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off. Behind the bell huddles a skinny little monk with the striker. Three years ago his master went to Yangguan to persuade the Hawk to let go of his burden, and he's still there cooking for the Hawk. The master once sent back one message: 'The account in the Hawk's heart is not one he can settle alone. He has to wait for someone to come back.'
column3: 秃狼的人被赶跑了。钟后面缩着一个瘦小的小和尚，手里拿着钟锤。他说师父三年前去了阳关，想劝鹞子放下心事，到现在还在阳关给鹞子做饭。师父托人带回过一句话：「鹞子心里那笔账，他一个人算不完，得等一个人回来。」

column2: Letter Thieves' Slope
column3: 截信坡

column2: The post road passes here, and a gang of Bald Wolf's men ambushes the couriers for letters, not horses or money, reading them for blackmail material. Intercepted letters fill half a room, and at the very bottom lies a dusty leather pouch sealed with a one-eyed hawk in wax, never opened.
column3: 驿道从这里过，一伙秃狼的人专截驿卒，不抢马、不抢钱，只抢信，拆开一封封读，从里面找能敲诈的事。被截下的信堆了半间屋子，最底下压着一个落满灰的皮囊，封口上盖着一个独眼鹞子的火漆印，从来没被打开过。

column2: The bandits flee and you reseal the letters for the couriers. The pouch holds a letter the Hawk wrote to the court ten years ago, in clumsy characters: 'Two hundred and ninety-nine of the Qianli caravan have entered the Sand Sea. The bookkeeper followed alone the next day. I let them go. If there is guilt, it is mine. I beg the court to send someone to find them.' The courier says it was robbed here back then. The court never received it.
column3: 沙匪被打跑了，你们把信重新封好交给驿卒。那个皮囊里是鹞子十年前写给朝廷的信，字写得很笨：「千里号二百九十九人已入沙海，账房于次日独往。我放之，若有罪，罪在我。乞朝廷遣人寻之。」驿卒说这封信当年在这里被劫，朝廷从来没收到过。

column2: Sandstorm Mouth
column3: 沙暴口

column2: The wind gap between two sand mountains has sandstorms eight days out of ten. A gang of sand bandits wearing goggles ground from horn robs only in the storms. But what they fear most, they say, isn't soldiers but the animals that pass through the gap in midnight storms: silent, file after file heading for Yangguan, not blinking as the sand strikes their faces.
column3: 两座沙山之间的风口，十天里有八天刮沙暴。一伙沙匪戴着牛角片磨的护目镜，专在沙暴里打劫。可他们说，最怕的不是官兵，是半夜沙暴里那些从风口穿过去的牲口：一声不吭，一队一队往阳关走，沙子打在脸上都不眨眼。

column2: Wet cloths over your faces, you win the fight in the storm and take the horn goggles. That midnight a file of animals does pass through the gap, led by an old camel wearing a bronze bell with no clapper, Qian on its shell. The bandits huddle behind the rocks and nobody dares make a sound.
column3: 你们蒙着湿布在沙暴里打赢了这一仗，抢下了牛角镜。那天半夜，风口里果然走过一队牲口，最前头是一峰老骆驼，脖子上挂着一只没有铃舌的铜铃，铃壳上一个「千」字。沙匪们缩在石头后面，谁也不敢出声。

column2: Black Rock Mine
column3: 黑石矿

column2: At the foot of the northern hills is a mine of burnable black rock, warmer than firewood. Every year the Hawk buys dozens of cartloads to keep a fire burning all night on Yangguan. Bald Wolf's men have seized the mine and forced twenty-odd villagers to dig on one bowl of gruel a day, boasting: 'Cut off his black rock and see how the Hawk gets through his nights.'
column3: 北山脚下有一座黑石矿，石头能烧，比柴火还暖。鹞子每年从这里买几十车黑石，夜里在阳关上烧一整夜的火。秃狼的人占了矿，抓了二十多个村民挖石头，一天只给一顿稀粥，还放话：「断了黑石，看鹞子夜里还怎么熬。」

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off and the miners walk out, faces so black only the whites of their eyes show. The Hawk never haggles over black rock, they say, and that fire at night is for the west to see: 'He says when those people went into the Sand Sea, if they looked back and saw this fire, they'd know the way home.' They give you a cartload and ask you to take it to Yangguan for them.
column3: 秃狼的人被打跑了，挖矿的人走出矿洞，脸黑得只看见眼白。他们说鹞子买黑石从不还价，夜里那堆火是烧给西边看的：「他说那年那些人进沙海，回头看得见这堆火，就知道往哪走。」他们送了你们一车黑石，说替他们捎给阳关。

column2: Hawk's Paddock
column3: 鹞子马场

column2: On an open grassland the Hawk's horsemen drill in a tidy wedge, splitting at one whistle and closing at the next, more soldierly than real soldiers. An old horse tag on a post reads 'Hexi Cavalry'. Yet at midnight these well-drilled warhorses break their tethers one by one and run off to kneel outside Yangguan, and their riders can't bring them back.
column3: 一片开阔的草滩上，鹞子的马队正在操练：楔子阵，一声呼哨分成两股，再一声又合拢，比边军还像边军。马场边上插着一块旧马牌，「河西骑营」。可到了半夜，这些操练得整整齐齐的战马会一匹匹挣脱缰绳，跑去阳关外头跪着，骑手们追都追不回来。

column2: The horsemen are routed. A captured old rider says the Hawk was a squad leader in the Hexi Cavalry before it was disbanded and he took to the hills. A dozen of these horses were the Qianli caravan's pack animals, unloaded and left behind before it entered the Sand Sea. 'When they kneel,' he says, 'the rest of the herd kneels too. Horses follow their leaders.'
column3: 马队被冲散了。被俘的老骑手说，鹞子年轻时是河西骑营的伍长，营散了才落草。这些马里有十几匹是当年千里号的驮马，商队进沙海前卸了货留下的。「它们一跪，」老骑手说，「营里别的马也跟着跪。马是跟着领头的。」

column2: Council Sands
column3: 会盟沙

column2: A ring of bonfires on the sand: chiefs from seven or eight gangs are drinking blood-wine, with Bald Wolf at the head demanding they elect him their new great chief. The Hawk is too sick to rise, he says, banging the table, and whoever helps him take Yangguan gets the Hawk's storehouse. A few chiefs are drawing blades over the seating. Bald Wolf is pleased with himself.
column3: 沙地上围着一圈篝火，七八伙沙匪的头领聚在一起喝血酒，秃狼坐在上首，要大家推他当新的大头领。他拍着桌子说，鹞子病得起不来了，谁跟他打下阳关，鹞子仓就是谁的。几个头领为座次吵得拔刀相向，秃狼正得意。

column2: You charge into the ring of fire and sweep them all up. Bald Wolf escapes on horseback, heading for the Hawk's storehouse north of Yangguan. The captured chiefs sit dejected. One mutters: 'The Hawk hasn't even fallen. What were we rushing for?' Another says: 'Bald Wolf says the Hawk's waiting for someone. Once they come, he'll give way.'
column3: 你们冲进篝火圈，一锅端了。秃狼骑着马跑了，跑的方向是阳关北边的鹞子仓。被俘的头领们垂头丧气，有一个嘟囔着：「鹞子都没倒，我们急什么。」另一个说：「秃狼说鹞子在等一个人，等到了，他就撑不住了。」

column2: Tethered Camel Camp
column3: 缚驼营

column2: Only a few dozen li from Yangguan, the Hawk's personal guard is camped here, and every camel's legs are bound tight with thick rope. They have to be, the guards say: at midnight the camels break free and kneel in rows outside the Hawk's tent, heads to the west, and won't get up for anything. The guards are red-eyed from lack of sleep and short-tempered.
column3: 离阳关只剩几十里，这里驻着鹞子的亲兵，营里的骆驼都用粗绳子拴着腿，拴得死死的。亲兵们说，不拴不行：一到半夜，这些骆驼就挣开缰绳，齐刷刷跪到鹞子的大帐外面，头朝西，怎么赶都不起来。亲兵们个个熬红了眼，脾气暴躁。

column2: The guard camp is broken. You untie one camel; it rises, walks slowly to the western edge of the camp, and kneels facing Yangguan. Its saddle is empty, but the girth ropes are neatly tied, as if waiting at any moment to be loaded. A guard sighs: 'Ten years. They're waiting for the Hawk to give something back.'
column3: 亲兵营被打垮了。你们解开一峰骆驼的绳子，它站起来，慢慢走到营地西头，朝着阳关跪下，一动不动。它背上的鞍子是空的，鞍绳却系得整整齐齐，像是随时等着人来装货。一个亲兵叹气：「十年了，它们在等鹞子还一样东西。」

column2: Echo Hollow
column3: 回声洼

column2: A great hollow in the sand with steep walls, where a shout echoes back several times. A din of war cries rises from it, like a hundred men, and a detachment sent by Bald Wolf has dithered at the mouth for ages, afraid to enter. You steel yourselves and walk in, and the shouting grows louder, with one line ringing through it: 'While the Hawk stands, Yangguan holds!'
column3: 沙地里一个大洼，四壁陡直，一喊话回音能响好几遍。洼里传出一片喊杀声，听着像有上百人，秃狼派来的一队人马在洼口犹豫了半天，不敢进。你们壮着胆子走进去，喊杀声更响了，还夹着一句：「鹞子在，阳关不乱！」

column2: Once it's over there turn out to be only five of the Hawk's old hands in the hollow, all hoarse. They were ordered to hold the back road to Yangguan, and too few to fight, they frightened people with echoes. Learning you fly the Qian banner, the five exchange a look and stand aside. 'The Hawk said: when you come, let you through.'
column3: 打完一看，洼里只有五个鹞子的老弟兄，嗓子全喊哑了。他们奉命守着去阳关的后路，人少，只好靠回音吓人。知道你们是千字旗，五个人对视一眼，让开了路：「鹞子说过，你们来，就让你们过。」

column2: Drunken Slope
column3: 醉卧坡

column2: A wine caravan bound for the Yangguan market was robbed here by Bald Wolf's men, who opened the casks and have been drinking for three days. Bodies lie sprawled across the slope, some snoring with their arms round casks, some waving blades at the sky and cursing the Hawk. The merchant, tied up to one side, weeps as cask after cask runs dry.
column3: 一支往阳关集送葡萄酒的商队在这里被秃狼的人劫了，劫道的打开酒桶，一喝就是三天。坡上横七竖八躺满了人，有的抱着酒桶打呼，有的拿着刀对着天大骂鹞子。酒商被绑在一边，看着自家的酒一桶桶见底，心疼得眼泪直流。

column2: The drunks can't hold their blades and fall in heaps. The freed merchant has seven casks left. A drunk you douse awake lets slip, still fuddled: Bald Wolf means to take the storehouse first, then buy over Yangguan's old hands with what's inside. 'But those old fossils don't care about money,' he hiccups. 'Only the Hawk.'
column3: 醉醺醺的人连刀都握不稳，没打几下就倒了一片。酒商被放了，还剩七桶。一个醉汉被你们泼醒，迷迷糊糊地说漏了嘴：秃狼要先抢鹞子仓，再拿仓里的东西去收买阳关的老弟兄。「可那些老东西不认钱，」他打了个酒嗝，「只认鹞子。」

column2: Cat Camp
column3: 猫儿营

column2: This bandit chief has a fearsome name and cuts men down without blinking, but since he stole a Persian cat from a foreign merchant he's a changed man, carrying it everywhere; in councils it sits on his head. Every camel, horse and dog in his camp runs off to kneel at Yangguan at midnight, he says. Only the cat stays, keeping him company, and only then can he sleep.
column3: 这伙沙匪的头领凶名在外，砍人从不眨眼，可他抢了一个胡商的波斯猫以后整个人都变了：走到哪儿都抱着猫，开会的时候猫趴在他头上。他说营里的骆驼、马、狗，半夜全跑去阳关跪着，只有这只猫不去，夜里陪着他，他才睡得着。

column2: Even in defeat the chief shields the cat, but it leaps down and rubs against your legs. You return it to the merchant, who laughs when he hears the story: 'A cat doesn't care who owes whom, so it sleeps. Animals that care don't. Nor do people.' The chief weeps harder than if he'd lost his fort.
column3: 头领被打败时还紧紧护着猫。猫却跳出来蹭了蹭你们的腿。你们把猫还给了胡商，胡商听说了这事，笑着说：「猫不认谁欠了谁，所以睡得着。牲口认，人也认。」头领哭得比丢了寨子还伤心。

column2: Pardon Sands
column3: 赦书沙

column2: Two gangs are fighting furiously over a scroll of yellow silk on the sand. It's the pardon the court sent out with the pioneers: any outlaw beyond the pass who helps the pioneers on their way west is forgiven. Bald Wolf's men want to burn it ('pardon us and how do we rob?'); the Hawk's old hands want to protect it: 'This is our road home.'
column3: 沙地上两伙人正为一卷黄绢打得不可开交。那是朝廷随开拓队一起发下来的赦书：凡关外落草者，能助开拓队西行的，一律赦罪。秃狼的人要烧了它，说「赦了还怎么抢」；鹞子的老弟兄要护着它，说「这是我们回家的路」。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off and the pardon saved. The old hands unroll it and find a line at the very end, and as they read it aloud they begin to weep: 'The Hawk of Yangguan has guarded goods untouched for ten years, and once wrote concerning the Qianli caravan. Though the letter never arrived, his heart deserves compassion. Specially pardoned.' His letter never reached the court, but somehow the court learned what he was waiting for.
column3: 秃狼的人被赶跑了，赦书保住了。老弟兄们展开黄绢，找到末尾的一行字，念着念着就哭了：「阳关鹞子，十年守货不动，曾具书言千里号事，虽书未达，其心可悯，特赦。」原来那封信没送到，朝廷却从别处知道了他在等什么。

column2: Crossroads Mound
column3: 十字墩

column2: Four roads meet below an earth mound, and Bald Wolf's men have set up a checkpoint on top. Everyone passing is asked: 'Whose man are you?' Say 'the Hawk's' and you're beaten. Say 'Bald Wolf's' and you pay. Say 'nobody's' and you're detained. The merchants below are frantic, not knowing how to answer.
column3: 四条路在一座土墩下交汇，秃狼的人在墩上设了卡，谁从这里过就问一句「你是谁的人」。答「鹞子的」，挨打；答「秃狼的」，交钱；答「谁的都不是」，扣下。商人们在墩下急得团团转，不知道该怎么答。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are thrown off the mound. Xiao Chai gives the merchants a tip: if anyone asks again, answer 'the Qianli caravan's'. It's the old hands' password, he says. For ten years, whoever spoke those words has been let through by Yangguan's men. 'Bald Wolf doesn't know it,' he says smugly. 'He came too late.'
column3: 秃狼的人被赶下了墩。小柴替商人们出了个主意：以后再有人问，就答「千里号的」。他说这是鹞子手下老弟兄的暗号，十年来谁说出这三个字，阳关的人都会放行。「秃狼不知道这个，」他得意地说，「他来得太晚了。」

column2: Arrow Tower Sands
column3: 箭楼沙

column2: On the sands before Yangguan, the Hawk's men have built three arrow towers of mud brick and camel bone, archers on watch in shifts. Ropes strung with bronze bells link the towers; touch one and arrows fly from all three. But every midnight, when the kneeling animals walk under the ropes and the bells clash, the archers never loose a single arrow.
column3: 阳关前的沙地上，鹞子的人用土坯和驼骨搭了三座箭楼，楼上的弓手轮班守着。箭楼之间拉着绳子，绳上挂满铜铃，谁碰了绳子，三座楼的箭就一起射过来。可每到半夜，跪拜的牲口从绳下走过，铃铛响成一片，弓手们却一箭也不放。

column2: All three towers come down. You check the bells on the ropes one by one; none bears Qian. A captured archer says the Hawk forbids using those bells: they must be returned as they are, to the camels' owners. 'Until the owners come back,' he says, 'the bells hang in the storehouse, silent.'
column3: 三座箭楼都被拔掉了。绳上的铃铛你们一个个看过去，没有一个是「千」字铃。被俘的弓手说，鹞子不许用那些铃，说那些铃得原样还回去，还给骆驼的主人。「主人不回来，」他说，「铃就挂在仓里，不响。」

column2: Gazelle Stampede
column3: 黄羊阵

column2: These desert raiders have a vicious trick: they drive whole herds of gazelles across the grassland so hundreds come stampeding through a caravan, then loot in the chaos. Today another herd is coming, dust boiling up, the ground shaking. The trick only works by day, they say: after dark the herds won't be driven, and wander off toward Yangguan on their own.
column3: 这伙大漠响马有个狠招：把成群的黄羊从草滩那头赶过来，几百只黄羊横冲直撞，冲乱了商队，他们再趁乱劫货。今天他们又赶来一群，远处尘土飞扬，大地都在抖。他们说，这招只能白天用：天一黑，黄羊群就不听赶，自己往阳关那边绕。

column2: You step aside for the gazelles and charge the raiders behind, scattering them. Even the wild gazelles circle Yangguan, their leader says, standing far off outside the old fort at night, not daring to approach, not willing to leave. 'Something weighs on that place,' he says, touching his chest. 'Not a ghost. Something owed and never repaid.'
column3: 你们闪到一边让过黄羊群，迎头冲向后面的响马，把他们打散了。领头的说，连野黄羊都绕着阳关走，夜里在故垒外头远远站着，不敢近也不肯走。「那地方有东西压着，」他摸着胸口说，「不是鬼，是一笔欠了没还的东西。」

column2: Yangguan Market
column3: 阳关集

column2: At the foot of the old Yangguan fort lies a market where grain from inside the pass and stone from the frontier once changed hands. Now Bald Wolf's men collect 'protection money', a tenth from every stall. The grain dealers have lost their profit and the stonemasons stopped coming. Half the market is empty, and the remaining stallholders glance at you, but not too much, for fear of being seen from the fort.
column3: 阳关故垒脚下有一片集市，从前关里的粮食、关外的石料都在这里交易。如今秃狼的人收「保护钱」，每个摊子交一成，粮商没了利，石匠也不来了。集市空了一半，剩下的摊主都在看你们，又不敢多看，怕被阳关上的人瞧见。

column2: The protection collectors are driven off and the market comes alive: grain carts unload, stonemasons haul in stone, grain for stone at nine thousand catties a day. An old flatbread seller says quietly that ten years ago the Qianli caravan restocked grain here. The bookkeeper weighed it himself and said 'that's enough', then came running back at dawn, white-faced: 'I'm a cartload short.' But the caravan had already entered the Sand Sea. That night, the camels at Yangguan knelt for the first time.
column3: 收保护钱的人被打跑了，集市活了过来：粮商卸下了粮车，石匠运来了石料，拿粮食换石头，一天九千斤。卖胡饼的老汉悄悄说，十年前千里号在这里补粮，账房先生亲手称的，称完了说「够了」，第二天一早又跑回来，脸都白了，说「少算了一车」。可那时商队已经进了沙海。那天夜里，阳关上的骆驼第一次跪下。

column2: Living Shrine Slope
column3: 生祠坡

column2: A new little shrine on the slope houses a clay statue of Bald Wolf himself, three times handsomer than the man, under a plaque reading 'The New Hawk'. His men force the herders to come and burn incense daily: Yangguan will belong to Bald Wolf now. The herders curse under their breath as they kowtow, and someone has secretly snapped off the statue's nose.
column3: 坡上新盖了一座小庙，庙里供的是秃狼本人的泥像，塑得比他本人英俊三倍，匾上写着「新鹞子」。秃狼的人逼着附近的牧民每天来上香，说以后阳关姓秃。牧民们一边磕头一边小声骂，泥像的鼻子已经被人偷偷掰掉了。

column2: Bald Wolf's men flee in disgrace and the herders topple the statue. In ten years, an old herder says, the Hawk never let anyone build him a shrine. Someone once gave him a plaque and he used it to prop up a manger: 'I'm a gatekeeper, minding things others left with me. Gatekeepers don't get incense.' The noseless clay head becomes the children's football.
column3: 秃狼的人落荒而逃，牧民们一拥而上把泥像推倒了。一个老牧民说，鹞子十年来从不许人给他立庙，有人送过他一块匾，他拿去垫了马槽：「我是看门的，看别人寄存的东西，哪有看门的受香火。」没了鼻子的泥像脑袋，被孩子们当球踢了。

column2: Mirage Flat
column3: 蜃影滩

column2: At noon on the flat, a line of figures floats on the horizon, hand in hand, walking west, very slowly, never getting far. The locals say it's the mirage of the Qianli caravan, appearing every noon for ten years. Bald Wolf's men lie in ambush beneath it, robbing anyone it lures out. Xiao Chai says the Hawk used to ride here alone every noon and sit watching the mirage for two hours.
column3: 正午的沙滩上，天边浮着一队人影，一个牵一个往西走，走得极慢，怎么也走不远。附近的人说那是千里号的蜃影，十年来天天正午都出现。秃狼的人在蜃影下面埋伏，专抢被蜃影引过来的人。小柴说，鹞子以前每天正午都一个人骑马到这里，看着蜃影坐一个时辰。

column2: The ambushers are driven off. You stand by the stone where the Hawk used to sit and watch the mirage. You count: two hundred and ninety-nine figures, and far behind them, across a long gap, one more, alone, hurrying after them with a book in his arms. As noon passes, the mirage fades.
column3: 埋伏的人被打跑了。你们站在鹞子常坐的那块石头边上看蜃影，数了数，二百九十九个人影，最后一个人影隔着很远的一段路，一个人追在后面，手里抱着一本书。正午一过，蜃影就散了。

column2: Sand School
column3: 沙书塾

column2: Beneath a poplar an old scholar teaches the herders' children to read. Among them is a little girl called Momo who writes everything down: who passed, when, under what banner, which way, in a little book she sewed herself, more complete than any post station's. Bald Wolf's men have heard and come to take it. The old scholar spreads his arms in front of her, armed only with a stick.
column3: 一棵胡杨树下，一个老秀才教牧民的娃娃识字。娃娃里有个叫墨墨的小姑娘，什么都记：哪天谁从这里过、带着什么旗、往哪边去，记在一本自己缝的小簿子上，记得比驿站还全。秃狼的人听说了，要抢她的簿子，老秀才张开胳膊挡在前面，手里只有一根树枝。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off. Momo opens her book for you: in the last three days, Bald Wolf's troops have marched toward the Hawk's storehouse in band after band, four hundred and twenty-seven in all. She learned record-keeping from a bookkeeper, she says. 'My dad says ten years ago a bookkeeper passed by and taught him: write everything down, and you'll never get your sums wrong.' She thinks a moment, then adds: 'But he still got his wrong.'
column3: 秃狼的人被打跑了。墨墨翻开簿子：这三天，秃狼的人一队队往鹞子仓去了，共四百二十七个。她说她爹当年跟一个路过的账房学记账：「什么都记下来，就不会算错。」她想了想，又补一句：「可他自己还是算错了。」

column2: Water Run
column3: 运水道

column2: The old Yangguan fort is short of water, so the Hawk's men haul it daily from a distant spring, every skin stamped with his seal. Bald Wolf's men are ambushing the run to make Yangguan die of thirst, and the old hands escorting it are fighting for their lives. Captured skins lie everywhere; some have been slashed and the water seeps into the sand, steaming faintly.
column3: 阳关故垒缺水，鹞子的人每天从远处的泉眼运水上去，水囊上都盖着鹞子的印。秃狼的人在半路截水，想把阳关渴垮，押水的老弟兄正跟他们拼命。被截下的水囊扔了一地，有的已经被刀划破，水渗进沙里，冒着一缕缕白气。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are scattered and most of the water saved. The Hawk drinks only one bowl a day himself, an old escort says; the rest goes into a stone trough outside his tent for the kneeling camels. Beside the trough is carved a line: 'Drink, on your masters' behalf.'
column3: 秃狼的人被打散了，水保住了大半。一个押水的老弟兄说，鹞子自己每天只喝一碗，剩下的倒进帐外的石槽，给那些跪着的骆驼喝。石槽边上刻着一行字：「替主人饮之。」

column2: Mirage Stall
column3: 蜃市摊

column2: At noon a stall appears in the shimmering heat, its keeper's face impossible to make out, though everything he sells is real: blades, salt, felt, copperware. People say he's a merchant from the mirage. Lately a gang of rogue soldiers keeps surrounding the stall, demanding the keeper hand over 'the gold of the mirage'. He wavers in and out of the haze and won't show himself.
column3: 正午时分，一片晃动的热气里会冒出一个摊子，摊主的脸看不清，卖的东西却样样是真的：刀、盐、毡子、铜器。人都说这是蜃楼里的商人。可最近摊子总被一伙兵痞围着，他们要摊主交出「蜃楼里的金子」。摊主在热气里晃来晃去，就是不肯露面。

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the keeper steps out of the haze: a small, wiry smuggler who has traded for ten years using the shadows in the heat. Impressed by you, he's glad to trade. He had a stall here ten years ago, he says, and remembers clearly: the camels started kneeling not on the day the caravan left, but on the night the bookkeeper chased after them into the Sand Sea alone.
column3: 兵痞被赶跑了，摊主从热气里走了出来：一个瘦小的走私客，靠着热浪里的影子做了十年买卖。他佩服你们，愿意拿货跟你们换。他说他十年前就在这里摆摊，记得清清楚楚：骆驼跪下，不是从商队走的那天，是从账房先生一个人追进沙海的那天夜里开始的。

column2: False Grave Mound
column3: 假坟岗

column2: A fresh grave on a barren slope, and every day a man kneels before it weeping his heart out, saying his old mother lies there. But the herders say his mother is alive and selling tofu inside the pass. The grave holds Bald Wolf's loot, saved to buy loyalty after he takes Yangguan, and the mourner is its guard. Three months of weeping have given him quite a voice.
column3: 荒坡上一座新坟，坟前天天有个汉子跪着哭，哭得撕心裂肺，说里面埋的是他老娘。可附近的牧民说他娘还活着，在关里卖豆腐。原来坟里埋的是秃狼抢来的赃物，准备打下阳关以后用来收买人心，那个哭坟的是专门守坟的，哭了三个月，嗓子都练出来了。

column2: The grave guard is driven off and you dig it open: crate upon crate of loot. Xiao Chai shakes his head. 'Bald Wolf thinks he can buy the Hawk's old hands with this? They won't even touch the Qianli goods in the storehouse. You think they'd want this?' You return the loot to the families it was taken from.
column3: 守坟的被打跑了，你们挖开坟，里面果然是一箱箱的赃物。小柴看了直摇头：「秃狼拿这些去收买鹞子的老弟兄？他们连鹞子仓里的千里号货都不碰，会要这个？」赃物你们分还给了附近被抢的人家。

column2: Bonfire Flat
column3: 篝火滩

column2: Every full moon, herders gather on this grassland for bonfires, dancing and trading. In past years the Hawk came too, his blind eye under a black cloth, dancing worse than anyone and longer than anyone. This year he didn't come, and Bald Wolf's men gallop in, kick over the fires, snatch the girls' silver, and announce the gathering is now their 'tribute fair'.
column3: 每逢月圆，四方的牧民都会聚到这片草滩上烧篝火、跳舞、换东西。往年鹞子也会来，独眼蒙着黑布，跳得比谁都难看，却跳得最久。今年鹞子没来，秃狼的人骑着马冲了进来，踢翻火堆，抢走姑娘们的银饰，说以后篝火会是他们的「收贡会」。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off, the silver returned, the fires relit, and the herders dance with you until dawn. When the Hawk danced, an old man says, he always faced west, and afterwards sat staring into space. 'He said it was a farewell dance. He never got to dance it that year.'
column3: 秃狼的人被打跑了，银饰还了回去，篝火重新燃起来，牧民们拉着你们跳到天亮。一个老人说，鹞子跳舞的时候总是朝着西边，跳完了就坐着发呆。「他说他跳的是送行的舞，那年没来得及跳。」

column2: Cockfighting Pit
column3: 斗鸡场

column2: A gang of Bald Wolf's men has dug a cockfighting pit here. One rooster has a black cloth tied over its head and is called 'Hawk'; the other has had its crown plucked bald and is called 'Bald Wolf'. Bets are piled round the pit on who wins at Yangguan. The local villages have lost every bird, not even a rooster left to crow, so everyone oversleeps.
column3: 一伙秃狼的人在这里挖了个土坑斗鸡，一只鸡头上绑着黑布，叫「鹞子」，一只脑门拔光了毛，叫「秃狼」，坑边押满了赌注，赌的是阳关这回谁赢。附近村子的鸡被抢得一只不剩，连打鸣的都没有了，村里人早上都睡过了头。

column2: The gamblers are run off and the chickens taken home in baskets. The black-hooded 'Hawk' never lost a single fight. Next morning before dawn, the village rings with crowing. More bets were on the Hawk than on Bald Wolf, a captive admits. 'Even Bald Wolf's own men aren't sure of him.'
column3: 斗鸡的人被打跑了，鸡装进筐里送回了村子。那只蒙黑布的「鹞子」，赌场上一次都没输过。第二天天还没亮，村子里此起彼伏全是鸡叫。被俘的人说，赌鹞子赢的比赌秃狼的多，「连秃狼的人心里都没底。」

column2: Night Watch Sands
column3: 夜哨沙

column2: The last night watch outside Yangguan, kept by a few archers in shifts. But they don't watch outward; they watch inward. The Hawk has ordered them to keep an eye on the camels outside his tent at midnight and record the hour they kneel, every single night, notched on a wooden pole. The pole is covered in notches, dense as a ledger.
column3: 阳关外的最后一道夜哨，几个弓手轮班守着，可他们值夜不看外面，看里面：鹞子吩咐过，半夜要盯着大帐外的骆驼，看它们跪下来的时辰，一天不落记在一根木杆上。木杆上刻满了道道，密密麻麻，像一本账。

column2: The sentries go down and you take the pole. Over three thousand six hundred notches: ten years, not one night missed. The last few are cut especially deep, as if the hand was shaking. The Hawk keeps accounts too, it seems. What he records is his own debt.
column3: 哨兵被打倒，那根木杆被你们带走了。数一数，三千六百多道，十年，一天没落。最后几道刻得特别深，像是刻的人手在抖。鹞子也在记账，记的是他自己欠下的那一笔。

column2: Ruined Beacon Fort
column3: 废烽寨

column2: An abandoned beacon tower on the gobi, thick-walled, with a cistern and views in every direction: an ideal bandit roost. Gang after gang has held it, and the walls are covered in charcoal scrawls of past chiefs' names. With Yangguan unsteady this year, drifters have flocked here on rumours that the Hawk is failing, and the latest lot is busy adding their names to the wall.
column3: 戈壁上一座废弃的烽燧，墙厚、有水窖、四面看得远，是落草的好地方。这里的匪寨换了一茬又一茬，墙上用炭条写满了前几任寨主的名号。这一年阳关不稳，各路流寇听说鹞子快不行了，都往这一带聚，新来的这一伙正忙着把自己的名号写上墙。

column2: This lot is driven off too, leaving half a name on the wall. As long as Yangguan stays unsettled, new drifters will keep coming at the rumour, and new names will go up. When they do, you'll just come back.
column3: 这一伙也被赶走了，名号只写了半个字。只要阳关一天不安稳，就总会有新的流寇闻风而来，在墙上写下新的名字。到时候，再来一趟就是。

column2: Runaway's Slope
column3: 逃卒坡

column2: In the grass below the slope hides an old underling from Yangguan, an arrow in his leg, a few of Bald Wolf's men on his heels. Seeing your banner, he crawls desperately toward you, crying: 'I've got a message for you! It's from the Hawk!' Bald Wolf's men already have their blades raised to silence him.
column3: 坡下的草丛里躲着一个从阳关出来的老喽啰，腿上中了一箭，后面追着几个秃狼的人。他看见你们的旗子，拼命爬过来，嘴里喊：「我有话要带给你们！是鹞子的话！」秃狼的人刀已经举起来了，要灭他的口。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are beaten back. Panting, the old underling says the Hawk sent him. 'The Hawk said: if people under the Qian banner come west, tell them someone at Yangguan has waited ten years for someone to ask him one question: why did you let them through that year.'
column3: 秃狼的人被打退了。老喽啰喘着气说，是鹞子派他出来的：「鹞子说，要是有挂着千字旗的人往西来，叫我告诉他们，阳关上有人等了十年，等着有人来问一句：那年你为什么放他们过去。」

column2: Shepherd's Inn
column3: 羊倌店

column2: A tiny roadside inn run by an old grandmother and her grandson Aji. Aji is twelve and herds the whole village's sheep. One midnight last month, thirty-seven of them broke through the fence on their own and followed a passing line of camels toward Yangguan, and never came back. Aji has run out crying every day since, and some rogue soldiers lodging here locked him in the woodshed for the noise.
column3: 古道边一间小小的车马店，店里只有一个老奶奶和她的孙子阿吉。阿吉十二岁，替全村放羊。上个月一个半夜，三十七只羊自己撞开栅栏，跟着一串路过的骆驼往阳关走了，再也没回来。阿吉天天哭着往外跑，几个兵痞嫌他吵，把他关进了柴房。

column2: The soldiers are driven out and Aji bursts from the woodshed and grabs your sleeve. 'Everyone else's animals come back at dawn, but mine didn't! Someone must have caught them. There's wool on the thorns along the road!' His grandmother sighs and tucks a packet of food into your bag.
column3: 兵痞被赶走，阿吉从柴房里冲出来拉住你们：「别人家的牲口天亮就回来，我的羊没回来！一定是被人截了。路上的刺上挂着羊毛！」老奶奶叹气，往你们包里塞了一包干粮。

column2: In the soldiers' bedding: dozens of catties of fried rice, a bag of horse feed, two fox pelts, and a finely made silver bracelet the grandmother recognises at once, her own dowry, stolen when she was young.
column3: 兵痞的铺盖里藏着几十斤炒米、一袋马料、两张狐皮，还有一只做工很好的银手镯，老奶奶一眼认出是她年轻时被人抢走的嫁妆。

column2: Aji always runs far out to meet you and insists on showing you his sheep. His grandmother steams a pot of milk buns, two each, and makes you take a few more for the road.
column3: 阿吉每次都远远跑出来迎你们，非要带你们去看他的羊。老奶奶蒸一锅奶馍馍，一人两个，还要你们捎几个在路上吃。

column2: Wool Thorns
column3: 挂毛棘

column2: Sure enough, white tufts of wool cling to the camel thorn on both sides of the road. Aji follows behind, counting bush by bush. The wool leads to a fork where a large band of sand-bandit blades is camped, and here the hoofprints tangle: half head on toward Yangguan, half turn off into the sand. Aji knows them: 'The lame one walks crooked!'
column3: 古道两边的骆驼刺上，果然一路挂着白花花的羊毛。阿吉跟在你们后面一棵一棵地数。羊毛一直挂到一个路口，路口驻着一大伙沙匪刀手，地上的蹄印到这里乱成一团，一半往阳关去，一半拐进了沙地。阿吉认得出来：「那只瘸腿的走路是歪的！」

column2: The blades are scattered. A captive says that night they caught the sheep following the camels at the fork, meaning to present them to Bald Wolf, but handed them over to 'the shearing yard' in the sands to the west instead. At the word 'shearing', Aji goes white: 'They'll freeze to death!'
column3: 刀手被打散了，被俘的一个说，那夜他们在路口截下了跟着骆驼走的羊，本想献给秃狼，后来交给了西边沙地里的「剪毛场」。阿吉一听「剪毛」两个字，脸都白了：「它们会冻死的！」

column2: Alfalfa Farm
column3: 苜蓿庄

column2: A lush alfalfa field that feeds the horses of Yangguan; the Hawk buys at a fair price every year and never pays late. Bald Wolf's men have seized the farm and stacked the hay, meaning to cut off Yangguan's fodder so the Hawk's horses go into battle hungry. Nobody's cutting the standing crop, which is going to seed, and the farmers are frantic.
column3: 一片绿油油的苜蓿地，是阳关的马吃的草料，鹞子每年按价收购，从不拖欠。秃狼的人占了庄子，把苜蓿一垛垛码起来，说要断了阳关的草料，让鹞子的马饿着肚子打仗。地里的苜蓿没人割，眼看着要老了，庄户们急得团团转。

column2: Bald Wolf's men are driven off, and the farmers take up their sickles and cut a whole field in a day. Every year, the old farmer says, the Hawk pays for one cartload more than he takes, 'making up for a man who was a cartload of grain short'. The farmer's little granddaughter weaves an alfalfa wreath and hangs it on your flagpole.
column3: 秃狼的人被赶跑了，庄户们抄起镰刀下地，一天割完一大片。老庄主说，鹞子收草料，每年都多付一车的钱，说是「替一个少算了一车粮的人补上」。庄主的小孙女编了个苜蓿花环，挂在你们的旗杆上。

column2: Hidden in the stacked hay: over twenty sacks of fine bean feed, a chest of coins, a few bolts of stolen silk, and a sketch marking the stables at Yangguan.
column3: 秃狼的人码好的草垛里藏着二十多袋精豆料、一箱铜钱、几匹抢来的绸子，还有一张画着阳关马厩位置的草图。

column2: Every time, the farmers load a cart with the tenderest first-cut alfalfa for your horses, and send you off with a jar of alfalfa honey.
column3: 庄户们每次都给你们的马装满一车最嫩的头茬苜蓿，临走还送一罐苜蓿花蜜。

column2: Hawk's Storehouse
column3: 鹞子仓

column2: The Hawk's storehouse lies in a blind gully north of the old Yangguan fort. Bald Wolf and his best troops have finally fought their way here. Only a dozen of the old hands guarding it remain, all wounded, still blocking the door beneath a flag: 'Not to be opened without orders.' Bald Wolf laughs from his saddle: 'The Hawk can't get up. Today this storehouse is mine!'
column3: 阳关故垒北边一条死沟里藏着鹞子仓。秃狼带着他最精锐的人马终于打到了这里，守仓的老弟兄只剩十几个，个个带伤，仍挡在仓门前。仓门上插着一面旗：「非令不开」。秃狼骑在马上狂笑：「鹞子起不来了，今天这仓是我的！」

column2: Bald Wolf's elite is broken and the old hands truss up Bald Wolf himself. The doors open on three hundred camel saddles and three hundred bronze bells, without a speck of dust, and a board on the wall: 'Left by the Qianli caravan. To be collected on return.' 'The Hawk has polished them every day for ten years,' says an old guard. 'He says none of it is his. It's what he owes.'
column3: 秃狼的精锐被打垮了，秃狼本人被老弟兄们捆成了一团。仓门开了，里面码着三百副驼鞍、三百只铜铃，一尘不染，墙上挂着一块牌子：「千里号寄存，回程取。」守仓的老弟兄说：「鹞子十年来天天擦一遍。他说这些不是他的，是他欠的。」

column2: Shearing Yard
column3: 剪毛场

column2: A ring of palisade in the sand holds a small mountain of wool. A gang of sand bandits is shearing with great shears, and the shorn sheep shiver naked in the wind. Aji lies on a dune counting for ages, then stamps his feet: 'None of these are mine! Where are mine?' Hearing the noise, the shearers charge, shears in hand.
column3: 沙地里一圈木栅栏，栅栏里堆着小山一样的羊毛。一伙沙匪正挥着大剪子剪羊毛，剪完的羊光溜溜地在风里发抖。阿吉趴在沙丘上数了半天，急得直跺脚：「这些都不是我的！我的羊呢？」剪毛的沙匪听见动静，拎着剪子就扑了过来。

column2: The shearers are driven off and the wool shared among the owners of the shorn sheep. A captive says Aji's flock wasn't sheared here. 'The boss wouldn't allow it. Said that flock walked with the Qianli camels and mustn't be touched. They're in a sandy hollow further west.'
column3: 剪毛的沙匪被打跑了，羊毛分给了被剪的羊的主人。被俘的人说，阿吉那批羊没在这里剪：「大哥不让剪，说那批羊是跟着千里号的骆驼走的，不能动。在更西边的沙窝子里。」

column2: Foster Son's Slope
column3: 义子坡

column2: The last slope below Yangguan is held by a troop of young riders, the brothers Xiao Chai grew up with. They block your way: 'Our father is ill. Nobody disturbs him.' Xiao Chai stands on your side, head down, saying nothing. The riders look at him with reddened eyes: 'Xiao Chai, you've brought outsiders to fight our father?'
column3: 阳关脚下最后一道坡，守着一伙年轻的骑手，都是小柴从小一起长大的兄弟。他们拦住你们，不让上坡：「我们爹病着，谁也不许去惊他。」小柴站在你们这边，低着头不说话。骑手们看着他，眼睛都红了：「小柴，你带外人来打爹？」

column2: The young riders lose. Only then does Xiao Chai speak: he's an orphan the Hawk took in, and so are all his brothers here. 'I didn't bring you to fight him,' he says. 'He's waited ten years and can't wait any longer. Only if you come in those people's place can he finally say what he has to say.' His brothers stand aside.
column3: 年轻的骑手们输了。小柴这才开口：他是鹞子捡来的孤儿，坡上这些兄弟也都是。「我带你们来，不是打他，」他说，「是他等了十年，等不动了。你们替那些人来，他才能把话说出来。」兄弟们让开了路。

column2: Hollow Sheepfold
column3: 沙窝羊圈

column2: Deep in the sandy hollow stands a sheepfold woven from tamarisk, full of bleating. Aji bursts into tears: 'It's them!' A gang of sand bandits guards the fold, led by a big hard-faced man holding not a blade but a shepherd's whip. He blocks the gate: 'Nobody touches these sheep.'
column3: 沙窝深处一个红柳编的羊圈，圈里传出一片咩咩声。阿吉一听就哭了：「是它们！」守圈的是一伙沙匪，为首的是个满脸横肉的大汉，手里拿的却不是刀，是一根放羊的鞭子。他挡在圈门口：「谁也别想动这些羊。」

column2: The big man squats at the gate and wipes his face. He used to tend the Hawk's animals at Yangguan, and knows them better than anyone. That night, he says, the Hawk had the Qianli camels kneel to be unloaded, the goods stored away to be reloaded on the way home. 'The camels are still kneeling, waiting for someone to load them so they can go home. The sheep followed the camels. They wanted to go home too.' Aji rushes in calling them by name: thirty-seven, not one missing, plus eleven lambs. After a moment's thought, he gives one to the big man: 'You herd well too.' Red-eyed, the man says he'll come with you to Yangguan, whether to see the Hawk one last time or to see him finally let go.
column3: 那大汉蹲在圈门口抹了把脸。他原是阳关给鹞子放牲口的，最懂这些牲口。他说那年夜里，鹞子让千里号的骆驼跪下卸了货，存进仓里，说回程再装。「骆驼一直跪着，是在等人来给它们装货，好回家。羊跟着骆驼，也想回家。」阿吉冲进圈里一只只叫着名字，三十七只，一只不少，还多了十一只小羊羔。阿吉想了想，塞一只给大汉：「你也放得好。」大汉红着眼说，跟你们一起去阳关，见鹞子最后一面也好，见他放下也好。

column2: Old Yangguan Fort
column3: 阳关故垒

column2: The old Yangguan fort stands at the end of the road, walls half fallen, the one-eyed hawk on its black banner. The Hawk's old companions are drawn up three columns wide; not one is Bald Wolf's. Outside the great tent, a hundred and more camels kneel in rows, heads west, the trough full, the storehouse open. White-haired, his blind eye under black cloth, the Hawk leans on his blade on the tower and studies your banner a long time. 'Ten years. Come on, then. Let's see if you've earned the right to ask.'
column3: 阳关故垒立在古道尽头，城墙塌了一半，城楼上插着一面独眼鹞子的黑旗。鹞子的老弟兄们三路排开，没有一个是秃狼的人。大帐外，一百多峰骆驼齐刷刷跪着，头朝西，石槽里的水满着，仓门开着。鹞子一头白发，独眼蒙着黑布，扶着刀站在城楼上，看了你们的旗子很久：「十年了。来吧，看看你们配不配问。」

column2: Beaten, the Hawk sits on the steps and talks. 'I stopped the Qianli caravan for a toll. The bookkeeper showed me his ledger, every debt along the road, all to be repaid on the way home. I said blades are no use in the Sand Sea, sent the guards back, kept the goods as pledge. He said the grain was enough, and I believed him. Next day he found he was a cartload short, and went in after them alone with the ledger.' He hands you the storehouse keys. 'That's the sum I got wrong. The Sand Sea is the Bandit King's. They say a woman there is looking for someone who can keep accounts too.' Outside, one by one, the camels rise.
column3: 鹞子败了，坐在台阶上开了口：「那年我拦下千里号要路钱，账房翻开账本给我看一路的欠账，说回程一并还。我说沙海里刀没用，赶回了护卫，扣下货当押。他说粮够，我信了。第二天他发觉少算一车，抱着账本一个人追进去了。」他把仓门钥匙交给你们：「这是我算错的一笔。沙海是马贼王的地盘，听说那里有个女人，也在找会算账的人。」帐外的骆驼，一峰接一峰站了起来。

column2: The Sea of Sand
column3: 沙海

column2: Roll-Call Stone
column3: 报名碑

column2: At the edge of the Sand Sea stands a waist-high stone, freshly painted in red: 'Whoever enters the Sand Sea, give your name.' A table sits beneath it, and a few bandit footmen guard a fat register, making every traveller state a name and press a thumbprint. Those who refuse get tied to the stone to bake. The Bandit King's rule, they say, and not one character may be skipped. To the east, dune after dune, like waves that froze mid-swell.
column3: 沙海的边上立着一块半人高的石碑，碑上新刷了一行红字：「入沙海者，报上名来。」碑下摆着一张桌子，几个马贼步卒守着一本厚厚的名簿，挨个让过路人报名字、按手印，不报的就绑在碑上晒。他们说这是马贼王的规矩，一个字也不能少。往东看，沙丘一道接一道，像凝住的浪。

column2: The bandits drop the register and run. Ten years of names fill it, everyone who ever walked into the sand. Pasted onto the first page is a yellowed slip in a neat hand: 'The Qianli caravan, three hundred souls. Names in a separate book, pledged with the King.' Pledged for what, it doesn't say. You add your own banner to the last page and step into the Sand Sea.
column3: 马贼们丢下名簿跑了。名簿记了十年，密密麻麻全是进沙海的人。第一页贴着一张发黄的纸条，字迹工整：「千里号三百人，名另册，押于王处。」押的是什么，纸条上没写。你们在名簿最后添上自己的旗号，迈进了沙海。

column2: False Lantern Fair
column3: 假灯市

column2: At dusk a string of white paper lanterns lights up along the dunes and someone hollers, 'The ghost market is open!' Traders hurry over, pay the entry fee, and find only bandits under the lanterns: footmen taking coins, archers on the slope, riders blocking the way out. The real ghost market only comes on the night of the full moon, and tonight is the seventh. Cheated traders squat in the sand; one old man still clutches a bundle of old shoes he meant to sell to the dead.
column3: 天一黑，沙丘上亮起一串白纸灯笼，有人吆喝：「鬼市开张！」赶来的商客交了「入市钱」，才发现灯笼底下只有一伙马贼，步卒收钱，射手守坡，骑手堵着退路。真鬼市只在月圆之夜出现，今天才初七。被骗的商客蹲了一地，有个老头还攥着一包要卖给鬼的旧鞋。

column2: The fake lanterns are stamped out one by one. But on the bandits' pole hangs one real lantern they never dared take down: an abacus painted on white paper, its wick cold for ten years and still not rotted. That, says the old man, is a lantern of the true ghost market, where a mute stallholder sells the things the Sand Sea has lost. 'The real market,' he says, 'finds you on the night of the full moon.'
column3: 假灯笼被一盏盏踩灭。马贼的灯杆上，却挂着一盏他们不敢摘的真灯：白纸上画着一架算盘，灯芯冷了十年也没烂。老头说，这是真鬼市的灯，市上有个哑巴摊主，专卖沙海里丢掉的东西。「真鬼市啊，」他说，「月圆那天自己会找你。」

column2: Moonwatch Terrace
column3: 观月台

column2: On an earthen terrace by the old road lives a moon-watcher with a bronze armillary sphere. Every month he announces the full moon for the ghost market, and he may be neither early nor late. Bandit footmen have ringed the terrace for three days, demanding to know where this month's market will open so they can raid it. The old man hugs his sphere and will only give the weather: 'Clear tonight. Good for travel. Bad for robbery.'
column3: 古道边一座土台，台上住着个观月的老人，守着一架铜浑仪，每月替鬼市报一次月圆，报早报晚都不行。一伙马贼步卒把台子围了三天，要他说出这个月鬼市开在哪儿，好去抢。老人把浑仪抱在怀里，只肯报天气：「今夜无云，宜赶路，不宜抢劫。」

column2: The bandits scatter. The old man shows you the moon: nine more days to full. Ten years ago, he remembers, another party asked about the ghost market, led by a young bookkeeper's apprentice with a big abacus on his back. 'He asked whether the market gave credit.' The old man smiles. 'It does. But a debt to the dead is harder to repay than a debt to the living.'
column3: 马贼散了。老人请你们看月亮，说再过九天就圆。他记得十年前也有一伙人来问过鬼市，领头的是个年轻的账房学徒，背着一架大算盘。「他问鬼市收不收赊账。」老人笑了，「鬼市收。可欠鬼的账，比欠人的难还。」

column2: Gleaners' Cart
column3: 拾遗车

column2: A family of gleaners drives a creaking cart, picking up whatever the sandstorms dig out: broken hairpins, coins, half a boot, a split drum. When the cart is full they haul it to the ghost market at full moon. Bandit footmen have stopped them, declaring that 'everything in the sand belongs to the Bandit King', and are stuffing the junk into their own pockets. The gleaners' little girl sits on top of the load, pinging the backs of their heads with a slingshot.
column3: 一家子拾荒人赶着一辆吱呀作响的大车，专捡沙暴刮出来的东西：断簪、铜钱、半只靴子、一面裂了的鼓，攒满一车，等月圆拉去鬼市卖。一伙马贼步卒拦住大车，说「沙里的东西都归马贼王」，正把车上的破烂往自己口袋里塞。拾荒人家的小闺女坐在车顶上，拿弹弓打他们的后脑勺。

column2: The bandits run off. The girl puts away her slingshot and digs a bronze steelyard weight from under the cart, cast with the character Qian. That mute at the ghost market, her father says, takes anything marked Qian, however battered. He never pays in coin, only in water, a pound of water for a pound of bronze. 'It's like he's buying it all back, piece by piece.'
column3: 马贼被打跑，小闺女收起弹弓，从车底翻出一枚铜秤砣给你们看，上面铸着个「千」字。拾荒人说，鬼市上那个哑巴，见了带「千」字的东西，不论多破都收，不付钱，付水，一斤铜换一斤水。「他好像在一件件往回买。」

column2: The Ice Cellar
column3: 藏冰窖

column2: Nobody expects ice in the Sand Sea. Every winter the old ice-keeper cuts blocks in the mountains and buries them in a deep cellar on the shady side of a dune; in summer he digs them out one at a time, and a bowl of ice water can save a life. Now bandit archers hold the cellar mouth and charge a tael of silver a bowl. Those who can't pay stand there and watch the ice melt. The ice-keeper is tied up at the bottom, sneezing with cold.
column3: 谁也想不到沙海里有冰。老冰户每年冬天从山里凿冰，埋在沙丘背阴处的深窖里，夏天一块块挖出来卖，一碗冰水能救一条命。如今窖口被一伙马贼射手占了，冰水卖到一两银子一碗，买不起的就在窖口看着冰化。老冰户被他们捆在窖底，冻得直打喷嚏。

column2: With the bandits gone, the ice-keeper climbs out in three layers of fur and the first thing he does is chip you each a bowl of ice. Ten years ago, he says, the Qianli caravan came through and the apprentice took twenty bowls on credit, with an IOU. Last year a mute turned up and paid it off with ten years' interest, to the copper. 'I asked who worked out the interest. He pointed at the sky.'
column3: 马贼被赶走，老冰户裹着三层皮袄爬上来，第一件事是给你们每人凿一碗冰。他说十年前千里号路过，账房学徒赊了二十碗冰，写了欠条；去年一个哑巴来了，按十年的利息还清了，一文不差。「我问他利息是谁算的，他指指天上。」

column2: From the cellar you seize the bandits' hoard: thirty whole blocks of ice, a vat of chilled grapes, two baskets of fish frozen stiff, and a ledger titled 'Ice Sales'. Its last line reads: 'Ice melted. Made a loss.'
column3: 窖里抄出马贼囤的三十块整冰、一缸冰镇的葡萄、两篓冻得梆硬的鱼干，还有一本记着「卖冰进账」的流水，最后一行写着：「冰化了，亏本。」

column2: Every time, the ice-keeper is waiting at the cellar mouth. He wraps ice in felt and packs it in your saddlebags, where it lasts a whole day, and drops a few frozen grapes into your waterskins 'to keep you company on the road'.
column3: 老冰户每次都在窖口等你们，把冰块裹在毡子里塞进驮袋，一天也化不完；临走还往你们水囊里丢几颗冰葡萄，说是「路上解闷」。

column2: The Banknote Kiln
column3: 印钞窑

column2: Black smoke rises from a ruined kiln on the plain. Bandit footmen have caught a few failed examination scholars and keep them carving blocks and printing day and night. Not silver notes: spirit money, the paper burned for the dead. Word is the ghost market only takes the currency of the dead, so the bandits mean to print a roomful and buy the whole market out at full moon. The scholars' hands are black with ink, and they're made to write poems on every note.
column3: 荒原上一座废窑冒着黑烟，一伙马贼步卒抓了几个落第秀才，日夜刻版印钞，印的不是银票，是冥钞：听说鬼市只收烧给死人的钱，他们要印一屋子，月圆那天去鬼市把东西全买空。秀才们印得手都黑了，还被逼着在钞上题诗。

column2: The kiln goes out and a roomful of spirit money blows across the sky. The market won't take any of it, the scholars say: that mute stallholder accepts nobody's money at all, only an honest settling of some account. The bandit chief doesn't believe it and runs west hugging a bundle. The scholars keep one note. The poem on it is rather good.
column3: 窑火熄了，满屋冥钞被风吹得漫天飞。秀才们说，这些钱鬼市根本不收：那个哑巴摊主谁的钱都不要，只要人跟他把一笔账算清楚。马贼头子不信，抱着一捆冥钞往西跑了。秀才们留下一张钞，上面的诗写得还不错。

column2: Wooden Ox Slope
column3: 木牛坡

column2: At the foot of the slope lies a strange half-buried wagon: a wooden ox harnessed in front, its legs full of gears, so that one push makes it walk three steps by itself. A few bandit footmen have moved in, cooking in the wagon bed, and have taken off one of the ox's legs for a rolling pin. Half a brand survives on the shaft. It is plainly the character Qian.
column3: 坡下半埋着一辆怪车，车身木头做的，前面装着一头木牛，腿上有机括，推一下能自己走三步。几个马贼步卒把木牛车当了窝，在车厢里生火做饭，还拆了一条木牛腿当擀面杖。车辕上有半块烙印，看得出是个「千」字。

column2: You chase the bandits out and fit the leg back on, and the ox actually clacks forward another three steps. The floorboards are cut with rows of tally marks, sack after sack of grain, and the last line is gouged deep: 'Axle broken here. One cartload of grain short. Bought on credit at the ghost market.' So the cartload the Hawk said the bookkeeper miscounted is this one.
column3: 马贼被赶出来，你们把木牛腿装了回去，它居然咔嗒咔嗒又走了三步。车厢底板上刻着一排排记号，是一袋袋粮的数目，最后一行刻得很深：「此车轴断，粮短一车，鬼市赊之。」原来鹞子说账房「少算一车」，少的就是这一车。

column2: Smuggler's Hollow
column3: 私盐窝

column2: A salt smuggler called Whitebeard hides in this hollow. The beard is truly white, the salt is truly white, only the scales are crooked, and he admits it. Bandit footmen have taken his salt wagons as tribute for the Bandit King, down to the pinch he seasons his supper with. Whitebeard sits on his empty cart cursing until he's hoarse, then beckons you over. 'Whoever gets it back for me gets a discount.'
column3: 沙窝里藏着个私盐贩子，外号「白胡子」，胡子是真白，盐也是真白，只有秤是假的，他自己也承认。一伙马贼步卒抢了他的盐车，说要整车拿去给马贼王纳贡，连他吃饭的那撮盐都搜走了。白胡子坐在空车上骂了半天，骂到嗓子哑了，冲你们一招手：「谁替我抢回来，便宜卖。」

column2: You bring back the wagons. Whitebeard smashes his crooked scales in front of you and hangs up an honest pair: 'No tricks on the people who saved me.' He starts trading with you and mentions, in passing, that the mute from the ghost market buys a pound of salt every month, never haggles, and heads east with it. 'Can't think how one man eats that much salt.'
column3: 盐车抢回来了，白胡子当着你们的面把假秤砸了，换上一杆真秤，说「对恩人不使诈」。他跟你们做起了买卖，还顺口说：鬼市那个哑巴每月都来买一斤盐，从不还价，买完就往东走，「也不知道一个人吃得了那么咸」。

column2: Shadow-Tax Slope
column3: 量影坡

column2: Tax men from some tiny desert kingdom sit on this slope collecting a shadow tax: they measure your shadow in the sun, one coin per foot. They only collect at sunset, when shadows are longest and a thin man can measure thirty feet. Bandit archers serve as their muscle and shoot the shadow of anyone who won't pay, until the sand bristles with arrows.
column3: 坡上坐着一个小沙国的税丁队，收的是「影子税」：太阳下量你的影子，一尺影子一文钱。他们专挑傍晚收，那时候影子最长，一个瘦子能被量出三丈。马贼射手给他们当打手，谁不交就射谁的影子，射得沙地上全是箭。

column2: The tax men flee with their measuring cords and leave their ledger behind. It lists everyone who paid the shadow tax in ten years, and one entry is marked 'exempt': a mute with an abacus who 'comes by moonlight and goes by moonlight, no shadow to measure'. So he only travels at night. In the margin the chief tax man has written: 'Odd fellow. Leave him be.'
column3: 税丁们抱着量绳跑了，丢下一本税簿。簿上记着十年来每个交过影子税的人，只有一条写着「免」：一个背算盘的哑巴，「月下来，月下走，无影可量」。原来他只在夜里赶路。税丁头子在簿边批了一句：「此人怪，勿惹。」

column2: Tribute Plain
column3: 纳贡原

column2: A ring of felt tents stands on the plain, and bandit riders gallop circles around it demanding this month's tribute. The herders lay their offerings out front: a bag of dried curd, two fox pelts, a mynah bird that mimics people. The rider captain says it's not enough and reaches for the mynah, which speaks first: 'King's rule, one in ten! One in ten!'
column3: 荒原上几顶毡帐围成一圈，一伙马贼骑手绕着帐子跑马，喊着要这个月的贡。牧人们把东西摆在帐前：一袋奶疙瘩、两张狐皮、一只会学人说话的八哥。骑手头目嫌少，说要把八哥带走，八哥抢先开了口：「王的规矩，十取一！十取一！」

column2: The riders are driven off. The Bandit King's tribute isn't heavy, the old herder says: one in ten, and no killing. The cruel ones are the small gangs collecting in his name. The King laid down three rules everyone in the Sand Sea can recite: 'Never rob the Qian banner. Never raid the ghost market. Never close the old road.' The mynah recites them again, more fluently than any person.
column3: 骑手们被赶跑了。老牧人说，马贼王的贡其实不重，十取一，还不许杀人；凶的是那些打着王旗号私收的小股。王立过三条规矩，沙海里人人会背：「不劫千字旗，不抢鬼市，不断古道。」八哥又背了一遍，背得比人还熟。

column2: Fallen Dove Slope
column3: 落鸽坡

column2: In the days before each full moon, flocks of pigeons fan out across the Sand Sea, little bamboo tubes on their legs: the ghost market's notices to its regulars. Bandit archers squat on this slope shooting them down and opening the messages, hoping to find the market first. Feathers cover the slope, and the bandits curse as they read: no words, only drawings of abacus beads.
column3: 每到月圆前几天，沙海上空就有成群的鸽子往四面飞，鸽腿上绑着小竹筒，是鬼市给熟客报信的。一伙马贼射手蹲在坡上专射鸽子，射下来拆信，想抢在别人前头找到鬼市。坡下落了一地鸽毛，马贼们一边拆信一边骂：信上没字，只画着算盘珠子。

column2: With the archers gone you save one living pigeon. You can't read the bead drawing in its tube, but an old trader nearby can: the mute never speaks, he says everything in beads. 'Two up, three down is the moon; one up, four down is the market.' He's telling his regulars that this month the market opens south of the old road. The pigeon flaps away to the southeast.
column3: 射手被赶走，你们救下一只还活着的鸽子。竹筒里的珠图你们看不懂，旁边一个老商客倒认得：哑巴不说话，所有的话都拨在珠子上，「上二下三是月，上一下四是市」。他在告诉熟客，这个月，市开在古道南边。鸽子扑棱棱往东南飞去了。

column2: Sand Teahouse
column3: 沙茶寮

column2: By the old road stands a tea shack kept by a squinting old woman who can read anything in the leaves, and what she reads best is where next month's ghost market will be. She is in fact the market's broker, matching buyers and sellers. Bandit archers have taken over the shack and make her read their leaves every day. Three hundred bowls later, all she has seen is: 'You're in for bad luck.'
column3: 古道边有间茶寮，卖茶的是个眯眼老婆婆，什么都能从茶叶渣里看出来，看得最准的是鬼市下个月开在哪。她其实是鬼市的牙婆，替买家卖家牵线。一伙马贼射手霸着茶寮，天天逼她看茶渣，喝了三百碗，看出来的只是「你们要倒霉」。

column2: 'Told you. Bad luck.' The old woman clears the bowls, brews you one, and studies the leaves. This month's market will be in the courtyard of the old inn south of the road, opening when the moon stands overhead. And the mute, she adds, won't sell to anyone whose accounts aren't square. 'Whether you owe him anything, you'll find out when you get there.'
column3: 「看吧，倒霉了吧。」老婆婆收拾茶碗，给你们泡了一碗，看了看渣：这个月的鬼市在古道南边的旧客栈院里，等月亮正当头才开。她又说，哑巴的摊子不卖给没算清账的人。「你们欠没欠他的账，去了就知道。」

column2: Tally Tree
column3: 欠签树

column2: A dead poplar is hung all over with wooden tallies that clack in the wind. Each records a debt: 'Forty skins of water', 'One guide, three days', 'Two bundles of camel thorn'. All are signed 'Qianli', followed by two words: 'to follow'. Bandit archers are taking them down one by one, meaning to collect from the caravan's heirs, and already have a basketful.
column3: 一棵枯死的胡杨上挂满了木签，风一吹叮叮当当。每根签上写着一笔账：「水四十囊」「向导一人三日」「骆驼草两捆」，落款都是「千里号」，后面跟两个字：「后补」。一伙马贼射手正一根根往下摘，说要拿着签去找千里号的后人讨钱，摘下来的签堆了一筐。

column2: The archers run and you hang the tallies back up. Forty-one. On forty of them someone else's hand has added the word 'settled', the ink fresher year by year. Only the highest remains: 'Bandit King. Road toll. Three hundred souls. Payable on the way home.' Its 'settled' is only half written, and beside it are cut over a hundred tiny strokes.
column3: 射手们跑了，你们把签挂回去，一数，四十一根。四十根上都用另一个人的笔迹添了个「清」字，墨色一年比一年新。只剩最高的一根：「马贼王，路钱，三百人，回程付。」那上面的「清」只写了一半，旁边刻着密密麻麻的一百多道小横。

column2: Sleeping Elephant Flats
column3: 卧象原

column2: An elephant lies on the plain, grey as a boulder. They say a western embassy brought it as tribute over ten years ago, lost it in the Sand Sea, and it never found the way out. Bandit footmen want it to carry their loot. They've tried whips and they've tried melons; it won't get up, and it has already sat their tent flat. A faded saddlebag hangs from its neck, just out of their reach.
column3: 荒原上卧着一头大象，灰得像块石头。听说是十几年前西边的使团进贡的，在沙海里走丢了，一直没走出去。一伙马贼步卒想让它驮赃物，拿鞭子抽、拿瓜哄，它就是不起，一屁股坐塌了马贼的帐篷。大象脖子上挂着个褪了色的鞍袋，马贼们够不着。

column2: The bandits flee and the elephant slowly stands and hands you the saddlebag with its trunk. Inside: a bag of melon seeds and a bead drawing. A passing salt carrier says the elephant walked with the Qianli caravan for a stretch, and the mute from the ghost market couldn't bear to leave it; for ten years he has come once a month to feed it melons. It follows you a while, then turns back and lies down in its old spot to wait.
column3: 马贼被打跑，大象慢慢站起来，用鼻子把鞍袋递给你们。袋里是一包瓜子和一张珠图。过路的盐贩说，这象当年跟着千里号走过一段，鬼市的哑巴舍不得它，十年来每月来喂它一回瓜。它跟着你们走了一程，又自己回去，卧在原地等了。

column2: Scale Stone
column3: 判秤石

column2: A great blue stone stands in the sand with a bone steelyard on top, and beside it sits a thin old man in a worn official's cap who calls himself the Market Warden. Every deal in the ghost market passes his scale and goes in his book: the living buying from the dead, the dead buying from the living. Bandit archers want his book to see who bought treasure there. He doesn't move. 'Everything written here,' he says, 'is a debt.'
column3: 沙里立着一块大青石，石上放着一杆骨头秤，秤旁坐着个戴旧官帽的瘦老头，自称「鬼市市令」。鬼市里的每一笔买卖都要过他的秤、记他的簿，人买鬼的、鬼买人的，都记。一伙马贼射手想抢他的簿子，翻看谁在鬼市买了宝贝。老头不躲，只说：「簿子上记的，都是欠账。」

column2: The bandits gone, the warden opens his book to a page from ten years ago. The Qianli caravan took a cartload of grain and forty skins of water on credit, pledging eighteen bolts of silk, an iron pot, a drum... Signed: A Suan, apprentice bookkeeper. Beside it, in small characters: 'The apprentice stays at the market of his own will to redeem the pledges. Until they are redeemed, he will not speak.' So the mute is silent by choice.
column3: 马贼跑了，市令翻开簿子给你们看十年前的一页：千里号在鬼市赊了一车粮、四十囊水，押的是十八匹丝、一口铁锅、一面鼓……落款是账房学徒阿算。旁边一行小字：「学徒自愿留市，赎回所押。赎清之前，不开口。」原来那个哑巴，是自己不说话的。

column2: Forged Receipt Slope
column3: 伪票坡

column2: On this slope a gang of bandit footmen, short of this month's tribute, has grabbed an old scholar and is forcing him to forge the Bandit King's tribute receipts. His brushwork is beautiful, but every receipt sticks at the last step: he can't carve the King's seal. The bandits pace in a panic and hold a blade to his throat: 'Get it right, or you're the tribute.'
column3: 坡上一伙马贼步卒交不上这个月的贡，抓了个会写字的老先生，逼他伪造马贼王的收贡凭票，想蒙混过关。老先生写得一手好字，可每张票都卡在最后一步：王的印他刻不出来。马贼们急得团团转，拿刀架在他脖子上：「再刻不像，你就去给王纳贡！」

column2: The bandits flee and the old scholar shows you a genuine receipt. The King's seal isn't the character for 'King' at all. It's Qian, in seal script. Three days he's held the knife and not dared to cut. 'A bandit who uses a caravan's name for his own seal,' he says. 'There's a story in that.'
column3: 马贼被打跑，老先生拿出一张真票给你们看：王的印不是「王」字，是一个篆书的「千」。他说他刻了三天都不敢下刀，「一个马贼，拿商队的字号当自己的印，这里头有故事」。

column2: The Widow's Hold
column3: 寡妇寨

column2: The chief of this sand fort died and his widow, a woman who shoots two bows at once, took it over. When the King's collectors came, she said the chief was dead so the tribute was cancelled; the collectors said rules were rules. They've traded arrows for three days, her archers holding the wall against all comers, and they take you for collectors too.
column3: 这座沙寨的寨主死了，寨子归了他的遗孀，一个使双弓的女人。王的收贡队上门，她说寨主死了，贡就免了，收贡的说规矩就是规矩。两边对射了三天，女寨主的射手守着寨墙，谁也不让进，连你们也被当成了收贡的。

column2: Once the mistake is cleared up she lowers her bows. Her husband, she says, broke the King's rule and robbed a caravan flying a Qian banner, and the King cut him down himself. But he sent the body home in a fine coffin, with a year's grain. 'He keeps his rules,' she says, 'even if it means killing his own. I hate him, and I respect him.'
column3: 误会说开了，女寨主收了弓。她说寨主是犯了王的规矩，劫了一面带「千」字的旗，被王亲手砍了。可王把尸首用一口好棺材送了回来，还送了一年的粮。「他讲规矩，」她说，「讲到连自己的人都杀。我恨他，可我服他。」

column2: Moonfall Ambush
column3: 伏月营

column2: Behind a sand ridge south of the old road lies a big bandit band, foot, bow and horse, with sacks and ropes piled up, waiting for the full moon to storm the ghost market the moment it opens. Their chief sharpens his blade at the moon every night until it shines brighter than the moon does. A board hangs at the gate with its words scraped off by a knife, all but one: 'King'.
column3: 古道南边的沙梁后面伏着一大伙马贼，步卒、射手、骑手都有，营里堆着麻袋和绳子，专等月圆那夜鬼市一开就冲进去抢个干净。他们的头目天天对着月亮磨刀，磨得刀比月亮还亮。营门口挂着一块木牌，上面的字被人用刀刮掉了，只剩一个「王」字。

column2: The band broken, you find the rest of the board's words in the chief's tent, a decree of the Bandit King: 'The ghost market is not to be robbed. Offenders lose a hand.' The chief came without the King's knowing. Nobody understands the King's rules, a prisoner says. That mute from the market brings the King something every month, and the King won't let anyone lay a finger on him.
column3: 马贼被打散，你们在头目帐里找到那块木牌刮下来的另一半，是马贼王的禁令：「鬼市不许抢，违者剁手。」头目是瞒着马贼王来的。俘虏说，王的规矩谁都不懂，鬼市里的哑巴每月去给王送东西，王从来不许人碰他一根指头。

column2: Impostors' Camp
column3: 冒名营

column2: A caravan flies a great Qianli banner and claims to be the very caravan that vanished ten years ago, back to collect what it's owed. They wave a sheaf of IOUs at everyone: 'Qianli left goods with you. Hand them over!' Nobody can say they're lying, so people pay. A band of bandit archers guards them. The banner is freshly dyed, and the ink on the IOUs isn't dry.
column3: 一支商队打着「千里号」的大旗，说他们就是十年前失踪的千里号，回来收账了，见人就拿出一叠欠条：「当年千里号在你这儿存过货，交出来！」谁也说不清真假，只好掏钱。护着这支商队的是一伙马贼射手，旗子是新染的，欠条上的墨还没干。

column2: The fake banner comes down to reveal another firm's name stitched underneath. Their leader confesses: they saw a mute at the ghost market paying off the Qianli caravan's debts one by one, and thought they'd turn it around and collect in Qianli's name. You tear up the IOUs. The real Qianli banner, says an old man they cheated, was a huge white cloth like a sail. 'In the wind it looked like a ship. Yours is far too small.'
column3: 假旗被扯下来，底下缝着另一家商号的名字。领头的招了：他们在鬼市见过一个哑巴，替千里号一笔一笔还旧账，就想反过来冒充千里号去讨账。你们把欠条撕了。被骗的老人说，真千里号的旗子是一面白帆一样的大布，「风一吹，像船，你们这面太小了」。

column2: Full-Moon Ghost Market
column3: 月圆鬼市

column2: With the moon overhead, white lamps light one by one in the courtyard of the old inn south of the road, and stalls appear out of nowhere: broken swords for sale, old dreams, lost names. The stallholders are pale, and their voices make no echo. But tonight bandit riders storm the courtyard with drawn blades; the stalls go dark one after another and their keepers retreat into the moonlight. Only one stall in the corner stays, kept by a young man with an abacus on his back, saying nothing.
column3: 月亮正当头，古道南边的旧客栈院子里一盏盏亮起白灯，摊子凭空摆了出来：卖断剑的，卖旧梦的，卖丢了的名字的。摊主们脸色都很淡，说话没有回声。可今夜一伙马贼骑手闯进了院子，挥着刀要抢，摊子一个个暗下去，摊主们退进了月光里。只有角落里一个摊子没走，摊主是个背算盘的年轻人，一声不吭。

column2: The riders are driven out and the white lamps come back one by one. The ghost market is open again: timber from beyond the Sand Sea trades for oasis grain, and the dead buy wood too, for coffins. The mute stallholder flicks his abacus. The beads stop at three hundred, then at a hundred and twenty. From under his stall he hands you the cover of a ledger marked 'Qianli: the Sand Sea', its pages gone. In the sand he writes four words: 'The account is with the King.'
column3: 马贼被赶出院子，白灯又一盏盏亮回来，鬼市重新开张：沙海外的木料拿来换绿洲的粮食，鬼也收木头，说是打棺材用。那个哑巴摊主拨了拨算盘，珠子停在「三百」，又停在「一百二十」。他从摊下取出一本账簿的封皮递给你们，上面写着「千里号·沙海段」，里面是空的。他在沙上写了四个字：「账在王处。」

column2: Debt Collectors' Camp
column3: 讨债营

column2: After the market fades, a big camp goes up on the plain under a sign reading 'Old Qianli Debts Collected'. These people bought up every Qianli IOU in the Sand Sea for next to nothing and hired a large bandit force, foot, bow and horse. Now they're hunting the mute: if he's paying Qianli's debts, let him pay these, principal and interest, ten times over.
column3: 鬼市散后，荒原上扎起一座大营，营门挂着「代收千里号旧债」的幌子。这伙人低价收了满沙海的千里号欠条，雇了一大伙马贼，步、射、骑俱全，正四处搜那个哑巴：听说他替千里号还账，那就找他要，连本带利，要十倍。

column2: The camp torn down, you go through a chest of IOUs. Every one is in the bookkeeper's hand, and half of them already say 'settled' on the back; the collectors never turned them over. Their leader moans that he's ruined. You give the settled ones to the Market Warden, and keep the few unsettled ones to hand to the mute yourselves.
column3: 讨债营被拔了，你们翻出一箱欠条，一张张对过，全是账房的笔迹，可有一半早已在背面写了「清」字，是收债人自己没翻过来看。领头的哭丧着脸说亏大了。已清的你们交给了鬼市市令，剩下几张没清的，你们收好，打算亲手交给那个哑巴。

column2: Redemption Shed
column3: 赎货棚

column2: Following the way the mute drew in the sand, you find a small shed on the plain, its walls made of old crates, every board branded Qian. Bandit riders are inside smashing crates open in search of silver. What they find are bolts of old silk folded just so, an iron pot scrubbed till it shines, a mended drum.
column3: 循着哑巴在沙上画的路，你们找到荒原上一座小棚，四壁是用旧货箱拼起来的，箱板上都烙着「千」。一伙马贼骑手正在棚里翻箱倒柜，把一只只箱子劈开找银子，找到的却是一匹匹叠得整整齐齐的旧丝，一口擦得锃亮的铁锅，一面补好的鼓。

column2: The riders driven off, you close the crates again. A list is pinned to the wall: the forty-seven things pledged at the ghost market. Thirty-one are crossed out, each with a note of how much water, how much salt and how many years it took to buy it back. Among the sixteen left is one line: 'With the King. Three hundred names.'
column3: 骑手们被赶跑，你们把箱子一只只合上。墙上贴着一张单子，是当年在鬼市押出去的四十七样东西，已经划掉三十一样，每划一样，旁边记着用多少水、多少盐、多少年换回来的。剩下没划的十六样里，有一样写着：「王处，名字三百。」

column2: Tooth-Puller's Cart
column3: 拔牙铺

column2: A wandering tooth-puller works this plain with a cart, a pair of pliers and a banner reading 'Painless Extractions', which is a lie. Bandit riders have seized him and are making him pull the gold teeth of every passer-by; those whose teeth won't come out get carried off teeth and all. His hands shake. All his life, he protests, he has pulled bad teeth, never good ones.
column3: 荒原上有个走方的牙医，一辆车、一把钳子、一面写着「拔牙不疼」的幌子，幌子是骗人的。一伙马贼骑手把他扣下，逼他把过路人的金牙全拔下来，拔不下来的连人带牙一起抢走。牙医被逼得手直抖，说他这辈子只拔坏牙，好牙不拔。

column2: The riders flee and the tooth-puller packs his pliers. He knows the mute, he says. Ten years ago, right here, he pulled a bad tooth for the Qianli apprentice. The boy cried with the pain, and when he was done crying he said: 'Until I've paid every debt we ran up on this road, I won't open my mouth again.' It was the last thing the tooth-puller ever heard him say.
column3: 骑手们跑了，牙医收好钳子，说他认识那个哑巴。十年前在这儿，他给千里号的账房学徒拔过一颗坏牙，那孩子疼得直哭，哭完了说：「这一路欠下的账，我不还清，就不再张嘴。」牙医说，那是他听见那孩子说的最后一句话。

column2: Sandfish Flats
column3: 沙鱼滩

column2: The sand on these flats is loose as water, and beneath it swim sandfish, palm-long and slippery, good for medicine once dried. Bandit riders gallop back and forth dragging nets through the sand to sell the catch at the ghost market, the sand rolling in waves behind them. Today the net has hauled up something odd: a little pouch sewn from fish skin, tied up tight.
column3: 这片滩上的沙子松得像水，底下游着一种沙鱼，手掌长，滑溜溜的，晒干了能入药。一伙马贼骑手拖着大网在沙里来回跑，捞鱼去鬼市换东西，网过之处沙浪翻滚。今天网里捞上来一只奇怪的东西：一个鱼皮缝的小口袋，扎得严严实实。

column2: With the riders gone you open the pouch: a bead drawing, with a charcoal translation beside it, apparently by the old broker from the teahouse. 'What my master owed, I repay. The King's sum, a tael a month, I can never finish.' A thin cord is tied to the pouch. Someone let it into the quicksand on purpose, like a letter with nowhere to go.
column3: 马贼被打跑，你们打开鱼皮袋，里面是一张珠图，旁边有人用炭写了译文，像是茶寮牙婆的手笔：「师父欠的，我还。王的那一笔，每月一两，我还不完。」袋口拴着一根细绳。是有人故意把它放进流沙，像一封寄不出去的信。

column2: Waiting-Word Slope
column3: 等话坡

column2: A flower girl lives on this slope, with a yard of tamarisk blooms she coaxed out of the desert. At every ghost market she sets up her stall next to the mute's. For ten years she has been waiting for him to say one word. Now a bandit archer chief has taken a fancy to her and sent men to carry her off. Half the garden is trampled, and she stands in the doorway with her shears: 'Whoever comes in loses his beard.'
column3: 坡上住着个卖花的姑娘，在沙海里种出一院子红柳花，每逢鬼市就去摆摊，摊子挨着那个哑巴。她等他开口说一句话，等了十年。一伙马贼射手的头目看上了她，派人来抢亲，花院子被踩烂了一半，姑娘拿着花剪站在门口：「谁敢进来，我剪谁的胡子。」

column2: The would-be grooms flee clutching their chins. As she props up her flowers, the girl tells you the mute leaves a sprig of oleaster blossom on her stall every time he packs up, and hasn't missed once in ten years. 'He doesn't speak. I know it's because his accounts aren't square.' She presses a bunch of tamarisk on you. 'When you see the Bandit King, ask him how much is still owed.'
column3: 抢亲的射手们捂着下巴跑了。姑娘一边扶花一边说，那个哑巴每次收摊都会在她摊上留一枝沙枣花，十年没断过。「他不说话，我知道他有账没还完。」她把一束红柳花塞给你们：「你们见了马贼王，替我问问，还差多少。」

column2: Vulture Terrace
column3: 养鹫台

column2: A dozen vultures roost on an earthen terrace. The bandit archers who keep them use them to find the dead: wherever vultures circle, some trader has died of thirst, and his baggage is easy pickings. For days the flock has been circling the terrace, and the archers, thinking a big haul is near, are about to set out, until they realise the vultures are staring at you.
column3: 一座土台上歇着十几只秃鹫，养鹫的马贼射手靠它们找死人：哪里有鹫在打转，哪里就有渴死在沙里的商客，去扒他们的行李最省事。这几天鹫群一直在台上打转，射手们以为来了大买卖，正准备出发，却发现鹫们盯着的是你们。

column2: The archers scatter and the old vulture-keeper sighs. His birds never fly over the old road. The King sends men along it to gather the dead; whoever dies on the road is buried the next day, with a wooden marker bearing his name. 'The King says no nameless bones on the old road.'
column3: 射手们被打散，养鹫的老头叹气：这些鹫从来不往古道上飞。王派人沿着古道收尸，谁死在古道上，第二天就有人埋了，坟前插一根木签，写上名字。「王说，古道上不许有没名字的骨头。」

column2: Seven-Notch Post
column3: 七刀桩

column2: An old wooden post stands in the sand, cut with seven knife notches. Every bandit says this is where the Bandit King began: ten years ago he and six brothers swore blood oaths here. Now a band of bandit archers has fenced it off as a shrine, kowtowing and burning incense daily, and anyone who stares too long gets his hat shot off.
column3: 沙里立着一根老木桩，桩上砍着七道刀痕。马贼都说这是马贼王起家的地方，十年前他带着六个兄弟在这儿歃血。如今一伙马贼射手把木桩围起来当了神，天天磕头上香，不许外人走近，谁多看一眼，就射谁的帽子。

column2: The archers driven off, you brush the sand from the foot of the post and find a line of small characters: 'Dingwei year. Seven sworn to bring the Qian banner out of White Dragon Mound.' Of the seven notches, six are old and one is new, cut only last year, very deep, as if someone came here alone and sat all night.
column3: 射手们被赶跑，你们拂开桩脚的沙，底下还刻着一行小字：「丁未年，七人立誓，护千字旗出白龙堆。」七道刀痕，六道旧，一道新，新的那道是去年才砍的，砍得很深，像是有人一个人来这里坐了一夜。

column2: Abacus Rock
column3: 算珠石

column2: A huge flat-topped rock lies by the old road, its face cut with a dozen grooves holding three hundred round pebbles, like an abacus for a giant. Bandit footmen are using the pebbles as slingshot ammunition, betting on distance, and half the rock is already bare. A small wooden sign stands beside it: 'One bead a month. Do not touch.'
column3: 古道边卧着一块平顶巨石，石面凿着十几道槽，槽里嵌着三百颗圆石子，活像一架给巨人用的算盘。一伙马贼步卒拿石子当弹丸打赌，谁打得远谁赢，石面已经空了一半。石边插着一块小木牌，写着一行字：「每月一珠，勿动。」

column2: You chase the bandits off and gather the pebbles back into the grooves, following the marks on the back of the sign. A hundred and twenty have been moved to the left; a hundred and eighty remain on the right. Every month the mute pays the Bandit King one tael of Qianli's road toll, and comes here to move one bead. Three hundred taels, three hundred beads. He has been at it ten years.
column3: 马贼被打跑，你们把石子一颗颗捡回槽里，按木牌背面的记号摆好：左边已拨过去一百二十颗，右边还剩一百八十颗。原来哑巴每月替千里号还马贼王一两路钱，就来这里拨一颗。三百两，三百颗。他已经拨了十年。

column2: Mirror Lake Camp
column3: 照湖营

column2: A rare little lake lies in the sand, its surface flat as a bronze mirror. Bandit riders are camped by it, and every noon they flash bronze mirrors at the sun, bouncing the light to dunes tens of miles away, where someone flashes back: the Bandit King's gangs talk to each other this way. When they see strangers they send a frantic flicker, and every bandit for miles knows.
column3: 沙海里少见的一汪小湖，水面平得像铜镜。一伙马贼骑手在湖边扎营，每天正午拿铜镜对着太阳晃，把光打到几十里外的沙丘上，那边也有人晃回来：这是马贼王各路人马传话的法子。他们见了生人，就晃一阵乱光，四面八方的马贼便都知道了。

column2: With the riders scattered you find their signal book: one flash for all clear, two for visitors, three long and a short for soldiers. The last page holds one more signal, labelled 'The Qian banner has returned', and below it: 'Unused for ten years.' The mirrors are polished bright, as if someone waits every day to send it.
column3: 骑手们被打散，你们翻出一本镜语簿：一闪是平安，两闪是来客，三长一短是官兵。最后一页有个暗号，旁边注着「千字旗回来了」，下面又注一行：「十年未用」。镜子擦得锃亮，像是天天都有人在等着用它。

column2: Recruiting Camp
column3: 招马营

column2: At the far end of the plain stands the Bandit King's recruiting camp under a great banner: 'Join us: one horse, one blade.' Herd boys, runaway debtors and farmhands sick of farming drift in by twos and threes. The recruits, foot, bow and horse, are learning to ride and shoot, their voices bigger than their skills. This is where the mute hands over his monthly tael.
column3: 荒原尽头扎着马贼王的招兵营，营门口插着一面大旗：「来投者，给马一匹，刀一把。」附近的放牧娃、逃债汉、不想种地的庄稼人，三三两两往里走。营里新兵步、射、骑都有，正学着骑马射箭，嗓门比本事大。哑巴每月的那一两银子，就是交在这里。

column2: This batch of recruits is scattered and sent home. You catch the camp's paymaster and find his receipt book: 'Qianli, one tael a month, one hundred and twenty payments', and a note: 'By the King's order: keep this silver apart, not in the common chest.' But the banner still stands and the King's name carries far. In a few days new recruits will come.
column3: 这一回的新兵被打散，各回各家去了。营里管银子的被你们抓住，翻出收银簿：「千里号，每月一两，一百二十笔」，簿上写着「王令：此银另存，不入公账」。可大旗还插着，马贼王的名声在外，过不了几天，又会有新人来投。

column2: Hot Spring Bathhouse
column3: 温汤馆

column2: A hot spring bubbles up on the plain and someone has built a bathhouse over it. After half a month on the sand, one soak here washes the grit out of your bones. Bandit archers have taken it over and never get out of the pool, wrinkled white, while the paying guests queue outside the door. The owner squats on the step, sighing into a scrubbing towel.
column3: 荒原里冒出一眼温泉，有人在上面盖了个澡堂，叫温汤馆，赶了半个月沙路的人进去泡一回，能把骨头里的沙都泡出来。一伙马贼射手占了澡堂，天天泡在池子里不出来，泡得浑身发白，把客人全赶到门外排队。澡堂老板蹲在门口，手里攥着一条擦背的毛巾直叹气。

column2: The archers are hauled out of the pool and run off bare-chested. The owner changes the water. The mute comes for a soak once a month, he says, and always falls asleep in the pool, murmuring numbers in his dreams: 'a hundred and nineteen, a hundred and twenty...' Only asleep will he make a sound.
column3: 射手们被从池子里拎出来，光着膀子跑了。老板换了一池新水。他说那个哑巴每月来泡一回，泡着泡着就睡着了，梦里嘴里念的全是数：「一百一十九，一百二十……」只有在梦里，他才肯出声。

column2: The back yard holds the bandits' stores: two great vats of soap beans, a dozen cakes of perfumed soap robbed from foreign traders, a chest of towels embroidered with the names of half the trading houses on the road, and a barrel of rosewater they couldn't bring themselves to drink. It smells better than it tastes.
column3: 澡堂后院堆着马贼的存货：两大缸澡豆、十几块抢来的胡商香皂、一箱绣着各家商号字号的毛巾，还有一桶他们舍不得喝的玫瑰露，闻着比喝着香。

column2: Whenever you pass, the owner lets you bathe first, then brings out a basket of white buns steamed over the spring, and washes and dries your clothes by the hot water so they're still warm when you put them on.
column3: 每次路过，老板都让你们先泡，泡完端上一笼用温泉蒸的白面馍，再把你们的衣裳拿去泉边洗一洗、烘一烘，穿上身还是热的。

column2: Ransom Hollow
column3: 绑票坳

column2: In a hollow at the foot of the mountains hides a band of down-at-heel escorts from an agency inside the pass. They took a bounty: ten thousand taels for news of the Qianli caravan. Unable to find the caravan, they kidnapped the nearest thing to it, the mute. They've gone over to the bandits and guard the mouth of the hollow on stolen horses. From inside comes the clack of abacus beads: the mute, counting.
