column3: 山脚的坳里藏着一伙落魄的镖师，原是关内一家镖局的，接了个悬赏：找到千里号的下落，赏银万两。他们找不到千里号，就绑了个跟千里号沾边的人：那个哑巴。镖师们投了马贼，骑着抢来的马守在坳口，坳里传出算盘珠子噼啪响，是哑巴在里面拨珠子。

column2: The escorts are driven off and you untie him. The mute rubs his wrists and bows to you. Three days they pressed him and he never said a word. When you ask where the caravan went, he beads out a direction, northeast, then a number, three hundred. Then he points to the mountains in the south.
column3: 镖师们被打跑，你们解开绳子，哑巴揉揉手腕，冲你们鞠了一躬。镖师逼了他三天，他一个字也没说。你们问他千里号在哪，他拨出一个方向：东北；又拨出一个数：三百。然后指了指南边的山。

column2: Stallholders' Graves
column3: 摊主冢

column2: The mute leads you to a stretch of sand where rows of stones poke up, each carved with a number, like stall numbers at a fair. Bandit footmen are digging between them with spades: the ghost market's stallholders are dead men, they reckon, and dead men bury things, so there must be treasure. The mute stamps his feet in distress but can't stop them.
column3: 哑巴把你们领到一片沙地，沙里露出一排排石头，每块石头上刻着一个数，像是摊位的号。一伙马贼步卒正拿铁锹在石头间乱挖，说鬼市的摊主都是死人，死人埋东西，底下准有宝。哑巴急得直跺脚，拦又拦不住。

column2: The bandits gone, the mute fills the holes back in, handful by handful. Now you understand: these are the stallholders' graves. Ten years ago a sandstorm buried A Suan here, and it was these people, long dead in the Sand Sea, who dug him out. He promised to keep their stalls and sell the things they had lost in the sand, until someone came to buy. He leaves an oleaster berry in front of every stone.
column3: 马贼被赶跑，哑巴把挖开的沙一捧捧填回去。你们这才明白，这是鬼市摊主们的坟。十年前沙暴把阿算埋在这里，是这些早死在沙海里的人把他扒了出来。他答应替他们守摊，卖他们生前丢在沙里的东西，等着有人来买。他在每块石头前放了一颗沙枣。

column2: Tribute Trail
column3: 贡银道

column2: Along a trail beaten hard in the sand comes a tribute convoy, foot, bow and horse, guarding a dozen chests eastward: this month's dues from the western gangs to the Bandit King. The convoy captain rides in front reading the tribute list aloud, and every time he reaches the last line he pauses and clicks his tongue. 'This one. The King's a strange man.'
column3: 一条被踩实了的沙道上，走来一支押贡的马队，步、射、骑都有，护着十几口箱子往东去，是西边各路马贼这个月给马贼王的贡。押队的头目骑在最前面，手里举着一本贡单，一路走一路念，念到最后一行，总要停一下，咂咂嘴：「这一笔，王真怪。」

column2: The convoy scattered, you open the list. The last line: 'Qianli, one tael, month one hundred and twenty-one.' Beside it, the King's own note: 'Accept. Keep apart. Not one copper to be spent.' Every month, the captain says, the King looks at that one tael himself before it's locked away, 'like it isn't silver at all, but a letter'.
column3: 押队的人被打散，你们打开贡单，最后一行是：「千里号，一两，第一百二十一月。」旁边批着马贼王的话：「收下，单存，一文不许花。」押队头目说，王每个月都要亲手看看这一两银子，看完锁进箱子，「好像那不是银子，是一封信」。

column2: Turncoat Camp
column3: 叛旗营

column2: A camp sits in a sandy valley. These bandits used to pay the Bandit King tribute too, but now they've risen against him: they want to rob the ghost market and his rules are in the way. They have foot, bow and horse, and still fly the King's banner, only with a knife slash through the character 'King'. Their chief is haranguing his men: 'The King's gone soft. Why protect a bunch of ghosts?'
column3: 沙谷里扎着一座营，营里的马贼原本也给马贼王纳贡，如今扯旗反了：他们要抢鬼市，嫌王的规矩碍事。营里步、射、骑都有，旗子还是王的旗子，只是上面那个「王」字被划了一刀。营中头目正对手下喊：「王老了，护着一帮鬼做什么？」

column2: The rebel camp broken, the chief sits trussed up and still defiant. 'You know why the King protects the market? Ten years ago he got a bowl of water there on credit. Says it's the only debt he's ever had.' He spits. 'One bowl of water, ten years of guarding. Fool.'
column3: 叛营被打散，头目被捆着，嘴还是硬的：「你们知道王为什么护着鬼市？十年前他在那儿赊过一碗水，他说那是他这辈子欠过的唯一一笔账。」头目啐了一口：「欠一碗水，护十年，傻子。」

column2: Fallen Sail Camp
column3: 落帆营

column2: In a big bandit camp stands a strange pole flying a torn sail, and tied up below it are several sun-blackened men with southern accents who say 'port' and 'starboard' and still sway as they walk on the sand. The bandits have held them for days and got nothing useful, only the same sentence over and over: 'The captain is looking for someone who can keep accounts.'
column3: 一伙马贼的大营里竖着根怪杆子，杆上挂着一面破帆，营里绑着几个皮肤黝黑的汉子，说的是南边的口音，一开口就是「左舷」「右舷」，在沙地上走路还摇摇晃晃。马贼们抓了他们好几天，问不出一句有用的，只听他们反复说：「船主在找会算账的人。」

column2: With the bandits scattered, the men explain: they're sailors who followed a woman captain into the Sand Sea and lost her in a sandstorm. She is looking for someone who can keep accounts, 'not just anyone with an abacus, someone who can carry on the Qianli caravan's books'. When you mention the mute, their eyes light up and they dash off east to tell her.
column3: 马贼被打散，汉子们说他们是海上来的水手，跟着一位女船主进了沙海，沙暴里走散了。船主要找一个会算账的人，「不是随便会打算盘的，是能把千里号的账接着算下去的」。你们提起那个哑巴，水手们眼睛都亮了，一溜烟往东报信去了。

column2: Paper and Ink Wagon
column3: 纸墨车

column2: A big wagon crawls east loaded not with gold but with paper, ink, brushes, inkstones and a stack of The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art. The bandit archers guarding it are jumpier than any treasure escort and shoot at anyone who comes near. Tied to the tailboard is a poor scholar in spectacles, looking miserable. He says he's been kidnapped 'to be the King's tutor'.
column3: 一辆大车慢吞吞往东走，车上不是金银，是纸、墨、笔、砚，还有一摞《九章算术》。护车的马贼射手比护金银还紧张，谁靠近就放箭。车尾绑着个戴眼镜的穷书生，哭丧着脸，说他是被抢去「给王当先生」的。

column2: The archers driven off, the scholar tells the truth: the Bandit King is learning accounts. Three years now; he can add, subtract, multiply and divide, but can't write his own name. All he can write is 'Qianli caravan', lopsided, a whole page at a time. 'He says when they come back he'll check the books with his own hands.' After some thought the scholar heads east of his own accord.
column3: 射手们被赶跑，书生说出了实情：马贼王在学算账。他已经学了三年，加减乘除都会了，就是不会写自己的名字，只会写「千里号」三个字，写得歪歪扭扭，一写就是一整张。「他说要等人回来，亲手把账对清楚。」书生想了想，自己往东去了。

column2: White-Hair Dunes
column3: 白头沙

column2: In a sheltered hollow live a crowd of white-haired old bandits, too old to ride or draw a bow, who get by on a monthly pension of grain from the King. A gang of young bandit riders has heard of it and come to take the old men's rations: 'useless mouths', they call them. The old bandits line up on their walking sticks, hardly a tooth among them, and curse loud enough.
column3: 背风的沙窝里住着一群白发老马贼，老得骑不动马、拉不开弓了，靠王每月发的一份养老粮过日子。一伙年轻马贼骑手听说了，跑来抢老人们的粮，说「老东西吃白饭」。老马贼们拄着拐杖排成一排，牙都没几颗，骂起人来倒还响亮。

column2: The youngsters chased off, the old bandits cook you a pot of gruel. The oldest of the King's men, they say, is Old Han, once a company captain in the border army and the King's first follower. He wants to wash his hands of it all, but the King won't let him go: 'Your men aren't paid off yet.' 'Paid off how?' The old men shake their heads. 'The King's accounts, only the King and Old Han know.'
column3: 年轻人被打跑，老马贼们给你们烧了一锅糊糊。他们说王手下最老的一个叫老韩，当年是边军的队正，跟王最早，如今想金盆洗手，王不放，说「你的人还没还清」。「什么还清？」老人们摇头，「王的账，只有王和老韩知道。」

column2: Tribute Weighing Yard
column3: 称贡场

column2: The biggest tribute yard in the north of the Sand Sea: a giant steelyard hangs from a tripod of beams, and every gang's tribute must be weighed on it. A large bandit force, foot, bow and horse, guards the yard, and the weighmaster is a lame old man who works an abacus at lightning speed. Today one gang has accused the scale of cheating, blades are out, and the yard is in uproar.
column3: 沙海北边最大的收贡场，一杆巨秤吊在三根木架上，各路马贼押来的贡都要在这儿过秤。场子由一大伙马贼守着，步、射、骑都有，秤官是个瘸腿老头，一手算盘打得飞快。今天来缴贡的一伙人嫌秤不准，两边拔了刀，场子乱成一锅粥。

column2: Order restored, the lame weighmaster shows you his book. Every load of tribute is split in two: nine parts to the King's store, one part marked 'old road'. That tenth pays men to dig the sand off the old road after every storm, and has for ten years without a break. 'The King says the road must stay open. What if they come back?'
column3: 乱子平了，瘸腿秤官把秤簿给你们看：每一份贡都分成两份，九成入王库，一成写着「古道」。他说这一成专门雇人，沙暴一过就去把古道上的沙扒开，十年没断过。「王说，路要一直开着，万一他们回来呢。」

column2: Mast in the Sand
column3: 沙中桅

column2: East along the old road the dunes roll like sea swell, and from the crest of one sticks a ship's mast, too thick for one man to hug, crusted white with salt, a storm lantern hung at its tip. Bandit archers are shooting at it to bring the lantern down. It's a demon, they say: it shines at night and draws every passing caravan toward it.
column3: 古道往东，沙丘起伏得像海浪，浪尖上竟戳出一根桅杆，粗得两人合抱，杆身长满了白花花的盐壳，顶上挂着一盏防风灯。一伙马贼射手正朝桅杆放箭，想把灯射下来，说这是妖物，夜里亮着，引得过路的商队全往那边走。

column2: The archers driven off, you dig at the foot of the mast and find a section of hull, its timber long turned to stone, sea snails lodged between the planks. The old folk always said the Sand Sea really was a sea once, and when it dried, the ships were buried under the sand. But the lantern is new. A sailor with a southern accent pops up from behind a dune. 'Our captain hung it. She says the Sand Sea's a sea too, and a sea needs lighthouses.'
column3: 射手们被打跑，你们扒开桅杆脚下的沙，底下是一截船身，木头早就成了石头，船板缝里嵌着海螺壳。老辈人讲，沙海以前真是海，干了，船就埋在沙底下。灯却是新挂的。一个南方口音的水手从沙丘后面钻出来：「我们船主挂的。她说沙海也是海，得有灯塔。」

column2: Ledger Niche
column3: 藏账龛

column2: Clicking his beads, the mute leads you to the foot of the southern mountains. A small niche is cut in the cliff, and bandit archers are camped in front of it. They don't know what's inside, only that the mute spends a little while here every month, so it must be treasure. But the niche is sealed with clay stamped with a tiny abacus, and none of them dares break it.
column3: 哑巴拨着珠子领你们到南山脚下，崖壁上凿着一个小龛，龛前有一伙马贼射手扎营。他们不知道龛里有什么，只知道哑巴每月都来这里待一会儿，便断定里面藏着宝。可龛口用泥封着，封泥上按着一枚小算盘的印，谁也不敢砸。

column2: The archers gone, the mute breaks the seal himself. Inside is a hand-copied ledger, the master record of 'Qianli: the Sand Sea': grain, water, guides, tolls, entry by entry. The last page is in the bookkeeper's hand: 'Sand Sea accounts: road toll outstanding. Balance to be settled in full at the Thousand Buddha Caves.' The mute looks at it a long time, then puts the ledger in your hands.
column3: 射手被赶跑，哑巴亲手揭开封泥。龛里是一本手抄的账，「千里号·沙海段」的底账：粮、水、向导、路钱，一笔一笔。最后一页是账房的字：「沙海之账，路钱未清，余款到千佛洞一并结算。」哑巴看了很久，把账簿交到你们手里。

column2: First-Word Cliff
column3: 开口崖

column2: The mute means to take the ledger to the Bandit King, but a troop of the King's riders waits under the cliff with orders to let no one bring Qianli's accounts through: the King says the account must be settled by Qianli in person. When they see the mute they dismount, polite as can be, and still won't make way. The mute grips the ledger. His lips move, and close again.
column3: 哑巴要带账簿去见马贼王，马贼王的一队骑手却守在崖下，奉命不许任何人把千里号的账带过去：王说，账要千里号的人亲自来算。骑手们见了哑巴，倒都下了马，客客气气，只是不让路。哑巴攥着账簿，嘴唇动了动，又闭上了。

column2: The riders give way, and their leader says, 'The King is waiting for Qianli. The mute doesn't count. Do you?' That night the mute speaks, his voice rough as sand. 'My name is A Suan. My master isn't dead. He went to the Thousand Buddha Caves to check the books. I've paid the King a hundred and twenty-one taels. The rest, Qianli owns to.' He hands you his abacus too. 'Make it clear to the King for me.'
column3: 骑手们让开了路，领头的说：「王等的是千里号的人，哑巴不算，你们算吗？」那天夜里，哑巴开口了，声音哑得像沙子：「我叫阿算。师父没死，他去千佛洞对账了。王的路钱我还到一百二十一两，剩下的，千里号认。」他把算盘也交给了你们：「替我跟王说清楚。」

column2: The Fat Cook's Inn
column3: 胖厨店

column2: A little inn by the old road belongs to a fat cook whose oven-baked layered flatbread is famous far and wide; travellers can find the place by smell. Bandit archers have taken it over and make him cook eight meals a day, with a beating whenever the bread isn't thick enough. He's grown noticeably thinner, and slips a note under the door: 'Help. Almost out of flour.'
column3: 古道边一家小客店，店主是个胖厨子，一手炉火烤的千层饼远近闻名，过路的人闻着味就能找来。一伙马贼射手占了店，逼胖厨子天天给他们做饭，一天做八顿，饼不够厚就打。胖厨子瘦了一圈，从门缝里递出一张纸条：「救命，面快没了。」

column2: The archers driven off, the fat cook first bakes you a stack of flatbread. A few days ago, he says, some odd guests came through: a woman with a dozen sailors, who ate their bread with dried fish they'd carried all the way from the coast. 'The woman kept asking while she ate whether I'd seen anyone along this road who could keep accounts.'
column3: 射手们被赶跑，胖厨子先给你们烙了一摞饼。他说前些天来过一伙怪客人，一个女人带着十几个水手，吃饼要就鱼干，鱼干是他们自己从海边背来的。「那女人一边吃一边问我，这一路有没有见过一个会算账的人。」

column2: From the inn you seize the bandits' stores: half a vat of sesame, three smoked geese, a bag of dried apricots, two unopened jars of sorghum spirit, and a menu they wrote themselves, headed: 'Layered flatbread, eight layers minimum.'
column3: 店里抄出马贼的存货：半缸芝麻、三只熏鹅、一袋杏干、两坛没开封的高粱酒，还有一张他们自己写的菜单，最上面一行是「千层饼，要八层以上」。

column2: The fat cook always has the oven lit early, and the moment you arrive the hot bread comes out, one each, with more layers every time. 'Next time,' he promises, 'twelve.'
column3: 胖厨子每次都早早生好炉子，你们一到，热饼就出炉，一人一张，层数一张比一张多，他说「下回给你们烙十二层」。

column2: Hired Swords Camp
column3: 雇兵营

column2: Below a sand ridge stands a large, tidy camp, foot, bow and horse, all in identical grey, though they fly a bandit flag. They are hired blades from a great merchant house inside the pass, ordered to stop the court's pioneers so the house can keep the western trade to itself. A price board hangs at the gate: 'Stop any caravan: 500. Stop the pioneers: 5,000.'
column3: 沙梁下扎着一座整整齐齐的大营，营里的人步、射、骑都有，穿的是统一的灰衣，打的却是马贼的旗。他们是关内一家大商号雇来的刀客，奉命拦住朝廷的开拓队，好让商号独吞西边的买卖。营门口还挂着一块价目牌：「拦一队，赏五百；拦开拓队，赏五千。」

column2: The hired blades scattered, you find the merchant house's secret letter in the commander's tent. It mentions something else: 'A woman sea captain in the Sand Sea is hiring, and paying better than we do. Stop her at all costs. Do not let her find the bookkeeper's people.' It seems you're not the only ones looking for the Qianli caravan.
column3: 刀客们被打散，你们在营主帐里找到商号的密信。信上还写着另一件事：「沙海里有个女船主在招人，出价比我们高，务必拦住，别让她找到账房的人。」看来想找千里号的，不止你们一家。

column2: Sand-Sweepers' Slope
column3: 扫沙坡

column2: A sandstorm has just passed and half the old road is buried. Bandit footmen on the slope, shouldering wooden shovels and dragging great rakes, charge you on sight, shouting 'More saboteurs!' A few days ago someone dug pits on the road to lay an ambush, and they think you're with them.
column3: 一场沙暴刚过，古道被埋了半截。坡上一伙马贼步卒扛着木锨、拖着大耙，见了你们就扑上来，嚷嚷着「又是来搞破坏的」。原来前几天有人在古道上挖坑设伏，他们以为你们也是一伙的。

column2: Only after the fight is the matter cleared up: these bandits are the King's road sweepers, and all year long they do one job, digging the old road out. As they work they sing: 'A foot of sand comes, a foot of sand goes; when the Qian banner returns, the road runs straight.' You help clear a stretch, and the flagstones show ruts from ten years ago.
column3: 打完才说清楚，这伙马贼是王雇来扫沙的，一年到头只干一件事：把古道扒出来。他们一边干活一边唱：「沙来一尺，扫去一尺，千字旗回，路是直的。」你们帮着扫了一段，古道露出来，青石上还有十年前的车辙。

column2: The Second King's Tent
column3: 二王帐

column2: Behind a dune stands a great tent with a gilded roof. Its master calls himself the Second King, the strongest bandit in the north of the Sand Sea, and he is set on pulling the Bandit King down. His riders, all in red cloaks, are drilling charges outside, and he stands on his saddle to address them: 'Ten years guarding a road nobody walks, hoarding money he never spends. What use is a king like that?'
column3: 沙丘后面扎着一顶金顶大帐，帐主自称「二王」，是沙海北边势力最大的马贼头子，一心想把马贼王拉下来。他的骑手个个披着红斗篷，正在帐前操练冲锋，二王站在马鞍上训话：「十年了，守着一条没人走的路，收着钱不花，这样的王，留着干什么？」

column2: The red cloaks are broken and the Second King, pinned in the sand, is still shouting. 'You'd fight for him? The chair he sits on is a debt, pledged against three hundred Qianli lives!' The King's chair is made of bones, he says, its back carved full of names. 'A bandit who sits on other people's names every day. What's he after?'
column3: 红斗篷们被冲散，二王被你们按在沙里，还在嚷：「你们替他卖命？他坐的那把椅子，是拿千里号三百条命抵的账！」他说王的椅子是骨头做的，椅背上刻满了名字，「一个马贼，天天坐在别人的名字上，你说他图什么？」

column2: Runaway Bride Dunes
column3: 逃婚沙

column2: A girl in a wedding dress gallops between the dunes, a band of bandit riders behind her yelling 'Come back, bride!' She is a bandit chief's daughter, promised to the Second King to seal an alliance. As she rides she shouts over her shoulder: 'I won't marry a bandit! I'm going to learn accounts!'
column3: 一个穿嫁衣的姑娘骑着马在沙丘间狂奔，后面追着一伙马贼骑手，喊着「新娘子回来」。她是一个马贼头子的女儿，被许给了二王，好让两家结盟。姑娘一边跑一边回头喊：「我不嫁马贼！我要去学算账！」

column2: The pursuers chased off, the girl tears away her veil. She's heard that a woman sea captain in the sandstorms to the south is taking on anyone who can keep accounts, no questions about family. 'My father's run thieves all his life and still can't count his own horses.' She gives you a bronze mirror from her dowry as thanks, turns, and rides south.
column3: 追亲的骑手被打跑，姑娘扯掉盖头，说她听说南边沙暴里有个女船主在招会算账的人，不问出身。「我爹管了一辈子贼，连自己有多少马都数不清。」她把嫁妆里的一面铜镜送给你们当谢礼，掉头往南去了。

column2: The Bumbling Burrow
column3: 笨贼洞

column2: Three dim-witted thieves heard the Bandit King has a vault that only takes in and never pays out, so they hired bandit archers as lookouts and started tunnelling toward it from ten miles away. Two months on the tunnel has wandered badly, and today it broke through, not into silver, but into water: they've struck an old underground channel buried under the sand. The archers think someone is trying to drown them and are shooting wildly into the hole.
column3: 三个蠢贼听说马贼王有一座库，十年只进不出，便雇了一伙马贼射手望风，自己从十里外往库底挖地道。挖了两个月，地道越挖越歪，今天挖穿了，冒出来的不是银子，是水：他们挖通了一条埋在沙下的老坎儿井。射手们以为有人放水淹他们，正对着洞口乱射。

column2: The archers flee and the three thieves crawl out caked in mud. The water runs down their tunnel to a village that has been dry for three years, and the villagers come running with gongs to drape the three in red silk as their saviours. Torn between laughing and crying, the thieves show you their map of the vault: chests stacked by year, every one sealed.
column3: 射手们跑了，三个蠢贼浑身是泥爬出来。水顺着地道一路流到下游一个干了三年的村子，村里人敲着锣跑来，给三人披红挂彩，非要认他们当恩人。三人哭笑不得，掏出库图给你们看：箱子按年份码好，都贴着封条。

column2: Sailcloth Camp
column3: 帆布营

column2: The sandstorm has blown a day and a night when a camp suddenly appears in the yellow murk: tents rigged from ship's sails, ropes tied in sailors' knots, a mast standing as a flagpole. Bandit archers are using the storm to surround the camp and shoot in, and the sailors inside are seasick on their camels. A woman in an oilcloth cloak stands at the foot of the mast, her voice louder than the wind: 'Anyone who can keep accounts, up here! Everyone else, man the sails!'
column3: 沙暴刮了一天一夜，黄沙里忽然露出一片营地：帐篷是用船帆搭的，绳子打的是水手结，营中竖着一根桅杆当旗杆。一伙马贼射手趁着风沙围营放箭，营里的水手们骑在骆驼上晕得直吐。一个披着油布斗篷的女人站在桅杆下，嗓门盖过了风声：「会算账的上来，不会的去守帆！」

column2: The archers are beaten back and the wind drops. The woman names herself Shen Du, ship master of the Qianli caravan's fleet. She brings out half a sea chart, its margins crammed with figures in the bookkeeper's hand. 'His accounts. The sea route's half. The other half he kept, here in the Sand Sea.' She has lost her ship, she says, and she wants the bookkeeper, or anyone who can take up his books where he left off. 'Can you keep accounts?'
column3: 射手们被打退，风也小了。女人自称沈渡，是千里号船队的船主。她掏出半张海图，图边写满了数，是账房的字迹。「这是他的账，海路那一半。另一半在他手里，在沙海里。」她说她的船丢了，她要找账房，或者任何一个能把他的账接着算下去的人。「你们会算账吗？」

column2: Windgap Gang
column3: 风口帮

column2: Between two great sand ridges lies a windgap, and every sandstorm blows things out of it that were buried who knows how long: rusted blades, silver bowls, whole chests of coins. So after every storm a new gang of road robbers springs up in the gap, foot, bow and horse thrown together, robbing the finds first and then the travellers, before the Bandit King's rules can even reach them.
column3: 两道大沙梁之间有个风口，每次沙暴一过，风口里就会刮出些埋了不知多少年的东西：锈刀、银碗、整箱的铜钱。于是每次沙暴之后，风口里就会冒出一伙新的劫道帮，步、射、骑凑一凑就开张，抢完东西抢过路人，马贼王的规矩还没传到，他们就先抢了。

column2: This gang is scattered, leaving behind loot they never got round to splitting, including a copper bowl stamped Qian on the base. But the Sand Sea's wind never stops. After the next storm the gap will blow out new treasure, and blow in a new gang with it. You'll have to come back next time.
column3: 这一伙被打散了，风口里散落着他们没来得及分的东西，有一只铜碗底刻着「千」。可沙海的风不会停，下一场沙暴过后，风口里又会刮出新的宝贝，也会刮来新的劫道帮。你们只能等下回再来。

column2: Camel Bell Dunes
column3: 驼铃沙

column2: Shen Du's water train was lost in the sandstorm, a dozen camels and six sailors, still not back. Her camel bells were made specially, she says, one note to each animal, together a fisherman's song. Pushing through the sand you really do hear the tune, faint and broken, but a band of bandit riders is following it too, after those dozen skins of water.
column3: 沈渡的运水驼队在沙暴里走散了，十几峰骆驼、六个水手，至今没回营。沈渡说她的驼铃是特意配的，一峰一个音，连起来是一支渔歌。你们顶着风沙走，隐隐约约真听见了歌，可循着歌声走过去的，还有一伙马贼骑手，他们也想要那十几囊水。

column2: The riders driven off, you find the train behind a sand ridge, every sailor alive. They came this way, the lead sailor says, following a deep hum like drums far off. Shen Du's guide points to the ridge's steep face: when dry, even-sized grains slide down it in a sheet, the dune booms like that. Singing sand. Where the booming stopped, a stone pokes out of the sand, carved with the character Qian.
column3: 骑手们被打跑，你们在一道沙梁背后找到了驼队，一个不少。领头的水手说，他们是跟着一阵嗡嗡声走过来的，像远处在擂鼓。沈渡的向导指着沙梁陡坡：沙粒又干又匀，一大片往下滑，就会这样轰鸣，叫鸣沙。轰鸣停处，沙里露出一块石头，刻着个「千」字。

column2: Sail-Cart Road
column3: 帆车道

column2: Strange carts are hurtling along the old road: wheels below, sails above, and with a good wind they outrun horses. Bandit footmen ride them whooping, charging any caravan they see and robbing it once it scatters. The sails are patched, and the stitching on the patches is a sailor's work.
column3: 古道上呼啸着几辆怪车：车底装着轮子，车上竖着帆，风一吹跑得比马还快。车上坐着一伙马贼步卒，一边开车一边怪叫，见商队就冲，冲散了就抢。车帆上补着补丁，补丁上的针脚是水手的手艺。

column2: The bandits are tipped off, and Shen Du's sailors whoop as they take the sail-carts back: Shen Du built them, and they were stolen a few days ago. She slaps a sail. 'The Sand Sea's a sea. Where there's wind, a ship can go.' The Qianli bookkeeper said the same thing once, she tells you, and she laughed at him back then.
column3: 马贼被掀下车，沈渡的水手们欢呼着把帆车抢了回来：车是沈渡造的，前几天被偷了。沈渡拍着车帆说：「沙海也是海，有风就能走船。」她说千里号的账房当年也说过这话，那时候她还笑他。

column2: The Sealed Vault
column3: 封箱库

column2: A vault is cut into the sandstone, the very one the three thieves were tunnelling for. A large force guards its door, foot, bow and horse, all veterans from the King's own guard and far fiercer than any elsewhere. Ten seals cross the door, one for each year, the oldest faded white. In ten years, the captain says, this door has only opened to put things in. Not one copper has ever come out.
column3: 沙岩里凿出一座库，就是三个蠢贼想挖的那座。库门前守着一大伙马贼，步、射、骑都是王身边的老兵，比别处的凶得多。库门上贴着十道封条，一年一道，最早的那道已经发白。守库的头目说，这库十年来只开门往里放，从没往外拿过一文。

column2: The veterans fall back. You leave the seals alone and only look through the crack of the door. Chests are stacked to the ceiling, each bearing the same red label: 'Travel money for the Qianli caravan's journey home.' For ten years the King has taken tribute: one part to sweep the road, nine parts saved here, for the three hundred to spend on the way back.
column3: 守库的老兵退开了，你们没动封条，只从门缝往里看：一口口箱子码到顶，箱上贴着同一张红纸，「千里号回程盘缠」。原来王收了十年的贡，一成扫沙，九成全攒在这里，等那三百人回来时在路上用。

column2: Search Party Dunes
column3: 找人沙

column2: Bandit footmen are searching hollow after hollow with a portrait of a wrinkled old man captioned 'Old Han'. The King has ordered him brought back: a few days ago Old Han walked off carrying a copper basin, saying he was going to wash his hands of it all. Unable to find him, the bandits are taking it out on the shops along the way, and have just smashed a flatbread stall.
column3: 一伙马贼步卒拿着画像挨个沙窝搜，画像上是个满脸褶子的老头，下面写着「老韩」。他们奉王的命令把老韩找回去：老韩前些天端着一只铜盆走了，说要金盆洗手。马贼们找不到人，就拿沿路的小店撒气，砸了一家卖馕的铺子。

column2: The bandits chased off, the flatbread seller whispers that Old Han went northeast, and every day before dawn he washes his hands on top of a dune. 'Very solemn about it, only someone always comes and kicks his basin over.' Old Han took ten flatbreads on credit before he left, he adds: 'I'll pay once my hands are clean.'
column3: 马贼被打跑，卖馕的老板偷偷告诉你们：老韩往东北去了，每天天不亮就在沙丘顶上洗一回手，「洗得可认真了，就是总有人去踢他的盆」。老板还说，老韩临走在他这儿赊了十个馕，说「等我洗干净了来还」。

column2: Hand-Washing Dune
column3: 洗手沙

column2: At first light an old man kneels on top of a dune before a polished copper basin holding half a skin of water he has saved. He scrubs his hands over and over, murmuring something. A few bandit riders charge up and kick the basin over, and the water sinks into the sand. The old man doesn't get angry. He picks the basin up and pours in a little more. 'Again.'
column3: 天蒙蒙亮，沙丘顶上跪着个老头，面前一只锃亮的铜盆，盆里是他省下的半囊水。他一遍遍搓手，嘴里念着什么。几个马贼骑手冲上来，一脚把盆踢翻，水渗进了沙里。老头不恼，把盆捡起来，又倒上一点水：「再洗。」

column2: The riders driven off, Old Han dries his hands and tells you the truth. He was a company captain in the border army; ten years ago he led a company escorting the Qianli caravan, and at Yangguan the Hawk sent them back. Halfway home he turned round and came after them alone. He never caught the caravan, but in the Sand Sea he met the King. 'My whole company ended up riding with him as bandits.' He wants to leave, but 'I brought those men here. I have to take them home.'
column3: 骑手们被打跑，老韩擦干手跟你们说了实话。他原是边军的队正，十年前带一队兵护送千里号，到阳关被鹞子赶了回来。他半路一个人折回来追，没追上商队，却遇上了王。「我这一队兵，后来全跟着王当了马贼。」他说他想走，可「人是我带来的，得我带回去」。

column2: Old Company Slope
column3: 旧部坡

column2: Old Han has walked with you less than half a day when bandit riders pour down a slope and block the road. Their leader, a big bearded man, reins in when he sees Old Han, and after a long pause manages: 'Captain, the King sent us to bring you back.' The riders behind him hang their heads, raising their blades and lowering them, lowering them and raising them again.
column3: 老韩跟着你们走了不到半天，坡上就冲下来一伙马贼骑手，把路堵死了。领头的是个大胡子，见了老韩却勒住了马，半天憋出一句：「队正，王让我们来接你。」后面的骑手一个个低着头，手里的刀举起来又放下，放下又举起来。

column2: After a fight the bearded man dismounts and gives Old Han a military salute, so long unused the gesture is rusty. Half the old company still rides for the King, he says; the other half are scattered across the Sand Sea herding and growing melons. 'Captain, you still have the token. If you call, we'll all come back to the colours.' Old Han says nothing. He only nods.
column3: 打过一场，大胡子下了马，冲老韩行了个军礼，十年没行过，手势都生了。他说当年这一队兵，有一半还在王的手下骑马，另一半散在沙海里放牧、种瓜。「队正，令牌还在你那儿。你要是喊，我们都回营。」老韩没说话，只是点了点头。

column2: Date Grove
column3: 枣林

column2: Hidden in a hollow is a grove of jujubes, planted by a widow twenty years ago, and its dates are sweeter than any others. Bandit footmen have taken the grove, beaten every date off the branches, and, finding the stones hard on their teeth, are making the widow and her children pit them one by one. The children cry as they work. The widow says nothing, and keeps every stone in a jar.
column3: 沙窝里藏着一片枣林，林子是一个寡妇种的，种了二十年，结的枣比别处的甜。一伙马贼步卒占了林子，把树上的枣打得精光，又嫌枣核硌牙，逼寡妇带着孩子们一颗颗去核。孩子们边剥边哭，寡妇一声不吭，剥下的枣核一颗也不扔，都攒在一只罐子里。

column2: The bandits chased off, the widow pours the jar of stones into a freshly dug pit. 'Next year, another grove.' Shen Du stays on in the grove, and that night under the trees she tells you that ten years ago all three routes set out on the same day; she sailed from Quanzhou, with some of the three hundred on her ships too. 'We agreed: whoever arrived first would wait for the others.'
column3: 马贼被赶跑，寡妇把那罐枣核倒进新挖的坑里：「明年又是一片林子。」沈渡在林子里住了下来，夜里坐在树下跟你们说，十年前三路同一天出发，她带船从泉州出海，船上也有三百人名单里的人。「我们约好了：谁先到，谁等谁。」

column2: From the grove you seize the bandits' stores: twelve sacks of pitted dried dates, a basket of stolen honey, three axes for cutting down jujube trees, and a ledger in which they recorded how many dates each of them sneaked every day.
column3: 林子里抄出马贼的存货：十二麻袋去了核的干枣、一筐抢来的蜂蜜、三把砍枣树用的斧头，还有一本他们记的账，记的是每人每天偷吃了几颗。

column2: Whenever you pass, the widow's children run out of the grove and stuff bags of freshly dried dates into your saddlebags, and the littlest always pushes the one he thinks is sweetest into your hand and watches until you've eaten it.
column3: 每次路过，寡妇的孩子们都会跑出林子，把一兜兜新晒的枣塞进你们的鞍袋，最小的那个还会塞一颗他觉得最甜的到你们手里，盯着你们吃完。

column2: Half-Buried Gate
column3: 半城门

column2: The sandstorm has blown away half a dune and uncovered the gate of an ancient city, its top half showing, the archway so low you must stoop to enter. Bandit riders are racing in ahead of everyone else to loot, hooves drumming on the brick. Beside the gate stands a stone pillar worn with deep grooves all the way round, as if by mooring ropes.
column3: 沙暴刮走了半座沙丘，露出一座古城的城门，城门只露出上半截，门洞要弯着腰才进得去。一伙马贼骑手赶在别人前头冲进城里抢东西，马蹄踩在城砖上咚咚响。城门旁边立着一根石柱，柱上一圈圈磨出了深槽，像是被缆绳磨的。

column2: The riders driven off, Shen Du runs her hand over the grooves. 'A mooring post.' This city was once a port on a lake; only when the lake dried did the sand bury it. On the gate tower is a line in chalk that ten years of wind haven't erased: 'Qianli passed here, awaiting word from the sea route.' Shen Du stands beneath it a long time without speaking.
column3: 骑手们被打跑，沈渡摸着石柱上的槽：「这是系船柱。」原来这座城当年是湖边的港口，湖干了，城才被沙埋了。城门楼上有一行粉笔字，十年了还没被风磨掉：「千里号过此，候海路信。」沈渡站在字下面，很久没有说话。

column2: Letter Niche Lane
column3: 信龛巷

column2: In the old city runs a narrow lane whose walls are cut full of little niches; passing caravans used to leave letters in them for whoever came later to carry on. Bandit archers have lit a fire in the lane and are pulling the old letters out one by one for kindling, and the whole lane smells of burnt paper.
column3: 古城里有一条小巷，两边墙上凿满了小龛，从前来往的商队把信放在龛里，等后来的人顺路带走。一伙马贼射手在巷子里生火取暖，把龛里的旧信一封封掏出来当引火纸，烧得满巷子都是纸灰味。

column2: The archers driven off, you snatch half a bundle of letters from the fire. One is addressed 'Kindly deliver to Shen Du, ship master of the Qianli caravan', in the bookkeeper's hand, dated autumn ten years ago. Shen Du opens it. Only a few lines: 'If the sea route arrives first, please wait for me to settle the books. There is one sum in the Sand Sea I have not yet worked out.' The letter is ten years late. 'He'd written all along,' says Shen Du.
column3: 射手们被赶跑，你们从火边抢出半捆信，其中一封封皮上写着「烦交千里号船主沈渡」，是账房的字，落款是十年前的秋天。沈渡拆开，信上只有几行：「海路若先到，请等我对账。沙海里的账，有一笔我还没算清。」信晚了十年。沈渡说：「原来他早就写了。」

column2: The Doctor's Tent
column3: 郎中帐

column2: A white tent stands in a hollow, and the doctor inside treats everyone, bandits, traders and camels alike. A few days ago a bandit chief died here of his wounds, and his men are now holding the doctor in his own tent, demanding a life for a life. Bandit footmen guard the flap while the doctor goes on changing dressings inside, and scolds the guards for not washing their hands.
column3: 沙窝里有一顶白帐篷，帐里的郎中谁都治，马贼、商客、骆驼，一视同仁。前几天一个马贼头目在这儿治伤没治好，死了，他的手下就把郎中扣在帐里，说要他偿命。马贼步卒守着帐门，郎中在里面照样给伤号换药，换完还骂守门的不洗手。

column2: The guards driven off, the doctor says the King paid for this tent, and has come to be treated himself: an old arrow scar on his left leg, taken in White Dragon Mound ten years ago, that aches whenever the sky clouds over. 'He says he took that arrow for someone else.' The doctor washes his hands as he talks. 'Ask him who, and he won't say.'
column3: 守门的被赶跑，郎中说这顶帐篷是王出钱搭的，王自己也来治过伤：左腿上一道旧箭疤，十年前在白龙堆里落下的，一到阴天就疼。「他说那一箭是替别人挨的。」郎中一边说一边洗手，「问他替谁，他不说。」

column2: Old Market of the Sand City
column3: 沙城旧市

column2: The old city's market survives: a ring of stone stalls and, in the middle, a smooth stone slab carved with the prices of long ago. Bandit riders have seized the market and dragged in stonemasons from outside the walls to dig for treasure. A month of digging has turned up nothing but stone. The oasis folk nearby want to trade timber for that stone to build houses, but the bandits hold the market gate and allow no trade.
column3: 古城的市场还在：一圈石砌的摊台，中间一块平整的石板，石板上刻着从前的价目。一伙马贼骑手霸住了市场，抓来城外的石匠给他们挖宝，石匠们挖了一个月，挖出来的全是石头。附近绿洲里的人想拿木料来换石料修房子，可马贼守着市口，谁也不许做买卖。

column2: The riders are driven out of the city and the market reopens: the stone the masons dug out goes out by the cartload, and oasis timber comes back. From under the slab the market elders bring out a lease the Qianli caravan signed: 'This market rented for three days, awaiting word from the sea route.' On the back: 'Second day. Grain gone. Moving on.' They waited only two days. Shen Du reads it three times and says softly, 'I was only one day late.'
column3: 骑手们被赶出古城，市场重新开张了：石匠们挖出来的石料一车车拉出去，换回绿洲的木料。市场的老人们从石板底下取出一张租约，是千里号当年签的：「租此市三日，候海路信。」可租约背面写着：「第二日，粮尽，先行。」他们只等了两天。沈渡把租约看了三遍，轻声说：「我只晚到了一天。」

column2: Abandoned Garrison Store
column3: 废屯仓

column2: Old Han brings you to an old border-army garrison store, one corner of its earth wall collapsed, an army bronze lock still on the door. This is what his company left behind. Now a gang of deserters holds it, footmen on the door, trying to pick the lock every day. A year of picking and it's still shut, though they've snapped several of their own blades on it.
column3: 老韩领你们来到一座边军的旧屯仓，土墙塌了一角，仓门上还挂着军中的铜锁。这是他那一队兵当年留下的家底。如今一伙逃兵占了仓，步卒守着门，天天撬锁，撬了一年也没撬开，倒把自己的刀撬断了好几把。

column2: The deserters driven off, Old Han takes a bronze key from inside his coat, and the lock opens with a click. A board is nailed to the inside wall listing his company's names, one hundred, each followed by a small circle. 'Circled ones are still alive.' He counts. Ninety-one.
column3: 逃兵被赶跑，老韩从怀里掏出一把铜钥匙，咔嗒一声打开了门。仓壁上钉着一块木板，上面是他那一队兵的名字，一百个，每个名字后面都画着一个小圈。「圈的是还活着的。」他数了数，九十一个。

column2: From the store you seize the deserters' goods: twenty sacks of army biscuit hard enough to crack walnuts, three bundles of arrows, forty pairs of felt boots, a split army drum, and a stack of self-criticisms written after each failed attempt at the lock, each one shorter than the last.
column3: 仓里抄出逃兵的存货：二十袋硬得能砸核桃的军饼、三捆箭、四十双毡靴、一面破了的军鼓，还有一摞他们撬锁失败后写的检讨，一张比一张字少。

column2: Word spreads among Old Han's old company that you opened the store. Every time you come, the ones herding and farming nearby have already filled waterskins and stacked fresh flatbread at the door, weighted with a stone painted with their company's emblem.
column3: 老韩的旧部听说你们打开了屯仓，散在附近放牧种瓜的，每次都早早把水囊灌满、把烤好的馕码在仓门口，压一块石头，石头上画着他们那一队的旗号。

column2: The Envoy's Question
column3: 问使坡

column2: On top of the slope stands an envoy from the Bandit King with a troop of archers. The King has heard that a caravan flying the court's banner has entered the Sand Sea, and sent him to ask one question: 'Have you come to pay a debt, or to collect one?' Answer wrong and the archers shoot. He throws a bone at your feet.
column3: 坡顶站着一个马贼王派来的使者，带着一队射手，拦住你们，说王听说有一支打着朝廷旗号的商队进了沙海，让他来问一句话：「你们是来还账的，还是来讨账的？」答错了，射手们就放箭。使者说完，把手里的一根骨头扔在你们脚下。

column2: The archers scattered, the envoy is not offended. 'Anyone who can win a fight, the King is willing to see.' You pick up the bone: a length of camel bone carved with a person's name, the cuts crooked, as if the man carved his own name. This one fell off a leg of the King's chair, the envoy says. 'The King told me to return it to its owner. But the owner never came back.'
column3: 射手们被打散，使者倒也不恼，说「能打赢的，王都愿意见」。你们捡起那根骨头，是一截驼骨，上面刻着一个人的名字，刀口歪歪扭扭，像是自己给自己刻的。使者说，这根是从王的椅子腿上掉下来的，「王让我还给名字的主人，可主人没回来」。

column2: Sea-Gazing Dune
column3: 望海沙

column2: Shen Du's sailors are homesick. A band of bandit riders seizes the moment: ride with the Bandit King, they say, and you'll eat and drink well, a horse and ten taels each, better than trailing round a desert after a captain who's lost her ship. A few young sailors are tempted and pack their bundles. On the dune the two sides are shoving, and blades are about to come out.
column3: 沈渡的水手们想家了。一伙马贼骑手趁机找上门来，说跟着马贼王有吃有喝，一人给一匹马、十两银子，比在沙漠里跟着一个丢了船的船主强。几个年轻水手动了心，收拾了包袱就要跟着走，两边在沙丘上推推搡搡，眼看要动刀。

column2: The riders driven off, Shen Du doesn't scold anyone. She climbs to the top of the dune and sings a Quanzhou fishing song. One by one the sailors join in, and when it ends the bundles are on the ground. The figures in the margin of her half chart, she tells you, are the bookkeeper's handover list: where each route's goods were to change hands, and how much. 'If the books don't balance, the three routes can never join up.'
column3: 骑手们被打跑，沈渡没骂人，只是站到沙丘顶上，唱起了一支泉州的渔歌。水手们一个接一个跟着唱，唱完包袱都放下了。沈渡对你们说，她那半张海图边上的数，是账房开的「接货单」：三路的货在哪里交、交多少，都写在上面。「账对不上，三路就合不起来。」

column2: No-North Ridge
column3: 禁北岗

column2: Along a ridge in the north of the Sand Sea, bandit archers stand in a line facing north, backs to the south, letting no one go north, not even their own. A board on the ridge reads: 'By the King's order: none shall follow the north road.' A few bandits who tried to go north treasure-hunting lie trussed at the foot of the ridge, still yelling: 'What's up there anyway?'
column3: 沙海北边一道岗子上，马贼射手们排成一排，面朝北，背朝南，不许任何人往北走，连他们自己的人也不许。岗上插着一块木牌：「王令：北路不许跟。」几个想往北去找宝的马贼被捆在岗下，嘴里还在嚷：「北边到底有什么？」

column2: The archers fall back, and their leader explains. The north is the road the Qianli caravan took, and where they were going, bandits have no business following. 'The King saw them this far. Further north, he said, wasn't his land any more.' A north wind blows past, carrying a faint scent of incense.
column3: 射手们退开了，领头的说王的意思是：北边是千里号走的路，他们要去的地方，马贼不该跟去。「王当年送他们到这儿，再往北，他说不是他的地界了。」北风吹过来，带着一点香火的味道。

column2: Sand Tower Light
column3: 沙塔灯

column2: On top of a dune stands a half-collapsed earth tower, and at its summit sits a great lamp bowl that could hold a vatful of oil. This is what Shen Du wants: a lighthouse in the Sand Sea, so that anyone lost can find the way back at night. But bandit archers crouch on the tower using it as a lookout, and shoot anyone who climbs.
column3: 沙丘顶上有一座塌了半边的土塔，塔顶留着一个大灯盏，能盛下一缸油。沈渡说这是她要的东西，在沙海里点一座灯塔，走散的人夜里就能找回来。可塔上蹲着一伙马贼射手，把这儿当了瞭望台，谁往上爬就射谁。

column2: The archers driven off the tower, Shen Du lights the lamp herself, and its glow reaches for miles. Half an hour later, far to the east, another point of fire appears, flaring and dimming as if in answer. Her sailors say that's the Bandit King's camp. 'He knows this light,' says Shen Du. 'The Qianli camel train hung lamps like it at night.'
column3: 射手们被赶下塔，沈渡亲手把灯点着了，火光照出去几十里。过了半个时辰，东边很远的地方也亮起一点火，一明一暗，像在回话。沈渡的水手说那是马贼王的营地。「他认得这灯，」沈渡说，「当年千里号的驼队，夜里也挂这样的灯。」

column2: The Old Water Seller
column3: 老水摊

column2: At the end of a hollow stands a water stall whose old keeper measures with a small hourglass: when the sand runs out, the bowl is full, not a drop more, not a drop less. Bandit riders have seized his water cart, tied him up in front of his stall, and are selling his water dear. Tied up, the old man isn't worried, only watches their bowls. 'Wrong measure. Wrong measure.'
column3: 沙窝尽头摆着一个水摊，卖水的老人用一只小沙漏量水：沙漏漏完，一碗水就倒满了，不多一滴，不少一滴。一伙马贼骑手抢了他的水车，把老人绑在摊前，自己守着水卖高价。老人被绑着也不急，只是盯着他们手里的碗：「量错了，量错了。」

column2: The riders driven off, the old man reopens his stall. Same measure, not a copper dearer, as much as you like. Ten years ago, he tells you, a man stumbled in here, wasted to the bone, a ledger on his back, and traded his own boots for three bowls of water. He asked: 'Have you seen which way three hundred people went?' 'He was two days behind his caravan,' says the old man. 'I pointed east.'
column3: 骑手们被打跑，老人重新开了摊，价钱一文不涨，要多少卖多少。他说十年前一个人跌跌撞撞走到这里，瘦得脱了相，背着一本账，用自己的靴子换了三碗水，问他：「有没有看见三百个人往哪边去？」「他比他的商队晚了两天，」老人说，「我指了东边。」

column2: Map-Sellers' Dunes
column3: 卖图沙

column2: A band of bandit riders camps in this hollow running a map stall: ten taels a sheet for 'The Qianli Treasure Map'. They're copies. The original is Shen Du's half chart, stolen on the road and copied hundreds of times to sell across the Sand Sea to anyone dreaming of riches. Buyers follow the map and every one of them walks straight into the sea. The sea on the map, of course.
column3: 沙窝里扎着一伙马贼骑手，摆了个卖图的摊子，一张图卖十两银子，说是「千里号藏宝图」。图是抄的，原本是沈渡的半张海图，被他们半路偷去，抄了几百份，满沙海卖给做发财梦的人。买图的人照着图找，一个个都走进了海里去，当然是图上的海。

column2: The riders scattered, you recover a chest of maps. The coastlines are neatly drawn, but the bookkeeper's figures in the margins meant nothing to the copyists and come out garbled. Shen Du leafs through them and laughs. 'They thought the treasure was on the map. The treasure is in the numbers.' She burns every copy but one, and corrects its wrong figures one by one.
column3: 骑手们被打散，你们抄回了一箱图，图上的海岸线画得工工整整，可边上那些账房写的数，抄的人看不懂，抄得七零八落。沈渡翻了翻，笑了：「他们以为宝藏在图上，宝藏在数里。」她把抄本全烧了，只留下一张，边上抄错的数被她一个个改了回来。

column2: Buried-Alive Dunes
column3: 埋身沙

column2: This stretch of sand looks empty, but step on it and a hand shoots up to grab your ankle. It's a gang of bandit footmen who burrow: when a sandstorm comes they bury themselves, and when it passes they pop up as lively as ever, waiting for storm-bound travellers to walk over them.
column3: 这片沙地看上去空空荡荡，脚一踩，沙子里却伸出一只手来抓你的脚脖子。这是一伙会钻沙的马贼步卒，沙暴来了他们就把自己埋进沙里，沙暴过了照样活蹦乱跳，专等被风沙困住的人走过来。

column2: The burrowing bandits are pulled out of the sand one at a time. Their chief says they've hidden from sandstorms here for twenty years, and the biggest they ever saw was ten years ago. That wind split a caravan of three hundred in two. 'The front half went off toward White Dragon Mound behind a young bandit. The back half shouted all night in the sand, shouting the front half's names.'
column3: 钻沙的马贼被一个个从沙里拔出来。头目说他们在这儿躲了二十年沙暴，见过最大的一场是十年前：那场风把一支三百人的商队劈成了两截，「前半截跟着一个年轻的马贼往白龙堆去了，后半截的人在沙里喊了一夜，喊的是前半截的名字」。

column2: Turning-Back Sand
column3: 回头沙

column2: Old Han stops before a stretch of sand. Ten years ago, he says, this is where he caught up with the tail of the Qianli caravan. Now a patrol of the King's riders is camped here, and they close in when they see him: the King's orders, they follow Old Han wherever he goes. Old Han sighs. 'Fight them. Afterwards I'll tell you what happened that day.'
column3: 老韩在一片沙地前停下，说十年前他就是在这儿追上了千里号的尾巴。如今这里扎着王的一支巡哨骑手，见了老韩就围上来，说王有令，老韩到哪儿他们跟到哪儿。老韩叹口气，对你们说：「打吧，打完了我把那天的事说给你们听。」

column2: The patrol scattered, Old Han sits in the sand and tells it. That day he caught the caravan, but the bookkeeper wouldn't let him come along. 'He said the road ahead wasn't one for blades. Go back and guard the road behind us.' Old Han didn't go back; he stayed and followed the King. 'Ten years I've guarded the road behind them,' he says. 'Not one of the ones ahead has come back.'
column3: 巡哨被打散，老韩坐在沙上说：那天他追上了商队，账房却不让他跟。「账房说，前面的路不是刀能走的，你回去，替我们守着后头的路。」老韩没回去，留下来跟了王。「我守了十年后头的路，」他说，「前头的人，一个也没回来。」

column2: The Parting Ridge
column3: 分驼岭

column2: A long sand ridge, its surface baked by salt into a hard crust that cracks underfoot. Set in the salt is a great expanse of hoofprints and footprints, preserved for ten years where the wind could not erase them. Bandit archers have laid a trap on the ridge: whoever stoops to look at the prints gets shot from behind a dune.
column3: 一道长长的沙岭，岭上的沙被盐壳结成了硬板，踩上去咔咔响。盐壳上留着一大片蹄印和脚印，结在盐里十年没被风吹掉。一伙马贼射手在岭上设了套，等人蹲下来看脚印，就从沙丘后面放箭。

column2: The archers driven off, you and Shen Du walk the length of the prints. Halfway along the ridge they split in two: one stream northeast into White Dragon Mound, one south, growing ragged, until one by one they turn back and rejoin the northeast stream. In front of them all runs a line of small bare footprints. 'That's the guide,' says Shen Du. 'Not very old.'
column3: 射手们被打跑，你们和沈渡顺着脚印走了一遍：到岭中间，脚印分成了两股，一股往东北，进白龙堆；一股往南，渐渐散乱，最后又一个个折回来，汇进了东北那一股。走在最前面的是一行光脚的小脚印，「这是带路的，」沈渡说，「年纪不大。」

column2: Buried Token Mound
column3: 埋令墩

column2: Old Han leads you to an earthen mound with a flagpole on top, its flag long gone. Years ago he buried his company captain's token under the pole and swore to dig it up only when the Qianli caravan returned, and hand it back to the court. But a troop of the King's archers already holds the mound. The King knows the token is here; while it stays buried, Old Han's company can't be released.
column3: 老韩带你们来到一座土墩，墩上立着一根旗杆，旗早没了。他说当年他把队正令埋在旗杆底下，发过誓，等千里号回来再挖出来，交还给朝廷。可王的一伙射手早就守在墩上：王知道那块令牌在这儿，令牌在，老韩那一队兵就散不了。

column2: The archers withdraw. Under the flagpole Old Han digs up a bronze token carved 'Company Captain', his company's number on the back. This is the Company Captain's Token: a border company was a hundred men, mustered by this token. 'Take it to a barracks, a range or a stable and call out, "Han's company, back to the colours," and the veterans scattered across the Sand Sea will come, every one with ten years in the saddle.' He hands it over, then sets his copper basin upside down on top of the pole. 'Clean at last. Tell the King I've gone, and I've handed my men to you. Ten years he's waited on that bone chair. It's time it ended.'
column3: 射手们退了，老韩在旗杆下挖出一块铜令牌，上刻「队正」二字，背面是他那一队的番号。这就是队正令：边军一队百人，凭令点卯。「拿去兵营、靶场、马厩，宣一声『韩字营的兄弟，回营』，散在沙海里的老兵就会来投，个个是十年的老手。」他把令牌交给你们，又把铜盆扣在旗杆顶上：「这回洗干净了。替我告诉王，我走了，人我交给你们了。他坐在骨椅上等了十年，该有个了结。」

column2: Sea-Barring Camp
column3: 拦海营

column2: Across the road east stands a big camp of the Bandit King's southern bands, foot, bow and horse drawn up in three lines, and over the gate hangs the King's command arrow: 'No one who comes from the sea may go east.' Shen Du's sailors have been stopped three times, each time politely escorted back, with a bag of provisions. 'So polite,' says Shen Du, 'it makes me furious.'
column3: 东去的路上扎着马贼王南边的一座大营，步、射、骑排成三道，营门口挂着王的令箭：「凡从海上来的人，不许东去。」沈渡的水手们被拦了三回，每回都被客客气气地请回来，还送了一袋干粮。沈渡说：「客气得让人生气。」

column2: The camp broken, you corner its captain, and he finally comes clean: the King's order has a second half, passed on by word of mouth. 'The woman from the sea: let her bring someone who can keep accounts, and come to see me together.' The captain scratches his head. 'What the King means is, she's not to come alone. If she comes, she brings the accountant.' Shen Du glances at you.
column3: 大营被冲开，营头被你们拦下，这才交了底：王的令箭后面还有半句，是口传的，「海上来的女人，让她带上会算账的，一起来见我」。营头摸着脑袋：「王的意思是，她一个人不许来。要来，得带着算账的。」沈渡看了你们一眼。

column2: Bound Monk Post
column3: 缚僧桩

column2: A young monk is tied to a post in the sun, his face burnt red, still chanting: 'Repaying debts is the law of heaven and earth.' A band of bandit riders tied him there. He was sent from the Thousand Buddha Caves to collect debts and has collected his way this far, insisting they repay ten pounds of lamp oil borrowed three years ago, and showing them the ledger page by page.
column3: 一个小和尚被绑在一根木桩上晒太阳，晒得脸通红，嘴里还在念：「欠债还钱，天经地义。」绑他的是一伙马贼骑手：小和尚是千佛洞派来讨债的，一路讨到这里，非要他们还三年前借的十斤灯油，还一本一本地翻账给他们看。

column2: The riders driven off, the monk rubs his wrists and introduces himself: his dharma name is Liaozhang, 'Settle the Account'. He opens his thick ledger: everyone in the Sand Sea who owes the Caves for lamp oil, from petty bandits up to the Bandit King. On the oldest page is written 'Qianli caravan', and after it, nothing: no sum. 'My master says that one can only be written once we see the people.'
column3: 骑手们被打跑，小和尚揉着手腕，自报法号「了账」。他翻开厚厚的债簿给你们看：沙海里欠千佛洞香油钱的，从小马贼到马贼王，一个都不少。翻到最旧的一页，写着「千里号」三个字，后面空着，没写欠多少。「师父说，这一笔要见了人才能写。」

column2: Sea-Story Dunes
column3: 听海沙

column2: Bandit footmen have kidnapped Shen Du's first mate and demand a strange ransom: no silver, only Shen Du herself, coming to tell them about the sea. Born and raised in the Sand Sea, not one of them has ever seen it. To keep the ransom valuable they treat the mate like an honoured ancestor, meat three times a day, wine with every meal, a shade awning of his own. He has grown visibly fatter and sends word back: 'No hurry, captain.'
column3: 一伙马贼步卒绑走了沈渡的大副，要的赎金很怪：不要银子，要沈渡亲自来给他们讲海。他们生在沙海，长在沙海，谁也没见过海。为了让赎金值钱，他们把大副当祖宗供着，一天三顿肉，顿顿有酒，还给他搭了个凉棚。大副被养胖了一圈，捎信回来说：「船主，不急。」

column2: After a fight, Shen Du sits down anyway and tells the bandits about the sea all night: how high the waves stand, how big the whales are, how a ship finds its way in fog. The bandits listen with tears in their eyes, and at dawn they not only release the mate but press all his leftover jerky on him. He leaves looking back every third step, sorry to go.
column3: 打完一场，沈渡还是坐下来给马贼们讲了一夜的海：浪有多高，鲸有多大，船怎么在雾里认路。马贼们听得眼泪汪汪，第二天一早，不但放了大副，还把大副吃剩的肉干全塞给了他。大副走的时候一步三回头，舍不得。

column2: Cave of the Sail
column3: 藏帆窟

column2: A deep cave is cut into the sandstone, its mouth guarded by the Bandit King's finest troops, foot, bow and horse in three ranks, all veterans who came out of White Dragon Mound with him ten years ago. They neither rob nor raid. They only guard one thing in the cave, day and night in shifts, and fight to the death against anyone who comes near. Inside hangs a huge cloth, white as a sail. When wind pours into the cave mouth the cloth billows, and the whole cave seems to breathe.
column3: 沙岩里有一座深窟，窟口守着马贼王最精锐的一支人马，步、射、骑三路排开，都是十年前跟王出过白龙堆的老兵。他们不抢不劫，只守着窟里的一样东西，日夜轮班，谁靠近就拼命。窟里挂着一面大布，白得像帆，风从窟口灌进去，布鼓起来，整座窟都在呼吸。

column2: The veterans give ground. Shen Du runs her hand along a row of stitches at the cloth's edge, and her eyes redden. 'This is my sail.' When the three routes parted ten years ago she gave the camel train a sail from her own ship, and they sewed it into a great banner marked Qian: the very Qian banner the Bandit King's rule forbids anyone to rob. 'My sail has flown in the Sand Sea ten years,' says Shen Du. 'It's travelled further than my ship.'
column3: 老兵们退了，沈渡摸着大布边上的一处针脚，眼圈红了。「这是我的帆。」十年前三路分别时，她把自己船上的一面帆送给了驼队，驼队把它缝成了大旗，大旗上写着「千」，就是马贼王规矩里那面「不许劫的千字旗」。「我的帆在沙海里飘了十年，」沈渡说，「比我的船走得还远。」

column2: Compound Interest Dunes
column3: 利滚沙

column2: In a big camp of bandits, foot, bow and horse, a crowd surrounds a long table on which lies a huge ledger, while several clerks rattle their abacuses. This is the Bandit King's debt office, and its ledger holds only one entry: 'Road toll owed by the Qianli caravan.' Their orders are to compound the interest every year. Ten years on, the figure runs off the edge of the table.
column3: 一座大营里，一伙马贼步、射、骑都有，正围着一张长桌，桌上摊着一本大账，几个账房先生打算盘打得噼里啪啦。这是马贼王手下的收账营，账上只有一笔：「千里号欠路钱」。他们奉命每年把利息滚一遍，滚了十年，数字已经写到了桌子外面。

column2: The debt office scattered, Shen Du leafs through the great ledger and bursts out laughing. 'They've got it wrong.' Compounding is fine, she says, but every year they counted the previous year's interest twice over, so after ten years the sum is thousands of times too big. 'The King's clerks can't keep accounts. No wonder he wants someone who can.'
column3: 收账营被打散，沈渡把那本大账翻了一遍，笑出了声：「这账算错了。」她说利滚利是没错，可他们每年都把前一年的利息又算了两遍，十年下来多算了几千倍。「王雇的账房不会算账，难怪他要找会算账的人。」

column2: Wind-Worship Dunes
column3: 拜风沙

column2: On the dunes a crowd in grey robes spin with arms outstretched, faster and faster, crying 'Wind, come and take me!' They are the Whirlwind Sect, who believe the Sand Sea's dust devils are heaven's palanquins and that anyone swept up ascends. Some of their footmen are pushing a passing pedlar into a whirlwind 'to see him on his way'. He clings to his carrying pole for dear life.
column3: 沙丘上一群穿灰袍的人张开双臂转圈，越转越快，嘴里喊着「风来接我」。他们是旋风教的信徒，信沙海里的旋风是上天的轿子，被卷走的人都升了天。几个信徒的步卒正把一个过路的货郎往旋风里推，说是送他一程。货郎抱着货担死活不撒手。

column2: The sect is scattered and the pedlar can't stop shaking. Their scripture says that ten years ago a great wind carried off three hundred people: 'Three hundred ascended together, their banner like a white sail.' Liaozhang rolls his eyes. 'Ascended nothing. They went to our Caves. I'll find the proof sooner or later.'
column3: 信徒们被打散，货郎吓得直哆嗦。旋风教的经卷上写着：十年前一场大风卷走了三百人，「三百人一齐升天，旗如白帆」。了账和尚翻了个白眼：「升什么天，那是去我们千佛洞了。我早晚找出证据来。」

column2: Sand Harbour
column3: 沙港

column2: Shen Du gathers her sail-carts, camels and sailors in a sheltered bay of sand, as if mooring in a harbour. She has decided to go with you to see the Bandit King. But a troop of the King's riders already blocks the mouth of the bay with orders to 'invite' her, and her alone. The sailors grab oars for weapons, and Shen Du stands on a sail-cart. 'I told you. If we go, we go together.'
column3: 沈渡把帆车、驼队和水手们聚到一片背风的沙湾里，像在港里泊船。她决定和你们一起去见马贼王。可王的一队骑手已经守在沙湾口，奉命「请」她去，只请她一个。水手们抄起船桨当刀，沈渡站在帆车上：「我说了，要去就一起去。」

column2: The riders are beaten back and gallop off to report. Shen Du solemnly hands you her half of the sea chart. 'When we reach the King, you do the accounts. I only care about my ship.' She doesn't believe all three hundred of the Qianli caravan are gone. 'A man like the bookkeeper doesn't die with his sums unfinished.' The sailors strike sail and weigh anchor, and a long work-chant rings across the bay.
column3: 骑手们被打退，回去报信了。沈渡把她那半张海图郑重地交给你们：「到了王那儿，账你们算，我只认船。」她说她不信千里号三百人都没了，「账房那样的人，账没算完，不会死的」。水手们收帆起锚，沙湾里响起一声长长的号子。

column2: Wind-Chasers' Column
column3: 随风阵

column2: In the distance a tawny dust devil spins, and behind it marches a long column of Whirlwind Sect believers, foot, bow and horse. Wherever the wind goes they follow, taking over every road and trampling every tent on the way: 'The wind's path. Mortals stand aside.' Today the whirlwind is twisting straight toward your camp.
column3: 远处卷起一根黄褐色的旋风，旋风后面跟着长长一队旋风教的信徒，步、射、骑都有，旋风往哪儿走，他们就往哪儿跟，见路占路，见帐踩帐，说是「风的路，凡人让开」。今天旋风正往你们的营地这边扭过来。

column2: The column is broken and so is the whirlwind, and where it passed it has scoured an old stone marker out of the sand, a small Buddha carved at its head and the words: 'Thousand Buddha Caves, three hundred li north.' Liaozhang says the monastery set up such stones long ago for travelling monks, all the way north. 'So the wind did us one good turn.'
column3: 信徒们被冲散，旋风也散了，沙地上被它刮出一块埋了多年的石碑，碑首刻着一尊小佛，碑上的字是：「千佛洞，北三百里。」了账说，这是寺里早年给往来僧人立的路碑，一路往北都有，「旋风也替我们干了件好事」。

column2: Donkey-Back Slope
column3: 驴背坡

column2: Liaozhang's donkey has been led off by bandit footmen, two big chests of the monastery's old ledgers on its back. The bandits thought the chests held offering money, prised them open, found nothing but accounts, and are now furious enough to burn them. The donkey is stubborn: all four hooves are planted in the sand and it won't move, and the bandits are whipping it.
column3: 了账和尚的毛驴被一伙马贼步卒牵走了，驴背上驮着两大箱寺里的旧债簿。马贼以为箱子里是香火钱，撬开一看全是账，气得要拿去烧火。毛驴倔得很，四蹄钉在沙里不肯走，马贼推不动，正拿鞭子抽它。

column2: The bandits driven off, the donkey trots back to Liaozhang by itself. From the bottom of a chest he digs out a ledger from ten years ago and reads it to you: 'Autumn, Dingwei year. The Qianli caravan borrows three hundred pounds of lamp oil and one sutra; the bookkeeper pledges his seal, to be redeemed on the way back.' That seal, he says, has sat before the Buddha ever since. In ten years, no one has come to redeem it.
column3: 马贼被打跑，毛驴自己颠颠地跑回了了账身边。了账从箱底翻出十年前的一本，念给你们听：「丁未年秋，千里号驼队借寺中灯油三百斤、经卷一部，账房押印一方，言回程来赎。」他说寺里那方印一直供在佛前，十年没人来赎。

column2: The Tael Collectors
column3: 收两营

column2: Along the sand track bandit footmen escort a small wooden box east. It holds just one tael of silver, yet they guard it tighter than ten chests of gold. This, their leader says, is the sum the King values most: one tael a mute brings in on the dot every month. 'The King says if this tael goes missing, none of us need bother coming back.'
column3: 沙路上一伙马贼步卒押着一只小木匣往东走，匣子里只有一两银子，可他们护得比十箱金子还紧。领头的说这是王最看重的一笔：一个哑巴每月准时交来的一两，「王说，这一两要是丢了，我们全都别回去」。

column2: The escort scattered, the box is unharmed; you reseal it just as it was and let them deliver it. When Shen Du hears about the mute she is speechless for a long moment. 'The bookkeeper's apprentice? Trained by his master. That's someone who can keep accounts.' She sends sailors west at once to find him. 'All this time I've been looking, and he was at the ghost market, paying the King a tael a month.'
column3: 马贼被打散，木匣完好无损，你们原样封好，让他们继续送去。沈渡听了哑巴的事，愣了半天：「账房的学徒？他师父教出来的，那就是会算账的人。」她让水手赶紧往西去找他。「我找了这么久，他就在鬼市上，每月给王送一两银子。」

column2: The Mirror Seller's Tent
column3: 镜商帐

column2: A brightly striped tent stands on the plain. Its owner, a Sogdian woman, sells bronze mirrors, big enough to see yourself whole or small enough to hide in a sleeve. She hired bandit riders as escorts, and halfway here they changed their minds and are holding her and her mirrors for ransom. She sits among her mirrors putting on rouge. 'There's nobody at home. You'll have to pay the ransom yourselves.'
column3: 荒原上一顶彩帐，帐主是个粟特女商，专卖铜镜：大的能照全身，小的能藏在袖里。她雇了一伙马贼骑手护货，走到半路，骑手们反悔了，把她和镜子一起扣下，说要等她家里拿钱来赎。她坐在镜子堆里涂胭脂，说：「我家里没人，赎金你们自己出吧。」

column2: The riders driven off, she opens shop briskly and trades with you. Her best customers, she says, are the Thousand Buddha Caves: the grottoes run so deep that the monks bounce sunlight in from mirror to mirror to see the murals. 'Ten years ago I sold a cartload of mirrors to a caravan. They said they were taking them to the Caves, to give the Buddhas some light.'
column3: 骑手们被打跑，女商人爽快地开了张，跟你们做买卖。她说她的大主顾是千佛洞：洞窟太深，僧人们用一面面铜镜把日光一层层照进去，才看得清壁画。「十年前我卖过一车镜子给一支商队，他们说要送去千佛洞，给佛像照个亮。」

column2: Mouth of White Dragon Mound
column3: 白龙堆口

column2: East along the old road the ground heaves up into rows of white earthen ridges, carved by the wind into dragon backs, one after another as far as you can see. This is White Dragon Mound, and nine in ten who enter get lost. At the entrance bandit footmen run a stall: pay and they'll guide you, except that once paid they vanish halfway in. On the ridge behind the stall a faded red cord is tied.
column3: 古道往东，地上隆起一道道白色的土垄，被风削得像龙背，一条接一条，一眼望不到头，这就是白龙堆。走进去的人十个有九个迷路。入口处一伙马贼步卒摆了个摊子，说给钱就带路，可收了钱，带到一半就不见了。摊子后面的土垄上，系着一根褪色的红绳。

column2: The bandits chased off, you follow the red cord with your eyes. Every few dozen paces another length is tied to a ridge, length after length, leading deep into the maze. The cords have faded almost white, the knots tied tight, the kind the wind can't undo. Whoever tied them went carefully, as if afraid those behind would fall behind.
column3: 马贼被赶跑，你们顺着那根红绳往里看：每隔几十步，土垄上就系着一截红绳，一截接一截，伸进了迷宫深处。红绳褪得快成白的了，结打得很密，是不会被风吹开的那种。系绳的人走得很仔细，像是怕后面的人跟不上。

column2: The Prophet's Tent
column3: 先知帐

column2: The Whirlwind Sect's prophet lives in a pointed tent; ten years ago, they say, he saw three hundred people ascend with his own eyes. Believers stand guard at the flap, letting no one in, and outside a long queue waits to ask whether the wind will come for them. Inside, the prophet coughs, and sounds very much like an ordinary old man.
column3: 旋风教的先知住在一顶尖帐里，据说十年前亲眼见过三百人升天。一群步卒信徒守着帐门，不许人进，帐外排着长队，都是来求先知卜一卦、看自己能不能被风接走的。先知在帐里咳嗽，咳得很像一个普通的老头。

column2: The guards scattered, the prophet comes out of the tent himself. He admits he never saw an ascension. He saw three hundred people walk into the north mouth of White Dragon Mound through a sky full of yellow sand, and when the wind died they were gone. 'No one believed me, so I said they'd gone up to heaven.' Liaozhang says: 'They came out of the Mound and went north. What you saw was their backs.'
column3: 守门的信徒被打散，先知自己掀开帐门出来了。他承认那天他没看见升天，只看见三百人顶着漫天黄沙走进白龙堆的北口，等风停了，人都不见了。「没人信我，我只好说他们升了天。」了账说：「他们是出了白龙堆往北走了，你看见的是背影。」

column2: Dragonspine Ridge
column3: 龙脊垄

column2: The highest ridge in White Dragon Mound is called the Dragonspine; from its top you can see half the maze. The Bandit King keeps a large force here, foot, bow and horse, solely to guard the red-cord trail, and anyone who tries to untie a cord is arrested on the spot. 'The King says,' their captain declares, 'the red cords are for coming back.'
column3: 白龙堆里最高的一道土垄叫龙脊，站在上面能望见半个迷宫。马贼王在这儿驻着一大队人马，步、射、骑都有，专守红绳那条路，谁想把红绳解下来，就当场拿下。守垄的头目说：「王说了，红绳是给人回来用的。」

column2: The garrison falls back, and on the earthen face of the Dragonspine you find a row of carvings. At the top: 'Dingwei year. Led three hundred through here.' Below are seven names, the last cut deepest, with two characters beside it: 'Seventeen.' That, says an old guard, was the King's age that year.
column3: 守垄的人马退了，你们在龙脊的土壁上找到一排刻痕，最上面刻着一行字：「丁未年，领三百人过此。」下面是七个名字，最后一个名字刻得最深，旁边注着两个字：「十七」。守垄的老兵说，那是王那年的岁数。

column2: Holy Boot Camp
column3: 圣靴营

column2: The Whirlwind Sect's great camp enshrines a relic: an old leather boot, said to have fallen from one of the ascended. Foot, bow and horse guard it day and night in shifts, and believers queue to touch it, one touch to keep sand out of your eyes for a year. The sole has been rubbed shiny, still with a little ten-year-old mud stuck to it.
column3: 旋风教的大营里供着一件圣物：一只旧皮靴，说是升天的人落下来的。营里步、射、骑都有，日夜轮班守着，信徒们排队来摸靴子，摸一下能保一年不被风沙迷眼。靴子底已经被摸得发亮，上面还粘着一点十年前的泥。

column2: With the guards gone you turn the holy boot over. Nailed into the sole is a cobbler's bronze tack stamped 'Wang's, Dunhuang', and stuffed in the shaft is a slip of paper: 'Resole at the Thousand Buddha Caves.' Liaozhang laughs until he can't stand. 'The ascended need new soles?' He tucks the slip into his ledger.
column3: 守营的信徒散了，你们把圣靴翻过来，靴底钉着一枚鞋匠的铜钉，刻着「敦煌王记」，靴筒里还塞着一张纸条：「到千佛洞换底。」了账笑得直不起腰：「升天的人还要换鞋底？」他把纸条收进了债簿。

column2: Apricot Slope Farm
column3: 杏坡屯

column2: Below the southern mountains a slope of apricot trees shelters a few households who grow and dry the fruit. Bandit footmen have taken the village; finding the apricots sour, they make the villagers boil the whole crop into jam, vat after vat, until the mountainside reeks sweet and sour. An old farmer, eyes streaming from the smoke, says this year's firewood is all gone.
column3: 南山脚下有一片杏树坡，坡上几户人家种杏、晒杏干。一伙马贼步卒占了村子，嫌杏子酸，逼村里人把杏子全熬成杏酱，熬了一缸又一缸，熬得满山都是酸甜味。村里的老汉被熏得直流眼泪，说今年的柴都烧光了。

column2: The bandits chased off, the jam at least has turned out perfectly. Shen Du leaves half her sailors here to help repair houses until she returns. Ten years ago, says the old farmer, another large party rested here, too many to share the apricots, and their leader traded a piece of jade for the whole village's dried fruit. 'Said they were off to pay the Bandit King his road toll, and the King wouldn't take silver.'
column3: 马贼被赶跑，杏酱倒是熬得正好。沈渡把一半水手留在这里，帮着村里修房子，等她回来。老汉说十年前也有一伙人在这儿歇过脚，人多，杏子不够分，领头的拿一块玉换了全村的杏干，「说要去给马贼王付路钱，王不收银子」。

column2: From the village you seize the bandits' stores: twenty vats of apricot jam, two sacks of apricot kernels, a cartload of split poplar firewood, and the big copper pot they boiled the jam in, engraved on the bottom 'Property of So-and-So's Bandit Hold'.
column3: 村里抄出马贼的存货：二十缸杏酱、两袋杏仁、一车劈好的胡杨柴，还有一个他们拿来熬酱的大铜锅，锅底刻着「某某马贼寨公用」。

column2: Whenever you pass, the villagers leave freshly dried apricots and a jar of jam on a stone at the top of the slope, and the sailors who stayed behind grease your axles and patch your tents, the stitches neat as a ship's.
column3: 每次路过，村里人都把新晒的杏干和一罐杏酱放在坡口的石头上，留下的水手们还会把你们的车轴上好油、把帐篷的破洞补好，针脚整整齐齐。

column2: Wind-Listening Mound
column3: 听风墩

column2: A blind old man sits on an earthen mound, his ear pressed to the wall, listening to the wind. He is the best guide in White Dragon Mound, finding his way by the sound of wind through the ridges, and has never once been lost. Bandit footmen are holding him to lead them to treasure in the maze; when he refused they broke his walking stick. 'No use,' says the old man. 'I walk with my ears.'
column3: 一座土墩上坐着个瞎眼老人，耳朵贴着土壁听风。他是白龙堆里最好的向导，靠风穿过土垄的声音认路，从没迷过一次。一伙马贼步卒把他扣下，要他带路去找白龙堆里的宝藏，老人不肯，马贼就把他的拐杖折了。老人说：「折了也没用，我是用耳朵走路的。」

column2: The bandits chased off, the old man smiles. Listening to the wind is no magic, he says. The wind has blown one way through White Dragon Mound for ages and carved these ridges, so the ridges run the way the prevailing wind runs; follow them and you never walk in circles. Over ten years ago he taught it to a wild boy. 'Later that boy led three hundred people out of the Mound. Said they were his road toll, and he had to wait for them to come back.'
column3: 马贼被赶跑，老人说听风不玄。白龙堆的土垄是风朝一个方向吹了千万年削出来的，垄的走向就是常年的风向，顺着垄走，就不会转圈。他十几年前把这手教给一个野小子，「后来那小子领着三百人走出了白龙堆，说那些人是他的路钱，他得等他们回来」。

column2: Bone Shore
column3: 骨岸

column2: Deep in White Dragon Mound lies a lake, and its shore is white all over. Not salt, bones, large and small, all camels'. The Bandit King's riders water their horses here and let no outsider near this stretch of shore. In a small shed by the water an old carver is polishing a length of camel bone, and doesn't look up at the sound of hooves.
column3: 白龙堆深处藏着一汪湖，湖岸上白花花一片，不是盐，是骨头，大大小小，都是骆驼的。马贼王的骑手在湖边饮马，不许外人靠近这片湖岸。湖边一座小棚里，一个老刻工正在打磨一根驼骨，听见马蹄声也不抬头。

column2: The riders driven back, the old carver finally looks up. Ten years ago, he says, that sandstorm killed more than half the Qianli caravan's camels, and their bones were left by this lake. 'Those three hundred names, I didn't carve them. They carved them themselves, one person, one blade, on the camels' bones. When they'd finished, the bookkeeper said: "Our names stay here in pledge. We'll redeem them on the way back."'
column3: 骑手们被打退，老刻工才抬起头。他说十年前那场沙暴，千里号的骆驼死了一大半，尸骨就留在这片湖边。「那三百个名字不是我刻的，」他说，「是他们自己一人一刀刻在骆驼骨头上的。刻完了，账房说：『名字押在这儿，回来赎。』」

column2: Wild Ass Flats
column3: 野驴川

column2: A herd of wild asses, several hundred strong, roams the northern plain, and every autumn they walk north along the same path. Bandit archers lie in ambush beside it, shooting them as they pass and selling the hides. Liaozhang chants sutras in distress: the asses have walked this way for centuries, he says. 'Donkeys remember better than people.'
column3: 北边的荒原上有一群野驴，几百头，每年秋天都沿着同一条路往北走。一伙马贼射手埋伏在路边，等驴群过来就放箭，射下来剥皮卖钱。了账和尚急得直念经，说这条路走了几百年，「驴比人记性好」。

column2: The archers driven off, the herd ambles past and treads out a clear path. The old monks at the monastery used to say, Liaozhang tells you, that the monks travelling to the Caves in the old days followed the wild asses, which knew where the grass and water were. 'If the Qianli caravan went north, this is the road they took.' Beyond the end of the herd, the northern sky shows a smudge of dark red, like a cliff face.
column3: 射手们被赶跑，驴群慢慢走了过去，踩出一条清清楚楚的路。了账说，寺里的老僧人讲过，早年往来千佛洞的僧人就是跟着野驴走的，驴知道哪里有草、哪里有水。「千里号要是往北，走的也是这条路。」驴群尽头，北边的天上有一点暗红色，像是崖壁。

column2: Sandstone Buddha Niche
column3: 砂佛龛

column2: A small stone niche is cut into the back of a dune, and in it lives an old monk who carves one thumb-sized Buddha a day; after decades, the walls are lined with them. Bandit footmen are holding him and demanding a life-size statue of their chief, more imposing than a Buddha. The old monk grips his chisel and will only carve little ones. 'I can't do big ones. My heart's too small.'
column3: 沙丘背面凿着一个小石龛，龛里住着一个老和尚，每天刻一尊拇指大的小佛，刻了几十年，龛壁上排满了小佛。一伙马贼步卒把他扣下，逼他给他们的头目刻一尊等身像，要刻得比佛还威风。老和尚握着刻刀，只肯刻小佛：「大的我刻不来，心太小。」

column2: The bandits chased off, the old monk points to an empty stretch of the niche wall. Ten years ago three hundred little Buddhas stood there. A caravan came through and each person took one, for safe travel: 'On the road to the Thousand Buddha Caves it's easier going with a Buddha along.' Liaozhang says: 'Master, when they come back, the Buddhas will come back too.' The old monk picks up his chisel again.
column3: 马贼被赶跑，老和尚指着龛壁上一块空出来的地方给你们看：十年前这里摆着三百尊小佛，一支商队路过，每人请走一尊，说是保平安，「去千佛洞的路上，带着佛好走」。了账说：「师父，等他们回来，佛也回来。」老和尚又拿起了刻刀。

column2: Pilgrim Tax Post
column3: 佛税卡

column2: A checkpoint blocks the road north, manned by tax men from some little oasis kingdom who've hired bandit riders to guard it, and they levy a 'Buddha tax': one coin a head for anyone bound for the Thousand Buddha Caves, double for monks, since 'monks are closer to the Buddha and get more out of it'. Liaozhang, stopped at the barrier, is arguing with them: 'Where would a monk get money?'
column3: 北去的路上设了一道卡子，是沙海里一个小绿洲国的税丁，雇了一伙马贼骑手看卡，专收「佛税」：凡是往千佛洞去的，一人一钱，和尚加倍，因为「和尚离佛近，占的便宜大」。了账被拦在卡外，正跟税丁吵：「出家人哪来的钱！」

column2: The tax men flee and leave their register. Turning back to the year ten years ago, you find one large entry that autumn: 'Camel train of three hundred, bound for the Thousand Buddha Caves. Buddha tax, three hundred coins, paid in full by the bookkeeper, plus one coin extra, "paid in advance for whoever comes after".' For ten years the tax men have kept that coin on the books, and no one has come to claim it.
column3: 税丁们跑了，丢下一本税簿。你们翻到十年前那一年，秋天有一笔大的：「驼队三百人，往千佛洞，佛税三百钱，账房一次缴清，另付一钱，言『替后面的人先缴』。」那一钱，税丁记了十年也没人来用。

column2: Jade Diggers' Hollow
column3: 采玉坳

column2: A hollow in the southern mountains yields jade as white as mutton fat. Bandit footmen have rounded up the local jade diggers and keep them down the pits day and night. Their foreman is a one-armed old man who can prise a whole block of jade from the rock one-handed. When he sees you he says just one thing: 'After the fight, I've something to tell you.'
column3: 南山的一道山坳里出玉，石缝里的玉白得像羊脂。一伙马贼步卒抓了附近的采玉人，逼他们日夜下坑。采玉人的头儿是个独臂老人，一只手也能把整块玉从石头里撬出来。他见了你们，只说了一句：「打完了，有话跟你们说。」

column2: The bandits driven out of the hollow, the one-armed old man tells you that ten years ago the Qianli people bought a cartload of jade from him to pay the Bandit King's road toll. Later the whole load came back untouched, driven by the King's men, with a message: 'The King doesn't want jade. Only names.' 'A bandit who'd rather have names than jade,' says the old man. 'When you see him, ask him why for me.'
column3: 马贼被赶出山坳，独臂老人说：十年前，千里号的人从他这儿买了一车玉，说要拿去付马贼王的路钱。后来那车玉原封不动地退了回来，赶车的是王的人，捎了句话：「王不要玉，只要名字。」老人说：「一个马贼，不要玉要名字，你们见了他，替我问问为什么。」

column2: Bee Mother Hollow
column3: 蜂娘坳

column2: In a hollow at the foot of the southern mountains lies a field of alfalfa with dozens of beehives at its edge, kept by a white-haired old woman. Bandit archers came to steal honey, got stung all over their faces, and are now shooting at the hives, several already knocked over. The old woman stands motionless among the swarm; the bees circle her and not one stings.
column3: 南山脚下的坳里有一片苜蓿地，地头摆着几十只蜂箱，养蜂的是个白头发的老婆婆。一伙马贼射手跑来偷蜜，被蜂蛰得满脸包，干脆放箭射蜂箱，射翻了好几只。老婆婆站在蜂群里一动不动，蜂子绕着她飞，一只也不蛰她。

column2: The archers flee clutching their faces and the old woman rights her hives one by one. Her son, she says, is the Bandit King. Every autumn he comes home once and takes a jar of honey, to send along with the lamp oil for the monks in the north. 'The year he was seventeen he came back from White Dragon Mound with an arrow in his leg, and he hasn't smiled since.' She cuts you a piece of honeycomb. 'When you see him, tell him to come home for a meal.'
column3: 射手们捂着脸跑了，老婆婆把蜂箱一只只扶起来。她说她儿子是马贼王，每年秋天回来一趟，带走一罐蜜，说是给北边的和尚送灯油时捎上。「他十七岁从白龙堆回来，腿上带着箭，再没笑过。」她给你们切了一块蜂巢：「见了他，让他回来吃顿饭。」

column2: Melon and Iron Market
column3: 瓜铁市

column2: Outside the east mouth of White Dragon Mound, melon fields line the lake, and every year the farmers haul their melons and grain to the lakeside fair to trade with smiths come down from the southern mountains for ironware. This is the Melon and Iron Market. But this year bandit riders have closed it, claiming the best melons must first be picked for the King. A month later they're still picking, and the melons are rotting in the fields. The smiths wait at the gate with hoes and sickles on their backs, cursing.
column3: 白龙堆东口外的湖边有一片瓜田，瓜农们每年把瓜和粮食拉到湖边的集上，跟南山下来的铁匠换铁器，这就是瓜铁市。可今年一伙马贼骑手把集市封了，说要先给王挑最好的瓜，挑了一个月还没挑完，瓜都烂在地里了。铁匠们背着锄头、镰刀在集口干等，等得直骂娘。

column2: With the riders driven off the market reopens: grain and melons come in by the cartload and go out as hoes, ploughshares and iron pots. The King never knew his riders had closed the fair, an old farmer at the gate tells you. The King made only one market rule: 'Anyone who comes under the Qian banner gets melons free.' 'Ten years,' says the old farmer, 'and nobody under a Qian banner has come to eat one. This year you're the first.' He hugs over the biggest melon he has and tells you the King's camp lies north of the lake.
column3: 骑手们被赶走，瓜铁市重新开了张：粮食和瓜一车车拉进来，换走铁匠的锄头、犁铧和铁锅。集口的老瓜农告诉你们，王的骑手私自封集，王根本不知道，王只立过一条集规：「打千字旗来的，瓜白给。」「十年了，」老瓜农说，「没有一个打千字旗的来吃过瓜。今年，你们算头一个。」他抱来一个最大的瓜，说王营就在湖北边。

column2: Lamp-Oil Debtors' Hold
column3: 欠油寨

column2: A bandit hold on the plain belongs to the biggest debtor in Liaozhang's ledger: three years ago its chief borrowed a hundred pounds of lamp oil from the Caves, saying burning it would make him rich, and hasn't paid back a drop. When Liaozhang came to collect, the chief's riders threw him out of the gate and posted a sign: 'No monks or dogs.' The dogs got in anyway.
column3: 荒原上一座马贼寨，寨主是了账债簿上欠得最多的一个：三年前从千佛洞借了一百斤灯油，说点了能发财，至今一滴没还。了账上门讨债，寨主的骑手把他扔出了寨门，还在门口贴了一张告示：「和尚与狗不得入内。」狗倒是进去了。

column2: The chief, well beaten, leads out ten horses to clear his debt, grumbling all the while: 'What are you dunning me for? The King sends oil north every year. The oil he's paid back for the Qianli caravan is ten times what I owe.' Liaozhang starts and flips through his ledger. Sure enough, the Qianli page shows payments on someone else's behalf, one every autumn, signed with a lopsided character: 'King'.
column3: 寨主被打服了，牵出十匹马抵债。他还嘟囔：「讨什么讨，王每年都往北边送油，替千里号还的油比我欠的多十倍。」了账一愣，赶紧翻债簿，千里号那一页后面果然有一行别人代缴的记录，每年秋天一笔，署名是一个歪歪扭扭的「王」字。

column2: Ledger-Burning Slope
column3: 焚账坡

column2: On the slope stands a great pile of firewood, and Whirlwind Sect believers holding several monks prisoner mean to burn every ledger of the Thousand Buddha Caves. Their slogan is 'No debts in heaven': burn the books, and every debtor can be carried off by the wind. Their footmen circle the pyre in a spinning dance, torches already lit. Liaozhang is hopping mad. 'Your own debts are in there!'
column3: 坡上堆着一大堆柴，旋风教的信徒们押着几个和尚，要把千佛洞的债簿全烧了。他们的口号是「升天无债」：烧了账，欠债的人就都能被风接走了。信徒的步卒围成一圈，跳着转圈舞，火把已经点着了。了账急得直跳：「那里面也有你们的账！」

column2: The believers scattered, not one ledger caught fire. Liaozhang hugs them and chants for a long while, then turns to the Qianli page: half of the three hundred pounds of lamp oil has been repaid already, and the 'King' entries beside it have grown by another line. 'This Bandit King,' he says, 'is more reliable than half our monastery's patrons.'
column3: 信徒们被打散，债簿一本没烧着。了账抱着债簿念了半天经，翻到千里号那一页，发现灯油三百斤已经还上了一半，旁边那个「王」字的代缴记录又多了一行。「这个马贼王，」他说，「比我们寺里大半的施主都守信用。」

column2: Lamp-Keeping Platform
column3: 续灯台

column2: On top of a dune stands a stone platform set with dozens of oil lamps left one by one by monks and pilgrims. Each who leaves a lamp tops up the oil, and those who come after top it up again; they have never gone out. Archers of the Whirlwind Sect have taken the platform, declaring that the flames block the wind's path, and are blowing the lamps out one by one, shooting over any that won't go out.
column3: 沙丘顶上一座石台，台上摆着几十盏油灯，是往来的僧人和香客一盏一盏留下的，留灯的人添一回油，后来的人再添一回，从来没熄过。一伙旋风教的射手占了石台，说灯火挡了风的路，把灯一盏盏吹灭，吹不灭的就射翻。

column2: The archers driven off, Liaozhang relights the lamps one by one. The lamp at the very end has a stand carved with Qian, and its oil is full: someone has kept topping it up. The old monks at the Caves say, Liaozhang tells you, that there's a lamp just like it inside the Thousand Buddha Caves that hasn't gone out in ten years. 'Whoever fills it comes once every autumn.'
column3: 射手们被赶跑，了账一盏盏把灯重新点上。最边上一盏灯的灯座刻着「千」字，灯油是满的，有人一直在添。了账说，寺里的老僧讲，千佛洞里也有一盏这样的灯，十年没熄，「添油的人，每年秋天来一回」。

column2: Scorpion Quicksand
column3: 沙蝎流沙

column2: At the foot of the mountains lies a stretch of quicksand, flat to look at; step on it and you sink. Beneath it nest sand scorpions, the big ones as long as your hand, generation after generation, crawling out at night to the terror even of bandits. Now a band of bandits, foot, bow and horse, uses the quicksand as a natural moat and camps on its edge, running for it whenever anyone gives chase.
column3: 山脚下有一片流沙，看着平平的，一脚下去就往下陷。流沙底下是沙蝎的巢，蝎子大的有巴掌长，一窝接一窝地生，夜里爬出来，连马贼都怕。如今一伙马贼把这片流沙当了天险，在边上扎营，步、射、骑都有，谁追他们，他们就往流沙边上跑。

column2: The scorpions and bandits are cleared out for now. At the edge of the quicksand an iron chest has surfaced, belonging to that merchant house from inside the pass. In it is an undelivered letter: 'The King takes no bribes. He only asks whether one is of the Qianli caravan, and if not, will not receive them.' Shen Du reads it. 'It isn't money he's waiting for.' But the scorpions under the sand will keep breeding, nest after nest, and before long this place will need clearing again.
column3: 这一窝蝎子和马贼都清干净了。流沙边上露出一只铁箱，是关内那家商号的，里面有一封没送出去的信：「王不收贿，只问是不是千里号的人，不是就不见。」沈渡看了信说：「他等的不是钱。」可流沙底下的蝎子还会一窝窝生出来，过一阵，这里又得来清一回。

column2: Wrong-Map Dunes
column3: 错图沙

column2: An old mapmaker has been seized by Whirlwind Sect riders who want him to draw 'the road to heaven'. He has spent his life mapping the Sand Sea, but the dunes walk, so his maps have never once been right; every one is wrong, and famously so. The riders followed his map for three days and ended up back where they started, and are now whipping him.
column3: 一个画地图的老先生被旋风教的骑手抓了，逼他画出「升天之路」。老先生画了一辈子沙海的地图，可沙丘会走，他的图从来没对过，画一张错一张，错得远近闻名。骑手们拿着他的图走了三天，又回到了原地，正拿鞭子抽他。

column2: The riders chased off, the old man explains why his maps are always wrong: dunes walk. A crescent dune creeps downwind, its two horns always pointing the way the wind goes, the gentle slope facing the wind and the steep one turned away. So in the end he learned to draw only what doesn't move. He digs out the one map he ever got right, from ten years ago: a dotted line out of the north mouth of White Dragon Mound, running northeast, labelled 'Thousand Buddha Caves'.
column3: 骑手们被赶跑，老先生说他的图错，是因为沙丘会走：月牙形的沙丘顺着风挪，两只角总指着下风，迎风那面坡缓，背风那面坡陡。后来他只画不会走的东西。他翻出十年前唯一画对的一张：一条虚线从白龙堆北口出来，一路往东北，旁边注着「千佛洞」。

column2: Repainted Banner Camp
column3: 改旗营

column2: North of the lake stands the Bandit King's guard camp, foot, bow and horse in neat ranks, his great banner over the gate: white on black, the single character 'King'. But when the wind blows, the shadow of another character shows through from the back, with far more strokes than 'King'. The moment the guards see your colours, they beat their drums.
column3: 湖北边扎着马贼王的亲兵大营，步、射、骑三路排得整整齐齐，营门口飘着王的大旗。大旗是黑底白字，写着一个「王」字，可风一吹，旗子背面透出另一个字的影子，笔画比「王」字多得多。亲兵们见了你们的旗号，立刻敲起了鼓。

column2: The guards fall back and you turn the banner over. It originally read 'Qian'; someone later added strokes to make it 'King'. When the King started out he had no banner, the guard captain explains, so he borrowed the Qianli caravan's character. 'The King says when Qianli comes back, he'll give them back their banner and go back to plain banditry.'
column3: 亲兵们退了，你们把大旗翻过来看：旗子原本写的是「千」，后来有人在上面添了几笔，改成了「王」。亲兵头目说，王起家时没有旗，就借了千里号的字，「王说，等千里号回来，旗还给他们，他再做马贼」。

column2: Footprint Flats
column3: 留印滩

column2: By the lake lies a stretch of hardpan where nothing is usually seen, but on every full moon the night wind blows the loose sand off and a great field of footprints appears, deep and shallow, leading north. By the next day the wind has buried them again. Bandit archers have made it a holy place, kowtowing on its edge every full-moon night and allowing no one to set foot on it.
column3: 湖边一片硬滩，平时什么也看不见，每逢月圆，夜风把浮沙一刮，滩上就露出一大片脚印，深深浅浅，一直通向北边，第二天风一吹又埋上了。一伙马贼射手把这儿当了圣地，月圆夜守在滩边磕头，不许任何人踩一脚。

column2: The archers beaten back, it happens to be a full moon that night, and you watch the footprints surface from the sand one by one: men's, camels', cartwheels', and the hoofprints of a wooden ox. In front of them all runs a line of small bare footprints, which every few steps turn back to look, then go on, then turn back again. On every full moon, the archers say, the King comes here and sits alone until dawn.
column3: 射手们被打退，那夜正好月圆，你们看着脚印一个个从沙里露出来：大人的、骆驼的、车轮的，还有一辆木牛车的蹄印。最前面是一行光脚的小脚印，走几步就回头，走几步又回头。射手说，王每逢月圆都来这里，一个人坐到天亮。

column2: Before the King's Tent
column3: 王帐前

column2: From the dune crest you can finally see the King's camp: a great tent, a sand terrace before it, and on the terrace a chair gleaming white. The King's footmen hold the last sand ridge before the tent, rank on rank with long spears, little bells hung from the points. They don't shoot at you. They only stamp their spear butts into the sand all at once, and the bells ring out: the rule of the King's camp is that visitors must pass this line first.
column3: 沙丘顶上远远能望见王营了：一座大帐，帐前一座沙台，台上一把白得发亮的椅子。离王帐最近的一道沙梁上守着王的步卒，一排排扛着长矛，矛尖上挂着小铃。见了你们，他们没有放箭，只是一齐把矛顿在沙里，铃声响成一片：这是王营的规矩，来客要先过这一关。

column2: The footmen give way and their leader salutes with joined fists. 'The King says whoever passes this ridge may come to the foot of the terrace.' He points to the chair. 'That's the bone chair. Three hundred bones, not one missing. The King has sat on it every day for ten years.' Before the tent a drum rolls three times, as if in welcome.
column3: 步卒们让开了路，领头的抱拳：「王说，能过这道梁的，可以去台下。」他指着那把椅子，「那就是骨椅，三百根骨头，一根不少。王每天坐在上面，坐了十年。」帐前的鼓擂了三通，像在请人。

column2: North-Gazing Terrace
column3: 望北台

column2: A mud terrace stands on the northern plain, and every autumn people come here to burn incense facing north: families of the Qianli caravan's three hundred, who walk all the way from inside the pass and, when the incense is burnt, all the way home again. A dozen came this year, and they'd barely set out their candles when bandit footmen charged in to take their travel money: 'Money for the dead is better spent on the living.'
column3: 荒原北边一座土台，每年秋天都有人来这里朝北烧香：都是千里号三百人的家眷，从关内一路走过来，烧完香再一路走回去。今年来了十几个，刚摆上香烛，一伙马贼步卒就冲上来抢他们的盘缠，说「烧给死人的钱，不如给活人」。

column2: The bandits chased off, the incense is lit again. An old woman brings out a letter, the last her husband ever sent home, entrusted to someone from this very spot ten years ago: 'We're through the Sand Sea and heading for the Thousand Buddha Caves. The bookkeeper says once the books are checked there, we can go home.' 'Ten years,' she says. 'Are they still not done checking?' Liaozhang chants a sutra for her, and has no answer.
column3: 马贼被赶跑，香重新点上。一个老妇人拿出一封信，是她丈夫十年前从这儿托人捎回去的最后一封：「过了沙海，要去千佛洞了，账房说到那儿把账一对，就能回家。」她说：「十年了，账还没对完吗？」了账给她念了一段经，没有回答。

column2: Quarrel-of-Names Slope
column3: 争名坡

column2: The prophet has a band of zealous archers who refuse to accept his confession. The three hundred did ascend, they insist, and the names carved on the Bandit King's bone chair have nailed their souls to the earth. They mean to go and smash his chair, and are sharpening arrows on the slope, from which the banners of the King's camp can already be seen.
column3: 旋风教的先知手下有一伙激进的射手，不肯认先知的话，说三百人就是升了天，而马贼王的骨椅上刻着他们的名字，是把升天的魂钉在了地上。他们要去砸王的椅子，正在坡上磨箭，坡下已经能望见王营的旗子。

column2: The archers scattered, Liaozhang picks up one of their arrows. 'Names carved on bone don't nail down souls. They pledge a debt.'
