He opens his ledger: for ten years the King has repaid the Qianli caravan's lamp oil, every payment on time. 'Only people who owe keep hold of names. And only people who mean to pay pledge them.'
column3: 射手们被打散，了账捡起他们的一支箭，说：「名字刻在骨头上，不是钉魂，是押账。」他翻开债簿给你们看：王替千里号还了十年的灯油，每一笔都按时，「欠债的人才会记着名字，要还的人，才会押上名字」。

column2: Hired Blade Plain
column3: 雇刀原

column2: A large force crosses the plain toward the King's camp, foot, bow and horse, flying the Whirlwind Sect's banner but dressed in identical grey. Their leader counts silver in the saddle, tucks it into his coat and shouts to his men: 'Smash the bone chair and there's another five hundred!' Liaozhang recognises that grey: there's another party in the Sand Sea that doesn't want the Qianli accounts settled.
column3: 荒原上一支大队人马朝王营开去，步、射、骑都有，打的是旋风教的旗，穿的却是统一的灰衣。领头的骑在马上数银子，数完了往怀里一揣，对手下喊：「砸了骨椅，再拿五百两！」了账认出了那身灰衣：沙海里还有一家，也不想让千里号的账被人算清。

column2: The men in grey are scattered, and on their leader you find a letter from that great merchant house inside the pass: 'Once the names on the bone chair are destroyed, the Qianli caravan's account has no owner, and the western trade is ours.' Liaozhang files the letter in his ledger. 'This one goes on their account.'
column3: 灰衣人被打散，你们在领头的身上搜出一封信，是关内那家大商号写的：「骨椅上的名字一毁，千里号就成了无主之账，西路买卖归我号。」了账把信收进债簿：「这一笔，记在他们账上。」

column2: Old Camel Pasture
column3: 老驼苑

column2: A fenced pasture by the lake, the grass richer than anywhere else, is guarded by the Bandit King's finest troops, foot, bow and horse, more closely than his own tent. Bandits outside say the King's treasure is kept in there, though none has seen it. Every now and then a long cry comes from inside, like a camel, but older.
column3: 湖边一片围起来的草场，草长得比别处都好，是马贼王最精锐的一支人马在守，步、射、骑三路，守得比王帐还严。外头的马贼都说里面关着王的宝贝，谁也没见过。草场里不时传出一声长长的叫唤，像骆驼，又比骆驼的嗓门老。

column2: The veteran guards at last give way and you walk into the pasture. Thirty-seven old camels lie in the grass, their coats gone white, so fat they can barely stand, each branded Qian on the rump. These are the camels that survived the Qianli caravan's sandstorm, the old guards explain, left with the King when the caravan went north, and he has had them cared for these ten years. 'The King says when their owners come back, the camels have to remember the way.'
column3: 守苑的老兵终于退开，草场里卧着三十七峰老骆驼，毛都白了，胖得站不起来，屁股上烙着「千」字。老兵说，这是千里号那场沙暴里活下来的骆驼，商队往北走时留给了王，王让他们养了十年，「王说，主人回来，骆驼得认得路」。

column2: Sand's End Inn
column3: 沙尾店

column2: The last inn at the east mouth of White Dragon Mound; beyond it begins the Bandit King's own ground. The landlady makes a fine mutton broth, but for days a band of bandit archers claiming to be the King's guard has eaten and drunk here for free, shooting into the sky when drunk until the inn sign is riddled like a sieve. The landlady stands by the stove with her ladle and refuses to serve them another drop.
column3: 白龙堆东口的最后一家客店，过了这家，就是马贼王的地界。店里的老板娘做得一手好羊肉汤，可这几天一伙马贼射手占了店，说是王的亲兵，在店里白吃白喝，喝醉了就往天上放箭，把店招射成了筛子。老板娘拎着汤勺站在灶边，一勺汤也不肯再盛给他们。

column2: The archers chased off, it turns out they were impostors cadging meals in the King's name. The landlady relights her stove. Ten years ago, she tells you, the Qianli caravan ate its last hot meal in the Sand Sea here: three hundred bowls of broth. The bookkeeper couldn't pay and she told him to forget it, but he insisted on writing it in her book: 'Owed: three hundred bowls of broth, to be repaid on the way home.'
column3: 射手们被赶跑了，后来才知道是冒充王的亲兵来混饭吃的。老板娘重新开了灶。她说十年前千里号在这儿吃过沙海里最后一顿热饭，三百碗汤，账房付不出钱，她说不要了，账房硬是在她的账本上记了一笔：「欠汤三百碗，回程还。」

column2: From the inn you seize the bandits' stores: two sides of wind-dried mutton, a vat of pickled desert chives, a sack of white flour, and the fake guard's tally they used to pose as the King's men, with the character 'King' carved backwards.
column3: 店里抄出马贼的存货：两扇风干的羊肉、一缸腌沙葱、一袋白面，还有他们冒充亲兵用的一块假腰牌，牌上的「王」字刻反了。

column2: Whenever you pass, the landlady brings you each a bowl of hot broth with an extra egg at the bottom, and as you leave she stuffs your saddlebags with flatbread and a jar of broth stock. 'Just add water on the road.' Not a word goes in her book.
column3: 每次路过，老板娘都给你们端上一碗热汤，汤底多卧一个蛋；走的时候往鞍袋里塞一包烙饼和一罐汤底，说「路上兑水就能喝」，账本上一个字也不记。

column2: Herald's Plain
column3: 传令原

column2: On an open stretch of grassland the Bandit King's herald, on a white horse, blocks your way with a troop of riders. He unrolls a sheet of paper and reads aloud: 'By the King's command: the one who keeps accounts, the one who wants to leave, the one from the sea, the one collecting debts, and those who come under the Qian banner, all of you, come before the bone chair.' He rolls it up again. 'But the King says you have to beat us first.'
column3: 一片开阔的草原上，马贼王的传令官骑着一匹白马，带着一队骑手拦住了你们。传令官展开一张纸，大声念：「王令：会算账的、要走的、海上来的、讨债的，还有打千字旗来的，都到骨椅前来。」念完，他把纸一收：「不过王说了，先得赢了我们。」

column2: The riders beaten back, the herald hands you the paper with good grace. On the back the King has written a few words himself, in a lopsided hand: four names, A Suan, Old Han, Shen Du, Liaozhang, and after them one empty space. 'That last space,' says the herald, 'the King left for whoever comes under the Qian banner. The King hears everything. Everyone you met on the way, he knows about.'
column3: 骑手们被打退，传令官倒也痛快，把那张纸交给了你们。纸背面是王自己写的几个字，歪歪扭扭：阿算、老韩、沈渡、了账，四个名字，后面又空着一格。传令官说：「最后那一格，王说留给打千字旗的。王的消息灵，这一路你们碰见了谁，他都知道。」

column2: Vanguard Dunes
column3: 前锋沙

column2: On the last sand ridge before the bone-chair terrace, the Bandit King's vanguard is drawn up in a great formation, foot, bow and horse, the best fighters he has. Their leader, a one-eyed giant, shoulders a white banner with no character on it. He grins when he sees you. 'King's rule: before you see him, you see us.'
column3: 骨椅台前最后一道沙梁上，马贼王的前锋排成了一个大阵，步、射、骑三路俱全，全是王手下最能打的。领头的是个独眼大汉，扛着一面没有字的白旗。他见了你们，咧嘴一笑：「王的规矩，见他之前，先见我们。」

column2: The vanguard broken, the one-eyed giant plants his white banner in the sand. The King had it made ready for the Qianli caravan, he says, to fly when they return. 'Every night the King sits on the bone chair facing northeast. All night. Ten years we've followed him, and we've never seen him sit facing any other way.'
column3: 前锋被冲开，独眼大汉把白旗插在沙里，说这面旗是王给千里号预备的，等他们回来时挂。「王每天夜里坐在骨椅上，脸朝东北，」他说，「一坐就是一夜。我们跟了他十年，从没见他朝别的方向坐过。」

column2: Alms Farmstead
column3: 化缘庄

column2: A small farmstead on the plain serves as a resting place for monks of the Thousand Buddha Caves crossing the Sand Sea: one stove, a few monks' cells, a yard of vegetables. Whirlwind Sect footmen have taken it over and turned the cells into an 'Ascension Hall', where they make travellers spin in circles; whoever falls down dizzy is declared 'taken by the wind', and his baggage confiscated.
column3: 荒原上一座小庄子，是千佛洞的僧人往来沙海时歇脚的地方，庄里有一口灶、几间僧房、一院子菜。一伙旋风教的步卒占了庄子，把僧房改成了「升天堂」，逼过路人在堂里转圈，转晕了倒下的，就说是「被风接走了」，把行李充公。

column2: The believers chased off, the cells become cells again. The old monk who keeps the farmstead says that Liaozhang's own teacher, the very monk who lent the Qianli caravan its lamp oil, is still at the Thousand Buddha Caves. 'Every autumn he asks: has anyone come from the Sand Sea yet?'
column3: 信徒们被赶跑，僧房又成了僧房。管庄子的老僧说，了账师父的师父，就是当年给千里号借灯油的那位，如今还在千佛洞里，「他每年秋天都要问一句：沙海那边，有人来了没有？」

column2: From the farmstead you seize what the believers had hoarded: a chest of stolen incense, forty pairs of straw sandals, two bags of red dates, and a stack of their own 'Ascension Sutra' with more misprints than characters. Liaozhang shakes his head as he reads.
column3: 庄里抄出信徒们攒的东西：一箱抢来的香、四十双草鞋、两袋红枣、一摞他们自己写的《升天经》，经文里错字比字还多，了账看了直摇头。

column2: Whenever you pass, the old monk steams you a basket of vegetable buns, fills your lamps with oil, and presses into each hand a safe-travel charm copied out by himself. 'The wind's strong in the Sand Sea. Keep it against your chest.'
column3: 每次路过，老僧都会给你们蒸一笼素包子，灌满灯油，再往每个人手里塞一张亲手抄的平安符，说「沙海里风大，符要贴在胸口」。

column2: Messenger's Dunes
column3: 送信沙

column2: A boy novice comes walking from the north with an oilcloth bundle on his back: a letter to Liaozhang from the old abbot of the Thousand Buddha Caves. Whirlwind Sect footmen stop him among the dunes, calling the Caves' monks frauds, and want to tear the letter up. The boy curls up around his bundle, murmuring, 'Master says a letter matters more than a life.'
column3: 一个小沙弥从北边走来，背着一只油布包，是千佛洞的老方丈给了账的信。一伙旋风教的步卒在沙丘间拦住了他，说千佛洞的和尚都是骗子，要把信撕了。小沙弥抱着包缩成一团，嘴里念着：「师父说，信比命要紧。」

column2: The believers chased off, Liaozhang opens the letter, reads it a long while, then reads it aloud: 'The Qianli caravan's lamp is still lit. There is a ledger in the Caves, waiting for whoever comes next to check it.' He folds it away and looks north. 'It seems our monastery owes the Qianli caravan more than the Qianli caravan owes us.'
column3: 信徒们被打跑，了账拆开信，看了半天，念给你们听：「千里号的灯，还点着。洞里有一本账，等后来的人对。」了账把信叠好，望着北边：「看来，我们寺里欠千里号的，比千里号欠我们的多。」

column2: Night Drum Dunes
column3: 夜鼓沙

column2: As soon as night falls, drums sound from the top of the dunes: boom, boom, boom, three beats at a time, all night long. A band of bandit riders keeps three great drums and charges down on anyone who comes near. Traders nearby complain they can't sleep, though some say that anyone lost in White Dragon Mound can follow the sound of these drums out.
column3: 天一黑，沙丘顶上就响起鼓声，咚、咚、咚，隔一阵敲三下，一夜不停。敲鼓的是一伙马贼骑手，守着三面大鼓，谁靠近就冲下来赶。附近的商客被吵得睡不着，可也有人说，在白龙堆里迷了路的，听着这鼓声，就能走出来。

column2: The riders scattered, the drums still mustn't stop, and their leader begs you to beat them for him till morning. It's the King's order, he says, unbroken for ten years: three rolls every night, to guide anyone who can't find the way out of White Dragon Mound. 'The King says if Qianli comes back from the north, they'll find their way home even in the dark.' You beat the drums until dawn.
column3: 骑手们被打散，鼓却不能停，他们的头目求你们替他敲完这一夜。他说这是王的命令，十年没断过：每夜三通鼓，给白龙堆里走不出来的人引路，「王说，千里号要是从北边回来，夜里也能找着家门」。你们替他敲到了天亮。

column2: The IOU Casket
column3: 欠条匣

column2: By the lake a cave opens in the sandstone, its mouth held by the Bandit King's personal guard, foot, bow and horse, every man carrying scars ten years old. Inside there is only an iron casket with a single lock, the key hanging on the King's neck. The casket holds, the guards say, the most valuable thing the King owns, worth more than all the silver in his vault.
column3: 湖边一座沙岩洞，洞口守着马贼王的贴身卫士，步、射、骑三路，个个身上带着十年前的伤疤。洞里只放着一只铁匣，铁匣上一把锁，钥匙挂在王的脖子上。卫士们说，匣子里是王这辈子最值钱的东西，比他库里的所有银子都值钱。

column2: The guards fall back. You leave the casket unforced, but through a gap under the lid you can see a yellowed sheet, in the bookkeeper's hand: 'Hereby hired: one Sand Sea guide and six guards, to lead the Qianli caravan's three hundred out of White Dragon Mound. Road toll, three hundred taels, payable on the way home. Pledged against the names of the three hundred.' Below are three hundred red thumbprints, and last of all a lopsided 'King', like a child's writing.
column3: 卫士们退了，你们没撬铁匣，从匣缝里看见一张发黄的纸，纸上的字是账房的：「今雇沙海向导一人、护卫六人，领千里号三百人出白龙堆。路钱三百两，回程付。以三百人之名为押。」落款处按着三百个红手印，最后是一个歪歪扭扭的「王」字，像个孩子写的。

column2: Seven Graves Plain
column3: 七冢原

column2: On the grassland outside the east mouth of White Dragon Mound lie six graves in a row; the seventh place is empty, the pit dug but never filled. They are guarded by the oldest company the Bandit King has, foot, bow and horse, every man white-haired, who let no one approach, not even the King's own guard. 'The King's brothers lie here,' says their leader. 'The empty one is the King's own.'
column3: 白龙堆东口外的草原上有六座坟，排成一排，第七个位置空着，挖好了坑，没有填。守坟的是马贼王手下最老的一支人马，步、射、骑都有，个个白了头。他们不许任何人靠近坟地，连王的亲兵也不许。为首的老兵说：「这里埋的是王的兄弟。空着的那个，是王自己的。」

column2: The old guards sheathe their blades and tell you about that day. Ten years ago the King led the Qianli caravan to the east mouth of White Dragon Mound, and the gangs of the northern Sand Sea, hearing of an unguarded caravan, came together to rob it. The King's six brothers held the gap and not one fell back. The caravan got through, and all six fell here. 'The King says he owes Qianli one life, and Qianli owes him six. That account takes a long time to settle.'
column3: 守坟的老兵们收了刀，给你们讲了那一天：十年前王领着千里号走到白龙堆东口，沙海北边的几路马贼听说有一支没护卫的商队，一齐来抢。王的六个兄弟守在口子上，一个也没退，商队出去了，六个人都倒在了这里。「王说他欠千里号一条命，千里号欠他六条，账得慢慢算。」

column2: Oil-Repaid Road
column3: 还油道

column2: Liaozhang has decided to go and see the Bandit King, to thank him in person for ten years of lamp oil repaid on the Qianli caravan's behalf, and to ask why he pays someone else's debt. But the King's footmen hold the trail to his camp, with orders to let no monk through: 'The King says monks only come to collect debts, and he owes monks nothing.' Liaozhang stamps his feet. 'I've come to thank him!'
column3: 了账决定去见马贼王，当面谢他十年替千里号还的灯油，顺便问问那一笔为什么要替别人还。可通往王营的山道上守着一伙王的步卒，奉命不许和尚过去：「王说了，和尚来是讨债的，王不欠和尚的。」了账气得直跺脚：「我是来谢他的！」

column2: The guards beaten back, Liaozhang shows their leader the ledger, page after page of payments made by the King. The leader scratches his head. 'So the King's a good debtor.' He stands aside, and adds that lately the King sits on his bone chair every day staring north, 'like he's waiting for someone to come from the north, or someone to come back from it.'
column3: 守路的步卒被打退，了账把债簿翻开给他们的头目看，一笔笔都是王的代缴。头目看完挠头：「原来王是好债户。」他让开了路，又说王最近天天坐在骨椅上往北看，「像是在等北边来人，又像在等北边有人回来」。

column2: Surplus Tribute Shop
column3: 贡余铺

column2: At the edge of the grassland stands a shop kept by the Bandit King's quartermaster, piled with tribute from every gang: felts, hides, bronzeware, medicines, stacked so high the door barely shuts. But the King has ordered that tribute may not be sold, so the quartermaster sits on a houseful of goods and can't make a single sale, and has riders patrol outside every day in case of thieves.
column3: 草原边上一座铺子，掌柜是马贼王的军需官，铺里堆满了各路马贼纳上来的贡：毡子、皮子、铜器、药材，堆得连门都快关不上。可王有令，贡品不许卖，掌柜守着一屋子货，一笔买卖也做不成，只好天天让骑手在铺外巡逻，防着有人来偷。

column2: The riders beaten back, the quartermaster is actually delighted. 'The King said tribute could only be traded with someone who beat us. Ten years, and you're the first.' He throws open the door and starts trading, explaining as he works his abacus that nine parts of the tribute go into the King's vault, and these are just the goods that would spoil. 'The King says better to trade them to Qianli's people than let them rot.'
column3: 骑手们被打退，掌柜反倒高兴了：「王说过，贡品只能跟打赢了我们的人换。十年了，你们是头一个。」他打开铺门跟你们做起了买卖，一边拨算盘一边说，九成的贡王都存进了库，剩下这些是放坏了可惜的，「王说，与其烂了，不如换给千里号的人」。

column2: Dragon's Tail Gate
column3: 龙尾门

column2: At the northeast exit of White Dragon Mound two ridges close into a narrow gate, like a dragon's tail. It is held by the Bandit King's oldest guards, foot, bow and horse, and what they guard is not the outside but the inside: by the King's order, no one may leave through this gate going north. On the earthen wall of the archway are two handprints, one large, one small, pressed in deep.
column3: 白龙堆的东北出口，两道土垄在这里收拢成一道窄门，像龙的尾巴。守在这里的是马贼王最老的亲兵，步、射、骑三路，他们守的不是门外，是门里：王有令，谁也不许从这道门往北出去。门洞的土壁上，有两只手印，一大一小，印得很深。

column2: The old guards fall back and you look closely at the handprints in the archway. Beside the large one is carved 'Bookkeeper'; beside the small one, 'Young Wang'. Below runs a line: 'From here, the Thousand Buddha Caves. Young Wang, your road toll is payable on the way home, not one copper short.' Beyond the gate a beaten road runs off northeast, and at its end red cliffs shimmer on the horizon.
column3: 老亲兵们退了，你们站在门洞里细看那两只手印：大的旁边刻着「账房」，小的旁边刻着「王小哥」，下面一行字：「此去千佛洞。王小哥，路钱回程付，一文不少。」门外，一条被踩实了的路往东北伸过去，路的尽头，红色的崖壁在天边若隐若现。

column2: The Wind Gate
column3: 风门

column2: Between two yardangs runs a narrow gap where the wind pours through moaning. The Whirlwind Sect calls it the Wind Gate: beyond it, they say, lies the Ascension Platform. Believers on foot, white cloths bound round their heads, guard the gap; if outsiders go in, they claim, the wind will stop coming. On the rock walls of the gap are knife marks cut by people ten years ago, stroke after stroke, beyond counting.
column3: 两座雅丹之间夹着一道窄口，风从这里灌过去，呜呜地响，旋风教叫它「风门」，说过了风门就是升天台。一伙信徒步卒把守着窄口，个个头上缠着白布，说外人进去，风就不来了。窄口的石壁上，有十年前的人用刀划下的一道道记号，一道一道，数不清。

column2: The believers pushed aside, Liaozhang counts the knife marks: three hundred. The rock wears a glossy black skin of desert varnish that takes ages to grow, and a blade cuts straight through to the pale stone beneath, so ten-year-old scratches still show white. Beside each mark is a tiny carved Buddha. 'They passed through here carrying their Buddhas,' says Liaozhang. 'Through, not up.'
column3: 信徒们被冲开，了账数石壁上的刀痕，三百道。石壁外面裹着一层黑亮的荒漠漆，要很多年才长得成，刀一划就露出底下浅色的石头，所以十年前的刀痕还是白的。每道刀痕旁都刻着一尊小佛。「他们带着佛从这儿过去的，」了账说，「过去的，不是升上去的。」

column2: Ascension Platform
column3: 升天台

column2: Beyond the Wind Gate rises a platform ringed by yardangs, and on it stands the Whirlwind Sect's great altar. The sect's fiercest believers are gathered here, foot, bow and horse holding the steps, an undying fire burning on top beside a ragged banner, said to have been left by the ascended. The high priest stands by the fire, arms spread wide. 'Ten years ago, the wind took three hundred people from this place. Today it will take you.'
column3: 风门后面是一座雅丹围成的高台，旋风教的总坛就在台上。教中最凶的信徒都聚在这里，步、射、骑三路守住台阶，台顶燃着一堆不灭的火，火边插着一面破旗，说是升天的人留下的。旋风教的大祭司站在火边，张开双臂：「十年前，风从这里接走了三百人。今天，风会接走你们。」

column2: The high priest is knocked off the platform and his followers scatter. Brushing aside the sand behind the fire, you uncover a stone tablet set up by the Thousand Buddha Caves: 'Autumn, Dingwei year. The Qianli camel train, three hundred souls, passed here going north to the Thousand Buddha Caves. The bookkeeper said: the Sand Sea road toll is unpaid, owed to the Bandit King, and will be settled with all other accounts at the Caves.' The ragged banner is only a tent flap the caravan threw away. Liaozhang bows three times before the tablet and closes his ledger. 'I'm going back to the monastery. If you head north, come and find me at the Caves, and we'll check the books together.'
column3: 大祭司被打下了台，信徒们一哄而散。你们拂开火堆后面的沙，露出一块千佛洞立的石碑：「丁未年秋，千里号驼队三百人过此北行，往千佛洞。账房言：沙海路钱未清，欠马贼王，到洞里与诸账一并结算。」碑旁的破旗，不过是驼队丢下的帐帘。了账在碑前拜了三拜，把债簿合上：「我回寺里去。你们要是往北走，到千佛洞来找我，账一起对。」

column2: The Bone Throne
column3: 骨椅台

column2: On the sand terrace stands a chair of camel bone: back, arms and legs all bone, three hundred bones carved with three hundred names, no two cuts alike. The Bandit King sits on it, a man of about forty, left leg stretched stiff before him, face turned northeast. His forces are drawn up three columns wide: riders in front, archers on the wings, foot holding the rear. He looks over what you've brought: an abacus, a copper basin, half a sea chart, a monk's ledger, a camel bone that fell from his own chair. 'Qianli owes me road toll. Three hundred souls, ten years. You've come to pay it for them? Then fight me first, and we'll see if you're fit to.'
column3: 沙台上摆着一把驼骨椅，椅背、扶手、椅腿全是骨头，三百根骨头上刻着三百个名字，刀口各不相同。马贼王坐在上面，四十来岁，左腿伸得笔直，脸朝东北。他的人马三路排开：骑手在前，射手两翼，步卒压阵。他看着你们带来的东西：一架算盘、一只铜盆、半张海图、一本债簿、一根从椅腿上掉下来的驼骨。「千里号欠我路钱，三百人，十年。你们是来替他们还的？那先打一场，看看你们配不配。」

column2: Beaten, the Bandit King pushes himself up on the arms of the bone chair. He was seventeen, he says, leading six brothers to rob an unguarded caravan, when the bookkeeper opened his ledger and offered a deal instead: hire on as guide out of White Dragon Mound, toll payable on the way home, and three hundred names carved on dead camels' bones as pledge. His six brothers died outside the Dragon's Tail Gate, and the caravan went on to the Thousand Buddha Caves. 'A Suan's silver, I never touched a copper. Old Han's men, I kept them for him.' He presses the fallen bone back into the chair leg. 'I'll keep the names. The toll, you go and collect for me at the Caves, and while you're there, ask the bookkeeper whether he's finished that sum.'
column3: 马贼王败了，撑着骨椅站起来。他说那年他十七，带着六个兄弟想劫一支没护卫的商队，账房却翻开账本跟他谈买卖：雇他领路出白龙堆，路钱回程付，三百人在死驼骨上刻名作押。六个兄弟死在龙尾门外，商队往千佛洞去了。「阿算还的银子，我一文没动；老韩的兵，我替他看着。」他把那根掉了的骨头按回椅腿：「名字我守着。路钱，你们去千佛洞替我讨，顺便问问账房，这笔账他算完了没有。」

column2: The Thousand Buddha Caves
column3: 佛窟

column2: Red Cliff Gate
column3: 红崖口

column2: Three days north-east of the Dragon's Tail Gate, a red cliff rises out of the end of the gravel plain, its face riddled with cave mouths like a honeycomb eaten hollow. Below it runs a line of desert poplars, their leaves a shining yellow. A wooden barrier blocks the road, held by swordsmen and crossbowmen in golden masks that flash in the sun. Their leader raps on the bars: 'The Thousand Buddha Caves have been closed for ten years. Pilgrims, merchants, monks: all of you, turn back!'
column3: 出了龙尾门往东北走三天，戈壁尽头忽然立起一道红崖，崖面上密密麻麻全是窟口，像一面被虫蛀空的蜂巢。崖下一溜胡杨，叶子黄得发亮。路口横着一道木栅，一队戴金面具的刀卫和弩手守着，面具在太阳底下晃眼。领头的敲着栅栏喊：「千佛洞闭山十年，香客、商人、和尚，一概回去！」

column2: The Gold Masks fall back into the poplars. Nailed to the barrier is an old board: 'The mountain is closed. By order of the Lord of the Caves, Wuxiang.' Beneath it someone has scrawled in charcoal: 'Liaozhang was here. Couldn't get in. Waiting for you at Temple Gate Slope.' The wind off the cliff smells of incense ash and old paint. Ten years ago the Qianli caravan's three hundred walked in through this very gap.
column3: 金面卫退进了胡杨林。木栅上钉着一块旧木牌：「闭山令。洞主无相。」牌子底下有人用炭写了一行小字：「了账到此，进不去，在山门坡等你们。」风从崖上吹下来，带着香灰和旧颜料的味道。千里号三百人，十年前就是从这道口子走进去的。

column2: Tonsure Slope
column3: 剃度坡

column2: A row of monks stands on the slope at the foot of the hills, new robes, new shaven heads still nicked from the razor. Alms bowls out, they stop everyone: 'Benefactor, leave an offering and the Buddha will see you safely over the slope.' Refuse, and the bowl drops and a cudgel comes out of a sleeve. One of them has a woman's name, Cuihua, tattooed on the back of his head.
column3: 山脚的坡道上站着一排和尚，袈裟是新的，光头也是新的，头皮上还带着刮破的小口子。他们托着钵见人就拦：「施主，留下香火钱，佛祖保佑你平安过坡。」不给的，钵一扔，袖子里就掏出了短棍。其中一个和尚的后脑勺上，刺着「翠花」两个字。

column2: The false monks scatter and leave a litter of ordination papers, all stamped with the seal of the Golden Body Temple, the ink still wet. The pilgrims they'd stopped tell you this lot only shaved their heads this spring. They've taken over the porridge shed in front of the temple, and now the porridge costs money. 'Ten years that shed gave porridge away and never took a coin.'
column3: 假和尚们被打得四散，落了一地度牒，个个盖着「金身寺」的大印，印泥还没干。被拦的香客告诉你们，这伙人今年春天才剃的头，占了千佛洞寺前的粥棚，粥从此要钱了。「那粥棚施了十年粥，从没收过一文。」

column2: The Porridge Stele
column3: 施粥碑

column2: By the road before the temple stands a stele, and false monks are hammering the inscription off it, stone chips flying, while pilgrims watch in silent fury. Half the text is gone already; you can still make out 'Qianli caravan', 'porridge' and 'free of charge'. The abbot's orders, say the chiselers: the porridge belongs to the Golden Body Temple and has nothing to do with any Qianli caravan.
column3: 寺前的路边立着一块石碑，几个假和尚正抡着锤子凿碑上的字，凿得石屑乱飞，围观的香客敢怒不敢言。碑上的字已经凿掉了一半，剩下的还能认出「千里号」「施粥」「不取分文」几个字。凿碑的说，方丈有令：粥是金身寺的粥，跟什么千里号没关系。

column2: The false monks drop their hammers and run. An old pilgrim runs his fingers over the stele and reads out the damaged words: 'Winter of Dingwei. The three hundred of the Qianli caravan leave three hundred measures of grain before this temple, to give porridge to travellers free of charge. When the grain runs out, others will continue.' 'Three hundred measures,' the old man reckons. 'Three years at most. But the porridge has kept coming for ten.' Who kept it coming, the stele doesn't say.
column3: 假和尚扔下锤子跑了，一个老香客拿手指摸着碑，把凿坏的字一个个念全了：「丁未冬，千里号三百人留粮三百石于寺前，施粥过客，不取分文。粮尽，自有人续。」「三百石粮，」老香客算了算，「顶多施三年。可这粥一施就是十年。」续粮的人是谁，碑上没写。

column2: The Face Stall
column3: 卖脸摊

column2: A cloth awning by the road is hung with palm-sized flakes of plaster, each bearing part of a human face: an eye, the bridge of a nose, the paint flecked with tiny points of gold. 'Golden faces of the Qianli caravan!' the stallholder cries. 'Stick one on your door against evil, five coins a piece!' Toughs dressed as monks guard the stall and shove away anyone who asks where the faces came from. An old man buys one, squints at it against the sun, and says he knows that eye.
column3: 路边一顶布棚，挂满了巴掌大的泥皮，每片泥皮上是半张人脸：一只眼、一截鼻梁，颜色里闪着细细的金星。摊主吆喝：「千里号的金脸，贴门上辟邪，一片五钱！」几个假和尚模样的打手守着摊子，谁多问一句来路，就把谁推出去。有个老汉买了一片，对着太阳看了半天，说这只眼睛他认得。

column2: The toughs bolt, the stallholder slips away, and one flake is left behind: half a face with heavy eyebrows, and beside it in ink, 'Cao San, camel driver.' The gold is gold dust mixed into the paint. Ten years ago, the old man says, three hundred merchants were painted in one of the caves. Later someone scraped every face off, and the scrapings ended up on stalls like this.
column3: 打手一跑，摊主也溜了，只落下一片泥皮。上面的脸只剩半边，眉毛很粗，旁边题着一行墨字：「驼户曹三」。金星原来是调在颜料里的金粉。老汉说，十年前千佛洞的窟里画过三百个商人，后来不知被谁把脸全刮了，刮下来的渣子就流到了这种摊上。

column2: Night Grain Gully
column3: 夜粮沟

column2: People here say that every autumn a grain cart appears behind the porridge shed in the middle of the night, loaded with sacks, no driver to be seen, and is gone by dawn. This year the false monks got wind of it and have laid an ambush in the gully behind the shed to seize the grain and sell it at their temple. The moon has just risen, and in the distance a cart wheel creaks.
column3: 附近的人都说，每年秋天，总有一辆粮车半夜出现在粥棚后面，车上满满的粮袋，赶车的却看不见人，天一亮车就没了。今年假和尚们得了信，在粥棚后面的沟里埋伏了一圈，就等着把这车粮截下来，拉回金身寺卖钱。月亮刚上来，远处传来了吱吱呀呀的车轮声。

column2: The false monks driven off, the cart stands at the mouth of the gully, its two old oxen waiting on their own; whoever drove it has already slipped back into the dark. Every sack is stamped in red with a mask that has no features. You unload the grain into the porridge shed. The oxen know the way. Once they're unloaded they haul the empty cart off to the north-east by themselves.
column3: 假和尚们被打跑，粮车停在沟口，两头老牛自己站着，赶车的影子早已退回了黑处。每一只粮袋上都盖着一个红印，印的是一张没有五官的面具。你们把粮卸进了粥棚。老牛认得路，卸完粮，自己拉着空车往东北走了。

column2: The Qianli Porridge Shed
column3: 千里粥棚

column2: A long shed before the temple gate, ten great pots beneath it. Once they steamed every morning before dawn, and pilgrims, camel drivers and beggars queued for porridge. Now fat monks sit at the entrance taking a coin a bowl, and the porridge is thin enough to see your face in. The fire is tended by a half-deaf old cook, bent over the kindling, who answers everyone with 'Eh?'
column3: 寺门前一座长棚，棚下十口大锅，从前每天天不亮就冒白气，过路的香客、驼夫、乞丐排着队喝粥。如今棚口坐着几个胖大和尚收钱，一钱一碗，粥稀得照得见人影。烧火的是个半聋的老火头，弓着背添柴，谁跟他说话，他都只会「啊？」

column2: At the end the false monks' leader charges with his staff raised, and the old cook, without turning round, cracks him on the forehead with a ladle backhand. Down he goes. Only now do the pilgrims learn the old man was a fighting monk in his youth: 'Bad ears, good hands.' The ten pots steam thick and white again, and the old board, 'Qianli Porridge, Free', goes back up on the post.
column3: 打到最后，假和尚的头目举棍冲上来，那老火头头也不回，反手一勺子敲在他脑门上，头目就躺下了。香客们这才知道，老火头年轻时是寺里的武僧，「耳朵不好，手可好」。十口大锅又冒起了稠稠的白气，那块「千里粥·不要钱」的旧木牌重新挂上了棚柱。

column2: The false monks' store gives up two sacks of white rice (for themselves), forty jars of pickled radish, a chest of collected coppers, a bundle of ordination papers, and a box of false topknots. They'd clearly planned to rejoin the world once they'd made their pile.
column3: 假和尚的库里抄出两袋白米（他们自己吃的）、四十坛腌萝卜、一箱收来的铜钱、一捆度牒，还有一箱假发髻：看来早就打算好了，捞够了就还俗。

column2: Every time you pass, the old cook ladles each of you a bowl of thick porridge with a piece of pickled radish on top and wraps up a big bundle of crispy rice crust for the road, still saying the same thing: 'Eh? It's free!'
column3: 每次路过，老火头都给你们每人盛一碗稠粥，粥上卧一块腌萝卜，再包一大包锅巴让你们路上嚼，嘴里还是那句：「啊？不要钱！」

column2: The Tracing School
column3: 描红塾

column2: In a mud-brick schoolhouse at the edge of a village, a dozen children bend over their desks tracing, not characters, but a face: round, laughing eyes, a mole by the mouth. The original is a sheet of yellowed paper whose every line is pricked with pinholes. Deserters have taken over the back yard as a barracks; the children annoy them, and they mean to chop up the desks for firewood. The teacher stands in the doorway with his ruler, his hand shaking.
column3: 村口一间土坯学堂，十几个娃娃趴在桌上描红，描的不是字，是一张人脸：圆脸，笑眼，嘴边一颗痣。原稿是一张发黄的厚纸，线条上扎满了针眼。一伙逃兵占了学堂后院当营房，嫌娃娃吵，要把桌子劈了烧火。先生拿着戒尺挡在门口，手直哆嗦。

column2: With the deserters run out of the village, the teacher shows you the original. The pinholes are for pouncing: tap charcoal dust through them and the line transfers onto a wall. Painters call it a pounce pattern. In the corner: 'Qianli caravan. Old Yang, cook. No. 41.' 'It belonged to Wu the painter, from Half Wall village,' the teacher says. 'Three years of tracing, and the children draw Old Yang better than I do.'
column3: 逃兵被赶出了村，先生把那张原稿捧给你们看：针眼是画匠「拍粉」用的，炭粉拍过针眼，线就印到墙上，这叫粉本。纸角写着「千里号·伙夫老杨·第四十一」。「这是半壁村吴画匠的东西，」先生说，「娃娃们描了三年，描得比我还像老杨。」

column2: The Scraped Shrine
column3: 刮金龛

column2: A wayside shrine is surrounded by half a dozen men with bamboo slivers, scraping the gilt off the Buddha's face stroke by stroke. They call themselves the Gold Scrapers, and in seven or eight years every Buddha along this road has gone grey-faced. Their leader, a gap-toothed old man, brags as he works: 'This is nothing. The three hundred golden faces of the Qianli caravan? Men in golden masks scraped those. I saw it with my own eyes!'
column3: 一座路边小佛龛被围住了，五六个人拿着竹片，一下一下刮佛像脸上的金。他们自称「刮金帮」，刮了七八年，沿路的佛像个个成了灰脸。领头的是个缺牙老头，一边刮一边吹：「刮金算什么？千里号那三百张金脸，是戴金面具的人刮的，我亲眼看见的！」

column2: The Scrapers scatter, and you pin the old man in front of the shrine to tell it again. A moonless night, a band in golden masks went into the cave and scraped away until dawn. 'The Gold Masks. No mistake.' But halfway through he changes his tune: the masks 'looked like paper, now I think of it, painted gold'. You write down what he said.
column3: 刮金帮四散，老头被你们按在龛前，把那晚的事又讲了一遍：月黑夜，一群戴金面具的人进了窟，叮叮当当刮到天亮，「金面卫，错不了」。可他说着说着又改口，说那些面具「好像是纸糊的，刷了金漆」。你们把他的话记了下来。

column2: Golden Body Temple
column3: 金身寺

column2: A big compound at the foot of the hills, 'Golden Body Temple' over the gate, though the walls are a grain merchant's walls and the hitching posts are still outside. In the hall sits a gilded 'living Buddha'; pilgrims must kowtow, then donate. The false monks guarding the place, foot, crossbow and horse, outnumber real monks three to one. As you enter the hall, the golden Buddha sneezes.
column3: 山脚下一座大院，门匾上写着「金身寺」，可院墙是粮栈的墙，门口还留着拴牲口的石桩。大殿里供着一尊金身「活佛」，香客进来要先磕头再捐钱。护院的假和尚步、弩、骑都有，比真和尚多三倍。你们进殿的时候，那尊金身打了个喷嚏。

column2: The false monks routed, the 'living Buddha' abandons his pose and runs out the back, wiping gold paint off his face. He is the temple's abbot, born Qian Mancang, 'Granary-Full Qian', a grain merchant beyond the Pass who shaved his head when his business failed. Hidden on a beam in the hall is a note of his: 'Someone tops up the Qianli porridge shed every autumn. Find out where the grain comes from.' That's why he took the shed: he's after whoever sends the grain.
column3: 假和尚们被冲散，「活佛」也顾不得端坐了，抹着脸上的金漆从后门跑了。他是金身寺的方丈，俗名钱满仓，原是关外的粮商，粮栈倒了才剃的头。大殿梁上藏着他的一张单子：「千里粥棚，每年秋有人续粮。粮从何来，查。」原来他占粥棚，图的是那个续粮的人。

column2: The Steward's Kitchen
column3: 典座寮

column2: The temple steward, a tall thin old monk, has hated waste all his life; a grain of rice on the floor gets picked up, blown on and eaten. The false monks took his kitchen and ordered him to stew meat. He'd rather starve than lift a knife, so they locked him in the woodshed. In the kitchen, their half-eaten buns lie all over the floor.
column3: 寺里管伙食的典座是个瘦高的老和尚，一辈子最恨糟蹋粮食，掉在地上一粒米也要捡起来吹吹吃了。假和尚占了他的厨房，逼他炖肉，他宁可饿着也不动刀，被锁进了柴房。厨房里，假和尚们吃剩的馒头扔得满地都是。

column2: Once the false monks are gone the steward comes out of the woodshed and gathers up the buns one by one, dusting them off, and only then will he talk. He opens for business, trading the temple's vegetarian food, beans and dried greens, not a coin over the fair price. Master Shouzhou, who runs the porridge shed, went up the mountain two months ago, he says, to find whoever sends the grain. 'And his novice, Douzi, has gone missing too.'
column3: 假和尚被撵走，典座出了柴房，先把地上的馒头一个个捡起来掸掉灰，才肯跟你们说话。他开了张，拿斋饭、豆子、干菜跟你们换东西，一文不多收。他说管粥棚的守粥师父两个月前上了山，去找续粮的人，「他徒弟豆子也跟着不见了」。

column2: The Face Collector's Cart
column3: 收脸车

column2: A big cart under oilcloth, escorted fore and aft by guards from inside the Pass, their blades freshly ground. Riding in it is a fat antiques dealer who collects nothing but the Qianli caravan's 'golden faces'. He has seventeen so far, wrapped in silk floss, bound for the great houses back home. 'The name Qianli is worth more than gold.' Seeing your banner, the guards draw their bows first.
column3: 一辆蒙着油布的大车，前后跟着一队关内来的镖师，刀都是新磨的。车上的掌柜是个收古董的胖子，专收千里号的「金脸」，一路收了十七片，用丝绵包着，要运回关内卖给大户人家，「千里号三个字，比金子值钱」。镖师们见你们打着旗，先把弓拉开了。

column2: The guards abandon the cart and the fat dealer sighs over his box of plaster. He has done the sums, at least: the gold dust in all three hundred faces, scraped together, comes to barely a tenth of an ounce. 'Not enough for a ring.' It was never the gold that was worth anything, only the name. You take the seventeen flakes. Not one of them fits against another.
column3: 镖师们丢下车跑了，胖掌柜抱着他那箱泥皮直叹气。他倒是把账算得清：三百张脸的金粉加在一起，刮下来也不过一钱多，「不够打一只戒指」。值钱的从来不是金，是名声。十七片泥皮你们收下了，没有一片拼得上另一片。

column2: Shepherdess Slope
column3: 放羊坡

column2: A girl has grazed her sheep on this slope, not far from the caves' north cliff, for ten years. She tells everyone what she saw one night, and now a few Gold Mask riders have come to take her up the mountain for 'spreading rumours'. She cracks her whip and plants herself among her sheep: 'What I saw, I saw!'
column3: 坡上一个放羊的姑娘，十年来都在这片坡上放羊，离千佛洞的北崖不远。她到处跟人讲那天夜里看见的事，几个金面骑卫找上门来，说她「造谣惑众」，要把她带回山上问话。姑娘把鞭子一甩，站在羊群中间不肯走：「我看见的就是看见的！」

column2: Once the riders are driven back up the mountain, she finishes her story. The moon was bright that night. Walking home late, she saw something drifting out of a cave mouth on the north cliff, gust after gust, glittering like snow. 'The faces fell off by themselves.' She shivers as she says it. You think of the Gold Scraper's version: was that night moonlit or moonless?
column3: 金面骑卫被打回了山，姑娘这才把话说完：那夜月亮很亮，她赶夜路回家，看见北崖一个窟口里往外飘东西，一阵一阵，亮晶晶的，像下雪，「是脸自己掉下来了」。说完她自己打了个寒战。你们想起刮金帮的话：那一夜到底是有月亮，还是没月亮？

column2: The Incense Kilns
column3: 香灰窑

column2: A row of kiln caves at the foot of the hill belches black smoke. The false monks make incense here: sawdust and cow dung rolled into sticks, dried, painted red, and sold as 'Consecrated Incense of the Thousand Buddha Caves' at twenty coins a bundle. A big crowd of toughs, foot, crossbow and horse, guards the kilns, and anyone who comes close is 'stealing the temple's secret recipe'. Pilgrims light it at home, weep from the smoke, and take it for a miracle.
column3: 山脚的一排窑洞冒着黑烟，假和尚们在这里做香：锯末掺牛粪，搓成条，晒干了刷一层红，就是「千佛洞开光香」，一捆卖二十钱。窑口守着一大帮打手，步、弩、骑都有，谁靠近就说是「偷佛门秘方」。香客买回去一点，熏得直流眼泪，还以为是佛祖显灵。

column2: The toughs scattered, you turn up a letter from Qian Mancang to his men in the kilns: 'Keep taking the incense money. Also: whoever sends the grain must come down from the mountain. Watch that fat monk Shouzhou. He knows.' The kiln workers say Master Shouzhou never bought their incense; he only lit a plain oil lamp in the porridge shed. 'He said the Buddha doesn't lack incense. People lack porridge.'
column3: 打手们被打散，你们在窑里翻出钱满仓给手下的一封信：「香钱照收。另，续粮之人必从山上来，盯住守粥那个胖和尚，他知道。」窑工们说，守粥师父从不买他们的香，只在粥棚里点一盏清油灯，「他说佛不缺香，人缺粥」。

column2: Half Wall Village
column3: 半壁村

column2: All that's left of Half Wall village is half a wall, with half a flying apsara painted on it; the other half was never finished. Wu the painter's house sits beneath it, rows of empty paint dishes drying in the yard. Vagrants have taken the west room, picking their teeth with his brushes and stacking his dishes into stools. His wife, Aunt Wu, guards the kitchen door with a rolling pin and won't give an inch.
column3: 半壁村只剩半堵墙，墙上画着半幅飞天，另外半幅没画完。吴画匠的家就在墙下，院里晒着一排排空颜料碟。一伙流民占了他家的西屋，把画笔拿来剔牙，把颜料碟摞起来当凳子。吴画匠的老伴吴婶攥着擀面杖守在灶房门口，一步不让。

column2: The vagrants chased off, Aunt Wu brews you a pot of tea. Old Wu painted the Qianli caravan's three hundred as donors, she says, a whole winter's work, one face for each. A few years later the faces were scraped. He packed his paints that same night and left, saying he wouldn't come home until all three hundred were back. That was seven years ago. The bundle of three hundred pounce patterns he kept at home was stolen and sold by a peddler long since.
column3: 流民被撵走，吴婶给你们烧了一锅茶。她说老吴给千里号画了三百个供养人，画了一冬天，一人一张脸。几年后脸被刮了，他连夜收拾了颜料担子出门，说「不把三百张脸补回来不回家」，一走七年。家里那捆三百页的粉本，早被一个货郎偷去卖了。

column2: Dig Slope
column3: 挖仓坡

column2: A barren slope has been dug into a sieve: dozens of false monks swinging hoes, pit beside pit. They're hunting for the Qianli Granary. Legend says the caravan left more than the three hundred measures on the stele; there was a whole granary, and whoever finds it owns the porridge shed. A month of digging has turned up potsherds and a nest of jerboas. Their overseers see you coming and level their hoes.
column3: 一面荒坡被挖得像筛子，几十个假和尚抡着锄头，坑挨着坑。他们在找「千里仓」：传说千里号当年留下的粮，不止碑上写的三百石，还有一座藏粮的仓，谁找到谁就是粥棚的主。挖了一个月，挖出来的只有碎陶片和一窝跳鼠。监工的打手见你们来了，把锄头一横。

column2: The overseers scattered, the false monks drop their hoes and run. An old pilgrim resting below laughs till he cries. 'Fools. Who digs a granary into the ground? One damp spell on this plain and the grain all rots. Everything at the caves is either up on the cliff or inside a cave.' He points at the hills to the east. 'Master Shouzhou said the same.'
column3: 打手们被打散，假和尚扔了锄头就跑。坡下一个歇脚的老香客笑出了眼泪：「傻子，粮仓哪有挖在土里的？戈壁上的土一返潮，粮全霉了。千佛洞的东西，要么在崖上，要么在窟里。」他指了指东边的山：「守粥师父也这么说过。」

column2: Rack of Three Hundred Bowls
column3: 三百碗架

column2: Behind the porridge shed stands a long wooden rack hung with three hundred wooden bowls, a name carved into the bottom of each. False monks are unhooking them into baskets: 'sacred bowls of the Qianli caravan', worth a fortune back inside the Pass. The half-deaf old cook keeps blocking the basket. They knock him over; he gets up and blocks it again.
column3: 粥棚后面一排木架，架上挂着三百只木碗，每只碗底刻着一个名字。几个假和尚正把碗一只只摘下来装进筐，说是「千里号圣碗」，拿到关内能卖大价钱。架子底下，那个半聋的老火头拦着筐不放，被推了一个跟头，爬起来又拦。

column2: The false monks chased off, the old cook hangs the bowls back one by one. That winter, he shouts, the three hundred ate porridge here every day and went up the cliff by day to build walkways and plaster walls. 'A bowl of my porridge, a day of their work.' He has washed every bowl every night for ten years. At the very end hangs one bowl with no name: it belonged to the little monk who tended the fire back then. 'He ate the most. Then he stopped coming.'
column3: 假和尚被打跑，老火头把碗一只只挂回去。他说，那年冬天三百人天天在这儿喝粥，白天上崖修栈道、抹墙泥，「喝我一碗粥，还我一天工」。碗他每晚都洗，洗了十年。架子尽头还有一只没刻名字的碗，是当年烧火的小和尚的，「他喝得最多，后来不来了」。

column2: Bat Pagoda
column3: 蝙蝠塔

column2: A roofless earthen pagoda stands on the gravel plain, its belly packed with bats that pour out at sunset in a cloud that blots out half the sky. Locals say it's haunted and keep away. You go in with torches and the bats come at your faces, their wings whipping the flames about. On the inner walls something is drawn in charcoal, layer on layer, half buried under droppings.
column3: 戈壁上一座塌了顶的土塔，塔肚子里住满了蝙蝠，太阳一落山就黑压压地涌出来，遮住半边天。附近的人说这塔闹鬼，谁也不敢靠近。你们点着火把进去，蝙蝠扑面而来，翅膀扇得火苗乱窜。塔壁上隐约有炭笔画的东西，一层一层，被蝙蝠粪盖住了一半。

column2: This lot of bats is smoked out. Scraping the droppings off the walls, you find dozens of charcoal faces, all drawn at speed, and beside them two words: 'Afraid I'll forget.' Wu the painter drew them from memory once, sheltering from the rain. But the bats know this pagoda. Drive them out and in a few days they're back, burying the faces again. Someone will have to come and clear it every so often.
column3: 这一回的蝙蝠被烟熏了出去。你们刮掉塔壁上的粪，底下是几十张炭笔画的人脸，个个画得飞快，旁边写着「怕忘」两个字，是吴画匠当年躲雨时凭记忆画的。可蝙蝠认这座塔，赶走了，过几天又飞回来，粪又一层层盖上去，只能隔一阵来清一回。

column2: The Painted Tavern
column3: 照壁店

column2: The screen wall of a tavern carries a long row of donors in fine robes, each holding a censer, and every face is a local one: Wang the oil seller, the landlord's mother-in-law, the village simpleton. Wu the painter did it to settle his bar bill, the landlord says: 'The Qianli caravan, in theory. The faces were whoever he grabbed while drunk.' Now a gang of soldiers-turned-thugs has taken the tavern, drunk it dry, and wants every face on the wall changed to theirs.
column3: 一家酒店的照壁上画着一长溜供养人，个个手捧香炉，衣冠楚楚，可脸全是附近的熟面孔：卖油的老王、店主的丈母娘、村口的二傻子。店主说这是吴画匠当年拿来抵酒钱的，「画的是千里号，脸是他喝醉了随手抓的」。如今一伙兵痞占了酒店，喝光了酒，要店主把照壁上的人脸都改成他们自己。

column2: The thugs thrown out, the landlord pours you the last of the wine. Wu used to boast in his cups that he had all three hundred faces in his head and could paint them without any patterns. 'All he lacked was colour. Good colour costs, gold dust more.' On the wall, the mother-in-law regards you with a stern smile.
column3: 兵痞被打出了门，店主请你们喝了一碗剩下的酒。他说吴画匠酒后吹过牛：三百张脸他都记在脑子里，不用粉本也画得出来，「只是缺颜色。好颜色贵，金粉更贵」。照壁上的丈母娘看着你们，笑得很威严。

column2: The Search Road
column3: 搜面道

column2: A small troop of Gold Mask riders blocks the road, searching every traveller's bundle. Not for money, for plaster: any flake or scrap of paper with a face on it is confiscated, not a copper paid. A peddler caught with two 'golden faces' is on his knees begging. The riders' masks glint in the sun and show nothing at all.
column3: 一小队金面骑卫拦在路上，挨个搜过路人的包袱。搜的不是钱，是泥皮：凡是带着画了人脸的泥皮、纸片的，一律收走，一个铜子儿也不赔。一个货郎被搜出两片「金脸」，正跪在地上求饶。骑卫的面具在阳光下一晃一晃，看不出喜怒。

column2: The riders withdraw and leave behind a leather bag of plaster flakes collected along the road, each wrapped in paper marked with where and when. In the bag is an order: 'Not one fragment of the Qianli faces is to leave. All to be recovered and stored. Wuxiang, Lord of the Caves.' So that's what the Gold Masks have been gathering up all over the country: the three hundred faces.
column3: 骑卫们退了，丢下一只皮口袋，里面是一路收来的泥皮，每片都用纸包好，纸上写着收的日子和地方。口袋里还有一道令：「千里号残面，一片不许流出，收回入库。洞主无相。」原来金面卫满世界收的，就是那三百张脸。

column2: Fake Face Gully
column3: 换脸沟

column2: A row of sheds lines the gully, and in them painters dab faces onto old wall plaster, smoke them yellow, sprinkle on brass filings for gold, and call them 'genuine Qianli'. The man in charge was once Wu the painter's apprentice, and he's hired toughs to mind the sheds. When you arrive he is painting a passing traveller's face, and charging him ten coins for the privilege.
column3: 沟里搭着一溜棚子，棚里坐着几个画匠，正往旧墙皮上画脸，画好了用烟熏黄，再撒一把铜粉冒充金星，就成了「千里号原件」。领头的是吴画匠早年的徒弟，雇了一帮打手看棚子。你们进沟的时候，他正照着一个过路人的脸画，画完还收了人家十个钱。

column2: The toughs gone, the apprentice kneels and owns up. A true pounce pattern leaves a line of fine dots on the wall; fakes are drawn in one stroke and give themselves away at a glance. Seven years ago, he says, he saw his master once, heading east with his paints on a carrying pole, off to the southern hills to find 'a red for faces and a green for robes'. 'When the master says he'll find something, he'll spend his life finding it.'
column3: 打手散了，那徒弟跪下认了错。他说真粉本印上墙的线是一串细点，假的都是一笔画成，一看就破。他还说七年前见过师父一面，师父挑着颜料担子往东去了，要去南边山里找「能画脸的红、能画衣的绿」。「师父那人，说找就找一辈子。」

column2: Lantern Camp
column3: 灯笼营

column2: Here's the peddler who stole the patterns. He's done well for himself, hired swordsmen as bodyguards, and pitched a camp at the crossroads to sell sundries. A lantern hangs at the gate, papered with the outline of a face pricked full of holes, so that when it's lit the face is printed on the ground in points of light. The bodyguards see you staring at it and draw.
column3: 偷粉本的货郎找到了：他如今发了点小财，雇了几个刀手当保镖，在路口扎了个营卖杂货。营门口挂着一只灯笼，糊灯笼的纸上有一张人脸的线条，针眼一排排的，灯一点，脸就在地上印出一圈光点。保镖们见有人盯着灯笼看，抽出了刀。

column2: The guards run and the peddler, hands over his head, confesses. He split up the three hundred sheets and sold them off: for lanterns, for wrapping oil cakes, for shoe soles. The thickest stack left was bought outright by men in golden masks. You take down the lantern. In the corner of the paper: 'Qianli caravan. Little Ding, groom.'
column3: 保镖们跑了，货郎抱着头交代：那捆粉本三百页，他拆开卖了，糊灯笼的、包油饼的、纳鞋底的都有，剩下最厚的一沓，被几个戴金面的人一口价买走了。你们把灯笼摘下来，纸角写着「千里号·马夫小丁」。

column2: Shouzhou's Hut
column3: 守粥庵

column2: Down a dead end at the foot of the hill is a small hermitage, Master Shouzhou's, with a patch of beans planted by the door. False monks are ransacking it, even raking out the stove, hunting for the 'grain clue' Qian Mancang told them about. A rosary of dried beans hung on the door frame; they've torn it and the beans have rolled everywhere.
column3: 山脚死胡同里一间小庵，是守粥师父住的地方，门口种着一畦豆子。一伙假和尚正在庵里翻箱倒柜，连灶膛都掏空了，要找钱满仓说的「续粮的线索」。门框上挂着一串干豆子编的念珠，被他们扯断了，豆子滚了一地。

column2: With the false monks thrown out, you find a note on the stove in Shouzhou's hand: 'Gone up the mountain to find whoever sends the grain. Back in three days. Douzi, mind the house.' It's dated two months ago. Below it, in a wobbly child's hand: 'Douzi is not minding the house. Douzi has gone to find Master.'
column3: 假和尚被撵走，你们在灶台上找到一张纸条，是守粥的字：「上山找续粮的人，三日回。豆子看家。」日子是两个月前的。纸条底下还有一行歪歪扭扭的小字，显然是孩子写的：「豆子不看家。豆子去找师父。」

column2: Paper Soles
column3: 千层底

column2: A band of deserters rests by the road in thick new cloth shoes bought from the peddler. The soles are layered cloth and paper, good stout paper, and across the sand they leave a faint trail of printed faces. The deserters haven't noticed. Seeing you follow their footprints, they take you for deserter-catchers and come at you swinging.
column3: 一伙开小差的兵卒在路边歇脚，脚上的新布鞋纳得厚厚的，是从货郎那儿买来的。鞋底一层布一层纸，纸是厚实的好纸，走过沙地，竟在地上留下一串淡淡的人脸印子。兵卒们自己都没发觉，见你们追着他们的脚印看，以为是来抓逃兵的，拔刀就砍。

column2: The deserters flee barefoot and leave a heap of shoes. Unpicking the soles, you draw out more than thirty patterns, some blurred with sweat, some still crisp: a big beard, a little man, someone missing a piece of one ear. Each has a name and number in the corner. You lay them out to dry on the rocks, thirty-odd faces looking up at the sky.
column3: 兵卒们光着脚跑了，鞋留下了一堆。你们拆开鞋底，抽出三十多张粉本，有的被汗渍得模糊，有的还清清楚楚：一个大胡子，一个小个子，一个耳朵缺了一块的。每张纸角都有名字和编号。你们把它们晾在石头上，三十多张脸看着天。

column2: Casket Road
column3: 抬匣道

column2: A troop of Gold Mask swordsmen carries a wooden casket along the road, stepping smoothly so as not to jolt it. The seal on it reads 'No. 153'. Seeing you, they close round the casket and unsheathe. 'What's in here,' says their leader, 'you aren't fit to see.'
column3: 一队金面刀卫抬着一口木匣赶路，走得很稳，生怕颠着。匣子上贴着封条：「第一百五十三号」。他们见有人过来，把匣子护在中间，刀出了鞘。领头的说：「匣里的东西，你们不配看。」

column2: Beaten, the swordsmen still don't drop the casket; they carry it off with them. Their leader says over his shoulder: 'Half a man's face. The Lord found it piece by piece. It's still missing an eye.' So every face has a number and a casket, and the Gold Masks gather up the three hundred faces the way a family gathers up its dead.
column3: 刀卫们败了，却没扔下匣子，抬着它退走了。领头的临走说了一句：「匣里是一个人的半张脸，洞主一片片找回来的，还缺一只眼睛。」原来每张脸都有一个号、一口匣，金面卫像收殓亲人那样，收拾着三百个人的脸。

column2: The Beggars' Court
column3: 叫花坛

column2: Hundreds of beggars crowd before a ruined shrine for a Beggars' Assembly, and on trial are the false monks of the Golden Body Temple: charging for porridge beggars can't afford is taking away their living. A few captured false monks kneel in the middle. But the temple's toughs have arrived, and both sides have their dog-sticks and knives out. It's about to turn into a brawl.
column3: 一座破土地庙前围了上百个乞丐，正在开「叫花大会」，审的是金身寺的假和尚：粥要了钱，叫花子喝不起，这是断了他们的活路。几个被抓来的假和尚跪在当中，可金身寺的打手也赶到了，两边抄起了打狗棍和短刀，眼看就要打成一锅粥。

column2: The toughs beaten back, the beggars cheer and run the false monks home. Their chief, a one-eyed old man, sleeps behind the porridge shed every autumn and has seen the night cart. The men driving the oxen wear bronze masks and carry no torches; once the grain is down they head off north-east into the gravel desert. 'Not a sound from their feet. Like soldiers on night watch.'
column3: 打手被打退，叫花子们拍手叫好，把假和尚轰回了金身寺。丐头是个独眼老汉，他说他每年秋天都睡在粥棚后头，见过那辆夜里来的粮车：赶牛的人戴着铜面具，不打火把，卸了粮就往东北的戈壁里走，「脚底下一点声儿没有，跟巡夜的兵一样」。

column2: The Market Below the Caves
column3: 窟前市

column2: Below the cliff lies an open square that was once the liveliest market at the caves. The cave carvers would carry out the stone they'd cut and sell it, and pilgrims and farmers from below would bring grain to trade for it, taking the stone home for walls, stoves and pigsties. Now Qian Mancang's toughs have set up a checkpoint at the entrance and take three tenths of all grain coming in. The carvers are too hungry to cut, and the stone piles up unsold.
column3: 崖下一片空场，从前是千佛洞最热闹的集：凿窟的石匠们挑着凿下来的石料出来卖，香客和山下的庄户拿粮食来换，换了石头回去垒墙、砌灶、修猪圈。如今钱满仓的打手在场口设了卡，粮食进场要抽三成，石匠们饿得凿不动，石料堆成了山也卖不出去。

column2: With the toughs driven off, the market opens again: grain comes in by the shoulder-load and leaves as stone, and the daily trade is lively once more. An old stonemason squats on a stone pile with a bowl of porridge. That winter, he says, the Qianli caravan cut and carried stone alongside them, three hundred men as good as three hundred masons. 'When they left they said the stone belongs to the Buddha and the grain belongs to people. Trade one for the other and neither goes hungry.' And Qian Mancang has run off into the eastern hills with half a map, he adds. 'Gone looking for the Qianli Granary.'
column3: 打手们被赶走，窟前市重新开了张：粮食一担担挑进来，换走崖下的石料，每天的交易又热闹起来。一个老石匠捧着一碗粥蹲在石堆上说，那年冬天千里号的人跟他们一起凿石、一起扛，三百人顶得上三百个匠人，「他们走的时候，说石头是佛的，粮食是人的，换一换，两边都饿不着」。他还说钱满仓带着半张图往东山跑了，「找千里仓去了」。

column2: The Statue Mender
column3: 补佛婆

column2: At the end of a small village lives an old woman who mends clay Buddhas, patching on noses and fingers they've lost. Some Gold Scraper stragglers have come to make her tell them where gilded Buddhas are still to be found, or they'll smash her clay basins. She slaps a lump of clay on the table: 'I know what every Buddha is missing. I don't know which ones have gold.'
column3: 小村尽头一间屋，住着个补泥塑的老婆婆，专给缺了鼻子、掉了手指的佛像补泥。刮金帮的几个残兵找上门，逼她说出哪里还有贴金的佛，不说就砸她的泥盆。老婆婆把一团泥拍在桌上：「我只知道哪里的佛缺什么，不知道哪里的佛有金。」

column2: Once the Scrapers are gone she tells you why there was gold at all. When the Qianli caravan were painted, they insisted on gold in their faces and the painter couldn't talk them out of it. The bookkeeper said that when the lamps were lit in the cave, all three hundred faces would shine at once, 'so when we come back, we'll know at a glance who's who'. 'It was for recognising each other, not for show,' she sighs. 'And it brought the scrapers.'
column3: 刮金帮被赶走，老婆婆跟你们讲了金粉的来由：千里号的人画像时，非要往脸上调金，画匠劝都劝不住。账房说，窟里点灯的时候，三百张脸一齐亮起来，「回来的时候，一眼就认出谁是谁」。「是为了认人，不是为了富贵，」她叹口气，「偏偏招来了刮金的。」

column2: Sesame Oil Mill
column3: 胡麻油坊

column2: A sesame oil mill at the crossroads, its millstone turning for decades and the smell carrying a mile. A local bully and his men have seized it and tripled the price of oil; even the lamp oil for the caves must pay him first. The oil cakes they sell come wrapped in thick paper printed with faces, and people toss the wrappers on the ground when they've eaten.
column3: 路口一家胡麻油坊，榨油的石碾子转了几十年，香味飘出二里地。本地一个恶霸带着打手霸占了油坊，油价涨了三倍，连千佛洞点灯的油都要先给他交钱。他们卖的油饼用厚纸包着，纸上是一张张人脸，吃完的人顺手就扔在了地上。

column2: With the bully run off, the millstone rumbles round again. The miller picks up the wrappers one by one, smooths them out and hands them to you: pounce patterns, soaked translucent with oil, the lines clearer than ever. From now on he'll wrap his cakes in lotus leaves. 'You don't wrap cakes in people's faces.'
column3: 恶霸被打跑，石碾子又咕噜噜转了起来。油坊老板把地上的包饼纸一张张捡回来，捋平了交给你们：都是粉本，被油浸得透亮，线条反倒更清楚了。他说以后包饼改用荷叶，「人家的脸，不能拿来包饼」。

column2: The bully's storeroom yields twenty jars of sesame oil, half a room of sesame cakes, thirty pounds of mutton fat, a stolen copper pot, and a box of his 'oil tax', whose ledger has even the old monk of the caves owing him a coin.
column3: 恶霸的库房里抄出二十坛胡麻油、半屋子芝麻饼、三十斤羊油、一口抢来的铜锅，还有一匣子他收的「过油税」，账上连千佛洞的老和尚都欠他一钱。

column2: Every time you pass, the miller fills your lamps for the road and presses on you a stack of sesame flatbreads fresh from the pan, wrapped in lotus leaves. 'Hot. Eat them slowly on the way.'
column3: 每次路过，油坊老板都给你们灌满一路的灯油，再塞一摞刚出锅的胡麻饼，用荷叶包着：「烫手，路上慢慢吃。」

column2: Wall Peelers' Camp
column3: 揭壁营

column2: A big camp of mural thieves on the gravel plain, foot, crossbow and horse. Their chief is a craftsman from inside the Pass who knows how to paste wet cloth over a painting and, when it dries, peel the whole thing off with the plaster attached. They're practising in camp, peeled apsaras stacked by the tents. Word is the next thing they'll peel is a row of donors with no faces.
column3: 戈壁上一座大营，住着一伙盗壁贼，步卒、弩手、骑手都有。领头的是个关内来的巧手，会用湿布糊住壁画，等布干了一揭，整片画就连着泥皮下来了。他们正在营里试手，揭下来的飞天一块块堆在帐篷边。听说他们下一个要揭的，是一排没有脸的供养人。

column2: The thieves scattered, you find a map in the chief's tent: the north cliff of the caves, with a circle round one mouth on the third tier and the note 'Qianli Cave. Three hundred donors. Faces scraped, bodies intact. Can be peeled.' On the back: 'Gold Masks guard the mouth day and night. Must be lured away first.' Those three hundred faceless people have had someone watching over them all along.
column3: 盗壁贼被打散，你们在领头的帐里搜出一张图，画的是千佛洞北崖，第三层一个窟口画了圈，旁边写着「千里窟，供养人三百身，脸已刮，身尚全，可揭」。图背面还有一行：「窟口有金面卫昼夜看守，须先引开。」那三百个没有脸的人，一直有人守着。

column2: The Glue Pen
column3: 熬胶圈

column2: At the end of a dead-end track is a sheep pen where painters used to boil glue: hides rendered down and mixed into the paint, so the colour would hold to the wall. A big gang of soldier-thugs, foot, crossbow and horse, has taken it over and stews mutton in the glue cauldron, grease running down their chins. A board nailed to the wall, covered in paint recipes, has become their chopping block.
column3: 死胡同尽头一座羊圈，从前是画匠们熬胶的地方：皮子熬成胶，调进颜料，颜色才粘得住墙。如今一伙兵痞占了圈，把熬胶的大锅拿来炖羊肉，步、弩、骑一大帮，吃得满嘴流油。圈墙上钉着一块木板，写满了颜料的配方，被他们拿来当了砧板。

column2: The thugs driven off, you scrub the chopping block and the recipe still reads clearly: 'Faces: white earth for the ground, red earth for the cheeks, malachite green for robes, ink for the eyes. A little gold dust, mixed with glue, shows only by lamplight.' Signed Wu Banbi. The red and green he went looking for are both on this board. The old shepherd who boiled the glue says Wu cooked a whole pot here before he left and carried it off on his back.
column3: 兵痞被撵走，你们把那块砧板洗干净，配方还看得清：「人面：白土为底，土红晕颊，石绿描衣，墨点睛。金粉少许，调胶，灯下方见。」落款吴半壁。原来他要找的红和绿，都写在这块板子上。熬胶的老羊倌说，吴画匠临走前在这里熬了一锅胶，背走了。

column2: Little Temple of a Thousand Buddhas
column3: 千佛小寺

column2: A painter-monk lives in a little roadside temple; he and Wu the painter learned from the same master. He has been painting a wall of a thousand Buddhas for ten years and has reached number six hundred. Scouts for the mural thieves have moved in and want him to draw them a plan of the north cliff. He refuses, so they are snapping his brushes one by one.
column3: 路边小寺里住着个画僧，和吴画匠是一个师父教出来的。他在给小寺画一墙千佛，画了十年，才画到第六百个。一伙盗壁贼的探子赖在寺里，逼他画一张千佛洞北崖的窟图，他不肯，他们就把他的笔一支支掰断。

column2: The scouts run off and the monk picks up his broken brushes. 'I paint slowly. Old Wu paints fast. A face in a quarter of an hour, and alive.' Wu came by before he left, he says, to borrow his finest brush, and said the hardest of the three hundred faces was the bookkeeper's. 'The man's eyes look like they're working out what you're worth.' It took Wu three tries to get it.
column3: 探子被赶走了，画僧捡起断笔：「我画得慢，老吴画得快。他画脸，一张一刻钟，画得活。」他说老吴临走前来过，跟他借了一支最细的笔，说那三百张脸里最难画的是账房，「那人一双眼睛像在算你」。老吴画了三遍才画成。

column2: The Water Mill
column3: 水磨坊

column2: A water mill by the irrigation channel grinds the porridge shed's grain day and night. The Golden Body Temple's men are forcing the miller to cut every measure of grain with half a measure of sawdust: 'Pilgrims can't tell how thick it is.' He refused, so they nailed his door shut with him and his donkey inside. Toughs sit outside eating his roasted beans.
column3: 渠边一座水磨坊，磨盘日夜转，磨的是粥棚的粮。金身寺的人押着磨坊老板，逼他每磨一斗米掺半斗锯末，「粥稠不稠，香客看不出来」。老板不肯，磨坊的门就被钉死了，他和他的驴一起被关在里面。门外守着一伙打手，吃着老板家的炒豆子。

column2: The toughs chased off, you prise open the door and the miller and his donkey burst out together. The grain in those mask-stamped sacks isn't like the grain from down here, he says: small, hard-hulled, gritty with sand, grown on land broken at the edge of the desert. 'Whoever grows it doesn't know farming. But it gets better every year.' He hands you a bag of fresh flour. 'Cleanest bag I've ground in ten years.'
column3: 打手被打跑，你们撬开门，老板和驴一起冲了出来。他说那些盖着金面印的粮袋，粮食跟山下的不一样：粒小、壳硬，夹着沙子，是戈壁边上开荒种出来的，「种的人不会种地，可一年比一年种得好」。他递过一袋新磨的面：「十年来最干净的一袋。」

column2: Panning Flats
column3: 淘金滩

column2: Dozens of people crouch on a dry riverbed with wooden pans, sifting sand and sweating. They heard that when the Qianli caravan's golden faces were scraped, the wind blew the gold dust out over the gravel plain, and they've been panning for it for three years. The flats belong to a panning boss who takes half of every pan an outsider washes. When you come near, they grab their shovels.
column3: 一片干河滩上蹲着几十个人，个个端着木盆淘沙，淘得满头大汗。他们听说千里号的金脸被刮下来以后，金粉让风吹到了戈壁上，就跑来淘，一淘三年。这片滩被淘金客的头子霸着，外人进来淘一盆要交一半。他们见你们走近，抄起了铁锹。

column2: With the panners dispersed, you look at what they've found: a pinch of red, green and white paint grit with a few bright specks, real gold, though three years' worth wouldn't make a grain of rice. Their boss hangs his head. The Gold Masks picked up the dust grain by grain long ago, he says. 'They're better panners than we are.'
column3: 淘金客散了，你们看看他们淘出来的东西：一小撮红的、绿的、白的颜料渣，夹着几粒亮闪闪的，倒真是金，可三年加起来还没有一粒米大。头子垂头丧气，说金粉早被金面卫的人一粒粒收走了，「他们比我们还会淘」。

column2: The Locked Cave
column3: 锁僧窟

column2: A small cave mouth at the foot of the hill has been boarded up, and from inside comes chanting, weak and tired. Qian Mancang has locked up all the real monks who wouldn't join him here, with one bowl of water a day. A few false monks guard the entrance cracking melon seeds, calling in every so often: 'Changed your minds yet? You've shaved your heads, what's it matter whose rice you eat?'
column3: 山脚的一个小窟口被木栅钉死了，里面传出念经声，念得有气无力。钱满仓把不肯入伙的真和尚都关在这里，每天只送一碗清水。窟口守着几个假和尚，嗑着瓜子，隔一会儿往里喊一声：「想通了没有？剃了头的，跟谁不是吃饭？」

column2: With the false monks gone you tear down the boards, and a dozen real monks feel their way out along the wall. Their first question: 'Is the porridge shed open?' What Qian Mancang fears most is the Gold Mask on the mountain, they say; only because the Gold Mask never comes down has he dared to take the shed. Before they were locked up, Master Shouzhou said the Gold Masks were blocking the main path, so he'd go round by the eastern gullies 'and ask to his face whether the grain will keep coming'.
column3: 假和尚被赶跑，你们拆了木栅，十几个真和尚扶着墙走出来，头一句问的是：「粥棚开着吗？」他们说钱满仓最怕山上的金面，金面不出山，他才敢占粥棚。守粥师父被关前说过，正路有金面卫拦着，他要从东边山沟绕上去，「当面问问，粮还送不送」。

column2: The Bookkeeper's Stone
column3: 账房石

column2: Carved on a boulder is a half-length portrait in a few plain lines: a thin face, narrowed eyes, a brush tucked behind one ear, an abacus at hand. A troop of Gold Mask swordsmen is under orders to guard it: no touching, no tracing, even shepherds must go round. Today a few mural thieves have crept up, meaning to chisel it off and sell it.
column3: 一块大石头上刻着一个人的半身像，线条简单：瘦脸，眯眼，耳朵后面夹着一支笔，手边一把算盘。一队金面刀卫奉命守着这块石头，不许人摸，不许人描，连放羊的都得绕着走。今天几个盗壁贼摸过来，想把它凿下来卖钱。

column2: Thieves and guards both gone, you study the stone. At its foot, small: 'Carved in jest by Wu Banbi: Master Bookkeeper. Winter, Dingwei year.' The painter warmed up on stone before he painted the man. The guard captain, leaving, says the Lord comes to look at it once a month, then goes without a word. Of all three hundred faces, this is the only one nobody scraped.
column3: 盗壁贼和刀卫都退了，你们细看石像，石脚刻着一行小字：「吴半壁戏刻账房先生，丁未冬。」是画匠给账房画像之前，先拿石头练的手。刀卫头目临走说，洞主每月来看它一回，看完就走，一句话不说。三百张脸里，只有这一张没被刮掉。

column2: The Felled Poplars
column3: 伐杨林

column2: Axes ring through a line of desert poplars. The Golden Body Temple's men are felling them for firewood to boil their coin-a-bowl gruel. Poplar wood is hard, half a day a tree, so they take the edge trees first; the margin of the wood is already bald and sand is pouring in through the gap. An old forester hugs a trunk and won't let go, and has been beaten black and blue for it.
column3: 一溜胡杨林里响着斧子声，金身寺的人在砍树，砍下来的胡杨劈成柴，拉回去熬他们一钱一碗的稀粥。胡杨的木头硬，砍一棵要半天，他们就先砍边上的，林子边已经秃了一片，沙子顺着缺口往里灌。一个看林子的老汉抱着树不肯撒手，被打得鼻青脸肿。

column2: With the woodcutters chased off, the old man strokes the bark. Poplars don't live on rain, he says; their roots go down and down until they reach the groundwater, so wherever poplars grow in a line there's an unseen stream beneath, most likely an old river course. Cut them and the sand moves in. He shows you fresh letters carved into one trunk, 'Shouzhou passed here', and an arrow pointing east.
column3: 砍树的被赶跑，老汉摸着树皮说：胡杨不靠天上的雨活，根往下扎，一直扎到地下水里，所以胡杨长成一溜的地方，底下准有一条看不见的水，多半是从前的河道。砍了它，沙就进来了。他指给你们看一棵树上新刻的字：「守粥过此」，旁边一个箭头，指着东边。

column2: Beam Thieves' Slope
column3: 拆梁坡

column2: Half an old plank walkway clings to a low cliff, its beams socketed one by one into holes in the rock. Swordsmen hired by a timber merchant from inside the Pass are dismantling it and stacking the beams on carts: fine old elm, they say, worth a lot back home. Every beam they pull out brings a curtain of sand pattering down the cliff.
column3: 一道矮崖上残留着半截旧栈道，木梁一根根插在崖壁的孔里。一伙关内木材商雇来的刀手正在拆，拆下来的梁码在车上，说是上好的老榆木，运回去能卖大价钱。他们拆一根，崖上就簌簌往下掉一层沙。

column2: With the swordsmen chased off you look at the beams on the cart. Every beam end bears the same brand: 'Qianli, winter of Dingwei.' The Qianli caravan built this walkway, and after ten years the beams haven't rotted. You fit them back into their sockets one by one, and the cliff stops shedding sand.
column3: 刀手们被赶跑，你们看了看车上的梁，每根梁头都烙着同一个印：「千里 丁未冬」。原来这截栈道是千里号的人修的，修了十年，梁还没朽。你们把梁一根根插了回去，崖不掉沙了。

column2: Cliff Burrowers
column3: 掏崖户

column2: A reddish cliff has been dug into a dozen holes, and a band of deserters lives in them. When a hole is too small they dig deeper, when it's cold they light fires inside, and the cliff face is blackened with smoke. Chunks have already fallen from its foot and they keep digging. Locals say that every night someone comes and fills a little of what they dug that day with mud, and the next day they dig it out again.
column3: 一面土红色的崖壁被掏出了十几个洞，一伙逃兵住在里面，嫌洞小就往里再掏，嫌冷就在洞里生火，熏得崖面一片黑。崖脚已经掉下来好几块，他们照掏不误。附近的人说，每天夜里，总有人来把他们白天掏的洞拿泥巴填上一点，第二天他们又掏开。

column2: The deserters are driven out. Where the holes were filled, the work is mud and straw in even layers, with camel hair mixed in. On the innermost patch someone has scratched a little camel with a fingernail, four legs, one of them bent. Whoever comes at night to mend the cliff knows the trade.
column3: 逃兵被赶走了。洞壁上填过的地方一层泥一层草，抹得很匀，泥里掺着骆驼毛。最里面的一处泥上，有人用指甲刻了一只小骆驼，四条腿，一条腿是弯的。夜里来补崖的，是个懂行的人。

column2: The Face Store
column3: 面库

column2: A stone storehouse at the end of a dead end, guarded by the best of the Gold Masks, sword, crossbow and horse, their masks polished bright. Seals cover the door layer on layer, the newest dated yesterday. From inside comes now and then a rustle of paper, as if someone is counting through something page by page.
column3: 死胡同里一座石砌的库房，门口站着金面卫最精的一队：刀卫、弩手、骑卫三路，个个面具擦得锃亮。库门上的封条一层盖一层，最新的一层是昨天的。库里不时传出纸张翻动的声音，像有人在里面一页页数着什么。

column2: The guards withdraw and you push open the door. Three hundred wooden caskets stand stacked to the ceiling, each with a number and a name. Inside are recovered flakes and patterns: some caskets nearly full, some holding one fingernail of plaster, some empty. The rustling was the wind through a crack in the wall. What the Gold Masks guard is three hundred faces, waiting piece by piece to be whole.
column3: 守库的人退走了，你们推开库门：三百口木匣码到房顶，每口一个号、一个名字。匣里是收回来的泥皮和粉本，有的快满了，有的只有指甲大一片，有的空着。翻纸声是风，从墙缝里吹进来。金面卫守的是三百个人的脸，一片一片，等它们凑齐。

column2: The Scrapers' Den
column3: 刮金窝

column2: The Gold Scrapers' old den lies at the end of a dry gully; the gang that scraped the Qianli Cave got its start here. Their hardest members, foot, crossbow and horse, are gathered inside. On the wall hangs a row of paper masks painted gold; on the floor, bamboo slivers, brushes and a small steelyard for weighing gold. They've heard you've been asking about 'the three hundred faces' all along the road, and they're waiting.
column3: 刮金帮的老窝藏在一道干沟尽头，当年刮过千里窟的那一伙就是从这里起家的。窝里聚着刮金帮最狠的一群，步、弩、骑都有，墙上挂着一排刷了金漆的纸面具，地上堆着竹片、刷子和一杆戥子。他们听说你们一路在问「三百张脸」，早早地等着了。

column2: The Scrapers are broken, and under the steelyard lies their old share-out note: 'Qianli Cave, three hundred faces. Gold obtained: one tenth of an ounce and a little more. Split seven ways.' That night they wore gold-painted paper masks to frighten the monks guarding the cave. The moonlight caught the gold dust drifting out and the shepherd girl saw snow; the gap-toothed old man even got the moon wrong. At the bottom, in red ink: 'Not one escapes.' The hand is the same as on the order closing the mountain.
column3: 刮金帮被打垮了，戥子底下压着分赃的字据：「千里窟三百面，得金一钱二分，七人均分。」他们戴金漆纸面具吓唬守窟的和尚，月光照着金粉往外飘，放羊姑娘看成了下雪，缺牙老头记岔了月亮。字据末尾有朱笔批的四个字：「一人不漏。」笔迹和闭山令一样。

column2: The Qian Granary
column3: 钱家仓

column2: At the end of a dead end stands a big granary, Qian Mancang's real fortune: a year's grain skimmed from the porridge shed and the night carts he seized, piled to the rafters. He's hired swordsmen from inside the Pass to guard it, foot, crossbow and horse, all ruddy and well fed. A new sign hangs at the door: 'Fair prices in lean years. No credit.'
column3: 死胡同尽头一座大仓，是钱满仓真正的家底：仓里堆的是这一年从粥棚扣下来的粮，还有截下的夜粮车，堆得顶到了房梁。他雇了一伙关内的刀客看仓，步、弩、骑都有，个个吃得红光满面。仓门口挂着一块新牌子：「荒年平价，概不赊欠」。

column2: The swordsmen scattered, the grain goes back to the porridge shed cart by cart. Qian Mancang's ledger lays out his plan precisely: wait for a disaster year and sell at five times the price. On its last page is pasted half a map: a cliff in the eastern hills with a circle on it and the note 'Qianli Granary. Half obtained. The other half is with Shouzhou.'
column3: 刀客们被打散，仓里的粮一车车拉回了粥棚。你们翻出钱满仓的账本，上面算得清清楚楚：等哪年遭了灾，粮价翻五倍再卖。账本最后一页贴着半张图，图上画着东山的一道崖，崖上一个圈，旁边写：「千里仓，得其半，余半在守粥处。」

column2: The Mountain Barrier
column3: 拦山卡

column2: The main path up the mountain is cut by a troop of Gold Masks: swordsmen on the stone steps, crossbowmen hidden in cracks in the cliff. They don't take money and won't say why, only: 'The Lord's orders. No one from below goes up.' A pilgrim tries to slip them a string of coins and has it pushed straight back into his hand.
column3: 上山的正路被一队金面卫截住了，刀卫守在石阶上，弩手伏在崖缝里。他们不收钱，也不说为什么，只说一句：「洞主有令，山下的人不许上山。」一个香客想塞给他们一串钱，被原样塞了回来。

column2: The Gold Masks withdraw up the mountain, though their leader says a little more. Two months ago a fat monk came with an empty grain sack asking to see the Lord. They didn't let him through: 'The Lord said no one.' So the fat monk went east, saying he'd go up by the eastern gully. The leader is quiet a moment, then adds: 'There are leopards in the eastern gully. If you're going that way, have a look for us.'
column3: 金面卫退上了山，领头的一个倒是多说了几句：两个月前有个胖和尚扛着一只空粮袋来，说要见洞主，他们没放，「洞主说过，谁都不放」。胖和尚就往东去了，说绕东沟上山。领头的沉默了一会儿，又说：「东沟有豹子。你们要是往那边走，替我们看一眼。」

column2: Temple Gate Slope
column3: 山门坡

column2: At the foot of the steps up to the temple gate sits a familiar face: Liaozhang the monk, his donkey tethered beside him, still carrying the two chests of debt books. He's come home to the temple, but a troop of Gold Mask swordsmen has stopped him outside the gate. 'The Lord's orders: monks who've left the gate don't come back.' Liaozhang is hopping mad. 'I'm a monk of this temple! My master is your Lord!'
column3: 上山门的石阶下坐着一个熟人：了账和尚，毛驴拴在一边，驴背上还驮着那两箱债簿。他回寺里来，却被一队金面刀卫拦在山门外，进不去。刀卫说：「洞主有令，出了山门的和尚不许回来。」了账急得跳脚：「我是这寺里的和尚！我师父就是你们洞主！」

column2: The swordsmen beaten back, Liaozhang brushes himself down and explains. His master's monastic name is Wuxiang, 'Without Form'; he was the temple's keeper of the caves. Seven years ago, the night the three hundred faces were scraped, his master took off his robe, put on the golden mask and closed the mountain, and since then sees no one, not even him. 'My master owes me an explanation and the Qianli caravan owes the temple a debt,' he says. 'We agreed in the Sand Sea: we settle the accounts together.'
column3: 刀卫们被打退了，了账拍着身上的土说：他师父法号无相，原是寺里管窟的和尚。七年前三百张脸被刮的那一夜，师父脱了袈裟，戴上金面，从此闭山，谁都不见，连他也不见。「师父欠我一个说法，千里号欠寺里一笔账，」他说，「沙海里说好的，账一起对。」

column2: Winter Camp Wood
column3: 冬棚林

column2: Deep in the poplar wood is a flat clearing dug with rows of shallow pits, each with a low wall around it, as if a great many people once wintered here. Now a sounder of wild boar has taken it over, rooting the ground into craters and charging anyone who comes near. Across a fork in an old poplar lies a beam covered in tally marks.
column3: 胡杨林深处有一片平地，地上挖着一排排浅坑，坑边垒着矮墙，像是有很多人在这里过过冬。如今一群野猪占了这里，拱得满地是坑，见人就冲。一棵老胡杨的树杈上，横担着一根刻满了道道的木梁。

column2: The boar are driven deep into the woods. You take down the beam. It holds a whole winter's work account, carved stroke by stroke: 'Stone carried, three thousand loads. Plaster laid, nine hundred zhang. Walkway built, seventy zhang. Cave ceilings repaired, eleven.' Signed 'Qianli caravan, camel train'. There are three hundred pits. That winter the three hundred slept here and worked on the cliff by day.
column3: 野猪被赶进了林子深处。你们取下那根木梁，上面是一冬天的工账，刻得一笔一画：「运石三千担，抹泥九百丈，修栈道七十丈，补窟顶十一处。」落款「千里号驼队」。坑一共三百个，那年冬天，三百人就睡在这里，白天上崖干活。

column2: Mirror Wood
column3: 挂镜林

column2: Flashes wink through the poplar wood: bronze mirrors hang in the branches, some the size of pot lids, some palm-sized. A troop of Gold Mask crossbowmen in the wood is angling them at the sun and flashing toward the mountain, flash and pause, signalling up the cliff that someone's coming. Spotting you, they flash faster and raise their crossbows.
column3: 胡杨林里一闪一闪的，树杈上挂着一面面铜镜，大的像锅盖，小的像巴掌。一队金面弩手守在林子里，拿镜子对着太阳往山上晃，一晃一停，是在给崖上报信：有人来了。他们看见了你们，镜子晃得更急了，弩也抬了起来。

column2: The crossbowmen withdraw. Liaozhang takes down a small mirror and turns it over to read the inscription: 'Made by the Kang family of Sogdiana.' 'This is that cartload of mirrors the Qianli caravan brought,' he says. 'They were meant to bounce light into the caves so people could see the murals. Master's been using them for signals.' He tucks it into his robe. 'I'll keep it. It may come in handy.'
column3: 弩手们退走了，了账摘下一面小镜子，翻过来看背面的铭文：「粟特康氏造」。「这是千里号送来的那一车镜子，」他说，「本来是给窟里引光照壁画的，师父拿它们报信了。」他把镜子揣进怀里：「留着，说不定用得上。」

column2: The Exorcists
column3: 驱鬼班

column2: The village below the cliff is haunted by a 'chisel ghost': every midnight the clink of a chisel sounds inside the cliff, and the next day there's a fresh patch of plaster on the rock. A troupe of shamanic exorcists has turned up, taken the whole village's money and stacked a great pile of firewood at the cliff foot, meaning to smoke the ghost out. The villagers don't know whether to stop them.
column3: 崖下的村子闹「凿鬼」：每到半夜，崖里就传出叮叮的凿石声，第二天崖上就多一块新补的泥。一伙跳大神的驱鬼班子跑来，收了全村的钱，在崖下堆了一大垛柴火，说要放火把崖里的鬼熏出来。村民拦也不是，不拦也不是。

column2: The exorcists scattered and the woodpile taken apart, you climb up to look at the ghost's repairs: wooden wedges driven into the cracks, mud smoothed over them, fingerprints pressed in by a big rough human hand, and beside them, as always, a little scratched camel. An old villager grumbles, 'What ghost works that hard? Ten years of patching.'
column3: 驱鬼班子被打散，柴火堆拆了。你们攀上去看那些「鬼补」的地方：裂缝里楔着木楔，外头抹着泥，泥上压着指印，是一只粗大的人手，指印旁边照例刻着一只小骆驼。村里一个老汉嘟囔：「哪有鬼这么勤快，补了十年。」

column2: The Tofu Shop
column3: 豆腐坊

column2: A tofu shop by the road: stone quern, big cauldron, a row of wooden pressing frames. A band of deserters has moved in and makes the tofu woman curdle batch after batch, eating it as fast as she makes it. In a month they've eaten the whole village's winter soybeans. Any more and she'll be feeding them the dregs.
column3: 路边一家豆腐坊，石磨、大锅、一排压豆腐的木框。一伙开了小差的兵痞占了作坊，天天逼着豆腐娘子点豆腐，点出来就吃，吃完了再点，一个月吃掉了全村一冬的黄豆。豆腐娘子说再吃下去，就只能拿豆渣喂他们了。

column2: The deserters run out, the tofu woman breathes again and the quern turns. Douzi, she tells you, was found nine years ago by Master Shouzhou in a sack of beans at the porridge shed; hence the name, which means Little Bean. A few days ago Douzi came by heading east with a bag of soybeans on his back. 'He said he'd drop beans all the way, so Master could find him if he turned back, and he could find Master.'
column3: 兵痞被撵走，豆腐娘子长出一口气，石磨又转了起来。她说豆子那孩子，是九年前守粥师父在粥棚的豆子袋里捡到的，所以叫豆子。前几天豆子路过这里，背着一袋黄豆往东走，「说是一路撒豆子，师父回头就能找着他，他回头也能找着师父」。

column2: Under the deserters' bedding you find twelve pounds of cured meat, three crocks of pickled cabbage, a stolen iron wok, seven looted sheepskin coats, and the tofu woman's bag of brine. They'd locked even her curdling salts away so she couldn't run.
column3: 兵痞们的铺盖底下抄出十二斤腊肉、三坛酸菜、一口偷来的铁锅、七件抢来的皮袄，还有一包豆腐娘子的卤水，他们怕她跑了，连点豆腐的卤都锁了起来。

column2: Every time you pass, the tofu woman brings out a pot of hot bean curd with a spoonful of chilli on top and wraps up sheets of dried tofu skin for you. 'Soak them on the road and they're ready. Softer than hard rations.'
column3: 每次路过，豆腐娘子都端出一锅热豆花，浇一勺辣子，再给你们包几张晾干的豆腐皮：「路上泡水就能吃，比干粮软和。」

column2: The Cliff Rules
column3: 崖规牌

column2: A board at the cliff foot lists five rules: '1. No splashing water at the foot of the cliff. 2. No fires in the caves. 3. No going on the walkways on days when the west wind blows. 4. If you hear chiselling inside the cliff at night, don't answer and don't go to look. 5. If you see a camel on the cliff, give way to it.' A troop of Gold Mask crossbowmen guards the board and looses an arrow at anyone who breaks a rule. Today some drunken traders are bent on testing it and are sloshing buckets of water up the rock.
column3: 崖脚立着一块木牌，上面写着五条规矩：「一、崖下不许泼水。二、窟里不许生火。三、刮西风的日子不许上栈道。四、夜里听见崖里有凿石声，不要应，也不要去看。五、看见崖上有骆驼，给它让路。」一队金面弩手守着木牌，谁犯一条就放一箭。今天几个醉醺醺的商贩偏要试试，拎着水桶往崖上泼。

column2: Traders and crossbowmen gone, an old stonemason explains. The cliff is conglomerate, pebbles and sand held together by clay and lime, so carving it is like slicing jelly; but once water seeps in, the glue softens and a wall can crumble. Smoke blackens the murals. The west wind drives sand that scours a layer off the face every time it blows. As for the chiselling and the camel, the old man smiles. 'That's a man who lives up on the cliff.'
column3: 商贩和弩手都散了，老石匠给你们讲：这崖是砾岩，卵石和沙子靠泥和石灰胶在一起，凿窟像切冻糕；可水一渗，胶就化，墙说酥就酥。烟熏黑壁画。西风卷沙，一刮就磨掉一层崖面。至于凿石声和骆驼，老石匠笑了：「那是崖上的一个人。」

column2: Reed Fence Ridge
column3: 苇篱梁

column2: On the sand ridge at the edge of the wood stand rows of reed fences, rank after rank like the teeth of a comb, keeping the sand blown from the west off the top of the cliff. A camel dealer's hands are pulling them up and bundling the reeds for camel fodder. They've cleared a large patch, and sand is already trickling through the gap toward the clifftop.
column3: 林边的沙梁上插着一道道芦苇篱笆，一排接一排，像梳子的齿，把西边刮来的沙挡在崖顶外面。一伙驼贩子的伙计正在拔篱笆，把芦苇捆成捆喂骆驼，拔了一大片，沙子已经顺着缺口往崖顶上流了。

column2: The camel hands chased off, you plant the reeds back bundle by bundle. Buried at the foot of a post is a small wooden tag: 'Winter of Dingwei. Twelve reed fences set by the Qianli caravan. Keep the sand off the cliff and it won't crush the cave roofs.' The posts are old but the reeds are new. Someone replaces them every year.
column3: 驼贩子的伙计被打跑，你们把芦苇一捆捆插了回去。篱笆桩子底下埋着一块小木牌：「丁未冬，千里号扎苇篱十二道。沙不上崖，窟顶不压。」桩子是旧的，芦苇却是新的，有人年年来换。

column2: Oil Camel Road
column3: 油驼道

column2: A string of camels kneels by the road, two oil jars slung on each. Their driver is a bandit boy of ten or so, his face caked in sand. A gang of oil thieves surrounds the train, unloading the jars one by one: lamp oil is precious, a jar will buy a sheep. The boy clings to one jar and won't let go, shouting, 'This is the King's, for the caves!'
column3: 路边卧着一排骆驼，每峰驮着两只油罐，赶驼的是个十来岁的小马贼，一脸的沙。一伙盗油贼围着驼队，正把油罐一只只卸下来：灯油金贵，一罐能换一头羊。小马贼抱着一只罐子不撒手，喊着：「这是王给千佛洞的！」

column2: The oil thieves chased off, the boy wipes his nose. Every jar's clay seal is pressed with a lopsided character, King. Liaozhang knows it at once: the King of the Sand Sea, who paid ten years of the Qianli caravan's lamp oil. The King's leg hurts this year and he couldn't travel, the boy says, so he sent him. 'The King said deliver it to the lamp, watch it lit, then come home.'
column3: 盗油贼被打跑，小马贼抹了一把鼻涕。每只油罐的封泥上都按着一个歪歪扭扭的「王」字，了账一眼就认了出来：沙海里那个替千里号还了十年灯油的王。小马贼说王今年腿疼，走不动了，派他送来，「王说，送到灯跟前，看着它点上，再回去」。

column2: Lamp Keeper's Path
column3: 守灯径

column2: A path leads to an old meditation hut at the foot of the hill, home of the temple's oldest monk, called the Lamp Elder. A troop of Gold Mask swordsmen guards the path: by the Lord's orders, the Lamp Elder is not to be disturbed. But the bandit boy's oil must be delivered to the lamp, and Liaozhang has things to say to the Elder. The guards won't give an inch. 'The Elder is ill. He can't see anyone.'
column3: 一条小径通往山脚的一座老禅房，禅房里住着寺里最老的和尚，人称灯公。一队金面刀卫守着小径，洞主有令，谁也不许打扰灯公。可小马贼的油要送到灯跟前，了账的话要说给灯公听，刀卫们一步不让：「灯公病了，见不得人。」

column2: The swordsmen beaten back, their leader sighs. 'Every day lately the Elder asks: has anyone come from the Sand Sea? We didn't dare answer.' Liaozhang's eyes redden. The Lamp Elder is his master's master; it was he who lent the Qianli caravan its lamp oil ten years ago. The guard steps aside. 'Go in. You're the ones he's been waiting for.'
column3: 刀卫们被打退，领头的叹了口气：「灯公这几天天天问一句：沙海那边，来人了没有？我们不敢答。」了账一听，眼圈就红了：灯公是他师父的师父，十年前借给千里号灯油的就是他。刀卫让开了路，说：「进去吧。他等的就是你们。」

column2: Winch Camp
column3: 绞盘营

column2: A big camp at the foot of the hills, and at its centre a huge wooden windlass whose thick rope runs all the way to the clifftop; it once hoisted timber and stone. Mercenaries, foot, crossbow and horse, have taken it over and use it to haul their loot up into an empty cave they treat as a warehouse. The windlass squeals and groans, and the rope is nearly worn through.
column3: 山脚扎着一座大营，营中间立着一架巨大的木绞盘，粗绳一直通到崖顶，从前是往崖上吊木料和石料的。一伙雇佣兵占了这里，步、弩、骑都有，拿绞盘把抢来的货往崖上的空窟里吊，当成了他们的仓库。绞盘吱吱嘎嘎地转，绳子磨得快断了。

column2: The mercenaries scattered, you replace the fraying rope. Carved on the windlass axle: 'Made by Lao Zao. Turned by the three hundred of the Qianli caravan.' Beside it, smaller, as if added later: 'One man can't turn it. Three hundred can.' Lao Zao, the local masons say, means Old Chisel, a master carver who has repaired caves all his life and now lives down a dead end at the foot of the hills. 'Harder-headed than stone.'
column3: 雇佣兵被打散，你们换下了快断的绳子。绞盘的轴上刻着一行字：「老凿造，千里号三百人共推。」旁边还有一行小的，像是后来补的：「一人推不动，三百人推得动。」附近的石匠说，老凿是修了一辈子窟的老匠头，如今住在山脚的死胡同里，「脾气比石头还硬」。

column2: Bean-Pickers' Camp
column3: 拾豆营

column2: Deserters are camped by the road, and one of them sits counting soybeans out of a bowl. Qian Mancang hired them to find Master Shouzhou; they have a portrait of the monk that looks like a winter melon. They spotted the beans scattered along the road and have been picking them up as they follow, getting closer all the time. Seeing you also looking at the beans on the ground, they think you're after their reward.
column3: 一伙逃兵扎营在路边，营里一个人捧着一碗黄豆，一颗颗地数。他们是钱满仓雇来找守粥师父的，手里有一张和尚的画像，画得像个冬瓜。他们发现了路上撒的豆子，一路捡过来，越捡越近，见你们也盯着地上的豆子，以为是来抢功的。

column2: The deserters scattered, the bean counter confesses. The trail ran to the mouth of a gully in the east, where they caught a little novice and handed him to Qian Mancang's men. 'Use the little one as bait and the big one will come out by himself.' He gives you the bowl of beans. 'Picked up three hundred and some. Didn't eat a single one.'
column3: 逃兵被打散，数豆子的那个交代：豆子一路撒到了东边的沟口，他们在沟口逮住了一个小沙弥，交给了钱满仓的人，「说是拿小的当饵，大的自己会出来」。他把那碗豆子还给你们：「捡了三百多颗，一颗没吃。」

column2: Porridge-Raised Slope
column3: 喝粥坡

column2: The road over the slope is blocked by a pack of half-grown lads on stolen camels, with knives they found and faces not yet finished growing. They're orphans raised on the Qianli porridge. Now that it costs money they can't afford it, so they've taken up robbery. Their leader is sixteen or seventeen, and when he shouts 'Pay the toll!' his breaking voice cracks.
column3: 坡上拦路的是一伙半大小子，骑着偷来的骆驼，刀是捡来的，脸还没长开。他们都是在千里粥棚喝粥长大的孤儿，粥要了钱，他们喝不起，就学人劫道。领头的十六七岁，喊「留下买路钱」的时候嗓子还在变声，喊劈了。

column2: Knocked off their camels, the lads take it well, and when they hear the porridge is free again their eyes light up. Master Shouzhou taught them to read, the leader says, from the names on the bottoms of those three hundred bowls. 'The first character I learned was Cao.' They swear to go back and guard the shed's door, and say that last month they saw Master Shouzhou heading for the eastern gully with an empty sack on his back.
column3: 小子们被打下骆驼，倒也服气，听说粥棚又不要钱了，眼睛都亮了。领头的说守粥师父教他们认字，就是照着那三百只木碗底下的名字认的，「我认的头一个字是『曹』」。他们发誓回去替粥棚看门，又说上个月看见守粥师父背着空袋子往东沟去了。

column2: Lamps Out Cave
column3: 灭灯窟

column2: In a row of caves at the foot of the hill, Gold Mask swordsmen are pinching out the oil lamps pilgrims have lit, one after another, and taking away the bowls. The pilgrims kneel outside weeping: lamps that have burned for a decade and more, snuffed just like that. The guards explain nothing, only pinch, cave after cave, until at the last one a few pilgrims link hands across the door: 'Not this one. You can't put this one out!'
column3: 山脚一排窟里，金面刀卫正一盏盏地掐灭香客点的油灯，掐完了还把灯碗收走。香客们跪在窟外哭，说十几年的长明灯，说灭就灭了。刀卫不解释，只是掐，一窟接一窟，掐到最后一窟门口，几个香客手拉手堵在门上：「这一盏，你们不能灭！」

column2: The swordsmen withdraw and Liaozhang explains to the pilgrims for them.
