Lamp smoke blackens murals; ten years of it turns a whole cave of Buddhas black-faced, which is why his master ordered the lamps out. In that last cave burns the Qianli caravan's lamp, the one lamp the Lord forbids anyone to put out. The pilgrims disperse at last, one murmuring, 'The Lord's hard-hearted, but soft about that lamp.'
column3: 刀卫们退了，了账替他们给香客们讲：灯烟熏黑了壁画，一窟的佛十年就熏成了黑脸，师父才下令灭灯。最后那一窟里点的，是千里号的灯，洞主唯独不许灭它。香客们这才散了，有人小声说：「洞主心狠，灯倒留得心软。」

column2: The Lapis Tent
column3: 青金帐

column2: An indigo tent belongs to a Sogdian woman who sells lapis lazuli, brought from mountains thousands of miles west and ground into the costliest blue on any mural. A gang of soldier-thugs surrounds her tent insisting her stones are dyed and must be 'confiscated for inspection'. She sits inside without moving, turning a blue stone in her fingers. 'I'll sell to whoever can tell real from fake.'
column3: 一顶靛蓝色的帐篷，帐主是个粟特女商，卖的是青金石：从西边几千里外的山里运来，磨成粉就是壁画上最贵的蓝。一伙兵痞围着她的帐篷，非说她的石头是染的，要「没收验货」。女商人坐在帐里纹丝不动，手里转着一块蓝石头：「谁认得出真假，我就卖给谁。」

column2: With the thugs chased off she's cheerful enough. 'The real stone has gold flecks in it, like the night sky.' She opens for trade. Ten years ago, she says, the Qianli caravan bought a big bag of lapis from her to paint a cave ceiling: 'a real blue sky over three hundred heads'. And an old painter called Wu has come by several times, couldn't afford it, only touched the stones and left. 'Next time he comes, I'll give it him on credit.'
column3: 兵痞被打跑，女商人倒也爽快：「真货里有金星，像夜里的天。」她开了张，跟你们换货。她说十年前千里号在她这里买过一大袋青金，要给一座窟画顶，「三百个人头顶上，要一片真的蓝天」。姓吴的老画匠来过好几回，买不起，摸一摸就走，「下回来，我赊给他」。

column2: The Seeping Cave
column3: 渗水窟

column2: In a small cave at the foot of the hill the murals are peeling away flake by flake: the ceiling is seeping, water runs down the walls, and the painted apsaras are about to lose their faces. A few mural peelers are taking advantage, pasting wet felt onto the wall: 'It's falling off anyway, might as well peel it and sell it.' Their hired toughs stand at the entrance telling everyone it's a 'rescue'.
column3: 山脚一个小窟里，壁画正一片片往下剥：窟顶在渗水，水顺着墙往下流，画上的飞天眼看就要没了脸。几个揭壁贼趁机拿湿毡子往墙上糊，说「反正要掉，不如我们揭了卖」。他们雇了几个打手守在窟口，谁来都说是在「抢救」。

column2: The peelers driven off, you climb above the cave to find where the water comes from. On the clifftop is a dug drainage channel, its mouth choked with sand and dead grass, so rain pools on top and seeps down bit by bit. A stone by the channel is carved 'Dug by the Qianli caravan'. You clear it, and the cave stops dripping. That winter the caravan mended more than walkways.
column3: 揭壁贼被赶走，你们爬上窟顶找漏水的来处：崖顶上有一道挖出来的排水沟，沟口被沙和枯草堵死了，雨水积在顶上，一点点往下渗。沟边的石头上刻着「千里号挖」。你们清开了沟，窟里不滴水了。千里号那年冬天修的，不光是栈道。

column2: Brothers' Slope
column3: 师兄坡

column2: A row of Gold Mask riders stands on the slope, and at the sight of Liaozhang a few of their leaders laugh behind their masks. 'Little brother Liaozhang! Back from collecting debts?' They were all monks of the temple who took off their robes with their master and became Gold Masks. Laugh as they may, the Lord's order is still the order, and they turn their horses across the slope. 'Little brother, no getting past without a fight.'
column3: 坡上站着一排金面骑卫，领头的几个一见了账，面具后面就笑出了声：「了账师弟，讨债讨回来了？」他们原来都是寺里的和尚，跟着师父脱了袈裟当了金面卫。笑归笑，洞主的令还是令，他们横马拦在坡上：「师弟，不打一场，你过不去。」

column2: Knocked off their horses, the brothers rub their backs and roar with laughter. Seven years ago that night, they say, their master stood in the Qianli Cave until dawn, then came out, folded his robe and laid it before the Buddha. 'He said a keeper who can't keep the caves isn't fit to wear it.' And the Lamp Elder is nearly gone, they add. 'Go, little brother. He has something in his hand he's waiting to give to whoever comes from the Sand Sea.'
column3: 师兄们被打下了马，揉着腰哈哈大笑。他们说七年前那一夜，师父在千里窟里站了一宿，天亮出来，把袈裟叠好放在了佛前，「师父说，守窟的守不住窟，不配穿这身衣服」。他们又说灯公快不行了：「去吧，师弟，他手里有样东西，等着交给沙海来的人。」

column2: The Walkway Foot
column3: 栈脚营

column2: A long plank walkway climbs from the foot of the cliff to its waist, and at its base camps a company of Gold Mask riders, horses tethered in a row, men posted at the bottom step. They let no one up the walkway and let no one take it apart. A few days ago a timber merchant came to measure the wood and they threw him, ruler and all, into the river.
column3: 一道长长的栈道从崖脚一直攀到崖腰，栈道脚下扎着一营金面骑卫，马拴了一排，人守在台阶口。他们不许任何人上栈道，也不许任何人拆栈道，前些天有个木材商想来量量木头，被他们连人带尺子扔进了河里。

column2: The riders beaten back, their leader holds his arm and says: 'Those three hundred camel men built this walkway. The Lord says while it stands, they'll have a road when they come back.' He jerks his chin at the cliff's waist. 'A man lives up there. The Lord won't let us touch him, or let anyone else. Whatever he asks for, we send up.'
column3: 骑卫们被打退，领头的捂着胳膊说：「这条栈道是那三百个驼夫修的。洞主说，栈道在，他们回来就有路走。」他朝崖腰努努嘴：「上面住着一个人，洞主不让我们碰他，也不让别人碰他。他要什么，我们就往上送什么。」

column2: The Lamp Elder's Cell
column3: 灯公禅房

column2: The cell is tiny: a straw mat and a lamp, its bowl carved with the character Qian, its flame the size of a bean, unextinguished for ten years. The Lamp Elder lies on the mat, a hundred and eight years old, thin as a dry twig. But outside is no peace. Sutra thieves have heard the Elder holds a pill 'that lets a man live his life over' and have come over the wall; their knives are already at the door.
column3: 禅房很小，一张草席，一盏灯，灯碗上刻着一个「千」字，火苗只有豆大，十年没熄过。灯公躺在席上，一百零八岁，瘦得像一截枯枝。可禅房外不太平：一伙盗经贼听说灯公手里有一颗「能让人重活一世」的丹，翻墙进了院子，刀已经抵在了门上。

column2: The thieves chased off, the bandit boy pours the King's oil into the lamp bowl and the flame leaps bright. The Lamp Elder opens his eyes and draws from under his pillow a small wooden box holding a recipe and a dark red pill: the Rebirth Pill. A lifetime of refining produced only three. One he couldn't bring himself to take. One he offered to the Qianli caravan's bookkeeper, who refused: 'This life's labour isn't over yet. I need my skills to finish the accounts.' 'It washes away a lifetime's toil and keeps a lifetime's skill,' the Elder says. 'It lets one who has reached the end walk the road again from the beginning, and walk it better.' He gives the box to Liaozhang and nods toward you. The lamp is full. The Elder closes his eyes as if falling asleep, and does not wake.
column3: 盗经贼被赶走，小马贼把王的油添进灯碗，火苗一下子亮了。灯公睁开眼，从枕下摸出一只小木匣，匣里是一张丹方和一颗暗红的丹：转世丹。他炼了一辈子，只成三颗：一颗他自己没舍得吃，一颗给过千里号的账房，账房没要，说「我这一世的劳苦还没完，本事还要留着算账」。「它能洗去一世的劳苦，留下一世的本事，」灯公说，「让走到头的人，从头再走一遍，走得比上回好。」他把匣子交给了了账，又指了指你们。灯油添满了，灯公闭上眼，像是睡着了，再没醒来。

column2: Rubbing Cliff
column3: 拓碑崖

column2: An inscription is carved on the rock at the foot of the hill, and a few rubbing thieves are dabbing ink pads onto paper over it, a sheet to sell for every sheet they take, with hired swordsmen keeping watch. To get sharper rubbings they've been picking out the grooves with knives, deeper each time, and flakes of rock skin keep falling.
column3: 山脚的崖壁上刻着一方题记，几个拓碑贼正拿墨包往纸上拍，拓一张卖一张，生怕拓坏了，还雇了一伙刀手在边上望风。为了拓得清楚，他们把题记上的石缝全用刀剔了一遍，越剔越深，石皮一块块往下掉。

column2: The rubbing thieves chased off, the inscription is saved. It reads: 'Winter of Dingwei. Three hundred of the Qianli camel train repaired the cliff here. Master mason: Lao Zao. Cao San, camel driver, fell from the walkway and broke his leg. Unable to travel, he stays on the mountain.' It's the bookkeeper's hand, every stroke precise. The last line is cut shallower: 'Those who stay behind are Qianli too.'
column3: 拓碑贼被赶走，题记总算保住了。你们读下来：「丁未冬，千里号驼队三百人修崖于此，匠头老凿。驼户曹三，坠栈折腿，不能行，留山。」字是账房的字，一笔不苟。最后一行刻得浅一些：「留下的也是千里号的人。」

column2: Goat Track
column3: 羊肠道

column2: At the mouth of the eastern gully the track narrows to the width of a goat. Qian Mancang's remaining toughs wait here for Master Shouzhou to come down: tripropes stretched across the path, rocks piled on the cliff above, the men crouched out of the wind gnawing dry flatbread. In the cracks of the rocks by the path, a few soybeans are wedged.
column3: 东沟口的山道窄得只容一只羊过，钱满仓剩下的打手守在这里，等着守粥师父从山上下来。他们在路上拉了绊马索，崖上堆了石头，自己蹲在背风处啃干饼。路边的石缝里，卡着几颗黄豆。

column2: The toughs are driven off the track. Following the beans in the cracks upward, you find behind a boulder a rosary of dried beans, the twin of the one on the hermitage door frame, its string half broken. The beans lead on into the gully, more and more sparsely, as if whoever was dropping them had started to run short.
column3: 打手们被赶下了山道。你们顺着石缝里的豆子往上找，在一块大石头背面捡到一串念珠，是干豆子编的，和守粥庵门框上那串一模一样，只是绳子断了一半。豆子一路往沟里去，越撒越稀，像是撒的人舍不得了。

column2: The Bait Post
column3: 饵僧桩

column2: Tied to a dead poplar at the mouth of the gully is a little novice of eight or nine, an empty bowl in front of him with a chopstick stuck upright in it: Qian Mancang's men call it the 'summoning bowl'. Master Shouzhou loves his pupil, so when he sees it he'll surely come down. The novice isn't crying. He's reciting the Heart Sutra at his guards, and at every line a guard covers his ears.
column3: 沟口一棵枯胡杨上绑着个八九岁的小沙弥，面前摆着一只空碗，碗里插了一根筷子，是钱满仓的人摆的「招魂碗」，说守粥师父心疼徒弟，看见了准下山。小沙弥倒不哭，正冲着看守的打手背《心经》，背一句，打手就捂一回耳朵。

column2: The guards chased off, you untie the rope and the novice rubs his wrists and introduces himself. 'I'm Douzi. I'm looking for my master.' From his robe he pulls a flat bean bag with seven beans left in it. Before he left, Master said, 'The grain comes from the east, so you look for people in the east too.' He won't go back. 'If you won't take me, I'll go by myself.'
column3: 看守被打跑，你们解开绳子，小沙弥揉着手腕自报家门：「我叫豆子，我找师父。」他从怀里掏出一个瘪了的豆袋，里面只剩七颗豆子。他说师父临走前讲过，「粮是从东边来的，人也要往东边找」，他不肯回去：「你们不带我，我自己走。」

column2: The Ageing Workshop
column3: 做旧坊

column2: Hundreds of yellowed sutra scrolls hang drying in a courtyard. A few copyists, shackled at the ankle, copy sutras day and night; the finished scrolls are soaked in tea, smoked, trodden underfoot and turned into 'ancient sutras' centuries old, to be sold to collectors inside the Pass. Toughs guard the yard, and the overseer checks against a genuine scroll: 'One wrong character, one finger off.'
column3: 一座院子里晾着几百张发黄的经卷，几个抄经生被锁着脚，日夜抄经，抄完了用茶水泡、用烟熏、拿脚踩，做成几百年前的「古经」，卖给关内的收藏家。看院子的是一伙打手，监工拿着一卷真经对照，说「错一个字，剁一根指头」。

column2: The toughs chased off, the copyists' shackles are struck off. Liaozhang studies the overseer's 'genuine' scroll: it was stolen from the temple's library cave. The oldest copyist says there's a remarkable sutra in the library cave, one the Qianli three hundred copied that winter, a section each, bound into one. 'Good hands and bad, but not one wrong character.' The library cave is down by the river.
column3: 打手被打跑，抄经生们卸了镣。了账捧着监工那卷「真经」看了半天，说这是藏经洞里被盗出来的。最老的抄经生说，藏经洞里还有一部了不得的经，是千里号三百人那年冬天一人抄一段合成的，「字有好有坏，可一个字都不错」。藏经洞就在河边。

column2: Red Earth Slope
column3: 红土坡

column2: A hillside as red as a fresh-butchered ox: grab a handful of earth and it stains your hand. A gang of kiln bosses has taken the slope, digging the red earth for bricks, riddling it with pits and selling the bricks across the district. At the bottom, a white-bearded old man with empty paint baskets on a carrying pole has argued with them for three days for one small basket of the reddest earth, and been kicked back down for his pains.
column3: 一面山坡红得像刚宰了牛，坡上的土抓一把能把手染红。一伙窑霸占了这面坡，挖红土烧砖，挖得坡上全是大坑，烧出来的砖卖到四乡。坡下一个白胡子老头挑着空颜料担子，跟窑霸们磨了三天嘴皮，只想要一小筐最红的土，被一脚踹了回来。

column2: The kiln bosses chased off, the old man kneels on the slope sorting earth: a handful, rub it between his fingers. Red earth is earth with iron in it, he says; iron rusts red, and the truest layer, on a cheek, looks like a man who's had a drink. He gives his name: Wu Banbi, the painter of Half Wall village. He means to restore the three hundred faces scraped from the caves. 'I've got the red. I still need green, and white.' Hugging his basket of earth, he comes along with you.
column3: 窑霸被赶跑，老头跪在坡上挑土，挑一捧，捻一捻。他说土红是含铁的土，铁一锈就红，最正的那一层，抹在脸颊上像喝了酒。他报了名字：吴半壁，半壁村的画匠，要把千佛洞里被刮掉的三百张脸补回来，「红有了，还差绿、差白」。他抱着那筐土，跟着你们走了。

column2: The Library Cave
column3: 藏经洞

column2: At the foot of the cliff by the river is an unremarkable opening, rooms within rooms: the place where the caves keep their scriptures. The open ground outside used to be where the temple traded with the world: it needs timber for casting bells and mending statues, and pays in old bronze melted down. Now sutra thieves hold the entrance and are ransacking the inside, and all trade outside has stopped. The innermost chamber is pitch black; even with torches they can't see, and they're about to light a fire 'for a bit of light'.
column3: 河边的崖脚有一个不起眼的洞口，里头一层套一层，是千佛洞藏经的地方。洞外一片空地，从前是寺里和山外换货的地方：寺里铸钟、修佛要木料，就拿化了的旧铜器跟山外换。如今一伙盗经贼占了洞口，在里面翻箱倒柜，洞外的买卖也全断了。最里面一间黑漆漆的，他们点着火把也看不清，正要放一把火「照个亮」。

column2: The thieves driven out, trade starts again outside: timber comes in by the cartload and goes out as the temple's bronze. Liaozhang takes out the bronze mirror and catches the sun at the entrance, and a beam strikes into the innermost chamber and lights a whole wall. It is covered in accounts in ink, from the Pass through the Sand Sea to here, every debt and to whom and every repayment. The last passage is in the bookkeeper's hand: 'Thousand Buddha Caves: lamp oil borrowed, three hundred jin. One sutra borrowed. One seal pledged. All the road's accounts are reconciled to this point, save one cart, whereabouts unknown. Until this cart is cleared the books will not balance. Inquire at the Oasis King's city.' The strokes are heavy, as if the writer had pressed until the brush broke.
column3: 盗经贼被赶出了洞，洞外又做起了买卖：木料一车车拉进来，换走寺里的铜。了账掏出那面铜镜，对着洞口的太阳一照，一束光打进最里间，照亮了一整面墙：墙上是用墨写的账，从出关、沙海一路记到这里，每一笔欠了谁、还了谁。最后一段是账房的字：「千佛洞：借灯油三百斤，借经一部，押印一方。诸路之账，至此对毕，独差一车，不知落在何处。此车不清，账不能合。往绿洲王城问。」字写得很重，像是写的人把笔按断了。

column2: The Chisel Den
column3: 赌凿坊

column2: A stone hut at the foot of the hill rings with shouting: a crowd of stonemasons playing dice, staking their own chisels. The bank is run by card sharps from out of town with loaded dice, and the masons have lost everything but their hands. The sharps' hired muscle stands at the door, and anyone who wants to buy back his chisel gets a beating first.
column3: 山脚一间石屋里吆五喝六，一群石匠围着桌子赌骰子，押的是自己的凿子。坐庄的是几个外地来的老千，骰子灌了铅，石匠们输得只剩一双手。门口站着老千雇的打手，谁想把凿子赎回去，就先挨一顿揍。

column2: The sharps and their muscle thrown out, every chisel goes back to its owner. The masons blush scarlet. They're all Lao Zao's apprentices; the master's been ill for half a year and with no one keeping them in line they went bad. That winter the Qianli three hundred learned to work the cliff from him. 'Master said three hundred amateurs did the work of three hundred masons.' Lao Zao lives at the very end of the dead end at the foot of the hill.
column3: 老千和打手被撵走，凿子物归原主。石匠们臊得满脸通红，说他们都是老凿的徒弟，师父病了大半年，没人管着，就学坏了。那年冬天千里号三百人跟着师父学凿崖，「师父说，三百个门外汉，干出了三百个匠人的活」。老凿住在山脚最里头的死胡同里。

column2: Walkway Gate
column3: 栈道口

column2: A stone gate has been built across the way to the broken-cliff walkway, held by the toughest troop of Gold Masks: swordsmen in the gateway, crossbowmen up on the rock, riders patrolling outside. They aren't guarding against outsiders. A man lives on the walkway beyond, and by the Lord's order he doesn't come down and nobody goes up. On the lintel someone has drawn a little camel in charcoal.
column3: 通往断崖栈道的路口筑了一道石门，金面卫最硬的一队守在这里，刀卫堵门，弩手上了崖，骑卫在门外来回巡。他们守的不是外敌：门内的栈道上住着一个人，洞主有令，他不下来，别人也不许上去。门楣上有人用炭画了一只小骆驼。

column2: The Gold Masks give way and you look up. The walkway on the cliff's waist is broken into several stretches, and on the highest one stands a man on a crutch with an old lame camel lying beside him. He sees your banner and stands stunned a long moment, then bellows down: 'What flag is that? Come closer, let me see it properly!'
column3: 金面卫让开了石门，你们抬头往上看：崖腰的栈道断成了好几截，最高的一截上站着一个拄拐的汉子，身边卧着一峰瘸腿的老骆驼。他看见你们的旗子，愣了好半天，扯着嗓子往下喊：「打的什么旗？走近点，让我看清楚！」

column2: Driftwood Bend
column3: 漂木湾

column2: The Dangquan river bends here, and timber floating down from upstream jams in the bend. The latest arrivals are squared elm beams, and a gang of river bullies has hooked them all ashore: 'What's in the river belongs to whoever catches it.' They're splitting them for firewood. An old raftsman on the bank slaps his thighs in despair: 'Those are for the walkway!'
column3: 宕泉河在这里拐了个弯，上游漂下来的木头都卡在湾里。最近漂下来的是一批削好的榆木梁，一伙河霸用长钩子把木头全捞上岸，说是「河里的东西谁捞归谁」，正劈了当柴烧。湾边一个放木排的老汉急得直拍大腿：「那是给栈道上送的！」

column2: The bullies driven into the river, the old man lashes the remaining beams into a raft. Each is carved: 'For the walkway. Deliver to Cao.' The Lord pays for this timber, the raftsman says, and every autumn a batch is floated down from upstream for the man on the walkway to mend it with. Ten years, never missed. 'The Lord,' he says, 'is hard on the living and kind to timber.'
column3: 河霸被赶下河去，老汉把剩下的木梁捆成排。每根梁上都刻着几个字：「送栈道，交曹。」老汉说这木头是洞主出钱买的，年年秋天从上游放一批下来，栈道上那人拿去修栈，十年没断过。「洞主那人，」老汉说，「对活人凶，对木头好。」

column2: Camel Thieves' Slope
column3: 牵驼坡

column2: A big gang of camel thieves, foot, crossbow and horse, surrounds an old lame camel on the slope, hauling at its halter and whipping it. Every day the camel comes down the cliff to drink at the river and climbs back up to the walkway on its own; today they've cornered it. The old camel plants all four feet and spits a faceful into the chief thief's eyes.
column3: 山坡上一大伙偷骆驼的贼，步、弩、骑都有，围着一峰瘸了腿的老骆驼，又拽缰绳又抽鞭子。那骆驼每天下崖到河边喝水，喝完自己再爬回栈道，今天被他们堵住了。老骆驼四蹄钉在地上，冲着贼头喷了一脸口水。

column2: The thieves chased off, the old camel shakes its neck and plods back up the cliff with you behind it. Its saddle is branded with the character Qian, and on its halter hangs a little wooden tag: 'Lao Huang. Qianli camel train. Lame, stays on the mountain to keep Cao San company.' The rule on the cliff board, 'give way to the camel', means him.
column3: 偷驼贼被打跑，老骆驼甩了甩脖子，慢吞吞地往崖上走，你们跟在后面。它的鞍子上烙着一个「千」字，缰绳上拴着一只小木牌：「老黄，千里号驼队。腿瘸，留山，与曹三作伴。」崖规牌上那条「看见骆驼给它让路」，说的就是它。

column2: Qian Mancang
column3: 钱满仓

column2: A fat monk crouches on a big rock, gold paint still not quite off his face: Qian Mancang, abbot of the Golden Body Temple. His hirelings have mostly run off, his food is long gone and he's dizzy with hunger, but he still clutches half a map to his chest. The few toughs he has left are discussing selling him and the map together to the sutra thieves.
column3: 一块大石头上蹲着一个胖和尚，脸上的金漆还没掉干净：正是金身寺的方丈钱满仓。他雇的人跑得只剩几个，干粮早吃光了，饿得两眼发直，怀里却还死死抱着半张图。剩下的几个打手正商量着，把他和图一起卖给盗经贼。

column2: With the toughs chased off, Qian Mancang slumps on the rock. Douzi fishes two beans out of his bag and pops them into the man's mouth. Qian Mancang bursts into tears. Three years ago his grain business collapsed and he survived on a month of the Qianli porridge. 'And I thought, a porridge shed this good, if only it were called Qian's.' He hands over his half of the map. 'The other half's with Shouzhou.'
column3: 打手们被打跑，钱满仓瘫在石头上。豆子从袋里摸出两颗豆子，塞进他嘴里。钱满仓哭了：三年前他的粮栈倒了，在千里粥棚喝了一个月的粥才活过来，「我就想，这么好的粥棚，要是姓钱该多好」。他把半张图交了出来：「另外半张在守粥那儿。」

column2: Broken Steps Cliff
column3: 断阶崖

column2: Counting his last beans, Douzi leads you to the foot of a cliff. A flight of steps is cut into it, broken off halfway up, and in the rubble below the break is wedged a straw sandal worn to a thin sole. Douzi knows it at once: his master's. But a pack of dholes circles the rubble, snarling over a sack of spilled grain.
column3: 豆子数着剩下的豆子领路，一直走到一道崖下。崖上凿着一溜石阶，走到半截断了，断口下面的乱石里卡着一只草鞋，鞋底磨得只剩薄薄一层。豆子一眼认出那是师父的鞋。可乱石堆边上围着一群豺狗，正为一袋撒了的粮食龇牙咧嘴。

column2: The dholes are scattered. The spilled grain is that small, hard-hulled desert-edge kind, the sack stamped with the Gold Mask's red seal. Above the break, someone has scratched a line into the rock with a stone: 'Steps broken, can't get down. Enough grain to eat. Don't worry.' Douzi scatters his last seven beans at the foot of the cliff. 'Master, I'm here.'
column3: 豺狗被赶散了。撒了的粮食是戈壁边上那种粒小壳硬的粮，袋子上盖着金面的红印。断口上方的崖壁上有人用石头划了一行字：「阶断，下不去。粮够吃。勿念。」豆子把最后七颗豆子都撒在了崖下：「师父，我来了。」

column2: The Verdigris Mine
column3: 铜绿洞

column2: Wu Banbi needs green, and he leads you to an abandoned copper mine whose entrance rocks are blotched green and blue as if with moss. A band of miners whose crew broke up has taken it over, foot, crossbow and horse, and robs travellers from here. At the sight of the colours on the walls Wu's eyes go wide, and he nearly charges in by himself.
column3: 吴半壁要找绿，领着你们来到一座废弃的铜矿，矿洞口的石头上一片片绿斑和蓝斑，像长了苔。一伙散了伙的矿工占了矿洞，步、弩、骑凑了一大帮，在这儿剪径。吴半壁一看见洞壁上的颜色，眼睛就直了，差点自己冲进去。

column2: The miners scattered, Wu throws himself at the wall and chips away. 'Malachite and azurite grow side by side. Both come from copper ore near the surface, slowly rusted out by water and air. One green, one blue, brothers.' He fills two bags: green for robes, blue for sky. 'The Qianli people wore blue coats and green robes that year. This time the colours will match.'
column3: 矿工们被打散，吴半壁扑到洞壁上一块块地敲：「石绿和石青常长在一处，都是铜矿露出地面，叫水和气慢慢锈出来的，一个绿，一个蓝，亲兄弟。」他敲了满满两袋，绿的画衣裳，蓝的画天。「千里号的人那年穿的是青衣绿袍，这回颜色对得上了。」

column2: River Bend Garden
column3: 河湾菜园

column2: A vegetable garden in the river bend, cabbage, chives and radishes bed by bed, tended by the temple for decades. Soldier-thugs have taken it, dug pits in the beds to roast sheep, use the temple's bronze chime bowl as a cooking pot, and send the old gardener to haul water from the river, eighty loads a day or no supper.
column3: 河湾里一片菜园，白菜、韭菜、萝卜一畦畦的，是寺里种了几十年的。一伙兵痞占了园子，在菜地里挖坑烤羊，拿寺里的铜磬当锅，把种菜的老园头赶到河边去挑水，一天挑八十担，挑不够不给饭吃。

column2: The thugs thrown out, the old gardener drops his carrying pole and goes to look at his chives first. Half of what this garden grows goes to the Lamp Elder's cell, he says; the Elder ate vegetarian all his life and loved nothing better than a bowl of noodles with chives. Liaozhang tells him the Elder has passed. The gardener stands frozen a long while, then cuts a handful of the tenderest chives to lay as an offering.
column3: 兵痞被撵走，老园头扔下扁担，先去看他的韭菜。他说这园子种的菜，有一半是送到灯公禅房的，灯公吃了一辈子素，最爱一碗韭菜面。了账说灯公走了，老园头愣了半天，割了一把最嫩的韭菜，说要送去供上。

column2: In the thugs' camp you find eight half-roasted sheep, twelve jars of wine (hidden in a temple garden; the gardener mutters prayers), the bronze chime bowl they used as a pot, and three cartloads of stolen firewood.
column3: 兵痞的营里抄出八只烤了一半的羊、十二坛酒（在菜园里藏酒，老园头直念佛）、一口当锅使的铜磬，还有三车偷来的柴火。

column2: Every time you pass, the old gardener pulls a basket of crisp cabbages and radishes, ties up a bundle of chives and slips in a bag of dried red dates. 'The Lamp Elder's rule: travellers get all the vegetables they want.'
column3: 每次路过，老园头都从地里拔一筐水灵灵的白菜萝卜，捆一把韭菜，再塞一包晒干的红枣：「灯公留下的规矩，过路的人，菜管够。」

column2: The Broken Cliff Walkway
column3: 断崖栈道

column2: You climb the walkway stretch by stretch, beams creaking underfoot. On the highest section the man on the crutch holds a bronze token high over his head, cast with the words 'Qianli Caravan: Camel Train'. But from the far end a band of sutra thieves has crept up; they want to use the walkway to get into the upper caves and steal sutras, and since the cripple's in their way they're hacking at the beams behind him.
column3: 你们攀上栈道，一截一截往上走，木梁在脚下咯吱响。最高那截栈道上，拄拐的汉子把一块铜牌高高举过头顶，牌上铸着「千里号·驼」四个字。可栈道另一头摸上来一伙盗经贼，他们想借这条栈道爬进上层的窟里偷经，嫌这个瘸子挡路，正拿刀砍他身后的栈道梁。

column2: With the thieves knocked off the cliff, the man lowers the token. He is Cao San. That winter, building the walkway, he fell and broke his leg. When the caravan left in spring, the bookkeeper pressed the camel train's token into his hand: 'Those who stay behind are Qianli too.' So he settled on the cliff and has mended it by night for ten years. He studies your banner and asks, 'Are they back yet?' You shake your heads. Cao San nods. 'Then I'll patch for another year.'
column3: 盗经贼被打下了崖，汉子放下铜牌：他就是曹三。那年冬天修栈道，他摔断了腿，商队开春要走，账房把驼队的令牌塞给他：「留下的也是千里号的人。」他就在崖上住下了，夜里补崖，一补十年。他问：「他们回来了没有？」你们摇头。曹三点点头：「那我再补一年。」

column2: Farewell Camp Sands
column3: 别营沙

column2: An open patch of gravel desert laid with hearthstones in neat rows, three to a set, set after set, further than you can see. A band of salt smugglers uses it as a rest camp, boiling salt over the hearths, and has pulled several sets apart, sure something must be buried underneath. This, says Liaozhang, is where the Qianli caravan camped the night they left the caves in spring.
column3: 戈壁上一片空地，地上排着整整齐齐的灶石，三块一组，一组挨一组，一眼望不到头。一伙私盐贩子把这里当成了歇脚的营盘，拿灶石支锅煮盐，还把好几组灶石扒开，说底下准埋着什么。了账说，这是千里号开春离开千佛洞那一夜扎营的地方。

column2: The smugglers chased off, you put the hearthstones back. Beneath every set is buried a small clay lamp with a film of dried oil in its bowl. Liaozhang counts: one lamp to a set, three hundred sets. That night, he says, each of the three hundred lit a lamp, and before setting off at dawn they buried them under the hearths. 'Meaning: the fire stays here, and the people will come back.'
column3: 私盐贩子被赶走，你们把扒开的灶石摆回原处。每组灶石底下都埋着一只小陶灯，灯碗里还有一层干了的油。了账数了数，一组一灯，三百组。他说那一夜三百人每人点了一盏灯，天亮出发前把灯埋在灶下，「意思是：火还在这儿，人会回来」。

column2: Old Chisel's Cave
column3: 老凿洞

column2: At the very back of the dead end at the foot of the hill, a small cave is Lao Zao's home, crammed with chisels, hammers and chalk lines of every size. The old man lies sick on his platform bed, coughing double. Contractors from inside the Pass have blocked the entrance with their bullies, pushing him to put his thumbprint on a contract selling them his hand order. Every mason in these parts obeys Lao Zao's hand order; whoever holds it can command them all.
column3: 山脚死胡同的最里头，一个小窟就是老凿的家，窟里堆满了大大小小的凿子、锤子和墨斗。老凿病在炕上，咳得直不起腰。一伙关内来的包工头带着打手堵在窟口，逼他在一张契上按手印，把他的「手令」卖给他们：这一带的匠人只认老凿的手令，有了它，就能使唤所有的匠人。

column2: The contractors chased off, Lao Zao props himself up and draws a wooden tablet from under his mat, an order carved in his own hand: 'Urgent work. All who see this order work day and night without rest; one day counts for three.' That winter an overhang on the north cliff cracked, right above the newly painted Qianli Cave. He wrote this order, and the masons and the three hundred worked a day and a night by torchlight and shored it up. 'This is the Building Hand Order,' he says, giving it to you. 'Show it on any site and the masons know it's a rush job. They'll do several days' work in one.' He coughs again. 'When those three hundred left, they said they'd come back and work for me again. I'm waiting.'
column3: 包工头被打跑，老凿撑着坐起来，从炕席底下摸出一块木牌，牌上是他亲手刻的令：「急工。见令者，昼夜不歇，一日抵三日。」那年冬天，北崖一块悬岩裂了缝，底下就是刚画好的千里窟，他写了这道令，匠人和千里号三百人举着火把干了一天一夜，把悬岩撑住了。「这是营造加速令，」他把木牌交给你们，「拿到工地上一亮，匠人们就知道是急活，一天能干完好几天的工。」他又咳了几声：「那三百个人走的时候，说回来还跟我干活。我等着。」

column2: Masons' Strand
column3: 匠人滩

column2: Masons' shacks crowd the riverbank, straw hats and puttees drying in the sun. A band of sutra thieves has crept in and is forcing them at knifepoint to dig a tunnel from the strand right into a sealed cave. The masons cling to their chisels and won't budge, so the thieves are throwing them in the river one at a time. Three have gone in already.
column3: 河滩上搭着一片匠人的窝棚，晒着草帽和裹腿。一伙盗经贼摸了过来，拿刀逼匠人们给他们打一条地道，从河滩一直通到一座封了门的窟里去。匠人们抱着凿子不肯动，盗经贼就一个一个地往河里扔，已经扔下去三个了。

column2: The thieves chased off, the three who went in the river climb out shivering. 'Lao Zao taught us,' their foreman says. 'No digging holes in the cliff at random. Every hole is a wound.' The Qianli caravan kept the same rule back then, they tell you. The bookkeeper even copied it out three hundred times so each of them carried one. 'When they left, they said they'd keep it wherever they went.'
column3: 盗经贼被打跑，掉进河的三个也爬了上来，冻得直打哆嗦。匠头说：「老凿教的，崖上不许乱打洞，一个洞就是一道伤。」他们说千里号的人当年也这么守过规矩，账房还把规矩抄了三百份，每人揣一份，「走的时候说，到了别的地方也照着办」。

column2: The Qianli Granary
column3: 千里仓

column2: Put the two halves of the map together and there's the Qianli Granary: a row of storage chambers cut into the cliff at the end of a dead end, their mouths boarded up. But someone got here first. Swordsmen from inside the Pass bought the location from the sutra thieves and now hold the chambers, foot, crossbow and horse, waiting to prise off the boards and make their fortune.
column3: 两半张图一拼，千里仓找到了：死胡同尽头的崖壁上，一排凿出来的仓洞，洞口用木板封着。可有人先到了一步：一伙关内的刀客从盗经贼那里买了消息，占了仓洞，步、弩、骑三路守着，等着撬开封板发一笔大财。

column2: The swordsmen beaten back, you prise off the boards. The chambers hold only rows of empty jars. On the walls are notches for every withdrawal of grain. For the first three years the mark is the character Qian, until in the third autumn the jars stand upside down. From the fourth year the mark becomes a mask with no features, one a year, seven in all. The Qianli caravan's grain lasted three years. The porridge of the seven years since was the Gold Mask's.
column3: 刀客们被打退，你们撬开封板：仓洞里只有空陶瓮。洞壁上刻着取粮的记号，头三年刻的是「千」字，刻到第三年秋天，瓮底朝天。从第四年起，记号换成了一张没有五官的面具，一年一个，刻了七个。千里号的粮三年就施完了，后七年的粥，是金面续上的。

column2: Leopard Gully
column3: 豹子沟

column2: Claw marks cover the stones of the gully, and a pair of yellow eyes flashes now and then in a crack in the cliff. Every winter the goitered gazelles come down this gully from the mountains looking for grass, and the leopards follow, family after family, lying in wait. The herders nearby have lost several sheep and no one dares go in. To get up the mountain, Master Shouzhou would have had to pass through here.
column3: 沟里的石头上全是爪印，崖缝里时不时闪过一双黄眼睛。每年冬天，山里的黄羊顺着这条沟下来找草，豹子就跟着黄羊下来，一窝一窝地守在沟里。附近的牧人丢了好几头羊，谁也不敢进沟。守粥师父要上山，就得从这里过。

column2: This time the leopards are driven back into the hills and the gully goes quiet. Under a rock Douzi finds half a dry cake with a row of tooth marks, human, not leopard. 'That's how Master eats. He always bites the edge first.' But the leopards follow the gazelles, and the gazelles come down every winter. Before long someone will have to clear this gully again.
column3: 这一回的豹子被赶回了山里，沟里安静了。豆子在一块石头底下捡到半块干粮，上面有一排牙印，是人的，不是豹子的：「师父咬东西就是这样，先咬边。」可豹子跟着黄羊走，黄羊每年冬天都下山，过一阵，这沟里还得再来清一回。

column2: The Hanging Ledge
column3: 悬粥台

column2: Above the broken steps is a narrow ledge halfway up the cliff with a straw shelter on it and a thread of cooking smoke rising. Douzi tilts back his head and calls 'Master!' and out of the shelter looks a monk grown much thinner. But a band of sutra thieves is waiting at the cliff foot. Seeing Master Shouzhou can't get down, they mean to wait until he starves and then go through the sack of grain the Gold Mask gave him; there must be something of the Lord's in it, they say.
column3: 断阶上面，崖腰有一道窄窄的石台，台上搭着个草棚，一缕炊烟往上飘。豆子仰着脖子喊了一声「师父」，草棚里探出一个瘦了一大圈的和尚。可崖下守着一伙盗经贼，他们看守粥师父在台上下不来，想等他饿死，好去翻他身边那只金面送的粮袋，说里面准有洞主的东西。

column2: The sutra thieves scattered, you mend the broken steps and help Master Shouzhou down. Douzi flings himself at him and master and pupil weep together. Shouzhou did see the Lord. He wouldn't come down, only said, 'The porridge goes on, I'll send the grain, nobody leaves the mountain,' and filled his sack. On the way down the steps gave way, and he has been cooking porridge on this ledge for over a month. 'He said the Qianli grain was meant for travellers, and when it ran out, the road mustn't be cut.' Shouzhou looks north-east. 'He's guarded those three hundred on the cliff for ten years and won't even come down for a bowl of porridge himself. When you see him, tell him the porridge below hasn't stopped.'
column3: 盗经贼被打散，你们接上断阶，把守粥师父扶了下来。豆子扑上去，师徒俩抱着哭了一场。守粥说他见到了洞主：洞主不肯下山，只说「粥照施，粮我送，人不出山」，又往他袋里装满了粮。下山时石阶断了，他就在台上熬粥，熬了一个多月。「他说千里号留的粮是给过路人的，粮吃完了，路不能断。」守粥望着东北：「他守着崖上那三百个人，守了十年，自己连碗粥都舍不得下山喝。你们见了他，告诉他山下的粥没断。」

column2: White Earth Kilns
column3: 白土窑

column2: A slope of dazzling white earth with a few lime kilns below it, where kiln men dig white clay and burn lime for plastering the cliff. A gang of kiln thugs has driven the workers off, sealed the kilns and sold lime at sky-high prices, so no one on the cliff can mix plaster. Wu Banbi squats at the foot of the slope, holding a pinch of white earth up to the sun. 'This is the ground for a face.'
column3: 一片白花花的土坡，坡下几座石灰窑，烧窑的人从这里挖白土、烧石灰，供崖上抹墙用。一伙窑痞赶走了窑工，把窑口一封，石灰卖出天价，崖上补墙的泥都和不起来。吴半壁蹲在坡下，捏起一撮白土对着太阳看：「画脸的底子，就是它。」

column2: The thugs gone, the kiln men come back, white smoke rises again and lime goes up to the cliff by the cartload. Wu Banbi digs a bag of the finest white earth, and now he has all three colours. He pats each bag in turn. 'Only the gold is missing.' The kiln foreman says the Qianli caravan carried lime from here that year, a song for every basket, a whole day without repeating one.
column3: 窑痞被赶走，窑工们回来了，窑口又冒起白烟，一车车石灰往崖上送。吴半壁挖了满满一袋最细的白土，三样颜色凑齐了。他把袋子挨个摸了一遍：「只差金。」窑工头说那年千里号的人也来这里背过石灰，背一筐唱一句，唱一整天不重样。

column2: The thugs' shed holds thirty cartloads of lime, five of charcoal, a cellar of salted fish, a dozen stolen trowels, and a stack of lime IOUs written out in advance; even the cripple on the cliff owes them two baskets.
column3: 窑痞的棚子里抄出三十车石灰、五车木炭、一窖腌咸鱼、十几把抢来的瓦刀，还有一摞写好的「石灰欠条」，连崖上那个瘸子都欠了他们两筐。

column2: Every time you pass, the kiln men peel a few flatbreads baked golden on the kiln wall, the stone's pattern still on their undersides, and load two baskets of lime onto your cart. 'Your camp'll have walls to patch. You'll need it.'
column3: 每次路过，窑工们都从窑壁上揭下几张烤得焦黄的面饼，饼底还带着石头的纹路，再给你们的车上捎两筐石灰：「营里要补墙，用得着。」

column2: The Debt Buyers
column3: 收账营

column2: A camp of 'debt collectors' from inside the Pass stands by the road under a banner: 'Qianli caravan debts bought. Thirty per cent in silver.' They've bought up stacks of Qianli IOUs cheap from the Sand Sea, the ghost market and everywhere else, and mean to take them to the caves and to the homes of all three hundred families and collect door to door. They've hired swordsmen, who curse at the sight of Liaozhang's robe: 'Another debt collector, come to steal our business!'
column3: 路边扎着一营关内来的「收账人」，帐篷上挂着幌子：「专收千里号旧账，三折现银」。他们从沙海、从鬼市、从各路人手里低价收来一摞摞千里号的欠条，打算拿着欠条去千佛洞，去千里号三百家的家里，挨家挨户地讨。营里雇了一帮刀手，见了账的和尚袍就骂：「又是个讨债的，抢生意来了！」

column2: The swordsmen scattered, Liaozhang leafs through the IOUs and, at the end, gives a cold laugh: hand, seal and date, not one matches the accounts on the library cave wall. 'The only genuine Qianli debts are ours at the temple and the King's in the Sand Sea. I've copied every entry the bookkeeper made.' He throws the stack of fakes on the fire. 'That one goes on their own account.'
column3: 刀手们被打散，了账一张张翻那些欠条，翻完了冷笑一声：字迹、印章、日子，没有一张对得上藏经洞墙上的账，「千里号的账，只有我们寺里的和沙海那个王的是真的，账房记的每一笔，我都抄着」。他把一摞假欠条扔进了火里：「这一笔，记在他们自己账上。」

column2: The Westward Road
column3: 西去道

column2: Beyond the Farewell Camp, an old trodden road runs out into the gravel desert, and a troop of Gold Mask riders sits across its mouth. No one may set foot on it: the Lord's orders. 'The road the Qianli caravan took is not to be followed by anyone.' Passing camel trains have to go the long way round, three extra days.
column3: 别营沙往外，一条被踩实了的旧路伸进戈壁，路口横着一队金面骑卫。他们不许人往这条路上走，说洞主有令：「千里号走过的路，谁也不许跟。」过路的驼队只好绕远道，多走三天。

column2: The riders beaten back, their leader says the order isn't the Lord's own idea. The bookkeeper asked it of him: 'If anyone comes looking for us, don't let them follow. I'll settle the accounts in the King's city myself.' But in ten years of waiting the Lord has had only face-scrapers, sutra thieves and impostors. At intervals along the roadside stand little stone niches, each holding a dry lamp.
column3: 骑卫们被打退，领头的说这条令不是洞主自己想出来的，是账房当年托付的：「后面要是有人来找我们，别让他跟。王城的账，我自己去算。」可洞主等了十年，只等来刮脸的、盗经的、冒名的。路边隔一段就有一个小石龛，龛里摆着一盏干了的灯。

column2: Chisel Grove
column3: 凿子林

column2: On a big boulder at the end of a dead end, iron chisels stand so thick they look from afar like a grove of bare saplings. Mercenaries buying up iron have their eyes on them and hold the boulder with foot, crossbow and horse, pulling the chisels out one by one: melt them down and they'll make three hundred swords. But they're driven in deep, and after all this time only a dozen are out.
column3: 死胡同尽头的一块大石上插着密密麻麻的铁凿，远看像一片光秃秃的小树林。一伙收铁的雇佣兵盯上了这些凿子，步、弩、骑三路守在石头边，正一根根往外拔，说熔了能打三百把刀。可凿子插得太深，拔了半天，才拔出来十几根。

column2: The mercenaries beaten back, you drive the chisels back in one by one. Each wooden handle is carved with a name, and the blades are worn down to half their length. These are the Qianli three hundred's chisels, the masons say. When they left in spring each man drove his into this boulder. 'They said they'd borrowed Lao Zao's craft and would collect it when they came back. While the chisels are here, so is the craft.' Three hundred, not one missing.
column3: 雇佣兵被打退，你们把凿子一根根插了回去。每根木柄上都刻着名字，凿头磨得只剩半截。匠人们说，这是千里号三百人的凿子，开春走的时候一人一根插在这块石头上，「说是借老凿的手艺，回来再拿。凿子在，手艺就在」。三百根，一根不少。

column2: Riverside Fodder Yard
column3: 河边草场

column2: A fodder yard by the river, stacked with hay and alfalfa, where the camels and horses coming to the caves are fed. Soldier-thugs have seized it and sell fodder at a coin a pound; the pilgrims' donkeys are so hungry they gnaw the door frames. The old yard keeper has been sent to feed the pigs, and his two grandsons hide in a haystack, scarcely daring to breathe.
column3: 河边一座草料场，码着一垛垛干草和苜蓿，是千佛洞来往驼马吃草的地方。一伙兵痞霸了草场，马料一斤卖一钱，香客的驴饿得啃门框。看草场的老汉被他们赶去喂猪，他的两个孙子躲在草垛里，大气不敢出。

column2: The thugs chased off, the old man's grandsons wriggle out of the haystack, straw all over their heads. Every winter, the old man says, he keeps the best stack of alfalfa for Lao Huang, the old camel on the walkway, on the Lord's orders. 'The Lord says people can go hungry, but that camel mustn't. It's a Qianli camel.'
column3: 兵痞被赶走，老汉的两个孙子从草垛里钻出来，头上全是草。老汉说，栈道上那峰叫老黄的老骆驼，每年冬天他都给它留一垛最好的苜蓿，是洞主吩咐的。「洞主说，人可以饿，那峰骆驼不能饿，那是千里号的骆驼。」

column2: From the yard you recover six hundred bales of hay hoarded by the thugs, thirty sacks of bean fodder, twenty camel-hair blankets, and a stolen chestnut horse that the old man recognises as a neighbour's and leads home.
column3: 草场里抄出兵痞们囤的六百捆干草、三十袋豆料、二十条驼毛毡子，还有一匹偷来的枣红马，老汉一眼认出是邻村的，牵回去还了。

column2: Every time you pass, the old man's grandsons fight over leading your horses to the river to drink, brushing their coats and braiding their manes, and as you leave they stuff a bag of roasted soybeans into your saddlebags. 'Half for you, half for the horses.'
column3: 每次路过，老汉的两个孙子都抢着把你们的马牵到河边饮水，刷毛、编鬃，临走往鞍袋里塞一包炒黄豆：「人吃一半，马吃一半。」

column2: The Trial Wall
column3: 试脸墙

column2: With his colours finally gathered, Wu Banbi has plastered a fresh wall under an earth bank to try one face first. 'If it works, I'll go into the cave and do all three hundred.' He has barely brushed on the white ground when mural thieves close in; they've tailed him the whole way, waiting for him to complete his set. The old man gathers his paint dishes to his chest like a grandchild.
column3: 吴半壁带着凑齐的颜料，在一处土崖下抹了一面新墙，要先试画一张脸，「试成了，再去窟里补那三百张」。他刚把白土刷匀，一伙盗壁贼就围了上来：他们跟了一路，就等他把颜料凑齐。老头把颜料碟往怀里一揽，像抱着孙子。

column2: The thieves scattered, Wu washes his hands, mixes glue, grinds pigment and paints stroke by stroke. He starts with the bookkeeper: thin face, narrowed eyes, brush behind the ear, eyes that seem to be reckoning you up. When it's done he steps back three paces and looks a long while. 'The colours are right. Only the gold is missing.' He could paint all three hundred with his eyes shut, he says; the patterns only gave him courage. He asks you to take a message to the man behind the golden mask: 'Give back the gold and I'll go into the cave.' The bookkeeper on the wall watches you as if about to name a figure.
column3: 盗壁贼被打散了，吴半壁洗了手，调胶，研色，一笔一笔地画。他先画的是账房：瘦脸，眯眼，耳后夹一支笔，眼睛像在算你。画完他退后三步看了很久：「颜色对了，就差金。」他说三百张脸他闭着眼都画得出，粉本只是给自己壮胆的。他托你们带句话给金面后头的人：「金子还回来，我就进窟。」墙上的账房看着你们，像是要开口报一个数。

column2: The King's Oil Cellar
column3: 王油窖

column2: Down a dead end by the river is a cellar cut into the cliff, its door pressed with that lopsided character, King: the lamp oil sent by the King of the Sand Sea, and whatever wasn't burned is stored here. River bandits have got in and hold the mouth with foot, crossbow and horse, hauling out jar after jar to ship downriver and sell, shouting 'Rich!' with every jar.
column3: 河边死胡同里有一座凿进崖里的窖，窖门上按着一个歪歪扭扭的「王」字：沙海的王送来的灯油，用不完的都存在这里。一伙河匪摸进了窖，步、弩、骑三路把住窖口，正一坛坛往外搬，准备顺河运出去卖，搬一坛，喊一声「发财」。

column2: The bandits beaten back, you count the oil: one row a year, ten rows, the earliest seal carved with the autumn of Dingwei. Liaozhang does the sums: the three hundred jin the Qianli caravan owed the temple were paid off by the King's third year. 'The seven years after that, he sent because he wanted to.' The jar at the very end is still sealed, a paper slip on its mouth: 'For the bookkeeper. Light it when he's back.'
column3: 河匪被打退，你们清点窖里的油：一年一排，十排，最早的那排封泥上刻着丁未年秋。了账算了算：千里号欠寺里的三百斤灯油，王第三年就还清了，「后面七年，是他自己要送的」。最边上一坛没开封，坛口贴着纸条：「给账房，回来时点。」

column2: Three-Step Banks
column3: 三级滩

column2: The riverbanks rise in terraces, step above step like a giant staircase. A gang of river bandits camps on the lowest strand, handy for watering their horses, and raids all around. It's summer, the mountain snow is melting and the river is rising day by day; muddy yellow water is already coming down from upstream, and they're drinking on the strand and jeering that you daren't come down and fight.
column3: 河两岸是一级一级的台地，像大台阶，一级比一级高。一伙河匪在最低的一级河滩上扎营，靠着水好饮马，四处劫掠。夏天山里的雪化了，河水一天比一天涨，上游已经冲下来浑黄的泥水，他们还在滩上喝酒，笑话你们不敢下来打。

column2: Liaozhang won't let you camp on the low strand. 'These steps along the river are old riverbeds the river left behind as it cut down. The higher, the older, and a flood only reaches the lowest.' You hold the high ground overnight. At midnight the flood crest drowns the bandits' camp, and at dawn you haul them out of the water one by one. The Qianli caravan carried the library cave's sutras up to caves on the highest terrace for the same reason.
column3: 了账不让你们在低滩扎营：「河边这一级级台地，都是河往下切留下的旧河滩，越高越老，洪水只淹得上最低那一级。」你们在高处守夜，半夜水头下来，河匪的营盘泡进了水里，天亮时被你们一个个捞上岸。千里号也把藏经洞的经搬上了最高一级。

column2: The Pledged Seal
column3: 押印龛

column2: In a small shrine, a bronze seal rests on the Buddha's knees, its handle a crouching camel. A band of treasure-hunting knights-errant has heard the seal is 'the key to the Qianli treasure' and is prising at the statue's fingers to get it out. The old monk who tends the lamps here clings to the statue's leg and has been dragged several yards.
column3: 一座小佛龛里，佛像膝上供着一方铜印，印纽是一只蹲着的骆驼。一伙寻宝的游侠听说这方印是「千里号宝藏的钥匙」，正围着佛龛撬佛像的手指头，想把印拿下来。看龛的老香灯和尚抱着佛像的腿，被拖出去好几丈。

column2: The knights-errant chased off, Liaozhang presses the seal into his palm: 'Qianli Caravan Bookkeeper.' This is the 'one seal pledged, to be redeemed on the way back' in his debt book. He opens the book at the Qianli page and writes: 'Lamp oil, three hundred jin: paid on their behalf by the King. One sutra: borrowed, taken to the King's city. One seal: before the Buddha.' Then he stares at the blank space below for a long time.
column3: 游侠们被打跑，了账拿起铜印往掌心一按，四个字：「千里号账房」。这就是债簿上那一行「账房押印一方，言回程来赎」。了账翻开债簿，在千里号那一页写：「灯油三百斤，王已代还；经一部，借往王城；印一方，在佛前。」写完，他盯着空白处看了很久。

column2: Three Hundred Lamp Niches
column3: 三百灯龛

column2: The little stone niches along the westward road run one after another deep into the gravel desert, each with a dry lamp. A gang of quicksand bandits lives among them, using the niches as dens and the lamp bowls as wine cups. Liaozhang has the bandit boy unload the King's oil to light the lamps one by one along the road, but the bandits won't have it. 'Light them and we won't get any sleep at night!'
column3: 西去道两旁的小石龛一个接一个，一直排到戈壁深处，每个龛里一盏干了的灯。一伙流沙匪住在龛群里，拿龛当窝，把灯碗掏出来当酒碗。了账让小马贼把王的灯油卸下来，要沿路把灯一盏盏点上，流沙匪却不让：「点了灯，我们夜里睡不着！」

column2: With the bandits gone, Liaozhang fills and lights the lamps one by one while you follow, counting: three hundred. As dark falls the flames join into a single line, one end at the Farewell Camp, the other curving across the desert toward a gate gleaming gold on the mountain to the north-east, and only beyond it the road to the Oasis King's city. 'They wanted whoever came after to find the way, even at night,' says Liaozhang.
column3: 流沙匪被赶走，了账一盏一盏添油点灯，你们跟在后面数，一共三百盏。天黑下来，灯火连成一线，一头接着别营沙，一头弯过戈壁，指着东北边一座金光闪闪的山门，再往外才是去绿洲王城的路。了账说：「他们是想让后来的人，夜里也找得着路。」

column2: Supply Ferry
column3: 送粮渡

column2: At a little ferry by the river, every few days the Gold Masks pole a boat upstream to the foot of the cliff with supplies: grain, timber, lamp oil, alfalfa for Lao Huang. Today the boat has barely touched the bank when river bandits burst out of the reeds and start hauling the cargo onto their own rafts. There are only two Gold Masks poling, fending them off with their poles.
column3: 河边一处小渡口，每隔几天，金面卫就从这里撑船往上游的崖下送东西：粮、木料、灯油、给老黄的苜蓿。今天船刚靠岸，一伙河匪就从芦苇里冲了出来，把船上的东西往自己筏子上搬。撑船的金面卫只有两个，拿着篙子左支右挡。

column2: The bandits scattered, one of the boatmen takes off his mask to wipe his sweat. He's a young man. From the hold he brings out a bronze token and hands it to you: Cao San sent it down with him, the very 'Qianli Caravan: Camel Train'. Cao San's message: 'I can't go, so the token will go for me. Show it to the Lord, he knows it. Tell him I can hold the walkway, and he needn't keep his own watch so hard.'
column3: 河匪被赶散，撑船的金面卫摘下面具擦汗，是个年轻人。他从船舱里取出一块铜牌递给你们，是曹三托他捎下来的，正是那块「千里号·驼」。曹三带话说：「我走不了，牌子替我走。拿给洞主看，他认这块牌。告诉他，栈道我守得住，叫他也别守得太苦。」

column2: No Disciples Camp
column3: 拒徒营

column2: A large camp of Gold Mask riders on the gravel plain, with more banners, blades and horses than anywhere else. Their leader takes one look at Liaozhang and tosses a letter at his feet. 'The Lord says Liaozhang goes back to the temple to chant sutras. He doesn't come up the mountain. You least of all.' The riders and crossbowmen are already drawn up; it seems they've been waiting specially for him.
column3: 戈壁上一大营金面骑卫，旗子、刀、马都比别处多。领头的一见了账，就把一封信扔到他脚下：「洞主说，了账回寺里念经，不许上山，尤其不许你上。」营里的骑卫和弩手已经列好了阵，看来是专门等他的。

column2: The riders beaten back, Liaozhang picks up the letter. It holds a single line: 'I am no longer your master. The accounts need not be settled.' He folds it into his debt book. 'The first thing Master taught me was that accounts must always be settled. Even if he isn't my master any more, he still owes me a why.' The lead rider says quietly, 'The Lord doesn't want you to see what he's become.'
column3: 骑卫们被打退，了账捡起那封信，信上只有一句话：「我已不是你师父，账不必对。」了账把信折好塞进债簿：「师父教我的头一条，就是账一定要对。他不是我师父，也还欠我一个『为什么』。」领头的骑卫低声说：「洞主是怕你看见他现在的样子。」

column2: The Gold Hunters
column3: 追金骑

column2: A line of yellow dust rolls across the gravel desert: a big company of Gold Mask riders sweeping back and forth among the dunes, foot soldiers prodding every sand heap with long poles, riders blocking the gaps ahead. They're looking for someone, and they turn back the collar of everyone they meet. Your camels have barely crested the ridge when they surround you. 'Any gold hidden in your collars?'
column3: 戈壁上卷起一溜黄尘，一大队金面骑卫在沙丘间来回搜，步卒拿长杆一路戳沙堆，骑卫在前头堵口子。他们在找一个人，见了谁都要掀开领子看看。你们的驼队刚翻过沙梁，就被他们团团围住：「领子里藏没藏金子？」

column2: The riders beaten off, their leader drops a little book: the Gold Masks' tally of the hunt. 'Seven gold scrapers, six taken. One tenth of an ounce recovered. Two hundredths still owed, held by the seventh man.' Below is a sketch of a boy of twelve or thirteen. Seven years the Lord has hunted it down grain by grain, and only these last two hundredths are missing.
column3: 骑卫们被打退，领头的丢下一本小册子，是金面卫追金的账：「刮金七人，已获其六。追回金一钱，尚欠二分，在第七人处。」底下画着一个十二三岁的孩子的模样。七年了，洞主一分一厘地追，就差这最后两分。

column2: The Wick Stall
column3: 灯芯摊

column2: A pilgrims' stall at the crossroads selling incense, candles and lamp wicks, run by an old woman with a voice louder than a gong. The Gold Masks won't allow incense in the caves, so her incense doesn't sell, and a troop of Gold Mask swordsmen comes every day to inspect her wicks in case she's selling them into the caves on the sly. She grabs her wick-rolling board, plants herself before her stall and curses them for half an hour without repeating herself once.
column3: 路口一个香客摊，卖香、卖蜡、卖灯芯，摊主是个嗓门比铜锣还大的老太婆。金面卫不许香火进窟，她的香卖不出去，一队金面刀卫还天天来查她的灯芯，说怕她偷偷往窟里卖。老太婆抄起擀灯芯的木板，站在摊前骂了半个时辰，没一句重样。

column2: Half cursed and half beaten back, the swordsmen withdraw, and the old woman opens for trade, sharp of tongue but honest at the scales. She recognises Liaozhang at once. 'If it isn't the little baldy who used to steal my sesame candy!' For ten years she's rolled the wicks for the Qianli lamp, camel hair twisted with cotton. 'Every bit of fur that old camel the caravan left behind sheds each year comes to me.'
column3: 刀卫们被骂退一半、打退一半，老太婆这才开了张，嘴上不饶人，秤上不亏人。她一眼认出了账：「这不是小时候偷我麻糖的小秃子吗！」她说十年来千里号那盏灯的灯芯都是她搓的，驼毛掺棉线，「千里号留下的老骆驼，每年掉的毛都归我」。

column2: Sutra Ambush Road
column3: 截经道

column2: A band of sutra thieves runs out across the desert with bulging bundles and blunders straight into you. Their leader has a scroll clutched to his chest, tightly wrapped and clinking as he runs: the bronze rollers at either end. Seeing Liaozhang's robe they take him for the temple in pursuit, leave a few men to cover them and dive for the dunes.
column3: 戈壁上一伙盗经贼背着鼓鼓囊囊的包袱往外跑，正撞上你们。领头的怀里揣着一卷经，包得严严实实，跑起来叮当响，是经卷两头的铜轴。他们见了账穿着僧袍，以为是寺里追来的，扔下几个人断后，其余的拼命往沙里钻。

column2: The rearguard knocked down, you wrest the leader's scroll from him. Liaozhang unrolls it: the first fascicle of a sutra, each section signed with a name, some neat, some crooked, some just a mark. At the end: 'Copied together by the three hundred of the Qianli caravan, winter of Dingwei.' Liaozhang stamps his foot. 'The Qianli Sutra! There are ten fascicles, and they've stolen every one!'
column3: 断后的被打倒，领头那卷经被夺了下来。了账展开一看，是一部经的第一卷，每段末尾都署着一个名字，有工整的，有歪扭的，有的只画了押。卷尾写着：「千里号三百人，丁未冬合抄。」了账直跺脚：「这是千里经！一共十卷，他们全偷走了！」

column2: Seven Banners Post
column3: 七旗卡

column2: A checkpoint stands where the main road turns up the mountain, and on its wall are planted seven banners, each bearing a great character Qian, some brand new, some faded. The Gold Mask swordsmen on guard see your banner and laugh coldly. 'Another one. Number eight.' Swords and crossbows close in together.
column3: 上山的大路口立着一道卡子，卡墙上插着七面旗，旗上都写着一个大大的「千」字，有的崭新，有的已经褪了色。守卡的金面刀卫看见你们的旗，冷笑一声：「又来一个。第八面。」刀卫和弩手一齐压了上来。

column2: The swordsmen beaten back, the post officer shows you the seven banners. One came from a merchant house inside the Pass that wanted to claim the Qianli caravan's trade. One from sutra thieves who wanted to slip into the caves. One from a swindler claiming to be the bookkeeper's son. All seven said they were the ones who came after. 'Each time, the Lord believed, and each time he was fooled,' says the officer. 'By the fifth he stopped believing anyone.'
column3: 刀卫们被打退，卡官领你们看那七面旗：一面是关内商号的，想冒认千里号的买卖；一面是盗经贼的，想混进窟里；一面是个骗子的，说自己是账房的儿子……七拨人都说是千里号的后来者。「洞主见一个信一回，被骗一回，」卡官说，「到第五拨，就谁也不信了。」

column2: Bronze Mask Camp
column3: 铜面营

column2: A big Gold Mask camp sits by the river, but these men are different: they wear bronze masks, not gold, each engraved with a number from one to six. They hold the river crossing and let no cargo through toward the mountain, and when they fight they hold nothing back, as if paying off a debt to someone.
column3: 河边扎着一大营金面卫，营里的人跟别处不一样：脸上戴的不是金面，是铜面，铜面上还刻着一个数，从一刻到六。他们守着河边的渡口，不许任何人往山上运东西，打起来却不要命，好像在跟谁赎罪。

column2: The bronze masks beaten back, number one takes his off: a middle-aged man with a deeply lined face. The six of them, he says, are the Gold Scrapers who scraped the Qianli Cave, caught one by one by the Lord. He didn't kill them; he masked them in bronze and set them to guard the caves. 'Wear this face and you'll remember whose faces you scraped.' He looks out over the desert. 'The seventh was only a kid. Twelve, that year.'
column3: 铜面卫被打退，戴「一」的那个摘下面具，是个满脸褶子的中年人。他说他们六个就是当年刮千里窟的刮金帮，被洞主一个个抓了回来。洞主没杀他们，叫他们戴上铜面守窟，「戴着这张脸，就记得自己刮过谁的脸」。他望着戈壁：「第七个还小，那年才十二。」

column2: A-Qi's Village
column3: 阿七村

column2: A little village by the river, boats tied under the willow at its edge. River bullies have seized the village ferry, ten coins a head to cross, and those who can't pay have their animals taken. They've shoved an old man into the river, and when he crawls out he's still muttering: 'A-Qi's mother's grave is still on the other bank...'
column3: 河边一个小村，村口的柳树下拴着几条船。一伙河霸占了村里的渡船，过河一人十钱，交不起的就扣下牲口。村里一个老汉被他们推进了河里，爬上来还在念叨：「阿七他娘的坟，还在对岸呢……」

column2: The bullies chased off, the old man poles the ferry across and shows you a small grave on the far side. Seven years ago, he says, A-Qi went to the caves once with a bad crowd and came back like a lost soul, and never touched gold again. His mother died last winter. He buried her and went off to lead camels for a caravan. 'He knelt at her grave all night before he left and said, Mother, the debt I owe, I'm going to pay it.'
column3: 河霸被赶走，老汉把船撑过去，领你们看对岸的一座小坟。他说阿七七年前跟着一伙坏人跑了一趟千佛洞，回来就像丢了魂，再不肯碰金子。去年冬天他娘死了，他埋了娘，去给驼队拉骆驼，「临走在坟前跪了一夜，说娘，我欠的那一笔，我去还」。

column2: Settling Slope
column3: 两清坡

column2: On the last slope before the mountain, Gold Mask swordsmen and crossbowmen stand in three ranks, every mask turned toward Liaozhang. But Liaozhang is in no hurry now. He sets up a little table at the foot of the slope, lays out his debt book and inkstone, and sets on it one by one the library cave's accounts, the Lamp Elder's pill, the King's oil and the seal from before the Buddha. He calls up the slope: 'Brothers, let me write this one entry, then we can fight.'
column3: 上山的最后一道坡上，金面卫的刀卫、弩手排成三排，个个面具冲着了账。了账却不急了，在坡下支起一张小桌，摆开债簿和砚台，把藏经洞的账、灯公的丹、王的油、佛前的印，一样样摆在桌上。他对坡上喊：「师兄们，等我写完这一笔，再打不迟。」

column2: The Gold Masks on the slope give way. On the Qianli page Liaozhang writes the last two lines: 'Owed by the Qianli caravan to the Thousand Buddha Caves: one seal, now redeemed. Owed by the caves to the Qianli caravan: ten years of porridge, one cliff, one road, three hundred lamps.' He lays down the brush. 'All square. What's left is what my master owes himself.' He closes the book and looks up at the gate. 'I'm going to collect that one.'
column3: 坡上的金面卫让开了。了账在千里号那一页写下最后两行：「千里号欠千佛洞：印一方，已赎。千佛洞欠千里号：粥十年，崖一面，路一条，灯三百盏。」他放下笔：「两清了。剩下的，是我师父欠他自己的。」他把债簿合上，抬头看着山门：「我去讨这一笔。」

column2: Sutra Drying Strand
column3: 晒经滩

column2: The riverbank is spread with sutra scrolls laid open to dry, and old monks kneel among them fanning gently. A few days ago water seeped into a cave upstream and soaked every scroll in it; the Gold Masks carried them down through the night to dry. But sutra thieves lie in wait at the edge of the strand, ready to strike when the sun dips and the monks begin rolling them up.
column3: 河滩上铺满了经卷，一卷一卷摊开晒着，几个老和尚跪在边上，用扇子轻轻地扇。上游一个窟前几天渗了水，一窟的经都湿了，金面卫连夜一卷卷背下来晒。可滩边埋伏着一伙盗经贼，等太阳偏西、和尚们收经的时候下手。

column2: The thieves chased off, not a scroll is lost. One of the Gold Masks, helping roll them up, says that the night the water came in, the Lord was first into the cave, running out with armfuls of scrolls, and slipped into the river. 'The Lord can't swim. He thrashed about and still wouldn't let go.' An old monk laughs. 'Same as when he tended the fire at the porridge shed as a boy. Pot tipped over, still wouldn't let go of the ladle.'
column3: 盗经贼被打跑，经卷一卷没少。一个金面卫一边帮着收经一边说，那天夜里窟里进水，洞主第一个冲了进去，抱着经卷往外跑，脚下一滑掉进了河里，「洞主不会水，扑腾着也不撒手」。老和尚笑了：「他小时候在粥棚烧火，就这样，锅翻了也不撒勺子。」

column2: The Gold Scale Market
column3: 金秤市

column2: A little market at the edge of the desert, where all the gold within a few hundred miles of the caves is bought and sold: gilding for the caves, gold dust for painters, and the fine stone cut from the cliff comes here to be traded for gold. By the Lord's order every grain of gold in the market may be sold only to the Gold Masks, weighed on their scale. A gang of sand bandits has seen its chance, seized the Gold Masks' scale platform and set themselves up as the 'Gold Masks', taking every scrap of gold and fleecing everyone.
column3: 戈壁边上一座小集，是千佛洞方圆几百里买卖金子的地方：修窟要贴金，画匠要金粉，崖上凿出来的好石料也拿来这儿换金。洞主有令，集上所有的金子只许卖给金面卫，一分一厘都要过他们的秤。如今一伙沙匪看准了这条规矩，劫了金面卫的秤台，自己当起了「金面」，见金就收，见人就宰。

column2: The sand bandits driven off, the market opens again: stone from the cliff comes in by the cartload and leaves as gold, and trade is lively once more. The old man who keeps the scale says the Lord buys gold not to get rich but to make up a sum, grain by grain. 'He says he owes three hundred people one tenth of an ounce and a little more, and he'll pay back every grain.' Last month a young camel driver came asking how to give a little gold back to the temple without anyone knowing who gave it. 'I told him,' says the old man, 'the best way is to pay it back face to face.'
column3: 沙匪被赶走，金秤市重新开了张：崖上的石料一车车拉来，换走金子，买卖又热闹起来。管秤的老头说，洞主收金，不是为了自己发财，是一分一分地凑：「他说欠了三百个人一钱二分金，要一分不少地还回去。」上个月有个拉骆驼的年轻人来问过他，怎么把一点金子还给寺里，又不让人知道是谁还的。老头说：「我告诉他，最好的法子，是当面还。」

column2: The Fence's Tent
column3: 销赃帐

column2: In a sandy hollow stands a big oilcloth tent: the sutra thieves' fence. Inside hang scroll after scroll, a price tag dangling from each, and the dearest reads 'Qianli Sutra, set of five, not sold separately'. Outside, toughs are checking the goods, and a buyer has already brought out his silver. Liaozhang sees the bronze rollers on those scrolls and throws himself at them.
column3: 沙窝里一顶油布大帐，是盗经贼的销赃铺，帐里挂着一卷卷经，每卷底下吊着一块价牌，最贵的一卷标着「千里经，五卷一套，不拆卖」。帐外一伙打手正在验货，一个买主已经掏出了银子。了账一看那几卷经的铜轴，就扑了上去。

column2: Toughs and buyer both run, and five fascicles of the Qianli Sutra are recovered. At the end of the fifth is the bookkeeper's hand: 'One sutra borrowed from the temple, taken to the King's city. One sutra copied and left with the temple as surety. The handwriting is ugly; Buddha, don't laugh. May this road be smooth.' Liaozhang reads it aloud and presses the scroll to his chest. 'He borrowed one and gave one back, with three hundred people's handwriting thrown in.' The last few fascicles are still missing.
column3: 打手和买主都跑了，五卷千里经被抢了回来。第五卷的末尾，是账房的字：「借寺中经一部，携往王城；抄经一部留寺，以为抵押。字丑，佛莫笑。愿此路平。」了账念完，把经卷贴在胸口：「他借走一部，还了一部，还多附了三百个人的字。」还差最后几卷。

column2: Siege Camp
column3: 攻崖营

column2: A big camp stands on the grassland, heaped with scaling ladders, grappling hooks and crowbars, where mercenaries from inside the Pass, foot, crossbow and horse, are drilling cliff assaults. Their captain holds a plan of the caves with a dozen circled in red. 'Which caves have sutras, which have paintings, which have gold: it's all here.'
column3: 草滩上扎着一座大营，营里堆着云梯、绳钩、撬棍，一伙关内的雇佣兵正在操练攀崖，步、弩、骑都有。他们的头领拿着一张千佛洞的崖图，用朱笔圈了十几个窟：「哪个窟里有经、有画、有金，都在这儿了。」

column2: The mercenaries scattered, you find a contract in the captain's tent: 'All sutras and murals taken from the caves to be split half and half with the patron.' The patron is a great merchant house inside the Pass. Now you understand: the Lord closed the mountain for ten years and kept a camp of Gold Masks not against the odd petty thief, but against camps like this, one after another.
column3: 雇佣兵被打散，你们在头领的帐里搜出一张契：「千佛洞内经卷壁画，得者与东家对半。」东家是关内一个大商号。你们这才明白，洞主闭山十年、养着一营金面卫，防的不是一两个小贼，是一个个这样的营盘。

column2: The Camel Boy
column3: 拉驼郎

column2: A small camel train has been stopped on the road by sutra thieves, who want it to carry their loot or they'll butcher the camels. The lead camel's driver is a lad of eighteen or nineteen, thin as a stick, one hand clamped to his collar, the other gripping a camel stick, standing in front of his animals.
column3: 一支小驼队被一伙盗经贼截在路上，盗经贼要驼队帮他们驮赃，不驮就把骆驼宰了。拉头驼的是个十八九岁的小伙子，瘦得像根柴，一只手死死按着自己的衣领，另一只手攥着一根赶驼棍，挡在骆驼前面。

column2: The thieves chased off, the lad's legs give way and he sits down hard. He is A-Qi, youngest of the Gold Scrapers. He unpicks his collar: sewn inside is a tiny paper packet, his share of the gold dust, two hundredths of an ounce, untouched for seven years. 'I was twelve. All I remember is three hundred faces in the cave looking at me. I wanted to give it back, but I was scared of the Gold Mask. Seven years scared.' He begs you to take him up the mountain.
column3: 盗经贼被打跑，小伙子腿一软坐在地上。他就是阿七，当年刮金帮里最小的一个。他拆开衣领，里面缝着一个小纸包，是他分到的两分金粉，七年一粒没动。「我那年十二，就记得窟里三百张脸看着我，」他说，「想还，又怕金面，怕了七年。」他求你们带他上山。

column2: Sand Basket Slope
column3: 背沙坡

column2: On the sand slope behind the clifftop, a line of pilgrims with baskets on their backs carries sand down off the cave roofs. The Gold Mask swordsmen at the head of the slope have made a rule: anyone going up the mountain must carry one basket of sand first. Some rich merchants from inside the Pass think it beneath them, hired toughs to force their way through, and are brawling with the guards, sand baskets rolling all over the slope.
column3: 崖顶背后的沙坡上排着一溜香客，每人背一只筐，从窟顶上往下背沙。坡口的金面刀卫定了规矩：上山的人，先背一筐沙才许走。几个关内来的富商嫌脏，雇了打手要硬闯，跟刀卫打成一团，沙筐滚了一坡。

column2: Toughs and guards both dispersed, you take up baskets and carry sand. Sand left on a cave roof soaks through with the next rain and the roof collapses, an old pilgrim says. 'The Lord's rule is harsh, but it shields the Buddhas from harm.' A-Qi says nothing and carries ten baskets without stopping. As he shoulders the eleventh, the guard captain claps him on the shoulder. 'Enough, lad. That's enough.'
column3: 打手和刀卫都散了，你们拿起筐背沙。一个老香客说，沙压在窟顶上，下一场雨就渗下去，窟顶就塌，「洞主这条规矩，凶是凶，是给佛挡灾」。阿七一声不吭，背了十筐还不肯停，背到第十一筐，刀卫的头目拍了拍他的肩：「够了，小子，够了。」

column2: Sutra Thieves' Warren
column3: 盗经窝

column2: Half a ruined cave lies buried in the sand, its mouth burrowed by sutra thieves into a rat's nest of tunnels running every which way. Scrolls from the caves, silver from collectors inside the Pass and passing thieves all come and go through here. The thieves have foot, crossbow and horse, and sentries hidden in the tunnels. In the innermost chamber hang the last fascicles of the Qianli Sutra.
column3: 沙里埋着半座废窟，窟口被盗经贼掏成了老鼠洞，一条条地道通到四面八方。千佛洞的经卷、关内收藏家的银子、过路的贼，都在这里进进出出。窝里的贼步、弩、骑都有，地道里还藏着暗哨。最里面的洞里，挂着千里经的最后几卷。

column2: This nest of thieves is cleared out and all ten fascicles of the Qianli Sutra are together again. At the end of the last, all three hundred names are there, but the final passage is only half copied, with a small note below: 'This section copied by the bookkeeper. Unfinished. To be completed on the way back.' The bookkeeper owes half a sutra more, says Liaozhang. But while the caves have scriptures and collectors inside the Pass have silver, there'll be no end of sutra thieves. Clear this nest and before long a new one will crawl into the tunnels.
column3: 这一窝贼被清了出去，千里经十卷凑齐了。最后一卷的末尾，三百个名字一个不少，最后一段经文却只抄了一半，下面一行小字：「此段账房抄，未毕，回程补。」了账说，账房欠的，又多了半段经。可千佛洞的经还在，关内的银子还在，盗经贼就杀不完；这一窝清了，过一阵，地道里又会钻进新的一窝。

column2: The Gold Mask Camp
column3: 金面大营

column2: A great camp on the gravel desert, banners thick on both sides of its gate, Gold Mask swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders drawn up in three formations, their masks joined into one blaze of gold in the sun that makes you squint. This is the Gold Masks' home camp, half a day from the Lord's gate. At the entrance a Gold Mask beats a bronze gong, stroke after stroke, as if counting.
column3: 戈壁上一座大营，营门两侧插满了旗，金面刀卫、弩手、骑卫列成三阵，面具在太阳底下连成一片金光，晃得人睁不开眼。这里是金面卫的老营，离洞主的山门只剩半天的路。营门口一个金面卫敲着铜锣，一声一声，像在数着什么。

column2: The Gold Masks fall back to the gate. The gong is struck every night, says the man who beats it, three hundred strokes. When they're done the Lord takes a lamp into the Qianli Cave and sits before the three hundred faceless figures until dawn. 'Ten years, and he's never missed a night.' Before he goes in he always takes off the golden mask and hangs it at the cave mouth. 'He says in front of them he can't wear someone else's face.'
column3: 金面卫退回了山门，敲锣的那个说锣是每晚敲的，三百下，敲完了，洞主就提着一盏灯进千里窟，在三百个没有脸的人跟前坐到天亮。「十年了，一晚上都没落下。」他说洞主进窟以前，总要摘下金面挂在窟口，「他说在他们跟前，不能戴别人的脸」。

column2: The Boulder Fan
column3: 乱石扇

column2: Outside the mountain mouth spreads a great fan of broken stone crisscrossed by dry gullies. The Gold Masks have an outpost in the widest gully guarding the path up to the gate, though no outsider can find where that path runs. Your old camel guide crouches to look at the stones and his face changes. 'The clouds are black over the mountains. We have to get them out of that gully, fast.'
column3: 山口外铺开一大片扇形的碎石滩，滩上横七竖八全是干沟。金面卫在一条最宽的干沟里扎了个哨营，守着通往山门的小路，可小路在哪儿，外人谁也找不着。带路的老驼夫蹲下来看了看石头，脸色变了：「山里的云黑了，得赶紧把他们从沟里弄出来。」

column2: You drive the outpost out of the gully and have barely reached high ground when the flood comes down it from the mountains, and the camp is gone in a blink. The shaken Gold Masks are won over. This is an alluvial fan, the old guide says: water rushing out of the mountain mouth drops the big boulders first, and the further out, the finer the stones. 'Walk toward where the stones get bigger and you'll reach the mountain mouth.' The path is behind the biggest pile of boulders.
column3: 你们把哨营从沟里打了出来，刚上高处，山洪就顺着干沟冲下来，营盘眨眼没了。金面卫惊魂未定，对你们服了气。老驼夫说，这是洪积扇：水冲出山口，大石头先落下，越往外石头越细，「顺着石头越来越大的方向走，就是山口」。小路就在最大那堆石头后面。

column2: The Goldbeater's
column3: 金箔铺

column2: In a little shop at the foot of the hill an endless tink-tink rings out: an old goldbeater sandwiches gold between sheets of black paper and beats it, stroke by stroke. Mountain bandits have heard there's gold here and burst in to rob him, but the gold is so thin one breath would blow it away, and all they grab is crumpled paper. The old man doesn't look up and keeps beating. 'What's the hurry? Not one stroke can be skipped.'
column3: 山脚一间小铺子里叮叮当当响个不停，一个老金箔匠把金子夹在乌金纸里，一锤一锤地打。一伙山匪听说铺子里有金，闯进来要抢，可铺子里的金子薄得一口气就能吹飞，抢到手里的全是一团团揉皱的纸。老匠人头也不抬，接着打：「急什么，一锤也不能少。」

column2: The bandits chased off, the old man lays down his hammer and opens for trade. He made the Lord's golden mask, he says: a wooden face underneath, and every grain of gold the Lord recovered, brought in a little at a time, he beat into leaf and laid on layer by layer. 'One tenth of an ounce, beaten out, will cover a table.' It is the gold scraped from the three hundred faces. Two hundredths are still missing; the left end of the mask's eyebrow has always been bare.
column3: 山匪被打跑，老匠人放下锤子，开了张跟你们做买卖。他说洞主的金面是他打的：底子是木面，洞主追回来的金子一分分送来，他打成箔，一层层贴上去，「一钱金打成箔，能铺满一张桌子」。那是三百张脸上刮下来的金。还差二分，金面左眉梢一直空着。

column2: Days Cave
column3: 刻日窟

column2: A small cave at the foot of the hill, its mouth guarded by Gold Mask crossbowmen who let no one in: it's where the Lord used to live. Sutra thieves think he keeps his private treasure inside, and have circled up the cliff to lower men down to the entrance on ropes. The crossbowmen shoot at those above while blocking those at the door, and can't cover both.
column3: 山脚一座小窟，窟口守着一队金面弩手，不许人进，说是洞主从前住的地方。一伙盗经贼以为里面藏着洞主的私宝，绕到崖上，拿绳子往窟口吊人。弩手们一面射崖上的，一面挡窟口的，顾头顾不了尾。

column2: The thieves chased off, you look into the cave. No treasure, only walls covered in scratches, one a day, in fives, with a line of writing here and there: 'Another day. No one came.' 'Today impostors came.' 'Today the fourth scraper was caught.' Beside the newest mark: 'Today the mirrors signalled someone coming under the Qian banner. Real or false, I don't know.'
column3: 盗经贼被打跑，你们往窟里看：没有宝，四面墙上刻满划痕，一天一道，五道一组，偶尔有一行字：「又一日，无人来。」「今日来了一伙冒名的。」「今日刮脸的抓到第四个。」最新的一道旁边写着：「今日镜子报信，有人打千字旗来，不知真假。」

column2: Bronze Face Slope
column3: 铜面坡

column2: On the open grassy slope a great troop of riders and foot soldiers blocks the way, led by six in bronze masks numbered one to six. They've heard someone called A-Qi is travelling with you, and charge without a word: for seven years they've been caught, punished and masked, and the youngest never showed his face. A-Qi hides behind a camel, white as chalk.
column3: 开阔的草坡上，一大队骑卫和步卒拦住了去路，打头的六个戴着铜面，从一到六。他们听说你们身边跟着一个叫阿七的，二话不说就冲了上来：七年了，他们被抓、被罚、被戴上铜面，那个最小的却一直没露面。阿七躲在骆驼后面，脸色煞白。

column2: The bronze masks beaten back, number one takes off his mask, walks over to A-Qi and looks at him a long while, then brushes the sand off him. 'You've grown.' They weren't hunting A-Qi to beat him, he says; it was the Lord's word: 'Not one of the seven can be missing. Miss one and the sum can't be made up.' He takes out a blank bronze mask engraved 'seven'. 'Wear it or don't. Your choice.'
column3: 铜面卫被打退，戴「一」的那个摘下面具，走到阿七跟前看了半天，抬手拍掉他身上的沙：「长这么高了。」他说追阿七不是要揍他，是洞主说的：「七个人一个不能少，少一个，那一钱二分就凑不齐。」他掏出一张空着的铜面，刻着「七」：「戴不戴，你自己定。」

column2: The Waiting Scaffold
column3: 候画架

column2: Under the cliff at the edge of the desert stands a tall wooden scaffold, solidly built, with a little glue pot on top kept warm over a small fire. Mural thieves have their eyes on it, meaning to climb up and peel the paintings above, and are grappling with the two Gold Masks who mind it. The scaffold sways with every blow.
column3: 戈壁边的崖下立着一座高高的木脚手架，搭得结结实实，架顶摆着一口小胶锅，锅底下还温着火。一伙盗壁贼看中了这座架子，想爬上去揭崖上的画，正跟看架子的两个金面卫打成一团，架子被撞得直晃。

column2: The thieves chased off, the guard breathes again. The Lord put up this scaffold seven years ago, he says, and the glue pot has been kept warm every day. 'The Lord says whatever day the painter comes, he must be able to go straight up. He mustn't be kept waiting.' A few days ago word came that Wu the painter had tried a face on an earth wall. 'When the Lord heard, he didn't sleep all night. Then he filled the glue pot again.'
column3: 盗壁贼被打跑，看架子的金面卫松了口气。他说架子是洞主七年前搭的，胶锅天天温着，「洞主说，画匠哪天来，哪天就能上架，不能让人家等」。前几天有人捎来话，说吴画匠在一面土墙上试画了一张脸，「洞主听了，一夜没睡，又把胶锅添满了」。

column2: The Golden Mask Gate
column3: 金面山门

column2: Before the gate rises a long flight of stone steps, and at the top stands a man in a golden mask, a piece missing at the left end of its eyebrow so the wood shows through. Behind him Gold Masks crowd the steps, swords drawn, crossbows spanned. Liaozhang stands at the bottom, looks up and calls, 'Master.' The masked man doesn't move. He says two words, 'Go back,' turns and goes in through the gate, and the Gold Masks charge down.
column3: 山门前是一道长长的石阶，石阶尽头站着一个人，脸上一张金面，左边眉梢缺了一块，露出底下的木头。他身后的金面卫刀出鞘、弩上弦，压满了台阶。了账站在阶下，仰着头喊了一声「师父」。金面人一动不动，只说了两个字：「回去。」说完转身进了山门，金面卫冲了下来。

column2: The Gold Masks are beaten back inside the gate. Liaozhang raises his debt book high toward it and shouts word by word: 'What the Qianli caravan owed the temple is settled! What the temple owes the caravan, I've written down too! Master, all that's left is what you owe yourself!' No answer from within. After a long time the gate creaks open a crack, and stays that way.
column3: 金面卫被打退到门里，了账冲着山门把债簿高高举起，一字一字地喊：「千里号欠寺里的，两清了！寺里欠千里号的，我也记上了！师父，就剩你欠你自己的那一笔！」山门里没有回音。过了很久，那扇门「吱」地开了一道缝，没有关上。

column2: The Loading Yard
column3: 装粮场

column2: A dozen big carts stand in an open yard where dozens of masked men are loading grain, the sacks stamped with that red featureless mask, small hard desert grain trickling from their mouths. The moment they see you they grab carrying poles and span crossbows and close round the carts, as if caught at something shameful.
column3: 一片空场上停着十几辆大车，几十个戴金面的人正往车上装粮，粮袋上盖着那张没有五官的红印，袋口还漏着粒小壳硬的戈壁粮。他们一见你们，抄起扁担、拉起弩，把车围在中间，好像被人撞破了什么见不得人的事。

column2: The loaders beaten back, their leader begs you with clasped hands: 'Whatever you do, don't tell the porridge shed below.' The Lord and his men broke land at the desert edge and planted it themselves: seven years, from crops that wouldn't take to a full granary, carted down by night every autumn. 'The Lord says the porridge is the Qianli caravan's treat. He's only keeping it going for them. It's not his merit, and no name goes on it.'
column3: 装粮的金面卫被打退，领头的拱手求你们：「千万别跟山下的粥棚说。」这些粮是洞主带着他们在戈壁边开荒种的，七年，从种不活到种满仓，每年秋天夜里送下去，「洞主说，粥是千里号请的，他只是替千里号续上，不是他的功德，不许留名」。

column2: Desert Fields
column3: 戈壁田

column2: At the foot of the hills, along the edge of the fan, a field has been broken: the ridges are crooked, as if dug hoe by hoe by people who didn't know farming, yet the millet stands waist high. Sand bandits have charged in at harvest time and reaped a broad swathe for themselves, and a few masked men are fighting them with sickles, which are shorter than swords, and getting the worst of it.
column3: 山脚的扇边上开出了一片田，田埂歪歪扭扭，像是不会种地的人一锄头一锄头挖出来的，田里的粟子却长得齐腰高。一伙沙匪趁着秋收冲进了田里，抢割了一大片，几个戴金面的人拿着镰刀跟他们拼，镰刀比刀短，吃了大亏。

column2: The bandits chased off, the masked men crouch to pick up the trampled ears. The first year this field gave nothing, one says, so the Lord went down to learn from old farmers and was laughed at: 'Even the Gold Mask has to learn farming!' The second year they got two sacks, the third a cartload. 'The Lord ploughs harder than any of us. He says the porridge shed mustn't go short for a single year.'
column3: 沙匪被打跑，戴金面的人们蹲下来捡被踩倒的穗子。一个人说，这片田头一年颗粒无收，洞主就去山下请教种地的老农，被人笑话「金面的人也要学种地」；第二年收了两袋，第三年收了一车。「洞主犁地比我们都狠，」他说，「他说粥棚一年都不能断。」

column2: Two Chisels
column3: 双凿声

column2: At night you rest beneath a cliff outside the gate, and from inside the rock comes the clink of chisels, one high, one low: two of them. A band of sutra thieves has followed the sound too, thinking someone's digging for treasure in the cliff, and they draw their knives to block the hole and snatch whatever's found. The chiselling stops.
column3: 夜里，你们在山门外的一处崖下歇脚，崖里传来叮叮的凿石声，一声高一声低，是两把凿子。一伙盗经贼也循着声音摸了过来，以为是有人在崖里挖宝，拔刀要堵住洞口抢个现成。凿石声一下子停了。

column2: The thieves chased off, a Gold Mask pokes his mud-covered head out of a crack in the cliff. The other chisel is Cao San from the walkway, he says. Every few days the Lord creeps into the cliff by a hidden passage from the back of the mountain and patches the rock with Cao San until dawn. 'Half that chisel ghost the villagers talk about is the Lord.' The two never exchange a word. When the work's done, one bowl of cold porridge each, and they go their separate ways.
column3: 盗经贼被打跑，一个金面卫从崖缝里探出满是泥的头。他说另一把凿子是栈道上的曹三：每隔几天，洞主就从后山暗道摸进崖里，跟曹三一起补崖，补到天亮，「村里人说的凿鬼，有一半是洞主」。两人从不说话，凿完了一人一碗凉粥，各走各的。

column2: The Nameless Bowl
column3: 无名碗

column2: Beside the gate is a small kitchen with a pot of porridge simmering on the stove. Mountain bandits have barged in, turned the place upside down, and, finding the porridge too thin, kicked the pot over. On the stove sits an old wooden bowl with nothing carved on its bottom, and they're using it as a dice cup.
column3: 山门旁边一间小伙房，灶上蹲着一口锅，锅里熬着粥。一伙山匪闯了进来，把伙房翻得乱七八糟，嫌粥稀，一脚踢翻了锅。灶台上摆着一只旧木碗，碗底什么字也没刻，被他们拿起来当了骰盅。

column2: The bandits chased off, the old Gold Mask who keeps the kitchen picks up the bowl and wipes it clean. This is the Lord's bowl, he says, turned from the same log as the three hundred in the porridge shed below. That winter the Lord was the little monk who tended the porridge fire; the Qianli caravan ate what he cooked, and the bookkeeper taught him the abacus between mouthfuls. When he went up the mountain to keep the caves, the bowl went with him, and he never let anyone carve a name on it. 'The names are for them.'
column3: 山匪被打跑，伙房的老金面卫捡起木碗擦干净。他说这是洞主的碗，跟粥棚那三百只是一块木头旋的。那年冬天，洞主是粥棚里烧火的小和尚，千里号的人喝他熬的粥，账房边喝边教他打算盘。后来他上山管窟，碗跟着他，从不许刻名字：「名字留给他们。」

column2: Steps of a Thousand Lamps
column3: 千灯阶

column2: Inside the gate another flight of steps climbs between rock walls lined with lamp niches, every lamp unlit. The Gold Masks' best have all fallen back here: swordsmen hold the steps, crossbowmen the niche mouths on either side, riders gallop back and forth on the terrace at the top. At the top is the Qianli Cave, and at its mouth hangs one lamp, lit.
column3: 山门里面又是一道石阶，两边的石壁上凿满了灯龛，龛里的灯都灭着。金面卫的精锐全退到了这里，刀卫守阶，弩手占了两侧的龛口，骑卫在阶顶的平台上来回奔驰。阶顶就是千里窟，窟口挂着一盏灯，一盏，亮着。

column2: The Gold Masks' line breaks and they fall back to the top of the steps without pursuing. Looking round, you see Liaozhang, A-Qi and all the others who followed you along the way standing on the steps behind you. On the terrace above, the man in the golden mask waits beneath the lamp at the Qianli Cave's mouth, a monk's staff in his hand.
column3: 金面卫的阵被冲开，他们退到了阶顶，没有再追。你们回头看，了账、阿七，还有一路跟上来的人，都站在你们身后的台阶上。阶顶的平台上，那个戴金面的人站在千里窟的灯下，手里提着一根禅杖，等着你们。

column2: Sandbag Wall
column3: 沙袋墙

column2: A long wall of sandbags lies across the desert, the Lord's inner court behind it. Gold Mask crossbowmen line its top, swordsmen stand at its foot, and riders kick up dust behind it. Every few paces a small mirror is planted on the wall, and as you approach they flash signals up the mountain.
column3: 戈壁上横着一道沙袋垒成的长墙，墙后是洞主的内院。墙头上一排金面弩手，墙下一队金面刀卫，墙后还有骑卫在扬尘。墙上每隔几步插着一面小镜子，你们一靠近，镜子就一闪一闪地往山上报信。

column2: The Gold Masks on the wall withdraw and you climb up to look over. The inner court is empty save for a path to the cliff, where one cave mouth on its waist glows with lamplight. The mirrors on the wall are still flashing, but the message has changed. The wall guards say it means 'Not thieves.'
column3: 墙上的金面卫退了，你们爬上墙头往里看：内院空空荡荡，只有一条小路通到崖上，崖腰一个窟口亮着一点灯火。墙上的镜子还在一闪一闪，可报的信变了，守墙的人说，那是「来者非贼」。

column2: Rules of the Inner Gate
column3: 内门规

column2: A black lacquered board hangs at the door of the Lord's inner court with four rules: '1. On entering, say whom you owe. 2. Do not ask about the Lord's face. 3. When you see the lamp at the cave mouth, put down what you are holding. 4. Anyone under the Qian banner who cannot name the camel may not enter.' The Gold Masks on the door question you rule by rule, and at the fourth, out come their swords.
column3: 洞主内院的门口挂着一块黑漆木牌，写着四条规矩：「一、进门先报自己欠谁的账。二、不许问洞主的脸。三、见了窟口的灯，手里的东西放下。四、打千字旗的，答不出骆驼的名字，不许进门。」守门的一队金面卫照着牌子一条条盘问你们，问到第四条，刀就出鞘了。

column2: The door guards beaten back, you answer: 'Lao Huang.' Their captain stares, then explains. Saying whom you owe: everyone who comes here owes the Qianli caravan something. Not asking about the face: the Lord's face belongs to three hundred people. Putting things down: no blades before that lamp. And the camel: seven parties of impostors came and not one could answer. 'Anyone who's really walked a stretch with the Qianli caravan knows Lao Huang.'
column3: 守门的被打退，你们答：「老黄。」头目愣了，这才讲：报账，是因为来这里的人都欠千里号点什么；不问脸，是因为洞主的脸是三百个人的；放下东西，是那盏灯前不许带刀；问骆驼，是因为冒名的七拨没一个答得上，「真跟千里号走过一段的，都认得老黄」。

column2: Pilgrims' Lodge
column3: 香客寮

column2: Outside the gate stands a pilgrims' lodge, meant for those climbing the mountain to rest. It's run by a Gold Mask quartermaster who, since the Lord never comes down, has made his own rules: pilgrims leave their shoes at the door and a tenth of their baggage is 'kept for the Lord'. The storeroom behind is heaped with shoes, and the pilgrims queue barefoot in the yard, angry and silent.
column3: 山门外一座香客寮，本是给上山的香客歇脚的。管寮的是金面卫的一个粮官，仗着洞主不下山，私设规矩：香客进寮，鞋要脱下来留着，行李抽一成，说是「替洞主保管」。寮后的库房里，鞋堆成了山，香客们光着脚在院子里排队，敢怒不敢言。

column2: The quartermaster and his men, beaten into submission, are tied up and sent up the mountain; even the Gold Masks say 'the Lord will flay him when he hears'. The pilgrims get their own shoes back, the lodge heats water again, and the first old woman to soak her feet groans with pleasure.
column3: 粮官和他的手下被打服了，捆了送上山去，金面卫自己都说「洞主知道了得扒他一层皮」。香客们穿回了自己的鞋，寮里重新烧起了热水，第一个泡脚的老太太舒服得直哼哼。

column2: The quartermaster's storeroom yields over four hundred pairs of shoes, seventy pilgrims' bundles, two chests of embezzled gold leaf, a dozen jars of honey, and a private ledger recording every coin he squeezed out of the pilgrims.
column3: 粮官的库房里抄出四百多双鞋、七十包香客的行李、两箱私吞的金箔、十几坛蜂蜜和一本黑账，黑账上记着他从香客身上刮下来的每一文钱。

column2: Every time you pass, the pilgrims who got their shoes back have left things for you at the lodge: a bag of dried apricots, a few flatbreads, and a pair of newly stitched shoes with 'Safe Journey' embroidered on the insoles.
column3: 每次路过，拿回了鞋的香客们都托寮里的人给你们留东西：一包杏干、几个馕、一双纳好的新鞋，鞋垫上绣着「平安」两个字。

column2: The Impound Yard
column3: 扣驼场

column2: A big camel yard with dozens of camels crammed in its pens, all impounded from caravans that passed themselves off as the Qianli. The yard is minded by a pack of old lags among the Gold Masks who don't report the camels but sell them on the quiet across the desert, three days' drinking per camel. The animals are bellowing with hunger; the pens were grazed bare long ago.
column3: 一座大驼场，圈里挤着几十峰骆驼，都是从冒名千里号的商队手里扣下来的。看场的是一伙金面卫里的兵油子，扣下骆驼不报上去，偷偷卖到戈壁那边，卖一峰喝三天酒。骆驼饿得直叫，圈里的草早就啃光了。

column2: The old lags chased off, you open the pens and the camels surge toward the river to drink. The yard's old camel hand says he knows camels, not people. 'The impostors were false, but the camels aren't. They're good camels.' He registers each impounded camel and says that when the Lord gives the word, the ones that should go back will go back to their owners.
column3: 兵油子们被打跑，你们开了圈门，骆驼们涌向河边喝水。驼场的老驼工说，他认得骆驼，不认得人：「冒名的人假，骆驼不假，骆驼是好骆驼。」他把扣下的骆驼一峰峰登记好，说等洞主发话，该还的还给原主。

column2: The yard gives up forty impounded camels, twenty good saddles, six sacks of bean fodder, a bundle of camel sale contracts, and, hidden in the hay, the old lags' three jars of wine and a set of dice.
column3: 驼场里抄出四十峰扣下的骆驼、二十副好鞍子、六袋豆料、一捆卖驼的契约，还有兵油子们藏在草堆里的三坛酒和一副骰子。

column2: Every time you pass, the old camel hand fills a few skins with camel milk and stuffs a pouch with sun-hardened camel-milk curds. 'Keep one in your mouth and it'll stave off thirst for half a day.'
column3: 每次路过，老驼工都给你们灌满几皮囊驼奶，再塞一兜晒得硬邦邦的驼奶疙瘩：「含在嘴里，能顶半天渴。」

column2: The Qianli Cave
column3: 千里窟

column2: A lamp hangs at the mouth of the Qianli Cave, its wick twisted from camel hair, its oil sent by the King of the Sand Sea. Inside, three hundred donors hold censers in blue-green robes under a lapis sky, and every face is blank. The Lord of the Caves stands beneath the lamp, a piece missing from his mask's left brow, his Gold Masks drawn up before the steps in three ranks. 'Seven parties have come under the Qian banner,' he says. 'Every one said they were the ones who came after. You're the eighth.'
column3: 千里窟口挂着一盏灯，灯芯是驼毛搓的，灯油是沙海的王送的。窟里三百个供养人手捧香炉，衣袍青绿，头顶一片青金的天，脸全是空的。千佛洞主站在灯下，金面左眉缺了一块，金面卫三路列在阶前。「前面来过七拨打千字旗的，」他说，「每一拨都说自己是后来者。你们是第八拨。」

column2: The Lord is beaten. One by one you lay things before the lamp: Cao San's token, Liaozhang's debt book, Wu Banbi's message, crispy rice from the porridge shed; last of all A-Qi sets down his two hundredths of gold.
