The Lord takes off his mask. Beneath is the face of a man about thirty, eyes red from sleepless nights: the little monk who tended the porridge fire. 'In spring the Qianli caravan left for the Oasis King's city. The bookkeeper said one cart was missing and he'd settle it there, and no one was to follow. Ten years, and not one came back.' He hands the mask to Wu Banbi. 'Scrape it. Give it back to them.' Then: 'Go to the King's city. He may not own you. But you've seen his face.'
column3: 洞主败了，你们把东西一样样放在灯前：曹三的铜牌、了账的债簿、吴半壁的话、粥棚的锅巴，阿七把二分金放在最后。洞主摘下金面，是一张三十来岁的脸，眼睛熬得通红。他就是当年粥棚里烧火的小和尚。「千里号开春往绿洲王城去了，账房说差一车，到王城再对，不许人跟。十年，没一个回来。」他把金面交给吴半壁：「刮下来，还给他们。」又说：「你们去王城，他未必认你们。可他的脸，你们见过了。」

column2: The Royal Boundary Stone
column3: 王城界碑

column2: Beyond the camel yard a new stone stands on the gravel plain: 'Boundary of the Oasis King's City.' Beside it is a toll shed manned by tax men in the city's livery who stop everyone to collect 'city entry tax' in advance, and every traveller's name, goods and origin must be entered in the books. They find your banner of doubtful origin, call up a band of swordsmen and block the road.
column3: 驼场再往外，戈壁上立着一块新碑：「绿洲王城界。」碑旁搭着一座税棚，几个穿王城号衣的税丁守着，见人就拦，要先交「进城税」，过往的人名字、货物、来路，一样一样都得上账。他们嫌你们的旗来历不明，叫了一伙刀手来，把路堵死了。

column2: The swordsmen scattered, the tax men meekly take down your names. Their ledger is meticulous, every stroke neat, recording down to how many hairs a camel has shed. Their leader says the city's rule these days is: 'Before a person enters the city, his accounts enter first.' Beyond the stone a road stretches west, and at its end, faint in the haze, is a patch of green like a lake.
column3: 刀手被打散，税丁们乖乖收了你们的名字。他们的账簿记得极细，一笔一画，连骆驼掉了几根毛都要记。领头的说，王城如今的规矩是：「人进城，账先进城。」界碑后面，一条路伸向西边，路尽头隐约有一片绿，像一块湖。

column2: The Oasis Kingdom
column3: 绿洲王城

column2: Green Sight Rise
column3: 望绿坡

column2: Past the boundary stone the gravel climbs and climbs, and at the top of the rise lies the oasis. But a blue cloth curtain thirty feet long is strung across the crest, hiding everything beyond. Beside it sit the Royal Uncle's household men, collecting a 'green-sight fee': ten coppers for one look. Those who won't pay are blindfolded and led past. People who've been long in the gravel, they say, weep at their first sight of green. 'Weeping costs extra.'
column3: 过了界碑，戈壁一路往上抬，抬到坡顶，前面就是绿洲了。可坡顶横着一道三丈长的青布帘子，把前头遮得严严实实。帘子边坐着一伙国舅府的家丁，收「看绿钱」：一人十文，看一眼；不给钱的，蒙上眼睛牵过去。他们说，戈壁里走久了的人，头一眼看见绿，会哭，「哭也得给钱」。

column2: Down comes the curtain. Below lies a great lake ringed with woods so green they're almost black; a river runs east glittering, and at its end stands a wall of yellow earth. One of your men really does weep. The household men, as they flee, shout back over their shoulders: 'You owe ten!' An old camel man says you're the first to come under the court's banner in ten years.
column3: 帘子扯下来了。坡下是一片大湖，湖边一圈林子，绿得发黑，一条河亮闪闪地往东流，河的尽头是一道土黄的城墙。有个伙计真哭了，家丁跑之前还回头喊了一声「欠十文」。牵骆驼的老汉说，打朝廷旗号来的，十年里你们是头一拨。

column2: The Locked Shaft
column3: 锁井台

column2: A mound at the edge of the fields, and on it a well shaft capped with an iron lid and a lock bigger than a man's head. Household men of the Royal Uncle sit on the lock selling water at three coppers a ladle, and the queue runs out along the field banks. At the back an old man with knotted ropes wound round his waist is cursing at the top of his voice, a half-grown boy beside him hugging a wicker basket with a short-handled spade in it.
column3: 田边一个土台，台上一口竖井，井口扣着一块铁盖，挂着一把比人头还大的锁。国舅府的家丁坐在锁上卖水，一瓢三文，排队的人一直排到田埂上。一个腰上缠满打结绳子的老汉在队尾破口大骂，身边一个半大孩子抱着一只柳条筐，筐里是一把短柄铁锹。

column2: The lid is prised off, and carved on the stone lip is a line: 'Qian. Well 170. Zhao Mancang.' The old man is Grandpa Kan, a karez digger all his life; the boy is his grandson Little Spade. This underground channel, he says, was dug ten years ago by three hundred outsiders: three hundred shafts, a name on each. Now it's silting to death. 'I'm clearing it shaft by shaft to the mother well. Coming?'
column3: 铁盖撬开了，井口的石沿上刻着一行字：「千·第一百七十井·赵满仓」。老汉叫坎爷，掏了一辈子坎儿井，孩子是他孙子小铲。他说这条暗渠是十年前三百个外乡人挖的，三百口竖井，一口一个名字，如今渠快淤死了。「我要一口口掏到母井。跟不跟？」

column2: Horseback Ferry
column3: 驮渡口

column2: The river isn't deep, but the mud comes to your knees. A band of riders who deserted the royal cavalry have taken the crossing and named themselves Ferry Lords: to cross you must ride one of their horses, a hundred coppers a trip, and walking isn't allowed. Grandpa Kan had no money, so they took the knotted rope from his waist as his fare. He says that rope matters more than his life, and he's hopping mad to get it back.
column3: 河水不深，可淤泥没膝。一伙从王城铁骑里逃出来的骑手占了渡口，自封「渡爷」：想过河，就得骑他们的马，一趟一百文，不坐还不行。坎爷没钱，被他们扣下了腰上那根打结的绳子当船钱。坎爷说那绳子比他的命还要紧，跳着脚要去抢。

column2: The Ferry Lords go into the mud, horses and all. Grandpa Kan winds the rope back round his waist and, eyes shut, feels along it knot by knot: three hundred knots, and the length between two knots is the distance between two shafts. 'It's the map of the channel,' he says. 'I can't read. The rope can.' The very last knot is tied strangely and nobody can undo it. He calls it the dead knot.
column3: 渡爷们连人带马滚进了泥里。坎爷把绳子一圈圈缠回腰上，闭着眼睛一个结一个结地摸：三百个结，两个结之间的长短，就是两口井之间的远近。「这是渠的图，」他说，「我不识字，绳子识。」最末一个结打得古怪，谁也解不开，他管它叫死结。

column2: Cormorant Bend
column3: 鸬鹚湾

column2: A dozen little boats drift in the bend, cormorants squatting at each bow with straw rings round their necks. A troop of royal horse has camped on the bank, under orders to 'patrol the river'. In fact they sit all day watching the cormorants fish and keep every catch, leaving each fishing family two small ones a day. The birds cry with hunger, and the children cry louder.
column3: 河湾里漂着十几条小船，每条船头蹲着几只鸬鹚，脖子上套着草环。一队王城铁骑在岸上安营，说是奉命「巡河」，实际天天坐着看鸬鹚捉鱼，捉上来的都归他们，渔户一家人一天只分到两条小的。鸬鹚饿得直叫，渔户的孩子比鸬鹚叫得还响。

column2: The horsemen gone, the cormorants eat their fill. The old fisherman remembers the channel diggers: every evening after work they'd wash in the river, three hundred heads bobbing side by side. A thin gentleman never went in. He sat on the bank counting heads, twice a night. 'If one was missing, he wouldn't eat.' Grandpa Kan nods. 'That was the gentleman who reckoned the wells.'
column3: 铁骑跑了，鸬鹚吃了个饱。老渔户记得那些挖渠的人：每天收工都下河洗澡，三百个脑袋一个挨一个冒在水面上。有个瘦先生从不下水，坐在岸上数人头，一晚上数两遍，「少一个，他就不吃饭」。坎爷在一旁点头：「那就是算井的先生。」

column2: Sand-Filler Ridge
column3: 填沙梁

column2: A sand ridge lies across the underground channel, and along its crest a row of shaft mouths shows like a string of beads half swallowed. At night a crew comes with donkey carts and tips sand down the shafts load after load, swordsmen at either end, archers lying along the crest, riders patrolling back and forth. They work harder than any digger. Little Spade lies behind a dune and counts: three shafts filled a night.
column3: 一道沙梁压在暗渠上头，梁脊上露着一排井口，像一串被沙子吞了一半的珠子。夜里有一伙人赶着驴车来，一车车往井口里倒沙子，刀手守在两头，弓手趴在沙脊上，马队来回巡。他们干得比挖渠的还卖力。小铲趴在沙丘后头数：一夜填三口。

column2: The fillers flee, and the pay tallies stuck in their carts are stamped 'House of the Royal Uncle'. Lying at a shaft mouth listening to the water below, Grandpa Kan explains why the channel runs underground: send water ten li through an open ditch and the sun drinks most of it; under the sand the sun can't reach it and the wind can't dry it. 'They're not filling sand. They're filling a whole city's water.'
column3: 填沙的人跑了，驴车上插着的工钱签刻着「国舅府」。坎爷趴在井口听底下的水声，说这条渠为什么要走在地底下：明渠走十里，太阳就喝掉一大半；暗渠在沙底下走，太阳喝不着，风也吹不干。「他们填的不是沙，是一城人的水。」

column2: The Well-Children's School
column3: 井娃塾

column2: A mud hut at the village entrance, 'SCHOOL' written over the door in charcoal. A squad of royal halberdiers has taken the benches and is gambling on the children's slates, roaring over the dice. The children crowd at the window, clinging to the lattice to peer in, one girl still clutching a stub of slate pencil. The diggers built this hut, Grandpa Kan says, and after work they taught the village children to count.
column3: 村口一间泥屋，门楣上用炭写着「塾」。屋里的长凳被一队王城戟士占了，他们把孩子们的石板拿来当骰盘，赌得吆五喝六。孩子们挤在窗外，扒着窗棂往里看，一个女孩手里还攥着半截石笔。坎爷说，这屋子是当年挖渠的人搭的，收工了就教村里的娃娃数数。

column2: The halberdiers pocket their dice and go, and the children win back their benches and chant you a counting song: 'One well, one man; ten wells, ten men; three hundred wells, three hundred men, and Teacher isn't counted.' What does 'Teacher isn't counted' mean? Not one of them can say. That's how the gentleman sang it, says Grandpa Kan. 'He reckoned everything. He never reckoned himself.'
column3: 戟士们揣着骰子走了，孩子们抢回长凳，齐声背了一段数数的歌给你们听：「一口井，一个人；十口井，十个人；三百口井，三百人，先生不算人。」问「先生不算人」是什么意思，没一个说得上来。坎爷说那先生教的时候就这么唱，「他算账，从来不算他自己」。

column2: The Wheel Mill
column3: 转轮磨坊

column2: A watermill by the river, its wooden wheel standing still: upstream, the Royal Uncle's riders have blocked the channel mouth with sacks of straw. The mill is their granary now, piled with the 'water grain' the villages pay. The miller, a pockmarked man, has been set to feeding their horses. For every trough of fodder he fills, he quietly spits in it once.
column3: 河边一座水磨坊，木轮子停着不转，上游的渠口被国舅府的马队拿草袋堵了。磨坊成了他们的粮仓，附近几个村子交的「水粮」都堆在这里。磨坊主是个麻脸汉子，被派去给马喂料，他喂一槽料，偷偷往马槽里吐一口唾沫。

column2: The straw sacks dragged away, the channel water rushes down, and with a creak the wheel turns again. The diggers helped him mount this wheel, the miller says. 'The gentleman worked it out: so much water, so big a wheel, not an inch off.' He polishes his millstone till it gleams. From now on, when you come, his flour is free.
column3: 草袋扒开了，渠水冲下来，木轮子吱呀一声又转了。磨坊主说，这轮子是挖渠的人帮他装的，「先生算的，水多大，轮多大，一寸不差」。他把磨盘擦得锃亮，说以后你们来，他磨的面不收钱。

column2: The riders' store yields twelve sacks of wheat, a cartload of baked naan, two jars of mutton fat, half a sack of raisins, and a 'water grain' register in which every household is in debt. The one that owes most has only a single well.
column3: 马队的仓里抄出十二袋麦子、一车烤好的馕、两坛羊油、半麻袋葡萄干，还有一本「水粮簿」，上头每户都欠着，欠得最多的那户只有一口井。

column2: Every time you pass, the miller fills your flour bags from the fresh grinding, his pocked face crinkling into a grin, and stuffs a handful of roasted wheat into the mouth of each bag. 'For when you're hungry on the road. Chew these.'
column3: 每次路过，磨坊主都把刚磨的新面装满你们的面袋，麻脸笑成一朵花，又往袋口塞一把炒熟的麦粒：「路上饿了，嚼这个。」

column2: Name-Stone Sands
column3: 拆名沙

column2: A line of shafts across the sand, their stone lips prised off one by one and stacked on camel backs. A squad of royal halberdiers is doing it, ordered by the Royal Uncle to wall his garden in the city; the stones, they say, are 'square and lay well'. Every stone bears a name, and they've ground half of each away. Little Spade throws himself over one well lip to guard it and gets kicked aside.
column3: 沙地里一溜井口，井沿的石头被一块块撬了下来，码在骆驼背上。撬石头的是一队王城戟士，奉国舅之命去城里给他的花园砌墙，说这些石头「方正，好砌」。石头上都刻着名字，被他们磨得只剩半边。小铲急得用身子护住一口井沿，被一脚踹开。

column2: The halberdiers leave with empty camels. Forty-one stones go back in place, and Little Spade traces the worn names back with charcoal one by one. Each digger, says Grandpa Kan, carved his own name only when his shaft first gave water. 'They made a contract with the well by their names: while the well lasts, the man is still here.'
column3: 戟士们空着驼背走了。四十一块石头搬回原处，小铲拿炭把磨掉的名字一个个描回去。坎爷说，每个挖渠的人，自己那口井第一回出水时，才亲手刻上自己的名字，「他们拿名字给井立契：井在，人就算还在这儿」。

column2: Golden Carp Pond
column3: 金鲤塘

column2: Where the channel comes up it used to feed the village ditches. Now a new dam turns the water aside, and all of it pours into the Royal Uncle's square pond, where a hundred golden carp swim beneath a pavilion inscribed 'The Joy of Fish'. The village fields are cracking open. Archers, riders and swordsmen guard the dam in three camps on three shifts a day, more closely than a city gate.
column3: 暗渠出口原本流进村里的水沟，如今被一道新坝拦住，水拐了个弯，全灌进国舅家的一口方塘。塘里游着上百条金鲤，塘边搭着凉亭，亭子上挂着「鱼乐」二字。村里的田裂着口子，守坝的弓手、骑手、刀手三路扎营，一天三班，比守城门还严。

column2: The dam breaks, the water rushes back into the village ditches, and the golden carp flounder in the mud. The villagers fill a basket for soup. The dam was built from the old bricks of the channel outlet, each one stamped with the character 'Qian'. Grandpa Kan picks them out one by one. 'When we rebuild the outlet, we'll use them again.'
column3: 坝扒开了，水哗地回到村沟里，金鲤在泥里扑腾，村里人捡了一筐回去炖汤。坝是拿暗渠出口的旧砖砌的，每块砖上压着一个「千」字。坎爷把砖一块块拣出来：「等渠口重砌，还用它们。」

column2: Horse-Thief Kiln
column3: 偷马窑

column2: A great brick kiln stands on the waste ground, its mouth wide enough for two horses abreast. The fire went out long ago, but neighing comes from inside: a band of royal riders turned outlaw keeps all the horses they've stolen nearby in the kiln, archers on the flue at the top, foot soldiers at the door. There are over thirty horses, every mane clipped to the same shape so their owners won't know them.
column3: 荒地上一座大砖窑，窑口能并排进两匹马。窑早就熄了，里面却传出马嘶：一伙落草的王城骑手把附近偷来的马全藏在窑里，弓手守着窑顶的烟道，步卒守着窑门。偷来的马有三十多匹，每匹的鬃毛都被剪成了一个样子，好让失主认不出来。

column2: The thieves driven off, the owners come with their own whistles, and the horses walk out of the kiln one by one. The kiln wall is covered with the diggers' scratchings: 'Three years. Bricks: one hundred and ten thousand four hundred', each stroke as neat as a ledger. Below, someone has carved a crooked verse: 'Firing bricks into the third year, I met my wife by the kiln fire.'
column3: 马贼被赶走，失主们拿着各家的口哨来唤，马一匹匹自己走出了窑。窑壁上满是挖渠的人留下的刻划：「三年，砖十一万又四百」，一笔一画像账本。下面还有人刻了一句歪诗：「烧砖烧到第三年，媳妇是窑火边认的。」

column2: The Naan Pit
column3: 馕坑铺

column2: A naan pit dug in the sand, a reed-mat shelter beside it, where a fat cook slaps dough on the pit walls with a skill that's plainly palace-trained: the loaves even carry stamped flowers. But no one dares buy. The Royal Uncle's household men stand guard and say the cook was thrown out of the palace. 'Bread from a man the palace threw out is poisoned.' The cook tosses his burnt loaves to the stray dogs one by one, and the dogs eat with relish.
column3: 沙地上挖着一个馕坑，坑边搭着芦席棚，棚里一个胖厨子正往坑壁上贴馕，手艺一看就是宫里出来的：馕上还压着花。可没人敢买：国舅府的家丁守在棚前，说这厨子是被王城赶出来的，「宫里赶出来的人做的馕，有毒」。厨子把烤焦的馕一个个扔给野狗，狗吃得很香。

column2: The household men gone, you eat three loaves and nobody dies. The delighted cook shakes out his flour sacks and trades whatever he's got. Five years he ran the stove in the palace kitchen, he says. The King never showed himself, but every meal had to have one extra bowl and pair of chopsticks laid, the food served into it and cleared away untouched. 'The King said: keep it for whoever comes after.'
column3: 家丁跑了，你们吃了三个馕，谁也没死，厨子乐得把面口袋都抖了出来，有什么就换什么。他说他在王城的膳房掌了五年勺：王从不露面，每顿饭却都要多摆一副碗筷，饭菜照盛，原样撤下来。「王说，给后头来的人留着。」

column2: The Royal Channel Stele
column3: 王渠碑

column2: Where the channel line bends stands a new stele in large characters: 'The Qianli Channel is royal property. Clearing it without leave is punishable by death.' A rank of royal archers stands before it, bows strung. Grandpa Kan reads it and his beard shakes. 'Rubbish! This channel was dug for the common people!' The archers don't argue. They simply lower their arrowheads a little, to his feet.
column3: 渠线拐弯的地方新立了一块碑，碑上大字：「千里渠属王产，私掏者斩。」碑前站着一排王城弓手，弓都上了弦。坎爷看完碑文，胡子直抖：「放屁！这渠是挖给老百姓的！」弓手们不跟他吵，只把箭头往下压了压，对准了他的脚。

column2: The archers fall back, and their captain, an honest man, comes clean: the stele was put up last year by the Royal Uncle's house. Grandpa Kan won't be cowed and has his men dig under it, and out comes an older stele, small characters cut neat and square: 'The channel complete, it belongs to the people. The King takes not one ladle.' It bears the royal seal, dated the spring of the digging's fourth year.
column3: 弓手们退了，领头的是个老实人，交了底：碑是去年国舅府立的。坎爷不信邪，带人在碑底下一刨，刨出一块旧碑，字小，刻得端端正正：「渠成，归民，王不取一瓢。」落款盖着一方王印，年份是挖渠第四年的春天。

column2: The Polo Ground
column3: 击鞠场

column2: A stretch of flat ground has been fenced off as a polo field, right on top of the channel line. Some young masters of the Royal Uncle's house come every day with mounted retainers to play, and every time a hoof lands a shaft caves in. They aim for the shafts on purpose: the ball dropping into a well 'makes a lovely sound'. Someone at the side keeps score: a point for every collapsed well.
column3: 一片平地被圈成了马球场，正好圈在渠线上。国舅府的几个少爷带着家丁骑手天天来打马球，马蹄子一踩，井口就塌一个，他们还专挑井口打，说球滚进井里「有声响，好听」。场边有人记分，塌一口井，记一分。

column2: The young masters' horses bolt and the mallets lie scattered. Grandpa Kan has red willow cut and woven into hoops, lining the collapsed shafts layer by layer. One young rider left behind doesn't run but crouches to help weave. His grandfather drove a cart for the Qianli caravan, he says. 'I grew up hearing him talk about this channel.' He splits the scoreboard for firewood.
column3: 少爷们的马被惊散了，球杆扔了一地。坎爷带人砍来红柳枝，编成圈子一层层衬进塌了的井口里。一个被扔下的小骑手没跑，蹲下来帮着编，说他爷爷也是当年给千里号赶车的，「我从小听他说这渠」。他把那块记分牌劈了当柴。

column2: Drought Camp
column3: 旱民寨

column2: At the edge of the salt flat that was once a lake bed, a sprawl of shacks has grown into a stronghold. Its people fled the drought villages to the west. Hungry enough, they use hoes for swords, rob travellers of grain, ride gaunt horses and shoot arrows they whittled themselves. A board hangs at the gate: 'Borrowing grain. Not returning it.' Grandpa Kan sighs at it. 'Once the channel runs, they won't need to come here.'
column3: 旧湖底的盐滩边上，一片窝棚连成了寨子。住的是西边旱村里逃出来的人，饿急了，拿锄头当刀，拦路抢粮，骑的是瘦马，射的是自己削的箭。寨口挂着一块木牌：「借粮，不还。」坎爷看着那块牌子叹气：「渠通了，他们就不用来这儿了。」

column2: This time the camp breaks up and the stolen grain goes back to the households along the road. But the villages to the west are still dry, and as long as their land is cracking, more desperate people will drag their families here and put up another 'borrowing grain' board. Before long you'll have to come again.
column3: 这一回寨子散了，抢来的粮分回了路上的人家。可西边的村子还旱着，只要那边还有地裂着口子，就还会有饿急了的人拖家带口来这里，再竖起一块「借粮」的牌子。过一阵，还得再来一趟。

column2: Windlass Flats
column3: 辘轳滩

column2: Half buried in the sand stands a row of wooden windlasses the diggers used to haul up earth, three hundred of them side by side like a line of kneeling men. A band of royal archers has camped here, breaking them up and whittling the axles into arrow shafts, cursing with every one: 'This wood's damned hard.' A bundle of new arrows already lies by their fire.
column3: 沙滩上半埋着一排木头辘轳，是当年挖渠时往上吊土用的，三百副，一副挨一副，像一排跪着的人。一伙王城弓手在这里扎营，把辘轳拆开，木轴削成箭杆，削一根骂一句：「这木头真硬。」营火边已经堆了一捆新箭。

column2: The archers withdraw and you set the unbroken windlasses upright. The crossbeams are carved all over with the diggers' little debts: 'Li Si owes Wang Wu one bowl of noodles', 'Zhao Mancang owes Meng Xiaoshan one pair of shoes', each followed by 'repaid'. All but one: 'Teacher owes everyone a round of wine.' Grandpa Kan laughs. 'That round never did get drunk.'
column3: 弓手们退了，你们扶起没拆的辘轳。横梁上刻满了挖渠人的小账：「李四欠王五面一碗」「赵满仓欠孟小山鞋一双」，每一笔后头都刻着「已还」。只有一笔没有：「先生欠众人酒一顿。」坎爷笑了：「这顿酒，到底也没喝上。」

column2: Muffled Bells
column3: 闷铃驼队

column2: At night a caravan passes behind the dunes, every camel bell stuffed with wool so not one rings. The loads aren't goods but skins of water. These are water thieves who winch water up secretly from the channel shafts and carry it deep into the desert to sell to travellers at ten times the price, guarded by foot soldiers, archers and riders, moving fast.
column3: 夜里沙丘后头走过一支驼队，骆驼脖子上的铃铛都塞了羊毛，一声不响。驼背上不是货，是一囊囊水。这是一伙偷水贩子，从暗渠的井口偷偷往上吊水，运进沙漠深处，十倍价钱卖给过路的人。步卒、弓手、骑手护着，走得飞快。

column2: The water thieves are caught and their skins emptied back into the channel. Their biggest customers, the leader says, weren't travellers but a troop of men heading east in golden masks. 'Gold masks, paid in gold, wanted water badly.' Grandpa Kan frowns. 'Men from the Thousand Buddha Caves? What are they doing near the King's city?'
column3: 偷水贩子被截住，水囊卸了一地，倒回渠里。领头的说，他们的大主顾不是过路人，是一队往东去的金面人，「戴着金面具，给的是金子，要水要得急」。坎爷皱眉：「千佛洞的人，跑到王城来做什么？」

column2: IOU's Grave
column3: 欠条冢

column2: A small grave in the sand with a stone before it: 'Dog. Here lies IOU.' A band of riders is digging it up, sure the Qianli people buried treasure in a dog's grave where no one would think to look. Furious, Grandpa Kan whacks their horses' rumps with his spade. 'It's a dog! A real dog!' The riders dig all the harder: the more he says it, the more it sounds like treasure.
column3: 沙地上一座小坟，坟前一块石头，刻着「犬·欠条之墓」。一伙骑手在这里挖坟，说千里号的人把宝贝埋在了狗坟里，好让人想不到。坎爷气得拿铁锹敲他们的马屁股：「那是条狗！一条真狗！」骑手们挖得更来劲了：越是这么说，越像有宝。

column2: The riders dig to the bottom, find only a dog's skeleton and a brass-tagged collar, and ride off swearing. The tag reads 'Qianli caravan. Well watch.' The dog had sharp ears, says Grandpa Kan: whenever a shaft was about to cave in, it barked first, and it saved men twice. The gentleman entered its wages in the ledger, one bone a day, for three years, and never missed a day. You heap the grave up again.
column3: 骑手们挖到底，只有一副狗骨头和一只铜牌项圈，骂骂咧咧地跑了。项圈上刻着「千里号·看井」。坎爷说这狗耳朵灵，哪口井要塌，它先叫，救过两回人。先生在账上给它记工钱，一天一根骨头，记了三年，一天没欠。你们把坟重新堆好。

column2: The Silting Camp
column3: 封渠营

column2: The sand fillers, the stone thieves, the outlet blockers all draw their orders from here. A large camp sits on the middle of the channel line, halberdiers, archers and cavalry in three ranks, mounds of straw sacks and sandbags piled inside. A great notice on the wall assigns the work month by month: which shafts to block this month, which to fill the next. It's as methodical as building a channel, only in reverse.
column3: 填沙的、拆石的、堵渠口的，原来都从这里领差。一座大营扎在渠线的中段，戟士、弓手、铁骑三路排开，营里堆着成山的草袋和沙包，墙上贴着一张大告示，按月分派：这个月堵哪几口，下个月填哪几口，像修渠一样有章法，只是反着修。

column2: The camp falls. On the back of the notice is a written order from the Royal Uncle's steward: 'If the channel runs, water is cheap; if water is cheap, the House's stores are worthless. Fill it slowly. Let no one notice.' Grandpa Kan tucks it into his coat. 'Keep it. When we reach the city, we'll show the King.'
column3: 大营破了，告示揭下来，背面是一道国舅府管家的手谕：「渠通则水贱，水贱则府仓无用。缓缓填之，勿使人觉。」坎爷把手谕揣进怀里：「留着，到了王城，给王看。」

column2: The House of Niches
column3: 三百龛屋

column2: A long earthen house, its walls cut with niches the size of a sleeping man, tier upon tier: the diggers' lodgings. Now a gang of hired swords runs it as a carters' inn at fifty coppers a niche a night. Travellers curl up in the niches to sleep, and the gang charges a 'name fee' on top: whoever's name is carved at the niche mouth, the sleeper must answer 'present' for him.
column3: 一座长长的土屋，墙上凿满了能躺一个人的土龛，一层叠一层。这是当年挖渠人的住处。如今一伙雇刀手占了这儿开大车店，一个龛一晚上五十文，过路的人缩在龛里睡觉，他们还要另收「借名费」：龛口刻着谁的名字，睡的人就得替那人喊一声到。

column2: The swords are turned out, and you count: two hundred and ninety-nine niches carved with names and laid with straw mats. One has no name and no mat, only a flat stone for a desk, its walls written over with sums, the ink soaked into the earth. One line was changed three times: 'one year' struck out, 'two years' struck out, 'three years'. 'The gentleman's estimate,' says Grandpa Kan. 'He reckoned one year. It took three.'
column3: 刀手们被赶了出去。你们数了一遍：二百九十九个龛刻着名字，铺着草垫；只有一个龛没名字，没垫子，里面放着一块平石当桌子，龛壁写满了算式，墨都渗进了土里。其中一行改了三回：「一年」划掉，「两年」划掉，「三年」。坎爷说：「先生算的工期。他算一年，挖了三年。」

column2: Washing-Bat Beach
column3: 捶衣滩

column2: Clotheslines are strung all along the river beach, and a white-haired granny sits on a stone beating laundry, glancing at the far bank between strokes. A squad of royal archers is camped over there with nothing to do but shoot at her washing, a hole an arrow, a hit on the collar wins. She neither scolds nor hides. She just gathers the shot clothes into her basket and mends them one by one at night.
column3: 河滩上拉着一道道晾衣绳，一个白头发的阿婆坐在石头上捶衣裳，捶一下，看一眼对岸。对岸扎着一队王城弓手，闲得没事，拿她晾的衣裳当靶子，一箭一个洞，射中领口的算赢。阿婆不骂也不躲，只把射破的衣裳收进篮子，晚上一件件补。

column2: The archers gone, the granny washes a tub of your sweat-stained shirts. She washed for the diggers for three years. In the fourth spring the channel ran, and two hundred and ninety-nine men shouldered their bundles and set off in a line. The thin gentleman stood on this beach counting them one by one, and when he'd finished he didn't follow. 'After that, no one saw him,' she says. 'Some said he went into the city.'
column3: 弓手们走了，阿婆给你们洗了一盆汗衫。她给挖渠的人洗了三年衣裳。第四年开春，渠通了，二百九十九个人背着包袱排成一行上了路，那个瘦先生站在河滩上，一个一个地数，数完了，自己没跟上去。「后来就不见他了，」阿婆说，「有人说，进城了。」

column2: The Sealed Tool Store
column3: 封锹库

column2: At the far edge of the waste stands a stone storehouse, three paper seals across its door, all stamped by the Royal Uncle's house. Picked troops guard it: royal cavalry, armoured halberdiers, archers on the roof. When the channel was finished, Grandpa Kan says, the diggers stored all their gear here 'for whoever clears the channel later'. For years the Royal Uncle's house has let no one in.
column3: 荒野尽头一座石砌的库房，门上贴着三道封条，盖的都是国舅府的印。库前守着一支精兵，有王城铁骑，有重甲戟士，弓手站在库顶上。坎爷说渠挖完以后，挖渠人的家伙什都收在这里，「留给以后掏渠的人用」。可这些年，国舅府谁也不许进。

column2: The picked troops withdraw, the seals come off, and the door creaks open: three hundred iron spades hang on the walls, three hundred miners' lamps stand on shelves, their oil long dried. A measuring rod leans in the corner, marked with fine divisions. Grandpa Kan picks out fifty spades for the village lads. 'Clear the channel first. Hang them back when you're done.'
column3: 精兵退了，封条揭下，库门吱呀开了：三百把铁锹挂在墙上，三百盏矿灯排在架子上，灯里的油早就干了。墙角立着一根量杆，刻满了细细的格。坎爷挑了五十把锹分给村里的后生：「先掏渠，掏完了再挂回来。」

column2: Snow-Watch Road
column3: 望雪道

column2: In the southern sands an old road climbs away, its mouth barred with cheval-de-frise and held by picked troops: archers on the heights, halberdiers in the centre, cavalry roving on the flanks. The Royal Uncle's orders: no one goes south along this road, for the south is 'the King's water source, and even a look is theft'. Grandpa Kan walked it when he was young. 'At the end of it you can see snow.'
column3: 南边沙地里有一条往上走的旧路，路口横着鹿角拒马，一支精兵守着：弓手居高，戟士压阵，铁骑在两边游走。他们奉国舅的令，不许任何人沿这条路往南走，说南边是「王的水源，看一眼都是偷」。坎爷说他年轻时走过这条路，「路的尽头能看见雪」。

column2: The barriers come down, you climb to the road's end, and there it is: a line of snow peaks on the edge of the sky. Grandpa Kan points to the vast gravel fan below them. Snowmelt doesn't run on the surface; it sinks into the gravel and seeps downhill, and only at the fan's foot, where the ground turns fine, does it come up again. That's why oases grow at the foot of the fans. 'The water's source is in the sky,' he says. 'Is the Royal Uncle in charge of that?'
column3: 拒马拆了，你们爬到路尽头，果然看见天边一线雪山。坎爷指着山脚那一大片碎石滩：雪化了的水不走河面，钻进碎石滩里一路往下渗，渗到滩脚土细了，才冒出来，所以绿洲都长在滩脚。「水源在天上，」他说，「国舅管得着吗？」

column2: The Bitter Salt Pans
column3: 苦盐田

column2: In the southern desert lies a blinding whiteness: a great salt pan. Dozens of men in leg irons bend over raking salt, a day's raking for two naan. The overseers are the Royal Uncle's salt wardens with archers, cavalry and halberdiers, each holding a whip soaked in brine. Among the rakers is a lad of eighteen or nineteen whose irons are a size heavier than the rest. He's 'a thief', the warden says, 'and a thief's son too'.
column3: 南边沙漠里一片白，白得晃眼，是一大片盐田。几十个戴脚镣的人弯着腰耙盐，耙一天，换两个馕。看守是国舅府的盐监，带着弓手、铁骑和戟士，一人一根浸了盐水的鞭子。耙盐的人里有个十八九岁的后生，脚镣比别人粗一圈，盐监说他是「贼，还是贼的儿子」。

column2: The wardens flee and the irons are smashed. The lad is Ge Xiaolun; his father, Ge Dalun, was the Qianli caravan's carter. He followed his father's trail all the way to the King's city, where the old case register reads: 'Ge Dalun. Stole one royal water cart. At large.' He set out to clear his father's name, and within a month was a thief himself. He scoops up a handful of salt. 'This was a lake once. Year by year the sun dried the water off. The water could leave. The salt couldn't.'
column3: 盐监跑了，脚镣砸开。后生叫葛小轮，他爹葛大轮是千里号的车把式。他找爹找到王城，旧案簿上写着：「葛大轮，盗王城水车一辆，在逃。」他要替爹洗冤，没过一个月，自己也成了贼。他捧起一把盐：「这儿原先是湖，太阳把水一年年晒干，水走了，盐走不了。」

column2: Alfalfa Camel Yard
column3: 苜蓿驼场

column2: A great camel yard in the sand, a hundred camels penned and haystacks piled like hills: the Royal Uncle's yard, feeding the camel trains that haul his water. Archers sit atop the stacks, and when a herder's camel wanders up to nibble they put an arrow in the sand in front of its hooves. The herders' camels are so hungry they gnaw their own halters.
column3: 沙地里一座大驼场，圈着上百峰骆驼，草垛垒得像小山。这是国舅府的驼场，专给府里运水的驼队喂料。一队弓手坐在草垛顶上，看见附近牧民的骆驼来蹭草，就一箭射在驼蹄前头。牧民的骆驼饿得啃自己的缰绳。

column2: The archers tumble off the haystacks and run, and the herders drive their camels in to eat their fill. On the yard wall the old herdsman finds marks the diggers drew: one stroke per camel, a whole wall of them. 'Back then the spoil was carried off on camels. The gentleman kept accounts even of the camels.'
column3: 弓手们从草垛上滚下来跑了，牧民们把骆驼赶进来吃了个饱。老牧民在驼场的墙上找到当年挖渠人画的记号：一道线一峰骆驼，画了整整一面墙，「那时候他们的土是骆驼驮出去的，先生连骆驼都记了账」。

column2: The yard yields forty bales of alfalfa, two hundred empty waterskins, eight new camel saddles, six sacks of wind-dried mutton, and a 'water price list' issued by the Royal Uncle's house: the drier the year, the higher the price. The top column reads 'price of a life'.
column3: 驼场里抄出四十捆苜蓿、两百只空水囊、八副新驼鞍、六口袋风干羊肉，还有一张国舅府开的「水价单」：越旱越贵，最贵的那一栏写着「人命价」。

column2: Every time you pass, the herders lead over a few well-rested camels to carry your goods, a knotted cord tied round each bale of fodder, the knots exactly your number. 'Grandpa Kan taught us. Lend so many, get back so many.'
column3: 每次路过，牧民们都牵来几峰歇足了的骆驼替你们驮货，草料捆上系一根打了结的绳子，结数正好是你们的人数：「坎爷教的，借多少，还多少。」

column2: Three-Inch Law Booth
column3: 三寸讼棚

column2: A reed-mat booth by the road, a board at its door: 'Petitions written. Win guaranteed. Pay one melon if you win.' It's being torn down by the Royal Uncle's thugs, foot, archers and horse together, no small party. The owner is a scrawny advocate nicknamed Three-Inch Ma, for his three-inch tongue; he himself stands not much taller than it. He's huddled under his table clutching a pile of petitions, mouth still going: 'Assault is against the law! The booth is a separate charge!'
column3: 路边一个芦席棚，门口挂着块木牌：「代写状纸，包赢，赢了给个瓜。」棚子正被一伙人拆：国舅府的打手，步卒、弓手、骑手都有，来头不小。棚主是个瘦小的讼师，外号麻三寸，舌头三寸，个子也就比舌头高一点。他抱着一摞状纸缩在桌子底下，嘴还没停：「打人犯律！拆棚子另算！」

column2: The thugs gone, Three-Inch Ma crawls out from under the table, dusts himself off, hears Ge Xiaolun out and slaps the table. 'I'll take it. One melon.' He counts on his fingers: first find the 'stolen' silver bowl, then find someone who saw, and last dig out the ten-year-old accounts of that water cart. 'Get all three,' he says, 'and I can talk a dead case back to life.'
column3: 打手们跑了，麻三寸从桌子底下爬出来，掸掸灰，听葛小轮讲完，一拍桌子：「这案子我接了，一个瓜。」他扳着指头数：先找那只「偷来」的银碗，再找一个看见的人，最后翻十年前那辆水车的旧账。「三样齐了，」他说，「死案也能说活。」

column2: The Red Veil Tent
column3: 红盖头帐

column2: A tent in the wilds hung all over with red cloth, but it's no wedding. The Royal Uncle's steward has his men at the door, pressing the woman inside to remarry his distant nephew. 'Your man left six years ago. He's long dead out there.' She's called Yue Niang and holds a plot by the door whose head is the very outlet of a channel shaft. She stands in the doorway with a spade, her six-year-old son hiding behind her.
column3: 荒野里一顶帐篷挂满了红布，却不是喜事：国舅府的管家带着家丁堵在帐门口，逼帐里的女人改嫁给他的远房侄子，「你男人走了六年，早死在外头了」。女人叫月娘，守着门口一块地，地头正好是一口渠井的出水口。她拿着一把铁锹站在门口，六岁的儿子躲在她身后。

column2: The steward and his men flee. Yue Niang's husband, Meng Xiaoshan, was a digger. He left with the others in the fourth spring, saying, 'I'll be back next spring.' She takes you to see the well: two names carved on its lip, Meng Xiaoshan and Yue Niang. The boy lies on the lip counting the shafts down the line, gets muddled at thirty, and starts again.
column3: 管家和家丁跑了。月娘的男人叫孟小山，是挖渠的人，第四年开春跟着大伙上了路，走时说「明年开春就回」。她带你们去看那口井，井沿刻着两个名字：孟小山，月娘。孩子趴在井沿上一口口地数渠井，数到三十就乱了，从头再数。

column2: Night Ledger Slope
column3: 夜账坡

column2: A young shepherd sits crying on a sandy slope: a band of riders has driven off his sheep to trade for the Royal Uncle's water tickets. As a boy, he says, he grazed his flock on this slope every night, and the diggers' camp lay just below. 'Every night they lit a fire and read out the accounts, and I listened up here.' Even as he cries, he can still recite a few lines.
column3: 一个放羊的后生坐在沙坡上哭，他的羊被一伙骑手赶走了，那伙人说要拿羊去换国舅府的水票。后生说他小时候天天夜里在这坡上放羊，坡下就是挖渠人的营地，「他们每晚点着火念账，我就在坡上听」。他一边哭一边还能背出几句来。

column2: The sheep are brought back, and the shepherd recites those years of night accounts for you, day by day, word perfect. The last night went like this: 'Such a day of such a month: the mother well gives water. Owed to the King's city: one cart of water, paid off with the channel. The channel is complete. Still owing...' Here, he says, the gentleman shut the ledger, sat half the night, and never read on.
column3: 羊追回来了。后生把那几年的夜账背给你们听，一天一天，一字不差。最后一晚的账是这样的：「某月某日，母井出水。欠王城水一车，以渠抵之。渠已成。尚欠……」他说念到这里，先生把账本合上了，坐了半夜，再没念下去。

column2: The Water Hoard
column3: 囤水仓

column2: A high-walled compound on the plain, rows of great jars buried in the ground, their mouths sealed with clay stamped by the Royal Uncle's house: his water store, three thousand jars, more than a village drinks in ten years. The house's best troops guard it in three ranks, with crossbows mounted on the walls. The villagers say that in the dry years, not one jar was opened.
column3: 荒原上一座高墙大院，院里一排排埋在地下的大缸，缸口封着泥，泥上盖着国舅府的印。这是国舅的水仓，三千缸水，比一个村子十年喝的还多。守仓的是府里最精的兵，三路列阵，墙上还架着弩。附近村里的人说，旱的那几年，这仓一缸都没开过。

column2: The store falls, the clay seals are knocked open one by one, and the water goes to the villages around. Years are carved on the jars, the oldest from the great drought eleven years ago, before the Qianli caravan ever came. An old guard says the Royal Uncle began hoarding water that year and has done it for eleven years, 'so the city would never go thirsty again'. Yet no one could ever drink from his store.
column3: 仓破了，泥封一个个敲开，水分给了附近的村子。缸身上刻着年份，最早的一批是十一年前的大旱那年，比千里号来得还早。看仓的老兵说，国舅从那年起就开始囤水，囤了十一年，「说是再也不让城里渴着」，可他自己的仓，谁也喝不上。

column2: West Gate Iron Market
column3: 西关铁市

column2: Outside the King's city's west gate there used to be an iron market, forges in a row, villagers bringing gold dust panned from the river to trade for spades, picks and iron rings to line their wells. Now every forge is cold. The Royal Uncle's house has posted halberdiers at the entrance and declared iron goods 'a House monopoly', one spade for a tael of gold, and no private smithing allowed. The smiths squat by their cold forges sharpening knives: their own kitchen knives.
column3: 王城西关外原本有个铁市，打铁的炉子一字排开，村里人拿河里淘的金沙来换锹、换镐、换箍井的铁环。如今炉子全熄了：国舅府派了一队戟士守着市口，宣布铁器「归府专卖」，一把锹卖一两金子，还不许私铺打。铁匠们蹲在冷炉边磨刀，磨的是自家的菜刀。

column2: The halberdiers are driven from the market and the forges light up one after another, hammering ringing half the street. Villagers bring gold dust to trade for iron, and the smiths forge Grandpa Kan a hundred new spades and won't take a coin. The old smith remembers the three years of digging: all three hundred men's well rings were made here. 'When that gentleman paid, if he was one copper short he'd make it up. If he couldn't, he'd write it down and come back next day without fail.' With the new spades Grandpa Kan hires crews. The channel will be cleared shaft by shaft.
column3: 戟士被赶出市口，炉子一个接一个生起了火，叮当声响了半条街。村里人捧着金沙来换铁，铁匠们给坎爷打了一百把新锹，说不要钱。老铁匠还记得挖渠那三年，三百人的铁环都是在这儿打的：「那先生付账，差一文都要补上，补不上就记着，第二天准来。」坎爷用新锹雇了人手，渠要一口口掏通了。

column2: First Water Mouth
column3: 头水口

column2: Where the channel surfaces by the riverbank there's a stone mouth, and only a few drops trickle from it. Grandpa Kan and his new crews have cleared their way down from upstream shaft by shaft; only this last stretch remains. But a troop of royal horse has arrived on the Royal Uncle's orders 'to seize those clearing the King's channel without leave', and a whip has already cracked across Little Spade's back.
column3: 暗渠在河岸边冒出地面的地方，砌着一道石口，石口里只滴答着几滴水。坎爷带着新雇的后生从上游一口口掏过来，就差这最后一截。可一队王城铁骑赶到了，奉国舅府的令「拿私掏王渠的人」，马鞭子已经抽到了小铲的背上。

column2: The horsemen pull back. The last spadeful comes out, the stone mouth gurgles once, and then water gushes from it, ice cold, tasting of snow. The children leap in and splash. Grandpa Kan crouches by the mouth catching the water in his hands, saying nothing for a long time. At last he says, 'Three hundred men's water. It's come back.'
column3: 铁骑退了。最后一锹下去，石口里先是咕嘟一声，接着水哗地冲了出来，冰凉，喝一口，有一股雪的味道。娃娃们跳进水里扑腾。坎爷蹲在石口边，用手接着水，接了很久也不说话，后来说了一句：「三百个人的水，回来了。」

column2: The Sand Pawnshop
column3: 沙底当

column2: A cellar dug into a hollow in the sand with a 'PAWN' sign at its mouth: a smugglers' black pawnshop that takes anything and asks nothing. Riders guard the entrance and circle any stranger, kicking up sand. Three-Inch Ma has learned that the silver bowl Ge Xiaolun was convicted of stealing is pawned here: a vine spray engraved on the bottom, exactly as the ticket describes.
column3: 沙窝里挖了个地窖，窖口挂着个「当」字，是走私客开的黑当铺，什么都收，不问来路。一伙骑手在窖口守着，见生人就绕着你转圈子扬沙。葛小轮被判偷的那只银碗，麻三寸打听到就当在这里：碗底刻着一枝葡萄，跟当票上写的一模一样。

column2: The riders scattered, the pawnbroker meekly produces his ledger. The bowl was pawned three months before, a full month before Ge Xiaolun supposedly stole it, and the pawner signed 'Liu of the House'. Three-Inch Ma tears out the page, folds it and tucks it in his shoe. 'The bowl was pawned while it was still supposed to be in the palace. So which bowl did he steal?'
column3: 骑手们被打散，当铺掌柜乖乖翻出了底簿。那只银碗当在三个月前，比葛小轮「偷碗」还早了一个月，当碗的人画的押是「府中刘」。麻三寸把底簿那一页撕下来，叠好塞进鞋里：「碗还在宫里就被当了，那他偷的是哪只？」

column2: Press-Gang Slope
column3: 抓匠坡

column2: With the channel running, karez skills are suddenly worth something. The Royal Uncle's riders are seizing men all over the slope: anyone who can go down a shaft is tied up and taken to dig a 'House channel' for the Royal Uncle. A row of wooden cages stands on the slope, a dozen lads inside, all Grandpa Kan's newly trained apprentices. Leaning on his spade at the foot of the slope, he says: 'My apprentices. I'll collect them myself.'
column3: 渠一通，掏渠的手艺忽然值钱了。国舅府的骑手满坡抓人：凡是会下井的，一律绑了带走，说是去给国舅府挖「府渠」。坡上一排木笼，笼里关着十几个后生，都是坎爷新教出来的徒弟。坎爷拄着锹站在坡下，说：「我的徒弟，我自己来领。」

column2: The riders flee and the cages are split open. The apprentices crawl out one by one and bow to Grandpa Kan. He lines them up to number off, and when they reach thirteen he nods. 'All here.' The gentleman taught him that, he says. 'When men go out, count them. When they come back, count them again. Only when the count's right is the day done.'
column3: 骑手们跑了，木笼劈开，徒弟们一个个钻出来，先给坎爷磕了个头。坎爷让他们排成一行报数，报到十三，他点点头：「齐了。」他说这是先生教他的：「人出门，先点数；人回来，再点数。数对了，才算一天。」

column2: Channel Watchtower
column3: 望渠楼

column2: An earthen tower beside the channel line, a squad of royal archers crouched on top putting an arrow at the feet of anyone who goes near a shaft. The Royal Uncle's house built it recently, officially 'to protect the royal channel', in fact to stop anyone clearing it. Grandpa Kan's apprentices lie in a sandy gully clutching their spades; every time one raises his head, an arrow flies over it.
column3: 渠线边一座土楼，楼顶蹲着一队王城弓手，谁走到渠井边上，就一箭射在他脚前。楼是国舅府新盖的，名义上「护王渠」，实际上是不许人掏。坎爷的徒弟们抱着锹趴在沙沟里，抬一下头，一支箭就从头顶飞过去。

column2: The archers come down. You climb to the top and look east: the shaft mouths run off along the channel line like a string of beads, all the way to the woods by the lake, and beyond that, the city wall. Grandpa Kan looks for a long time. 'The gentleman used to say: this string of beads is off an abacus.'
column3: 弓手们下了楼。你们爬上楼顶往东看：一口口井口顺着渠线排出去，像一串珠子，一直串到湖边的林子，再往东，是王城的城墙。坎爷看了很久，说：「先生说过，这串珠子，算盘上的。」

column2: The Water-Sharing Stone
column3: 分水石

column2: Here the channel splits into seven streams for seven villages. The divider is a great stone set across the channel, cut with seven grooves of different widths. A band of the Royal Uncle's riders is holding some masons down, forcing them to widen the groove that runs to his estate and narrow the others. With every blow of the chisel, an old villager nearby lets out a sob.
column3: 渠水在这里分成七股，流进七个村子，分水的是一块横在渠里的大石，石上凿着宽窄不一的七道槽。一伙国舅府的骑手按着几个石匠，逼他们把通往国舅庄子的那道槽凿宽，别的槽凿窄。石匠凿一下，旁边村里的老人就哭一声。

column2: The riders flee, and the masons patch the widened groove back. Those seven grooves, says Grandpa Kan, were cut by the gentleman after counting every household. 'Not a household off, not a mouth off.' In the stone beside them his small writing remains: 'As the people increase, the grooves change with them.' Grandpa Kan says he'll go and count tomorrow. 'There've been a lot of babies these last years.'
column3: 骑手们跑了，石匠们把凿宽的槽又补上了一截。坎爷说七道槽是先生当年一户户数过人口才凿的，「一户不差，一口不差」。槽边的石面上还留着先生的小字：「人增，槽随之改。」坎爷说他明天就去数，「这几年，村里多了好些娃娃」。

column2: Bird-Net Wood
column3: 捕雀林

column2: In the woods on the lake's south shore fine nets hang everywhere, yellow finches fluttering in them. A gaunt old bird catcher is kept here under guard by the Royal Uncle's archers, netting birds for the Royal Uncle's garden every day and going hungry when he falls short. He's the witness, says Three-Inch Ma: on market day he was squatting right beside Ge Xiaolun selling birds. As soon as he sees you, the old man ducks behind his cages.
column3: 湖南岸的林子里张满了细网，网上挂着扑腾的黄雀。一个干瘦的捕雀老汉被一队国舅府的弓手看着，天天替国舅的花园捕鸟，捕不够数就挨饿。麻三寸说要找的证人就是他：那天集市上，他就蹲在葛小轮旁边卖鸟。老汉一看见你们，赶紧把头埋进鸟笼后头。

column2: The archers flee and the old man opens the cages one by one; finches flutter out all through the wood. Only then does he talk. That day a man in the House's livery slipped something shiny into Ge Xiaolun's bundle from behind, then turned and shouted 'Thief!' As he left he laughed: 'The old one steals a cart, the young one steals a bowl. A family of thieves.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，老汉把笼门一个个打开，黄雀扑棱棱飞了一林子。他这才开口：那天一个穿府里衣裳的人，从背后往葛小轮的包袱里塞了一样亮东西，转身就喊「抓贼」。那人走时还笑了一句：「老的偷车，小的偷碗，一家子贼。」

column2: Deserters' Dunes
column3: 逃营沙

column2: Among the dunes stands a ragged camp of halberdiers, archers and riders in the uniforms of the King's guard, every badge torn off. Deserters: they hide from anyone they see and fight when they can't. Ge Xiaolun recognises their leader as the man who marched him off to the salt pans. The leader recognises him too and reddens, but doesn't lower his blade.
column3: 沙丘间扎着一座破营，营里戟士、弓手、骑手都有，穿的是王城禁军的号衣，可号衣上的徽记都拆了。这是一伙逃兵，见人就躲，躲不过就打。葛小轮认出了领头的：当初押他去盐田的就是这人。领头的也认出了他，脸一红，刀却没放下。

column2: The deserters yield, and their leader apologises to Ge Xiaolun. They ran, he says, because once the Royal Uncle took over the guard, drill became carrying water jars for his house. Only one man in the guard ever taught real skills: Drill Master Tie. After the Ge case he was driven from the city, and they hear he's somewhere in the southern sands, still drilling. 'Drilling a pack of children.'
column3: 逃兵们服了，领头的跟葛小轮赔了不是。他们逃出来，是因为国舅接管禁军以后，操练改成了给府里扛水缸。他说禁军里只有一个人教过真本事：铁教头。葛小轮的案子以后，铁教头就被赶出了城，听说在南边沙里，还在练兵，「练的是一帮孩子」。

column2: The Burning Cart
column3: 焚卷车

column2: A line of carts rolls along the desert road, loaded with wooden chests and guarded fore and aft by halberdiers, archers and cavalry, a barrel of lamp oil dragging behind. One look at the seals on the chests and Three-Inch Ma jumps: the old case files of the city's court of punishments. The Royal Uncle's house has ordered all files more than ten years old burnt. The Qianli water cart case is exactly ten.
column3: 沙路上走着一队车，车上装满了木箱，前后押着戟士、弓手和铁骑，车尾还拖着一桶火油。麻三寸一看箱子上的封条就跳了起来：是王城刑房的旧案卷，国舅府下了令，「十年以上的旧卷，一律焚毁」。千里号那桩水车案，正好十年。

column2: The escort flees and the oil barrel rolls into a gully. After much rummaging Three-Inch Ma finds the roll: 'Ge Dalun stole one royal water cart.' But tucked at the end is the city gate's log: the cart went out of the west gate at night, and the gatekeeper noted four words: 'Left bearing royal warrant.' Ma narrows his eyes. 'A thief who steals with the King's warrant in his hand. That's a first.'
column3: 押车的跑了，火油桶滚进了沙沟。麻三寸翻了半天，翻出了那一卷：「葛大轮盗王城水车一辆」。可卷末还夹着城门的出入记：水车是夜里从西门出去的，守门的批了四个字：「持王令出。」麻三寸眯起眼：「拿着王令偷东西的贼，我还是头一回见。」

column2: Tripwire Gully
column3: 绊马沟

column2: The channel passes beneath a dry gully. A band of the Royal Uncle's riders lies in ambush on both sides, with several tripropes strung across the gully floor for the clearing crews. On Grandpa Kan's knotted rope only the last few knots remain, and the dead knot that nobody can undo is just ahead. 'The mother well's on the far side of the gully,' he says. 'Close now.'
column3: 渠线从一道干沟底下穿过去。沟两边埋伏着一队国舅府的骑手，在沟里拉了好几道绊马绳，专等掏渠的人走过来。坎爷腰上的打结绳子只剩最后几个结没摸到，那个谁也解不开的死结就在前头。他说：「母井就在沟那头，近得很。」

column2: Tripped on their own ropes, the riders flee. Grandpa Kan reaches the second-to-last knot, crouches and measures, and there at his feet is a shaft, its lip carved 'Qian. Well 299. Old Zhou.' One more, he says, and that's the mother well, and the man who dug it carved no name. 'The gentleman said he'd carve his when the accounts were settled.'
column3: 骑手们被绊了自己的绳子，跑了。坎爷摸到了绳上倒数第二个结，蹲下来一量，脚下正是一口井：井沿刻着「千·第二百九十九井·老周」。他说，再往前一口，就是母井，挖的人没刻名字。「先生说，他的那口，账清了再刻。」

column2: Wine Ambush Ridge
column3: 截酒岗

column2: In the northern open country a camel train has been cut off at the foot of a ridge, dozens of camels loaded with stacks of wine jars. The ambushers are the Royal Uncle's household men and hired blades, halberdiers, archers and riders, yelling 'Leave the wine and get lost!' The caravan's leader, a woman, has nothing but a long-handled wine ladle. She stands on the pile of jars knocking down each man who climbs up, one ladle a man.
column3: 北边野地里，一支驼队被人截在岗下，几十峰骆驼驮着一摞摞酒坛子。截路的是国舅府的家丁和雇来的刀手，戟士、弓手、骑手都有，嚷嚷着「酒留下，人滚」。驼队的女头领手里只有一把长柄酒勺，站在坛子堆上，一勺一个，把爬上来的人敲下去。

column2: The ambushers flee and the woman jumps down from the jars. She's Liu Sanniang, wine carrier for the northern vineyards. This is the spring wine for the King's city: every spring the palace orders two hundred and ninety-nine jars, not one more, not one less. 'My father delivered for six years and never missed a jar.' This is her first year, and the Royal Uncle's house has given out that not one jar of spring wine is to enter the city.
column3: 截路的人跑了，女头领从坛子堆上跳下来，自称柳三娘，北边葡萄园的酒驼子。她说这是给王城送的春酒：每年开春，宫里都订二百九十九坛，一坛不多，一坛不少，「我爹送了六年，从没错过一坛」。今年是她头一回送，国舅府却放话：春酒一坛都不许进城。

column2: The Tasting Post
column3: 尝酒卡

column2: A wooden barrier at a crossroads hung with a sign, 'Wine Inspection', manned by a squad of royal halberdiers who say they're ordered to check the spring wine for poison. Their method: drink it, jar by jar. By the time the caravan arrives they've inspected three, every face flushed and neck swollen, and they're hugging the jars shouting at Sanniang for 'another one, this one wasn't checked properly'.
column3: 路口一道木卡，卡上挂着「验酒」的牌子，守卡的是一队王城戟士，说是奉命查春酒里有没有毒。查法是：一坛一坛地喝。驼队到的时候，他们已经验了三坛，个个脸红脖子粗，抱着坛子喊三娘「再来一坛，这坛没验准」。

column2: The halberdiers collapse beneath their barrier, snoring like thunder. Liu Sanniang stamps her foot at the three empty jars: three short, and it isn't two hundred and ninety-nine any more. 'The palace men count three times every year,' she says. 'One jar short and they won't take any.' She grits her teeth and decides to detour to the old cellar in the north to make them up. 'Better three extra days than a short count.'
column3: 戟士们醉倒在卡下，鼾声震天。柳三娘看着三只空坛子直跺脚：少了三坛，就不是二百九十九了。「宫里收酒的人每年都数三遍，」她说，「少一坛都不收。」她咬咬牙，决定绕路去北边的老窖里补上，「宁可多走三天，也不能缺数」。

column2: The Leaking Wood
column3: 漏酒林

column2: As the caravan enters the woods north of the lake, a flight of arrows suddenly comes out of the trees. They don't hit people. They hit jars, a hole an arrow, wine streaming down the camels' flanks, so fragrant the squirrels poke their heads out. The archers are hired by the Huang winery, kin of the Royal Uncle's house, jealous of the Liu family's royal order. 'Leaky jars, and next year's order is ours.'
column3: 驼队走进湖北边的林子，林子里忽然飞出一阵箭，不射人，专射坛子，一箭一个洞，酒顺着驼背往下淌，香得林子里的松鼠都探出了头。放箭的是黄家酒坊雇的弓手：黄家是国舅府的亲戚，眼红柳家的王单，「坛子漏了，明年的单子就是我们的」。

column2: The archers flee, and the caravan's silent giant of a cooper plugs the holes in the jars one by one with his fingers, then daubs them with clay. When her father took on this order, Liu Sanniang says, a thin clerk came from the palace, didn't taste a drop, and counted out the money to the last copper. 'One copper over and he'd return it; one under and he'd make it up.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，驼队里那个不说话的大个子箍桶匠拿手指头一个个堵住坛子上的洞，再糊上泥。柳三娘说她爹当年接这张单子，是宫里来了个瘦瘦的文书，一口酒没尝，就把钱数得清清楚楚，「多一文退一文，少一文补一文」。

column2: Hunting Lodge Wood
column3: 猎屋林

column2: A log hunting lodge in the woods, once a resting place for the lakeside hunters, now taken by a squad of the Royal Uncle's household men as a roadside watch post, wild ducks and gazelles hanging everywhere inside and out. Old Qin the hunter has been turned out to live in the dog shed behind, while his hound is tied at the door to guard it for them. Whenever it sees Old Qin it wags its tail, too scared to bark.
column3: 林子里一座木头猎屋，原来是湖边猎户歇脚的地方，如今被国舅府的一队家丁占了，当成了伏路的哨所，屋里屋外挂满了打来的野鸭和黄羊。猎户老秦被赶到屋后的狗棚里住，他的猎狗倒被家丁拴在门口，替他们看门，看见老秦就摇尾巴，不敢叫。

column2: The household men driven off, the hound breaks its rope and leaps into Old Qin's arms. Old Qin knows Ge Xiaolun: two years ago the boy came asking his way here, 'Have you seen a royal water cart?', and Qin put him up for three days. 'Stubborn boy,' says Old Qin. 'Like his father. His father spent a night in this lodge too, back then.'
column3: 家丁被赶跑，猎狗挣开绳子扑进了老秦怀里。老秦认得葛小轮：两年前那孩子一路问到这里，问「有没有见过一辆王城的水车」，老秦留他住了三天。「这孩子死心眼，」老秦说，「跟他爹一样。他爹当年也在这屋里住过一宿。」

column2: The lodge yields twenty wind-dried wild ducks, four gazelle legs, a crock of dried curd, a bundle of arrows, and the household men's 'ambush register' with circles drawn after the names Ge Xiaolun and Three-Inch Ma.
column3: 猎屋里抄出二十只风干野鸭、四条黄羊腿、一坛酸奶疙瘩、一捆箭，还有家丁们记的「伏路簿」：葛小轮、麻三寸，名字后面都画了圈。

column2: Every time you pass, Old Qin takes down a string of smoked ducks from the rafters and has his hound lead you by a short cut round the lakeside mud. 'A dog knows the way better than a man.'
column3: 每次路过，老秦都从梁上取下一串熏好的野鸭，再让猎狗领你们走一条近道，绕开湖边的烂泥：「狗认路，比人强。」

column2: The Besieged Drill Ground
column3: 围场沙

column2: In the southern sands lies a ground ringed with stones, a row of stakes hung with straw men. Outside it a band of bounty archers waits: the Royal Uncle's house has offered a hundred taels of gold for Drill Master Tie's manual of the King's guard. They don't shoot at people. They shoot the straw men, and every time one is hit a child inside cries out. In the middle stands a one-armed old man, silent, gripping a wooden spear.
column3: 南边沙里有一片用石头圈出来的场子，场上插着一排木桩，桩上挂着草人。场子外头围着一伙赏金弓手，国舅府出了一百两金子，要铁教头那本禁军操典。他们放箭不往人身上射，专射场上的草人，射一个，场子里就有孩子哭一声。场子中央站着一个独臂老头，一声不吭，手里攥着一根木枪。

column2: The bounty archers flee and some thirty children emerge from the ground, the oldest twelve or thirteen, the youngest six or seven, each holding a wooden staff. Drill Master Tie doesn't thank you. First he has the children re-form their broken ranks and counts them one by one; only then does he turn round. 'Come back tomorrow. Today's drill isn't finished.'
column3: 赏金弓手跑了，场子里钻出三十来个孩子，大的十二三，小的才六七岁，个个手里一根木棍。铁教头没道谢，先让孩子们把散了的队列站好，一个个点过数，才转过身来：「明天再来。今天的操，还没练完。」

column2: The Old Gatekeeper
column3: 守门翁

column2: A half-collapsed mud hut in the sand, home to a hard-of-hearing old man who was gatekeeper of the city's west gate ten years ago. Some of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers are tearing off his roof, saying 'the House wants this land', and when they're done they mean to send him to the salt pans. He sits on his doorstep hugging an old lantern and won't budge for anyone. 'Thirty years I sat at a gate. I'm used to it.'
column3: 沙地里一间半塌的土屋，住着一个耳朵背的老头，十年前是王城西门的守门人。一伙国舅府的戟士正在拆他的屋顶，说这片地「府里要了」，拆完了还要把他送去盐田。老头坐在门槛上，抱着一只旧灯笼，谁拆都不挪窝：「我在门口坐了三十年，坐惯了。」

column2: The halberdiers flee. The old man remembers that night: it was the old King's own cart, the driver a dark-faced man, the cart loaded with waterskins, and beside him a thin gentleman with a lamp, who handed over a royal token. The old man asked whether to log it. 'No need,' the gentleman said. 'I've entered this cart in my accounts.' Three-Inch Ma lets out a long breath. 'What's entered in the accounts is a loan, not a theft.'
column3: 戟士们跑了。老头记得那一夜：水车是老王的车，车夫是个黑脸汉子，车上装满了水囊，旁边坐着一个瘦先生，提着盏灯，递给他一块王令。老头问要不要登记，那先生说：「不必，这车我记在账上了。」麻三寸听完，长出一口气：「记在账上的，叫借，不叫偷。」

column2: The Nameless Mother Well
column3: 无名母井

column2: The mother well is the deepest, thirty fathoms, its mouth covered by a newly built stone hut with the Royal Uncle's lock on the door and halberdiers outside calling the well 'House property'. Grandpa Kan has reached the dead knot at the end of his rope and won't move from the hut. Little Spade peers through a crack in the door. No bucket inside. Only a bowl, and the bowl is full.
column3: 母井最深，三十丈，井口盖着一座新砌的小石屋，屋门上挂着国舅府的锁，门口站着一队戟士，说井是「府产」。坎爷摸到了绳子尽头的死结，站在石屋前不走了。小铲扒着门缝往里看：屋里没有水桶，只有一只碗，碗里是满的。

column2: The hut is smashed open. There's no name on the lip, only six tally marks, the newest still pale: cut this spring. The water in the bowl is clear. Grandpa Kan bites the dead knot open, and inside is rolled a slip of paper: 'Well 300. No name to be carved until the accounts are settled.' He hands it to you and looks at the six marks on the lip. 'Every spring, someone has been here.'
column3: 石屋砸开了。井沿上没有名字，只有六道刻痕，最新的一道还发白，是今年春天刻的。碗里的水是清的。坎爷用牙把死结咬开，结里卷着一张小纸条：「第三百井，不落名，账清再刻。」他把纸条交给你们，看着井沿上的六道痕，说：「每年开春，有人来过。」

column2: The Sand Court
column3: 沙公堂

column2: A judge's bench has been set up on the sand, a judge kept by the Royal Uncle's house sitting behind it, halberdiers in two rows, ready to 'retry in absence': Ge Xiaolun has escaped the salt pans, so his crime is raised a degree. The judge laughs at the sight of Three-Inch Ma. 'A melon beggar like you, fit to plead in court?' He squints at your banner. 'And what beggars' caravan is this? Three patches on the flag.'
column3: 沙地上摆了一张公案，国舅府养的一个判官坐在后头，戟士两排站开，要「缺席再判」：葛小轮私逃盐田，罪加一等。判官看见麻三寸就笑：「你个讨瓜吃的，也配上堂？」又瞅瞅你们的旗子：「哪儿来的叫花子商队，旗子都补了三块。」

column2: Once the halberdiers go down, the judge crawls out from under his bench and kneels to present his verdict to Three-Inch Ma with both hands. Then he buys two melons out of his own pocket, one for Ma and one pressed on your standard-bearer. Ma tears the verdict in half and wipes melon juice off with one half. 'Next time you hold court, bring the King's seal.'
column3: 戟士们一倒，判官从公案底下爬出来，跪着把那份判词双手捧给麻三寸，又自己掏钱买了两个瓜，一个给麻三寸，一个塞给你们的旗手。麻三寸把判词撕成两半，一半擦了瓜汁：「下回升堂，带着王的印来。」

column2: The Stilt Thieves
column3: 高跷贼

column2: The caravan camps in the open, and at night a row of figures taller than the camels rises outside the tents: a troupe of stilt-walking acrobats, swapping empty jars for full ones balanced on their heads and stilting off with each swap. Their archers shoot from stilts too, swaying so much not one arrow finds its mark, but no one can reach them either.
column3: 夜里驼队宿在野地，帐篷外忽然冒出一排人影，比骆驼还高，原来是一伙踩高跷的杂耍艺人，顶着空坛子来换满坛子，换完一个踩着高跷就跑。他们的弓手也站在高跷上放箭，晃晃悠悠，一箭都射不准，可也让人够不着。

column2: The giant cooper hugs the acrobats down one at a time, stilts and all. The Huang family hired them at twenty coppers a day, and they were starving. Liu Sanniang hears them out and hires them on the spot. 'You carry jars steadier than camels. Thirty coppers a day and meals.' Next morning the caravan has a row of stilt-walkers with jars balanced on their heads, not a drop spilt.
column3: 大个子箍桶匠一抱一个，把高跷艺人连人带跷放倒了。他们是黄家雇来的，一人一天二十文，饿得慌。柳三娘听完，反手雇了他们：「顶坛子走路比骆驼稳，一人一天三十文，管饭。」第二天，驼队里多了一排踩高跷的，坛子顶在头上，一滴没洒。

column2: Whip-Crack Slope
column3: 鞭哨坡

column2: Ge Xiaolun has run off alone, saying he'll find that water cart himself. You track him to a slope and find him ringed by the Royal Uncle's riders, lashing the sand with their whips to bait him. He grips a whip too, old and blackened, and when he cracks it, it rings louder than any of theirs.
column3: 葛小轮一个人跑了，说要去找那辆水车。你们追到一道坡上，看见他被一伙国舅府的骑手围在中间，骑手们拿马鞭抽着沙子逗他。他手里也攥着一根鞭子，旧得发黑，甩起来啪的一声，比骑手们的都响。

column2: The riders driven off, Ge Xiaolun, red-eyed, shows you the whip: the character 'Qian' is branded on its stock. He bought it two days ago at the horse market from a pedlar, spending every coin he had. The pedlar said he found it in the woods by the lake, 'hung on a tree, like someone put it there on purpose'.
column3: 骑手们被打跑，葛小轮红着眼把鞭子给你们看，鞭杆上烙着一个「千」字，是他前天在马市上从一个货郎手里买的，花光了身上的钱。货郎说鞭子是在湖边林子里捡的，「挂在一棵树上，像是有人特意挂的」。

column2: The Forest Warden's Lodge
column3: 林官小屋

column2: The woods north of the lake are kept by an old forest warden, and every spring the wine caravan spends a night outside his lodge on its way through. This year a squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers has taken the lodge and tied the warden to a tree at the door, tearing up his forest register to light their fire and declaring that these woods 'belong to the Huang family from now on'. When the old warden sees the caravan, his first words are: 'Is the count right?'
column3: 湖北的林子归一个老林官管，每年春酒过林子，都要在他的小屋前歇一夜。今年小屋被国舅府的一队戟士占了，林官被绑在门口的树上，戟士们把他的林册撕了生火，说这片林子「从今往后归黄家」。老林官看见驼队，第一句话是：「数够了吗？」

column2: The halberdiers flee, and the old warden, rubbing his arms, helps Sanniang count the jars once, then again. Every year, he says, the palace men wait at the edge of the wood, count three times, and leave without another word. He asked only once: 'Why two hundred and ninety-nine?' The palace man said: 'The King's word. That's the only number his order has ever had.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，老林官揉着胳膊，帮三娘把坛子数了一遍，又数一遍。他说宫里收酒的人每年在林边等，数三遍，数完就走，从不多说一句。他只问过一回：「为什么是二百九十九？」收酒的人说：「王说的，王的单子上，从来只有这个数。」

column2: The Recall Riders
column3: 回营骑

column2: In a woodland clearing a troop of royal cavalry blocks the caravan. They don't want wine; they want a man: the silent giant cooper, who they say is a deserter from the King's guard and served in the palace ten years ago. The giant sets down his jars one by one, steps in front of Sanniang and clenches his fists. He says nothing, but anyone can see he has no intention of going with them.
column3: 林中空地上，一队王城铁骑截住了驼队，不要酒，要人：他们要带走那个不说话的大个子箍桶匠，说他是禁军逃兵，十年前在宫里当过差。大个子把坛子一个个放下，挡在三娘前头，攥紧了拳头。他不说话，可谁都看得出来，他不打算跟他们走。

column2: The cavalry driven off, that night the giant carves words on a board with his knife to show you. He used to guard the palace wine cellar. Every spring, the night the wine went in, the King would come down alone, with no lamp, and count the jars by touch, one by one; then sit among them for a long time. 'I never saw the King's face,' he carves. 'I only heard him counting.'
column3: 铁骑们被打跑了。夜里大个子拿刀在一块木板上刻字给你们看：他以前守过宫里的酒窖。每年春酒入窖那一夜，王会一个人下来，不带灯，摸着坛子一个个数，数完坐在坛子中间，很久不走。「我看不见王的脸，」他刻道，「只听见他在数。」

column2: The Forbidden Park
column3: 禁苑林

column2: Deep in the lakeside woods a high fence encloses the Royal Uncle's private park, stocked with deer and peacocks. At its gate stands the house's finest company: cavalry outside, archers in the trees, halberdiers at the gate. Three-Inch Ma has learned that Steward Liu, who signed 'Liu of the House', has hidden here ever since the case started to turn. He spends all day with the peacocks; peacocks, he says, can't testify.
column3: 湖边林子深处圈着一道高篱笆，里头是国舅府的禁苑，养着鹿和孔雀。篱笆门口守着府里最精的一支人马：铁骑在外，弓手上树，戟士守门。麻三寸打听到，那个画押「府中刘」的刘管事，案子一翻，就躲进了这里，整天跟孔雀待在一块儿，说孔雀不会作证。

column2: The picked troops scatter, and you haul Steward Liu out from behind the peacock cages, covered in feathers. He confesses everything: the Royal Uncle had him plant the bowl, because the boy kept asking about that water cart. 'The Royal Uncle said not one more word about the Qianli caravan.' But the cart itself he knows nothing about. 'That was in the old King's time. Ask Drill Master Tie. He served in the palace that year.'
column3: 精兵散了，刘管事被你们从孔雀笼后头揪了出来，一身羽毛。他全招了：碗是国舅让他塞的，因为那小子到处打听那辆水车，「国舅说，千里号的事，一个字都不许再提」。可水车的事他不知道，「那是老王时候的事，问铁教头，那年他在宫里当差」。

column2: The Children's Drill Ground
column3: 童子操场

column2: Next day you return to the ground, and Drill Master Tie has his thirty children drawn up, each on a scrawny horse, wooden staves swapped for real weapons. 'You want my manual,' he says. 'Spar with them first. They've drilled three years and never faced a real opponent.' The children puff out their chests. The smallest couldn't climb onto his horse and had to be lifted up.
column3: 第二天你们回到场子，铁教头已经把三十个孩子排好了，个个骑着瘦马，手里换了真家伙。「你们要我的操典，」他说，「先跟他们练一场。他们练了三年，还没跟真人交过手。」孩子们挺着胸脯，最小的那个骑不上马，是被人抱上去的。

column2: The children lose, but not one breaks rank. With his one arm Drill Master Tie takes from his coat a book wrapped in oilcloth: the drill manual of the King's guard, which he taught for thirty years, adding a page here, correcting a page there. 'Drill by this and one day counts for several,' he says. 'Take it to your camp. The soldiers will thank you.' Then: 'I'm the one who arrested the Ge boy. I took Steward Liu's word to the palace and begged, and the palace sent back a slip of paper, ‘Verify before sentencing’, in a very neat hand. Before that paper even left the palace gate, the Royal Uncle had thrown me out. I'll testify for the boy.'
column3: 孩子们输了，可一个也没掉队。铁教头用独臂从怀里掏出一本油布包着的册子：王城禁军的操典，他教了三十年，一页页添，一页页改。「照着它操，一天顶别人好几天，」他说，「拿去营里用，兵会谢你们。」他又说：「葛家那孩子是我抓的。我拿着刘管事的话去宫里求，宫里回了一张纸：「查实再判」，字写得极工整。可纸还没出宫门，我就被国舅赶了出来。我替那孩子作证。」

column2: The Witness Ferry
column3: 拦证渡

column2: To take the petition into the city you must first cross this river. The Royal Uncle's halberdiers hold the ferry, every boat tied up on the far bank, and a notice posted on the shore: 'No one testifying in the Ge case may cross.' The old bird catcher, the gatekeeper and Drill Master Tie are all following behind you. The bird catcher has a finch tucked in his coat and means to take it into the city. 'It saw too.'
column3: 要进城递状子，得先过这条河。渡口被一队国舅府的戟士拦着，渡船全拴在对岸，岸边贴着一张告示：「凡为葛案作证者，不得渡河。」捕雀老汉、守门翁、铁教头都跟在你们后头，捕雀老汉怀里还揣着一只黄雀，说要带着它进城，「它也看见了」。

column2: The halberdiers jump in the river and flee, and the boats are untied. Before boarding, the gatekeeper lights his old lantern: the thin gentleman carried one just like it the night the water cart left the city. In midstream Three-Inch Ma takes stock: three witnesses, two exhibits, one finch. 'One thing still missing,' he says. 'That cart.'
column3: 戟士们跳河跑了，渡船解了下来。守门翁上船前把旧灯笼点上了，说那年夜里水车出城，那个瘦先生提的就是这样一盏灯。船到河心，麻三寸清点人数：证人三个，证物两样，黄雀一只。「还差一样，」他说，「那辆车。」

column2: Stone Wheel-Ruts
column3: 石车辙

column2: A stretch of cracked mud flats with two deep wheel-ruts pressed into it; the mud dried and the ruts set hard as if carved in stone. Some of the Royal Uncle's archers have built a lookout shelter here and treat the ruts as a boundary: cross them and you're shot. Ge Xiaolun crouches to measure the wheel gauge, his fingers shaking. 'A big royal water cart. The same width as the one my father drove.'
column3: 一片干裂的泥板地，泥板上压着两道深深的车辙，泥干了，辙印硬得像刻在石头上。一伙国舅府的弓手在这里搭了个瞭望棚，把辙印当成了界线：越过辙的，射。葛小轮蹲下来量了量车轮的宽窄，手指头都在抖：「是王城的大水车，跟我爹赶的一样宽。」

column2: The archers flee and you follow the ruts for a li. They grow deeper as you go, as if the cart was heavily laden, running east into the lakeside woods. Beside them runs a line of footprints, one pair big, one pair narrow booted, walking side by side. 'The big ones are my father's,' says Ge Xiaolun.
column3: 弓手们跑了，你们顺着辙走了一里。辙印越走越深，像车上装着很重的东西，一直往东，进了湖边的林子。辙边还有一行脚印，一个大脚，一个窄靴子，并排走的。葛小轮说：「大的是我爹。」

column2: Pettifoggers' Slope
column3: 讼棍坡

column2: Three law booths stand on the slope, ten times grander than Three-Inch Ma's, belonging to pettifoggers kept by the Royal Uncle's house and a gang of their bruisers. The moment they see Ma they serve him three suits on the spot: one for stealing melons, one for impersonating an advocate, and one for 'a tongue of excessive length, injurious to public morals'. The bruisers nail the suits to a post in the middle of the road: no passing until he signs for them.
column3: 坡上搭着三顶讼棚，比麻三寸那顶阔气十倍，是国舅府养的讼棍，带着一帮打手。他们一见麻三寸，就当场递了三张状子告他：一告他偷瓜，二告他冒充讼师，三告他「舌头过长，有伤风化」。打手们把状子钉在了路中间的木桩上，不签收不许过。

column2: The bruisers driven off, the pettifoggers pack up their suits. The oldest of them draws Three-Inch Ma aside and quietly turns up a law book from the old King's time, pointing to one article: 'Where a thing is borrowed under contract, though not yet returned, it is not theft.' He sighs. 'When I was young I wanted to be a good advocate too. Then I got scared of going hungry. Take this article and use it.'
column3: 打手被打跑，讼棍们收起了状子。有个最老的讼棍拉住麻三寸，悄悄翻出一本老王时候的律书，指着一条给他看：「借物有契，虽未还，不为盗。」老讼棍叹口气：「我年轻时也想当个好讼师，后来饿怕了。这条你拿去用。」

column2: Vineless Slope
column3: 无园坡

column2: In the open a band of horse thieves stops the caravan. Not for the wine; for the camels. Their leader says they used to pick grapes in the northern vineyards, but the Huang family bought the vineyards up one by one, cut down the vines and planted cotton. With no picking work left they took to horses and robbery. Their mounts are thin, their saddles nailed together from old trellis wood.
column3: 野地里一伙马贼拦住驼队，不抢酒，抢骆驼。领头的说他们原本是北边葡萄园里摘葡萄的，园子被黄家一片片买走，葡萄藤砍了改种棉花，摘葡萄的没了活路，只好骑上马抢东西。他们的马都瘦，马鞍是拿葡萄架子的木头钉的。

column2: The horse thieves are scattered, but Liu Sanniang calls the leader back: her old cellar needs hands to make up the wine and move jars. 'Hands that can pick grapes won't drop a jar.' The leader stares a long while, eyes reddening. Back then, he says, the Qianli people worked a season in the northern vineyards too. 'Three hundred men picked a whole autumn of grapes for three hundred jars of wine. They said they'd store it and drink it the day they came back.'
column3: 马贼们被打散，柳三娘却把领头的叫了回来：她的老窖还要人补酒、搬坛，「会摘葡萄的手，搬坛子不会摔」。领头的愣了半天，红了眼。他说当年千里号的人也在北边园子里帮过一季工，「三百个人，摘了一秋的葡萄，换了三百坛酒，说是存着，回来那天喝」。

column2: The Glass-Bead Tent
column3: 琉璃珠帐

column2: A great tent hung with glass-bead curtains out in the open country, its owner a Persian jeweller with a high nose and curled beard who speaks the court tongue with an accent. For three months no one has dared go in. The Royal Uncle's house wanted him to swear the silver bowl was palace property; he wouldn't, so the house posted archers outside to shoot at the feet of anyone who came to buy. He sits inside polishing his beads one by one until they shine brighter than mirrors.
column3: 野地里一顶挂满琉璃珠帘的大帐，主人是个波斯珠宝商，鼻梁高，胡子卷，会说一口带腔的官话。他的帐子三个月没人敢进：国舅府要他把那只银碗认作宫里的东西，他不肯，府里就派了弓手守在帐外，谁来买珠子就往谁的脚边射一箭。他坐在帐里，一颗颗擦珠子，擦得比镜子还亮。

column2: The archers driven off, the jeweller parts his curtains and invites you in: beads, gems and silverware, trade what you like. Three-Inch Ma shows him the pawn ticket and he barely glances at it. 'Vine pattern. That's the Royal Uncle's private mark. Palace bowls are engraved with pomegranates.' Then: 'I vouch for things, not people. Things don't lie. People do.'
column3: 弓手们被赶走，珠宝商掀开珠帘请你们进去，珠子、宝石、银器随便换。麻三寸把当票给他看，他只瞄了一眼：「葡萄纹，是国舅府的私纹，宫里的碗刻的是石榴。」他又说：「我只认东西，不认人。东西不会撒谎，人会。」

column2: The Liu Press House
column3: 柳家榨房

column2: An old press house in the woods, a massive press beam across the rafters with a lump of black iron hung from its end as a weight, left by Liu Sanniang's father. A band of riders bursts in to break up the beam for firewood and sell the weight. Sanniang blocks the door with her ladle. 'Pull the house down if you like, but don't touch the weight. My father said it isn't ours.'
column3: 林子里一座老榨房，房梁上横着一根粗大的榨杆，杆头吊着一块黑沉沉的铁疙瘩当坠子，是柳三娘她爹留下的。一伙骑手冲进榨房，要拆了榨杆当柴，铁坠子拿去换钱。三娘拿着酒勺堵在门口：「这房子你们拆，坠子不许碰。我爹说过，那坠子不是我家的。」

column2: The riders flee and the giant takes down the iron weight. One wipe of his sleeve and under the black rust shows bronze, and characters: 'Qianli caravan. Captain of the escort.' Only now does Sanniang remember her father's dying words: that year the caravan's escort captain pledged it to the Liu family and stored three hundred jars of wine. 'When the men come back, the token opens the jars.' Afraid of thieves, her father hung it on the press beam. 'Put it where the weight is heaviest and no one can take it.' In his three years at the King's city the captain trained a whole battalion of the guard, and the veterans he made all know this token. Read it out in a barracks, 'The Captain's back', and they'll come. Sanniang says: 'I'll keep the wine for them. Take the token and call the men.'
column3: 骑手们跑了，大个子把铁坠子取了下来，拿袖子一擦，黑锈底下露出铜色和字：「千里号护卫都头」。三娘这才想起她爹临死前的话：那年千里号的都头拿它押在柳家，存下三百坛酒，「人回来，凭令开坛」。她爹怕人偷，就挂在榨杆上，「压在最重的地方，谁也拿不走」。都头在王城三年，教过一营禁军，带出来的老兵都认这块令。拿到兵营宣一声「都头回来了」，他们就来投。三娘说：「酒我替他们守着，令你们拿去，叫人。」

column2: The Old Liu Cellar
column3: 柳家老窖

column2: The three jars Sanniang needs are in the old cellar under a wooded slope. Its door stands wide open, and some of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers are carrying jars out and carrying jars in: out go the Liu family's good wines, in come jars exactly like them, but with a fine red string tied round each neck. Sanniang leans in to sniff and her face changes. 'There's something in this wine.'
column3: 三娘要补的三坛酒，存在林中山坡下的老窖里。窖门大开，一伙国舅府的戟士正往外搬坛子，又往里搬坛子：搬出去的是柳家的好酒，搬进来的坛子一模一样，只在坛口拴了一根细细的红绳。三娘凑过去一闻，脸色变了：「这酒里下了东西。」

column2: The halberdiers flee and the red-string jars are smashed in the gully one by one. At the back of the cellar stand three hundred jars in neat rows, each clay seal stamped 'Qian', untouched for ten years. Sanniang makes up her three jars from the family's own stock and simply bows to the three hundred. 'Somebody else's. Not to be touched.' The giant carves on the wall: the red-string wine was meant for the palace to drink at the spring banquet.
column3: 戟士们跑了，红绳坛子一个个砸碎在沟里。窖的最里头整整齐齐码着三百坛，坛口封泥上都压着「千」字，十年了没人动过。三娘从自家的存酒里补足了三坛，对那三百坛只鞠了个躬：「人家存的，动不得。」大个子在墙上刻：红绳酒，是要在春宴上给宫里喝的。

column2: The Jar-Label Pavilion
column3: 题坛亭

column2: In a small pavilion in the woods a failed scholar is kept prisoner. He writes labels for wine jars in a beautiful hand, and every winery in the city wants him. The archers hired by the Huang family guard him in the pavilion and force him to write advertisements for Huang wine. He writes one, the archers read it out, and every time they say it isn't loud enough. By the thirtieth he's written: 'Drink Huang wine: live for ever and take ten wives.'
column3: 林中小亭里关着一个落第秀才，专给酒坛写签，字写得漂亮，城里的酒坊都找他。黄家雇的弓手把他看在亭子里，逼他给黄家的酒写广告，他写一条，弓手念一条，念完都说不够响亮。秀才写到第三十条，已经写出了「喝黄家酒，长生不老，娶妻十房」。

column2: The archers flee, and the scholar crumples all thirty advertisements into a ball and throws it in the lake. He's written labels for the Liu family's royal order too, he says, but the palace has an odd rule: two hundred and ninety-nine jars, a label on every jar, and nothing written on any label. 'The palace writes them itself. I asked what, and the wine receiver said: names.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，秀才把三十条广告揉成一团扔进了湖里。他说柳家的王单他也写过签，可宫里有个怪规矩：二百九十九坛，坛坛贴签，签上不许写字。「宫里自己写，」他说，「我问写什么，收酒的人说，写名字。」

column2: Night-Raid Camp
column3: 夜袭棚

column2: Three-Inch Ma has pitched a makeshift law booth in the open country, with all the evidence kept in a melon basket. At midnight some of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers creep up with torches to burn it. Woken, Ma runs about hugging the basket and yelling, 'Burning evidence raises the crime three degrees!', louder than the halberdiers' footsteps.
column3: 麻三寸在野地里搭了个临时讼棚，证据都收在一只瓜筐里。半夜里一伙国舅府的戟士摸了过来，手里拎着火把，要烧筐。麻三寸被惊醒，抱着瓜筐满地乱跑，边跑边喊：「烧证据，罪加三等！」喊得比戟士的脚步声还响。

column2: The halberdiers driven off, the basket is saved. From that day Three-Inch Ma sleeps with the pawn ticket in his mouth, the verdict under his pillow and the law book under his backside. He takes stock: pawn ticket, testimony, gate log, the law. 'Just the cart missing.' Ge Xiaolun doesn't sleep at all. He stands outside cracking his whip, crack after crack, as if calling someone.
column3: 戟士们被打跑，瓜筐保住了。从这天起，麻三寸睡觉把当票含在嘴里，判词压在枕下，律书垫在屁股底下。他清点了一遍：当票、证词、出城记、律条，「就差车」。葛小轮一夜没睡，在棚外甩鞭子，一声一声，像在叫谁。

column2: The Petition Drum
column3: 登闻鼓

column2: Beside the high road outside the city stands a great drum, the Petition Drum. Under the old King's rule, anyone with a grievance could beat it and the King had to hear. Its skin has been slashed to ribbons; two of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers stand on top of it and a squad below, and anyone who comes to drum gets twenty strokes first. Three-Inch Ma looks at the ruined drum and his petition rustles in his fist.
column3: 王城外的大道边立着一面大鼓，叫登闻鼓，老王时候的规矩：有冤的人来敲，王必须听。鼓面被人用刀划成了一条条，鼓上站着两个国舅府的戟士，下面还有一队守着，谁来敲鼓，先打二十棍。麻三寸看着破鼓，把状纸攥得哗哗响。

column2: The halberdiers flee and you stretch a camel hide over the drum. Ge Xiaolun swings the drumstick three times and the boom carries into the city. At dusk a young eunuch runs out with a slip of paper bearing four words: 'Bring the cart.' The hand is very neat, the last stroke lifted off a little too fast, trailing a fine tail.
column3: 戟士们跑了，你们剥了一张驼皮给鼓重新蒙上。葛小轮抡起鼓槌敲了三下，鼓声传进城里。傍晚，城里跑出来一个小内侍，递来一张纸条，只有四个字：「带车来见。」字写得很工整，最后一笔像是收得太快，带出一道细尾巴。

column2: The Cart Breaker's Yard
column3: 破车场

column2: A yard heaped with broken carts, wheels, shafts and bodies stacked like hills: the whole stock of an old scrap man. For days now the Royal Uncle's archers have occupied it, dousing the old carts collected from all over the city with oil and setting them alight one by one, the sky black with smoke, 'clearing out old rubbish'. The old man squats at the edge and bends down a finger for each cart burnt.
column3: 一片堆满破车的场子，车轮、车辕、车厢摞得像小山，是个收破烂的老汉的家当。可这几天场子被国舅府的弓手占了，他们把全城收来的旧车一辆辆浇油点火，烧得满天黑烟，说是「清理旧物」。老汉蹲在场边，烧一辆，他就掰一下指头。

column2: The archers flee and the fires are beaten out; the old man has run through his ten fingers twice. The Royal Uncle is burning the city's water carts, he says, 'so there'll be none left to find'. But there's one he knows isn't here. 'There's one in the woods by the lake. Ten years nobody's dared touch it. They say it's haunted: at night someone lights a lamp beside it.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，火扑灭了，老汉的十个指头已经掰完了两轮。他说国舅这是在烧王城的水车，「烧了就没得找了」。可有一辆，他知道不在这里：「湖边林子里有一辆，十年了没人敢碰，说是闹鬼，夜里有人在车边点灯。」

column2: The Huang Wine Depot
column3: 黄家酒栈

column2: A large wine depot in the open country under a 'HUANG' signboard: the Huang winery's roadside storehouse, archers on its gate tower. Inside are stacks of jars, most of them sour wine cut with water. Sanniang sniffs over the wall and spits. 'Call that wine?'
column3: 野地里一座大酒栈，挂着「黄」字招牌，是黄家酒坊在路上的货栈，弓手守在门楼上。栈里囤着成垛的酒坛，可坛里装的多半是兑了水的酸酒。三娘隔着墙闻了闻，啐了一口：「这也配叫酒？」

column2: The archers flee and the sour wine all goes into the ditch, where the frogs croak all night. Sanniang collects every empty jar in the depot to fill with good wine next year. 'The jars aren't to blame.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，酒栈里的酸酒全倒进了沟里，沟里的青蛙叫了一夜。三娘把栈里的空坛子都收了，说明年装好酒，「坛子是无辜的」。

column2: The depot gives up eight jars of undiluted old wine (kept for the Huangs' own table), two carts of raisins, a basket of walnuts, thirty new sheepskins, and a Huang account to the Royal Uncle's house: 'Red-string wine for the spring banquet: one hundred jars.'
column3: 酒栈里抄出八坛没兑水的陈酿（黄家留着自己喝的）、两车葡萄干、一筐核桃、三十张新羊皮，还有一本黄家给国舅府的账：「春宴红绳酒，一百坛」。

column2: Every time you pass, the grape pickers who now haul jars at the depot fill your waterskins, not with water but with fresh-pressed grape juice so sweet it sticks to your lips. 'Sanniang's orders. Travellers don't drink wine.'
column3: 每次路过，在栈里改行搬坛子的摘葡萄汉子们都给你们灌满水囊，囊里不是水，是新榨的葡萄汁，甜得粘嘴：「三娘说的，赶路的人不喝酒。」

column2: Crocodile Reeds
column3: 鳄苇荡

column2: The wine caravan must cross a reed marsh at the lake's northern corner, reeds taller than camels and a pack of great crocodiles lurking beneath the water, the biggest two fathoms long with scales on its back like a row of roof tiles. At night they haul out to bask; by day they hide among the reed roots, and at the sound of camel bells they swim for the edge. Sanniang loses a camel or two here every year. 'They know the bells.'
column3: 酒驼队要过湖北角的一片苇荡，苇子比骆驼还高，水下趴着一群大鳄，最大的那条有两丈长，背上的鳞像一排瓦。它们夜里上岸晒肚皮，白天藏在苇根里，听见驼铃就往水边游。三娘说每年送酒都要在这里折几峰骆驼，「它们认得驼铃」。

column2: The great crocodiles are driven back to the middle of the lake and the caravan crosses the reeds without losing a camel. But clutches of eggs lie buried in the mud along the shore, and with the sun on them there'll be a new brood next year. The oasis crocodiles hatch year after year and can't be wiped out; all you can do is come back every so often and clear them, so those crossing the lake can go in peace.
column3: 大鳄们被赶回了湖心，驼队一峰不少地过了苇荡。可岸边的泥里埋着一窝窝鳄蛋，太阳一晒，明年又是一群小鳄；绿洲的大鳄一年年孵下去，杀不尽，只能隔一阵来清一回，让过湖的人走得安稳些。

column2: North Shore Stone Market
column3: 湖北石市

column2: In the woods on the lake's north shore lies a stone market, where bluestone quarried in the hills is cut into millstones, well rings and jar seals and traded for ironware from outside. Now it's deserted: the Royal Uncle's halberdiers hold the entrance and say iron is a House monopoly; masons may not trade for it privately. With no iron chisels, the masons are reduced to knocking stone with stone. A white-bearded old mason sits among heaps of small round stones, each hollowed to fit over the mouth of a jar.
column3: 湖北岸的林子里有个石市，山里采来的青石在这里凿成磨盘、井圈、封坛石，换外头运来的铁器。如今石市冷冷清清：国舅府的戟士守着市口，说铁器归府里专卖，石匠不许私换。石匠们没铁凿，只好拿石头敲石头。一个白胡子老石匠坐在一堆小圆石中间，每块石头上都凿了个坑，正好扣住坛口。

column2: The halberdiers leave, iron comes in by the cartload and stone goes out by the cartload, and the market rings with chisels again. The old mason has cut the seals for the palace's spring wine for six years. He digs out the very first order from six years ago: 'Jar seals: three hundred'. 'Three hundred' is struck through with a single stroke and corrected to 'two hundred and ninety-nine', and below, a line in small writing: 'Previous figure in error. Counted one too many.' 'The only time a King's order was ever wrong,' says the old mason. Sanniang looks at that line and says nothing for a long while.
column3: 戟士们走了，铁器一车车拉进来，石料一车车拉出去，石市又响起了叮叮当当。老石匠是给宫里春酒凿封坛石的，凿了六年。他翻出六年前头一回的单子给你们看：「封坛石三百枚」，「三百」被一笔划掉，旁边改成「二百九十九」，下面一行小字：「前数误，多算了一个。」老石匠说：「王的单子，就错过这一回。」三娘看着那行字，半天没说话。

column2: The Forest Patrol
column3: 巡林骑

column2: A new bridle path has been cut through the lakeside woods, and the Royal Uncle's riders patrol it three times a day, questioning everyone: 'Looking for a cart?' Those who say yes are seized. Those who say no are seized too: 'The ones who say no are the suspicious ones.' The old bird catcher knows a footpath into the woods, but the patrol's horses happen to be tethered right at its mouth.
column3: 湖边林子里新开了一条马道，国舅府的骑手一天三趟来回巡，见人就盘问：「找车的？」答「是」的抓走，答「不是」的也抓走，说「不是的才可疑」。捕雀老汉说他认得进林子的小路，可小路口正好拴着几匹巡林的马。

column2: The patrol is knocked from the saddle and flees. The bird catcher leads you down the footpath, whistling birdcalls all the way, the birds of the wood answering. Where birds build, he says, no one has been for a long time. Half a li in, he points to an old nest in a tree: it's lined with a strip of faded cart curtain.
column3: 巡林的骑手被打下马，跑了。捕雀老汉领着你们钻进小路，一路学鸟叫，林子里的鸟一路应着。他说鸟窝搭在哪里，哪里就有人很久没去过。走了半里，他指着树上一只旧鸟窝：窝底垫着的，是一截褪了色的车帘。

column2: The Wheelwright's Prison
column3: 车匠囚屋

column2: A locked log cabin in the open country, guarded by the Royal Uncle's halberdiers, holds the King's city's old wheelwright. He built carts for the old King all his life and carved his own mark on the shaft of every one. Afraid of what he might recognise, the Royal Uncle's house has locked him up here to whittle hitching posts all day. The old wheelwright shouts through the window: 'I know every one of them!'
column3: 野地里一间上了锁的木屋，屋外守着一队国舅府的戟士，屋里关着王城的老车匠。他给老王造了一辈子车，每辆车的辕木上都刻着他自己的记号。国舅府怕他认出什么，把他关在这里，叫他天天削马桩子。老车匠隔着窗户喊：「我认得每一辆！」

column2: The halberdiers flee and the lock is smashed. Rubbing his wrists, the old wheelwright says he built twelve water carts for the old King. Eleven have been burnt; he watched them burn. The last one the old King gave to the Qianli caravan with his own hand. 'The old King said: the city can go thirsty a day, but those three hundred outside can't go thirsty one day.' He shoulders his plane. 'I'll come and identify the cart.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，门锁砸开。老车匠揉着手腕说，老王的水车一共造过十二辆，十一辆都烧了，他亲眼看着烧的。剩下那一辆，是老王亲手指给千里号的：「老王说，城里人能渴一天，外头那三百个人一天都渴不起。」他扛起刨子：「我跟你们去认车。」

column2: The North Road Barricade
column3: 截北道

column2: Three rows of abatis bar the high road to the city's north gate, the Royal Uncle's forces in three ranks: halberdiers holding the barricades, archers on earthen platforms by the road, cavalry blocking either end. A sign stands at the entrance: 'No spring wine to enter.' Below it, freshly added in small characters: 'Especially not the Liu family's.' Sanniang reads it and tucks her ladle into her belt. 'Let's see who says so.'
column3: 去王城北门的大路上横着三道鹿砦，国舅府的人马三路排开：戟士守鹿砦，弓手上了路边的土台，铁骑在两头堵着。路口竖着一块牌子：「春酒禁入。」后头一行小字是新添的：「柳家的尤其不许。」三娘看了，把酒勺往腰里一别：「那就看看谁不许。」

column2: The barricades go down and the Royal Uncle's forces fall back into the city. The caravan climbs a rise, and there before you is the city's north wall, a few small holes breathing cool air at its foot. Those are the vents of the palace wine cellar, says Sanniang. 'Wine in a cellar keeps warm in winter and cool in summer, and like a man, it has to breathe.'
column3: 鹿砦被推倒，国舅府的人马退回了城里。驼队爬上一道坡，王城的北墙就在眼前，墙根下有几个冒着凉气的小孔，三娘说那是宫里酒窖的气眼，「酒到了窖里，冬暖夏凉，跟人一样，要喘气」。

column2: The Counting Platform
column3: 验数台

column2: Outside the north gate is an earthen platform where every spring the palace's wine receiver stands to check the count, three times over, before letting the wine into the city. This year a squad of strange archers stands there instead, saying the receiver has 'fallen ill' and they'll take delivery, straight to the Royal Uncle's house. Sanniang sees through them at once. 'I've heard the receiver's voice for six years. None of you is him.'
column3: 北门外有一座土台，每年春酒到了，宫里的收酒官就站在台上验数，数三遍，才放进城。今年台上站的却是一队陌生的弓手，说收酒官「告病了」，由他们来收，收了直接送去国舅府。三娘一眼就看穿了：「收酒官的嗓子我听了六年，你们谁都不是。」
