column2: The fake receivers flee, and the real one is let out of a straw shed beneath the platform: a stammering old man. He climbs up and counts jar by jar, three times: two hundred and ninety-nine, no more, no less. Every year when he reports back to the palace, he says, the King asks him one thing: 'This year on the road, has anyone come back?' And he says no. 'Then the King says: keep it another year.'
column3: 假收酒的跑了，真收酒官被人从台底下的草棚里放了出来，一个结结巴巴的老头。他站上台，一坛一坛数了三遍：二百九十九，不多不少。他说每年交完酒回宫，王都要问他一句：「今年路上，有没有人回来？」他说没有。「王就说：那就再存一年。」

column2: Red-String Wood
column3: 红绳林

column2: In the woods east of the lake lies a disused hunting park, where the old master of the Huang winery is hiding under the guard of a squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers. With the red-string wine found out, he's preparing to flee overnight, a chest of gold and a hundred unused red strings on his cart. Sanniang chases him to the edge of the wood and gives a cold laugh. 'My father said: a wine seller who doctors his wine comes back next life as the dregs.'
column3: 湖东的林子里有一处废猎苑，黄家的老掌柜就躲在这里，身边护着一队国舅府的戟士。红绳酒的事露了，他准备连夜逃走，车上装着一箱金子和一百根没用完的红绳。三娘追到林子边，冷笑一声：「我爹说过，卖酒的人往酒里下东西，下辈子做酒糟。」

column2: The halberdiers flee, and Master Huang, roped to his own cart, confesses meekly: the red-string wine is drugged, and the Royal Uncle means to put the palace to sleep for a night at the spring banquet. 'While the King sleeps, take the King's seal.' He adds that the Royal Uncle recently met a band of men in golden masks. 'Said they came from the Thousand Buddha Caves. What they want is gold.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，黄掌柜被捆在车上，老老实实招了：红绳酒里下的是蒙汗药，国舅要在春宴上让宫里的人睡上一夜，「趁王睡着，取王的印」。他还说国舅最近见了一伙戴金面具的人，「说是从千佛洞来的，要的是金子」。

column2: The Firebrand Camp
column3: 纵火营

column2: A large camp sits at the edge of the woods, halberdiers, archers and cavalry in three ranks, stacks of dry firewood and a dozen barrels of lamp oil inside. The Royal Uncle's house has sent its last order: that cart in the woods is to be burnt 'along with the woods'. The camp captain is splashing oil along the tree line, and the wind blows towards the lake. One spark and half the forest is lost.
column3: 林子边上扎着一座大营，戟士、弓手、铁骑三路排开，营里堆着成垛的干柴和十几桶火油。国舅府的最后一道令传到了：林子里那辆车，「连林子一块儿烧」。营头正带人往林边泼油，风往湖那边吹，一点火，半片林子都保不住。

column2: The camp is broken up, the torches thrown in the lake, the oil barrels rolled into a mud pond. As he's tied up the captain is still muttering: 'All this for one broken cart?' The old wheelwright raps him with the handle of his plane. 'That's no broken cart. That's a day's water a whole city lent.'
column3: 大营被冲散，火把扔进了湖里，油桶滚进了泥塘。营头被绑起来的时候还在嘟囔：「一辆破车，至于吗？」老车匠拿刨子柄敲了他一下：「那不是破车，那是一城人借出去的一天的水。」

column2: Beached-Boat Slope
column3: 搁船坡

column2: On a dry slope more than ten li from the lake sits a great wooden boat, rollers under its hull and cooking smoke curling from the cabin: a family lives aboard. A squad of the Royal Uncle's archers has surrounded it to strip its planks for a pavilion at the House. The boatmaster, Old Hu, and his family of five are all leaning over the gunwale pelting them with pots and pans, sending the archers running with their arms over their heads.
column3: 离湖还有十几里的一道干坡上，搁着一条大木船，船底垫着滚木，船舱里炊烟袅袅，住着一家子。国舅府的一队弓手围着船，要拆船板去修府里的凉亭。船老大姓胡，一家五口全趴在船舷上，把锅碗瓢盆往下扔，扔得弓手们抱头乱跑。

column2: The archers flee. This boat has been on the lake since his grandfather's day, says Old Hu, but the lake moves of its own accord: four times in his life he's dragged the boat on rollers to chase it. 'Wherever the lake shifts, I drag.' Now it's moved south-east again and he must drag once more. The rings of white snail shells up the slope are the lake's old shores.
column3: 弓手们跑了。胡老大说这船从他爷爷那辈起就在湖上，可湖自己会走：他这辈子拿滚木拖着船追了四回湖，「湖往哪儿挪，我就往哪儿拖」。如今湖又往东南挪了，他得再拖一回。坡上一圈圈白色的螺壳，就是湖以前的岸。

column2: The Stilt Gate
column3: 高跷门

column2: The north wall is lined with the Royal Uncle's archers and the gate stands half closed, every cart turned upside down before it's let through. Sanniang's caravan is stuck outside the gate. Up come the stilt acrobats she hired with an idea: they'll perform 'The Eight Immortals Cross the Lake' on stilts in front of the gate, and while the archers gawp the wine can slip in by the side door.
column3: 北门城墙上站满了国舅府的弓手，城门半掩，谁的车进门都要翻个底朝天。三娘的驼队排在门外进不去，那伙被她雇来的高跷艺人凑过来出主意：他们踩着高跷，在城门前演一出「八仙过湖」，弓手们一看热闹，酒就从侧门溜进去。

column2: Halfway through the show the archers twig it, but too late: you're already up on the wall, and the acrobats keep singing as they fight. All two hundred and ninety-nine jars go in by the side door without a drop spilt. The leading acrobat leans down from his stilts and salutes Sanniang. 'Wages as agreed, plus a jar!' Sanniang says: 'Not one of these jars can be touched. I'll open one for you back home.'
column3: 戏演到一半，弓手们看出了门道，可已经晚了：你们冲上了城墙，高跷艺人一边打一边还在唱。二百九十九坛酒从侧门进了城，一滴没洒。领头的艺人从高跷上探下身来，冲三娘一抱拳：「工钱照算，再加一坛！」三娘说：「这里的一坛都不能动，回去给你们开。」

column2: The Old Vine Garden
column3: 老藤园

column2: Outside the north gate lies the last vineyard, one ancient vine spread over half an acre of trellis, its owner Old Vine Bai as old as his vine. The Huang family bought up every garden around, but he flatly refused to sell, so they posted archers at his gate to shoot the basket of anyone who came to buy grapes or raisins. This year's raisins lie heaped in the shed, going mouldy.
column3: 北门外剩下最后一片葡萄园，园里一棵老藤爬满了半亩架子，主人白老藤和他的藤一样老。黄家买走了周围所有的园子，只剩他这一片死活不卖，黄家就派弓手守在园门口，谁来买葡萄、买葡萄干，就射谁的筐。今年的葡萄干堆在棚子里，堆得发了霉。

column2: The archers gone, Old Vine Bai sorts out the mouldy raisins and loads the good ones cart after cart to trade with you, thirty per cent off. 'Thanks for guarding Sanniang's wine.' That old vine, he says, the Qianli people helped him graft. 'They said while the vine lives, the men can come home.' Every autumn the palace sends someone to buy the first bunch of grapes from it.
column3: 弓手们跑了，白老藤把发霉的挑出去，好的装了一车又一车，要跟你们换东西，价钱让了三成：「谢你们护着三娘的酒。」他说那棵老藤，是千里号的人当年帮他嫁接的，「他们说，藤活着，人就回得来」。每年秋天，宫里都派人来买这棵藤上的头一串葡萄。

column2: The King's Cellar
column3: 王窖口

column2: A flight of stone steps at the north corner of the palace wall leads underground: the King's wine cellar. A squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers has seized the entrance, saying that since the spring wine is in the city, the House will 'receive it on the King's behalf'. Sanniang's two hundred and ninety-nine jars stand at the foot of the steps, and the receiver is stammering in alarm: 'The c-cellar, the K-King allows no outsider in!' The halberdiers have already started carrying their own empty jars down.
column3: 宫墙北角一道石阶通向地下，是王的酒窖。窖口被一队国舅府的戟士占了，说春酒既然进了城，就由国舅府「代收」。三娘的二百九十九坛堆在阶前，收酒官急得直结巴：「窖，窖里，王，王不许外人进！」戟士们已经开始往窖里搬自家的空坛子了。

column2: The halberdiers are thrown out. Inside, row on row, stand six years of spring wine, not one jar opened, each with a label bearing a single name: Zhao Mancang, Meng Xiaoshan, Old Zhou... Two hundred and ninety-nine a year, the same every year. On the table lie this year's blank labels, a brush and an inkstone, the ink still wet. Sanniang sets the new wine in place jar by jar and says softly: 'None of these men has come back to drink yet.'
column3: 戟士们被赶了出去。窖里一排排码着六年的春酒，一坛没开，每坛贴着一张签，签上一个名字：赵满仓、孟小山、老周……一年二百九十九个，年年一样。案上放着今年的空签、一支笔、一方砚，墨还是湿的。三娘把新酒一坛坛放好，轻声说：「这些人，都还没回来喝。」

column2: The East Lake Inn
column3: 湖东客栈

column2: On the edge of the woods east of the lake stands an inn, the last resting place before the King's city. A band of the Royal Uncle's riders has moved in, paying nothing and taking the inn's horses for mounts. The landlady holds the kitchen with a rolling pin; the kitchen is her life, she says. 'No horsemen in here. No donkey men either.' On the wall is a notice from the city gate: 'Men enter the city; the accounts enter first.'
column3: 湖东的林子边上有一家客栈，是进王城前的最后一个歇脚处。一伙国舅府的骑手住了进来，不给房钱，还把客栈的马全牵去当了坐骑。老板娘拿擀面杖守着灶房，说灶房是她的命，「骑马的进不来，骑驴的也不行」。墙上贴着一张城门的告示：「人进城，账先进城。」

column2: The riders flee on their own horses, and the landlady tucks her rolling pin into her belt and boils up a huge pot of pulled noodles. Everyone going into the city is afraid of the clerk at the gate, she says. 'Your name, where you're from, what you carry, he remembers it all at a glance. If you came through ten years ago, he'll still remember what shoes you had on that day.'
column3: 骑手们骑着自己的马跑了，老板娘把擀面杖往腰里一插，下了一大锅拉面。她说进城的人都怕城门口那位录事先生：「谁叫什么，从哪儿来，带的什么，他一眼就记住，十年前进过城的，他还记得你那天穿的什么鞋。」

column2: Under the riders' bedding you find ten sacks of white flour, three jars of wine, a basket of dried naan, two bundles of horse feed, and their unpaid bill: twenty-three days, not a copper paid, the last line written by the landlady: 'Every man on a horse is a bastard.'
column3: 骑手们的铺盖底下抄出十袋白面、三坛葡萄酒、一筐风干的馕、两捆马料，还有他们赊账的账单：二十三天，一文未付，账单最后一行是老板娘写的「骑马的都是王八蛋」。

column2: Every time you pass, the landlady boils you a pot of pulled noodles stretched longer than a belt, and pushes two oily naan into each of your bundles. 'Once you're in the city you won't get mine. City noodles are all dead dough.'
column3: 每次路过，老板娘都给你们煮一锅拉面，面扯得比腰带还长，再往每人的包袱里塞两个油馕：「进了城就吃不着我的了，城里的面都是死面。」

column2: The Borrowed Cart
column3: 借水车

column2: In the deepest part of the woods, in a clearing, stands a great water cart, its wheels half sunk in earth, moss on its shafts, a pole beside it with a lamp hanging at the top, the oil in the lamp freshly topped up. The last band of the Royal Uncle's archers lies in ambush around it, waiting for the fire-setters. At the sight of the cart, Ge Xiaolun drops his whip.
column3: 林子最深处，一片空地上停着一辆大水车，车轮陷进了土里一半，车辕上长了青苔，车边一根木杆，杆头挂着一盏灯，灯碗里的油是新添的。车周围埋伏着最后一伙国舅府的弓手，等着放火的人来。葛小轮看见车，鞭子都掉在了地上。

column2: The archers flee. The old wheelwright finds his own mark on the shaft and nods. Pasted inside the cart is a sheet of paper: 'Borrowed: one royal water cart, carrying thirty skins of water, for the three hundred of the Qianli caravan. Entered by the bookkeeper. To be repaid next year with a channel.' Three-Inch Ma peels it off and puts it away. 'A contract. No theft.' Ge Xiaolun takes down the lamp and holds it to his chest: who has been coming every night to fill it? He'll haul the cart into the city and settle this account in front of the King.
column3: 弓手们跑了。老车匠摸到辕木上自己的记号。车厢里贴着一张纸：「借王城水车一辆，载水三十囊，予千里号三百人。账房记。来年以渠抵之。」麻三寸收好：「有契，不为盗。」葛小轮取下那盏灯抱在怀里：每夜是谁来添的油？他要把车拉进城，当着王的面对账。

column2: The Roller Road
column3: 滚木道

column2: Old Hu's boat must be dragged across this stretch of open country, but a large camp of the Royal Uncle's sits in the way, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, having cut down every tree nearby that could serve as a roller and stacked them in camp as firewood. The Royal Uncle's house has decreed, says Old Hu, that where the lake goes is for the House to decide. 'Drag a boat without leave and you're stealing the lake.'
column3: 胡老大的船要从这片野地上拖过去，路上却扎着一座国舅府的大营，戟士、弓手、铁骑都有，把附近所有能当滚木的树都砍了，堆在营里当柴烧。胡老大说国舅府放了话：湖往哪里走，归国舅府定，「谁私拖船，就是偷湖」。

column2: The camp is broken, the rollers recovered, and the Hu family of five haul the boat forward to their own chant, three li in a day. At night Old Hu points out the cracks in the ground: white lines of salt. 'Wherever the lake's been, it leaves salt.' All his life he's wanted to know why the lake moves. 'Asked my whole life. Nobody could tell me.'
column3: 大营被冲开，滚木都抢了回来，胡家五口喊着号子把船往前拖，一天拖了三里。夜里胡老大指着地上的裂纹给你们看：一道道盐白的纹路，「湖走过的地方，就留下盐」。他说他从小就想知道湖为什么会走，「问了一辈子，没人说得清」。

column2: The Lake Priestess's Altar
column3: 湖祝坛

column2: An earthen altar stands in the lakeside woods, and on it a woman in white hemp who calls herself the Lake Priestess. With her followers she stops travellers, snatches their waterskins one by one and pours them into the lake. The lake is dying, she says, because people have taken too much of its water. 'Give it back, and it won't leave.' Her followers guard the road with bows. An old traveller has collapsed of thirst below the altar, and she won't give him a mouthful.
column3: 湖边林子里筑着一座土坛，坛上站着一个披白麻的女人，自称湖祝，带着一群信徒拦住过路人，把人家的水囊一只只夺过来，倒进湖里。她说湖在死，是因为人从湖里拿走了太多的水，「还给它，它就不走了」。信徒们拿弓守着路口，有个过路的老人渴得倒在坛下，她也不给一口。

column2: The followers scatter, and the old man gets his water. Old Hu crouches and speaks to the priestess: the lake isn't dying, it's moving. A lake lives off its river, and when the river changes course upstream, the lake follows; the old bed dries in the sun into salt flats and a new lake rises wherever the river now reaches. 'Pour water all your life and you won't stop a river.' The priestess sits on her altar gazing at the lake and says not a word.
column3: 信徒们散了，老人喝上了水。胡老大蹲下来对湖祝说：湖不是死，是走。湖靠河养着，上游的河一改道，湖就跟着河挪，老湖底晒成盐滩，新湖在河到的地方涨起来，「你倒一辈子水，也拦不住一条河」。湖祝坐在坛上，望着湖，一句话也没说。

column2: The Forged Name Slips
column3: 假名帖

column2: A stall by the road selling 'name slips': to enter the city you must register at the gate, and these slips come with your name, origin and goods already written in. They're supposed to save three days of queuing. The sellers are a squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers at five taels a slip, and the buyers queue like a dragon. An old man who bought one was turned back at the gate and sits crying before the stall.
column3: 路边一个摊子，卖的是「名帖」：进城要在城门口报名，名帖上写好了名字、来路、货物，听说拿着它能少排三天队。卖帖的是国舅府的一伙戟士，一张帖五两银子，买的人排成了长龙。一个买了帖的老汉在城门口被退了回来，坐在摊前哭。

column2: The halberdiers flee and the old man gets his five taels back. The clerk at the city gate, he says, took one look at his forged slip and smiled: 'The number on this slip is wrong.' Every slip at the gate is numbered, and the clerk remembers every number. 'Ten years, and he's never missed one.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，老汉拿回了他的五两银子。他说城门口那位录事先生拿着他的假帖只看了一眼，就笑了：「这帖上的数，是错的。」原来城门的名帖每一张都编了号，录事先生记得每一个号，「十年，没漏过一个」。

column2: The Portrait Riders
column3: 画影骑

column2: A troop of the Royal Uncle's riders blocks the road to the city gate, their leader holding a portrait and comparing it face by face with everyone who passes. It's a drawing of your standard-bearer, all three patches on the banner included. The leader looks at the picture, looks at you, and slaps his thigh. 'That's them! The Royal Uncle said: nobody from the court enters the city.'
column3: 野地里一队国舅府的骑手拦住了去城门的路，领头的手里拿着一张画像，比着过路人的脸一个个看。画的是你们的旗手，旗子上的三块补丁都画上了。领头的看看画，看看你们，一拍大腿：「就是这伙！国舅说了，朝廷来的，一个都不许进城。」

column2: The riders flee, dropping the portrait. It's a good likeness, right down to the mole on the standard-bearer's face. On the back is written: 'Scout reports: travelling west the whole way, through Yangguan, the Sand Sea, the Thousand Buddha Caves.' The Royal Uncle's house has known your route for a long while. But along that route, you've learned a good deal about the Royal Uncle's house too.
column3: 骑手们跑了，画像落在了地上。画得很像，连旗手脸上的痣都点上了。画像背后写着：「探子报：一路西来，过阳关、沙海、千佛洞。」你们这一路的行踪，国舅府早就知道了；可这一路，你们也知道了国舅府的不少事。

column2: The Dividing Wall
column3: 隔市墙

column2: Inside the gate a broad street ought to run straight to the market. Now a new wall is going up across the middle of it, half built, halberdiers, archers and cavalry guarding the site and driving a gang of bricklayers to work day and night. Once it's done, anyone coming through the gate will have to detour past the Royal Uncle's front door, pay first, and then reach the market.
column3: 城门里头本该是一条直通集市的大街，如今街中间砌起了一道新墙，砌了一半，戟士、弓手、铁骑守着工地，逼着一帮泥瓦匠日夜赶工。墙一砌完，从城门进来的人就只能绕道国舅府门前，先交钱，再进市。

column2: The overseers fall back and the bricklayers push the wall down themselves. The King's city has a rule, says the old bricklayer, made when the present King first took the throne: 'From gate to market, not one step shall be walled off.' That year the King had it carved on a stone just inside the gate. The Royal Uncle carted the stone away later. 'But we all remember it.'
column3: 监工的人马退了，泥瓦匠们自己动手把墙推倒了。老瓦匠说王城有一条规矩，是现在这个王刚即位时定的：「门到市，一步不许隔。」他说那年王把这句话刻在城门里的一块石头上，石头后来被国舅搬走了，「可我们都记着」。

column2: The Royal Post House
column3: 王城驿馆

column2: The royal post house outside the city gate once received foreign envoys and the court's caravans. Now the Royal Uncle's household men hold it, drawn up before the door in three bodies. The steward looks your banner up and down. 'The court? The court forgot this road ten years ago.' He has your baggage thrown into the stables. 'The good rooms are for the Royal Uncle's guests. The stables are what you're fit for.'
column3: 城门外的王城驿馆，原本是接待各国使者和朝廷商队的地方，如今被国舅府的家丁占了，三路人马在门前排开。管事的斜眼打量你们的旗：「朝廷？朝廷十年前就把这条路忘了。」他让人把你们的行李扔到马棚里：「上房留给国舅府的客人，你们配住马棚。」

column2: Once the household men are down, the steward wears a different face. He kneels at the door, carries your baggage out of the stables into the best rooms himself piece by piece, fetches hot water and stands by holding a face towel. In a cupboard the post house still keeps its guest register from ten years ago. The last page reads: 'Qianli caravan, three hundred men, three nights. Account settled.' The handwriting is very neat.
column3: 家丁们一倒，管事的换了一副脸，跪在门口，亲自把你们的行李一件件从马棚里扛进了上房，又打了热水，捧着擦脸布站在一边。驿馆的柜子里还收着十年前的住客簿，最后一页写着：「千里号三百人，住三日，账已结。」字很工整。

column2: The Course-Change Rock
column3: 改道石

column2: Old Hu wants to see with his own eyes where the river changed course, and leads you deep into the woods to a dry riverbed wide enough to gallop down, tree roots hanging in mid-air along its banks. It's become a smugglers' hidden road: mounted, their contraband on pack horses, they come and go along the riverbed unseen by anyone outside. When they see you coming, they form up across the bed.
column3: 胡老大想亲眼看看河是在哪里改的道，领着你们往林子深处的一条干河床走。河床宽得能跑马，两岸的树根悬在半空，如今成了一伙走私客的暗道：他们骑着马，驮着私货，在干河床里来去，外头的人谁也看不见。见有人来，他们就在河床里拉开了阵势。

column2: The smugglers are driven from the riverbed. At its bend stands a great rock with a line carved on it, left by the old river wardens: 'Summer of the Bingwu year. Great flood. The river changed course and went south.' Old Hu works it out: eleven years ago. 'That year the lake began to move south and this side of the city went dry,' he says. 'Three whole years of drought, until those three hundred outsiders came.'
column3: 走私客被赶出了河床。河床拐弯的地方立着一块大石头，石头上刻着一行字，是从前守河的人留的：「丙午年夏，大水，河改道南去。」胡老大算了算：十一年前。「那年湖开始往南挪，城这边就旱了，」他说，「旱了整整三年，直到那三百个外乡人来。」

column2: The Lake-Turning Dam
column3: 拦湖坝

column2: At the edge of the woods the Royal Uncle's house has rounded up hundreds of labourers to build a great dam 'to turn the lake back'. Three years they've been building it, and still the lake moves south year by year; the dam is ever further from the water, and there's been none at its foot for ages. Halberdiers, archers and cavalry stand over them in three ranks, whipping anyone who's slow. The Royal Uncle drew up the dam himself, the labourers say. 'He says he won't believe a lake can move.'
column3: 林子边上，国舅府抓了几百个民夫，要修一道大坝，「把湖拦回来」。坝修了三年，湖还是一年年往南挪，坝离湖越来越远，民夫们修的坝底下早就没水了。监工的戟士、弓手、铁骑三路守着，修慢了就抽鞭子。民夫们说，这坝是国舅亲自画的，「他说他不信湖会走」。

column2: The overseers flee and the labourers drop their carrying poles and go home. Old Hu shakes his head at the dry dam. 'You can't drag a lake back. You can only follow it, or do what those three hundred did: dig a channel and bring the water to you.' An old labourer says the Royal Uncle's sister, the old Queen, died in the first year of the drought. 'Ever since, he can't bear to see the lake move.'
column3: 监工的人跑了，民夫们扔了扁担回家。胡老大看着那道干坝直摇头：「湖拉不回来，只能跟着走，要不就像那三百个人那样，挖一条渠，把水引过来。」一个老民夫说，国舅的姐姐，就是老王后，死在旱的头一年，「从那以后，他见不得湖走」。

column2: The Merchants' Encampment
column3: 万商营

column2: Outside the city's south gate sprawls a great encampment of tents, Persian, Sogdian, Uighur and Tibetan merchants crowded together, some of them here for half a year, their goods close to spoiling. The Royal Uncle's forces hold the road to the south gate: halberdiers blocking it, archers on the dunes, cavalry patrolling. To enter the city, first hand over a tenth of your goods. The merchants huddle and curse in seven or eight languages, all saying the same thing.
column3: 王城南门外扎着一大片帐篷，波斯的、粟特的、回鹘的、吐蕃的商人挤在一起，有的已经住了半年，带来的货都快放坏了。国舅府的人马守着去南门的路：戟士堵路，弓手上了沙丘，铁骑来回巡，要进城，先交一成的货。商人们凑在一起骂，七八种话，骂的是同一句。

column2: The Royal Uncle's forces are driven back to the gate. The merchants gather round your banner and look at it a long time. An old Sogdian says the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations in the city has twelve flagpoles: eleven fly the flags of the nations, and the twelfth has been bare ten years, kept for the court of the Central Plains. 'The Royal Uncle wants it sawn down,' he says. 'The King won't allow it. The King says keep the pole; the flag will come.'
column3: 国舅府的人马被赶回了城门口。商人们围着你们的旗子看了半天，一个粟特老商人说城里的万国商馆有十二根旗杆，十一根挂着各国的旗，第十二根空了十年，是留给中原朝廷的。「国舅要把那根杆子锯了，」他说，「王不许。王说杆子留着，旗会来。」

column2: The Envoy's Landing
column3: 钦差渡

column2: At the sight of your banner, the riverside customs master comes running out with his hat on crooked, convinced you're the court's envoy travelling incognito. He lays on a whole roast sheep, pushes a plate of gold across the table, then a niece, insisting you accept. You say you're a caravan. He doesn't believe it and smiles all the harder. 'Of course, of course, every envoy says that.' Under the table his riders have their swords half drawn.
column3: 河边的税关看见你们的旗子，关长连帽子都没戴正就跑了出来，一口咬定你们是朝廷微服私访的钦差。他摆了一桌全羊宴，席上塞来一盘金子，又塞来一个侄女，非要你们收下。你们说是商队，他不信，笑得更殷勤了：「懂，懂，钦差都这么说。」桌子底下，他的骑手们已经把刀拔出了半截。

column2: The customs master's riders, failing to buy the envoy, tried to silence him instead, and ended up knocked into the river. Kneeling in the mud the customs master hands over his ledger, every entry contraband run for the Royal Uncle's house. When he finally grasps that you really are a caravan, he faints on the spot. His first words on coming round: 'That gold. Can I have it back?'
column3: 关长的骑手们没收买成钦差，就想灭了口，结果被你们打下了河。关长跪在泥里递上账本，账上一笔笔全是替国舅府走的私货。等他听明白你们真是商队，当场晕了过去，醒来第一句是：「那金子，能还我吗？」

column2: The Gate Queue
column3: 候门长队

column2: Outside the city gate stretches a queue miles long. Some have pitched tents in it; one woman has given birth in it. It doesn't move because the Royal Uncle's halberdiers sell places at the head, a tael a place, and whoever won't buy gets pushed back. The clerk at the gate can register hundreds a day, the people in the queue say. 'It's this lot at the front blocking it, not him being slow.'
column3: 城门外排着一条长队，排了好几里，有人在队里搭了帐篷，有人在队里生了孩子。队伍不动，是因为国舅府的戟士在队头卖位子，一个位子一两银，不买的往后挪。队里的人说，城门口的录事先生一天能登记几百人，「是前头这帮人堵着，不是他慢」。

column2: The place-sellers flee and the queue lurches into motion. The camel man ahead of you says that whenever the clerk registers a caravan from the west he always asks one more thing: 'On the road...' and there he stops, waves his hand. 'Never mind. Next.' 'Ten years, always the same question,' says the camel man. 'He's never once finished it.'
column3: 卖位子的跑了，队伍一下子动了起来。排在你们前面的驼户说，那录事先生登记从西边来的商队时，总要多问一句：「路上……」问到这里就停住，摆摆手，「没什么，下一位」。「十年了，都这么问，」驼户说，「从来没问完过。」

column2: The Name Buyers
column3: 买名坊

column2: A compound in the open country north of the city with a sign reading 'Charity Mortuary'. It takes in no corpses, only names: the Royal Uncle's people seek out those who've died or left, buy their names, and send their own men into the city under them. Halberdiers guard the compound, stacking piles of names on the tables like bricks.
column3: 城北野地里一座院子，挂着「义庄」的牌子，却不收尸，收名字：国舅府的人四处打听死了的、走了的人，把他们的名字买下来，再让自己的人顶着这些名字进城。守院的戟士把一摞摞名字码在案上，像码砖头。

column2: The guards flee and you leaf through the names on the tables: all people who left the city in these years and never came back. You turn up one that reads 'Qianli caravan. Meng Xiaoshan', marked 'Sold'. Luckily the clerk at the gate didn't accept it. The man who tried to enter under that name was stopped on the spot. 'I remember Meng Xiaoshan. He didn't look like you.'
column3: 守院的跑了，案上的名字一张张翻过去，都是这些年出了城再没回来的人。你们翻到一张，写着「千里号·孟小山」，旁边批着「已售」。好在城门口那位录事先生不认：顶着这个名字去的人，被他当场拦下了，「孟小山我记得，他不是这个长相」。

column2: The Counting Drum Tower
column3: 点数鼓楼

column2: On the north corner of the wall stands a drum tower, and by old custom the drum is beaten every evening once for every person who entered the city that day, the whole city counting along. For months it's been silent: the Royal Uncle's archers seized the tower and sawed up the drumsticks. 'No need for the whole city to know how many came in.' At dusk the city's children still lean out of their windows from habit, waiting to count.
column3: 城墙的北角上有一座鼓楼，老规矩是每天傍晚擂鼓，当天进城几个人，就擂几下，全城的人听着数。这几个月鼓不响了：国舅府的弓手占了鼓楼，鼓槌都锯了，说「进了多少人，不用让全城知道」。城里的孩子们傍晚还是习惯性地趴在窗口等着数。

column2: The archers flee, and you whittle two new drumsticks. The old drummer beats out the number sent up from the gate, boom, boom, boom... four hundred and seventeen strokes, and the children count along without missing one. In ten years, says the old drummer, the gate's number has never once disagreed with the drum. 'That clerk's count is this city's count.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，你们削了两根新鼓槌，鼓楼上的老鼓手按城门送来的数擂了起来，咚、咚、咚……擂了四百一十七下，城里的孩子们跟着数，数得一个不差。老鼓手说城门的数，十年来从没跟鼓对不上过：「那录事先生的数，就是这城的数。」

column2: The Gate Clerk
column3: 城门录事

column2: In the gateway of the King's city the Royal Uncle's halberdiers are shoving the gates shut. 'No one from the court enters.' To one side of the passage stands a small table, and behind it sits a man with a thin face and narrowed eyes, a brush tucked behind his ear, head bent over his writing. That face you've seen on a wall at the Thousand Buddha Caves. Someone blurts out 'Master Bookkeeper!' He doesn't even look up. 'You've mistaken me, sir. I'm the gate clerk. When you've finished fighting, queue to register.'
column3: 王城的城门洞里，国舅府的戟士正推着城门要关，说「朝廷的人不许进」。门洞一侧一张小桌，桌后坐着一个人，瘦脸，眯眼，耳朵后头夹着一支笔，低头写字。那张脸，你们在千佛洞的墙上见过。有人脱口叫了声「账房先生」，他头都没抬：「客官认错人了，小的是城门录事。打完了，排队登记。」

column2: The halberdiers flee, and he registers your names one by one. At the end he asks, as if in passing: 'Out west in the Ghost Market, there was an apprentice who wouldn't speak. Is he still there?' You tell him the boy speaks now, and has been paying off the caravan's road money. The brush tip stops, and a drop of ink falls. 'Good. In you go.' As you leave the gateway you hear him say quietly behind you: 'Only once in my life have I got a sum wrong.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，他一个个登记你们的名字。写到最后，像是随口问：「西边鬼市上，有个不说话的学徒，还在吗？」你们说他开口了，还替商队还了路钱。笔尖一顿，落下一滴墨。「那就好。进城吧。」走出门洞时，你们听见他在身后低声说：「小的这辈子，只算错过一笔。」

column2: The Customs Warehouse
column3: 税关货仓

column2: Behind the customs post stands a large warehouse holding goods the customs master has impounded for the Royal Uncle's house, every nation's merchandise in one heap: bolts of silk, crates of pepper, bales of carpets. A troop of riders guards the door, the key round their leader's neck. He doesn't take it off even to sleep.
column3: 税关后头有一座大货仓，是关长替国舅府扣下的货，各国商人的东西堆在一处：成匹的丝、成箱的胡椒、成捆的地毯，一队骑手守着仓门，钥匙挂在领头的脖子上，睡觉也不摘。

column2: The riders flee and you yank the key off, cord and all. The warehouse door opens, and the impounded goods go back one by one to the merchants of the encampment, each claiming his own. When they've finished, a pile remains that no one claims: the Royal Uncle's house's own contraband.
column3: 骑手们跑了，钥匙连着绳子被你们拽了下来。货仓的门打开，扣下的货一样样还给了万商营的商人们，各家认各家的，认完了，还剩下一堆没人认的：都是国舅府自己的私货。

column2: The unclaimed pile gives up ten bolts of Shu brocade, three crates of pepper, two rolls of Persian carpet, a barrel of fine lamp oil, and a stack of blank 'House of the Royal Uncle passes', already stamped.
column3: 没人认的那堆里抄出十匹蜀锦、三箱胡椒、两卷波斯地毯、一桶上好的灯油，还有一摞空白的「国舅府通关牒」，印都盖好了。

column2: Every time you pass, the merchants of the encampment take turns to feed you: Persian pilaf today, Tibetan tsampa tomorrow, Uighur baked dumplings the day after, and each presses a bundle of provisions on you afterwards. Nobody will be outdone.
column3: 每次路过，万商营的商人们都轮流请你们吃饭，今天波斯的抓饭，明天吐蕃的糌粑，后天回鹘的烤包子，吃完各塞一包干粮，谁也不肯落在后头。

column2: The Banner Mender's
column3: 补旗铺

column2: To enter the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations, says the old Sogdian, your flag must be new. That one with three patches won't do. Outside the south gate an old tailor makes banners, but his shop has been sealed by the Royal Uncle's halberdiers and every bolt of yellow and red silk taken, 'banner cloth belongs to the House'. The old tailor sits at his door sewing the air with a needle, stitching a flag no one can see.
column3: 粟特老商人说，进万国商馆，旗得是新的，你们这面补了三块的可不行。南门外有个老裁缝专做旗子，可他的铺子被一队国舅府的戟士封了，铺里的黄绸红绸全被收走，说是「旗料归府」。老裁缝坐在门口，拿一根针在空中比画，比画的是一面谁也看不见的旗。

column2: The halberdiers flee and the silk is recovered. The old tailor picks up your old banner and studies it a long time, fingering the three patches, then sets the new silk aside. 'Not this one. A flag that's been patched three times is a flag that's travelled.' He just tidies the loose threads along the edge one by one and sews a band of red silk round the head of the pole. 'Hang it up. It'll look smart.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，绸子要了回来。老裁缝拿起你们的旧旗看了很久，摸着那三块补丁，把新绸子放下了：「这面不换。补过三回的旗，才是走过路的旗。」他只把旗边的线头一根根收好，又在旗杆头缝了一圈红绸，「挂上去，看着精神」。

column2: South Wall Flag Tower
column3: 南墙旗楼

column2: On the south wall stands a dilapidated flag tower where the old flag officer of the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations lives. The Royal Uncle declared him 'senile' and shut him up there with a squad of archers guarding the stair. Every day the old officer stands an hour at the tower window, gazing towards the Hall in the city. Round his waist is wound a long halyard thick as a wrist. It's the rope from the twelfth pole, he says.
column3: 南墙上一座破旗楼，住着万国商馆的老旗官，国舅说他「年老昏聩」，把他关在楼上，派了一队弓手守着楼梯。老旗官每天在楼窗前站一个时辰，望着城里商馆的方向。他腰上缠着一根长长的旗绳，粗得像手腕，他说那是第十二根杆子的绳。

column2: The archers flee and the old flag officer comes down, unwinding the halyard from his waist turn by turn, a good ten fathoms of it. The Royal Uncle wanted to fly his own house's flag on the twelfth pole, he says, so he took the rope down and wound it round himself. 'While the rope's on me, nobody can hoist anything.' He's worn it six years. He looks at your banner. 'It's come. That's what matters. Old is fine.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，老旗官下了楼，腰上的旗绳一圈圈解下来，足有十丈。他说国舅想在第十二根杆子上挂国舅府的旗，他就把绳子解下来缠在自己身上，「绳在我身上，谁也挂不上去」。一缠就是六年。他看着你们的旗：「来了就好，旧的也好。」

column2: The South Gate Barbican
column3: 南门瓮城

column2: The city's south gate is a barbican: the outer gate stands open, the inner gate shut, and whoever passes the outer gate is trapped inside to wait and pay. The Royal Uncle's forces hold the walls and the inner gate, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, all three. The merchants of the encampment follow behind you, and the old flag officer marches at the very front with the halyard over his shoulder, bellowing up at the wall: 'Open up! The court's flag is here!'
column3: 王城南门是一座瓮城，外门开着，内门关着，进了外门的人就被关在瓮城里，等着交钱。国舅府的人马守在城头和内门后：戟士、弓手、铁骑，三路都有。万商营的商人们跟在你们后头，老旗官扛着旗绳走在最前面，冲城头喊了一嗓子：「开门！朝廷的旗到了！」

column2: The inner gate is battered open and the merchants' camel trains stream into the city, bells jangling, seven or eight languages shouting the same word: 'Here!' Along the streets people push open their windows to look, and at the sight of that patched banner an old woman cries out: 'The court's people. They've come again.'
column3: 内门被撞开了，商人们的驼队一溜进了城，驼铃响成一片，七八种话喊着同一句「到了」。城里的街上有人推开窗户往外看，看见那面打着补丁的旗，有个老太太叫出了声：「朝廷的人，又来了。」

column2: The Raid on the Gatehouse
column3: 拿录事

column2: The day after you enter the city, a large force of the Royal Uncle's falls on the gate, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, declaring the gate clerk guilty of 'secret dealings with the court' and come to arrest him. The clerk's registers record every man the Royal Uncle's house has sent into the city under a false name, and the Royal Uncle has long been waiting for a pretext. The little table still stands in the gateway. No one sits behind it.
column3: 你们进城的第二天，一大队国舅府的人马扑向城门：戟士、弓手、铁骑，说城门录事「私通朝廷」，要拿人。录事的那些簿子里记着国舅府每一个顶名进城的人，国舅等这个借口等了很久。门洞里那张小桌还摆着，桌后没有人。

column2: The Royal Uncle's forces are beaten back, but the clerk has vanished. On the table lies his register, open at the page for the day you entered, a small circle drawn after every one of your names. In the margin is one extra word, the ink fresh: 'Arrived.'
column3: 国舅府的人马被打退了，可录事先生不见了。桌上摊着那本登记簿，翻在你们进城那一页，每个名字后头都画了一个小小的圈。页边还多了一行字，墨迹是新的：「到。」

column2: Hall of Ten Thousand Nations
column3: 万国商馆

column2: A great compound by the river in the King's city, 'HALL OF TEN THOUSAND NATIONS' carved over its gate. Twelve flagpoles stand in the courtyard: on eleven the flags snap in the wind, the twelfth is bare, yet its paint is fresh. A troop of the Royal Uncle's cavalry occupies the Hall, every nation's counter inside empty. From now on, they announce, the Hall trades with the Royal Uncle's house alone, and tomorrow the twelfth pole comes down.
column3: 王城的河边一座大院，院门上刻着「万国商馆」四个字，院里立着十二根旗杆，十一根上的旗被风扯得哗哗响，第十二根光秃秃的，杆身上的漆却是新刷的。商馆被国舅府的一队铁骑占着，馆里各国的柜台全空着，他们宣布：商馆从今往后只做国舅府一家的生意，第十二根杆子明天就锯。

column2: The cavalry are thrown out of the Hall. The old flag officer threads his ten fathoms of halyard through the pulley of the twelfth pole and your banner climbs it bit by bit, patches to the sun. One by one the nations' counters open again, gold from the west trading for timber from the east, the clerks' abacuses clattering all at once. The paint on the pole, the old officer says, the King has sent someone to renew every year, ten years without a break. And the King left a message for the first to hoist a flag on it: 'When the flag is up, it's time the accounts were settled.'
column3: 铁骑被赶出了商馆。老旗官把十丈旗绳穿进第十二根杆子的滑轮，你们的旗一点点升上去，补丁朝着太阳。各国的柜台一个个重新开张，西边的金子换东边的木料，账房的算盘噼啪响成一片。老旗官说杆子上的漆是王每年派人来刷的，十年没断过；王还留过一句话给第一个挂旗的人：「旗挂上了，账就该对了。」

column2: The Inner City Street
column3: 内城大街

column2: Along the street from the gate to the palace every door is shut and barred, and the Royal Uncle's forces stand at every corner, halberdiers, archers, cavalry, a sentry every three paces, a picket every five. They're searching for a man: thin face, narrowed eyes, a brush behind his ear. Everyone in the street walks with head down, afraid to look up in case they look like him.
column3: 从城门到王宫的大街上，家家关门闭户，街口都站着国舅府的人马，戟士、弓手、铁骑，三步一岗，五步一哨。他们说要搜一个人：瘦脸，眯眼，耳朵上夹笔的。满街的人都低着头走路，谁也不敢抬头，生怕自己长得像。

column2: The Royal Uncle's forces are driven from the street and doors and windows swing open one by one. The melon sellers and naan sellers set out their stalls again, and someone takes the brush from behind his ear and laughs: 'These last days nobody in the city who can write has dared tuck a brush there.' An old man says: 'If they really did catch that clerk, who'd keep this city's accounts?'
column3: 国舅府的人马被赶出了大街，门窗一扇扇推开了。卖瓜的、卖馕的又摆出了摊子，有人把耳朵上的笔拿了下来，笑着说：「这几天，全城会写字的都不敢夹笔了。」一个老头说：「那位录事先生要是真被抓了，这城的账，谁来算？」

column2: The Search Riders
column3: 搜城骑

column2: On an open square in the north of the city a troop of the Royal Uncle's riders has just come back from a sweep, every face grimy. They've turned the north of the city upside down, poked into wells, haystacks and dung pits, and still can't find that clerk. Their leader is lashing the ground with his whip in fury. Then he sees you and brightens. 'If we can't take him, we'll take you!'
column3: 城北的空场上，一队国舅府的骑手刚搜完一圈回来，个个灰头土脸。他们把城北翻了个底朝天：井里、草垛里、粪坑里都捅过了，就是找不着那个录事。领头的气得拿马鞭抽地，看见你们，眼睛一亮：「拿不着他，拿你们也行！」

column2: The riders are scattered, and their leader, tied up, is still shouting: 'Strange! A grown man, where could he hide? We've searched the whole city, all but the palace!' The words are no sooner out than he stops short himself, then shakes his head. 'Impossible. There's no one in the palace but the King.'
column3: 骑手们被打散了，领头的被绑起来还在嚷：「怪了，一个大活人，能藏到哪儿去？全城都搜遍了，就差王宫没搜！」话一出口，他自己先愣住了，又摇摇头：「不可能，王宫里只有王。」

column2: The Court Envoy's Residence
column3: 朝廷使馆

column2: A walled residence out in the wilds, the words 'COURT ENVOY'S RESIDENCE' over its gate half plastered over with mud. Ten years ago the court's envoy lived here. Then the road was cut, the man left, and the Royal Uncle sealed the house and set his finest troops to guard it, halberdiers at the gate, archers on the walls, cavalry circling outside. There's still something inside, says the old flag officer, that the Royal Uncle has always wanted to burn and the King has never allowed.
column3: 荒野里一座带围墙的宅院，门楣上「朝廷使馆」四个字被泥糊住了一半。十年前朝廷的使臣住在这里，后来路断了，人走了，宅子被国舅封了，派了最精的一支人马守着，戟士守门，弓手上墙，铁骑在外头绕。老旗官说，宅子里还有一样东西，国舅一直想烧，王一直不许。

column2: The picked troops fall back. The study is thick with dust, and on the desk lies a letter from the court eight years ago: 'Asking after the Qianli caravan.' Beneath it is a reply never sent, its ink of several ages, only one sentence long: 'The Qianli caravan's account, your servant will answer for himself.' The King never would call himself 'We', says the old flag officer. 'To anyone at all he just says I. And writing to the court, he puts your servant.'
column3: 精兵退了。使馆的书房里落满了灰，案上压着一封朝廷八年前的来书：「问千里号下落。」底下是一封没寄出去的回书，墨色新旧不一，只有一句：「千里号之账，臣自当之。」老旗官说王从来不肯自称「孤」，「跟谁说话都是一个我字，写信给朝廷，倒写起臣来了」。

column2: The Night Raid on the Flag
column3: 夜扯旗

column2: The first night the flag is up, a party of the Royal Uncle's forces creeps up under the Hall's back wall: halberdiers with ladders, archers nocking fire arrows, cavalry waiting at the mouth of the lane, all to burn the flag on the twelfth pole. Woken by the noise, the merchants of every nation charge out from behind their counters with steelyard beams, abacuses and cloth measures, none slower than the next.
column3: 旗挂上的第一夜，一伙国舅府的人马摸到了商馆后墙下：戟士扛着梯子，弓手搭着火箭，铁骑在巷口接应，要把第十二根杆子上的旗烧了。各国商人被惊醒，拎着秤杆、算盘、量布的尺子从柜台后头冲了出来，谁也不比谁跑得慢。

column2: The Royal Uncle's men are chased out of the lane and every fire arrow ends up in the river. At dawn the flag is still on its pole, one corner singed black. The merchants take turns keeping watch, the Persian jeweller the first half of the night, the old Sogdian the second. 'While this flag flies,' they say, 'someone stands behind our trade.'
column3: 国舅府的人被赶出了巷子，火箭全掉进了河里。天亮的时候，旗还在杆子上，只燎黑了一角。商人们轮流守夜，波斯珠宝商守上半夜，粟特老商人守下半夜。他们说：「这面旗挂着，我们的买卖就有人认。」

column2: The Twelve-Lamp Tower
column3: 十二灯楼

column2: At the corner of the south wall stands a lamp tower with twelve lamps on top. It's an old custom of the Hall of Ten Thousand Nations: when all twelve poles fly flags, all twelve lamps are lit together, bright enough to light half the lake. For ten years only eleven have burned. Tonight the merchants want to light the twelfth, but a squad of the Royal Uncle's archers holds the stair, and they've tipped the lamp oil into the ditch below the wall.
column3: 南墙的转角有一座灯楼，楼顶十二盏灯，是万国商馆的老规矩：十二根杆子都挂了旗，十二盏灯就一起点，照得半个湖都亮。十年来只点过十一盏。今夜商人们想点第十二盏，楼梯口却守着一队国舅府的弓手，灯油被他们倒进了墙下的沟里。

column2: The archers flee, the merchants pool lamp oil from their counters, and the twelfth lamp is lit. When all twelve blaze together, the lake turns to gold. After a while a single lamp lights up in the direction of the palace, just one, and burns a long time before going out. 'The King has seen,' says the old flag officer.
column3: 弓手们跑了，商人们从各家柜台凑来了灯油，第十二盏灯点着了。十二盏灯一起亮起来的时候，湖面上一片金光。过了一会儿，王宫的方向也亮起了一盏灯，就一盏，亮了很久才灭。老旗官说：「王看见了。」

column2: The Note-Runner
column3: 传条小内侍

column2: Under the palace's outer wall several of the Royal Uncle's archers have cornered a young eunuch to search him for notes: he's the palace's errand runner, and most of the notes going round the city these months he's carried. He's stuffing the notes into his mouth one by one and chewing, mouth full of ink, while the archers stamp in frustration.
column3: 王宫外墙下，几个国舅府的弓手围着一个小内侍，要搜他身上的纸条：他是宫里专门跑腿送条子的，这几个月城里的条子，大半是他送的。小内侍把纸条一张张塞进嘴里嚼，嚼得满嘴墨，弓手们急得直跺脚。

column2: The archers flee, and the young eunuch spits out a mouthful of paper pulp and wipes his lips. Every night the King stands writing notes, he says; there's no bed for the King in the palace, only a tall writing desk. The 'Bring the cart' note for the Petition Drum, he carried that. The last one, meant for you, he's kept in his coat all along, too precious to chew: 'Bring everything. Come to the palace to settle the accounts.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，小内侍吐出一嘴纸渣，抹抹嘴。他说王每夜站着批条子，宫里没有王的床，只有一张高高的书案。登闻鼓那张「带车来见」，是他送的；给你们的最后一张，他一直揣在怀里，没舍得嚼：「东西带齐了，进宫对账。」

column2: The Gathering at the Palace
column3: 宫前会齐

column2: On the open ground outside the palace's north gate, people from all along your road gather by ones and twos: an old well digger with a knotted rope, a lad hauling an old water cart, a wine woman with her camel train, an old flag officer with a halyard over his shoulder, a family who came by boat. The Royal Uncle's archers line the palace wall shouting down at the crowd: 'Disperse! Assembly will be treated as treason!'
column3: 王宫北门外的空地上，陆陆续续聚来了一路上的人：打着结绳的老井匠、拉着旧水车的后生、赶着驼队的酒娘子、扛着旗绳的老旗官，还有撑船来的一家子。国舅府的弓手在宫墙上站成一排，冲着人群喊：「散了！聚众者，以谋逆论！」

column2: The archers on the wall are shot down and the crowd stays. Everyone lays what they brought before the palace gate: a slip of paper reading 'Well 300', a cart-loan contract, a receipt for two hundred and ninety-nine jars, a halyard ten fathoms long. When it's done, nobody speaks. From inside the gate comes a voice: 'Come in. It's time the accounts were settled.'
column3: 宫墙上的弓手被射了下来，人群没有散。大家把带来的东西一样样摆在宫门前：一张「第三百井」的纸条、一张借车契、二百九十九坛的收条、一根十丈长的旗绳。摆完了，谁也没说话。宫门里传出一个声音：「进来吧。账，该对了。」

column2: The Palace North Gate
column3: 宫北门

column2: The palace gate opens a crack. Inside, a line of halberdiers the Royal Uncle has planted bars the way to the main hall, which stands by the river across one courtyard. Their leader says the Royal Uncle's orders are that no one sees the King before the spring banquet. Across the courtyard the hall doors stand open. It's dark inside but for a single lamp, and beneath it a figure stands behind a tall writing desk.
column3: 宫门开了一道缝，门里站着一排国舅府安插进来的戟士，堵住了去正殿的路，正殿就在河边，隔着一道院子。领头的说国舅有令，春宴之前，谁也不许见王。院子那头，正殿的门开着，殿里很暗，只有一盏灯，灯下有个人影站在一张高高的书案后面。

column2: The Royal Uncle's halberdiers are thrown out of the palace gate, and only then do the palace's own guards come out from all sides and line the courtyard in good order. Not one of them stops you. The old groom stands in a corner of the yard holding the old camel called Remainder, and the camel, facing the hall, kneels down.
column3: 国舅府的戟士被赶出了宫门，宫里的禁军这才从各处出来，整整齐齐列在院子两边，没有一个人拦你们。老马夫牵着那峰叫「余数」的老骆驼站在院角，骆驼冲着正殿的方向，跪了下来。

column2: The Dungeon Breakouts
column3: 地牢逃囚

column2: On waste ground outside the city a ragged band has taken over a few derelict kilns, sleeping by day and robbing by night. They're escapees from the city dungeon. These past years the Royal Uncle has crammed it full: those who didn't pay their water money, those who said the wrong thing, those who looked like the clerk. Packed that tight, the walls leak, and men keep wriggling out a batch at a time.
column3: 王城外的荒地上，一伙衣衫破烂的人占了几间废窑，白天睡觉，夜里出来抢东西。他们是从王城地牢里逃出来的：国舅这几年把地牢塞得满满的，不交水钱的、说错话的、长得像录事的，都往里关，关多了，墙就漏了，人就一拨拨往外钻。

column2: This batch of escapees is broken up; some go home, some head for the hills. But the dungeon is still full, the Royal Uncle's house is still locking people up, and the walls still leak. Before long another batch will wriggle out, take the kilns and waylay travellers by night. As long as that dungeon stays so full, you'll have to come and clear this place every so often.
column3: 这一拨逃囚被打散了，有的回了家，有的进了山。可地牢还满着，国舅府还在往里关人，墙还在漏，过一阵又会有一拨人钻出来，占了废窑，在夜里拦路。只要那座地牢还这么满，这里就得隔一阵来清一回。

column2: The Debt Wall
column3: 记债墙

column2: On the inner face of the south wall runs an old stretch covered in chalk writing, a custom of the King's city for decades: who owes whom is written on the wall for the whole city to witness, and when it's paid, the debtor comes and wipes it off himself. A squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers is slapping lime wash over it, turning it blank white: the Royal Uncle's house's debts are all written on this wall.
column3: 南墙里侧有一段老墙，墙砖上密密麻麻写满了粉笔字，是王城几十年的老规矩：谁欠谁的，写在墙上，全城作证；还清了，自己来擦。一队国舅府的戟士正拿石灰浆往墙上刷，刷得白花花一片：国舅府欠的债，都写在这面墙上。

column2: The halberdiers flee. The lime isn't yet dry and the writing beneath can still be read. Under the eaves is one brick the rain never reached and the lime missed, its writing ten years old: 'The Qianli caravan owes the King's city one cart of water.' After it, in another, smaller hand: 'Repaid with a channel. Still owing: one man.' Nobody has ever come to wipe those words off.
column3: 戟士们跑了，石灰还没干透，底下的字还能认。屋檐底下有一块砖，雨淋不着，石灰也没刷到，字是十年前的：「千里号欠王城水一车。」后面跟着另一个人的字，小一些：「以渠抵。尚欠一人。」那几个字一直没人来擦。

column2: Where the Boat Meets the River
column3: 拖船入河

column2: The Hu family has dragged their boat all the way from the open country to the river outside the palace, the rollers under the hull worn to slivers. But a troop of the Royal Uncle's cavalry holds the bank, saying the river belongs to the House. 'Only the House's boats may sail this river.' They mean to push the Hu boat back up the slope. Old Hu's little granddaughter stands at the bow and spits at them.
column3: 胡老大一家把船从野地一路拖到了王宫外的河边，船底的滚木都磨成了薄片。可河岸上守着一队国舅府的铁骑，说河归国舅府管，「这河上只许走国舅府的船」，要把胡家的船推回坡上。胡老大的小孙女站在船头，冲铁骑们吐了一口唾沫。

column2: The cavalry driven off, the Hu family give one heave together and the boat slides into the river, sinks, bobs back up, rocks twice and steadies. This time, says Old Hu, he isn't chasing the lake but waiting for it. 'The lake follows the river. The river's here, so one day the lake will come.' He'll pole the boat to the palace water gate, he says, 'and take a look at the King who wouldn't let them saw down the flagpole'.
column3: 铁骑被赶跑了。胡家五口一声号子，大船滑进了河里，船身一沉，又浮了起来，晃了两晃，稳了。胡老大说这回不是追湖，是等湖：「湖跟着河走，河在这儿，湖总有一天会来。」他说他要把船撑到王宫的水门下，「去看看那个不让锯旗杆的王」。

column2: The South Wall Garrison
column3: 南墙戍营

column2: At the foot of the south wall stands the Royal Uncle's garrison, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, hauling timber and iron locks into the gateway to seal the south gate from inside. The merchants of the Hall have learned the plan: on the day of the spring banquet the south gate shuts, the Hall is locked and the twelfth pole sawn down. 'In one day, make this city as it was ten years ago.'
column3: 南墙根下扎着国舅府的戍营，营里戟士、弓手、铁骑都有，正往城门洞里运木头和铁锁，要把南门从里头封死。万国商馆的商人们打听到：春宴那天，南门要关，商馆要锁，第十二根杆子要锯，「一天之内，叫这城像十年前一样」。

column2: The garrison scatters, its timber and locks thrown into the moat. Under the captain's command arrow is a sheet of paper, an order in the Royal Uncle's hand: 'On the day of the spring banquet, close the city for three days.' On the back is another line, the ink as if he wrote it and then tried to strike it out and didn't quite: 'That man in the city. Within three days, it will be settled.'
column3: 戍营散了，木头和铁锁扔进了护城河。营头的令箭上压着一张纸，是国舅的手令：「春宴之日，闭城三日。」纸背面还有一行，墨迹像是写完又想划掉，没划干净：「城里那个人，三日之内，要见分晓。」

column2: The Deed-Collecting Camp
column3: 收契营

column2: A camp stands in the open country north of the city, the Royal Uncle's forces going house to house collecting 'water deeds': every household in the city has a deed stating how much water it may draw from the channel each day. They give a peck of rice per deed, and whoever won't sell gets the channel mouth at their door blocked with stones. The deeds already fill half a room in the camp, and outside stands a weeping queue.
column3: 城北野地里扎着一座营，国舅府的人马挨家挨户收「水契」：王城每户人家都有一张水契，写着自家每天能从渠里分多少水。他们一张契给一斗米，不卖的，就把门口的渠口用石头堵上。营里的水契已经堆了半间屋子，营外排着一溜哭哭啼啼的人。

column2: The deed collectors are scattered and the deeds handed back house by house. An old woman holding her own deed says the Royal Uncle means to hold all the city's water in his fist. 'Come the spring banquet, it won't matter who wears the crown. With the water in his hand, the city's in his hand.'
column3: 收契的人马被打散，水契一张张还给了各家。一个老太太捧着自家的契，说国舅这是要把全城的水攥在自己手里：「到了春宴那天，谁戴王冠都不要紧，水在他手里，城就在他手里。」

column2: The Deed House
column3: 水契房

column2: In the north of the city the Royal Uncle's house has opened a 'Deed House' where all the collected water deeds are kept, with the rice used to buy them stacked in the storeroom behind. A troop of riders guards the door, and a price list is posted beside it: 'One water deed, one peck of rice. In a dry year, half a peck.'
column3: 国舅府在城北开了一间「水契房」，收来的水契都存在这里，房后的库里堆着拿来换契的米。一队骑手守着门，门口贴着价目：「水契一张，米一斗；旱年，米半斗。」

column2: The riders flee, the doors of the Deed House are taken off, the deeds handed back one by one to the queuing households and the rice in the storeroom shared out. One deed is left unclaimed, for a small room beside the city gate. Under 'Householder' it says: 'The clerk.'
column3: 骑手们跑了，水契房的门板卸下来，契纸一张张发还给排队的人家，库里的米也分了。最后剩下一张没人来领的契，是城门边一间小屋的，户主一栏写着：「录事。」

column2: The storeroom yields thirty pecks of white rice, twelve sacks of beans, four jars of clear oil, a chest of the Royal Uncle's blank water deeds, and a deed register, every deed clearly entered but every entry's rice a pint short.
column3: 库里抄出三十斗白米、十二袋豆子、四坛清油、一箱国舅府的空白水契，还有一本收契簿，每一张都记得清清楚楚，可每一笔的米数都少写了一升。

column2: Every time you pass, the households who got their deeds back set a bowl of clear water and a handful of roasted beans by their doors and bring them out one house after another as you go by. 'The water's from the channel, no charge. The beans we roasted ourselves.'
column3: 每次路过，拿回了水契的人家都会在门口放一碗清水、一把炒豆子，你们走过，一家接一家地端出来：「水是渠里的，不收钱，豆子是自家炒的。」

column2: The False Ledger Tower
column3: 假账楼

column2: A corner tower on the city wall, its door shut, lamps burning and an abacus clicking day and night. Master Gou, a bookkeeper kept by the Royal Uncle's house, is forging accounts in there: he's to produce a 'City Water Ledger' proving that these past years the King has given away the city's water to outsiders for nothing. A troop of riders guards the foot of the tower, and two big dogs are chained at the stairs.
column3: 城墙上一座角楼，楼里关着门，点着灯，日夜有算盘声。国舅府养的账房苟先生在里头造假账：要拿出一本「王城水账」，证明王这几年把城里的水都白白送给了外乡人。楼下一队骑手守着，楼梯口还拴着两条大狗。

column2: The riders flee and Master Gou cowers in a corner hugging his abacus. Three months, and he hasn't forged a single ledger. 'I copied from the King's accounts, and wherever I copied, it all tallied: which well the water came from, which household it went to, not a ladle out.' He sighs. 'First time in my life I've seen accounts you can't alter.' He gives up whom the Royal Uncle means to meet on the wall: men in golden masks.
column3: 骑手们跑了，苟先生抱着算盘缩在墙角。他造了三个月，一本也没造成：「王的账我照着抄，抄到哪儿都对得上，水从哪口井来，到哪户去，一瓢都不差。」他叹了口气：「我这辈子头一回见着不能改的账。」他供出了国舅要在城墙上见的人：戴金面具的。

column2: The Impound Yard
column3: 扣货场

column2: A yard fenced with stakes outside the city, called the 'inspection yard'. Every caravan entering must have its goods inspected here, but the inspection never ends; some have waited a year and still aren't done. Dozens of camels are tethered inside and grass grows on the stacked goods. The Royal Uncle's forces guard it in three ranks, and the inspection has only one rule: those who pay are inspected first.
column3: 城外一片用木栅圈起来的场子，叫「验货场」，进城的商队都要在这里「验货」，可验起来没完没了，有的验了一年还没验完。场里拴着几十峰骆驼，货堆上长了草。守场的是国舅府的人马，三路排开，验货的规矩就一条：交钱的先验。

column2: The guards flee, the stakes are pushed down and the caravans file out one by one. The last is a small pack-horse train come up from the Tea Road in the south, held here two years. Its leader takes a letter from his coat. On the cover: 'Kindly deliver to the bookkeeper of the Qianli caravan, Silk Road.' It's signed with a single character: 'Lu'. 'We give it to him in person only,' he says. 'Two years we've searched. Nobody in the city knows any such bookkeeper.'
column3: 守场的跑了，木栅推倒，商队一支支出了场。最后一支是从南边茶路上来的小马帮，扣了两年，马帮头子从怀里掏出一封信，封皮上写着「烦交丝路千里号账房」，落款只有一个「陆」字。「我们只交给他本人，」他说，「找了两年，城里没人认这个账房。」

column2: The Flag Procession Road
column3: 献旗道

column2: The day before the spring banquet, by the Hall's old custom, merchants of twelve nations carry twelve flags in procession from the Hall to the palace's south gate to present them. This year your thrice-patched banner leads the way. At a street corner a large force of the Royal Uncle's bursts out, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, blocking the road solid. 'Where did this beggar's flag come from? Fit to enter the palace?'
column3: 春宴前一天，按万国商馆的老规矩，十二国的商人要扛着十二面旗，从商馆一路走到王宫南门献旗。今年走在最前头的是你们那面补了三块的旗。街口冲出来一大队国舅府的人马，戟士、弓手、铁骑，把路堵得水泄不通：「哪来的叫花子旗，也配进宫？」

column2: The blockers scattered, the procession reaches the palace gate. Inside stands a gauze screen, and behind it sits a figure in a crown hung with strings of beads. The twelve flags are presented one by one and the figure nods at each. When your patched banner comes, he stands and bows deeply, far lower than a king ought to.
column3: 拦路的人被打散了，献旗的队伍走到了宫门前。宫门里立着一道纱屏，屏后坐着一个戴珠旒冠的人影。十二面旗一面面献上去，人影一面面点头，轮到你们那面补丁旗，他站了起来，深深弯下了腰，比一个王该弯的低得多。

column2: The Palace Water Gate
column3: 王宫水门

column2: On its river side the palace has a water gate where palace boats once came and went. Old Hu has poled his great boat down the river to the foot of it, but the Royal Uncle's halberdiers have lowered its iron portcullis and a line of them stand on top jabbing their long halberds at the boat to sink this 'boat of unknown origin'.
column3: 王宫临河的一面开着一道水门，从前宫里的船从这里出入。胡老大撑着他那条大船顺河漂到了水门下，可水门的铁闸被国舅府的戟士放了下来，闸上站着一排人，拿长戟往船上捅，要把这条「来路不明」的船捅沉。

column2: The halberdiers end up in the river and the portcullis is winched up. The old water-gate keeper says the King comes up onto the gate every evening and stands a while looking west along the river until dark. 'Looking at what?' asks Old Hu. The keeper says: 'The King says: the road.'
column3: 戟士们掉进了河里，铁闸绞了上去。看水门的老头说，王每天傍晚都到水门上站一会儿，望着河往西去的方向，望到天黑才回。「看什么？」胡老大问。老头说：「王说，看路。」

column2: Royal Stable Slope
column3: 御厩坡

column2: On the slope south of the palace lie the royal stables, home to the guard's horses. A band of the Royal Uncle's riders has seized them and led all the good horses off to the Royal Uncle's house, leaving only one old camel they can't shift: it lies on the ground and won't get up however it's hauled, a blurred 'Qian' branded on its rump. The riders, losing patience, are whipping it.
column3: 王宫南边的坡上是御厩，养着禁军的马。国舅府的一伙骑手占了马厩，把好马都牵去了国舅府，只剩下一峰老骆驼他们牵不动：骆驼趴在地上，谁拉都不起来，屁股上烙着一个模糊的「千」字。骑手们急了，正拿鞭子抽它。

column2: The riders flee and the old camel gets up by itself and snorts at you. The old groom says it came with a band of outsiders ten years ago. When they left they didn't take it, so the King keeps it in the royal stables and comes every evening to see it and feed it a handful of beans. 'The King calls it Remainder,' says the groom. 'Don't ask me what that means.'
column3: 骑手们跑了，老骆驼自己站了起来，冲你们喷了口气。老马夫说这骆驼是十年前跟着一伙外乡人来的，那伙人走的时候没带走它，王就把它养在御厩里，每天傍晚来看一回，给它喂一把豆子。「王管它叫余数，」老马夫说，「我也不懂什么意思。」

column2: The Meeting on the Wall
column3: 城头密会

column2: At night a lamp burns in a disused arrow tower on the city wall. The Royal Uncle's steward sits inside, and opposite him a man in a golden mask, a red stone set between its brows. A squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers guards the foot of the tower, and a few words leak through the crack in the door: 'Gold... the spring banquet... the seal...'
column3: 夜里，城墙上一座废弃的箭楼里亮着灯。国舅府的管家坐在里头，对面是一个戴金面具的人，面具的眉心嵌着一颗红石头。楼下一队国舅府的戟士守着，门缝里漏出几句话：「金子……春宴……印……」

column2: The halberdiers flee and the steward, jumping from the window, breaks his leg and is picked up by you. He gives up the whole plan: at the spring banquet, red-string wine puts the palace to sleep for a night; the Gold Masks enter dressed as monks bringing gifts from the Thousand Buddha Caves and take the King's seal; and the Royal Uncle publicly 'invites the King to abdicate'. What the Gold Masks want is gold. 'The Lord of the Caves gave up his mask. These men didn't.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，管家从窗口跳下去摔断了腿，被你们捡了回来。他供出了全盘：春宴那天，红绳酒让宫里睡一夜，金面卫扮成千佛洞来献礼的和尚进宫，取了王的印，国舅当众「请王让位」。金面卫要的是金子，「千佛洞主把金面交了，这些人没交」。

column2: The Palace Kitchen Garden
column3: 御膳菜园

column2: Outside the palace lies a kitchen garden supplying the palace kitchens, a row of storehouses along its edge. The Royal Uncle's archers have taken it and are carting the storehouse contents off to the House by the wagonload, declaring the spring banquet 'will be catered by the Royal Uncle's house'. The old head gardener has been driven over to the dung pit and is still muttering: 'The chives want cutting. Leave them any longer and they'll go woody.'
column3: 王宫外有一片菜园，给宫里的膳房供菜，园边一溜库房。国舅府的弓手占了菜园，把库房里的东西一车车往府里运，说春宴的酒菜「由国舅府操办」。菜园的老园头被赶到了粪坑边上，嘴里还念叨着：「韭菜该割了，再不割就老了。」

column2: The archers flee, and the old gardener's first act is to go and cut the chives. The palace kitchen makes one extra portion every meal, he says, and nobody ever eats it; when it's cleared it goes to the city gate for the people queuing to come in. 'The King says food mustn't be cooked for nothing, and a bowl mustn't stand empty.'
column3: 弓手们跑了，老园头第一件事是去割韭菜。他说宫里的膳房每顿都多做一份，这一份从来没人吃，撤下来就送到城门口，给排队进城的人吃，「王说，饭不能白做，碗也不能空着」。

column2: The storehouses yield twenty baskets of fresh vegetables and melons, ten sides of mutton, four crocks of yoghurt, a chest of fine tea bricks stamped with a Tea Road merchant's mark, and the Royal Uncle's house's menu for the spring banquet, with a note in small writing under the first dish: 'Serve with red-string wine.'
column3: 库房里抄出二十筐新鲜瓜菜、十扇羊肉、四坛酸奶、一箱上好的茶砖（茶砖上印着南边茶路的字号），还有国舅府开的春宴菜单，第一道菜底下用小字注着：「红绳酒配」。

column2: Every time you pass, the old gardener picks you a fresh basket of melons and fruit and tucks in a handful of just-cut chives. 'Make dumplings on the road. Don't say they're from the palace. Say I grew them.'
column3: 每次路过，老园头都从菜园里现摘一筐瓜果给你们装上，顺手塞一把刚割的韭菜：「路上包饺子。别说是宫里的，就说是我种的。」

column2: The Old Servant's Stall
column3: 老仆摊

column2: In the river bend below the palace an old white-haired servant keeps a stall on the bank selling the palace's leftovers: candle ends, old cloth and worn-out writing brushes, bundles and bundles of brushes, more than anything else. The Royal Uncle's halberdiers guard the bend, saying palace staff may not sell privately. 'Whoever buys is a thief.' The old servant says nothing, smoothing the hairs of the bald brushes one by one.
column3: 王宫下游的河湾里，一个白头发的老仆在岸边摆了个摊，卖宫里用剩的东西：蜡烛头、旧布、写秃了的毛笔，毛笔一捆捆码着，比别的东西都多。国舅府的戟士守着河湾，说宫里的人不许私卖东西，「谁买，就当谁偷」。老仆不吭声，一支支给秃笔理毛。

column2: The halberdiers flee, and the old servant lets you take your pick from the stall. Once a month he polishes the King's crown. On its right side, he says, a faint groove has been worn into the gold, 'as if some slim thing rubbed there every day'. The bald brushes are all ones the King has worn out. 'Over three hundred a year. He gets through more brushes than the palace burns candles.'
column3: 戟士们跑了，老仆把摊上的东西随便你们挑。他每月替王擦一回冠。他说那顶珠旒冠的右边，金子上磨出了一道浅浅的槽，「像天天有一样细东西夹在那儿蹭的」。秃笔都是王用坏的，「一年三百多支，比宫里点的蜡烛还费」。

column2: The Gold Mask Camp
column3: 金面别营

column2: Under an old stretch of wall outside the city stands a camp with a row of golden masks hung over its gate; the crossbowmen inside all wear gold masks that dazzle in the sun. This is the band of the Thousand Buddha Caves' Gold Masks that wouldn't disband. After the Lord of the Caves gave up his mask, they came west and joined the Royal Uncle. Their leader is the one with the red stone between his brows.
column3: 城墙外的一段旧城根下扎着一座营，营门上挂着一排金面具，营里的弩手都戴着金面，在太阳下晃得人睁不开眼。这是千佛洞的金面卫里不肯散伙的一支，洞主交了金面以后，他们一路往西，投了国舅。领头的就是眉心嵌红石的那个。

column2: The Gold Masks are beaten, and one by one they take off their masks and throw them down in a clanking heap. These were made, says their leader, of the gold scraped long ago from the three hundred faces in the cave. 'When we scraped it I was nineteen. Ten years I've worn it and never had a good night's sleep.' He bags up the masks and hands them to you. 'Take them back. Give them to that old painter.'
column3: 金面卫败了，一个个把面具摘下来，扔在地上，叮叮当当一大堆。领头的说这些金子，是当年从窟里那三百张脸上刮下来的，「刮的时候我十九岁，戴了十年，没睡过一个好觉」。他把面具收进一只口袋交给你们：「带回去，还给那个画画的老头。」

column2: The Royal Uncle's Manor
column3: 国舅府

column2: The Royal Uncle's manor stands on the waste outside the city, high walls and deep courtyards, rows of water jars buried in the yards, more than in any water store. His finest forces are all here: halberdiers at the gates, archers on the walls, cavalry circling the compound. The Royal Uncle stands beside a great jar, fifty or so, his hair entirely white, and looks at you. 'You think I'm a villain. I just never want to see this city let one more person die of thirst.'
column3: 国舅府在城外的荒原上，高墙深院，院里一排排埋着水缸，比别处的水仓还多。府里最精的人马都在这里了：戟士守门，弓手上墙，铁骑绕着院子跑。国舅站在一口大缸边上，五十来岁，头发全白，看着你们：「你们以为我是坏人。我只是不想再看见这城渴死一个人。」

column2: The Royal Uncle, beaten, sits on the rim of a jar and talks for a long time. Eleven years ago the river changed course, the lake went south, this side of the city went dry, and his sister the old Queen died in the first year of the drought, begging for water to the end. Ever since he's hoarded water, bought up deeds, blocked roads. 'Open the road and caravans come and go, and the water goes with them.' He hates that King. 'He's not of the royal blood. He came in the drought, and he's the one who brought the water back. I hoarded water eleven years; he dug a channel in three. I hate him because I couldn't do it.' He hands you the keys to his water stores. 'Go to the palace. He's waiting for you to settle the accounts.'
column3: 国舅败了，坐在缸边上，说了很久。十一年前河改了道，湖往南走，城这边旱了，他的姐姐老王后死在旱的头一年，到死嘴里都在要水。从那以后他囤水、收契、拦路，「路一开，商队来来去去，水就跟着走了」。他恨那个王：「他不是王族，来的那年正旱，是他带人把水引了回来。我囤了十一年的水，他挖了三年渠。我恨他，是因为我没做到。」他把府里水仓的钥匙交给你们：「去宫里吧，他在等你们对账。」

column2: The Bead-Crown Hall
column3: 珠旒殿

column2: The main hall stands over the river, the King's guard drawn up below its steps in three ranks, halberdiers, archers and cavalry, every man ramrod straight. The figure on the throne wears a crown hung with strings of beads that hide his face. You lay before the steps what you've brought along the road: the slip of paper reading 'Well 300', the cart-loan contract, the receipt for two hundred and ninety-nine jars, the halyard of the twelfth pole, the letter signed 'Lu'. The King looks at each in turn, then lifts his hands and takes off the crown. Beneath it, tucked behind his right ear, is a brush. Thin face, narrowed eyes, eyes that seem to be reckoning you up: the clerk at the city gate, the face on Wu Banbi's wall. 'Ten years ago,' he says, 'I got one sum in the caravan's accounts wrong.' He takes the brush from behind his ear. 'A wrong account has to be gone over again. The guard has held this city six years. If you can beat them, the city's gate can be handed to you.'
column3: 正殿临着河，王城禁军三路列在阶下：戟士、弓手、铁骑，一个个站得笔直。殿上的人戴着珠旒冠，珠子一串串垂下来，看不清脸。你们把一路带来的东西摆在阶前：「第三百井」的纸条、借车契、二百九十九坛的收条、第十二根杆子的旗绳、陆字的信。王一样一样看完，抬手摘下了王冠。冠底下，右耳后夹着一支笔。瘦脸，眯眼，眼睛像在算你：是城门口的录事，是吴半壁墙上的那张脸。「十年前，」他说，「我把商队的账算错了一笔。」他把笔从耳后取下来：「账错了，要重对。禁军守了这城六年，你们打得过他们，这城的门才能交给你们。」

column2: The guard falls back, and he opens an old ledger. That year he reckoned the water by an old map, which showed a lake west of the city, and he counted one cartload of water as waiting in that lake. But in the Bingwu year the river changed course and the lake moved, and that cartload was gone. The old King lent his own water cart; he promised a channel within a year to repay it, and it took three. The year it was finished the old King died, the Royal Uncle meant to sell the water, and the people begged him to wear the crown. In the fourth spring he sent the two hundred and ninety-nine ahead with the goods to keep the three roads' appointment, and stayed behind himself as the 'one man still owing'. Six years, and no word back. He opens the letter signed Lu, reads it and smiles. 'The iron box is still safe.' On the last page of the ledger he writes 'Silk Road: accounts settled' and hands the book to you. 'Shen Du is waiting for someone who can keep accounts. Tell her for me: I'm late.'
column3: 禁军退了，他翻开一本旧账：当年照旧图算水，图上城西有湖，他把一车水记在了湖里。可丙午年河改道，湖走了，那一车水不在了。老王借出自己的水车，他许下一年挖渠抵账，挖了三年。渠成那年老王死了，国舅要卖水，城里人求他戴冠。第四年开春，他让二百九十九人带着货先走，去赴三路的约，自己留下，抵那「尚欠一人」。六年，没有回信。他拆开陆字的信，看完笑了：「铁匣还在。」最后一页账，他写下「丝路，对毕」，把账本交给你们：「沈渡在等会算账的人。替我告诉她，我晚到了。」

column2: The Tea-Horse Road
column3: 茶马古道

column2: The Fog Posts
column3: 雾驿

column2: Tea Gate of Yazhou
column3: 雅州茶关

column2: The tax clerk checks your goods and stamps the back of your pass twice. Why twice, you ask. "One for you," he says, "and one for the mule train I never finished stamping, ten years ago." He presses a mouldy brick of tea into your hand, Thousand Li pressed into it. "They said they would be back when the tea ran out.
column3: 茶关的税吏验完货，在通关文书背面盖了两个印。你问为什么是两个，他说：「一个给你们，一个给十年前没盖完的那支马帮。」他把一块发霉的茶砖塞进你手里，砖上压着「千里号」三个字。「他们走的时候说，茶砖吃完就回来。」

column2: Fogmouth Gate
column3: 雾口关

column2: Two ranges close in here to make a mouth, and the valley inside is brimming with fog, white as a bowl of rice gruel nobody has stirred. Deserters have strung a rope across the road hung all over with brass bells, and whoever rings one pays a 'fog-waking fee'. Their lead spearman says it with a straight face: fog can be woken. Mountain crossbowmen squat on both slopes, waiting for the next bell.
column3: 南北两道山在这里收拢成一个口子，口子里的河谷灌满了雾，白得像一碗没搅开的米汤。一伙流兵在路上横拉了一根麻绳，绳上挂满铜铃，谁碰响了铃，谁就得交一份「惊雾钱」。领头的流兵枪手说得一本正经：雾是会被吵醒的。山弩手蹲在两边的坡上，等着下一个碰铃的人。

column2: The rope is cut, the bells scatter, and the fog stays white and fast asleep. On the boundary post a weathered character 'Qian' is carved, and under it someone has added a line with a knife: 'Count no heads in the fog. Count, and one is missing.' You call the roll of your own people. Nobody missing. Only then do you walk in.
column3: 麻绳割断，铜铃落了一地，雾还是那么白，没醒。界桩上刻着一个风化了的「千」字，底下有人用刀补了一行小字：「雾里莫数人，数了少一个。」你们把队伍点了一遍，一个不少，这才走进雾里。

column2: Kindling Slope
column3: 拾柴坡

column2: A line of children comes down the slope under bundles of firewood taller than they are, headed for the lodge, one copper a bundle. At the top of the slope a few garrison bullies take the bundles off them one by one, a 'firewood tax for the crown', then sell them to the lodge for five coppers each. The smallest child won't let go. She sits in the dirt hugging her bundle and crying: 'Amo's fire is going out, it's going out.'
column3: 一群孩子背着比人还高的柴捆往坡下走，柴是送去锅庄的，一捆换一个铜板。坡口蹲着几个兵痞，把柴捆一捆捆截下来，说是「替官家收柴税」，转手又卖给锅庄，一捆要五个铜板。最小的孩子不肯撒手，抱着柴捆坐在地上哭，一边哭一边念叨：「阿嫫的火要灭了，要灭了。」

column2: The bullies hand the bundles back, and the children make them carry them a stretch too. Over the slope, they tell you, is a lodge with a hearth that hasn't gone out in ten years. The keeper, Amo Yangjin, buys exactly one bundle a day, and this year she can barely pay for that. She says the fire is kept for some people who haven't come back yet.
column3: 兵痞们把柴捆还了回来，还被孩子们逼着背了一程。孩子们说，坡那头的锅庄有一塘火，十年没熄过，掌柜央金阿嫫每天收一捆柴，不多不少，可今年连收柴的钱都快付不起了。她说那塘火是给一伙还没回来的人留的。

column2: Tea Pass Toll
column3: 茶关税卡

column2: The tea pass toll is one wooden hut and one barrier pole. The deserters have tied Clerk Pu to his own pole. Two seal cords hang from his belt: one holds a brass seal, the other holds nothing. The spearmen want him to stamp a stack of blank sheets so they can sell them as passes, and Pu swears at every sheet, faster than he stamps. 'This is the Into-the-Fog seal! You aren't even going in, what do you want it for?'
column3: 茶关的税卡只有一间木屋、一根栏杆。税吏老蒲被流兵绑在自己的栏杆上，腰里挂着两根印绶：一根拴着铜印，一根空着。流兵枪手们要他给一叠白纸挨张盖印，好拿去卖路引，老蒲盖一张骂一句，骂得比盖得快：「这是入雾的印！你们又不进雾，盖它做什么！」

column2: Rubbing his wrists, Pu stamps your manifest squarely: Into the Fog. When you ask about the empty cord he touches it. 'The Out-of-the-Fog seal. Ten years ago I lent it to a man who took it in with him. Said he'd stamp his people out at the far end and send it back.' He glares at the fog. 'It still hasn't come back.'
column3: 老蒲揉着手腕，给你们的货单端端正正盖了一个「入雾」。问起那根空着的印绶，他摸了摸，说：「出雾印。十年前借给一个人带进雾里，说到了那头替我盖完就捎回来。」他瞪着雾，「到今天也没捎回来。」

column2: Ledger Room
column3: 税簿房

column2: Behind the toll is Pu's ledger room, ten years of books stacked waist high. Some garrison bullies have moved in and use the ledgers to prop table legs, shake dice, and wipe their boots. Pu charges in to save them and gets kicked straight back out, clutching the one book he grabbed: the Dingwei year. He squats in the doorway with it and won't let anyone near. 'That year, a man paid tax here for three hundred people.'
column3: 税卡后面是老蒲的税簿房，十年的簿子码得齐腰高。几个兵痞占了屋子，拿簿子垫桌腿、当骰盅，撕下来擦鞋。老蒲冲进去抢救，被一脚踹了出来，怀里只抢到一本，是丁未年的。他抱着簿子蹲在门口，谁也不许碰：「那一年，有人在这儿交了三百个人的税。」

column2: The bullies are thrown out. The Dingwei page reads: 'Qianli mule train through the pass. Tax paid in full for three hundred. Paid on one road, walking three.' Below it, a thumbprint pressed hard. That was the escort chief Lu Jiu, Pu says. 'He said the three roads were one family and the account should sit in one place. He's the one who borrowed my Out seal, too.'
column3: 兵痞被赶了出去。丁未年那一页写着：「千里号马帮过关，税照三百人缴讫，一路交，三路走。」下面是一枚指印，按得很重。老蒲说那是镖头陆九：「他说三条路是一家，账记在一处。我的出雾印，也是他借走的。」

column2: Welcome Flats
column3: 迎官坝

column2: The village on the flats spots the red seal on your manifest from a long way off and decides you are an imperial inspector travelling in disguise. Out come gongs, drums and ten tables of wine; the elders kneel in a row and petitions pile up. Only the headman's retainers panic and come at you with staves to 'escort' you off the flats: for ten years the headman has collected the crown's grain and sent not one grain of it on.
column3: 坝子上的寨子远远看见你们货单上那方红印，以为来了微服查账的钦差，敲锣打鼓摆出十桌酒，寨老跪了一排，状纸递上来一大摞。只有里长的家丁慌了，拎着刀棍要把你们「请」出坝子：里长这十年替官家收的粮，一粒也没交上去。

column2: The retainers scatter and the headman flees that night with his books. You tell the elders you are not inspectors; they don't believe a word and stuff the petitions into your cart anyway. The one at the bottom is written most carefully: 'Dingwei year. The mule train owes my family one meal. The escort chief said he'd pay on the way back. Not paid yet.' Beside it, his mark: a little iron box.
column3: 家丁被打散，里长连夜卷着账本跑了。你们说自己不是钦差，寨老们不信，硬把状纸塞进车里。最底下一张写得最认真：「丁未年，马帮欠我家一顿饭钱，镖头说回来时还，至今未还。」旁边画着一个押：一只铁匣子。

column2: Trivet Camp
column3: 三脚灶

column2: Deserters have camped in the open with a big pot over the fire, and under the pot stands a black iron trivet older than the pot. The children say it belongs to the lodge hearth; the deserters carried it off two days ago, and now the lodge's tea kettle sits on stones. The spearmen guard their pot, waiting for the dog meat to go tender, and rap anyone who comes close with a spear shaft.
column3: 一伙流兵在野地里扎了营，营中间架着一口大锅，锅底下垫着一只黑铁三脚，比锅还老。孩子们说这三脚是锅庄火塘上的，前天被流兵扛走了，没了它，锅庄的茶锅只能拿石头垫着。流兵枪手们守着锅，正等狗肉炖烂，谁靠近就拿枪杆子敲谁。

column2: Pot, broth and dog meat go over in the dirt, and you carry the trivet back. One leg bears a line of carving: 'From the Qianli mule train to the lodge. While the fire burns, we will return.' The characters wobble, as if a muleteer had chipped them out one tap at a time with a horseshoe nail.
column3: 狗肉连锅带汤泼在地上，三脚被你们扛了回来。三脚的一条腿上刻着一行字：「千里号马帮赠锅庄，火不熄，人必归。」字刻得歪歪扭扭，像是赶马人用马掌钉一下一下凿出来的。

column2: Sneer Gate
column3: 冷眼卡

column2: Another checkpoint. A few bullies in old army tunics call themselves tax men, glance at your carts and snort: 'Shabby lot like you, walking the tea road?' They tip your goods out to 'inspect' them, keeping a piece of everything they inspect, then stamp your manifest again with a freshly carved Into-the-Fog seal. Pu's stamp doesn't count, they say. Pay again.
column3: 路上又是一道卡子，几个穿旧号衣的兵痞自称税丁，瞟了一眼你们的车，嗤笑一声：「就这寒酸样，也配走茶路？」把货掀了一地，说要「验货」，验一样扣一样，还拿一方新刻的「入雾」印在你们货单上又盖了一遍，说老蒲那个不算数，得再交一份。

column2: The 'tax men' kneel in the mud and hand back every confiscated item, then load your carts for you and tie the ropes tighter than you ever do. Their new seal is soapstone, still dusty from the knife. Their leader confesses meekly: the carver lives on a raft by the river, three taels of silver a seal.
column3: 「税丁」们跪在泥里，把扣下的货一件件捧回来，又帮着装车，捆得比你们自己捆的还结实。那方新印是皂石刻的，印面还沾着石粉。领头的老老实实交代：刻章的在河边的筏子上，一方印卖三两银子。

column2: Ember Carrier
column3: 送火翁

column2: An old man sits by the road with clay jars on a carrying pole, each holding live coals from the lodge hearth. When a village holds a wedding or raises a roof beam, they send for him to bring a jar of 'lodge fire', for luck that never goes out. Some bullies stop him and smash the jars one after another; pay the fire fee, they say, or stay. He clutches the last jar to his chest, his coat smoking, and won't let go.
column3: 路边坐着一位挑着陶罐的老人，罐里是锅庄火塘的炭火。寨里娶亲、新屋上梁，都要请他送一罐「锅庄火」去，图个不熄。几个兵痞拦住他，把罐子一个个敲碎，说要收「火钱」才许他走。最后一罐被他护在怀里，烫得衣襟冒烟，他也不撒手。

column2: The bullies run and the last jar is saved. The fire, the old man says, was struck ten years ago with a flint by a mule-train boss, who said the fog was dark and he wanted to see a glow from far off on the way home. 'Ten years I've carried fire,' the old man says, 'and never once got to carry it to him.'
column3: 兵痞们跑了，最后一罐火保住了。老人说，这塘火是十年前一个马锅头拿火镰打着的，那人说雾里黑，回来的时候要远远看得见一点亮。「我送火送了十年，」老人说，「就是没等到给他送一回。」

column2: Maize Yard
column3: 苞谷场

column2: Beside the old road lies a drying yard, its bamboo mats heaped with golden maize, but the granary beside it wears three padlocks. Deserters hold the yard: by day the villagers turn the grain for them, by night it goes into the locked store. A tea porter passing by asks for a bowl of maize rice; a spear shaft flips his basket and tea bricks roll everywhere.
column3: 古道边一片晒场，竹席上铺满金黄的苞谷，场边的谷仓却上了三把锁。一伙流兵占了晒场，白天逼寨民替他们翻晒，晚上把粮扛进仓里。背茶的背夫路过，想讨一碗苞谷饭，被流兵用枪杆子挑翻了背篓，茶砖滚了一地。

column2: Three locks smashed, the grain goes back to the village, and children chase sparrows across the yard again. Over their rice the porters tell you that ten years ago escort chief Lu bought every passing porter a bowl right here. 'I've borrowed a seal from old Pu,' he said, 'and it's a long walk through the fog. Remember this road for me.'
column3: 三把锁砸开，粮食还给了寨民，晒场上又有孩子追着麻雀跑。背夫们一边吃饭一边说，十年前陆镖头在这里请过路的背夫每人吃了一碗饭，说：「我借了老蒲一方印，进雾要走很久，你们替我记着这条路。」

column2: From the granary: forty loads of maize, twenty strips of cured pork, a jar of maize liquor, and thirty tea bricks the deserters took off the porters, still in their wrappings, not one opened.
column3: 仓里抄出苞谷四十担、腊肉二十条、一坛苞谷酒，还有流兵从背夫身上抢来的三十块茶砖，原样包着，一块没拆。

column2: Every time you pass, the villagers at the yard press a bag of popped maize on you. Something to chew in the fog, they say, and you won't be afraid.
column3: 每次路过，晒场的寨民都塞给你们一袋炒苞谷花，说走雾路嘴里嚼着点东西，就不怕了。

column2: Carver's Raft
column3: 刻印筏

column2: A bamboo raft is moored in the river bend with a thatched shelter on it, and from inside comes the tink-tink of a chisel on stone. Deserters guard the raft and keep an old carver at it day and night cutting fake seals: Into the Fog, Let Pass, Tax Exempt, anything. His eyes are nearly gone. Every seal he spoils, they dunk him in the river.
column3: 河湾里拴着一只竹筏，筏上搭着个草棚，棚里传出叮叮的凿石声。几个流兵守着筏子，逼一个老刻工没日没夜地刻假印：入雾、放行、免税，什么都刻。老刻工的眼睛已经快看不清了，刻坏一方，就被往河里按一回。

column2: The deserters go into the river and crawl out full of it and run. Wiping his eyes, the old carver says the real Out seal was his master's work, its knob a deer looking back over its shoulder. 'Looking back, hoping people come home out of the fog. That deer's neck... I've tried all my life and never got it right.'
column3: 流兵被扔进河里，喝饱了水才爬上岸跑掉。老刻工擦着眼睛说，真的出雾印是他师父刻的，印钮是一只回头的鹿：「回头，是盼着人从雾里回来。那只鹿的脖子，我刻了一辈子也刻不出来。」

column2: Tea Porters' Rest
column3: 背茶客

column2: A crew of porters rests by the road, leaning on their T-shaped staffs, tea bricks stacked in their baskets higher than their heads. Their headman, old Wang, used to run a little trade, tea for salt, but the deserters have pressed his porters into hauling their loot for nothing. Wang shakes his head at you. 'Trade? I can't even call my own back my own.'
column3: 一帮背夫靠着丁字拐歇在路边，背篓里的茶砖垒得比人头还高。他们的头人老汪本来做着茶砖换盐巴的小买卖，可流兵把背夫们拉了差，替他们背抢来的东西，背一趟不给一文钱。老汪冲你们直摇头：「买卖？我连自己的脊梁都做不了主。」

column2: The press-gang is chased off, the porters stamp their staffs on the ground and shout the stall open. Wang trades you tea bricks and gives full weight. A few days ago, he says, one of his porters got lost in the fog. At night you can still hear him singing at the foot of the mountains, a tune the mule train taught them ten years ago.
column3: 拉差的流兵被赶跑，背夫们把拐子往地上一顿，齐声吆喝着开了张。老汪拿茶砖跟你们换东西，秤给得很足。他说前些天有个背夫在雾里走丢了，夜里还能听见他在山脚唱歌，唱的是十年前马帮教的调子。

column2: Pass Mill
column3: 路引坊

column2: Deep in the woods is a camp bigger than any deserter band on the road so far. A dozen tables stand in rows; deserters queue to stamp fake seals onto blank paper, dry it, and bundle it to sell to travellers too scared to enter the fog. Crossbowmen keep watch from the trees, and a sign over the gate says 'Official'. Every pass is copied from the same old sheet, nailed to the post in the middle of the camp.
column3: 林子深处有一座大营，比路上见过的哪伙流兵都大。营里支着十几张案子，流兵们排着队往白纸上盖假印，晒干了一捆捆扎好，拿去卖给不敢进雾的过客。山弩手在树上放哨，营门口还挂着「官办」两个字。每张路引都照着同一张旧纸临摹，那张旧纸被钉在营中间的柱子上。

column2: The camp breaks; the fake passes go up in one bonfire. The old sheet on the post is a real pass from ten years ago: 'Qianli mule train. Into the Fog.' Pu's seal, Lu Jiu's thumbprint beside it, and only the 'Out' box left blank. You peel it off carefully and keep it for Pu.
column3: 大营散了，假路引堆成小山，一把火烧了。柱子上那张旧纸是十年前的真路引：「千里号马帮，入雾」，印是老蒲的，旁边按着陆九的指印，只有「出雾」那一栏是空的。你们小心地把它揭下来，替老蒲收着。

column2: Red Clay Kiln
column3: 红泥窑

column2: On the slope at the forest's edge the earth is red, red as rusted iron. A woman who runs a kiln mixes seal paste from it, and every seal for miles around uses her paste. Now deserters surround her kiln and order her to make fake paste so their fake passes will look real. She mixes a pot and flings it on the ground. 'It won't come out! Look for yourselves. That's red-earth red, not cinnabar red.'
column3: 林边的坡上土是红的，红得像生了锈的铁。一个烧窑的妇人用这红土调印泥，四乡八寨的印都用她的泥。如今流兵把她的窑围了，逼她拿红土调假印泥，好让假路引看着像真的。她调了一锅，往地上一泼：「调不出来！你们自己看，这是红土的红，不是朱砂的红。」

column2: Once they've gone she explains. Red earth is rock that has rotted for ages and ages where it's hot and wet; the rain washes everything else away and what's left is the iron, rusted, so it's red. A brownish red, and a seal in it looks fake at a glance. And she remembers: ten years ago an escort chief bought a box of her true paste, 'enough for three hundred stamps', he said.
column3: 流兵走了，妇人才跟你们细说：红土是石头在又湿又热的地方烂了很多很多年，别的都叫雨水淋走了，剩下的铁锈了，所以红；红得发褐，盖出来一眼就假。她还记得，十年前有个镖头在她这儿买过一盒真印泥，说要「够盖三百下」。

column2: Butter Churn
column3: 酥油坊

column2: At the far end of the open ground is a butter house, its churns taller than a man, the churners plunging the staves down and down. Deserters have taken it over and grab every pat of butter for lamps and gun grease, leaving none for the lodge. No butter in the butter tea, their leader says, and the guests drift away, and nobody's left to mind that fire.
column3: 野地尽头一间酥油坊，木桶比人还高，打酥油的汉子们站在桶边一下一下地捣。流兵占了坊子，把打好的酥油全抢去点灯、擦枪，一块都不给锅庄留。领头的说了，锅庄的酥油茶没了油，客人自然就散了，那塘火也就没人守了。

column2: The deserters are run off and the butter is wrapped and sent to the lodge again. Every day for ten years, the master churner says, the lodge has ordered one extra pound. 'Amo Yangjin says the extra bowl of tea is kept for someone. And every morning the bowl is empty, and nobody has ever seen who drinks it.'
column3: 流兵被撵走，酥油又一块块包好往锅庄送。坊主说，锅庄每天都多要一斤酥油，十年没断过：「央金阿嫫说，多的那一碗茶是给一个人留的。可是每天早上碗都是空的，也没人看见是谁喝的。」

column2: Fog Boundary Stone
column3: 界雾碑

column2: A boundary stone stands on the plain: sunshine on this side, fog on that, as if cut with a knife. Its face is covered in chalk strokes, one for every traveller, centuries of them. Deserters have stopped a crowd of travellers holding fake passes: those won't get you through, buy a 'real' one. Someone shoves out of the crowd with an empty seal cord at his belt. It's Pu.
column3: 平野上立着一块界碑，碑这边是太阳，碑那边是雾，像一刀切出来的。碑上划满了白道，过一个人划一道，划了几百年。一群拿着假路引的过客被流兵挡在碑前，流兵说假路引过不了雾，得再买一张「真的」。人群里挤出一个人来，腰上一根空印绶，正是老蒲。

column2: The deserters fall back, and the travellers cross with real passes you helped check. Pu says he's made up his mind: until his Out seal comes back, his books can never be closed. 'Three hundred people's tax, gone into the fog and never stamped out. What kind of account is that?' He shoulders his bundle and slips into the fog a step ahead of you. He'll wait for you further on.
column3: 流兵退了，过客们拿着你们帮着验过的真路引过了碑。老蒲说他想通了：出雾印不回来，他的簿子就一辈子合不上。「三百个人的税，进了雾，没出来，我这账算什么？」他背起包袱，先你们一步钻进了雾里，说在前头等你们。

column2: Fog-Raid Moor
column3: 雾劫原

column2: Whenever fog rises on this moor, a troop of native soldiers comes out of it with bamboo spears and crossbows, takes whatever goods they find, and melts back in. Nobody knows where their stockade is. The odd thing is that they never touch anyone carrying firewood or butter to the lodge. When they see the lodge's banner they even stop and salute.
column3: 这片野地一起雾，就有一队土兵从雾里钻出来，扛着竹枪，背着弩，见货就抢，抢完又退回雾里，没人知道他们的寨子在哪儿。奇怪的是，他们从不碰往锅庄送柴、送酥油的人，远远看见锅庄的旗子，还要停下来行个礼。

column2: This time the soldiers are beaten back and flee into the fog, dropping crossbows. But as soon as the fog rises again they'll be back, and here the fog always rises again. A prisoner says his stockade has an old pact with the lodge. Ten years ago a mule-train boss drank blood wine with them: 'Nobody touches the lodge fire.'
column3: 这一回的土兵被打退了，丢下几张弩逃回雾里。可只要雾再起，他们就会再来，而这里的雾，什么时候都会再起。俘虏说，他们寨子跟锅庄有个老约定，十年前一个马锅头跟他们喝过血酒：「锅庄的火，谁也不许碰。」

column2: Trough Ridge
column3: 抢槽岭

column2: At the foot of the mountains a band of caravan swordsmen has blocked the road to the lodge. They want the lodge's spot for their own caravan halt.
