Their boss is past fifty with a voice louder than a mule's. 'The fire's nearly out, why guard it? Taking it over is doing her a favour!' His men have tethered mules along the whole roadside and nobody can pass.
column3: 山脚下一伙马帮刀客截住了去锅庄的路，他们想把锅庄那块地方占下来，改成自家马帮的歇脚处。领头的马锅头年过五十，嗓门比骡子还大：「火都快灭了，还守它做什么？我们占了，是帮她！」他手下的刀客把骡子拴满了路边，谁都过不去。

column2: The swordsmen sheathe their blades and lead the mules aside. The old boss takes a pull of liquor. When he was young, he says, he guided the Qianli train as far as the lodge and no further. 'That night they danced round the hearth half the night and went into the fog before dawn. Before they left, the chief set a bowl of tea by the fire and said nobody was to drink it.'
column3: 刀客们收了刀，骡子牵到一边。老马锅头喝了口酒，说他年轻时给千里号当过向导，送到锅庄就止步了：「那一夜他们围着火塘跳了半宿，天不亮就进了雾。走之前，镖头往火边摆了一碗茶，说谁也不许喝。」

column2: Charcoal Hoard
column3: 炭王窖

column2: At the end of the open ground is the chieftain's charcoal store, three rammed-earth walls around its mouth, guarded by native soldiers in rattan armour with poisoned bolts on their crossbows. Inside are ten years of hard charcoal, hoarded for some bitter winter when it will fetch a fortune. The lodge is nearly out of wood; Amo Yangjin has come begging three times and not got a single lump.
column3: 野地的尽头有一处土司家的炭窖，窖口夯着三道土墙，守窖的土兵一身藤甲，弩上的箭都淬过药。窖里囤着十年的硬炭，土司打算等哪年冬天大冷了再一口气卖出去，卖个天价。锅庄的柴快断了，央金阿嫫来求过三回，一块炭也没讨着。

column2: The rattan-armoured guards are driven off and the store thrown open; basket after basket of charcoal goes to the lodge, enough for several winters. At the very bottom, though, is a stack of firewood, and on the rope that binds it a cloth tag: 'Left by the Qianli train, for the lodge to draw on.' The chieftain's people had buried it under everything else, and left it there ten years.
column3: 藤甲土兵被打退，炭窖敞开了，一筐筐硬炭往锅庄送，够那塘火烧好几个冬天。窖底最深处却堆着一垛柴，捆柴的绳子上系着布条，写着「千里号寄存，锅庄取用」。土司家把它压在最底下，一压就是十年。

column2: Deer Track Wood
column3: 鹿径林

column2: A path trodden by deer runs through these woods; hunters say if you follow it you'll find your way out however thick the fog. On the bark of an old fir is a red square seal, 'Out of the Fog', stretched out of shape as the tree has grown. Some mountain crossbowmen are using the fir for a target, betting on who can put a bolt through the character 'Out'.
column3: 林子里有一条鹿踩出来的小径，猎户说顺着它走，雾再大也能摸出林子。一棵老杉树的树皮上有个红印，印文是「出雾」，四四方方，已经被树皮撑得变了形。几个山弩手把这棵树当了靶子，正比谁能把箭射进那个「出」字里。

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off and the seal is saved. Ten years ago, the old hunter says, an escort chief carrying a seal box asked him the way out of the woods. Told to follow the deer track, he was so pleased he stamped the tree: 'This one's out of the fog first.' Pu hears and hurries over, touches the print, and says yes, it's real, the looking-back deer. His eyes go red as he says it.
column3: 山弩手被赶走，树上的印保住了。老猎户说十年前有个镖头背着印匣问他出林的路，听说顺着鹿径就能出去，一高兴，在树上盖了一下：「这棵树先出雾了。」老蒲闻讯赶来，摸着那个印，说是真的，是鹿回头的那一方，说着说着眼圈红了。

column2: Looking-Back Deer Rock
column3: 鹿回头

column2: Out on the open ground is a boulder that from a distance looks like a deer glancing back. The old carver says his master modelled the seal knob on it. Now some bullies have set up a stall at its foot selling 'out-of-the-fog charms', a deer's head drawn on yellow paper: stick it on your back and you'll find your way out. Plenty buy, because the bullies say a whole company went into the fog from beside this rock ten years ago.
column3: 野地里一块大石，远看像一只回头张望的鹿，老刻工说他师父当年就是照着这块石头刻的印钮。如今几个兵痞在石头底下支了摊子，卖「出雾符」：一张黄纸画个鹿头，说贴在背上就走得出雾。买的人还不少，因为他们说，十年前有一伙人就是从这块石头边上进的雾。

column2: The charm stall is overturned and the money returned. And at the foot of the rock someone really did cut an arrow with a knife, pointing east, with two words beside it: 'Out. Fog.' A trace of red is still packed in the groove, paste from the red clay kiln, not quite faded after ten years.
column3: 兵痞的符摊被掀了，钱退给了过客。鹿回头的石脚下，确实有人用刀刻了一道箭头，指向东，旁边两个字：「出雾」。刻痕里还嵌着一点红，是红泥窑的印泥，十年了也没褪尽。

column2: The Unquenched Hearth
column3: 不熄锅庄

column2: Push open the lodge door and the room is full of butter tea and woodsmoke, and the fire in the middle of the hearth is down to a flame one finger high. The keeper, Amo Yangjin, sits by it and won't add her last bundle yet; she's saving it for nightfall. Bullies block the door demanding a 'fire fee', or they'll throw water on it. 'Ten years it's burned and nobody's come back. What's the point?'
column3: 锅庄的门一推开，满屋子是酥油茶的香气和柴烟，火塘正中的火只剩一指高的苗。掌柜央金阿嫫守着火，不肯添最后一捆柴，她要留到天黑再添。一伙兵痞堵在门口，要她交「火钱」，不交就拿水泼了这火：「烧了十年，谁也没回来，还烧什么？」

column2: The bullies are thrown out the door. Yangjin feeds in the last bundle and the flame leaps high. Ten years ago, she tells you, the Qianli people spent a night here, and as he left, escort chief Lu Jiu said: 'Keep the fire lit and we'll find our way back.' The bowl by the hearth is still there. Filled every night, empty every morning.
column3: 兵痞们被扔出门外，央金把最后一捆柴添了进去，火苗一下子窜起老高。她告诉你们，十年前千里号的人在这里歇了一夜，镖头陆九临走时说：「火不灭，人就回得来。」火塘边那只碗还摆着，每晚倒满，每早都是空的。

column2: Singing Slope
column3: 唱山腔

column2: A mountain song drifts out of the fog at the foot of the slope, long and drawn out: 'Brother drives his mules over the fog mountain...' A line, then a pause, as though waiting for someone to answer. A few deserters creep toward it with their spears. They've heard the singer is a lost porter with a basket of good tea on his back, and they mean to catch both.
column3: 山脚的雾里飘来一阵山歌，调子拖得很长：「哥哥赶马过雾山哟……」唱一句停一会儿，像在等人接。几个流兵端着枪顺着歌声摸过去，他们听说唱歌的是个走丢的背夫，背上有一篓好茶，要把人和茶一起抓来。

column2: You head the deserters off, but the song has drifted further away. A porter's T-staff lies by the road with 'Shiwa' carved in its crosspiece. Old Wang of the tea porters knows it: his youngest, sixteen, with the clearest voice of them all. The mule train taught the porters that tune ten years ago.
column3: 流兵被你们截住，歌声却又飘远了。路边扔着一根背夫的丁字拐，拐子头上刻着「石娃」两个字。背茶客的老汪认得：是他手下最小的背夫，十六岁，嗓子最亮，那支调子是十年前马帮教给背夫们的。

column2: Notch Cliff
column3: 刻痕崖

column2: At the foot of the mountains is a rock face where porters cut one notch for every trip; some have cut hundreds, and the cliff looks like an old comb. Mountain crossbowmen below are shooting at the notches, whoever hits the longest column wins. Near the top, though, one line is different, cut deep and neat: 'Qianli mule train. One notch going, one more coming back.' Under it, a single notch.
column3: 山脚一面石崖，背夫们每走一趟就在崖上刻一道，有的人刻了几百道，崖面像一把老梳子。崖下几个山弩手拿刻痕当靶子，谁射中最长的那一列谁赢。崖顶却有一行字跟别的不一样，刻得又深又整齐：「千里号马帮，去刻一道，回添一道。」下面只有一道。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off. The porters say that one notch was cut ten years ago, waiting for someone to come back and add the second, and no one ever has. As you leave, an old porter goes up on tiptoe and traces the air beside it, but doesn't cut. 'They'll have to come back and do it themselves.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走了。背夫们说那一道是十年前刻的，等着有人回来添第二道，一直没人添。你们临走时，有个老背夫踮着脚，在那一道旁边虚虚比划了一下，终究没刻：「得他们自己回来刻。」

column2: Old Forest Toll
column3: 林中旧卡

column2: Deep in the woods is a half-collapsed old toll booth, used by the clerk before Pu and abandoned when the road moved. Mountain crossbowmen live in it and burn its old ledgers for heat. Pu got here first and is wrestling them for the books, an arrow through his hat, still shouting: 'Burn anything you like, not the ledgers!'
column3: 林子深处有一间塌了半边的旧税亭，是上一任税吏用过的，后来商路改道就荒了。几个山弩手住在里面，拿亭子里的旧簿子生火。老蒲早到了一步，正跟他们抢簿子，帽子上挨了一箭还在骂：「烧什么都行，别烧簿子！」

column2: The crossbowmen run. Pu digs out a ledger from the last dynasty; on its flyleaf is an old rule: 'Entry counted by heads, exit counted by seals. Where heads and seals disagree, the seal decides.' Pu stares at it a long while. 'Meaning: nobody without an Out stamp counts as out.' He tucks the book into his coat and heads east again.
column3: 山弩手跑了。老蒲翻出一本前朝的旧簿，扉页上写着一条老规矩：「过雾以人计，出雾以印计，人印不合，以印为准。」老蒲看了半天，说：「意思是，没盖出雾印的，不算出来了。」他把簿子揣进怀里，又往东去了。

column2: Reed Stage
column3: 草台戏

column2: A reed stage stands in the open, and a travelling troupe is stuck between deserters and native soldiers: the deserters want a show, the soldiers forbid it, and both sides have blades out. The troupe master is sweating, but the show must go on. It's their new piece, 'The Mule Train's Night at the Lodge', and the escort chief on stage has already lost half his beard.
column3: 野地里搭着一座草台，一个走乡的戏班子被夹在流兵和土兵中间：流兵要他们唱，土兵不许他们唱，两边都举着刀。班主急得满头汗，戏还得唱下去，唱的是新排的《马帮夜宿锅庄》，台上那个镖头的胡子已经掉了一半。

column2: Both bands are chased off and the play goes on to the end. The master says he got the story from Amo Yangjin at the lodge, but she tells it a little differently every year: one year the chief has a huge beard, the next he's clean-faced and pale. Only one thing never changes: they went into the fog singing. He asks you: 'Should I change the ending next year?'
column3: 两伙人都被赶跑，戏唱完了。班主说这出戏是听锅庄的央金阿嫫讲的，可阿嫫每年讲的都不太一样，有一年说镖头是个大胡子，有一年说他白白净净，只有一件事从来不变：他们是唱着歌进雾的。他问你们：「明年这出戏的结尾，要不要改？」

column2: Stuck-in-Fog Camp
column3: 困雾营

column2: A band of deserters stops you in the woods, and when they hear your manifest bears Pu's seal their eyes go red. Ten years ago they were labourers pressed into building road on the far side of the fog. When the work was done no one stamped them out, so they can't re-register at home; on paper they are still 'in the fog', and they turned deserter. Their leader draws: 'Pu won't let us out, so you don't get in!'
column3: 林中一伙流兵拦住你们，一听说你们的货单上有老蒲盖的印，个个红了眼。原来他们是十年前被拉去雾那头修路的民夫，修完了没人给盖出雾印，回乡落不了户，簿子上他们还「在雾里」，只好当了流兵。领头的拔刀：「老蒲不让我们出来，你们也别想进去！」

column2: Beaten, the deserters sit in the dirt wiping their eyes. You promise that once Pu has his Out seal back, they'll get their stamps. Their leader reads out names for you to write down: forty-one. And he says: 'That mule train that went in ten years ago, they came out with stamps. We saw it with our own eyes.'
column3: 流兵们被打服了，坐在地上抹眼泪。你们答应他们，等老蒲找回出雾印，一定替他们补盖上。领头的把名字一个个报给你们记下：四十一个。他还说：「十年前进雾的那伙马帮，是盖着印出来的。我们亲眼看见的。」

column2: Official Scales
column3: 官秤坪

column2: On the square of the tea-and-horse market stands the great official steelyard, its beam thicker than a roof beam, but its counterweight is gone, and without the scales no deal can be struck. Deserters and bullies hold the square, each with his own crooked scale, short on grain, light on firewood; the lodge's buyers go home in tears. The old weigh-master is locked in the scale house and his ledgers are lining a horse trough.
column3: 茶马互市的坪子上竖着一杆大官秤，秤杆比房梁还粗，秤砣却不见了，没秤，买卖就没法做。几伙流兵和兵痞占了坪子，各拿各的私秤，称粮缺斤，称柴短两，锅庄来买柴的人被克扣得哭着回去。老秤官被关在秤房里，簿子被他们拿去垫了马槽。

column2: The square is retaken. The old weigh-master digs his ledgers and an old counterweight out from under the trough, and the great scale swings again. Grain comes in, wood goes out, every weighing true, and the grain-for-timber trade reopens. In the Dingwei year he finds an entry: 'Qianli train prepays the lodge 3,650 bundles of firewood. One a day, for ten years.' He counts on his fingers. 'That's this year.' The chief had said: if we're not back in ten years, let the fire go out.
column3: 坪子收回来了，老秤官从马槽底下抠出簿子和一枚老秤砣，大秤又吊了起来。粮来柴往，一称一个准，粮换柴的买卖重新开张。老秤官翻到丁未年，有一笔账：「千里号预付锅庄柴三千六百五十捆，日供一捆，十年为限。」他掐指一算，说：「就是今年。」镖头当年说过，十年不回，火就让它灭了吧。

column2: Mailbag Slope
column3: 劫信坡

column2: On the slope some bullies have waylaid a courier and dumped his mailbag out, hunting for banknotes. The courier, tied to a tree, shouts that some of those letters have been on the road ten years, saved up one by one at the posts beyond the fog and only sent out this year. The bullies rip one open, toss it, rip another. The slope is covered in paper.
column3: 坡上几个兵痞截了一个驿差，把邮袋倒在地上翻，说里头有夹带的银票。驿差被绑在树上，嚷着那些信有的已经在路上走了十年，是雾那头的驿站一封封攒下来、今年才托人捎出来的。兵痞们拆一封扔一封，满坡都是信纸。

column2: You gather the letters one by one. Nine were sent ten years ago, and each envelope bears a square red seal: 'Out of the Fog', the looking-back deer. They were all posted from beyond the fog on the same day, the courier says. So Pu's seal did reach the far side, and was used. It just never came home.
column3: 信一封封捡了回来。其中九封是十年前寄的，信封上都盖着一个四四方方的红印：「出雾」，鹿回头的那一方。驿差说这些信是同一天从雾那头寄出来的。老蒲的印确实到过雾的那一头，盖过了，只是没有回来。

column2: Press-Gang Camp
column3: 拉差营

column2: A big camp at the foot of the mountains holds twenty-odd porters, pressed by the deserters to carry loot: grain, salt, iron pots. When the fog rises at night the song drifts in from outside again, and the porters hum along; rifle butts can't stop them. The deserter chief gives his order: catch the singer tonight and cut out his tongue.
column3: 山脚一座大营，营里拴着二十几个背夫，都是被流兵拉来背抢来的东西的，背上压着粮、盐、铁锅。夜里雾一起，营外又飘来那支山歌，背夫们听见就跟着哼，流兵枪手拿枪托砸也砸不住。领头的流兵下了令：今夜就把唱歌的抓来，割了他的舌头。

column2: You flatten the camp, and the porters throw off their loads and run home one by one. The voice is Shiwa's, they say. But every time Shiwa sings a line, another voice answers from deep in the fog, a grown man's, more practised than his. The singing has moved off over the mountain.
column3: 大营被你们踏平，背夫们扔下背篓，一个个跑回了家。他们说那歌声是石娃的，可石娃每唱一句，雾深处就有另一个嗓子接一句，是个中年汉子的声音，唱得比石娃还老练。歌声往山那边去了。

column2: Matchmaker's Pavilion
column3: 说媒亭

column2: In the roadside pavilion sits a matchmaker rouged to the eyebrows, with a cartload of betrothal gifts. She's come to propose the bully chief to Amo Yangjin: marry him and there'll be someone to feed the fire and haul the wood, and he can run the lodge all nice and proper. A few bullies guard the cart. They've waited three days for the lodge to say yes.
column3: 路边亭子里坐着个涂了满脸胭脂的媒婆，拉着一车彩礼，要替兵痞头子向锅庄的央金阿嫫提亲：嫁过去，火就有人添，柴就有人送，还能「名正言顺」地管着锅庄。几个兵痞押着彩礼车，已经在亭子里等了三天，就等锅庄点头。

column2: The gift cart goes over, the matchmaker hitches her skirts and flees, and the bully chief never shows his face. When you tell the lodge, Yangjin laughs till she cries. Her husband Zhaxi went into the fog with the Qianli train ten years ago; three mountains, he said, and he'd be back. 'It's not the fire I'm waiting for. It's him. The fire is just so he can see the way.'
column3: 彩礼车被掀翻，媒婆提着裙子跑了，兵痞头子连面都没敢露。你们把这事讲给锅庄听，央金笑出了眼泪。她说她男人扎西十年前跟着千里号进了雾，走前说过三座山就回：「我等的不是火，是人。火只是让他看得见。」

column2: Thorny-Rose Stockade
column3: 刺梨寨

column2: Deserters have built a stockade in a thicket of thorny wild rose and brew wine from the hips. Hanging at the gate, an arrow still through his hat, is Pu. He only stopped to ask the way, he says, but the moment they heard 'tax clerk' they strung him up and demanded ten years of tax silver. 'What silver? All I've got is ledgers!'
column3: 林子里一伙流兵在刺梨丛中搭了寨子，摘刺梨酿酒。寨门口吊着一个人，帽子上还插着一支箭，正是老蒲。他说他只是来问路，流兵一听他是税吏，二话不说就把他吊了起来，要他交出这十年的税银。「我哪有税银！我只有簿子！」

column2: It's the second time you've cut Pu down, and he's a little embarrassed. But he's found something out: at the east end of the fog there's a chain of posts called the Fog Posts, and someone there is collecting a 'fog tax'. 'There's no such thing as fog tax!' He's shaking with rage. 'Who authorised it?' He stuffs his ledger into his coat and is off again.
column3: 老蒲第二回被你们解下来，有点难为情。他说他打听到了：雾的东头有一串驿站，叫雾驿，那里有人在收「雾税」。「这世上哪有雾税？」他气得直哆嗦，「谁准他收的？」他把簿子往怀里一塞，又走了。

column2: Counterweight Hill
column3: 秤砣坡

column2: The great scale hangs again, but with only one old counterweight it can't weigh small lots. The rest, big and small, were stolen by a gang of bullies who sit up on the hill cracking walnuts with them. No weights, no weighing, and the yak train carrying wood to the lodge is stuck outside the square, the animals bawling with hunger.
column3: 官秤是吊起来了，可只有一枚老秤砣，称不了零碎。其余大大小小的秤砣都被一伙兵痞偷了去，躲在坡上拿秤砣当锤子砸核桃。没有秤砣，往锅庄运柴的牦牛队就过不了秤，一头头堵在坪子外头，饿得直叫。

column2: Every weight is recovered. The weigh-master's call rings across the square again, and the first weighed loads of wood go up on the yaks and off into the fog toward the lodge. Old Wang of the tea porters leads them, thumping his chest: that fire won't go out this year.
column3: 秤砣一枚不缺地找了回来。坪子上又响起老秤官的吆喝，第一批称好的柴装上牦牛，冒着雾往锅庄去了。领驮的是背茶客的老汪，他拍着胸口说，锅庄的火今年一定熄不了。

column2: Fog-Tax Gate
column3: 雾税卡

column2: A new checkpoint in the open, its board reading 'Fog Tax': one coin a head to go in, one tael a head to come out. Mountain crossbowmen run it and even write proper receipts, stamped with a seal that says 'Fog Post'. Pu has been arguing with them for two hours and is hoarse. 'A tael to come out? Can anyone even come out, that you charge for it?'
column3: 野地里一道新卡子，牌子上写「雾税」：进雾一人一钱，出雾一人一两。收税的是一伙山弩手，还像模像样地开收据，收据上盖着一个印，印文是「雾驿」。老蒲站在卡子前跟他们吵了一个时辰，嗓子都哑了：「出雾收一两？出得来吗你们就收！」

column2: The gate is torn down and the money box emptied back to the travellers. The seal on the receipts is genuine, cut by a practised hand. The crossbow captain admits the checkpoint was their own idea, but the Fog Post seal itself was a gift from the Master of the Fog Posts ten years ago, a licence to collect a few scraps outside the fog. Pu goes white.
column3: 卡子被拆了，钱箱里的钱退给了过客。收据上的印是真刻的，刀工老到，不是假货。山弩手的头目说，卡子是他们自己设的，可这方「雾驿」印，是十年前雾驿主赏给他们的，许他们在雾外收点零碎。老蒲的脸一下子白了。

column2: Wives' Slope
column3: 媳妇坡

column2: On this day every year a dozen muleteers' wives climb this slope and look east into the fog. Their men left with the Qianli train ten years ago. This year a band of caravan swordsmen is here too, offering a pittance for the families' mules: 'Your men aren't coming back. Why feed mules for nothing?' One wife swings her carrying pole at them and gets shoved to the ground.
column3: 每年这一天，十几个马帮媳妇都会到这道坡上来，朝东边的雾里望。她们的男人十年前跟着千里号走了。今年坡上多了一伙马帮刀客，牵着骡子来压价收她们家的骡马：「人回不来了，留着骡子白吃草料？」有个媳妇抄起扁担就打，被刀客推倒在地。

column2: The swordsmen are driven off and not one mule is sold. Yangjin is on the slope too, and the wives bring out the only letter any of them has had in all these years, sent back by Zhaxi: 'Out of the fog. Three more mountains to go. Don't worry.' The handwriting is awful and every one of them knows it by heart. Three mountains, they say. Surely ten years is enough to cross three mountains.
column3: 刀客们被打跑了，骡子一头也没卖。央金也在坡上，媳妇们拿出这些年收到的唯一一封信，是扎西托人带回来的：「已出雾，再走三座山，勿念。」字写得很丑，媳妇们却人人会背。她们说，三座山，十年也该走完了。

column2: Echo Hollow
column3: 回声坳

column2: Following the song you come to a hollow where the fog is so thick you can't see your own hand. Shiwa sits on a rock, voice cracked, still singing. Native soldiers stand around him with bamboo spears raised, but they don't strike; they seem to be listening. Shiwa says he daren't stop. Someone in the fog is singing back to him, and if he stops, they stop, and then he'll never find the way.
column3: 你们循着山歌找到一处山坳，坳里的雾浓得伸手不见五指。石娃坐在一块石头上，嗓子已经哑了，还在唱。他身边围着一群土兵，举着竹枪，却没有动手，像是在听。石娃说他不敢停：雾里有人跟他对歌，他一停，那人也停，他就再也找不着路了。

column2: The soldiers withdraw and you carry Shiwa out on your back. You hear it too: each line Shiwa sings, someone deep in the fog answers, all the way to the mouth of the hollow. There the voice stops answering and sings one last line alone: 'Go back and tell the lodge I drank the tea in the bowl.' It's the mule train's tune, Shiwa says, but he was never taught that line. You look back. There's nothing in the fog.
column3: 土兵们退走了，你们把石娃背了出来。你们也听见了：石娃唱一句，雾深处就有人接一句，一直接到坳口。到了坳口，那声音不接了，只唱了最后一句：「回去告诉锅庄，碗里的茶我喝了。」石娃说，那是马帮的调子，可最后这一句他从来没学过。你们回头望，雾里什么也没有。

column2: Yak Track
column3: 牦牛道

column2: The yak train hauling wood to the lodge has been ambushed at the foot of the mountains by crossbowmen; the yaks are driven into a gully and the wood tossed everywhere. Wood is worthless, says their captain, yaks are money, and the chieftain's men will buy them. The yak driver is a girl of twelve or thirteen, calling the animals one by one by name. At the seventh she starts to cry.
column3: 往锅庄运柴的牦牛队在山脚被一伙山弩手截了，牦牛被赶进山沟，柴扔了一地。山弩手的头目说柴不值钱，牦牛值钱，等土司家来收。赶牦牛的是个十二三岁的丫头，一头一头地喊着牦牛的名字，喊到第七头就哭了。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the girl calls her yaks back one at a time: eleven, all there. The wood is re-tied and loaded, and she means to reach the lodge before dark. 'Amo says tonight she'll put on a big bundle, so the people on the other side of the fog can see it.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走，牦牛被丫头一头头喊了回来，一共十一头，一头不少。柴重新捆好上了驮，丫头说要赶在天黑前送到锅庄：「阿嫫说今晚要添一大捆，让雾那头的人看得见。」

column2: Winter Camp Flats
column3: 冬营坝

column2: A big deserter camp sits on the flats, ringed with banners. Their chief has announced that before winter he'll take the lodge for barracks: a hearth, butter, and a landlady who works for free. He has spearmen, crossbowmen and swordsmen, more men than every village within ten li of the lodge put together.
column3: 坝子上扎着一座流兵大营，旗子插了一圈。流兵头子放话，入冬前要把锅庄占下来当兵营：有火塘，有酥油，还有个不要钱的老板娘。营里枪手、弩手、刀客样样都有，人数比锅庄方圆十里的寨子加起来还多。

column2: The camp is broken and abandoned. A few dozen deserters with nowhere left to go squat on the flats and ask whether they could cut wood for the lodge in exchange for meals. Yangjin thinks it over and agrees: 'One bundle, one meal.' The lodge will never be short of firewood again.
column3: 大营被你们打散，营盘扔得一干二净。剩下几十个走投无路的流兵蹲在坝子上，问能不能去锅庄砍柴换饭吃。央金想了想，答应了：「砍一捆，管一顿。」锅庄的柴，从此不愁了。

column2: Watch-Drum Jitters
column3: 怯更营

column2: Halfway along the road a deserter camp sits stuck, neither going on nor back. Three li ahead is an old post station abandoned for ten years, yet every night someone beats the watches there right on time, first watch, second, all the way to the fifth, never a stroke off. The deserters went in by daylight: nobody there, but the quilts on the beds were warm. Terrified, and too stubborn to go round, they stop every traveller and force them to scout the station first.
column3: 半道上扎着一座流兵大营，不前不后。营前三里有座荒了十年的老驿站，夜里却准时打更，一更、二更……一直打到五更，一下不差。流兵们白天进去看过，屋里没人，床上的被窝却是热的。他们怕得要命，又不肯绕路，就堵着过路人，逼人先去驿站里探一探。

column2: The camp is scattered. That night, from the abandoned camp ground, you listen: sure enough, the watch drum sounds from the old station, steady and exact, like someone who has beaten the watches all his life. After the fifth watch, a cough from inside the station. Then silence.
column3: 大营被冲散了。夜里你们在营地上听着，更鼓果然从老驿站里传出来，打得又稳又准，像是打了一辈子更的人。五更打完，驿站里传出一声咳嗽，然后静了。

column2: Miasma-Edge Garden
column3: 瘴边茶园

column2: On the edge of the miasma forest lies an old tea garden. The pickers climb up before dawn with their baskets and finish before the bad air rises. Mountain crossbowmen have seized the garden and make them pick through the night, when the fog and miasma are thickest; two have already fallen ill. The girls sing as they pick, a picking song made up by old Master Wen below the pass: 'Pick early, three parts tea; pick late, seven parts poison.'
column3: 瘴林的边上是一片老茶园，采茶的女人们背着竹篓，天不亮就上山，赶在瘴气起来之前收工。一伙山弩手占了茶园，逼她们连夜采，夜里雾重瘴浓，已经有两个人病倒了。姑娘们一边采一边唱，唱的是关下温夫子编的采茶歌，歌里说：「早采三分，晚采七分毒。」

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off the hill and the sick women carried home to drink Master Wen's tea remedy. Master Wen lives below the pass, the girls tell you, and has spent his life copying out the Classic of Tea, until in the end he started changing it. 'He says Lu Yu left a chapter out. The chapter about fog.'
column3: 山弩手被赶下了山，病倒的女人被抬回去，喝了温夫子开的茶汤方。姑娘们说温夫子住在关下，一辈子在抄一部《茶经》，抄到后来连字都改了：「他说陆羽写漏了一章，雾里的那一章。」

column2: Hitching-Post Flats
column3: 千桩坝

column2: The main body of the deserters blocks the great road east. They're camped on flats among a forest of hitching posts, row upon row, many times more posts than they have horses. Spearmen hold formation across the road, crossbowmen shoot from behind the posts, caravan swordsmen charge back and forth. Until you break them, the way east stays shut.
column3: 东去的大路被一支流兵的主力堵住了，他们在一片坝子上扎营，营盘围着一大片拴马桩，桩子一排挨一排，比他们的马多出好几倍。流兵枪手结阵挡在路口，山弩手藏在桩子后面放冷箭，马帮刀客来回冲杀。打不过这一阵，往东去的路就一直断着。

column2: The deserter host collapses and the road is open. The hitching posts were driven in ten years ago when the Qianli train rested here. Old halters still hang on them, mostly rotted; one is still sound, tied in the muleteers' 'return knot': whoever unties it must come back and tie it again. Carved on top of the post, small: 'Rest one night, walk a lifetime.'
column3: 流兵主力溃了，路通了。坝子上的拴马桩是十年前千里号马帮歇脚时打下的，桩上还系着当年的缰绳，大多烂了，只有一根还结实，打的是马帮的「回头结」：解开它的人，得回来再系上。桩顶刻着一行小字：「歇一夜，走一生。」

column2: Bronze Drum Hold
column3: 铜鼓寨

column2: At the end of a blind road at the mountain foot is the chieftain's Bronze Drum Hold. Inside hangs a great bronze drum: strike it once, and every native soldier within a hundred li must come home. The chieftain's household troops guard it, swordsmen and crossbowmen in ring after ring, fiercer than any you've met. For ten years the chieftain has let no one touch it. Strike it, he says, and something terrible will happen.
column3: 山脚死路尽头是土司家的铜鼓寨，寨里供着一面大铜鼓，敲一下，方圆百里的土兵都得回寨。守寨的是土司的家兵，刀客、弩手一层套一层，比别处凶得多。十年来土司不许任何人碰那面鼓，说一敲就要出大事。

column2: The household troops are beaten back. The drum is thick with dust. Ten years ago, an old man of the hold says, the chieftain sent a troop of soldiers to escort the mule train into the fog, and never beat the drum to call them home. You strike it once. After a long time, from deep in the fog, three beats come back, very slow, as if to say: not yet. We can't come back yet.
column3: 家兵被打退，铜鼓上落满了灰。寨里的老人说，十年前土司派了一队土兵护送马帮进雾，后来一直没敲鼓召他们回来。你们敲了一下，雾的深处隔了很久，传回来三声鼓，很慢，像是在说：还不能回。

column2: One-Arm's Mule Inn
column3: 独臂骡店

column2: A mule inn at the mountain foot whose troughs should be full of fodder and are full of the bullies' wine jars instead. They've taken the inn and hold passing caravans' mules as 'deposit', no fee, no mule. The innkeeper, an old man with one arm, has been banished to the stable and spends his days feeding their horses and emptying their chamber pots.
column3: 山脚一家骡马店，槽子里本该是草料，如今全是兵痞们的酒坛。兵痞占了店，把过路马帮的骡子扣下当押金，不交钱不许牵走。店主是个独臂老汉，被赶去睡了马棚，每天给兵痞们喂马、倒尿壶。

column2: The bullies are chased out, the jars smashed, the troughs heaped with fresh grass again. The one-armed keeper goes back behind his counter and returns the mules to their caravans one by one. If the lodge fire ever went out, he says, every caravan on this road would lose heart. 'Where there's a fire, there's a road.'
column3: 兵痞被赶跑，酒坛砸了，槽子里重新堆满青草。独臂店主回到柜台后面，把扣下的骡子一头头还给马帮。他说锅庄的火要是灭了，这条路上的马帮都没了奔头：「有火的地方，才算有路。」

column2: From the bullies' stores: thirty sacks of bean fodder, twelve saddles, two loads of salt, and a chest of confiscated harness bells, over a hundred of every size. Going by the marks on them, you return most to their owners.
column3: 抄出兵痞囤的豆料三十袋、马鞍十二副、盐巴两驮，还有一箱扣下的马铃，大大小小一百多个，你们照着铃上的记号，还了一大半给原主。

column2: Every time you pass, the one-armed keeper leads your animals off to be brushed and shod and fed full, and won't write any of it down. 'A guest of the lodge is a guest of mine.'
column3: 每次路过，独臂店主都把你们的骡马牵去刷一遍、钉好掌，草料喂得饱饱的，账一概不记：「锅庄的客，就是我的客。」

column2: Felled-Tea Wood
column3: 伐茶林

column2: In the woods a band of crossbowmen is chopping down tea trees. Climbing to pick is too slow for them, so they fell whole old trees, strip one basket of leaf, and leave them. A tree several centuries old is already cut half through, sap oozing white from the bark. When the old picker kneels beneath it and begs, they stuff his mouth with fresh leaves.
column3: 林子里一伙山弩手在砍茶树。他们嫌爬树采茶太慢，干脆把整棵老茶树放倒了采，放倒一棵，采一篓，扔下。一棵几百年的老茶树已经被砍了半边，树皮里渗出白浆。采茶的老人跪在树下求他们，他们就拿刚采下的鲜叶塞他的嘴。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven away and half the old tree survives. On its trunk is an ancient blaze, long since grown over, with the character 'Qian' cut beside it. Ten years ago, the old man says, the mule train picked from this very tree, and the bricks they pressed weren't like anyone else's. 'A deep groove pressed down the middle of each brick, so it would snap into two halves.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走，老茶树保住了半边。树干上有一道很老的刀口，早已长平了，刀口旁边刻着一个「千」字。老人说，十年前马帮在这棵树上采过一回叶子，压出来的茶砖跟别家不一样：「一块砖从中间压一道深槽，能掰成两半。」

column2: Fake-Ghost Post
column3: 假鬼驿

column2: The old post station stands at the mountain foot, white funeral banners at the door and paper figures in the yard. The moment you step in, a gang of 'ghosts' in white sheets drops from the roof. They're salt smugglers using the station as a warehouse and playing at spooks to scare people off. When you don't scare, they tear off the sheets and draw knives.
column3: 老驿站就在山脚，门口挂着白幡，院里摆着纸人。你们一进门，屋顶上就跳下一伙披着白布的「鬼」，原来是一帮走私盐巴的，把驿站当了货仓，装神弄鬼吓唬路人。他们见你们不怕，扯下白布，抽出了刀。

column2: The smugglers are knocked flat, and their salt sacks fill half the yard. But they swear on their mothers it isn't them beating the watches, and it isn't them warming the beds. 'We're the ones being haunted! When that drum starts we crawl under the beds.' That night the watch drum sounds again, stroke by stroke.
column3: 走私客被打得满地找牙，盐包堆了半个院子。可他们赌咒发誓，说打更不是他们打的，被窝也不是他们睡的：「我们才是被吓的那个！那更鼓一响，我们就往床底下钻。」当天晚上，更鼓又一下一下地响了起来。

column2: Pickers' Loft
column3: 采茶楼

column2: At the foot of the tea garden stands a bamboo loft where pickers rest, spread leaf to wither and eat their midday meal. Bullies have taken it over, using the withering trays as dinner tables and the tea-roasting wok to stew chickens. The pickers squat in the mud below eating cold rice, and aren't allowed upstairs even when it rains.
column3: 茶园脚下一座竹楼，是采茶人歇脚、晾茶、吃午饭的地方。一伙兵痞占了竹楼，把晾茶的竹匾当饭桌，把炒茶的铁锅拿去炖鸡。采茶人只能蹲在楼下的泥地里吃冷饭，下雨了也不许上楼。

column2: The bullies are thrown out; the trays fill with leaf again, the wok is scrubbed, and the scent of roasting tea drifts over the slope. Every good tea on this road, the old tea-maker says, has to pass Master Wen below the pass: one sip and he knows which mountain and which year. 'The mule train's tea ten years ago, he tasted that too before it went on.'
column3: 兵痞被撵走，竹匾重新摊满了茶叶，铁锅洗干净，炒茶的香气飘了满坡。楼里的老茶工说，茶路上的好茶，都要过关下温夫子那一关：他尝一口，就知道茶是哪座山、哪一年采的。「十年前马帮的茶，也是他尝过才放行的。」

column2: In the loft: six baskets of new tea the bullies stole, three loads of sticky rice, a string of cured pork, and a dozen bamboo tea tubes sealed with wax. You return them all to the pickers, who insist you take half.
column3: 楼里搜出兵痞抢的新茶六篓、糯米三担、腊肉一串，还有十几只装茶的竹筒，筒口用蜡封着，原样还给采茶人，大家硬分了你们一半。

column2: Every time you pass, the pickers fill a few tubes with freshly roasted tea for you. It's the custom on the edge of the miasma wood: a strong bowl before you go in, and your head stays clear.
column3: 每次路过，采茶人都给你们装几筒新炒的茶，说是瘴林边上的规矩：进林子前喝一碗浓茶，头不晕。

column2: Ghost-Fire Fen
column3: 鬼火泽

column2: Every night balls of blue fire rise over the fen, bobbing high and low. A cult calling themselves Envoys of the Fog God guards its edge: the fog god is lighting his lamps, they say, and travellers must offer lamp oil and coppers or the blue fire will follow them home. They carry long poles wrapped at the tip with oil-soaked rag, and when they wave them over the fen at night, the blue fires flare.
column3: 泽地里每到夜晚就冒起一团团蓝火，忽高忽低。一伙自称「雾神使者」的邪教徒守在泽边，说那是雾神在点灯，过路人得献上灯油和铜钱，否则蓝火会跟着回家。他们手里举着长竿，竿头缠着浸过油的布，夜里往泽上一晃，蓝火就跟着亮起来。

column2: You scatter the cultists. Master Wen's book-boy Ayan comes looking with a lantern and squats by the fen half the night watching. 'It's gas. Rotting leaves and reeds stewing under the mud give it off, and when it bubbles up it'll catch from any flame. They just light it with their poles.' He writes it in his notebook. Useful for the master's fog chapter, he says.
column3: 邪教徒被你们赶散了。温夫子的书童阿砚提着灯笼找来，蹲在泽边看了半夜，说：「这是烂草烂叶在泥底下沤出来的气，冒上来，见火就着，他们拿火竿去引罢了。」他把这句话记进本子里，说夫子的雾篇用得上。

column2: Book-Burning Camp
column3: 烧书营

column2: Deserters are camped in the woods with a roaring fire, and what they're burning is paper. Ayan says it's Master Wen's manuscripts, stolen from below the pass a few days ago for kindling, dozens of pages a night. The spearmen complain that pages with lots of writing burn slowly, and pick out the ones with fewer words first.
column3: 林中一伙流兵扎营，营火烧得很旺，烧的却是纸。阿砚说那是温夫子的书稿，前些日子被他们从关下抢来，当引火纸用，一夜烧几十页。流兵枪手们嫌字多的纸烧得慢，还专挑字少的先烧。

column2: The deserters scatter and you snatch half a bundle of manuscript from the flames, edges charred. One page is from the fog chapter, and in its margin is someone else's hand, hard and blunt: 'Can tea remember a road?' Beneath, in Master Wen's small script: 'Tea remembers the mountain. People remember the road.' Ayan says the man who asked was an escort chief.
column3: 流兵被打散，火里抢出半捆书稿，边都烧焦了。有一页正是「雾」那一章，页边写着另一个人的字，写得很硬：「茶能记路否？」下面是温夫子的小字回答：「茶记山，人记路。」阿砚说，问话的是个镖头。

column2: Bear Gully
column3: 熊瞎子沟

column2: Up a blind gully at the mountain foot lives a family of black bears. Every autumn they come down and go for the lodge's butter loads, one swipe to knock the pack over, then off with the butter churn in their arms. This year two mothers with cubs have come, and a one-eyed old male, and they've taken over the whole path. Even the porters won't use it.
column3: 山脚死路里有一窝黑熊，每年秋天下山，专挑锅庄的酥油驮子下手，一巴掌拍翻驮子，抱起酥油桶就跑。今年来了两头带崽的母熊，还有一头独眼的老公熊，把整条小路都占了，连背夫都不敢走。

column2: The bears are driven back into the mountains and the butter loads can pass again. But these bears have a taste for butter now; they'll be down again before long, and someone will have to drive them off every autumn. In the den you find a rusted mule bell with 'Zhaxi' cut inside it, and keep it for Yangjin.
column3: 熊被赶回了深山，酥油驮子又能过了。可这一窝熊吃惯了酥油，过一阵子还会下山，年年秋天都得来赶一回。熊洞里还有一只锈了的骡铃，铃里刻着「扎西」，你们替央金收了起来。

column2: Herb Raft
column3: 药筏

column2: A herb raft is moored at the riverbank, and the old herbalist aboard has sweet wormwood, woad root and atractylodes, all good against miasma fever. Yet not one sick person in the forest can buy any. Smugglers have surrounded the raft and want the lot, to resell to the sick at ten times the price. The old man hugs his bundles to his chest. He'd rather they rot on the raft.
column3: 河边泊着一只药筏，卖草药的老药客守着一筏子的青蒿、板蓝根、苍术，都是治瘴的好药。可瘴林里的病人一样也买不到：一伙走私客把药筏围了，要他把药全卖给他们，好转手翻十倍卖给病人。老药客把药捆抱在怀里，宁可烂在筏上。

column2: The smugglers go into the river and the old herbalist opens for trade at the same prices as ten years ago. Half his recipes came from Master Wen, he says. 'The master says: to treat the miasma, first treat the tea. Drink the right tea and you need half the medicine.' And lately, he adds, someone has been watching Master Wen. After that secret book of his.
column3: 走私客被赶下了河，老药客开了张，价钱跟十年前一样。他说他的方子有一半是温夫子给的：「夫子说，治瘴先治茶，喝对了茶，药能少用一半。」他还说温夫子最近被人盯上了，盯的是他那本秘本。

column2: Half-Brick Stockade
column3: 半砖寨

column2: Deep in the miasma wood is a big stockade, home of the crossbow tea smugglers, piled with bricks stolen and robbed from everywhere, waiting to be run out past the toll. Poisoned bolts hang on the walls and dozens of dogs live inside. When the fog rises they all bark at once, the sound circling through the trees so you can't tell where it comes from.
column3: 瘴林深处一座大寨，是走私茶叶的山弩手的老窝，寨里堆满了从各处偷来、抢来的茶砖，等着偷运出关。寨墙上挂着毒箭，寨里养着几十条狗，雾一起，狗就一齐叫，叫声在林子里绕来绕去，分不清从哪边来。

column2: The stockade falls, and the bricks go back to the gardens and workshops. At the very bottom of the pile is a very old brick, only half of one, the break perfectly clean along a groove pressed in when it was made. Half a character 'Qian' is stamped on its face. The other half, says the old tea-maker, isn't anywhere on this road.
column3: 大寨破了，茶砖还给了茶园和茶坊。茶堆最底下压着一块很老的茶砖，只有半块，断口整整齐齐，是压的时候就留好了槽。砖面上印着半个「千」字。老茶工说，另外那半块，不在这条路上。

column2: Hearth Dance
column3: 跳锅庄

column2: On the ground before the lodge the villagers dance the guozhuang around a bonfire, ring inside ring, with Yangjin leading at the centre. A band of drunk caravan swordsmen barges in, ordering everyone out of their way and demanding Yangjin dance for them alone. When someone refuses, they kick over a wine jar by the fire, and the flames roar up a man's height.
column3: 锅庄前的空地上，寨子里的人围着火堆跳锅庄，一圈套一圈，央金在最里面领舞。一伙喝醉了的马帮刀客闯进来，要大家给他们让道，还要央金单给他们跳一支。有人不肯，刀客就踢翻了火堆边的酒坛，火苗被酒一浇，呼地窜起一人高。

column2: The drunks are thrown out of the ring and the dance goes on. When it ends, Yangjin brings you a little packet of hearth ash tied in red cloth to carry east. 'The Fog Post people used to say: carry lodge ash through the fog and the fog knows you for family.' If you meet Lu Jiu, she says, tell him the fire is still burning, and someone drinks the tea in the bowl every day.
column3: 醉刀客被扔出圈外，舞又跳了起来。散场时，央金捧来一小包火塘灰，用红布扎着，托你们往东边带：「雾驿的人说过，锅庄的灰带过雾，雾就认得是自家人。」她说要是遇见陆九，就告诉他火还烧着，碗里的茶每天都有人喝。

column2: Watchman's Post
column3: 更夫驿

column2: At midnight you creep into the old post station and wait under the eaves. Just after the third watch a hunchbacked old watchman comes out of the back yard with his drum and beats it, stroke by stroke, then goes into each room in turn and lies down on every bed for a while before getting up again. Some bullies hiding in the station, scared half to death, are raising their knives to hack at this 'ghost' when you stop them.
column3: 你们半夜摸进老驿站，躲在廊下等。三更刚过，一个驼背的老更夫从后院出来，提着更鼓，一下一下地敲，敲完一遍，挨个屋子钻进去，在每张床上躺一会儿再起来。几个躲在驿站里的兵痞被他吓得不轻，正举刀要砍这个「鬼」，被你们拦住了。

column2: The watchman is the last of this station's old staff. Ten years ago the Qianli people slept here one night and asked him to wake them at the fifth watch. He did, they left, and he has kept beating the watches ever since. 'If they come back, they'll need to know the hour.' He warms the beds one by one so they won't go damp. As chief Lu left, he says, he made a point of it: get through the fog when the Fog Posts open. 'The Master of the Fog Posts opens only at the fifth watch. After that, the fog counts one extra.'
column3: 老更夫是这驿站的老人。十年前千里号的人在这里住过一夜，临睡前托他五更叫醒他们。他叫了，他们走了，他就一直这么敲了下去：「万一他们回来，总得知道是什么时辰。」被窝是他挨个躺暖的，怕潮。他说陆镖头走时交代过，一定要赶在雾驿开门时过雾：「雾驿主只在五更开门。过了五更，雾里就要多数一个人。」

column2: Tea Fork
column3: 茶分岔

column2: The road forks here, one branch down to the pass, one into the miasma wood. Deserters have fenced the fork and seize every porter carrying tea: Master Wen below the pass owes their chief money, they say, and tea will settle it. The spearmen have stacked tea bricks into a wall and fight from behind it.
column3: 大路在这里分成两岔，一岔往关下，一岔往瘴林。岔口一伙流兵设了栅栏，凡是背茶的一律扣下，说关下的温夫子欠了他们头领一笔钱，要拿茶抵债。流兵枪手们把茶砖垒成一道墙，躲在茶墙后面放枪。

column2: The tea wall comes down and the porters surge through. Under the signpost is a notice in Master Wen's own hand: 'This school copies books and owes nobody money. What it owes is one chapter of the Classic of Tea.' And below, as if added later: 'The tea in two halves, the people on three roads.' Ayan says it's a line the master once traded with an escort chief.
column3: 茶墙推倒了，背茶人一拥而过。路牌底下压着一张告示，是温夫子亲手写的：「本塾抄书，概不欠债，欠的是一章《茶经》。」后面还有一行，像是后来添的：「茶分两半，人分三路。」阿砚说，这是夫子当年跟一个镖头对的一句话。

column2: Punt-Pole Fen
column3: 撑篙泽

column2: Narrow channels thread the fen, and smugglers pole flat-bottomed boats along them, running tea out past the toll. This crew robs travellers on the side, jabbing them off the paths with punt poles and tipping them into the muck. The fen water is black and glossy, and one wrong step sinks you to the thigh.
column3: 泽地里一条条窄水道，走私客撑着平底船往外偷运茶叶，避开茶关的税。这一伙走私客还兼着劫道，见了外人就拿竹篙往水里捅，把人掀进烂泥。泽水黑得发亮，一脚下去能陷到大腿。

column2: The smugglers surrender and their cargo is handed over, every brick counted. Lately, their leader says, several parties of strangers have come down to the pass asking about Master Wen's secret book, some with big money, some with blades. 'They say that book tells you how to walk the fog.'
column3: 走私客投降了，船上的茶照数交了公。领头的说，这些日子关下来了好几拨生人，都在打听温夫子的秘本，有出大价钱的，也有扛着刀的：「听说那本书里，写着雾里怎么走。」

column2: Change-of-Trade Stockade
column3: 改业寨

column2: A large deserter stockade in the woods, ruled by a big pockmarked man with several hundred spearmen, crossbowmen and swordsmen. They've lived by robbing tea for ten years and never got rich; his men only get thinner. When you attack, he stands on the wall ordering volleys and shouting at the same time: 'When this is over, can we talk?'
column3: 林中一座流兵大寨，寨主是个满脸麻子的大汉，手下枪手、弩手、刀客好几百。他们靠劫茶过活，劫了十年也没发财，寨里的人反倒越来越瘦。你们打上门来，寨主站在寨墙上，一边下令放箭，一边大喊：「打完了能不能谈谈？」

column2: The stockade falls, and the pockmarked chief kneels, not for mercy but for lessons. 'Robbing tea never made me rich. Teach me to sell it.' You do the sums with him: right on the high road, water, firewood; a teahouse here would earn more than robbery ever did. He tears down his own gate on the spot. It'll make a fine counter.
column3: 寨子破了，麻子寨主跪在地上，不是求饶，是求教：「劫茶劫不富，你们教我卖茶吧。」你们给他算了一笔账：寨子在大路边，有水有柴，开一家茶铺，比劫道挣得多。他当场拆了寨门，说要改成柜台。

column2: Contested Ferry
column3: 争渡口

column2: Crossbowmen hold the river ferry, the boat tied on the far bank, crossing only those who pay; those who can't have waited three days on the shore. The old ferryman is lashed to the bow as a living anchor. Even while they curse him he keeps muttering how many inches the river has risen today.
column3: 河上的渡口被一伙山弩手占了，渡船拴在对岸，只渡肯交钱的人，交不起的在岸边已经等了三天。摆渡的老艄公被他们捆在船头，当作活的船锚。艄公一边挨骂，一边还在念叨河水今天又涨了几寸。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the old ferryman poles boatload after boatload across. Ten years ago, he says, this boat carried an escort chief and an old scholar who argued the whole way: tea is for drinking, said the scholar; tea is for knowing people by, said the chief. 'When they got out on the bank, each had half a tea brick, and they were friends again.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走，老艄公重新撑起了船，一船一船往对岸送。他说十年前这条船上渡过一个镖头和一个老学究，两人吵了一路，学究说茶是喝的，镖头说茶是认人的：「上了岸，两人一人拿着半块茶砖，又好了。」

column2: Reformed Teahouse
column3: 改邪茶铺

column2: The new teahouse at the mountain foot belongs to the pockmarked ex-chief, its counter made from his old stockade gate. It's barely open when a gang of bullies turns up claiming he's on their turf and demanding 'opening money', or they'll smash the place. His hands itch for a blade, but he remembers he's a shopkeeper now, swallows it, and hides behind the counter making eyes at you to help.
column3: 山脚那家新开的茶铺，是麻子寨主改行开的，柜台就是拆下来的寨门。开张没几天，就来了一伙兵痞，说他抢了他们的地盘，要他交「开张钱」，不交就砸铺子。麻子寨主手痒，想拿刀，又想起自己现在是掌柜，硬生生忍住了，躲在柜台后面给你们递眼色。

column2: You run the bullies off and the pockmarked keeper slaps the counter: 'Tea's on the house today!' He shows you his account book, every entry neat. Back when he robbed for a living he never kept accounts, he says; no wonder he never got rich. A new sign goes up over the door: The Reformed Teahouse.
column3: 兵痞被你们打跑，麻子掌柜一拍柜台：「今天茶钱全免！」他把账本摊开给你们看，一笔一笔记得清清楚楚，说当年劫道从来不记账，难怪发不了财。门口挂起了新招牌：「改邪茶铺」。

column2: What the bullies left behind: three iron pots, two stacks of tea bowls, a sack of sugar and half a mutton carcass. The keeper counts it all as tea money and forces a slip on you that reads: Free for Life.
column3: 兵痞丢下的东西：铁锅三口、茶碗两摞、一袋砂糖、半扇羊肉。麻子掌柜全折成茶钱，还硬塞给你们一张条子，上面写着「终身免单」。

column2: Every time you pass, the keeper brings out some new tea cake he's invented and won't let you go until you've tasted it and named a price. Business keeps growing, he says, and his old brothers from the stockade are all getting fat.
column3: 每次路过，麻子掌柜都端出新琢磨的茶点，非要你们尝过了给个价，说生意越做越好，寨里的老弟兄都吃胖了。

column2: Scholar's Bridge
column3: 夫子桥

column2: The way to Master Wen's cottage crosses a fen, and some bullies have laid a narrow plank bridge over it with a sign at the end: 'Books Surrendered Here.' Someone has offered a big reward for Master Wen's secret book. No book, no crossing; and handing over a book doesn't get you across either. They want the book and the man who brings it.
column3: 去温夫子茅屋的路要穿过一片泽地，几个兵痞拿木板在泽上搭了一道窄桥，桥头立着牌子：「过桥交书」。原来有人出了大价钱悬赏温夫子的秘本，他们守在这里，不交书的不许过，交了书的也不许过，非要连人带书一起拿下。

column2: The bullies go into the fen and the plank bridge is the public's again. The reward notice at the bridgehead reads: 'Wanted by the Fog Posts: a copy of the fog chapter of the Classic of Tea. One hundred taels.' Ayan sniffs. 'The Master of the Fog Posts can't write it himself, so he wants to grab ours.'
column3: 兵痞们掉进了泽里，木板桥归了路人。桥头的悬赏告示上写着：「雾驿收《茶经》雾篇抄本，赏银百两。」阿砚看了，冷笑一声：「雾驿主自己写不出来，就想抢我们夫子的。」

column2: Hoof-Stone Road
column3: 马蹄石

column2: A stretch of flagstone road runs through the wood, its stones pitted with hollows the size of a bowl's mouth, hoofprints worn in one step at a time over a thousand years; the deepest would hold a fist. Deserters are levering up the flags with iron bars to build their stockade wall. The highland horse dealer Gonbu crouches at the roadside wringing his hands. 'Pull up the stones and the old horses won't know the way.'
column3: 林子里一段石板路，石板上布满了碗口大的小坑，是千百年来马蹄一下一下踩出来的，最深的能放进一只拳头。一伙流兵正拿铁钎把石板撬起来，搬去修他们的寨墙。番人马贩贡布蹲在路边，心疼得直搓手：「撬了石板，老马就不认路了。」

column2: The deserters are driven away and the flags laid back one by one. An old horse on the tea road doesn't watch the road, Gonbu says, it feels for the hollows: when a hoof drops into one, it knows it's on the right track. He has an old grey that walked this road with the Qianli train ten years ago and came back by itself. 'It remembers these hollows.' Pity no one will buy it.
column3: 流兵被赶走，石板一块块铺了回去。贡布说老马走茶路，不看路，看石坑：蹄子落进坑里，就知道走对了。他有一匹老青马，十年前跟着千里号走过这条路，后来是自己走回来的，「它记得这些坑」。可惜谁也不肯买它。

column2: Leech Pond
column3: 蚂蟥塘

column2: A foul pond in the fen, alive with leeches. A deserter band has camped right beside it anyway, because the tea-firing works' pine wood is stacked there and they mean to sell it. Anyone who comes for the wood gets shoved into the pond, and the deserters double over laughing as the leeches climb his legs.
column3: 泽地里一处烂塘，水里全是蚂蟥，一伙流兵却偏偏在塘边扎营，因为塘边堆着焙茶坊的松柴，他们想拿去换钱。谁去搬柴，他们就把谁推进塘里，看他腿上爬满蚂蟥，笑得前仰后合。

column2: This time it's the deserters who go into the pond, and they crawl out covered in leeches and run off howling. The pine is loaded and carted to the tea works. Firing tea needs pine, says the old master there: a steady fire, a fragrant smoke. Run out of pine and the whole works stops.
column3: 流兵自己被推进了塘里，爬出来满腿蚂蟥，哭爹喊娘地跑了。松柴装上了车，送去焙茶坊。焙茶的老师傅说，焙茶得用松柴，火要稳，烟要香，柴一断，整坊的茶都焙不成。

column2: Tea-Firing Works
column3: 焙茶坊

column2: In the heart of the wood lies the biggest tea-firing works on the road: a dozen roasting baskets in a row, stone brick-moulds filling half the yard. Caravan swordsmen have seized it. The fires are cold and the moulds serve as whetstones. They want the masters to sell them leaf for nothing, and the masters would sooner let it rot in the store.
column3: 林子正中是茶路上最大的焙茶坊，十几座焙笼一字排开，压砖的石模摆了半个院子。如今坊子被一伙马帮刀客占了，焙笼冷了，石模被拿去当了磨刀石。他们逼焙茶的师傅们把茶叶贱卖给他们，师傅们宁肯让茶叶烂在仓里。

column2: The swordsmen are driven off, the fires relit, and the smell of roasting tea drifts out of the wood. The works needs new stone moulds, and the masters will trade timber for stone; the wood-for-stone trade opens. The old master digs out an order from ten years ago: the Qianli train ordered three hundred bricks, each pressed with a deep groove, 'one half to travel with the people, one half to wait for their return'. The three hundred waiting halves the chief didn't leave here. He had them sent south to the villages, to be kept by an elder.
column3: 刀客们被赶跑，焙笼重新点上，茶香飘出了林子。坊里缺压砖的石模，师傅们愿意拿木料跟你们换石头，木换石的买卖就此开张。老师傅翻出十年前的单子：千里号订压茶砖三百块，每块压一道深槽，「一半随人走，一半等人回」。等人回的那三百个半块，镖头没留在坊里，托人送往南边的寨子，交给一位寨老保管。

column2: Hive Wood
column3: 蜂箱林

column2: Wooden hives hang all through this wood, and a white-bearded old man is cutting honey beneath them. Some crossbowmen came to steal it and were stung lumpy, and now, furious, they're about to set fire to the hives. The old man was once Pu's runner. Ten years ago it was he who carried the box with the Out seal and led the Qianli mule train through this wood.
column3: 林子里挂满了木头蜂箱，一个白胡子老汉在树下割蜜。几个山弩手来抢他的蜜，被蜜蜂蛰得满头是包，越蛰越恼，正要放火烧蜂箱。这老汉是老蒲当年的跑腿税丁，十年前就是他背着出雾印的印匣，领着千里号马帮穿过这片林子的。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the hives saved. Beyond this wood, the old man says, is the far side of the fog. The chief stood at the edge of the trees and called out a number for every man who came out. 'At two hundred and ninety-nine he stopped calling. He stood there and waited, right through till dawn.' At daybreak the chief sent him home and took the seal box on to the Fog Posts himself.
column3: 山弩手被赶走，蜂箱保住了。老汉说，出了这片林子就是雾的那一头，镖头在林口站着，每出来一个人，就报一个数。「报到二百九十九，他就不报了，站在林口等，一直等到天亮。」天亮后，镖头让他先回家，自己带着印匣往雾驿去了。

column2: Copyist's Hut
column3: 抄经庐

column2: At the end of the open ground stands a thatched hut, books heaped inside and out. White-haired Master Wen bends over his desk copying; his hand shakes badly, yet every stroke comes out steady. Native soldiers ring the hut, their leader holding out an ingot: the Master of the Fog Posts requests the fog chapter of the Classic of Tea. The master doesn't look up. 'Books are copied for those who come after, not sold to the fog.' The soldiers lose patience and start throwing torches onto the roof.
column3: 野地尽头一间茅屋，屋里屋外堆满了书。白发的温夫子伏在案上抄书，手抖得厉害，一笔一笔却很稳。茅屋外围着一伙土兵，为首的捧着一锭银子，说雾驿主请夫子把《茶经》的雾篇交出来。夫子头也不抬：「书是抄给后来人看的，不是卖给雾看的。」土兵们不耐烦了，开始往屋顶上扔火把。

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the fire put out, with only a corner of the eaves burned. Master Wen hands you a hand-copied volume: The Classic of Tea, Chapter on Fog. Lu Yu wrote ten chapters, he says; he walked the tea road all his life and added an eleventh. Which mountain's tea to pick when, how many firings, and what to drink to study through the night, so that one night's reading is worth three. 'Take it. For your academy.' Ten years ago, he adds, an escort chief read the first draft and asked only one thing: 'Can tea remember a road?'
column3: 土兵被赶跑，火扑灭了，只烧了一角屋檐。温夫子把一本手抄的册子交给你们，封皮上写着《茶经·雾篇》。他说陆羽的《茶经》十章，他走了一辈子茶路，补上了第十一章：哪座山的茶什么时候采，焙几道火，喝了能熬夜读书，读书人一夜抵得上三夜。「拿去，给你们的学堂用。」他还说，十年前一个镖头读过这一篇的初稿，只问了一句：「茶能记路吗？」

column2: Cloud-Banner Shoal
column3: 云旗滩

column2: A big camp of caravan swordsmen fills the river shoal, mules tethered all over it, and the swordsmen are loading stolen tea bricks onto boats to float away downstream. This band came from the Fog Posts. Their banner shows a cloud, they don't mix with the local deserters, and they speak with an eastern accent.
column3: 河滩上扎着一支马帮刀客的大营，骡子拴了满滩，刀客们正把从各处劫来的茶砖往船上搬，要顺水运走。这一伙是从雾驿那边过来的，旗子上画着一团云，不跟本地流兵来往，说话也带着东边的口音。

column2: The camp breaks up and the bricks come back ashore. The prisoners say they haul tea for the Master of the Fog Posts. He lacks nothing except good tea, and takes a thousand jin a year. 'It's cold in the fog. He says only tea makes a man remember who he is.' In the hold is an old manifest, its top line reading: 'Tea-firing works. Three hundred bricks. Halves.'
column3: 大营散了，茶砖卸回岸上。俘虏说他们替雾驿主运茶，雾驿主什么都不缺，就缺好茶，每年要收上千斤：「雾里冷，他说只有茶能叫人记得自己是谁。」船舱里还有一张旧货单，最上面一行写着：「焙茶坊，三百块，半。」

column2: Broken-Terrace Slope
column3: 塌埂坡

column2: A hillside is cut into tea terraces, their red-earth banks like a staircase. Bullies building a watchtower ripped the stone out of several of the banks. Two days ago a heavy rain brought the red earth of the top three terraces sliding down and buried half the young tea below. The old grower sits dazed in the mud, and the bullies want him to pay for their tower.
column3: 一面坡上修着一级一级的茶梯田，红土田埂像一道道台阶。一伙兵痞为了取石头修碉楼，把田埂上的石头扒走了好几级。前天一场大雨，上面三级梯田的红土全冲了下来，把底下的茶苗埋了一半。种茶的老汉坐在泥里发呆，兵痞还要他赔「碉楼钱」。

column2: The bullies are driven off and the stones carried back. As you help him rebuild the banks, the old man explains: terraces cut a slope into flat steps, so the rain runs off slowly and can't carry the soil away. Pull out the banks and one big storm washes the red earth off the hill, and ten years won't grow it back. Ayan writes it down. The master always talks about soil before he talks about tea, he says.
column3: 兵痞被赶走，石头搬了回来。老汉带着你们重新垒埂，说梯田是把一面坡切成一级级平台，雨水落下来走得慢，土就冲不走；埂一扒，一场大雨就能把红土冲下山，十年也长不回来。阿砚在一旁记下，说夫子讲茶，总是先讲土。

column2: Lead-Mule Barrier
column3: 头骡关

column2: A caravan of swordsmen blocks the forest road, their lead mule in red tassels and a big brass bell standing crosswise in the middle, and nobody is allowed to pass it. By their rule, whoever's lead mule walks in front owns the tea road. Blades out: if you want through, first send your mules to the back.
column3: 林中大路被一支马帮刀客的队伍堵住了，他们的头骡戴着红缨、挂着大铜铃，横在路当中，谁也不许超过去。他们的规矩是，茶路上谁的头骡走在前头，谁就是这条路的主人。刀客们拔了刀，说要过，就先把你们的骡子赶到后头去。

column2: The swordsmen are beaten and their tasselled mule led aside. Their boss is sore but daren't show it. 'Ten years ago another caravan wouldn't give way either,' he grumbles. 'Their lead was a grey horse, more stubborn than our mule.' That caravan went into the fog, he says, and the grey came back on its own later. Gonbu the horse dealer took it in.
column3: 刀客们败了，红缨头骡也被牵到了路边。马锅头不服气，又不敢不服，嘟囔着说：「十年前也有一支马帮不肯让道，头马是一匹青马，比我们的骡子还犟。」他说那支马帮进了雾，那匹青马后来自己回来了，被番人马贩贡布牵走了。

column2: Horse-God Shrine
column3: 马神祠

column2: In the wood stands a tiny shrine to the horse god, where muleteers tie a strip of red cloth before a long journey. Deserters have taken it over, using the god's statue for target practice and the red strips for foot-wrappings. The shrine keeper, a mute young man, is pinned to the ground, still clutching a fistful of strips.
column3: 林子里有一座小小的马神祠，赶马人出远门前都来这里系一根红布条。一伙流兵占了祠，把马神像搬出来当靶子，把布条扯下来裹脚。看祠的是个哑巴小伙子，被他们按在地上，手里还死死攥着一把布条。

column2: The deserters are driven off and the statue set upright. The mute keeper ties the strips back on the beam one by one, signing as he goes. One is very old, embroidered with a grey horse and the character 'Jiu'. He points east, mimes riding back, then shakes his head. The horse came back. The man didn't.
column3: 流兵被撵走，马神像扶了回去。哑巴小伙子比划着，把攥着的布条一根根系回祠梁上。其中一根很旧，绣着一匹青马和一个「九」字。他指指东边，又做了个骑马回来的手势，再摇摇头。意思是：马回来了，人没回来。

column2: Paper-Cutter's Shed
column3: 裁纸坊

column2: In a tumbledown paper shed out on the open ground, Pu sits under a lamp cutting sheets. He's preparing three hundred Out-of-the-Fog forms, so that when he finds his seal he can stamp them one by one and close his books. Bullies burst in, take him for a banknote printer, grab half and run. Pu gives chase, trips flat, and still hangs on to the other half.
column3: 野地里一间破纸坊，老蒲在里头点着灯，一张张地裁纸。他要预备三百张出雾单，等印找回来，一张一张补盖上，簿子就能合上了。一伙兵痞闯进来，以为他印的是银票，抢了一半就跑，老蒲追出去绊了个跟头，还死死抱着剩下的那一半。

column2: The bullies are run down and every sheet recovered. Pu stacks the three hundred forms neatly to show you. Each has a name written in, copied from the ledger of ten years ago. On the last, the name box is empty. 'That's how it is in the ledger. Three hundred, and the last one with no name. Chief Lu said that one was coming along behind.'
column3: 兵痞被追了回来，纸一张不少。老蒲把三百张出雾单码得整整齐齐给你们看，每一张上都写好了名字，是照着十年前的簿子抄的。最后一张，名字那一栏空着。「簿子上就是这么写的，三百个，最后一个没写名字。陆镖头说，那个人在后头。」

column2: Rubbing Cliff
column3: 拓字崖

column2: At the mountain foot is a cliff carved with an old tea poem in characters as big as grain measures. Ayan is up on the rock taking rubbings for the master's book. Some crossbowmen found him in the way and took his ladder, and now he's stuck halfway up the cliff, still shouting: 'Wait till I finish this character!'
column3: 山脚一面摩崖，崖上刻着一首前人的茶诗，字有斗大。阿砚趴在崖上拓字，要拓回去给夫子补书。一伙山弩手嫌他碍事，把梯子抽走了，他挂在半崖上下不来，还在喊：「等我拓完这一个字！」

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and Ayan is brought down, rubbings and all. The poem's last line reads: 'One bowl drunk, and you recall the road you came.' It's signed by a tea merchant of the old dynasty who crossed the fog. The master says, Ayan tells you, that the Master of the Fog Posts loves tea because tea makes you remember where you came from. 'It's not the tea he wants. He wants the people crossing the fog not to forget where they came from.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走，阿砚连人带拓片被接了下来。诗的最后一句是「一碗喝罢记来路」，落款是前朝一个过雾的茶商。阿砚说，夫子讲过，雾驿主爱茶，是因为茶能叫人想起来路：「他要的不是茶，是让过雾的人别忘了自己从哪儿来。」

column2: Paper-Boat Teahouse
column3: 纸船楼

column2: A stilt-house teahouse stands by the river, windows open on four sides, its customers sipping as they watch fog wander over the water. Today caravan swordsmen surround it. Every day the landlady floats a paper boat of tea leaves down the river, 'sending tea' to the Master of the Fog Posts, and it's spoiling their tea-hauling business. She denies it, and they mean to tear the place down.
column3: 河边一座吊脚楼茶馆，四面敞着窗，茶客们一边喝茶一边看雾在河面上走。今天茶馆被一伙马帮刀客围了，他们说老板娘每天往河里放一只纸船，船里装着茶叶，是给雾驿主「送茶」，坏了他们运茶的买卖。老板娘不认，刀客就要拆楼。

column2: The swordsmen are chased off, and the landlady sets another paper boat on the water from her window, a pinch of tea inside, and it drifts away into the fog. An old scholar taught her ten years ago, she says: the Master of the Fog Posts never shows himself, only accepts tea, and 'the fog goes easy on those who've sent it tea'. On the side of the boat are two words: 'A Traveller.'
column3: 刀客们被打跑，老板娘在窗口又放下一只纸船，船里一撮茶叶，顺着水漂进了雾里。她说这是十年前一个老学究教她的：雾驿主不见人，只收茶，「送过茶的人，雾里不为难」。纸船的船帮上写着两个字：「过客」。

column2: Tea Bureau Store
column3: 茶马司仓

column2: A high-walled warehouse by the river, the old Tea and Horse Bureau's official store, sealed ten years ago. Picked troops now live in it, guarding it for the Fog Posts: swordsmen on the gate, crossbowmen on the walls, a volley for anyone who comes one step closer. The Fog Posts' seal strip is pasted across the door, dated the Dingwei year.
column3: 河边一座高墙大仓，是前朝茶马司的官仓，十年前封了门。如今仓里住着一伙替雾驿看仓的精兵，刀客守门，弩手站墙，谁靠近一步就是一排箭。仓门上贴着雾驿的封条，封条上的日子是丁未年。

column2: The store's doors swing open on rack after neat rack of tea bricks, all halves from the tea-firing works. These, say the guards, are the 'homecoming tea' the Master keeps for the Qianli people. 'He says they'll want a drink when they come back, and they're not to drink stale tea, so it's replaced with new every year.' On the innermost rack, one space is empty.
column3: 官仓的门开了，里面整整齐齐码着茶砖，一架一架都是焙茶坊压的半块。守仓的精兵说，这是雾驿主替千里号存的「回程茶」：「他说那些人回来时要喝，不能叫他们喝陈的，每年换一回新茶。」最里面一架，空着一格。

column2: Three-Line Stone
column3: 三痕石

column2: At a fork in the wood a ring of boulders, strewn with dung and ash, marks an old caravan halt. Crossbowmen lie in ambush inside it: anyone leading a horse past, shoot the horse first, then rob the rider. On a big bluestone in the middle, someone has scratched three lines with a horseshoe nail: one east, one south, one back the way you came.
column3: 林中一处岔道，几块大石围成一圈，石头上落满了马粪和炭灰，是马帮歇脚的老地方。一伙山弩手在石圈里设了伏，凡是牵马路过的，先射马，再抢人。石圈中间一块大青石上，有人用马掌钉划了三道线，一道往东，一道往南，一道往回。

column2: The crossbowmen scatter and the ring is quiet again. Gonbu's hand says the Qianli train scratched those lines ten years ago. East was the fog road the main body would take, back was for the messengers. The south line is the shallowest. 'As if whoever cut it wasn't sure either.'
column3: 山弩手被打散，石圈清静了。贡布的伙计说，那三道线是十年前千里号划的：往东的是大队要走的雾路，往回的是送信的人，往南的那一道，划得最浅，「像是划的人自己也拿不准」。

column2: Tail-Croppers' Camp
column3: 剪尾营

column2: A big camp in the wood belongs to deserters who do nothing but steal horses. Over a hundred are penned inside, tails cropped so their owners won't know them. Stolen horses come in three grades: the best sold to the Fog Posts, the middling kept for riding, the old ones eaten. Spearmen guard the pens, crossbowmen the woods, and the swordsmen go out stealing.
column3: 林子里一座大营，是专偷马的流兵，营里圈着上百匹偷来的马，马尾巴都剪了，免得原主人认出来。偷来的马分三等：好的送去雾驿那边卖，次的留着自己骑，老的杀了吃肉。营里枪手守栏，弩手守林，刀客出去偷。

column2: The camp is broken and the horses let loose into the wood; the ones that know their way home trot off. A wooden board on the pen records the buyer's terms: 'Fog Posts. Greys wanted. Nothing else.' Every year, the deserter chief says, the Fog Posts ask whether he has a grey. 'Like they're looking for one horse in particular.'
column3: 大营破了，马一匹匹放回林子，认得家的自己跑回去了。马栏上挂着一块木牌，写着买主的话：「雾驿，要青马，别的不要。」流兵头子说雾驿那边每年都来问有没有青马，「像是在找一匹特定的马」。

column2: Seal-Asking Wood
column3: 讨印林

column2: In the wood a troop of native soldiers has stopped Pu. He brandishes his Into-the-Fog seal: he's the tea pass clerk and demands to see the Master of the Fog Posts. The soldiers look at his seal, then at the empty cord on his belt, and without a word lower their bamboo spears across his path. Pu hops with rage. 'Where's my seal? Your Master took my Out seal and he's just going to keep it?'
column3: 林子里一队土兵拦住了老蒲。老蒲举着他那方入雾印，说自己是茶关的税吏，要见雾驿主。土兵们看了看印，又看了看他腰上那根空印绶，一句话不说，只把竹枪横了过来。老蒲气得直跳脚：「我的印呢？你们雾驿主拿了我的出雾印，就不还了？」

column2: You beat the soldiers back. One of the wounded says the Out seal hangs round the neck of their camp captain in the wood, a gift from the Master, to stamp each person who leaves the fog. 'But in ten years the captain hasn't stamped once. The Master said: until the count comes right, nobody leaves the fog.'
column3: 土兵被你们打退。一个受了伤的土兵说，出雾印挂在他们林中营头的脖子上，营头说那是雾驿主赏的，每有一个人出雾，就盖一下：「可这十年，营头一下也没盖过。雾驿主说了，数没对上，谁也不许出雾。」

column2: Tea King Tree
column3: 茶王树

column2: At the end of a blind track at the mountain foot grows an old tea tree so thick it takes three people to circle its trunk. Over a thousand years old, they say, the ancestor of every tea tree on the road. Elite crossbowmen guard it from a tower they've built at its foot; next spring they mean to dig it up whole as a birthday gift for the Master of the Fog Posts. They drove off the old grower who tended it, and every day he stands on the slope watching from afar.
column3: 山脚死路尽头长着一棵老茶树，树干要三个人才合抱得过来，说是有一千多岁了，是这条茶路上所有茶树的祖宗。一伙山弩手的精锐守着它，在树下修了碉楼，打算明年开春把它整棵挖走，送给雾驿主当寿礼。树下的老茶农被他们赶走了，天天在山坡上远远地望。

column2: You pull down the tower and the old tree is saved. The grower comes back and buries a packet of new tea at its roots. It was under this tree, he says, that Master Wen wrote the last line of the fog chapter. Escort chief Lu Jiu rested here too, and put a leaf in his mouth, and said: 'I'll know this taste even up on the snow mountains.'
column3: 碉楼被你们推倒了，老茶树保住了。老茶农回来，在树根下埋了一包新茶。他说当年温夫子就在这棵树下写完了雾篇的最后一句，镖头陆九也在这棵树下歇过脚，摘了一片叶子含在嘴里，说：「这个味道，以后到了雪山上也认得。」

column2: Running Letter Plain
column3: 追信原

column2: Out on the plain Ayan catches up with you, sweating, a letter Master Wen has just finished tucked in his coat for you to take to the Master of the Fog Posts. But bullies have caught him on the way, sure there's a banknote inside, and pinned him to search him. Ayan curls round the letter, yelling: 'It's the Classic of Tea! It's tea writing for the Master of the Fog Posts!'
column3: 野地里阿砚追上了你们，跑得满头是汗，怀里揣着温夫子刚写完的一封信，要你们带给雾驿主。路上一伙兵痞截住了他，以为信里夹着银票，把他按在地上搜身。阿砚死死护着信，嘴里喊：「是茶经！是给雾驿主的茶经！」

column2: The bullies are driven off and Ayan hands you the letter. 'For the Master of the Fog Posts, by his own hand.' Inside is a single page, the last passage of the fog chapter: 'Tea remembers the mountain, people remember the road. The fog remembers people; let people remember the fog too.' The master says, Ayan tells you, that the Master of the Fog Posts has counted people for ten years. It's time someone remembered him.
column3: 兵痞被赶走，阿砚把信交给你们。信封上写着「雾驿主亲启」，里面只有一页纸，是《茶经·雾篇》的最后一段：「茶记山，人记路；雾记人，人亦记雾。」阿砚说，夫子讲了，雾驿主数了十年的人，也该有人记一记他了。

column2: Per-Hoof Road
column3: 过蹄道

column2: On the high road to the horse market a gang of bullies is charging muleteers a 'hoof toll': one copper per hoof, four hooves four coppers, and a mule lame in one leg still pays for four. Anyone who won't pay has his animals seized and lined up by the road: 'requisitioned for the crown'.
column3: 去马市的大路上，一伙兵痞拦着赶马人收「过蹄钱」：一个蹄子一个铜板，四个蹄子四个铜板，瘸了一条腿的骡子也照四个算。不交的就把马扣下，牵到路边一字排开，说是「官家征马」。

column2: The bullies are chased off and the seized animals returned. The horse market has been dead for ten years, an old muleteer tells you, and nobody dares go. When the old horse registrar died, someone took the horse register. Without it no sale has any proof, and a horse stolen back and forth belongs to nobody anyone can name.
column3: 兵痞被赶走，扣下的马还给了赶马人。一个老赶马人说，马市已经荒了十年，没人敢去：老马官死后，马籍册被人拿走了，没有马籍，买卖就没有凭据，一匹马偷来偷去，谁也说不清是谁的。

column2: Headcount Shoal
column3: 数人滩

column2: Fog has risen by the river, and a row of native soldiers stands in it. They don't block the road or take anything. They count each traveller, one, two, three, and only let them go when the count is done. Get it wrong and they start over; a dozen-strong caravan has been counted back and forth for two hours. When someone tries to push past, every bamboo spear comes up at once.
column3: 河边起了雾，雾里站着一排土兵，不拦路，也不抢东西，只是一个一个地数过路的人：「一、二、三……」数完了才放行。数错了就从头再数，一支十几人的马帮被他们来回数了一个时辰。有人不耐烦想冲过去，土兵的竹枪就一齐竖了起来。

column2: The soldiers scatter, dropping a bamboo tally stick covered in notches. A young one you catch says they serve the Fog Posts, and the Master's rule is to count everyone who crosses and report the number. 'Ten years ago a count came out wrong once. The Master still hasn't got over it.'
column3: 土兵被打散，丢下一根刻满了道道的竹签。抓到的一个小土兵说，他们是雾驿的人，雾驿主的规矩是凡过雾的都要数，数清楚了报上去：「十年前有一回数出了错，雾驿主到今天也没消气。」

column2: Grey Horse Stall
column3: 青马栏

column2: In highland horse dealer Gonbu's stall at the mountain foot, dozens of good horses have sold, leaving one old grey with half its teeth gone that nobody wants. Lately Gonbu can't sell anything at all: a band of caravan swordsmen has put it about that anyone who buys from him crosses the Fog Posts. What they want is the old grey, and Gonbu won't sell it at any price.
column3: 山脚下番人马贩贡布的马栏里，几十匹好马都卖光了，只剩一匹老青马，牙口老得掉了一半，没人要。可贡布这几天连一匹马也卖不出去了：一伙马帮刀客放话，谁买他的马，就是跟雾驿过不去。他们要的就是那匹老青马，贡布死活不卖。

column2: The swordsmen are chased off and Gonbu's stall opens for business again. The old grey studies you a long while, snorts, walks over by itself and rests its head on your cart, and won't be shooed away. Gonbu sighs. 'It's chosen you. Ten years it hasn't let anyone ride it, only carry loads. It knows the road. Go where it takes you.'
column3: 刀客们被赶跑，贡布的马栏重新开了张。老青马盯着你们看了半天，打了个响鼻，自己走过来，把头往你们的车上一搁，赶都赶不走。贡布叹了口气：「它挑了你们。十年了，它不让任何人骑，只肯驮东西。它认得路，你们跟着它走吧。」

column2: White-Pole Wood
column3: 白杆林

column2: Along the old road through the wood, every hundred paces, stands a white-painted pole for caravans to steer by in the fog. Deserters have been chopping them down for firewood and planting new ones at the forks, luring passing caravans into a gully where they wait in ambush. Two caravans have already lost their loads there.
column3: 林中的古道两旁每隔百步立着一根白漆木杆，是给雾天赶路的马帮认路用的。一伙流兵把木杆一根根砍了当柴烧，又在岔路上另立了几根，引着过路的马帮走进他们设伏的山沟。已经有两支马帮在沟里丢了货。

column2: The deserters are beaten off, the false poles pulled up and the true ones replanted. Finding your way in fog, says the old pole-setter, is a matter of poles, bells and horses; human eyes are the least use of all. He lowers his voice. 'There are poles on the Fog Post side too. Only those ones move a little by themselves every night.'
column3: 流兵被打跑，假杆子拔了，真杆子重新立了起来。立杆的老匠人说，雾里认路，靠的是杆，是铃，是马，人眼最不中用。他压低了声音：「雾驿那头也有杆子，只是那头的杆子，每天夜里会自己挪一挪。」

column2: Bellmaker's Hold
column3: 铃匠寨

column2: In the wood lives a coppersmith who casts harness bells; most caravans' bells are his work, and no two sound alike, so a muleteer can tell whose train is coming through the fog by ear. Crossbowmen are holding him, ordering bells that sound exactly like other people's so they can slip into a train and steal horses. He casts one and smashes it, casts one and smashes it, until his hands are swollen.
column3: 林子里有一户打马铃的铜匠，马帮的铃大半出自他手，每一只铃声音都不同，赶马人隔着雾就能听出是谁家的马队。一伙山弩手把铜匠扣了，逼他打一批跟别家一模一样的铃，好混进马队里偷马。铜匠打一只砸一只，手都砸肿了。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the coppersmith freed. Then he hears the old bell on the grey's neck and goes still. 'I made that for the Qianli train ten years ago. Three of them, each lower than the last.' The grey wears the lowest, the one hung on the very last horse in the line. 'The rearguard.'
column3: 山弩手被打跑，铜匠放了出来。他听见老青马脖子上那只旧铃，愣住了：「这是我十年前给千里号打的，一共三只，声音一只比一只低。」老青马戴的是最低的那只，拴在队伍最后一匹马的脖子上，「是压阵的」。

column2: Tripwire Wood
column3: 绊索林

column2: The deeper into the wood, the thicker the fog, until the front of the line can't see the back. Deserters have strung trip ropes through the fog, waiting for a caravan to go down so they can rob it. Suddenly the old grey stops, nose to the ground, and won't be led a step further. From the fog ahead comes a deserter's whisper: 'Here they come. Soon as the horses drop...'
column3: 林子越走雾越浓，前面的人看不见后面的人。一伙流兵在雾里设了绊马索，专等马队摔倒了来抢。老青马走着走着忽然停下，鼻子贴着地嗅，怎么牵也不走了。前头的雾里传来流兵压低了嗓子的说话声：「来了来了，等马一倒……」

column2: The deserters pounce on nothing and you wrap them up from behind. The grey steps round every trip rope as if it knew exactly where they were, then leads you to an old tree with a board nailed to it, rotted by the fog until only a few words remain: '...train passed here. The horse knows the way...' The grey stands under the tree a long time before it will go on.
column3: 流兵扑了个空，被你们反手包了饺子。老青马绕开了每一道绊马索，像是早就知道在哪儿。它把你们领到一棵老树下，树上钉着一块被雾泡烂了的木牌，只剩几个字：「……号过此，马识途……」老青马在树下站了很久，才肯继续往前走。

column2: Seal-Box Eddy
column3: 印匣湾

column2: In the still water of a river bend a wooden box floats, wedged among driftwood. A few deserters on the bank have been poking at it with bamboo poles forever without reaching it, and they won't wade in, because a huge catfish lives there that once bit off one of their toes. Pu knows it at a glance from far off. 'My seal box! That's my seal box!'
column3: 河湾的死水里漂着一只木匣，卡在一堆浮木中间。几个流兵站在岸上，拿竹竿够了半天也够不着，又不敢下水，因为水里有一条大鲶鱼，咬掉过他们一个人的脚趾头。老蒲远远一看就认出来了：「印匣！我的印匣！」

column2: The deserters are chased off and you fish the box out. It's empty, but under the lining is a slip of paper in Lu Jiu's hand: 'The seal has reached the Fog Posts. Lent to the Master for a while; returned when the count is full.' Pu holds the slip a long time before he speaks. 'When the count is full... How many is he going to stamp?'
column3: 流兵被赶跑，你们捞上了木匣。匣子是空的，匣底却压着一张字条，是陆九的笔迹：「印到雾驿，借雾驿主一用，盖足了数就还。」老蒲捧着字条，半天才开口：「盖足了数……他到底要盖多少？」

column2: Deer-Seal Camp
column3: 鹿印营

column2: A large native-soldier camp in the wood, commanded by a man with a face full of scars and a stone seal round his neck, its knob a deer looking back. Hundreds of soldiers, coming and going in the fog, not saying a word to outsiders. Pu stands outside the camp and bellows: 'That's my seal!' The captain touches the seal at his throat, shakes his head, and waves his men to shoot.
column3: 林子里一座土兵大营，营头是个满脸刀疤的汉子，脖子上挂着一方石印，印钮是一只回头的鹿。营里几百个土兵，雾里来，雾里去，见了外人连话也不说。老蒲站在营外大喊：「那是我的印！」营头摸了摸脖子上的印，摇摇头，挥手让土兵放箭。

column2: The camp breaks and the captain, taken prisoner, hands over the seal. Pu's hands shake as he holds it. He turns it over: the red clay kiln's paste is still on its face, ten years dry. With it is a stamp sheet crowded with two hundred and ninety-nine red impressions. 'The Master stopped there,' says the captain. 'He said the last stamp has to wait till that person arrives.'
column3: 大营被你们打散，营头被俘，把印交了出来。老蒲捧着印，手抖得厉害，翻过来一看印面，红泥窑的印泥还在，干了十年。印旁还有一张盖过印的底单，密密麻麻二百九十九个红印。营头说：「雾驿主盖到这里就停了手，说最后一下，得等那个人到了再盖。」

column2: Rest-Hoof Lodge
column3: 歇蹄店

column2: The grey leads you to a caravan inn at the mountain foot and heads straight for the stable, as if coming home. But bullies hold the inn, its stable full of their stolen horses and the guest rooms roaring with gambling. The landlady, locked in the kitchen, calls through the crack of the door: 'Is that the grey? Has it come back?'
column3: 老青马领着你们到了山脚一处马帮客栈，自己就往马厩里走，像回了家。可客栈被一伙兵痞占着，马厩里拴的全是他们偷来的马，客房里赌钱的吆喝声震天。老板娘被锁在灶房里，隔着门缝喊：「是那匹青马？它回来了？」

column2: The bullies are thrown out, and the landlady runs out and weeps with her arms round the grey's neck. The Qianli train spent its last night here ten years ago, she says, and the grey was the chief's own mount. Later it came back alone, stood all night at the inn door, and left again the next day, never to return. 'I thought it had died in the fog.'
column3: 兵痞被撵走，老板娘冲出来抱着老青马的脖子哭了一场。她说十年前千里号在这里歇过最后一夜，老青马是镖头的坐骑；后来马自己回来了，在店门口站了一宿，第二天又自己走了，再没回来过：「我还以为它死在雾里了。」

column2: Under the gaming tables: two chests of coppers, a bundle of halters and thirty jin of barley flour. The landlady bakes you a stack of flatbreads with the flour. A welcome-home dinner for the grey, she says.
column3: 兵痞的赌桌底下搜出两箱铜钱、一捆马笼头、三十斤青稞面。老板娘拿青稞面给你们烙了一摞饼，说是老青马的接风饭。

column2: Every time you pass, the landlady keeps a trough of the best beans for the grey and a pot of hot soup for you. Whenever the grey turns up, she says, business picks up.
column3: 每次路过，老板娘都给老青马留一槽最好的豆料，也给你们留一锅热汤；她说老青马一来，店里的生意就好。

column2: Fog-Reader's Hut
column3: 看雾婆

column2: Halfway up the mountain lives an old woman who reads the fog, and every caravan asks her before going in: when will it rise today, when will it lift? Native soldiers surround her hut. By order of the Master of the Fog Posts, she is to read no more fog for anyone. Shut inside, she still points out through the window for you: 'See? The fog is all pooled in the valley bottom, like a bowl filled to the brim with milk.'
column3: 山腰上住着一个看雾的老婆婆，马帮进雾前都来问她：今天雾几时起，几时散。一伙土兵把她的小屋围了，说雾驿主有令，不许她再给人看雾。婆婆被困在屋里，隔着窗子还在给你们指：「看见没有？雾都积在谷底，像一碗倒满了的奶。」

column2: The soldiers are beaten back. On a clear, still night, the old woman says, the ground on the slopes cools first, and the cold air slides down the hillsides and pools in the valley bottom; the moisture in the valley chills and turns to fog. When the sun comes up and warms the valley, the fog burns away. 'The Master's soldiers are fearsome in the fog. Come noon, they're nothing.' Strike at midday, she tells you.
column3: 土兵被打退。婆婆说，晴天没风的夜里，山坡上的地先凉下来，冷气顺着坡往下淌，积在谷底，谷里的水汽一冷就凝成了雾；太阳出来把谷底晒暖了，雾就散了。「雾驿主的兵在雾里厉害，到了晌午就不行了。」她叫你们挑晌午动手。

column2: First Fog Post
column3: 头雾驿

column2: By the river stands the first of the nine Fog Posts, a stilt house of bamboo and timber, horses stabled below, travellers lodged above, a drum hanging by the door. Bullies have taken it. The post-keepers have been driven out to huts on the shoal, the drum is being used as a wine tub, and when caravans knock, the bullies tip their foot-washing water on them from upstairs.
column3: 河边是九座雾驿里的头一座，一座竹木搭的吊脚楼，楼下拴马，楼上住人，门口挂着一面鼓。如今驿站被一伙兵痞占了，驿卒被赶到河滩上搭草棚，鼓被兵痞拿去装酒。来往的马帮在门口敲门，兵痞就从楼上往下泼洗脚水。

column2: The bullies go into the river; the keepers move back upstairs and wipe the drum clean and hang it up again. The nine Fog Posts were built to give people crossing the fog a rest and tell them the hour, the old keeper says. Then ten years ago the Master came, and since then the posts only count people and never rest them. 'Today, at last, someone can rest here again.'
column3: 兵痞被扔进了河里，驿卒们回到楼上，把鼓擦干净挂了回去。老驿卒说，九座雾驿本是给过雾的人歇脚、报时的，十年前雾驿主来了，驿站就只管数人，不管歇脚了：「今天总算又能让人歇一歇了。」

column2: From the bullies' stores: ten jars of sticky-rice wine, six hams, a crate of candles, a bundle of straw rain capes, and a battered gong. The gong is the post's own, say the keepers; they'll keep it for calling the hours in fog.
column3: 楼里抄出兵痞的存货：糯米酒十坛、火腿六只、一箱蜡烛、一捆蓑衣，还有一面破锣。驿卒说锣是他们自己的，留着雾天报时用。

column2: Every time you pass, the keepers boil you a pot of ginger broth and beat a roll on the drum. An old Fog Post custom, they say: when the drum sounds, those out in the fog know someone here is waiting for them.
column3: 每次路过，驿卒都给你们烧一锅姜汤，敲一通鼓，说是雾驿的老规矩：鼓一响，雾里的人就知道这里有人在等。

column2: Saddle-Bone Cave
column3: 鞍骨洞

column2: In a cave at the end of the wood lives a gang of deserters who steal saddles. They strip the leather for boots, burn the wooden trees for firewood and melt the brass fittings to sell. Saddle frames are heaped like a small hill at the cave mouth, where spearmen sit warming themselves at a fire made of them.
column3: 林子尽头的山洞里窝着一伙流兵，专偷马鞍。他们把偷来的鞍子剥了皮做靴子，木架拿去烧火，铜饰熔了卖钱。洞口堆着小山一样的鞍架，一伙枪手守在洞口烤火，烤的正是鞍架。

column2: The deserters are driven from the cave and the good saddles returned. Under the heap is a half-burned stack of old books: the horse market's missing register, every horse's age, coat and owner written down clear. With this, the horse market can open again.
column3: 流兵被赶出洞，好鞍子还给了失主。洞里还压着一摞烧了一半的旧册子，是马市失踪的马籍册：哪匹马、几岁、什么毛色、主人是谁，都记得清清楚楚。有了它，马市就能重开了。

column2: Family of Six
column3: 六口渔家

column2: A fishing family by the river, five of them. The native soldiers have counted them three times and got six every time. Their leader has decided the extra one 'followed them out of the fog' and must be taken away. The mother hugs her children one by one and counts them for him: one, two, three, four, five. The soldier counts. Six again.
column3: 河边一户打鱼人家，一家五口，土兵来数了三遍，回回都数出六个。领头的土兵认定多出来的那一个是「雾里跟出来的」，非要带走。当娘的把孩子们挨个搂着数给他们看：一、二、三、四、五。土兵一数，又是六。

column2: You drive the soldiers off and do your own count: five people, plus the big yellow dog crouched under the eaves. Six. The fisherman doesn't know whether to laugh or cry. But the Fog Post men really are terrified of miscounting, the old man says. 'Ten years ago they counted a mule train and came out one short, and the Master sent the whole post into the fog as punishment.'
column3: 土兵被你们赶跑了。你们数了数，五个人，加上屋檐下蹲着的那条大黄狗，正好六个。打鱼的哭笑不得。可老渔夫说，雾驿的人是真怕数错：「十年前他们数一支马帮，少了一个，雾驿主就把整座驿站的人都罚进了雾里。」

column2: Third Sister's Whip
column3: 三娘鞭

column2: Out in the open a band of caravan swordsmen is robbing another caravan; the two strings of mules are tangled together, bells clanging. The victims are few, led by a young woman in a blue head-cloth with a riding whip, standing alone in front of her lead mule and lashing the swordsmen back. But there are too many of them.
column3: 野地里一伙马帮刀客正在抢另一支马帮，两边的骡子搅成一团，铃铛响成一片。被抢的那支马帮人少，领头的是个年轻女子，头上包着青布，提着一根马鞭，一个人挡在头骡前面，鞭子抽得刀客们直往后退，可架不住人多。

column2: You drive the swordsmen off. The woman is He Sanniang. Her husband was a caravan boss who died of fever on the road last year, and she took the caravan over. 'He promised people their goods. Somebody has to deliver them.' If the horse market ever opens, she'll be the first to register.
column3: 刀客被你们打跑了。女马锅头叫何三娘，丈夫是个马锅头，去年病死在路上，她就接着把这支马帮带了下去：「他答应人家的货，总得有人送到。」她说马市要是开了，她第一个去登记。

column2: Mule-Seizure Post
column3: 扣骡卡

column2: He Sanniang's caravan has barely reached the mountain foot when a checkpoint stops it. The deserters on duty declare her lead mule 'stolen property', lead it off on the spot, and keep three loads of her goods for good measure. The mule is called Black Bean; her husband raised it by hand, and the bell round its neck he tied himself. Without the lead mule, the rest won't take a step.
column3: 何三娘的马帮刚到山脚，就被一道卡子拦住了。守卡的流兵说她的头骡是「贼赃」，当场牵走，又扣了她三驮货。那头骡叫黑豆，是她男人生前一手养大的，脖子上挂着他亲手系的铃。没了头骡，后面的骡子一步也不肯走。

column2: You beat the deserters back and recover the three loads, but Black Bean is already gone into the hills. A note pinned to the checkpoint post reads: 'Good mules to the camp behind the mountain, to trade for Fog Post passes.' He Sanniang tucks her whip into her belt. 'I'm going to get it back.'
column3: 流兵被打退，三驮货抢了回来，黑豆却早被牵进了山里。卡子的木桩上贴着一张条子：「好骡送往山后大营，换雾驿的路引。」何三娘把马鞭往腰里一插：「我去把它要回来。」

column2: Horse-Washing Brook
column3: 洗马溪

column2: By a brook in the wood lives the horse-washing woman. Before a long trip, muleteers bring their animals for her to wash, for a safe road. Some crossbowmen have dammed the brook and charge for every wash. At the water's edge the old grey stops and stretches its neck toward her, and when she sees it, the wooden ladle falls from her hand into the stream.
column3: 林中小溪边住着一个洗马婆，赶马人出远门前把马牵来让她洗一遍，图个一路平安。几个山弩手把溪水拦了，要洗马的先交钱。老青马一到溪边就不走了，伸着脖子往洗马婆那边够。洗马婆看见它，手里的木瓢掉进了水里。

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off and the brook runs free. The washing woman washes the grey from nose to tail until it snorts with pleasure. Ten years ago the chief brought it here to be washed, she says, and left a message: 'If it ever walks back on its own, wash it once more for me, and tell it it doesn't have to wait any longer.' When she's said it, the grey stands in the brook for a long, long time.
column3: 山弩手被赶跑，溪水又流了起来。洗马婆给老青马从头到尾洗了一遍，洗得它直打响鼻。她说十年前镖头牵它来洗过，交代过一句：「它要是自己走回来，替我再洗一回，告诉它，不用再等了。」老青马听完，在溪里站了很久。

column2: Great Mule Fair
column3: 骡马大集

column2: The great mule and horse fair on the open ground has lain dead for ten years, its stone hitching posts still standing, its stables half collapsed. Caravan swordsmen and bullies have taken it together: every horse is 'stolen', every mule 'confiscated', the good ones led off and the bad ones sold back to their owners at a premium. They tore down the registrar's office and used the stone for their own corrals.
column3: 野地上的骡马大集荒了十年，拴马的石桩还在，马棚塌了一半。一伙马帮刀客和兵痞合伙占了集，谁的马都说是偷的，谁的骡子都要「充公」，好马牵走，劣马高价卖回给原主。马官的衙门被他们拆了，石料拿去垒了自家的马圈。

column2: Swordsmen and bullies alike are driven out and the fair comes alive again. With the recovered register, the market reopens its books, and He Sanniang is first in line to enter her caravan. The pastures need stone for corrals and the villages need grain; the stone-for-grain trade opens. The new registrar turns to the Dingwei page: 'Qianli train. One grey horse. Owner: Lu Jiu.' Beside it, added later in a small hand: 'Horse returned. Owner not.' At the fair's gate the old grey whinnies once, and you know: it wants to go east.
column3: 刀客和兵痞被你们一并赶走，大集又热闹起来。凭着找回的马籍册，马市重开了登记，何三娘头一个来报了她的马帮。牧场缺石头垒圈，寨子缺粮，石换粮的买卖开了张。新马官翻到马籍册丁未年那一页：「千里号，青马一匹，主陆九。」旁边后来添了一行小字：「马归，人未归。」老青马在集口嘶了一声，你们知道，它要往东去了。

column2: Sunning-Snake Scree
column3: 晒蛇滩

column2: Deep in the miasma wood lies a scree of broken rock where snakes by the hundred, by the thousand, nest in the cracks and cover the path whenever the weather turns warm. Pu has his seal back and wants a shortcut to have it out with the Master of the Fog Posts, and the shortcut runs across this scree. Snakes bask on every rock, tongues flickering. Some deserters who catch snakes for wine are there too, and seeing Pu clutching something, they decide it's gold and close in.
column3: 瘴林深处一片烂石滩，石缝里窝着成百上千条毒蛇，一到暖和天就爬满了路。老蒲拿回了印，要抄近路去找雾驿主讨个说法，偏偏要穿过这片石滩。蛇在石头上晒太阳，一条条吐着信子；滩边还有几个捕蛇泡酒的流兵，见老蒲手里攥着东西，以为是金子，也围了上来。

column2: The snakes are driven back into the cracks and the deserters run, and Pu finally gets across. But under that rubble is where the snakes have always wintered, and the sun keeps the stones warm; they come back every year, and the scree will need clearing again before long.
