At the far edge Pu turns round. 'Three hundred forms, and I've stamped two hundred and ninety-nine. The last one, I'm going to ask the Master who it's for.'
column3: 蛇被赶回石缝，流兵也跑了，老蒲总算过了石滩。可这片烂石底下是蛇冬眠的老窝，石头又被太阳晒得暖，蛇年年都回来，过一阵子还得再清一回。老蒲站在滩头回过身来：「三百张单子，我盖了二百九十九张。最后一张，我去问雾驿主，该盖给谁。」

column2: Grey Horse Ridge
column3: 青马岭

column2: The grey leads you up into the mountains to a ridge with a big camp on it: caravan swordsmen who buy horses for the Fog Posts, several hundred strong. Word that a grey is coming has turned out the whole camp, blades drawn, crossbows spanned, nobody getting past. Their chief says the Master of the Fog Posts has named his price: one grey horse for a hundred good ones.
column3: 老青马领着你们往山里走，走到一道山梁前，梁上扎着一座大营。营里是替雾驿收马的马帮刀客，好几百人，听说有匹青马往这边来了，全营都出来了，刀出鞘，弩上弦，谁也不放过去。他们的头目说，雾驿主出过价：一匹青马，换一百匹好马。

column2: The camp is smashed and the swordsmen flee in all directions. Captured, their chief admits the Master doesn't want the grey to ride. He wants 'to shut the road it led back'. 'Any road that grey has walked, the fog can't close.' The grey ignores him entirely and walks on deeper along the ridge.
column3: 大营被打垮了，刀客们四散逃命。头目被俘后老实交代，雾驿主要这匹青马，不是要骑，是要「把它领回来的那条路关上」：「青马走过的路，雾就封不住。」老青马不理他，自顾往山梁深处走了。

column2: Homesick Camp
column3: 思乡营

column2: A big native-soldier camp out in the open, where nobody sleeps at night; they sit by the fires playing bamboo flutes, all tunes from the mountain villages to the west. They guard the gate and let no one east, but when the fighting starts their hearts aren't in it and their bolts fly crooked. One old soldier stops playing mid-tune and shouts into the fog: 'The drum at Bronze Drum Hold, did it sound?'
column3: 野地里一座土兵大营，营里的人夜里不睡觉，坐在营火边吹竹笛，吹的都是西边山寨里的调子。他们守着营门，谁也不许往东走，可打起仗来却心不在焉，箭射得歪歪扭扭。有个老土兵吹着吹着就停了，冲雾里喊：「铜鼓寨的鼓，是不是响过了？」

column2: The camp is scattered, and the soldiers just sit on the ground; not one of them wants to run. They're the troop the chieftain sent ten years ago to escort the mule train into the fog. When the train came out one short, the Master kept them back. 'He said when that one is found, he'll let us go home.' They ask you to take word back to Bronze Drum Hold: everyone's still here, everyone's still alive.
column3: 大营被你们打散了，土兵们坐在地上，没一个想跑。他们是十年前土司派来护送马帮进雾的那一队，出雾的时候少了一个人，雾驿主就把他们留下了：「他说，等找到那一个，再放我们回去。」他们托你们捎个话回铜鼓寨：人都还在，都还活着。

column2: Mistaken Camp
column3: 错认营

column2: A troop of native soldiers sees you from afar, throws down their spears and drops to their knees: 'The Master of the Fog Posts has come back!' None of them has ever seen what he looks like; they only heard he would one day come from the west at the head of a company. Before you can explain, their crossbowmen decide you're impostors and loose a ragged volley, and the kneelers and the shooters start fighting each other first.
column3: 一伙土兵远远望见你们，扔下竹枪就跪了一地：「雾驿主回来了！」原来他们从没见过雾驿主的模样，只听说他会带着一支队伍从西边来。你们刚想解释，营里的弩手又认定你们是冒充的，一阵乱箭射过来，跪着的和放箭的就先打了起来。

column2: You knock both factions into submission and they sit together still bickering. They've stood guard in the fog for ten years, says an old soldier, and the Master has never once shown his face; only orders come out of the depths: 'Count people. Wait for one.' They've long since forgotten who it is they're waiting for.
column3: 两拨土兵都被你们打服了，坐在一起吵个没完。一个老土兵说，他们在雾里守了十年，雾驿主一面也没露过，只有命令从雾深处传出来：「数人，等人。」他们早就记不清，等的到底是谁了。

column2: Fog-Map Camp
column3: 雾图营

column2: In a big camp in the wood, deserters have robbed an old map-maker of everything he owned: long scrolls covered in lines. Convinced they're treasure maps, they're checking them sheet by sheet against the land. Crossbowmen hold the gate, and the old man's apprentice hangs from a tree, yelling that they're not treasure maps, they're fog maps.
column3: 林中一座大营，流兵们抢了一个画图老先生的家当：一卷卷画满了线条的长纸，他们以为是藏宝图，正挨张对着找宝。营门口山弩手把守，老先生的徒弟被吊在树上，嚷着那不是藏宝图，是雾图。

column2: The camp breaks up, the maps are recovered, and the apprentice cut down. His name is Xiaoding. His master has been drawing the fog for ten years, he says: where it rises each night, which way it flows, where it clears at dawn. 'Master says fog has roads too. Cold fog runs downhill like water.' A few days ago the master went deep into the wood and never came back.
column3: 大营散了，图收了回来，徒弟也放了下来。他叫小钉，说师父画了十年雾：每天夜里雾从哪儿起，往哪儿流，天亮从哪儿散。「师父说，雾也有路，冷雾跟水一样往低处淌。」师父前几天进了林子深处，就再没回来。

column2: Wind-and-Rain Bridge
column3: 风雨桥

column2: A covered bridge spans the river, its gallery hung all over with wooden tags, each bearing the name of someone who crossed the fog. Native soldiers guard it: to cross, you write your name on a tag and hang it up, and take it down yourself when you come back out. The tags have hung here for centuries, says the old keeper at the bridgehead, and fewer and fewer get taken down. When you won't write your names, the soldiers lower their spears.
column3: 河上一座风雨桥，桥廊里挂满了木牌，每块牌子上写着一个过雾的人名。一伙土兵守着桥，凡要过桥的，先把名字写在牌子上挂起来，出雾回来的再自己摘下。桥头的老驿卒说，牌子挂了几百年，摘下来的越来越少。土兵们见你们不肯写名字，横起了竹枪。

column2: The soldiers fall back. In the deepest part of the gallery hangs a long row of old tags under thick dust, all Qianli names, not one ever taken down. At the end of the row is an empty nail wrapped round with a strip of red cloth, as if kept for someone. Ten years, says the old keeper, and nobody has dared hang a tag on that nail.
column3: 土兵退了。桥廊最深处挂着长长一排旧牌子，落满了灰，都是千里号的名字，一个也没摘过。排尾空着一根钉子，钉子上缠着一圈红布条，像是给谁留的。老驿卒说，十年了，没人敢在那根钉子上挂牌。

column2: Pass-Barter Camp
column3: 换引营

column2: He Sanniang has crept round the mountain alone and found the camp that trades good mules for passes. The deserters are driving a dozen mules up the trail toward the Fog Posts. Black Bean is among them, its bell taken off, a muzzle over its mouth so it can't call. Sanniang whistles once; Black Bean's head snaps up, and the deserters behind draw their blades.
column3: 何三娘一个人摸到了山后，找到了那座拿好骡换路引的营子。营里的流兵正把十几头骡子赶上山道，说要送去雾驿。黑豆就在里头，脖子上的铃被摘了，嘴上套着笼头，叫不出声。何三娘吹了一声口哨，黑豆猛地一扬头，后面的流兵就拔了刀。

column2: The deserters scatter and the dozen mules are saved, all but Black Bean, which snapped its rope and bolted up the trail. At the end of the trail, the camp men say, is a stone keep where the Fog Posts pen all the good mules they collect. He Sanniang picks the discarded bell up off the ground and tucks it inside her coat.
column3: 流兵被打散，十几头骡子都抢了下来，唯独不见黑豆：它挣断了缰绳，顺着山道往上跑了。营里的人说，山道尽头是一座关骡子的石堡，雾驿收的好骡都先关在那里。何三娘捡起地上那只被摘下的铃，揣进了怀里。

column2: Old Horses' Meadow
column3: 老马甸

column2: At the mountain foot lies a high meadow where muleteers turn out their old horses. A horse too old to work is neither killed nor sold; it's brought here and set loose to graze out its days. Crossbowmen have found it and are shooting the horses one by one to salt the meat. The old horses can't run; they huddle in the middle of the meadow in a ring, the very oldest shielded at the centre.
column3: 山脚一片高草甸，是赶马人放老马的地方：走不动了的老马不杀也不卖，牵到这里放了，让它们吃草终老。一伙山弩手发现了这里，正拿弩一匹一匹地射，要把马肉腌了卖。老马们跑不快，挤在草甸中间，围成一圈，把最老的几匹护在当中。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the old horses spread out to graze again. The grey stands at the edge of the meadow, calling back and forth with them across a ditch. One old horse crosses over to lead it in; the grey steps back, turns, and returns to your cart. All old horses end up here at last, Gonbu had said. 'This one still has road left to walk.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走，老马们又散开吃草了。老青马站在草甸边上，跟它们隔着一条沟对嘶了很久。有一匹老马跨过沟来，想领它进去，它退了一步，转身回到你们的车边。贡布说过，老马最后都要来这里，「它是还有路没走完」。

column2: Questioning Camp
column3: 盘问营

column2: A big camp blocks the road east, its banners a jumble: deserters, swordsmen, bullies, all hired by the Master to hold his outer ring. They don't rob. They interrogate. Where from, where to, and are you carrying a grey horse, an Out-of-the-Fog seal, ash from the lodge hearth, the Classic of Tea? One wrong answer and you're held.
column3: 野地里一座大营挡在东去的路上，营里旗号杂乱，流兵、刀客、兵痞都有，是雾驿主雇来守外围的。他们不劫道，只盘问：从哪儿来，往哪儿去，带没带青马，带没带出雾印，带没带锅庄的灰，带没带《茶经》。答错一样，就扣下。

column2: The camp is broken. On the questioning sheet four things are listed plainly: grey horse, Out seal, lodge ash, fog chapter of the Classic of Tea. Ten years ago, the camp captain says, the Master ordered that anyone carrying these be stopped, questioned, and reported to him. 'He said the day all four come together, he'll have to open the gate.'
column3: 大营被你们打散了。营里的盘问单子上，四样东西写得清清楚楚：青马、出雾印、锅庄灰、茶经雾篇。守营的头目说，雾驿主十年前就交代了，凡是带着这四样的人，都要先拦下，问清楚再报给他。「他说，这四样凑齐的那天，他就得开门了。」

column2: Old Saddle Valley
column3: 旧鞍谷

column2: The grey leads you into a valley that seems to go nowhere. At the bottom stands a stone hut, and on the hitching post outside hangs an old saddle. A few crossbowmen live in the hut, sent by the Fog Posts to guard it. When they see the grey they look as if they've seen a ghost and loose all at once. The grey doesn't flinch. It walks straight into the bolts, all the way to the foot of the post.
column3: 老青马领着你们进了一条死胡同似的山谷，谷底一座石屋，屋外的拴马桩上挂着一副旧鞍。几个山弩手住在石屋里，是雾驿派来看守这副鞍子的，见了老青马，像见了鬼，一齐放箭。老青马不躲，迎着箭往前走，一直走到拴马桩底下。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off. The grey rests its head on the old saddle and doesn't move. The saddle is Lu Jiu's. In its bag is a bamboo whistle of a kind made only in the villages to the south, and a note: 'The grey knows the way. Send it back. I'm going up the mountain; the others are going south. Keep an eye on them for me.' The grey stands there until dark. Then it turns by itself and walks toward the Fog Posts. Only now do you understand: all this way, it has been leading you to the Fog Posts' gate.
column3: 山弩手被打跑了。老青马把头搁在旧鞍上，一动不动。鞍是陆九的，鞍袋里有一支南边寨子里才有的竹哨，还有一张字条：「青驹认路，送它回去。我往山上走，大伙往南走，替我看着点。」老青马在那里站到天黑，然后自己转过身，往雾驿的方向走去。你们这才明白，它领着你们走了这一路，是要把你们送到雾驿门口。

column2: Answering Drum Terrace
column3: 回鼓台

column2: At the mountain foot stands a drum terrace with a great hide drum and, beside it, an old drummer half deaf. The nine Fog Posts pass messages by drum, post to post. Some days ago the drum at Bronze Drum Hold in the west sounded once, and the old drummer answered with three beats. Now native soldiers have him under guard for answering without orders, and mean to haul him to the Fog Posts for judgement.
column3: 山脚一座鼓台，台上一面大皮鼓，鼓边坐着一个老鼓手，耳朵已经半聋了。雾驿九座驿站靠鼓传话，一站接一站。前些日子西边铜鼓寨的鼓响了一声，老鼓手回了三声，土兵就把他看了起来，说他私自回鼓，要押去雾驿问罪。

column2: The soldiers are chased off, and the old drummer pats his drum. Three beats is the answer the Master set, he says. It means 'not yet'. For ten years, whenever the west has drummed, he's sent back three. But this time, having sent them, he feels uneasy. 'Ten years I've beaten not yet. Surely one day I get to beat we're coming home?' When you stand before the Master, he asks, put the question to him.
column3: 土兵被赶走，老鼓手拍着鼓说，三声是雾驿主定下的回话，意思是「还不能回」，十年来西边一敲，他就回三声。可这一回他回完了，心里不踏实：「我回了十年的『不能回』，总该有一回，回一声『回来了』吧？」他托你们到了雾驿主跟前，替他问一问。

column2: Silk-Coat Toll
column3: 绸衫卡

column2: A tax booth by the river, the Fog Posts' outer toll. The tax men wear fine silk coats, and seeing you caked in mud they hold their noses and wave you back. 'Paupers going into the fog? Even the fog finds you filthy.' They toss your manifests into the river: the Fog Posts honour only their own seals, everyone else's are void, the tea pass seal included.
column3: 河边一座税亭，是雾驿的外税卡，收税的税丁穿着体面的绸衫，见你们一身泥水，捏着鼻子不让靠近：「穷鬼进雾，雾都嫌脏。」他们把你们的货单扔进河里，说雾驿只认雾驿的印，别处的印一概作废，连茶关的印也算废纸。

column2: The silk-coated tax men kneel at the riverside, fish out your manifests, dry them one by one and hand them back, and brush down your mules into the bargain. When you show them Pu's Into-the-Fog stamp, their chief's face changes. That seal the Master honours. 'The Master says: whoever comes in under this seal must go out under the looking-back deer.'
column3: 绸衫税丁们跪在河边，把货单捞上来，一张张晾干了捧回来，还给你们的骡子刷了毛。你们把货单上老蒲的「入雾」印亮给他们看，税丁头儿脸色一变，说这方印雾驿主认：「雾驿主说过，盖着这方印进来的，出去时都要盖那方回头鹿。」

column2: Unsent Letter Pavilion
column3: 不送亭

column2: At the mountain foot stands a little letter pavilion with ten sealed bamboo tubes stacked inside, one a year, all official dispatches from the Fog Posts to the tea pass in the west, and not one ever sent. Crossbowmen guard it under orders: 'Write the letters. Do not send them.' The old courier paces in circles. 'If they're not to be sent, why write them?'
column3: 山脚一座小小的信亭，亭里堆着十只封好的竹筒，一年一只，都是雾驿发往西边茶关的公文，一只也没送出去。一伙山弩手守着信亭，奉的令是「信照写，不许送」。送信的老驿差急得团团转：「不送，那写它做什么？」

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and you open one tube. Inside is a single line: 'To Pu, clerk of the tea pass: seal retained for now, count not yet right, do not press.' Ten tubes, ten years, the same sentence in each. Every year the Master writes it, the courier says, and every year forbids it to be sent. 'Like a man who wants to say sorry and can't get the words out.'
column3: 山弩手被赶走，你们拆开一只竹筒，里面只有一行字：「茶关税吏蒲某：印暂留，数未对，勿催。」十只竹筒，十年，写的都是这一句。老驿差说，雾驿主每年都写，写完又不让送，「像是想认个错，又开不了口」。

column2: Camp of the Waiting Lantern
column3: 等字营

column2: A great camp in the open, a tall watchtower at its centre, and on the tower a single lantern with one huge character on its paper: 'Wait'. A thousand native soldiers, swordsmen and crossbowmen, the Master's outer host. They don't march out, and they let no one in. They just stand in the fog, all day long.
column3: 野地里一座大营，营中间搭着一座高高的望楼，望楼上挂着一盏灯笼，灯笼纸上写着一个大大的「等」字。营里的土兵、刀客、弩手加起来有上千人，都是雾驿主的外营。他们不往外打，也不许人往里走，只在雾里站着，一站就是一整天。

column2: The outer host is scattered. Nobody dares take down the Wait lantern. When the wind turns it, there are small characters on the back: 'Wait for the last one out of the fog.' Looking east you see the fog thinning, and at its end, the Master of the Fog Posts' hold.
column3: 外营被你们打散了。望楼上那盏「等」字灯笼没人敢摘，风一吹，灯笼转了过来，背面还有几个小字：「等最后一个出雾」。你们往东望去，雾已经薄了，雾驿主的大寨就在雾的尽头。

column2: Fog-Road Hollow
column3: 雾道坳

column2: Xiaoding leads you deeper into the wood by his master's fog maps. The fog roads drawn on them fit the lie of the land exactly: wherever there's a gully, that's where the fog runs. In a hollow you come on a band of native soldiers sitting in the fog as if waiting for it to clear. They have a fog map like the master's, only finer, with a Fog Post seal in the corner.
column3: 小钉带着你们沿着师父的雾图往林子深处找，图上画的雾道，跟林子里的地势分毫不差：哪里是沟，雾就往哪里淌。走到一处山坳，一群土兵正坐在雾里，像是在等雾散。他们手里拿着一张跟师父一样的雾图，只是画得更细，图角盖着「雾驿」的印。

column2: The soldiers are driven off and drop their map. Xiaoding compares the two for a long while. His master's is drawn from the fog, he says, and this one from the roads: the Master of the Fog Posts knows how the fog moves each day, which is how his soldiers come and go in it so easily. A red line on it runs from the wood straight to his master's hut.
column3: 土兵被打退，丢下了那张雾图。小钉对着两张图看了半天，说师父的图是照着雾画的，这一张是照着路画的：雾驿主知道雾每天怎么走，所以他的土兵能在雾里来去自如。图上有一条红线，从林子一直画到师父的小屋。

column2: Noon Gate
column3: 晌午关

column2: By the river stands the last gate before the Master's hold, the fog in front of it like a wall, too thick to see your hand. The soldiers on the gate move freely in it, their bamboo spears jabbing out of the white, the men themselves unseen. You charged twice in the morning and were stabbed back both times. Now the fog-reader's words come in useful: wait for noon, when the sun has warmed the valley and the fog thins.
column3: 河边是去雾驿主大寨的最后一道关，关前的雾浓得像一堵墙，伸手不见五指。关上的土兵在雾里来去自如，竹枪从雾里一下一下地捅出来，却看不见人。早上冲了两回，都被捅了回来。看雾婆说过的话，这时候用上了：等到晌午，太阳把河谷晒暖了，雾就薄了。

column2: Noon comes and the fog thins layer by layer, the soldiers on the gate take shape, and you carry it in one rush. The old gate captain sighs: that mule train ten years ago came through at noon too. 'The chief said fog isn't a wall, it's a breath. When the sun comes, it has to let go.' Beyond the gate, drums sound faintly, as if waiting for you.
column3: 晌午一到，雾果然一层层薄了下去，关上的土兵露出了形，被你们一鼓作气打了下来。守关的老土兵叹气说，十年前那支马帮也是晌午过的关：「镖头说，雾不是墙，是一口气，太阳一来，它就得喘。」关后鼓声隐隐，像在等你们。

column2: Fodder Yard
column3: 草料场

column2: A caravan fodder yard out on the open ground, stacks side by side, the last place to provision before heading east. Bullies who collect fodder for the Fog Posts have taken it and sell only to Fog Post horses; everyone else's animals are gnawing the fence rails. He Sanniang's caravan is stuck here too, and she squats under a haystack haggling louder than the bullies, shouting between offers: 'Black Bean's run into the stone keep behind the mountain. I'm going after it once my horses are fed.'
column3: 野地里一座马帮的草料场，草垛一个挨一个，是往东的马队最后补给的地方。一伙替雾驿收草料的兵痞把场子占了，草料只卖给雾驿的马，别家的马饿得啃栏杆。何三娘的马帮也被困在这儿，她蹲在草垛底下跟兵痞讨价还价，嗓门比对方还大，一边吵一边说：「黑豆跑进山后的石堡了，我喂饱了马就去。」

column2: The bullies are chased out, the yard opens again, and He Sanniang is first to load up. East of here is the Fog Posts, she says, and a caravan going into the fog feeds its horses full, waters them well and sets the bells ringing. 'People can panic. Horses mustn't.'
column3: 兵痞被撵走，草料场重新开了门，何三娘头一个装满了草料。她说再往东就是雾驿，马帮走雾，要先喂饱马、灌好水、敲响铃：「人可以慌，马不能慌。」

column2: From the bullies' hoard: eighty stacks of dried alfalfa, twenty baskets of bean cake, a bucket of horseshoe nails and two big barrels of tung oil. Half goes to the caravans trapped in the yard.
column3: 抄出兵痞囤的苜蓿干草八十垛、豆饼二十筐、一桶马掌钉、两大桶桐油，你们分了一半给困在场子里的马帮。

column2: Every time you pass, the yard hands have a sack of salted bean cake ready for your horses, and if He Sanniang's caravan is there, she slips you an extra one to settle what she owes you from last time.
column3: 每次路过，场子里的人都给你们的马备好一包拌了盐的豆饼；何三娘的马帮要是也在，她还要多塞你们一袋，说是还上次的情。

column2: Mule Keep
column3: 骡堡

column2: At the end of a blind valley behind the mountain stands a stone keep where the Fog Posts pen their mules, its walls thicker than a city's, held by elite Fog Post troops: swordsmen on the gate, crossbowmen on the walls, spearmen in the yard. Hundreds of fine mules wait inside to be driven into the fog. He Sanniang stands below the walls and shakes the bell once. A commotion breaks out inside, and one mule brays louder than all the rest.
column3: 山后死胡同里一座石堡，是雾驿收骡子的地方，堡墙比城墙还厚，守堡的是雾驿的精兵：刀客守门，弩手守墙，枪手守院。堡里关着几百头好骡，等着赶进雾里。何三娘站在堡下，掏出那只铃摇了一下，堡里一阵乱响，有一头骡子叫得特别响。

column2: The keep falls and hundreds of mules pour out, Black Bean first through the gate and straight into He Sanniang's arms. She ties the bell back on its neck, crying and scolding it at once. Inside is the keep's mule ledger. The Fog Posts collect mules to carry tea; where to, it doesn't say, only 'south, deliver to the villages'. From now on, Sanniang says, her caravan will walk this road for you. 'I've finished what he promised. Now I'll do what you need, too.'
column3: 石堡破了，几百头骡子涌了出来，黑豆第一个冲出堡门，一头撞进何三娘怀里。她把铃重新系上它的脖子，一边哭一边骂了它一顿。堡里还有一本收骡的账：雾驿收骡是为了驮茶，驮到哪里却没写，只写着「往南，交寨」。何三娘说，她的马帮以后就替你们走这条路：「他答应过的事，我替他做完了；你们的事，我也替你们做。」

column2: Stockade on the Water
column3: 竹栅水寨

column2: In a blind reach of the river is a water stockade, its palisade driven into the riverbed, dozens of bamboo rafts moored inside, guarded by the Master's picked troops. It holds no cargo. It holds people: everyone who, in ten years of crossings, made the count 'one too many'. The Master says they followed others out of the fog and may not go home. The guards keep crossbows spanned and blades bare, and no boat may come near.
column3: 河边死胡同里一座水寨，木栅插进河里，寨里泊着几十条竹筏，由雾驿主的精兵守着。寨子里关的不是货，是人：十年来过雾时被「数多了」的人，雾驿主说他们是从雾里跟出来的，不许回家。守寨的精兵弩上弦、刀出鞘，河面上一条小船也不许靠近。

column2: The water stockade falls and dozens of people pour out: old folk, porters, even a distant nephew of the fishing family. The Master never mistreated them, they say. Three meals a day, only they couldn't leave. 'He said when the count came right, we could go home.' All these years, and the count never once came right.
column3: 水寨破了，被关的几十个人涌了出来，有老人，有挑夫，还有那户打鱼人家的远房侄子。他们说雾驿主从没为难过他们，一日三餐都有，只是不许走：「他说，等数对了，就放我们回去。」可他们被关了这么多年，数从来没对过。

column2: Recorder's Cell
column3: 书办屋

column2: A stone hut at the mountain foot with soldiers outside and, locked within, the Fog Posts' old recorder. He kept the Master's counts for ten years, until the other day he made bold to say: 'That count ten years ago wasn't wrong. Someone really was missing. It wasn't a mistake.' The Master had him locked up. He's covered the wall with charcoal sums, a whole wall of them, every one coming to the same number.
column3: 山脚一座石屋，屋外守着一伙土兵，屋里关着雾驿的老书办。他替雾驿主记了十年的数，前些天斗胆说了一句：「十年前那个数没有错，是真少了一个人，不是数错了。」雾驿主就叫人把他关了起来。老书办在墙上用木炭写满了算式，一整面墙，写的都是同一个数。

column2: The soldiers are chased away and the old recorder sits out in the sun. It isn't that the Master can't count, he says. 'He won't accept it. Three hundred went into the fog and he led them through himself, and one fewer came out, so he tells himself he miscounted and counts again and again.' What the Master owes, he says, isn't a number. It's an answer.
column3: 土兵被打跑，老书办出来晒着太阳，说雾驿主不是不会数：「他是不认。三百个进了雾，他亲手领着走的，出来的时候少了一个，他就说是自己数错了，一遍一遍地数。」他说，雾驿主欠的不是一个数，是一个交代。

column2: Dripping Pines
column3: 滴雨松

column2: The red line ends at a bark-walled hut ringed by old pines. The ground is soaked; it isn't raining, yet under the trees it drips and patters like rain. The old fog-map maker sits inside under the eyes of a few native soldiers, a huge unfinished map spread on his table. They want him to finish it for the Master of the Fog Posts. He refuses, and hasn't eaten in three days.
column3: 红线的尽头是一间树皮小屋，屋外围着一圈老松，地上湿漉漉的，明明没下雨，树底下却滴滴答答，像在落雨。画雾的老先生坐在屋里，被几个土兵看着，桌上铺着一张没画完的大图。土兵们要他把图画完交给雾驿主，他不肯，已经三天没吃东西了。

column2: You drive the soldiers off and the old man comes round over a bowl of hot soup. The 'rain' under the trees comes from the fog, he says. The tiny droplets strike the pine needles, gather until they're heavy, and drip; on a thick-fog night you could catch half a bucket of water under one pine. His unfinished map shows the whole of the Fog Posts: nine posts, one road, where the fog rises and where it lies thinnest. 'The Master wants it because he's afraid someone will use it to walk in. I drew it for whoever wants to walk in.' He gives it to you and adds one last stroke: the gate of the hold, at noon.
column3: 土兵被你们赶走，老先生喝了口热汤才缓过来。他说树下的「雨」是雾给的：雾里的小水珠撞在松针上，攒多了就滴下来，雾大的夜里，一棵松树底下能接半桶水。他那张没画完的大图，画的是整个雾驿：九座驿站，一条路，雾从哪里起，在哪里最薄。「雾驿主想要它，是怕有人照着它走进去。我画它，就是给要进去的人。」他把图交给了你们，又添了一笔：大寨的门，在晌午。

column2: Tea Cellar Cave
column3: 茶窖洞

column2: Up a blind track at the mountain foot is a cave, its mouth hung with drying tea leaves: the Master of the Fog Posts' tea cellar. Caravan swordsmen guard it. The Master drinks only tea from here all year round, they say, and anyone who touches a single leaf loses a finger. The cave smells wonderful, and the swordsmen themselves daren't take a sip; they stand there swallowing hard.
column3: 山脚死路里一处岩洞，洞口挂满了风干的茶叶，是雾驿主的茶窖。一伙马帮刀客守着，说雾驿主一年到头只喝这里的茶，谁碰一片叶子就剁谁一根指头。洞里茶香扑鼻，刀客们自己却一口不敢喝，馋得直咽唾沫。

column2: The swordsmen run, each sneaking a handful of tea as he goes. The tea in the cave is heaped like a hill, but in the innermost layer are a few half bricks with clean breaks, the kind the tea-firing works presses. A prisoner says they were left ten years ago by an escort chief as his 'fog toll'. Every year the Master breaks off one small corner to brew. Ten years, and he hasn't been able to bring himself to finish a single brick.
column3: 刀客们被打跑，临走还偷偷揣了一把茶叶。洞里的茶堆得像小山，最里面一层却是几块半截的茶砖，断口齐整，就是焙茶坊压的那种。俘虏说，这是十年前一个镖头留下的「过雾钱」，雾驿主一年只掰一小角泡来喝，十年了，一块也没舍得掰完。

column2: Wandering-Pole Slope
column3: 挪杆坡

column2: White poles line the fog road on this slope too, but these ones move: on the left of the path at night, on the right by morning, and muleteers walk all night only to find themselves at dawn back where they started. You keep watch half the night and see a squad of native soldiers tiptoeing through the fog with poles on their shoulders, counting under their breath: 'This one three steps, that one five...'
column3: 山坡上的雾道两旁也立着白杆，可这里的杆子会挪：夜里还在路左，早上就到了路右，赶马人走了一夜，天亮发现又回到了原地。你们守了半夜，看见一伙土兵扛着杆子在雾里蹑手蹑脚地走，一边走一边小声数：「这根挪三步，那根挪五步……」

column2: The soldiers are caught and the poles driven back where they belong. The Master's orders, they say: while the count is wrong, no one is to walk out of the fog, so the road must go in circles. 'He said when the last one comes back, the poles get fixed for good.' You drive every pole in hard, and the road runs straight at once, pointing directly at the Master's hold.
column3: 土兵被捉住了，杆子一根根钉回原处。土兵说是雾驿主的令：数不对，就不许人走出雾，只好让路绕起来。「他说，等最后那一个回来，杆子才钉死。」你们把每根杆子都钉得死死的，路一下子直了，直直地指着雾驿主的大寨。

column2: Portrait Stall
column3: 画像摊

column2: A gang of bullies has a stall out in the open selling 'true likenesses of the Master of the Fog Posts': hang one by your door and the fog soldiers won't dare come in. Refuse to buy and you're disrespecting the Master, and get dragged over to kowtow to his portrait. No two pictures agree: one has three heads and six arms, one is a white-bearded old man, one is simply a big fish. Every one is genuine, say the bullies.
column3: 野地里一伙兵痞支着个摊子，卖「雾驿主真容」，说挂在门口，雾里的兵就不敢进门。谁不买，就说谁对雾驿主不敬，要拉去给真容磕头。摊上的画一张一个样：一张三头六臂，一张是个白胡子老头，一张干脆画了条大鱼，兵痞们张张都说是真的。

column2: You send the frauds running with their hands over their heads, portraits scattered everywhere. The real fog soldiers watch from a distance without joining in, only giving you a bow of thanks. None of them has ever seen the Master's face, they say, and the Master himself has said the face doesn't matter. 'He says he's just the one who leads the way.'
column3: 冒牌货被你们打得抱头鼠窜，画像撒了一地。真土兵远远看着，也没上来帮忙，只冲你们拱了拱手。他们说谁也没见过雾驿主长什么样，雾驿主自己说过，脸不要紧：「他说，他就是那个领路的。」

column2: Nine-Tier Drum Tower
column3: 九层鼓楼

column2: At the end of a blind valley at the mountain foot rises the Master's drum tower, nine tiers high, a drum on every tier, the source of every signal sent to the nine Fog Posts. His finest guards hold it floor by floor: crossbowmen at the windows, swordsmen on the stairs, spearmen three ranks deep below. The drum at the top has beaten only one rhythm in ten years.
column3: 山脚死胡同的尽头是雾驿主的鼓楼，楼高九层，每层一面鼓，九座雾驿的鼓声都从这里发出去。守楼的是雾驿主最精的亲兵，一层一层都有人，弩手在窗，刀客在梯，枪手在楼下排成三排。楼顶那面鼓，十年来只敲过一种鼓点。

column2: You take the tower. On the head of the top drum, in cinnabar, is the drum score of that night ten years ago: beat after beat written out all the way to the rim, the very last left blank. That was the roll-call drum, the guards say, one beat for each person. At the last one, the Master stopped. 'He said the last beat waits for that person to come back and strike it himself.'
column3: 鼓楼被你们攻了下来。楼顶那面鼓的鼓面上，用朱砂写着十年前那一夜的鼓谱：一下一下，一直写到鼓边，最后一下空着没写。守楼的亲兵说，那是点名鼓，一下一个人，点到最后一个，雾驿主停了手：「他说，最后一下，要等那个人回来自己敲。」

column2: Ninth Post
column3: 第九驿

column2: Below the Master's hold stands the last of the Fog Posts, the Ninth, its stilt house lit night and day. With the Master's troops all pulled back to guard the hold, a gang of bullies has seized it, locked the keepers in the stable, cleared out the rice, flour, cured meat and lamp oil, and hung a board on the door: 'Post Full.'
column3: 雾驿主大寨下面是最后一座雾驿，第九驿，吊脚楼里灯火不熄。一伙兵痞趁着雾驿主的兵都调去守大寨，占了驿站，把驿卒锁进马厩，把驿站的米面、腊肉、灯油搬了个精光，还在门口挂了块牌子：「本驿已满」。

column2: The bullies are thrown out and the Ninth Post lights its lamps again. From here the road goes up to the Master's hold, the old keeper says, and for ten years everyone who went up was marched up under guard. 'You're the first to walk up of your own accord.' He shows you the way and stuffs cloth into your harness bells. The Master doesn't care for noise.
column3: 兵痞被撵走，第九驿重新点上了灯。老驿卒说，从这里往上就是雾驿主的大寨，十年来走上去的人，都是被押上去的，「你们是头一回自己走上去的」。他给你们指了路，又把马铃塞上了布，说雾驿主不喜欢吵。

column2: You recover what the bullies took: ten sacks of rice and flour, a basket of cured meat and four barrels of lamp oil, plus a bundle of letters they'd searched off travellers. The old keeper says he'll see every one of them carried out of the fog.
column3: 抄回兵痞搬走的米面十袋、腊肉一筐、灯油四桶，还有他们从过路人身上搜来的一包信，老驿卒说要替他们一封封送出雾去。

column2: Every time you pass, the keepers of the Ninth Post save you the warmest room upstairs with a good charcoal fire, and give you tomorrow's fog forecast: when it will rise, and when it will lift.
column3: 每次路过，第九驿的驿卒都把楼上最暖的那间屋子留给你们，炭火烧得旺旺的，还替你们把明天的雾报好：几时起，几时散。

column2: Old Post Foundations
column3: 旧驿基

column2: At the far end of the open ground is a field of mounds like forgotten graves, really the foundations of old abandoned post stations. A band of deserters is digging for treasure: the Master buried the Qianli gold here ten years ago, they say. Half a year's digging has turned up broken tiles and one stone stele, and they still won't give up, and attack anyone who comes near.
column3: 野地尽头一片土堆，像一座座荒坟，其实是一个个废弃了的旧驿站的地基。一伙流兵在这里挖宝，说雾驿主十年前在这里埋了千里号的金子。他们挖了半年，只挖出一堆碎瓦和一块石碑，还不死心，见人来就打。

column2: The deserters are driven off. The stele they dug up bears the Fog Posts' old rules: 'For those who cross the fog, the posts shall give rest, give the hour, and lead the way.' Not one word about counting. Only now do you understand: the counting began ten years ago. The Master made that rule himself.
column3: 流兵被赶走了。他们挖出来的石碑上刻着雾驿的旧规矩：「过雾者，驿为之歇，为之报时，为之引路。」一个字也没提数人。你们这才知道，数人是十年前才有的规矩，是雾驿主自己定的。

column2: Silver-Bell Herbalist
column3: 银铃药客

column2: At the end of a blind track at the mountain foot sits a herbalist from the south, a huge basket of herbs at her side hung with a string of silver bells. She wants to go home south to her village, but the Master's men won't let her: she's 'the extra one in the count', they say, and they're holding her basket. She sits by the road with a few herbs laid out to sell, but with soldiers standing over her, nobody dares buy.
column3: 山脚死路的尽头有个南边来的草药客，背着一大篓草药，篓上挂着一串银铃。她想往南回寨子，可雾驿主的人不许她走，说她是「数出来的那一个」，扣着她的药篓不放。她坐在路边，摆开几味药卖，可土兵站在一旁，谁也不敢来买。

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the herbalist opens her stall, trading herbs for your salt and cloth. She's from the Gu villages to the south. Three days' walk south and this fog clears, she says, and in the forests there an elder keeps half a tea brick, waiting for someone to collect it. 'Not waiting for the Master of the Fog Posts. Waiting for whoever has the other half.' She packs her basket and sets off south ahead of you. She'll wait for you in the villages.
column3: 土兵被赶走，草药客的摊子开了张，她拿草药跟你们换盐和布。她是南边蛊寨的人，说这雾往南走三天就散了，那边的林子里，有个寨老守着半块茶砖，等人去取：「等的不是雾驿主，是拿着另外半块的人。」她收拾好药篓，先往南去了，说在寨子里等你们。

column2: Hold of the Fog Master
column3: 雾驿主寨

column2: At the end of the fog stands a hold you can't quite see: a gate, walls, ranks of soldiers with bamboo spears, and beyond them only fog, and in the fog a drum, beat by beat, as if counting. The Master of the Fog Posts never shows himself. His voice comes out of the fog, neither loud nor soft: 'Three hundred walked in. When they walked out of the fog, there were two hundred and ninety-nine. Have you come to make up the one, or to take my count away from me?' Out of the fog, rank on rank, come the soldiers, the mountain crossbowmen, the caravan swordsmen.
column3: 雾的尽头是一座看不清的寨子：你们只看见寨门、寨墙和一排排举着竹枪的土兵，再往里就全是雾，雾里有鼓声，一下一下，像在数数。雾驿主从不露面，他的声音从雾里传出来，不高不低：「三百人，走出雾的时候只剩二百九十九。你们来，是来补那一个，还是来带走我的数？」雾里的土兵、山弩手、马帮刀客，一层一层压了过来。

column2: The soldiers fall back and the drum falls silent. Still the Master does not show himself. Out of the fog a hand passes one bamboo tally: two hundred and ninety-nine notches, and beside the last, an empty space. 'Ten years ago I led them through the fog, and one fewer came out. Ten years I searched the fog and never found that one, so all I could do was count, and count again.' The things you've brought, the tea pass seal, the lodge ash, the master's book, the grey horse's road, he knows them all. 'They've come together. It's time I opened the gate.' A corner of the fog lifts, showing a road running south. 'The rest of them went south, into the Gu villages,' the Master says at last. 'Whatever became of that one is tied up there too.'
column3: 土兵退去，鼓声停了。雾驿主还是没露面，雾里只递出来一根竹签，刻着二百九十九道，最后一道旁边空着一块。「十年前我领他们穿过雾，出来少了一个。我在雾里找了十年，没找着，就只好一遍一遍地数。」他说你们带来的东西，茶关的印、锅庄的灰、夫子的书、青马的路，他都认得：「凑齐了，我也该开门了。」雾散了一角，露出一条往南的路。「剩下的人往南去了，进了蛊寨。」雾驿主最后说，「那一个的下落，也拴在那边。」

column2: The Gu Villages
column3: 蛊寨

column2: Grass-Knot Gap
column3: 草标口

column2: Three days south of the fog it finally thins away, and ahead lies forest with no end in sight. At the mouth of the slope stands a bamboo pole with a knot of grass at its tip, wound with red thread: a Miao 'grass marker'. Where one stands, the villages are closed and strangers stop. Village guards with javelins hold the foot of the pole, blowgunners lie flat in the thatch, and as your carts roll up every bamboo tube rises to a pair of lips.
column3: 出了雾往南又走了三天，雾终于散尽，眼前是望不到头的林子。坡口插着一根竹竿，竿头挽着个草结，草结上缠着红线：这是苗寨的「草标」，插了它，就是封寨，外人止步。几个寨丁端着梭镖守在竿下，吹箭手伏在茅草里，见你们的车过来，一齐把竹管举到了嘴边。

column2: The guards fall back into the trees, but nobody dares pull up the marker. An old guard looks back as he goes: it was planted ten years ago, he says, and the grass renewed every year without a miss. 'It isn't there to keep you out. It's there to keep what's inside from getting out.' He nods at the red thread and won't say who tied it, only that whoever did has clever hands: in ten years the knot has never once slipped.
column3: 寨丁退进了林子，草标却没人敢拔。一个老寨丁临走回过头来，说这根草标十年前插下，一年换一回新草，从没断过：「不是不让你们进，是不让里头的东西出来。」他指了指草结上的红线，没说是谁系的，只说系线的人手巧，十年了，线头一回也没松过。

column2: Mule-Bell Track
column3: 马铃道

column2: Salt smugglers resting in the open have snatched a mule bell from a little Miao boy and hung it on the end of a carrying pole, jangling it for fun. The boy has followed them for two miles. He can't catch up, but he doesn't cry; he just trails behind, stopping when the pole stops and walking when it walks. Sick of him, the porters turn round and swing the pole at him.
column3: 野地里一伙贩私盐的挑夫歇脚，抢了一个苗家小娃的马铃，挂在扁担头上叮当乱响取乐。小娃追了二里地，追不上也不哭，就在后头跟着，扁担停他停，扁担走他走。挑夫们嫌他烦，回身抡起扁担要打。

column2: The smugglers chased off, the bell comes back. The boy is Zhou Xiaoman, nine years old, and the bell was his father's, a Han caravan bell with 'Man' carved on its clapper. His father, Zhou Mancang, wintered in the villages with the caravan ten years ago, left in spring and never returned. 'People say the gu took him,' Xiaoman says. 'I don't believe it. I'm going to find out for myself.'
column3: 私盐贩子被撵走，马铃还了回来。小娃叫周小满，九岁，铃是他阿爸留下的，汉人马帮的铃，铃舌上刻着一个「满」字。他阿爸周满仓十年前跟着马帮在寨里过了一冬，开春走了，再没回来。「寨里人说他是被蛊走的，」小满说，「我不信，我要自己问清楚。」

column2: The Gate of Rules
column3: 规矩门

column2: On the gate of the first village hangs a fir board with five rules in ink. One: if someone outside the bamboo wall calls your name at night, do not answer. Two: clay jars sealed with red cloth, do not count them, do not touch them. Three: if you hear silver bells and see no one, stand still until the bells have passed. Four: if a person sitting alone by the road offers you food, do not take it. Five: if you are counting and reach three hundred, stop and start again. The guards won't let you in until you know them by heart. You ask who made the rules. Their faces change, and out come the blowguns.
column3: 寨门上钉着一块杉木牌，墨写五条规矩：一、夜里竹墙外有人喊你名字，莫应；二、红布封口的陶罐，莫数，莫碰；三、听见银铃响却不见人，原地站住，等铃过去；四、路边独坐的人递来吃食，莫接；五、数数数到三百，就停，从头再数。守门的寨丁要你们背熟了才许进寨。你们问规矩是谁定的，他们脸色一变，摸出了吹箭。

column2: Pinned to the ground, the guards are still muttering the rules under their breath. Their leader says the board went up overnight ten years ago, and by the next morning the whole village was keeping it. Nobody knows who wrote it and nobody dares ask. 'Those who keep the rules are all still here. Those who didn't all walked off into the forest.' Lean close and the ink gives off a faint smell of herbs.
column3: 寨丁们被按在地上，嘴里还在小声背规矩。领头的说，这块牌子是十年前一夜之间钉上去的，第二天全寨就照着守了，没人知道是谁写的，也没人敢问：「守着的人都还在。不守的，都走进林子里去了。」你们凑近了闻，牌上的墨里有一股淡淡的草药味。

column2: Loom Terrace
column3: 织机坎

column2: A row of stilt houses stands on the terrace, and Xiaoman's mother A Xiu sits weaving under hers. The chieftain's tax men have come for the cloth tax, two bolts for every one, and when she can't pay they pick up her loom, half-woven bolt and all, and carry it off. Xiaoman flies at them and bites one, is slapped to the ground, gets up and flies at them again.
column3: 坎上一排吊脚楼，小满的阿妈阿秀坐在楼下织布。土司家的税丁来收布税，一匹布要收两匹，阿秀交不出，他们就把织机连同机上没织完的那匹一起抬走。小满扑上去咬了税丁一口，被一巴掌扇倒在地上，爬起来又扑。

column2: The tax men beaten off, the loom comes home. A Xiu doesn't want to talk about Zhou Mancang. She says only that the morning he left, he put a new pair of straw sandals on the floorboards for the child. 'Xiaoman was still in my belly. He said, for when the baby can walk.' The sandals have hung from the rafter ever since. Xiaoman's feet outgrew them long ago.
column3: 税丁被打跑，织机抬了回来。阿秀不愿多提周满仓，只说他走的那天早上，在楼板上留了一双新草鞋，是给娃娃的：「那时小满还在我肚子里，他说，娃娃会走路了穿。」草鞋一直挂在梁上，小满的脚早就穿不下了。

column2: Rice-Rack Slope
column3: 禾晾坡

column2: Tall drying racks stand in rows up the slope, hung thick with sheaves of sticky rice still on the ear, a wall of gold that is the whole village's food for winter. A band of deserters who slipped south through the fog has taken the racks: they sleep under them by day and feed the sheaves to their horses by night. When villagers come to ask, they laugh. 'You lot aren't allowed out at night, are you? So the night rice is ours.'
column3: 坡上立着一排排高高的禾晾架，挂满了带穗的糯禾，金黄一片，是全寨一冬的口粮。一伙从北边雾里逃过来的流兵占了禾晾，白天在架子底下睡觉，夜里拿糯禾喂马。寨民来讨，他们就笑：「你们不是不许夜里出门吗？那夜里的禾，就归我们。」

column2: The deserters are chased back north and the racks belong to the village again. The villagers tell you about the first rule. Last winter three people answered a name at night and followed the voice into the forest. They were found next morning at the forest's edge, unharmed, except that each had a fine gold thread wound round the wrist: scissors won't cut it, hands can't pull it off, and every night it draws tight toward the south-east.
column3: 流兵被撵回了北边，禾晾又归了寨子。寨民说起第一条规矩：去年冬天有三个人夜里应了名，跟着声音走进林子，第二天在林边被找到，人好好的，只是手腕上缠了一圈细细的金丝，剪不断，扯不掉，一到夜里就往东南方向绷。

column2: From the deserters' hoard: two hundred sheaves of sticky rice, two strings of smoked fish, a jar of sweet fermented rice, four bony horses ridden down from the north, and one ragged deserter's banner, which a granny takes home to patch her chicken coop.
column3: 抄出流兵囤的糯禾两百把、腊鱼两串、一坛甜酒酿、四匹从北边骑来的瘦马，还有一面流兵的破旗，寨里的阿婆拿去补了鸡笼。

column2: Every time you pass, a granny presses a parcel of sticky rice on you, wrapped in banana leaf with a piece of smoked pork buried in the middle. 'For the forest. Sticky rice keeps hunger off longest.'
column3: 每次路过，寨里的阿婆都塞给你们一包糯米饭，用芭蕉叶包着，里头埋一块腊肉：「走林子，糯的顶饿。」

column2: The Red-Thread Bed
column3: 红线床

column2: In a stilt house a lad of seventeen or so is tied to the bedpost with red thread, and his mother hasn't closed her eyes all night beside him. Two nights ago he answered his name and sleepwalked toward the forest; only the thread stopped him. Now a crowd from the 'Silkworm Listeners' stands below, knocking bamboo clappers. The voice is a blessing, they say, whoever it calls has somewhere to go, and they want him untied so he can 'follow'.
column3: 一座吊脚楼里，一个十七八岁的后生被红线拴在床柱上，他阿妈守在床边，一夜没合眼。前天夜里他应了名，梦游着往林子里走，被拴住了才没走成。楼下来了一伙「听蚕会」的人，敲着竹梆，说那声音是福气，喊谁谁就有了去处，要把后生解下来，送他「跟着去」。

column2: The Listeners are driven off, clappers strewn across the ground. The lad wakes and says the voice that called him was his father's, though his father was asleep in the next room. He answered once, and the voice stopped calling him. It moved on to another name and kept on calling, a Han name: 'Zhou Mancang... Zhou Mancang...'
column3: 听蚕会的人被赶走，竹梆扔了一地。后生醒过来说，那天夜里喊他的是他阿爸的声音，可阿爸就睡在隔壁。他应了一声，那声音就不再喊他了，换了个名字接着喊，是个汉人的名字：「周满仓……周满仓……」

column2: The Rename Stall
column3: 改名摊

column2: A stall stands by the road, run by a fortune-teller from beyond the hills. His banner reads 'Change your name, escape the calling, one coin a name': the voice at night knows names, he says, so change yours and it can't find you. Villagers queue for red slips with new names on them; some have changed three times already. Anyone who won't queue gets surrounded by his hired muscle, who say that one must 'want to be called away'.
column3: 路边支着个摊子，摊主是个山外来的算命先生，幌子上写「改名避喊，一名一钱」：他说夜里那声音认名字，改个名，它就喊不着你。寨民排着长队，交了钱领一张红纸新名，有人已经改了三回。不肯排队的，摊主雇来的打手就围上去，说他「想被喊走」。

column2: The muscle scattered, the fortune-teller refunds every coin on his knees. He does let slip one honest thing: he eavesdropped for half a month, and the voice only ever calls Han names, never a single Miao one. 'The ones who answered all have someone they're waiting for.' He hunches his shoulders. 'People who wait have sharp ears.'
column3: 打手被打散，算命先生跪着把钱退了。他倒说了句实话：他偷偷听了半个月，那声音只喊汉人的名字，一个苗名也没喊过。「应了声的那几个，都是家里有人在等的。」他缩着脖子说，「等人的人，耳朵尖。」

column2: The Carved-Horse Fir
column3: 刻马杉

column2: Deserters in the forest are felling trees to sell the timber, and old firs come crashing down one after another. Xiaoman is stamping with panic: his mother told him one of these firs has a little horse carved on it, cut by his father that winter. The deserters already have their saw set to that very tree, its teeth an inch into the bark.
column3: 林子里一伙流兵在砍树卖木头，一棵棵老杉被放倒。小满急得直跺脚：阿妈说过，有一棵杉树上刻着一匹小马，是他阿爸那年冬天刻的。流兵已经把锯子架在了那棵树上，锯齿咬进树皮一寸。

column2: The deserters chased away, the fir is saved. There on the bark is a little horse, and beside it a crooked line of characters: 'Mancang wintered here, back next year.' Ten years of growth have stretched the letters huge. Xiaoman traces them one by one with his finger, and when he reaches 'next year', he stops.
column3: 流兵被赶走，那棵杉保住了。树皮上果然刻着一匹小马，旁边一行歪歪扭扭的字：「满仓过冬于此，明年还来。」树长了十年，字被撑得老大。小满拿手指一个字一个字地描，描到「明年」两个字，停住了。

column2: The Fire-Watch Tower
column3: 望火楼

column2: A fire-watch tower stands in the open, and an old night guard lives at the top. Ten years ago, on the night the caravan left, it was he who kept the watch up here. Xiaoman climbs up to ask him, and the old man has barely opened his mouth when Gu riders arrive below: the Gu King forbids anyone to speak of that night, and they've come to take him.
column3: 野地里一座望火楼，楼上住着守夜的老寨丁。十年前马帮走的那个夜里，是他在楼上值更。小满爬上楼去问他，老寨丁刚张开嘴，楼下就来了一伙蛊骑，说蛊王不许人提那一夜，要把老寨丁绑走。

column2: The riders driven off, the old guard tells what he saw. In the middle of that night the caravan men walked out of the village one after another, eyes wide open, not speaking, no torches, as if something were leading them by a string. 'The gu took them,' he says. 'I saw it with my own eyes.' Xiaoman bites his lip and remembers every word.
column3: 蛊骑被打退，老寨丁说了他看见的：那天半夜，马帮的人一个接一个从寨子里走出来，眼睛睁得大大的，不说话，也不点火把，像被什么东西牵着走。「是被蛊走的，」他说，「我亲眼看见的。」小满咬着嘴唇，把这句话记下了。

column2: Curfew-Gong Camp
column3: 落锣营

column2: A big camp in the forest belongs to the guards who keep the curfew, led by Yan Bao, a tall man with one eye. At sundown the camp beats its gongs through seven villages, and anyone still abroad after the gongs is tied up and hung from a tree till morning. Today they have strung up a peddler who was travelling late. He sobs that he only lost his way, and the gongs beat faster.
column3: 林子里一座大营，是寨丁们的宵禁营，营头岩保是个独眼的高个子。太阳一落山，营里就敲锣，一路敲过七个寨子，锣响之后还在外头走的，一律绑了吊在树上过夜。今天他们吊了一个赶夜路的货郎，货郎哭着说他只是迷了路，寨丁的锣却敲得更急了。

column2: The camp scattered, the peddler is cut down. Yan Bao rubs his one good eye, now swelling, and says the curfew comes from the rules too. At night silver bells ring through the forest in gusts; whoever they pass must stand still, and whoever doesn't can't be found next day. 'Ten years I've kept the night watch,' he says, 'and not once have I seen who rings them.'
column3: 宵禁营被冲散，货郎放了下来。岩保揉着肿起来的那只好眼，说宵禁也是规矩里来的：夜里林子里有银铃一阵阵地响，响到谁身边，谁就得站住；不站住的，第二天就找不着了。「我守了十年夜，」他说，「那摇铃的，一回也没见过。」

column2: The Silver-Bell Stall
column3: 银铃药摊

column2: Under the great banyan in the middle of the village a woman has laid out herbs, a string of silver bells on her basket: the herb seller you met at the edge of the fog. She said she'd wait for you in the villages, and here she is. But she has no customers. Every time she gets up and takes a step, the bells ring and every passing villager freezes on the spot. Guards stand beside her stall: she is 'a person sitting alone by the road', and by rule four nobody may take anything from her. Meanwhile a few herb thieves use the confusion to reach into her basket.
column3: 寨子当中的大榕树下，一个女人摆开了草药摊，药篓上挂着一串银铃，正是在雾驿边遇见的那个草药客。她说过在寨子里等你们，果然等着。可摊前没有买主：她每起身挪一步，银铃一响，路过的寨民就齐刷刷站住不动。寨丁守在摊边，说她「一个人坐在路边」，按第四条，谁也不许接她的东西；几个偷药的小贼却趁乱往她篓里伸手。

column2: The thieves run, and the guards step aside. Her name is A Kou. She trades herbs for your salt and cloth and gives generous weight. You ask whether the rules frighten her. She smiles. 'They're good rules. Keep them.' At the bottom of her basket sits a little clay jar sealed with red cloth; yeast for rice wine, she says, and drops a bundle of herbs on top of it.
column3: 偷药贼被打跑，寨丁也让开了。她叫阿蔻，拿草药跟你们换盐和布，秤给得很足。你们问她怕不怕那些规矩，她笑了笑：「规矩是好规矩，守着吧。」她篓底放着一只小陶罐，罐口封着红布，她说是酿甜酒的曲子，顺手拿药包往上一盖。

column2: The Indigo Pits
column3: 蓝靛池

column2: A row of indigo pits lies in the open, and bolts of batik hang drying on bamboo poles beside them, white patterns on blue. Toughs hired by a dye house beyond the hills have seized the pits to buy up every scrap of indigo and ship the cloth out to sell. The grannies who do the dyeing have been pushed aside, and the toughs' boss is wiping his knife on an old piece of batik, the oldest cloth in the village.
column3: 野地里一排蓝靛池，池边竹竿上晾着一匹匹蜡染布，蓝底白花。一伙山外染坊雇来的打手占了池子，要把这里的蓝靛全包下来，染了布拉出山去卖。染布的阿婆们被赶到一边，打手头子拿一匹旧蜡染当抹布擦刀，那是寨里最老的一匹。

column2: The toughs gone, the old cloth is rescued, washed and spread out: on the blue, a white silkworm, and from its body run threads, dense as rain, a tiny person at the end of each. A granny says a woman drew the wax for it ten years ago and taught them to dye it. 'She said that's what calls names at night.' The granny starts to count the threads, gets halfway, and stops herself.
column3: 打手被赶走，那匹旧布抢了回来，洗干净摊开：蓝底上一只白蚕，蚕身上牵出密密麻麻的细线，每根线头上一个小人。阿婆说这是十年前一个女人画了蜡、教她们染的：「她说，夜里喊名字的，就是这个。」阿婆想数一数线有多少根，数到一半，又不敢数了。

column2: The Oil-Tea House
column3: 油茶铺

column2: At a crossroads stands a little shop that brews oil tea, tea leaves, puffed rice and peanuts toasting in an iron wok, the smell carrying a mile; it's where porters stop to rest. A bully from the next village has taken it over with his household thugs: the road belongs to his family, he says, and one bowl costs the price of three. The porters can't afford it and walk past on the smell alone, swallowing hard.
column3: 路口一家打油茶的小铺，铁锅里炒着茶叶、米花、花生，香气飘出一里地，是过路背夫歇脚的地方。邻寨的恶霸带着家丁占了铺子，说这条路是他家的，一碗油茶收三碗的钱。背夫们喝不起，只能闻着味儿走过去，咽着口水。

column2: The bully is sent packing to his own village and the shop steams again. The granny who brews the tea says that winter the caravan men came every morning. Zhou Mancang drank three bowls at a time and, having no money, paid with a Han ditty. 'He owes me a whole winter of songs.' She ladles extra peanuts into Xiaoman's bowl. 'Will you pay it for him?'
column3: 恶霸被撵回了自家寨子，铺子又冒起了热气。打油茶的阿婆说，那年冬天马帮的人天天早上来喝，周满仓一喝三碗，没钱，就唱一支汉人的小调抵账。「他欠我一冬天的歌，」阿婆给小满多舀了一勺花生，「你替他还？」

column2: From the bully's store: four jars of tea-seed oil, two sacks of peanuts, a big basket of puffed sticky rice, a brand-new iron wok, and a wooden sign reading 'This road belongs to Wang', which the granny splits on the spot and feeds to the stove.
column3: 抄出恶霸囤的茶油四坛、花生两袋、一大筐糯米花、一口新铁锅，还有一块写着「此路姓王」的木牌，阿婆当场劈了添进灶里。

column2: Every time you pass, the granny brews you a wokful of oil tea. 'Three bowls, three days' walking.' If Xiaoman is with you, she won't take the bowls back until he's sung her a song.
column3: 每次路过，阿婆都给你们打一锅油茶，「喝三碗，走三天」；小满要是跟着，她还要他唱一支歌才肯收碗。

column2: Wild Mule Slope
column3: 野骡坡

column2: A herd of wild mules runs on the slope, small but sure-footed; villagers say they're the offspring of the sick mules the caravan left behind ten years ago. Horse thieves have set snares all over the slope and sell every mule they catch beyond the hills. Xiaoman says his father's mule was called Black Date, with a tuft of white on its forehead, and he wants to see if any of its young are here.
column3: 坡上跑着一群野骡子，个头不大，脚力却好，寨里人说是十年前马帮留下的病骡下的崽。一伙偷马贼在坡上下了套，套住一头就往山外卖。小满说他阿爸的骡子叫「黑枣」，额头上一撮白毛，他要看看坡上有没有它的崽。

column2: The thieves run and every snare is cut. Up the slope one young mule with a white tuft on its forehead stands watching Xiaoman from afar, neither fleeing nor coming closer. When the caravan left, the villagers say, they left all their sick mules behind: 'Look after them, we'll ride them when we're back.' Ten years on the young have had young of their own, and the riders still haven't come.
column3: 偷马贼被撵走，套索都割断了。坡上有一头小骡，额头一撮白毛，远远看着小满，不跑也不过来。寨里的人说，马帮走的时候把病骡都留下了，交代寨里「好生养着，回来骑」。十年了，崽又生了崽，等着骑它的人还没来。

column2: Blowgun Wood
column3: 吹箭林

column2: Blowgunners crouch in the trees, bamboo tubes poking out between the leaves, aiming for passers-by's necks. The darts aren't poisoned; they carry a sleeping draught, and whoever drops is dragged away. They've waited here for days, and it's Xiaoman they're waiting for: the Gu King has heard a half-Han child is going round asking about that night.
column3: 林子里的树上蹲着一伙吹箭手，竹管从叶子缝里伸出来，专射过路人的脖子：箭上抹的不是毒，是让人昏睡的药，射倒了就拖走。他们在这里等了好几天，等的是小满：蛊王听说有个汉人的娃娃到处打听那一夜。

column2: The blowgunners are knocked out of the trees and their tubes snapped. A prisoner says the Gu King gave only one order: 'If that child finds his answer, bring him to me.' Xiaoman grips the mule bell till his knuckles go white. 'He needn't bring me. I'll go myself.'
column3: 吹箭手被打下了树，竹管折了一地。俘虏说蛊王只交代了一句：「那个娃娃要是问出了答案，就带他来见我。」小满攥着马铃，攥得指节发白：「不用他带，我自己会去。」

column2: The Quack's Lean-To
column3: 郎中棚

column2: A Han doctor has put up a lean-to by the road and tells everyone he was one of the Qianli caravan ten years ago, 'come back at last'. The villagers believe him, bring chickens and rice, and queue for his remedies, while his hangers-on collect the gifts and shove out anyone who asks too many questions. Xiaoman hears this, runs straight over and tugs at his sleeve. 'Do you know Zhou Mancang?'
column3: 路边一个汉人郎中搭了个棚子，逢人就说自己是十年前千里号马帮的人，「回来了」。寨民信了，送鸡送米，排着队请他看病。他身边几个跟班专管收礼，谁问多了就把谁推出棚外。小满一听，拔腿就跑过去，扯着他的袖子问：「你认不认得周满仓？」

column2: The hangers-on chased off, the quack is exposed: he never went near the fog, and his stories come from a tea stall beyond the hills. But one thing he heard is true. Wintering in the Gu villages, each caravan man was adopted by a 'hearth family' and ate and slept by their fire, and the day they left, hundreds of households wept together. Xiaoman thinks about it, head down: his mother's house was his father's hearth family.
column3: 跟班被打跑，郎中露了馅：他压根没进过雾，故事是在山外茶棚里听来的。可他听来的有一件是真事：马帮在蛊寨过冬，每个人都认了一家「火塘亲」，吃住都在那家火塘边，走的那天，几百户人家哭成一片。小满低头想了想：阿妈家，就是阿爸的火塘亲。

column2: Nine-Horn Toll
column3: 九角酒

column2: A row of road-blocking wine stands at the crossroads: by Miao custom, guests drink rice wine from a horn before they enter a village. But a gang of drunks has taken the crossroads and turned welcome into toll: a coin for every horn, nobody passes till all nine are drunk, and whoever can't manage gets held down and the rest poured into him. They've pinned Xiaoman and poured half a horn into him, and he's choking, red in the face.
column3: 路口摆着一排拦路酒，本是苗寨迎客的规矩：牛角里斟满米酒，喝了才进寨。如今一伙酒鬼占了路口，把迎客酒改成了收钱酒，喝一角交一钱，九角不喝完不许过，喝不下的就按住灌。小满被他们按着灌了半角，呛得满脸通红。

column2: The drunks laid out in a puddle of their own making, villagers arrive and pour you three horns, as the real custom has it. The old man in charge of the wine says that when the caravan came ten years ago they drank ninety-nine jars, Zhou Mancang most of all, and when he was drunk he sang Han songs that all said the same thing: 'Back next year, back next year.'
column3: 酒鬼们被打倒，自己醉成了一滩。寨里的人赶来，照真规矩只给你们斟了三角。管酒的老人说，十年前马帮进寨那天，喝掉了九十九坛，周满仓喝得最多，醉了就唱汉人的歌，唱的都是一个意思：「明年还来，明年还来。」

column2: The Bullfight Green
column3: 斗牛坪

column2: The green is ringed with people and two great water buffalo lock horns in a spray of mud: the village's yearly bullfight. A gang of gamblers has taken over the ring. They've quietly poured liquor into their own bull and sprinkled purgative beans in the other side's trough. When the losing villagers come to argue, out come the knives. 'A bet's a bet. The bull's ours.'
column3: 坪子上围满了人，两头大水牯顶得泥浆四溅，是寨里一年一回的斗牛。一伙赌棍把斗牛场包了，偷偷给自家的牛灌了酒，又往对家的牛槽里撒巴豆。输了牛的寨民来理论，赌棍们就亮出刀子：「愿赌服输，牛归我们。」

column2: The gamblers thrown off the green, the bulls go home to their owners. The old herdsman says that ten years ago, on this very green, a Han caravan brought their mules to fight the village bulls. Mules can't butt like buffalo, and they lost everything, then came back next day to stand the whole village a drink. They left the following spring. A year after that, for the first time, a voice began calling names at night.
column3: 赌棍被撵出坪子，牛还给了原主。看牛的老汉说，十年前也是在这片坪子上，一伙汉人马帮拉着骡子来跟寨里斗了一回，骡子顶不过水牯，输得精光，第二天却来请全寨喝酒。第二年开春他们走了。又过了一年，夜里头一回有了喊名字的声音。

column2: The Fenced Herb Plot
column3: 圈药田

column2: A patch of herbs in the forest has been fenced with bamboo hung with thorny vines and traps, and guards and blowgunners watch it day and night. The plant growing inside has purple flowers; the villagers call it 'thread-loosener', because a brew of it slackens the gold thread on a wrist by one turn. The guards say it's the Gu King's order: the herb plot belongs to him, and anyone who picks a single plant loses a finger.
column3: 林中一片药田被竹篱圈了起来，篱上挂着刺藤和兽夹，寨丁带着吹箭手日夜守着。田里长的是一种开紫花的草，寨民叫它「松丝草」，煎水喝了，手腕上的金丝能松一圈。守田的寨丁说，这是蛊王的令：药田归蛊王，谁采一棵，砍一根指头。

column2: The guards beaten back and the fence pushed over, villagers flood in. The three with gold thread on their wrists drink the brew, and the thread does loosen by a turn, but it doesn't break. A Kou turns up too, crouches at the edge, pinches a sprig and sniffs it. 'Right herb, not enough of it. Loosening it won't do. It needs feeding.'
column3: 寨丁被打退，竹篱推倒了，寨民一拥而进。那三个手上缠了金丝的人喝了药汤，金丝果然松了一圈，却还是没断。阿蔻也来了，蹲在田边掐了一把草闻了闻：「草是对的，只是不够。光松它不行，得喂饱它。」

column2: The Weaver's Loft
column3: 织锦楼

column2: In a stilt house at the forest's edge lives a brocade weaver with gold thread round her wrist. It has been there nine years; she was the first in the village to answer the call. She isn't afraid. She weaves every day, and always the same picture: a road running south and a string of horses on it. Brocade dealers have taken a fancy to her work and come with men to take it by force. She stands in front of her loom, the gold thread biting her wrist white.
column3: 林边的吊脚楼里住着个织锦的女人，手腕上缠着金丝，缠了九年，是寨里头一个应名的人。她不怕，每天照样织锦，织来织去是同一幅：一条路往南，路上一串马。一伙贩锦缎的商贩看上了她的锦，带着人上门硬抢，她把织机护在身后，金丝勒得手腕发白。

column2: The dealers are thrown down the stairs and the loom is safe. On the night she answered, she says, the voice called 'Luo Yao', the name of the man she waits for, in his very voice. She followed it to the forest's edge, and the gold thread wound itself round her wrist. 'Right then I knew he was still alive.' She touches the thread. 'The other end is tied to him.'
column3: 商贩被赶下了楼，织机保住了。女人说她应名那一夜，喊的是「罗幺」，她等的那个人的名字，那声音学得一模一样。她跟着走到林子边，金丝就缠上了手。「那一下我就知道，他还活着，」她摸着金丝说，「丝那头，是拴在他身上的。」

column2: Hearth-Tax Camp
column3: 火塘税营

column2: In a big forest camp the chieftain's tax men and their swordsmen are collecting 'hearth tax' door to door: every family that lit a hearth and gave lodging to the Han caravan ten years ago must pay again each year, because, they say, those families got rich on Han silver. More than two hundred households are on the list, and A Xiu's is on the first page. Those who can't pay have their hearthstones prised up in lieu.
column3: 林中一座大营，土司派来的税丁带着刀手，挨家挨户收「火塘税」：十年前给汉人马帮烧过火塘、留过宿的人家，每年都得补交一份，说他们那年挣了汉人的银子。名单上两百多户，阿秀家在第一页。交不起的，就扒了火塘边的灶石抵税。

column2: The camp scattered, the list is yours: over two hundred households, a Han name written after each, and after A Xiu's, 'Zhou Mancang'. The last page also notes where the caravan wintered: a big stone-walled compound down the slope, which the Gu King sealed after they left and set elite guards on. Xiaoman holds the list and his hands won't stop shaking.
column3: 税营被打散，名单落到你们手里：两百多户人家，每户后面写着一个汉名，阿秀家后面写的是「周满仓」。名单最后一页还记着马帮冬营的地方：坡下一座石墙大院，马帮走后被蛊王封了，派精兵守着。小满拿着名单，手一直在抖。

column2: Bell-Thief Slope
column3: 偷铃坡

column2: On the rocky slope at the end of this dead end lives a big troop of monkeys the villagers call 'mountain imps'. They stole a few strings of silver bells from the villages and learned a trick: ring them at the edge of the trees, and the villagers freeze where they stand, as the rules say. Then the troop pours in, tips over the pots, grabs the food and runs off with sacks of sticky rice, while the frozen villagers watch, not one daring to move a foot.
column3: 死路尽头的石坡上住着一大群猴子，寨里叫它们「山魈」。它们从寨里偷了几串银铃，学会了一招：先在林边摇铃，寨民照规矩原地站住，猴群就趁机冲进寨子，掀锅抢饭，扛起糯米就跑。站着不动的寨民眼睁睁看着，一个也不敢挪步。

column2: The troop is driven back up the slope and a few strings of bells recovered. But they breed litter after litter, and the clever ones teach the trick to the young, so they'll be down again before long; all you can do is clear them out every so often. The string round the troop king's neck rings loudest, and it sounds familiar: exactly the note of the bells on A Kou's basket.
column3: 猴群被赶回了石坡，银铃抢回来几串。可这群猴子一窝接一窝地生，聪明的几只把招数教给小的，过一阵还会下山再来，只能隔些日子来清一回。猴王脖子上那串铃最响，你们听着耳熟：跟阿蔻篓上那一串，是一个声。

column2: The Winter Compound
column3: 冬营院

column2: At the end of the dead end below the slope stands a big stone-walled compound: the caravan's winter quarters from the list. The gate bears a seal stamped with the golden silkworm, blowgunners squat on the walls and Gu riders stand inside the gate, the Gu King's best, on watch for ten years, and anyone who comes near gets a volley of bamboo darts. Xiaoman lies flat on the slope watching. His mother told him his father slept in the third bunk from the east end that winter.
column3: 坡下死路尽头一座石墙大院，就是名单上记的马帮冬营。院门上贴着金蚕印的封条，墙头蹲着吹箭手，门里站着蛊骑，都是蛊王最精的人，守了十年，谁走近就是一排竹箭。小满趴在坡上看，说阿妈讲过，阿爸那年冬天就睡在院子东头第三个铺位。

column2: The elite guards beaten back, the seal is torn down. Rows of straw bunks are still inside. Under the third from the east end lies a little carved wooden horse, 'for the baby' cut into its belly. A watch board is nailed to the wall, and its last line is in deputy chief Song Ge's hand: 'Fifteenth of the first month, midnight, whole company to the Gu King's village.' Xiaoman tucks the horse inside his coat and stares at that line for a long time.
column3: 精兵被打退，封条撕了。院里一排排草铺还在，东头第三个铺位底下压着一只木刻的小马，马肚子上刻着「给娃」。墙上钉着一块值更牌，最后一行是副镖头宋戈的字：「正月十五，子时，全队往蛊王寨。」小满把小马揣进怀里，盯着那行字看了很久。

column2: The Gu Buyers' Sheds
column3: 收蛊棚

column2: A sprawl of sheds in the open flies a banner: 'Gu bought, top prices'. A rich merchant from beyond the hills has hired a crowd of caravan guards to collect a few jars of real gu to take home and slip to his business rivals. They go village to village seizing jars, and the ones sealed with red cloth most of all. The villagers beg them not to touch those. The guards roar with laughter and stack them on the carts, one in each hand.
column3: 野地里搭着一大片棚子，挂着「高价收蛊」的旗，是山外来的富商，雇了一大帮镖师，想收几罐真蛊回去，下给生意场上的对头。他们挨寨上门，见罐子就抢，红布封口的抢得最凶。寨民拦着说那罐子碰不得，镖师们哈哈大笑，一手一个往车上码。

column2: The guards scattered, the seized jars fill half a shed, and you keep the rule: you don't count a single one. One guard can't help himself, lifts a corner of red cloth and peeks inside, goes white and scrambles away on all fours. There's no insect in the jar. Only a lock of hair, a letter never opened, and the sole of a shoe, half stitched.
column3: 镖师们被打散，抢来的罐子堆了半个棚子，你们照着规矩，一个也没数。一个镖师贪心不死，掀开一角红布往里瞧，瞧完脸都白了，连滚带爬地跑了。罐里没有虫：只有一绺头发、一封没拆的信，和一只纳了一半的鞋底。

column2: Calling Ridge
column3: 喊名岗

column2: As soon as night falls, torches flare on the earthen ridge and a troop of Gu riders sits their horses bellowing names down at the village below: Han names, one after another, like a roll call. The villagers bar their doors and windows and cover their children's ears. One old man at the foot of the ridge can't stand it, throws open his window and curses them, and the riders spur straight down at him.
column3: 天一黑，野地的土岗上就亮起火把，一伙蛊骑骑在马上，对着岗下的寨子扯着嗓子喊名字，喊的都是汉名，一个接一个，像在点卯。寨里人关紧门窗，捂着孩子的耳朵。岗下有个老汉忍不住，开窗骂了一句，蛊骑们就打马冲了下去。

column2: The riders are knocked off the ridge, their torches dropped in the grass. A prisoner says it's the Gu King's order: the thing in the forest is too hungry to call loud enough now, so the King sends them to call for it. 'One comes, one feeds it.' Inside his coat is a list of Han names copied out line by line. It stops at line two hundred and ninety-nine.
column3: 蛊骑被打下了岗，火把丢了一地。俘虏说这是蛊王的令：林子里那东西饿得喊不动人了，蛊王就派他们来帮着喊，「喊来一个，喂它一个」。他怀里揣着一张名单，汉名一行行抄着，抄到二百九十九行，就没了。

column2: Low-Flame Cave
column3: 矮火洞

column2: At the foot of the hill where the dead end stops there's a limestone cave, its mouth stacked with sacks: the den of smugglers who boil saltpetre earth on the sly. You creep in by night. The cave is quiet, the stalactites dripping. Along the lowest stretch of the floor the smugglers lie in a row, heads pillowed on sacks, sleeping so soundly not one of them snores. You carry your torches down toward them, and the flames shrink lower with every step, down to a bead of blue. Not one chest in that row is rising.
column3: 死路尽头的山脚有个溶洞，洞口垒着麻袋，是一伙偷熬硝土的私贩的窝。你们趁夜摸进去，洞里很静，钟乳石滴着水，私贩们沿着洞底最低的那一片躺了一排，枕着麻袋睡得正熟，连鼾声都没有。你们举着火把往下走，火苗越走越矮，矮成豆大的一点蓝光。躺着的那一排人，胸口一个也没有起伏。

column2: The few smugglers sleeping up on a stone ledge wake and fight, and end up tied. You drag the row from the cave floor up to the high ground one by one, and after a long while they gasp back to life one after another. The trussed smugglers explain: a 'dead air' gathers at the bottom of the cave, heavier than the wind, lying in the lowest places; lie down in it and you don't wake, and when torches shrink, it's there. 'The caravan men taught the villages that, back then,' one mutters. 'We didn't listen.'
column3: 高处石台上睡着的几个私贩被惊醒，打了一场，被捆了。洞底那一排人被你们拖上高处，好一阵才喘过气来。私贩说，洞底积着一层「闷气」，比风重，沉在最低处，人躺进去就醒不过来，火把矮了，就是它到了。「马帮的人当年教过寨里，」他嘟囔，「是我们不听。」

column2: The Bean-Counting Shrine
column3: 数豆庙

column2: At the edge of the open ground stands a little earth-god shrine, and on its threshold sits a small boy who counts beans every day. At two hundred and ninety-nine he stops, tips them back into the bowl and starts again. Some passing soldiers-turned-bullies find him in the way, kick over the bowl and scatter the beans, then grab his collar and order him to keep counting. 'Go on, count to three hundred for us. Let's see what happens!'
column3: 野地边一座小土地庙，门槛上坐着个小娃，每天数豆子，数到二百九十九就停，倒回碗里，从头再数。几个兵痞路过，嫌他碍事，一脚踢翻了碗，豆子撒了一地，又揪着他的领子逼他当面往下数：「数到三百给我们听听，看能出什么事！」

column2: The bullies gone, the beans are picked up one by one. His grandpa taught him, the boy says: count to three hundred and the thing in the forest thinks you're calling the roll of its people, and when you reach the last one it comes to claim him. 'Grandpa says it has one place that's always been empty. Ten years it's looked and found nobody.' He hugs the bowl and whispers, 'Whoever counts to three hundred, it thinks that's him.'
column3: 兵痞被赶走，豆子一颗颗捡了回来。小娃说是阿爷教的：数到三百，林子里那东西会当你在点它的人，点到最后一个，它就要来认。「阿爷说，它那里有一个位子一直空着，找了十年也没找着人，」他捧着碗小声说，「谁数到三百，它就当是谁。」

column2: Duck-Shed Marsh
column3: 鸭棚泽

column2: A few duck sheds stand at the marsh's edge. Every morning the widow A Rong lets her ducks out onto the water and every evening whistles them back with a bamboo whistle. A party of fowlers with matchlocks has camped by the marsh, roasting her ducks daily until the bones make a little hill, and now they demand ten more a day. A Rong blows her whistle fit to shake the sky, and the fowlers net every duck that comes.
column3: 沼泽边几座鸭棚，养鸭的寡妇阿蓉一早放鸭下泽，傍晚吹竹哨收回。一伙扛火铳的打鸟客在泽边扎了营，天天偷她的鸭子烤着吃，鸭骨头堆成了小山，还逼她每天再交十只。阿蓉把竹哨吹得震天响，鸭子却被他们拿网兜了个干净。

column2: The fowlers are pitched into the mud and the ducks set free one by one. A Rong hears that Xiaoman is asking about that night and purses her lips. 'Why ask me? Go and ask Granary-Keeper Long. Those Han men left owing him a whole winter's grain, and he's cursed them to anyone who'll listen for ten years.'
column3: 打鸟客被赶进了泥里，鸭子一只只放了回去。阿蓉听说小满在打听那一夜，撇了撇嘴：「问我做什么？去问仓官老龙。那伙汉人走的时候欠了他一冬天的粮，他见人就骂，骂了十年了。」

column2: Market-Day Flat
column3: 赶场坝

column2: This flat in the forest is where the seven villages hold market, on every fifth and tenth day, trading mountain goods, timber and stone. But it has been dead for years: the Gu King's guards planted grass markers at its four corners and closed it, saying that when crowds gather the voice calls all the harder at night. Villagers' timber rots in the woods, the masons' stone finds no buyer, and the old stone scale in the middle of the flat is furred with moss.
column3: 林中坝子是七寨赶场的地方，逢五逢十一场，山货、木料、石料都在这里换。可场子已经冷了好几年：蛊王的寨丁在坝子四角插了草标，说赶场的人一多，夜里那声音就喊得凶，封了。寨民的木料堆在林子里烂，石匠的石料没人要，坝子当中的老石秤长满了青苔。

column2: Markers pulled, guards scattered, scale scrubbed clean, and the market crowds come pouring in from all seven villages again. The hills have plenty of wood and little stone, and the masons below the flat need timber to burn their lime, so trade in wood for stone opens here.  As the market breaks up, Yan Bao arrives with his curfew men and says he won't stand in the way: 'The rules never said no market.' He hands you a twist of wood shavings scraped from the back of the board on the village gate. 'Your noses are sharp. Tell me what that smells of.' Herbs: exactly the smell of the silver-bell stall.
column3: 草标拔了，寨丁散了，石秤擦干净，赶场的人又从七个寨子涌了过来。山里木多石少，坝下的石匠缺木头烧石灰，木换石的买卖就此开张。散场时，岩保带着宵禁营的人来了，说他不拦了：「规矩里又没写不许赶场。」他交给你们一小包木屑，是寨门那块规矩牌背面刮下来的：「你们鼻子灵，闻闻是什么味儿。」一股草药味，跟银铃药摊上的一模一样。

column2: The Unpaid Granary
column3: 欠粮仓

column2: At a big granary in the open, Granary-Keeper Long and a crew of debt-collecting guards are hauling A Xiu's family's grain into his store. Ten years ago the Han caravan ate a winter of his grain and left without paying back a single kernel, and since Zhou Mancang belonged to A Xiu's hearth, her family owes the debt. Xiaoman blocks the granary door, and Long raps him on the head with his pipe, again and again.
column3: 野地里一座大粮仓，仓官老龙带着一帮讨债的寨丁，正押着阿秀家的谷子往仓里搬：十年前汉人马帮吃了他一冬天的粮，走的时候一粒没还，周满仓是阿秀家的火塘亲，这账就该阿秀家还。小满拦在仓门口，老龙拿烟杆一下下敲他的脑袋。

column2: The collectors scattered, the grain goes back. Long gives his version. 'They slipped off in the middle of the night! Ate the grain and ran, what more is there to say?' He flings down an IOU: 'Owed to the Gu villages, one winter's grain. Next first month, every man comes back to repay.' Below it, fingerprints packed tight. Xiaoman starts counting them, and before he's done A Xiu puts her hand over his. The fifth rule.
column3: 讨债的寨丁被打散，谷子搬了回去。老龙讲他的说法：「他们是半夜偷偷溜的！欠了粮就跑，还有什么好说？」他甩出一张欠条：「欠蛊寨一冬粮，来年正月，人人回来还。」底下按着密密麻麻的指印。小满数了起来，没数完，阿秀就按住了他的手：第五条规矩。

column2: Song-Ban Hamlet
column3: 禁歌寨

column2: On a hamlet's dancing ground in the forest, a young man is tied to a post with a rag stuffed in his mouth. He's the apprentice of the song master Bang Gong, and two days ago he sang a passage of the old songs here, the one about that night of the fifteenth of the first month ten years ago, and was seized halfway through: the Gu King forbids anyone to sing it. Sing again, say the guards, and he goes to feed the jars.
column3: 林中一座寨子的坪上，一个后生被寨丁绑在柱子上，嘴里塞着布。他是歌师榜公的徒弟，前天在坪上唱了一段古歌，唱的是十年前正月十五那一夜，唱到一半就被抓了：蛊王不许人唱那一段。寨丁们说，再唱，就把他送去喂罐。

column2: The guards chased off, the young man spits out the rag, and his first words are 'Where's my master?' Bang Gong was taken by the Gu King's men and is locked in the Old Song Hall deep in the forest. 'He's the only one who can sing that passage through.' The apprentice learned just the opening: 'Fifteenth night, the moon stands high, three hundred Han lads climb the village stair...' What comes next, he doesn't know.
column3: 寨丁被打跑，后生吐掉嘴里的布，头一句就问：「我师父呢？」榜公被蛊王的人带走了，关在林子深处的古歌堂里，「那一段只有他会唱全」。后生只学了开头两句：「正月十五月当头，三百汉郎上寨楼……」后面是什么，他不知道。

column2: The Empty Herb House
column3: 空药楼

column2: At the end of a dead end stands a stilt house with its stairs hacked away, ringed below by the Gu King's best blowgunners and Gu riders, who have kept watch here for ten years. Villagers say it was once the house of the Gu woman. She fell out with the Gu King and vanished in a single night, so he set men to watch the place for the day she walks back into the trap. A row of dried herbs hangs under the eaves, and after ten years they still smell when the wind stirs them.
column3: 死路尽头一座吊脚楼，楼梯被砍断了，楼下围着蛊王最精的吹箭手和蛊骑，一守就是十年。寨民说这是从前蛊婆的屋子，蛊婆跟蛊王翻了脸，一夜之间不见了，蛊王就派人守着，等她回来自投罗网。楼檐下挂着一排风干的草药，十年了，风一吹还有味儿。

column2: The elite guards beaten back, you climb in. Dust lies everywhere. On the table sits a stack of unused fir boards exactly like the one on the village gate, and the ink in the inkstone is mixed with herb dregs. An empty bell rack is nailed to the wall, its bells all gone. In the corner the floor is worn in a ring, the very shape of a basket that stood there for years.
column3: 守楼的精兵被打退了。楼里落满了灰，桌上留着一叠没用完的杉木牌，跟寨门那块一模一样，砚台里的墨掺着药渣。墙上钉着一只空的铃架，铃都不在了。墙角还有一圈磨出来的印子，正是一只背篓常年靠在那里的形状。

column2: Bell-Return Slope
column3: 回铃坡

column2: On a slope in the open, Gu riders have A Kou surrounded. Her basket is knocked over and her herbs lie strewn on the ground. Their leader holds up a silver bell and laughs. 'Ten years we've looked for you, and you were hiding on the far side of the fog!' The villagers watch from a distance, none daring to move. A Kou doesn't hurry. She crouches and gathers her herbs handful by handful, then slowly unties the string of bells from her basket and takes it in her hand.
column3: 野地坡上，一伙蛊骑把阿蔻围在了中间，她的药篓被挑翻，草药撒了一地。领头的蛊骑举着一只银铃大笑：「找了你十年，原来躲到雾那头去了！」寨民远远站着，谁也不敢动。阿蔻不慌，蹲下来把草药一把把拢好，然后慢慢解下篓上那串银铃，拿在了手里。

column2: With the riders beaten off, the villagers finally gather round, though not too close. A Kou ties her bells back on and tells the truth. She is the one they call the Gu woman. She wrote the rules; the bells in the night are hers. 'At night threads go through the forest looking for people. When my bells ring, you stand still, and the thread goes past you.' She pats the red-sealed jar at the bottom of her basket. 'That's no wine yeast. That's my gu. I did tell you: don't take food from a person sitting alone by the road.'
column3: 蛊骑被打退，寨民这才围上来，又不敢靠太近。阿蔻系好银铃，说了实话：她就是寨民嘴里的蛊婆，规矩是她写的，铃是她摇的。「夜里林子里有丝在找人，铃一响，你们站住，丝就过去了。」她拍拍篓底那只红布罐：「这里头不是酒曲，是我的蛊。我说过，路边独坐的人递的东西，莫接。」

column2: Rustlers' Camp
column3: 偷牛营

column2: In a big forest camp, rustlers from beyond the hills, dozens of them, are driving dozens of stolen buffalo toward the outside world. The bells round the beasts' necks come in every size, and one old buffalo wears a Han brass bell just like Xiaoman's. He spots it at once and dives in among the herd, and the rustlers' whips come cracking after him.
column3: 林子里一座大营，是一伙山外来的偷牛贼，几十号人，赶着几十头偷来的水牛往山外走。牛脖子上的铃大大小小，有一头老水牛挂的却是汉人的铜铃，跟小满那只一个样。小满一眼认出来，拔腿就往牛群里钻，偷牛贼的鞭子跟着就抽了过来。

column2: The rustlers scattered, the buffalo are driven home. The old buffalo's owner says the caravan gave the brass bells as they left, one to each hearth family. 'They said, when you hear it ring, pretend it's us coming back.' Xiaoman knocks his own bell against it. The two ring with the same voice.
column3: 偷牛贼被打散，牛一头头赶回了寨。那头老水牛的主家说，铜铃是马帮走的时候送的，每家火塘亲一只：「他们说，听见铃响，就当是我们回来了。」小满拿自己那只铃跟它碰了碰，两只铃一个声。

column2: Midnight Slope
column3: 子时坡

column2: On a forest slope A Xiu catches up with you, and on her heels comes a pack of guards the Gu King has sent for Xiaoman. She plants herself in front of her son, gripping her wooden shuttle like a knife. The King wants only the child, the guards say, not the grown-ups; she should stand aside. She doesn't give an inch.
column3: 林中坡上，阿秀追了上来，后面跟着一伙寨丁，是蛊王派来抓小满的。阿秀拦在儿子前头，手里攥着织布的木梭，像攥着一把刀。寨丁们说蛊王只要娃娃，不要大人，叫她让开。她一步也不让。

column2: The guards are driven off. Catching her breath, A Xiu finally speaks. That night she followed too, all the way to the Gu King's gate, and saw Zhou Mancang turn and smile at her before he went in with the rest. 'He went in smiling,' she says. 'That's what I've been afraid of. That he went because he wanted to.'
column3: 寨丁被打退了。阿秀喘着气，终于说了：那一夜她也跟出去了，一直跟到蛊王寨门口，看见周满仓回头冲她笑了一下，就跟着大伙进去了。「他是笑着进去的，」她说，「我怕的就是这个。我怕他是心甘情愿走的。」

column2: Song-Guard Camp
column3: 守歌营

column2: In the forest outside the Old Song Hall stands a big camp, Gu riders and blowgunners guarding the way in. A brass gong hangs at the gate with two big words painted on it: 'No Singing'. Hum a single tune in this camp and you're dragged out and beaten, so it is uncannily quiet. Even the horses hardly whinny.
column3: 古歌堂外的林子里扎着一座大营，蛊骑和吹箭手守着去古歌堂的路，营门口挂着一面铜锣，锣上写着「禁歌」两个大字。营里谁哼一句小调就要被拖出来打一顿，所以这座营出奇地静，连马都不怎么叫。

column2: You break the camp, and Xiaoman kicks over the 'No Singing' gong. It hits the ground with a clang that echoes through the whole forest. The captured rider captain says the Gu King doesn't fear that song for being ugly. 'He's afraid that once people hear it, they won't seal anything into the jars any more.'
column3: 大营被你们冲破，那面「禁歌」锣被小满一脚踢翻，咣当一声，满林子都是回音。被俘的蛊骑头目说，蛊王怕那段古歌，不是嫌它难听：「是怕寨里人听完了，就不肯再往罐里封东西了。」

column2: The Empty Brick Rack
column3: 空砖架

column2: On the upper floor of a stilt house in the forest, the walls are lined with bamboo pigeonholes, three hundred of them, each meant to hold half a tea brick, and most stand empty. Blowgunners are turning the place over, stuffing the remaining halves into sacks: the Gu King wants them. The old woman who keeps the house sits at the top of the stairs hugging one brick, and whacks the feet of anyone who comes up with her stick.
column3: 林中一座吊脚楼的二楼，墙上钉着一排排竹格，三百格，每格本该放半块茶砖，如今大半空着。一伙吹箭手正在楼里翻箱倒柜，把剩下的半砖往麻袋里塞，说是蛊王要的。看楼的老阿婆抱着一块砖坐在楼梯口，谁上来就拿拐棍敲谁的脚背。

column2: The blowgunners chased downstairs, the halves are tipped back into their pigeonholes: nine of them. The old woman says these bricks came from the tea-pressing works up north ten years ago and were given into the keeping of the elder Yan Gong, each tied with a bamboo tag bearing a name. 'The Gu King wants them to feed his silkworm. Yan Gong refused and took the rest into the Elders' Council house to hide. These nine were too many for him to carry.'
column3: 吹箭手被赶下楼，麻袋里的半砖倒回竹格，一共九块。老阿婆说，这些砖是十年前从北边焙茶坊送来的，交给寨老岩公收着，每块系一根竹签，签上一个名字。「蛊王要拿去喂蚕，岩公不肯，带着剩下的砖躲进寨老会去了。这九块，是他搬不动落下的。」

column2: Brass-Basin Flat
column3: 铜盆坝

column2: News travels faster than wind. The guards of a village on the flat block the road with burning torches, banging brass basins to drive the Gu woman out. 'Let the Gu woman in and the children sicken!' They pelt A Kou with mud; she doesn't dodge, and it spatters all over her. Yan Bao is in the crowd, torn both ways, until at last he swings his javelin crosswise and plants himself in front of her.
column3: 消息比风传得还快。野地上一座寨子的寨丁敲着铜盆、举着火把堵在路口，要把蛊婆撵出去：「蛊婆进寨，娃娃要病！」他们朝阿蔻扔泥巴，她不躲，泥点子溅了一身。岩保也在人群里，左右为难，最后把梭镖往前一横，挡在了她前面。

column2: You and Yan Bao hold the guards back, and the torches go out. A Kou brushes off the mud and tells the old story. She was the Gu King's apprentice. Ten years ago, when the Qianli caravan wintered in the villages, she was the one who nursed them through the miasma fever, and in spring she watched the Gu King bind their hearts with his golden silkworm. Then they didn't come back, the silkworm went hungry, and the King meant to fill it with the villagers. She refused, wrote the rules in a single night, and was driven out.
column3: 寨丁们被拦了下来，火把灭了。阿蔻拍掉身上的泥，讲起旧事：她原是蛊王的徒弟，十年前千里号在寨里过冬，是她治好了他们的瘴病；开春，她眼看着蛊王拿金蚕给他们拴了心。后来他们没回来，金蚕饿了，蛊王要拿寨里的人去填，她不肯，连夜写了规矩，被撵了出去。

column2: Bounty Wood
column3: 悬赏林

column2: Bounty hunters bar your way in the forest. Their leader shows you a notice: 'Fifty taels to whoever takes the Gu woman', stamped with a golden silkworm seal. They come from beyond the hills and believe in silver, not gu. The Gu woman is worth fifty taels, they say, and your cartload stays here too. A Kou sits at the back of your cart, head down, pounding herbs, as if she hasn't heard a word.
column3: 林子里一伙赏金客拦住了你们，领头的亮出一张告示：「擒蛊婆者，赏银五十两」，落款盖着一只金蚕的印。他们是山外来的，不信蛊，只信银子，说蛊婆一个值五十两，你们这一车货也得留下。阿蔻坐在你们车后头低头捣药，像没听见。

column2: The bounty hunters run, and A Kou uses their notice to steady her mortar. She went north into the fog, she says, to find one of the Qianli people and bring him back to feed the silkworm. 'It knows their hearts. Anything else it eats doesn't fill it.' She found nobody, but she found you. She glances at your cart. 'You've got half a tea brick in there, haven't you.'
column3: 赏金客被打跑了，告示被阿蔻拿去垫了药臼。她说她往北进雾，是想找一个千里号的人带回来喂蚕：「金蚕认的是他们的心，喂别的都不顶饿。」人没找着，倒找着了你们。她看了一眼你们的车：「你们车上，有半块茶砖吧。」

column2: Reed-Pipe Ground
column3: 芦笙场

column2: Out in the open lies a reed-pipe ground where young men should play their pipes and girls dance; now it's grown over with grass. Blowgunners use it as a range, competing to hit the pipes: the reed pipes villagers hid under their floorboards, dug out one by one and stuck in the ground as targets. Xiaoman recognises one. Its wind chest is carved with the Han character 'Man'.
column3: 野地里一片芦笙场，本该是后生吹芦笙、姑娘跳舞的地方，如今长满了草。一伙吹箭手把场子当了靶场，比赛射芦笙管：寨里人藏在楼板底下的芦笙，被他们一支支翻出来插在地上当靶子。小满认出其中一支，笙斗上刻着个汉字「满」。

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the pipes are gathered up. The carved one is a pipe Zhou Mancang learned to make from the village lads that winter; he finished only half, and the other pipes are still missing. Bang Gong's apprentice puts it to his lips. It leaks air, but it can still play the first two lines of that old song. The Old Song Hall is in the forest just ahead.
column3: 吹箭手被赶走，芦笙一支支捡了回来。那支刻字的芦笙，是周满仓那年冬天跟寨里后生学着做的，只做好一半，另一半笙管还空着。榜公的徒弟接过去吹了一口，漏风，却还吹得出那段古歌的头两句。古歌堂就在前面林子里。

column2: The Old Song Hall
column3: 古歌堂

column2: Pine torches burn in the Old Song Hall, and the song master Bang Gong, past eighty, white beard down to his chest, is tied to a pillar. The guards won't let him speak, so he keeps his eyes shut and taps out a rhythm on the pillar with one finger. Xiaoman bursts in and pours out all three stories at once: the night guard says the gu took them, the granary keeper says they ran from a debt, his mother says they walked in smiling. 'Which one is it?' The guards raise their javelins.
column3: 林中古歌堂里点着松明，歌师榜公被绑在堂柱上，八十多岁了，白胡子拖到胸口。守堂的寨丁不让他开口，他就闭着眼，一根手指在柱子上敲拍子。小满冲进来，一口气把三个人的话说给他听：守夜人说是被蛊走的，仓官说是欠了债跑的，阿妈说是笑着进去的。「到底是哪一个？」寨丁们举起了梭镖。

column2: The guards thrown out, Bang Gong clears his throat and sings the passage through. That night the Han lads went to the Gu King's village of their own accord and begged the golden silkworm to tie their hearts together: 'We lost one in the fog. We won't lose another.' With their hearts tied, they owed a promise to come back each year and feed the silkworm. At dawn they left the village singing and went on south. Bang Gong opens his eyes. 'All three told you the truth, and each told you only half.'
column3: 寨丁被赶出堂，榜公把那段古歌唱全了：那一夜，汉郎们自己去了蛊王寨，求金蚕把他们的心拴在一处，「雾里丢过一个，不能再丢」；拴了心，就欠下了年年回来喂蚕的约；天亮时，他们唱着歌往南去了。榜公睁开眼：「三个人说的都对，又都只说了一半。」

column2: Rice-Fish Paddies
column3: 稻鱼田

column2: A few terraced paddies lie among the trees, rice seedlings standing in the water and carp swimming beneath them: the village's fish and rice for the year. The chieftain's household men have taken the fields and are netting the fish to pickle as sour fish, a whole roomful of it, tribute for the Gu King, they say. The villagers can only crouch on the dykes and watch their fish taken one by one.
column3: 林间几块梯田，田里插着秧，秧底下游着鲤鱼，是寨里一年的鱼和米。土司家的家丁占了田，把鱼捞上来腌成酸鱼，堆了一屋子，说是献给蛊王的贡。寨里的人只能蹲在田埂上，看着鱼一条条被捞走。

column2: The household men thrown out, fresh fry go back into the fields. Ten years ago, the villagers say, the caravan ate rice-blossom carp here all winter. When they left, each man took half a brick inside his coat and handed the other half to Yan Gong one at a time, calling out his name, and each time Yan Gong answered 'Kept.' 'For the last brick nobody called a name,' an old man says. 'Yan Gong answered all the same.'
column3: 家丁被赶走，田里又放下了鱼苗。寨里人说，十年前马帮在这里吃了一冬的稻花鱼，走时每人揣走半块砖，另一半挨个交到岩公手里，每交一块喊一声名字，岩公就应一声「收着」。「最后一块没人喊名字，」一个阿公说，「岩公也照样应了一声。」

column2: From the household men's store: six jars of pickled sour fish, thirty loads of sticky rice, a brood of ducks, and seven silver combs snatched from girls' hair, each one returned to its owner.
column3: 抄出家丁腌好的酸鱼六坛、糯米三十担、一窝鸭子，还有他们从姑娘们头上抢来的七把银梳，一把把还给了原主。

column2: Every time you pass, the old man at the field's edge scoops out two fat carp, threads a rice straw through their gills and hands them over. 'Paddy fish grow on rice blossom. Roast them on the road. You'll see.'
column3: 每次路过，田边的阿公都从田里捞两尾肥鲤鱼，拿稻草穿了鳃递给你们：「田里的鱼吃稻花长的，路上烤了吃，香。」

column2: The Black-Mark Shed
column3: 黑印猎棚

column2: In a hunters' shed deep in the forest lies the hunter Wu Dagong, his face blue-grey, a black mark the size of a coin on his chest that makes him writhe if anything touches it. Two days ago he caught Gu riders herding people into the forest and loosed an arrow at them, and took a blowgun dart for it. Now riders have tracked him to the shed to drag him off 'for the jars', and he grips his bow with hands that shake too hard to draw it.
column3: 林子深处的猎棚里躺着猎户吴大弓，脸色发青，胸口一块铜钱大的黑印，一碰就疼得打滚。他前天撞见蛊骑往林子里赶人，放了一箭，回头就挨了一支吹箭。几个蛊骑追到了棚外，要把他拖回去「喂罐」，他抓着弓，手抖得拉不开弦。
