column2: The riders run. A Kou lifts Wu Dagong's eyelid and looks: the Gu King's 'heart-lock gu', she says, and it takes three medicines to undo. Grass-leaved sweet flag from Red Dhole Ridge, seven-leaf paris from Seven-Leaf Slope, and the last one must be taken from the Gu King's own people: the droppings the golden silkworm sheds while it spins. She lays a leaf on his chest and the black mark stops spreading.
column3: 蛊骑被打跑了。阿蔻翻开吴大弓的眼皮看了看，说是蛊王的「锁心蛊」，要三味药才解：一味是红豺岭上的石菖蒲，一味是七叶坡上的七叶一枝花，最后一味，得去蛊王的人手里拿：金蚕吐丝时落下的蚕沙。她在猎户胸口贴了一片草叶，黑印停住了，没再往外长。

column2: The Tag-Maker's Shop
column3: 篾签铺

column2: In a bamboo-weaver's shop in the forest lives an old craftsman with clever hands, who whittled three hundred bamboo tags for the elder ten years ago. Bullying ex-soldiers are holding him in his own shop and forcing him to cut fakes: they've stolen a few half bricks and want to swap in false name tags and sell them to tea dealers beyond the hills as 'genuine old Qianli tea', an ingot of silver a brick.
column3: 林中一间篾匠铺，老篾匠手巧，十年前替寨老削过三百根竹签。一伙兵痞把他扣在铺里，逼他削假签：他们手里偷来了几块半砖，想换上假名签，拿去卖给山外的茶商，冒充「千里号旧茶」，一块卖一锭银子。

column2: The bullies chased off, the fakes go into the fire and the three stolen halves are recovered. The old craftsman says he cut all three hundred tags the same length, and the names were written by the Han deputy chief, stroke by stroke by the hearth, all night long. 'When he came to the last tag,' the old man says, 'he put down his brush and said that one stays blank for now.'
column3: 兵痞被赶走，假签扔进火里烧了，偷来的三块半砖收回。老篾匠说，那三百根签他削得一般长，写名字的是那个汉人副镖头，在火塘边一笔一笔写了一夜。「写到最后一根，他搁了笔，」老篾匠说，「说这一根先空着。」

column2: White-Blaze Wood
column3: 白额林

column2: Bird catchers from beyond the hills have strung great nets across the forest road. Thrushes and bamboo partridges flap in the mesh, and so does a young mule with a white tuft on its forehead: the one from Wild Mule Slope, which has followed Xiaoman at a distance all this way. Delighted with their catch, the bird catchers reach for a rope to noose its neck.
column3: 林中路上，一伙山外来的捕鸟人张着大网，网里扑腾着画眉、竹鸡，还网住了一头小骡：额头一撮白毛，正是野骡坡上那一头，它一路远远跟着小满，跟到了这里。捕鸟人见网到了骡子，喜出望外，拿绳子去套它的脖子。

column2: The bird catchers run off, the nets are slashed, the birds fly, and the mule trots up to Xiaoman and butts his hand. His eyes still red from the song, Xiaoman says he's going to the Gu King's village to ring his father's bell, so the silkworm can carry the sound down the thread to his father. The mule snorts as if it means to come along.
column3: 捕鸟人被赶走，网割开了，鸟飞了，小骡跑到小满身边拿脑袋拱他的手。小满听完古歌，眼睛还红着，说他要去蛊王寨摇一摇阿爸的铃，让金蚕顺着丝把铃声带给阿爸。小骡打了个响鼻，像是要跟着去。

column2: The Old Tea Depot
column3: 旧茶栈

column2: A big tea depot stands in the forest, run by a dealer from beyond the hills with dozens of hired swordsmen to guard it. Its sign reads: 'Old Qianli tea, ten years aged, an ounce of gold an ounce.' The tea is half bricks bought from Gu riders, smashed and sold in little packets, with the bamboo tags thrown in, the names on them being 'the tea's provenance'. The queue runs out the door, and some buyers come for the names alone.
column3: 林中一座大茶栈，栈主是山外来的茶贩，雇了几十个护栈的刀手。栈里挂着招牌：「千里号旧茶，十年陈，一两一金」。茶是从蛊骑手里收来的半砖，敲碎了分成小包卖，竹签当添头，说签上的名字就是「茶的来历」。买主排到栈外，有人专门来买「名字」。

column2: You break up the depot and rescue twelve halves not yet smashed, matching their tags one by one. Some names are long and some short; one tag reads 'Luo Yao', another 'Zhou Mancang'. The dealer, on his knees, says he took it for ordinary old tea until he drank some. 'All night I was walking a road in my dreams. Woke up with aching soles.'
column3: 茶栈被你们打散，还没敲碎的半砖抢回来十二块，竹签一根根对上了。签上的名字有长有短，有一根写着「罗幺」，一根写着「周满仓」。栈主跪在地上说，他原以为是寻常的老茶，喝了才知道不寻常：「喝完一宿都在梦里赶路，醒来脚底板都是酸的。」

column2: Hold-the-Boy Hollow
column3: 拦娃坳

column2: In a forest hollow a few village elders and their own guards bar the way. They aren't the Gu King's men, just cautious old folk from the villages: a half-Han brat making trouble at the Gu King's door, and when the King loses his temper all seven villages will pay. The guards hold bamboo poles crosswise, saying 'it's for your own good' while they lay on with no mercy at all.
column3: 林中山坳里，几个寨老带着自家的寨丁拦住了去路。他们不是蛊王的人，是寨里怕事的长辈：小满一个汉人的崽，跑去蛊王寨闹，蛊王一发怒，七个寨子都要遭殃。寨丁们横着竹竿，嘴里说着「为你好」，手上却一点不留情。

column2: The guards pushed aside, the elders give up. The oldest sighs and presses a small cloth bundle into Xiaoman's hands: a packet of steel needles Zhou Mancang gave him that winter, Han needles, not one used in ten years for fear of wasting them. 'Tell your father the needles are good.' Xiaoman nods. He says he will.
column3: 寨丁们被推开，寨老们也不拦了。年纪最大的一个叹口气，掏出一个小布包塞给小满：是周满仓那年冬天送他的一包钢针，汉人的针，十年了一根也没舍得用。「替我跟你阿爸说，针好用。」小满点点头，说他会说的。

column2: Starve-Out Picket
column3: 断粮哨

column2: On the road to the Elders' Council house, blowgunners have set up a picket to stop anyone bringing food: sticky rice, smoked pork, even water, all confiscated, and the elders inside have gone hungry three days. A little girl tried to slip through with rice balls hidden in a bamboo tube. They found them and threw them on the ground for the dogs.
column3: 去寨老会的路上，一伙吹箭手设了哨卡，专截往寨老会送饭的人，送糯米的、送腊肉的、送水的，一律扣下，寨老们在会堂里已经饿了三天。一个小姑娘把饭团藏在竹筒里想混过去，被搜了出来，饭团扔在地上喂了狗。

column2: The picket pulled up, the food carriers surge through. The girl brushes the mud off her tube and says she is A Mei, Yan Gong's great-granddaughter. 'Great-grandpa says he won't eat until they stop asking for the bricks.' She pouts. 'He says the silkworm's been hungry ten years, so what's a few days.'
column3: 哨卡被拔了，送饭的人一拥而过。小姑娘拍掉竹筒上的泥，说她是岩公的曾孙女阿梅：「太公说了，砖不交出去，他就不吃饭。」她噘着嘴，「他说金蚕饿了十年，他饿几天算什么。」

column2: The Silent-Whistle Shed
column3: 哑哨棚

column2: In a thatched shed by a forest road hides the old groom from the Gu King's stables, who ran away some days ago. Gu riders have tracked him to the shed and are shouting that they'll tie him up and take him back. The old groom cowers in the straw clutching a tattered cloth bundle, and won't let go of it for anything.
column3: 林中路边一座草棚，棚里躲着蛊王马厩的老马倌，前些日子逃了出来。几个蛊骑追到了棚外，嚷着要把他捆回去，老马倌缩在草堆里，怀里抱着一只破布包，死也不撒手。

column2: The riders chased off, the old groom breathes again. The riders' horses are all fed on gu grass, he says, so they fear neither blade nor fire, though they won't take to strangers. He ran because he couldn't stand the night raids on the villages for bricks. 'The silkworm smells tea and frets, so the King sends the horses to grab it.' Before he goes he fishes a bone whistle out of his bundle and gives it to you. 'Makes no sound. Give it to some child to play with.'
column3: 蛊骑被打跑，老马倌松了口气。他说蛊骑的马都喂过蛊草，不怕刀不怕火，就是不认生人；他是受不了半夜去寨里抢砖才逃的：「金蚕一闻见茶味就闹，蛊王就派马去抢。」临走他从布包里摸出一只骨哨塞给你们：「吹不响的，给娃娃当个玩意儿吧。」

column2: Red Dhole Ridge
column3: 红豺岭

column2: A stream runs down the forested ridge, and the cracks in its rocks are thick with sweet flag, slender-leaved, so fragrant that one pinch scents your whole hand. But for days now a pack of red dholes has haunted the stream, a dozen of them, each thinner than the last, circling the water and showing no fear of people, stalking forward step by step with bared teeth. Herb pickers have been chased off the ridge twice already.
column3: 林中山岭上一道山溪，溪边石头缝里长满了石菖蒲，叶子细长，一掐满手香。可溪边这几天来了一群红毛豺，十几只，一只比一只瘦，围着溪口打转，见了人也不怕，龇着牙一步步往前逼。采药的人已经被撵下山两回了。

column2: The pack is driven into the deep forest and you pick a full bundle of sweet flag. Wu Dagong drinks the first medicine, a layer of grey leaves his face and he can sit up. Those dholes never used to come down, he says; the Gu riders have been driving the forest game every which way, and the dholes came out because they're starving. 'The Gu King doesn't leave even the beasts alone.'
column3: 豺群被赶进了深林，石菖蒲采了满满一捆。吴大弓喝了第一味药，脸上的青色退了一层，能坐起来了。他说这群豺本来不下山，是林子里的野物被蛊骑赶得四处乱跑，豺饿急了才出来：「蛊王连山里的东西都不放过。」

column2: Invitation Fork
column3: 喜帖岔

column2: At a fork in the forest road Gu riders are tearing down wedding notices: red paper giving the day A Tao and Yan Sheng will marry, pasted on the trees, ripped off one by one and trampled into the mud. The Gu King's order: no weddings, not for ten years now. An old granny crouching nearby picks the notices up one at a time, until a hoof kicks over her basket.
column3: 林中岔路口，一伙蛊骑在撕喜帖。红纸上写着阿桃和岩生成亲的日子，贴在岔口的树上，被他们一张张扯下来踩进泥里：蛊王有令，十年不许办喜事。一个老阿婆蹲在边上一张张捡，被马蹄踢翻了竹篮。

column2: The riders chased away, the notices are gathered up. In the old days, the granny says, a couple marrying would go to the Gu King's village for a single strand of golden silk to tie round their wrists, called 'one heart'. Ten years ago the King took the silk back and gave no more. Bang Gong hears this and says, 'Tying hearts was always a wedding custom. That night, those Han lads married one another.' Then, says Xiaoman, he's going to drink at Sister A Tao's wedding.
column3: 蛊骑被打跑，喜帖捡了起来。阿婆说，从前寨里成亲，新人要去蛊王寨讨一根金蚕丝拴在手腕上，叫「同心」；十年前蛊王把丝收了，不再给。榜公听了说：「拴心本来就是成亲的规矩。那一夜，那些汉郎是跟彼此成了亲。」小满说，那他要去喝阿桃姐的喜酒。

column2: The Bridal Path
column3: 迎亲路

column2: Down a forest track comes a bridal procession playing reed pipes, the bride A Tao in a silver crown, silver all over her, chiming with every step. Halfway along, Gu riders burst out, tear the crown from her head and gallop off, and the groom Yan Sheng sprints after them. The wedding party falls into chaos, and a few riders wheel back to carry off the bride as well.
column3: 林中山路上，一队迎亲的人吹着芦笙走过来，新娘阿桃头戴银冠，满身银饰，一步一响。半道上冲出一伙蛊骑，一把扯下了银冠，打马就跑，新郎岩生拔腿追了上去。送亲的人乱成一团，又有几个蛊骑掉头回来，要把新娘也一起带走。

column2: The riders who turned back are driven off and the bride is safe, but the crown is gone and the groom has run out of sight. The granny escorting the bride weeps: for ten years, whoever marries in these villages has bad luck; the Gu King gives no one-heart silk and takes the wedding silver besides. By custom a couple first goes to the Elders' Council for a blessing from Yan Gong, but the council house is under siege, and even that can't be had.
column3: 掉头的蛊骑被打跑，新娘保住了，银冠却没了，新郎也追得没了影。送亲的阿婆哭着说，十年来寨里谁成亲谁倒霉，蛊王不给同心丝，还要收喜银。按规矩新人要先去寨老会讨岩公一句吉利话，可寨老会被围着，这一句也讨不着。

column2: Yellow Dog Path
column3: 黄狗道

column2: A yellow dog streaks through the forest with a bamboo tube tied to its neck, guards pelting stones after it. It's Yan Gong's dog. Since the council house was besieged it has run back and forth every day between the house and the villages, carrying messages in the tube. The guards have chased it for a fortnight without catching it, and today they have finally cornered it in a ditch.
column3: 林子里一条黄狗飞奔而过，脖子上拴着个竹筒，后面追着几个寨丁，边追边扔石头。黄狗是岩公家的，寨老会被围以后，它天天在会堂和寨子之间来回跑，竹筒里装着话。寨丁们追了它半个月也没追上，今天总算把它堵在了一道沟里。

column2: The guards chased off, the dog wags its tail at you. Rolled in the tube is a note in Yan Gong's very shaky hand: 'While the bricks stand, the men stand. Folk outside, don't panic, and don't let them eat the bricks.' The dog takes the note back in its teeth and is gone like smoke, toward the council house.
column3: 寨丁被赶走，黄狗冲你们直摇尾巴。竹筒里卷着一张纸条，是岩公的字，抖得厉害：「砖在人在。外头的人莫慌，莫让他们吃了砖。」黄狗叼回纸条，一溜烟跑了，跑的是寨老会的方向。

column2: The Dream-Tea Lodge
column3: 梦茶楼

column2: In a chieftain's country lodge in the forest, the steward bought a piece of 'old Qianli tea' from the Gu riders, broke off a corner and brewed it for his master. The chieftain drank it and has slept three days and nights without waking. Terrified, the steward has sealed the lodge tight as an iron bucket with his household men and lets nobody in, for fear people will say he poisoned his lord.
column3: 林中一座土司家的别院，管家从蛊骑手里买了一块「千里号旧茶」，敲下一角泡给土司喝了。土司喝完睡了三天三夜没醒，管家吓坏了，带着家丁把别院守得铁桶一般，谁也不许进，怕人说是他毒死了主子。

column2: The household men scattered, you go in and find the chieftain snoring, muttering in his sleep. That evening he wakes with tears in his eyes. He dreamed, he says, that he walked three days with a load on his back along plank roads pinned to a cliff, a river below and snow above, and someone ahead turned round and called to him, 'Keep up.' The half brick is recovered, one corner short.
column3: 家丁被打散，你们进屋一看，土司打着鼾，梦里还念叨着什么。到了晚上他醒了，眼泪汪汪地说，他梦见自己背着货，在悬崖上的木栈道走了三天，脚下是江，头顶是雪，前头有个人回头冲他喊：「快跟上。」那半块砖收了回来，少了一角。

column2: The Water-Hammer Mill
column3: 水碓房

column2: A row of water hammers stands by a forest stream: the current turns the wheels, the wheels lift the pestles, and they fall into the mortars, thud, thud, husking the rice of several villages. Bandits in black headscarves have taken the mill and put up a sign at the door: 'One quart for every mortar', which comes to half of all the rice. Anyone who won't pay has his grain tipped into the stream.
column3: 林中溪边一排水碓，溪水推着木轮，木轮带着碓杵一下一下地舂米，咚、咚，几个寨子的米都在这里舂。一伙戴黑头巾的山匪占了碓房，在门口立了块牌子：「舂一臼，交一升」，舂好的米一半归他们。不交的，就把谷子倒进溪里。

column2: The bandits chased away, the pestles thud again. The old man who husks the rice says a band of 'sealers' has been going door to door: anyone who misses someone so much they can't sleep can have that longing sealed up in a jar, and eat and sleep well ever after. 'My old woman went and had hers sealed,' he says. 'She smiles all day now. But she never asks me any more if I'm hungry.'
column3: 山匪被撵走，碓杵又咚咚地响起来。舂米的阿公说，近来有一伙「封念人」挨寨上门，说谁家想人想得睡不着，就把那份想念封进罐子里，从此吃得下睡得着。「我老伴去封了，」阿公说，「如今她倒是天天笑，可再也不问我饿不饿了。」

column2: From the bandits' stores: twenty sacks of white rice, a string of sausages, two wood-cutting knives, and a great heap of rice chaff left from the husking, piled like a little hill. More chaff than the pigs can ever eat, says the old man; if you've any use for it, carry off all you like.
column3: 抄出山匪的存货：白米二十袋、一串腊肠、两把柴刀，还有舂米剩下的一大堆谷糠，堆得像座小山。阿公说谷糠喂猪都喂不完，你们要用尽管背走。

column2: Every time you pass, the old man at the mill husks you a fresh sack of rice, white and fine. 'The water works the hammers. Costs nothing.'
column3: 每次路过，碓房的阿公都给你们舂一袋新米，舂得又白又细：「水推的碓，不要钱。」

column2: Brick-Demand Camp
column3: 逼砖营

column2: A big forest camp holds the main force the Gu King has sent to make the council give up the bricks: riders, blowgunners and guards. A board at its gate reads: 'Give up the bricks and the seven villages are spared. Refuse, and they'll never know peace.' Each morning the camp shoots a volley of fire arrows at the council house and burns a hole in the roof; each night villagers creep up and patch it.
column3: 林中一座大营，是蛊王派来逼寨老会交砖的主力，蛊骑、吹箭手、寨丁都有。营门口竖着木牌：「交砖，饶七寨；不交，七寨无宁日。」每天早上营里朝寨老会放一轮火箭，烧穿一个屋顶窟窿，晚上寨里人再偷偷爬上去补好。

column2: You scatter the camp and split the board. A prisoner says the King doesn't want the bricks to drink. 'The silkworm's starving. The King means to feed it those few hundred halves to tide it over.' You ask what would happen then. The prisoner shakes his head. 'Yan Gong says: eat one, and the man tied at the far end loses his thread.'
column3: 大营被你们打散，木牌劈了。俘虏说蛊王要砖，不是自己喝：「金蚕饿得狠了，蛊王想拿那几百个半块先喂它一回。」你们问喂了会怎样，俘虏摇头：「岩公说，吃一块，拴在那头的人就断一根丝。」

column2: The Hidden-Brick Barn
column3: 藏砖仓

column2: In an empty grain barn in the forest, A Mei and a few lads are hiding. Last night they carried a basket of half bricks out of the council house to hide deep in the woods, ran into blowgunners, and are now trapped inside. A Mei has pushed the basket into the grain pile and sits on top of it, gripping a pair of scissors.
column3: 林中一座空粮仓里躲着阿梅和几个后生，他们夜里从寨老会背出来一篓半砖，想藏进林子深处，却被一伙吹箭手撞见，堵在仓里出不来。阿梅把篓子塞进谷堆，自己坐在上面，手里攥着一把剪刀。

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the basket of halves is safe. Great-grandpa is ninety-three, A Mei says, and ten years ago he made a promise to the Han deputy chief: 'One brick, one man. Until the man comes back for it, the brick doesn't leave the villages.' The deputy's name was Song Ge, and the day he handed over the bricks he knelt and bowed his head to the floor before Great-grandpa. A Mei shoulders the basket. 'I'll take you to him.'
column3: 吹箭手被打跑，一篓半砖保住了。阿梅说太公九十三岁，十年前答应了那个汉人副镖头：「一块砖一个人，人不回来拿，砖就不离寨。」副镖头叫宋戈，交砖那天给太公磕了一个头。阿梅背起篓子：「我带你们去见太公。」

column2: Seven-Leaf Slope
column3: 七叶坡

column2: On the shady side of a steep forest slope grow a few clumps of seven-leaf paris, seven leaves to a stem and one flower on top; villagers say it cures snakebite and undoes gu. When you arrive, a band of the Gu King's blowgunners is splashing tung oil up the slope to set a fire and burn the clumps root and all. The King has heard someone is looking for a cure.
column3: 林中陡坡的背阴处，长着几丛七叶一枝花，一根茎上七片叶子，顶上开一朵花，寨民说能治蛇毒，也能解蛊。你们赶到时，一伙蛊王的吹箭手正往坡上泼桐油，要放一把火，把这几丛花连根烧了：蛊王听说有人在找解药。

column2: The blowgunners scattered and the fire never lit, a few clumps of paris survive. A Kou picks one and pats earth back over the remaining roots. Wu Dagong drinks the second medicine and can walk. All five rules, A Kou says, were for dodging the threads. 'Once the silkworm's fed, the board can come down.' She looks south-east. 'The last medicine is in the Gu King's droppings store.'
column3: 吹箭手被打散，火没点起来，七叶一枝花保住了几丛。阿蔻采了一棵，又把剩下的根拿土盖好。吴大弓喝了第二味药，能下地走路了。阿蔻说五条规矩都是为了躲那根丝，「等金蚕吃饱了，牌子就能摘了」。她望着东南：「最后一味，在蛊王的蚕沙仓里。」

column2: Centipede Gully
column3: 百足谷

column2: A dank gully at the end of a dead end, every rock hiding centipedes, scorpions and venomous spiders, the biggest centipede as long as a carrying pole. Every Duanwu festival someone in the villages secretly raises gu, and the failed insects get tipped into this gully. Year after year they pile up and grow fiercer, and at night they swarm out to burrow into the nearest village's granary.
column3: 死路尽头一道阴湿的山谷，乱石底下全是蜈蚣、蝎子和毒蛛，最大的蜈蚣有扁担长。每年端午，寨里有人偷偷养蛊，养废了的虫子就往这谷里倒，一年年倒下来，谷里的毒虫越养越凶，夜里成群爬出谷，钻进最近那座寨子的谷仓。

column2: Realgar and mugwort smoulder at the gully's mouth and the creatures are smoked back into the cracks. But as long as anyone raises gu, new insects will be tipped in every Duanwu and out they'll crawl again before long; all you can do is smoke them out every so often. Wedged in a crack at the bottom is a half brick, its tag still on. The insects crawl round it. Not one touches it.
column3: 谷口点起雄黄和艾草，毒虫被熏回了石缝。可只要还有人养蛊，每年端午就有新的虫子倒进来，过一阵它们还会爬出来，只能隔些日子来熏一回。谷底石缝里卡着一块半砖，竹签还在，虫子都绕着它爬，一只也不碰。

column2: Bound-Groom Post
column3: 绑郎哨

column2: At a Gu riders' outpost in the forest, the groom Yan Sheng is tied to a hitching post with his arms behind him and mud all over his face. Two days ago on the bridal path he chased the riders who stole the silver crown all the way here, flattened two of them single-handed, and was lassoed from behind by the third. The riders jeer: 'The crown's gone to the silver vault. Wait here and be a bachelor for life.'
column3: 林中一座蛊骑的哨卡，新郎岩生被反绑在马桩上，满脸是泥。前天迎亲路上，他追着抢走银冠的蛊骑一路追到这里，一个人打翻了两个，第三个从背后套住了他。蛊骑们笑他：「银冠送进银库了，你在这儿等着当一辈子光棍吧。」

column2: You take the outpost and cut Yan Sheng loose, and his first question is whether A Tao was frightened. A prisoner confesses that the crown went into the Gu King's silver vault, where ten years of confiscated wedding silver lies under lock. 'The King says: no tying of hearts, no marrying.' Yan Sheng rolls up his sleeves. 'Then we'll fetch it from the vault.'
column3: 哨卡被你们端了，岩生松了绑，头一句就问阿桃有没有被吓着。俘虏交代，银冠送进了蛊王的银库，库里锁着十年来收走的全部喜银：「蛊王说了，不许拴心，就不许成亲。」岩生把袖子一捋：「那就去库里拿。」

column2: The Sealers' Road
column3: 封念路

column2: On a forest road a party of sealers is leading mules door to door, the beasts loaded with stacks of empty clay jars and a bale of red cloth. They're coaxing a widow: 'Why go on missing him? Seal it up and it won't hurt any more.' A girl of thirteen or fourteen charges up and pelts their mules with stones until the mules buck and several jars smash. The guards with the sealers swing their clubs and go after her.
column3: 林中路上，一伙封念人赶着骡子挨寨上门，骡背上驮着一摞摞空陶罐和一捆红布。他们正劝一个寡妇封念：「想他做什么？封了就不疼了。」一个十三四岁的姑娘冲过来，拿石子砸他们的骡子，砸得骡子乱跳，罐子摔碎了好几只。封念人身边的寨丁抡起棍子就追她。

column2: The guards chased off, the sealers flee too. The girl is A Zha. Three years ago her grandpa had his longing sealed, his missing of a Han caravan cook: that winter the cook, Xiao Cong, lodged by his hearth and taught him to roll noodles. 'Since it was sealed Grandpa smiles all day,' A Zha says, 'but he can't even be bothered to call my name. I'm going to find his jar and bring it back.'
column3: 寨丁被打跑，封念人也跑了。姑娘叫阿扎，她阿公三年前封了念，封的是想一个汉人伙夫的心：那年冬天伙夫小葱住在他家火塘边，教他擀面条。「阿公封了以后天天笑，」阿扎说，「可他连我的名字都懒得喊了。我要把他的罐子找回来。」

column2: The Stone-Man Cave
column3: 石人洞

column2: Incense smoke hangs at the mouth of a limestone cave in the forest. Inside stands a stalagmite shaped like a stooping man. A wandering Taoist who keeps the cave says it is one of the Qianli guards: he rested here ten years ago, the Gu King turned him to stone, and the dripping limestone wrapped him up drop by drop. Villagers come to burn incense and pray to the 'Stone Guard' to bring their travellers home. The Taoist's hired toughs guard the offering box. No coin, no look.
column3: 林中一个溶洞口挂满了香火，洞里一根石笋，模样像个弯腰的人。一个游方道士守着洞，说这是千里号的一个镖师，十年前在洞里歇脚，被蛊王点成了石头，钟乳一滴滴把他裹了起来。寨民来烧香，求「石镖师」保佑出门的人回来。道士雇的打手守着功德箱，不交钱不许看。

column2: The toughs chased off, the Taoist tries to argue, and an old stonemason who came along silences him with one question. Dripstone grows a fraction of a millimetre a year; in ten years it adds a millimetre or two at most, and to wrap up a whole man would take thousands of years at the very least. 'That stone man is older than the village.' In the offering box you find a half brick the Taoist bought from the riders as a 'holy relic'.
column3: 打手被打跑，道士还想狡辩，一个老石匠一句话就把他问住了：钟乳石一年才长零点几毫米，十年也就一两毫米，要把一个人裹起来，少说要几千年。「这根石人，比寨子还老。」功德箱里翻出一块半砖，是道士从蛊骑那里买来当「法器」的。

column2: Smiling Hamlet
column3: 笑面寨

column2: In a forest hamlet every household is smiling. Old folk smile on their doorsteps, women smile as they pound rice, they smile at strangers, and whatever you ask, the answer is 'Fine, all fine.' This hamlet was the first to have its longing sealed, almost every house. A Zha's grandpa sits at the hamlet gate, beaming. Gu riders guarding the place block your way. 'These people are doing perfectly well. Don't come stirring them up.'
column3: 林中一座寨子，家家户户都在笑：老人坐在门槛上笑，妇人舂着米笑，见了生人也笑，问什么都答「好，都好」。这寨子封念封得最早，差不多家家封过。阿扎的阿公也坐在寨口，笑眯眯的。几个守寨的蛊骑拦住你们：「这里的人过得好好的，你们别来搅。」

column2: The riders driven off. Grandpa knows A Zha and smiles and calls her 'child', but can't come up with her name. A rolling pin hangs by his stove, worn glossy, and when you ask whose it is he smiles and says he can't remember. 'Some guest left it, I think. Fine, all fine.' A Zha turns her back and tucks the rolling pin inside her coat.
column3: 蛊骑被赶走。阿公认得阿扎，笑着叫她「娃娃」，却叫不出名字。他灶上挂着一根擀面杖，磨得油光发亮，你们问是谁的，他笑着说想不起来了，「好像是哪个客人落下的，好，都好」。阿扎背过身去，把擀面杖揣进了怀里。

column2: The Siege Camp
column3: 围会营

column2: A ring of tents encircles the Elders' Council house, and the Gu King's men have it sealed tight: guards on the paths, blowgunners up the trees, riders circling outside. Now and then a cough drifts from the house, the elders holding out within. The camp has great pots of meat stewing, and someone is fanning the smell toward the council house on purpose.
column3: 寨老会四周扎着一圈营帐，蛊王的人把会堂围得水泄不通：寨丁守路，吹箭手爬在树上，蛊骑在外圈来回巡。会堂里偶尔传出几声咳嗽，是寨老们在里头熬着。营里架着几口大锅炖肉，香气被故意往会堂那边扇。

column2: You break the siege, and the stewed meat goes in to the council. The door opens a crack and A Mei's yellow dog is first out. Seven elders stand holding the door frame, each thinner than the last, the oldest supported in the middle, a wooden box clasped tight against his chest.
column3: 围营被你们冲开，锅里的肉都给寨老会送了进去。会堂的门开了一条缝，阿梅的黄狗第一个钻了出来。七个寨老扶着门框站着，一个比一个瘦，最老的那个被扶在中间，怀里抱着一只木匣，抱得紧紧的。

column2: The Elders' Council
column3: 寨老会

column2: The Elders' Council is a great stilt house on nine pillars where the seven villages settle their weighty matters. The siege is broken, but a squad of the Gu King's elite still holds the stairs and swears to burn the house if anyone climbs them. Upstairs, ninety-three-year-old Yan Gong sits by the hearth with a rack of three hundred pigeonholes behind him, stacked with half bricks, a bamboo tag on each. The seven villages used to weigh their grain-for-gold trade under this house. Now there's nothing under it but blades.
column3: 寨老会是一座九根柱子的大吊脚楼，七寨的大事都在这里商量。围营虽破，蛊王的一队精兵还守在楼下，堵着楼梯，扬言谁上楼就烧楼。楼上，九十三岁的岩公坐在火塘边，身后是三百格的竹架，码满了半块茶砖，每块拴着一根竹签。七寨的粮换金买卖从前就在这楼下过秤，如今楼下只剩刀枪。

column2: The elite driven off, the scales hang under the house again. The villages have grain and the river yields gold dust, so trade in grain for gold reopens.  Yan Gong asks you to bring up the half brick from your cart. He feels his way along the rack pigeonhole by pigeonhole, reaches the last, draws out a half, and fits it to yours. It closes without a crack. Two hundred and ninety-nine tags carry names; this one's tag alone is blank. 'Deputy Song said this one waits for whoever comes after with the other half.' Yan Gong counts along the rack and sighs. 'A dozen and more still empty. Stolen, over the years.'
column3: 精兵被打退，楼下的秤又挂了起来。寨里有粮，河里淘得出金沙，粮换金的买卖重新开张。岩公让你们把车上那半块茶砖拿上来。他在竹架上一格一格地摸过去，摸到最后一格，抽出一块，跟你们那块一合，严丝合缝。二百九十九根签都写着名字，只有这一块的签是空的。「宋副镖头说，这一块，等后头的人拿着另一半来合。」岩公数了数架子，又叹口气：「还空着十几格，是这些年被偷走的。」

column2: The Droppings Store
column3: 蚕沙仓

column2: At the end of a dead end stands a stone storehouse lined with tier on tier of bamboo trays, spread with glossy black droppings shed by the golden silkworm as it spun. The Gu King mixes his gu with them and won't part with a grain. His elite guard it, blowgunners on the beams and Gu riders at the door. The black mark on Wu Dagong's chest has begun to spread again, and A Kou has carried him here on her back, her forehead running with sweat.
column3: 死路尽头一座石砌的仓，仓里一层层竹匾，铺着黑亮的蚕沙，是金蚕吐丝时落下的，蛊王拿它配蛊，一粒都舍不得给人。守仓的是蛊王的精兵，吹箭手在梁上，蛊骑在门前。吴大弓胸口的黑印又开始往外长了，阿蔻背着他一路赶来，额头全是汗。

column2: The elite beaten back, the door opens. A Kou scoops up a handful of droppings, holds them to her nose, and stops short. 'Tea.' The golden silkworm eats tea; that winter ten years ago it ate the Qianli caravan's tea. And the newest layer on the trays is ten years old too. Nothing has been added since. The three medicines are brewed together, Wu Dagong drinks, and the black mark on his chest fades bit by bit. He sits up and says that the day he loosed his arrow, he'd seen the riders driving a string of people with gold thread on their wrists toward the Gu King's village. A Kou packs away her pot. 'Ten years it's gone hungry. If it isn't fed soon, it won't be tea it eats.'
column3: 精兵被打退，仓门开了。阿蔻抓起一把蚕沙凑到鼻子底下，愣了一下：「是茶。」金蚕吃的是茶，十年前那一冬，它吃的是千里号的茶；竹匾上最新的一层蚕沙也是十年前的，此后再没添过。三味药煎在一处，吴大弓喝了，胸口的黑印一点点淡下去。他坐起来说，那天他放箭，是看见蛊骑赶着一串手腕缠金丝的人往蛊王寨去。阿蔻收起药罐：「它饿了十年了。再不喂，它要吃的就不是茶了。」

column2: The Silver-Crown Vault
column3: 银冠库

column2: The cave at the end of the dead end is the Gu King's silver vault: two timber stockades at the mouth, Gu riders on guard, blowgunners lying on the rock above. Inside, chest after chest of wedding silver, crowns, horns, collars, bracelets, ten years of it taken from the villages, and not one piece ever worn at a tying of hearts. Yan Sheng and A Tao have come, and Xiaoman and his mother too. Yan Sheng carries a carrying pole.
column3: 死路尽头的山洞是蛊王的银库，洞口两道木栅，蛊骑把守，吹箭手伏在洞顶。库里一箱箱全是喜银：银冠、银角、项圈、手镯，都是十年来从寨里收走的，没有一件拴过同心。岩生、阿桃，还有小满娘儿俩都跟来了，岩生手里拎着一根扁担。

column2: The elite routed, the stockades flattened, the crown goes back to its owner and ten years of wedding silver is carried out chest by chest. The wedding is held right there at the cave mouth: Bang Gong sings, A Xiu combs the bride's hair, and Xiaoman rings his father's mule bell for a wedding bell. There's no golden silk, so Bang Gong ties the couple's wrists with a plain red thread. 'One heart never needed a silkworm.' As the feast breaks up, Xiaoman tells you he knows now why his father left. 'He married those uncles. They have to walk the road to the end together.' He hangs the bell back round his neck. 'I'll wait for him to come back and pay the oil-tea granny her songs.'
column3: 精兵溃散，木栅推倒，银冠物归原主，十年的喜银一箱箱抬了出去。婚礼就在洞口办了：榜公唱歌，阿秀给新娘梳头，小满摇着阿爸的马铃当喜铃。没有金蚕丝，榜公就拿一根红线把两人的手腕拴在一起：「同心本来就不用蚕。」散席时，小满对你们说，他知道阿爸为什么走了：「他跟那些叔叔成了亲，要一起把路走完。」他把马铃挂回脖子上：「我等他回来，还油茶阿婆的歌。」

column2: The Silver-Pin Smithy
column3: 银针铺

column2: In a silversmith's shop in the forest the forge is cold and the bellows furred with dust. Old Wu used to make silver crowns and collars, but the Gu King's men have taken all his silver and make him produce one thing only: silver pins to seal the jars, one pin per jar, its head engraved with the household's mark. His hands are covered in blisters, and two Gu riders stand at the door as overseers.
column3: 林中一间银匠铺，炉子冷着，风箱蒙了灰。银匠老吴本来打银冠、银项圈，如今蛊王的人把他的银子全收了，逼他只打一样东西：封罐子用的银针，一只罐一根针，针头刻着那户人家的记号。他打得满手血泡，门口还站着两个蛊骑监工。

column2: The overseers chased off, the forge roars again. Old Wu trades silverwork for your goods and insists on throwing in a pair of silver bells. Silver tests for poison, he says; the jars are sealed with silver pins because a sealed longing turns the silver black, and that shows whether the seal holds. A Zha asks if he could recognise her grandpa's jar. Old Wu leafs through his book of marks. 'His household's mark is a rolling pin.'
column3: 监工被赶走，炉子重新烧了起来。老吴拿银器跟你们换货，说什么也要多送一对银铃。他说银能试毒，封罐用银针，是因为念头封进去会让银发黑，看得出封牢没有。阿扎问他认不认得出阿公的罐子，老吴翻出记号簿：「他家的记号，是一根擀面杖。」

column2: Boar Wood
column3: 野猪林

column2: This is a stand of old chestnut trees. Years ago, afraid of thieves, Yan Gong secretly buried two half bricks under one of them and marked the spot with a stone. The chestnut crop is thin this year, and a herd of wild boar, mad with hunger, has rooted up the wood like a ploughed field and turned the marker stone over. The lead boar, tusks a foot long, is nosing at a bamboo tag sticking out of the earth.
column3: 林中一片老栗树林，岩公早年怕砖被抢，偷偷把两块半砖埋在一棵老栗树底下，拿石头做了记号。今年栗子结得少，一群野猪饿得发了狂，把林子拱得像翻过的地，记号石也被拱翻了。领头的公猪獠牙有一尺长，正拿鼻子拱着一根露出土的竹签。

column2: The boar driven into the deep woods, you dig through the churned soil and find both halves, their tags caked in mud but readable once wiped. A Mei hugs them, laughing: Great-grandpa was muddled even when he buried them, she says, and drew the spot on his tobacco pouch. 'And what he drew was a pine.'
column3: 野猪被赶进深林，你们刨开拱乱的土，两块半砖还在，竹签上的名字被泥糊了，擦干净还认得出。阿梅抱着砖直乐，说太公埋砖的时候就糊涂了，把地方画在了自己的烟袋上，「烟袋上画的是棵松树」。

column2: Brick-Pillow Hold
column3: 枕砖寨

column2: A little bandit hold in the forest is run by an enormous fat chief who can't sleep without a half brick for a pillow. With it under his head, he says, he dreams every night that he's on the road, walking till his whole body feels wonderful, and wakes fresher than if he'd never slept. His men want a turn too, one night each, and they brawl daily over whose turn is next.
column3: 林中一座山匪的小寨，寨主是个大胖子，睡觉非得枕着一块半砖，说枕着它夜夜梦见自己在赶路，走得浑身舒坦，醒来比没睡还精神。手下的喽啰也想枕，排着队一人枕一夜，为了谁先谁后，天天在寨里打架。

column2: The bandits scattered, the fat chief clutches his brick and won't let go, so you carry him out brick and all. The road in his dreams always runs south, he says, across a river and up a cliff with planks pinned to its face. 'When I get onto the cliff, I wake up. Never once got across.' The brick goes back to Yan Gong, and the fat chief, long-faced, says he'll have to sleep on a stone from now on.
column3: 山匪被打散，胖寨主抱着砖不撒手，被你们连人带砖抬了出来。他说他梦里的路一直往南，过一条江，上一面崖，崖上钉着木板：「走到崖上，梦就醒了，一回也没走过去。」砖还给了岩公，胖寨主哭丧着脸说，往后只能枕石头了。

column2: Jar-Mule Trail
column3: 驮罐道

column2: A mule train carries dozens of red-sealed jars east along a forest path, packed in straw, knocking gently together as they go. Escorting it are caravan guards the Gu King hired from beyond the hills, every one with a blade, who shout off anyone who comes near; look at the jars too long and you get the flat of a sword. A Zha trails the train at a distance, checking the silver pin on every jar.
column3: 林中小道上，一支骡队驮着几十只红布封口的陶罐往东走，罐子用稻草垫着，一路轻轻相碰。护送的是蛊王从山外雇来的镖客，个个带刀，见人就喝退，谁敢多看一眼罐子，先挨一刀背。阿扎远远跟在骡队后头，挨个看罐口的银针。

column2: The escort scattered, the mules stand by the path. A Zha goes over every pin: no rolling pin. The old muleteer says all these jars are bound for the Jar Forest. 'Ten years they've been hanging them there, thousands at the least.' And the old jars, once full, get thrown down the sinkhole at the far end of the forest.
column3: 镖客被打散，骡子停在路边。阿扎一根根针看过去，没有擀面杖的记号。赶骡的老汉说，这些罐都是送去罐林的，「罐林里挂了十年，少说几千只了」；挂满了的旧罐，就从林子尽头的落水洞丢下去。

column2: The Letter-Pole Camp
column3: 挑信营

column2: A big camp of the Gu King's sits across the forest road, Gu riders patrolling back and forth. At its gate a bamboo pole holds up a letter with a golden silkworm drawn on the envelope. Word has gone out from the camp: the letter is for whoever holds 'the other half', and whoever comes for it must get through the camp first.
column3: 林中大路上扎着蛊王的一座大营，蛊骑来回巡着，营门口插着一根竹竿，竿上挑着一封信，信封上画着一只金蚕。营里放出话来：这封信是给拿着「另外半块」的人的，谁来取，先过了这一营再说。

column2: The camp broken, you take down the letter. It has only a few lines, in a thin, bony hand: 'Three hundred threads, and one is empty. The silkworm's hunger is all in that one. Bring me the brick with the blank tag and I will find someone to tie to it, and the seven villages will have peace.' It is signed with a golden silkworm. Yan Gong reads it and tosses it into the hearth. 'He means to fill that thread with a living man.'
column3: 大营被打散，你们取下了那封信。信里只有几行字，笔迹很瘦：「三百根丝，一根是空的。金蚕饿，就饿在这一根上。把那块空签的砖送来，我替它找个人拴上，七寨从此太平。」落款是一只金蚕。岩公看了，把信扔进火塘：「他想拿活人去填那一根。」

column2: Song Ge's Hearth
column3: 宋家火塘

column2: By the hearth of an old stilt house in the forest sits a blind old woman, who was deputy chief Song Ge's hearth mother ten years ago. Every day she adds one stick to the fire; Song Ge asked her to, she says, when he left. Guards sent by the Gu King hold the stairs and let no outsider up: the old woman knows about 'that one thread', and the King wants her silent.
column3: 林中一座老吊脚楼，火塘边坐着个瞎眼的老婆婆，是十年前副镖头宋戈的火塘亲。她天天往火塘里添一根柴，说是宋戈走时托过她。几个蛊王派来的寨丁守在楼下，不许外人上去，说婆婆知道「那一根丝」的事，蛊王要她闭嘴。

column2: The guards chased off, the old woman holds your hands as she talks. The night Song Ge handed over the bricks, he told her why the last tag had no name: that man was lost in the fog. 'Write his name, and the silkworm will follow the name to find him. Leave it blank, and we wait for him to find his own way here.' She adds a stick to the fire. 'He said that man would come sooner or later. And if he couldn't, someone would come in his place.'
column3: 寨丁被赶走，婆婆摸着你们的手说话。宋戈交砖那一夜跟她讲过：最后那根签不写名字，是因为那个人在雾里走丢了，「名字一写，金蚕就会顺着名字去找他；不写，就等他自己找来」。婆婆添了一根柴：「他说那个人迟早会来。来不了，也会有人替他来。」

column2: Weight-Cheat Tower
column3: 砣子碉

column2: In a stone watchtower in the forest lives a petty headman who buys mountain produce. Short of scale weights, he has tied two half bricks to his steelyard instead, and for mushrooms and dried bamboo shoots he pays the price of eight ounces for every pound. Hill folk who carry their goods here are held at the foot of the tower by his men, and anyone who complains about the scale is thrown out.
column3: 林中一座碉楼，碉主是个收山货的小寨主，秤砣不够用，竟拿两块半砖拴在秤杆上当砣，收菌子、收笋干，一斤只给八两的钱。山民们背着山货来卖，被他的家丁挡在碉楼下，谁嫌秤不准，就被打出去。

column2: The men scattered, the two halves come off the steelyard. The headman still insists that tea bricks 'weigh truer' than iron. You check against an honest scale: each brick cheats at least two ounces in the pound. The hill folk storm the tower and reckon up every coin they were shorted over the years, and the pages of the headman's ledger fly.
column3: 家丁被打散，两块半砖从秤杆上解了下来。碉主还嘴硬，说茶砖比铁砣「压秤」。你们拿真秤一比，一块砖一斤少说亏人二两。山民们冲进碉楼，把这几年少给的钱一笔笔算了回来，碉主的账本被翻得哗哗响。

column2: The Asking-Back Gate
column3: 讨念门

column2: At the gate of a little hamlet a woman kneels before the sealers, begging them to give back what they sealed away. Three years ago she lost her son and missed him past bearing, so she had it sealed. Now it doesn't hurt, but she can't remember what her son looked like. 'I'd rather it hurt.' The sealers sneer that the jar went off long ago and tell the guards to drag her away.
column3: 林中一座小寨门口，一个妇人跪在封念人面前，求他们把封进去的念还给她：三年前她儿子没了，她想得受不了，就封了念；如今她不疼了，可连儿子长什么样都想不起来。「我宁愿疼。」封念人冷笑，说罐子早送走了，叫寨丁把她拖开。

column2: The sealers driven off, the woman sits at the gate a long while without a word. The register the sealers dropped is clear: her jar hangs in the seventh row at the east end of the Jar Forest. A Zha crouches and takes her hand. 'I'm looking too. When we find them, we'll open them together.' Only then does the woman weep aloud, like someone who hasn't wept in a very long time.
column3: 封念人被赶跑了。妇人坐在寨门口，半天没说话。封念人丢下的簿子上记得清楚：她的罐子在罐林东头第七排。阿扎蹲下来握着她的手：「我也在找，找到了一起开。」妇人这才哭出声来，像是很久很久没哭过了。

column2: Hoof-Stop Slope
column3: 停蹄坡

column2: On a forest slope a troop of Gu riders is galloping toward the Gu King's village with sacks slung across their saddles, the corner of a half brick poking from one. Their horses are fed on gu grass and fear neither blade nor fire; they charge like a wall, and twice your front rank is knocked apart. In the confusion someone remembers the bone whistle that makes no sound, pulls it out and blows with all his might.
column3: 林中山坡上，一队蛊骑驮着几只口袋往蛊王寨跑，袋口露出半块茶砖的角。他们的马喂过蛊草，不怕刀也不怕火，冲起来像一堵墙，你们的前排被撞开了两回。慌乱中，有人想起怀里那只吹不响的骨哨，掏出来，使劲吹了一口。

column2: The whistle still makes no sound, but every horse on the slope stops dead, ears pricked, and however the riders lash them, they won't take another step. You haul the riders out of their saddles one by one. It was the groom's whistle for calling horses, pitched too high for human ears and not for theirs. In the sacks are four half bricks, tags and all.
column3: 骨哨还是没有声音，可坡上的马一齐站住了，竖着耳朵，任凭蛊骑怎么抽也不肯再迈一步，蛊骑被你们一个个从马上拽了下来。原来那是马倌唤马的哨，声音尖得人听不见，马听得见。袋里是四块半砖，竹签都在。

column2: The Pointing Stone
column3: 指南石

column2: At a fork in the forest road lies a great slab of bluestone carved with an arrow pointing to the mountains in the south, and beside it a line cut deep: 'Song Ge leads the company south, up the cliffs, to find the chief.' The Gu King's stonemasons, guarded by village guards, are chiselling the words away bit by bit. A big-footed old man sits by the stone cursing them, spitting at the masons' feet after every curse.
column3: 林中岔路口有块大青石，石面上刻着一个箭头，指向南边的大山，箭头旁一行字刻得很深：「宋戈领众往南，上崖，寻镖头。」一伙蛊王的石匠在寨丁护着下，正拿錾子一点点把字凿掉。一个大脚老汉坐在石头边上骂，骂一句，往石匠脚边吐一口唾沫。

column2: The guards and masons chased off, only half of 'find' has been chiselled away. The big-footed old man is Lei Dajiao. Ten years ago it was he who guided the Qianli caravan out of the Gu villages, all the way to the river in the south. 'They went south without a moment's doubt,' he says, slapping the stone, 'as if they already knew where their chief was.'
column3: 寨丁和石匠被赶跑，字只凿掉了「寻」字的半边。大脚老汉叫雷大脚，十年前就是他给千里号带的路，把他们送出蛊寨，一直送到南边的江边。「他们往南走，一个都没犹豫，」他拍着石头说，「像是早就知道镖头在哪儿。」

column2: The Rag-Doll Loft
column3: 布娃楼

column2: At the end of a dead end stands a little stilt house, and upstairs lives a girl of seven or eight who carries a cloth bundle everywhere like a doll and sings it to sleep at night. Inside the bundle is a half brick she found by the river. Blowgunners have come to take her 'dolly'. She stuffs the bundle inside her clothes and huddles in a corner without a sound.
column3: 死路尽头一座小吊脚楼，楼上住着个七八岁的小姑娘，天天抱着一个布包，像抱娃娃一样，夜里还给它唱歌。布包里是一块半砖，是她在河边捡的。几个吹箭手找上门来，要抢她的「布娃娃」，小姑娘把布包塞进衣服里，缩在楼角，一声不吭。

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the girl hears that the brick has an owner. Crying, she unwraps it. She sang to it every night, she says, 'so the uncle wouldn't be scared alone on the road'. The tag reads 'Song Ge'. Yan Gong takes the brick and makes her a promise: every day from now on, she can still come and sing it a song.
column3: 吹箭手被打跑了。小姑娘听说这块砖是有主的，一边哭一边把布包解开，说她每天晚上给它唱歌，「怕那个叔叔一个人在路上害怕」。竹签上写着「宋戈」。岩公接过砖，跟小姑娘说好了：以后每天，她还来给它唱一支。

column2: Gold-Thread Camp
column3: 金丝营

column2: Outside the Jar Forest stands a big camp of Gu riders, every one with gold thread round his wrist: the Gu King's trusted men, their own hearts tied to do his bidding. Each evening the camp calls the roll, and then dozens of riders ride a circuit through the Jar Forest, where no one is allowed to stop.
column3: 罐林外扎着一座蛊骑大营，营里的人手腕上都缠着金丝，是蛊王的亲信，丝拴着他们自己的心，听蛊王使唤。营里每天傍晚点一次卯，点完卯，几十个蛊骑骑马进罐林巡一圈，谁也不许在林里停步。

column2: You scatter the camp. A prisoner with thread on his wrist tells the truth. 'The silkworm eats hearts. The Qianli men's hearts are tied at the far end of the threads, too far away to reach. If it can't eat them, it eats the hearts that miss them.' The bitterer the longing, the more it fills, and that's why the sealers pick the households that have waited longest.
column3: 大营被你们打散。一个手腕缠丝的俘虏说了实话：「金蚕吃的是心。千里号那些人的心拴在丝那头，太远了，吃不着；吃不着他们，就只好吃想他们的心。」想得越苦越顶饿，所以封念人专挑等人等得最久的人家。

column2: Sour-Soup Kitchens
column3: 酸汤灶

column2: At a five-way fork in the forest, big stoves simmer sour soup; travellers on the Jar Forest road stop here to eat, and one bowl of rice in sour soup keeps you walking a whole day. A band of swordsmen has taken the stoves. The soup still simmers, but they sell it only to Gu riders, and hill folk passing by can't buy a bowl; they're driven off with a ladle rapped on the forehead.
column3: 林中一处五岔路口，几口大灶熬着酸汤，是来往罐林那条路上歇脚吃饭的地方，一碗酸汤泡饭，够走一天山路。一伙刀客占了灶，汤照熬，却只卖给蛊骑，过路的山民一碗也买不着，还被他们拿汤勺敲着脑门赶走。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the stoves blaze again and hill folk queue with their bowls. The woman who brews the soup says people can often be heard crying in the Jar Forest at night: sealed folk who walk into the woods by themselves and stand under their own jars. They can't remember anything. They just cry. 'And when they're done crying, they go home smiling.'
column3: 刀客被赶走，灶里的火又旺了，山民端着碗排起了队。熬汤的大婶说，罐林里夜里常有人哭，是封了念的人自己走进林子，站在自家的罐子底下，什么也想不起来，就是哭，「哭完了，又笑着回家」。

column2: From the swordsmen's hoard: six jars of fermented chilli, two baskets of pickled bamboo shoots, a vat of rice-sour starter, twenty air-dried pheasants, and a copper pot, which the soup woman says is a family heirloom and chases you to get back.
column3: 抄出刀客囤的糟辣椒六坛、腌笋两筐、一缸米酸、二十只风干的山鸡，还有一口铜锅，大婶说是她家祖传的，追着要了回去。

column2: Every time you pass, the soup woman fills you a brimming bowl of rice in sour soup with an extra spoon of fermented chilli. 'A good burn wakes the heart.'
column3: 每次路过，大婶都给你们盛满满一碗酸汤泡饭，多放一勺糟辣椒：「辣一下，心就醒了。」

column2: The South Pass
column3: 南关

column2: On the old road south through the forest stands a stone pass built by the chieftain, its walls manned by his finest household troops, swordsmen, crossbowmen and horse alike. Ten years ago the pass was open; later the chieftain sealed it and let no one through southward. Lei Dajiao says this is the very pass he led the caravan through.
column3: 林中往南的老路上有一道石关，是土司设的，关墙上站着土司最精的家兵，刀手、弩手、马队一样不少。十年前这道关是开着的，后来土司把它封了，谁也不许往南过。雷大脚说，当年他就是从这道关把马帮送出去的。

column2: The household troops beaten back, the gate opens. In the gatehouse the pass register, turned to the spring of the dingwei year, has a line: 'Qianli caravan through the pass, southbound, entered by Song Ge.' After it the gatekeeper has added in small characters: 'All walked with a hand on the wrist, as if something drew them.' Turn on, and the next year's page holds only: 'Cliff road collapsed. Pass sealed.'
column3: 家兵被打退，关门开了。关楼里的过关簿翻到丁未年开春，有一行：「千里号马帮过关，往南，宋戈具」，后面是守关人添的小字：「众人皆手抚腕，似有物牵之。」再往后翻，第二年那一页只写着：「崖路塌，封关。」

column2: The Empty Cage
column3: 空笼楼

column2: An empty birdcage hangs under the eaves of a stilt house in the forest, its door open. The family says it held a green parrot that Song Ge left in their care when he went. Last year the parrot flew off and has been shrieking in the forest at night, and the villagers, taking it for the thing that calls names, raised a band of blowgunners who comb the woods shooting at anything green. Today they've found the house and mean to burn the cage too.
column3: 林中一座吊脚楼，屋檐下挂着一只空鸟笼，笼门开着。主家说笼里原本养着一只绿鹦鹉，是宋戈走时寄养的。去年鹦鹉飞了，夜里在林子里乱喊，寨民以为是那个喊名字的东西，组了一队吹箭手满林子找，见绿的就射。今天他们找到了这座楼，要把笼子也烧了。

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the cage is saved. The parrot is called A Cui, the family says, and it does Song Ge better than anything; when it speaks, the whole village thinks the deputy chief is back. 'It isn't calling those names,' the man of the house says. 'It calls "keep up, keep up". Song Ge called that every day when he led the company.' A few green feathers still lie in the bottom of the cage.
column3: 吹箭手被赶走，笼子保住了。主家说鹦鹉叫阿翠，学宋戈学得最像，一开口，全寨都以为宋副镖头回来了。「它喊的不是那种名字，」主家说，「它喊『跟上，跟上』，宋戈带队的时候天天这么喊。」笼底还留着几根绿毛。

column2: The Red-Jar Kiln
column3: 红罐窑

column2: At the end of a dead end a dragon kiln crawls a hundred feet up the hillside, its fire never out day or night, firing nothing but jars for sealing. The potters work in iron chains, guarded by the Gu King's best blowgunners and riders. New jars are heaped like a hill at the kiln mouth, and the red cloth, already cut, is stacked beside them bale by bale.
column3: 死路尽头一座龙窑，顺着山坡爬了十几丈，窑火日夜不熄，烧的全是封念用的陶罐。窑工们被铁链拴着干活，守窑的是蛊王最精的吹箭手和蛊骑。窑口堆着小山似的新罐，红布已经裁好，一捆一捆码在旁边。

column2: The elite beaten back, the potters' chains are struck off and the kiln fire dies. The old master potter turns over the tally board at the kiln mouth, notch after notch: more than three thousand jars in ten years. 'Every jar I fire, the villages lose one more person who can miss someone,' he says. 'Ten years I fired them, and had my own longing sealed too. Only today do my hands hurt.'
column3: 精兵被打退，窑工的铁链砸开了，窑火也熄了。老窑工翻开窑口的记数板，一道一道的刻痕，十年烧了三千多只罐。「烧一只，寨里就少一个会想人的人，」他说，「我烧了十年，自己的念也封了，今天才觉得手疼。」

column2: The Man Who Forgot Home
column3: 忘乡人

column2: In a little forest hamlet lives a man with a northern accent who has herded the village dogs for seven years, cheerful as anything, and nobody remembers where he came from. Neither does he. Seven years ago he was so homesick he wanted to die, had it sealed, and never mentioned home again. Today blowgunners have come for him: the Gu King wants him to watch over the jars. 'A man with no longings does as he's told.'
column3: 林中一座小寨里有个北方口音的汉子，在寨里放了七年狗，乐呵呵的，谁也想不起他是从哪儿来的。他自己也想不起来：七年前他想家想得要寻死，封了念，从此再不提家。今天一伙吹箭手来抓他，说蛊王要他去罐林看罐：「这人没念头，最听话。」

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the man goes on feeding the dogs, smiling. You ask where his home is. He thinks a long while and comes up with one line: 'There's a big river. Freezes in winter.' A Zha says that when she finds her jar she'll look for his too. He scratches his head and smiles and says all right, as if agreeing to something for somebody else.
column3: 吹箭手被打跑，汉子还笑着给狗喂食。你们问他家在哪儿，他想了半天，只想出一句：「有条大河，冬天冻上。」阿扎说等找到罐子，也帮他找他的那一只。他挠挠头，笑着说好，像在答应别人的事。

column2: Hornet Ridge
column3: 胡蜂岭

column2: On a forest ridge an old maple holds a hornets' nest as big as a water vat, and the swarm comes down on anyone who passes. The sealers always take this ridge, because the hornets don't sting them: they're smeared with a salve the Gu King gives them. A Zha wants the shortcut to the Jar Forest, and you've barely set foot on the ridge before the swarm comes humming out.
column3: 林中山岭上一棵老枫树挂着个水缸大的胡蜂窝，过路的人一靠近，蜂群就扑下来。封念人专走这条岭，因为蜂子不蜇他们：他们身上抹着蛊王给的药膏。阿扎要从这里抄近路去罐林，你们刚上岭，蜂群已经嗡嗡地飞了出来。

column2: You light wet grass, smoke the swarm back into its nest and cross the ridge. From the crest the forest below is spattered with red, as if tree after tree were loaded with ripe fruit, red as far as the eye can reach. A Zha looks for a long time. 'So many.'
column3: 你们拿湿草点起浓烟，把蜂群熏回了窝，翻过了岭。站在岭上往下看，林子里星星点点全是红的，像一树树结满了熟透的果子，一直红到看不见的地方。阿扎看了很久，说：「那么多。」

column2: The Listeners' Altar
column3: 听蚕坛

column2: In the woods beside the Jar Forest the Silkworm Listeners have built a bamboo altar with a silkworm of gold paper on it. The faithful kneel in a ring around it, knocking their clappers and chanting, 'The silkworm is hungry, the silkworm is hungry.' They block the road to the Jar Forest: outsiders going in will startle the silkworm god.
column3: 罐林边的林子里，听蚕会的人搭了一座竹坛，坛上供着一只金纸扎的蚕，信徒们围着竹坛跪了一圈，一边敲竹梆一边念：「蚕饿了，蚕饿了。」他们拦着去罐林的路，说外人进林，会惊了蚕神。

column2: The faithful scattered, the paper silkworm blows away into a ditch. Their leader, caught, says miserably that they never meant harm; they're afraid. 'If the silkworm starves, the threads break, and everyone tied by them will never find the way back.' A Zha answers coldly: 'Then feed it what it ought to eat. Not my grandpa.'
column3: 信徒们被赶散，纸蚕被风吹进了沟里。会首被捉住后哭丧着脸说，他们并不想害人，只是怕：「蚕要是饿死了，丝就断了，那些拴着丝的人，就再也找不着回来的路了。」阿扎冷冷地说：「那就拿该喂的东西去喂，别拿我阿公喂。」

column2: Lei's Hearth
column3: 雷家火塘

column2: By Lei Dajiao's hearth the chieftain's household men are ransacking his chests: he guided Han strangers and smuggled them through the pass, they say, and must be fined three oxen. His wife stands in front of the chests brandishing the fire tongs, while Lei Dajiao himself is so furious his beard shakes and not a word comes out.
column3: 雷大脚家的火塘边，几个土司家的家兵正在翻箱倒柜，说他当年给汉人带路、私放过关，要罚他三头牛。雷大脚的老伴拿火钳挡在箱子前头，雷大脚自己气得胡子直抖，一句话也说不出来。

column2: The household men chased off, Lei Dajiao tells it slowly. Once their hearts were tied, those Han men walked like different people: no torches at night, and anyone who strayed only had to touch his wrist to find his way back. 'At the river Song Ge said the thread was pulling uphill: the chief was up there. So up the cliffs they went. I watched from the riverbank. Not one of them looked back.'
column3: 家兵被打跑，雷大脚才慢慢讲：拴了心以后，那些汉人走路跟换了个人似的，夜里不用点火把，谁走散了，摸摸手腕就找得回来。「走到江边，宋戈说丝往山上拽，镖头在上头，」他说，「他们就往崖上去了。我在江边看着，一个都没回头。」

column2: The Rope Yard
column3: 麻绳院

column2: An old rope-maker lives in the forest, his yard hung with rope thick as an arm and thin as a finger. Ten years ago the Qianli caravan ordered three thousand fathoms of hemp rope from him, for the cliffs, they said. Now rope merchants from beyond the hills have taken over his yard and won't let him eat until he writes down his family's secret method.
column3: 林中一个打麻绳的老匠人，院里挂满了绳子，粗的像胳膊，细的像手指。十年前千里号在他这里订过三千丈麻绳，说是上崖用的。如今一伙山外来的绳商占了他的院子，逼他把祖传的打绳法写出来，不写就不许他吃饭。

column2: The merchants thrown out, the old man rubs his empty belly and says the three thousand fathoms were Song Ge's order. 'He said the plank road up on the cliffs was broken in several places, and the chief was up there mending it, and wanted them to bring rope.' Every year since, he's twisted one more coil and stacked it in his shed. 'In case they need more.'
column3: 绳商被赶走，老匠人揉着饿瘪的肚子说，那三千丈绳是宋戈订的：「他说崖上的栈道断了好几截，镖头在上头修，叫他们带绳子上去。」这些年他每年还照样打一捆，码在仓里，「万一他们还要」。

column2: The Ghost Doctor's Lodge
column3: 鬼医寮

column2: At the end of a dead end stands a bamboo lodge where Doctor Ma, the villages' ghost doctor, has healed the sick all his life. Swordsmen and blowgunners he has paid stand at his door, and in bamboo cages behind the lodge he keeps a dozen or so travellers from outside: peddlers, porters, Han folk visiting kin. Every few days the doctor picks one and hands him to the sealers. A row of children's shoes is set out to dry at his door.
column3: 死路尽头一座竹寮，住着寨里的鬼医麻先生，治了一辈子病。门口守着他花钱雇来的刀客和吹箭手，寮后的竹笼里关着十几个人，都是过路的外乡人：货郎、背夫、走亲戚的汉人。麻先生每隔几天挑一个，送去给封念人封念。寮门口晒着一排小孩的鞋。

column2: The swordsmen scattered, the cages are smashed open. Doctor Ma doesn't run. He sits at his door and explains. Last year the silkworm grew so hungry it began calling village children's names at night, and two of them walked away. 'I feed it strangers' longings, and it stops calling the children. I've saved eleven children.' The shoes at his door belong to those eleven. No one pleads for him. No one can quite bring themselves to curse him either.
column3: 刀客被打散，竹笼砸开了。麻先生不跑，坐在门口说：去年金蚕饿极了，夜里开始喊寨里娃娃的名字，喊走了两个。「我拿外乡人的念喂它，它就不来喊娃娃了。我救下了十一个娃娃。」门口那排鞋，是那十一个娃娃的。没人替他求情，也没人骂得出口。

column2: The Jar Ledger House
column3: 罐账楼

column2: A timber house in the forest is the sealers' counting house, its shelves of ledgers recording every jar: which household, what longing, what day it was sealed, which row of the Jar Forest it hangs in. A few clerks and their guards hold the house, and when they see you coming they start throwing ledgers into the brazier in a panic.
column3: 林中一座木楼是封念人的账房，楼里一排排账簿记着每一只罐：哪一家、封的什么念、哪一天封的、挂在罐林哪一排。几个账先生带着寨丁守楼，见你们来了，慌着往火盆里扔账簿。

column2: The clerks pinned down, most of the ledgers are saved. A Zha finds the page with the rolling-pin mark and goes white. 'Sealed three years ago, hung west end, second row. Last tenth month: jar full, thrown down the sinkhole.' The clerk, hunching, explains: a longing sealed long enough fills its jar, full jars can't all be hung, so they're dropped down the sinkhole. 'The water carries them to the Gu King.'
column3: 账先生被按住，账簿抢下了大半。阿扎翻到擀面杖记号那一页，脸一下白了：「三年前封，挂西头第二排。去年十月，罐满，丢落水洞。」账先生缩着脖子解释：念封久了，罐就满了，满了挂不下，就丢进落水洞，「水会把它们带到蛊王那儿去」。

column2: The Levy Ground
column3: 征夫坪

column2: On an open ground outside the Jar Forest the Gu King's men are raising a levy: able-bodied men of the seven villages dragged in to carry and hang jars, ten from each village, and if one fails to come, someone in his household has their longing sealed to make up the number. Banners ring the ground, guards, blowgunners and riders each holding a corner, while the conscripts queue to be handed their jars one by one.
column3: 罐林外一片开阔的坪子，蛊王的人在这里征夫：七寨的青壮被拉来扛罐、挂罐，一寨十个人，不来的，就封他家一个人的念抵数。坪上旗子插了一圈，寨丁、吹箭手、蛊骑各占一角，被征来的人排着长队，一个个领罐子。

column2: You break up the levy, and the conscripts drop their jars and run home. The captured guard captain talks about the sinkhole. It's at the far west end of the Jar Forest, black all the way down, and no one ever hears a jar land. 'There's water at the bottom, flowing east. Where it goes, nobody knows.'
column3: 征夫坪被你们打散，被征来的人扔下罐子跑回了家。领头的寨丁被捉住，说起落水洞：那洞在罐林最西头，洞口往下全是黑的，丢下去的罐从来听不见落地，「底下是水，一直往东流，流到哪儿谁也不知道」。

column2: The Cinnabar Pits
column3: 朱砂坑

column2: The forest slope is pocked with pits where a gang boss of illegal miners, with hired thugs, forces a dozen half-grown children down narrow shafts to dig cinnabar, and the red stone goes out of the hills by the basketful. The shaft mouths are propped with crooked timbers, and the children come up red-dusted to the eyes, coughing without end.
column3: 林中山坡上挖满了坑，一伙盗矿的把头雇了打手，逼着十几个半大孩子钻进窄坑里挖朱砂，挖出来的红石头一筐筐运出山卖。坑口拿木头撑着，撑得歪歪斜斜，孩子们一个个满脸红粉，咳个不停。

column2: The thugs chased away, the children are hauled out one by one and the shafts sealed with stones. The smallest says that working down the pits at night he often heard a strange voice in the forest calling 'Keep up, keep up', and whenever it called he stopped being afraid. 'Like there was a grown-up out in front, leading the way.'
column3: 打手被打跑，孩子们一个个从坑里拉了上来，坑口拿石头封死了。最小的一个说，夜里在坑底干活，常听见林子里有个怪声喊「跟上，跟上」，一喊，他就不怕了：「像是有个大人在前头领路。」

column2: The Jar Forest
column3: 罐林

column2: The Jar Forest. Thousands of trees hung with clay jars sealed in red cloth, and when the wind blows they knock softly together, tock, tock, like many people tapping quietly at a door. It is very still. A few people with thread on their wrists stand beneath the trees, faces upturned, not moving. Gu riders on watch step out from behind the trunks.
column3: 罐林到了。千百棵树上挂满了陶罐，罐口封着红布，风一吹，罐子轻轻碰在一起，咚、咚，像很多人在小声敲门。林子里很静，有几个手腕缠丝的人站在树下，仰着头，一动不动。几个守林的蛊骑从树后转了出来。

column2: The riders driven off, A Zha finds the second row at the west end: on that tree, one empty hook. In the seventh row at the east end the woman's jar is still there. She stands on tiptoe, lifts it down, and doesn't dare open it. Not yet, A Zha tells her; Old Wu the silversmith warned them. 'Open a jar before the silkworm's been fed, and it'll smell it and come to snatch it back.'
column3: 守林的蛊骑被赶走。阿扎找到西头第二排，那棵树上空着一个钩子。东头第七排，那个妇人的罐子还在，她踮着脚把罐子抱了下来，没敢开。阿扎说先别开，这是银匠老吴叮嘱的：「金蚕没喂饱以前，开了罐，它闻着味儿，又要来抢。」

column2: The Jar-Hanger's Song
column3: 挂罐歌

column2: Deep in the Jar Forest lives the old man who has hung every jar in it for ten years. For each jar he hangs he makes up a line of song to remember its place, which household's jar is on which branch of which tree, all of it in his song. The Gu riders have heard, and mean to drag him off to be sealed so he'll forget the song too. The old man hugs a tree trunk and won't let go, still singing.
column3: 罐林深处住着个挂罐的老汉，十年来林里的罐子都是他挂的。他每挂一只，就编一句歌记下位置，哪家的罐在哪棵树哪根枝，全在他的歌里。蛊骑听说了，要拉他去封念，叫他把那支歌也忘掉。老汉抱着树干不撒手，嘴里还在唱。

column2: The riders chased off, the old man, still panting, sings for A Zha. At the second row of the west end he stops. 'That one went down the sinkhole last tenth month.' He'd like to know where the dropped jars go himself. 'The water runs east, but where it comes up in the east, seventy years I've lived and never found out.' A Zha thinks of the great heap of chaff at the water mill.
column3: 蛊骑被打跑，老汉喘着气把歌唱给阿扎听，唱到西头第二排，停了：「那一只，去年十月丢进了落水洞。」他说他也想知道丢下去的罐子去了哪儿，「水往东流，可东边哪儿冒出来，我活了七十年也不知道」。阿扎想起了碓房里那一大堆谷糠。

column2: The Silkworm's Bite
column3: 蚕口坑

column2: Out on the open ground the earth suddenly drops away into a huge pit, walls sheer as if knife-cut, mist drifting far below, a whole forest growing at the bottom and the sound of water rising from it. The villagers say the Gu King's golden silkworm bit it out in one mouthful, and call it the Silkworm's Bite. Gu riders stationed at the rim collect 'silkworm-honouring money' from travellers, and anyone who won't pay is to be pushed in 'to feed the silkworm'.
column3: 野地里忽然塌下去一个大坑，四壁陡得像刀切，往下看云雾缭绕，坑底长着一片林子，听得见水声。寨里人说这是蛊王的金蚕一口咬出来的，所以叫「蚕口」。一伙蛊骑守在坑边，向过路的人收「敬蚕钱」，不交的，就推下去「喂蚕」。

column2: The riders driven off, Lei Dajiao lies at the rim and looks for a long time. No silkworm bit this, he says. The mountain is limestone; groundwater dissolved great caves in it over the ages, and when the cave roof could no longer hold, it fell in and left this pit. 'That water at the bottom is the underground river that hollowed the mountain in the first place.' Song Ge lay here and looked too, he says, and said: 'Water digs the pits. People walk the roads.'
column3: 蛊骑被打退。雷大脚趴在坑边看了半天，说这不是蚕咬的：山肚子是石灰岩，地下水一年年溶出大洞，洞顶撑不住塌下来，就成了这个坑，「坑底那股水，就是掏空山肚子的那条暗河」。当年宋戈也在这儿看过，说：「坑是水挖的，路是人走的。」

column2: Cattle-Market Flat
column3: 牛场坝

column2: On the open ground lies a cattle-market flat where, on market days, people from all the villages around bring their cattle and their grain. At its southern end a stone gateway opens onto the old road to the river, half fallen in. Now the Gu King's guards hold the flat and have turned the cattle market into a 'silkworm market': everyone must lay a handful of tea on the silkworm altar first, and hill folk with no tea are kept out, carrying their grain all the way here and all the way home again.
column3: 野地里一片牛场坝，逢场天，四乡八寨牵着牛、背着粮来赶场。坝子南头一道石门通往江边的老路，石门塌了一半。如今坝子被蛊王的寨丁占了，牛场改成了「蚕场」，赶场的人要先往蚕坛上供一把茶叶，没茶的山民被拦在坝外，粮背来又背回去。

column2: The guards chased off and the altar pushed over, the cattle market bustles again. The villages round the flat have plenty of grain and little stone, and stone is exactly what they need to reopen the southern gateway and the old road to the river, so trade in stone for grain opens here.  Under the fallen gateway the road-menders dig up an old stele: 'Spring of dingwei. The Qianli caravan passed and mended this gate.' Every year on the night of the fifteenth of the first month, the old folk say, a single bell sounds from the cliffs to the south, far off and faint. 'They're still up there,' says an old cattle drover. 'They just can't get down.'
column3: 寨丁被赶走，蚕坛推倒，牛场又热闹起来。坝子四周的寨子粮多石少，要修通南头的石门和江边的老路，缺的正是石头，石换粮的买卖开了张。修路的石匠在塌了的石门底下刨出一块旧石碑，刻着：「丁未春，千里号过，修此门。」老人们说，每年正月十五夜里，南边崖上会传下来一声铃，很远，很轻。「他们还在上头，」赶牛的老汉说，「就是下不来。」

column2: The Sinkhole
column3: 落水洞

column2: At the far west end of the Jar Forest a stream runs up to the foot of the hill and plunges into a black hole and is gone: the sinkhole. A bamboo grille fences the mouth, and the guards posted there are tipping a basket of old, full jars into it. They fall into the dark without a sound.
column3: 罐林最西头，一条溪水流到这里，一头扎进山脚的一个黑洞，不见了，这就是落水洞。洞口拦着竹栅，几个寨丁守着，正把一筐满了的旧罐往洞里倒，罐子落进黑暗里，一点声音也没有。

column2: The guards chased off, you lean over the mouth and hear only water rushing far below. A Zha empties a big sack of chaff from the water mill into the stream, and it swirls and vanishes into the hole with the water. 'Wherever the water comes up, the chaff comes up with it,' she says. 'We go downstream and wait.'
column3: 寨丁被打跑，你们扒着洞口往下看，只听见底下哗哗的水声。阿扎把从碓房背来的一大袋谷糠倒进溪里，谷糠打着旋，跟着溪水钻进了洞。「水从哪儿冒出来，糠就从哪儿冒出来，」她说，「我们去下游等。」

column2: Pardon-Seekers' Wood
column3: 免死林

column2: A dozen or so deserters from a chieftain's army are hurrying through the forest toward the Gu King's village with a sack of half bricks. There's a bounty on their heads, and the King's land is the one place the chieftain won't follow, so they mean to trade the bricks for a pardon from the Gu King. The landlady of the stilt-house tavern chases after them, cursing: 'Those are my bricks! I bought them back!'
column3: 林中一伙土司家的逃兵，十几个人，扛着一袋半砖往蛊王寨的方向赶。他们开了小差，土司悬了赏，只有蛊王的地盘土司不敢去，就想拿砖跟蛊王换一张「免死帖」。吊脚楼酒家的老板娘追在后头骂：「那是我买回来的砖！」

column2: The deserters scattered, you recover the sack: three bricks. Panting, the landlady says she bought these back from thieves one at a time and hid them in her wine cellar, and this lot stole them last night. Two more she never managed to buy; a Gu rider called Old Ma took them. She pauses. 'Old Ma is my husband.'
column3: 逃兵被打散，袋里的砖抢了回来，是三块。酒家老板娘喘着气说，这三块是她一块一块从贼手里买回来的，藏在酒窖里，昨夜被这伙人偷了。还有两块她没买着，被一个叫老麻的蛊骑带走了。她顿了一下：「老麻是我男人。」

column2: Black-Scarf Stockade
column3: 黑巾寨

column2: A big stockade in the open is the lair of the black-scarf bandits, several hundred strong; the gang at the water mill was sent out from here. It sits square across the road south-east, and travellers pay 'scarf money' and are given a black headscarf to wear, which makes them 'one of us'. In her hurry to get downstream for the chaff, A Zha runs straight into their gate.
column3: 野地里一座大寨，是黑头巾山匪的老窝，几百号人，碓房那伙就是从这里派出去的。寨子横在往东南去的路上，过路的要交「头巾钱」，交了钱领一条黑头巾戴上，才算「自己人」。阿扎急着去下游等谷糠，一头撞上了他们的寨门。

column2: The bandits scattered, the ground is littered with discarded scarves. The captured chief does let slip something useful: every rainy season a spring in the south-eastern marshes coughs up broken pottery and scraps of rotten red cloth. 'We thought some village was making offerings into it.' A Zha hears that and takes off running south-east.
column3: 黑头巾山匪被打散，满地是扔掉的头巾。匪首被捉住，倒说了件有用的事：每到雨季，东南泽地里有一处泉眼会冒出碎陶片和烂红布，「我们还以为是哪个寨子往泉眼里祭神」。阿扎听完，拔腿就往东南跑。

column2: Straw-Sandal Slope
column3: 草鞋坡

column2: An old granny on a forest slope weaves a hundred pairs of straw sandals every year and sends them with anyone heading up into the mountains, to the foot of the southern cliffs, because cliff roads are hard on shoes. This year's pairs are freshly stacked when some soldiers-turned-bullies come by, pile them on the slope and light a bonfire to roast maize, jeering: 'Ten years? Who wears them, ghosts?' She rushes to save them and is shoved flat.
column3: 林中坡上住着个老阿婆，每年打一百双草鞋，托上山的人捎往南边的崖下，说崖路费鞋。今年的草鞋刚码好，一伙兵痞路过，抢去堆在坡上点了篝火烤苞谷，还笑她：「十年了，给鬼穿啊？」阿婆扑上去抢，被推了个跟头。

column2: The bullies chased off and the fire stamped out, most of the sandals are saved. Every year, the granny says, her sandals reach the foot of the cliffs, and every year the wrapping cloth comes back empty. Just once there was a slip of paper inside, folded round a single tea leaf: 'Shoes received. They fit.' She has sewn that paper into the lining of her jacket. 'If they were gone, who'd be telling me they fit?'
column3: 兵痞被赶走，火踩灭了，草鞋抢下来大半。阿婆说，她的草鞋年年送到崖底，包袱年年空着捎回来，只有一回，里头夹着一张纸，包着一片茶叶，纸上写着：「鞋收到，合脚。」她把那张纸缝在了衣襟里：「人要是没了，谁会说合脚？」

column2: Egret Marsh
column3: 鹭羽泽

column2: Hundreds upon hundreds of egrets roost in the south-eastern marsh, and hunters from beyond the hills are shooting them with poisoned arrows for the fine plumes on their backs, to sell in the cities for hat tassels. Plucked birds float on the water while the hunters stand waist-deep in mud and swing their bows round at anyone who comes. In her hurry to find the spring, A Zha has stepped right into their line of fire.
column3: 东南的沼泽里栖着成百上千只白鹭，一伙山外来的猎户张着毒箭，专射白鹭取它背上的蓑羽，拿去卖给城里做帽缨。泽面上漂着拔光了毛的鹭鸟，猎户们站在齐腰深的泥水里，见有人来，弓就转了过来。阿扎急着找泉眼，一脚踩进了他们的箭道里。

column2: The hunters driven out of the marsh, the surviving egrets settle back on the water. One hunter says that in winter, when the rest of the marsh freezes, one spring never does, and the egrets all crowd round it. 'The water comes up from under the ground. Warm to the touch in winter, cool in summer.' He points east: wherever the egrets are thickest, that's it.
column3: 猎户被赶出了泽地，剩下的白鹭又落回了水上。一个猎户说，泽里冬天别处结冰，只有一处泉眼不冻，鹭鸶冬天都挤在那儿：「水从地底下冒上来，冬天摸着是暖的，夏天摸着是凉的。」他朝东一指，那片白鹭最密的地方就是。

column2: The Box Hunters
column3: 寻匣客

column2: A dozen treasure hunters from beyond the hills, carrying spades and ropes, are trying to force the village hunters to guide them up to the cliffs in the south. They've heard there's an escort chief up there carrying an iron box with three locks, and it must hold gold or a treasure map. A hunter who refused is hanging from a tree, toes barely touching the ground.
column3: 野地里一伙山外来的寻宝客，十几个人，扛着铁锹绳索，逼着寨里的猎户给他们带路往南边的崖上去。他们听说崖上有个镖头，背着一只上了三道锁的铁匣，匣里不是金子就是宝图。不肯带路的猎户被他们吊在树上，脚尖刚够着地。

column2: The treasure hunters scattered, the hunter is cut down. Their leader carries a crooked hand-drawn map: a plank road winding along a cliff, and at its end a box with a lock on it. The hunter spits. 'Plenty have gone up those cliffs after that box in ten years. The ones who came back were half dead.'
column3: 寻宝客被打散，猎户放了下来。寻宝客的头儿揣着一张画得歪歪扭扭的图，崖上一条栈道弯弯曲曲，栈道尽头画着一个箱子，箱上一把锁。猎户啐了一口：「十年来上崖找匣子的人多了，回来的，都只剩半条命。」

column2: The Chieftain's Camp
column3: 土司营

column2: A big camp of the chieftain's household troops, several hundred strong, sits across the road south through the forest. Its standard officer still keeps the order of ten years ago: the south road is closed, and no one goes toward the cliffs. Swordsmen, crossbowmen and horsemen deploy rank on rank, and the officer bellows from the camp gate: 'By the chieftain's order, whoever disobeys dies!'
column3: 林中一座土司家兵的大营，几百人，横在往南的路上。营里的旗官还守着十年前的老令：南路封死，谁也不许往崖那边去。家兵的刀手、弩手、马队一层层排开，旗官站在营门口喊：「土司有令，违令者斩！」

column2: You scatter the camp. At dusk the chieftain himself rides up, none other than the one who drank the old Qianli tea and slept three days. In front of everyone he revokes the order closing the road. 'I've walked that cliff road in a dream,' he says. 'The man ahead kept telling me to keep up. Ten years they've been mending the road up there and ten years I've kept it closed down here. It's a disgrace.'
column3: 家兵大营被你们打散。傍晚，土司本人骑着马赶来，正是喝了千里号旧茶睡了三天的那一位。他当着众人收回了封路的令：「我在梦里走过那条崖路，」他说，「前头那个人一直叫我跟上。人家在上头修了十年路，我在下头封了十年，不像话。」

column2: The Brothers' Stockade
column3: 兄弟寨

column2: A stockade on the open ground is ruled by twin chiefs, identical in every feature, each of whom can't stand the other; a bamboo fence splits the stockade down the middle. Each brother holds half of an old route map the caravan left ten years ago; they fell out over who should keep it and tore it in two. Today their guards are brawling at both ends of the fence again, and your carts are stuck right in the middle.
column3: 野地里一座寨子，寨主是一对双胞胎，长得一模一样，却谁也看不上谁，寨子当中拿竹篱隔成了两半。两兄弟手里各有半张老路图，是十年前马帮留下的，当年为了谁拿着吵翻了，一撕两半。今天两边的寨丁又在竹篱两头打起来了，你们的车正好卡在当中。

column2: Both sets of guards beaten into submission, you lay the two halves together on a table: one half runs south, the other runs up. The elder brother always said the caravan went south, the younger always said it went up, and they've quarrelled ten years with neither of them wrong. The twins stare at the joined map a long while, and that night the fence comes down.
column3: 两边的寨丁都被打服了。你们把两半张图往桌上一拼，一张往南，一张往上：哥哥一直说马帮往南走了，弟弟一直说马帮往上走了，吵了十年，谁也没说错。两兄弟对着拼好的图看了半天，竹篱当晚就拆了。

column2: The Silkworm Gate
column3: 蚕门

column2: At the far end of the open ground stands the gate of the Gu King's village, a string of shrivelled cocoons hung from the gatehouse, and before it the King's last camp of men: guards, blowgunners, Gu riders. The sun is nearly down, and only now do you see it: across the sky above the gate stretch a thousand fine gold threads, glittering in the low light, reaching out from the village in every direction.
column3: 野地尽头是蛊王寨的寨门，门楼上挂着一串干瘪的蚕茧，门前排着蛊王最后的一营人马，寨丁、吹箭手、蛊骑都在。太阳快落山了，你们这才看清：门楼上方的天上，横着千百根细细的金丝，夕阳一照，亮闪闪的，从寨子里伸出去，往四面八方。

column2: The camp before the gate scattered, the gate stands open. From beneath it you look up at the threads. Most run south, each pulled straight as a drawn bowstring; some droop toward the seven villages, tied to the wrists of those who wait; and a single one runs off alone to the north, hanging slack. Deep in the village, that shrill cry comes again.
column3: 门前的人马被你们打散，寨门开了。你们站在门下抬头看那些丝：大半往南，一根根绷得笔直，像拉满的弓弦；有些垂向七寨，拴着那些等人的手腕；有一根孤零零地往北去，松松地垂着。寨子深处，那尖尖的叫声又响了一下。

column2: The Sealing Hall
column3: 封念堂

column2: At the end of a dead end below the sinkhole stands a bamboo hall, the sealers' headquarters. On a long table lie a stack of red cloth, a bowl of clear water and a handful of silver pins. The master sealer, a soft-spoken man of middle years, has hired swordsmen to guard the door, and he's in the middle of sealing a young man whose mother remarried and left him sleepless with missing her. The red cloth already lies over the mouth of the jar.
column3: 落水洞下游死路尽头一座竹堂，是封念人的老窝，堂里摆着一张长案，案上一摞红布、一碗清水、一把银针。封念师是个说话细声细气的中年人，雇了一伙刀客守门，正给一个后生封念：后生的阿妈改嫁了，他想得睡不着。红布已经盖在了罐口上。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the young man's jar isn't yet sealed tight. The red cloth comes off and he bursts into tears, and when he's done he says he still misses his mother but feels steady inside. The captured master sealer confesses: a sealed longing knows its way home, but the jar must be opened in front of the person it came from, or the longing won't go back. 'Open it away from them, and it scatters.' A Zha grips the rolling pin inside her coat.
column3: 刀客被打跑，后生的罐子还没封牢，红布一掀，后生「哇」地哭了出来，哭完说他还是想阿妈，可是心里踏实。封念师被捉住，老实交代：封进去的念认得家，罐子要当着封念的人打开，念头才会回去，「隔着人开，就散了」。阿扎听完，攥紧了怀里那根擀面杖。

column2: Ma's Tavern
column3: 麻嫂酒家

column2: A stilt-house tavern stands in the forest, wine jars stacked taller than a man downstairs, where night travellers used to rest. Now a squad of the Gu King's guards has commandeered it as a way station for hauling goods to his village, drinking free, and the landlady, Sister Ma, has to hide in the kitchen. Her husband, Old Ma, was a Gu rider until half a month ago, when he vanished with two half bricks, and the guards press her daily to say where he is.
column3: 林中一座吊脚楼酒家，楼下酒坛码得比人还高，往日赶夜路的都在这里歇脚。如今楼被蛊王的一队寨丁征了，当作往蛊王寨运东西的歇站，酒白喝不给钱，老板娘麻嫂只能缩在灶房里。她男人老麻原是蛊骑，半个月前带着两块半砖不见了，寨丁们天天逼她说人在哪儿。

column2: The guards thrown out, the tavern reopens, and Sister Ma trades you rice wine, measured to the brim. Old Ma's no thief, she says. Ten years a Gu rider, every night hearing the silkworm crying in its cave until he couldn't sleep, and half a month ago he took two bricks, saying he'd 'hide them for those two men so the King can't feed them'. He rode off east on his piebald toward the cliffs.
column3: 寨丁被撵走，酒家重新开张，麻嫂拿米酒跟你们换货，打得满满的。她说老麻不是贼：他当了十年蛊骑，夜夜听金蚕在洞里叫，叫得他睡不着，半个月前揣了两块砖，说要「替那两个人藏起来，不叫蛊王喂了」。他骑着花马往东边的崖下去了。

column2: The Mushroom Yard
column3: 菌子场

column2: In a forest clearing, mushrooms dry on bamboo trays, termite mushrooms, porcini, matsutake, all carried here from the mountainsides after rain. A gang of guards who deserted from the Gu King's village has taken over the yard; they do no work, just collect everyone else's dried mushrooms and sell them out of the hills. The pickers climb the hills by day and come home empty-handed at night.
column3: 林中一片晒菌子的场子，竹匾上摊着鸡枞、牛肝菌、松茸，雨后满山的菌子都背到这里来晒。一伙从蛊王寨开小差的寨丁占了场子，不干活，专收别人晒好的干菌，转手卖出山去。采菌的山民白天上山采，晚上空着手回家。

column2: The deserters chased off, the trays fill again. That spring, Lei Dajiao says, the caravan spent half a month drying mushrooms here and carried them off sack by sack. 'Song Ge said there's nothing up on the cliffs. Dried mushrooms weigh nothing, and one handful makes a whole pot of soup.'
column3: 开小差的寨丁被赶跑，竹匾又摆满了。雷大脚说，那年开春马帮在这里晒了半个月的菌子，晒干了一袋袋背走：「宋戈说崖上什么都缺，干菌子轻，一把能煮一锅汤。」

column2: From the deserters' hoard: four sacks of dried termite mushrooms, a small basket of dried matsutake, a bundle of bamboo trays, two earthenware vats for smoking mushrooms, and a crock of salt they stole from the Gu King's village when they ran.
column3: 抄出寨丁囤的干鸡枞四袋、干松茸一小篓、一捆竹匾、两口熏菌子的瓦缸，还有他们开小差时从蛊王寨偷出来的一罐盐。

column2: Every time you pass, the pickers press a packet of freshly dried mushrooms on you. 'Throw a handful in the pot. Better than meat.'
column3: 每次路过，采菌的山民都塞给你们一包刚晒好的干菌：「抓一把丢进锅里，比肉还香。」

column2: Marsh-Pirates' Landing
column3: 水匪埠

column2: On the open ground at the marsh's edge lies a landing, a pirates' den, a dozen flat-bottomed boats tied to its posts. They pole about the marsh fishing out the broken jars the spring coughs up, pull out the silver pins to melt and sell, and dry the red cloth for foot wrappings. A Zha spots a basket of pins on the landing and dives in to search it, and a pirate's punt pole comes sweeping at her head.
column3: 泽边野地上一处旱码头，是水匪的窝，十几条平底船拴在木桩上。他们撑船在泽里转，专捞泉眼冒出来的碎罐子，拔下罐口的银针拿去熔了卖，红布晒干了当包脚布。阿扎一眼看见码头边一筐银针，扑过去就翻，水匪的竹篙兜头就扫了过来。

column2: The pirates are knocked into the water and scatter. The basket of pins is searched to the bottom: no rolling pin. Whenever the marsh rises, new pirates pole in to fish for jars, since every haul pays; this lot is cleared, but another will come before long, so all you can do is clear them out every so often. Before leaving, A Zha hands the whole basket to Old Wu the silversmith to match each pin back to its owner.
column3: 水匪被打下了水，四散逃了。一筐银针翻了个遍，没有擀面杖。泽里水一涨，就有新的水匪撑着船来捞罐子，捞一回赚一回，这一伙清了，过一阵又会来一伙，只能隔些日子来清一回。临走，阿扎把那筐银针都交给了银匠老吴，让他一根根认回原主。

column2: The Wantong Camp
column3: 万通营

column2: A big camp in the open flies the banner of the Wantong Company, a great merchant house from beyond the hills, with a caravan guarded by a hundred hired swordsmen blocking the road south. Their master has announced that since the Qianli caravan hasn't come back in ten years, the cliff road belongs to Wantong now, and no other caravan may go south. The guards form up and laugh themselves silly at your shabby carts.
column3: 野地里一座大营，挂着「万通号」的旗，是山外一家大商号的马帮，雇了上百个镖师，堵在往南去的路口。他们的东家放话：千里号十年没回来，崖上那条路以后归万通号走，别家的马帮一律不许往南。镖师们排开阵势，嫌你们的车寒酸，笑得前仰后合。

column2: The guards scattered, the Wantong master on his knees confesses something. Every year in the first month an old mule comes down from the cliffs alone, carrying a bundle of tea toward the Gu villages. For nine years his men have waylaid it and sold the tea beyond the hills as 'Clifftop Snow Tea', worth its weight in gold. 'This year's mule,' he says, trembling, 'is tied up in a shed to the north.'
column3: 镖师们被打散，万通号的东家跪在地上，供出一件事：每年正月，崖上会有一头老骡子独自下来，驮着一包茶往蛊寨走。九年来，他的人年年把骡子截下，茶拿出山去卖，叫「崖顶雪茶」，一两值一两金。「今年那头骡子，」他哆嗦着说，「拴在北边的草棚里。」

column2: Stilt Camp
column3: 高脚营

column2: In the middle of the marsh stands a camp on stilts, its platforms a man's height above the water: the Gu King's post guarding the spring. Blowgunners shoot down from behind the railings, riders lead their horses back and forth along the mud dykes, and no one in the marsh may go near the stretch of water where the egrets are thickest.
column3: 泽地中央扎着一座高脚营，营盘架在木桩上，离水面一人多高，是蛊王的人守泉眼的营。营里的吹箭手从栏杆后面往下射，蛊骑牵着马在泥埂上来回巡，泽里的人谁也不许靠近那片白鹭最密的水面。

column2: You storm the stilt camp. A prisoner explains: the underground river from the sinkhole runs right beneath the Gu King's village, and the King has stretched nets across it in his cave. Most of the jars dropped in are caught and carried to the silkworm; the ones that slip through come up here at the spring. 'The King doesn't want outsiders knowing. He's had us guarding it three years.'
column3: 高脚营被你们攻了下来。俘虏说，落水洞下去的暗河从蛊王寨底下流过，蛊王在洞里拦了网，丢下去的罐子大多被网住，送到金蚕跟前；漏网的，就从这里的泉眼冒出来。「蛊王怕外人知道，」他说，「派我们在这儿守了三年。」

column2: Bell-Thread Ground
column3: 铃丝坪

column2: Over a wide open ground run dozens of gold threads, stretching south from the Gu King's village. His men have hung a little brass bell on every one and set a camp of Gu riders to watch: touch a thread and ring a bell, and the arrows fly. In the grass at the edge, several travellers' hats lie shot through and still pinned to the ground.
column3: 野地上一片开阔的坪子，头顶横过几十根金丝，从蛊王寨往南伸去。蛊王的人在每根丝上拴了一只小铜铃，派一营蛊骑守着，谁碰了丝、铃一响，就放箭。坪子边的草里，好几个过路人的帽子被射穿了，还钉在地上。

column2: The riders scattered. You're standing beneath the threads about to move on when every bell overhead rings softly at once, ting, as if people very far away had all stirred together. They ring like that several times a day, a prisoner says; the King hung the bells to hear whether the people at the far end still move. 'They move,' he says. 'Every day for ten years.'
column3: 守坪的蛊骑被打散。你们站在丝底下，正要走，头顶的铃忽然一齐轻轻响了一下，叮，像有人在很远的地方同时动了一动。俘虏说，铃每天都会这么响几回，蛊王拴铃，就是要听那头的人还动不动。「动，」他说，「十年来天天都动。」

column2: The Tea-Mule Shed
column3: 茶骡棚

column2: In a thatched shed on the open ground stands an old mule, grey going white, its pack frame worn glossy, an oilcloth bundle on its back. A few Wantong hands guard the shed, not yet knowing their master is on his knees, and are haggling over how much this year's tea will fetch. The old mule makes no sound, neck stretched toward the south.
column3: 野地里一座草棚，棚里拴着一头老骡子，毛色灰白，背上的驮架磨得发亮，驮着一个油布包。几个万通号的伙计守着棚，还不知道东家已经跪下了，正商量着今年这包茶该卖多少钱。老骡子一声不吭，直着脖子朝南边望。

column2: The hands chased off, the halter comes untied. Lei Dajiao walks round the mule once and slaps his thigh: this is a mule the caravan bought from the villages back then, and he shod it with his own hands. Untied, it doesn't head back south. It turns straight for the Gu King's village, walks a few steps, looks back at you, as if waiting for you to keep up.
column3: 伙计们被赶跑，缰绳解开了。雷大脚围着骡子转了一圈，一拍大腿：这是当年马帮从寨里买走的骡子，他亲手钉的掌。骡子一松开，也不往南回，转身就朝蛊王寨的方向走，走几步，回头看你们一眼，像是在等你们跟上。

column2: Hostage-Guide Slope
column3: 押路坡

column2: On a slope in the open, Gu riders have tied Lei Dajiao across a horse and mean to drive him south: the Gu King can't wait any longer, and is sending men up the cliffs to drag the Qianli people down one by one to feed the silkworm, and they need someone who knows the way. Lei Dajiao curses at the top of his voice from the saddle, and with every curse a rider lashes the horse.
column3: 野地坡上，一伙蛊骑把雷大脚绑在了马背上，要押着他往南去：蛊王等不及了，要派人上崖，把千里号的人一个个拖下来喂蚕，非得找个认路的。雷大脚在马背上破口大骂，骂一句，马就挨蛊骑一鞭子。

column2: The riders knocked out of their saddles, you untie Lei Dajiao, who rubs his wrists and grumbles. The Gu King really is desperate, he says, but desperation won't help. 'The cliff road's collapsed. Horses can't get up, and a man needs hands and feet both. They can't come down, and the King's men can't go up.' He looks south. 'Anyone who wants to go up will have to mend it, stretch by stretch.'
column3: 蛊骑被打下了马，雷大脚被你们解了下来，揉着手腕直哼哼。他说蛊王是真急了，可急也没用：「崖路塌了，马上不去，人上去还得手脚并用。他们下不来，蛊王的人也上不去。」他望着南边：「要上去，得有人一截一截地修。」

column2: Missing-Nail Gully
column3: 缺钉沟

column2: In a forest gully a line of hoofprints leads east through the mud: Old Ma's piebald, its near fore shoe missing a nail, the print unmistakable. A troop of Gu riders is tracking the same prints, their leader swearing, 'Catch Old Ma, the bricks go to the King and the man goes in a jar.' You and the riders meet head-on at the mouth of the gully.
column3: 林中一道山沟，泥里一串马蹄印往东去，是老麻那匹花马的，左前掌缺了一颗钉，印子一看就认得。一伙蛊骑也顺着蹄印在追，领头的扬言：「抓住老麻，砖归蛊王，人归罐子。」你们和蛊骑在沟口撞了个正着。

column2: The riders beaten back, you follow the prints to the bottom of the gully. The piebald is tied to a tree, so hungry it's gnawing the bark, and its rider is gone. Round the saddle is a sash woven by Sister Ma, and tucked inside it a scrap of paper showing a cave mouth with three bends drawn in front of it.
column3: 蛊骑被打退，你们顺着蹄印走到沟底，花马拴在一棵树上，饿得直啃树皮，人不在。马鞍上系着一条麻嫂织的腰带，腰带里塞着一张纸，画着一个洞口，洞口前画了三道弯。

column2: Chaff Spring
column3: 冒糠泉

column2: Amid the water where the egrets are thickest wells a spring, pulsing up from the bottom of the pool, so clear you can see the floor, churning like a pot about to boil. A few of the Gu King's blowgunners on a bamboo raft guard it, scooping up whatever surfaces with long-handled nets. A Zha squats on a mud dyke, staring at the spring without blinking.
column3: 白鹭最密的那片泽水当中，有一眼泉，水从塘底一股股往上翻，清得见底，翻起来像锅里的水快开了。几个蛊王的吹箭手撑着竹筏守在泉边，拿长柄网兜捞水里冒出来的东西。阿扎蹲在泥埂上，一眼不眨地盯着泉眼。

column2: The blowgunners knocked off their raft, the spring chooses that moment to boil up a scatter of yellow chaff, spreading in rings. A Zha leaps up. 'It's the mill chaff!' In limestone hills, rain over the ages dissolves the mountain hollow, and water that sinks into a hole runs through caves underground and comes up somewhere far away; scatter chaff where it goes in, watch where it comes out, and you know its road. Caught in the reeds is a clay jar, unbroken, the silver pin in its seal engraved with a rolling pin.
column3: 吹箭手被打下竹筏，泉眼里正好翻上来一层黄黄的谷糠。阿扎跳起来：「是碓房的糠！」石灰岩的山被雨水溶空了肚子，水钻进落水洞，在山底下的洞里走，到老远的地方再冒出来；在进水的地方撒糠，就知道水去了哪儿。苇丛里卡着一只没破的陶罐，银针上刻着一根擀面杖。

column2: Jar-Snatch Slope
column3: 抢罐坡

column2: A Zha is carrying the jar back, and on a slope in the open a party of sealers with Gu riders catches up to take it. 'That belongs to the Gu King!' A Zha clutches it to her chest and curls up round it. Hard behind come the woman from the Asking-Back Gate and the northern dog-herder, each hugging a jar taken down from the Jar Forest, gasping for breath.
