column3: 阿扎抱着罐子往回走，到了野地的坡上，一伙封念人带着蛊骑追了上来，要把罐子抢回去：「这是蛊王的东西！」阿扎把罐子抱在胸口，蹲下来缩成一团。后面还跟来了讨念门那个妇人和放狗的北方汉子，各自抱着从罐林里取下的罐子，跑得气喘吁吁。

column2: The sealers and riders chased away, the three sit on the slope to rest, three jars in their arms, none of them opened. A Zha says the master sealer told her the jar must be opened in front of its owner; her grandpa is back in the village, and she must bring him to the jar. The northern man scratches his head. He's right here beside his own, he says, but he doesn't know if he should. 'Will it hurt, opening it?'
column3: 封念人和蛊骑被打跑了。三个人抱着三只罐坐在坡上歇气，谁也没开。阿扎说，封念师讲了，罐要当着封念的人开，阿公在寨子里，得把他接到罐子跟前来。北方汉子挠着头说，他自己就在跟前，可他不知道该不该开：「开了，会疼吧？」

column2: Tea-Bundle Rise
column3: 茶包岗

column2: On an earthen rise in the open the old mule stops and won't go on, and some of the Gu King's blowgunners rise out of the grass, eyes on the oilcloth bundle on its back: the silkworm has smelled tea, and the King has sent men to collect it. They aim their tubes at the mule's neck. The mule doesn't move, only turns the bundle a little toward you.
column3: 野地的土岗上，老骡子停下来不走了，几个蛊王的吹箭手从草里钻出来，盯上了它背上那个油布包：金蚕闻见了茶味，蛊王派人来接。他们把竹管对准了骡子的脖子，骡子一动不动，只把油布包往你们这边侧了侧。

column2: The blowgunners chased off, you open the bundle: a newly pressed tea brick with a deep groove down the middle, and stuck into it a bamboo slip cut with a few words: 'This year's tea. Everyone well. Road still broken. Song Ge.' You count back: nine years, nine such slips should have come down. Not one ever arrived.
column3: 吹箭手被打跑。你们解开油布包，里头是一块新压的茶砖，中间一道深槽，砖上插着一根竹片，刻着几个字：「今年的茶。人都在，路未通。宋戈。」你们算了算，这样的竹片，九年来该有九根，一根也没送到。

column2: The Peddler's Load
column3: 山货担

column2: On the open ground outside the Gu King's gate a peddler sits guarding two great baskets of mountain goods: honey, musk-deer hides, kudzu starch, little woven bamboo toys, all gathered village by village. He's sat here a month and sold nothing. The King's riders have closed the road outside his gate to all trade, and every day they turn over his baskets looking for hidden tea.
column3: 蛊王寨门外的野地上，一个挑山货的货郎守着两大筐货：蜂蜜、獐子皮、葛根粉、竹编的小玩意儿，都是走村串寨收来的，在这里坐了一个月，一样也没卖出去。蛊王的蛊骑封了寨门外的路，谁也不许做买卖，还天天来翻他的筐，看有没有藏着茶叶。

column2: The riders chased off, the peddler opens for business, trading mountain goods for cloth and needles, his abacus clicking at speed. Thirty years he's walked these mountain roads, he says, and never seen the Gu King like this. 'Not out of his cave in a month. His men say he's wasted to a bundle of bones, sits all day holding that silkworm and talking to it.'
column3: 蛊骑被打跑，货郎的担子开了张，拿山货跟你们换布匹针线，算盘打得飞快。他说他走了三十年山路，从没见过蛊王这样：「一个月没出过洞，洞口的人说他瘦得只剩一把骨头，天天抱着那只蚕，跟它说话。」

column2: Gaur Slope
column3: 野牛坡

column2: A herd of gaur blocks the slope, every one a head taller than a water buffalo, glossy black backs and four legs white as if in stockings. The Gu King's starving men tried to hunt them and missed, and only enraged the herd; now anyone who walks below the slope gets the lead bull charging down at them, horns low. The old mule has to pass this way, and stands at the foot of the slope pawing the ground.
column3: 野地坡上横着一群野牛，个个比水牯还高一头，黑亮的背，白袜子似的四条腿。蛊王的人饿急了要打它们，没打着，倒把牛群惹怒了，如今谁从坡下走，领头的公牛就低着角冲下来。老骡子要从这里过，站在坡脚刨着蹄子。

column2: You drive the gaur up onto the ridge and the road below clears. That herd never used to bar anyone, Lei Dajiao says; the old mule came through here every year and they always made way for it. 'The gaur know the mule, the mule knows the road. It's only people who don't.' The old mule walks slowly past below the slope without looking back.
column3: 野牛被你们赶上了山梁，坡下的路空了出来。雷大脚说，这群野牛从前不拦人，老骡子年年从这里过，它们都给它让道：「牛认得骡子，骡子认得路，就是人不认得。」老骡子头也不回，从坡下慢慢走了过去。

column2: Missing-Cake Hamlet
column3: 丢糕寨

column2: In a little hamlet at the edge of the open ground, a squad of the Gu King's grain levy has seized the granary and is carrying the rice off to his village load by load, leaving the villagers only wild greens. Stranger still, every morning a few of the sticky rice cakes the levy men steam go missing, and by the steamer you can hear a voice say 'keep up'. The levy men are sure the villagers are stealing them, and have tied the hamlet elder to the granary door until he hands over the thief.
column3: 野地边一座小寨，寨里的谷仓被蛊王的一队粮丁占了，米一担担往蛊王寨挑，寨民只剩野菜。更怪的是，粮丁们蒸好的糯米糕，每天早上都少几块，蒸笼边还能听见一声「跟上」。粮丁们认定是寨民偷的，把寨老绑在仓门口，要他交出贼来。

column2: The levy men chased off, the elder is untied. That very night the steamer lid gives a little clink, and a green flash shoots up to the rafters with half a rice cake in its beak, mumbling round it: 'Keep up.' A green parrot. It cocks its head at you from the beam a moment, then flutters out of the hamlet.
column3: 粮丁被赶走，寨老松了绑。当天夜里，蒸笼盖子轻轻一响，一道绿影一闪就上了房梁，嘴里叼着半块糯米糕，含含糊糊地说了一声：「跟上。」是只绿鹦鹉。它在梁上歪着头看了你们一会儿，扑棱棱飞出了寨子。

column2: Recovered from the levy: twelve loads of white rice, two steamers of sticky rice cakes, a vat of pickled greens, and a brass gong they brought with them, which the elder says he'll keep for chasing parrots.
column3: 抄回粮丁搬走的白米十二担、糯米糕两笼、一缸腌酸菜，还有他们自己带来的一面铜锣，寨老说留着，以后赶鹦鹉用。

column2: Every time you pass, the hamlet wraps you a few sticky rice cakes and always one little extra. 'That's for the parrot. If it's following you, feed it.'
column3: 每次路过，寨里都给你们包几块糯米糕，还特意多包一块小的：「给那只鹦鹉留的，它要是跟着你们，就喂它。」

column2: Three-Bend Cave
column3: 三弯洞

column2: Under a forest cliff, at the end of a path with three bends, a cave mouth is surrounded by blowgunners. They're tossing burning bundles of dried chillies inside to smoke out whoever is there. From the cave comes coughing, fit after fit, and a hoarse voice swearing: 'Smoke me to death, you still won't get the bricks!'
column3: 林中崖脚下，三道弯的小路尽头有个洞口，被一伙吹箭手围着。他们正往洞里扔点着的干辣椒捆，想把里头的人熏出来。洞里一阵阵咳嗽，还有个哑着嗓子的声音在骂：「熏死我，砖也不给！」

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the chilli smoke clears from the mouth. Old Ma crawls out, coughing till tears stream down his face, two half bricks still hugged tight to his chest. The cave goes further in, he says, and there's something more important inside. He has to show you.
column3: 吹箭手被打跑，洞口的辣椒烟散了。老麻从洞里爬出来，咳得满脸是泪，怀里还紧紧抱着两块半砖。他说这洞往里还有一截，里头有更要紧的东西，他得带你们进去看。

column2: Noodle Hamlet
column3: 擀面寨

column2: The last little hamlet before the Gu King's village has been seized by a squad of his guards as a supply depot; its rice, smoked pork and salt are all locked in their store, and the villagers live on wild greens. A Zha has brought her grandpa here, and the old man sits at the hamlet gate, beaming, asking nothing. The guards won't let outsiders in: it's too close to the King. 'Startle the silkworm, and who'll answer for it?'
column3: 蛊王寨外最后一座小寨，蛊王的一队寨丁占了寨子当粮台，寨里的米、腊肉、盐巴都被搬进了他们的仓，寨民只能吃野菜。阿扎把阿公接到了这里，老人坐在寨口笑眯眯的，什么也不问。寨丁们不许外人进寨，说这里离蛊王太近，「惊了蚕，谁担得起」。

column2: The guards chased off. A Zha can't wait any longer, and in front of her grandpa she lifts off the red cloth. The old man sits stunned for a moment, then the tears come all at once. 'Xiao Cong, Xiao Cong,' he murmurs, and then he hugs A Zha and calls her by her name. He asks for the rolling pin, sets up a board at the hamlet gate and rolls a whole potful of noodles. At that very moment, from the cave in the Gu King's village, comes a long, shrill cry, and every gold thread on every wrist pulls tight at once.
column3: 寨丁被打跑。阿扎等不及了，当着阿公的面揭开了红布。阿公愣了一会儿，眼泪一下子下来了，念着「小葱，小葱」，接着一把抱住阿扎，喊了她的名字，又要过擀面杖，擀了一大锅面。就在这时，蛊王寨的洞里传来一声尖尖的长叫，大伙手腕上的金丝一齐绷紧了。

column2: Recovered from the guards' store: fifteen sacks of white rice, two great strings of smoked pork, a pack-load of salt, and a jar of honey they'd hoarded for themselves, which the villagers call interest for their trouble.
column3: 抄回寨丁搬走的白米十五袋、腊肉两大挂、盐巴一驮，还有他们自己囤的一坛蜂蜜，寨民说就当是这些天的利息。

column2: Every time you pass, A Zha's grandpa rolls you a potful of noodles, Han craft in Miao sour soup, saying as he rolls, 'A cook called Xiao Cong taught me this.'
column3: 每次路过，阿公都给你们擀一锅面，汉人的手艺，苗家的酸汤，一边擀一边说：「这是一个叫小葱的伙夫教的。」

column2: The Empty Hamlet
column3: 空寨楼

column2: You follow the green flash into an empty hamlet. There's no one at all; every stilt-house door stands open, the ash in the hearths is still warm, cloth sits half woven on a loom with the shuttle caught in the warp. The crying from the Gu King's village has grown so fierce at night, you've heard, that everyone here went to stay with relatives two days ago. You rest upstairs, drinking the cold tea you brought, and nobody says a word. Then, from between the floorboards under your feet, someone softly calls the name of Old Zhong, who drives your lead cart.
column3: 你们跟着那道绿影走进一座空寨。寨里一个人也没有，吊脚楼的门都开着，火塘里的灰还是温的，织机上的布织了一半，梭子还夹在经线里。听说蛊王寨那边夜里叫得越来越凶，寨里的人前天都躲到亲戚家去了。你们在楼上歇脚，喝着自带的凉茶，谁也没说话。这时，脚下的楼板缝里，有人轻轻喊了一声赶头车的老钟的名字。

column2: No one answers; everyone remembers the first rule. Holding your breath, you prise up the floorboards, and below sits the green parrot, perched on a basket of sticky rice. All afternoon you've been shouting 'Old Zhong, Old Zhong' heaven knows how many times, and it's learned every one. It blinks at you, then changes voices: deep, gruff, with a northern accent. 'Keep up, keep up.'
column3: 谁也没应，第一条规矩大伙都记得。你们屏着气撬开楼板，底下是那只绿鹦鹉，正蹲在一只装糯米的箩筐上。一下午你们「老钟、老钟」地喊了不知多少回，它全学会了。它冲你们眨眨眼，又换了一个声音，粗粗的，带着北边口音：「跟上，跟上。」

column2: The Crack in the Wall
column3: 隔壁石缝

column2: Deep in the cave only a wall of rock separates you from the Gu King's village, and there's a crack in it. Put your ear to it and you hear the other side: a faint, faint crying, like a silkworm gnawing a mulberry leaf, or someone very far away calling names. This is where Old Ma has listened for ten years. A squad of the King's bodyguards is creeping in from the other side to seal the crack with mud.
column3: 洞的深处离蛊王寨只隔一道石壁，石壁上有条缝，凑近了能听见那边的声音：一种很细很细的叫声，像蚕在啃桑叶，又像有人在很远的地方喊名字。老麻说他就是在这里听了十年。一队蛊王的亲兵从石缝那头摸了过来，要拿泥浆把这条缝堵死。

column2: The bodyguards beaten back, the crack stays open. Old Ma hands you the two bricks. He never meant to steal them, he says, only to hide them for their two men. 'If the silkworm wants to eat, let it eat me first.' One name on the tags he knows: a Han lad he taught to ride that winter. Through the crack you see a great cavern, a thousand gold threads hanging from its roof, and every one of them gathered into a single man: an old man wasted to a bundle of bones. 'That's the Gu King,' Old Ma whispers.  Word goes back to the Elders' Council, and Yan Gong sends a message: the rack is full. Two hundred and ninety-nine, and your one besides.
column3: 亲兵被打退，石缝保住了。老麻把两块砖交给你们，说他没想偷，是想替这两个人藏着：「金蚕要吃，先吃我。」竹签上有一个名字他认得，是那年冬天跟他学骑马的汉人小伙。从石缝里望过去，那边是一个大洞，洞顶垂下千百根金丝，丝都收在一个人身上：一个瘦得只剩一把骨头的老人。「那就是蛊王，」老麻低声说。消息传回寨老会，岩公捎来一句话：架子满了，二百九十九格，加上你们那一块。

column2: Parrot-Talk Slope
column3: 学舌坡

column2: On an open slope at the end of a dead end, the Gu King's blowgunners have spread nets round a lone old tree and are climbing it, the green parrot huddled at the top. The King has heard of a bird that speaks in Song Ge's voice and wants it caught, to stand at the foot of the cliffs and call 'Keep up, keep up' until the people above are lured down one by one. The parrot cowers at the treetop, every feather puffed out.
column3: 死路尽头的野坡上，一伙蛊王的吹箭手张着网，正围着一棵孤零零的老树往上爬，树梢上蹲着那只绿鹦鹉。蛊王听说有只鸟会学宋戈说话，要把它捉回去，让它站在崖下喊：「跟上，跟上」，好把崖上的人一个个骗下来。鹦鹉在树梢上缩成一团，羽毛都炸开了。

column2: The blowgunners chased off, the nets in shreds, the parrot lands on your cart shaft: A Cui. It cocks its head and thinks for a long while, then in Song Ge's gruff voice recites a message word by word, as if it has rehearsed it for ten years: 'Tell Yan Gong, leave the bricks alone. We'll send tea down every year, so feed the silkworm for us. The chief is up on the cliffs mending the road, and when it's through, we'll come down one by one and pay what we owe.' Then, in its own voice, it adds: 'Keep up.' And it flutters off toward the Gu King's village, looking back every few wingbeats.
column3: 吹箭手被打跑，网扯烂了。鹦鹉落到你们的车辕上，正是阿翠。它歪着头想了好一会儿，用宋戈那粗粗的嗓子，一字一句地说了一段话，像是背了十年：「告诉岩公，砖别动。茶年年送下来，蚕替我们喂着。镖头在崖上修路，等路修通，我们一个一个下来还。」说完，它又用自己的嗓子补了一句：「跟上。」然后扑棱棱飞起来，朝蛊王寨的方向去了，飞几下，回头看一眼。

column2: The Golden Silkworm Cave
column3: 金蚕洞

column2: The Gu King's village stands on the rim of a great sinkhole, and beneath it lies the Golden Silkworm Cave. A thousand gold threads reach out of it, most of them south, pulled straight. At the cave mouth sits the Gu King, wasted to a bundle of bones, and on his chest clings a golden silkworm the size of a thumb, so thin the light shows through it. Every thread is drawn from its body, and every one is wound about his. He lifts his eyelids. 'Ten years ago I tied their hearts, and they promised to come back each year and feed it. Ten years I've waited. The silkworm is hungry, and so am I.' Behind him guards, blowgunners and Gu riders rise rank on rank. 'Leave the brick. Leave the people.'
column3: 蛊王寨建在一个天坑边上，寨子底下就是金蚕洞。千百根金丝从洞里伸出去，大半往南，绷得笔直。洞口坐着蛊王，瘦得只剩一把骨头，胸口趴着一只拇指大的金蚕，薄得透光，丝全从它身上抽出来，也全缠在他身上。他抬起眼皮：「十年前我替他们拴了心，他们答应年年回来喂。我等了十年，蚕饿，我也饿。」他身后，寨丁、吹箭手、蛊骑一层层站起来：「把砖留下，把人留下。」

column2: The Gu King falls, and in the cave the golden silkworm is still crying faintly. A Kou steps forward ringing her silver bells, and the old mule walks into the cave with the new tea sent down from the cliffs. The leaves are scattered, the silkworm dives in and eats until it glows from end to end, and all the southward threads pull taut together, and every gold thread on every wrist in the seven villages loosens by a turn. The Gu King hears that the tea was sent down every single year, and says nothing for a long time.  Only one thread runs north, hanging slack, unbroken. You set the joined tea brick beneath it, and the thread stirs, very slightly. 'That's the empty one,' A Kou says. 'Still alive. Still on the road.' Of the threads running south, the thickest points straight at the plank roads on the southern cliffs. 'Chief Lu is up there,' says Lei Dajiao. 'Waiting for someone to come and mend the road.'
column3: 蛊王倒下了，洞里那只金蚕还在细细地叫。阿蔻摇着银铃上前，老骡子驮着崖上送下来的新茶走进洞。茶叶一撒，金蚕埋头就吃，吃得浑身发亮，往南的丝一齐绷紧，七寨手腕上的金丝都松了一圈。蛊王听说茶年年都送下来过，半天没出声。只有一根丝往北，松松地垂着，没有断。你们把合好的茶砖放在它底下，丝轻轻动了一下。阿蔻说：「是空着的那一个。还活着，还在路上。」往南最粗的一根，直直地指着悬崖上的栈道。「陆镖头在上头，」雷大脚说，「等人去修路。」

column2: The Cliff Galleries
column3: 悬崖栈道

column2: Gallery-Gaze Gap
column3: 望栈口

column2: South of the Gu villages the mountains stand straight up. Three ranges crowd together and a great river splits them, so far below that it looks like a white thread. Rows of wooden posts are driven into the cliff faces on both sides, carrying narrow plank galleries; some run on, some stop dead in mid-air. An iron chain is stretched across the road with a board hung on it: 'Closed by the Wantong Company. Turn back.' A band of gallery swordsmen sits behind it cracking melon seeds.
column3: 出了蛊寨往南，山一下子立了起来。三道山脉挤在一处，一条大江把山劈开，江面在几百丈底下，细得像一根白线；两边崖壁上一排排木桩钉进石头，架着窄窄的栈道，有的连着，有的断在半空。路口横着一道铁链，挂着木牌：「万通号封山，闲人回头」。一伙守栈刀手坐在链子后头嗑瓜子。

column2: The swordsmen scattered, the chain comes down. Lei Dajiao goes no further than this. He points at a speck on the far cliff. 'That's a man on the galleries. Ten years now, there every morning.' The speck moves and is gone. Beyond lie the Cliff Galleries.
column3: 刀手被打散，铁链摘了下来。雷大脚送到这里就不走了，指着对面崖上一个小黑点：「那是栈道上的人。十年了，每天早上都在那儿。」黑点动了动，不见了。往里，就是悬崖栈道。

column2: The Tea Bounty Board
column3: 寻茶榜

column2: On the open ground stands a wooden arch plastered with Wantong Company notices: 'Find where the Cliff-Top Snow Tea grows: three hundred taels reward.' Cliff crossbowmen camp beneath it, stopping and searching everyone and seizing any tea they find as 'stolen Wantong snow tea'. A pedlar's tea jar has been tipped out on the ground; he wails that it's only the coarse leaf he roasted himself.
column3: 野地上一座木牌楼，贴满了万通号的告示：「寻崖顶雪茶出处，告者赏银三百两」。牌楼底下扎着一伙崖上弩手，见人就拦下搜身，搜到茶叶就扣，说是「偷了万通号的雪茶」。一个货郎的茶罐被倒了一地，他哭丧着脸说，那是他自家炒的粗茶。

column2: The crossbowmen chased off, the pedlar gathers up his tea. Snow tea fetches its weight in gold, he says; every spring an old mule carried it down, and every year Wantong waylaid it. 'This year the mule never came,' he whispers. 'Wantong are frantic, combing the mountains for the tree it's picked from.'
column3: 弩手被打跑，货郎捡回了他的粗茶。他说崖顶雪茶一两换一两金，往年开春有头老骡子驮下山，万通号年年在半路截。「今年骡子没来，」他压低声音，「万通号急了，满山找茶是从哪棵树上摘的。」

column2: Cut-Rope Landing
column3: 断索口

column2: By the river stands an anchor stone the size of a millstone, three snapped bamboo ropes still wound round it, their ends clean-cut. A white-bearded old man squats beside it twisting new bamboo: Old Fan, whose family strung this rope crossing for three generations. Wantong swordsmen stand over him, and one kicks his bamboo strips into the river. 'The master says only Wantong rafts cross this river.'
column3: 江边野地上立着一块磨盘大的锚石，石上缠着三根断掉的篾索，断口齐刷刷的。一个白胡子老汉蹲在锚石边搓新篾，他叫范老索，这道溜索是他家三代人拉起来的。几个万通号的刀手围着他，一脚把篾条踢进了江里：「东家说了，这江上只许走万通号的排子。」

column2: With the swordsmen gone, Old Fan fishes his strips back out. Ten years ago, he says, he slid the Qianli men across one by one, two hundred and ninety-nine of them and their mules; a few days later the ropes were down. 'Not worn through,' he says, fingering the ends. 'Cut, from the far side. I mean to find out who.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，范老索把篾条捞了回来。他说十年前就是他把千里号的人一个个溜过江去，二百九十九个，外加骡马；过完没几天，索就断了。「不是磨断的，」他摸着断口，「是从对岸砍的。我倒要看看是谁。」

column2: Raft Beach
column3: 放排滩

column2: The river slows here, and a dozen bamboo rafts are tied along the beach: the Wantong ferry. One bolt of cloth a head to cross, three for a mule. Raft-boss Qian Bapai stands arms akimbo on the biggest raft, swordsmen and crossbowmen in two rows behind him and riders patrolling the bank. Villagers on the far side have been shouting across for days; those without cloth can only watch.
column3: 江水在这里缓了一缓，滩上拴着十几张竹排，是万通号的渡口。过一趟江，一个人收一匹布，一头骡收三匹。排头钱八排叉着腰站在最大的那张排上，身后刀手、弩手排成两排，岸上还有骑手来回巡。对岸的寨民隔着江喊了好几天，没钱的，只能干看着。

column2: Pinned to his raft, Qian Bapai swears the ropes weren't Wantong's doing. 'We only came the year after. They were already down; that's when the master thought of running rafts.' The rafts go to the villages on both banks, free for anyone. Old Fan narrows his eyes at the far shore for a long while.
column3: 钱八排被按在排上，赌咒发誓：索不是万通号砍的。「我们第二年才来，来的时候就断了，东家才想起摆排子挣钱。」竹排归了两岸的寨民，谁过江都不收钱。范老索听完，眯着眼往对岸看了半天。

column2: Listening-Clapper Slope
column3: 听梆坡

column2: On the slope lives a blind man who earns his keep 'listening' with a pair of wooden clappers: for the road, for the weather, for where lost things are. Mountain riders have led off the grey donkey that carries his gear, and now they circle him on horseback, rapping his clappers for fun. 'Listen, blind man: where's your donkey?' He tilts his head and says nothing.
column3: 坡上有个瞎子，靠一副梆子替人「听」：听路、听天、听丢了的东西在哪。他那头驮梆子的灰驴被一伙山马骑牵走了，骑手们骑着马围着他转圈，敲着他的梆子取乐：「瞎子，你听听，你的驴在哪？」瞎子侧着耳朵，一声不吭。

column2: The riders driven off, the donkey is led home. Stroking its ears, the blind man recalls a night ten years ago when he slept by the river: nine axe blows, each harder than the last; then a gruff voice: 'Sorry, Old Fan.' Last, iron knocking on stone. 'Like a man with an iron box on his back, turning and walking off.'
column3: 骑手被打跑，驴牵了回来。瞎子摸着驴耳朵，说起十年前那夜他就睡在江边：先是九声斧头响，一声比一声狠；然后一个粗嗓子说：「老范，对不住。」最后是铁器磕石头的声音，「像有人背着个铁箱子，转身走了。」

column2: Salt-Rack Terrace
column3: 晒盐坝

column2: Tier upon tier of wooden racks climb the slope, spread with clay boards for drying salt; brine is carried up from a salt spring at the foot of the hill, dried and scraped off as red salt. Rowdy soldiers have driven Sister Zhuoga, who runs the racks, down off them and seized the boards: one chicken for a catty of salt. Crossbowmen perch on top and loose an arrow at the feet of anyone who comes near.
column3: 野地坡上一层层木架子，架上铺着晒盐的泥板，卤水从山脚的卤泉挑上来，晒干刮下来就是红盐。管盐的卓嘎阿姐被一伙兵痞赶下了架子，兵痞把盐板占了，一斤盐要换一只鸡。弩手坐在架子顶上，谁靠近就往谁脚边射一箭。

column2: The soldiers chased off the racks, Zhuoga climbs back up to scrape salt. For ten years, she says, an old mule came by alone each spring and licked salt under her racks for a while. 'When it had had enough it went on by itself, a bundle of tea on its back. Smelt wonderful.'
column3: 兵痞被赶下了架子，卓嘎重新上架刮盐。她说十年来每年开春，都有头老骡子独自路过，在她的盐架底下舔一会儿盐：「舔够了自己就走，背上一包茶，香得很。」

column2: From the soldiers' hoard: forty catties of red salt, twelve strips of cured pork, a jar of barley wine, and a bag of silver scraps taken off travellers, which Zhuoga hands back to their owners one by one.
column3: 抄出兵痞囤的红盐四十斤、腊肉十二条、一坛青稞酒，还有一袋他们从路人身上搜来的碎银，卓嘎把银子一份份退给了原主。

column2: Every time you pass, Zhuoga is waiting by the road to tuck two cakes of red salt into your packs. 'This one's for the mules to lick, that one's for you. Don't mix them up.'
column3: 每回路过，卓嘎都在路边等着，往你们的驮袋里塞两块红盐：「这块给骡子舔，那块给人吃，别弄混了。」

column2: Pilot-Line Bluff
column3: 引线崖

column2: The river is narrowest here, the two clifftops only a few dozen yards apart. Old Fan's granddaughter Xiaomie, twelve years old, carries a bow taller than she is, a fine hemp thread tied to the arrow: shoot a thread across, the thread pulls a cord, the cord pulls the rope. That's how the old folk always did it. She has barely drawn when Wantong riders come charging to snatch the bow. 'No ropes across this river!'
column3: 江在这里最窄，两岸崖头相隔不过几十丈。范老索的孙女小篾十二岁，背着一张比她还高的弓，箭尾拴着一根细麻线：先射过去一根线，线拉绳，绳拉索，老辈人都是这么接的。她刚拉开弓，一伙万通号的山马骑就冲了过来，要抢她的弓：「这江不许接索！」

column2: The riders driven off, Xiaomie's arrow flies across and the thread catches fast on the old anchor post opposite. Old Fan shades his eyes and his hand starts to shake: a black triangular pennant flies on that post, marked with the character Lu. 'Chief Lu?' the old man murmurs. 'He paid me double fare, back then.'
column3: 骑手被赶走，小篾一箭射过江去，线稳稳挂在对岸的老锚桩上。范老索手搭凉棚一看，手抖了：对岸锚桩上插着一面黑三角旗，旗上一个「陆」字。「陆镖头？」老汉喃喃，「当年他给的过江钱，是双份的。」

column2: Salvage Bend
column3: 捞江湾

column2: The river bends here, and whatever comes down from upstream fetches up in the bend. A crew of salvagers pole about on rafts swinging long hooks: timber, dead beasts, bundles, all theirs once hooked, and anyone who claims a thing pays ransom. Their haul hangs drying on the bank, and in the middle of it a brass mule bell engraved with two characters: Qianli. Seeing you eye the bell, their headman swings his hook across your path.
column3: 江水在这儿打个弯，上游冲下来的东西都搁在湾里。一帮捞江客撑着排、甩着长钩，木头、死畜、包袱，捞着了就是他们的，谁来认都要交赎钱。湾边晾着一排捞上来的东西，当中挂着一只铜骡铃，铃上刻着「千里」两个字。捞江客的头儿见你们盯着铃，把钩子一横。

column2: The salvagers scattered, the bell comes down. Their headman says they hooked it that winter ten years ago: on the night of the earthquake a mule fell from a gallery upstream, pack and all, into the river. 'Never got the pack. It went on down, towards the Whirlpool.' Shake the bell and it still rings clear.
column3: 捞江客被打散，铜铃取了下来。头儿说这铃是十年前那个冬天捞的：地动那夜，上游栈道上掉下来一头骡子，连骡带驮子摔进江里。「驮子没捞着，冲下去了，往回水沱那边去了。」铃一摇，还是脆的。

column2: The Tasting Hut
column3: 品茶寮

column2: A thatched hut on the open ground bears the sign 'Wantong Company Tea Inspection'. Inside, chained by the ankle, sits a thin scholar called Zhou One-Tongue: one touch on his tongue and he can tell which mountain, which slope a tea grew on. Wantong want him to taste out where the snow tea comes from, and the swordsmen on guard say no answer, no dinner.
column3: 野地里一座茅寮，门口挂着「万通号验茶处」的牌子，里面关着个瘦先生，人称周一舌：舌头一沾，就说得出茶长在哪座山、哪面坡。万通号拿铁链拴着他的脚，逼他把这几年截下的雪茶尝出来历，守寮的刀手说，尝不出来，不给饭吃。

column2: The swordsmen gone and his chain off, Zhou gulps a bowl of cold water to rinse his mouth. Nine years he's tasted snow tea, he says, and found out only two things: it grows high, with cloud sitting on it at noon; and at the bottom of the cup there's a taste at the root of the tongue 'like river stones'. 'What river is there on a mountaintop?' He can't work it out either.
column3: 刀手被打跑，周一舌解了链子，先灌了一碗凉水漱口。他说雪茶他尝了九年，只尝出两样：一是长得高，晌午有云压着；二是喝到底，舌根上有一股「河里石头的味儿」。「山顶上哪来的河？」他自己也想不通。

column2: Rope-Bamboo Flat
column3: 篾竹坪

column2: At the edge of the open ground grows a stand of bitter bamboo, straight and long-jointed, the best stuff for rope. Old Pu the rope-maker and his wife have lived beside it all their lives, but this week they've been at each other's throats: a local bully's men have roped off the grove and say every cane costs a coin. Pu wants to cut anyway, his wife is afraid and holds him back, and the bully's men stand by laughing.
column3: 野地边一片苦竹林，竹子直、节长，是搓篾索的好料。老篾匠蒲公和老伴在林边住了一辈子，这几天却吵得掀了锅：一伙寨霸的家丁拿绳子把竹林圈了，说竹子是他们东家的，砍一根交一钱。蒲公要砍，老伴怕事拦着，家丁在一边看笑话。

column2: The bully's men gone, cut all you like. Splitting cane, Old Pu says that ten years ago a dark-faced giant asked him the quickest way to cut a bamboo rope. 'I said slant the blade: three strokes a rope.' He stops. 'The man thanked me and gave me a tea brick.' His wife chips in: 'We still haven't had the heart to drink it.'
column3: 家丁被赶走，竹子随便砍。蒲公一边破篾一边说，十年前一个黑脸大汉来问过他，篾索最快怎么断。「我说斜着砍，一根三刀。」老汉停了手，「那人谢了我，给了一块茶砖。」老伴插嘴：「那砖我们到今天也没舍得喝。」

column2: The Whirlpool
column3: 回水沱

column2: The river slams into a great rock and spins into a whirlpool behind it, where anything washed down circles for days and nights. Gold panners hold the sandbar beside it, sieving for grains and keeping everyone else away. A line of seedlings grows on the sand, glossy green and startling among the bare stones, and the panners are hoeing them out because they're in the way.
column3: 江水撞上一块大石，在石后转成一个大旋涡，上游冲下来的东西都要在这里转上几天几夜。一伙淘金客占着沱边的沙滩，筛沙找金粒，不许外人靠近。沙滩上长着一溜小树苗，叶子油绿，在一片乱石里格外显眼；淘金客嫌碍事，正拿锄头刨。

column2: The panners chased off, you crouch to look at the seedlings: tea. The panners say they come up out of the whirlpool every spring. 'There's a whole grove on a bar downstream, dropping seed every year. No idea who planted it.' Half a rotten pack strap lies buried in the sand, branded with the character Qian.
column3: 淘金客被打跑，你们蹲下来细看那些树苗：是茶苗。淘金客说这些苗每年春天都从沱里冒出来，「下游滩上长了一大片，年年往这里掉种子，不知道谁种的。」沙里还埋着半截烂驮带，烙着一个「千」字。

column2: The Cook's Shed
column3: 灶头棚

column2: A bamboo shed by the river, a great iron wok on the stove. Old Peng who cooks here was the Qianli caravan's cook; he turned his ankle as they went up the mountain and stayed by the river to open this place. Wantong swordsmen have taken it over: Peng may cook for them alone, and anyone else who eats a mouthful gets the wok smashed. A few hungry porters squat outside, sniffing.
column3: 江边一座竹棚，灶上一口大铁锅。掌勺的老彭当年是千里号马帮的伙夫，队伍上山时他扭了脚，留在江边开了这个棚子。万通号的刀手把棚子包了，老彭只许给他们做饭，别人来吃一口就砸锅。几个过路的背夫饿着肚子，蹲在棚外闻味儿。

column2: With the swordsmen gone, Old Peng relights the fire: food for everyone, and he'll trade for anything. Slicing pork, he says that on the night of the crossing Chief Lu came to the shed and borrowed his woodcutting axe. 'Said he'd bring it straight back.' He taps the board with the back of his cleaver. 'Ten years. No axe, and no Lu.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，老彭重新生火，饭菜管够，什么货都肯换。他边切腊肉边说，过江那夜陆镖头来棚里，借走了他劈柴的斧头。「说用一下就还，」他拿刀背敲敲案板，「十年了，斧头没还，人也没下来。」

column2: Snow Leopard Crag
column3: 雪豹岩

column2: Each winter a flock of blue sheep comes down this jumbled crag to graze, and three or four snow leopards follow them, grey-white coats flat against the rock and the same colour as it. The sheep track is the very path the old mule walked every year; salt carriers and drovers who come this way get pounced on without warning. A few hunters wait below, none of them willing to go up.
column3: 山脚的乱石崖上，冬天一群岩羊从高处下来找草，跟在后头的是三四只雪豹，灰白的毛趴在石头上，跟石头一个颜色。羊群踩出的小路，正是老骡子年年走的那条，背盐的、赶脚的走到这里，冷不丁就被扑一回。几个猎户守在崖下，谁也不敢往上走。

column2: The leopards are driven back up. But the blue sheep come down every winter and the leopards follow them, so they'll be back before long; all anyone can do is clear them out each year. A hunter prises open the mouth of a dead sheep: it's full of tea leaves. 'This flock came down from somewhere tea trees grow.'
column3: 雪豹被赶回了高处。可岩羊每年冬天都要下来，雪豹跟着羊走，过一阵还会再来，只能年年来清一回。猎户掰开一只被咬死的岩羊的嘴：满嘴都是茶叶。「这群羊，是从有茶树的地方下来的。」

column2: The Tung-Oil Press
column3: 桐油榨

column2: A press by the river makes tung oil: bamboo rope has to be soaked in it to stand up to the river mist. Deserters have taken the press over. They can't press oil, so they pour the finished barrels into the river for fun, calling it 'an offering to the river god'. The owner, who can't speak, tugs at your sleeve and points indoors: there's something he wants you to see.
column3: 江边一座油坊，榨的是桐油：篾索得拿桐油泡过，才经得住江上的雾。油坊被一伙逃兵占了，他们不会榨油，就把榨好的油一桶桶往江里倒着玩，说是「给河神上供」。油坊主人是个哑巴，拉着你们的袖子往屋里指，比划着要你们看样东西。

column2: The deserters gone, three barrels of oil are left. From a crack in the wall the mute owner digs out a receipt ten years old: 'Tung oil, ten catties, for the locks, against rust. Lu Jiu.' Below is a handprint a size bigger than yours. Old Fan says, 'The river mist rusts iron solid in a single winter. He was afraid the box wouldn't open.'
column3: 逃兵被打跑，桐油剩下三桶。哑巴从墙缝里抠出一张十年前的买油单：「桐油十斤，擦锁用，免锈。陆九。」底下一个手印，比你们的大一圈。范老索说：「江上雾重，铁的一个冬天就锈死。他是怕匣子打不开。」

column2: The Tea-Hound Kennels
column3: 闻香犬舍

column2: At the foot of the mountain stand kennels where Wantong keep twenty-odd lean hounds raised on snow-tea dregs to sniff out tea. Mountain riders run them over the hills, and wherever the dogs bark, they set the slope alight to smoke the tea trees out. A whole hillside is already black, and a few farmhouses burned with it.
column3: 山脚下一座犬舍，万通号在这里养了二十几条细犬，拿雪茶的茶渣喂大，专门闻茶味。管犬的是一伙山马骑，牵着狗满山转，狗朝哪儿叫，他们就往哪儿放火烧山，想把茶树逼出来。山脚已经烧黑了一片，几户山民的房子也跟着烧了。

column2: The riders scattered, the hounds are masterless and wag round your legs. But all twenty-odd bark in the same direction: across the river, upstream. The hill folk say there have been three fires, and every time the dogs barked that way. 'Wantong can't get across, so they just burn this side.'
column3: 骑手被打散，细犬没人管了，摇着尾巴围着你们转。可二十几条狗齐刷刷朝着同一个方向叫：江对岸，上游。山民说火烧了三回，每回狗都冲那边叫，「万通号过不去江，就只会在这边烧。」

column2: Tea-Sprung Bar
column3: 茶生滩

column2: Down past the Whirlpool, at a dead end, a sandbar by the river is covered in tea trees taller than a man, so thick their branches lock together, startlingly green in the bare gorge. Wantong swordsmen are digging them up, one tree to a basket, to sell outside the mountains as 'snow tea trees'. Under the oldest tree lies a leather pannier, half rotted away.
column3: 顺着回水沱往下走到死路尽头，江边一片沙洲上长着一大片茶树，一人多高，枝叶挤得密密实实，在光秃秃的峡谷里绿得扎眼。一伙万通号的刀手正拿锄头挖树，挖出一棵装一筐，要运出山去当「雪茶树」卖。最老的那棵树底下，压着一个烂了半边的皮驮子。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the trees go back in the ground. You open the pannier: packets of tea seed that sprouted long ago and rotted to mud, and a wooden tag, the ink washed pale but readable: 'Seed of the Tea King Tree. Half to plant on the cliff, half to keep.' The mule that fell on the night of the earthquake was carrying the tea seed the Qianli men brought from the fog country; it washed up on this bar and grew into a grove by itself. The other half was planted on the cliff, and that's where snow tea comes from. Zhou One-Tongue chews a leaf. 'Same mother.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，挖出来的树又栽了回去。你们扒开那个皮驮子：一包包茶籽早就发了芽、烂成了泥，还有一块木牌，墨迹泡得发白，还认得出：「茶王树籽。一半栽崖上，一半留种。」地动那夜掉下江的骡子，驮的是千里号从雾驿带来的茶种，冲到这片沙洲上，自己长成了林子。另一半，栽到了崖上：雪茶就是从那里来的。周一舌揪片叶子嚼了嚼：「一个娘生的。」

column2: Night-Crossing Hollow
column3: 夜渡坳

column2: From the mouth of the hollow a goat track runs down to the river, and by night smugglers cross from here on sheepskin rafts, carrying opium and black-market salt. They sleep in the hollow by day and attack any stranger. Their boss grumbles that the escort guards on the far bank shoot every time: 'Ten years, and not one raft has made it over.'
column3: 山脚的坳口有条羊肠小路通到江边，夜里走私客从这里扎羊皮筏偷渡，背的是烟土和私盐。他们白天在坳里睡觉，见了生人就打。走私客头子骂骂咧咧：对岸的镖师每回都放箭，「十年了，一个筏子都没过去过。」

column2: The smugglers chased off, you pick up one of their rafts: not a hole in the skins, but every lashing cut clean, half an arrow still stuck in one. 'Those guards are uncanny,' the boss mutters. 'Never shoot a man, only the ropes.' Old Fan nods. 'Won't let anyone cross, and won't hurt anyone either.'
column3: 走私客被打跑。你们拎起他们的羊皮筏：皮子一个窟窿也没有，绑筏子的绳子却断得整整齐齐，断口上还插着半截箭。头子嘟囔：「那帮镖师邪门，从不射人，专射绳子。」范老索点点头：「不让人过江，又不伤人。」

column2: Shouting Narrows
column3: 喊江口

column2: The river squeezes to a slit here, the cliffs almost touching; shout and the far side hears you. The chieftain's tax men have set up a table at the brink with a sign: 'Ten coppers a shout.' Old Fan empties his purse and has enough for three, and the tax men say his voice is too loud and want more.
column3: 江在这里窄得只剩一条缝，两岸崖壁几乎碰头，扯开嗓子对面就听得见。土司的税丁在崖口摆了张桌子，挂出一块牌子：「喊话一句，铜钱十文」。范老索掏光了钱袋，只够喊三句，税丁还嫌他嗓门大，要加钱。

column2: The tax men gone, Old Fan bellows across: 'Who cut my ropes?' After a long pause a young voice comes back through the mist: 'Grandad, no use joining them! The road up top is broken!' He shouts again and no one answers. Fan stands stunned. 'Broken?'
column3: 税丁被赶走，范老索扯着嗓子朝对岸喊：「谁砍的我的索？」半晌，对岸的雾里传回一个年轻的声音：「老人家，接上也没用，上头的路是断的！」再喊，就没人应了。范老索愣了好一会儿：「断的？」

column2: Three Locks Shop
column3: 三锁铺

column2: A little shop on the open ground has three big brass locks hung out for a sign; its owner, Three-Locks Zhang, is the best locksmith for miles. Wantong men have him tied up inside, a drawing spread on the table: an iron casket with three locks. They want keys made to match. 'Make them and the snow tea's ours.' Zhang won't, and a blade is already resting on his finger.
column3: 野地上一个小铺子，门口挂着三把大铜锁当招牌，铺主三锁张是这一带最好的锁匠。万通号的人把他捆在铺子里，桌上摊着一张画：一只铁匣，三道锁。他们要他照着画配钥匙：「配出来，雪茶就有了。」三锁张死不肯，刀已经架在了他的手指上。

column2: With the Wantong men gone, Zhang rubs his hands and says he made those three locks: a dark-faced escort chief ordered them overnight ten years ago, and wanted only two keys. 'The third lock has no keyhole. I asked how it opens, and he said it needs no key; it'll open when it's time.' He shakes his head. 'Forty years a locksmith, and I never saw a lock like it.'
column3: 万通号的人被打跑，三锁张揉着手说，那三道锁是他打的：十年前一个黑脸镖头连夜来订，只要两把钥匙。「第三道锁没有锁眼。我问他怎么开，他说用不着钥匙，到时候自然开。」他摇头，「干了四十年锁匠，没见过这种锁。」

column2: The Fake Tea Works
column3: 假茶坊

column2: A row of tea-roasting stoves smokes at the foot of the hill: the Wantong tea works. With no snow tea coming, they mix lowland coarse tea with lime powder, roast it pale, and pack it in bamboo tubes carved 'Cliff-Top Snow Tea' to sell for its weight in gold all the same. Swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders guard it tight, and the roasters are hill folk taken by force.
column3: 山脚下一溜焙茶灶，烟熏火燎，是万通号的茶坊。雪茶断了货，他们就拿山下的粗茶掺上石灰粉，焙得发白，装进刻着「崖顶雪茶」的竹筒，一筒照样卖一两金。坊里刀手、弩手、骑手守得严严实实，焙茶的伙计都是抓来的山民。

column2: You wreck the works and the hill folk go home. An old roaster says real snow tea has white down on the backs of the leaves and brews golden. 'Lime only fools city folk.' He adds that every year the old mule's tea came with a slip of paper tucked in, 'and every year the master tore it up and burned it, so nobody could read it.'
column3: 茶坊被你们砸了，抓来的山民放回了家。一个老伙计说，真雪茶叶背有一层白毫，泡开是金黄色，「掺石灰只骗得了城里人」。他还说，往年老骡子的茶包里总夹一张字条，「东家每回都撕了烧，不许人看。」

column2: Mid-River Slider
column3: 半江梆

column2: One leftover length of old rope still hangs from the far bank over the water, and on it dangles a wooden slider, the one Old Fan sent people across on, which nobody has been able to reach for ten years. River bandits sit on the bank using it for a target, a drink for every hit. It hurts Fan to watch. 'That was my father's.'
column3: 一根断剩的老篾索还从对岸垂下来，悬在江面上，索上挂着一只木溜梆，是范老索当年溜人用的，十年没人取得下来。一伙江匪拿它当靶子，坐在岸边比赛射箭，谁射中谁喝酒。范老索看着心疼：「那是我爹传下来的。」

column2: The bandits gone, Xiaomie hooks the slider back with a long bamboo pole. It's covered in little notches, one cut by Old Fan for every person he sent across: two hundred and ninety-nine. Next to the last, someone has added with a knife point: 'All across. Thank you, Old Fan.'
column3: 江匪被打跑，小篾拿长竹竿把溜梆勾了回来。木梆上刻满了小道道，是范老索当年溜一个人刻一道：二百九十九道。最后一道旁边，有人拿刀尖添了几个字：「都过去了。谢老范。」

column2: The Rope Store
column3: 麻绳仓

column2: A big storehouse on the open ground hangs Wantong lanterns at its door, and inside, hemp rope, rawhide rope and bamboo rope are stacked to the rafters. Any village wanting so much as a cord to tie firewood has to come and beg the storekeeper, a silver coin a length. The swordsmen on guard say the master's orders are clear: rope is sold, never lent, and nothing longer than ten fathoms is sold at all.
column3: 野地里一座大仓，门口挂着万通号的灯笼，仓里堆的全是麻绳、牛皮绳、篾索，一捆捆码到房梁。附近寨子要买根捆柴的绳子，都得来这里求管仓，一根一钱银子。守仓的刀手说：东家有令，绳子只卖不借，长过十丈的，一根也不卖。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the rope stands in mountains. The first page of the storekeeper's ledger reads: 'The year after the earthquake, buy up all rope for a hundred miles. Master's orders: so no one climbs the cliffs.' Old Fan picks the strongest coils and gives the rest to the villages. 'They were afraid of people going up,' he says. 'So are those fellows over the river.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，仓里的绳子堆成了山。管仓的账本第一页写着：「地动次年，尽收方圆百里之绳。东家谕：免得有人上崖。」范老索挑了几捆最结实的，剩下的分给了寨子。「他们怕人上去，」老汉说，「对岸那帮人也怕。」

column2: Chain Bridge Market
column3: 铁索桥市

column2: Two stone piers stand on the open ground where a chain bridge once hung; it fell in the earthquake year and only the piers are left. Beneath them was an iron market where smiths forged horseshoes, gallery spikes and chain, until Wantong bought up all the iron, the forges shut one by one, and the fires went cold for ten years. Wantong swordsmen and crossbowmen guard the last iron store, the lock on its door bigger than the door.
column3: 野地上两座石墩，从前架着一座铁索桥，地动那年桥塌了，只剩墩子。墩下原是个铁市，铁匠们在这里打马掌、打栈钉、打铁链，后来万通号把铁全收了，铁匠铺一家家关门，炉子凉了十年。万通号的刀手和弩手守着最后一座铁库，库门上的锁比门还大。

column2: The iron store opens and the iron comes out by the basketful; the smiths relight their forges and the hammering goes on till dark. The iron market reopens: gold for iron, as much as you like. The old master smith forges Old Fan a new set of slider hooks and says as he works that on the day the Qianli caravan left, Chief Lu bought three hundred gallery spikes from him, 'picked them out one by one, the longest ones'. He looks up at the far cliff. 'A man who buys spikes means to mend a road.'
column3: 铁库打开，铁一筐筐抬了出来，铁匠们重新生起炉子，叮叮当当一直响到天黑。铁市重开，金子换铁，有多少换多少。老铁匠头给范老索打了一副新溜钩，边打边说：十年前千里号走的那天，陆镖头在他这儿买走了三百根栈钉，「一根根地挑，专挑最长的。」他抬头看看对面的崖：「买钉子，是要修路的。」

column2: River-Bar Camp
column3: 拦江营

column2: A great camp on the open ground flies the word 'Wantong' over its gate: the company's den at the mouth of the gorge. Hearing someone is restringing the rope crossing, the master's third brother, Wan the Third, has come in person, and gallery swordsmen, cliff crossbowmen and mountain riders stand in three ranks. 'Nine years the Wan family has done business on this river, and you think you can just string a rope across?'
column3: 野地上一座大营，营门挂着「万通」两个大字，是万通号在峡口的老窝。听说有人在接溜索，东家的三弟万老三亲自来了，守栈刀手、崖上弩手、山马骑摆开了三路：「这条江上的买卖，我们万家做了九年，你们说接就接？」

column2: Pinned to the ground, Wan the Third tells the truth: before the earthquake, Wantong tried to follow the Qianli caravan up the cliffs to rob them, and Chief Lu's guards turned them back; a few days later the ropes were cut. 'We thought he wanted it all for himself,' he says with a wry smile. 'Only later did we hear most of the cliff road had fallen.'
column3: 万老三被按在地上，吐了实话：地动前，万通号想跟着千里号上崖抢货，被陆镖头的镖师拦了回来；没过几天，索就断了。「我们以为他是想独吞，」他苦笑，「后来才知道，崖上的路塌了一大半。」

column2: The Snow Tea Vault
column3: 雪茶库

column2: At a dead end stands a stone storehouse with three doors, guarded by Wantong's best men: a troop each of swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders. Inside is nine years of waylaid snow tea, never all sold, held back for the price to rise; old Master Wan used to come every year to count it and weigh every bundle himself.
column3: 死路尽头一座石砌的库房，三道门，门口站着万通号最好的一伙护院，刀手、弩手、骑手各一队。库里是九年来截下的雪茶，一包也没舍得卖完，压着等涨价；万东家从前每年来清点一回，一包一包亲手过秤。

column2: The guards scattered, the doors open: nine bundles of snow tea, one a year, each with its slip of paper. The storekeeper couldn't bring himself to burn them and kept them in secret. All in one big, heavy hand, a line a year: 'Tea is good. All are well.' 'Tea is good. All are well.' The ninth adds: 'The road is mended as far as the fifth break.'
column3: 护院被打散，库门开了：九包雪茶，一年一包，包上系着字条：管库的没舍得烧，偷偷留了下来。字是一个人写的，粗手大笔，一年一句：「茶好，人都好。」「茶好，人都好。」……第九张多了一句：「路修到第五处了。」

column2: Mule Ford
column3: 骡蹚滩

column2: A shallow ford, the water no deeper than a horse's belly. A duck girl called A Duo lives beside it, and she says that every spring the old mule came out of a side valley on the far bank and waded across here. Wantong laid ambushes by the ford, and every year A Duo crept out at night to warn the mule; this year they caught her and tied her up by the duck shed, and their swordsmen are feasting on her ducks.
column3: 江边一处浅滩，水只到马肚子。滩边住着放鸭的小姑娘阿朵，她说每年开春，那头老骡子都从对岸一条山沟里出来，在这里蹚水过江。万通号在滩边埋了伏，阿朵年年夜里偷偷去给骡子报信，今年被抓住了，绑在鸭棚边，几个刀手正拿她的鸭子开荤。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, half the ducks are left. Wiping her eyes, A Duo says the mule didn't come this year; she waited a month. She points to the side valley across the river: three terraces in it, each higher than the last. 'It always came down from the top one, smelling of tea.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，鸭子剩了一半。阿朵抹着眼泪说，骡子今年没来，她等了一个月。她指着对岸那条山沟：沟里三层台子，一层比一层高，「骡子是从最上面那层下来的，一身茶味。」

column2: The Tea Contest Stage
column3: 斗茶台

column2: On a tea-contest stage by the river, Wantong's master taster has set out his things and announces to the crowd that he has tasted out where snow tea grows: the great snow peaks to the west, and he'll lead a party to dig it up in a few days. Seeing Zhou One-Tongue, he sneers. 'Nine years on a chain and your tongue hasn't rotted?' His bruisers shove Zhou away from the stage.
column3: 江边一座斗茶台，万通号的大茶师在台上摆开了架势，当众宣布：雪茶的出处他已经尝出来了，在西边的大雪山，过几天就带人去挖。他看见周一舌，冷笑一声：「被拴了九年的人，舌头还没烂？」台下的打手把周一舌往外推。

column2: The bruisers thrown off, Zhou sits blindfold on the stage and names the source of ten cups one by one without a slip; the master taster tries three and gets two wrong, red to the ears. Then Zhou sips spring water fetched from the terraced valley across the river and smacks his lips. 'This is the water snow tea grew on. Not the west: over there.' The master taster takes off his taster's badge on the spot.
column3: 打手被赶下台，周一舌蒙着眼坐上斗茶台，十碗茶一碗碗报出产地，碗碗不差；大茶师喝了三碗，错了两碗，脸涨得通红。周一舌又尝了一口对岸三层台沟里打来的山泉，咂咂嘴：「雪茶就是这口水浇大的。不在西边，在对岸。」大茶师摘了自己的茶师牌子。

column2: The Winch House
column3: 绞盘屋

column2: In a stone house at the foot of the mountain stands a great wooden winch; it was what tensioned the rope crossing, a few men pushing it round until the rope sang like a lute string. Rowdy soldiers have turned the house into a gambling den, sawn off the winch bars for stools, and filled the place with the reek of wine; the old winchman has been driven out to a straw shelter.
column3: 山脚下一座石屋，屋里一架大木绞盘，当年绷溜索全靠它，几个人推着一转，索就绷得像琴弦。一伙兵痞把石屋占了当赌场，绞盘的推杆被锯下来当了板凳，屋里屋外都是酒气，管绞盘的老伙计被赶到屋外搭了个草窝。

column2: The soldiers thrown out, the bars go back in and the winch creaks round again. The old winchman pats it: ten years ago it held the rope taut while two hundred and ninety-nine people crossed, one by one. Old Fan ties on his new rope. 'This time it's your turn.'
column3: 兵痞被赶了出去，推杆重新装上，绞盘又咯吱咯吱转了起来。老伙计摸着它说，十年前也是它绷着索，把二百九十九个人一个个送过去的。范老索把新搓的篾索系上：「这回，换它送你们。」

column2: The soldiers' stakes are confiscated: three sets of dice, two strings of coppers, five links of sausage, an iron pot, and a jar of tung oil stolen from the press, just right for soaking the new rope.
column3: 抄出兵痞的赌本：骰子三副、铜钱两串、腊肠五挂、一口铁锅，还有一坛从桐油坊偷来的桐油，正好拿去泡新索。

column2: Every time you pass, the old winchman pushes the winch round once so you can hear it creak, then fetches a basket of baked buckwheat cakes from his shelter. 'Winch men get hungry fast. Fighting men get hungrier.'
column3: 每回路过，老伙计都推一圈绞盘给你们听个响，再从草窝里拎出一篮烤荞饼：「推绞盘的饿得快，你们打仗的更饿。」

column2: Three-Step Valley Mouth
column3: 三叠沟口

column2: Where the open ground ends lies the mouth of Three-Step Valley, its three terraces rising one above another. A Wantong survey party camps at the mouth with dozens of long ladders and a Yi shepherd they've seized as a guide, ordering him to lead them to the third step. He says it can't be climbed and gets a lash for it; swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders seal the valley mouth tight.
column3: 野地尽头就是三叠沟的沟口，沟里三层台子一层比一层高。万通号的勘山队扎在沟口，扛着几十架长梯，抓来一个彝家的放羊人当向导，逼他带路上第三层。放羊人说上不去，挨了一鞭子；刀手、弩手、骑手把沟口堵得严严实实。

column2: The survey party scattered, ladders strewn everywhere. Rubbing his shoulder, the shepherd says he has never been up the third step himself; only blue sheep can climb it, 'and when they come down in winter their mouths smell of tea'. Ten years ago, he adds, a band of Han men climbed up with baskets of earth on their backs, all spring long.
column3: 勘山队被打散，长梯扔了一地。放羊人揉着肩膀说，第三层他也没上去过，只有岩羊上得去，「岩羊冬天下来，嘴里一股茶味」。他又说，十年前有一伙汉人背着土筐往上爬，爬了整整一个春天。

column2: The Pigeon Tower
column3: 信鸽楼

column2: A tall wooden tower stands on the open ground, a hundred pigeons cooing on its roof: the Wantong pigeon loft, carrying every message into and out of the mountains. Its crossbowmen shoot any pigeon in the sky that isn't theirs, and a troop of swordsmen guards the foot. As you approach, a bird flaps off with a note on its leg: someone is asking about snow tea.
column3: 野地里一座高木楼，楼顶上咕咕叫着上百只鸽子，是万通号的信鸽楼，山里山外的消息全靠它们传。守楼的弩手见天上有不是自家的鸽子就射，楼下还守着一队刀手。你们刚靠近，一只鸽子扑棱棱飞出去，腿上绑着信：有人在打听雪茶。

column2: The tower's guards scattered, you turn out a heap of message tubes. The newest is in Wan the Third's own hand: 'If the snow tea can't be found, burn Three-Step Valley. Then no one has it.' Zhou One-Tongue goes white. 'Ten years of tea trees, gone in one fire.'
column3: 守楼的被打散，信筒翻出一大摞。最新的一封是万老三的亲笔：「雪茶出处若寻不着，便放火烧了三叠沟，谁也别想要。」周一舌看完，脸都白了：「十年的茶树，一把火就没了。」

column2: Cave Camp
column3: 岩洞营

column2: A great cave opens in the cliff at the mountain's foot, its mouth smoked black: an old resting camp for gallery travellers. On the wall is a charcoal drawing: a box with one lock on it, two hundred and ninety-nine neat strokes beside it, and under them an arrow pointing up the mountain. Deserters have taken the cave and are about to scrub the drawing off with a wet rag to draw a dice board.
column3: 山脚崖壁上一个大岩洞，洞口熏得漆黑，是走栈道的人歇脚的老营。洞壁上有一幅炭画：一只箱子，箱上一把锁，旁边整整齐齐画着二百九十九道杠，杠下一个箭头指着上山。几个逃兵占了岩洞，正拿湿布要把炭画擦掉，好在墙上画个骰子盘。

column2: The deserters driven out, most of the drawing is saved. By torchlight you study it: the box is drawn with care, a keyhole on the lock. Beneath the strokes, small writing: 'One night here. All present.' The arrow points the way the galleries climb. Deeper in, the walls bear one smoke-mark after another.
column3: 逃兵被赶走，炭画保住了一大半。你们举着火把细看：箱子画得很认真，锁上还画了钥匙眼。杠子底下一行小字：「宿此一夜，人齐。」箭头指的，正是栈道往上的方向。洞壁深处，还有一处处烟熏的痕迹。

column2: Cliff Toll Barrier
column3: 崖税卡

column2: Where the open ground meets the galleries, the chieftain's household has built a wooden barrier with a sign reading 'Cliff Tax': a coin a head to go up, double for mules, and again to come down. Tax men, archers and mounted troops hold it in three bands and call it the chieftain's law. The galleries have been down for ten years and no one who went up has come down, but they collect all the same.
column3: 野地通往栈道的路口，土司家修了一道木卡，挂着「崖税」的牌子：上栈道一人一钱，骡马加倍，下来再收一回。税丁、弓手、马兵三路守着，说是土司老爷的规矩。可栈道塌了十年，上去的人一个也没下来，他们照收不误。

column2: The tax men scattered, their ledger turns up. The page from ten years ago reads: 'Winter of the Dingwei year: two hundred and ninety-nine passed up the cliffs, persons and goods all in order.' The next line is scrawled: 'Earthquake in the twelfth month. Galleries broken in seven places. None who went up has returned.' Every page since then records only money taken, and not a single traveller.
column3: 税丁被打散，税簿翻了出来。十年前那一页写着：「丁未年冬，过崖者二百九十九人，人货俱清。」下一行字迹潦草：「腊月地动，栈断七处，上者未归。」从那以后每一页都只有收钱，没有一个过崖的人。

column2: The River Boom
column3: 拦江栅

column2: Wantong have stretched a timber boom across the river hung with nets, so that nothing floating down from upstream gets past: logs, dead sheep, bamboo tubes, tea seedlings. Camps stand at either end where swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders take turns on watch, and everything fished out goes before a Wan family eye first.
column3: 万通号在江面上横拉了一道木栅，栅上挂满了网，上游冲下来的东西一样也漏不过去：木头、死羊、竹筒、茶苗。栅子两头扎着营，刀手、弩手、骑手轮流守，捞上来的东西先过万家人的眼。

column2: You hack the boom open and find a bamboo tube caught in the net, its mouth sealed with wax. Inside is a slip in a big, heavy hand: 'The mule didn't come back this year. Who will take the tea?' The ink is fresh. It seems the man up on the cliffs drops a tube in the river every year, and nobody has ever received one.
column3: 木栅被你们砍开了，网里卡着一只竹筒，筒口拿蜡封着。打开，是一张字条，字又粗又大：「今年骡子没回来。茶谁送？」墨还是新的。看样子，崖上的人每年都往江里放一只竹筒，只是从来没人收到。

column2: Basket-Rest Slope
column3: 歇篓坡

column2: On the towpath by the river a crowd of porters blocks the way, their carrying baskets upturned as a wall; anyone coming through with goods must leave half behind. They all carried tea for Wantong, and since the snow tea stopped the Wans haven't paid them a copper: 'No tea, so what's to carry?' Their leader brandishes his T-shaped resting stick. 'We've been hungry all winter.'
column3: 江边纤道上，一伙背夫堵着路，背篓扣在地上当墙，谁带着货过来都要留下一半。他们都是给万通号背茶的，雪茶断了，万家一文工钱也不给，说「茶都没有，背什么」。背夫头子举着丁字拐：「我们饿了一个冬天了。」

column2: Beaten, then fed a square meal, the porters come round. Their leader says he carried snow tea for nine years and never saw where it grew; all he knows is the old mule never let anyone touch its pack. 'I reached for it once and it kicked me head over heels.' He rubs his leg. 'Respect to that mule.'
column3: 背夫被你们打散，又被你们请吃了一顿饭，这才服了气。背夫头子说他背了九年雪茶，从没见过茶树长在哪，只知道老骡子从不让人碰它的驮子：「有一回我伸手去摸，它一蹄子踢了我个跟头。」他揉着腿，「我服它。」

column2: Pebble Terrace
column3: 卵石台

column2: Above the mountain's foot lies a terrace as flat as a threshing floor, its surface strewn with pebbles, every one perfectly round. Wantong swordsmen have pitched camp on it and lit fires; they say they're waiting for the fire party to gather. The shepherd crouches at the edge, turning a pebble over and over in his fingers.
column3: 山脚往上一层平台，平得像打谷场，台面上铺满了鹅卵石，个个滚圆。一伙万通号的刀手在台上扎营生火，说是在这儿等放火的人到齐。放羊人蹲在台边捡了一颗卵石，翻来覆去地看。

column2: The swordsmen driven off the terrace, the shepherd hands the pebble to Zhou One-Tongue. 'Mountain stones are sharp. Only river stones are round.' Zhou slaps his forehead: the river once flowed this high, and year after year it cut downward, carving out the gorge and leaving its old bed stranded halfway up the mountain. 'River mud up here: tea can grow. The third step is the oldest riverbed of all.'
column3: 刀手被赶下了台。放羊人把卵石递给周一舌：「山上的石头是尖的，河里的才是圆的。」周一舌一拍脑门：江水从前就在这么高的地方流，一年年往下切，切出了这条峡，旧河床就留在了半山腰。「台上有河泥，种得了茶。第三层，就是最老的河床。」

column2: Pine-Torch Carts
column3: 松明车道

column2: A dozen wheelbarrows trundle across the open ground, piled with pine torches and jars of lamp oil: the Wantong fire party, hurrying to Three-Step Valley. Their leader carries Wan the Third's written order and riders escort them. Hill folk at the roadside clutch at the barrows, weeping. 'Fire in that valley and half the mountain burns!'
column3: 野地里一伙人推着十几辆独轮车，车上堆满松明和火油罐，是万通号放火的队伍，正往三叠沟赶。领头的拿着万老三的手令，后头跟着骑手护送。路边的山民拦着车哭求：「沟里一着火，半座山都要烧光！」

column2: The fire party scattered, every jar of oil goes in the river. On his knees, their leader confesses: Wan the Third reckoned that with the tea terrace burned, the man on the cliffs would have no tea and would come down to beg Wantong for it. 'Third Master says he's guarded those few trees for ten years.' The hill folk carry the torches home: just the thing for winter lamps.
column3: 放火队被打散，火油罐全倒进了江里。领头的跪着交代：万老三说，烧了茶台，崖上那个人没了茶，就会自己下山来求万通号。「三爷说，他守了十年，就守那几棵树。」山民们把松明扛回了家，冬天正好点灯。

column2: Chisellers' Huts
column3: 凿工寮

column2: A row of masons' huts at the mountain's foot rings with chisels. Old Gan the Chisel, who cut gallery holes all his life, is held here by a local bully to carve his family's tombstones and memorial arches, and has been for three years. The bully's men stand guard with whips, and Gan's apprentice Shi Dun, who crept in to fetch his master, hangs by the wrists from the tree by the door.
column3: 山脚一排石匠寮子，叮叮当当响个不停。凿栈孔的老匠人甘老凿被一个寨霸扣在这里，替他家刻墓碑、刻牌坊，一刻就是三年。寨霸的家丁拿鞭子守着，甘老凿的徒弟石墩偷偷来接师父，被吊在了门口的树上。

column2: The bully's men chased off, Shi Dun is let down from the tree. Brushing stone dust off himself, Old Gan says half the holes in these galleries he cut as a young man: 'three days a hole, three holes a fathom of gallery'. He studies your copy of the charcoal drawing and narrows his eyes. 'Whoever drew this knows galleries.'
column3: 家丁被打跑，石墩从树上放了下来。甘老凿拍着身上的石粉说，这一带的栈道，有一半是他年轻时凿的孔，「一个孔凿三天，一丈栈道凿三个孔」。他看了你们抄下的炭画，眯起眼：「这画的笔法，懂栈道。」

column2: Gallery-Men's Canteen
column3: 栈夫饭堂

column2: A great canteen stands on the open ground where the gallery builders used to eat, ten huge woks in a row. Rowdy soldiers have taken it over and are stewing stolen mutton in the woks, and the old cook has been sent off to feed the pigs. Crossbowmen squat on the roof and put an arrow at the feet of anyone who comes asking for food.
column3: 野地上一座大饭堂，从前是修栈道的栈夫吃饭的地方，十口大锅一字排开。一伙兵痞把饭堂占了，锅里炖着抢来的羊，老厨娘被赶去喂猪。弩手蹲在房顶上，见有人来讨饭，就往人脚下射一箭。

column2: The soldiers gone, the ten woks are scoured and the old cook returns to her stove. The gallery men scattered ten years ago, she says; only one wok of the ten is ever needed now. You pass on Old Gan's word: the galleries are going to be mended. She stares a moment, then turns and sets all ten woks on the fire.
column3: 兵痞被赶走，十口锅刷干净，老厨娘回了灶台。她说栈夫们散了十年，十口锅只用得上一口。你们带来甘老凿的话：栈道要修了。老厨娘愣了一下，转身把十口锅全架上了火。

column2: From the soldiers' stores: five sheep, three loads of buckwheat flour, two vats of pickles, and a stack of bamboo meal tallies the gallery men once used, which the soldiers had been gambling with.
column3: 抄出兵痞的存货：羊五只、荞面三担、腌菜两缸，还有一摞竹饭牌，是当年栈夫打饭用的，兵痞拿去当了赌筹。

column2: Every time you pass, the old cook has a pot of buckwheat dumplings waiting and hands each of you a bamboo meal tally. 'Road menders eat free.'
column3: 每回路过，老厨娘都给你们留一锅荞面疙瘩，竹饭牌一人发一块：「修路的人，吃饭不要钱。」

column2: Earthquake Cave
column3: 地动洞

column2: Another cave under the cliff at the end of the open ground, and another charcoal drawing: the same box, one lock; beside it a stretch of gallery broken in the middle, planks tumbling down. Quarry labourers are camped here, and their foreman wants this wall hacked out for paving, but the men won't touch it. The drawing, they say, 'means something'.
column3: 野地尽头的崖下又一个岩洞，洞壁上又是炭画：还是那只箱子，一把锁；箱子旁边画着一段栈道，从中间断开，几块木板往下掉。一伙采石的苦力在洞里落脚，工头要把这面墙凿下来铺路，苦力们不敢动手，说画上的东西「有讲究」。

column2: The foreman driven off, the labourers breathe again. Under this drawing too there's a line of writing: 'Earthquake the night we slept here. Road broken in seven places. All present.' The lines waver as if the hand that drew them shook, but not one of the two hundred and ninety-nine strokes is missing. Shi Dun counts the falling planks: seven.
column3: 工头被赶跑，苦力们松了口气。炭画底下又有一行字：「宿此夜，地动。路断七处，人齐。」线条歪歪扭扭，像是画的人手在抖，可二百九十九道杠一道也没少。石墩数了数往下掉的木板：七块。

column2: Nine-Mark Posts
column3: 九字桩

column2: A line of gallery holes runs along the cliff at the mountain's foot, most of them empty, but a few hold freshly whittled posts with the character for nine carved on their heads. Old Gan brings you to see them, but cliff crossbowmen hold the top and shoot at anyone who comes close: this stretch, they say, is their stronghold's land, and the posts are their firewood.
column3: 山脚崖壁上一排栈孔，大多是空的，有几个插着新削的木桩，桩头刻着一个「九」字。甘老凿带你们来看，一伙崖上弩手却占着崖顶，见人靠近就放箭，说这一段是他们山寨的地界，桩子是山寨的柴火。

column2: The crossbowmen chased off, Old Gan runs his hand over the posts. 'Ring-cup oak, well shaped, driven in true to the inch.' Whoever set them carried each one up and drove each one in himself. 'One man alone, he'd mend ten-odd fathoms a year at most.' Shi Dun asks what the nine means. Old Gan says nothing.
column3: 弩手被赶走，甘老凿伸手摸了摸那几根桩子：「青冈木，削得好，打进去一寸不差。」插桩的人是一根根背上来、一根根打进去的，「一个人干，一年也就修个十来丈。」石墩问那个九是什么意思，甘老凿没说话。

column2: Second Step
column3: 二层台

column2: Wantong's camp stands on the second step of Three-Step Valley, and chief steward Sun the Fat sits in a carrying chair directing men to put ladders up to the third. With no fire party coming, he has them hurling rocks upward instead, swearing he'll knock the tea terrace down if he can't burn it. Cliff crossbowmen guard his chair on both sides.
column3: 三叠沟的第二层台子上扎着万通号的营，大管事孙胖子坐在滑竿上，指挥人往第三层搭梯子。放火队没来，他就叫人搬石头往上砸，说砸也要把茶台砸塌。崖上弩手护在他滑竿两边。

column2: The crossbowmen scattered, Sun the Fat tumbles out of his chair. Panting, he says that for nine years the Wans took the old mule's tea hoping the man would come down in person to ask for it. 'He'd rather send another bundle every year than come down.' He looks up at the third step. 'Nine years we sold his tea, and he never said one word to us.'
column3: 弩手被打散，孙胖子从滑竿上滚了下来。他喘着气说，九年来万家截老骡子的茶，就是想等那个人亲自下山来讨，「他宁可每年再送一包，也不下来」。他抬头看着第三层：「卖了九年他的茶，他一句话也没跟我们说过。」

column2: Basket-Lending House
column3: 借篓屋

column2: A lone wooden house on the open ground belongs to the shepherd's grandmother, past eighty. Wantong swordsmen have burst in demanding the way up to the third step and thrown her spindle on the fire. She sits on the threshold, neither weeping nor cursing, telling her prayer beads over and over.
column3: 野地上一座孤零零的木屋，住着放羊人的阿奶，八十多岁了。几个万通号的刀手闯进来，逼她说出上第三层台子的路，把她的纺锤扔进了火塘。阿奶坐在门槛上，不哭也不骂，一遍遍地数手里的念珠。

column2: The swordsmen gone, she finally speaks. Ten years ago some Han men borrowed thirty carrying baskets from her and carried earth up from the river to the third step, basket by basket, all spring. 'There's no soil up there, only stone. They said they were planting tea, to feed a worm down the mountain.' She laughs toothlessly. 'Eighty years, and that's the first I've heard of planting tea for a worm.'
column3: 刀手被赶走，阿奶才开口：十年前一伙汉人在她这儿借了三十个背篓，从江边一筐筐往第三层背土，背了整整一个春天。「崖上没土，只有石头，」她说，「他们说要种茶，种给山下一条虫子吃。」她没牙地笑了：「活了八十年，头回听说给虫子种茶。」

column2: First-Slide Ledge
column3: 试溜台

column2: On the anchor ledge at the mountain's foot the new bamboo rope stretches taut across the river at last, humming in the wind. Old Fan ties Xiaomie to the slider to go first. But a line of escort guards steps out by the anchor post opposite, and the young man leading them lifts an axe and measures it against the rope. On this bank, Wantong riders come galloping up to cross before anyone else.
column3: 山脚的锚台上，新篾索终于绷过了江，在风里嗡嗡作响。范老索把小篾系在溜梆上，要她第一个溜过去。可对岸锚桩边站出来一排镖师，领头的年轻人举起斧头，对着新索比划。这边岸上，万通号的一伙骑手也赶来了，要抢在前头过江。

column2: The riders scattered. The young guard's axe hangs in the air a long while and finally comes down to his side. He shouts across: 'Old Fan! The chief's word: rope joined, Wantong follow, and the people up top can't stand that.' Fan shouts back: 'Wantong's been beaten off!' For a long time no sound comes from the far bank.
column3: 骑手被打散了。对岸那个年轻镖师的斧头迟迟没落，最后放下来，隔江喊：「老范！镖头的话：索一接上，万通号就跟着上来了，上头的人禁不起。」范老索喊回去：「万通号叫人打跑了！」对岸半天没有声音。

column2: Eagle-Traders' Tents
column3: 鹰贩帐

column2: Eagle traders have pitched tents on the open ground, and in a cage sit two golden eaglets not yet fully feathered, waiting to be sold as hunting birds to a prince's household beyond the mountains. They were taken from a nest on the cliff behind Eagle-Beak Rock, and the mother has circled after them for three days, screaming over the tents.
column3: 野地里一伙鹰贩子扎着帐篷，笼子里关着两只还没长齐毛的金雕崽，等着卖给山外的王府当猎鹰。崽子是从鹰嘴岩背后的崖上掏下来的，母雕追着他们盘旋了三天，在帐篷顶上一声声地叫。

column2: The traders chased off, the cage is opened; the eaglets huddle in a corner, unable to fly. A bound trader mutters that the nest sits on an old gallery post, 'and there's something red pressed under it; I didn't dare grab it with the mother diving at me'. The chicks must go back, but nobody knows how.
column3: 鹰贩被打跑，笼子打开，两只雕崽缩在角落里，飞不起来。一个被捆着的鹰贩嘟囔：那窝架在一根老栈桩上，「窝底下还压着红红的一截东西，我没敢拿，母雕扑得太凶」。雕崽得送回去，可谁也不知道怎么送。

column2: Bridal Path
column3: 迎亲道

column2: A wedding procession has halted by the road on the open ground, the groom going round in circles. The bride's family lives at the far end of the galleries, which have been broken for ten years; the two families agreed the match across a cliff, the day has come, and there's no way over. Deserters gather round, demanding the bride-price to sell him a 'short cut' they claim to know.
column3: 野地上一支迎亲的队伍停在路边，新郎急得团团转：新娘家在栈道那头，栈道断了十年，两家隔着一道崖说定了亲，日子到了，却过不去。一伙逃兵趁机围了上来，要新郎拿彩礼买路，说他们知道一条小路。

column2: The deserters chased off, their short cut turns out to be pure invention. But at dawn the groom comes running with news: in the night someone laid three new planks across that broken stretch, each carved with a nine. The procession crosses with pipes and drums. 'Who mended it?' asks the groom. Nobody can say.
column3: 逃兵被赶跑，他们的「小路」是瞎编的。可第二天一早，新郎跑来报信：那段断栈道，夜里被人补上了三块木板，板上刻着「九」。迎亲队吹吹打打地过去了。「谁补的？」新郎问，没人答得上来。

column2: Three-Lock Cave
column3: 三锁洞

column2: A third cave at the edge of the open ground has been made a horse pen by mountain riders, the dung knee-deep. Digging it aside, you uncover the corner of a charcoal drawing: the same box, this time with three locks. The riders' chief objects to you digging up his stable and leads his men round you.
column3: 野地边第三个岩洞，洞口被一伙山马骑拿来圈马，马粪堆到了膝盖。你们挖开马粪，洞壁上露出炭画的一角：还是那只箱子，这回是三把锁。马贼的头儿嫌你们挖他的马圈，牵着马就围了上来。

column2: The riders chased off, the wall is cleaned. The third lock is drawn unlike the other two: round, with no keyhole. Beside the box a crowd of little figures climbs upward, while one big figure with the box on his back stays where he is, facing down. The charcoal is much fresher than the others, and beneath it: 'Three locks. One man.'
column3: 马贼被打跑，洞壁清理干净了。第三把锁画得跟前两把不一样：圆圆的，没有钥匙眼。箱子旁边画着一大群小人往上走，只有一个大个子背着箱子站在原地，脸朝下面。这一幅的炭迹新得多，底下一行字：「锁三道，人一个。」

column2: Salt-Lick Wall
column3: 舔盐壁

column2: A herd of takin, dozens of them, each bigger than an ox, is jammed on the narrow way to the galleries, licking salt crust off a cliff face, and nothing will shift them. Hunters tried to snare one and only enraged the lead bull, which flattened two of them. Now the bull lowers its horns at everyone who comes along.
column3: 野地里横着一群扭角羚，几十头，块头比牛还大，挤在通往栈道的窄路上舔一面崖壁上的盐霜，谁也挪不动。一伙猎户想趁机下套，反倒惹恼了领头的公牛，一头撞翻了两个人。现在公牛把犄角对准了所有路过的人。

column2: The takin driven back into the woods and the hunters taught a lesson, the cliff face is left with a great hollow licked into it, and in the hollow shows half an old gallery post wrapped in faded red cloth. The Qianli men tied red cloths along their way to mark it, pointing the same way as the arrows in the caves.
column3: 扭角羚被轰散，钻回了林子，猎户也被教训了一顿，不敢再下套。那面崖壁被舔出了一个大凹坑，坑里露出半截旧栈桩，桩上缠着一截褪色的红布：千里号的人沿路系红布认路，跟岩洞里箭头指的方向一样。

column2: Barricade Stockade
column3: 拒马寨

column2: Under a rock face at the mountain's foot, deserters turned outlaw have torn down a stretch of old gallery, burned the planks and pulled out the posts to make a ring of barricades round a little stockade. The galleries are broken anyway, they say, so why waste good timber? Old Gan stamps with grief at the sight. 'I drove those in when I was young!'
column3: 山脚的石崖下，一伙落草的逃兵把一段旧栈道拆了，木板拿去烧火，木桩拔出来做拒马，围成了一座小寨子。他们说栈道反正断了，木头不用白不用。甘老凿看着那些栈桩，心疼得直跺脚：「这是我年轻时打进去的！」

column2: The deserters driven out, the posts are gathered up. Old Gan picks one out: two marks are cut in its butt, his own and a nine. 'I drove this one in, and he pulled it out and mended it.' He runs his hand over it a long time. 'It split, and he bound it with an iron hoop. More careful than me, this fellow.'
column3: 逃兵被赶走，栈桩一根根收了回来。甘老凿挑出一根，桩尾刻着两个记号：一个是他自己的，一个是「九」。「这根我打进去过，他又拔出来修过，」老汉摸了半天，「桩子裂了，他拿铁箍箍上了。这人比我细心。」

column2: Far-Bank Anchor Fort
column3: 对岸锚堡

column2: On the anchor rock across the river stands a small stone fort, the Lu escort's river post: for ten years they have shot through ropes and cut bamboo lines and let no one across. The new rope has reached them now, but the guards in the fort ring the anchor post, swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders all, and at their head is the same young man with the axe. 'Sorry, Old Fan. The chief's order still stands.'
column3: 江对岸的锚石上筑着一座小石堡，是陆家镖守江的地方，十年来就是他们射绳子、砍篾索，不放一个人过江。新索已经溜过去了，可石堡里的镖师把锚桩团团围住，刀手、弩手、骑手都在。领头的还是那个举斧头的年轻人：「老范，对不住，镖头的令还没撤。」

column2: The guards beaten, they hand Old Fan a cloth bundle: an ingot of silver under a note in Lu Jiu's hand. 'I cut the rope. This pays for it. With the road unmended, whoever goes up can't come back; and if Wantong follow, the people up top won't survive it. When the road is mended, join it again.' Fan pushes the silver back and pats the new rope. 'Rope's joined. Now he'll have to come down for a cup of tea.'
column3: 镖师们输了，交给范老索一个布包：一锭银子，压着陆九的字条：「索是我砍的，赔你。路没修好，上去的人回不来；万通号跟上来，上头的人也活不成。路修好了，你再接。」范老索把银子塞了回去，拍拍新索：「索接上了，他总得下来喝碗茶。」

column2: Blue-Sheep Ledge Path
column3: 岩羊道

column2: Beneath the third step rises a sheer cliff, and the path the blue sheep have worn is barely half a foot wide. Wantong's last troop has run up dozens of ladders and is climbing, crossbowmen covering from below, swordsmen on the rungs, riders holding the feet. Someone below bawls: 'A hundred taels to the first man up!'
column3: 第三层台子底下是一面陡崖，岩羊踩出的小道细得只放得下半只脚。万通号最后一队人搭了几十架梯子往上爬，弩手在下面掩护，刀手在梯子上，骑手守着梯脚。有人在下面喊：「谁先上去，赏一百两！」

column2: You push the ladders over and the Wantong men tumble every which way; nobody tries again. The shepherd leads you up the blue-sheep path, hands and feet, for the better part of an hour, and you haul yourselves onto the third step: the scent of tea meets you full in the face.
column3: 梯子被你们推倒，万通号的人摔得七零八落，没人再往上爬。放羊人领着你们走岩羊道，手脚并用爬了半个时辰，翻上了第三层：一股茶香迎面扑来。

column2: The Falconer's House
column3: 鹰把式屋

column2: In a stone house at the mountain's foot lives an old falconer who has kept birds all his life, and his eyes light up at the eaglets you carry in. But a party of the prince's falcon officers waits outside, come to collect from the traders; the chicks are the prince's order, they say, and whoever takes them back is defying the prince.
column3: 山脚的石屋里住着一个老鹰把式，养了一辈子鹰，看见你们抱来的雕崽，眼睛一亮。可他屋外守着一伙王府的鹰差，就是来收鹰贩子货的，说雕崽是王府订下的，谁送回去，谁就是跟王府作对。

column2: The officers chased off, the old falconer explains that golden eagles keep to their nest: one nest may be used for decades, and every year they come back and add more sticks, higher and higher. 'That nest behind Eagle-Beak Rock was there when I was young. These years they've been adding more than sticks: planks fallen from the galleries too.' He agrees to help you take the chicks home.
column3: 鹰差被打跑，老鹰把式说，金雕认窝，一个窝能用几十年，每年回来都要往上添树枝，越堆越高。「鹰嘴岩背后那个窝，我年轻时就在了。这些年窝里添的不光是树枝，还有栈道上掉下去的木板。」他答应带你们把雕崽送回去。

column2: Three-Step Hill Store
column3: 三叠山货铺

column2: A hill-goods store at the edge of the open ground sells wool, buckwheat flour and honey; the shepherd's elder brother runs it. Wantong have put the word out that the Three-Step folk are hiding the snow tea, and trading with them is crossing Wantong. The shop has had no custom for half a year, and Wantong swordsmen stand at the door taking down the name of anyone who goes in.
column3: 野地边一间山货铺，卖羊毛、荞面、蜂蜜，是放羊人的哥哥开的。万通号放出话来：三叠沟的人藏着雪茶，谁跟他们做买卖就是跟万通号作对。铺子半年没开张，门口还守着几个万通号的刀手，见人进门就记名字。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the store opens again and will trade for anything. The brother says that every autumn an escort guard came to buy twenty catties of salt and fifty of buckwheat flour and carried them up to the third step, 'never haggled, never said one word more than he had to'. He tucks an extra jar of honey into your packs. 'That's for up top.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，铺子重新开了门，什么都肯换。哥哥说，每年秋天都有个镖师来买二十斤盐、五十斤荞面，背上第三层台子，「从不还价，也从不多说一句」。他往你们驮袋里多塞了一罐蜂蜜：「这是给上头的。」

column2: Stranded-Troupe Flat
column3: 困戏坝

column2: A theatre troupe of a dozen players is stranded under the cliff at the mountain's foot, their costume trunks making the mules wheeze. They were on their way to sing the New Year plays at a village beyond the cliff, but the galleries are impassable, and bandits have caught them. The bandit chief makes them perform for him every day, a meal docked for every fluffed line, and the troupe master's voice is already gone.
column3: 山脚崖下困着一个戏班子，十来个人，戏箱压得骡子直喘：他们要去崖那头的寨子唱年戏，栈道过不去，又被一伙土匪截住。土匪逼他们天天唱戏给寨主听，唱错一句扣一顿饭，班主的嗓子已经哑了。

column2: The bandits chased off, the troupe master thanks you over and over. They have a play called 'Chief Lu Crosses the Cliffs', he says, made up ten years ago from what passing caravan hands told them: the chief, an iron casket on his back, helps two hundred and ninety-nine people across the broken cliffs one at a time. 'In the play he never comes down,' says the master. 'We don't know what happened after.'
column3: 土匪被赶跑，班主千恩万谢。他说班里有一出《陆镖头过崖》，是十年前听过路的马帮伙计讲了编的：镖头背着铁匣，把二百九十九个人一个个扶过断崖。「戏里他最后没下来，」班主说，「我们也不知道后来怎样。」

column2: Black-Pennant Tower
column3: 黑旗箭楼

column2: A stone archery tower on the open ground flies the black triangular pennant marked Lu: an outpost of the Lu escort. At its foot a side path is walled off with stones, and a board stands at the opening: 'This road is not yet mended. No passing.' The guards stand straight as spears; when you arrive their leader first salutes, fist in palm, then draws his blade.
column3: 野地上一座石箭楼，楼顶插着黑三角旗，旗上一个「陆」字，是陆家镖的前哨。楼下拿石头封了一条小路，路口立着木牌：「此路未修好，不许过」。镖师们一个个身板笔直，见你们来，领头的先抱了抱拳，然后拔刀。

column2: The guards lose and don't dispute it; they salute and step aside. Behind the walled-off path is a newly laid stretch of gallery, the planks still pale and untrodden. 'The chief says it's three planks short, and no one walks on it till it's done,' their leader says. He looks at the new stretch. 'Ten years. He laid it one plank at a time.'
column3: 镖师们输了，也不赖，抱拳让开。封着的那条小路，后面是一段刚铺好的栈道，木板白生生的，还没叫人踩过。领头的说：「镖头说，还差三块板，不许人上去踩。」他望着那段新路，「十年了，他一块一块铺的。」

column2: Eagle-Beak Rock
column3: 鹰嘴岩

column2: A great rock juts from the cliff like an eagle's beak, and the gallery passes beneath it. A troop of escort guards holds the foot of it, swordsmen in front and crossbowmen up on the rock, and as soon as they see you they shout: 'Chief Lu says no one goes up the mountain!' Then they add: 'Unless you can beat us. That's different.'
column3: 一块大岩石从崖壁上伸出来，形状像鹰嘴，栈道从鹰嘴底下钻过去。岩下守着一队镖师，刀手在前，弩手在岩上，看见你们就喊：「陆镖头说了，谁也不许上山！」喊完了，又补一句：「打得过我们的，另说。」

column2: Driven back a few paces, the guards don't break; they stand under the rock catching their breath. It's the chief's rule, their leader says: until the road is mended, anyone who goes up either falls or gets robbed. 'If you can't beat us, you can't beat what's up there.' He stands aside, then adds: 'Under the beak, keep a hand on the rock and don't look at the river.'
column3: 镖师们被打退几步，没散，站在岩下喘气。领头的说这是镖头定的规矩：路没修好以前，上山的人不是摔死就是被劫，「打不过我们，就打不过上头的」。他让开了路，又叮嘱：「过鹰嘴的时候扶着石头，别看江。」

column2: Post-Pullers' Camp
column3: 拆桩营

column2: A big camp on the open ground houses mercenaries in Wantong's pay. Hearing that someone is mending the galleries, they've been sent to pull it down again: mend a stretch, pull a stretch. Heaped at the camp gate are piles of freshly whittled posts, every one carved with a nine, all wrenched out of their holes.
column3: 野地上一座大营，营里是一伙给万通号卖命的雇佣兵，听说栈道上有人在修路，他们奉命来拆：修一段，拆一段。营门口堆着一大堆新削的木桩，桩头都刻着「九」，全是从栈孔里拔出来的。

column2: The mercenaries scattered, the posts are gathered up and Shi Dun carries them back. One mercenary says they pulled for three years and the man mended for three years. 'We pulled by day, he mended by night, never missed one.' He sighs in grudging admiration. 'Does the man never sleep?'
column3: 雇佣兵被打散，木桩一根根收了回来，石墩背着往回走。一个雇佣兵说，他们拆了三年，那人就修了三年，「我们白天拆，他夜里修，一天也没落下」。他服气地叹了一声：「这人不睡觉的吗？」

column2: Offset Cliff
column3: 错层崖

column2: A great cliff at the mountain's foot is banded with coloured rock, red, grey and yellow, like a closed book. The gallery runs along it in fine shape until halfway, where the rest of it sits more than a fathom higher and won't join. The quarrymen say it's 'the ghosts lifting the road' on the night of the earthquake and are burning incense to the cliff, while local thugs collect a 'cliff-worship fee'.
column3: 山脚下一面大崖，崖壁上一道道彩色的石层，红的、灰的、黄的，像一本合起来的书。栈道走到这里，前半截好好的，后半截却高出了一丈多，接不上。采石的人说这是「鬼抬路」，地动那夜鬼把路抬高了，正拿香纸拜崖，一伙地痞趁机收「拜崖钱」。

column2: The thugs chased off, Old Gan points at the bands: the red layer on the left, once past the crack, only picks up again more than a fathom higher on the right. 'No ghosts. The mountain shifted itself.' The rock underground is squeezed until it can't hold, then lurches all at once along a crack; that lurch is an earthquake, and it left the two halves of the road at different heights. 'To join them, we cut a flight of steps here.'
column3: 地痞被赶走，甘老凿指着崖上的石层：左边那道红层，过了裂缝，右边要高一丈多才接上。「不是鬼抬的，是山自己错开了。」地底下的石头被挤着，绷不住了就沿着一道裂缝猛地错一下，那就是地动；两边的路，就这么一高一低了。「要接，就在这儿凿一道台阶。」

column2: Snow Tea Terrace
column3: 雪茶台

column2: On the third step of Three-Step Valley stand thirty-odd tea trees in neat rows, and at the terrace edge a stone hut and a mule manger, empty. A troop of Lu escort guards holds the terrace, swordsmen and crossbowmen, and their leader says: 'This is the chief's tea. No one touches it.' Behind them this year's new buds have come out all over, and nobody has picked them.
column3: 三叠沟第三层台子上，三十几棵茶树排得整整齐齐，台边一间石屋、一个骡槽，槽里空着。茶台上守着一队陆家镖师，刀手、弩手都有，领头的说：「这是镖头的茶，谁也不许碰。」他们身后，今年的新芽已经冒了一层，没人采。

column2: The guards beaten, their leader sighs: with the mule gone this year they didn't dare leave the terrace to deliver it. 'The chief says the tea must go, and the terrace must be guarded.' You help them pick the new buds, roast them and pack them in oilcloth. Nine strokes are cut on the hut wall, nine years. You cut the tenth and hire a porter to carry the tea north to the Gu villages.
column3: 镖师们输了，领头的叹了口气：今年骡子没回来，他们不敢离开茶台去送，「镖头说，茶要送，台也要守」。你们帮着采了新芽，焙好，装进油布包。石屋墙上刻着九道杠，九年。你们刻上第十道，雇了个背夫，把茶往北送去了蛊寨。

column2: Yak Flats
column3: 牦牛滩

column2: The goods of a yak caravan lie scattered over the open ground: butter, wool, highland barley; half the yaks have been driven off by mountain riders. The Tibetan trader Ciren squats by the pile, swearing and counting, one fewer every time. He came down from beyond the snow peaks meaning to rest and trade at the Snowline Post, but the post has been shut for ten years, so he camped in the open and the horse thieves found him.
column3: 野地上散着一支牦牛帮的货：酥油、羊毛、青稞，牦牛被一伙山马骑赶走了一半。藏商次仁蹲在货堆边，一边骂一边数，数一遍少一头。他是从雪山那边下来的，原想在雪线驿歇脚换货，可驿站关了十年，只好在野地上扎营，被马贼盯上了。

column2: The thieves chased off, the yaks are driven home. The Snowline Post, Ciren says, was once the busiest station under the snow peaks, where everyone coming down from the snows and everyone going up from the gorge traded. 'It shut after the earthquake. Only the postmaster's son keeps it now, and he still lights a lamp every night.'
column3: 马贼被打跑，牦牛赶了回来。次仁说雪线驿从前是雪山下最热闹的驿站，雪山上下来的、峡谷里上去的，都在那里换货。「地动以后就关了，」他说，「只剩驿丞的儿子守着，每天晚上还点一盏灯。」

column2: The Golden Eagle Nest
column3: 金雕巢

column2: At a dead end, on an old gallery post jutting from the cliff, sits a huge nest taller than a man: the golden eagles' ancient home. The mother and several half-grown birds dive at the face of anyone who comes near the cliff; several porters have been clawed, and many of the hill folk's lambs carried off. Holding the eaglets, the old falconer signals you to draw the mother away first.
column3: 死路尽头的崖壁上，一根伸出来的老栈桩上架着一个大鸟窝，一人多高，是金雕的老巢。母雕带着几只半大的雕，见人靠近崖壁就俯冲下来抓脸，过路的背夫被抓伤了好几个，崖下山民的羊羔也被叼走了不少。老鹰把式抱着雕崽，示意你们先把母雕引开。

column2: The eagles driven off, the old falconer sets the two chicks back in the nest. It is layer upon layer of sticks with old gallery planks wedged among them, and at the very bottom lies a faded red banner, the character Qian stitched in its corner: a Qianli banner hung on the galleries to mark the way, knocked down in the earthquake and carried home by the eagles. But the eagles come back to this nest to breed every year, and every brood grows up to take lambs, so the hill folk must come and drive them off every so often. 'You can drive them off,' says the falconer, 'but never away. They know this post.'
column3: 雕群被赶开，老鹰把式把两只雕崽放回了窝里。窝里一层层压着树枝，夹着几块栈道的旧木板，最底下压着一面褪了色的红旗，旗角绣着「千」字：千里号挂在栈道上认路的号旗，地动时掉下来，被雕叼回了窝。可雕年年回这个窝孵崽，一窝窝长大了又要叼羊，山民隔些日子就得来轰一回。老鹰把式说：「轰得走，赶不尽，它们认这根桩。」

column2: The Gallery Manual House
column3: 栈经屋

column2: An abandoned gallery workers' camp lies on the open ground, most of its dozens of huts fallen in, a lamp burning in just one. There lives an old gallery builder's widow, keeping her late husband's toolbox: a set of chisels and a book, The Gallery Manual. Wantong men have come to buy it for ten taels; she won't sell, so they mean to take it.
column3: 野地上一座废弃的栈夫营，几十间木屋塌了大半，只有一间还亮着灯。屋里住着个老栈夫的寡妇，守着亡夫的工具箱，箱里一套凿子、一本《栈经》。一伙万通号的伙计找上门来，要买那本《栈经》，出价十两，寡妇不卖，他们就要抢。

column2: The Wantong men chased off, the widow gives the Manual to Old Gan. 'He always said you'd come back to mend the road one day.' The last pages are newly written in a big heavy hand: where each break is, how wide, how many posts and planks it needs; five of the seven breaks are crossed out. 'Chief Lu borrowed it to write in,' says the widow, 'and brought it back after.'
column3: 伙计被打跑，寡妇把《栈经》交给了甘老凿：「他说过，有一天你会回来修路的。」最后几页是新抄上去的，字迹粗大：每一处断口在哪、多宽、要几根桩、几块板，七处断口划掉了五处。「这是陆镖头借去抄的，」寡妇说，「抄完又送回来了。」

column2: Gallery Timber Fair
column3: 栈木集

column2: A wide open square was once the Gallery Timber Fair: oak and fir felled in the forests were sawn into planks and shaped into posts here and sold to the gallery builders, who paid in grain. Ten years without road work and the fair is gone; horse thieves hold the square, the timber stacks are their stables, and the great saw-frames have been broken up for firewood.
column3: 野地上一片大空场，从前是栈木集：林子里伐下来的青冈木、冷杉在这里锯成板、削成桩，卖给修栈道的人，栈夫们拿粮食来换。十年没修路，集散了，空场被一伙马贼占了，木料垛子当了马厩，锯木的大架子拆了当柴烧。

column2: The thieves driven off and the square cleared, Old Gan climbs onto a timber stack and roars: 'We're mending the galleries!' Loggers from the forests, gallery men from below, young men from the villages: more than a hundred turn up at once. The Timber Fair reopens, timber for grain, over twenty thousand catties a day. Leafing through the Manual, Old Gan reads out the timber the last two breaks need: 'One above Eagle-Beak Rock, and one...' He turns to the last page. Nothing is written there; there is only a drawing of a box with three locks.
column3: 马贼被赶走，空场清了出来。甘老凿站在木垛上喊了一嗓子：「修栈道了！」林子里的伐木人、山下的栈夫、寨子里的后生，一下来了一百多人。栈木集重开，木料换粮食，一天换得两万多斤。甘老凿翻着《栈经》报剩下两处断口要的木料：「一处在鹰嘴岩上头，一处……」他翻到最后一页，那一页什么也没写，只画了一只箱子，三把锁。

column2: The Log Chute
column3: 溜木槽

column2: A log chute runs from the top of the forest right down to the foot of the cliff, so felled timber can slide straight down. Bandits hold the top, and whenever travellers pass below they send a great log hurtling down to scatter them, then come down to rob. Smashed logs lie every which way across the road beneath.
column3: 山脚有一道溜木槽，从林子顶上一直通到崖下，伐好的木头从槽里一溜就下来。一伙山贼占了槽顶，专等崖下有人路过，就放一根大木头溜下去，砸散了队伍好下来抢。崖下的路上，横七竖八躺着砸断的木头。

column2: The bandits driven off the chute, it goes to the Timber Fair. The first oak log rumbles down and comes to rest neatly at the bottom, and Old Gan slaps it, laughing. 'That saves a hundred porters.' At the foot of the chute Shi Dun finds an old wooden tag carved: 'The Qianli caravan felled timber here and borrowed the chute. Thanks.'
column3: 山贼被赶下了槽，溜木槽归了栈木集。头一根青冈木轰隆隆滑下来，稳稳停在崖下，甘老凿拍着木头笑：「省了一百个背夫。」石墩在槽底捡到一块旧木牌，刻着：「千里号伐木于此，借槽一用，谢。」

column2: Buckwheat Flat
column3: 荞麦坪

column2: A field of buckwheat in pinkish-white flower spreads over the open ground, a watermill at the bottom of the slope. A local bully's rent collectors have taken the mill: seven pints of every peck harvested, and anyone who can't pay is taken in lieu. The old couple who run the mill are locked in the granary, and crossbowmen squat on the mill roof watching the people in the field.
column3: 野地上一片荞麦地，开着粉白的花，坡下一座水磨房。一伙寨霸的收租人占了磨房，荞麦收一斗要交七升，交不出就拿人抵。磨房的老两口被锁在仓房里，弩手蹲在磨房顶上，盯着地里干活的人。

column2: The collectors chased off, the old couple are let out and the mill creaks round again. Ten years ago, the old man says, the Qianli men bought two hundred catties of buckwheat flour here to carry up the cliffs: 'said it's cold up top, and buckwheat keeps you going'. The dark-faced escort chief bought twenty catties more as he left. 'Said that was for himself. He wasn't going on with them.'
column3: 收租人被赶走，老两口放了出来，水磨又吱呀吱呀地转了。老汉说十年前千里号的人在这里买过两百斤荞面背上崖，「说上头冷，荞面耐饿」。那个黑脸镖头走的时候又多买了二十斤，「说是给自己的，他不跟他们走。」

column2: From the collectors' store: twenty loads of buckwheat, three jars of honey, a cartload of firewood, and a stack of IOUs, burned in front of everyone on the flat.
column3: 抄出收租人的仓：荞麦二十担、蜂蜜三罐、一车柴，还有一摞借据，当着全坪人的面烧了。

column2: Every time you pass, the old couple leave a bag of fresh-ground buckwheat flour at the mill door with a stone on it, a box drawn on the stone. 'You know that sign, so we know you.'
column3: 每回路过，老两口都把新磨的荞面装好一袋放在磨房门口，袋上压一块石头，石头上画个箱子：「你们认得这个，我们就认得你们。」

column2: Charcoal-Kiln Wall
column3: 炭窑壁

column2: A charcoal kiln at the mountain's foot puffs blue smoke. Deserters hold it, selling the charcoal to the Timber Fair after throwing out the burners. On the cliff beside it there used to be a charcoal drawing, but the deserters thought it unlucky and splashed it with mud. The burners say 'the man with the box on his back' drew it, and asked them for a stick of charcoal to do it.
column3: 山脚下一座烧炭窑，窑口冒着青烟。一伙逃兵占着窑，把炭卖给栈木集，却把烧炭的山民赶了出去。窑边的崖壁上原有一幅炭画，逃兵嫌它晦气，泼了一层泥。山民说那画是「背箱子的汉子」画的，画完还在窑里讨了一根炭条。
