column2: The deserters gone, you wash off the mud: this drawing is not a box but a gallery with seven breaks, a mark beside each. Five are ticked, the sixth half-ticked, the charcoal still black. 'He's close,' says Old Gan. 'He was here last month.'
column3: 逃兵被赶走，你们洗掉泥：这一幅画的不是箱子，是一条栈道，七处断口，每处旁边一个记号，五处打了勾，第六处打了半个，炭迹还是黑的。甘老凿说：「他就在附近，上个月还来过。」

column2: One-Eyed Wolf Slope
column3: 独眼狼坡

column2: A wolf pack has fastened onto Ciren's yak caravan, trailing it at a distance by day and closing in by night to bring down stragglers. The caravan has only two guards, one of them lame. Among the wolves is a one-eyed old dog wolf that goes for the yaks' hind legs, bites once and runs, and waits for the beast to drop.
column3: 野地上，一群狼跟上了次仁的牦牛帮，白天远远吊着，夜里就围上来咬落单的牛。牦牛帮的护卫只有两个，一个还瘸了腿。狼群里有一头独眼老狼，专咬牛的后腿，咬一口就跑，等牛自己倒下。

column2: The pack broken up, the one-eyed wolf leads the rest away up the snow slopes. Ciren says the wolves followed them down from the Snowline Post. 'When the post was manned, wolves never came this low. With it empty they've stopped fearing people.' He looks towards the snowline. 'That post has to open.'
column3: 狼群被打散，独眼老狼带着剩下的狼跑上了雪坡。次仁说狼是从雪线驿那边跟下来的：「驿站有人的时候，狼不敢下来；驿站空了，狼也就不怕人了。」他望着雪线的方向：「驿站得开。」

column2: Dendrobium Shed
column3: 石斛药棚

column2: A herb shed on the open ground is drying basketfuls of fritillary, caterpillar fungus and cliff dendrobium: the shed of the herb gatherer He Sanqi. He went up for dendrobium growing on the cliffs and hasn't been back for three days; his wife kept the shed until rowdy soldiers took it. They stuff the herbs in their pockets: 'He won't be back, so what's the use of medicine?' She sits outside with her baby, eyes never leaving the cliff.
column3: 野地上一座药棚，晒着成筐的贝母、虫草、石斛，是采药人何三七家的。何三七进山采崖上的石斛，三天没回来；他媳妇何嫂守着药棚，却被一伙兵痞占了。兵痞把药材往自己口袋里装，说「人回不来，药也用不着了」。何嫂抱着孩子坐在棚外，眼睛一直望着崖上。

column2: The soldiers driven off, most of the herbs come back. He Sanqi went after an old clump of dendrobium in a crack in the rock, his wife says, and as he came down the stretch of gallery under his feet gave way and left him stuck halfway up the cliff. 'When I shout he still answers. A little fainter every day.'
column3: 兵痞被赶走，药材收回了大半。何嫂说，何三七去采一丛长在石缝里的老石斛，下来时脚底那段栈道塌了，人困在了半崖上。「我在下面喊，他还应，」她说，「一天比一天应得轻。」

column2: From the soldiers' stores: a bag of roasted barley flour, three catties of brown sugar, half a jar of wine, and the dendrobium and fritillary they'd pocketed, which Sister He claims back item by item.
column3: 抄出兵痞的存货：一袋糌粑、三斤红糖、半坛酒，还有他们揣走的石斛、贝母，何嫂一样样认了回去。

column2: Every time you pass, Sister He presses a packet of herbs on you, for bleeding, for fever, for swollen feet, with instructions written on it. 'Sanqi always says: on the galleries, your feet are worth more than your life.'
column3: 每回路过，何嫂都塞给你们一包草药：止血的、退烧的、治脚肿的，包上写着用法：「三七说过，走栈道的人，脚比命金贵。」

column2: The Tally Rock-House
column3: 记日岩屋

column2: A rock-house on the open ground flies the Lu escort's black pennant: a resting post for the guards. A few of them are sharpening blades at the door, and the moment they see you they form up without a word. The walls inside are dense with charcoal marks; from the doorway you can't make out what they are.
column3: 野地上一座岩屋，门口挂着陆家镖的黑三角旗，是镖师们的歇脚处。几个镖师正在门口磨刀，见你们来，二话不说就摆开了阵势。门里的墙上满是炭迹，密密麻麻，从门口看不清画的是什么。

column2: The guards fall back and you go in: the walls are covered in little strokes in groups of five, row after row filling three whole walls. Old Gan counts for a long time. 'Over three thousand six hundred.' Ten years, one a day. At the end of the last group is written: 'Seven breaks. Working on the sixth.'
column3: 镖师们退了，你们进屋一看：满墙都是小道道，五道一组，一组组排下去，排满了整整三面墙。甘老凿数了半天：「三千六百多道。」十年，一天一道。最后一组末尾写着：「七处，修到第六处。」

column2: The Fake-Map Pavilion
column3: 假图亭

column2: In a half-collapsed roadside pavilion, swindlers sell maps showing 'a short cut round the galleries' at five silver coins apiece. Several parties of travellers have followed them and ended up at the bottom of a ravine. The swindlers have hired swordsmen to mind the stall and beat anyone who comes back to complain.
column3: 野地里一座塌了半边的路亭，一伙骗子在亭里摆摊卖地图，图上画着一条「绕开栈道的近路」，一张五钱银子。好几拨过路的人照着图走，掉进了山沟。骗子们雇了一伙刀手看摊，谁来找后账就打谁。

column2: The swindlers chased off, a great pile of fake maps goes on the fire. At the bottom is a real one, stolen from some traveller: all seven breaks drawn exactly, the seventh at the very top, with a note beside it: 'Hardest of all. Too much for one man.' Old Gan looks at it. 'The last one. He can't do it alone.'
column3: 骗子被打跑，假地图烧了一大摞。最底下压着一张真图，是从一个过路人身上偷的：栈道七处断口画得一清二楚，第七处在最高的地方，旁边写着「此处最难，一人难成」。甘老凿看了：「最后一处，他一个人修不下来。」

column2: Road-Block Camp
column3: 堵路营

column2: A big camp on the open ground holds Wantong's last band, hired swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders, squatting on the road to the seventh break: hearing someone means to mend the last stretch, they've blocked the way first. 'Mend that and the man up top comes down,' their steward says. 'And when he comes down, the snow tea trade is finished.'
column3: 野地上一座大营，是万通号最后的一伙人，雇了刀手、弩手、骑手，扎在通往第七处断口的路上：他们听说有人要修最后一段栈道，抢先把路堵了。「这段修通了，崖上的人就下来了，」营里的管事说，「下来了，雪茶的买卖就完了。」

column2: You break the camp and the steward runs his men all the way out of the mountains. The road is clear, and Old Gan and Shi Dun shoulder their tools and set off for the seventh break. 'As for the mending,' the old man says over his shoulder, 'we'll need a hand from you.'
column3: 营被你们破了，管事带着人一路跑出了山。路通了，甘老凿和石墩背着家伙往第七处断口走。「修路的事，」老汉回过头，「得你们搭把手。」

column2: The Old Post Yak
column3: 老驿牛

column2: Beside a prayer-flagged mani cairn at the mountain's foot stands an old yak: the Snowline Post's own, turned loose when the post shut ten years ago, and living here on its own ever since. Horse thieves have their eye on it and are roping its horns. A young man comes charging down the slope. 'That's the post's yak!'
column3: 山脚下一座经幡飘飘的玛尼堆，旁边拴着一头老牦牛，是雪线驿的驿牛，十年前驿站关门时放了出来，自己在这儿活了十年。一伙盗马贼看中了它，正拿绳子套它的角。一个年轻人从坡上冲下来：「那是驿里的牛！」

column2: The thieves chased off, the old yak tosses its head and follows the young man. He is Nie Xiaolou, the postmaster's son, keeper of the empty post for ten years, and he lights a lamp every night. 'My father said: keep it lit, and people on the snow road know the post is still here.' Ten years ago his father guided the Qianli caravan up into the snow mountains and never came down.
column3: 盗马贼被打跑，老牦牛甩甩脑袋，跟在年轻人身后。他叫聂小楼，驿丞的儿子，守着空驿站十年了，每晚点一盏灯：「我爹说，灯点着，走雪山的人就知道驿站还在。」他爹十年前给千里号带路上了雪山，再没下来。

column2: The Cliff-Waiters
column3: 等崖帮

column2: At the foot of the cliff where He Sanqi is stuck camps a gang that preys on herb gatherers, the Cliff-Waiters: swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders. They won't rescue anyone or let anyone else try; they just sit in a shelter below and wait, because when a man falls, his herb basket is theirs. In his crack halfway up, He Sanqi hears them laughing below and curses them in a voice gone hoarse.
column3: 何三七困着的那面崖底下，扎着一伙打劫采药人的「等崖帮」，刀手、弩手、骑手都有。他们不救人，也不许别人救，就在崖下搭棚子等着：人掉下来，药篓就是他们的。何三七在半崖的石缝里听见崖下有人笑，骂了一声，嗓子已经哑了。

column2: The Cliff-Waiters scattered, you shout up and He Sanqi answers. There's no reaching him from below; a rope must go down from the top, and the top is a fortified camp. A bound robber mutters that the reason He Sanqi is still alive after so many days is that 'every night someone up top lowers a rice ball down to him'.
column3: 等崖帮被打散。你们朝上喊，何三七应了一声。从崖下够不着，只能从崖顶放绳下去，可崖顶是一座营寨。一个被捆着的强盗嘀咕：何三七困了这么多天还活着，是因为「每天夜里，有人从崖顶给他吊一个饭团下去」。

column2: The Post-Pickers' Loft
column3: 拾驿楼

column2: A crooked wooden loft on the open ground houses a gang of 'post-pickers' who strip the Snowline Post and sell the pieces: doors, mangers, brass bells, the post flag; in ten years they've taken nearly half of it. They've just carried out the great signboard, 'Snowline Post' in flaking gold lacquer, and are about to split it for firewood.
column3: 野地里一座歪歪斜斜的木楼，住着一伙「拾驿人」，专拆雪线驿的东西卖：门板、马槽、铜铃、驿旗，十年拆了小一半。他们刚从驿里扛出一块大匾，匾上「雪线驿」三个字金漆剥落，正要劈了当柴烧。

column2: The pickers chased off, the signboard is saved, and Nie Xiaolou hugs it with tears in his eyes. The pickers' boss says there was one thing in the post they never dared touch: the book in the postmaster's room. 'Every time we reached for it, the lamp outside went out.' Nie Xiaolou turns red. 'That was me blowing it.'
column3: 拾驿人被打跑，大匾保住了，聂小楼抱着匾直抹眼泪。拾驿人的头儿说，驿里只有一样东西他们不敢碰：驿丞房里那本簿子，「每回伸手去拿，外头那盏灯就灭」。聂小楼脸一红：「是我吹的。」

column2: Post Quarry
column3: 驿石场

column2: A big quarry on the open ground once supplied the Snowline Post's building stone. A masons' gang has taken it over and sells stone only to Wantong for their warehouses. Nie Xiaolou wants a few blocks to patch the post's walls; the gang boss asks a tael a block, sneers at his poverty and has him shoved out of the quarry.
column3: 野地上一个大石场，从前是雪线驿采石盖房的地方。一伙石匠帮子把石场占了，石头只卖给万通号盖仓库。聂小楼要几块石头补驿站的墙，石匠头子开价一块一两银子，嫌他穷，叫手下把他推出了石场。

column2: The masons beaten, their boss picks out twenty fine blocks for Nie Xiaolou with an ingratiating smile and sends men to help carry them. He whispers that the Qianli men helped build the post's walls. 'They stayed a month that winter and did the whole post over. Said they'd lodged in someone's house and owed it.'
column3: 石匠帮子被打散，头子赔着笑脸给聂小楼挑了二十块好石头，还派人帮着运。他悄悄说，雪线驿的墙是千里号的人帮着砌的：「那年冬天他们在驿里住了一个月，把整座驿站翻修了一遍，说住了人家的，要还。」

column2: The Register Room
column3: 驿簿房

column2: A stone post-house stands on the open ground, one corner of its wall fallen, its gate shut, a bare space over the door where the signboard hung. Deserters camp around it using the stables as barracks, and at night they order Nie Xiaolou to light their way. When he refused, they smashed his lamp and swore they'd burn the post if he lit it again.
column3: 野地上一座石头驿站，墙塌了一角，大门紧闭，门楣上原来挂匾的地方空着。驿站周围扎着一伙逃兵，拿马厩当营房，夜里还逼聂小楼给他们点灯照路。聂小楼不肯，他们就砸了他的灯，说再点就烧了驿站。

column2: The deserters driven off, the gate opens. Nie Xiaolou brings the register out of the postmaster's room: ten years ago one winter night, two hundred and ninety-nine guests checked in, their names filling nine pages. The last line is in his father's hand: 'Twenty-third of the twelfth month. Guiding the Qianli party to the snow mountain temple. Back when the snow melts.' The snow has melted ten times, and no one came back.
column3: 逃兵被赶走，驿站大门开了。聂小楼从驿丞房里捧出那本驿簿：十年前的冬天，一夜之间住进了二百九十九个人，名字一个挨一个签满了九页。最后一行是他爹的字：「腊月廿三，引千里号诸人往雪山神庙，雪化即还。」雪化了十回，人没回来。

column2: Stone Gate Post
column3: 石门卡

column2: A small wooden post at the mountain's foot flies a black triangular pennant. Six young escort guards keep it, the eldest no more than twenty. Seeing you, they salute in unison, fist in palm, and announce themselves: 'Lu Escort, Stone Gate Post.' Then they draw. 'The chief's orders: no one goes up the mountain who can't beat us. Forgive us.'
column3: 山脚下一座小木卡，卡前立着一面黑三角旗。守卡的是六个年轻镖师，最大的不过二十，见了你们，先齐刷刷抱拳行礼，报了家门：「陆家镖，石门卡。」然后拔刀：「镖头有令，打不过我们的，不许上山。得罪了。」

column2: The guards lose, help each other up and salute again. Their leader, A Gang, says it's the chief's rule: 'Give your name before you stop a man, and own it when you lose.' You ask where Chief Lu is, and he points up. 'Mending the road. With the casket on his back. He never puts it down.'
column3: 镖师们输了，互相扶着站起来，又抱了一回拳。领头的叫阿岗，说这是镖头教的规矩：「拦人先报名，输了要认。」你们问陆镖头在哪，他往上一指：「修路呢。背着匣子修，匣子从不离身。」

column2: Gallery-Foot Teahouse
column3: 栈口茶棚

column2: A tea shed at the edge of the open ground: a few bamboo stools, a brass kettle, and the old woman who pours is the guard A Gang's grandmother. With the guards turning everyone back from the mountain, she hasn't sold a cup in three months. A few rowdy soldiers ignore all that and come every day to drink for free and smash the bowls when they're done.
column3: 野地边一座茶棚，几张竹凳，一口铜壶，卖茶的阿婆是镖师阿岗的外婆。镖师有令不许外人上山，过路的人都被拦了回去，茶棚三个月没卖出一碗茶。几个兵痞却不管这一套，天天来白喝，喝完了还砸碗。

column2: The soldiers driven off, the old woman pours you each a bowl filled to the brim. She agreed to her grandson following Chief Lu, she says. 'In the earthquake year his mother and father both died, and it was Chief Lu who dug him out from under the fallen house.' She'll trade anything for anything; only Wantong silver she won't take.
column3: 兵痞被赶走，阿婆给你们一人倒了一碗，碗碗满到边上。她说外孙跟着陆镖头，是她答应的：「地动那年他爹娘都没了，是陆镖头从塌了的房子底下把他刨出来的。」她什么货都肯换，只是不收万通号的银子。

column2: Casket-Betting Flat
column3: 押匣坪

column2: On a flat at the mountain's foot, off-duty guards crowd round a gambling table betting on what's in the chief's casket: gold, a severed head, the emperor's jade seal, love letters from the chief's wife. The stakes are a day's rations. Mid-argument, red in the face, they're set upon by passing swordsmen who've spotted the coppers on the table.
column3: 山脚的平坝上，一群歇班的镖师围着一张赌桌，赌镖头匣子里装的是什么：押金子的、押人头的、押皇帝玉玺的、押镖头媳妇情书的，押注是一天的伙食。正吵得面红耳赤，一伙路过的刀客看见桌上的铜钱起了贪心，拔刀就抢。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the game goes on. You ask if anyone has ever seen the casket open; they look at one another. Ten years, never once. The oldest, Humpback Luo, has his bet on 'half a sheet of paper', and everyone laughs at him. Luo doesn't laugh. 'I steadied that casket for him once. Light as anything. Shake it and it rustles.'
column3: 刀客被打跑，赌局接着开。你们问有没有人见匣子开过，镖师们面面相觑：十年，一次也没有。年纪最大的罗驼子押的是「半张纸」，大伙都笑他。罗驼子不笑：「我扶过那匣子一回，轻得很，晃一晃，里头沙沙响。」

column2: Plank-Gate Stockade
column3: 板门寨

column2: At a dead end under the cliff, bandits have built a stockade whose gate is a dozen gallery planks nailed together. Old Gan is short of timber for the seventh break, and it's that gate he has his eye on. Hearing so, the bandit chief nails on two more layers and stands on the gate tower, hands on hips. 'Want it? Pay with your lives!'
column3: 死路尽头的崖脚下，一伙土匪搭了座寨子，寨门是拿十几块栈道木板钉成的。甘老凿修第七处断口木料不够，看中的就是这扇门。土匪头子听说了，又把门加钉了两层，站在门楼上叉着腰：「想要？拿命来换！」

column2: The bandits gone, the gate comes apart and the planks are carried out. Old Gan turns one over: a name is carved on the back, Zhang Sanfu; the next, Li Mancang; one name a plank. 'The Qianli men mended this stretch, one plank each, and carved their names,' the old man says. 'Then it fell, and this lot picked them up for a gate.'
column3: 土匪被打跑，寨门拆了，十几块木板背了出来。甘老凿翻过一块，背面刻着名字：「张三福」「李满仓」……一块板一个名字。「千里号的人修过这段路，一人修一块，刻上名字，」老汉说，「后来塌了，被这帮人捡去钉了门。」

column2: Ice-Carriers' Track
column3: 背冰道

column2: A crew of ice carriers works the mountain's foot, cutting ice at the snowline and carrying it down to sell to rich city households for chilling plum drinks. The ice caves lie behind the Snowline Post, and fearing the post will charge them if it reopens, they've posted hired fists on the road to beat anyone heading that way.
column3: 山脚下一伙背冰人，从雪线上凿冰背下山，卖给城里的大户镇酸梅汤。冰洞就在雪线驿的后山，他们怕驿站重开了要收钱，派了一伙打手守在路口，谁往驿站方向去就打谁。

column2: The fists scattered, the ice crew's boss squats down to reason: all they want is a living. Nie Xiaolou says the post won't charge for ice and will feed them a meal besides. The boss stares, then grins and has a block of ice brought over: frozen inside is a brass bell, the post's own. 'Cut it out of the ice cave last year. Yours again, as it was.'
column3: 打手被打散，背冰人的头儿蹲在地上讲理：他们只要条活路。聂小楼说驿站开了也不收冰钱，还管一顿饭。头儿愣了，咧嘴一笑，叫人抬来一块冰：冰里冻着一只铜铃，正是驿站的驿铃，「去年在冰洞里凿出来的，原样还你。」

column2: Snow-Pass Stone Gate
column3: 雪口石门

column2: At a dead end at the mountain's foot stands a stone gate, and beyond it the old post road from the Snowline Post into the snow mountains. Horse thieves have made it their hiding place for stolen stock, a whole hollow full of horses and yaks, guarded rank on rank by swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders. Nie Xiaolou says this is the gate his father led the Qianli people through.
column3: 死路尽头的山脚有一道石门，门后是雪线驿通往雪山的老驿道。一伙盗马贼把石门占了，当成藏马的地方，抢来的马和牦牛关了一山坳，刀手、弩手、骑手层层守着。聂小楼说，他爹就是从这道门带千里号的人上的山。

column2: The thieves scattered, the horses and yaks go home to their owners. On the old post road beyond the gate the snow is already knee-deep. A line of small characters is carved on the gatepost in Nie Xiaolou's father's hand: 'Twenty-fourth of the twelfth month. Passed here. All present.' Beyond lie the snow mountains.
column3: 盗马贼被打散，马和牦牛放回了各家。石门后的老驿道上，雪已经齐膝深。门柱上刻着一排小字，是聂小楼他爹的手迹：「腊月廿四，过此，人齐。」再往上，就是雪山了。

column2: Rice-Ball Cliff
column3: 吊饭崖

column2: On top of the cliff where He Sanqi is stuck stands a small stone camp, held by cliff crossbowmen and swordsmen who shoot at anyone climbing up. But tied at the cliff edge beside the camp is a thin hemp cord, hanging straight down to He Sanqi's crack, and on its end dangles an empty bamboo basket.
column3: 何三七困着的那面崖顶上有一座石头小营，守着一伙崖上弩手和刀手，见有人上来就放箭。可营边的崖沿上，系着一根细麻绳，垂下去正对着何三七的石缝，绳头上挂着一只空竹篮。

column2: The camp's guards scattered, you haul He Sanqi up on that very cord. He's gaunt, and still clutches his clump of dendrobium. The guards turn out to be Lu escort men who lowered a rice ball and a tube of water every night. 'The chief said: a man stuck on a cliff, keep him fed till the road reaches him.' They kept climbers off for fear the crowd would bring the edge down. He Sanqi bows towards the clifftop. 'Nine days in that crack, and every day I watched a man on the gallery opposite, a box on his back, nailing planks.'
column3: 守营的被打散，你们顺着那根麻绳把何三七吊了上来。他瘦了一圈，怀里还紧抱着那丛石斛。守营的原来是陆家的镖师，每天夜里往下吊一个饭团、一竹筒水：「镖头说，人困在崖上，先养着，等路修到这儿再接。」他们拦着不让人上来，是怕人多踩塌了崖沿。何三七回头冲崖顶作了个揖：「我在缝里九天，天天看见对面栈道上有个人背着箱子钉木板。」

column2: Yak-Raiders' Camp
column3: 截牛营

column2: A big camp on the open ground holds horsemen bought by Wantong to stop every yak heading for the Snowline Post with goods: with the post shut, the caravans from beyond the snows have to sell cheap to Wantong. By day the riders circle the open ground seizing any yak they see; they've robbed Ciren twice already.
column3: 野地上一座大营，是万通号收买的一伙骑兵，奉命截住所有往雪线驿送货的牦牛：驿站开不了，雪山那边的牦牛帮就只能把货贱卖给万通号。营里的骑手白天在野地上兜圈子，见牛就抢，已经抢了次仁两回。

column2: You break the camp and the plunder goes back pile by pile. Ciren gathers his drovers and turns the yaks towards the post. 'Once it's open, we trade for ourselves, no Wantong hands in it.' In the camp you find a Wantong notice: 'The Snowline Post shall never reopen.' Nie Xiaolou uses it to light a fire.
column3: 营被你们破了，抢来的货一垛垛还了回去。次仁把牦牛帮的伙计叫齐，赶着牛往驿站走：「驿站一开，我们自己换，不经万通号的手。」营里搜出一张万通号的告示：「雪线驿永不得开」。聂小楼拿去生了火。

column2: The Seventh Break
column3: 第七断口

column2: At the end of the open ground lies the seventh break: a line of empty post holes climbing the cliff for more than twenty fathoms, not a post or plank among them. At this end of the gap a small stack of posts and planks, carved with nines, is piled neatly under oilcloth. Mountain bandits are pulling the cloth off to haul the timber away and sell it.
column3: 野地尽头，栈道的第七处断口：崖壁上一排空栈孔往上延伸了二十多丈，没有一根桩、一块板。断口这头堆着一小堆木桩和木板，桩头刻着「九」，码得整整齐齐，盖着油布。一伙山匪正掀开油布，要把木料搬走卖钱。

column2: The bandits chased off, the timber is saved. Old Gan measures the gap: twenty-three fathoms, sixty-nine holes; one man carrying, driving and planking would need a year at the very least. 'He couldn't do it alone, so this pile has been sitting here waiting.' You roll up your sleeves: the mending starts here.
column3: 山匪被打跑，木料保住了。甘老凿量了断口：二十三丈，栈孔六十九个，一个人背桩、打桩、铺板，最快也要一年。「他一个人修不了，所以这堆木头一直码在这儿等。」你们卷起袖子：从这里开始修。

column2: Fir Wood
column3: 冷杉林

column2: In the forest, firs felled by the loggers lie every which way, and mountain riders have camped among them and built stables from the cut timber. The Snowline Post needs a new roof and Nie Xiaolou has come to buy wood, but the loggers say the riders have taken it all and they can't sell a single log.
column3: 林子里，伐木人砍倒的冷杉横七竖八躺了一地，一伙山马骑在林子里扎营，拿砍好的木头搭了马棚。雪线驿要修房顶，聂小楼来林子里买木料，伐木人说木头早叫马贼占了，他们一根也拿不出来。

column2: The riders driven out of the wood, the firs are dragged out one by one. The old logging foreman says the Qianli men felled timber in this wood ten years ago too, and for every tree they cut they planted a sapling by the stump. 'They're as thick as a rice bowl now.' He takes you to see: a row of firs, neat as a fence.
column3: 马贼被赶出了林子，冷杉一根根拖了出来。伐木人的老把头说，十年前千里号的人也在这片林子伐过木，伐一棵，在树桩边种一棵小树，「现在都长到碗口粗了」。他领你们去看：一排冷杉，整整齐齐。

column2: Welcome-Chief Village
column3: 迎镖寨

column2: From afar the people of a small village see you coming and rush out with gongs and drums, slaughter a pig, lay a feast, and hail you as 'the new chief'. It seems Chief Lu once told them that one day someone would fight their way up from below and beat his guards. But the village's own young guards won't have it: they block the feast and say you haven't beaten them yet, so no drinking.
column3: 野地上一个小寨子，寨民远远看见你们，敲锣打鼓迎了出来，杀猪摆酒，管你们叫「新镖头」。原来陆镖头跟寨里说过，有一天会有人从山下一路打上来，打得过他的镖师。可寨里的年轻镖师不认：一帮人拦在酒席前，说你们还没打过他们，这酒不许喝。

column2: The guards lose, fair and square, and raise their bowls to you. The village elder, well in his cups, clasps your hands. 'Chief Lu's getting old. That casket's too heavy for him now.' You tell him you aren't escort chiefs, you're opening a trade road. He bangs the table. 'Even better! The road was mended for traders in the first place!'
column3: 镖师们打输了，心服口服，端起酒碗敬你们。寨老喝多了，拉着你们的手说：「陆镖头老了，背不动那匣子了。」你们说你们不是镖头，是开商路的。寨老一拍桌子：「那更好！路就是给开商路的人修的！」

column2: Barley Granary
column3: 青稞仓

column2: Below the Snowline Post stands the barley granary where the post once stored grain, ten stone bins in a row. The chieftain's household troops have taken it, saying that with the post shut the granary belongs to the chieftain, and they sell barley at three silver coins a peck. The yak caravans can't afford it and circle outside, hungry.
column3: 雪线驿山下的青稞仓，是从前驿站囤粮的地方，十间石仓连成一排。一伙土司的家兵把仓占了，说驿站关了，仓归土司，青稞一斗卖三钱，牦牛帮买不起，饿着肚子在仓外打转。

column2: The troops driven out, the bins are opened one by one. Nie Xiaolou checks the accounts against the register, and the last entry reads: 'Qianli party borrowed twenty measures of barley, to repay next year.' Beneath it are newer slips, one added every autumn: 'Two measures repaid.' 'Two measures repaid.' Nine in all. 'Someone's been paying it back for them,' says Nie Xiaolou.
column3: 家兵被赶走，石仓一间间打开。聂小楼拿着驿簿对账，账上最后一笔：「千里号借青稞二十石，来年还。」底下压着几张新纸，是这几年每年秋天添上的：「还二石。」「还二石。」……一共九张。「有人在替他们还，」聂小楼说。

column2: From the troops' hoard: thirty measures of barley, twenty lumps of butter, a chest of brick tea, and the chieftain's command flag, which Nie Xiaolou takes to fly as the post flag.
column3: 抄出家兵囤的东西：青稞三十石、酥油二十坨、一箱砖茶，还有土司家的一面令旗，聂小楼拿去当了驿旗。

column2: Every time you pass, the yak caravans have left a load of butter and roasted barley flour for you at the granary. 'As long as the post is open,' says Ciren, 'we remember who opened it.'
column3: 每回路过，牦牛帮都在仓前给你们留一驮酥油糌粑。次仁说：「驿站开着，我们就记你们的情。」

column2: The Lu Escort Camp
column3: 陆家镖营

column2: A big guards' camp stands on the open ground with wooden practice posts and stone weights, and dozens of guards are drilling. Hearing that a hard-fighting company has come up from below, their drillmaster Humpback Luo calls everyone together, swordsmen in front, crossbowmen behind, riders on the wings. 'The chief said: if real fighters come, the whole camp goes at them together, and don't shame the Lu name.'
column3: 野地上一座镖师的大营，摆着练武的木桩、石锁，几十个镖师正在操练。听说山下来了一伙能打的人，营里的教头罗驼子把大家都叫齐了，刀手在前，弩手在后，骑手两翼：「镖头说过，来的人要是真能打，就全营一起上，别丢陆家镖的脸。」

column2: The whole camp beaten, Humpback Luo rubs his back and roars with laughter: first time in ten years he's lost so handsomely. Everyone in the camp, he says, Chief Lu took in one by one: children left homeless by the earthquake, porters who ran off from Wantong, two bandits gone straight. 'The chief says when a road falls, the people on it scatter too. Gather the people first, then mend the road.'
column3: 全营打输了，罗驼子揉着腰哈哈大笑，说十年来头一回输得这么痛快。他说营里的人都是陆镖头一个个收来的：地动没了家的娃娃、给万通号背跑了的背夫、两个金盆洗手的山贼。「镖头说，路塌了，路上的人也就散了。先把人收拢，再修路。」

column2: The Shelter Pavilion
column3: 风雨亭

column2: In a roadside shelter pavilion sits a wounded escort guard, his leg bound in cloth, surrounded by Wantong swordsmen demanding to know where the chief hides his casket. The guard clenches his teeth and says nothing, so they bend his fingers back one by one.
column3: 野地里一座风雨亭，亭里坐着一个受了伤的镖师，腿上缠着布，身边围着几个万通号的刀手，逼他说出镖头的匣子藏在哪。镖师咬着牙不吭声，刀手就一根根掰他的手指。

column2: The swordsmen chased off, the guard finally talks: the casket is never put down, the chief even sleeps with it on his back. 'Wantong think there's a snow tea recipe in it,' he laughs, gasping. 'The chief says what's in there is no use to Wantong. Wouldn't fetch a copper.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，镖师才松了口：匣子从不放下，镖头睡觉都背着。「万通号以为里头是雪茶的方子，」他喘着气笑，「镖头说，里头的东西万通号拿了也没用，换不来一文钱。」

column2: Bent-Bed Holes
column3: 弯岩孔

column2: Halfway across the seventh break the post holes suddenly stop: the cliff ahead is smooth, not a hole in it, and no telling where the line goes on. Wantong crossbowmen snipe from the opposite cliff and Shi Dun takes an arrow in the shoulder. Old Gan lies flat against the rock, feeling it inch by inch.
column3: 第七处断口修到半当中，栈孔忽然断了：前面的崖壁光溜溜的，一个孔也没有，不知道往哪里接。一伙万通号的弩手从对面崖上放冷箭，石墩肩上中了一箭。甘老凿趴在崖壁上，一寸寸地摸石头。

column2: The crossbowmen driven off, Old Gan points at the layers in the rock. 'The old builders only cut holes in this one bed of hard sandstone. The others are too crumbly to hold a post.' Follow that pale grey hard bed along and you see it arch up ahead, bent into a great curve like a carrying pole squeezed from both ends. The holes run along that curve, climbing on. 'The mountain was squeezed until it bent,' says the old man. 'So the road bends with it.'
column3: 弩手被赶走。甘老凿指着崖上的石层：「栈孔只凿在这层硬砂岩上，别的层太酥，吃不住桩。」顺着那道灰白的硬层看过去，它在前面拱了起来，弯成一道大弧，像一根被两头往中间挤弯的扁担。栈孔就在那道弧上。「山是被挤弯的，」老汉说，「路只好跟着弯。」

column2: Bear-Oil Wood
column3: 熬油林

column2: In a forest clearing, hunters have a great cauldron rendering bear fat, four or five bearskins hung beside it. They've strewn the woods with traps, and Nie Xiaolou's old yak has stepped in one and is bellowing in pain. The hunters say a yak counts as game and they'll boil it down too, and their crossbowmen already surround it.
column3: 林中一片空地上，一伙猎户支起大锅熬熊油，锅边挂着四五张熊皮。他们在林子里下满了兽夹，聂小楼的老牦牛一脚踩进夹子，疼得直叫。猎户说牦牛也算猎物，要拿去熬油，几个弩手已经围上了牦牛。

column2: The hunters chased off, the traps are lifted one by one and the old yak's leg is bound. Their boss grumbles that for ten years someone has sprung the traps in this wood: comes by night, gone before dawn, and stacks the sprung traps in a neat pile. 'Ruined our trade for ten years.' Nie Xiaolou looks at the pile: under each trap is a small wooden chip carved with a nine.
column3: 猎户被赶走，兽夹一个个起了出来，老牦牛的腿包好了。猎户头子嘟囔，这片林子的兽夹，十年来年年有人踩翻：夜里来，天亮前走，踩翻了还把夹子码成一堆，「坏了我们十年生意」。聂小楼看着那堆夹子：每个底下都垫着一块小木片，刻着「九」。

column2: The Mess Accounts Hut
column3: 伙食账房

column2: A small hut on the open ground belongs to the guards' 'accountant', an old guard missing half an arm, who keeps the whole camp's mess accounts. Bandits have seized his ledger, sure it records where the chief hides his treasure, and are holding a knife on him to make him read it out page by page.
column3: 野地上一座小屋，住着镖师们的「账房」，一个少了半条胳膊的老镖师，专管全营的伙食账。他的账本被一伙山贼抢了，山贼以为账上记的是镖头藏宝的地方，正拿刀逼他一页页念。

column2: The bandits chased off, the ledger comes back. It records every post, every catty of salt, every rice ball bought, year by year, and on the last page stands a single entry: 'Every autumn: two measures of barley repaid to the Snowline Post.' The old guard says, 'The chief's rule. Whatever the Qianli party owes, we pay for them.'
column3: 山贼被打跑，账本拿了回来。哪年买了几根桩、几斤盐、几个饭团，记得清清楚楚；最后一页单列着一笔：「每年秋，还雪线驿青稞二石。」老镖师说：「镖头的规矩，千里号欠的账，我们替他们还。」

column2: The Snowline Post
column3: 雪线驿

column2: The Snowline Post stands just below the snowline: stone walls, a timber hall, a tall flagpole, and before it the square where yak caravans down from the snows once traded with mule caravans up from the gorge. The post is repaired, but its gate still can't open: the chieftain's household troops camp outside, saying their master has taken Wantong money and will arrest whoever opens it.
column3: 雪线驿就在雪线底下，石墙、木楼、一根高高的旗杆，驿前的空场上，从前雪山下来的牦牛帮和峡谷上去的马帮在这里换货。驿站补好了，门却还开不了：一伙土司的家兵扎在驿前，说土司收了万通号的钱，这驿站谁开就抓谁。

column2: The troops scattered, Nie Xiaolou hangs the 'Snowline Post' signboard back over the gate and lights the lamp. Ciren's yak caravan is first through the door, unloading stone, salt bricks and wool and taking away ironware and tea: the Snowline Post is open again, iron for stone, twelve thousand catties a day. That night Nie Xiaolou writes your names on a fresh page of the register, then turns back to his father's line and looks at it a long time: 'To the snow mountain temple.' 'When the road's through,' he says, 'I'm going too.'
column3: 家兵被打散，聂小楼把「雪线驿」的大匾挂回门楣，点起了那盏灯。次仁的牦牛帮第一个进门，卸下石料、盐砖、羊毛，换走铁器和茶：雪线驿重开，以铁换石，一天一万二千斤。夜里，聂小楼在驿簿新的一页写下你们的名字，又翻到他爹那一行，看了很久：「往雪山神庙。」他说：「等路修通了，我也去。」

column2: Reformed-Bandit Post
column3: 洗手卡

column2: A guard post at the mountain's foot is kept by two old bandits gone straight, now in escort guards' coats but still talking like brigands. 'This mountain is mine... no, wait, this road the chief built! Want to pass? Fight first!' Their men, all former hangers-on from the old stronghold, are rubbing their hands.
column3: 山脚下一座镖师的哨卡，守卡的是两个金盆洗手的老山贼，如今穿着镖师的衣裳，说话还是山贼的腔调：「此山是我……不对，此路是镖头修的！要过去，先打一场！」两人的手下都是从前山寨的喽啰，一个个摩拳擦掌。

column2: Beaten, the old bandits grin and own up: they once tried to rob the Qianli caravan on this very road, and Chief Lu flattened their whole stronghold single-handed. 'And when he'd finished he didn't leave,' says one. 'He squatted down and asked us: can you carry timber?' That's how they came to follow him for ten years.
column3: 老山贼输了，笑嘻嘻地揭了自己的底：当年他们在这条路上劫过千里号，被陆镖头一个人打翻了一寨子的人。「打完了他不走，」一个说，「蹲下来问我们：会不会扛木头？」他们就这么跟了镖头十年。

column2: The Fair-Wind Banner
column3: 顺风旗

column2: A red banner reading 'Fair Wind' flies on the open ground: a big escort agency from outside the mountains, hired by Wantong to drive the Lu escort off this road. 'Escort work has one set of rules under heaven. What right has a wildcat chief to hold a road?' Fair Wind's men carry gleaming weapons and outnumber the Lu guards two to one.
column3: 野地上插着一面红旗，旗上「顺风」两个大字，是山外一家大镖局，万通号花钱请来的，要把陆家镖赶下这条路：「护镖的规矩天下一家，你一个野镖头凭什么占着路？」顺风镖局的人刀枪鲜亮，比陆家镖多出一倍。

column2: Fair Wind furls its banner in defeat. Their head escort is a reasonable man after all; hearing that Chief Lu has mended the galleries alone for ten years, he says nothing for a long while, then leaves behind the fifty iron spikes he brought. 'From one escort man to another. Give him these.'
column3: 顺风镖局被打得卷了旗。他们的总镖头倒还讲理，听说陆镖头一个人修了十年栈道，半天没说话，最后把带来的五十根铁钉留下了：「同行一场，这个给他。」

column2: Plank-Hoist Ledge
column3: 吊板台

column2: Halfway across the seventh break, the posts are in but the planks won't go down: each one must be hauled up from below, and there aren't enough winches or hands. The guard A Gang comes with a few young guards to look, and they draw and stand across the half-built gallery. 'The chief never said outsiders could mend this road!'
column3: 第七处断口修到一半，木桩打进去了，木板却铺不上：板子要从崖下一块块吊上来，绞盘不够，人手也不够。镖师阿岗带着几个年轻镖师来看，拔刀拦在半截栈道上：「镖头没说过外人能修这条路！」

column2: Unable to win, the guards sheathe their blades and help haul planks instead. A Gang is a fine worker and talks as he lays them. 'Ten years the chief's been mending, and he never let us near the seventh break. Said it was too dangerous.' By dark most of the seventh break is done. Shi Dun carves a name on the back of every new plank, and the first is yours.
column3: 镖师们打不过，干脆收了刀，跟着一起吊板子。阿岗干活是一把好手，一边铺板一边说：「镖头修了十年，从不许我们碰第七处，说太险。」铺到天黑，第七处修了一大半。石墩在每块新板背面刻一个名字，第一块刻的是你们。

column2: Drunken Wood
column3: 醉汉林

column2: On one slope of the forest every tree leans, this way and that, some trunks bent into hooks; the forest folk call it the Drunken Wood. Horse thieves camp in it, saying it's so eerie no pursuer will follow them in. Nie Xiaolou won't set foot inside: his father told him this wood walks.
column3: 林中的一面坡上，树全是歪的，东倒西歪，有的树干弯成了钩子，林子里的人管这里叫醉汉林。一伙盗马贼在林子里扎营，说这里怪，追兵不敢进来。聂小楼不肯进林子，说他爹讲过：这片林子会走路。

column2: The thieves are driven out of the wood. Nie Xiaolou was right: the whole slope is creeping downhill, the roots carried along with the soil while the trunks keep trying to grow upright, and so they bend; the worse the lean, the longer the slope has been moving. In the earthquake year this slope gave way and took a stretch of gallery below the post with it. 'We'll have to pile its foot,' says Nie Xiaolou, 'or one day it goes again.'
column3: 盗马贼被打出了林子。聂小楼没说错：这面坡在一点点往下滑，树根跟着土走，树干却总要朝上长，就长弯了；树歪得越厉害，坡滑得越久。地动那年，就是这片坡塌下去，带走了驿下的一段栈道。「得在坡脚打桩挡着，」聂小楼说，「不然哪天又塌。」

column2: The Plank Mules
column3: 驮板骡队

column2: A dozen mules are tethered at a gully mouth at the mountain's foot, wearing special pack frames for long planks: the Lu escort's plank train. Mule thieves have taken it and are changing the halters and cropping the manes to sell the animals beyond the mountains. The young guard who minded them is tied to a tree, still cursing.
column3: 山脚的沟口拴着十几头骡子，驮架都是特制的，能驮长木板，是陆家镖运栈板的骡队。一伙盗骡贼把骡队劫了，正给骡子换笼头、剪鬃毛，准备牵到山外去卖。看骡的小镖师被捆在树上，嘴里还骂个不停。

column2: The thieves chased off, the mules are claimed back one by one. The young guard says they were bought one at a time over the years. 'The chief said the Qianli caravan's old mule is too old to go down with the tea every year; if anything happened on the way, these would take over.' This year the old mule never came back and they thought it had fallen. You tell him it got the tea to the Gu villages. He breaks into a grin.
column3: 盗骡贼被打跑，骡子一头头认了回来。小镖师说这些骡子是这几年一头头买的：「镖头说千里号的老骡子太老了，年年下山送茶，路上出了事，就靠它们接班。」今年老骡子没回来，他们以为它摔了。你们说它把茶送到了蛊寨。小镖师咧嘴笑了。

column2: The Name Stone
column3: 记名石

column2: A great boulder on the open ground is carved all over with names, one above another. A masons' gang under Wantong orders means to chisel it smooth and carve the Wan family tree on it instead. A few escort guards defend the stone, outnumbered and already bleeding.
column3: 野地上一块大石头，石面上刻满了名字，一个摞一个。一伙石匠帮子奉万通号的命，要把石头凿平，刻万家的家谱。几个镖师守在石头前，人少，已经挂了彩。

column2: The masons chased off, the guards bind their wounds and explain: the names are those killed on this road in ten years, by falls, by rockfalls, by Wantong robbers. 'The chief carved every one himself.' There are forty-seven, the last still unfinished. Chief Lu keeps outsiders off the mountain, they say, because he doesn't want to carve any more.
column3: 石匠被打跑，镖师们包着伤口说，石头上的名字是这十年里被路摔死、被落石砸死、被万通号劫死的人，「镖头一个个刻上去的」。名字有四十七个，最后一个还没刻完。他们说，陆镖头不许外人上山，就是不想再往石头上添名字。

column2: Across the Gorge
column3: 隔峡望

column2: At the forest's edge the cliff across the gorge comes into view, and you see him: a dark-faced giant with an iron casket on his back, standing at the broken end of a gallery, one hand on the rock, the other swinging a hammer to drive a post into its hole. The blows carry across the gorge, one, then another. Wantong crossbowmen in the wood have seen him too and are drawing on that broad back.
column3: 林子边上，峡谷对面的崖壁正好露出来。你们看见了他：一个黑脸大汉，背上一只铁匣，站在栈道的断头上，一手扶崖，一手抡锤往孔里打桩。锤声隔着峡谷传过来，一下，一下。林子里一伙万通号的弩手也看见了，正张弓搭箭，瞄着对面那个背影。

column2: The crossbowmen scattered before they loose a single arrow. Across the gorge the giant stops hammering, turns, and looks your way for a moment. He says nothing, and turns back to drive the next post. 'That's Chief Lu,' Nie Xiaolou whispers. 'Ten years, every day like that.'
column3: 弩手被打散，箭一支也没射出去。对面的大汉停了锤，回过头，隔着峡谷朝你们这边看了一眼，什么也没说，转回去打下一根桩。聂小楼小声说：「那就是陆镖头。十年了，他天天这样。」

column2: Chain-Gang Road
column3: 押夫道

column2: On the open ground Wantong guards are driving a line of shackled labourers towards an iron mine beyond the hills. Among them is a white-haired old man who keeps shouting 'I know a Lu escort man!' and gets the whip for it every time. Hearing of it, the guards send Humpback Luo to see, but Luo doesn't know him.
column3: 野地上一伙万通号的护院押着一串戴脚镣的苦力往山外的铁矿去。苦力里有个白头发老汉，一路喊「我认得陆家镖的人」，护院就抽他一鞭子。镖师们听说了，派罗驼子来认，罗驼子却不认得他。

column2: The guards chased off, the shackles are broken. 'Five years I was held at that mine,' says the old man. 'There's a man there who's been held even longer and talks about Chief Lu every day. Name of Shen Liu.' Luo's face changes: Shen Liu is the man Chief Lu sent down to buy spikes ten years ago, and who never came back.
column3: 护院被打跑，脚镣砸开了。白头老汉说：「我在矿上关了五年。矿里有个人比我关得还早，天天念叨陆镖头，叫申六。」罗驼子一听，脸色都变了：申六是陆镖头十年前派下山买钉子的，再没回来。

column2: Wedding-Tent Gully
column3: 喜棚沟

column2: A small village sits in a gully at the mountain's foot, and it has rained for three days. A wedding is under way with pipes and drums, and local thugs are blocking the gate demanding 'wedding money', or the bride doesn't get in. Some passing escort guards stop dead: the stream in the gully has suddenly dropped.
column3: 山脚的一条沟里有个小寨子，连下了三天雨。寨里正办喜事，吹吹打打，一伙讨喜钱的地痞堵着寨门要钱，不给就不让新娘进门。几个镖师路过，忽然停住了脚：沟里的水一下子小了。

column2: The thugs chased off, the guards forget the wedding wine and bellow at the whole village to climb the ridges on either side. 'Not down the gully, up the sides!' No sooner are they up than a roaring mass of mud and rock comes down the gully and sweeps the wedding tent away. Their leader says the chief taught them: when a stream drops suddenly in heavy rain, something has dammed it upstream, and a debris flow is coming. The bride makes her vows up on the ridge.
column3: 地痞被打跑，镖师们顾不上喝喜酒，扯着嗓子喊全寨往两边的山梁上跑：「别往沟下跑，往两边！」人刚爬上梁，沟里轰隆隆冲下来一股泥石，喜棚冲得精光。镖师说是镖头教的：下雨天沟里的水突然变小，是上头堵住了，泥石流要来。新娘在山梁上拜了堂。

column2: Rockfall Bluff
column3: 落石崖

column2: At a dead end under a bluff, rockfall bandits keep piles of stones on the clifftop, and whenever someone passes on the road below they shove them over, then come down to rob the shattered party. The road beneath is littered with broken rock that the escort guards clear again and again, and it never stays clear.
column3: 死路尽头的崖下，一伙落石匪在崖顶堆着成堆的石头，崖下的路一过人，他们就推石头下去，砸乱了队伍再下来抢。崖下的路上全是砸碎的石头，镖师们清了又清，清不完。

column2: The bandits are driven off the clifftop and their stone piles tipped into the gully. But this bluff freezes and thaws every year and sheds stones by itself, so there's always rock ready up there to push, and it's easy money; another gang will be along before long, and all anyone can do is clear them out every so often. The guards put up a board at the foot: 'Falling rock. Keep moving.'
column3: 落石匪被赶下了崖，崖顶的石堆推进了沟里。可这面崖每年冻了又化，石头自己就往下掉，崖顶总有现成的石头可推，这营生来钱又容易，过一阵又会有新的一伙来占，只能隔些日子来清一回。镖师们在崖下立了块木牌：「此处落石，快走。」

column2: The Escort Kitchen
column3: 镖局伙房

column2: On the open ground stands a kitchen, woodshed, water vats and pickle jars all neatly in their places: the Lu escort's supply depot. Passing stragglers from some broken army fancied it, chased the cook out, and are carrying the grain away sack by sack, having dragged the wounded guards off their beds.
column3: 野地上一座伙房，柴棚、水缸、腌菜坛子摆得整整齐齐，是陆家镖的后方粮站。一伙路过的流兵看上了这里，赶走了伙夫，把粮食一袋袋往外扛，还把镖师们的伤号从炕上拖了下来。

column2: The stragglers chased off, the cook returns and the wounded are back in their beds. Half the depot's grain the guards grow themselves, the cook says, and half the villages below send up. 'The chief mends the road, so the villages send food. Ten years, never missed.'
column3: 流兵被打跑，伙夫回来了，伤号重新躺回了炕上。伙夫说粮站的粮食，一半是镖师们自己种的，一半是山下寨子送的：「镖头修路，寨子里就送饭。十年了，没断过。」

column2: From the stragglers' loot, what they hadn't yet eaten: eight sacks of millet, a side of cured pork, three jars of salted greens, and a basket of eggs they'd stolen somewhere else.
column3: 抄出流兵还没吃完的：小米八袋、腊肉一扇、咸菜三坛，还有一筐他们从别处抢来的鸡蛋。

column2: Every time you pass, the cook brings out a pot of hot soup with eggs poached in it. 'The chief's rule: anyone passing through has soup before they go.'
column3: 每回路过，伙夫都端出一锅热汤，汤里卧着鸡蛋：「镖头的规矩，从这儿过的人，喝完汤再走。」

column2: New-Gallery Toll
column3: 新栈卡

column2: With most of the seventh break mended, people walk the new gallery for the first time: salt carriers, shepherds, vegetable sellers, queuing to cross. A Gang's grandmother has set up her tea shed at its foot. Mountain bandits, green with envy, have put up a toll at this end, a coin a head, claiming they 'look after' the road.
column3: 第七处断口修通了大半，新栈道上头一回有人走了：背盐的、赶羊的、卖菜的，排着队过。阿岗的外婆在栈道口支起了茶棚。一伙山匪看着眼红，在新栈道这头设了卡，过一个人收一钱，说路是他们「看着」的。

column2: The bandits thrown off the gallery, even more people use the new road, and the tea shed sells three hundred bowls a day; the old woman can't stop smiling. Old Gan does his sums: at this rate, a fodder shop and a cobbler's at the gallery foot and the road will pay for itself. 'Open a road,' he says, 'and people come by themselves.'
column3: 山匪被打下了栈道。新路上来往的人更多了，茶棚一天卖出三百碗茶，阿婆笑得合不拢嘴。甘老凿算了算：照这样，栈道口再开一间草料铺、一间补鞋铺，修路的钱自己就挣回来了。「路通了，」他说，「人就自己来了。」

column2: The Fake Pass Stall
column3: 假路条摊

column2: A party of pilgrims bound for the mountain has been stopped on the open ground by 'pass sellers' who say no one may go up to the snow mountain temple without a pass, five taels apiece, and the temple turns away anyone without one. The pilgrims, old and young, can't raise the money and kneel begging. Swordsmen stand behind the sellers.
column3: 野地上一群朝山的香客，被一伙「卖路条」的人拦着：说上雪山神庙得有路条，一张五两银子，没有路条的，神庙不收。香客里有老有少，凑不齐钱，跪在地上求。卖路条的身后站着一伙刀手。

column2: The pass sellers chased off, their passes turn out to be fakes stamped with a seal carved from a turnip. An old pilgrim says the snow mountain temple has never asked for passes. 'Only, these ten years, more go up than come down.' Nie Xiaolou copies out his father's page from the register and asks the old pilgrim to carry it up the mountain.
column3: 卖路条的被打跑，路条是假的，盖的印是萝卜刻的。一个老香客说，雪山神庙从来不要路条，「只是这十年，上去的人多，下来的人少」。聂小楼把他爹那一页驿簿抄了一份，托老香客带上山。

column2: Erya's Fork
column3: 二丫岔

column2: At a fork on the open ground, a little girl in a guard's coat stands in the middle of the road, hands on hips: Erya, Humpback Luo's daughter, who has stolen her father's sword and insists on fighting you, because winning will make her a guard. Some Wantong scouts try to slip up the mountain by the other branch in the confusion; she spots them and holds off three at once.
column3: 野地上的岔路口，一个穿着镖师衣裳的小姑娘站在路中间，叉着腰：她是罗驼子的闺女二丫，偷了爹的刀，非要跟你们比一场，说打赢了就能当镖师。几个万通号的探子想趁乱从岔路溜上山，被她发现，一个人拦着三个。

column2: The scouts chased off, Erya sheathes the sword and asks if that counts as her winning. You say it does. She runs off delighted with the news, then runs back and hands you something: a brass key. 'The chief gave it to my dad to keep. Said if ever someone came who could beat the whole camp, give it to them.' The character for two is cut into its bow.
column3: 探子被打跑了。二丫收了刀，问你们她算不算赢，你们说算。她高兴地跑回去报信，又跑回来递给你们一样东西：一把铜钥匙。「镖头让我爹收着的，说哪天来了打得过全营的人，就交出去。」钥匙柄上刻着一个「二」。

column2: The Numbered Mine
column3: 号码矿

column2: At the far end of the open ground lies an iron mine under a Wantong flag, worked by press-ganged labourers chained at the ankle for years at a time. The overseer guards the entrance with swordsmen and crossbowmen, and hearing that someone has come for Shen Liu, he sneers. 'Looking for a man? There are only numbers in this mine, not names.'
column3: 野地尽头一座铁矿，矿洞口竖着万通号的旗子，矿工都是抓来的苦力，脚上拴着铁链，一干就是好几年。监工带着刀手、弩手守着洞口，听说有人来找申六，冷笑一声：「找人？矿里只有号码，没有名字。」

column2: The overseer chased off, the miners file out one by one, squinting at the sun. Shen Liu isn't among them: one miner says he made too much trouble and three years ago was taken alone to the deepest pit, 'guarded by Wantong's nastiest crew'. Every day, he adds, Shen Liu says the same thing: 'The spikes. I've still got the spikes.'
column3: 监工被打跑，矿工们一个个出了洞，眯着眼看太阳。申六不在这里：一个矿工说，申六太能闹，三年前被单独押去了最深的一个洞，「洞口有万通号最凶的一队人守着」。他还说，申六天天念叨一句：「钉子，钉子还在我这儿。」

column2: Halt Camp
column3: 止步营

column2: At the forest's end the gallery turns up the last cliff face. The Lu escort's main camp stands in the wood, ringed with black pennants, swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders drawn up in three bodies, and a board hangs at the gate: 'By the chief's order: go no further.' These guards are older hands than the ones below, and they watch you in silence.
column3: 林子尽头，栈道从这里折上最后一段崖壁。林子里扎着陆家镖的大营，黑三角旗插了一圈，刀手、弩手、骑手三路摆开，营门口挂着木牌：「镖头有令：至此止步。」营里的镖师比山下的老练，一个个盯着你们，不说话。

column2: The camp's guards fall back, and their grizzled leader takes the board down and turns it over. On the back, written long ago: 'If you can beat us, go on up.' The board has hung there ten years, he says, and today is the first time it's been turned. Above lies the last stretch of gallery, where Chief Lu keeps watch.
column3: 大营的镖师退开了，领头的老镖师把木牌摘下来，翻了个面：背面早写好了一行字：「打得过的，请上。」他说这块牌子挂了十年，今天头一回翻过来。往上，就是陆镖头守着的最后一段栈道。

column2: Windgap Stone
column3: 风口石

column2: On a windy gap in the open ground, Humpback Luo sits alone on a boulder drinking, a pennant planted behind him. The chief lets no one up, he says, so he stops them; and yet in his heart he's hoping someone gets through. Wantong stragglers are creeping up behind him, and he's too drunk to notice.
column3: 野地的风口上，罗驼子一个人坐在大石头上喝酒，背后插着一面镖旗。他说镖头不许任何人上去，他就拦着；可他心里又盼着有人上去。一伙万通号的残兵从他身后摸了上来，他喝多了，没察觉。

column2: The stragglers chased off, Luo hiccups and for the first time talks about the casket. Ten years ago at the Snowline Post, the two hundred and ninety-nine each pressed a handprint on one list. The chief tore it in two, gave them one half to take with them, locked the other in the casket and closed the second lock. 'Where the casket is, there am I. The day they come back, the halves go together again.'
column3: 残兵被打跑，罗驼子打了个酒嗝，第一回讲起那只匣子：十年前在雪线驿，二百九十九个人在一张名单上按了手印，镖头把名单撕成两半，一半让他们带走，一半锁进匣子，上了第二道锁：「匣在人在。他们回来那天，两半合上。」

column2: The Chief's Cave
column3: 镖头洞

column2: At a dead end at the mountain's foot is a cave, its mouth closed with a timber palisade: where Chief Lu has lived for ten years. The Lu escort's best troop guards it, and they say the chief is away and no one may look at anything inside.
column3: 死路尽头的山脚下有个岩洞，洞口拿木栅封着，是陆镖头住了十年的地方。守在这里的是陆家镖最好的一队镖师，他们说镖头不在，洞里的东西谁也不许看。

column2: The guards beaten, they let you look in: a stone bed, an old felt blanket, a pile of hammers worn blunt, and on the wall the sack that held three hundred gallery spikes, empty but for one. Carved on the wall above the bed: 'When the seven breaks are mended, go up and find them.'
column3: 镖师们输了，让你们进去看了一眼：一张石床，一床旧毡子，一堆磨秃了的锤子，墙上挂着装三百根栈钉的钉袋，空得只剩一根。石床头的墙上刻着一行字：「七处修完，上山寻他们。」

column2: Little Lama Slope
column3: 小喇嘛坡

column2: On the open ground a young lama down from the snow mountains, a scroll of scripture on his back, has been stripped of his robe by bandits and is shivering with cold. He has come down from the snow mountain temple, he says; the old lama sent him to take one look: 'Is the gallery road mended yet?'
column3: 野地上，一个从雪山上下来的小喇嘛背着一卷经，被一伙山贼扒了袈裟，冻得直哆嗦。他说他是从雪山神庙下来的，庙里的老喇嘛让他下山来看一眼：「栈道修通了没有。」

column2: The bandits chased off, the little lama gets his robe back. Nie Xiaolou shows him the nine pages of names in the register, and he reads them off one by one until he stops short. 'These names. They're all on the prayer flags at the temple.' The old lama only let him look, he says, and then he must go back; and off he runs towards the snowline.
column3: 山贼被打跑，小喇嘛穿回了袈裟。聂小楼把驿簿上那九页名字给他看，他一个个念过去，念着念着停住了：「这些名字，庙里的经幡上都有。」他说老喇嘛只许他看一眼，看完就得回去，转身就往雪线上跑。

column2: The Last Plank
column3: 最后一板

column2: Only the last stretch of the seventh break is left: the new gallery climbs from this end to just under the clifftop, and between it and the old gallery hanging down from above is a gap of exactly one plank, with the river hundreds of fathoms below. Wantong's last few men crouch at the old gallery's end, hacking at its posts: lay that plank and the road is through.
column3: 第七处断口只剩最后一段：新栈道从这头往上铺，铺到崖顶下面，跟上头垂下来的一段老栈道还差一块板的空，空当正对着几百丈下的江。万通号最后一伙人蹲在老栈道那头，拿刀砍着桩子：这块板一铺上，路就通了。

column2: The Wantong men are driven off the gallery and flee to the last man. Old Gan hands you the final plank: one of those taken from the Plank-Gate Stockade, a Qianli name carved on its back. You lay it and nail it down. A Gang jumps on it and stamps: solid. All seven breaks are mended. From the clifftop comes a single hammer blow, then silence. The man up there has heard.
column3: 万通号的人被打下了栈道，逃得一个不剩。甘老凿把最后一块板递给你们：是从板门寨拆下来的那一批，背面刻着千里号的名字。你们把它铺上，钉牢。阿岗跳上去跺了跺：结实。七处断口，全通了。崖顶上传来一声锤响，又停了：上头那个人，听见了。

column2: The Deepest Pit
column3: 最深洞

column2: At the mouth of the deepest pit in the mine stands Wantong's nastiest troop of guards, swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders. From inside a hoarse voice sings an escort's road chant over and over, breaking into coughs halfway through. Humpback Luo's eyes go red. 'That's Shen Liu. Twenty years he's sung that chant off-key.'
column3: 矿里最深的那个洞口，守着万通号最凶的一队护院，刀手、弩手、骑手都在。洞里传出一个沙哑的声音，一遍遍唱一首跑镖的号子，唱到一半就咳嗽。罗驼子一听，眼圈红了：「是申六。这号子他跑调跑了二十年了。」

column2: The guards scattered, Shen Liu is helped out, his hair gone white, a leather bag still on his back that he hasn't let go of in ten years: a hundred gallery spikes. 'The chief sent me down to buy spikes. I bought them, and on the way back Wantong took me.' He asks, gasping, 'How far's the road got? Does he still need spikes?' 'All seven breaks are through,' says Luo, 'but the railings aren't nailed yet.' Shen Liu shoulders his spikes and heads up the mountain faster than any of you.
column3: 护院被打散，申六被扶了出来，头发全白了，背上还背着一只皮袋，十年没离身：袋里是一百根栈钉。「镖头叫我下山买钉子，我买着了，回来路上叫万通号截了。」他喘着问：「路修到哪儿了？还要钉子吗？」罗驼子说：「七处都通了，可栏杆还没钉。」申六背起钉子往山上走，走得比谁都快。

column2: Horse Thieves' Camp
column3: 盗马营

column2: On the open ground is a band of horse thieves down from the snow mountains with the temple's horses, driving them out of the hills. Hearing that the galleries are mended, they're overjoyed: 'Down the galleries, we'd be out in a day!' They've camped at the head of the gallery, swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders across the road, to claim the new route for themselves.
column3: 野地上一伙从雪山上下来的盗马贼，抢了神庙的马，正往山外赶。他们听说栈道修通了，乐坏了：「以后从栈道下山，一天就出去了！」他们在栈道口扎了营，刀手、弩手、骑手横在路上，要占下这条新路。

column2: The thieves scattered, the temple's horses are rounded up and handed to pilgrims going up. A mended road, says Nie Xiaolou, is there for good men and bad alike. 'Is that why Chief Lu won't let anyone up?' He thinks a moment. 'But you can't just not mend a road.'
column3: 盗马贼被打散，神庙的马赶了回来，交给了上山的香客。聂小楼说，路修通了，好人能走，坏人也能走，「所以陆镖头才不放人上去吧？」他想了想，「可路总不能不修。」

column2: Wild Yak Ridge
column3: 野牦牛梁

column2: A herd of wild yaks, dozens of them, blacks out the road to the top of the galleries: down from the snowline for the winter. Hunters tried to shoot one for its horns and wounded a calf, and the herd has gone wild; now the hunters crouch behind boulders using every passer-by as a shield.
column3: 野地上一群野牦牛，几十头，黑压压地堵在通往栈道顶的路上，是从雪线上下来过冬的。一伙猎户想趁机射牛取角，射伤了一头小牛，牛群发了疯；猎户们躲在石头后面，把路过的人都当成了挡箭牌。

column2: The hunters driven off, the wild yaks slowly drift apart and open the road. Every winter, Nie Xiaolou says, the wild yaks come down from the snowline, and this year they're early. 'Heavy snow's coming up there.' He looks up at the snowline. 'If we're going to the temple, it has to be before the snow shuts the passes.'
column3: 猎户被赶走，野牦牛慢慢散开，让出了路。聂小楼说野牦牛每年冬天都从雪线下来，今年下来得早：「雪山上要下大雪了。」他抬头看看雪线：「上神庙的路，得赶在大雪封山前走。」

column2: All-Camp Barrier
column3: 全营关

column2: The last escort barrier at the mountain's foot: Humpback Luo, A Gang, Erya, Shen Liu, nearly every Lu guard is here. They haven't drawn; they sit in a ring. Luo stands up. 'The chief's rule: at the last barrier the whole camp stands together. If we can't stop you, we see you up.' Only then does he draw.
column3: 山脚的最后一道镖卡，罗驼子、阿岗、二丫、申六……陆家镖的人差不多都在这里了，他们没拔刀，围成一圈坐着。罗驼子站起来：「镖头的规矩，最后一关，全营一起拦。拦不住，就送你们上去。」说完才拔刀。

column2: The guards can't stop you, so they do see you up. A Gang carries the pennant, Luo helps Shen Liu along, and the whole band follows you upward. 'These ten years,' says Luo, 'what the chief feared most wasn't someone getting up.' He pauses. 'It was no one ever getting up at all.'
column3: 镖师们拦不住，就真的送。阿岗扛着镖旗，罗驼子扶着申六，一行人跟在你们身后往上走。罗驼子说：「这十年，镖头最怕的不是有人上去，」他顿了顿，「是一直没人上去。」

column2: Frost Gallery
column3: 冰霜栈

column2: The last stretch of gallery: ice on the cliff, frost on the planks. Bandits who slipped up in the confusion want to reach Chief Lu before you do: 'they say there's treasure in his casket'. Scrambling up the ice, one slips and takes a whole string of them with him, left dangling and howling off the edge of the gallery, and the rest turn and draw on you.
column3: 栈道的最后一段，崖壁上结着冰，木板上一层霜。一伙趁乱摸上来的山贼想抢在你们前头见陆镖头，「听说他匣子里有宝」。他们踩着冰往上爬，一个滑倒带倒了一串，挂在栈道边上嗷嗷叫，剩下的回过头冲你们拔刀。

column2: The bandits knocked off the gallery and the dangling ones hauled up and tied in a string, you reach the end: a stone terrace, and on it a man with an iron casket on his back, leaning on an old axe. Old Peng's woodcutting axe, ten years unreturned.
column3: 山贼被打下了栈道，挂着的那几个也被你们拉上来，捆成了一串。栈道尽头是一块石台，台上站着一个人，背着铁匣，手里拄着一把旧斧头：正是老彭那把劈柴斧，十年没还。

column2: The False Escort
column3: 假镖队

column2: On the open ground a party under the Lu pennant blocks the road, all in guards' coats, but they hem and haw and even make the salute the wrong way round. Humpback Luo sees through them at a glance. 'There's no face like these in the Lu escort.' They're Wantong men in disguise, hoping to pass as guards and get close enough to snatch the casket.
column3: 野地上一伙打着「陆」字旗的人拦住了路，个个穿着镖师衣裳，说话却吞吞吐吐，抱拳都抱反了。罗驼子一眼就看穿了：「陆家镖没有这几张脸。」是万通号的人假扮的，想冒充镖师混上去抢匣子。

column2: The false guards are stripped of their coats and tied up by the road. Luo takes back the pennant and says the chief has been alone up there ten years and hasn't had a proper conversation in all that time. 'When you go up, if he swings first, don't hold it against him. It's the only greeting he knows.'
column3: 假镖师被扒了衣裳，捆在路边。罗驼子把旗子收回来，说镖头一个人在上头，十年没跟人好好说过话：「你们上去，他要是先动手，别怪他。他就会这一种打招呼。」

column2: Post-Horn Ledge
column3: 驿号台

column2: At a dead end a stone ledge juts out over nothing, a slab pressed down on it with something underneath. Vultures squat on the edge and beat their wings at anyone who comes near, while treasure-hunting hill folk lie below it, wanting to lever up the slab and afraid of the birds. Nie Xiaolou says this is where his father used to rest when he guided travellers.
column3: 死路尽头一块向外探出的石台，台上压着一块石板，板下压着一样东西。几只秃鹫蹲在石台边上，见人来就扑翅膀；一伙捡宝的山民趴在石台下，想撬石板，又怕秃鹫。聂小楼说，这是他爹当年带路时歇脚的地方。

column2: The vultures driven off, the slab comes up: beneath it lies a horn post-trumpet, Nie Xiaolou's father's. Three words are cut on the underside of the slab: 'Keep the lamp lit.' Nie Xiaolou blows the horn, and the note rolls up the gorge towards the snow peaks. 'It never went out,' he says.
column3: 秃鹫被赶开，石板撬起来，底下是一只牛角驿号，聂小楼他爹的。石板背面刻着三个字：「灯别熄。」聂小楼把驿号吹响了，声音顺着峡谷往雪山那边滚过去。他说：「一直没熄。」

column2: Leeward Wall
column3: 背风墙

column2: Wind whips snow grains across the open ground. Deserters fleeing down from the snow mountains have robbed pilgrims of their food and camped behind a leeward stone wall. It's too cold to live up there, they say, and urge you not to go; when you won't listen, they try to take your mules to get down.
column3: 野地上风卷着雪粒，一伙从雪山上溃下来的逃兵抢了香客的干粮，在背风的石墙后头扎了营。他们说雪山上冷得活不了人，劝你们别上去；劝不住，就要抢你们的骡子下山。

column2: The deserters scattered, the food goes back to the pilgrims. Their leader, hunched against the cold, says he saw a temple up in the snows whose bell rings every evening, neither more nor less than two hundred and ninety-nine strokes. 'I counted three times.' He shivers and heads on down.
column3: 逃兵被打散，干粮还给了香客。逃兵头子缩着脖子说，他在雪山上见过一座庙，庙里的钟每天傍晚敲，不多不少，二百九十九下，「我数过三回」。他打了个寒战，往山下去了。

column2: Gallery-Top Flat
column3: 栈顶坪

column2: On the flat just below the top of the galleries, Wantong has spent its last money on a band of snow-mountain raiders, swordsmen, crossbowmen and riders in three bodies, to get up ahead of everyone and seize the casket. Their chief announces that if there's no treasure in it, he'll throw Lu Jiu in the river.
column3: 栈道顶下的空场上，万通号花了最后一笔钱，雇来一伙雪山马匪，刀手、弩手、骑手摆开了三路，要赶在所有人前头上去抢匣子。马匪头子放话：匣子里要是没宝，他就把陆九扔下江去。

column2: The raiders scattered, the flat falls quiet, and only now do you notice how many have followed you: Old Fan with his new rope, Zhou One-Tongue with a bundle of new tea, Old Gan and Shi Dun with their hammers, Nie Xiaolou with the post lamp, Humpback Luo with the whole camp. Nobody arranged it; they all came. 'Go on up,' says Luo. 'He's waiting.'
column3: 马匪被打散，空场上静了下来。你们这才发现，身后跟上来好多人：范老索拄着新篾索，周一舌背着一包新茶，甘老凿和石墩扛着锤子，聂小楼提着驿灯，罗驼子领着全营的镖师。谁也没约，都来了。罗驼子说：「上去吧，他在上头。」

column2: Cloudbreak Terrace
column3: 断云台

column2: The galleries end at a stone terrace hanging off the cliff, the river hundreds of fathoms below, the road to the snowline behind. Lu Jiu stands on it: dark face, grizzled beard, an iron casket with three locks on his back, leaning on Old Peng's woodcutting axe. Behind him, rank on rank, stand the oldest of the Lu escort, swordsmen, crossbowmen and mountain riders. He looks at you and says only: 'Ten years I've said it: no one goes up the mountain.' A pause. 'Beat me, and go.'
column3: 栈道尽头是一块悬在崖上的石台，台下几百丈是江，台后是往雪线去的路。陆九就站在台上：黑脸，花白胡子，背上一只铁匣，三道锁，手里拄着老彭那把劈柴斧。身后，陆家镖最老的一批人一层层站开，刀手、弩手、山马骑。他看着你们，只说了一句：「十年了，我说过，谁也不许上山。」顿了顿：「打得过我，就上。」

column2: Lu Jiu falls, leans on the axe a long while getting his breath, and laughs once. 'If you can beat me, you can walk the road up there.' With the road unmended, whoever went up could never come back, and anyone not strong enough to walk it he let no further. He unslings the casket and opens the first lock with the key at his throat; you hand him Erya's key and he opens the second. The third has no keyhole. He runs his thumb over it. 'This one isn't mine to open.' The lid lifts only a crack: half a name list covered in two hundred and ninety-nine handprints, and half a tea brick. 'They have the other halves. They're at the snow mountain temple, waiting for the road.' He shoulders the casket again and looks up at the snowline. 'The road's through. Time I went up too.'
column3: 陆九输了，拄着斧头喘了半天，笑了一声：「打得过我，上头的路就走得动。」路没修好，上去的人回不来；走不动的人，他一个也不放。他解下铁匣，用脖子上的钥匙开了第一道锁；你们递上二丫给的那把，开了第二道。第三道没有锁眼，他摸了摸：「这一道，不归我开。」匣盖只掀开一条缝：半张名单，按满了二百九十九个手印，还有半块茶砖。「另一半在他们手里。他们在雪山神庙，等路修通。」他把匣子背回背上，望着雪线：「路通了。我也该上去了。」

column2: The Store Hut
column3: 存料石屋

column2: At the top of the galleries stands a stone hut where Chief Lu keeps his stores: timber, spikes, grain, ten years' worth. Stragglers who came up in the confusion have broken in and are making off with whatever they can carry, and smashing up what they can't for firewood.
column3: 栈道顶上一座石屋，是陆镖头存东西的地方：木料、铁钉、粮食，十年攒下来的。一伙趁乱上来的流兵把石屋撬开了，扛起东西就跑，扛不动的就地拆了烧火取暖。

column2: The stragglers driven off, the stores are stacked again. On the wall hang a few old things, each with a slip of paper: a length of cut bamboo rope, 'Old Fan's rope, owed'; a bamboo tube, 'Tea terrace, nine years'; a gallery plank, 'Seven breaks, one'; the shade of a post lamp, 'Snowline Post lamp, borrowed'. Nie Xiaolou knows that lamp shade.
column3: 流兵被赶走，石屋里的东西重新码好。墙上挂着几样旧物，各贴一张纸条：一截断篾索，「老范的索，欠」；一只竹筒，「茶台，九年」；一块栈板，「七处，一块」；一个驿灯的灯罩，「雪线驿的灯，借」。聂小楼认出了那个灯罩。

column2: Searched from the stragglers: six bags of roasted barley flour, a packet of dried curd and two bundles of firewood robbed from pilgrims on the way up. What was the pilgrims' goes back to them; the rest is yours.
column3: 抄出流兵身上的：一路从香客那里抢来的糌粑六袋、奶渣一包、两捆干柴，香客的还给香客，剩下的你们收了。

column2: Every time you pass, there's a bundle of firewood and a pot of hot tea at the hut door. Nobody knows who leaves them, but a nine is carved on the bottom of the pot.
column3: 每回路过，石屋门口都放着一捆干柴和一壶热茶，不知道是谁放的，壶底刻着一个「九」。

column2: The Escort's Wares
column3: 镖局货担

column2: At the edge of the terrace at the top of the galleries, an old hand minds a carrying pole of goods Chief Lu has gathered: axes, a coil of bamboo rope, a few packets of snow tea. He's the Lu escort's steward and never trades with outsiders: the chief said no trade until the road is through. Guards stand behind him and step in front of the goods as you come up.
column3: 栈道顶的平台边，一个老伙计守着一副货担，担子里是陆镖头攒下的东西：几把斧子、一捆篾索、几包雪茶。他是陆家镖的管事，从不跟外人做买卖：镖头说过，这条路没通，买卖就不做。他身后站着几个镖师，见你们来，抱刀挡在货担前。

column2: The guards step aside and the old steward nods. 'The road's through. Now we can trade.' He opens up his goods, anything for anything at a fair price. This carrying pole, he says, the Qianli caravan left behind ten years ago. 'The chief said the first deal should be with whoever mended the road.'
column3: 镖师们让开了，老管事点点头：「路通了，买卖可以做了。」他把货担打开，要什么换什么，价钱公道。他说这副担子是十年前千里号留下的：「镖头说，第一桩买卖，要跟修通这条路的人做。」

column2: The Temple on the Snow Mountain
column3: 雪山神庙

column2: The Winter Stele
column3: 冬封碑

column2: The last plank of the gallery road is nailed into snow, and beyond it the sky suddenly opens: three snow ranges, north, south-east and in the middle, so white they look blue, and a high plateau rising gently underfoot, with butter and juniper smoke on the wind. At the top of the slope stands a stele carved with four words: NO CROSSING IN WINTER. Before it waits a line of temple warrior-monks, leather armour over their crimson robes, iron caps on their staves. Their leader says it is the Mountain God's rule: whoever wants to cross the mountain in winter must first get past them.
column3: 栈道的最后一块木板钉进了雪里，再往前，天一下子大了：北边、东南、正中，三道雪山白得发蓝，脚下是一片缓缓抬升的高原，风里有酥油和柏烟的味道。坡口立着一块石碑，刻着四个大字「冬不过山」。碑前站着一排护法僧兵，绛红袍子外头套着皮甲，长棍头上包着铁。领头的僧兵说，这是山神的规矩：冬天要过山的人，先过他们。

column2: The monks step aside rubbing their arms, and their leader even bows to you, palms together: 'If you can beat us, you can survive the pass. Those who can't, the mountain keeps.' On the back of the stele someone has cut a line of small characters with a knife. Snow has filled most of it; only the first two words can be read: 'Guard this'.
column3: 僧兵们揉着胳膊让开了路，领头的反倒向你们合十：「打得过我们，才走得过垭口。走不过的，山会把人留下。」碑的背面有人用刀刻了一行小字，被雪糊住了大半，只看得清前两个字：「护住」。

column2: Musk Deer Wood
column3: 麝香林

column2: The western wood is thick with mountain juniper, its branches bowed under snow. A little monk is tied to a tree, lips blue with cold, still murmuring sutras. A few musk-deer hunters stand guard over him with bows drawn: he cut every snare they had set and let three musk deer go. Oddly, the three deer have not gone far. They stand in a row at the edge of the wood, watching him.
column3: 西边的林子长满了高山柏，雪压弯了枝头。一个小喇嘛被反绑在树上，冻得嘴唇发紫，嘴里还在念经。几个猎麝的弓手张着弓守着他：他把他们下的套子全割了，放跑了三只香獐。怪的是那三只獐子没跑远，就在林边站成一排，眼巴巴地望着他。

column2: The hunters are chased out of the wood, and only then do the deer slip away into the snow. The little monk is Zhaxi, from the Hot Spring Temple. His bundle of juniper is tied with an old paper band printed with half of the character for 'thousand'. 'That's my master's tea paper,' he says. 'He has a brick of tea a Han man left. Ten years now, and he tastes just one mouthful a day.'
column3: 猎户被赶出了林子，香獐这才钻进雪里不见了。小喇嘛叫扎西，是温泉寺的。他背的柏枝捆用一条旧纸带扎着，纸上印着半个「千」字。「这是师父的茶纸，」他说，「师父有一块汉人留下的茶，十年了，每天只尝一口。」

column2: Kiln Flat
column3: 炭窑坪

column2: A row of earth kilns stands at the edge of the wood. They belong to the charcoal burners, and every temple and tent on the mountain gets through winter on their charcoal. A band of deserters has taken the kilns and fenced off the stacks: one basket of charcoal for one sheep. Families who can't pay burn dung, and their children cough in the smoke. The old charcoal burner has been put to carrying water, one lump of charcoal a trip.
column3: 林边一溜土窑，原是烧炭人的，冬天山上的寺庙和帐篷全靠这里的炭过冬。一伙逃兵占了窑，把炭垛围起来卖，一筐炭换一只羊，换不起的人家只好烧牛粪，烟熏得孩子直咳嗽。烧炭的老汉被他们赶去背水，背一趟给一块炭。

column2: The deserters scatter, and blue smoke rises from the kilns again. The old man says Lama Gonpo of the Hot Spring Temple has come for one stick of charcoal a day for ten years, never more, never less: 'One kettle, one mouthful of tea, that's enough.' He has worked it out: over three thousand six hundred sticks. 'That temple drinks its tea more sparingly than I burn charcoal.'
column3: 逃兵被打散，窑口又冒起了青烟。老汉说温泉寺的贡布喇嘛十年来每天来要一根炭条，不多不少：「烧一壶水，泡一口茶，够了。」他算过，十年三千六百多根，「这寺里的茶，喝得比炭还省」。

column2: You seize the deserters' hoard: forty sacks of good charcoal, a stolen copper kettle, two wolf pelts, a crate of army biscuits hard enough to crack walnuts, and a ledger of debts listing every family that couldn't pay. The old man feeds the ledger straight into a kiln.
column3: 查抄出逃兵囤的四十袋好炭、一口抢来的铜壶、两张狼皮、一箱硬得能砸核桃的军饼，还有一本赊账簿，记的全是换不起炭的人家，老汉当场把它塞进了窑里。

column2: Every time you pass, the charcoal families hand you a sack of charcoal fresh from the kiln, wrapped in felt and still warm, with a few roasted potatoes buried at the top: 'It's cold up the mountain. Keep these close.'
column3: 每次路过，烧炭的人家都塞给你们一袋刚出窑的炭，裹在毡子里，还热着，袋口埋着几个烤土豆：「上山冷，揣着走。」

column2: Sharing-Out Flat
column3: 分赃坪

column2: A band of horse thieves has just finished a job. The stolen horses are penned in the middle and the men sit round a fire sharing out the loot, shouting themselves red in the face. By the fire lies a map drawn on sheepskin: a small temple with a pool in the middle, and by the pool a circle with two words inside it: 'HAN TREASURE'. That temple is their next job.
column3: 野地上一伙盗马贼刚干完一票，抢来的马圈在中间，人围着篝火分赃，吵得脸红脖子粗。火边铺着一张羊皮画的地图，画的是一座小寺，寺中间一池水，水边画了个圈，圈里写着两个字：「汉宝」。他们下一票要干的，就是这座寺。

column2: The thieves are routed and the horses go back to the herders nearby. On the back of the map is the seal of Dorje, steward to the local chieftain: he hired them to fetch 'the treasure jar the Han man left' from the Hot Spring Temple, fifty taels on delivery. Zhaxi stamps his foot: 'Treasure jar? It's a tea caddy!'
column3: 盗马贼被冲散了，马群还给了附近的牧人。羊皮图背面盖着土司管家多吉的印：雇他们去温泉寺取「汉人留下的宝罐」，事成给五十两。扎西看了直跺脚：「哪有什么宝罐，就是一个茶罐！」

column2: Bath-Toll Bar
column3: 汤钱卡

column2: A pole bars the road to the hot spring, and a few yak riders sit beneath it: the chieftain's tax men, taking a 'bath toll' from everyone who comes to soak their frostbite. One lump of butter a person, one hide a yak. A few old pilgrims with rags round their feet have no butter to give, so they sit in the snow and wait, all day long.
column3: 往温泉去的路口横着一根木杆，几个牦牛骑守在杆下，是土司家的税丁，给每个去泡温泉治冻疮的人收「汤钱」：一个人一块酥油，一头牦牛一张皮。几个转山的老人脚上缠着破布，掏不出酥油，只好坐在雪地里等，一等就是一天。

column2: The tax men are tipped off their yaks and the pole is split for firewood. The last page of their tax book reads: 'Hot Spring Temple, ten years' toll unpaid. Pressed often; offered to take the temple's Han tea instead. The lama refused, saying: the tea is borrowed, it is not mine.' The old pilgrims limp off towards the spring, Zhaxi in front helping them along.
column3: 税丁被掀下牦牛，木杆劈了当柴。税簿最后一页写着：「温泉寺，欠汤钱十年。屡催，欲以寺中汉茶抵，喇嘛不允，云：茶是借的，不是我的。」老人们一瘸一拐地往温泉去了，扎西走在最前头扶着他们。

column2: The Old Uniforms
column3: 旧号衣

column2: A large band of highwaymen is out on the open ground, wearing faded frontier-army coats, patch on patch, swordsmen, archers and riders drawn up in surprisingly good order. They have just robbed a herders' pack train and are about to split the goods. Your leader barks 'Fall in!' without thinking, and half of them jump and snap to attention.
column3: 野地上一大伙劫道的，穿着褪了色的边军号衣，补丁摞补丁，刀手、弓手、骑手居然还排得有模有样。他们抢了一支牧人的驮队，正要散伙分东西。你们的领队随口喊了一声「列队！」，对面竟有一半人一激灵，啪地站直了。

column2: The highwaymen are scattered and the pack train returned to the herders. The old men who stood to attention say, red-faced, that they were soldiers of the Gravel Camp. Ten years ago an edict from the court disbanded the camp; five hundred men were turned loose where they stood, with no pay, and this was all that was left. Where did their commander go? They look at each other: 'He handed in his armour. Nobody knows where he went.'
column3: 劫道的被打散，驮队还给了牧人。站直的那几个老汉红着脸说，他们原是碎石营的兵：十年前朝廷一道旨意撤了营，五百人就地遣散，没了饷，只好干这个。问营将去了哪里，他们互相看看：「交了甲，不知去向。」

column2: The Bowl-Maker's
column3: 木碗铺

column2: Out in the open stands a bowl-maker's shop, its walls hung with bowls turned from birch burls, glossy with oil; a good one is worth a yak. Steward Dorje's servants block the door: the old bowl-maker is to make a hundred bowls for the chieftain's birthday, unpaid. He drove his knife into the bench and said no, so they have tied his apprentice to the doorpost.
column3: 野地里一间木碗铺，墙上挂满了桦木瘤子挖成的碗，油亮亮的，一只好碗能抵一头牛。管家多吉的家丁堵在门口，要老碗匠赶在土司寿辰前做一百只碗，一文不给。老碗匠把刻刀往案上一插，说不做，家丁就把他的徒弟拴在了门柱上。

column2: The servants are driven off, the apprentice untied, and the shop opens again. The old man trades his bowls for your goods and throws in butter for polishing them. He remembers a Han escort chief who ordered a bowl ten years ago, no bigger than a walnut, with a lid: 'He said it was for the lama at the temple. One taste a day. A bigger bowl and he'd drink too much.'
column3: 家丁被赶走，徒弟解了下来，铺子重新开张，老碗匠拿碗换你们车上的货，还附送擦碗的酥油。他记得十年前有个汉人镖头来订过一只碗，只有核桃那么大，带盖：「他说是给寺里的喇嘛，一天尝一口，碗大了就喝多了。」

column2: The Long-Life Tea Stall
column3: 长生茶摊

column2: A shed stands over the woodland path, piled with blackish 'tea bricks' under a sign: QIANLI CARAVAN LONG-LIFE TEA, ONE SIP, ONE MORE YEAR. The stallholder is a plump fake lama with a gang of bruisers in borrowed red robes, and no one passes without buying. An old herdsman has just bought a brick, taken a bite, and broken half a tooth.
column3: 林间小路上搭着个棚子，棚下堆着一块块黑乎乎的「茶砖」，招牌上写着「千里号长生茶，喝一口多活一年」。摊主是个白胖的假喇嘛，雇了一帮披着红袍的打手，过路的人不买就不放行。一个老阿爸刚买了一块，啃了一口，崩掉半颗牙。

column2: The bruisers scatter, and the 'tea' turns out to be pine bark pressed with butter. The fake lama confesses in tears: Lama Gonpo at the Hot Spring Temple is ninety, drinks a mouthful of Han tea every day and gets about better than anyone, so the valley says it's long-life tea. 'I only wanted a little of the shine.'
column3: 打手被打散，「茶砖」掰开一看，是松树皮掺酥油压的。假喇嘛哭着招了：温泉寺的贡布喇嘛九十岁了，天天喝一口汉人的茶，腿脚比谁都利索，山下都传那是长生茶，「我就想沾一点光」。

column2: Drolma's Tent
column3: 卓玛帐

column2: A black yak-hair tent stands in the open, and its mistress Drolma is trading insults with a band of yak riders from the next clan: they drove off twenty of her yaks in the night, saying her pasture had crossed the line. A nine-year-old boy stands in the doorway gripping a sling and shouting at the riders: 'I am Lu Jiu! Give our yaks back!'
column3: 野地上一顶黑牦牛毛的帐篷，女主人卓玛正跟一伙骑牦牛的邻部汉子对骂：他们趁夜赶走了她二十头牦牛，说她家草场越了界。帐篷门口站着个九岁的男孩，攥着一根抛石绳，冲牦牛骑大喊：「我是陆九！把牛还来！」

column2: The yaks come home. Drolma says her son is named after a Han man from ten years ago. He was climbing the mountain alone with an iron casket on his back, and rested one night in her tent. As he left he asked her to take a parcel of butter to the Hot Spring Temple every month: 'Tea wants butter. The lama drinks it alone; it'll be too bitter.' She has done it for ten years and never missed a month.
column3: 牦牛赶了回来。卓玛说儿子的名字是照十年前一个汉人起的：那人一个人背着铁匣上山，在她帐里歇了一夜，临走托她每月给温泉寺送一包酥油：「茶要配酥油，喇嘛一个人喝，太苦。」她送了十年，从没断过。

column2: Snow Wolf Gully
column3: 雪狼沟

column2: The snow at the mouth of the gully is trodden with paw prints, layer on layer. A snow wolf pack has denned here, and when winter starves them they come down on the herders' sheep and on pilgrims. Last year they brought down the Hot Spring Temple's old mule and dragged its saddlebag into the gully. The lead wolf has grey eyes and stands on a rock above you, perfectly still, watching.
column3: 沟口的雪地上全是爪印，一层压一层。雪狼群在沟里安了窝，冬天饿极了就下山，扑牧人的羊，扑转山的人，去年还扑倒了温泉寺的老骡子，骡背上的褡裢被叼进了沟里。头狼的眼睛是灰的，站在高处一动不动地看着你们。

column2: The pack is driven deep into the mountains. But snow wolves breed litter after litter, and when the snow lies deep they will come again; the herders have to clear the gully every year. In it you find the temple's saddlebag, and inside a little book in Lama Gonpo's hand, one line a day: 'Taste unchanged.' 'A little fuller.' 'Mellower.' Ten years of it.
column3: 狼群被赶进了深山。可雪狼一窝接一窝地生，雪一厚就又会下来，牧人们只能年年清一回沟。沟里找回了寺里那只褡裢，里头是一本小册子，贡布喇嘛的字，一天一行：「味如故」「略厚」「更醇」……写满了十年。

column2: The Drum Mound
column3: 更鼓墩

column2: A mound of earth stands in the open, and on it a great oxhide drum, kept by an old deaf soldier who beats the hours by the sun, one roll every two hours, and hasn't missed one in ten years. The local herd-owner's bullies say the drum frightens the yaks, and have come with clubs to smash it. The old soldier spreads his arms in front of it. He can't hear their curses; he can only see their clubs.
column3: 野地里一座土墩，墩上架着一面牛皮大鼓，一个聋了的老兵守着它，日头到哪儿，他就敲到哪儿，一个时辰一通鼓，十年没误过。附近牧主家的打手嫌鼓声吓着了牦牛，带着棍棒来砸鼓。老兵张开胳膊挡在鼓前，他听不见骂声，只看得见棍子。

column2: With the bullies gone, the old soldier tells you in signs: the last order he drummed was 'Strike camp'. That night the commander rode out alone towards the snow mountains, and came back on foot next day, with no horse and no armour. 'The camp isn't struck,' the old soldier says. 'The commander hasn't left, so neither have I.'
column3: 打手被赶走了，老兵比划着跟你们讲：他最后一回奉命擂的鼓是「撤营」。那天夜里营将一个人骑马出了营，往雪山去了，第二天走着回来，马没了，甲也没了。「营没撤完，」老兵说，「营将还没走，我就不走。」

column2: The Old Butts
column3: 旧箭场

column2: An old archery ground lies in the open, its row of target posts long bleached by wind and grit. A company of snow-mountain archers trains here, hired by salt smugglers to guard their loads over the pass in spring. They use passers-by as targets for fun: a hat shot off scores one, a sleeve pinned scores two. A shepherd boy stands frozen with a battered pot on his head.
column3: 野地上一片旧箭场，一排木靶桩早被风沙打得发白。一伙雪山弓手在这里操练，是盐枭花钱雇的，准备开春押盐过山。他们拿过路人当靶子玩，射掉人的帽子算一分，射穿袖子算两分。一个放羊的孩子顶着一只破锅，吓得不敢动。

column2: The archers are driven off and the boy drops the pot and runs. On the last target post a line has been cut with a knife, worn by the wind to the faintest trace: 'Winter, Dingwei year. By edict: strike camp, close the mountain. Huo.' The old soldiers say the commander carved it himself. The edict said close the mountain: let no one through.
column3: 弓手被赶跑，孩子扔下锅就跑了。最边上一根靶桩上，刀刻着一行字，被风磨得只剩浅浅的痕：「丁未冬，奉旨撤营，封山。霍。」老兵们说，那是营将亲手刻的：旨意里写的是封山，一个人也不许放过去。

column2: The Bone-Reading Rock
column3: 骨卦台

column2: A great flat-topped rock stands in the open, and on it a sheep's shoulder blade, scorched all over with cracks: the old diviner's reading stone. A band of snow-mountain archers has taken it and wants him to divine 'the best day to hit the Hot Spring Temple'. He keeps his eyes shut and refuses, so they toss his reading bones one by one into the fire.
column3: 野地里一块平顶大石，石上摆着一副羊肩胛骨，烧得满是裂纹，是老卦师的卦台。一伙雪山弓手占了台子，逼他算「哪天去温泉寺下手最好」。老卦师闭着眼不肯算，弓手们就把他的卦骨一块块扔进火里。

column2: With the archers gone, the old diviner rakes his oldest bone out of the ashes. Nine years ago in the second month, he says, Lama Gonpo came to ask for a reading: the tea had tasted bitter that day, and the lama was frightened. 'I burned the bone and the crack broke in two: the road is broken, the people are alive. Next day the tea was sweet again.' He winks. 'Truth is, a muleteer coming down the mountain had told me the day before.'
column3: 弓手被赶跑，老卦师从灰里扒出最旧的一块卦骨。他说九年前二月，贡布喇嘛来问过一卦：那天茶尝着是苦的，喇嘛吓坏了。「我烧了骨，纹断成两截：路断了，人还在。第二天，茶又甜了。」他眨眨眼：「其实是头天有个下山的骡夫告诉我的。」

column2: The Salt Trail
column3: 驮盐道

column2: Along the salt trail at the foot of the mountains, yaks carry blocks of salt down from the northern salt lakes to the Hot Spring Temple and the villages below. Steward Dorje has put a troop of yak riders across the trail to stop every load: anyone who brings salt to the temple is defying the chieftain. The head of the salt carriers squats by the road watching his blocks smashed one by one.
column3: 山脚下的驮盐道，牦牛驮着盐块从北边的盐湖下来，一路往温泉寺和山下的村子送。管家多吉派了一队牦牛骑堵在道上，盐一律截下：谁给温泉寺送盐，就是跟土司作对。盐帮的头人蹲在路边，看着自家的盐块被一块块敲碎。

column2: The riders are beaten back and the salt moves again. Dorje wanted to starve the temple into handing over the tea, the headman says: 'Tea without salt tastes like water. He thought the lama would give in.' He puts his whitest block in your cart: 'Take that to the lama for me. That Han man ten years ago gave us a piece of tea on this very trail.'
column3: 牦牛骑被打退，盐又驮了起来。头人说多吉想饿着温泉寺，逼喇嘛交出那罐茶：「茶里没盐，喝着跟水一样，他以为喇嘛就会松口。」他往你们车上放了一块最白的盐：「替我捎给喇嘛。十年前那个汉人，在这条道上也给过我们一块茶。」

column2: Warm River
column3: 热水河

column2: A little river steams through the open country. Snow lies deep on both banks, but the water never freezes, and hundreds of ruddy shelducks crowd onto it for the winter. A band of archers crouches behind the boulders on the bank, one arrow, one duck, for the chieftain's kitchen. Zhaxi is nearly in tears: the ducks are the Hot Spring Temple's guests and come every winter.
column3: 野地里一条小河冒着白汽，两岸积雪，河面却一冰不结，几百只赤麻鸭挤在水上过冬。一伙弓手蹲在岸边的石头后面，一箭一只，射了往土司府里送。扎西急得直掉眼泪：这些鸭子是温泉寺的客人，每年冬天都来。

column2: The archers are chased off and the ducks settle back on the water. The river runs out of the temple's hot spring, Zhaxi says: 'The water comes up from very deep under the ground, and it's hot down there, so it doesn't freeze even in winter.' The Han man ten years ago found the temple by following this unfrozen river: 'He said, follow the warm water and you'll find people.'
column3: 弓手被撵走，鸭子又落回了水上。扎西说河是从寺里的温泉流出来的：「泉水从很深的地底下上来，地底下热，所以冬天也不冻。」十年前那个汉人就是顺着这条不冻的河摸上来的：「他说，跟着热水走，就找得到有人的地方。」

column2: Hot Spring Temple
column3: 温泉寺

column2: The Hot Spring Temple is small: a few white-walled shrines round a steaming pool, where falling snow vanishes the moment it touches the water. Steward Dorje and his archers have the gate blocked and shout through it: hand over the Han man's treasure jar and they'll leave. By the pool sits Lama Gonpo, ninety years old, his eyebrows white, a walnut-sized wooden bowl on his knee with a few tea leaves in it. He doesn't look at the gate. He looks at the bowl.
column3: 温泉寺不大，几间白墙小殿围着一池冒热气的泉水，雪落进池里就没了。管家多吉带着弓手把寺门堵了，在门外喊话：交出汉人的宝罐，就撤兵。池边坐着贡布喇嘛，九十岁，眉毛全白，膝上放着一只核桃大的木碗，碗里只有几片茶叶。他没有看门外，只看着碗。

column2: The archers retreat down the mountain. Lama Gonpo brews one mouthful in the little bowl and gives each of you a taste: a dark tea that has only grown mellower with the years. Ten winters ago, he says, a Han man with an iron casket soaked his frostbitten feet in this pool for three days, and left this tea when he went: 'Taste it once a day for me. While the taste holds, we're all still alive.' In the caddy there is only a pinch left, the size of a fingernail.
column3: 弓手们退下山去了。贡布喇嘛用小碗泡了一口茶，请你们每人尝一点：一块黑茶，越放越醇。十年前的冬天，一个背铁匣的汉人在池里泡了三天冻伤的脚，临走留下这块茶：「每天替我尝一口。味不变，我们就都还在。」茶罐里，只剩指甲盖大的一撮了。

column2: The Chieftain's Ice Cellar
column3: 土司冰窖

column2: At the end of the open ground lies the chieftain's ice cellar, half sunk in the earth, icicles hanging from the stone lions at its door. Dorje's best men guard it, swordsmen, archers and riders, much fiercer than the lot at the temple gate. Zhaxi says most of what the temple has lost in recent years is in there: scriptures, a bronze bell, and a letter.
column3: 野地尽头是土司家的冰窖，半埋在地下，门口的石狮子挂着冰溜子。多吉手下最精的家兵守在这里，刀手、弓手、骑兵一样不缺，比堵寺门的那伙凶得多。扎西说寺里这几年丢的东西，十有八九藏在这里：经卷、铜铃，还有一封信。

column2: The guards fall back and the cellar door opens on a breath of cold. Frozen among the ice blocks are the temple's bell and scriptures, and a letter sent down from the mountain six years ago that Dorje intercepted, signed with the character Lu: 'Master Gonpo: if the tea runs out, it means those who come after have arrived. Please send them up the mountain.' Zhaxi tucks it inside his robe and runs all the way back to the temple.
column3: 家兵被打退，冰窖门开了，寒气扑面。冰块中间冻着寺里丢的铜铃和经卷，还有一封六年前从山上捎下来、被多吉截住的信，陆字落款：「贡布师父：茶若喝到了底，就是后来的人到了。请他们上山一趟。」扎西把信揣进怀里，一路小跑回寺。

column2: The Old Stables
column3: 老马厩

column2: A row of mud-walled stables stands in the open: the Gravel Camp's old horse lines, now home to a gang of yak rustlers whose stalls are full of other people's yaks with the brand marks sawn off their horns. The old groom has been kept on to feed them for one bowl of tsampa a day, and he secretly feeds his own bowl to the yaks too.
column3: 野地上一排土墙马厩，是碎石营当年的马营，如今住着一伙偷牦牛的牦牛骑，厩里拴满了别人家的牛，牛角上的记号都被锯掉了。看马厩的老马夫被他们留下来喂牛，一天给一碗糌粑，老马夫偷偷把自己的那碗也喂了牛。

column2: The rustlers are driven out and the yaks returned to their owners. The old groom points to the innermost stall. Ten years ago in the twelfth month, he says, the commander shut a man in there: a Han man with an iron casket on his back, who wanted to cross the mountain. 'The edict said close the mountain, so the commander locked him up here.' The man made no fuss at all, the groom says. He just sat against the wall with the casket in his arms.
column3: 牦牛骑被赶走，牛都还给了失主。老马夫指着最里头一间厩说，十年前腊月里，营将在这里关过一个人：一个背铁匣子的汉人，要过山。「旨意说封山，营将就把他关在这儿。」老马夫说，那人一点也不闹，靠着墙，抱着匣子，就那么坐着。

column2: Proclamation Slope
column3: 告示坡

column2: At the foot of the mountains Dorje's men are drawn up: shields in front, bows behind, yak riders on the wings. Dorje stands on a mound reading out the chieftain's proclamation, and after every line his men roar 'We obey!' But it's a long proclamation, and halfway through the back rank shouts too early and the front rank too late, so Dorje stamps his foot and starts again. He is on his third reading when you reach him.
column3: 山脚下，多吉的家兵摆开了阵势，前排举盾，后排拉弓，两边是牦牛骑。多吉站在土堆上念土司的告示，念一句，家兵齐喊一声「遵命」。告示太长，念到一半，后排喊早了，前排喊晚了，多吉气得跺脚，只好从头再念。他念到第三遍的时候，你们已经冲到了跟前。

column2: The men scatter and Dorje is hauled off his mound, clutching the proclamation and wailing, 'I hadn't finished!' Its last line is in the chieftain's own words: 'Bring me the Han tea, that I may live longer.' The chieftain is old and afraid of dying, Dorje says miserably, and he only wanted to please him. 'How was I to know it was a pinch of tea leaves?'
column3: 家兵四散，多吉被从土堆上拽了下来，抱着告示直嚷：「我还没念完！」告示最后一句是土司的原话：「取汉茶，献我延寿。」多吉哭丧着脸说土司老了，怕死，他就想讨个好，「我哪知道，那就是一撮茶叶」。

column2: The Half-Cooked Noodle Shed
column3: 夹生面棚
