column2: On the gravel flats stands a noodle shed, and its fat cook was once the Gravel Camp's cook. A band of archers has eaten without paying, saying his noodles are half raw, and smashed two of his pots. The fat cook is purple with rage: down in the valley his noodles were the best in the camp, but up on these flats they come out hard however he boils them, and he can't work out why.
column3: 碎石滩上一个面棚，掌勺的胖伙夫原是碎石营的厨子。一伙弓手吃完面不给钱，说他的面是夹生的，砸了他两口锅。胖伙夫气得满脸通红：在山下，他的面是全营最好的；一上了这滩，面怎么煮都硬，他自己也想不通。

column2: The archers are chased off. One of your people explains it: the higher you go, the thinner the air, so water boils before it gets as hot, and the noodles never cook through. The fat cook weighs his pot lid down hard with a flat stone to keep the steam in, and sure enough the noodles come out soft. The Han man locked in the stables ate his noodles once, he says, and told him: 'I'm not here to force the pass. I'm here to wait for people.' That night the commander sat up with him till dawn.
column3: 弓手被打跑了。你们里头有人点破：地方越高，气越薄，水不到那么烫就开了，面自然煮不透。胖伙夫拿平石头死死压住锅盖，憋住了气，面果然软了。他说当年关在马厩里的汉人吃过他的面，说：「我不是来闯关的，是来等人的。」那一夜，营将陪他坐到天亮。

column2: Saddlecloth Slope
column3: 鞍褥坡

column2: A troop of yak riders is lazing in the sun on an open slope, and their leader sits on a big tattered banner folded as a saddlecloth, its characters worn faint, its fringe bald. The old soldiers see it from afar and their eyes go red: it is the Gravel Camp's banner. When the leader hears they want it, he spits on it on purpose.
column3: 野地坡上一伙牦牛骑在晒太阳，他们的头领屁股底下垫着一块破旧的大旗当鞍褥，旗上的字被磨得模糊，边上的流苏都秃了。老兵们远远一看就红了眼：那是碎石营的营旗。头领听说他们想要，故意在旗上啐了一口。

column2: The riders are driven off the slope and the banner is pulled from the saddle. The old soldiers beat out the dust and spread it: in the middle one great character, Huo, and beside it a line of small ones: 'Gravel Camp, twelve years on guard at this mountain.' They raise it on a pole, and as it goes up an old herdsman down the slope actually salutes it.
column3: 牦牛骑被打下了坡，营旗从鞍上揭了下来。老兵们拍掉灰，把旗展开，正中一个斗大的「霍」字，旁边一行小字：「碎石营，戍此山十二年」。几个老兵把旗杆竖起来，旗一升起，坡下居然有放牧的老汉朝着它敬了个礼。

column2: The Prostration Path
column3: 磕头道

column2: On the pilgrim circuit at the mountain's foot an old man is making full prostrations: three steps, then down flat on the ground, a hard callus on his forehead. The way ahead is blocked by a band of 'temple guardians' in red robes but wolfskin hats, demanding a merit fee of one tael a circuit; those who can't pay turn back. The old man neither pays nor turns. He lies in the snow and keeps on bowing. They have their best men here, blades, bows and horses.
column3: 山脚的转山道上，一个老人在磕长头：三步一拜，五体投地，额头磕出了一块硬茧。道口被一伙「护法」拦住了，穿着红袍却戴着狼皮帽，说转山要交功德钱，一圈一两银子，交不起的往回走。老人不交也不回头，就趴在雪地里，一下一下地磕。他们最精的人手都压在这里，刀、弓、马，一样不少。

column2: The false guardians are scattered. The old man gets up and grins at you, two front teeth missing. He is Awang, and he means to walk thirteen circuits; this is his twelfth. Inside his coat he keeps one dry tea leaf Lama Gonpo gave him ten years ago: 'The lama said, taste it when you've done thirteen, and you'll know what waiting for someone tastes like.' He won't say who he walks for, only that when he's done he has 'something to hand back'.
column3: 假护法被打散了。老人爬起来冲你们笑，掉了两颗门牙。他叫阿旺，要转十三圈，这是第十二圈。他怀里揣着一片干茶叶，是贡布喇嘛十年前给的：「喇嘛说，转完十三圈再尝，就知道等人是什么滋味。」他没说为谁转，只说转完了，要去「交一样东西」。

column2: The Chieftain's Keep
column3: 土司官寨

column2: A stone keep rises from the open ground, seven storeys high, its windows barely wide enough for an arrow. Steward Dorje has fled, but the keep's men still follow his last order: no Han gets in. Yet at the top of the tower the old chieftain hangs out of a window, waving at you again and again, and his men keep pulling him back inside.
column3: 野地上一座石砌的官寨，碉楼七层，窗口小得只容一支箭。管家多吉跑了，寨里的家丁还守着他留下的令：汉人一个不许进。可碉楼顶上，老土司扒着窗口，一个劲地朝你们招手，被家丁一次次拉回去。

column2: With the guards scattered, the old chieftain comes down on his stick. He never wanted to live forever; he wants to make amends. Ten years ago on a night of snow, the Han man with the iron casket knocked at his gate half the night, and he didn't open it. 'Next day I sent men to look, and there was one line of footprints in the snow, heading for the hot spring.' He wants a taste of that tea, 'as if I'd let him in after all'.
column3: 家丁被打散，老土司拄着拐下了楼。他不是要长生，是要赔罪：十年前那个雪夜，背铁匣的汉人在寨门口敲了半夜，他没开门。「第二天我派人去找，雪地里只有一行脚印，往温泉去了。」他想尝一口那块茶，「就当是请他进了门」。

column2: Hot Pool Fair
column3: 热水塘集

column2: Below the hot spring lies Hot Pool, the only market for a hundred miles that stays open in winter: herders bring gold dust washed from the river and trade it for stone from the valleys to build pens and line the bathing pools. Now a band of snow-mountain archers holds the entrance. They call themselves the Masters of the Scales: all gold dust weighed at seventy parts in a hundred, a toll on every load of stone. Last year's flood broke the bathing pools, and no one has been able to afford the repair since.
column3: 温泉下游的热水塘是方圆百里唯一冬天不封的集市：牧人背来河里淘的金沙，换山下的石料，修羊圈，砌浴池。如今集口被一伙雪山弓手占着，他们自称「秤主」，金沙过秤一律七折，石料要另交过路钱。去年发大水冲垮了浴池，到现在也没人修得起。

column2: The Masters of the Scales are driven off, the market scales hung up again, and the trade of stone for gold opens. By evening the herders have rebuilt a corner of the bathing pool wall. For the first time in ten years Lama Gonpo comes down to the fair. He opens the caddy, takes a few leaves from the last pinch, and brews them for the old chieftain, who weeps as he drinks. Then the lama snaps the lid shut: 'The rest goes up the mountain.' He means to come with you. Zhaxi tugs frantically at his sleeve. His master is ninety.
column3: 「秤主」被赶跑，官秤重新挂上，石换金的买卖开了张，牧人们当天就把浴池的墙垒起了一角。贡布喇嘛十年来头一回下山赶集，捧着茶罐，把最后那一撮分出一点，泡给老土司尝了。老土司喝完，掉了眼泪。喇嘛把罐盖一扣：「剩下的，带上山去。」他要跟你们一起走。扎西急得直拽他袖子：师父九十岁了。

column2: The Empty Granary
column3: 空粮仓

column2: The Gravel Camp's old granary stands in the open. Salt smugglers have turned it into a salt store, stacked with contraband, with swordsmen at the door. Afraid of being seen, they have plastered over every mark on the walls. The old soldier who kept the granary says the walls held the camp's accounts for its last winter, and with them plastered over, no one will ever know what happened that winter.
column3: 野地里碎石营的旧粮仓，一伙盐枭把它改成了盐库，仓里码满了私盐，门口站着刀手。他们怕人看见，把仓墙上的字全拿泥糊上了。看仓的老兵说墙上记的是营里最后一个冬天的账，糊了，就再没人知道那年冬天的事了。

column2: The smugglers are driven off and their salt confiscated, and you wash the mud from the walls bit by bit. The last line, in charcoal, reads: 'Twelfth month, twenty-third day. Stables opened, one man let up the mountain. Grain two pecks, charcoal ten catties, paid by the commander himself.' The old soldiers stare at it a long time, and none of them speaks. Their commander had defied the edict.
column3: 盐枭被赶走，私盐充了公，你们拿水把墙上的泥一点点洗掉。最后一行炭字写着：「腊月廿三，开马厩，放一人上山。粮二斗，炭十斤，营将自出。」老兵们看了半天，谁也没说话。营将抗了旨。

column2: One-Ear's Forge
column3: 独耳掌

column2: Out in the open a troop of a herd-owner's yak riders is beating an old man with one ear, calling him a horse thief. He does steal horses, it's true, but only ones with badly set shoes. He leads them home, shoes them properly, and sneaks them back the next night. Their owners wake up to horses walking better than before, and don't know whether to be angry.
column3: 野地上，一伙牧主家的牦牛骑正围着一个独耳朵的老头打，说他偷马。老头确实偷马，可偷的都是掌钉得歪七扭八的马，牵回窝里重钉一副好掌，第二天夜里再悄悄送回去。失主们早上起来一看，马走得比原先还稳，又气又说不出话。

column2: The riders are scattered. One-Ear was the Gravel Camp's farrier, and it was he who took the locked-up Han man his meals. The man took half a sheet of paper from his casket and showed it to the commander, he says, covered in names: 'There are more coming over this mountain behind me. Close it, and they'll die at its foot.' The commander studied it all night, and next morning opened the stable door.
column3: 牦牛骑被打散了。独耳是碎石营当年的掌钉匠，营将关那汉人的那几天，是他去送的饭。他说那汉人从匣里取出半张纸给营将看，密密麻麻全是名字：「后头还有人要过这座山。你封了山，他们就死在山下。」营将看了一夜，第二天就开了马厩。

column2: The Testing Staves
column3: 试山棍

column2: On the gravel flats a squad of temple warrior-monks has stopped a pack train that wants to cross the mountain, and is testing them one by one: beat a monk and you pass; lose and you turn back. The pack men curse them for bullies, and the monks don't argue, only plant their iron-capped staves in the gravel. When your turn comes, the leading monk turns his staff crosswise.
column3: 碎石滩上，一队护法僧兵拦着一支想过山的驮队，一个个比试过去：赢一个，过一个；输了的，掉头回去。驮队的人骂他们欺负人，僧兵也不辩，只把包铁的长棍往碎石里一戳。轮到你们，领头的僧兵把棍子横了过来。

column2: The monks lower their staves and let the pack train through with you. 'No crossing in winter' doesn't mean no one crosses, their leader says. It means you must beat them first: 'Anyone who can't beat us would freeze to death on the col anyway.' The Mountain God made the rule nine years ago. It began as an edict closing the mountain, and the god turned it into a trial: 'We close the mountain only to those who'd die on it.'
column3: 僧兵们收了棍，放驮队和你们一起过去。领头的说，「冬不过山」不是不让过，是要打得过他们才能过：「打不过我们的，过了垭口也是冻死。」这规矩是山神九年前定的，原本是一道封山的旨意，山神把它改成了一场比试：「封山，封的是送死的人。」

column2: The Buried Camp
column3: 雪埋营

column2: At the foot of the mountains lies a slumped slope of snow. Nine years ago an avalanche buried a whole herders' winter camp beneath it. Now a gang of outsiders is digging here, blades in front, bows on watch, riders to carry the spoil, after the silver and coral on the dead. Zhaxi stands at the bottom of the slope and says nothing. His master told him this is where he was dug out.
column3: 山脚下有一片塌下去的雪坡，九年前一场雪崩把一整个牧人的冬营埋在了底下。如今一伙扒坟的外来客在这里挖，刀手开路，弓手放哨，骑手驮货，专挖死人身上的银饰和珊瑚。扎西站在坡下，一句话也不说。师父告诉过他，他就是在这里被挖出来的。

column2: The grave-robbers are chased off and their pits filled in again. At the foot of the slope half a wooden cradle shows through, a little bronze bell tied to its handle. Zhaxi unties the bell and shakes it; it rings dully. That winter, Lama Gonpo says, only one baby lived out of the whole camp: 'A man in a mask dug him out of the snow. He dug for a day and a night.'
column3: 扒坟客被打跑了，挖开的坑一个个重新填上。坡下露出半只木摇篮，摇篮把手上拴着一只铜铃。扎西把铃解下来，摇了摇，铃声闷闷的。贡布喇嘛说，那年整个冬营只活下来一个娃娃，「是一个戴面具的人从雪里刨出来的，刨了一天一夜」。

column2: Avalanche Mouth
column3: 雪崩口

column2: The pilgrim circuit at the mountain's foot has been cut by a fresh avalanche. A gang of 'road bosses' got there first and dug a narrow passage through the snow, and now they stand at both ends charging a lump of silver a head; anyone who won't pay can climb over the debris. Awang is on his thirteenth circuit, prostrate before the snow, his forehead bleeding, while they stand by laughing to see how he'll get over.
column3: 转山道在山脚被一场新雪崩截断了。一伙「路把头」抢先在雪里挖出一条窄道，守在两头收钱，一个人一块银子，不给的就从雪崩堆上爬。阿旺转到了第十三圈，趴在雪堆前，额头磕得出了血，他们还在一旁笑，看他怎么爬过去。

column2: The road bosses are driven off, and the passage is free to all. Awang sits on the snow heap to catch his breath, and at last tells you: he deserted from the Gravel Camp. The night the drum beat 'Strike camp' ten years ago he was the first to run, and only heard later that the commander hadn't gone, but stayed behind alone. 'I ran. The commander didn't.' He wipes the blood from his forehead. 'These thirteen circuits are for him.'
column3: 路把头被赶走了，窄道白给人走。阿旺坐在雪堆上喘气，这才说出来：他是碎石营的逃兵。十年前擂「撤营」那夜，他第一个跑了，后来才听说营将没走，一个人留了下来。「我跑了，营将没跑。」他擦掉额头的血，「这十三圈，是替营将转的。」

column2: The Boundary Posts
column3: 草场界桩

column2: A row of newly driven boundary posts cuts across the open ground, fencing in the pasture the buried camp left behind. A great herd-owner's guards stand over them and seize any beast that strays across. Had Zhaxi's father lived, this pasture would have been his. Lama Gonpo hobbles up to the posts on his stick; the guards raise their blades but dare not really strike a ninety-year-old lama, so they shout for you to settle it.
column3: 野地上一排新钉的界桩，把雪埋营留下的草场圈了进去。一个大牧主的护院守着界桩，谁的牛羊过界就扣下。扎西的老阿爸要是还在，这片草场本该是他家的。贡布喇嘛拄着拐走到界桩前，护院们举起了刀，又不敢真砍一个九十岁的喇嘛，只好喊你们来评理。

column2: The guards are scattered and the posts pulled up. The herd-owner's oldest herdsman comes running: he was on the slope the night of the avalanche. A man in a mask dug in the snow for a day and a night until his hands bled, and at last lifted out a baby, tucked it inside his coat and walked off towards the Hot Spring Temple without a word. 'He smelled of tea.'
column3: 护院被打散，界桩拔了。牧主家最老的牧人跑来说，雪崩那夜他就在坡上：一个戴面具的人在雪里刨了一天一夜，手刨出了血，最后抱出一个娃娃，揣在怀里往温泉寺走了，一句话没说。「那人身上，有一股茶味。」

column2: The Lone Beacon
column3: 孤烽墩

column2: A lone beacon tower stands on the gravel flats, the Gravel Camp's old signal post. A band of the salt smugglers' archers squats on top keeping watch for the contraband trains, loosing a whistling arrow whenever someone shows on the horizon. Under the tower lies a pile of beacon logs, torn up for kindling, burned down to the last few pages.
column3: 碎石滩上一座孤零零的烽墩，是碎石营的旧烽火台。一伙盐枭的弓手蹲在墩顶放哨，替私盐驮队望风，看见远处有人就放一支响箭。墩底下压着一摞烽火簿，被他们撕了引火，烧得只剩最后几页。

column2: The archers are driven down from the tower. The last surviving page reads: 'Day of striking camp: no beacon lit. Next night: one beacon, towards the mountain, lit by the commander himself.' That was a message to the temple on the snow mountain, the old soldiers say: someone is coming up, come down to meet him. And that night, sure enough, a lamp shone on the mountain, for a long time.
column3: 弓手被赶下了墩。烧剩的最后一页写着：「撤营之日，烽不举。次夜，营将亲举一烽，向山。」老兵们说，那是给雪山上的庙报信：有人要上山，下来接。那一夜，山上果然亮起一盏灯，亮了很久。

column2: Gravel Camp
column3: 碎石营

column2: A ring of stone walls stands at the mountain's foot, built of stones from the gravel flats: this is the Gravel Camp. Its gate stands open and a band of horse thieves has made it home; the commander's great tent is now their leader's horse pen. The old soldiers who have come with you stand at the gate, and none of them will go in first, as if afraid someone inside might call the roll.
column3: 山脚下一圈石墙，墙是拿碎石滩上的石头垒的，这就是碎石营。营门大开，一伙盗马贼在营里安了家，营将的大帐成了他们头领的马圈。几个跟着你们来的老兵站在营门口，谁也不肯先进去，像是怕营里有人点名。

column2: The horse thieves are thrown out. In the great tent an empty armour stand still stands, and the ground beneath it is swept clean, as if someone comes every month to sweep it. The last page of the camp book is in the commander's hand: 'Commander Huo Shan lays down his armour. The camp may be struck. The man stays.' The old soldiers press their thumbprints in the book one by one, and only then dare to sit down in the tent.
column3: 盗马贼被赶了出去。大帐里一个空甲架还立着，架下的地扫得干干净净，像是每个月都有人来扫。营簿最后一页是营将的字：「营将霍山，去甲。营可撤，人不走。」老兵们挨个在营簿上按了手印，按完了，才敢在帐里坐下。

column2: The Felt-Maker's Yard
column3: 毡匠院

column2: Out in the open is a felt-maker's yard hung with white felts. A gang of gamblers has made it their gambling den, rolling dice on felts spread on the ground and burning holes in them with their pipes. Zhaxi has always kept an old piece of felt inside his robe, the one he was wrapped in as a baby, and wants the old felt-maker to look at it. The gamblers find him in the way and shove him into a snowdrift.
column3: 野地里一个擀毡的院子，院里晾满了白毡。一伙赌徒占了院子当赌场，把毡子铺在地上掷骰子，烟锅烫出一个个窟窿。扎西怀里一直揣着一块旧毡，是他当年被裹着的那块，想请老毡匠认一认，赌徒们嫌他碍事，一把把他推进了雪堆。

column2: The gamblers are thrown out. The old felt-maker turns the old felt over in his hands for a long time. The felt is local, but the knots at its four corners are not. 'That's an escort's knot. Only Han escort men tie it that way; the harder you pull, the tighter it holds, and it won't come loose even if you fall off a cliff.' He hands it back to Zhaxi: 'Whoever wrapped you was an escort man.'
column3: 赌徒被轰了出去。老毡匠捏着那块旧毡看了半天：毡是藏地的毡，可四角的绳结不是。「这叫镖扣，汉人走镖的才这么打，越拽越紧，摔下山崖也散不开。」他把毡还给扎西：「裹你的人，是个走镖的。」

column2: Impostor's Slope
column3: 冒名坡

column2: At a fork below the mountains, a band of yak-riding thugs is pinning a half-grown boy against a rock, a branding iron glowing red. The boy runs a tea stall at the crossroads, his bricks stamped 'Qianli'. The thugs, hired by a lowland tea house, say he is a fraud and mean to burn 'FAKE' into his cheek. The boy shouts, “I am Zhou Qi of the Qianli!” The thugs howl with laughter: Zhou Qi of the Qianli would be forty by now.
column3: 山脚的岔路口，一伙骑牦牛的打手揪着一个半大孩子的领子往石头上按，手里的烙铁烧得通红。孩子在路口摆了个茶摊，茶砖上盖着「千里号」的戳子。打手们是山下一家茶号雇来的，说他冒名，要在他脸上烙个「假」字。孩子梗着脖子喊：「我就是千里号的周七！」打手们笑得前仰后合：千里号的周七，少说也四十了。

column2: The thugs scatter and the iron hisses in the snow. The boy is thirteen, a shepherd, with a polished birch tag round his neck: 'Qianli, tea train, Zhou Qi', a grown man's handprint burned into the back. “The real Zhou Qi hung it on me the day he left,” he says. “He lent me the name and asked me to mind the stall.” The temple fair is close, and he has a stall to open.
column3: 打手被打散，烙铁扔进了雪里。孩子十三岁，是个放羊娃，脖子上挂着一块磨亮的桦木腰牌：「千里号·茶队·周七」，背面烙着一个大人的手印。「真周七走的那天把它挂在我脖子上，」他说，「名字借我，摊子替他看着。」庙会快到了，他得赶去出摊。

column2: The Barley Terraces
column3: 屯田坝

column2: Out in the open lies a field of highland barley, the Gravel Camp's old military farm. The camp is gone but the fields remain, worked by soldiers' families who never left in ten years. An outsider with a gang of bullies has taken the threshing floor, claiming the land has no owner and half the harvest is his, or he'll burn it. A grey-haired woman stands before the grain with a flail raised, saying nothing.
column3: 野地里一片青稞地，是碎石营当年屯的田，营散了，地还在，种地的是些兵的家眷，十年没走。一个外来的地头带着打手占了打谷场，说地是无主的，收的青稞一半归他，不给就烧场。一个头发花白的妇人举着连枷挡在谷堆前，一声不吭。

column2: The bullies are driven off and the flails ring on the threshing floor again. The grey-haired woman says that every harvest an old yak herder comes to help with the reaping. He never says a word and leaves when it's done. 'He reaps faster than anyone. Like a man in a battle.' Then she bends to tie sheaves, very tight, as if she'd rather not say more.
column3: 打手们被赶走，打谷场上又响起了连枷声。花白头发的妇人说，每年秋收，都有个放牦牛的老汉来帮着割青稞，一句话不说，割完就走，「割得比谁都快，那架势，像在打仗」。她说完低头扎麦捆，扎得极紧，像是不想再多说。

column2: From the bully's store you take sixty sacks of barley, a stolen millstone, three crocks of butter, a string of silver earrings his men lost at dice, and a forged deed calling the land ownerless. The women use it to paper a window.
column3: 地头的仓里抄出青稞六十袋、一架抢来的水磨盘、三口酥油坛、一串打手们赌输了押下的银耳环，还有一张写着「无主地」的假地契，妇人们拿它糊了窗户。

column2: Every time you pass, the women of the terraces put a sack of freshly roasted barley on your cart, still crackling, and the grey-haired one always adds an extra handful: 'Soldiers on a long road. Chew on that and you won't go hungry.'
column3: 每次路过，屯田坝的妇人们都在你们车上放一袋新炒的青稞，炒得噼啪响，花白头发的那位总要多塞一把：「当兵的走远路，嚼着这个不饿。」

column2: The Armourer's Kiln
column3: 甲匠窑

column2: Out in the open is a kiln-cave where hammers have rung on leather armour for ten years, and the old armourer who works it came from the Gravel Camp. A gang of false monks in red robes holds him there, demanding thirty suits of iron lamellar so they can pass as temple guardians and frighten travellers. He has been lacing the plates in backwards on purpose; they've caught him, and he is being whipped.
column3: 野地里一座窑洞，窑里叮叮当当打了十年皮甲，打甲的老匠人原是碎石营的。一伙穿红袍的假僧兵把他扣在窑里，逼他赶制三十副铁叶甲，好扮成神庙护法去吓唬过路人。老匠人一边打一边故意把甲叶穿反，被他们发现了，正挨鞭子。

column2: The false monks are scattered, and the backwards armour lies all over the floor. The old armourer wipes his face. He made the commander's own armour, he says, seven hundred plates and a mirror over the heart. 'The commander laid it down, but not to the court. He hung it in the Mountain God's shrine on the gravel flats.' His words were: 'The armour belongs to the court. The man belongs to this mountain.'
column3: 假僧兵被打散，穿反的甲扔了一地。老匠人抹了把脸说，营将那副明光甲就是他打的，甲叶七百片，胸前一面护心镜。「营将交了甲，没交给朝廷，挂进了碎石滩上的山神祠。」他说营将的原话是：「甲是朝廷的，人是这座山的。」

column2: Bounty Tent
column3: 赏金帐

column2: A big tent stands in the open with a CAPTURE flag planted before it. A band of bounty hunters on yaks has set up here, stopping every passing herder to show him a yellowed portrait: a young general with heavy brows in bright plate armour. Anyone who says he hasn't seen him loses a yak, as a 'questioning fee'.
column3: 野地上一顶大帐，帐前插着一面「捕」字旗，一伙骑牦牛的赏金客在这里落脚，挨个盘问过路的牧人，拿一张发黄的画像给人认。画像上是个年轻的将军，浓眉，披着明光甲。谁说没见过，他们就扣下谁的一头牛，说是「问话钱」。

column2: The bounty hunters are driven out and the seized yaks returned. On the back of the portrait is a ten-year-old warrant: 'Huo Shan, commander of the Gravel Camp, defied the edict and let a man over the mountain, then abandoned his armour and fled. Reward three hundred taels.' The old soldiers look at the portrait. That's how the commander looked when he was young, they say. If he's still alive, no one would know him now.
column3: 赏金客被打出了帐，扣下的牛还了回去。画像背面是十年前的海捕文书：「碎石营营将霍山，抗旨纵人过山，弃甲潜逃。赏银三百两。」老兵们看着画像，说营将年轻时就是这个样子，如今要是还活着，谁也认不出了。

column2: Token Col
column3: 交牌垭

column2: The highest point of the pilgrim circuit is a col, crowned by a mani cairn taller than a man, every stone carved with scripture. This is where Awang's thirteenth circuit ends. The hardest men among the horse thieves hold the col, stripping the silver and coral offerings from the cairn, three ranks deep of blades, bows and horses. Awang doesn't look at them. He watches the cairn, gripping something inside his coat.
column3: 转山道的最高处是一道垭口，垭口上一座玛尼堆，比人还高，每块石头上都刻着经文。这是阿旺第十三圈的终点。一伙盗马贼里最狠的人马占了垭口，专扒玛尼堆里供着的银子和珊瑚，刀、弓、马排了三层。阿旺不看他们，只盯着那堆石头，攥紧了怀里一样东西。

column2: The horse thieves are driven off the col. Awang takes a worn wooden tag from his coat, a Gravel Camp soldier's tag, and pushes it into the cairn. His hand meets nothing but tags: dozens of Gravel Camp tags, one on another, left over the years by men who ran and came back. On the topmost stone a line has been carved: 'Those who come back are still soldiers of the Gravel Camp. Huo.' The cuts are fresh. Awang kneels there, puts the ten-year-old tea leaf in his mouth, and chews it a long time. 'It's sweet,' he says.
column3: 盗马贼被打下了垭口。阿旺从怀里掏出一块磨亮的木腰牌，碎石营的兵牌，压进玛尼堆里。手一伸进去，碰到的全是牌：几十块碎石营的兵牌，一块压着一块，都是这些年逃了又回来的人放的。最上面一块石头刻着一行小字：「回来的，都还是碎石营的兵。霍。」刻痕是新的。阿旺跪在那里，把那片十年的茶叶放进嘴里嚼了很久，说：「是甜的。」

column2: Yak Tracks
column3: 牛蹄印

column2: A line of yak tracks crosses the snow, one yak and one man, heading deep into the gravel flats. Some bounty hunters on yaks are following them, and the tracks have brought them to a herd boy's tent. They've hung the boy up to question him: who owns that yak, where does he live? The boy grits his teeth and says nothing.
column3: 野地的雪上有一行牦牛蹄印，一头牛，一个人，往碎石滩深处去。几个赏金客骑着牦牛顺着蹄印追，追到一个放牛娃的帐篷，把娃娃吊起来问话：那头牦牛的主人是谁，住在哪儿。娃娃咬着牙，一个字也不说。

column2: The bounty hunters are chased off and the boy let down. Rubbing his wrists, he says it's his master, an old yak herder who never says his name; everyone calls him Old Stone. 'Old Stone said, whoever asks, say you haven't seen him.' He thinks, then adds: 'He's got a finger missing on his left hand. Milks faster than anyone though.'
column3: 赏金客被打跑，娃娃被放了下来，揉着手腕说，那是他东家，一个放牦牛的老汉，从不说自己叫什么，大伙都叫他「老石头」。「老石头说，谁来问，都说没见过。」娃娃想了想又说：「他左手少一根指头，挤奶比谁都快。」

column2: The Lieutenant's Camp
column3: 副将帐

column2: A troop of yak riders has camped on the gravel flats, led by a middle-aged man with a face full of sword scars who calls himself the Gravel Camp's lieutenant. He has hated the commander for ten years: the commander defied the edict, and not one of the camp's five hundred came out of it well, scattered or arrested, and he himself got eighty strokes of the rod. He's here to drag the commander back with his own hands.
column3: 碎石滩上一伙牦牛骑扎了营，领头的是个满脸刀疤的中年汉子，自称碎石营的副将。他恨营将恨了十年：营将抗了旨，碎石营五百人一个也没落着好，散的散，抓的抓，他自己挨了八十军棍。这回他带人来，就是要亲手把营将拿回去。

column2: The riders scatter, and the lieutenant sits in the snow and won't get up. The old soldiers tell him everything, the camp book, the words on the target post, the accounts on the granary wall. He is silent a long while, then says: 'The edict to strike camp had come already. The camp was finished either way. And the man he let through went up to guard the mountain for us?' He puts his sword back in its sheath.
column3: 牦牛骑散了，副将坐在雪地里不肯起来。老兵们把营簿、靶桩上的字、粮仓墙上的账一样样讲给他听。他听完半天没出声，最后说：「撤营的旨意早就下了，营怎么都得散。他放的那个人，是替我们守山去了？」他把刀插回了鞘里。

column2: Stone Stair Col
column3: 石阶垭

column2: Here the mountain road turns into a stone stair of more than a thousand steps, laid stone by stone by generations of pilgrims. A troop of yak riders sits across the bottom, hired by the herd-owner you drove off to take out his temper: no one goes up today. Lama Gonpo has been walking for three days and his breath wheezes like a bellows. He leans on Zhaxi's shoulder, looks at the stair, then at you.
column3: 山脚上山的路在这里变成一道石阶，一千多级，是历代转山人一块块垒的。一伙牦牛骑横在阶下，是被赶走的那个大牧主雇来出气的，扬言谁也别想上山。贡布喇嘛已经走了三天，气喘得像风箱，扶着扎西的肩膀，看着石阶，又看了看你们。

column2: The yak riders are driven down the slope. Lama Gonpo sits down on the first step and stays there a long while. At last he smiles: 'I can't go up. I'll wait here, that's fine. I've waited ten years.' He has Zhaxi set up the little stove and light the one stick of charcoal to boil the last kettle of water.
column3: 牦牛骑被赶下了坡。贡布喇嘛在第一级石阶上坐下来，坐了很久，最后笑了：「上不去了。我在这里等着就好，十年都等了。」他让扎西把炉子支起来，用那根炭条，烧最后一壶水。

column2: Temple-View Terrace
column3: 望庙台

column2: Beside the stair is a terrace, and on a clear day you can see the golden roof of the temple on the eastern snow mountain from it, one small point of light. A band of snow-mountain archers has cut down the prayer flags here to feed their fire. They have come to rob the road, and when they see the lama's tea stove they think there's gold boiling in it, and all of them turn their arrows on you.
column3: 石阶边一块平台，天晴的时候，能望见东边雪山上那座神庙的金顶，一点点亮。平台上的风马旗被一伙雪山弓手割下来烤火，他们是来劫路的，看见喇嘛的茶炉，以为炉子里煮的是金子，一齐把箭对准了你们。

column2: The archers are scattered. The water boils, and Lama Gonpo divides the last pinch in two. Half he brews, and all of you share it. The other half he wraps in paper and puts in your hands: 'Take it to him. Tell him the taste never changed, and Zhaxi has grown up.' Gripping the little bronze bell, Zhaxi says he knows this smell. When he was very small, somewhere very cold, someone held him inside his coat, and that coat smelled just like this.
column3: 弓手被打散了。水开了，贡布喇嘛把最后一撮茶分成两半：一半泡了，分着喝；一半用纸包好，交到你们手里：「带给他。告诉他味没变，扎西长大了。」扎西攥着铜铃说，他认得这股味道：很小的时候，在一个很冷的地方，有人把他揣在怀里，怀里就是这个味道。

column2: Muster Slope
column3: 归营坡

column2: On an open slope a great force hired with the bounty hunters' silver is drawn up, swordsmen, archers and yak riders, two or three hundred strong, blocking the way deeper into the gravel flats. Below the slope, here and there, stand the Gravel Camp's old soldiers you have met along the road: the ones who robbed, the one who keeps the drum, the farrier, and the lieutenant too. None of them wears armour. They carry yak-driving sticks.
column3: 野地坡上，赏金客花钱雇来的一大帮人马排开了阵，刀手、弓手、牦牛骑，足有两三百，堵住了往碎石滩深处去的路。坡下，零零散散地站着你们一路遇见的碎石营老兵，有劫过道的，有守鼓的，有钉掌的，还有那个副将，谁也没穿甲，手里拿的是赶牛的棍子。

column2: The hired force is scattered. The old soldiers raise the Huo banner on the slope, and the lieutenant calls the roll, and each man answers 'Here!' as his name is called. Someone starts crying partway through. 'If the commander knew we'd stood together again...' says the lieutenant, and doesn't finish. He only says he's going to the Mountain God's shrine deep in the gravel flats, to guard the commander's armour.
column3: 雇来的人马被打散了。老兵们在坡上竖起那面「霍」字旗，副将一个个点名，点到谁，谁就喊一声「到」。有人点着点着哭了。副将说：「营将要是知道，我们又站齐了……」他没说完，只说要去碎石滩深处的山神祠，替营将守着那副甲。

column2: Ambush Flats
column3: 截驮滩

column2: Out on the open country a long yak train has been cut off, and every driver is a youngster with a birch tag round the neck. The tea house's hired men are out in force: archers shooting from the slope, yak riders charging back and forth, swordsmen slashing girths until tea bricks tumble into the snow. The children stand back to back, whirling slings and shouting to each other: “Old Han! Luo the Second! Big Gou!” Grown men's names, every one.
column3: 野地上一长串牦牛驮队被截在半道，赶牛的全是半大孩子，脖子上都挂着桦木腰牌。截道的是那家茶号雇来的大队人马，雪山弓手在坡上放箭，牦牛骑来回冲，刀手割断了牛肚带，茶砖滚了一地。孩子们背靠背围成一圈，甩着抛石绳，互相喊着名字：「老韩！罗二！苟大个儿！」喊的全是大人的名字。

column2: The raiders are driven off. You count thirty-one children and thirty-one tags. Their leader is a girl of sixteen whose tag says 'Sun Big-Bowl'. There are two hundred and ninety-nine of them, she says, herding all over the mountains, and once a year they gather for the temple fair. The raiders' captain carried a list of their names, to be crossed off one by one.
column3: 截道的人马被打退了。你们数了数，三十一个孩子，三十一块腰牌。领头的姑娘十六岁，牌子上写着「孙大碗」。她说他们一共二百九十九个，散在山前山后放牧，一年凑齐一回，赶神庙的庙会。截道的头目怀里揣着一张单子，抄着他们的名字，一个一个要划掉。

column2: Sea of Boulders
column3: 乱石海

column2: Below the mountains lies a jumble of stones, some big as houses, some small as fists, strewn all the way up to the snow line. A few children who scattered in the ambush have crept into the cracks. The tea house's men have brought mastiffs, and the handlers are whooping them in to search, while riders circle outside waiting for the children to be flushed out. Sun Big-Bowl wants to charge straight in.
column3: 山脚下一大片乱石，大的像房子，小的像拳头，横七竖八一直铺到雪线底下。几个跑散的孩子钻进了石头缝，茶号的人牵来一群獒犬，驯獒人吆喝着放狗进去搜，骑手在乱石外头一圈圈地转，等着孩子被撵出来。孙大碗急得要往里冲。

column2: The mastiffs are leashed, the handlers flee, and the children crawl out one by one; none of them got lost. The real Sun Big-Bowl taught her, the girl says: river stones are worn round by water, but stones a glacier pushes down are sharp-edged, big and small all mixed. “Follow stones like these uphill and you'll reach the ice.” That was how they found their way when they went east.
column3: 獒犬收了绳，驯獒人跑了，孩子们一个个从石缝里钻出来，谁也没迷路。孙大碗说是真孙大碗教的：河滩上的石头让水磨圆了；冰川推下来的石头有棱有角，大的小的混在一起，「顺着这种石头往上走，就走得到冰」。当年他们往东去，就是这么认的路。

column2: The Surgeon's Cave
column3: 军医窑

column2: At the end of the open ground is an earth cave hung with herbs, where the Gravel Camp's old surgeon lives. A band of snow-mountain archers has taken it and makes him treat their leader's frostbite every day, no food if he fails. The leader's feet are black with it. The old surgeon says they must come off; the leader refuses, and has his men hold an arrow to the back of the surgeon's head.
column3: 野地尽头一孔土窑，窑口挂着草药，住着碎石营的老军医。一伙雪山弓手占了窑，逼他天天给他们的头领治冻伤，治不好就不给饭吃。头领的两只脚冻得发黑，老军医说得截，头领不肯，叫手下拿箭顶着老军医的后脑勺。

column2: The archers are driven off and their leader carried down the mountain to lose his feet. The old surgeon says the finger he was sorriest to take in all his life was one little finger. That twelfth month, the commander walked the Han man to the foot of the snow mountain and waited all night in the blizzard for the people from the mountain to come down for him. When he came back, the little finger of his left hand was black. 'He didn't make a sound while I cut. He only asked if the man had got up safely.'
column3: 弓手被赶走，头领被抬下山去截脚了。老军医说他这辈子截过一根最舍不得的指头：那年腊月，营将送那个汉人到雪山脚下，在风雪里等山上的人下来接，等了一夜，回来时左手小指冻黑了。「我截的时候他一声没吭，只问那人上去了没有。」

column2: The Mailbag Cairn
column3: 驿袋堆

column2: On the gravel flats stands a cairn of stones with a mouldy mailbag stuffed into a crack: army post that never went out the year the mountain was closed. A band of horse thieves has lit a fire beside it and is pulling the letters out one by one for kindling, cursing as each one burns: 'All of them snivelling.' Only a few are left by the fire.
column3: 碎石滩上一个石头堆，石缝里塞着一只发霉的驿袋，是十年前封山那年没送出去的军邮。一伙盗马贼在石堆边生火，从驿袋里一封封抽信出来引火，烧一封骂一句：「全是哭哭啼啼的。」火边只剩最后几封了。

column2: The horse thieves are chased off and you snatch the last three letters from the fire. Two are too burnt to read. The third is whole, sealed with the Gravel Camp's wax, and addressed: 'To Liangzhou, to Mistress Qin of the house of Huo.' No one dares open it. There was only one man in the camp named Huo, the old soldiers say.
column3: 盗马贼被赶跑，你们从火边抢下了最后三封。两封已经烧得看不清，第三封完好，封口压着碎石营的火漆，信封上写着：「寄凉州，霍门秦氏」。没有人敢拆。老兵们说，营里姓霍的，只有一个。

column2: Aunt Qin's Stove
column3: 秦婶灶

column2: Out in the open stands a mud house belonging to the grey-haired woman from the barley terraces, whom everyone calls Aunt Qin. A few bounty hunters have her cornered in her kitchen: they've found out she is Huo Shan's wife, come from Liangzhou ten years ago to look for him, and if she won't say where he is, they'll take her back to answer for him. Aunt Qin feeds a stick into the stove and says she has been looking for ten years, and would like to know herself.
column3: 野地上一间土屋，屋主是屯田坝那个花白头发的妇人，大家叫她秦婶。几个赏金客把她堵在灶房里，说打听过了，她是霍山的老婆，十年前从凉州找来的，不说霍山在哪儿，就把她带回去顶罪。秦婶往灶里添了一把柴，说她找了十年，也想知道他在哪儿。

column2: The bounty hunters are chased off. When she came ten years ago, Aunt Qin says, everyone said the commander had fled; some said he died in the snow. So she stayed on the terraces and farmed barley. 'If he were alive he'd have come home long ago. If he hasn't, there's something he can't put down.' You don't mention the letter. She serves you each a bowl of noodles, cooked right through, a flat stone weighing down the pot lid.
column3: 赏金客被打跑了。秦婶说她十年前来时，人人都说营将逃了，有的说死在雪里了。她就在屯田坝住下种麦，「他要是活着，早该回家了。不回，就是有放不下的事」。你们没提那封信。她给你们一人盛了一碗面片，面煮得透透的，锅盖上压着一块平石头。

column2: Glacier-Stream Mill
column3: 冰溪磨

column2: A fast stream of glacier meltwater runs below the mountains, and on it stands a stone mill whose wheel creaks round, grinding roasted barley into tsampa for thirty miles about. A gang of horse thieves is wintering inside. They have cut the millrace to water their stolen horses, the stones have stopped, and every household is back to pounding grain in a mortar. The miller is tied up by his own wheel, brushing horses all day.
column3: 山脚下一条冰川融水冲下来的急溪，溪上一座石磨坊，水轮吱呀呀地转，方圆几十里的青稞都靠它磨成糌粑。一伙盗马贼在磨坊里过冬，把水渠截了去饮抢来的马，磨盘停了，各家只好拿石臼一下一下地捣。磨坊主被他们拴在水轮边，天天给马刷毛。

column2: The thieves are gone, the water runs back, and the wheel turns again. The miller says a Qianli carpenter rebuilt it their first summer on the mountain: “Not a wobble in it, and not one spoke replaced in nine years.” The children line up with their barley, and the first bag ground goes by the door for travellers, as the old rule says.
column3: 盗马贼被赶走，渠水放回来，水轮又转了。磨坊主说这座水轮是千里号的木匠修的，他们上山头一个夏天就修好了，「一圈不晃，九年没换过一根辐条」。孩子们排着队来磨青稞，磨出来的第一袋，照老规矩放在门口给过路的人。

column2: The thieves' hoard: twelve bags of ground tsampa, two silver-trimmed saddles, a stolen tub of butter, a bundle of halters, and a ledger of every horse they had taken and from whom. The miller returned them one by one by the book.
column3: 盗马贼囤下的：十二袋磨好的糌粑、两副镶银的马鞍、一桶抢来的酥油、一捆马笼头，还有一本盗马的账，记着偷了谁家几匹马，磨坊主照着账一匹匹给人送了回去。

column2: Every time you pass, the miller catches a bag of tsampa fresh from the stones, still warm, and stuffs a knob of butter in the top. “The Qianli carpenter's rule: travellers eat first.”
column3: 每次路过，磨坊主都从磨眼底下接一袋刚出磨的糌粑给你们，还温着，袋口塞一坨酥油：「千里号的木匠说的，过路的人先吃饱。」

column2: The Siege Camp
column3: 围祠营

column2: On the gravel flats all the bounty hunters' remaining men have gathered into one great camp, and inside it a dozen old yak herders are held: ones missing a finger on the left hand, ones who look a little like the portrait, or ones who simply wouldn't answer. The hunters say they'll question every one until they find Huo Shan. Outside the camp, the tracks in the snow lead on towards the Mountain God's shrine at the very heart of the flats.
column3: 碎石滩上，赏金客剩下的人马全聚到了一处，扎了一座大营，营里关着十几个放牦牛的老汉，都是左手少根指头的、长得有几分像画像的、或者只是不肯回话的。赏金客说一个个审，审出霍山为止。营外的雪地上，蹄印一直通向碎石滩最深处的那座山神祠。

column2: The camp is broken and the old men let out one by one, but Old Stone is not among them. One of them whispers that Old Stone saw trouble coming two days ago and drove his yaks towards the shrine: 'He said the armour's still in the shrine and he has to guard it.' The hunters' leader has gone after him with the last of his men.
column3: 大营被打破了，老汉们一个个放了出来，可里头没有老石头。一个老汉悄悄说，老石头前天就看出来不对，赶着牛往山神祠去了，「他说，甲还在祠里，他得守着」。赏金客的头领带着最后一拨人，也朝山神祠追了下去。

column2: The Name Buyer
column3: 收名客

column2: In a ragged tent on the gravel flats lives a strange old man who buys names, with a band of archers to guard his door. Sell him your name and he gives you a bag of salt; after that, when someone calls it, you don't hear and don't turn round. Deserters love to sell, since then the officials can never call them up. Under his bed is a sack, stuffed fat with strips of cloth each bearing a name.
column3: 碎石滩上一顶破帐篷，住着个收名字的怪老头，雇了一伙弓手看门。卖给他一个名字，他给一袋盐；名字卖了，再有人喊你，你就听不见，也不会回头。逃兵最爱来卖，卖了名字，官府就点不着他们了。老头床底下有一只口袋，鼓鼓囊囊，塞满了写着名字的布条。

column2: The archers are driven off, and the old man clutches his sack: a name can only be bought back with a name. The old soldiers give him their nicknames and take back their real names one by one. One of them hears his comrade call him by his true name, and is a long time turning round, tears running. The commander came here too, the old man says. He didn't sell. He only asked: 'Can I buy back other people's?'
column3: 弓手被赶走，老头抱着口袋说，名字只能拿名字换回去。老兵们报上各自的外号，把本名一个个换了回来。有个老兵听见同伴喊了一声他的本名，愣了好久才回头，眼泪就下来了。老头说营将也来过，没卖，只问：「能不能替别人赎？」

column2: The Banned-Name Board
column3: 禁名榜

column2: A board has gone up at a crossroads on the open country: 'Whoever falsely claims the Qianli name forfeits his goods and gets the cane.' Under it stand yak riders in borrowed constables' coats, their hats two sizes too big, so every nod drops the brim over their eyes. They turn back every traveller's collar, and any birch tag they find goes into a brazier. Zhou Qi clutches his throat and ducks behind you.
column3: 野地上的路口立起一块木榜，上书：「凡冒称千里号者，没其货，杖其人。」榜下站着一排牦牛骑，穿着借来的官差号衣，帽子大了两号，一低头就扣住了眼睛。他们挨个翻过路人的衣领，看见桦木腰牌就扯下来扔进火盆。周七捂着脖子往你们身后躲。

column2: The sham constables scatter and their hats roll everywhere. The seal on the board says 'Wantong Head Office', the account seal of the Wantong house's plateau branch. Sun Big-Bowl explains: Wantong's manager, Qian Mancang, wants the 'First Stall' at the temple fair. For nine years it has carried the Qianli sign, and whatever tea price is called from it, the whole plateau accepts.
column3: 假官差被打散，帽子滚了一地。木榜上的大印反刻着「万通总柜」，是山下万通号高原分号的账印。孙大碗说，万通号的掌柜钱满仓盯上的是神庙庙会的「第一摊」：九年来那个摊位一直挂着千里号的牌子，坐在那儿的人开出的茶价，全高原都认。

column2: Tent of Thirty Rugs
column3: 三十毡帐

column2: On the open country stands a great black tent with thirty felt rugs laid along its sides, a name stitched in red at the head of each. Its owner, Amma Lhamo, past sixty, is blocking the door with the fire tongs: some Wantong swordsmen are waving a promissory note, claiming the Qianli people owed Wantong money and the rugs are going as payment.
column3: 野地上一顶大黑帐，帐里沿着两边铺着三十张毡子，每张毡子枕头那头都用红线绣着一个名字。帐主拉姆阿妈六十多了，正拿着火钳挡在帐门口：几个万通号的刀手举着一张借据，说千里号的人欠了万通号的钱，这些毡子要拉去抵债。

column2: The swordsmen are run off; the note is forged. Lhamo says thirty of those Han men slept in her tent for four winters. They came up on the twenty-fourth of the last month, the cliff road below gave way, and they could not get down. By day they hauled stones for the temple; by night they taught the children knots. “Owed money?” She pats a rug. “They left me their cooking pot.” Now the children who borrowed those names sleep on the rugs.
column3: 刀手被打跑，借据是假的。拉姆说那三十个汉人在她帐里睡了四个冬天：腊月廿四上的山，山下的栈道塌了，下不去。他们白天给庙里背石头，晚上教孩子打绳结。「欠钱？」她拍拍毡子，「走的那天，连锅都留给我了。」如今毡子上睡的，是借了那些名字的孩子。

column2: The Fair Racecourse
column3: 庙前马道

column2: Before every fair there is a race on this flat, and the winning side picks its stalls first. Wantong has paid for the fastest riders on the plateau; the children's rider is a skinny lad who carries the name 'Ma Liu'. The night before, someone prised his horse's shoes loose. At dawn the hired riders simply block the starting line and won't let him race.
column3: 野地上一片平滩，庙会前照例要赛一场马，赢的一方先进集场挑摊位。万通号花大价钱雇来了高原上最快的一群骑手；孩子们这边上场的，是借了「马六」名字的瘦小子。比赛前一夜，他的马掌被人撬松了。天一亮，雇来的骑手干脆拦在起点，不许他上场。

column2: The hired riders are knocked from their saddles and the race goes ahead. Ma Liu, on one of your horses, wins by half a head. The real Ma Liu was the caravan's horse doctor, he says, and left him a hoof knife: “The hoof is a horse's life; the road is a man's.” The hired riders take the loss well and plant the race banner on the Qianli side.
column3: 骑手们被打下了马，比赛照跑。马六骑着你们队里的一匹马，赢了半个马头。他说真马六是千里号的马医，走之前给了他一把修蹄刀：「蹄子是马的命，路是人的命。」雇来的骑手输得服气，把赛马的彩旗插到了千里号那边。

column2: Antelope Gully
column3: 羚角沟

column2: In a gully at the mountain's foot, fur poachers have penned a dozen Tibetan antelope inside a ring of felt, waiting to shear and skin them. Their hired riders hold the gully mouth. The chief poacher wears a birch tag on his belt as a charm, 'Old Han' carved on it, snatched from a herd boy's neck. The boy has followed you all the way, his eyes never leaving it.
column3: 山脚的一条沟里，一伙偷猎藏羚的皮货贩子拿毡子围了个圈，圈里关着十几只藏羚，等着剪绒剥皮。贩子雇来的骑手守着沟口。贩子头腰上挂着一块桦木腰牌当护身符，上头写着「老韩」，是从一个放牧的孩子脖子上抢的。那孩子一路跟着你们，眼睛一直盯着那块牌子。

column2: The riders break, the antelope burst through the felt and race up the slope. The tag goes back round little Old Han's neck, and he turns it over to show you a grown man's handprint, a whole ring larger than his own hand. “Every tag has one,” he says. “They pressed them the day they left. When my hand grows that big, I can take the road myself.”
column3: 骑手被打散，藏羚撞开毡子，一溜烟跑上了山坡。腰牌回到了小老韩的脖子上，他翻过来给你们看：背面烙着一个大人的手印，跟他自己的手一比，大出一圈。「每块牌子后面都有，」他说，「是他们走那天按的。等手长到这么大，就能自己上路了。」

column2: The Letter-Writer's Stall
column3: 代书摊

column2: At the edge of the gravel flats is a stall that writes letters home, with a sign: LETTERS OVER THE MOUNTAIN, TEN DAYS GUARANTEED. A few swordsmen guard it, and once the stallholder has his money he tosses the letter into the chest behind him. You bring him the letter for Liangzhou to ask the way, and when he sees the wax seal he goes white and tells his swordsmen to snatch it.
column3: 碎石滩边上一个代写家书的摊子，招牌写着「寄书过山，十日必达」。几个刀手守着摊子，摊主收了钱，信就往身后的箱子里一扔。你们拿着那封「寄凉州」的信去问路，摊主一看封口的火漆，脸就白了，叫刀手把信抢下来。

column2: The swordsmen are scattered and the chest spills out hundreds of unsent letters. The stallholder kneels and confesses: the mountain has been closed ten years, no letter can get over, he just takes the money. He knows that wax: 'It's the commander's private seal. Ten years ago he came to ask if a letter could be sent, and I said yes. Later he came back and took it away again, said there was no need to send it.' He can't think how it ended up in the mailbag.
column3: 刀手被打散，箱子里倒出来几百封没寄的信。摊主跪着说山封了十年，信根本过不去，他只是收钱。他认得那块火漆：「是营将的私印。十年前他来问过，信能不能寄，我说能。后来他又来，把信要了回去，说不用寄了。」他想不通，信怎么又落到了驿袋里。

column2: The Armour-Scale Stall
column3: 甲片摊

column2: On the gravel flats a gang is selling amulets: rusty iron armour scales laid out in rows, said to have been broken off the 'god's armour' in the Mountain God's shrine. Wear one and no avalanche can bury you. A few swordsmen bawl and block the way so people will buy, one sheep a scale, and old pilgrims queue up with their money, afraid of missing out.
column3: 碎石滩上一伙卖护身符的，摊上摆着一片片生锈的铁甲叶，说是从山神祠里那副「神甲」上掰下来的，戴一片，雪崩埋不着。几个刀手吆喝着拦人买，一片要一头羊。转山的老人们排着队掏钱，生怕晚了买不着。

column2: The swordsmen are chased off. The old armourer picks up a scale, looks at it and throws it away: 'Cut from horseshoe iron. Every scale I made has my mark.' Not one scale is missing from the armour in the shrine, he says: 'Someone polishes it every month till it shines.' The old pilgrims lead their sheep home, though one old woman keeps a scale anyway. Whether it works or not, she says, it eases the heart.
column3: 刀手被打跑了。老甲匠拿起一片看了看就扔了：「这是马掌铁剪的，我的甲叶，片片有记号。」他说祠里那副甲一片也没少过，「有人每个月去擦，擦得锃亮」。老人们把羊牵了回去，有个老阿妈还是揣走了一片，说灵不灵的，图个心安。

column2: Shrine Slope
column3: 祠前坡

column2: Deep in the gravel flats a gentle slope rises, and at its top stands the Mountain God's shrine. The bounty hunters' leader has the last of his yak riders drawn up across the foot of it. Up on the slope you can just make out one yak and one man, sitting motionless at the shrine door. The leader whistles and lines his men up to charge: 'Three hundred taels, right up there.'
column3: 碎石滩深处一道缓坡，坡顶就是山神祠。赏金客的头领带着最后一拨牦牛骑堵在坡下，坡上隐约有一头牦牛，一个人，坐在祠门口不动。头领吹着口哨，让手下排成一排往上冲：「三百两，就在上头。」

column2: The yak riders are scattered, their leader tied up and the warrant torn to shreds. The lieutenant comes up with the old soldiers and they form a line at the foot of the slope, and none of them goes further. The man at the top still sits at the shrine door. He watches you a long time, then slowly gets up, turns, and goes into the shrine.
column3: 牦牛骑被打散，头领被你们捆了，海捕文书撕成了碎片。副将带着老兵们走上来，在坡下排成了一排，谁也没往上走。坡顶那个人还坐在祠门口，看了你们很久，才慢慢站起来，转身进了祠。

column2: Old Stone's Fold
column3: 老石头圈

column2: At the mountain's foot is a low wall of dried dung enclosing Old Stone's winter fold and a stone hut. Before they left, the bounty hunters posted a few swordsmen here to lie in wait. They have slaughtered and eaten Old Stone's cattle, thrown everything in the hut on the floor, and are burning his bedding to keep warm.
column3: 山脚下一圈牛粪垒的矮墙，墙里是老石头过冬的牛圈和一间石屋。赏金客走之前留了几个刀手在这里蹲守，把老石头的牛全宰了吃，石屋里的东西扔了一地，正在拿他的被褥烤火。

column2: The swordsmen are driven out. You tidy the hut: a Han teacup hangs on the wall, and the old soldiers fold the quilt on the bed into a perfect square block. Running his hand over it, the lieutenant says only one man in the camp ever folded a quilt that square: 'Twelve years, every single day.'
column3: 刀手被赶走了。石屋收拾干净，墙上挂着一只汉人的茶碗，炕上的被子被老兵们叠成了方方正正的一块。副将摸着叠好的被子说，营里只有一个人叠被子叠得这么方，「十二年，天天这么叠」。

column2: What the swordsmen couldn't carry off: two half-eaten yak carcasses, a skin of barley beer, a bundle of stolen leather rope, a few of the hunters' wanted posters, and Old Stone's milk pail, which they had been using for horse feed.
column3: 刀手们来不及带走的东西：两腔吃剩的牦牛肉、一皮袋青稞酒、一捆抢来的皮绳、几张赏金客的通缉画像，还有老石头的一只奶桶，被他们拿来装了马料。

column2: Every time you pass, the herd boy is minding the fold for Old Stone, and he brings out a pail of fresh yak milk from the hut, still steaming: 'Old Stone said, when soldiers come, let them drink their fill.'
column3: 每次路过，放牛娃都替老石头守着圈，见你们来，就从石屋里捧出一桶刚挤的牦牛奶，冒着热气：「老石头交代的，当兵的来了要给喝饱。」

column2: The Drying Racks
column3: 晒茶架

column2: Rows of wooden racks stand on the open country, drying the tea bricks the children pressed themselves, glossy black, each stamped 'Qianli' with a wooden seal. Snow-mountain archers hired by Wantong lie behind the slope shooting fire arrows, meaning to burn the whole season's tea so the Qianli stall has nothing to sell at the fair. Two rows are already alight.
column3: 野地上一排排木架，架上晾着孩子们自己压的茶砖，一块块黑亮，盖着「千里号」的木戳。万通号雇来的雪山弓手埋伏在坡后，往架子上射火箭，要把这一季的茶烧干净，让千里号的摊子在庙会上无茶可卖。架子已经烧着了两排。

column2: The archers are chased off and the children smother the flames with snow, saving more than half. The leaf comes from the salt caravans, Sun Big-Bowl says; the pressing the real Sun Big-Bowl taught: seven layers, seven treads each. The seal the real Zhou Qi carved. He couldn't read, so he traced the characters off a tea wrapper for three months. “We pressed the tea,” she says. “The seal is real.”
column3: 弓手被赶走，孩子们拿雪扑灭了火，抢出了一大半。孙大碗说茶叶是跟山下的盐帮换的，压法是真孙大碗教的：七层，一层踩七脚。木戳是真周七刻的，他不识字，照着茶纸上的字描了三个月。「茶是我们压的，」她说，「戳子是真的。」

column2: Qian Mancang's Train
column3: 满仓驮队

column2: Wantong's caravan has jammed the main road to the fair: sixty yaks of lowland tea, swordsmen front and rear, racing to reach the fairground before anyone else. In the middle, on the biggest yak, sits a little sedan chair, and in it a fat man with a hand-warmer in one hand and an abacus in the other. This is Qian Mancang.
column3: 往庙会去的大路上，万通号的驮队把路堵得严严实实：六十头牦牛，驮着山下运上来的茶，刀手前后押着，要抢在所有人前头进集场。驮队正中，一头最壮的牦牛背上架着一顶小轿，轿里坐着一个胖子，一手捧手炉，一手打算盘。这就是钱满仓。

column2: The swordsmen break, Qian Mancang tumbles into the snow and crawls away, and the sedan tips over. Inside is a deed: 'The First Stall of the temple fairground, sold by Zhou Qi of the Qianli to the Wantong house', signed 'Zhou Qi'. Young Zhou Qi takes one look and laughs. “The real Zhou Qi couldn't write. He signed with his handprint.”
column3: 刀手被打散，钱满仓连滚带爬钻进了雪地，轿子歪在一边。轿里有一张地契，写着「神庙集场第一摊，千里号周七卖与万通号」，底下签着「周七」两个字。小周七看了一眼就笑了：「真周七不会写字。他画押，是按手印的。」

column2: The Bard's Tent
column3: 说唱帐

column2: Yak riders ring a tent on the open country, and inside sits an old bard of the Gesar epic. The herd-lord's son wants a new verse that makes him King Gesar, and the bard won't be let go until it's sung. The old man closes his eyes and sings something else: “Two hundred and ninety-nine Han men carrying stones...” The riders raise their whips to cut him off.
column3: 野地上一顶帐篷外围着一圈牦牛骑，帐里坐着一位说唱格萨尔的老艺人。牧主家的少爷要他编一段新唱，把少爷唱成格萨尔王，唱不好就不放人。老艺人闭着眼，张口唱的却是另一段：「二百九十九个汉人背石头……」牦牛骑抡起鞭子，要抽断他的话头。

column2: The riders are driven away and the bard sings it to the end: the Han men hauled stones up from the boulder field below the glacier, two a day each, all one summer, and built two hundred and ninety-nine stone stalls beneath the temple, so the fair that once lasted three days now lasts seven. The young lord, red-faced, asks to learn that verse.
column3: 牦牛骑被赶跑了，老艺人接着唱完：二百九十九个汉人从冰川底下的乱石滩背石头，一人一天两块，背了一个夏天，在神庙脚下垒出二百九十九个石摊，庙会从三天赶成了七天。少爷听完，红着脸说，他也要学这一段。

column2: The Fair-Master's Stone
column3: 集头石

column2: By the fairground lies a flat-topped boulder where Kelsang the fair-master sits; whatever he says there is the fair's law. He is past seventy and leans on the long rule he measures stalls with. Wantong's men have taken his grandson and want him to give the First Stall to Qian Mancang with his own mouth on opening day. Kelsang has sat on the stone all night without closing his eyes.
column3: 集场边一块平顶大石，是集头格桑坐的地方，庙会的规矩都由他一句话定。格桑七十多了，拄着一杆量摊位的长尺。万通号的家丁扣下了他的小孙子，要他在开集那天亲口把「第一摊」划给钱满仓。格桑坐在石头上，一夜没合眼。

column2: The men are driven off and the boy runs into Kelsang's arms. The First Stall, Kelsang says, the Han men built themselves, and they left the rule too: whoever sits in it must use the Qianli name. The spring they left, they gave him a letter for the hot-spring temple, “signed just 'Lu'. They said the tea train's letters always carry the escort chief's name.”
column3: 家丁被打跑，小孙子扑进了格桑怀里。格桑说第一摊是那二百九十九个汉人自己垒的，规矩也是他们留的：谁坐在里头，就得用千里号的名字。他们走的那年春天，托他捎一封信去温泉寺，「落款写个『陆』。他们说，茶队的信，都署镖头的姓」。

column2: The Dead Post Station
column3: 断邮驿

column2: Out in the open stands an army post station, with stables, a kitchen and a little room for receiving letters, and not one post horse has come in ten years. A band of snow-mountain archers has made it their base for robbing travellers and set the old postman to feeding their horses. Every day he still wipes down the station gate and hangs a lamp in the doorway. A station can't be without its lamp, he says.
column3: 野地上一座军驿，马棚、灶房、一间收信的小屋，十年没来过一匹驿马。一伙雪山弓手占了驿站，把这里当成了抢劫过路人的据点，驿卒被他们赶去喂马。老驿卒每天还是照样把驿门擦一遍，在门口挂起一盏灯，说驿站不能没有灯。

column2: The archers are chased off and the station set to rights. The old postman holds the letter for Liangzhou and says he knows it. Ten years ago the commander took it back from the letter-writer and gave it to him to keep; later horse thieves stole the mailbag and the letter was lost. 'The commander comes once a month. He never asks about the letter. He only asks if the mountain is open yet.' He gives it back to you: 'If he won't take it, give it to Aunt Qin.'
column3: 弓手被打跑，驿站收拾了出来。老驿卒捧着那封「寄凉州」的信，说他认得：十年前营将从代书摊要回这封信，是交给他保管的，后来驿袋被马贼劫走，信就丢了。「营将每个月来一趟，不问信，只问山开了没有。」他把信还给你们：「他要是不收，你们就交给秦婶。」

column2: The archers' hoard in the station: a cartload of looted brick tea, two bags of tsampa, a post horse's saddle, and a stack of unclaimed parcels. The old postman logs every one in his book and says he'll deliver them all once the mountain opens.
column3: 弓手们囤在驿站里的：一车劫来的砖茶、两袋糌粑、一副驿马的鞍子、一摞没人认领的包裹，老驿卒挨个登了簿，说等山开了一样样送出去。

column2: Every time you pass, the old postman is waiting at the station gate with the lamp already lit and a pot of butter tea warming on the stove. He checks your passes by the old station rules and stamps them red: 'While the station has a lamp, the road isn't broken.'
column3: 每次路过，老驿卒都在驿门口等着，灯已经点上了，灶上煨着一壶酥油茶。他照驿站的老规矩给你们验过路条，盖一个红印：「驿站有灯，路就不算断。」

column2: The Night Pen
column3: 夜牛圈

column2: The night before the fair, the children's yaks are penned out on the open country. Horse thieves creep up with felt tied round the yaks' hooves so they make no sound, leading them out one after another. Luo the Second is on watch, and by the time he notices, nine are gone. Qian Mancang hired the thieves: one tael of silver a head.
column3: 庙会前一夜，孩子们的牦牛圈在野地上过夜。一伙盗马贼摸了过来，牛蹄上裹着毡子，走起来一点声音都没有，一头接一头地往外牵。守夜的是罗二，等他发现，已经少了九头。盗马贼的头子是钱满仓花钱请的，牵走一头，算一两银子。

column2: The thieves run and all nine yaks come back. Begging for mercy, their chief lets slip that Qian Mancang offered another price as well: a good horse for a Qianli tag. Luo the Second clutches his own. People really did come offering, he says, “a fine horse, too”, and not one of the two hundred and ninety-nine took it.
column3: 盗马贼被打跑，九头牦牛一头不少地牵了回来。盗马贼头子讨饶时说，钱满仓还出过一个价：一块千里号的腰牌换一匹马。罗二攥着自己的牌子说，这几年真有人来换，「换一匹好马呢」，可二百九十九个人，没有一个换的。

column2: The Swordsmen's Camp
column3: 刀客营

column2: A ring of tents on the open country belongs to Khampa swordsmen, red tassels in their hair and long blades at their belts, hired with Qian Mancang's last money to hold the First Stall on opening day. Their code is to do what they're paid for, and to do it in the open: they send you a formal challenge to meet them pair by pair before the camp.
column3: 野地上扎着一圈康巴刀客的帐篷，个个头缠红穗，腰插长刀，是钱满仓用最后一笔钱请来的，要在开集那天守住第一摊。刀客的规矩是收了钱就办事，也讲究打得光明正大：他们派人送来战书，约你们在营前一对一对地比。

column2: The swordsmen lose, sheathe their blades and send Qian Mancang's deposit back untouched. Their leader's little brother is one of the name-bearers, 'Big Gou'. “I hire out my sword down below; he minds a stall up here. Neither of us has shamed the family.” He has the tents struck, and next day his men are at the fairground putting up awnings.
column3: 刀客们输了，收刀入鞘，把钱满仓的定金原样退了回去。领头的刀客说他弟弟就是借了名字的孩子之一，叫「苟大个儿」，「我在山下替人卖命，他在山上替人守摊，谁也没给家里丢脸」。他让手下拆了帐篷，第二天去集场帮着搭棚。

column2: The Roll-Call Stones
column3: 点卯石

column2: A circle of stones stands on the open country, a name carved on each, where the children hold roll call before every fair. Sun Big-Bowl stands in the middle calling names. At two hundred and ninety-eight, no one answers: Zhou Qi is missing. Beyond the circle some tea-house hands are galloping off on yaks with a trussed-up child across a saddle. The rest of them block the road and draw on you.
column3: 野地上一圈石头，每块刻着一个名字，是孩子们每年开集前点名的地方。孙大碗站在圈中间点名，点到二百九十八，没人应了：周七不见了。石圈外，几个茶号的伙计骑着牦牛跑远，牛背上横着一个捆起来的孩子。剩下的伙计横在路上，拔刀拦住了你们。

column2: The hands are knocked off their yaks and Zhou Qi untied, his own felt cap stuffed in his mouth. He spits it out and shouts “Here!” towards the stones. Only then does Sun Big-Bowl call the last: “Two hundred and ninety-nine. All present.” That rule came from them too, the children say: they counted heads every morning and never set out until everyone was there.
column3: 伙计们被打下了牦牛，周七被解了下来，嘴里还塞着他自己的毡帽。他吐掉帽子，冲着石圈喊了一声「到」。孙大碗这才往下点：「二百九十九，到齐。」孩子们说，这个规矩也是那些人留的：他们每天出门前点一回，点齐了才走。

column2: The Temple Fairground
column3: 神庙集场

column2: Beneath the temple, two hundred and ninety-nine stone stalls stand in rows, packed with yak dealers, butter grannies, thangka painters and salt caravans: the yearly fair has opened. The foremost stall carries an old wooden sign, 'Qianli', but Qian Mancang's men hold it, snow-mountain archers crouched on its roof aiming at anyone who comes near. The children stand outside with the tea they pressed in their arms.
column3: 神庙脚下，二百九十九个石摊一行行排开，牦牛贩子、酥油阿妈、唐卡画师、盐帮的马队挤得水泄不通，一年一回的庙会开集了。最前头那个石摊挂着一块旧木牌，刻着「千里号」，却被钱满仓的人占了，雪山弓手蹲在摊顶上，谁走近就拿箭指着谁。孩子们抱着自己压的茶砖，站在摊外。

column2: The archers are driven off the roof. Zhou Qi wipes the sign clean and the children file in. The fair trades again: the herders' barley and butter for lowland iron pots and horseshoes, twelve thousand jin a day, until dark. Kelsang reads the roll from the stall's old ledger, and all two hundred and ninety-nine names are answered. The last page, six years old, says: 'Goods sold out. Gone east. Stall left to those who come after.' Now you see it: the doubles were never impostors. The men left, and their names stayed to keep the fair for them.
column3: 弓手被赶下了摊顶。周七把木牌擦干净，孩子们一个挨一个坐了进去。集场重开，牧人的青稞、酥油换山下的铁锅、马掌，一天一万二千斤，买卖做到天黑。格桑捧着摊上的旧账点名，二百九十九个名字，个个有人答「到」。旧账最后一页是六年前的字：「货尽。人东去。摊留后来者。」这时你们才明白，替身不是冒名：他们走了，名字还在这儿替他们赶集。

column2: The White-Mask Holdup
column3: 白面劫

column2: Out on the open country, men in white masks have stopped a salt caravan, bellowing like cracked gongs: “Toll for the Mountain God's guardians!” The salt men drop to their knees and start unloading. The masks are felt daubed white with paste, and fox-fur hats poke out behind. A young lama travelling with the caravan stays on his feet and mutters, “The guardians never take money.”
column3: 野地上，一伙戴白面具的人截住了一支盐帮的驮队，嗓门粗得像破锣：「山神的护法收路钱！」盐帮的人扑通扑通跪了一地，把盐块往外搬。面具是拿面糊刷白的毡片，后脑勺还露着狐皮帽。跟着驮队的一个年轻喇嘛站着没跪，嘟囔了一句：「护法从来不收钱。」

column2: The masks come off: horse thieves. The young lama is Phuntsok, who left the temple's guardians. Real masks, he says, are carved from birch, gleaming white, with no mouth, no nose, and eyeholes no bigger than grains of barley. “The strangest is their leader. In winter he stands in the wind and fog pours from under his mask.”
column3: 假护法被扯下了面具，原来是一伙盗马贼。年轻喇嘛叫平措，是从神庙护法里退出来的，他说真面具是桦木刻的，白得发亮，没有嘴，没有鼻子，眼孔只有麦粒大。「最怪的是领头的那一位，」他说，「冬天站在风里，面具底下往外冒雾。」

column2: The Fair Wall
column3: 护集墙

column2: On the fair's second day the biggest horse-thief band of the northern grassland arrives, swordsmen, archers and riders bearing down on the fairground in three columns; every year they come when the fair is at its richest. A chest-high stone wall rings the ground, and the children are already behind it with their slings. That wall the Han men built as well, Kelsang says: “They said a fat market brings the wolves.”
column3: 开集第二天，北边草原上最大的一伙盗马贼来了，刀手、弓手、骑手三路压向集场，他们年年挑庙会最热闹的时候来抢一回。集场外有一道齐胸的石墙，孩子们早早守在墙后，手里攥着抛石绳。格桑说这道墙也是那些汉人垒的：「他们说，集市肥了，狼就来。」

column2: The thieves fall back to the grassland, leaving a litter of whips outside the wall. For the first time the children have held the fair without losing a single yak. A stone at the wall's foot is carved small: 'Wall, three feet. Tea, seven layers. Leave only when all are here.' Sun Big-Bowl runs her fingers over it. Those men had to leave a rule for everything.
column3: 盗马贼退回了草原，墙外丢了一地马鞭。孩子们头一回守住了集，没丢一头牛。墙根下一块石头上刻着小字：「墙，三尺。茶，七层。人，齐了再走。」孙大碗摸着字说，这些人，什么都要留个规矩。

column2: The Mountain God's Shrine
column3: 山神祠

column2: At the very heart of the gravel flats stands a small stone shrine. There is no god's image inside, only a suit of bright plate armour hung on a wooden frame, its seven hundred scales polished till they gleam, the heart-mirror clear enough to see your face in, the helmet set squarely on top. At the door a dozen herders who worship the armour sit on their yaks with long whips raised, letting no outsider near their 'god's armour'. Inside, an old man stands with his back to the door, polishing it with an old piece of felt.
column3: 碎石滩最深处一座小小的石祠，祠里没有神像，只有一副明光甲挂在木架上，七百片甲叶擦得锃亮，护心镜照得见人影，头盔端端正正扣在架顶。祠门口，十几个拜甲的牧人骑在牦牛上，举着赶牛的长鞭，不许外人走近他们的「神甲」。祠里那个老汉背对着门，正拿一块旧毡擦甲。

column2: The armour's worshippers draw back. The old man turns round. His left hand is missing its little finger. You hand him the letter. He looks at the seal, doesn't open it, and tucks it inside his coat: 'It was going to say I'd be home on the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month. I didn't go, so I didn't send it.' Aunt Qin has been reaping barley on the terraces for ten years, and every year he has gone to help, and never dared tell her who he is. He lifts down the helmet and takes from inside it a bronze token engraved COMMANDER, GRAVEL CAMP: 'Take it. Go into a barracks and call out Gravel Camp, fall in!, and the old lads will come.' That twelfth month, the Han man with the casket told him: 'I'll guard the mountain for you. You guard the foot of it for me.' He has, for ten years. Now that you've come, he's going back to the terraces to help Aunt Qin with the harvest.
column3: 拜甲的牧人退开了。老汉转过身，左手少一根小指。你们把那封信递给他，他看了看封口，没拆，揣进了怀里：「本来要写『腊月廿五回家』，不回了，就没寄。」秦婶就在屯田坝割了十年麦，他每年去帮着割，一直没敢认。他摘下头盔，从盔里取出一块铜令，刻着「碎石营营将」：「拿去。到兵营里喊一声『碎石营，归营』，老兄弟们会来的。」那年腊月，背匣子的汉人跟他说：「山我替你守，山下你替我守。」他守了十年。如今你们来了，他要回屯田坝，帮秦婶割麦去了。

column2: The Butter Stall
column3: 酥油摊

column2: At the fair's edge is a butter stall kept by a round-faced old woman, her butter sewn into sheep's stomachs and stacked like a small hill. She traded with Wantong once, was beaten down to half price, and has trusted nobody since: a sign hangs out front, 'Not for outsiders'. Qian Mancang's men are still planted there, pressing her to sell the lot to Wantong at their price.
column3: 集场边一个酥油摊，摊主是个圆脸的老阿妈，酥油拿羊肚包着，一包一包码得像小山。她跟万通号做过一回买卖，被压了半价，从此谁也不信，摊前挂着块牌子「不卖外人」。钱满仓的几个家丁还守在摊前，逼她把酥油全数作价卖给万通号。

column2: The men are driven off. The old woman looks you over a long while, then turns the sign round: 'For sale'. The real Sun Big-Bowl had the stall next door, she says, and traded tea for her butter every day for four years. She also sells rebirth pills for the temple doctor, 'washing away a lifetime's toil and keeping a lifetime's skill', though the ninety-year-old Lama Gonpo won't take one: “He says this life isn't finished yet.”
column3: 家丁被打跑，老阿妈打量你们半天，把牌子翻了个面：「卖」。她说真孙大碗当年就在她隔壁，天天拿茶换她的酥油，一换四年。她还替庙里的曼巴代卖转世丹，「洗去一世的劳苦，留下一世的本事」，可九十岁的贡布喇嘛不肯吃：「他说这一世还没过完。」

column2: Qian Mancang's Tent
column3: 满仓帐

column2: In a patched old tent on the open country Qian Mancang is hiding, with only a few unpaid archers left, arrows trained on the door, guarding his last chest of silver. What comes out of the tent is not cursing but sobbing: Qian Mancang is clutching a yellowed sheet of paper and crying like a child.
column3: 野地上一顶缝缝补补的旧帐篷，钱满仓躲在里头，身边只剩几个讨不到工钱的弓手，拿箭对着帐门，守着他最后一箱银子。帐篷里传出来的不是骂声，是哭声：钱满仓抱着一张发黄的纸，哭得像个孩子。

column2: The archers bolt. The yellowed sheet is the Qianli hiring roll from ten years ago, and one name on it is blotted out with ink: Qian Mancang. Wantong sent him to join, and on the night before departure he lost his nerve. “That stall should have had a seat for me.” Sun Big-Bowl thinks it over, then sets a stool for him in the First Stall. “Sit. Under your own name.”
column3: 弓手们一哄而散。那张发黄的纸是十年前千里号招伙计的名帖，上头有一个名字被墨涂掉了：钱满仓。他原是万通号派去的伙计，临出发那夜怕了，没去。「那个摊子，本来该有我一个座儿。」孙大碗想了想，在第一摊里给他搬了个马扎：「坐吧。用你自己的名字。」

column2: White-Hair Blizzard
column3: 白毛风

column2: A white-hair blizzard blows up on the open country, the snow stinging too hard to keep your eyes open. A few children travelling east huddle outside a tent that a band of unpaid hired archers has taken over; the archers won't let them in, saying there's only warmth enough for their own. The wind keeps rising, and the children's yaks have turned their backs to it, heads pressed together.
column3: 野地上忽然起了白毛风，雪粒子打得人睁不开眼。几个往东赶路的孩子缩在一顶帐篷外头，帐篷让一伙讨不到工钱的雇佣弓手占了，他们不许孩子进去，说帐里只够自己人暖和。风越刮越大，孩子们的牦牛已经背过身去，头抵着头。

column2: You throw the archers out, then call them back in, and everyone crams into one tent for the night. Too cold to sleep, the children sing an escort's hauling song, badly off key. The archers listen a long time and ask where they learned it. The real Old Han taught them, Sun Big-Bowl says. “He said Chief Lu sang it even worse.”
column3: 弓手被撵了出去，又被你们喊了回来，大伙挤在一顶帐里熬了一夜。半夜冷得睡不着，孩子们唱起一首跑镖的号子，跑调跑得厉害。弓手们听了半天，问是哪里学的。孙大碗说是真老韩教的：「他说陆镖头唱得比他还跑调。」

column2: The Freak-Show Cart
column3: 奇人车

column2: A gaudy wagon is parked on the open country, painted 'Wonders of the World': a travelling show from the lowlands. Its master has heard of a 'man without a face' on the snow mountain and hired snow-mountain archers to catch one for a cage. They haven't caught the real one, but they've caught Phuntsok and are stuffing him into the cage, his mask torn off in the dirt.
column3: 野地上停着一辆花花绿绿的大车，车上写着「天下奇人」，是山下来的杂耍班子。班主听说雪山上有个「无面人」，雇了一伙雪山弓手，要捉一个回去关在笼子里给人看。真的没捉着，倒把平措捉住了，正往笼子里塞，他的面具被扯落在地上。

column2: The archers are chased away and Phuntsok climbs out of the cage, brushing snow from his mask. The showman stares at his face a long while: young, sun-burnt, with chilblains. Bitterly disappointed, he still asks, “And the one with the fog?” No one has ever seen his face, Phuntsok says. He has led the guardians for nine years, and everyone just calls him Faceless.
column3: 弓手被赶跑，平措从笼里爬出来，拍掉面具上的雪。班主盯着他的脸看了半天：一张晒得黑红的年轻脸，还长着冻疮。班主大失所望，又不死心：「那个冒雾的呢？」平措说没人见过他的脸，九年来他是护法的头，大伙就叫他「无面」。

column2: Under-the-Lake Village
column3: 湖下村

column2: A small village on the open country lies below a lake hanging in the valley behind it. The villagers call it the Dragon Lake: every few decades, they say, the dragon comes down and scours the valley flat. The water rose this summer, and a sorcerer has turned up with a gang of toughs, forcing every house to carry its year's butter up and throw it in to feed the dragon. By now the temple guardians usually come to subdue the dragon. This year they haven't.
column3: 野地上一个小村子，村后的山谷里悬着一个湖，村里人叫它龙湖，说湖里的龙每过几十年就下山一回，把整条谷冲平。今年夏天湖水涨了，村里来了个巫师，带着一帮打手，逼各家把一年的酥油都扛上山扔进湖里喂龙。往年这时候，神庙的护法会来镇龙，今年还没来。

column2: The sorcerer and his toughs are run off and the butter stays home. Amma Yangdzom says the dragon came down twice in fifty years, and not once since the white-masked guardians arrived nine years ago. Every summer they go up to 'subdue the dragon' and come back mud to the thighs, their picks worn blunt. “Subduing a dragon,” she says, “how does that get you so muddy?”
column3: 巫师和打手被赶下了山，酥油留在了各家。央宗阿妈说，五十年里龙下来过两回；自从九年前戴白面具的护法来了，一回也没有。护法们每年夏天上去「镇龙」，回来时泥浆糊到大腿，镐头都磨秃了。「镇龙，」她说，「怎么镇得一身泥？」

column2: The Bay Lookout
column3: 湖湾哨

column2: In a bay of the holy lake some men dressed as horse herders squat behind rocks all day watching the fairground's horses: horse-thief lookouts, plainly. After every fair the children drive their yaks round the lake, bowing a circuit for the two hundred and ninety-nine. Afraid of being recognised, the lookouts draw blades across the mouth of the bay.
column3: 圣湖边的湖湾里，几个牧马人模样的人整天蹲在石头后面，望着集场那边的马群，一看就是盗马贼的眼线。孩子们要赶着牦牛去湖边转湖，替那二百九十九个人磕一圈头，这是每年散集后的规矩。眼线们怕被认出来，拔刀堵在了湖湾口。

column2: The lookouts scatter, and the one who escapes runs deeper into the bay, where the thieves' den lies. The children finish their bows and scatter a pinch of tea dust on the water. Those men came here too before they left, Sun Big-Bowl says. “They said the lake water runs east, and at the end of it is the sea.”
column3: 眼线被打散，跑掉的那个往湖湾深处去了：盗马贼的老窝就在那里。孩子们在湖边磕完头，往湖里撒了一把茶末。孙大碗说那些人走前也来过这里：「他们说，湖水往东流，流到底就是海。」

column2: The Crampon Store
column3: 冰爪库

column2: At the far end of the open ground behind the fair stands a stone storehouse half sunk in the earth, a great iron lock on its door. The fiercest crew of the northern thieves has made it their fort, three ranks of blades, bows and horses at the door and a stolen crossbow mounted on the roof. The two hundred and ninety-nine sealed it before they left, the children say, and gave the key to Kelsang. No one has ever opened it.
column3: 集场后头的野地尽头，一座半埋进土里的石库房，门上一把大铁锁。北边盗马贼里最狠的一帮占了它当堡子，刀、弓、马三层守着门，库房顶上还架着抢来的弩。孩子们说，这座库房是那二百九十九个人走前封上的，钥匙交给了格桑，谁也没打开过。

column2: The thieves are driven out and Kelsang turns the key. Inside, row on row of iron crampons hang on the walls, their straps oiled, and a line is written above them: 'For the ice. Those left over are for whoever comes after.' At the very end hangs one pair on its own, a size larger, its straps tied in escort knots, a small tag nailed beneath: 'The chief's.' Every year, the children say, Kelsang unlocks the door to oil it.
column3: 盗马贼被打出了库房。格桑开了锁：墙上一排排挂着铁打的冰爪，绑带都上过油，墙上写着：「过冰用。余者留给后来的人。」最边上单挂着一副，比别的大一号，绑带上打着镖扣，底下钉着一块小木牌：「镖头的。」孩子们说，格桑每年开一回锁，给它上一回油。

column2: Dhole Hut
column3: 豺口屋

column2: A pack of dholes circles a little stone hut on the open country, red-coated and sharp-muzzled, yelping in chorus. Inside is trapped Gunga, an old temple guardian, long blind, who lives here alone watching a boundary stone. The pack chased blue sheep all night, and now, smelling tsampa, they're clawing at the door. That's his teacher, Phuntsok says.
column3: 野地上一座小石屋，屋外一群豺狗围着打转，红毛尖嘴，一叫一大片。屋里困着神庙的老护法贡嘎，眼睛早瞎了，一个人住在这里看守一块界石。豺群撵了一夜岩羊，又闻见屋里的糌粑味，开始拿爪子刨门。平措说，那是他的师父。

column2: The dholes are driven up the mountain and Gunga laughs, feeling Phuntsok's face. Ten years ago, he says, the temple's guardians were down to three old men; the winter rules went unkept and several travellers froze on the pass every year. That last month, two hundred and ninety-nine Han men arrived who couldn't get back down, and knelt to the old lama: “Give us work.” He gave them two hundred and ninety-nine white masks.
column3: 豺群被赶上了山，贡嘎摸着平措的脸笑了。他说十年前庙里的护法只剩三个老头，冬天的规矩没人守，过山的人一年冻死好几个。那年腊月来了二百九十九个汉人，下不了山，跪下来求老喇嘛：「让我们干点活。」老喇嘛给了他们二百九十九张白面具。

column2: Horse-Thief Bay
column3: 盗马湾

column2: A bay of the holy lake, cliffs on three sides and water on the fourth, where the northern horse thieves have their den: stolen horses penned under the cliffs, tents strung along the shore, fires burning all night. The busier the fair grows each year, the more of them come. They have blades, bows and horses; the ones guarding the bay mouth are new recruits still holding their swords the wrong way round.
column3: 圣湖的一处湖湾，三面陡崖，一面临水，北边草原的盗马贼在这里扎了窝：抢来的马关在崖下，帐篷沿着湖岸搭了一溜，篝火彻夜不灭。庙会一年比一年热闹，他们也一年比一年来得多。刀、弓、马都有，守湾口的几个是刚入伙的，刀还拿反着。

column2: This nest is cleared and the horses go home. But as long as the fair goes on and its horses are fat, someone on the northern grassland will always take up the trade, and within months new tents will rise in the bay, so it has to be cleared before every fair. That's an old rule too, the children say: “A fat market brings the wolves; when the wolves come, you fight.”
column3: 这一窝被端了，马放回了各家。可只要庙会还在，集上的马肥，北边草原上就总有人来投这一行，过不了几个月，湾里又会搭起新帐篷，只能每年开集前来清一回。孩子们说这也是老规矩：「集市肥了，狼就来；狼来了，就打。」

column2: Frozen Hollow
column3: 冻雪坳

column2: In a herder's tent on the open country, a white mask sits in the household shrine, cracked and stitched with yak sinew. Horse thieves have heard that lowlanders pay a fortune for 'the Mountain God's face' and have burst in to take it, while the old herder hugs the shrine and won't let go for his life.
column3: 野地上一顶牧人的帐篷，帐里的佛龛上供着一张白面具，裂了一道缝，拿牛筋缝着。一伙盗马贼听说汉地有人出大价钱买「山神的脸」，闯进帐里要抢面具，牧人老阿爸抱着佛龛，死也不撒手。

column2: Eight years ago on a snowy night, the old man says, his father lay frozen on the pass and a white-masked guardian carried him down. Halfway, the guardian lifted his mask to catch his breath: a Han face, beard full of ice, and he said, laughing, “Don't tell anyone the Mountain God's a Han.” Phuntsok sees it at last: the fog under the mask is just warm breath, steaming from the eyeholes the moment it meets the cold wind.
column3: 老阿爸说八年前的雪夜，他阿爸冻僵在垭口，是一个白面具的护法背下山的。半路护法掀起面具喘气，底下是一张汉人的脸，胡子上全是冰碴，笑着说：「别跟人说，山神是个汉人。」平措恍然：面具下的雾，是人呼出的热气，从眼孔里冒出来，一碰冷风就成了白汽。

column2: The Gold-Panners' Dam
column3: 淘金坝

column2: By the lake a long bank of earth and stone holds back the Dragon Lake above, and its foot is swarming with gold panners hacking with picks and sluicing with water, leaving it riddled with holes. Their boss, Jin the Third, has hired snow-mountain archers to keep everyone away. A post stands on top of the dam with a board nailed to it, which the archers are using for target practice.
column3: 湖边一道长长的土石坝挡着上头的龙湖，坝脚下挤满了淘金客，拿镐刨，拿水冲，坝脚被挖出一个个窟窿。淘金客的头子金老三雇了一伙雪山弓手守着金场，不许人靠近。坝顶插着一根木桩，桩上钉着一块木牌，被弓手们拿来当了靶子。

column2: The archers are driven off and the panners scatter. The board is shot full of holes, but you can still read it: 'Not one spade on this dam.' It isn't signed with a name, only a drawing of a blank face. Phuntsok goes pale. With its foot dug out like this, the dragon will come down.
column3: 弓手被赶走，淘金客四散。木牌被箭扎得千疮百孔，字还认得出：「此坝不许动一锹。」落款不是字，是画的一张空白的脸。平措脸色发白：坝脚刨成这样，龙要下来了。

column2: Runaway Calf Slope
column3: 走犊坡

column2: A black yak calf has snapped its tether and gone frisking up a slope on the open country, chased by a ten-year-old herd boy whose nose has frozen into icicles. Horse thieves resting on the slope lasso it at once and declare it theirs. The youngest of them, thin as a stick, holds the rope and looks from the calf to the boy and back.
column3: 野地上一头黑牦牛犊子挣断了绳，一路撒欢跑上了坡，后头追着个十岁的放牛娃，鼻涕冻成了冰溜子。坡上一伙盗马贼正在歇脚，伸手就把牛犊套住了，说归他们了。盗马贼里有个最小的，瘦得像根柴，牵着绳子，看看牛犊，又看看娃娃。

column2: The thieves run, but the youngest is too slow and you haul him back, his stomach growling. You give him a tea cake and let him go. The herd boy, Dondrub, hugs his calf. “My mother is Yangchen. She reads the ice.” Six years ago she led a big band of Han men over the eastern glacier, he says, “and now people keep coming to grab her and make her do it again.”
column3: 盗马贼被打跑，最小的那个没跑掉，被你们拎了回来，肚子饿得咕咕响。你们给了他一块茶饼，放他走了。放牛娃叫顿珠，抱着牛犊直蹭：「我阿妈叫央金，是认冰的。」他说阿妈六年前领一大队汉人走过东边的冰川，「后来就有人来抓她，要她再领一回」。

column2: Flagpole Bay
column3: 旗杆湾

column2: In a bay of the holy lake stand a few big tents under the banner of Sangye, a chieftain from the eastern grassland. Dondrub's mother Yangchen is tied to the flagpole, yak riders around her, being pressed to guide them over the eastern glacier: the chieftain wants a short cut across the ice to raid the trade road beyond. Yangchen bites her lip, eyes on the lake, and says nothing.
column3: 圣湖边的湖湾里扎着几顶大帐，帐前插着东边草原桑杰头人的旗。顿珠的阿妈央金被绑在旗杆上，几个牦牛骑围着她，逼她带路过东边的冰川：头人想从冰上抄近路，去劫山那边的商道。央金咬着嘴唇，眼睛望着湖，一声不吭。

column2: The riders scatter and Yangchen, untied, sweeps Dondrub into her arms. The band she led over six years ago, she says, was two hundred and ninety-nine strong, every one in iron crampons. “They said they were going to the sea. I asked where the sea was. They said: follow the water; water always gets to the sea.” She refused the chieftain. “That ice is for good people to walk.”
column3: 牦牛骑被打散，央金解了下来，一把搂住顿珠。她说六年前领过冰的那队人，二百九十九个，个个脚上绑着铁冰爪，「他们说要去海里。我问海在哪儿，他们说，顺着水走，水总要到海里」。她不肯给头人带路：「那条冰，是给好人走的。」

column2: The Winter Fold
column3: 冬窝子

column2: On the open country is a winter fold where a few herding families stack the hay they cut in summer inside stone rings, kept for when the snow lies deep. Chieftain Sangye's rearguard has seized it and is feeding the herders' hay to its own horses, stack by stack; at this rate it won't last to spring. The herders circle outside with their thin cattle, unable to get in.
column3: 野地上一片冬窝子，几户牧人夏天割下的草一垛垛码在石圈里，留着雪大时喂牛。桑杰头人的后队把这里占了，拿牧人的草喂自己的马，一垛一垛地拆，眼看着撑不到开春。牧人们赶着瘦牛在圈外转，进不去。

column2: The rearguard is driven off and the hay restacked; more than half is left. The Han men enlarged this fold, Yangchen says: they rested here a night and, before leaving, raised the stone rings three feet. “So the snow wouldn't bury the hay, they said.”
column3: 后队被赶走，草垛重新码好，还剩大半。央金说这片冬窝子是那年汉人们帮着扩的：他们在这里歇过一夜，临走把石圈加高了三尺，「说草别让雪埋了」。

column2: What the rearguard left: two carts of bean fodder, a good tent, a dozen sets of horseshoes, a jar of barley wine, and the chieftain's own map of the glacier, so wrong that Yangchen laughed and used it to line Dondrub's boots.
column3: 后队留下的：两车豆料、一顶好帐篷、十几副马蹄铁、一坛青稞酒，还有一张头人画的冰川图，画得全不对，央金看了直笑，拿去给顿珠垫了靴子。

column2: Every time you pass, the herders pull a bundle out of a haystack for you: dried yak meat and a little crock of yoghurt. “Kept in the hay, it doesn't freeze.”
column3: 每次路过，冬窝子的牧人都从草垛里掏出一包东西塞给你们：风干的牦牛肉，还有一小罐酸奶，「在草里捂着，冻不硬」。

column2: The Dragon-Slaying Altar
column3: 斩龙坛

column2: An altar has gone up on the open country, bristling with yellow talismans, where a lowland Taoist named Zhang Tianzhen waves a peach-wood sword and vows to climb up and slay the dragon, for a fee of one ox per village. His hired toughs have shaved their heads to look like temple strongmen and carry kegs of gunpowder: 'heavenly thunder' for the slaying.
column3: 野地上搭起一座法坛，坛上插满了黄符，一个山下来的道士张天镇挥着桃木剑，说要上山斩龙，每个村收一头牛当法资。他雇来的打手都剃着光头，扮成力士，扛着几桶火药，说是斩龙用的「天雷」。

column2: The toughs scatter and the kegs are clapped down on the altar. Zhang Tianzhen, terrified, confesses everything. “Dragon? There's no dragon. That lake's held back by a heap of loose rubble. I saw one burst once down south; it took half a county.” He meant to scare a few villages, collect and leave; the 'thunder' was to blow a gap in the dam as a show of power. Phuntsok breaks into a cold sweat.
column3: 打手被打散，火药桶扣在了坛上。张天镇吓得全招了：「龙？哪有龙。那湖就是拿一堆乱石头挡着的，我在山下见过一回决口，冲走了半个县。」他本想吓唬几个村子收点钱就走，「天雷」是用来炸开坝口、显一显灵的。平措听得出了一身冷汗。

column2: Guardians' Rest House
column3: 护法歇房

column2: A low stone hut on the open country, dried dung stacked under its eaves and a stove, tsampa and a copper pot inside: the temple guardians rest here on patrol, and any traveller may come in to warm up. Horse thieves have taken it over, burned most of the fuel, eaten every scrap of tsampa, and hung a sign on the door: 'This house has an owner.'
column3: 野地上一间低矮的石屋，屋檐下码着一垛垛干牛粪，屋里有灶，有糌粑，有一口铜锅，是神庙护法巡山歇脚的地方，路过的人也能进来暖一暖。一伙盗马贼把这里占了，牛粪烧了大半，糌粑吃得精光，门口还挂了块牌子：「本屋已有主」。

column2: The thieves are chased out, the hut swept, the stove lit again. A row of pegs on the wall holds a few old white masks, yellowed round the eyeholes with smoke. The guardians stop here a night on patrol, Phuntsok says, and set off next morning only after a roll call. “Another rule the Han men left.”
column3: 盗马贼被赶跑，石屋收拾干净，灶又生了火。墙上一排木钉挂着几张旧白面具，眼孔边熏得发黄。平措说，护法们巡山在这里歇一夜，第二天一早点了名才走：「这也是汉人留下的规矩。」

column2: The thieves' stores: half a room of stolen dung fuel, four bags of tsampa, a looted copper kettle, a few fox-fur hats, and a stack of felt masks daubed white with paste, which Phuntsok feeds into the stove one by one.
column3: 盗马贼囤下的：半屋子劫来的干牛粪、四袋糌粑、一把抢来的铜壶、几顶狐皮帽，还有一摞拿面糊刷白的毡片面具，平措一张张扔进了灶里。

column2: Every time you pass, the people of Under-the-Lake have already left something in the rest house: a bag of tsampa, a strip of dried meat, a bundle of kindling, and under it a note with a smiling face drawn by the village children, who think the guardians' faces are far too white.
column3: 每次路过，湖下村的人都已经在歇房里放好了东西：一袋糌粑、一块风干肉、一把干柴，压着一张画着笑脸的纸条，是村里孩子画的，说护法的脸太白了。

column2: Name-Stone Beach
column3: 名石滩

column2: On the holy lake's eastern shore lies a ring of flat stones, each the size of a tea brick, each carved with a Han name and turned to face east. Some snow-mountain archers building quarters for the chieftain are prising them up and loading them on ox carts. Yangchen rushes to stop them and an archer shoves her down at the water's edge.
column3: 圣湖东岸一片湖滩，滩上摆着一圈扁石头，块块有茶砖那么大，每块刻着一个汉名，面朝东。几个雪山弓手替头人修营房，正把石头一块块撬起来装上牛车。央金冲上去拦，被一个弓手推倒在湖边。

column2: The archers are chased away and the stones set back one by one, all two hundred and ninety-nine. They laid these the night before they left, Yangchen says, “and talked to the lake all night.” The easternmost stone bears no name, only an arrow, and in front of the arrow a single character: 'Sea'.
column3: 弓手被打跑，石头一块块摆回原处，二百九十九块，一块不少。央金说这是他们走前一夜摆的，「对着湖说了一夜的话」。最东边那块没刻名字，只刻了一个箭头，箭头前面一个字：「海」。

column2: The Name Cave
column3: 面壁洞

column2: A small hill on the open country has a shallow cave in it, its walls crowded with charcoal writing. A band of snow-mountain archers uses it as a lookout and lights fires inside, the smoke blackening the walls until some lines can no longer be read. This is the guardians' name cave, Phuntsok says: on the day each one first puts on the mask, he writes his name here.
column3: 野地上一座小山包，山包上有个浅洞，洞壁上密密麻麻写满了炭字。一伙雪山弓手把这里当了望风的哨，在洞里生火，烟把墙熏得越来越黑，有几行字已经看不清了。平措说这是护法的名洞：每个人戴上面具那天，都要在这里写下自己的名字。

column2: By torchlight you read the wall. For the first four years: two hundred and ninety-nine Han names. For the six after: herders' names from below, Phuntsok's among them. The very first line is empty except for a drawn lamp. That's Faceless, Phuntsok says. “He never writes his name.” The white mask who dug a baby out of the buried camp must have been one of those two hundred and ninety-nine.
column3: 火把一行行照过去：头四年，是二百九十九个汉名；后面六年，是山下牧人的名字，平措的也在里头。最前头一行是空的，只画了一盏灯，平措说那是无面的，「他从来不写名字」。雪埋营里刨出娃娃的那个白面具，也该是这二百九十九个里的一个。

column2: The Boot-Felt Tent
column3: 靴毡帐

column2: In a little tent on the open country an old woman in a thimble is stitching felt boot liners, a pile of felt beside her taller than she is. Some of the chieftain's cavalry burst in demanding a hundred pairs in three days for his men to cross the glacier, or they'll burn the tent. She says she sews only one kind of boot, and only one pair a year.
column3: 野地上一顶小帐篷，帐里一个老阿妈戴着顶针，正缝一双毡靴里子，身边摞着的毡片比她人还高。头人的几个骑兵闯进来，要她三天内缝一百双，给头人的兵过冰川用，缝不完就烧帐篷。老阿妈说她只缝一种靴子，一年只缝一双。

column2: The cavalry are driven out. Six years ago, she says, she sewed liners for those Han men all one winter, until her fingers were full of needle pricks. But they ordered three hundred pairs: “There's one more, not here yet.” She has kept the three hundredth pair ever since, unpicking and resewing it every year so the felt won't rot. She wraps it and presses it on you. “When you meet that one, give it to him from me.”
column3: 骑兵被赶走了。老阿妈说六年前她给那队汉人缝过靴里子，缝了一个冬天，手指头全是针眼。可汉人们要的是三百双：「还有一个，没到。」第三百双她一直留着，每年拆了重缝一回，怕毡子朽了。她把那双靴里子包好，塞给你们：「见着那一个，替我给他。」

column2: Black Ice River
column3: 黑冰河

column2: A frozen river crosses the open country, and the chieftain's foot soldiers have set a checkpoint on it: one sheep from anyone crossing the ice. Yangchen leads you to the bank but won't use their crossing; she points to a dark, glossy patch. “That's thin.” The soldiers laugh at her for a coward, line up right on the black ice and draw on you.
column3: 野地上一条封冻的河，头人的步卒在冰面上设了卡，谁从冰上过河都要交一只羊。央金领你们走到河边，却不走他们的冰面，指着冰上一片发黑发亮的地方：「那儿薄。」头人的人不信，嘲笑她胆小，还在那片黑冰上排着队，拔刀拦住你们。
