column2: As the fighting starts, the black ice cracks and gives way, dropping a whole row into waist-deep water; you haul them out one by one, too cold to speak. Her father taught her, Yangchen says: ice that looks black is so thin you're seeing the water through it; thick ice is white and cloudy. That's how she brought all two hundred and ninety-nine across this river without losing one.
column3: 一交手，那片黑冰咔嚓塌了，一排人掉进齐腰的冰水里，被你们一个个拽上来，冻得说不出话。央金说是她爹教的：冰透着黑，是薄得能看见底下的水；又白又浑的，才是厚冰。那年她就这么领着二百九十九个人，一个不少过了这条河。

column2: The Chieftain's Camp
column3: 头人营

column2: Chieftain Sangye's main camp sprawls over the open country, swordsmen, archers and riders in three wings, a great banner showing a glacier and an arrow pointing east. Without a guide, he is drilling his men to force the ice on their own. At the gate lie dozens of hastily forged crampons, their spikes all crooked.
column3: 野地上扎着桑杰头人的大营，刀手、弓手、骑手三路，营里立着一面大旗，旗上画着冰川和一条往东的箭头。头人在营里练兵，没了向导，就要靠自己硬闯冰川。营门口堆着几十副临时打的冰爪，铁齿歪歪扭扭。

column2: The camp is broken and the chieftain flees on horseback towards the glacier. Yangchen picks up one of the crampons, looks it over and tosses it away. “Spikes like that, you'll slide.” The Han men forged their own, she says, the spikes set at a slant. “They said crossing ice is like crossing a cliff: the nail has to angle inward.”
column3: 大营被冲散，头人骑马往冰川那边逃了。央金拎起一副冰爪看了看就扔了：「这种齿，踩上去就打滑。」她说那队汉人的冰爪是自己打的，齿斜着打，「他们说，过冰跟过崖一样，钉子要往里斜」。

column2: The Ice Tongue
column3: 冰舌口

column2: The glacier's tongue runs right into the lake, its ice cliff blue going on black, and the beach at its foot keeps turning up things melted out of the ice: a leather boot, a length of rope, a bone. A gang of scavengers has hired archers to hold the ice foot and sells whatever they find. Today they've found a bronze bell and are quarrelling over it.
column3: 冰川的冰舌一直伸进湖里，冰崖蓝得发黑，冰脚下的湖滩上时不时冒出些从冰里化出来的东西：一只皮靴，一截绳子，一块骨头。一伙捡宝的山民雇了几个弓手守着冰脚，捡到什么都拿去卖。今天他们捡到一只铜铃，正为它吵架。

column2: You win the bell back: red thread wound round its clapper: a Qianli mule bell. A glacier moves, Yangchen says, very slowly, creeping down a little every year, and whatever falls into a crevasse comes out from under the tongue sooner or later. “A mule fell in a crevasse that year. Not a single person did.” She polishes the bell. “It took six years to walk this far.”
column3: 铜铃抢了回来，铃舌上缠着红线，是千里号骡队的驮铃。央金说冰川是在走的，走得极慢，一年往下挪一截，掉进冰缝的东西，过几年总会从冰舌底下吐出来。「那年过冰缝，掉下去一头骡子，人一个没掉。」她把铃擦干净：「它走了六年，才走到这儿。」

column2: Staves Across the Road
column3: 封路棍

column2: A line of guardian monks stands across the main road, leather armour over crimson robes, iron-shod staves planted in a row. Their leader relays Faceless's word: “The Dragon Lake's channel is to be opened. This road is closed three days.” Phuntsok tells them about the panners and the Taoist's powder, and still they won't budge: “Rules are rules. To pass, get past us.”
column3: 大路上横着一排护法僧兵，绛红袍外罩着皮甲，包铁的长棍齐刷刷戳在地上。领头的传无面的话：「龙湖要开渠放水，这条路封三天。」平措上前说淘金客刨坏了坝脚、道士要拿火药炸坝，护法们听了也不让：「规矩就是规矩，要过，先过我们。」

column2: The monks lower their staves and their leader grins. “If you can beat us, you've the strength to dig.” The road was never closed to keep people out; they're short of hands. The spillway on the dam is choked with stones and the temple hasn't the men to clear it. Phuntsok rolls up his sleeves and goes up to the lake with them.
column3: 僧兵们收了棍，领头的反倒笑了：「打得过我们，就有力气挖渠。」他们封路不是为了拦人，是缺人手：坝口的泄水渠被石头堵了，要清开，庙里人不够。平措卷起袖子，跟着他们往湖上去。

column2: Ladder Valley
column3: 冰梯谷

column2: At the end of the open country is a narrow valley crossed by crevasse after crevasse, each bridged by a wooden ladder spiked into the ice: the ladders for crossing the glacier. Chieftain Sangye's best troops hold the valley mouth, three ranks of blades, bows and horses, and they have pulled up every ladder and stacked them behind them for firewood. Two are already burnt.
column3: 野地尽头一条窄谷，谷里横着一道道冰裂缝，每道缝上搭着一架木梯，梯脚拿铁钉钉进冰里：这就是过冰川的冰梯。桑杰头人手下最精的人马把守在谷口，刀、弓、马三层，冰梯全被抽了上来，码在他们身后烤火，已经烧了两架。

column2: The chieftain's elite are routed and the unburnt ladders laid back in place. The Han men built them six years ago, and the rungs are carved: 'One rung, one man. Each one across, call out.' That day, Yangchen says, she heard them call two hundred and ninety-nine times, not one missing.
column3: 头人的精兵被打散，没烧的冰梯一架架搬回原处。梯子是六年前那队汉人做的，横档上刻着字：「一档一人，过一个，喊一声。」央金说那天过梯，她听他们喊了二百九十九声，一声不少。

column2: Snow-Line Slope
column3: 雪线坡

column2: On the slopes east of the lake a white line cuts across the mountainside: above it the snow never melts all year, below it is grass. Some of the chieftain's scouts are planting little flags along the snow line to mark a way for the main body, every one on the shady side. Yangchen says they'll lead men to their deaths, and the scouts draw blades to stop her pulling the flags.
column3: 湖边往东的山坡上，一道白线拦腰划过：线以上的雪一年四季不化，线以下是草。几个头人派来的探子正顺着雪线插小旗，给后面的大队标路，旗全插在背阴的那一面。央金说他们要把人往死路上领，探子拔刀不许她拔旗。

column2: The scouts are chased off and the flags pulled. Yangchen shows you: on the same mountain the snow line sits higher on the sunny face and lower on the shady one. “Going east, keep to the sunny slope. Shallower snow, a day less on the ice.” Just below the snow line on the sunny side, every so often, stands a little cairn the Han men left as a waymark, a tea leaf crumbled to dust on top of each.
column3: 探子被打跑，小旗全拔了。央金指给你们看：同一座山，向阳那面的雪线高，背阴那面的低，「往东走，要走向阳坡，雪浅，少走一天冰」。向阳坡的雪线底下，每隔一段就有一个小石堆，是那队汉人留的路标，石堆顶上压着一片茶叶，早成了渣。

column2: Jin the Third's Riders
column3: 金场队

column2: Jin the Third is back with a fresh troop of hired yak riders, blocking the main road: the best gold is at the foot of the dam and he won't leave it. If the lake were really going to burst, he shouts, it would have burst long ago. “Nine years and nothing. Why should it happen now I'm digging?” His riders stretch in a line, barring the monks heading up to dig.
column3: 金老三带着重新雇来的牦牛骑回来了，横在大路上：坝脚的金子最多，他不肯走。他嚷嚷说湖要是真会决口，早就决了，「九年都没事，凭什么我一挖就有事？」他身后的骑手一字排开，挡着上湖挖渠的僧兵。

column2: The riders break and Jin the Third sits down hard in the snow. Nine years with nothing, Phuntsok tells him, because every summer someone went up to dig the channel and let water out. “You dig the foot, they dig the spillway, and you dig faster.” Jin gapes a long while, then shoulders his pick and follows you up. “Then... I'll dig the spillway.”
column3: 骑手被打散，金老三瘫在地上。平措告诉他：九年没事，是因为每年夏天都有人上去挖渠放水，「你挖坝脚，他们挖渠口，你挖得比他们快」。金老三愣了半天，扛起镐头跟着你们上了湖：「那……我挖渠口去。」

column2: The Ice-Wall Camp
column3: 冰墙营

column2: On the last flat ground before the eastern glacier pass, Chieftain Sangye has gathered what remains of his force, yak riders, swordsmen and archers, into a great camp walled in front with blocks of ice. He shouts from the top of the wall: “If I can't cross this ice, neither can you!”
column3: 野地上，东边冰川垭口前的最后一片平地，桑杰头人收拢了剩下的人马，牦牛骑、刀手、弓手扎下一座大营，营前拿冰块垒了一道墙。头人站在墙上喊：「这条冰，我过不去，你们也别想过！」

column2: The ice wall comes down and the chieftain is dragged off it, still muttering. He has been on the ice once before: six years ago he trailed the Han men in secret and turned back halfway, frightened. “They looked back and called to me,” he says, red in the face. “'Keep up,' they called. I didn't dare.”
column3: 冰墙被推倒，头人被拖下了墙，嘴里还在嘟囔。他其实过过一回冰：六年前偷偷跟在那队汉人后头，走到一半怕了，回来了。「他们回头喊我，」他红着脸说，「喊『跟上』。我没敢跟。」

column2: The Dragon Lake's Lip
column3: 龙湖口

column2: Here, halfway up the mountain, hangs a milky blue lake held back by a long bank of rubble and silt, with Under-the-Lake village below it. A glacier tongue reaches into the water, now and then dropping a block of ice that sends a ring of waves across. One of Zhang Tianzhen's disciples hasn't given up: he has stolen a keg of powder and crept onto the dam, a few toughs guarding him while he lights it.
column3: 湖边，一汪奶蓝色的湖水悬在半山上，被一道乱石和泥沙堆成的长坝拦着，坝下面就是湖下村。冰川的冰舌伸进湖里，时不时掉下一块冰，激起一圈浪。张天镇的一个徒弟不死心，偷了一桶火药摸上坝顶，几个打手护着他点火。

column2: The toughs go down, the keg rolls into the lake, gives one bubble and is silent. Phuntsok crouches on the dam and scoops up a handful: gravel, mud, sand, everything mixed. “The glacier pushed this up. It isn't solid rock. Let the water rise, or a block of ice fall and raise a big wave, and it can break open.” Subduing the dragon means digging the spillway a foot deeper every year, so the lake drains away slowly by itself.
column3: 打手被打翻，火药桶滚进了湖里，冒了个泡就没声了。平措蹲在坝上抓起一把土：碎石、泥、沙，什么都有，「这是冰川推出来的，不是石头山。水一涨，或者冰块砸下来掀起大浪，就能冲开」。所谓镇龙，就是年年把泄水渠挖深一尺，让湖水自己慢慢流走。

column2: Timber-for-Gold Market
column3: 木金市

column2: Below the lake on the open country is an old market where the villagers trade gold dust panned from the stream for timber the western woodcutters bring by yak, one side rebuilding houses, the other getting through the winter. Jin the Third's leftover toughs hold the gate now, taking all the gold for themselves and leaving the timber to rot because it's worth less. And the guardians need big beams to repair the spillway gate.
column3: 湖下的野地上有一处老集，湖下村的人在溪里淘金沙，西边林子的伐木人赶着牦牛驮木头来，两样一换，一个修房，一个过冬。如今集口被金老三剩下的打手占着，金沙一律归他收，木料他嫌不值钱，堆在一边烂。护法们要修泄水渠的闸门，正缺大木头。

column2: The toughs are run off and the market trades again: gold dust for timber, eleven thousand jin a day. The woodcutters won't take gold for the first good beams; they carry them straight up to the lake for the guardians' gate. Phuntsok brings back word from Faceless: the old gate was built by the Han men nine years ago and has rotted. “Put in new, and the dragon sleeps another nine years.” And one more thing: the Mountain God has come back.
column3: 打手被赶跑，木金市重开：金沙换木料，一天一万一千斤。头一批好木头，伐木人不要金子，直接扛上了湖，给护法修闸。平措带回无面的话：闸门的木头是九年前汉人做的，烂了，「换上新的，龙就再睡九年」。无面还捎了一句：山神回来了。

column2: Mercy Gap
column3: 放生口

column2: A narrow gap on the open country is the last way before the glacier, held by horse thieves under a one-eyed man called One-Horn Dawa, among the fiercest thief chiefs of the north. Hearing someone means to cross the ice, he has his men draw their bows. Behind him a child, thin as a stick, is tugging at his sleeve.
column3: 野地上一道窄口，是下冰川前最后的路，一伙盗马贼守在这里，领头的是个独眼汉子，绰号独角达瓦，北边最凶的盗马贼头子之一。他听说有人要过冰，叫手下把弓都拉开了。他身后站着个瘦得像根柴的孩子，正扯他的袖子。

column2: The thieves are beaten back and Dawa doesn't follow. The child is his son, little Drakpa, the boy you sent off from Runaway Calf Slope with a tea cake. “My son says you fed him and didn't beat him.” Dawa stands aside, and adds that the Han men who crossed the ice once shared a brick of tea with him at this very gap. “I was half starved then. This son came after.”
column3: 盗马贼被打退，达瓦没再追。那孩子是他儿子小扎巴，就是走犊坡上被你们塞了块茶饼放走的那个。「我儿子说，你们给他吃的，没打他。」达瓦让开了路，又说那年过冰的汉人也在这口子上分过他一块茶，「那时候我差点饿死，后来才有了这个儿子」。

column2: The Doubters
column3: 疑面帮

column2: On the open country a band of young guardian monks has stopped the timber train, led by Phuntsok's senior brother. They won't accept Faceless. “Nine years, and who's seen his face? A man who won't show it and won't write his name, why should he lead the guardians?” Until they know who he is, not one beam goes up the mountain.
column3: 野地上，一伙年轻的护法僧兵截下了送木头的驮队，带头的是平措的师兄。他们不服无面：「九年了，谁见过他的脸？一个不肯露脸、不肯写名字的人，凭什么当护法的头？」他们说，不弄清无面是谁，木头一根也不许上山。

column2: The young monks are beaten fair and the timber goes through. The senior brother mutters that he only wanted to know who Faceless is. Phuntsok tells him what he heard at Frozen Hollow: “For the first four years, everyone under the masks was Han. Who the god is, whose face it is, what does it matter?” His brother thinks, then shoulders a beam and walks at the front.
column3: 年轻僧兵被打服了，木头放了行。师兄嘟囔说，他其实只是想知道无面是谁。平措把冻雪坳听来的话讲给他：「头四年戴面具的，都是汉人。山神是谁，脸是谁，有什么要紧？」师兄想了想，扛起一根木头走在了最前面。

column2: The Last Camp Wall
column3: 末营墙

column2: A half-collapsed stone hut on the open country is the last shelter below the glacier, its walls covered in charcoal writing. Passing hunters are skinning foxes inside and honing knives on the plaster, scraping off a whole patch. Yangchen storms in and snatches a knife away. “Those words are worth more than your lives.” The hunters reach for their bows.
column3: 野地上一座塌了半边的石屋，是冰川下面最后一个能避风的地方，屋里的墙上写满了炭字。一伙路过的猎户在屋里剥狐皮，拿墙皮磨刀，刮掉了一大片。央金冲进去，一把夺过刀：「这墙上的字，比你们的命还金贵。」猎户们抄起了弓。

column2: The hunters are run off. The scraped patch is lost, but the rest can still be read, written on their last night: 'Fourth spring. Going east, down the water to the sea, to keep the three roads' appointment.' And beneath, smaller: 'If the chief comes, tell him: we carry our half of the list. His half, let those who come after bring it.'
column3: 猎户被赶走，刮掉的那片补不回来了，剩下的还看得清，是那队人最后一夜写的：「第四年春，东去，顺水到海，赴三路之约。」底下一行小字：「镖头若来，告之：名单那一半，我们带着；他那一半，请后来的人带来。」

column2: The Dragon's Sluice
column3: 泄龙闸

column2: At the lake's dead end is the Dragon Lake's outlet: a stone-lined channel cut down through the top of the dam, with a wooden sluice gate. But Jin the Third's men walled it up with stones to pan its bed, and all summer the lake has filled with nothing let out; the water stands level with the crest. The roughest of Jin's crew still hold the channel, blades, bows and horses, swearing to cut down anyone who moves a stone.
column3: 湖边的死路尽头就是龙湖的泄水口：一条石砌的渠从坝顶切下去，渠口一道木闸。可渠口被金老三的人拿石头垒死了，他们在渠底淘金，一整个夏天湖水只进不出，已经涨到齐坝顶。金老三手下最凶的一伙还守在渠口，刀、弓、马都有，说谁动石头就砍谁。

column2: With the monks, the woodcutters and even Jin the Third, you lift the stones out one by one and hang the new gate. The lake rushes into the channel and drops a foot overnight. At dawn Phuntsok points to the channel walls: a Han name carved on every stone. There never was a dragon. The men behind the masks guarded the village below for nine years with two hundred and ninety-nine stones.
column3: 你们和僧兵、伐木人，连金老三一起，把渠口的石头一块块搬开，换上新闸。湖水哗地冲进渠里，一夜落下去一尺。天亮时，平措指着渠壁：每块石头上都刻着一个汉名。龙从来没有过；那些戴面具的人拿二百九十九块石头，替山下的村子守了九年。

column2: Yeti Caves
column3: 雪人窟

column2: Under an ice cliff by the lake gape several black holes, and the herders say yetis live there, taller than a man, walking upright, able to kill a yak with one blow. This spring they came out again, tore open several sheepfolds and left a line of footprints in the snow bigger than washbasins. The herders ask you to go and look.
column3: 湖边的冰崖下有几个黑洞洞的窟窿，牧人们说里头住着雪人，一人多高，能站着走，一掌能拍死一头牦牛。今年开春雪人又出来了，扒了好几家的羊圈，还在雪上留下一串比脸盆还大的脚印。牧人们请你们去看看。

column2: What charges out of the caves is three Tibetan brown bears, which you drive up onto the glacier. Yangchen has hunted yetis all her life, she says, and always found bears: upright they stand taller than a man, and once a print melts a little in the snow it's bigger than a basin. The caves stay mild all winter, so bears come back to sleep in them every year and wake hungry in spring; drive one family off and another moves in, so it has to be cleared every year.
column3: 洞里冲出来的是三头藏棕熊，被你们赶上了冰川。央金说雪人她也找过一辈子，找着的从来都是熊：站起来一人多高，脚印在雪里化一化，就比脸盆还大。冰崖下的洞冬暖夏凉，熊年年来这里冬眠，开春饿着肚子出来，赶走一窝，明年又来一窝，只能年年来清。

column2: The Painter's Tent
column3: 画师帐

column2: In a white tent on the open country hangs an unfinished thangka three feet wide: a great glacier, and a string of tiny figures walking east across it. The painter, a young woman named Norbu, stands in front of it brandishing her brush. Some of Chieftain Sangye's cavalry have burst in to take the painting as a route map for him, and they've already carried off her box of pigments.
column3: 野地上一顶白帐篷，帐里挂着一幅没画完的唐卡，三尺宽，画着一条大冰川，冰上一串小人往东走。画师诺布是个年轻姑娘，正举着画笔挡在唐卡前：桑杰头人的几个骑兵闯进来，要把唐卡拿去给头人当路图。他们已经抢走了她的颜料箱。

column2: The cavalry are driven off and the thangka saved, but the pigment box is gone. Those Han men commissioned this painting six years ago, Norbu says, paying the deposit with their last brick of tea: “Paint the road we took, for whoever comes after.” Two colours are still missing, lapis for the lake and gold for the road, and both were in the box.
column3: 骑兵被打跑，唐卡保住了，颜料箱却被他们带走了。诺布说这幅画是六年前那队汉人请她画的，拿最后一块茶付的定钱，说要画「我们走的路，给后来的人看」。还差两样颜色：画湖的青金石，画路的金粉，都在颜料箱里。

column2: Bell-Counting Road
column3: 数钟道

column2: On the main road to the temple, the chieftain's last few archers are sniping from behind a wall of mani stones; they've heard the temple keeps treasure the Han men left and want a share before they go. Dusk is coming, and Yangchen hurries you on. “If we're quick, we'll hear the bell.”
column3: 往神庙去的大路上，桑杰头人的最后一伙弓手躲在玛尼石墙后头放冷箭，他们听说神庙里供着汉人留下的宝，想抢一把再走。天快黑了，央金催着赶路：「赶得上的话，能听见钟。」

column2: The archers are chased away. Just as the sun goes down the temple bell begins, one stroke, then another; you count to two hundred and ninety-nine and it stops. Since that band left, Yangchen says, the guardians have rung it every dusk, one stroke per man. “As long as it's rung, it means they're still on the road.”
column3: 弓手被赶跑。正好日头落山，神庙的钟响了，一下，一下，你们数到二百九十九，停了。央金说那队人走后，护法们每天傍晚敲一回，一个人一下：「敲着，就是说他们还在路上。」

column2: Conch Ridge
column3: 法螺岗

column2: On a ridge of the open country, horse thieves have stolen a white conch from the temple, the trumpet blown there morning and evening, and are drinking out of it and blowing it between swigs, honking like a cow. The little lamas chasing them to the foot of the ridge have been driven back by their blades.
column3: 野地上一道土岗，一伙盗马贼刚从神庙里偷出一只白海螺，是庙里早晚吹的法螺，正拿它当酒碗，一边喝一边往外吹，吹得像牛叫。庙里的小喇嘛追到岗下，被他们的刀逼了回去。

column2: The thieves are chased off and the conch returned. Polishing it, a little lama says it was traded up from a seashore thousands of miles away and has been passed down for generations. When the Han men heard that, they stopped work every time it sounded. “This came from the sea. So the sea is where we'll go.”
column3: 盗马贼被打跑，法螺还了回去。小喇嘛擦着螺说，这只螺是从几千里外的海边换来的，传了好几代。那队汉人听了，每回听见它吹，都要停下手里的活：「这东西从海里来，我们就往海里去。」

column2: Hall of Masks
column3: 挂面殿

column2: In the temple's lower court is a hall whose walls are lined with pegs, two hundred and ninety-nine of them, each with its white mask. From the centre peg a red cloth bundle used to hang. Now it's bare. The old lama who keeps the hall is frantic: last night someone came over the wall and took the bundle. Footprints lead downhill through the snow, and some hired toughs guard the foot of the wall to cover the thief's escape.
column3: 神庙下院有一间殿，墙上一排排木钉挂满了白面具，二百九十九枚钉子，钉钉有主。最中间一枚钉子上原本挂着一个红布包，如今空了。看殿的老喇嘛急得团团转：昨夜有人翻墙进来，偷走了布包。墙外的雪地上，一行脚印往山下去，几个雇来的打手守在墙根下断后。

column2: The toughs go down and the bundle is found in their coats, a corner of the red cloth already torn. Phuntsok holds it shut and won't let anyone look. “This is the Mountain God's face. It waits for the one who will wear it.” The Han men gave it to Faceless when they left six years ago, the old lama says. It has hung there more than two thousand days, and no one has opened it.
column3: 打手被打倒，布包从他们怀里搜了出来，红布一角已经撕开了。平措拿手按住，不让任何人看：「这是山神的脸，要等戴它的人。」老喇嘛说，布包是六年前汉人们走时交给无面的，挂了两千多个日子，没人打开过。

column2: The Connoisseur's Camp
column3: 掌眼营

column2: A big camp has gone up on the open country, belonging to a lowland antique dealer called Jia the Eye, who collects idols and ritual objects from everywhere. He has heard the temple keeps a 'golden face of the Mountain God' and hired hundreds of swordsmen, archers and riders to take the bundle from the guardians by force. At his camp gate sits a table with a chest of silver on it: buy or seize, he doesn't mind which.
column3: 野地上扎起一座大营，主人是山下来的古董客贾掌眼，专收各地的神像法器。他听说雪山神庙有一张「山神的金脸」，雇了刀手、弓手、骑手几百人，要从护法手里硬抢那只布包。他在营门口摆了张八仙桌，桌上压着一箱银子，说买也行，抢也行。

column2: The hired men are routed. Jia the Eye strokes his empty chest and sighs. All his life he has collected gods, gold, bronze, wood, and every face was carved by a craftsman from a pattern book. “I only wanted to see,” he says, “what face a mountain would choose for itself.”
column3: 雇来的人马被打散了。贾掌眼摸着空了的银箱叹气：他走南闯北收了一辈子神像，金的、铜的、木的，每一尊的脸都是匠人照着画谱刻的。「我就想看看，」他说，「一座山自己挑的脸，长什么样。」

column2: The Questioning Slope
column3: 问名坡

column2: At the foot of the temple's mountain, a crowd of herders and young monks blocks the way up with torches, blades, bows and yaks. They've heard Faceless means to give the Mountain God's face to an outsider and won't have it: “He's our Mountain God. Why should he wear a Han face?” Phuntsok stands among you clutching the bundle, shouting at them until his voice gives out.
column3: 神庙那道雪山的山脚，一大群牧人和年轻僧兵堵在上山的路口，举着火把，刀、弓、牦牛都有。他们听说无面要把山神的脸交给一个外人，都不答应：「山神是我们的山神，凭什么是汉人的脸？」平措抱着布包站在你们中间，冲他们喊，嗓子都哑了。

column2: The crowd breaks, then slowly gathers again, this time without torches. The old herder from Frozen Hollow pushes to the front. His father was carried down by a Han man; the dam behind the village was built by Han men; the fair's stalls were raised by Han men. “For nine years, the ones guarding this mountain were the men under those masks.” No one says another word, and the crowd parts.
column3: 人群被打散，又慢慢聚拢来，这回没举火把。冻雪坳的老阿爸挤到前头说：他阿爸是汉人背下山的，村后的坝是汉人砌的，庙会的石摊是汉人垒的。「九年里护着这座山的，就是那些面具底下的人。」没人再说话，大伙让开了路。

column2: Sea-Stone Slope
column3: 海石坡

column2: On the slope below the temple, stone sellers with hired snow-mountain archers are hammering 'dragon-scale stones' out of the rock to sell for a sheep apiece, as charms against avalanches. Each stone is coiled with a spiral like a snail shell or a rolled-up whip. The Han men chipped stones on this slope too before they left, Yangchen says, and the archers turn their arrows on her.
column3: 神庙下面的野地坡上，一伙石贩子雇了几个雪山弓手，拿锤子从岩层里敲「龙鳞石」，一块卖一只羊，说揣着能避雪崩。石头上一圈圈盘着纹，像蜗牛壳，又像卷起来的鞭子。央金说那队汉人走前，也在这片坡上敲过石头，弓手们就拿箭对着她。

column2: The archers are driven off. Someone in your company knows what these are: ammonites, sea creatures. Very long ago this snow mountain was the floor of a sea, and was slowly pushed up into the sky. One of the Han men knew too, Yangchen says, and each of them pocketed one. “It came from the sea; we'll take it back to the sea.” The Mountain God waits in the temple at the top of the slope.
column3: 弓手被赶走。你们队里识货的人认出来：这是菊石，海里的东西，很久很久以前，这座雪山还是海底，后来被一点点挤上了天。央金说那队人里也有人认得，他们一人揣了一块：「从海里来的，带回海里去。」山神就在坡顶的庙里，等着你们。

column2: The Pigment Raiders' Camp
column3: 抢色营

column2: On the open country the cavalry who stole the pigment box have fled back to the chieftain's baggage camp, guarded by swordsmen, archers and riders. They take the lapis for gemstones and are prising it apart with knives to sell piece by piece; the gold powder has spilled and been swept into the snow as dirt. Norbu lies on the snowy slope outside, chewing her sleeve in anguish.
column3: 野地上，抢走颜料箱的骑兵跑回了头人的辎重营，营里刀手、弓手、骑手三路守着。他们把青金石当成了宝石，正拿刀撬，要一块块拿去山下卖；金粉撒了一地，被当成沙子扫进了雪里。诺布趴在营外的雪坡上，急得直咬袖子。

column2: The baggage camp is broken and the box recovered, the lapis all there; the gold you sift back out of the snow grain by grain, and only a small half-packet remains. Norbu cradles the box. Half a packet is enough, she says. For a road, you only need a fine line.
column3: 辎重营被打散，颜料箱抢了回来，青金石一块没少，金粉从雪里一点点筛回来，只剩小半包。诺布捧着箱子说，小半包也够了：画路，只要一道细线。

column2: The Lamp Gate
column3: 灯门

column2: At the temple's last gate a lamp hangs from the lintel, its shade freshly papered, turned west towards the cliff roads. Beneath it stands a man in a white mask and crimson robe, leaning on a polished post-station staff, white breath streaming from the eyeholes. Rows of guardian monks line up behind him and level their staves. “The rule doesn't change.”
column3: 雪山神庙的最后一道山门，门楣上挂着一盏灯，灯罩是新糊的，朝着西边，正对着悬崖栈道的方向。门下站着一个戴白面具的人，绛红袍子，手里拄着一根磨光的驿杖，面具的眼孔里一缕缕往外冒白汽。几排护法僧兵在他身后排开，长棍横了过来：「规矩不改。」

column2: The monks step aside. Faceless takes the bundle from Phuntsok and lifts off his mask: a thin old man with frost on his eyebrows. It is Nie, stationmaster of Snowline Post, who led the two hundred and ninety-nine up ten years ago and never came down after the road below fell. Every night he lights a lamp facing west. “Xiaolou lights his too. I can see it.” He carries the bundle into the hall. “The Mountain God came back last night.”
column3: 僧兵们退开了。无面接过平措手里的布包，摘下了面具：一个瘦老头，眉毛上结着霜。是雪线驿的聂驿丞，十年前领那二百九十九人上山，山下的路塌了，就再没下去。他每夜朝西点一盏灯：「小楼也点着，我看得见。」他把布包捧进了殿：「山神昨夜回来了。」

column2: Birch Slope
column3: 白桦坡

column2: Below the snow mountain grows a birch wood, bark as white as paper. A large band of horse thieves is wintering there in three camps of swordsmen, archers and riders, felling every tree they see for firewood. The old forest-keeper is tied to a trunk at the wood's edge, watching birch after birch come down, too stricken even to cry.
column3: 雪山的山脚下有一片白桦林，树皮白得像纸。一大伙盗马贼在林子里过冬，刀手、弓手、骑手扎了三个营，见树就砍，劈了烤火。林边守林的老汉被他们捆在树上，眼看着一棵棵白桦倒下去，哭不出声。

column2: The thieves are driven out of the wood. Every guardian's mask was carved from this birch, the old man says. Six years ago the Han men came to choose the straightest tree, and before felling it all two hundred and ninety-nine bowed to it. A tea wrapper is still nailed to the stump: 'The Mountain God's face was taken from here.' The carving was done by Lobsang, down the slope.
column3: 盗马贼被赶出了林子。老汉说护法的面具全是这片林子的白桦刻的。六年前那队汉人来挑过一棵最直的，砍之前，二百九十九个人围着树磕了个头。树桩上还钉着一张茶纸：「山神的脸，取于此。」刻脸的，是坡下的洛桑。

column2: The East Pass
column3: 东垭口

column2: At the far end of the open country is the East Pass at the glacier's crest; beyond it the road goes down. Chieftain Sangye has fled here and spent the last of his fortune on the hardest crew he could hire, blades, bows and horses holding the pass, meaning to tax everyone who crosses the ice for ten years, twenty. The wind up here won't let you stand, and they've pushed a stone marker over into the snow.
column3: 野地尽头，冰川最高处的东垭口，再往东就是下山的路。桑杰头人逃到这里，拿最后的家底雇了最狠的一帮人，刀、弓、马守着垭口，要收过冰的人一道「垭口税」，十年、二十年地收下去。垭口上的风刮得人站不住，一块石碑被他们推倒在雪里。

column2: The pass guards are routed and the chieftain trudges back down with his crampons on his back. You raise the marker. It reads: 'Two hundred and ninety-nine of the Qianli tea train passed here. You who come after, keep up.' Looking east, the ice melts into streams, the streams join into a river, and the river runs on eastward until it vanishes beneath the clouds. At the river's end is the sea, Yangchen says, and in the middle of the sea, three roads meet.
column3: 守垭口的人被打散，头人背着冰爪下山去了。你们把石碑扶起来，碑上刻着：「千里号茶队二百九十九人，过此。后来者，跟上。」往东望去，冰化成溪，溪汇成河，河一路向东，消失在云底下。央金说，河的尽头就是海，海的中间，三条路汇到一处。

column2: The Thank-You Cart
column3: 谢礼车

column2: Out on the open country Amma Yangdzom is driving an ox cart to the temple, loaded with butter the whole village pooled for the Mountain God's lamps, in thanks for nine years of guarding the dam. Halfway there, Zhang Tianzhen's last few shaven-headed strongmen jump out and seize it: the master's fee was never paid in full. Yangdzom stands on the shaft facing them down with her ox whip.
column3: 野地上，湖下村的央宗阿妈赶着一辆牛车往神庙去，车上是全村凑的酥油，给山神点灯，谢他护了九年的坝。半道上，张天镇剩下的几个光头力士跳出来截了车，说道长的法资还没收齐。央宗阿妈站在车辕上，拿赶牛的鞭子跟他们对峙。

column2: The strongmen are chased off and Yangdzom pulls over to rest. Some years ago, she says, the carver Lobsang came asking questions. Not about the masks, about the men beneath them: “What they said carrying people down, what they sang digging past midnight.” She told him everything. “So there's a share of our village in that face too.”
column3: 力士们被打跑，央宗阿妈把车赶到路边歇气。她说前些年刻匠洛桑来村里问过一回，问的不是护法的面具，是面具底下的人：「他们背人下山时说什么，挖渠挖到半夜时唱什么。」她都告诉他了，「那张脸，也有我们村的一份」。

column2: The Milking Bank
column3: 挤奶坝

column2: At the mountain's foot is a milking bank with a row of stone troughs, where the women of Under-the-Lake and the carvers' village milk, churn butter and dry curd every day. The fake guardians who lost their masks a while back have drifted here, daubed new felt masks white, and impounded every milk pail: the Mountain God wants milk, they say, and no one takes any home.
column3: 山脚下一处挤奶坝，坝上一溜石槽，湖下村和刻匠村的女人们天天在这里挤奶、打酥油、晒奶渣。前些天被扯了面具的那伙假护法流窜到这里，又戴上了面糊刷白的毡面具，把奶桶全扣下，说山神要喝奶，谁也不许拿回家。

column2: The fake guardians lose their masks again, and this time squat meekly by the troughs helping churn. The carver Lobsang lives just down the slope, the women say, and has been chiselling day and night. “The Mountain God's come back to the temple, so he says he'll carve another, to keep.”
column3: 假护法又被扯下了面具，这回老老实实蹲在石槽边帮着打酥油。女人们说刻匠洛桑就住在坡下，这几天叮叮当当刻个不停：「庙里的山神回来了，他说要再刻一张，留个底。」

column2: What the fake guardians had seized: twenty-odd pails of yak milk, a basket of curd, three fresh lumps of butter, and their new stack of felt masks, which the women didn't burn this time but used to pad the pails.
column3: 假护法扣下的：二十几桶牦牛奶、一筐奶渣、三坨新打的酥油，还有他们新刷的一摞毡面具，这回女人们没烧，拿去垫了奶桶。

column2: Every time you pass, the women at the milking bank ladle you each a bowl of fresh yoghurt sprinkled with crumbled curd. “Guests of the Mountain God drink before they go.”
column3: 每次路过，挤奶坝的女人们都给你们舀一碗刚打好的酸奶，上面撒一层碎奶渣：「山神的客人，喝了再走。」

column2: The Thangka Shop
column3: 唐卡铺

column2: At the end of the open country stands a little stone shop, Norbu's studio, its walls hung with thangkas and its doorway selling pigments, prayer flags and carvings. When Norbu gets back, debt collectors have occupied it: the chieftain pledged her shop against his own debts before he fled. She means to finish the painting here, and the toughs say no shop, no painting.
column3: 野地尽头一间石头小铺，是诺布的画坊，墙上挂满了唐卡，门口卖颜料、经幡、木雕。诺布回来那天，铺子已经叫一伙收债的打手占了：头人逃走前把铺子抵了自己的债。诺布要在铺子里画完那幅唐卡，打手们说铺子不还，画也别想画。

column2: The toughs are chased out and the shop reopens: pigments, thangkas and prayer flags for the goods on your carts, at fair prices. Norbu shuts herself in for three days and the thangka is finished. The lapis lake flows east into a river and on into the sea; a fine gold line starts at the feet of two hundred and ninety-nine tiny figures on the glacier and runs to an island in the middle of the sea where three roads meet. On the snow mountain stands one man with a casket on his back, watching them go. “They said,” Norbu tells you, “this one should be painted still on the road.”
column3: 打手被打跑，铺子重新开张，诺布拿颜料、唐卡、经幡换你们车上的货，价钱公道。她关起门画了三天，唐卡画完了：青金石的圣湖，湖水往东流成一条河，一直流进海里；金粉的一道细线，从冰川上二百九十九个小人脚下画起，画到海中间一座岛，岛上三条路汇在一处。雪山上站着一个人，背着匣子，望着他们的背影。「他们说，」诺布说，「这一个，要画成还在路上的样子。」

column2: The Carver's Yard
column3: 刻匠坊

column2: At the mountain's foot stands a carver's workshop, its yard heaped with birch, half-carved masks hanging under the eaves. A lowland idol-carving guild has heard the Mountain God now has a face, and has hired a big band of swordsmen, archers and riders to surround the place: Lobsang must hand over the pattern so they can carve thousands to sell. Lobsang has barred the door and goes on silently carving inside.
column3: 山脚下一座刻匠坊，院里堆满了桦木，屋檐下挂着刻了一半的面具。山下一家刻像行听说了山神有脸的事，雇了一大伙刀手、弓手、骑手把作坊围了，要刻匠洛桑交出那张脸的样子，好照着刻几千张拿去卖。洛桑把门顶上，在屋里一声不吭地刻他的木头。

column2: The guild's men are routed. Lobsang opens the door, covered in shavings, eyes red from sleepless nights. In his hands is a face just finished: dark, heavy-browed, a scar at the corner of one eye. “One stays in the temple, one stays with me,” he says. “Neither is for sale.”
column3: 刻像行的人马被打散了。洛桑开了门，满身木屑，眼睛熬得通红。他手里是一张刚刻好的脸，黑脸，浓眉，眼角一道疤：「一张在庙里，一张留在我这儿，」他说，「谁也不卖。」

column2: Lobsang's Shop
column3: 洛桑铺

column2: Next to the workshop is Lobsang's shop, selling wooden bowls, printing blocks and masks. It hasn't opened in six years: all his life he has wanted to carve one face well, he says, and until then nothing else was worth selling. A few of the guild's toughs still loiter at the door, waiting for him to change his mind.
column3: 刻匠坊旁边是洛桑的铺子，卖木碗、经版、面具。洛桑六年没开过张：他说他这辈子只想刻好一张脸，刻好之前，别的东西都不配卖。刻像行留下的几个打手还赖在铺子门口不走，说要等他回心转意。

column2: The toughs are sent packing and the shop opens: bowls and blocks for your goods, at a fair price. That face took a month, Lobsang says. The two hundred and ninety-nine came in turns, each with one line: “Thicker brows.” “A scar by the eye.” “He looks bad smiling, don't carve a smile.” When the last cut was made, none of the two hundred and ninety-nine said anything at all.
column3: 打手被赶走，铺子开张了，木碗、经版换你们的货，价钱公道。洛桑说那张脸刻了一个月：二百九十九个人轮流来，一人说一句，「眉毛再浓些」「眼角有道疤」「他笑起来不好看，别刻笑」……最后一刀刻完，二百九十九个人都不说话了。

column2: The Mountain God's Hall
column3: 山神殿

column2: Before the temple's great hall, two hundred and ninety-nine prayer flags crack together in the wind, a name on each. The stone seat empty for ten years has someone on it today: the Mountain God, in a crimson cloak, an iron casket on his back, a birch mask on his face, dark, heavy-browed, a scar by one eye, breath streaming from the eyeholes. Guardian monks, snow-mountain archers and yak riders line the steps below; Stationmaster Nie stands to one side with his lamp. The Mountain God speaks, and the voice is Lu Jiu's: “No crossing in winter. Beat me, and you can walk the eastern ice.”
column3: 雪山神庙的大殿前，二百九十九面经幡在风里一齐响，每面写着一个名字。殿前那张空了十年的石座，今天坐着山神：绛红大氅，背上一只铁匣，脸上一张桦木面具，黑脸，浓眉，眼角一道疤，哈气从眼孔里一缕缕冒出来。护法僧兵、雪山弓手、牦牛骑在阶下排开，聂驿丞提灯站在一旁。山神开口，是陆九的声音：「冬不过山。东边那道冰，打得过我，才走得过。」

column2: The Mountain God lifts off his mask, and beneath it is the same face. Lu Jiu turns the mask over: on the back, each of the two hundred and ninety-nine carved one stroke of a line: 'Guard this road, and wait for those who come after.' So that is how the two words on the winter stone go on. He chews Gonpo's tea and pulls on the three hundredth pair of boot liners. “The one the Fog Master counted missing, that was me.” They went east six years ago, taking their half of the list. Lu Jiu puts the casket's half list and his half tea brick into your hands, the third lock still shut. “Where the three roads meet, someone will open it.” He puts the mask back on. “I'll guard this road. When everyone who comes after has gone through, I'll take the road too.”
column3: 山神摘下面具，底下是同一张脸。陆九把面具翻过来，背面是二百九十九人一人一刀刻的字：「护住这条路，等后来的人。」冬封碑上那两个字，原来是这样接下去的。他嚼了贡布的茶，穿上第三百双靴里子：「雾驿主数少的那一个，是我。」他们六年前就往东去了，带着那半张名单。陆九把匣里的半张名单、半块茶砖交到你们手里，第三道锁仍扣着：「到了三条路汇合的地方，自有人开。」他重新戴上面具：「我守着这条路。守到后来的人都过去了，我也上路。」

column2: The Sea Route
column3: 海上航线

column2: The Harbour
column3: 港口

column2: The Port of Quanzhou
column3: 泉州港

column2: The harbour official takes the half chart you brought, draws the other half from a cabinet, and lays them together: they fit to a hair. "Ten years ago the Thousand Li's ship sailed from here," he says. "Its captain left half the chart behind and said that when the other half came back, someone would be able to find them." Out in the harbour an old ship is raising sail; the lantern at its stern bears the character for thousand.
column3: 市舶司的官员接过你们带来的半张海图，从柜子里取出另外半张，两张一拼，严丝合缝。「十年前千里号的船从这里出海，」他说，「船主把半张图留在这里，说等另一半回来，就有人能找到他们。」窗外的港口里，一条旧船正在升帆，船尾的灯笼上写着一个「千」字。

column2: Sea-Sight Ridge
column3: 望海岗

column2: The post road from inland climbs one last ridge, and suddenly the wind tastes of salt. Far off lies a thin white line: the sea. A barricade stretches across the crest; dockside raiders ride back and forth while blades and bows guard a table collecting 'sea-sighting money': anyone seeing the sea for the first time pays a coin, by the Dragon King's rule. A pedlar with a carrying pole squints at the ground, afraid to look south in case it costs him.
column3: 从内地来的官道翻过最后一道岗，风里忽然有了咸味，远处一线白光，那就是海。岗顶横着一道拒马，码头劫骑来回巡着，刀手和弓手守着一张桌子收「见海钱」：头一回看见海的人，每人一钱，说是海龙王定的规矩。挑担的小贩眯着眼不敢往南看，生怕多看一眼就得交钱。

column2: The barricade goes rolling down the slope and the pedlar looks at the sea properly for the first time. The old tea-seller on the ridge says that ten years ago, one August night, people lined this crest to watch the Qianli fleet leave harbour at midnight, three hundred lanterns strung out across the water. Halfway out, they all went dark at once. 'Put out, or gone into fog? Nobody can say.'
column3: 拒马被推下了坡，小贩头一回放开眼睛看海。岗上卖茶的老婆婆说，十年前八月，这道岗上站满了人，看千里号的船队半夜出港，三百盏灯排成一线往海里去。走到一半，灯一齐灭了。「是灭了，还是进了雾，没人说得清。」

column2: Pavilion of Two Notices
column3: 两榜亭

column2: A roadside pavilion, its pillars layered thick with notices. The bottom layer is handwritten: 'Seeking my granddaughter Xu A'xi, sixteen, rope calluses on her left hand. Tell Granny Xu at the Fish-Drying Flats.' Over it, printed from a carved block: 'Reward: the Xu girl, carrying a tide book. Deliver her to the Long Brokerage. Fifty taels.' A few pirate archers are peeling off the bottom layer and feeding it to a brazier.
column3: 路边一座歇脚的凉亭，柱子上的告示一层压一层。底下那层是手写的：「寻孙女许阿汐，十六岁，左手有网绳勒的茧，见者请告晒鱼坪许婆。」上面那层是刻版印的：「悬赏许家女，携潮信簿一本，送龙记牙行，赏银五十两。」几个海寇弓手正把底下那层撕下来，扔进火盆。

column2: The archers flee. An old woman with a paste bucket hurries up and kneels to smooth the scorched notices flat: Granny Xu. A'xi's father, Xu Chaosheng, was the Qianli fleet's harbour pilot; ten years ago he led the ships out and never came back. Half a month ago A'xi ran off with the tide book he left, leaving one sentence: 'I'm going to wait for the tide.'
column3: 弓手们跑了。一个挎着浆糊桶的老婆婆赶到，蹲下把烧焦的寻人帖一张张抚平，她就是许婆。阿汐的爹许潮生是千里号的领港，十年前带船出港，再没回来。半个月前，阿汐揣着爹留下的潮信簿跑了，只留下一句：「我去等潮。」

column2: Fish-Drying Flats
column3: 晒鱼坪

column2: The flats should be covered in racks of drying fish, eels hung out like banners. Now pirate swordsmen hold the racks: a fish boss claims the ground, one rack of fish for every rack you dry. The fisherfolk refuse, so the fish rot in their baskets and the place stinks enough to make the flies think twice. Granny Xu's house stands at the edge, a fat fish drawn by A'xi as a child still pasted on the door.
column3: 坪上本该晒满鱼干，竹架一排排，鳗鲞像晾着的旗。如今竹架被一伙海寇刀手占了，渔霸说这片地是他的，晒一架鱼交一架鱼。渔家不肯，鱼就烂在筐里，整个坪子臭得连苍蝇都犹豫。许婆的屋子就在坪边，门上还贴着阿汐小时候画的一条胖鱼。

column2: The fish boss is driven into the sea and the racks fill again. The morning A'xi left, folk say, she begged a bowl of porridge with no money to pay, and said instead, 'The tide turns at the first quarter of the Hour of the Goat.' At exactly that quarter the water crept up the beach. 'Her father was the same,' says Granny Xu. 'One look at the moon and he beat the yamen's water clock.'
column3: 渔霸被赶下了海，竹架重新挂满。坪上的人说，阿汐走那天来讨过一碗粥，付不出钱，就说「今天未时初刻涨潮」。到了未时初刻，潮水分毫不差地漫上了滩。许婆说：「她爹也这样，看一眼月亮，比衙门的漏刻还准。」

column2: You seize the fish boss's hoard: two hundred catties of dried eel, three jars of shrimp paste, half a boatload of coarse salt, and a 'fish-levy ledger' whose most repeated entry reads: 'Granny Xu, owes two racks. Fierce. Not collected.'
column3: 抄出渔霸囤的两百斤鳗鲞、三坛虾酱、半船粗盐，还有一本「抽鱼账」，记得最多的一笔是：「许婆，欠鱼两架，人凶，未收。」

column2: Every time you pass, the folk on the flats stuff a string of dried fish into your packs, and the children carry out a pot of fishball soup and won't let you go until they've watched you finish it.
column3: 每次路过，坪上的人都往驮袋里塞一串鱼干，孩子们捧来一锅鱼丸汤，非要看着你们喝完才放人。

column2: Recitation Slope
column3: 念白坡

column2: A band of pirate archers leaps onto the slope. Their leader clears his throat: 'This road, this road is mine, this tree I...' He turns round. 'What's the next line?' Someone at the back flips open a storybook to check. Having read the reward notice, they stop anyone carrying a book, and have so far seized an almanac, a cookbook and a ledger. Seeing you, they start again from 'This road is mine.'
column3: 坡上跳出一伙海寇弓手，为首的清了清嗓子：「此、此路是我开，此树是我……」他回头问：「下一句是啥？」后面的人翻开一本话本对词。他们看了悬赏，专拦带书的过路人，已经扣下一本黄历、一本菜谱、一本账簿。见你们来，又要从「此路是我开」重新念起。

column2: Afterwards the leader squats in the dirt, aggrieved. 'The book says once you finish the speech, they kneel.' A few days ago a girl went by with calluses on her hands and a book on her back. They'd only reached the second line when she recited the whole speech for them, added 'Your copy has a misprint', and was long gone while they were still checking.
column3: 打完了，为首的蹲在地上委屈：「话本上写的是喊完就有人跪。」他说前几天过去一个手上有茧、背着书的丫头，他们才念到第二句，她就替他们把整段念完了，还说「你们这本印错了一个字」，趁他们翻书的工夫走远了。

column2: White Brine Pans
column3: 白卤埕

column2: Salt pans spread in white squares across the coastal plain. Smugglers' swordsmen drive the salt workers, a straw rope tied from leg to leg like a string of crabs. Half a month ago a girl passed and said, 'Big tide on the night of the third. Raise the dykes.' The workers raised them overnight; the smugglers didn't believe her, piled their contraband salt on low ground, and by morning it was all brine. Now they want the workers to pay.
column3: 滨海的平野上铺着一方方盐埕，晒得发白。一伙私盐贩子的刀手押着盐丁干活，盐丁腿上拴着草绳，像一串螃蟹。半个月前有个丫头路过，说「初三夜里潮大，埕堤要加高」，盐丁连夜加了堤；私盐贩子不信，把私盐堆在低处，一夜全化成了卤水。如今他们要盐丁赔。

column2: The ropes come off and the workers bang their rakes on the pans and sing. The girl didn't just read the tide, they say; she asked the way to the pawnshop in town, to pawn something for travel money. The head worker gives you a packet of fresh salt. 'Thank her for us. That night of brine was the best night we've had in years.'
column3: 草绳解了，盐丁们拿刮板敲着盐埕唱起来。他们说那丫头不光会看潮，还问了去县城当铺怎么走，说要当一样东西换路费。盐丁头送你们一包新盐：「替我们谢谢她。卤水那一夜，是这些年最痛快的一夜。」

column2: Yongchang Pawnshop
column3: 永昌当

column2: The Yongchang Pawnshop at the town crossroads: high counter, tiny window, a pawnbroker who normally can't be bothered to lift his eyelids. For three days it has been shut, dockside raiders' horses tied outside while the riders pound the boards for one pledge: a bronze compass, the ticket made out to 'Xu A'xi'. Through the crack the old pawnbroker says, 'The term isn't up. I wouldn't hand it to the King of Heaven.'
column3: 县城十字街口的永昌当，高柜台，小窗口，平日朝奉连眼皮都懒得抬。这三天当铺关着门，门外拴着一排码头劫骑的马，骑手们拍着门板要一样当物：一只铜罗盘，当票上写着「许阿汐」。老朝奉隔着门缝说：「当期未满，天王老子来也不给。」

column2: The riders are driven off and the shutters come down. Impressed, the old pawnbroker will trade you goods from his stores. He'll keep the compass for the girl, past its term if need be. At the end he fishes out a conch, its mouth packed with sand. 'She pawned this too. Said it won't blow. One copper. Take it, and you'll have redeemed one thing for her.'
column3: 骑手们被赶走，当铺卸了门板。老朝奉佩服你们，肯拿库里的旧货跟你们换。罗盘他替那丫头留着，过期也留。临了他从柜底摸出一只螺口塞满了沙的海螺：「她一起当的，说吹不响，一文钱。你们拿着，就当替她赎一样。」

column2: Players' Cart Hollow
column3: 戏车坳

column2: In the hollow stands a troupe's great wagon with a stage on top. Pirate swordsmen sit round it; for three days and nights they've made the players perform, pelting the stage with fish bones whenever a line stops. The leading lady's voice is gone, the young lead yawns through his somersaults, and the gong master has fallen asleep mid-beat, his gong still going, one stroke at a time.
column3: 山坳里停着一辆戏班的大车，车上搭着台子。一伙海寇刀手围坐台下，逼着戏班唱了三天三夜，唱停一句就往台上扔鱼骨头。花旦的嗓子已经哑了，小生打着呵欠翻跟头，锣鼓师傅敲着锣睡着了，锣还在一下一下地响。

column2: The swordsmen run off and the troupe collapse into sleep. When the leading lady wakes she says a girl rode their wagon a few days back. They have a play, 'Leaving Harbour by Night', about the Qianli, with the pilot at the bow calling depths: 'Five fathoms! Four and a half!' At that scene the girl crouched at the back of the wagon and cried. Next day she got off at the fork and went into the woods.
column3: 刀手被打跑，戏班倒头就睡。醒来的花旦说，前几天有个丫头搭过他们的车。他们有一出《夜出港》，演千里号，领港站在船头喊水深：「五托！四托半！」那丫头看到这里，蹲在车尾哭了，第二天在岔路口下车，往林子里去了。

column2: Hand-Inspection Arch
column3: 验手坊

column2: At a junction stands a stone memorial arch, and under it dockside raiders have set a checkpoint for women only, turning each one's palms up: a fisher girl who hauls nets has a callus across her left hand. A dozen are already held: a washerwoman, a blacksmith's wife, a lion-dancing woman, and a lady of eighty who held out her own hands to see if she could claim the fifty taels.
column3: 路口一座石牌坊，码头劫骑在坊下设卡，专拦女人，挨个翻手看掌心：打渔的姑娘拉网，左手有一道横茧。卡边已经扣了十几个：洗衣妇、铁匠婆、舞狮的大姐，还有个八十岁的老太太，是自己伸出手来的，说想试试能不能领五十两。

column2: The checkpoint comes down; the lady of eighty is disappointed. The blacksmith's wife remembers a girl who had her mend a sounding lead with a hollow in its base for tallow. 'She said her father would drop it to the seabed and look at what stuck to the tallow, mud or sand or broken shell, and know where the ship was.'
column3: 卡子拆了，八十岁的老太太很失望。铁匠婆想起一件事：有个丫头请她修过一只测深锤，锤底有个凹窝要填牛油。「她说她爹把锤沉到海底，看牛油上粘的是泥、是沙还是碎贝壳，就知道船在什么地方。」

column2: Chained-Boat Cove
column3: 锁船澳

column2: Every boat in the little fishing cove is chained to one great post, and pirate archers on the rocks shoot anyone who goes near the chain. Afraid the girl with the tide book will slip away by sea, they've simply stopped the whole cove sailing. The fishermen squat on the beach mending nets, then unpick them, then mend them again.
column3: 小渔澳里的船都被铁链锁在一根大桩上，一伙海寇弓手守在礁石上，谁去解链子就放箭。他们怕那个带潮信簿的丫头从海上溜走，干脆让整个澳的船都出不了海。渔民们只能蹲在滩上补网，补完了拆，拆完了再补。

column2: The chain parts and the boats slide into the water one by one. The old fishermen laugh that the archers guarded for nothing. 'That girl never meant to go by sea. These are neap-tide days, the water over the bar is shallow, nothing gets across, and she knows that better than anyone.' She went overland, toward the river mouth.
column3: 铁链一断，船一条条推下了水。老渔民笑那伙弓手白守了：「那丫头根本没想走海。这几天是小潮，沙坝上水浅，大船小船都过不去，她比谁都清楚。」她走的是陆路，往河口去了。

column2: Camphor Elder Wood
column3: 樟公林

column2: Deep in the wood stands an old camphor tree five men couldn't circle with their arms. Shipwrights call it the Camphor Elder and bow to it before every season's work. Pirate swordsmen have set a great saw to it: the Dragon King wants a single trunk for a mast. The teeth are only two inches in, but the camphor reek has their eyes streaming; they saw and weep as if at the Elder's funeral.
column3: 林子深处有一棵老樟树，五个人合抱不过来，造船的人叫它「樟公」，每年开工前都来磕头。一伙海寇刀手架着大锯在锯它，说海龙王要一根整木做桅杆。锯齿才吃进去两寸，冒出来的樟脑味就熏得刀手们眼泪直流，一边锯一边哭，像在给樟公送葬。

column2: The saw goes into a ditch and the cut is plastered with mud. In the hollow among the roots lie a bedroll, half a sweet potato, and a note for Granny Xu: 'Granny, I've gone to the river mouth to wait for the tide. Dad's book says the bar rises every year. This year's eighteenth of the eighth month is the last tide a big ship can cross.'
column3: 大锯被扔进了沟里，锯口用泥糊上了。树根的空洞里有一卷铺盖、半块番薯，还有一张写给许婆的纸条：「阿嬷，我去河口等潮。爹的簿子上说，河口沙坝一年比一年高，今年八月十八，是大船最后一回能过的潮。」

column2: Hound Office
column3: 寻犬铺

column2: A big compound by the post road hangs a sign: 'Long Brokerage, Persons Found'. Twenty dogs are chained in the yard and dozens of swordsmen, archers and riders come and go. This is the headquarters of the hunt for the Xu girl, training dogs to sniff out fisher girls by the smell of fish. But the whole district smells of fish, so every day the dogs lead them straight to the fish market, and every day the dogs get shouted at. The dogs feel hard done by.
column3: 驿路边一座大院挂着「龙记寻人」的牌子，院里拴着二十条狗，几十个刀手、弓手、劫骑进进出出。这是悬赏许家女的总铺，专训狗闻鱼腥味找渔家姑娘。可这一带满地都是鱼腥味，狗每天都把他们领到鱼市，一回来就挨骂，狗也很委屈。

column2: The hired men scatter and the twenty dogs crowd round you wagging; one follows you and won't leave. In the office is the brokerage's commission, with a line in small script: 'The Xu tide book. Original copy, no pages torn. For Master Long's own eyes.' The bounty was never for the girl. It was for the book.
column3: 打手们散了，二十条狗围着你们摇尾巴，有一条跟上就不走了。账房里翻出牙行的委托书，一行小字：「许家潮信簿，取原本，不许撕页，龙爷亲阅。」悬赏的不是人，是那本簿子。

column2: Kidnapped Doctor's Stockade
column3: 劫医寨

column2: To cure their chief's toothache, a gang of hill bandits kidnapped a doctor from town. When the locals heard there was a doctor in the stockade who charged nothing, they tied on bandanas, dressed as bandits and slipped in for treatment. Now the stockade claims two hundred blades, bows and riders, half of them old men with bad backs. The chief, clutching his jaw, has no idea how many brothers he really has.
column3: 一伙山贼为了治寨主的牙疼，从县城绑来一个郎中。附近的百姓听说寨里有大夫，还不要钱，就扎上头巾扮成山贼混进来看病。如今寨里刀手、弓手、骑手号称两百人，一半是来看腰腿的老汉。寨主捂着腮帮子，算不清自己到底有多少兄弟。

column2: The real bandits flee; the fake ones won't leave and keep queueing. The doctor decides to stay and hangs a sign on the gate: 'Hall of Healing'. A few days ago, he recalls, he bound the ankle of a girl who'd twisted it, and she still insisted on walking through the night. 'She said the tide waits for no one.'
column3: 真山贼跑了，假山贼们不肯走，排着队等号。郎中干脆留下，在寨门上挂了块「济世堂」的牌子。他记得几天前给一个崴了脚的丫头裹过脚踝，她还非要连夜赶路：「她说潮水不等人。」

column2: Moon-Counting School
column3: 数月塾

column2: In the woods stands a small village school. Its teacher is ninety, deaf but sharp of memory. Pirate archers have taken the schoolroom as a lookout post and sent the pupils home. The back wall is covered with charcoal strokes, row upon row, as if someone had counted thousands of days on it. The archers want it whitewashed; the old teacher plants himself before it on his stick. 'My pupil drew these.'
column3: 林间一座小私塾，老塾师九十岁了，耳朵背，记性却好。一伙海寇弓手占了塾舍当哨所，把学童赶回了家。塾舍后墙上画满了炭道道，一排一排，像有人在墙上数了几千个日子。弓手们要刷掉，老塾师拄着拐挡在墙前：「这是我学生画的。」

column2: The archers leave. The man who drew on the wall, says the teacher, was Xu Chaosheng, who as a boy loved only counting moons, marking the hour of high tide every day. He found that the tide follows the moon, coming back a little under an hour later each day, and that at new moon and full moon, when sun and moon line up and pull together, the tides are biggest. A few days ago his daughter came and copied the whole wall through one night.
column3: 弓手走了。老塾师说，画墙的是许潮生，小时候只爱数月亮，每天记一笔涨潮的时辰。他数出潮水跟着月亮走，每天比前一天晚来将近半个时辰；初一、十五，日月排成一线一齐拉，潮最大。前几天他女儿来过，把整面墙抄了一夜。

column2: Waiting-Sedan Slope
column3: 候轿坡

column2: A bridal sedan sits on the slope, musicians dozing beside it, while a plump matchmaker fans herself, clutching a portrait that is unmistakably A'xi. Dockside raiders guard the sedan. The matchmaker tells everyone, 'We're fetching a bride for a relative of the Dragon King's house. All the dowry we ask is one old book.' The bride hasn't been found, and the sedan has waited seven days; its curtains are bleached by the sun.
column3: 坡上停着一顶花轿，吹鼓手蹲在轿边打瞌睡，一个胖媒婆摇着扇子，手里攥着一张画像，画的正是阿汐。护轿的是一队码头劫骑。媒婆逢人就说：「接新娘的，龙王府上的亲戚，陪嫁只要一本旧簿子。」新娘还没找着，轿子已经等了七天，轿帘都晒褪了色。

column2: Once the raiders flee, the matchmaker stops fanning and confesses. The Dragon King's steward paid her twenty taels to 'marry' the tide book, and kept asking one thing: 'Does the book have the depths of the new channel at the river mouth?' Thirty years a matchmaker, she says, and the first time she's seen a betrothal gift worth more than the bride.
column3: 劫骑一跑，媒婆扇子也不摇了，老实交代：龙王府的管家给了她二十两，让她「娶」那本潮信簿，还反复问一句：「簿子里有没有河口新水道的深浅？」媒婆说她做了三十年媒，头一回见聘礼比新娘还金贵。

column2: Banded Krait Reef
column3: 青环礁

column2: At low tide a spine of rock runs from the beach far out to sea. Banded sea kraits coil in its cracks, ringed black and blue-grey, coming ashore each season to lay their eggs. Pirates are on the reef catching them for snake wine: swordsmen turn the stones, archers guard the gaps, riders carry the jars to town. At the reef's tip stands a post notched all over, a new red string tied to it.
column3: 退潮时，一道礁石从滩上一直伸进海里，礁缝里盘着青环海蛇，一圈黑一圈青，每年这个时节都上礁产卵。一伙海寇在礁上抓蛇泡酒：刀手掀石头，弓手守口子，劫骑把蛇酒一坛坛驮去城里卖。礁尖上立着一根刻满道道的木桩，桩上系着一根新红绳。

column2: This lot of snake-catchers is driven off the reef. The post is the tide gauge Xu Chaosheng set up years ago; the red string marks the highest notch, A'xi's measure of this year's great tide. But the kraits return to breed every year and snake wine always sells, so before long new snakes and new catchers will both be back.
column3: 这一回的捕蛇人被赶下了礁。木桩是许潮生当年立的潮尺，红绳系在最高一道刻痕上，是阿汐量下的今年大潮。可海蛇年年回礁产卵，蛇酒年年好卖，过一阵，新的蛇和新的捕蛇人都还会再来。

column2: Walking-Anchor Wood
column3: 走锚林

column2: In a clearing lies a great rusty anchor a good ten li from the sea. The villagers say it walks, a step closer to the sea every year, for ten years now. Dockside raiders have yoked oxen to drag it off as scrap; a few children cling to the flukes and won't let go, crying so hard their snot drips onto the iron.
column3: 林中空地上卧着一只生锈的大铁锚，离海足有十里。村里人说这锚会走，每年往海边挪一步，已经挪了十年。一伙码头劫骑套了牛要把它拖走卖铁，几个孩子抱着锚爪不撒手，哭得鼻涕挂在锚上。

column2: Once the oxen are led away the children own up: they drag it themselves. Ten years ago a harbour pilot passing by told them it was a spare anchor fallen off a cart bound for the Qianli, and teased them: 'When the anchor walks to the sea, the ships come home.' Sure enough, the ring is cast with Qianli. Half a month ago a big sister with calluses on her hands helped them drag it one big step.
column3: 牛被牵回去，孩子们才说实话：锚是他们拖的。十年前一个领港路过，说这是千里号运锚时掉下的备锚，还逗他们：「锚走到海边，船就回来了。」锚环上果然铸着「千里」。半个月前，一个手上有茧的姐姐帮他们拖了一大步。

column2: False-Tide Board
column3: 错潮牌

column2: A big board on the beach lists each day's high and low tide, and the fishermen sail by it. But pirate swordsmen wrote it wrong on purpose: boats that sail by it meet the ebb, run aground on the bar and stick fast, and the swordsmen wade out to unload them. Three stranded boats already lie on the sand, their owners at the bows cursing the sky.
column3: 海滩上立着一块大木牌，写着每天几时涨潮、几时落潮，渔民出海全看它。可这牌子是一伙海寇刀手故意写错的：船照着出海，正撞上落潮，搁在沙坝上动弹不得，刀手们就涉水过去搬货。滩上已经躺着三条搁浅的渔船，船主坐在船头骂天。

column2: The swordsmen are driven off and the board pulled up. On its back someone has corrected every time in chalk, each stroke neat. One night, the fishermen say, a girl crept up to fix it, was spotted, and chased inland. A boat owner slaps his gunwale. 'Hers were the right ones. If we'd listened, we wouldn't be stuck here.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，木牌拔了。牌子背面有人用白垩改过一遍时辰，一笔一画很工整。渔民说，那天夜里有个丫头偷偷来改牌，被刀手撞见，追进了内陆。船主拍着船帮：「她改的才是对的，早听她的，船就不会搁在这儿。」

column2: Tethering-Post Flat
column3: 绑桩埔

column2: In the middle of the flat stands an ox post, and tied to it a skinny sunburnt boy, still swearing, a fish spear with bent tines beside him. Pirate swordsmen sit round him eating, smacking their lips on purpose. The boy is A'man, A'xi's neighbour. When he heard she'd run off he grabbed a fish spear and came after her, took on a band of swordsmen single-handed, and lost.
column3: 平埔中间钉着一根拴牛的木桩，桩上绑着个黑瘦少年，嘴里还在骂，旁边扔着一柄叉尖都弯了的鱼叉。几个海寇刀手围着他吃饭，故意吃得吧唧响。少年叫阿鳗，是阿汐的邻居，听说她跑了，拿起鱼叉就追出来，一个人挑了一伙刀手，挑输了。

column2: As soon as he's untied, A'man straightens his tines. He knows what A'xi means to do: the old channel at the river mouth has gone shallow and the new one has shifted, so she'll use her father's soundings to plant marker poles along both sides of it. 'In case the Qianli comes back. It'll need a way in.' He shoulders his spear and falls in behind you.
column3: 绳子一解，阿鳗先把叉尖掰直。他知道阿汐要做什么：河口的旧水道浅了，新水道挪了位置，她要照着她爹的测深记录，在新水道两边插上标杆。「万一千里号回来，总得有条路进港。」他扛起鱼叉，跟在你们后面走了。

column2: Pole-Makers' Sheds
column3: 竹篙寮

column2: A few thatched sheds stand by a bamboo grove where the weavers make punting poles. Half a month ago a girl ordered thirty long poles here, each with red cloth bound at the top. Dockside raiders heard, surrounded the sheds and fired the drying racks, swearing nobody would make them for her. The old pole-maker curses as he throws water, and the fire singes his beard.
column3: 竹林边搭着几间草寮，篾匠们专做撑船的竹篙。半个月前，一个丫头在这里订了三十根长篙，每根顶上缠一块红布。一伙码头劫骑听说了，把竹寮围住，点着了晾竹的架子，说谁也不许给她做。老篾匠一边泼水一边骂，火燎到了他的胡子。

column2: The fire is out and twenty-two of the thirty poles saved. Stroking his scorched beard, the old pole-maker says a harbour pilot ordered thirty just the same ten years ago. 'That time it was white cloth. He said white for going out, red for coming home.' A'man ties the poles in a bundle and shoulders them; he'll make up the other eight with fish spears.
column3: 火扑灭了，三十根篙抢出来二十二根。老篾匠摸着烧焦的胡子说，十年前有个领港在这儿订过一模一样的三十根，「那回缠的是白布。他说白布出港，红布回港。」阿鳗把篙捆成一捆扛上肩，说剩下八根拿鱼叉凑。

column2: Sand-Marked Wall
column3: 刻水墙

column2: An old stretch of city wall stands with its footings in the river, the stones cut with horizontal lines, a year beside each. Dockside raiders are hammering at them to chisel them flat. The old folk say a young man cut them a dozen years ago, one a year. Then he was gone, yet the marks kept adding up year by year, and no one knows who carried on.
column3: 河边一段旧城墙，墙脚泡在水里，石头上刻着一道道横线，每道线旁一个年份。一伙码头劫骑正拿锤子凿墙，要把刻痕凿平。附近的老人说，那是十几年前一个后生刻的，每年一道；后来人没了，刻痕却还一年年多下去，不知是谁接着刻的。

column2: The raiders are driven off and the marks survive. They record the height of the sand at the wall's foot, higher every year as sand piles up at the river mouth. The newest still has sharp edges, with small characters beside it: 'Continued by Chaosheng's daughter.' Granny Xu has cut one every year; this year it was A'xi. Beneath it, one more line: 'Sand up three feet. The old channel is dying.'
column3: 劫骑被赶跑，刻痕保住了。刻的是墙脚沙面的高低：一年比一年高，河口的沙一年年堆上来。最新一道刀口还新，旁边小字：「潮生之女续刻。」原来许婆年年来刻，今年换了阿汐。底下还有一行：「沙高三尺，旧道将死。」

column2: Iron Scale Wood
column3: 铁秤林

column2: In the middle of the wood is a clearing that was once a toll station of the Maritime Trade Office. Smith families from the hills carried down iron pots, nails and ship spikes, weighed them on the official steelyard here, and traded them for harbour rice. The steelyard is an iron beam ten feet long; dockside raiders have carried it off to weigh fodder in their stable. The smiths have squatted at the wood's edge with their loads for a month, and the pots have rusted.
column3: 林子中间有片空场，从前是市舶司设的抽分场：山里的铁匠户把铁锅、铁钉、船钉挑下山，在这里过官秤，换港口的米。官秤是一杆一丈长的大铁秤，如今被一伙码头劫骑扛走，挂在自家马棚里称草料。铁匠们挑着铁货在林边蹲了一个月，锅都生了锈。

column2: The steelyard is carried back and hung from its beam; the first thing weighed is a basket of ship spikes. Iron for grain is back in business: hill iron comes down by the load and harbour rice goes up. The station's old clerk brings out a ledger from ten years ago and points to a line: 'Qianli barge No. 7. Zhuang kiln porcelain, three thousand pieces. Duty unpaid. Seized and sealed.' 'That porcelain,' he says, 'is still sealed to this day.'
column3: 官秤抬了回来，重新挂上横梁，第一秤称的是一筐船钉。铁换粮的买卖又做起来了：山里的铁一担担下来，港口的米一担担上去。抽分场的老书吏捧出一本十年前的账，指着一行：「千里号七号驳，庄窑瓷器三千件，抽解未纳，扣封。」「这船瓷，」他说，「到今天还封着。」

column2: Sugarcane Press
column3: 甘蔗寮

column2: A field of sugarcane spreads over the plain, a sugar shed at its head where a stone mill turns and the juice runs into great pans to boil into brown sugar. Pirate swordsmen have taken the shed and carry the cane in by the bundle to chew it themselves, pulp all over the floor, the pans gone cold. The proprietress sits on a field ridge watching them, so angry she picks up a cane and chews one too.
column3: 平野上一片甘蔗田，田头一座糖寮，石磨一转，蔗汁流进大锅熬成红糖。一伙海寇刀手占了糖寮，把甘蔗一捆捆扛进去自己啃，啃得满地蔗渣，糖锅都凉了。糖寮的老板娘坐在田埂上看着他们啃，气得自己也拿起一根啃。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown out, the mill turns again and the pans send up sweet smoke. Yesterday, says the proprietress, a troop of raiders rode hard for the river mouth, their leader saying Master Long wanted 'the mouth surrounded before the eighteenth of the eighth month'. A'man grabs his poles to rush ahead, and you have to hold him back.
column3: 刀手被赶出去，石磨又转起来，糖锅冒起了甜烟。老板娘说昨天有一队劫骑往河口去了，骑得飞快，领头的说龙爷吩咐「赶在八月十八之前把河口围了」。阿鳗一听扛起竹篙就要先走，被你们按住了。

column2: In the shed you seize the swordsmen's stash: ten baskets of brown sugar, two vats of syrup, a chest of stolen coppers, and a pair of dice carved from sugarcane, half chewed away.
column3: 糖寮里抄出刀手们藏的十筐红糖、两缸糖水、一箱抢来的铜钱，还有一副甘蔗刻的骰子，被啃得只剩半截。

column2: Every time you pass, the proprietress wraps a packet of sugar fresh from the pan, says people travelling far need something sweet in their mouths, and presses a peeled length of cane on each of you.
column3: 每次路过，老板娘都包一包刚出锅的糖块，说出远门的人嘴里要有点甜，又硬塞给每人一根削好的甘蔗。

column2: Oyster-Bed Bridge
column3: 蛎房桥

column2: A long stone bridge spans a creek where it meets the sea, its piers crusted thick with oysters. Dockside raiders have hitched ropes to their horses to drag the deck stones down and cut the road to the river mouth. The horses snort and heave for ages and the stones don't budge; the riders switch to crowbars and sweat buckets.
column3: 一座长长的石桥架在入海的溪口上，桥墩下长满了牡蛎壳。一队码头劫骑拴了绳子套着马，要把桥板拉下来，断了去河口的路。马喷着气拉了半天，桥板纹丝不动，骑手们又换撬棍，撬得满头大汗。

column2: The raiders flee and the bridge stands untouched. The old bridge-keeper says the builders seeded oysters in the cracks between the pier stones; layer upon layer, the oysters glued the stones into one mass. 'Stronger than iron hoops. Horses can't pull it, men can't prise it.' Across the bridge the river mouth isn't far, and A'man runs on ahead.
column3: 劫骑跑了，桥好好的。守桥的老汉说，当年修桥的人在桥墩石缝里养牡蛎，牡蛎一层层长，把石头粘成了一整块，「比铁箍还牢，马拉不动，人撬不开。」过了桥，河口就不远了，阿鳗跑在最前头。

column2: Cold Dragon Kiln
column3: 冷龙窑

column2: A dragon kiln lies along the hillside, climbing the slope for dozens of yards; it hasn't been fired in ten years and grass covers its roof. Pirate swordsmen have dragged the kiln master, Zhuang Dalu, out of his house to make him fire a batch of fake antiques to cheat foreign merchants. The old man clings to the kiln door. 'I swore it. Until that boatload sails, this kiln stays cold.'
column3: 山坡上卧着一条龙窑，窑身顺坡爬上去几十丈，十年没生过火，窑顶长满了草。一伙海寇刀手把窑主庄大炉从屋里拖出来，要他开窑烧一批假古瓷去骗番商。老窑主死死抱着窑门：「我发过誓，那船瓷不出海，这窑不点火。」

column2: The swordsmen are driven off. Those three thousand pieces, Zhuang Dalu says, went to the Qianli on credit, to be settled once sold overseas. On loading day the shipmaster, Shen Du, had him paint twelve blue-and-white plates: no flowers or birds, just a stretch of coast, a few islands and a line. 'She said a chart on paper gets lost, but on porcelain, so long as it doesn't break, it won't.' But that boatload never sailed.
column3: 刀手被赶下了山。庄大炉说，那三千件瓷是千里号赊去的，说好卖到海外再结账。装船那天，船主沈渡请他画了十二只青花盘，盘心不画花鸟，画一段海岸、几座岛、一条线。「她说海图画在纸上会丢，画在瓷上，不碎就丢不了。」可那船瓷没走成。

column2: Dusk River Barrier
column3: 暮江关

column2: Dusk is falling. A row of the Long house's big boats lies across the river, chained one to the next and crowded with swordsmen and archers, while raiders patrol the bank. The river road to the mouth is sealed tight. A thin mist rises on the water and nothing can be seen beyond. A'man stamps in frustration. 'A'xi's just across that mist!'
column3: 天快黑了，江面上横着一排龙记的大船，船与船之间拉着铁链，船上站满了刀手、弓手，岸上劫骑来回巡，把去河口的江路堵得死死的。江上起了薄雾，对面什么也看不清。阿鳗急得跺脚：「阿汐就在雾那边！」

column2: The chains part and the boats fall into disorder. You remember the one-copper conch from the pawnshop, dig the sand from its mouth and blow: a long note rolls across the river. A'man freezes. 'That's the horn off the Xu boat!' Lights flare through the mist and a dozen fishing boats row out. Everyone who fishes this river knows that sound. They haven't heard it in ten years.
column3: 铁链一断，船队乱了。你们想起当铺那只一文钱的海螺，掏净螺口的沙一吹，呜的一声长音滚过江面。阿鳗愣住了：「这是许家船上的螺号！」雾里应声亮起一片渔火，十几条渔船摇了出来：江上打渔的人都认得这个声音，十年没听见了。

column2: Cross-River Toll
column3: 横江卡

column2: An old toll post by the river flies a flag reading 'Maritime Trade Office Duty', long faded to white. Dockside raiders man it, calling themselves tax collectors. Every boat pays a tenth, then 'flag money', 'tea money' and 'riders' fodder money'. One bamboo boat was levied down to its last pole, and its owner punted away with it in tears.
column3: 江边的老税卡挂着「市舶司抽解」的旗子，旗子早褪成了白色。守卡的是一队码头劫骑，自称税丁，过往的船都要抽一成，抽完再抽「旗钱」「茶钱」「骑手的马料钱」。一条运竹子的船被抽到最后，船主只剩一根竹竿，撑着哭着走了。

column2: The fake tax men are chased off and the bamboo boat comes back for its cargo. In the toll house is a stack of ten-year-old passage slips. One reads: 'Qianli barge No. 7. Did not pass. Towed back by order to the river-mouth bonded store.' The porcelain never got out of the river.
column3: 假税丁被赶跑，竹船摇回来捡回了竹子。卡房里有一摞十年前的过卡单，其中一张写着：「千里号七号驳，未过卡，奉令拖回，入河口封库。」那船瓷连江口都没出，就被拖了回去。

column2: The New Spit
column3: 新沙嘴

column2: Beyond the river mouth a long spit of sand reaches out like an arm laid across the harbour gate, squeezing the old channel to a narrow slot. A row of red-flagged poles stands along its tip, and a slight, limping girl is planting the last few in the water. At the spit's root the Long house's raiders have closed in, their leader shouting, 'Xu girl! Hand over the book and Master Long will credit your father for it!'
column3: 河口外伸出一条长长的沙嘴，像一只手臂横在港门前，把旧水道挤得只剩一条窄缝。沙嘴尖上插着一排红布竹篙，一个瘦小的姑娘一瘸一拐，正往水里插最后几根。沙嘴根上，龙记的劫骑已经围了上来，领头的喊：「许家丫头，把簿子交出来，龙爷给你爹记一功！」

column2: The raiders are driven off the spit. Her father worked it out, A'xi says: the current along the coast pushes sand this way all year, and where it slackens at the river mouth the sand drops, so the spit grows a little every year and the old channel silts to death. The book's last page reads: 'Eighteenth of the eighth month. Great tide. Midnight. Wait for the ships.' She looks at the empty berth in the harbour. 'Master Long wants the book. Yet he's kept that berth for my father all this time.'
column3: 劫骑被赶下了沙嘴。阿汐说：沿岸的海流一年到头把沙往这边推，到了河口流缓下来，沙就落下，沙嘴一年长一截，旧水道就这样淤死了。簿子最后一页写着：「八月十八，大潮，子时，候船。」她望着港里的空泊位：「龙爷要簿子，可那个泊位，他一直给我爹留着。」

column2: Shard Beach
column3: 碎瓷滩

column2: In a bend of the river lies a white, glittering beach that crunches underfoot: decades of kiln rejects. Dockside raiders ride up and down it turning over shards, hunting for 'the plates with the sea chart', and when they find none they stamp with their hooves, sending chips flying and cutting their own horses.
column3: 江湾里有一片白花花的滩，踩上去咔嚓咔嚓响，全是几十年来窑户倒的碎瓷。一队码头劫骑骑着马在滩上来回趟，翻着碎片找「画了海图的盘子」，找不着就拿马蹄踩，瓷片飞溅，划伤了自己的马。

column2: The raiders flee, leaving the beach pocked with hoofprints. A shard-picking child turns up a blue-and-white fragment painted with half an island and a curving line. People have come hunting plates for years, the child says. 'They say a few pieces from the bonded store got sold on the quiet.'
column3: 劫骑跑了，滩上留下一片马蹄坑。捡瓷片的孩子从坑里翻出一块青花碎片，画着半个岛和一段弯弯的线。孩子说这几年常有人来找盘子：「听说封库里的瓷，有人偷偷卖过几只。」

column2: Loggers' Camp
column3: 伐木营

column2: A great bald patch has been cut in the forest with the Long house's logging camp in the middle: swordsmen drive woodcutters to fell pines, archers guard the timber yard, riders drag logs to the river to raft down, for the Dragon King's ships. The camp's fat cook has a loud voice and a fine hand, and serves his own portion on the same plate every meal, flying off the handle if anyone touches it.
column3: 林子被砍出一大片秃斑，龙记的伐木营扎在中间：刀手押着樵夫砍松，弓手守着木场，劫骑把原木拖到河边放排，说是给海龙王造船。营里的胖伙夫嗓门大，手艺好，每顿都拿同一只盘子盛自己那份，谁碰一下跟谁急。

column2: The camp breaks up. The fat cook clutches his plate: his 'lucky plate', bought from a rag-and-bone man for three coppers and used for eight years without a chip. In its centre are a stretch of coast and a string of islets, and a line running off the rim. Face crumpled, he trades it to you for a sack of rice.
column3: 伐木营散了。胖伙夫抱着盘子不撒手，说这是从收破烂的手里花三文钱买的「福盘」，用了八年没摔过。盘心画着一段海岸、一串小岛，一条线一直画出盘沿。他哭丧着脸，拿盘子换了你们一袋米。

column2: Seal-Keepers' Camp
column3: 守封营

column2: Deep in the forest hides a stockade of deserters who haven't come down the hill in ten years, once guards at the Maritime Trade Office's bonded store. In the middle of the camp five crates stand like an altar, still sealed 'Maritime Trade Office', the strips untouched in ten years. By day the deserters drill; by night they take turns guarding the crates. Their clothes are rags, but their blades and bows gleam and their horses are fat.
column3: 密林里藏着一座营寨，住着一伙十年没下过山的逃兵，原是市舶司封库的库丁。营中间供着五只木箱，箱上贴着「市舶司封」，十年没人敢揭。逃兵们白天操练，夜里轮流给木箱站岗，衣裳破破烂烂，刀和弓倒擦得锃亮，劫骑的马也养得膘肥。

column2: Outmatched, the deserters kneel and weep. The night the store was sealed they shouldered five crates in the confusion and fled, but never dared break the seals: 'Break an official seal and it's your head.' You peel them off. Every bowl is bedded in rice husk, and on top lie five blue-and-white plates. That night, their leader says, the man sealing the barge was a young registrar who cried as he pasted the strips. 'Name of Ke. He's Superintendent now.'
column3: 逃兵们打不过，跪下就哭。那年封库，他们趁乱扛了五箱瓷逃进山，可封条不敢揭：「揭了官封要砍头。」你们揭开，碗都裹着稻壳，最上面是五只青花盘。领头的说，那夜封船的是个年轻主簿，一边贴封条一边掉泪，「姓柯，如今是提举了。」

column2: Cormorant Bay
column3: 鸬鹚湾

column2: The fishermen of this bay fish with cormorants, a grass ring on each bird's neck so it can't swallow big fish and brings them back to spit into the boat. Pirate archers have seized the bay, caged the birds and make the fishermen hand over fish daily. The old cormorant man has kept back only his oldest bird, tucked inside his coat. It makes no sound, just glares at the archers.
column3: 湾里的渔人养鸬鹚捕鱼，鸬鹚脖子上套着草环，吞不下大鱼，叼回来吐进船舱。一伙海寇弓手占了湾，把鸬鹚都关进笼子，逼渔人天天交鱼。老鸬鹚翁只留下一只最老的没交，揣在怀里，那鸟也不叫，只拿眼睛瞪着弓手。

column2: The cages open and the cormorants flap back to the prows. From the old man's rafters hangs a yellowed oil-paper lantern bearing Qian. At dawn on the nineteenth of the eighth month, ten years ago, his cormorant brought it back from the sea. 'Not burnt, not torn. As if someone blew it out and set it on the water.' Stamped on its base: Chen's Lanterns.
column3: 笼子打开，鸬鹚扑棱棱飞回了船头。老鸬鹚翁的屋梁上挂着一盏发黄的油纸灯笼，写着「千」字，是十年前八月十九清早，他的鸬鹚从海上叼回来的。「没烧也没破，像是有人吹灭了放进海里的。」灯笼底下印着一行小字：陈记灯笼。

column2: River-Mouth Bonded Store
column3: 河口封库

column2: Beside the river mouth stands a great high-walled warehouse, 'Maritime Trade Office Bonded Store' over its door, a bronze lock as wide as a bowl. It's guarded not by soldiers but by the Long house's best: swordsmen at the gate, archers on the walls, raiders riding the perimeter. 'Master Long rents it,' they say, though how much, and who pays whom, nobody knows. Inside lie goods that haven't moved in ten years.
column3: 河口边一座高墙大库，门上「市舶司封库」五个大字，铜锁有碗口大。可守库的不是官兵，是龙记的精锐打手：刀手守门，弓手站墙头，劫骑绕墙巡逻。他们说这座库「龙爷租了」，租金多少、谁付给谁，没人知道。库里堆着十年没动过的货。

column2: The guards are beaten and the doors creak open. At the very back sits an old barge, 'Qianli 7' on its bow, its hold stacked with husk-packed porcelain under thick dust. The register reads: 'Porcelain, 3,000 pieces, five crates short. Blue-and-white plates, twelve: six taken into keeping by Registrar Ke, five with the missing crates, one...' The last has no entry, only a tiny character in the margin: Long.
column3: 打手们败了，库门吱呀一声开了。最里头停着一条旧驳船，船头漆着「千里·七」，舱里码着裹稻壳的瓷器，落了厚厚一层灰。库簿记着：「瓷三千件，缺五箱。青花盘十二只，六只柯主簿取存，五只随失箱，一只……」最后一只没写去处，只在页边画了个小小的「龙」字。

column2: Chen's Lanterns
column3: 陈记灯笼

column2: A row of shops lines the foot of the old wall, and Chen's Lanterns is the oldest, its door hung thick with bamboo-and-oil-paper lanterns, red and white, each lettered with a family name. Dockside raiders storm in, ripping the characters off and stamping on every Qian they see, and on anything that even sounds like it. Granny Chen sits on her threshold pasting lanterns: for every one they stamp, she makes another.
column3: 老城墙根下一溜铺子，陈记灯笼是最老的一家，门口挂满竹骨油纸的灯笼，红的白的，写着各家的姓。一队码头劫骑冲进铺子，挨个撕灯笼上的字，见「千」字就踩，连同音的「迁」「仟」都不放过。陈婆坐在门槛上糊灯笼，劫骑踩一个，她糊一个。

column2: The raiders are thrown out and Granny Chen dusts the paste off her hands. Ten years ago Shipmaster Shen Du ordered six hundred lanterns from her: 'Three hundred to hang going out, three hundred coming home.' She lettered the outgoing three hundred herself; the homecoming ones were confiscated by the harbour fort before delivery. Since then the fort lets no ship with a Qian lantern leave, and she may not write the character at all.
column3: 劫骑被赶出去，陈婆拍掉手上的浆糊。十年前，船主沈渡在她这里订了六百盏灯：「三百盏出港挂，三百盏回港挂。」出港那三百盏是她亲手写的字；回港那三百盏还没交货，就被炮台收走了。从那以后，炮台不放挂「千」字灯笼的船出港，她也不许再写这个字。

column2: Brokers' Hall
column3: 牙行楼

column2: A three-storey timber hall by the river houses Quanzhou's oldest brokerage; foreign merchants and shipowners need a broker to stand surety for any deal. Pirate swordsmen have taken it and hung the old broker out of an upstairs window to make him hand over the surety registers from ten years ago. Dangling in mid-air, he's still haggling with a vegetable seller below: 'Two coppers a bunch? Did you grow those scallions from gold?'
column3: 江边一座三层木楼，是泉州最老的牙行，番商和船主做买卖都要请牙人作保。一伙海寇刀手占了楼，把老牙人吊在二楼窗口，逼他交出十年前的保状底册。老牙人吊在半空，还在跟楼下卖菜的讨价还价：「两文钱一把？你那葱是金子种的？」

column2: Let down, the old broker rubs his arms and digs out the register. Barge No. 7's surety bears three thumbprints: kiln master Zhuang Dalu, Office registrar Ke, and the young heir of the Long house, whose mark is a wobbly little dragon. 'They stood surety for the porcelain's duty. Three guarantors, and in the end not one copper was paid.'
column3: 老牙人被放下来，揉着胳膊翻出底册。七号驳的保状上按着三个手印：窑主庄大炉，市舶司主簿柯某，还有龙记的少东家，画押是一条歪歪扭扭的小龙。「保的是那船瓷的抽解税。三个人作保，到头来一个铜板也没交上。」

column2: Angler's Rock
column3: 垂钓矶

column2: On a big rock by the river sits a middle-aged man in a worn official robe, holding a rod with no bait on the hook. The locals say he comes every day and has fished ten years without catching a thing. Today pirate swordsmen have surrounded the rock to snatch the seal pouch at his belt. He doesn't run. He just lets his line down a little deeper.
column3: 江边一块大石上坐着个穿旧官袍的中年人，手里一根钓竿，钩上没挂饵。附近的人说他天天来，钓了十年，一条鱼也没钓上来。今天一伙海寇刀手把石头围住，要抢他腰上的印袋。他也不跑，只把钓线往水里又放深了一点。

column2: The swordsmen are knocked into the river. The angler is Ke Shen, Superintendent of the Maritime Trade Office; ten years ago it was he who sealed that porcelain. 'That was the law. I had no choice.' He has always carried half a paper chart in his sleeve, and the six plates are locked in the Office. 'The Office hasn't opened its doors in ten years. Help me open them, and I'll show you the two halves together.'
column3: 刀手被打下了江。钓鱼的人是市舶司提举柯慎，十年前那船瓷的封条就是他贴的，「律法如此，我没得选。」他袖里一直揣着半张纸海图，取存的六只青花盘也锁在司里。「市舶司十年没开过门了。你们若能帮我把门打开，我就把两半拼给你们看。」

column2: Fish-Sauce Works
column3: 鱼露坊

column2: A row of great earthenware vats lines the shore, small fish salting inside. Left in the sun a year or so, they drip fish sauce savoury enough to lift your eyebrows off. Pirate archers have taken over the works and won't leave until the sauce has all dripped out, but it only drips one vat a year. The owner cooks for them every day and is nearly pickled himself.
column3: 海边一排大陶缸，缸里腌着小鱼，晒上一年半载，滴出来的就是鱼露，鲜得能把人眉毛掀起来。一伙海寇弓手占了鱼露坊，说要等鱼露滴完才走，可鱼露一年才滴一缸。坊主天天给他们做饭，做得自己都快腌成了咸鱼。

column2: The archers are run off and the owner lifts the vat lids to air them. His most regular customer on credit, he says, is the harbour fort's cook, who rambles when drunk about the strange rules at the shore watch post below the fort. 'Three of them, each spookier than the last. Every recruit knows them by heart and nobody knows why.'
column3: 弓手被赶走，坊主把缸盖一个个揭开透气。他说常来赊鱼露的是炮台的伙夫，伙夫喝多了就念叨炮台下海边哨铺的怪规矩：「三条，一条比一条邪门，新兵都背得滚瓜烂熟，谁也不知道为什么。」

column2: You seize the archers' hoard: twelve vats of fish sauce, strings of dried shrimp and squid, and one barrel of 'ten-year vintage' nobody dares drink. When the lid comes off, the archers' captain is the first to faint.
column3: 坊里抄出弓手们囤的十二缸鱼露、成串的虾干和鱿鱼干，还有一桶没人敢喝的「十年陈」，盖子一揭，弓手头目先晕了过去。

column2: Every time you pass, the owner fills a jar with fresh fish sauce for you and fries a pan of oyster omelette. 'On the road,' he says, 'a meal needs something savoury.'
column3: 每次路过，坊主都灌一罐新滴的鱼露给你们，再煎一锅海蛎煎，说「出门在外，吃饭得有个鲜味」。

column2: Painted-Barge Casino
column3: 花舫赌局

column2: A painted barge lies at anchor mid-river, red lamps and wine, the rattle of dice carrying over the water. Pirate swordsmen run a gambling den aboard, staking not silver but stacks of blank sailing certificates, the Office's permits for seagoing ships, stolen ten years ago. With one, a smuggler can pass as a licensed merchantman. At this table a certificate buys a ship, and three ships have changed hands tonight.
column3: 江心泊着一条花舫，灯红酒绿，骰子声隔着水都听得见。一伙海寇刀手在舫上开赌，押的不是银子，是一摞摞空白公凭：市舶司发给出海船只的凭证，十年前从司里偷出来的。有了它，私船就能装成官准的商船。赌桌上一张公凭换一条船，今晚已经输掉了三条。

column2: The gamblers dive overboard and the dice sink. One certificate in the stack is different: headed 'Qianli: Continued Voyage', ship, cargo and date left blank, stamped only with a small seal, 'Ke, Registrar, Maritime Trade Office', its ink long faded. It was stamped ten years ago.
column3: 赌徒们跳江跑了，骰子沉了底。那摞公凭里有一张不一样：抬头写着「千里号续航」，船名、货物、日期都空着，只盖着一方小小的「市舶司主簿柯」，印泥都褪了色，是十年前就盖好的。

column2: Old Powder Magazine
column3: 旧药局

column2: Where the city wall turns, a brick building lies half buried: the fort's old powder magazine, walls three feet thick, door clad in iron, where everything the fort confiscated ten years ago is piled. It's guarded now by fort soldiers and Long house bruisers together, swordsmen, archers and riders mixed, uniform tunics beside short jackets, drinking from the same jar.
column3: 城墙拐角下有一座半埋在土里的砖房，从前是炮台存火药的药局，墙厚三尺，门上包铁，十年前炮台收走的东西都堆在这里。如今守着它的是炮台的兵和龙记的打手，刀手、弓手、劫骑混在一起，一个穿号衣，一个穿短打，喝的是同一坛酒。

column2: The guards fall back and the door is forced. The powder kegs are long empty; instead the room is stacked with folded oil-paper lanterns, three hundred exactly, perfectly dry. Granny Chen hurries up on her stick and opens one. The last downstroke of its Qian is drawn out long. She did that on purpose, she says. 'It's a long way home, so I wrote it long.'
column3: 守兵败退，铁门撬开。火药桶早空了，屋里码着一摞摞折起来的油纸灯笼，整整三百盏，干干爽爽。陈婆拄着拐赶来，打开一盏，「千」字最后一竖拖得老长。她说那是故意的：「回来的路长，字也写长一点。」

column2: Rivet-Mender's Stall
column3: 锔瓷摊

column2: At a crossroads a rivet-mender staples broken bowls together with copper. On display is a strange bowl he riveted over ten years from hundreds of pieces picked off Shard Beach, bristling with copper like a hedgehog. Pirate archers have heard it shows a treasure map and want to carry it off, stall and all. Hugging it, the mender says there's only one sentence in it.
column3: 路口一个锔瓷匠的摊子，专拿铜钉把碎碗锔起来。摊上供着一只怪碗，是他十年间从碎瓷滩捡回几百片碎瓷，一片片锔成的，满身铜钉，像只刺猬。一伙海寇弓手听说碗上拼出了藏宝图，要连摊子一起抬走。锔瓷匠抱着碗说，碗里只有一句话。

column2: The archers are run off and the mender turns the bowl over: the base pieces into the Zhuang kiln's mark, 'Zhuang: Qianli'. The night before the fleet sailed, he says, he saw Shipmaster Shen arguing with the young Long heir right here. She said, 'Advance the duty and I'll repay you tenfold when the ships come home.' He said, 'I don't want tenfold. I want my brother off that ship.' After that the porcelain was sealed.
column3: 弓手被赶走，锔瓷匠把碗翻过来，碗底拼出庄窑的款「庄记·千里」。他说开船前一夜，他就在这路口，看见沈船主和龙家少东家吵架。沈船主说：「这笔税你先垫，船回来我还你十倍。」少东家说：「我不要十倍，我要我弟弟下船。」后来那船瓷就封了。

column2: Shore Watch Post
column3: 戍卒铺

column2: On the shore below the fort stands a watch post with a board of three rules nailed to its door. 'One: no lamps at midnight. Two: if on a summer night you see three hundred lights on the sea, do not count them and do not row after them. Three: if anyone asks whether the Qianli has come back, answer No, and not one word more.' Pirate swordsmen hold it now, and they keep the rules too, huddled silent in the dark at midnight.
column3: 炮台下的海边有座哨铺，门口钉着一块木牌，写着三条规矩：「一、子时不许点灯。二、夏夜海上若见三百点光，不许数，不许划船去追。三、有人来问千里号回来没有，答『没有』，不许多说一个字。」哨铺如今被一伙海寇刀手占着，他们也照规矩办，半夜黑灯瞎火，缩在墙角不敢出声。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown out. That night the sea does light up blue, flickering with each wave: tiny glowing creatures that shine when summer waves stir them. Years ago two recruits took it for the Qianli's lanterns, rowed after it and never returned, so the old gunner made rule two. Rule one keeps lights from drawing pirates. Rule three? The midnight asker is Captain Wu, drunk; say one word more and he weeps till dawn.
column3: 刀手被赶走。当夜海上果然亮起蓝光，一浪一闪：是海里的夜光虫，夏夜被浪一搅就发光。几年前两个新兵当成千里号的灯，划船去追，没再回来，老炮手才定了第二条。第一条是怕灯光招海寇。第三条？来问的是喝醉的吴把总，多说一句他能哭到天亮。

column2: Storyteller's Booth
column3: 说书棚

column2: In a straw booth by the docks a storyteller with a clapper-block tells 'The Qianli' every day. His audience is packed with pirate archers who can't stand a story without an ending and make him change it nightly: tonight it comes home laden with gold, tomorrow it marries the Dragon King's daughter, the night after it conquers thirty kingdoms. His throat is parched, and he's up to ending number three hundred and seven.
column3: 码头边一座草棚，说书先生一块醒木，天天讲《千里号》。台下坐满了海寇弓手，他们不爱听没结局的故事，逼先生每晚换个结局：今晚满载金银回港，明晚娶了龙女，后晚打下海外三十国。先生讲得口干舌燥，结局已经编到第三百零七个了。

column2: The archers are shown out. The story never had an ending, the storyteller says; he only told it as far as barge No. 7 being towed back. Every August a turbaned foreign merchant comes to hear that part, leaves a silver coin and goes, never asking the ending, only one thing: 'That porcelain. When will it arrive?'
column3: 弓手们被请出了棚子。先生说这故事本来没有结局，他只讲到七号驳被拖回去就停。每年八月，有个包头巾的番商来听这一段，听完放下一枚银币就走，从不问结局，只问一句：「那船瓷，什么时候到？」

column2: Ship-Tally Workshop
column3: 舶牌坊

column2: Deep in an alley a workshop carves ship tallies: one wooden tag for every seagoing ship, carved with name, master and number, checked on every entry and departure. Pirate swordsmen have taken it and make the old carver cut fake tallies for smugglers. He does, but secretly carves a tortoise, the old insult, on the back of each. On the wall hangs one dusty tally nobody has collected in ten years.
column3: 小巷深处一间作坊，老匠人专刻舶牌：出海的船每条一块，刻着船名、船主、编号，进出港都要验。一伙海寇刀手占着作坊，逼他给私船刻假牌。他刻是刻了，每块背后都偷偷刻一只王八。墙上还挂着一块落了灰的旧牌，十年没人来领。

column2: The swordsmen are chased out and the carver takes down the old tally and blows off the dust: 'Qianli 7'. He carved all seven of the Qianli's tallies; six were collected, and this one has hung here since. 'To sail you need three things: the Office's certificate, my tally, and the fort's leave.' He hands it over. 'The other two, go and get yourselves.'
column3: 刀手被打跑，老匠人摘下那块旧牌吹掉灰：「千里·七」。千里号七条船的舶牌都是他刻的，六块领走了，这块一直挂着。「出海要三样：市舶司的公凭，我这块牌子，还得炮台放行。」他把牌子交给你们，「剩下两样，你们去讨。」

column2: Enlistment Green
column3: 投军坪

column2: A black flag flies over a green outside town: 'Join the pirates: meals provided, blades issued.' With the Office shut ten years, the dock porters, carriers and stevedores have no work and come here wave after wave. The recruiting chief calls names behind a table, taking swordsmen, archers and riders alike. The newest hold their blades backwards and still clamour to be captains.
column3: 城外一片坪地上插着一面黑旗：「投海寇者，管饭，发刀。」市舶司关门十年，码头的脚夫、挑夫、扛包的没活干，一拨拨往这里来。招兵头目坐在桌后点名，刀手、弓手、劫骑都收，新来的连刀都握反了，还嚷着要当大头领。

column2: This wave is scattered and most throw down their blades and go back to town for work. The roll reads: 'Porters 17, carriers 9, former Office store guards 3.' But the black flag still flies and there are always idle men on the docks, so in a few days another wave will come. Once the Office truly opens, perhaps fewer will.
