column3: 这一拨新兵被打散，多半扔了刀回城找活。招兵簿上记着：「脚夫十七，挑夫九，市舶司旧库丁三。」可黑旗还插着，码头上没活的人总有，过不了几天又会来一拨。等市舶司的门真开了，来的人或许会少一些。

column2: Signal-Flag Tower
column3: 旗语楼

column2: A timber tower on the plain carries a flagpole the fort once used to talk to ships by flag: red to heave to, yellow for inspection, black for cannon fire. Pirate archers have stolen the fort's flag book and taken the tower, hoisting nonsense, so ships in the harbour stop, flee or spin in circles while the archers laugh and slap the rail.
column3: 平野上一座木楼，楼顶竖着旗杆，从前炮台用旗语跟港里的船说话：红旗停船，黄旗验货，黑旗开炮。一伙海寇弓手偷了炮台的旗谱，占了旗楼，挂起乱七八糟的旗，港里的船有的停、有的跑、有的原地打转，弓手们在楼上笑得直拍栏杆。

column2: The archers are driven down and the flags lowered. Tucked in the back of the flag book is a night log from ten years ago: 'Eighteenth of the eighth month, midnight. Three hundred Qian lanterns in harbour. By the Captain's order, black flag hoisted: lights out, ships to stop. Lights out. Fourth watch: one lantern relit. Ships departed.' The lights went out. The ships didn't stop.
column3: 弓手被赶下楼，乱旗都降了。旗谱后面夹着十年前的值夜记：「八月十八子时，港内见千字灯三百，奉把总令挂黑旗，令其灭灯停船。灯灭。四更，灯复亮一盏，船出。」灯是灭了，船没停。

column2: Outer Battery Slope
column3: 外炮坡

column2: A row of earthwork batteries lines the slope outside the wall, guns on the harbour gate. The garrison stopped fighting pirates long ago and runs an 'outbound inspection' at the foot of the slope: every departing ship stops and pays, and only when it has paid enough do they hold fire. Swordsmen check cargo, archers man the guns, riders chase anyone slipping past. Boatmen say this slope is worse than the pirates.
column3: 城墙外的山坡上一排土炮台，炮口对着港门。守炮的兵早不打海寇了，在坡下设了一道「出港查验」，出港的船都要停下交钱，交够了才不开炮：刀手查货，弓手站炮位，劫骑去追想溜的船。港里的船家说，这道坡比海寇还难过。

column2: The checkpoint is torn down and the gunners slink back. In its accounts, besides the tolls, is another income, every month for ten years without a miss: 'Long house, lamp-oil money, twenty taels.' The note beside it is four words: 'No Qian goes out.'
column3: 卡子拆了，炮手们灰溜溜缩回了炮位。卡房账上，除了过路钱，还有一笔进账，十年里每月一次，一次不少：「龙记，灯油钱，二十两。」旁边只注了四个字：「千字不出」。

column2: Maritime Trade Office
column3: 市舶司

column2: The grandest yamen in the harbour, stone lions at the gate, its vermilion doors peeling. Ten years ago foreign merchants thronged here; now the gates are shut and pirate swordsmen have set up stalls outside charging 'handling fees': to sail or to unload, everything goes through them. Superintendent Ke stands at the foot of the steps looking up at his own yamen, unable to get in.
column3: 港口最气派的一座衙门，门前两只石狮子，朱漆大门剥得斑斑驳驳。十年前这里番商云集，如今大门紧闭，门前被一伙海寇刀手占了，摆摊收「代办费」：要出海、要卸货，都得经他们的手。柯提举站在台阶下，看着自己的衙门，进不去。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown out, the gates open for the first time in ten years, and trade resumes: foreign merchants' gold for shipyard timber. In the hall Superintendent Ke spreads his half paper chart and sets the twelve plates in a ring around it. The lines in the plates join one to the next and meet the coast on the paper: out of Quanzhou, southeast, on into a blank space marked with one character: Fog. 'A continued voyage needs the three guarantors to sign again,' he says. 'Master Zhuang, myself, and the Long house.'
column3: 刀手被赶走，大门十年来头一回打开，番商的金子换船坞的木料，买卖又做起来了。柯提举在大堂上摊开半张纸海图，把十二只青花盘围成一圈：盘心的线一只接一只，连上纸上的海岸，从泉州出港往东南去，一直画进一片空白，空白上写着一个「雾」字。「续航要三个保人重新画押，」他说，「庄窑主，我，还有龙家。」

column2: Foreign Quarter Inn
column3: 蕃坊驿

column2: The Foreign Quarter is where the overseas merchants lived, and at its entrance stands a large inn with a fountain basin and domed roofs. With the merchants gone ten years, dockside raiders have taken it, watering their horses at the fountain and lounging on the carpets chewing cane. The old innkeeper speaks seven foreign tongues and now uses them for one thing only: cursing.
column3: 蕃坊是番商住的街坊，街口一座大驿馆，院里有喷水的石池，屋顶是圆的。番商走了十年，驿馆被一伙码头劫骑占了，马拴在石池边饮水，骑手们躺在番商的地毯上啃甘蔗。驿馆的老掌柜会说七种番话，如今只用来干一件事：骂人。

column2: The raiders are turned out and the carpets get three days' beating. As word spreads that the Office has opened, foreign ships begin to come in; some, says the innkeeper, have waited outside the bar for years for the Office's lamps to light. 'They say Quanzhou is the gate of the sea. Shut the gate and the sea shrinks.'
column3: 劫骑被赶出去，地毯拍了三天灰。市舶司开门的消息一传开，港外就有番船靠过来了。老掌柜说，有几条番船在沙坝外等了好几年，就等市舶司的灯一亮。「他们说，泉州是海上的大门，门一关，海就小了。」

column2: In the inn you seize the raiders' hoard: twenty sacks of foreign rice, a chest of pepper, three Persian carpets used as saddle blankets, and a big jar of honeyed dates the merchants left, eaten down to the bottom.
column3: 驿馆里抄出劫骑囤的二十袋番米、一箱胡椒、三张垫在马鞍下的波斯毯，还有一大罐番商留下的蜜枣，已经被吃得只剩罐底。

column2: Every time you pass, the old innkeeper greets you in all seven tongues and serves cardamom tea and flatbread. The merchants asked him, he says, to look after 'the ones who opened the door'.
column3: 每次路过，老掌柜都用七种番话问候你们一遍，再端上一壶加了豆蔻的番茶和一盘烤饼，说番商们托他招待「开门的人」。

column2: Pledge Shed
column3: 押契寮

column2: A straw shed on the plain flies a Long Bank flag. Pirate archers watch a boy of ten or so, hands caked in clay, made to shape clay bowl after clay bowl. He's Zhuang Dalu's grandson: the kiln master has lived on Long Bank loans these past years and can't repay, so the boy is held against the interest. The archers use the bowls as wine cups; for every one they smash, he makes another.
column3: 平野上一间草寮，寮外插着龙记钱庄的旗，一伙海寇弓手看着一个十来岁的男孩，男孩满手是泥，被逼着捏一只又一只泥碗。他是庄大炉的孙子：窑主这些年靠借龙记的钱过日子，还不上，孙子就被押在这里抵利钱。弓手们拿泥碗当酒碗，摔一只，他捏一只。

column2: The archers are beaten off and the boy runs home to the kiln with his last clay bowl. Zhuang Dalu hobbles to the Office and presses his thumbprint on the new surety so hard he seems to push it into the paper. 'I stand surety with these old bones. This time that porcelain goes to sea.'
column3: 弓手被打跑，孩子揣着最后一只泥碗跑回了龙窑。庄大炉拄着拐来到市舶司，在新保状上按下手印，按得很重，像要按进纸里去：「我这把老骨头作保，那船瓷，这回得出海。」

column2: Gunner's Noodle House
column3: 铳头面馆

column2: On the little street below the fort is a noodle house run by a retired gunner, Iron-Mouth Qin, deafened long ago by cannon, who talks like thunder. Pirate swordsmen come daily to eat without paying and demand another bowl. Qin reads lips and takes everything as 'another bowl'. He's served them forty, and they're too stuffed to move.
column3: 炮台下的小街上有一家面馆，老板是退伍的老炮手，人称秦铁口，耳朵早被炮震聋了，说话像打雷。一伙海寇刀手天天来吃面不给钱，吃完还要再来一碗。秦铁口听不见，只看口型，一律当成「再来一碗」，已经下了四十碗，刀手们撑得走不动了。

column2: The swordsmen leave on hands and knees. Wiping the stove, Qin says that on that night he was gun captain, ordered to fire one shot into the harbour to scare the Qianli. 'I loaded the powder. I didn't load the ball.' All noise, no strike; the fleet put out its lights, relit one, and sailed. 'That's the shot that deafened me. Worth it.'
column3: 刀手们是爬着出去的。秦铁口擦着灶台说，那一夜他是炮长，把总下令往港里开一炮吓住千里号。「我装了火药，没装炮子。」那一炮只响不打，船队灭了灯，又亮起一盏，就出去了。「我这耳朵就是那一炮震聋的。值。」

column2: Laver Rocks
column3: 紫菜岩

column2: Laver grows on the rocks beneath the fort's cliff. At low tide the women who gather it tie ropes round their waists and press against the slick rock, scraping it off sheet by sheet. Pirate archers have taken the rocks: a basket gathered, a basket taken. The lead gatherer, A'lan, scrapes fastest and ties her rope loosest. She says she isn't afraid of falling.
column3: 炮台崖下的礁岩上长着紫菜，退潮时，采菜的女人们腰上拴着绳子，贴着湿滑的岩壁一片片刮。一伙海寇弓手占了礁岩，说紫菜归他们，刮一篮收一篮。领头的采菜女叫阿蓝，刮得最快，绳子拴得最松，她说她不怕掉下去。

column2: The archers are driven off and the laver spread to dry on the clifftop. A'lan's husband was one of the two recruits who rowed after the blue lights. She blames no one, but says Qin has given her half his pay every month. 'He says he made that rule too late.' She gives you a bundle of laver and adds, 'The Captain gives too, on the quiet. He daren't let the Long house know.'
column3: 弓手被赶下礁，紫菜晒上了岩顶。阿蓝的男人就是哨铺那两个划船追蓝光的新兵之一。她不怪谁，只说秦铁口每月都从饷里拿一半给她，「他说那条规矩定晚了。」她送你们一捆紫菜，又补一句：「把总也给，偷偷的，不敢让龙家知道。」

column2: Dark Market
column3: 摸黑市

column2: For ten years the night market outside town has been forbidden lamps. 'The lamp-oil money's paid to the fort,' says the Long house; 'nothing lights up at night', except Long lanterns, at ten times the price. The people won't buy, so the market trades in the dark: feeling fish scales for freshness, pinching cloth to guess its colour, counting coppers by fingertip. Swordsmen, archers and riders prowl the dark, robbing anyone who fumbles.
column3: 城外的夜市十年不许点灯，龙记说「灯油钱交给炮台了，夜里不许再亮」，只准买龙记的灯笼，一盏顶十盏的价。百姓不买，夜市就摸黑做买卖：摸鱼鳞猜新鲜，捏布料猜颜色，数铜钱全凭手指头。刀手、弓手、劫骑在黑地里来回转，专抢摸错了的人。

column2: The bruisers are chased off. Someone feels out a flint and lights a lamp, then another, until the whole market glows. The cloth-seller looks at her bolts and shrieks: 'I've been selling the red as green for ten years!' The old folk say that on that night in the eighth month the whole market ran to the shore with lamps to see the ships off; at the fort's command every lamp went out, and the next day came the rule of no lights.
column3: 打手们被赶跑，有人摸出火石点起灯，一盏接一盏，整条夜市亮了。卖布的大嫂一看自己的布，惊叫：「我把红的当绿的卖了十年！」老人们说，那年八月十八夜里，夜市的人都跑到海边点灯送船，炮台一声令下，灯全灭了，第二天就有了不许点灯的规矩。

column2: Litigator's Loft
column3: 讼师楼

column2: In an alley stands a little loft where a skinny litigator lives. In ten years he has sued the fort fifty-two times on Granny Chen's behalf, for 'forcible seizure of three hundred lanterns, unpaid'. Fifty-two petitions, fifty-two dismissals, and he's writing the fifty-third. The fort has hired pirate swordsmen to wreck the loft; he hides under his desk, still grinding ink.
column3: 巷子里一座小楼，住着个瘦讼师，十年里替陈婆告了炮台五十二回，告的是「强收灯笼三百盏，未付分文」。状子递了五十二回，驳回五十二回，他还在写第五十三回。炮台雇了一伙海寇刀手来砸他的楼，他躲在桌子底下，还在磨墨。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown downstairs. The litigator crawls out and leafs through the fifty-two rulings: each ends with the same sentence: 'The Qian ban was not issued by the authorities and so cannot be revoked.' He slaps the desk and roars. 'The authorities never issued it! Then who did?' On the fifty-third petition he adds a defendant: the Long house.
column3: 刀手们被赶下楼。讼师爬出来翻开五十二份批文，每一份末尾都是同一句：「千字禁令，非官府所颁，无从撤销。」他拍桌大笑：「官府没颁过！那是谁颁的？」他在第五十三份状子上添了个被告：龙记。

column2: Inspection Dock
column3: 验货坞

column2: The Office's inspection dock is a long stone jetty where every foreign ship tied up to open its holds. With no inspections for ten years, it's a contraband landing: every midnight pirate swordsmen unload smuggled salt, iron and spice here without a light, by feel. By day they sleep on the jetty with the inspector's inkpad for a pillow.
column3: 市舶司的验货坞是一道石砌长堤，番船进港都要靠在这里开舱验货。十年没人验货，长堤成了私货码头，一伙海寇刀手每到半夜就在这里卸私盐、私铁、私香料，灯也不点，全凭摸。白天他们睡在堤上，拿验货官的印台当枕头。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown off and the inkpad washed and set back on its desk. Superintendent Ke has barge No. 7 towed from the bonded store to the inspection dock, and all three thousand pieces are weighed, counted and relabelled. In the end the five missing crates and the twelve plates are all accounted for. All that's lacking is the Long house's thumbprint.
column3: 刀手被赶下堤，印台洗干净摆回了桌上。柯提举叫人把七号驳从封库拖来，靠上验货坞，三千件瓷一件件过秤、点数、贴新签。点到最后，缺的五箱和十二只盘都对上了数，只差龙家一个手印。

column2: Three Hundred Bowls
column3: 三百碗

column2: By the harbour is a porridge shop. Every year when the eighth month comes, its proprietress sets three hundred coarse bowls before her door, fills them with hot porridge every night, leaves them till dawn, then gives them to the beggars. Pirate archers say she's 'calling up ghosts' and demand 'ghost-quelling money', or they'll shoot the bowls to pieces. She stands among her ranks of bowls banging the pot with her ladle and cursing, refusing to give up one.
column3: 港边一间粥铺，每年一进八月，老板娘就在门口摆开三百只粗碗，每晚盛满热粥，摆到天亮，再端给街上的乞丐。一伙海寇弓手说她「招鬼」，要她交「镇鬼钱」，不交就把碗一只只射碎。老板娘站在碗阵中间，拿勺子敲着锅沿骂，一只也不让。

column2: The archers are driven off; only seven bowls broke. She stood in this doorway that year, she says, and saw three hundred lanterns go out at once, the harbour black as ink. After a while one lantern lit again at a bow, just one, and moved steadily out of the harbour gate. 'The shipmaster's lantern. I knew it.' Every year since, she's set out three hundred bowls. 'Someone has to keep a meal ready for them.'
column3: 弓手被赶跑，碎了的碗只有七只。老板娘说，那年她就站在这门口，看见三百盏灯一齐灭了，港里黑得像墨；过了一会儿，船头又亮起一盏，就一盏，一直往港门外去。「那是船主的灯，我认得。」从那年起，她每年摆三百只碗：「总得有人替她们备着饭。」

column2: Seal-Vault Islet
column3: 印房洲

column2: On a small islet mid-river stands a stone house behind three iron doors, once the vault of the Office's great seal. Ten years ago, when barge No. 7's duty went unpaid, the law required the Superintendent to pledge the great seal as security. To whom, Superintendent Ke still won't say. The Long house's finest guard it now: swordsmen at the door, archers on the shore, riders splashing through the shallows.
column3: 江心小洲上有一间石屋，铁门三道，从前是市舶司存大印的印房。十年前七号驳的税没交上，按律提举要把大印押出去作保，押给了谁，柯提举至今不肯说。如今石屋由龙记最精锐的打手守着：刀手堵门，弓手守岸，劫骑在浅滩上来回踏水。

column2: The three doors open. The great seal sits squarely on its stone altar, its case still tied with that year's red cord. Beside it is a chest holding exactly the duty on the porcelain plus ten years' interest, to the copper. On top lies a note in the Long heir's hand: 'I'll pay the duty. On the day the ships come home, I'll pay it.'
column3: 三道铁门打开，大印端端正正摆在石台上，印匣上还系着当年的红绳。旁边一口箱子，装着那船瓷的税银，外加十年的利息，一文不差。箱上压着龙家少东家的字条：「税我交。船回来那天，再交。」

column2: Fourth-Watch Tower
column3: 四更楼

column2: A drum tower stands on the city wall where the watchman beats the hours each night: first watch, second, third. The fourth he never beats; he skips straight to the fifth. Pirate archers have taken the tower and, sick of the noise, thrown his drum off the wall. The old watchman sits on the battlements hugging his sticks. He's skipped the fourth watch ten years, he says, and one more night won't hurt, but that drum mustn't be lost.
column3: 城墙上一座更楼，更夫每夜打更：一更、二更、三更，到了四更却从来不敲，直接跳到五更。一伙海寇弓手占了更楼，嫌吵，把更鼓扔下了城墙。老更夫抱着鼓槌坐在墙垛上，说他少打了十年四更，再少一夜不碍事，可这鼓不能丢。

column2: The archers are driven off and the drum fetched from the wall's foot. In the watch book, on the page for that night ten years ago, under the fourth watch: 'The Qianli departs. The fort fires one blank.' Afterwards the Captain declared the fourth watch 'unlucky' and forbade it. Tonight, after a moment's hesitation, the old man beats the fourth watch once, very softly.
column3: 弓手被赶下城，鼓从墙根捡了回来。老更夫翻开更簿，十年前八月十八那页，四更底下写着：「千里号出港，炮台放空炮一声。」那以后把总说四更「不吉利」，不许再打。今夜他犹豫了一下，轻轻敲了一记四更。

column2: Notice Wall
column3: 抄榜墙

column2: A big notice has just gone up on the screen wall outside the Office: 'Qianli barge No. 7, continued voyage. Hiring sailors, helmsmen, cooks.' The ink isn't dry before pirate archers have shot it full of holes and pasted up their own: 'Anyone who dares board, ask Master Long first.' Would-be sailors stand at a distance craning their necks, not daring to come closer.
column3: 市舶司门外的照壁上新贴了一张大榜：「千里号七号驳续航，招水手、舵工、伙夫若干。」墨迹未干，一伙海寇弓手就拿箭把榜射成了筛子，又贴上自己的一张：「谁敢上船，先问龙爷。」想报名的水手们站在远处探头探脑，不敢走近。

column2: The archers are driven off, the notice goes back up, and the sailors form a long queue, a white-bearded old helmsman at its head. Beneath the notice someone has added in charcoal: 'Porcelain, certificate, tally: all here. If the Dragon King doesn't nod, no ship leaves Berth One.'
column3: 弓手被赶跑，大榜重新贴上，水手们排起长队，一个白胡子老舵工排在第一。榜底下不知谁用炭写了一行小字：「瓷有了，凭有了，牌有了。龙王不点头，船出不了一号泊。」

column2: Sea-Cut Cave
column3: 海蚀洞

column2: In the sea cliff below the fort opens a great cave whose mouth is drowned at high tide and shows only at the ebb. Beside it stands a lone pillar of rock like a finger stuck in the sea. Dockside raiders ride in at every low tide to stash contraband, and when the tide rises the mouth seals itself. The tide has just gone out, and hoofbeats echo inside.
column3: 炮台下的海崖上开着一个大洞，涨潮时洞口没在水里，只有退潮才露出来。洞边立着一根孤零零的石柱，像一根插在海里的手指。一伙码头劫骑专趁退潮骑马进洞藏私货，等潮一涨，洞口自己封上，谁也找不着。今天潮刚退，马蹄声正在洞里回响。

column2: The raiders are cornered inside and dealt with. Qin says the waves dug this cave: they pound the cliff's foot, cut a notch, scoop it into a cave; one day it breaks through into an arch, the arch roof falls, and the outer part is left standing like that pillar. At the back lies a rotted skiff holding an oilpaper-wrapped letter: 'Please let us pass. The duty owed, Shen Du alone will answer for.' That night it never reached the fort.
column3: 劫骑被堵在洞里收拾了。秦铁口说这洞是浪掏出来的：浪专打崖脚，先打出凹槽，再掏成洞，哪天打穿成了石拱，拱顶一塌，外头那截就成了旁边那样的孤柱。洞底一条烂舢板里有封油纸裹的信：「请放行。所欠之税，沈渡一人担。」那夜，这信没送到炮台。

column2: Silver-Cart Road
column3: 银车道

column2: A wagon under an oilcloth rolls along the road, wheels biting deep, a troop of dockside raiders riding escort. On the first of every month it travels from the Long Bank to the fort, and everyone along the way knows what it carries: the Long house's 'lamp-oil money'. This month's wagon has just set out, and the riders crack their whips, sending a flock of ducks flapping across the sky.
column3: 一辆蒙着油布的马车在路上走，车轮压得很深，前后一队码头劫骑护着。每月初一它都走这条路，从龙记钱庄到炮台，路边的人都知道车上是什么：龙记给炮台的「灯油钱」。这个月的车刚上路，劫骑们挥着鞭子，把挡路的鸭群赶得满天飞。

column2: The riders scatter and, sure enough, the wagon holds twenty taels sealed in red paper marked 'Lamp oil'. The old carter has driven this run ten years, and every time Master Long came to watch it loaded. Once, drunk, he patted the silver and said, 'This isn't paying them not to let ships out. It's paying them not to let the wrong ship out.' The carter still hasn't worked that out.
column3: 劫骑被打散，车上果然是二十两银子，红纸封着，写「灯油」。老车夫说他赶这趟车十年，每回龙爷都亲自看着装车。有一回龙爷喝多了，摸着银子说：「这钱不是买他们不放船，是买他们别放错了船。」老车夫到今天也没想明白。

column2: Thousand-Lantern Lane
column3: 千灯巷

column2: Behind Chen's Lanterns runs a lane of thirty-odd households, every one with someone who worked for the Qianli ten years ago: sewing sails, loading cargo, cooking. Granny Chen hands out the lanterns recovered from the magazine. Each time one is hung, pirate archers at the lane's mouth shoot it down, and each time one falls, another is hung. The fallen lanterns burn, and the blaze turns the lane red.
column3: 陈记灯笼背后有一条小巷，住着三十几户人家，十年前家家都有人给千里号做过活：缝帆的、装货的、做饭的。陈婆把药局里找回来的灯笼分给各家，巷里挂上一盏，一伙海寇弓手就在巷口射下一盏；射下一盏，巷里又挂出一盏。掉在地上的灯笼烧起来，火光把巷子照得通红。

column2: The archers are driven out and the lane hangs full of Qian lanterns, not one household missing. The soldiers on the fort watch from afar and no one fires. Granny Chen lights the last lantern and hangs it at her own door. 'We have the lanterns and the people. All that's left is the fort's nod, and the Long house's berth.'
column3: 弓手被赶出巷口，巷子里挂满了「千」字灯笼，一家不少。炮台上的兵远远看着，没人开炮。陈婆点着最后一盏，挂在自家门口：「灯有了，人也有了。现在就差炮台点头，还有龙家那个泊位。」

column2: Frankincense Lodge
column3: 乳香栈

column2: Outside town stands a foreign merchant's warehouse, frankincense smoke drifting from its door. Its master is an old turbaned trader named Hassan, beard dyed red. For ten years he has traded with no one in Quanzhou and has hired pirate archers to shoot back anyone who comes to talk business. He does one thing each day: sit at his door and look toward the harbour.
column3: 城外一座番商的货栈，门口飘着乳香的烟。栈主是个包头巾的老番商，叫哈桑，胡子染成了红色，十年来不跟泉州任何人做买卖，还雇了一伙海寇弓手守门，谁来谈生意都被射回去。他每天只做一件事：坐在门口，望着港口的方向。

column2: The archers are driven back and Hassan looks you over, stroking his red beard. He respects anyone who can fight their way in and will open his stores to trade. He shows a contract from ten years ago: three thousand pieces of Zhuang porcelain for Srivijaya, 'price raised a tenth on delivery, however many years it takes'. 'I'm waiting for that porcelain, and for the woman shipmaster who kept her word. Go and get the Long house's thumbprint. It's all that's missing.'
column3: 弓手被打退，哈桑摸着红胡子打量你们，说佩服能打进来的人，愿意开栈换货。他拿出十年前的契约：庄窑瓷三千件，卖往三佛齐，「货到之日，价加一成，不论几年」。「我等那船瓷，也等那个说话算数的女船主。去请龙家按手印吧，只差它了。」

column2: Long House Godowns
column3: 龙记货栈

column2: Behind the harbour sprawl the godowns, dozens of storehouses joined into a street, every lintel hung with a gilded Long, dragon. Whatever a Quanzhou merchant sells must first be stored here, and only once storage is paid may it be sold. The guards, swordsmen, archers and riders, number over a hundred, and at the gates the clank of steelyard weights is as loud as the cursing. A lychee seller who didn't pay has watched his fruit rot at the door into a puddle of wine.
column3: 港后一大片货栈，几十间库房连成一条街，门楣上都挂着金色的「龙」字。泉州的商人不论卖什么，都得先把货存进这里，交了栈钱才能卖。守栈的刀手、弓手、劫骑上百人，门口的秤砣声跟骂声一样响。一个卖荔枝的小贩没交栈钱，荔枝在门口烂成了一摊酒。

column2: The guards are scattered and merchants pour in to haul out their goods. The ledger's first page lists every berth in Quanzhou. Against Berth One, every year for ten years, the same line: 'Qianli. Berth fee. Paid by the Long house.' His own money into his own godown, and not one copper missed from the books.
column3: 守栈的打手被打散，商人们涌进去搬自己的货。栈簿第一页列着泉州港所有的泊位，一号泊那一栏，十年来年年同一行：「千里号，泊费，龙记自付。」自己的钱付进自己的栈，一文没少记。

column2: Pigeon Loft
column3: 鸽楼

column2: By the city wall stands a loft of homing pigeons, Captain Wu's private property. Each day he ties a slip to a pigeon's leg and sends it to the Long house. Dockside raiders guard the loft and chase off anyone who comes near. The pigeons eat well and fly lazily; one is so fat it can't clear the wall and delivers its messages on foot.
column3: 城墙边一座鸽楼，养着几十只信鸽，是吴把总的私产。他每天写一张纸条绑在鸽腿上，放往龙记。一队码头劫骑守在楼下，谁靠近就赶。鸽子吃得好，飞得懒，有一只胖得飞不上墙头，每天在楼下走着去送信。

column2: The raiders are driven off just as the fat pigeon waddles back, a Long house reply tied to its leg: 'Does the pioneer party carry the lanterns? If so, don't stop them.' You show it to Captain Wu. He stares a long while, then crumples it. 'First time in ten years Master Long has answered like that.'
column3: 劫骑被赶跑，那只胖鸽子正好走回来，腿上绑着龙记的回条：「开拓队带灯否？带，则不拦。」你们拿去给吴把总看，他看了半天，把纸条揉成一团：「龙爷十年里头一回这么回话。」

column2: Sea-Guard Battery
column3: 镇海炮台

column2: The fort's highest tier: twelve great guns in a row, muzzles on the harbour gate. Not all who man it are soldiers: a troop of dockside raiders is here too, sent by the Long house to 'help watch the guns'. Captain Wu says he's stopped blocking anyone, but the raiders answer only to the Long house's token, and they crank the muzzles lower, aiming at the red glow of Thousand-Lantern Lane.
column3: 炮台最高的一层，十二门大炮排成一排，炮口对着港门。守炮顶的不全是炮台的兵，还有一队龙记派来「帮着看炮」的码头劫骑。吴把总说他已经不拦了，可劫骑们不认他的话，只认龙记的令牌，把炮口又往下压了压，对准了千灯巷那片红光。

column2: The raiders are driven off. Captain Wu lays a yellowed paper on a gun barrel: his receipt to the Long house from ten years ago. 'Ships bearing Qian: the fort will not release them, until the Long house says the word.' He was greedy for the twenty taels then, he says, and afterwards dared not stop. 'I set the ban. But the key is in Master Long's hand.'
column3: 劫骑被赶下炮台。吴把总把一张发黄的纸压在炮身上，是十年前他写给龙记的回执：「千字之船，炮台不放，凭龙记一言而解。」他说当年贪那二十两，后来是不敢收手。「禁令是我立的，可钥匙在龙爷手里。」

column2: Dragon Gate Arch
column3: 龙门坊

column2: To enter the Long house's ground you pass a stone arch carved 'Dragon Gate', a stone dragon crouched beneath. The pirate archers guarding it have a rule: everyone pats the dragon's head and says 'Good fortune to Master Long', and if it isn't loud enough, says it again. The head is polished to a shine. A stammering porter has been at it for two hours and still hasn't got one sentence out.
column3: 进龙家地界要过一座石牌坊，坊额刻着「龙门」，坊下蹲着一条石龙。守坊的海寇弓手立了规矩：过坊的人要摸一下石龙的脑袋，说一句「龙爷发财」，不够响就重说。石龙脑袋被摸得锃亮，一个结巴挑夫在坊下说了一个时辰，还没说完一句。

column2: The archers are run off and the stammering porter curses them out in one whole sentence without a stumble. The old man at the tea stall under the arch says that ten years ago Master Long was a young heir with one cargo ship; in ten years he's swallowed most of Quanzhou's docks. 'Everything's for sale with him. Except Berth One. Whatever anyone offers, he won't sell it.'
column3: 弓手们被赶跑，结巴挑夫一口气骂完一整句，一个字没卡。坊下摆茶摊的老头说，龙爷十年前还是个只有一条货船的少东家，十年里吃下了泉州大半的码头。「什么都能买，什么都能卖，就是一号泊，谁出多少钱他都不卖。」

column2: Cricket Pit
column3: 斗蟋场

column2: A big courtyard is crowded with clay pots of fighting crickets, gamblers packed round them. The pit is the Long house's, kept by pirate archers who stop any winner from leaving and make him keep betting. On the wall hangs a red board with the wager Master Long places every year on the eighteenth of the eighth month: 'The Qianli comes home this year.' A hundred to one.
column3: 一座大院里摆满瓦罐，罐里斗着蟋蟀，四面围着赌客。场子是龙记开的，海寇弓手看场子，谁赢了钱想走，弓手就拦着让他接着押。墙上挂着一块红牌，写着龙爷每年八月十八必押的一注：「千里号今年回港。」一赔一百。

column2: The archers are thrown out and the gamblers scatter clutching their pots. The old pit master shows the betting book: Master Long has placed this wager for ten years, lost every year, paid every year, never once welshed. This year's went down last month, bigger than ever. 'Ten years losing and still betting,' says the old man. 'Tell me: does he believe, or doesn't he?'
column3: 弓手被赶出去，赌客们抱着罐子散了。老场主翻出赌账：这一注龙爷押了十年，年年输，年年照赔，一次没赖过。今年的注上个月就押下了，比哪年都大。「输了十年还在押，」老场主说，「你说他是信，还是不信？」

column2: Sailcloth Hall
column3: 帆布行

column2: In a long workshop women sit in two rows sewing sails, stiff battened sails propped along the walls. Dockside raiders, claiming the Long house ships need new sails, have taken all the cloth, so the women are stitching the raiders' saddle covers. Behind the workshop is a locked storeroom; when the raiders try to force it, the old sailmaker jabs their hands with her needle.
column3: 长长的作坊里，女工们坐成两排缝帆，篾片撑开的硬帆一面面靠在墙上。一队码头劫骑说龙记的船要换帆，把作坊里的布都收走了，女工们没布可缝，只好缝劫骑的马鞍套。作坊后面有一间锁着的库房，劫骑想撬，老帆匠拿针扎他们的手。

column2: The raiders are driven off and the cloth carried back. The old sailmaker unlocks the storeroom: inside hangs a full set of battened sails, ribs new, Qian painted on the canvas. The Long house orders a set every three years and swaps out the old: three sets in ten years, not one ever aboard a ship. 'Master Long says if the sails get old, the ships will have nothing to use when they come home.'
column3: 劫骑被赶跑，布匹扛了回来。老帆匠打开库房，里面挂着一整套硬帆，篾骨崭新，帆上画着「千」。龙家每三年订一套，旧的拆了换新的，十年换了三套，没一套上过船。「龙爷说，帆旧了，船回来没得用。」

column2: Night Talk at the Fort
column3: 炮台夜话

column2: At night a table is set in the little yard below the fort. Iron-Mouth Qin, Captain Wu, Granny Chen, the litigator and the old watchman sit round a pot of cold tea, and nobody wants to speak first. Outside the gate, pirate swordsmen sent by the Long house to watch the Captain pace up and down, ready to burst in at the first Qian. Granny Chen sets an unlit lantern in the very centre of the table.
column3: 夜里，炮台下的小院摆了一张桌子，秦铁口、吴把总、陈婆、讼师和老更夫围着一壶冷茶，谁也不先开口。院门外，龙记派来盯着把总的一伙海寇刀手来回踱步，听见里面说一个「千」字就要冲进来。陈婆把一盏没点的灯笼放在桌子正中。

column2: The swordsmen at the gate are driven off. Captain Wu speaks first: from tonight the fort won't stop any ship with Qian lanterns. Qin bellows that he'll load powder once more, and once more no ball: a send-off. Granny Chen lights the lantern. 'She left with one lantern. We'll send her ship out again with three hundred.' The litigator pockets his petition. 'Defendant: the Long house. Court sits at Berth One.'
column3: 门外的刀手被赶走了。吴把总先开口：从今夜起，炮台不拦挂「千」字灯笼的船。秦铁口吼着说，再装一回火药，还不装炮子，给船送行。陈婆点亮了灯：「她用一盏灯出的港，我们用三百盏送她的船再出去。」讼师揣好状子：「被告龙记，就在一号泊开庭。」

column2: Driftwood Cove
column3: 浮木澳

column2: After every big blow a layer of timber washes into this cove: broken masts, planks, whole logs. Dockside raiders hold the beach, saying every stick that lands belongs to the Long house. A girl with a short braid ignores them, shoulders a heavy dark log and runs, too slowly, so the raiders chase her round and round the rocks while she yells, 'This one's ironwood, you don't know what you're looking at!'
column3: 每次刮过大风，这片海湾都会漂来一层木头：断桅、船板、整根原木。一队码头劫骑占着海滩，说漂上岸的木头都归龙记。一个扎短辫的姑娘不管不顾，扛起一根黑沉沉的木头就跑，跑不快，被劫骑追着绕礁石转圈，嘴里还喊：「这根是铁力木，你们不识货！」

column2: The raiders are driven off. The girl plants the log upright and, breathing hard, says she's A'qiang, apprentice to the shipwright Gong Modou. Her master has spent ten years building a ship to the Qianli's model and is short only a few things. 'Ironwood for the rudder post. It won't rot in ten years.' She pats the log. 'Master says once this ship is done, it can go after the Qianli.'
column3: 劫骑被赶下海滩，姑娘把木头往地上一戳，喘着气说她叫阿樯，是船匠龚墨斗的徒弟。师父照着千里号的船样造了十年船，还差几样东西。「铁力木做舵杆，十年都不烂。」她拍拍木头，「师父说，这条船造好了，就能去追千里号。」

column2: Charity Granary
column3: 义仓

column2: On high ground behind the harbour stands a stone charity granary. Its stele reads: 'For the three hundred households of the Qianli, three piculs of rice a year. Erected by Long Sihai.' Every year it opened to the families of the Qianli's crews. But these two years the steward has been robbing his own charge: he's hired dockside raiders to lock the gates and sells the rice on, and families who come for it go home with a whipping.
column3: 港后的高地上有一座石砌义仓，门口石碑刻着：「千里号三百家，岁给米三石，龙四海立。」每年开仓放米给千里号的家眷。可这两年管仓的管事监守自盗，雇了一队码头劫骑锁了仓门，把米倒卖给米行，家眷们来领米，只领回一顿鞭子。

column2: The steward is trussed up and sent to the Long house, and the granary opens again. The 'Long Sihai' on the stele is the Dragon King's real name. The old women in the queue say Master Long has a hard mouth and a soft heart: ten years without a good word for the Qianli, yet never a year short of rice. He just never lets anyone say it came from him.
column3: 管事被捆了送去龙记，仓门重开。碑上的「龙四海」，就是海龙王的本名。排队领米的老太太们说，龙爷嘴硬心软，十年没说过千里号一句好话，米却一年没少过，只是从不许人说是他给的。

column2: You find what the steward hid: forty piculs of old rice, two cellars of dried sweet potato, and his ledger of sales, whose last entry reads: 'Sold 100 piculs for 30 taels. If Master Long asks, say rats ate it.'
column3: 仓里抄出管事藏的四十石陈米、两窖番薯干，还有一本倒卖账，最后一笔写着：「卖米一百石，得银三十两，龙爷若问，就说鼠吃了。」

column2: Every time you pass, the old women wrap you a string of salt-pork rice dumplings, with the same request each time: 'Keep an eye on the sea for us. See if any ships are coming home.'
column3: 每次路过，领米的老太太们都给你们包一串咸肉粽子，还要叮嘱一句：「替我们看看海上，有没有船回来。」

column2: Red-Headband Hold
column3: 红头寨

column2: A new stockade stands on the plain, its pirates all in red headbands, archers especially. Their chief, Red-Head San, came up from the southern seas boasting he'll take over the Dragon King's docks: 'The Dragon King's gone soft, mooning over an empty berth. Quanzhou needs new blood.' He's sent the Long house three declarations of war, and all three came back unopened.
column3: 平野上一座新扎的寨子，寨里的海寇都扎红头巾，弓手尤其多。头领红头三是从南边海上来的，扬言要接海龙王的码头：「龙王老了，守着个空泊位发呆，泉州该换人了。」他给龙记下过三回战书，三回都原样退了回来，连封口都没拆。

column2: The hold is broken and Red-Head San flees back to sea. In the stockade is his spy's report: 'Long Sihai goes to Berth One every midnight and sits two hours, no escort, no lamp.' The spy added: 'Could be snatched.' Beside it Red-Head San wrote one word: 'Don't.' It seems even a pirate felt robbing him then wouldn't be decent.
column3: 红头寨被打散，红头三逃回了海上。寨里搜出他的探子报：「龙四海每夜子时到一号泊，坐一个时辰，不带人，不点灯。」探子添了一句：「此人可劫。」红头三在旁批了两个字：「不劫。」大概连海寇也觉得，这时候劫他不像话。

column2: Tung-Oil Slope
column3: 桐油坡

column2: Tung trees cover the hillside above a small oil press. Tung oil is the lifeblood of shipbuilding, for caulking seams. Dockside raiders have taken over the press and send every drop to the Long shipyard, selling none to anyone else. A'qiang says her master's ship is only missing the caulking in its last few holds, and this is the oil it needs.
column3: 山坡上一片油桐树，树下一座榨油的小作坊，桐子榨出的桐油是造船补缝的命根子。一队码头劫骑把作坊包了，榨出来的油全运去龙记船厂，一滴也不卖给别人。阿樯说师父的船只差最后几舱没艌好，要的就是这里的油。

column2: The raiders are driven off and the mistress of the press fills three barrels for you. Tying them down, A'qiang explains: mix tung oil with lime and pounded hemp, beat it into putty, ram it into the seams. Dry, it's harder than stone and not a drop of seawater gets through. 'That's how every seam on the Qianli was caulked.'
column3: 劫骑被赶走，油坊老板娘装了三桶桐油给你们。阿樯一边捆桶一边说：桐油掺上石灰和捣碎的麻丝，捶成油灰塞进船板缝里，干了比石头还硬，海水一滴也渗不进。「千里号的缝，当年就是这么一道道艌出来的。」

column2: Ropewalk Field
column3: 打绳场

column2: A long, narrow field where women with hanks of hemp at their waists twist as they walk backwards; a few hundred feet later, a long rope is made. Dockside raiders insist on riding straight through; the horses' legs snarl the ropes, the raiders are tangled off their saddles and thrash on the ground, pulling it tighter. The ropewalk women watch with hands on hips. Nobody moves to untie them.
column3: 一块又长又窄的空地，女人们腰上缠着麻团，一边搓一边往后退，退出几十丈，一根长绳就成了。一队码头劫骑偏要从绳场中间骑过去，马腿把绳子缠成一团乱麻，劫骑自己也被缠下了马，在地上越挣越紧。绳场的大姐们叉着腰看，谁也不去解。

column2: The raiders are cut loose and thrown out. Ten years ago, the women say, Shipmaster Shen ordered an anchor cable here, 'one that could hold three ships', and it took a month to twist. They cut off a length as a pattern before it went aboard; it still hangs on the wall, thicker than a man's arm. Working from it, they twist another for Gong Modou.
column3: 劫骑被解开扔出了场。大姐们说，十年前沈船主在这里订过一根锚缆，要「一根能拴住三条船的」，搓了整整一个月。上船前剪下一截留作样子，至今挂在墙上，比人的胳膊还粗。她们照着那截样子，给龚墨斗又搓了一根。

column2: Hold-Your-Tongue Teahouse
column3: 禁言茶楼

column2: A two-storey teahouse where the Long house steward, Uncle Fu, conducts business. A red notice on the wall: 'In this house no one may say the Qianli is lost. Offenders fined one tael.' The pirate archers guarding it eavesdrop on every table. An out-of-town trader said offhand, 'That ship sank long ago, surely,' and was fined a tael on the spot, then another for asking, 'On whose say-so?'
column3: 一座两层茶楼，是龙家管家福伯议事的地方，墙上贴着一张红纸：「本楼不许说千里号没了，违者罚银一两。」守楼的海寇弓手竖着耳朵听每一桌。一个外地客商随口说了句「那船早沉了吧」，当场罚了一两，又罚一两，因为他问了句「凭什么」。

column2: The archers are driven downstairs. Uncle Fu stays seated with his teapot. It's Master Long's rule, he says, across the whole Long house: for ten years no one has dared say 'lost' before him, and the fines all go to the charity granary. He pours you a cup. 'Master Long says not come back isn't the same as lost.'
column3: 弓手被赶下楼，福伯捧着茶壶没动。他说这是龙爷的规矩，整个龙记都这样，十年没人敢在龙爷跟前说那个「没」字，罚的银子都送去了义仓。福伯给你们倒了杯茶：「龙爷说，没回来，不等于没了。」

column2: Dragon Mother's Stall
column3: 龙母摊

column2: Before dawn a great pot is set up by the docks and a white-haired old woman stews thread-noodle porridge, the smell drifting half a street. But no one dares eat: a ring of pirate swordsmen stands round the pot, sent by the Long house to 'protect the old lady', glaring at anyone who comes near. She is Long Sihai's own mother. Her son won't let her keep a stall; she insists, so they stand guard round a pot nobody dares approach.
column3: 天不亮，码头边就支起一口大锅，一个白发老太太在熬面线糊，香气飘出半条街。可没人敢来吃：锅边站着一圈海寇刀手，是龙家派来「护着老太太」的，谁靠近就瞪谁。老太太是龙四海的亲娘，儿子不许她摆摊，她偏要摆，刀手们只好站成一圈，围出一口没人敢靠近的锅。

column2: The swordsmen are chased off and the dock coolies surge in. Ladling away, old Mother Long says she had two sons. The younger, A'zhou, sailed with the Qianli at seventeen, its youngest hand. 'Sihai tried to stop him and couldn't.' She taps the ladle on the rim. 'He talks about money, but what he wants is people. That berth is kept for A'zhou.'
column3: 刀手们被赶走，码头苦力一拥而上。龙老太一边舀一边说，她有两个儿子，小的叫阿舟，十七岁跟着千里号上了船，是船上最小的水手。「四海拦了，没拦住。」她拿勺子敲敲锅沿：「他嘴上要钱，心里要的是人。那个泊位，是给阿舟留的。」

column2: Model Loft
column3: 船样阁

column2: A little loft is crammed with wooden ships. The largest is as long as a table, masts, sails and rudder well complete, Qianli carved on its hull; a big ship starts as a model that is scaled up. Pirate archers have forced the door to steal it for the Long shipyard. The old keeper blocks the way with a carving knife, his hand shaking, his tongue sharp as ever: 'Touch it and I'll carve a tortoise on your forehead.'
column3: 一座小阁楼里摆满了木头小船，最大的一条有桌子那么长，桅、帆、舵孔一样不缺，船身刻着「千里」。造大船先做船样，照着样子放大。一伙海寇弓手撬了阁门，要把它偷去卖给龙记船厂。老阁主握着雕刀挡在门口，手抖得刀都快掉了，嘴还硬：「谁动它，我在他脑门上刻只王八。」

column2: The archers are run off and the old keeper lifts the model's deck: the belly is divided by bulkheads into thirteen holds. 'If one hold floods, the others still float and the ship can't sink.' That was what gave the Qianli the nerve for the far seas. But the rudder well is empty. 'The rudder model isn't here. The shipmaster took it, said she'd pledge it with someone.'
column3: 弓手被赶走，老阁主揭开船样的甲板：船肚子被一道道木板隔成十三个舱。「一舱破了进水，别的舱照样浮，船就沉不了。」这是千里号敢走远海的底气。可船尾的舵孔是空的。「舵样不在这儿，船主带走了，说要押在一个人手里。」

column2: Stone-Egg Quarry
column3: 石蛋埕

column2: The hillside behind the harbour is strewn with great round boulders, as if something had laid a clutch of giant eggs; the masons call them stone eggs, and Quanzhou's bridges, pagodas and quays are all this granite. Dockside raiders have sealed the quarry, saying the Long house will buy all the stone, so the masons sit idle on the stone eggs eating sweet potatoes. At the yard's edge stands a finished mooring post nobody has hauled away in ten years.
column3: 港后的山坡上滚满了圆溜溜的大石头，像谁在山上下了一窝巨蛋，石匠们叫它「石蛋」，泉州的桥、塔、码头都是这里的花岗石。一队码头劫骑把石场封了，说龙记要独家收石，石匠们没活干，只好坐在石蛋上啃番薯。场边立着一根刻好的系船石柱，十年没人拉走。

column2: The raiders are run off and the quarry reopens: mountain stone for harbour grain, and the chisels ring again. Patting a stone egg, the old mason explains: granite begins as one solid mass and splits into blocks along its cracks; rain seeps in and eats at them year after year, and the corners, attacked from three sides, round off first, until the square block becomes an egg. The mooring post is carved 'Qianli: Berth One'. Master Long ordered it ten years ago: 'On the day the ships come home, haul it to the quay.'
column3: 劫骑被赶跑，石场重开，山上的石料换港口的粮食，石匠们又叮叮当当干起来。老石匠拍着一颗石蛋说：花岗石本是一整块，顺着裂缝裂成方块，雨水渗进缝里一年年地蚀，棱角三面受蚀，最先磨圆，方石头就成了蛋。那根系船柱刻着「千里·一号」，是龙爷十年前订的：「等船回来那天，再拉去码头。」

column2: Letter-Writer's Stall
column3: 代笔摊

column2: On a street corner a failed scholar keeps a stall writing letters home for those who can't. Dockside raiders have overturned his table and are ransacking his chest on Uncle Fu's orders, they say: certain drafts in it 'mustn't be kept'. The scholar shields the chest, gets swatted in the face by a horse's tail, and keeps muttering, 'The letters are theirs. The drafts are mine.'
column3: 街角一个代人写信的摊子，摊主是个落第秀才，替不识字的人写家书。一队码头劫骑掀了他的桌子，在他箱子里乱翻，说是福伯交代的：箱里有些信的底稿「不能留」。秀才护着箱子，被马尾巴扫了一脸，还在念叨：「信是人家的，底稿是我的。」

column2: Once the raiders have gone, the scholar takes from the bottom of the chest ten drafts, one a year, all addressed to 'A'zhou'. Every August Long Sihai dictates one, the scholar writes it, and Master Long burns it at the quay. The first scolds the boy for not listening. The fifth asks if he's eating enough. The tenth is one line: 'The berth is still kept. Don't moor at the wrong one.'
column3: 劫骑走了，秀才从箱底取出一摞底稿，十封，一年一封，收信人都是「阿舟」。是龙四海每年八月口述、他代笔，写完龙爷拿去码头烧了。头一封骂他不听话，第五封问他吃得饱不饱，第十封只有一句：「泊位还留着，回来别靠错了。」

column2: Wreck Beach
column3: 沉船滩

column2: An old Fujian junk lies half buried in the sand, its planks long rotted, only the great keel left like a whale's spine. Pirate swordsmen have been prising out its nails and bronze fittings for three days. A'qiang takes one look and panics. 'That's the first ship my master built when he was young! There's a long-life hole in the keel!'
column3: 沙滩上半埋着一条老福船，船板早烂了，只剩一根粗大的龙骨，像鲸鱼的脊梁。一伙海寇刀手在上面拆铁钉、撬铜件，叮叮当当砸了三天。阿樯一看就急了：「那是我师父年轻时造的头一条船！龙骨里有保寿孔！」

column2: The swordsmen are driven off and A'qiang lies on the keel at the scarf joint, picking out a small hole's contents: a few copper coins and a palm-sized bronze mirror, green with corrosion. By shipwrights' custom a long-life hole is cut at the keel joint and coins and a mirror put in so the ship lives long. She pockets one coin. 'Master's new ship gets this one.'
column3: 刀手被赶走，阿樯趴在龙骨接口处，抠出小孔里的东西：几枚铜钱、一面巴掌大的铜镜，绿锈斑斑。造船的规矩，龙骨接口凿个「保寿孔」，放进铜钱和镜子，保船长寿。她揣起一枚铜钱：「师父的新船，就用这一枚。」

column2: Long House Counting Room
column3: 龙记账房

column2: A large building on the street holds twenty ledger desks and twenty clerks: the Long house's main counting room. In the middle hangs a great board bearing a single sum, and every day someone climbs a ladder to change a figure: 'Berth One, unpaid berth fees, principal and interest: 298,400 taels.' Dockside raiders guard the door; you may look, but not ask.
column3: 临街一座大屋，二十张账桌，二十个账先生埋头写字，是龙记的总账房。正中一块大木牌，写着一个数，每天都有人上梯子去改一笔：「一号泊欠泊费，本利合计二十九万八千四百两。」一队码头劫骑守着门，进来的人只许看，不许问。

column2: The raiders are thrown out and the chief clerk has to answer. The board has risen every day for ten years: whoever wants Berth One pays this sum. He turns the master ledger to its last page. Under the figure, in Master Long's own hand: 'Or: one piece of news.' Anyone who can't pay may bring news instead.
column3: 劫骑被赶出去，总账先生只好回话：这块牌子十年来天天涨，谁想要一号泊，就得交这个数。他把底账翻到最后一页，数目底下，龙爷亲笔添了一行小字：「或，一个消息。」交不起钱的，带个消息来也行。

column2: Sampan Ferry
column3: 舢板渡

column2: An old ferryman at the harbour's edge sculls a sampan out to the big ships at anchor. Dockside raiders have impounded it at its post: Master Long's orders, no more ferrying anyone to Berth One. The old man sits in the bow smoking his pipe. Ten years ago, he says, it was from this very post that he ferried a man out to chase the Qianli.
column3: 港边一个摆舢板的老艄公，专渡人去停在港里的大船。他的舢板被一队码头劫骑扣在桩上，说龙爷吩咐过，不许再渡人去一号泊。老艄公坐在船头抽旱烟，说十年前，他就是从这根桩子上，渡过一个人去追千里号。

column2: The raiders are driven off and the sampan untied. That night, the ferryman says, he carried the young Long heir, who cursed and rowed all the way and caught the Qianli's last ship. His brother A'zhou stood at the rail and wouldn't come down. 'Brother, keep the berth for me! When I come back I'm mooring at Berth One!' The heir stood in the sampan a long time, and after that never again spoke of getting his brother off.
column3: 劫骑被赶跑，舢板解了缆。老艄公说，那夜渡的是龙家少东家，一路骂一路划，追上了千里号最后一条船。弟弟阿舟站在船舷上不肯下来，冲他喊：「哥，泊位给我留着！我回来要靠一号泊！」少东家在舢板上站了很久，回来以后，再没提过让弟弟下船。

column2: Wrong-Tunnel Camp
column3: 错洞寨

column2: On waste ground outside the Gong shipyard stands a small camp of thirty-odd pirate archers. Their chief wanted the yard's good timber and had them dig a tunnel for half a month to come up under the fence. They dug the wrong way, into a stretch of mud, and kept hauling out big black logs, more and more, with less and less idea where they were.
column3: 龚家船坞外的荒地上扎着个小寨子，三十来个海寇弓手。头领想偷船坞里的好木料，带人挖了半个月地道，要从篱笆底下钻进去。他们方向挖反了，挖进一片烂泥地，挖出一根又一根黑乎乎的大木头，越挖越多，越挖越不知道自己在哪儿。

column2: The archers are run off, leaving the tunnel mouth piled with logs. A'qiang leaps in the air: it's old camphor buried in the mud by her master's master's generation. With no air down there it neither rotted nor split in decades, and in time everyone forgot where it lay. 'The fools dug for us for half a month!' She's doubled over laughing. 'That's the ship's last ribs sorted!'
column3: 弓手们被赶跑，地道口堆满了挖出来的木头。阿樯一看跳了起来：这是师父的师父那辈埋在泥里的老樟木，泥里不透气，几十年不腐不裂，后来谁也记不得埋在哪儿了。「蠢贼替我们挖了半个月！」她笑得直不起腰，「船上最后几根肋骨有着落了！」

column2: Saw Pit
column3: 锯木坑

column2: A deep pit with a log laid across it: one man should stand on top and one below, pulling a long saw to cut planks. Pirate swordsmen say the planks are forfeit to the Long house and are carrying them off. The old man in the pit ignores them, working a two-man saw alone, an ink-line reel at his waist, sawdust all over his head and face. He is Gong Modou.
column3: 地上挖着一个深坑，坑上架着一根原木，本该一人在上一人在下，拉一把长锯把它锯成船板。一伙海寇刀手说船板都要抵给龙记，正一块块往外扛。坑底的老人不管不顾，一个人拉着两个人的锯，腰上挂着一只墨斗，满头满脸都是木屑。他就是龚墨斗。

column2: The swordsmen are driven off and only then does Gong Modou climb out and brush off the sawdust. For ten years, he says, he's bought all his timber from the Long house on credit, until the ship was pledged to them before it touched water. 'Long Sihai says the ship is pledged to him. I say pledge or no, I'll keep building.' He looks over A'qiang's ironwood and nods. 'This will make a rudder post. But the rudder?'
column3: 刀手被赶走，龚墨斗才爬上来拍掉木屑。他说十年来造船的木料都是赊龙记的，赊到后来，船还没下水就先押给了龙记。「龙四海说船是押给他的。我说押归押，船我照样造。」他看了看阿樯带回的铁力木，点点头：「这根能做舵杆。可舵呢？」

column2: Berth One
column3: 一号泊

column2: The finest berth in Quanzhou: stone steps worn to a shine, new hemp rope round the mooring post, an unlit lamp at the water's edge. It's empty, and no ship has tied up here in ten years. A few pirate swordsmen sweep it daily, wipe the post and change the rope, more diligent than at their own doors, and wave off any ship that tries to come alongside. Today another out-of-town skipper is arguing with them.
column3: 泉州港最好的泊位，石阶磨得发亮，系船柱上缠着新麻绳，水边一盏没点的灯。泊位空着，十年没靠过一条船。几个海寇刀手每天在这里扫地、擦柱、换绳，比扫自家门口还勤快，见有船想靠就举刀撵走。今天又有一条外地船想靠，船老大正跟刀手吵。

column2: The swordsmen are pushed aside and the skipper poles away, grumbling. Under the lamp lies a small wooden tag rubbed smooth, carved A'zhou. On the steps at the far end sits a figure with his back to you. He doesn't turn, only lifts a hand to send the swordsmen away. This is the Dragon King. What he's waiting for, you can probably guess by now.
column3: 刀手被赶开，外地船骂骂咧咧撑走了。灯底下压着一块被摸得光滑的小木牌，写着「阿舟」。泊位尽头的石阶上坐着一个背影，没有回头，只抬了抬手，让刀手们退下。这就是海龙王。他在等什么，你们心里大概已经有数了。

column2: Long Mansion Back Gate
column3: 龙宅后门

column2: The Long mansion's back gate opens onto a narrow alley, and on the first of every month someone knocks: an old shipwright with an ink-line reel at his waist and a short-braided apprentice. Three knocks and a shout: 'Long Sihai, the ship's nearly done, give it back!' The pirate archers on the gate answer with shoving, and this month they shove hard; the old man falls on the steps.
column3: 龙家大宅的后门开在一条窄巷里，每月初一都有人来敲门：一个腰挂墨斗的老船匠，带着扎短辫的徒弟，敲三下，喊一句「龙四海，船要造好了，把船还我」。守门的海寇弓手开门就是一顿推搡，这个月推得特别狠，老船匠摔在了台阶上。

column2: The archers are run off and the old porter helps Gong Modou up with a sigh. 'Every time Master Long hears you knock he says the same thing: the ship is pledged to me, and so is the rudder model.' He pauses. 'But he's never once had the ship hauled away. He says when it's done, the man who built it can come and ask himself.'
column3: 弓手被赶跑，看门的老门房扶起龚墨斗，叹气说：「龙爷每回听你敲门，只说一句：船是押给我的，舵样也是押给我的。」他顿了顿，「可他从没让人把船拉走过。他说等船造好了，让造船的人自己来要。」

column2: Test-Float Cove
column3: 试水湾

column2: In a sheltered cove floats a length of hull with no mast or sail: a finished section of Gong Modou's ship's belly, towed here for a float test. Pirate archers on the shore use it as a target, betting who'll sink it first. All morning they've shot; the planks bristle with arrows and three holds spurt water, yet it still floats. The archers stamp in frustration.
column3: 避风的小海湾里浮着一段船身，没有桅也没有帆，是龚墨斗造好的一截船肚子，拖到这里试水。一伙海寇弓手在岸上拿它当靶子，一箭一箭地射，赌谁先把它射沉。射了一上午，船板扎满了箭，三个舱都在往外冒水，那截船身还漂着，弓手们急得直跺脚。

column2: The archers are chased off and Gong Modou rows over to check every hold, beaming so his beard sticks up. 'Three holds holed and the rest still hold her up. That's how the Qianli was built, and so is mine.' He pulls an arrow and scratches a mark on a plank. 'Patch this one before launch.'
column3: 弓手被赶跑，龚墨斗划过去挨个舱查了一遍，笑得胡子直翘：「破了三个舱，剩下的照样托得住。千里号当年就是这么造的，我这条也一样。」他拔下一支箭，在船板上划了个记号：「这一舱，下水前再补。」

column2: Lantern Porters
column3: 灯笼担

column2: Along the road to Berth One comes a line of porters with Qian lanterns hung from both ends of their poles: neighbours from Thousand-Lantern Lane, Granny Chen at the front. Pirate swordsmen block the junction: that character isn't allowed on Master Long's ground, and the lanterns are going into the sea. Granny Chen thumps her pole down. 'These are a delivery for Berth One. Go and ask Long Sihai if he dares accept them.'
column3: 去一号泊的路上走来一队挑担的人，扁担两头挂满「千」字灯笼，都是千灯巷的街坊，陈婆走在最前头。一伙海寇刀手拦在路口，说龙爷的地界不许挂这个字，要把灯笼一担担扔进海里。陈婆把扁担往地上一顿：「我这是给一号泊送的灯，你们问问龙四海，他敢不敢收。」

column2: The swordsmen are scattered. One runs to report and returns with a strange look. 'Master Long says... let the lanterns in.' Load after load is carried to the edge of Berth One and laid out in a long row. The figure at the far end stirs, as if counting them. Not one is missing.
column3: 刀手被打散，一个跑去报信，回来时脸色古怪：「龙爷说，灯笼……放进来。」灯笼一担担挑到一号泊外，摆了长长一溜。泊位尽头那个背影动了一下，像是数了一遍。一盏也没少。

column2: Long Shipyard
column3: 龙记船厂

column2: A great shipyard spreads along the shore, a dozen slipways holding Long house ships, hammering, sawing and work chants rolling together. Half its craftsmen were poached from the Gong yard; the pay is good and the work maddening. The foreman insists on building to stolen plans of the Qianli: three ships so far, and all three crab sideways once launched. The guards, swordsmen, archers and riders, outnumber the craftsmen.
column3: 海边一片大船厂，十几座船台上架着龙记的新船，锤声、锯声、号子声连成一片。厂里的工匠一半是从龚家船坞挖来的，工钱高，活干得憋屈：工头拿着偷来的千里号图样非要照着造，造了三条，下水全都歪着走。守厂的刀手、弓手、劫骑一大群，比工匠还多。

column2: The guards scatter and the craftsmen down tools; half follow A'qiang back to the Gong yard. The Long foreman squats under a slipway tearing at his scalp. 'Not one line of those plans is wrong. Why won't they sail straight?' Gong Modou glances over. 'You're missing the rudder. It's not on the model and not on the plans. The Qianli's rudder was made separately.'
column3: 打手们被打散，工匠们扔下家伙，一半跟着阿樯回了龚家船坞。龙记工头蹲在船台下抓头皮：「图样一根线都没画错，怎么就是不走直？」龚墨斗瞥了一眼：「你缺了舵。船样上没有，图上也没有。千里号的舵，是另造的。」

column2: Long Mansion Forecourt
column3: 龙宅外院

column2: The Long mansion's forecourt is paved with bluestone, a great tank in the middle holding nothing but one old sea turtle, a wobbly Zhou scratched into its shell. Pirate swordsmen are drilling in the yard, their war cries so loud the turtle has pulled in its head. Word has come that the pioneer party is on its way, and their orders are: hurt no one, but don't let anyone in easily.
column3: 龙家大宅的外院铺着青石板，院中一口大鱼缸，只养着一只老海龟，龟壳上刻着歪歪扭扭一个「舟」字。一伙海寇刀手正在院里操练，喊杀声震得海龟把头缩进了壳里。听说开拓队要来，他们得了令：不许伤人，可也不许让人轻易进来。

column2: The swordsmen are driven into the inner court and Uncle Fu comes out to settle things. The turtle, he says, was picked up off the beach by the second young master, A'zhou, as a boy, and the character is his work. 'Eight days to the eighteenth of the eighth month. In ten years Master Long hasn't slept that night. His orders: whoever comes before then bringing something, he'll see at Berth One.'
column3: 刀手被赶进了内院，福伯出来收拾场面。他说这海龟是二少爷阿舟小时候从海滩捡回来的，壳上的字是他刻的。「离八月十八还有八天，龙爷十年没在那一夜睡过觉。他吩咐了：那一夜之前，谁带着东西来，他在一号泊见。」

column2: Tide-Watching Pavilion
column3: 观潮亭

column2: On the highest headland above the harbour stands a pavilion facing the bar at the river mouth: a reclining chair, a copper kettle beside it, spout toward the sea. Dockside raiders guard the foot and let no one up. From up here the row of red-flagged poles on the spit's tip is plain to see, fluttering in the wind. A few raiders, blades in hand, are arguing over who should go and pull them up.
column3: 港口最高的崖头上有座亭子，正对着河口沙坝。亭里一张躺椅，椅边一只铜壶，壶嘴冲着海。一队码头劫骑守在亭下，不许人上去。从亭里往下看，沙嘴尖上那排红布竹篙清清楚楚，在风里一抖一抖。几个劫骑提着刀，正为谁去拔那些篙吵架。

column2: The raiders are driven down and their chief finally comes clean: Master Long has ordered that no one touches those poles; pull one and lose a hand. 'He sits here every day watching the girl plant them, counting one by one. We wanted them gone because we thought it hurt him to watch.' On the armrest lies a sketch of the new channel's curve, not very accurate.
column3: 劫骑被赶下去，头目才说实话：龙爷下过令，红篙谁也不许拔，拔一根打断一只手。「龙爷天天坐在这亭里看那丫头插篙，一根一根数。我们想拔，是怕他看着难受。」躺椅扶手上压着一张纸，画着新水道的弯，画得不太准。

column2: Shipwrights' Shrine
column3: 船匠祠

column2: A shrine to Lu Ban, patron of craftsmen, and home of the Quanzhou shipwrights' guild, where incense is lit at every season's start and every launch. Pirate swordsmen have made it a gambling den, using Lu Ban's altar as a table and snapping ink lines to mark the betting board. The guild's old foremen stand outside, seething; one has bitten clean through his pipe stem.
column3: 一座供着鲁班的祠堂，是泉州船匠的行会，每年开工、下水都在这里上香。一伙海寇刀手占了祠堂开赌，拿鲁班爷的供桌当赌桌，拿墨斗线弹赌局的界线。行会的老把头们站在门外敢怒不敢言，有一个气得把烟杆都咬断了。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown out, the altar wiped, the incense relit. Hearing that Gong Modou's ship needs only a few more days' work, the foremen confer for the length of a pipe and decide: the guild will send forty carpenters to finish it within eight days. 'Ten years ago the Qianli's launch incense was lit in this shrine,' says one. 'This time it will be too.'
column3: 刀手被赶出去，供桌擦净，香又点上了。老把头们听说龚墨斗的船只差最后几天的活，商量了一袋烟的工夫，拍板：行会出四十个木匠，八天里帮他收尾。「十年前千里号下水，是这间祠里上的香，」把头说，「这一回，也得是。」

column2: The Gong Cottage
column3: 龚家小院

column2: Beside the shipyard is a small cottage, much-mended clothes drying in its yard. Auntie Gong stands at the gate with a rolling pin facing a troop of dockside raiders: Gong Modou owes the Long house for timber and they'll take the house. She levels the pin. 'The house was my dowry, and the dowry went on timber long ago. If you want what's left of these shabby rooms, get past me first.'
column3: 船坞边一座小院，院里晾着补了又补的衣裳。龚婶握着擀面杖站在院门口，对面一队码头劫骑，说龚墨斗欠龙记木料钱，要拿房子抵。龚婶把擀面杖一横：「房子是我的嫁妆，嫁妆早卖了买木头。剩下这几间破屋，要拿，先过我这一关。」

column2: The raiders are driven off and Auntie Gong presses a bowl of hot noodle soup on you. Ten years she's railed at the old man, 'wastrel, mule, fonder of wood than of his wife', yet every noon she carries his meal to the yard. He builds this ship, she says, because Shipmaster Shen once looked at his work and said: 'You build good ships, but not good enough. Build one that can catch me.' 'All his life he's never been able to stand being told that.'
column3: 劫骑被赶跑，龚婶塞给你们一碗热汤面。她骂了老头子十年，「败家，倔，木头比老婆亲」，可每天中午照样把饭送到船坞。她说他造这条船，是因为沈船主看过他的船，说了一句：「你造的是好船，可还不够好。造一条能追上我的。」「他这辈子，最受不了这句。」

column2: Rat Drain
column3: 鼠沟

column2: Under the shipyard runs a great drain to the sea, home of the Rat Gang: petty thieves who live and steal underground alongside real rats. Every night the yard is short some copper nails, a length of rope, a dab of tung oil. The swordsmen, archers and riders guarding the drain mouth are all gang, the riders on donkeys that outrun horses down there. The rats outnumber the people and can gnaw through a cable in a night.
column3: 船坞底下有一条通海的大阴沟，住着一帮「老鼠帮」：在地下讨生活的小贼，跟真老鼠一起住，一起偷。船坞里的铜钉、麻绳、桐油，夜里总要少一截。守沟口的刀手、弓手、劫骑都是帮里的，劫骑骑的是驴，在沟里跑得比马快。沟里的老鼠比人还多，啃起缆绳来，一夜就是一根。

column2: This time the Rat Gang is flushed out and two baskets of nails fished back. But the drains run everywhere: block one end and there's another. The rats breed litter after litter, and there are always hungry children who'll crawl down there. Before long the gang will be back, and the yard folk will have to clear it out again every so often.
column3: 这一回老鼠帮被赶出了阴沟，偷去的铜钉捞回两筐。可阴沟四通八达，堵了这头还有那头；老鼠一窝窝地生，城里没饭吃的孩子也总有人往沟里钻。过一阵老鼠帮还会回来，船坞的人只好隔些日子就来清一回。

column2: Soaking-Timber Isle
column3: 泡木洲

column2: On a small island outside the harbour, great logs lie soaking in the shallows under stones: Gong Modou soaks his timber in seawater for years so the sap leaches out, and afterwards it neither splits nor gets worm. Pirate swordsmen have taken the island, found the logs a nuisance, and are splitting them for firewood, the best fir first.
column3: 港外一座小岛，岛边浅水里泡着一根根大木头，用石头压着：龚墨斗把买来的木料泡在海水里，泡上几年，浆水泡掉了，日后不裂不蛀。一伙海寇刀手占了岛，嫌木头碍事，捞上来劈了当柴烧，烧的偏是最好的几根杉木。

column2: The swordsmen are driven off and the remaining logs weighed back down; not many were burned. The old timber-keeper has watched this water ten years and can tell by touch, eyes shut, which year each log went in. He pats a fir trunk. 'These have soaked long enough. Haul them out now and they'll be just in time for the launch.'
column3: 刀手被赶下岛，剩下的木头又压回了水里，烧掉的不多。岛上的老看木人守这片水十年，每根木头哪年下的水，闭着眼都摸得出来。他拍着一根杉木：「这几根泡够了，捞上去，正好赶上船下水。」

column2: On the island you seize the swordsmen's stores: two boatloads of firewood, three vats of fresh water, a brood of new ducklings, and a cask of rice wine they'd bartered ship nails for.
column3: 岛上抄出刀手们囤的两船柴火、三缸淡水、一窝刚孵出来的鸭子，还有一桶拿船钉换来的米酒。

column2: Every time you pass, the old timber-keeper poles out with a basket of clams dug at the island's edge and a few dried offcuts. 'For your fires on the road. Burns better than kindling.'
column3: 每次路过，老看木人都撑船送来一筐岛边摸的花蛤，再捎几块晒干的边角木料，「路上烧火，比柴好烧」。

column2: Dock Guild Hall
column3: 码头公所

column2: The dock guild hall is in uproar, every shipping house in Quanzhou there, a copy of the Office's continued-voyage notice on the table. Some want to stand surety beside Superintendent Ke; some fear crossing the Long house; it ends in fists on tables. At the door stand pirate swordsmen sent by the Long house to 'observe', thumping their scabbards whenever anyone speaks too loudly.
column3: 码头公所里吵成了一锅粥，泉州各家船行的东家都来了，桌上摊着市舶司续航榜文的抄本。有人要跟着柯提举作保，有人怕得罪龙记，吵到最后拍了桌子。门口站着一伙龙记派来「旁听」的海寇刀手，谁嗓门大，刀手就把刀鞘往地上一顿。

column2: The swordsmen are shown out and the room goes quiet. Superintendent Ke arrives with barge No. 7's papers: porcelain counted, certificate stamped with the great seal, tally recovered, Master Zhuang's thumbprint pressed. One by one the shipowners add their names. 'One thumbprint missing,' says Ke, putting the surety away. 'The Long house's. He's waiting at Berth One.'
column3: 刀手被请了出去，屋里一下子静了。柯提举带着七号驳的文书赶来：瓷点清了，公凭盖了大印，舶牌找回了，庄窑主也按了手印。船东们一个个在后头添上名字。「就差一个手印，」柯提举收好保状，「龙家的。他在一号泊等着。」

column2: Tiller Pools
column3: 玩舵潭

column2: Among the shore rocks lie pools left by the ebb, where an old helmsman missing two fingers teaches a crowd of children to sail little wooden boats and work a tiller. Pirate swordsmen, sick of the noise, stamp the boats to pieces one by one. The old man shields the last against his chest. Its rudder slides up and down; he carved it himself.
column3: 海边礁石间有几汪退潮留下的水潭，一个缺了两根手指的老舵工带着一群孩子在潭里放木头小船，教他们怎么扳舵。一伙海寇刀手嫌孩子吵，把小船一条条踩碎。老舵工把最后一条护在怀里，那条船的舵能上下抽动，是他亲手刻的。

column2: The swordsmen are chased off and the children crowd back. He was too old to sail with the Qianli, the helmsman says, but he and Shipmaster Shen worked out its rudder together: a lifting rudder, raised over shoals and lowered in deep water. 'Crossing the bar depends on it.' There was one rudder model, and before she left Shen pledged it to the Long house. 'She said whoever comes to continue the voyage, the Long house hands it to them.'
column3: 刀手被赶走，孩子们又围了上来。老舵工说他年纪大没跟上千里号，可千里号的舵是他和沈船主一起琢磨的：升降舵，遇上浅滩提起来，到了深水再放下，「过沙坝全靠它」。舵样只有一个，沈船主走前押在龙家：「她说谁来续航，龙家就把舵交给谁。」

column2: Yard Approach Road
column3: 坞前路

column2: Only one dirt road leads to the Gong yard. The guild's forty carpenters hurry along it with tools and barrows of timber, but dockside raiders block the road, horses' heads in a line: the ship is pledged to the Long house, and not one more nail or plank goes into that yard. The carpenters shoulder their axes and glare back at the horses. Nobody gives way.
column3: 去龚家船坞只有一条土路，行会的四十个木匠扛着工具、推着木料往坞里赶，一队码头劫骑横在路上，马头一字排开，说船是押给龙记的，坞里不许再添一钉一木。木匠们把斧头扛在肩上跟马对瞪，谁也不让谁。

column2: The raiders are scattered and the forty carpenters pour into the yard chanting, hammers going all night. Leaving, the raiders' leader mutters, 'Master Long only said nobody hauls the ship away. He never said nobody builds it... We overdid it.'
column3: 劫骑被冲散，四十个木匠喊着号子涌进船坞，锤子一响就是一夜。领头的劫骑临走嘟囔了一句：「龙爷只说不许把船拉走，没说不许造……是我们多事了。」

column2: Eye-Dotting Platform
column3: 点睛台

column2: On a high platform outside the yard stands an incense table, where a new ship's eyes are dotted before launch: Quanzhou ships carry a pair of dragon eyes on the bow, and on launch day the pupils are dotted in so the ship can see its way. A'qiang has painted the eyes, the sockets still blank. Pirate archers have taken the platform demanding 'consecration money', or they'll shoot the eyes blind.
column3: 坞外的高台上摆着香案，是给新船下水「点睛」的地方：泉州的船头两边要画一对龙目，下水那天点上眼珠，船才认得路。阿樯已经把龙目画好了，眼眶里空着。一伙海寇弓手占了高台，说点睛得交「开光钱」，不交就拿箭把龙目射瞎。

column2: The archers are driven off and the table set upright. Gong Modou lifts a brush dipped in cinnabar but doesn't put it to the eyes. By the trade's custom, he says, the ship's owner does the dotting. 'The ship is pledged to the Long house, the berth is theirs, the rudder model is with them. This stroke has to be Long Sihai's.'
column3: 弓手被赶跑，香案扶了起来。龚墨斗提着蘸了朱砂的笔，却没有点下去。他说行里的规矩，点睛要请船的主家来点：「船押在龙家，泊位是龙家的，舵样也在龙家。这一笔，得请龙四海来点。」

column2: Old Anchor Chandlery
column3: 老锚记

column2: Beside Berth One stands a chandlery, its walls hung with anchors, cables, chains, compasses and storm lanterns, but the sign at the door reads 'Nothing for sale.' Ten years ago the Long house bought the lame old chandler's whole stock for the ships of Berth One, to be sold to no one else. Pirate archers sit in the shop and chase off every buyer.
column3: 一号泊旁边有一家船具店，锚、缆、铁链、罗盘、风灯挂了满墙，门口却挂着一块牌子：「本店不卖。」店主是个瘸腿的老船具商，十年前龙家把店里的东西全包了，说是给一号泊的船预备的，不许卖给别人。一伙海寇弓手坐在店里看着，来一个买主轰一个。

column2: The archers are turned out and the old chandler flips the sign: the back reads 'Open'. Impressed, he's willing to trade. 'Master Long kept me bottled up ten years, and I've been bored stiff.' As you go he hands you a coil of new rope. 'Laid by for Berth One. When you see him, say I lent it to you. He won't refuse to recognise it.'
column3: 弓手被赶出店门，老船具商把牌子翻过来，背面写着「开张」。他佩服你们，愿意换货：「龙爷包了十年，我也闷了十年。」临走他摘下一盘新缆递过来：「这是给一号泊备的。你们去见他，就说是我借你们的，他不会不认。」

column2: Fish-Market Isle
column3: 鱼市岛

column2: On a small island outside the harbour a fish market opens every dawn as the boats come in: grouper, yellow croaker, swimming crabs, all still flapping. For a month pirate archers have held it, claiming the island's ice house; without ice the fish stink, so the mongers must sell cheap to them. The fishwives have voices like foghorns and have cursed for a month, till the archers' ears are calloused.
column3: 港外的小岛上天天清早开鱼市，渔船一靠岸就卖，石斑、黄鱼、梭子蟹，活蹦乱跳。这一个月，鱼市被一伙海寇弓手占了，说岛上的冰窖归他们，没冰鱼就臭，鱼贩们只好贱卖给弓手。卖鱼的阿婆们个个嗓门大，骂了一个月，骂得弓手们耳朵都起了茧。

column2: The archers are driven off, the ice house opened, and the market bustles again. The fishwives, impressed, trade you their best fish, and say the fish market will feed the Gong yard's forty carpenters all eight days. One old woman says, 'If that ship goes looking for the Qianli, take my husband a message: keep the wages. Just come home.'
column3: 弓手被赶下岛，冰窖打开，鱼市又热闹起来。阿婆们佩服你们，拿最好的鱼跟你们换货，还说龚家船坞那四十个木匠八天的饭，鱼市包了。一个阿婆说：「那条船要是去找千里号，替我捎句话给我男人：工钱不要了，人回来就行。」

column2: Yard-Mouth Tea Shed
column3: 坞口茶寮

column2: At the yard mouth is a tea shed where a middle-aged man in a silk gown sits all day drinking tea and watching the new ship. He's the Long house's 'ship-watcher', a troop of dockside raiders at his side. Today forty carpenters have gone in and he can't sit still; he has the raiders block the mouth and paces the shed, his tea gone cold.
column3: 船坞口有间茶寮，一个穿绸衫的中年人天天坐在这里喝茶，盯着坞里的新船，一坐一整天。他是龙记派来的「看船人」，身边跟着一队码头劫骑。今天四十个木匠进了坞，他坐不住了，叫劫骑把坞口堵上，自己在茶寮里来回踱步，茶凉了也没喝一口。

column2: The raiders scatter and the ship-watcher has to sit and tell all. Every month he reports how far the ship has come; in ten years, from one part in ten to ninety-nine in a hundred. Every time Master Long asks only, 'And the rudder?' and he answers, 'The rudder model is in your hands, sir.' Today his report will be: 'The ship is complete, save the rudder and one dot of the eyes.'
column3: 劫骑被打散，看船人只好坐下交代：他每月给龙爷报一回船造到几成，十年里从一成报到九成九。龙爷每回只问一句：「舵呢？」他就答：「舵样在您手里。」今天他回去要报的是：「船齐了，只差舵和一笔点睛。」

column2: Long Guard Camp
column3: 龙家亲兵营

column2: On the last stretch of road to Berth One stands the Long house guard camp, dragon banners either side of the gate. Its swordsmen, archers and riders have followed Long Sihai for ten years, every one scarred. Their captain stands at the gate, blade folded in his arms, and gives Master Long's word: 'Whoever comes bringing something gets past the guard camp first. If you can't even manage that, don't go and embarrass yourselves at Berth One.'
column3: 去一号泊的最后一段路上扎着龙家的亲兵营，营门两边插着龙旗。营里的刀手、弓手、劫骑都是跟了龙四海十年的老人，个个身上有疤。头领抱着刀站在营门口，传龙爷的话：「谁带着东西来，先过亲兵营。连亲兵营都过不去，就别去一号泊丢人了。」

column2: The guards are beaten. Their captain sheathes his blade, steps aside and salutes you with clasped hands. 'Master Long said: whoever gets past the guard camp can take a ship out.' He points toward Berth One. 'Until the eighteenth, he'll be sitting there. Bring what you've come to bring.'
column3: 亲兵们败了，头领收刀让路，还冲你们拱了拱手：「龙爷说过，过得了亲兵营的，就是能把船带出去的人。」他朝一号泊一指：「八月十八之前，他都坐在那儿。带上你们该带的东西。」

column2: Dockhands' Canteen
column3: 船工饭堂

column2: Behind Berth One stands a great canteen where coolies, boatmen and carpenters eat at one long table for a hundred. Pirate swordsmen have taken it, saying Master Long is receiving guests and no idlers may gather, and turned the big pots upside down. Mealtime has come, and outside squats a ring of hungry people: a fisher girl, a man in an official robe, an old woman on a stick, all here for Berth One.
column3: 一号泊后面有座大饭堂，码头的苦力、船工、木匠都在这里吃饭，一张长桌能坐一百人。一伙海寇刀手占了饭堂，说龙爷要见客，码头上的闲人一律不许聚，把大锅都扣了过来。饭点到了，饭堂外蹲着一圈饿肚子的人：有渔家姑娘，有穿官袍的，有拄拐的老太太，都是来一号泊的。

column2: The swordsmen are thrown out, the pots set right, and the canteen fills. A'xi with her tide book, Superintendent Ke with his surety, Granny Chen guarding three hundred lanterns, Gong Modou and A'qiang still dusted with sawdust: for the first time they sit at one table. Old Mother Long brings a pot of thread-noodle porridge. 'Eat your fill, then go and see that mule-headed son of mine.'
column3: 刀手被赶走，大锅翻过来，饭堂里坐满了人。阿汐抱着潮信簿，柯提举揣着保状，陈婆守着三百盏灯，龚墨斗和阿樯身上还沾着木屑，头一回坐到了一张桌上。龙老太端来一锅面线糊：「吃饱了，再去见我那个犟儿子。」

column2: In the canteen you find what the swordsmen hid: thirty catties of salt pork, five sacks of rice, a basket of duck eggs, and a stack of Long house meal tickets stamped 'Berth One only' on the back, not one used in ten years.
column3: 饭堂里抄出刀手们藏的三十斤咸肉、五袋白米、一筐鸭蛋，还有一摞龙记饭票，背面盖着「一号泊专用」，十年里一张也没用过。

column2: Every time you pass, the head cook gives you an extra ladleful, 'Berth One's people eat their fill', and slips you a packet of fried sesame balls hot from the pan.
column3: 每次路过，饭堂的大师傅都给你们多盛一勺，说「一号泊的人，饭管够」，临走还塞一包刚出锅的炸枣。

column2: Mast Headland
column3: 桅杆岬

column2: A rocky headland juts into the sea, and on its tip lies a fir trunk a hundred feet long, chained to the rocks: the mainmast Gong Modou bought ten years ago, soaked and seasoned, then impounded here by the Long house against his debts. The Long house's fiercest bruisers guard it: swordsmen at the chains, archers on the heights, raiders patrolling the neck of the headland. When the sea wind blows, the timber hums.
column3: 海边一道伸进海里的石岬，岬头横躺着一根十来丈长的大杉木，用铁链锁在礁石上。这是龚墨斗十年前买下的主桅，泡好了，晾干了，却被龙记当成欠债扣在这里。守岬的是龙记最凶的打手：刀手守链，弓手占着高处，劫骑在岬颈上来回巡。海风一吹，桅木呜呜地响。

column2: The bruisers are driven off and the chains smashed. Chanting, the forty carpenters shoulder the mast and carry it step by step to the yard while people come out along the road to watch. Gong Modou runs a hand along it, smiling. 'Long Sihai impounded it and looked after it for me for ten years. Not a crack.'
column3: 打手被赶下岬，铁链砸开。四十个木匠喊着号子把主桅扛上肩，一步步抬回船坞，路边的人都出来看。龚墨斗摸着桅木笑：「龙四海扣着它，倒替我看了十年，一点没裂。」

column2: Yard Workers' Sheds
column3: 坞工棚

column2: A row of work sheds by the yard is too few for forty carpenters, and pirate archers are occupying the two biggest, lounging on the carpenters' bedrolls in the sun: Long house sheds, they say, and outside carpenters can sleep in the open. After a day's work the carpenters bed down under the hull clutching their axes, bitten all over by mosquitoes.
column3: 船坞边一排工棚，来了四十个木匠，根本住不下。一伙海寇弓手偏占着最大的两间，躺在木匠的铺盖上晒太阳，说这是龙记的工棚，外来的木匠只能睡露天。木匠们干了一天活，夜里抱着斧头在船底下打地铺，被蚊子咬得满身是包。

column2: The archers are turned out and the carpenters finally have beds. Granny Chen sends Thousand-Lantern Lane's children with dozens of lanterns to hang from the eaves and light the yard, and the carpenters work on through the night. On the new ship's bow A'qiang paints three characters in red lacquer: Later Qianli.
column3: 弓手被赶出工棚，木匠们总算睡上了铺。陈婆派千灯巷的孩子送来几十盏灯笼，挂在棚檐下照着船坞，木匠们连夜干活。新船的船头上，阿樯用红漆写了三个字：后千里。

column2: In the sheds you seize the archers' stores: twenty quilts, a chest of iron nails, two jars of aged wine, and a great wok stolen from the yard, Gong carved on its base.
column3: 工棚里抄出弓手们囤的二十条棉被、一箱铁钉、两坛老酒，还有一口从船坞偷来的大铁锅，锅底刻着「龚」字。

column2: Every time you pass, the carpenters press handmade wooden things on you: a spoon, a bowl, a tag carved with Qian. 'For the road. When they break, come back for more.'
column3: 每次路过，木匠们都塞给你们几件顺手做的小木器：一把木勺、一只木碗、一块刻着「千」字的木牌，说「路上用，坏了再来拿」。

column2: Later-Qianli Dock
column3: 后千里坞

column2: Hidden behind the rocks is a dock holding a new ship: three masts, thirteen holds, dragon eyes on the bow still undotted, the rudder well at the stern empty. This is the Later Qianli, Gong Modou's ten years of work. But the Long house's finest block the dock gate, swordsmen, archers and riders packed shoulder to shoulder, their leader brandishing a pledge deed: 'Ship pledged to the Long house. Debt unpaid. Not one inch touches water.'
column3: 礁石后面藏着一个船坞，坞里架着一条新船：三桅，十三舱，船头一对龙目还没点睛，船尾的舵孔空空的。这就是龚墨斗造了十年的「后千里」。坞门却被龙记最精锐的打手堵着，刀手、弓手、劫骑排得密不透风，领头的举着一张押契：「船押龙记，债未清，一寸也不许下水。」

column2: The bruisers are beaten and the pledge deed blows away into the sea. Gong Modou walks the ship bow to stern, rapping every plank, then stands by the empty rudder well a long time. 'She's done. She can catch her,' he says at last. 'But without a rudder she can't even cross the bar. The rudder model is in Long Sihai's hands. Come on. Let's go and ask for it.'
column3: 打手们败了，押契被风吹进了海。龚墨斗从船头走到船尾，一块板一块板地敲，最后站在空舵孔边半天没说话。「船好了，追得上她。」他终于开口，「可没有舵，连沙坝都过不去。舵样在龙四海手里。走，咱们去要。」

column2: The Dragon King's Steps
column3: 龙王阶

column2: At the end of Berth One the stone steps run down into the water. The Dragon King, Long Sihai, sits on the lowest: about fifty, an old silk gown, a wooden box on his knees, an unlit lamp beside him. Behind him his forces stand three columns wide: guard riders in front, swordsmen on the wings, archers holding the steps. What you've brought is laid out before him: a tide book, a surety, three hundred lanterns, a ship without a rudder. He glances at it all and doesn't rise. 'Ten years' berth fees, 298,400 taels. Pay, or bring me one piece of news. Neither? Then we fight. Win, and we'll settle accounts after.'
column3: 一号泊的尽头，石阶一级级没进水里。海龙王龙四海坐在最下面一级，五十来岁，一件旧绸衫，膝上一只木匣，身边一盏没点的灯。他身后三路人马排开：亲兵劫骑在前，刀手两翼，弓手压住石阶。你们带来的东西摆了一地：潮信簿、保状、三百盏灯笼、一条没有舵的船。他看了一眼，没起身：「十年泊费，二十九万八千四百两。要么交钱，要么拿一个消息来。都没有？那就打。打得过，咱们再算账。」

column2: Beaten, the Dragon King sits on the steps a long while catching his breath, then opens the box: inside is a carved wooden rudder that slides up and down. 'She pledged it to me. Said whoever came to continue the voyage should have it.' He presses his thumb to the surety, returns the tide book to A'xi, dots the Later Qianli's eyes with his own brush, and writes one line to the fort: 'Qian lanterns: let them pass.' 'That night I couldn't stop my brother. All I stopped was a boatload of porcelain. You haven't brought me news, so go and fetch it. The Qianli went southeast into the Fog Sea, where an admiral was ordered to stop it. If A'zhou is alive, he's in the fog.' At midnight on the eighteenth of the eighth month, on the full flood of the great tide, the Later Qianli, hung with three hundred lanterns, follows the red poles out through the harbour gate.
column3: 海龙王败了，坐在石阶上喘了半天，打开木匣：里面是一只能上下抽动的木舵。「她押在我这儿的，说谁来续航，就交给谁。」他在保状上按了手印，把潮信簿还给阿汐，提笔给后千里点了睛，又给炮台写了一句：「千字灯，放。」「那夜我没拦住弟弟，只拦下了一船瓷。消息你们没带来，那就替我去取。千里号往东南进了雾海，雾里有个提督奉命截船。阿舟要是还活着，就在雾里。」八月十八子时，大潮涨满，后千里挂着三百盏灯，沿着红篙出了港门。

column2: The Sea of Fog
column3: 雾海

column2: Fog Gate Strand
column3: 雾门滩

column2: On the seventh day out of port a white wall stands up from the sea, hanging from the sky to the water, no end to it either way. Axi turns her tide book to its last page; beyond it her father wrote nothing. The ship anchors off a bare strand at the fog's edge, where a freshly painted board reads: 'Sea of Fog. Forbidden. Any ship showing lights will be stopped.' Beneath it a squad of Fog Sea marines are stamping out their fire. They see the three hundred lanterns on Houqianli's masts and draw their blades as one.
column3: 后千里出港第七天，海上立起一堵白墙，从天顶垂到水面，左右望不到头。阿汐把潮信簿翻到最后一页，再往后，她爹一个字也没写。船在雾边一片荒滩下了锚，滩上插着一块新漆的木牌：「雾海禁地，挂灯之船，截。」牌下一队雾海水兵正把篝火踩灭，望见后千里桅上的三百盏灯笼，齐齐拔出了刀。

column2: The marines fall back into the fog and leave a watch log behind. Axi dips a hand in the sea. 'The water bites, but the wind is warm.' Warm, wet southerlies blowing over a cold sea: the moisture chills and turns to fog, and while the cold water stays, so does the fog. The log's first page reads: 'Eighth month of the Dingwei year. Ordered to stop the Qianli.' Every day for ten years after, one line: 'Not sighted.'
column3: 水兵退进雾里，丢下一本值哨簿。阿汐摸了摸海水：「水冰，风暖。」暖湿的南风吹过冷海，水汽一凉就凝成雾；冷水不走，雾不散。值哨簿头一页写着：「丁未年八月，奉令截千里号。」此后十年，每天一行：「未见。」

column2: Driftwood Rise
column3: 拾漂岗

column2: A rise above the strand where, at every spring tide, whatever the sea brings in fetches up below: broken masts, barrels, planks, shoes. A squad of Fog Sea marines has set a checkpoint on top. The fleet needs timber for repairs, they say, so all drifted wood is forfeit. The old lame beachcomber won't hand his over, so the marines unstrap his wooden leg as well and march off with it on a shoulder.
column3: 荒滩高处一道岗子，每逢大潮，海上漂来的东西都搁在岗下：断桅、木桶、船板、鞋。一队雾海水兵在岗上设了卡，说舰队修船缺木头，凡是漂来的木料一律充公。拾漂的老瘸子不肯交，水兵就连他那条木头假腿也卸了，扛在肩上走。

column2: The marines are chased off and the old man hops after his leg on one foot and gets it back. In his shed, set up like a shrine, is a hatch cover carved 'Qianli Six'. Early on the second day of the ninth month, ten years ago, a young man washed up on the strand clinging to it, lips blue with cold, saying only three words over and over: 'Berth Number One.'
column3: 水兵被赶跑，老瘸子单腿蹦着把假腿抢了回来。他棚子里供着一块舱盖板，刻着「千里·六」。十年前九月初二清早，一个后生抱着这块板子漂上了滩，冻得嘴唇发紫，嘴里只念三个字：「一号泊。」

column2: Firefly Butts
column3: 射萤坡

column2: Fireflies blink in the grass on the slope. A squad of Fog Sea crossbowmen lies along the crest and shoots at any light, and ten years of practice have taught them to hit a firefly with every bolt. The village below dares not light a lamp; supper is cooked by touch. The children keep fireflies in bottles for lamps, and the crossbowmen shoot the bottles too. A notice at the village gate: 'Along the Fog Coast, no light of any kind. Offenders will be treated as traitors.'
column3: 坡上草丛里飞着萤火虫，一闪一闪。一队雾海弩手趴在坡顶，见光就射，十年练下来，箭箭穿萤。坡下的村子夜里不敢点灯，做饭全凭摸，孩子们把萤火虫装进瓶子当灯，被弩手连瓶子一起射碎。村口贴着告示：「雾岸一线，片光不许，违者以通敌论。」

column2: The crossbowmen run, and the children fill their bottles again. From the eighth month ten years ago, the old people say, the admiral ordered the Fog Coast dark: fishing lights, window lamps, the undying lamps on graves, every one. The last to go out was the Qi family's Fogwatch Light on the north cape. 'It lit the Sea of Fog for a hundred years, and then it was just gone.'
column3: 弩手们跑了，孩子们又把萤火虫装进瓶子。村里老人说，十年前八月起，提督下令雾岸灭灯：渔火、窗灯、坟头的长明灯，一盏不留。最后灭的是北岬上戚家的望雾灯，「照了雾海一百年，说灭就灭了」。

column2: The Salt Boilery
column3: 煮盐场

column2: A salt boilery on the strand, dozens of iron pans over fires, seawater bubbling down, the steam mixing with the fog. It belongs to Third Sister Ge, a high-cheekboned widow whose voice is louder than her pans. Today a gang of Fog Sea boarders has come press-ganging: the fleet is short of men, and any man they see gets a rope round him. Third Sister plants herself before the fires with a salt rake: 'You want my men, you boil this pan dry first!'
column3: 滩头一片煮盐场，几十口铁锅架在灶上，海水熬得咕嘟咕嘟，白汽和雾搅在一起。盐场的主人葛三娘是个高颧骨的寡妇，嗓门比锅还响。今天一伙雾海跳帮手来「拉夫」，舰队缺人，见了男丁就套绳子。葛三娘抄起一把盐耙挡在灶前：「要拉人，先把我这锅盐熬干！」

column2: The boarders are scattered and the roped men come home. The young man who washed up, Third Sister says, was called Azhou, from Quanzhou. He boiled salt for her for a year and carved a '1' on every post he tied a boat to. When the fleet came press-ganging, he stepped up and signed on of his own accord. 'He said if you want to find the Qianli, you follow the people sent to stop it.'
column3: 跳帮手被打散，套走的盐丁都放了回来。葛三娘说那个漂上滩的后生叫阿舟，泉州人，在她这儿熬了一年盐，每回系船都在桩上刻个「一」。后来舰队来拉夫，他自己走上前报了名。「他说，要找千里号，就得跟着截它的人。」

column2: Bell Village
column3: 挂铃村

column2: No lights are allowed on the Fog Coast and the nights are thick, so people kept walking into each other; the Fog Sea marines made a rule that anyone out after dark wears a bell. Now the whole village jingles. Cows wear bells, dogs wear bells, the marines wear bells. The marines sell them, thirty coppers each. For days they have been searching house to house for 'the girl with no bell', who steals at night and makes no sound at all.
column3: 雾岸不许点灯，夜里雾又浓，人走路常撞个满怀，雾海水兵便立了规矩：天黑出门，腰上挂铃。如今全村叮叮当当，牛挂铃，狗挂铃，连水兵自己也挂。铃是水兵卖的，一只三十文。这几天他们挨家搜一个「不挂铃的丫头」，说她夜里偷东西，走路一点声都没有。

column2: The villagers unhook their bells and throw them in a basket. The girl, they say, is Qi Xiaoman, granddaughter of Qi Shouguang, the keeper of the north cape light, and she steals odd things: a sheet of copper, a length of wick, half a jar of fish oil. 'Her grandpa lit his lamp once, ten years ago, and they took him away. She wants to light it again.'
column3: 村里人把铃解下来，扔了一箩筐。他们说那丫头叫戚小满，北岬守灯人戚守光的孙女，偷的都是怪东西：一块铜皮、一截灯芯、半罐鱼油。「她爷爷十年前点了一回灯，被抓走了。她想把那盏灯再点起来。」

column2: The Tattoo Hut
column3: 刺青寮

column2: A grass hut by the road with a cloth of patterns hung at the door: anchors, carp, the goddess Mazu, a single eye. The tattoo granny inside has a steady hand, and sailors come to her before they ship out, so that if they drown they can be known. Fog Sea crossbowmen have taken over the hut and are making her ink each of them with his unit number, rapping the table with their crossbow stocks if she's slow. Her eyesight isn't good, and one man's 'Seventh Company' has already come out as 'Seventh Pipe'.
column3: 路边一间草寮，门口挂着一张画满花样的布：锚、鲤鱼、妈祖像、一只眼睛。寮里的刺青婆手稳，水手出海前都来刺一样东西，说是淹死了好认。一伙雾海弩手占着草寮，逼她给每人刺上营号，刺慢了就拿弩柄敲桌子。刺青婆眼神不好，已经把一个人的「七营」刺成了「七管」。

column2: The crossbowmen run off clutching their arms. The granny opens her pattern book to one page: a mooring bollard with a '1' on it. 'A young man from Quanzhou had this done, ten years ago, on his left forearm. His brother was keeping a berth for him, he said. He was afraid he'd forget, and afraid no one would know him.'
column3: 弩手们捂着胳膊跑了。刺青婆翻出花样本，指着一页：一根系船柱，柱上一个「一」。「十年前一个泉州后生让我刺的，刺在左小臂上。他说他哥给他留着一个泊位，怕自己忘了，也怕人家认不出他。」

column2: Upturned Hulls
column3: 倒船屋

column2: On the high ground above the strand stands a row of strange houses, each one a wrecked boat turned keel-up for a roof; on one lintel the ship's name reads upside down. They belong to wreckers who wait for ships to strike the reefs at night and row out for the cargo. Ten dark years have fattened them, and they have hired Fog Sea boarders to guard the place, who pounce on anyone passing with a lantern and knock it from his hand.
column3: 滩头高地上一排怪屋子，全是破船倒扣过来搭的，船底朝天当屋顶，有一间的船名倒写在门楣上。住的是一伙「吃礁的」，专等夜里船撞了礁，划过去捞货。灭灯十年，他们吃得满面红光，还雇了一伙雾海跳帮手看家，见有人提灯过路，就扑上去把灯打翻。

column2: The boarders are beaten and the wreckers' chief hides in his hull. In ten years, he says, they've salvaged everything except the Qianli. 'We crouched on the reef all that night, and the north cape light came on for a quarter of an hour. Just a quarter of an hour, and every one of those ships went round.' He still holds it against old Qi.
column3: 跳帮手们败了，吃礁的头子缩在船屋里不敢出来。他说这十年什么都捞过，就是没捞着千里号：「那一夜我们在礁上蹲了一整宿，北岬的灯偏偏亮了一刻钟。就一刻钟，那几条船全绕过去了。」他到今天还记恨戚老头。

column2: Scarecrow Field
column3: 草人田

column2: A sweet-potato field full of scarecrows in rain hats and straw capes, motionless in the fog. A squad of Fog Sea marines is jabbing each one with a spear and cursing: a deserter has run from the fleet, and someone says he's hiding in this field. At the thirty-seventh, the scarecrow says 'Ow.'
column3: 一片番薯地里插满了草人，戴斗笠，披蓑衣，在雾里一动不动。一队雾海水兵挨个拿枪捅草人，捅一个骂一句：舰上跑了个逃兵，有人说他就藏在这片地里。捅到第三十七个，草人「哎哟」了一声。

column2: The marines are chased off and the scarecrow takes off its own hat: Old Hook, a deserter. That night ten years ago he was in the boarding party. The Qianli's last ship suddenly doused its lights and rammed broadside into the fleet's line, and the five ahead slipped away in the confusion. 'We jumped aboard and found just one young fellow at the helm. He saw us and went straight over the side.'
column3: 水兵被赶跑，草人自己摘了斗笠：逃兵老钩。十年前那一夜他就在跳帮队里：千里号最后一条船忽然灭了灯，横着撞进舰队的阵里，前头五条趁乱溜了。「我们跳上去，船上只剩一个后生掌舵，见了我们，翻身就下了海。」

column2: The Hardtack Ovens
column3: 军饼坊

column2: A row of ovens by the high road where the villagers used to bake sweet-potato cakes. A squad of Fog Sea marines has taken every one and keeps the village women baking hardtack day and night, biscuits hard enough to drive nails, carted off load by load to the fleet. The village children are hungry enough to gnaw the oven ash, while the marines use the spare biscuits as pillows.
column3: 大路边一排烤炉，本是村里人烤番薯饼的。一队雾海水兵把炉子全占了，逼村妇日夜烤军饼，一块饼硬得能钉钉子，烤好了一车车运去舰队。村里的孩子饿得啃炉灰，水兵却拿多出来的饼当枕头。

column2: With the marines gone the ovens bake sweet-potato cakes again, and the smell carries half a li. The old head baker digs out the fleet's biscuit orders, one sheet a month, and one line hasn't changed in ten years: 'Zhenwu. Bugler Azhou. One ration. No sesame.' Azhou is alive, blowing the horn on the admiral's flagship.
column3: 水兵被赶走，炉子又烤上了番薯饼，香甜味飘出半里地。坊里的老面头翻出舰队的领饼单，每月一张，有一行十年没变过：「镇雾号，号手阿舟，饼一份，不要芝麻。」阿舟还活着，在提督的旗舰上吹号。

column2: In the oven house you find the marines' hoard: forty sacks of flour, three hundred biscuits, two crocks of lard, and a cloth bag full of sesame marked 'Bugler won't eat it. Don't waste it.'
column3: 炉房里抄出水兵囤的四十袋面粉、三百块军饼、两坛猪油，还有一只装满芝麻的布袋，上面写着「号手不吃，别浪费」。

column2: Every time you pass, the village women hand you a stack of sweet-potato cakes straight from the oven, the soft kind. 'The hard ones are for the fleet. The soft ones are for our own.'
column3: 每次路过，村妇们都塞给你们一摞刚出炉的番薯饼，软的，说「硬的留给舰队，软的给自己人」。

column2: Fog-Net Hill
column3: 网雾坡

column2: Rows of bamboo poles stand on the hill with fine nets strung between them, beaded with droplets that run down into clay jars.
