The old fog-netter lives on what the nets catch; no good well can be dug on the Fog Coast, and his jars hold the only clean water for ten li. A gang of Fog Sea boarders climbs up with empty buckets: the fleet is short of water, they say, and the jars are coming with them, and the ones too heavy to carry get smashed.
column3: 坡上竖着一排排竹竿，竿间张着细网，网上挂满了水珠，一滴滴流进底下的陶缸。网雾翁靠这些网接雾水过日子，雾岸打不出好井，他这几十口缸是十里内唯一的清水。一伙雾海跳帮手扛着空桶上了坡，说舰队缺水，要把缸一口口抬走，抬不动的就砸。

column2: The boarders run off with empty buckets. From the hilltop, the old man says, you can see the north cape. That night ten years ago the fog was thinner, and he saw the cape light flash three bright and one dark, three times over. Out in the fog three ship's lamps lit up side by side, answered once, and went east. 'Seventy years I've lived, and that was the first time I saw lights talk to each other.'
column3: 跳帮手们提着空桶跑了。网雾翁说坡顶望得见北岬：十年前那一夜雾薄了些，他看见北岬的灯三明一暗，打了三遍；雾里亮起三盏船灯，并排挂着，答了一遍，就往东去了。「活了七十年，头一回见灯跟灯说话。」

column2: Lights-Out Camp
column3: 灭灯营

column2: A big camp on the moor, with a hill of lamps heaped at its gate: fishing lamps, storm lanterns, palace lanterns, sky lanterns, the undying lamps from graves, ten years of confiscations. Marines, crossbowmen and boarders, the camp has them all, and its one job is keeping the coast dark. But the commandant is afraid of the dark. Every night he lights a little oil lamp in his tent under a black cloth that lets out a single thread of light, terrified his own men will notice.
column3: 荒原上一座大营，营门口堆着小山似的灯：渔灯、风灯、宫灯、孔明灯、坟前的长明灯，全是十年里收来的。营里雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手样样齐全，专管雾岸灭灯。可营官怕黑，夜夜在帐里点一盏小油灯，拿黑布罩着，只漏一线光，生怕被自己的兵瞧见。

column2: The commandant surrenders hugging his little lamp, red-faced: 'I'm only human.' The confiscation book, at the eighth month ten years ago: 'Qi Shouguang of the north cape lit the Fogwatch Light without leave, one quarter hour. Held in the Fog Coast fort gaol. One lamp mirror, one lamp chimney, seized.' A quarter hour of light, ten years in a cell.
column3: 营官抱着他那盏小灯投降了，红着脸说：「我也是人。」收灯簿翻到十年前八月：「北岬戚守光，私点望雾灯一刻，拘押雾岸营狱。灯镜一面、灯罩一具，没官。」一刻钟的灯，换了十年的牢。

column2: Conch Horn Camp
column3: 螺号营

column2: A signal camp on the moor that moans all day long: here the Fog Sea navy teaches recruits the conch, the drum and the bell, for in fog no one can see a flag and every order goes by sound. At the sight of you the camp's marines, crossbowmen and boarders blow dozens of conches at once, until your ears ring and the geese at the gate flap up onto the wall in fright.
column3: 荒原上一座号营，营里天天呜呜地响：雾海水师在这里教新兵吹海螺、打鼓、摇铃。雾里看不见旗，全靠声音传令。营里的水兵、弩手、跳帮手见你们来了，几十只海螺一齐吹响，震得人耳朵嗡嗡，营门口的鹅吓得飞上了墙。

column2: The camp breaks up and conches litter the ground. Azhou, says the old horn-master, was the best he ever taught. He could hold a note for half a joss stick and play Quanzhou's nanyin songs on a conch. On the day he passed he asked for one thing only: the flagship. 'He said the admiral's ship stands at the very front. If the Qianli ever comes back, that ship sees it first.'
column3: 号营散了，海螺扔了一地。老号头说，阿舟是他教过最好的号手，一口气能吹半炷香，还会拿海螺吹泉州的南音。学成那天他只求了一件事：上旗舰。「他说提督的船站在最前头，千里号要是回来，头一个看见的就是那条船。」

column2: Belching Marsh
column3: 吐气泽

column2: A marsh of black mud that bubbles under every step, with a rotten-egg stink that makes your eyes stream; the shore folk call it 'the ghost's breath' and no one goes in. A squad of Fog Sea marines is burning the reeds at its edge to smoke someone out. From the smoke comes a girl's voice, sharp and clear: 'Burn away! Burn every reed, I'm still not coming out!'
column3: 一片黑泥沼泽，一脚踩下去咕嘟冒泡，臭鸡蛋味熏得人睁不开眼，岸上人管它叫「鬼吐气」，谁也不敢进。一队雾海水兵在泽边烧芦苇，要把躲在里头的人熏出来。烟里传出一个丫头的声音，又尖又脆：「烧吧！芦苇烧光了，我也不出来！」

column2: The marines withdraw, and a skinny girl climbs out of the reeds, black mud to the knees and no bell at her waist: Qi Xiaoman. There's no ghost here, she says. Dead reeds and leaves buried in the mud get no air, and rotting shut away like that they give off this stink. It chokes you, it doesn't eat you, and it's perfect for hiding things. She hauls an oilcloth bundle out of the mud. Inside is a copper key: the door of the north cape lighthouse.
column3: 水兵撤了，一个瘦丫头从芦苇里钻出来，满腿黑泥，腰上没铃：戚小满。她说这里不闹鬼：烂草烂叶埋在泥底不透气，闷久了就放出这股臭气，熏人，不吃人，正好藏东西。她从泥里拽出一只油布包，包着北岬灯塔的铜钥匙。

column2: Sura's Bamboo House
column3: 苏拉竹楼

column2: A bamboo house by the high road hung with bright South Seas cloth. It belongs to Sura, a dark-skinned trader from the southern isles who came on a ship to trade ten years ago. The Fog Sea navy held the ship in the fog and she has never got home since, so she opened a shop on shore. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen loafs below demanding a 'stranded fee' every day; when she won't pay, they pin her cloth to the wall bolt by bolt.
column3: 大路边一座竹楼，挂满了花花绿绿的南洋布。楼主是个黑皮肤的蛮商娘子苏拉，十年前跟船来做买卖，船被雾海水师扣在雾里，从此回不了家，只好在岸上开铺。一伙雾海弩手赖在楼下，天天收她「滞留钱」；她不交，弩手就拿箭把她的布一匹匹钉在墙上。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and Sura pulls her cloth down from the wall bolt by bolt. Impressed, she opens her shop to you. A Quanzhou bugler from the fleet, she says, comes ashore every year and buys a stack of southern paper and a little bottle of ink. 'For letters. But I've never once seen him send one.'
column3: 弩手被打跑，苏拉把布一匹匹从墙上拔下来，佩服你们，开铺换货。她说舰上有个泉州号手，每年上岸都来买一沓南洋纸、一小瓶墨，「写信用的。可我从没见他寄过」。

column2: The Patchwork Quilt
column3: 百衲被

column2: A lone old house on the moor, a patchwork quilt airing out front, red, yellow, blue and white squares pieced into rings. A squad of Fog Sea marines is dragging it off the pole as 'goods aiding the enemy'. An old woman comes after them on her stick, scolding all the way: 'Ten years, and you won't even leave me a quilt!'
column3: 荒原上一座孤零零的老屋，屋前晾着一床百衲被，红黄蓝白的布块拼成一圈一圈的花样。一队雾海水兵正把被子从竹竿上扯下来，说是查抄的「通敌之物」。屋里的老太太拄着拐追出门，一边追一边骂：「十年了，你们连一床被子都不放过！」

column2: The quilt is won back. The old woman is Granny Qi, the keeper's wife. Xiaoman cries out at the sight of it: the pattern is lamp-talk, and her grandmother stitched it square by square for ten years. Three red patches and one black: 'Three bright, one dark. Safe passage, go east.' In one corner, a line of tiny stitches: 'Three lamps abreast. Thanks for the light. Until we meet.' That was the Qianli's answer.
column3: 被子抢回来了。老太太是戚守光的老伴戚婆。小满一看就叫起来：被面上的花样是灯语，奶奶十年里一针针缝的。三块红布一块黑：「三明一暗，平安，往东。」被角一行小字：「三灯并挂，谢灯，后会。」那是千里号的回话。

column2: Homecoming Rock
column3: 望归石

column2: At the moor's far end sits a great rock shaped like a crouching dog, facing the sea. Every evening Ge Qing, Third Sister's daughter, sits on it netting until dark. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen uses the rock for target practice, bolts thudding in all around her, and she never looks up; her shuttle goes on, back and forth.
column3: 荒原尽头一块大石头，像一只蹲着的狗，面朝大海。每天傍晚，葛三娘的女儿葛青都坐在石头上织网，织到天黑。一伙雾海弩手拿这块石头当靶子练箭，箭一支支钉在她身边，她头也不抬，梭子照样一来一回。

column2: Only when the crossbowmen are gone does Ge Qing put down her net. She and Azhou were betrothed. The day he joined the ship he left her a little wooden post carved with a '1': 'My brother's keeping Berth One for me. I'm keeping a one for you.' He comes ashore once a year and every time he says, 'Soon.' He has been saying 'soon' for nine years.
column3: 弩手们被赶走，葛青才放下网。她和阿舟定过亲，他上船那天给她留了一根小木桩，刻着一个「一」：「我哥给我留一号泊，我给你留一个『一』。」他每年上岸一回，每回都说「快了」。这句「快了」，说了九年。

column2: The Light Shop
column3: 卖光屋

column2: At a fork in the road stands a windowless mud hut with a sign: 'Light for sale. Ten coppers a joss stick.' Inside burns a single candle, and those who go in mend clothes, or read letters, or just look at their old husband's or wife's face. The owner is a shrewd lamp-oil dealer who has hired Fog Sea boarders for the door, and anyone short of coin gets kicked back out. A long queue waits in the dark, every hand clutching coppers.
column3: 岔路口有一间没窗的土屋，门口挂块牌子：「卖光，一炷香十文。」屋里点着一支蜡烛，进去的人或缝衣，或读信，或者只是看看老伴的脸。屋主是个精明的灯油贩，雇了一伙雾海跳帮手守门，交不起钱的一脚踹出来。屋外排着长队，个个在黑地里攥着铜钱。

column2: With the boarders gone, the owner has to burn his candle free till dawn. One old man finally reads his son's letter from three years ago and weeps like a boy. In the old ledger, ten years back: 'Twenty-sixth of the eighth month. Qi Shouguang, ten jin of whale oil on credit. Unpaid.' That night's light burned on borrowed oil. Xiaoman settles her grandfather's debt.
column3: 跳帮手被打跑，屋主只好把蜡烛免费点到天亮。一个老汉借着光读完了儿子三年前的信，哭得像个孩子。旧账上记着十年前：「八月廿六，戚守光，赊鲸油十斤，未还。」那一夜的灯，是赊来的油点的。小满替爷爷还了账。

column2: The White Veil Society
column3: 白纱会

column2: A line of people draped in white veils circles a great stone on the moor, chanting, 'Lady of the Fog, keep your face hidden.' The fog, they say, is the Lady's veil; a light pierces it, and in her anger she overturns ships. Their leader rides a donkey with a guard of Fog Sea boarders, and wherever a crack of light shows, they plaster the window over with wet mud.
column3: 一群披白纱的人在荒原上排成长队，绕着一块大石头转圈，嘴里念着「雾娘娘，莫揭面」。他们说雾是娘娘的面纱，灯光刺破面纱，娘娘就要发怒翻船。领头的香主骑一头驴，身边护着一队雾海跳帮手，谁家漏出一点光，就拿湿泥把窗户糊上。

column2: The boarders run, and so does the donkey. The leader turns out to be a retired marine, and he owns up: the Lights-Out Camp pays for the society. 'Getting people to worship the Lady is cheaper than guarding them with swords.' Under the altar lies an old painting of the north cape lighthouse with its lamp painted black and a note beside it: 'Enemy of the Lady: Qi.'
column3: 跳帮手跑了，香主的驴也跑了。香主是个退伍的水兵，老实交代：这个会是灭灯营出钱办的，「让人拜娘娘，比拿刀守着省事」。供桌下压着一张旧画，画的是北岬灯塔，灯被涂成了黑的，旁边写：「娘娘之敌，戚。」

column2: The Turf Ship Ground
column3: 草船校场

column2: On a great parade ground stands a 'ship' built of stacked turf, masts and holds and all, as big as the real thing. Every day Fog Sea marines, crossbowmen and boarders drill one thing here: leap aboard the turf ship, seize the helm, douse the lights, take the crew. Ten years of it, and they jump faster than monkeys. They've just finished their drill chant when you arrive, and they make you the target.
column3: 一片大校场上，拿草皮垒了一条「船」，有桅有舱，跟真船一般大。雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手每天在这里练一件事：跳上草船，夺舵、灭灯、拿人。练了十年，跳得比猴还快。今天他们刚喊完号子，见你们来了，就拿你们当了靶子。

column2: The parade ground empties and you climb up to look: nine holds, a helm on the port side, three masts. But the Qianli had thirteen holds. The drill book's first page says: 'Form of the Qianli, as described by Bugler Azhou.' Old Hook slaps his thigh. 'That boy! He joined the navy to work for the Qianli from the inside!'
column3: 校场散了，你们爬上草船看了看：九个舱，舵在左舷，三根桅。可千里号是十三舱。操典第一页写着：「千里号形制，据号手阿舟口述。」老钩一拍大腿：「这小子！他进水师，是给千里号当内应去的！」

column2: Egret Isle
column3: 白鹭洲

column2: In the middle of the marsh lies a reed island where egrets roost by the thousand; when they rise it looks like snow. Fog Sea crossbowmen squat at its edge shooting the birds and plucking their long back plumes to sell for hat tassels. The mute boy who minds the egrets pelts them with pebbles, and for every pebble he gets a bolt that just grazes his ear: the crossbowmen are having fun with him.
column3: 沼泽中间一片芦苇洲，白鹭成千上万，飞起来像下了一场雪。一伙雾海弩手蹲在洲边射鹭鸟，拔背上的长羽卖去做帽缨。看鹭的小哑巴拿石子砸他们，砸一颗，挨一箭，箭箭擦着耳朵过去：弩手们拿他取乐。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven out of the marsh and the egrets settle again. The mute boy draws in the mud for you: an old man and a youth under a lighthouse, the old man pointing where the egrets fly. Granny Qi says that was Shouguang's apprentice when he was younger, a fisher boy who learned fog-reading from him for three years and then joined the navy. 'His name was Cen.'
column3: 弩手被赶出沼泽，鹭鸟又落了回来。小哑巴在泥上画给你们看：一个老头，一个少年，坐在灯塔下，老头指着鹭鸟飞走的方向。戚婆说，那是守光年轻时收的徒弟，渔家小子，跟他学了三年看雾，后来去投了水师。「姓岑。」

column2: The Goddess Raft
column3: 天妃筏

column2: Deep in the marsh floats a temple to the Heavenly Consort built on a bamboo raft, with a black-faced Mazu inside and the raft's edges hung with wooden vow tablets that clatter in the wind. A squad of Fog Sea marines has taken over the temple; the tablets, they say, are full of 'secret dealings with the Qianli', and they mean to split them all for firewood. The temple keeper, a mute old woman, sits at the goddess's feet hugging a bundle of tablets and whips anyone who comes near with her horsetail whisk.
column3: 沼泽深处浮着一座竹筏搭的天妃庙，供着一尊黑脸妈祖，筏边系满了许愿的木牌，风一吹哗啦哗啦响。一队雾海水兵占了庙，说木牌上写的都是「私通千里号」的话，要一块块劈了烧火。庙祝是个哑巴老婆婆，抱着一捆木牌坐在神像脚下，谁靠近就拿拂尘抽谁。

column2: The marines are thrown off the raft and the keeper hangs the tablets back one by one. The oldest was hung by Shen Du, owner of the fleet, ten years ago: 'The Qianli's six ships passed here. May all six come home.' Beside it hangs a newer one in a crooked hand: 'Five ships got through. Number Six's crew are all with them. Only I am missing. Azhou.'
column3: 水兵被赶下筏，庙祝把木牌一块块挂了回去。最旧的一块是船主沈渡十年前挂的：「千里号六船过此，愿六船同归。」旁边一块新些，字歪歪扭扭：「五船过了。六号的人都在，只差我一个。阿舟。」

column2: The Letter Office
column3: 验信所

column2: A military post office on the moor, through which every letter home from the fleet must pass, opened and inspected before it goes. The office's marines, crossbowmen and boarders can't read much, so they inspect by one rule: any letter with the character qian in it gets burned. They have just burned one that said 'take a thousand cares', and the old marine who wrote it is hopping with rage at the door.
column3: 荒原上一座军邮所，舰上的家书都从这里过，信要先拆开验过才许送。所里的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手识字不多，验信全凭一条：凡有「千」字的，烧。今天他们刚烧了一封写着「千万保重」的，写信的老水兵在门口跳着脚骂娘。

column2: The office's soldiers scatter. The unburned letters sit in an iron chest, and at the very bottom is a bundle untouched by fire: one a year, ten in all, each addressed to 'Long Sihai, Quanzhou', and not a single qian in any of them, yet not one ever sent. 'The admiral's orders,' says the clerk. 'The bugler's letters are neither burned nor sent.'
column3: 所里的兵散了。烧剩的信堆在铁箱里，最底下一摞却一封没烧：每年一封，十封，收信人都是「泉州龙四海」，信里一个「千」字也没有，却一封也没寄出去。书办说：「提督吩咐过，号手的信，不烧，也不寄。」

column2: Black Sail Dock
column3: 黑帆坞

column2: At the moor's end a hidden channel runs to the sea, with a few black-painted ships moored in it and the bank piled with water casks, salt meat and cable: a pirates' supply dock. The Fog Sea navy stops only ships that show lights, and pirates never light a lamp, slipping in and out in the dark more freely than anyone. The marines, crossbowmen and boarders on guard are deserters the pirates pay, still wearing navy uniforms.
column3: 荒原尽头一条暗沟通着海，沟里泊着几条涂成黑色的船，岸上堆满水桶、腌肉、缆绳：这是海贼的补给坞。雾海水师只截挂灯的船，海贼从来不点灯，摸黑进出，比谁都自在。坞里的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手都是海贼花钱雇来的逃兵，身上还穿着水师的号衣。

column2: This lot of pirates is driven into the sea and half the stores are burned. As long as the navy stops only lit ships, says Old Hook, the black ships will keep coming one after another, and in a few days the dock will be full again. Someone has carved a line on the dock wall: 'Thank you, Admiral, for stopping lights and not men.' Whoever carved it was clearly pleased with himself.
column3: 这一回的海贼被赶下了海，补给烧了一半。老钩说，只要水师还只截有灯的船，黑船就会一条接一条地来，这座坞过不了几天又会塞满。坞墙上刻着一行字：「谢提督，截灯不截人。」刻字的人显然很得意。

column2: The Cen House
column3: 岑家老屋

column2: At the far end of the moor stands a stone house with two crooked pines at the door. Inside lives an old woman blind in one eye, who every year on this day wants to light a lamp on the sill for her son's birthday. The men guarding the house were sent by that son, Fog Sea boarders who keep their heads down and block the window: 'Madam, orders are orders. The admiral can't help it either.'
column3: 荒原尽头一座石屋，门前种着两棵歪脖子松。屋里住着个瞎了一只眼的老太太，每年这一天都要在窗台上点一盏灯，给儿子过生日。守屋的却是她儿子派来的雾海跳帮手，个个低着头，挡在窗前不让点：「老夫人，军令如山，提督也是没法子。」

column2: The boarders back out into the yard. Old Mrs Cen finds the flint and lights her lamp. Her son is Cen Dingbo, Admiral of the Sea of Fog. The night he arrested Qi Shouguang he came home and sat in the dark house till dawn, and said only one thing: 'My master lights the lamp, I put it out. Each of us does his duty.' In the ten years since, he has never come home.
column3: 跳帮手退到了院外。岑老太摸着火石把灯点上：她儿子就是雾海提督岑定波。抓戚守光那夜，他回家在黑屋里坐到天亮，只说了一句：「师父点灯，我灭灯，各尽各的本分。」此后十年，他没再回过家。

column2: Bare Windmills
column3: 空帆风车

column2: A row of windmills on the moor once pumped seawater up onto the salt pans. The Fog Sea marines tore away every sail, saying the fleet's canvas is in rags and there's nothing to patch it with. Now only bare frames remain, and the salt workers climb up and turn them by hand, round and round until they're dizzy, and the pans still won't dry. Today the marines are back to pull down the frames for firewood.
column3: 荒原上一排风车，本是盐户车海水上滩晒盐用的。风车的帆布全被雾海水兵扯走了，说舰队的帆破了没处补。如今只剩光秃秃的木架，盐户们只好爬上去拿手转，一圈一圈，转得头晕眼花，盐滩还是半干不湿。水兵又来了，这回要拆木架当柴烧。

column2: The marines are driven off and the frames saved, and Aqiang brings two old sails over from Houqianli. Once a month, the salt workers say, they deliver salt to the fort gaol, and the cook always asks for an extra half bowl. 'There's an old prisoner who bathes his eyes in salt water every day. Says his eyes mustn't fail, he still has a lamp to watch when he gets out.' Qi Shouguang is alive.
column3: 水兵被赶走，木架保住了，阿樯从后千里上拆下两面旧帆送了过来。盐户说他们每月往雾岸营狱送一回盐，狱里的伙夫每回都多要半碗：「有个老犯人，天天拿盐水洗眼睛，说眼睛不能坏，出去还要看灯。」戚守光还活着。

column2: Kumquat Orchard
column3: 金柑园

column2: A kumquat orchard on the slope, little fruits hanging in clusters, glowing gold in the fog. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen guards it: every kumquat belongs to the fleet and not one may be sold. Old Wei the grower wrings his hands. Unpicked, the fruit will rot on the trees, but the crossbowmen let him pick and not haul, because the fleet's boat hasn't come to collect.
column3: 坡上一片金柑园，小金柑一串串挂在枝头，在雾里黄得发亮。一伙雾海弩手守着园子，说金柑全归舰队，一颗也不许卖。园主老韦急得直搓手：柑子再不摘就要烂在树上，可弩手只许摘，不许运，因为舰队的船还没来取。

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off and Old Wei fills dozens of baskets. The fleet hasn't made port in ten years, he says, and without fresh fruit the men's gums bleed and their teeth work loose; these kumquats keep them going. Every spring the flagship's bugler comes ashore and picks a basket of the sourest. 'Lots of bad teeth aboard, he says. The sour ones do the job.'
column3: 弩手们被赶跑，老韦把金柑装满了几十只筐。他说舰上十年没靠过港，吃不上鲜果，好些人牙龈出血、牙齿松动，全靠这些柑子。每年春天，旗舰的号手都上岸来挑一筐最酸的：「他说船上牙不好的人多，酸的管用。」

column2: Cockcrow Mound
column3: 鸡鸣墩

column2: An earth mound on the moor where dozens of big roosters are kept. Every fisher family on the Fog Coast knows that in fog you can't tell morning from evening, so you wait for the cocks to tell you it's dawn, and boats out at sea find their way home by the crowing. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen is grabbing the roosters for the fleet and shooting the ones they can't catch. Feathers fill the air, and the old poultryman chases his birds in tears.
column3: 荒原上一座土墩，墩上养着几十只大公鸡。雾岸的渔家都知道：雾里分不清早晚，听鸡叫才知道天亮了，海上的船听着鸡叫也认得回家的方向。一伙雾海弩手抢鸡，说要送去舰上，抓不住的就射。鸡毛满天飞，养鸡的老汉追着自己的鸡哭。

column2: With the crossbowmen gone, the roosters stalk back to the mound grumbling. The loudest bird on the flagship, the old man says, a speckled cock, is one of his, carried aboard in Azhou the bugler's own arms. 'He said the men have drifted in the fog so long they can't even keep track of the days. They need a rooster to count them.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，公鸡们骂骂咧咧回了墩子。老汉说，旗舰上那只最响的芦花鸡就是他的，是号手阿舟亲手抱上船的：「他说船上的人在雾里漂久了，连过了几天都记不清，得有只鸡替他们数日子。」

column2: The Knot Shop
column3: 结绳铺

column2: A little sack shop by the road, kept by an old knotter who can tie anything: nets, hawsers, the necks of salt bags. Fog Sea marines have turned the shop upside down and are unpicking the cord on every salt sack, saying someone in the fort gaol is passing messages out in knots. Cord ends pile up on the floor and the shopkeeper clicks his tongue in grief: 'Those were good knots.'
column3: 路边一间卖麻袋的小铺，掌柜是个结绳的老手，渔网、缆绳、盐袋口，什么结都会打。一伙雾海水兵把铺子翻了个底朝天，一只只拆盐袋的袋口绳，说营狱里有人拿绳结往外递消息。拆下来的绳头堆了一地，掌柜心疼得直咂嘴：「这都是好结啊。」

column2: The marines leave. From under the counter the shopkeeper brings out a handful of old cord ends, untied over ten years from the empty salt sacks returned by the gaol. Every one carries the same knots: three tight, one loose. Xiaoman clutches them and the tears come at once. Three bright, one dark. Every month her grandfather has been saying, 'I'm well. The light still stands.'
column3: 水兵走了。掌柜从柜底摸出一把旧绳头，十年里从营狱退回来的空盐袋上解下的，每根都打着同样的结：三个紧，一个松。小满攥着绳头，眼泪一下子下来了：三明一暗，爷爷每个月都在说，「我好，灯还在」。

column2: The Stranded Circus
column3: 困班车

column2: A few covered wagons stand on the moor, their canvas painted with lions and rings of fire: a South Seas circus that tried to cross the sea ten years ago, had its ship held in the fog, and has been stuck on this moor ever since. A squad of Fog Sea marines surrounds the wagons, making them put on a show every night and docking their supper if it flops. The troupe's old bear has learned to dig the sweet-potato beds, and the tightrope girl sleeps on her rope.
column3: 荒原上停着几辆大篷车，车篷上画着狮子和火圈：一个南洋来的马戏班子，十年前要过海，船被扣在雾里，就困在了这片荒原。一队雾海水兵把篷车围住，逼他们每夜演一场，演砸了不给饭吃。班里的老熊已经学会帮着翻番薯地，走钢丝的姑娘在绳上睡觉。

column2: The marines are driven off and the ringmaster gives you a show for free. Last New Year, he says, the navy had them perform aboard the flagship, and in the crowd a young conch-blower slipped him a note in the confusion: 'Tell Third Sister at the salt pans I've found the way they went.' The ringmaster never dared deliver it.
column3: 水兵被赶走，班主请你们看了一场不收钱的戏。他说去年水师过年，叫他们上旗舰演过一回，台下有个吹海螺的年轻人，趁乱塞给他一张纸条：「告诉煮盐的三娘，我找到他们去的路了。」班主一直没敢去送。

column2: The Dispatch Road
column3: 传令驿道

column2: A ruler-straight dirt road across the moor, with a signal mound every five li: the dispatch road between the fleet and the shore forts. Smoke can't be seen in the fog, so they beat drums instead, boom boom boom, passed from mound to mound. A large force of marines, crossbowmen and boarders holds the road under a sign: 'Military dispatches. Civilians keep clear.' Today the drums are beating fast.
column3: 荒原上一条笔直的土路，每隔五里一座烟墩，是舰队和岸营之间递令的驿道。雾里看不见烟，他们就敲鼓，咚咚咚一路传过去。驿道上驻着一大队雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手，路边立着牌子：「军令往来，闲人回避。」今天的鼓敲得特别急。

column2: The couriers scatter and the drums fall silent. In the dispatch box lies a copy of the lights-out order, with two lines added at the end in the admiral's own hand: 'Qi Shouguang is not to be killed. Nor released.' Below, in fresher ink: 'If a ship comes showing Qian lanterns, report at once.' Today's urgent drums were about Houqianli.
column3: 驿卒们散了，鼓也停了。驿匣里压着灭灯令的抄本，末尾有提督亲笔添的两行：「戚守光不许杀，不许放。」底下又一行墨迹新些：「若有船挂千字灯来，速报。」今天急鼓报的，正是后千里。

column2: The Chart Copier's
column3: 抄图斋

column2: A little study with a 'Charts Copied' banner at the door, kept by a short-sighted old scholar who copies charts for the fleet: three copies of each, not one more. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen stands at the door collecting each chart as it's done and burning even his spoiled drafts. When no one is looking, the old scholar slips one draft under his inkstone.
column3: 一座小书斋，门口挂着「代抄海图」的幌子，斋主是个近视的老秀才，替舰队抄海图，一张图抄三份，一份不许多。一伙雾海弩手守在门口，抄完一张收一张，连画坏的草稿也要拿去烧。老秀才趁人不注意，把一张草稿塞进了砚台底下。

column2: With the crossbowmen gone the old scholar draws the draft from under his inkstone: a private chart the flagship's bugler brought him to copy last year. A thin line runs into the south-east corner of the Sea of Fog, and where it ends he drew no sea but towers and terraces, with a note: 'Eighteenth of the eighth month. The fog opens a crack. A city in the south-east. The Qianli went this way.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，老秀才从砚台底下抽出那张草稿：是旗舰号手去年拿来请他誊的一张私图，雾海东南角画着一条细线，线的尽头没画海，画了几座楼台，旁注：「八月十八，雾开一线，东南有城。千里号往此去。」

column2: Mud-Sled Flats
column3: 泥马滩

column2: On the mudflats at the marsh's edge, the flat-folk kneel on one leg on a board with an upturned nose and kick off the mud with the other, skimming along. They call it a mud-horse, and on the flats it's ten times faster than walking. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has stolen the mud-horses to race each other, and flattened the morning's whole catch of razor clams into mud cakes.
column3: 沼泽外缘的滩涂上，滩民一条腿跪在一块翘头木板上，一条腿在泥上蹬，嗖嗖地滑，这东西叫「泥马」，泥里跑得比人快十倍。一伙雾海跳帮手抢了泥马，在滩上赛着玩，把滩民挖了一早上的蛏子全压成了泥饼。

column2: The boarders are tipped into the mud and the mud-horses go back to their owners. From here, an old flat-man says, at low tide you can slide all the way to the back wall of the Fog Coast fort, where the foot of the wall sits in mud and is the weakest stretch of the whole fort. Xiaoman makes a note of it. It isn't only the lamp she wants. She wants her grandfather.
column3: 跳帮手被掀翻在泥里，泥马还给了滩民。滩上的老人说，从这里滑过去，退潮时能一直滑到雾岸营的后墙底下，那里的墙脚泡在泥里，是营里最松的一段。小满记下了：她要的不光是灯，还有爷爷。

column2: Fog Boardwalk Ferry
column3: 雾栈渡

column2: Where marsh meets sea, a row of stilt houses is joined by a long boardwalk with a ferry landing at its end. Old Pole the ferryman sees the lanterns on Houqianli's masts from far off, drops his pole and runs down the boardwalk, banging on every door: 'The Qianli's back! The Qianli's back!' A squad of Fog Sea marines comes after him and pins him to the planks for spreading wild rumours.
column3: 沼泽和海交界的地方，一排高脚木屋连成长长的栈道，栈道尽头是渡口。渡夫老篙远远望见后千里桅上的灯笼，扔下竹篙就往栈道上跑，一路敲着各家的门喊：「千里号回来了！千里号回来了！」一队雾海水兵追上来，把他按在栈板上，说他妖言惑众。

column2: The marines are pushed off the boardwalk. Old Pole stares at your lanterns a long time, a little disappointed and not yet ready to give up. He poles you to the floating market, telling you on the way that the Qianli took a shipload of goods on credit there, and took the market's best pilot too, Bao Laozhen. 'The whole market's waited ten years for it to come back and settle up. And for Old Needle.'
column3: 水兵被赶下栈道。老篙盯着你们的灯笼看了半天，有点失望，又不死心。他撑船送你们去海上集，一路上说：千里号当年在集上赊了一船货，还带走了集上最好的领港鲍老针。「满集的人等了十年，等它回来结账，也等老针。」

column2: The Mynah's Teahouse
column3: 八哥茶亭

column2: A roadside teahouse with a cage hanging from the beam, and in the cage a mynah that shouts at everyone, 'Pay up! Pay up!' The owner is the floating market's debt collector and the bird is his assistant. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has been drinking without paying, and the mynah has spent the afternoon screaming 'Admiral owes wages! Admiral owes wages!' at them. Now they've lost their temper and want to wring its neck.
column3: 路边一座茶亭，梁上挂着个鸟笼，笼里一只八哥，见人就喊：「欠钱！欠钱！」茶亭掌柜是海上集的讨债人，八哥是他养的帮手。一伙雾海弩手在亭里喝茶不给钱，八哥冲着他们喊了半天「提督欠饷！提督欠饷！」，弩手们恼了，要拧它的脖子。

column2: With the crossbowmen gone, the mynah shakes out its feathers, eyes your lanterns, and changes its tune: 'Qianli! Three hundred jin of tallow! Sixty bronze gongs! One pilot!' The owner goes red. That's the Qianli's tab, kept at the market for ten years; the bird heard it so often it learned it by heart. It recites that one only to ships with lanterns.
column3: 弩手们被赶走，八哥抖抖毛，瞅了一眼你们的灯笼，忽然换了一套词：「千里号！牛油三百斤！铜锣六十面！领港一个！」掌柜红了脸：那是集上记了十年的千里号赊账，八哥听多了，背熟了。它只对挂灯的船背这一段。

column2: Where Number Six Lies
column3: 六号搁浅处

column2: On the high ground at the moor's end lies a great ship, half a li from the sea, where a storm surge pushed it ten years ago. 'Qianli Six' is painted on its bow. A huge hole is stove in its side, and half of it has been patched with new planks. The Fog Sea navy keeps it as a war prize, guarded by its finest marines, crossbowmen and boarders, a company flag planted on the bow, and no one may approach.
column3: 荒原尽头的高地上搁着一条大船，离海足有半里，是十年前一场风暴潮把它推上来的。船头漆着「千里·六」，船舷被撞出一个大洞，已经拿新木板补了一半。雾海水师把它当战利品，派了最精的水兵、弩手、跳帮手守着，营旗插在船头，谁也不许靠近。

column2: The guards are beaten. Inside, the ship is swept clean, and the smallest bunk is carved all over with tally marks, a stroke a day for ten years. Someone has been patching the hole in the side, year by year, and is halfway done. Under the bunk's pillow end lies a sheet of paper: 'When the admiral lifts his order, I'll sail Number Six home to Quanzhou and moor at Berth One.' The hand is Azhou's.
column3: 守兵败了。舱里收拾得干干净净，最小的那张铺位上刻满了「正」字，一天一笔，刻了十年。船舷的破洞是有人一年年补的，补到了一半。铺头压着一张纸：「等提督撤了令，我就开六号回泉州，靠一号泊。」字是阿舟的。

column2: Peat Village
column3: 泥炭村

column2: Nobody on the moor burns wood; they burn peat, black bricks cut from the bog and dried to last a winter. A squad of Fog Sea boarders has taken the village and sealed every dried stack for the fleet's galleys, so the villagers must burn wet peat, and the smoke indoors is thicker than the fog. Every house is coughing.
column3: 荒原上的人不烧柴，烧泥炭：从沼地里切出一块块黑砖，晒干了能烧一冬。一队雾海跳帮手占了村子，把晒好的泥炭垛全封了，说舰上的伙房要用，村里人只能拿湿炭烧，屋里烟比雾还浓，家家咳嗽。

column2: The stacks are unsealed and the houses can breathe again. The headman takes you to see something: behind the village stands a stack of dry peat nobody may touch, a new layer added each year until it's a little hill. 'Old Qi burned whale oil in his lamp, and when that ran short he burned this. The day the north cape lights again, the fuel's ready.'
column3: 炭垛解了封，屋里总算不呛人了。村长领你们去看一样东西：村后有一垛谁也不许动的干炭，每年添一层，十年添成了小山。「戚老头点灯从前烧鲸油，鲸油没了就烧这个。哪天北岬要点灯，炭是现成的。」

column2: In the stacks you find the boarders' hoard: three hundred dry peat bricks, two sacks of roasted beans, a keg of salted eel, and a brass hand-warmer taken from the village, its coals still warm.
column3: 垛里抄出跳帮手囤的三百块干泥炭、两袋炒豆、一桶咸鳗，还有一只从村里抢来的铜手炉，炉里的炭还没凉。

column2: Every time you pass, the villagers stack dry peat on your carts and press on you a bag of taro baked in the embers. 'It's cold in the fog. Keep these in your coat.'
column3: 每次路过，村里人都往你们车上码几块干泥炭，再塞一兜炭火里煨熟的芋头，说「雾里冷，揣着走」。

column2: Fog Bell Temple
column3: 雾钟寺

column2: A small temple on the moor's edge with a great bronze bell. It used to ring once every quarter hour whenever the fog came in, and ships at sea found the shore by its sound. When the lights-out order came the marines banned the bell too, took away its striker and chained its mouth shut. Every foggy day the old monk goes and pats the bell and says 'dong' aloud, and counts that as ringing it. Today the marines are back to haul the bell off and melt it down for bolt heads.
column3: 荒原边一座小寺，寺里一口大铜钟，从前起雾就敲，一刻一响，海上的船听着钟声认岸。灭灯令下来，雾海水兵连钟也禁了，把钟锤摘走，拿铁链锁住钟口。老和尚每天起雾就去摸摸钟，嘴里「当」一声，算是敲过了。今天水兵又来，要把钟抬走熔了铸箭头。

column2: The marines are driven out of the gate and the bell is saved. That night, the old monk says, he and Qi Shouguang had an agreement. 'He lit the lamp and I rang the bell. A quarter hour of light, fifteen strokes.' At the fifteenth, the fort's men stormed the north cape. On the day they took the striker away, Shouguang shouted to him from the prison cart: 'Monk, remember for me! It was fifteen!'
column3: 水兵被赶出了山门，钟保住了。老和尚说那一夜他和戚守光约好了：「他点灯，我敲钟。灯一刻，钟十五响。」打完第十五下，营里的兵就冲上了北岬。钟锤被收走那天，守光在囚车里冲他喊：「和尚，替我记着，是十五下！」

column2: The Ask-Father Toll
column3: 问爹卡

column2: A pole blocks the crossroads, and behind it stands a row of children, the eldest no more than twelve. Travellers must pay a news toll: tell one thing about the fleet and you may pass. Every child's father serves in the Fog Sea navy, and none has been home in ten years. A few elderly marines on shore duty have been bossed into minding the pole, looking helpless.
column3: 路口横着一根木杆，杆后站着一排孩子，最大的不过十二岁，过路的人要交「消息钱」：说一件舰队上的事，才许过去。孩子们的爹都在雾海水师当兵，十年没回过家。几个上了年纪、留守岸上的雾海水兵被孩子们支使着看杆子，一脸无奈。

column2: The old marines are beaten fair and square and the pole goes up. You tell the children what you know: the fleet is short of water and sailcloth. They listen without a sound. 'While the order stands, the ships don't come home,' one old marine sighs. He has just come off a shift at the fort gaol, and says the old prisoner named Qi draws a lamp on the wall with his finger every night. Ten years of it, and the wall has gone shiny.
column3: 老兵们被打得心服口服，杆子抬了起来。你们说了舰队缺水缺帆的事，孩子们一声不吭。一个老兵叹气：「令不撤，船就不回港。」他刚从营狱换班出来，说那个姓戚的老犯人每夜拿手指在墙上画灯，画了十年，墙都画亮了。

column2: Oyster-Lime Kiln
column3: 蛎灰窑

column2: White smoke rises from the moor: a kiln that burns oyster shells to lime, which mixed with tung oil makes the putty that seals a ship's seams. A squad of Fog Sea marines has seized it and ships every bag to the fleet, leaving the kiln families none, not even enough to stop their own roofs leaking. Old Zao the kiln master is plastered white with lime, like the villain's painted face in an opera.
column3: 荒原上冒着白烟，是一座烧牡蛎壳的灰窑，壳烧成灰，掺上桐油就是补船缝的油灰。一队雾海水兵把窑占了，烧出来的灰全运去舰队，窑户们一袋也留不下，自家屋顶漏雨都补不上。窑主老灶脸上糊满了白灰，像戏台上的白脸奸臣。

column2: With the marines gone, the kiln families patch their own roofs for the first time. For ten years, says Old Zao, whenever fleet men came ashore, the flagship's bugler bought two bags of lime of his own and carried them off toward the high ground in the south-west. 'We never asked what he was patching. Every man who patches ships has a ship in his heart.'
column3: 水兵被赶走，窑户们头一回给自家屋顶补上了灰。老灶说，十年来每次舰队的人上岸，旗舰的号手都要单买两袋灰，背着往西南的高地去。「我们不问他补什么。补船的人，心里都有一条船。」

column2: In the kiln you find the marines' hoard: sixty bags of oyster lime, three kegs of tung oil, a basket of dried oysters, and a ledger whose column for the bugler reads 'Paid himself. Not on the public account.'
column3: 窑里抄出水兵囤的六十袋蛎灰、三桶桐油、一筐晒干的海蛎，还有一本账簿，号手那一栏写着「自付，不入公账」。

column2: Every time you pass, the kiln families load two bags of fresh lime onto your carts and cook a pot of oyster congee. 'Broken cart or leaking boat, this'll patch it.'
column3: 每次路过，窑户们都往车上搬两袋新灰，再煮一锅海蛎粥，说「车坏了船漏了，都拿它补」。

column2: Shouming Hamlet
column3: 守明村

column2: There is a little village in the fog, and two marines leaning on their spears at its gate say, 'Everyone in there died out ten years ago. What do you want with it?' But firelight shows at one window. A white-haired old man opens the door, delighted to see you, and cooks a pot of fish porridge; visitors are rare, he says, and asks whether the north cape light is lit yet. The porridge is good, the fire is warm. When he gets up to add wood you see, on the wall behind him, a spirit tablet bearing his own name: Qi Shouming, died on the twenty-sixth of the eighth month, ten years ago.
column3: 雾里有座小村，村口两个雾海水兵拄着枪说：「这村十年前就绝户了，进去做什么？」可村里有一扇窗透出火光。开门的白发老人见了你们很高兴，熬了一锅鱼片粥，说难得来客，又问北岬的灯点没点。粥很香，炉火很暖。他起身去添柴，你们这才看见他背后的墙上供着一块灵牌，写着他自己的名字：戚守明，卒于十年前八月廿六。

column2: The marines burst in to arrest the dead man and you throw them out. The old man laughs until he cries. He is Shouguang's younger brother, and that night he carried the oil up the lighthouse. After his brother was taken, the whole village reported him dead and put up a tablet, and the officials don't come for dead men. 'For a corpse, I sleep better than anyone.'
column3: 门外的水兵闯进来要抓「死人」，被你们打了出去。老人笑出了眼泪：他是守光的亲弟弟，那夜替哥哥扛油上灯塔。哥哥被抓后，全村人给他报了丧，立了牌位，官府就不来抓死人了。「我这个死人，活得比谁都踏实。」

column2: The Door with the Bundle
column3: 挂包门

column2: A house on the moor's edge with a faded cloth bundle hanging from its lintel, untouched for ten years. Its old owner once sailed the Quanzhou run, and on his last trip home ten years ago he brought a letter he'd been asked to deliver to 'Azhou, Fog Sea Navy'. But the fleet lets no civilian boat come near, so the letter has hung over the door ever since. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has heard the bundle holds 'a secret letter from Quanzhou' and is propping a ladder to take it down.
column3: 荒原边一户人家，门楣上挂着一只褪色的布包，十年没人碰过。老主人从前是跑泉州的船家，十年前最后一趟回来，带了一封托他捎给「雾海水师阿舟」的信，可舰队不许民船靠近，信就一直挂在门上。一伙雾海弩手听说布包里有「泉州来的密信」，正搭梯子要摘。

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off and the old boatman hands you the bundle with shaking hands. The letter was written for old Mrs Long, sent ten years ago: 'Azhou, Mother has made noodle porridge. Come home and eat. Your brother talks tough, but he's keeping the berth.' Tucked in the envelope is a copper coin, for him to buy sweets. The letter is ten years late, and the coin still shines.
column3: 弩手被赶跑，老船家颤着手把布包交给你们。信是龙老太托人写的，十年前寄出：「阿舟，娘熬了面线糊，回来吃。你哥嘴硬，泊位他留着。」信封里还夹着一枚铜钱，给他买糖的。信迟到了十年，那枚铜钱还亮着。

column2: Stilt Watchtower
column3: 高脚哨

column2: A watchtower on four tall stilts stands in the marsh, its top facing the north cape. Fog Sea crossbowmen keep watch up there day and night on the lighthouse that's been dark ten years, ready to loose a whistling arrow to warn the fort if the top so much as flickers. Bored stiff, they've carved the railing full of tally marks, five days to a mark.
column3: 沼泽里竖着一座高脚木哨楼，四根长柱插在泥里，楼顶正对着北岬。一伙雾海弩手日夜守在上面，盯着那座黑了十年的灯塔，哪怕塔顶闪一下，就要放响箭报营。弩手们闲得发慌，在栏杆上刻了密密麻麻的「正」字，一个字五天。

column2: The crossbowmen slide down the stilts and run. For ten years the watch log says only 'North cape, no light', except on the twenty-sixth of the eighth month each year, which has one more line: 'The admiral came alone by skiff to the north cape, climbed the tower, one quarter hour, came down.' Every year he goes and stands a quarter hour beneath the lamp no one may light.
column3: 弩手们顺着柱子溜下去跑了。哨簿上十年都是「北岬无光」，只有每年八月廿六那天多一行：「提督独乘小艇至北岬，登塔，一刻，下。」他每年都去，在那座不许点的灯下面，站一刻钟。

column2: House of a Hundred Needles
column3: 百针屋

column2: The walls of a small house are covered in compasses, more than a hundred large and small, every needle pointing its own way, no two alike. The house belongs to Auntie Bao, wife of the pilot Bao Laozhen. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen bursts in to seize the compasses: the fleet's ships get lost every time they reach the Black Sand Spit, and they want good needles. Auntie Bao sits on the doorstep shelling peanuts. 'Take them. There isn't an honest needle in the house.'
column3: 一间小屋的四壁挂满了罗盘，大大小小上百只，指针各指各的，没有两只朝同一个方向。屋主鲍婶是领港鲍老针的老伴。一伙雾海弩手闯进来抢罗盘，说舰队的船一到黑沙嘴就迷路，要好针。鲍婶坐在门槛上剥花生：「拿吧，这一屋子针，没一根准的。」

column2: The crossbowmen run a few steps with the compasses and throw them back. Old Needle, says Auntie Bao, never trusted a needle in his life. 'There's iron-stone under this sea, and when a needle gets there it lies.' He piloted by ear and by hand, listening to the surf, feeling the water. The Qianli paid him half his fee, the rest on the way back, and he said he'd be home in a month. That was ten years ago.
column3: 弩手们抱着罗盘跑了几步，又扔了回来。鲍婶说老针一辈子不信针：「这片海底下有铁石，针到了那儿就撒谎。」他听浪、摸水，凭耳朵和手领船。千里号付了他一半工钱，说好回来付另一半；他说一个月就回。那是十年前。

column2: Sail-Drop Reeds
column3: 落篷滩

column2: A reed bed at the marsh's edge with a few broad old grooves in the mud, as if big boats were hauled up here years ago. A squad of Fog Sea marines is cutting every reed to the ground: the admiral's orders, no hiding places for boats along the shore. The old reed-cutter follows behind gathering up the stalks and muttering, 'Hiding? Ten years ago they came in bold as you like.'
column3: 沼泽边一片芦苇滩，滩头有几道宽宽的旧泥槽，像是很多年前有大船拖过来。一队雾海水兵在这里割芦苇，割得一根不剩，说是提督有令：「沿岸不许留藏船之处。」割苇的老汉跟在后头捡苇子，嘴里嘀咕：「藏船？十年前人家是大大方方靠上来的。」

column2: The marines are driven off. Shouldering his reeds, the old man says that in the eighth month ten years ago six boats came out of the fog, from the Qianli, they said, and three hundred people came ashore by turns. They stayed three days, paid cash for everything, and when they left they returned every borrowed pot and bowl scrubbed bright. 'Three hundred people, three days, and not one left a debt.'
column3: 水兵被赶走，老汉扛着苇子说：十年前八月，雾里出来六条小艇，说是千里号的，三百人轮着上岸，在这一带住了三天，买东西个个付现钱，走的时候把借来的锅碗都刷得锃亮还回来。「三百个人，三天，没一个赖账的。」

column2: The Floating Market
column3: 海上集

column2: Hundreds of boats are lashed side by side at the marsh's edge, hull against hull, plank to plank, into one great market on the water: fish, cloth, medicine, compasses, the noise of a pot on the boil. The moment Houqianli's lanterns show, the whole market falls silent. Then someone weeps, someone laughs, someone bangs a gong: 'The Qianli's come back!' Dozens push forward clutching account books. But at the very front is a squad of Fog Sea marines who came to collect the 'navy levy' and walked straight into it.
column3: 沼泽边上几百条船并排拴着，船挨船，板接板，铺成一大片水上集市，卖鱼的、卖布的、卖药的、卖罗盘的，吵得像开了锅。后千里的灯笼一露头，整个集市忽然静了，接着有人哭，有人笑，有人敲锣：「千里号回来了！」几十个人捧着账本往前挤。可挤在最前头的是一队雾海水兵，他们来收「水师饷」，正好撞上。

column2: The marines are driven off the planks and the market crowds round and reads the name on your stern: Houqianli, After-Qianli. For a moment no one speaks. Then someone laughs first: 'Coming after counts!' Gold for timber, the trade starts up again, and ten years of account books open one by one. The market elder brings out the Qianli's credit note: 'Tallow, three hundred jin. Bronze gongs, sixty. Pilot Bao Laozhen, one. To be paid in full on the return voyage.' He gives the note to you. 'You who came after: find out for us where they went.'
column3: 水兵被赶下船板，集上的人围上来，看清了你们船尾的字：后千里。愣了一会儿，有人先笑出声：「后来的也算！」金子换木料的买卖重新做了起来，搁了十年的账本一本本摊开。集老拿出千里号的赊条：「牛油三百斤，铜锣六十面，领港鲍老针一人。回程付清。」他把赊条交给你们：「后来的，替我们看看，它们到底去了哪儿。」

column2: The Levy Stockade
column3: 抽饷寨

column2: A stockade on the water by the market, the Fog Sea navy's levy post: for every fish sold, it takes a scale. Marines, crossbowmen, boarders, it has them all, and the takings go off to the fleet by the cartload. A board at the gate reads 'By order, supplies to be drawn from the market.' Under it squat a few old fishwives, cursing and counting how many scales they've got left.
column3: 集市边一座水寨，是雾海水师的抽饷营，集上每卖一条鱼，营里抽一片鳞。营里的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手样样都有，饷一车车往舰队运。营门口立着块牌子：「奉令就市取给。」牌子底下蹲着几个卖鱼的老太太，一边骂，一边数自己还剩几片鳞。

column2: The stockade is broken up and its ledgers cover a table. The court hasn't paid the fleet a copper in ten years; this stockade is what keeps it fed. The last pages read: 'Seventh month: three hundred shi of rice levied, sent to the Zhenwu. The bugler came asking again whether the silver from Bao Laozhen's empty skiff is still in the store.'
column3: 抽饷寨被打散，账本摊了一桌：朝廷十年没发过一文饷，舰队全靠这座寨子吃饭。最后几页记着：「七月，抽米三百石，送镇雾号。号手又来问：鲍老针那条空舢板里的银子，可还在库里？」

column2: The Mirror Wok
column3: 镜锅灶

column2: A Fog Sea crossbowmen's cookhouse on the moor, where an enormous 'wok' sits over the stove: polished bronze, its bowl ground into perfect rings, so that when the fire catches it the whole cookhouse glows gold. The cook treasures it; he swapped it out of the fort stores, he says, and everything tastes better from it. Xiaoman jumps at the sight: 'That's our lamp mirror!'
column3: 荒原上一座雾海弩手的伙房，灶上架着一口奇大的「锅」，铜胎锃亮，锅底一圈圈磨得极圆，炒菜时火光一照，整个伙房金灿灿的。伙夫把它当宝，说是从营里库房换来的，炒什么都香。小满一看就跳了起来：「那是我家的灯镜！」

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off and Xiaoman won't let go of the 'wok'. The mirror is ground bronze; it gathers one lamp's light into a beam that reaches dozens of li. Its face is scored where the spatula scraped and coated with ten years of cooking grease. The cook, grieving, hands over a packet of fine ash. 'Scrub it with wood ash. It'll come back.'
column3: 弩手们被赶跑，小满抱着那口「锅」不撒手。灯镜是铜磨的，把一盏灯的光拢成一束，打出几十里去。镜面被铲出几道印子，还沾着十年的油烟。伙夫心疼地递来一包细灰：「拿草木灰擦，擦得回来。」

column2: Washing Creek
column3: 捣衣溪

column2: Behind the fort gaol runs a little creek where washerwomen squat on the rocks pounding laundry: the garrison's uniforms, and the prisoners' smocks. A gang of Fog Sea boarders stands guard and shakes out every smock for smuggled goods. The head washerwoman is a stout, loud auntie whose paddle rings louder than a sword, cursing as she pounds: 'Go on, check it! Find a louse and I'll give you a prize!'
column3: 营狱背后一条小溪，洗衣妇们蹲在石头上捣衣，替营里洗号衣，也替狱里洗囚衣。一伙雾海跳帮手守在溪边，每件囚衣都要抖开验过，说怕里头夹带东西。领头的洗衣妇是个大嗓门的胖婶，捣衣杵抡得比刀还响，一边捣一边骂：「验吧验吧，验出个虱子赏你！」

column2: The boarders are driven off, and the auntie pulls an old smock from the bottom of her basket: three little holes burned in the front with an incense tip and one space left bare, like every smock she has washed for ten years. 'I can't read, but I know that old man.' Once, she says, he gave her a message to pass on: 'Xiaoman, don't come. Mind the lamp.'
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，胖婶从洗衣篮最底下抽出一件旧囚衣：衣襟上用香头烫了三个小洞，留一处空着，十年里她洗过的每一件都这样。「我认不得字，可我认得这老头。」她说他托她带过一句话：「小满别来，看灯。」

column2: Turnkeys' Tavern
column3: 狱卒酒寮

column2: A low tavern outside the fort gaol where off-duty turnkeys come for a cup. Today a gang of Fog Sea boarders has taken the whole place; the admiral sent them to double the guard, and they think the turnkeys are slack, and they're pounding the table lecturing them. A few old turnkeys huddle in a corner holding cups they don't dare drink. One mutters, 'Ten years, and the old man's never once tried to run.'
column3: 营狱外一间矮酒寮，下了值的狱卒都来这里喝两盅。今天被一伙雾海跳帮手包了场，他们是提督派来加岗的，嫌狱卒看得松，正拍着桌子训人。几个老狱卒缩在墙角，端着酒不敢喝，有一个小声嘀咕：「看了十年，那老头一回也没想跑过。」

column2: The boarders are thrown out and the old turnkeys finally drink. Every year, they say, the admiral sends someone to put one question to old Qi: 'Promise never to light the lamp again and you can go home.' And for ten years the old man has given the same answer: 'Let me go and I'll light it.' So the door stays locked, though he has never missed a meal.
column3: 跳帮手们被扔出了门，老狱卒们这才喝上酒。他们说提督每年都派人问戚老头一句：「从此不点灯，就放你回家。」十年，老头答的都是同一句：「放我回去，我就点。」所以门一直锁着，饭倒从没少过一顿。

column2: Supply Boat Cove
column3: 送饷湾

column2: In a little cove on the moor's edge waits the fast supply boat that once a month carries rice, kumquats and letters from shore out to the flagship. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen guards it: no run this month. The shore forts report a ship with Qian lanterns has entered the Sea of Fog, and the admiral has closed the sea. Third Sister Ge and Ge Qing stand at the water's edge with a basket and won't leave.
column3: 荒原边的小湾里停着一条送饷的快艇，每月一回，把岸上的米、柑子、信送去旗舰。一伙雾海弩手守着艇，说这个月不送了：岸营报来，有一条挂千字灯的船进了雾海，提督下令封海。葛三娘和葛青提着一篮东西站在湾边，不肯走。

column2: The crossbowmen are scattered and the boatman agrees to sail as usual. Ge Qing puts the little post carved with a '1' in the basket and lays old Mrs Long's letter on top. The flagship lies among the islands to the south-east, the boatman says. 'Every twenty-sixth of the eighth month the bugler stands in the bow and blows his conch westward all night long.'
column3: 弩手们被打散，艇夫答应照常开船。葛青把那根刻着「一」的小木桩放进篮子，龙老太的信压在最上面。艇夫说旗舰停在东南的岛群里，「号手每年八月廿六都站在船头，往西吹一夜海螺」。

column2: Relay Drum Mound
column3: 转鼓墩

column2: A signal mound at the moor's eastern end, the last relay from the shore forts to the fleet, with a great oxhide drum on top. Fog Sea crossbowmen hold the mound. Each day the drummer beats three rolls for all-is-well, and out in the fog the fleet beats three back. Today the drummer has just raised his sticks for a different rhythm: fast, fast, slow; fast, fast, slow.
column3: 荒原东头一座烟墩，是岸营往舰队传令的最后一站，墩上架着一面牛皮大鼓。一伙雾海弩手守着墩子，鼓手每天敲三通平安鼓，舰队那边雾里也回三通。今天鼓手刚举起槌，要敲的是另一种点子：急、急、缓，急、急、缓。

column2: You wrest the sticks away and the message never goes out. In the crossbowmen's dispatch book it reads: 'Houqianli has landed, showing Qian lanterns. Suspected to be the Qianli.' On the page before, a message from the fleet: 'Zhenwu out of grain. Send rice from shore at once. The Freshwater Isle spring runs low this year too.' Out in the fog the fleet is living no better than the coast.
column3: 鼓槌被夺下，那通鼓没敲出去。弩手的传令簿上，这一通写的是：「后千里登岸，挂千字灯，疑即千里号。」上一页是舰队传来的：「镇雾号粮尽，请岸营速送米。淡水岛的水，今年也少了。」雾里的舰队，日子不比岸上好过。

column2: The Relief Crossroads
column3: 换防路口

column2: A squad of Fog Sea marines holds the crossroads on the way to the sea, just back from garrison duty at the floating market in the east and shouting all the way: 'The Qianli's back! Everyone at the market saw it, three hundred lanterns!' Their sergeant is in a hurry to tell the admiral and wants the road closed so no one goes east.
column3: 去海边的路口驻着一队雾海水兵，刚从东边的海上集换防回来，一路走一路嚷嚷：「千里号回来了！集上的人都瞧见了，三百盏灯！」领头的什长急着去报提督，要把这条路封了，谁也不许往东走。

column2: The marines are scattered and the sergeant finally understands that the 'Qianli' the market saw was your Houqianli. He scratches his head. When the fleet hears the news, the happiest man aboard will be the bugler and the one in the hardest spot will be the admiral. 'The order says the Qianli, stop it on sight. So does he stop you or not?'
column3: 水兵被打散，什长这才弄明白，集上看见的「千里号」就是你们的后千里。他挠着头说，舰上听见这个消息，最高兴的是号手，最难办的是提督：「令上写的是千里号，见了就截。他截还是不截？」

column2: Stilt Flats
column3: 高跷滩

column2: The marsh folk don't use boats; they walk on stilts, stepping over a channel in a stride, like a flock of egrets from far off. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has taken up stilts too, tottering all over, but they're good at stealing: one hook from up high and a crab is gone from a basket. One boy of twelve walks tallest and steadiest of all, and the boarders have chased him all morning without catching a hair of him.
column3: 沼泽里的滩民不坐船，踩高跷，一步跨过一条水沟，远远看去像一群白鹭。一伙雾海跳帮手也学着踩，踩得东倒西歪，倒是很会抢：从高处一钩，就把滩民背篓里的蟹钩走。滩上有个十二岁的男孩踩得最高最稳，跳帮手追了他一早上，连根毛都没捞着。

column2: The boarders topple into the mud. The boy leaps down from his stilts and introduces himself: Bao Xiaojiang, Old Needle's grandson. Grandpa taught him that in fog you don't walk by looking but by listening. 'Surf on rock goes pff. On sand it goes shhh. On a hull it goes boom.' He wants to come with you and find his grandfather.
column3: 跳帮手们摔进了泥里。那男孩从高跷上一跃而下，自报家门：鲍小桨，鲍老针的孙子。爷爷教过他，雾里走路不能靠看，要靠听：「浪打在礁上是噗，打在沙上是沙沙，打在船上是咚。」他要跟你们走，去找爷爷。

column2: The Old Soy Yard
column3: 老酱园

column2: A soy yard at the head of the village, hundreds of crocks of bean paste set out to sun, and even in fog you can smell it. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has taken the yard and goes from crock to crock, lifting lids and dipping their fingers. The old paste-maker is frantic: 'Don't lift those lids! One drop of raw water and the whole crock's ruined!'
column3: 村头一座酱园，几百口酱缸晒在太阳底下，雾里也闻得到豆酱的香。一伙雾海跳帮手占了酱园，掀开缸盖拿手指头蘸着吃，蘸完一缸换一缸。老酱工急得直跺脚：「缸盖不能乱掀！进了生水，一缸酱就毁了！」

column2: The boarders are driven off and the lids go back on one by one. The Qianli's head cook, Old Ding, came here back then, says the paste-maker. He tasted every crock, bought the three oldest without haggling, and left a tip: sun the beans three days longer. The village has done it ever since and calls it Qianli paste. 'The Qianli left. The paste stayed.'
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，缸盖一个个盖了回去。老酱工说千里号的大厨老鼎当年来过，挨缸尝了一遍，买走最老的三缸，没讲价，留下一个方子：豆子多晒三天。村里照着做，管它叫「千里酱」。「千里号走了，酱留下了。」

column2: The Blind Pilots' School
column3: 盲舟塾

column2: A thatched hall on the moor where seven or eight blind men sit, among the best pilots on the Sea of Fog; they can't see, and so in fog they are steadier than the sighted. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has come to drag them all off to pilot the fleet, which has struck far too many rocks in the fog these last years. The old schoolmaster blocks the door with his bamboo cane, head cocked: 'Nine of you. The one on the left limps.'
column3: 荒原上一间草堂，堂里坐着七八个盲人，都是雾海上数一数二的领港，眼睛看不见，雾里反倒比明眼人稳。一伙雾海跳帮手要把他们全抓去舰上领船：舰队这几年在雾里撞礁撞得太多了。老塾师拄着竹竿挡在门口，侧着耳朵：「来了九个，左边那个腿瘸。」

column2: The boarders are beaten. In fog, says the old master, you find your way by shouting. Call into the fog: if the echo comes back fast, it's a cliff; slow, an island; none at all, open sea. Bao Laozhen was his junior in the craft. 'One shout and he could tell you how many islands lay ahead.' Xiaojiang shouts at the top of his lungs. Nothing comes back out of the fog.
column3: 跳帮手们败了。老塾师说雾里认路靠喊：冲雾里喊一声，回声来得快，是崖；来得慢，是岛；没有回声，是开阔海。鲍老针是他的师弟，「他喊一嗓子，听得出前头有几座岛」。小桨扯着嗓子喊了一声，雾里什么也没回来。

column2: The Fog Recorder's Loft
column3: 记雾楼

column2: In the loft of a small building lives an old man who draws the fog: one chart a day, where it came from, how thick, which patch thin. More than ten years of them fill the room. A gang of Fog Sea boarders means to burn them all. 'A fog chart is a sea chart, and the admiral won't have them getting out.' With his beard in their fists the old man is still arguing: 'A fog chart is not a sea chart! Fog changes by tomorrow!'
column3: 一座小楼，楼上住着个画雾的老头，每天画一张雾图：雾从哪边来、有多厚、哪一片薄，十几年画了满满一屋子。一伙雾海跳帮手要把这些图全烧了，说「雾图就是海图，提督不许流出去」。老头被揪着胡子，还在跟他们争：「雾图不是海图！雾明天就变！」

column2: The boarders are driven off and most of the charts are saved. The old man finds one from the eighth month ten years ago: in the middle of thick fog someone has added a thin line in red, with a note, 'Thin fog where the water's warm', in Bao Laozhen's hand. Where a thread of warm water runs through the cold sea, the fog above it is thinner, and the Qianli followed that warm thread.
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，雾图抢回了大半。老头翻出十年前八月的一张：一片浓雾中间，有人用朱笔添了一条细线，旁注「水暖处雾薄」，是鲍老针的笔迹。一线暖水穿过冷海，上面的雾就淡些，千里号是贴着这条暖水走的。

column2: The Centenarian's Hall
column3: 百岁堂

column2: An old ancestral hall in the middle of the village, where the oldest person in the village sits, a hundred and two, hard of hearing and with the best memory of anyone. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has taken the hall for a guardhouse and wants the old man moved. He sits in his armchair and won't budge, so they carry him out chair and all, and at the threshold the chair sticks, and now it will go neither in nor out.
column3: 村中一座老祠堂，堂上坐着村里最老的人，一百零二岁，耳朵不好，记性比谁都好。一伙雾海弩手把祠堂占了做哨所，要老人挪地方。老人坐在太师椅上一动不动，弩手连人带椅子往外抬，抬到门槛，椅子卡住了，进不得，出不得。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the chair carried back to its place. Ten years ago, the old man says, a woman shipowner came to pay her respects, a short sword at her belt, and asked whether the fog had an end. He told her what the old folk passed down: at the end of the fog there's a tower, and the people in it never grow old. She laughed. 'Good. We have a long way to go.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，椅子抬回了原处。老人说十年前有个女船主来拜过他，腰上挂一柄短刀，问他雾有没有尽头。他说老辈传下来，雾尽头有一座楼，楼里的人不会老。她笑了：「那正好，我们要走很久。」

column2: Fog Salvage Auction
column3: 捞雾拍卖

column2: In a big shed by the market, Fog Sea marines auction off whatever's been fished out of the fog: a shoe, half a sail, an ownerless chest, to the highest bidder. Today's final lot is a bronze gong. A marine strikes it once and the boom rolls out a long way. At the sound, the bidding stops, and an old man stands up: 'That's the Qianli's gong.'
column3: 集市边一座大棚，雾海水兵在这里拍卖从雾里捞上来的东西：一只鞋、半张帆、一口没主的箱子，价高者得。今天的压轴货是一面铜锣，水兵敲了一下，锣声嗡嗡地传出去老远。台下的人一听这声音就不叫价了，有个老头站起来：「这是千里号的锣。」

column2: The marines are chased off and the gong goes back to the market. 'Qianli Three' is carved on its back, and Bao Laozhen's knot is wound round the striker. That night, the old man says, gongs sounded in the fog the whole time, one stroke per ship, six ships, round after round, each one saying 'I'm here.' Then, partway through, one stroke went missing.
column3: 水兵被赶跑，铜锣还给了海上集。锣背刻着「千里·三」，锣槌上缠着鲍老针打的结。老头说那一夜雾里一直有锣声，六条船一船一声，一轮一轮地报，报的是「我在」。报着报着，就少了一声。

column2: The Sealed Oil Cellar
column3: 封油窖

column2: On the slope below the north cape lies a half-buried cellar where the Qi family kept their lamp oil; the seal on its door has rotted to paper ash. A squad of Fog Sea boarders has occupied it, pried open one crock and sniffed it, and declared it good oil, fit to ship to the fleet for the galleys. Qi Shouming comes after them on his stick, shouting, 'That's lamp oil! For the lamp! Not for frying!'
column3: 北岬脚下的荒坡上有个半埋的地窖，是戚家存灯油的地方，窖门上的封条已经烂成了纸灰。一队雾海跳帮手占了地窖，撬开一坛闻了闻，说是好油，要整坛整坛运去舰上点伙房。戚守明拄着拐追来，指着他们骂：「那是灯油！点灯的！不是炒菜的！」

column2: The boarders are driven off and not one crock is broken. Each is sealed with thick beeswax, and whale oil kept from the air has not spoiled in ten years. Shouming pats the crocks. The last time his brother came down here, he scratched a line on the wall: 'Leave three crocks. Wait for me.' Exactly three are left. The dry peat from Peat Village has been carried up too. All that remains is the climb.
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，油坛一只没碎。坛口封着厚厚的蜂蜡，鲸油不见风，十年也没坏。守明拍着坛子说，哥哥当年最后一回下窖，在墙上划了一道：「留三坛，等我。」剩下的正好三坛。泥炭村的干炭垛也扛来了，就等上塔。

column2: The Number-One Post
column3: 一字桩

column2: On the south-western headland stands a lone mooring post with a '1' carved on top, worn shiny by ropes. Every time Azhou came ashore, he tied his skiff to it. Now a Fog Sea outpost camps beside it, marines, crossbowmen and boarders, under a fresh order: 'Anyone who comes asking after this post is to be seized and sent to the flagship.'
column3: 西南的岬角上孤零零立着一根系船桩，桩顶刻着「一」，被缆绳磨得发亮。阿舟每回上岸，都把小艇系在这根桩上。如今桩边扎着一座雾海水师的哨营，水兵、弩手、跳帮手都有，奉的是新到的令：「凡有人来认此桩，拿下，押送旗舰。」

column2: The outpost is scattered. Buried at the foot of the post is an oilcloth box holding a hand-drawn chart and a letter: 'Brother, I've found where they went. At the end of the fog there's a tower. While the admiral's order stands I can't leave. If I left, who would watch this sea for them?' Ge Qing plants her little post beside it, the big one and the small one standing together.
column3: 哨营被打散。桩脚下埋着一只油布匣，装着一张手画的海图和一封信：「哥，我找到他们去的地方了，雾尽头有一座楼。提督不撤令，我不能走；我走了，谁替他们看着这片海？」葛青把小木桩插在旁边，一大一小并排站着。

column2: Fog Coast Gaol
column3: 雾岸营狱

column2: The high walls of the Fog Coast gaol stand in the mudflats, bristling with arrow towers; inside are ten years of people who broke the lights-out order. The marines, crossbowmen and boarders the admiral sent are three ranks deep and the front gate is sealed tight. But the tide is out, and the flat-folk of Mud-Sled Flats have pushed a dozen mud-horses quietly up to the back wall, where the soaked foot of it wobbles at a shove.
column3: 雾岸营狱的高墙泡在泥滩里，墙头插满了箭楼，墙里关着十年来违了灭灯令的人。提督加派的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手里外三层，前门密不透风。可退潮了，泥马滩的滩民推着十几架泥马，悄悄滑到了后墙脚下：那一段墙根泡软了，一推就晃。

column2: A stretch of the back wall collapses and the garrison breaks. The walls of the innermost cell are covered in drawn lamps, rubbed shiny by fingers. Qi Shouguang is skin and bone, but his eyes are clear. He squints a long while at the lantern in Xiaoman's hand. 'Ten years without seeing a light, and I still know one.' His first question: 'Have you scrubbed the mirror?'
column3: 后墙塌了一段，守兵溃散。最里头的牢房墙上画满了灯，被手指磨得发亮。戚守光瘦得只剩骨头，眼睛却清亮，看见小满提着的灯笼，眯了半天：「十年没见过光了，倒还认得。」他第一句问的是：「灯镜擦了没有？」

column2: The Dispatch Jetty
column3: 报讯码头

column2: The moment the gaol falls, a few Fog Sea boarders race to the little jetty behind it and leap into a fast boat to carry word into the fog: the prisoner is out, Houqianli has come. They fumble at the mooring line, and the more they hurry the less it comes loose. Qi Shouguang walks over leaning on Xiaoman's shoulder, watches them, and, to everyone's surprise, waves a hand.
column3: 营狱一破，几个雾海跳帮手冲到营后的小码头，跳上一条快艇，要去雾里给舰队报信：犯人跑了，后千里到了。他们手忙脚乱解缆绳，越急越解不开。戚守光拄着小满的肩走过来，看着他们，反倒摆了摆手。

column2: The boarders are knocked off their boat, but Shouguang has them let go. 'Go and tell Cen Dingbo I've gone home to light the lamp.' That night, he tells you, the Qianli asked him by lamp, 'Where is water?' and he answered, 'Freshwater Isle, go east.' The ship's owner Shen Du signalled with her own hands. 'Steadier than mine, her lamp.'
column3: 跳帮手们被打下了艇，守光却让把他们放了：「去告诉岑定波，我回北岬点灯了。」他对你们说，那夜千里号拿灯问他一句：「何处有水？」他答：「淡水岛，往东。」后来是船主沈渡亲手打的灯语，「灯打得比我还稳」。

column2: The Boat in the Reed Shed
column3: 芦棚藏舟

column2: Hidden in a reed shed is a small boat with a sharp bow, painted the grey-white of fog. It's called Needle, and it was Bao Laozhen's. Bao Xiaojiang wants to push it into the water and go east alone to find his grandfather. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen hears the noise and surrounds the shed to burn the boat: 'Fleet's orders. Not one more boat on the Sea of Fog.' Xiaojiang spreads his arms in front of the bow.
column3: 芦苇棚里藏着一条小船，船头尖尖，船身漆成雾一样的灰白，叫「针」，是鲍老针的船。鲍小桨想把它推下水，自己去东边找爷爷。一伙雾海弩手听见动静，围住棚子要把船烧了：「舰上有令，雾海里不许多一条船。」小桨张开胳膊挡在船头。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the boat is saved. Auntie Bao arrives and doesn't scold her grandson; she just tucks a parcel of food into the boat. 'Your grandpa left just like this.' It's settled: Needle will be towed behind Houqianli, and Xiaojiang will sit in Houqianli's bow and listen to the surf.
column3: 弩手们被赶跑，船保住了。鲍婶赶来，没骂孙子，只往船舱里塞了一包干粮：「你爷爷当年也是这么走的。」说定了：「针」拴在后千里船尾一起走，小桨坐在后千里的船头听浪。

column2: Black Sand Spit
column3: 黑沙嘴

column2: A spit of sand runs from the marsh into the sea, the sand glossy black and heavy underfoot. Axi sets her compass down on it and the needle swings round twice and points at her own feet. In the cove behind the spit lie ten years of cargo from ships that sank here, and the pirates' best fighters are camped on it, waiting for ships with lying needles to wreck themselves. They guard the heap like a mountain of gold.
column3: 沼泽伸进海里一道沙嘴，沙子黑得发亮，踩上去沉甸甸的。阿汐把罗盘往沙上一放，指针转了两圈，指向了自己脚底下。沙嘴背后的小湾里堆满了十年来撞沉的船货，海贼的精锐在这里扎了营，专等迷了针的船自己撞上来。他们守着这堆货，像守着一座金山。

column2: The pirates are beaten. Gong Modou dips a lodestone into the sand and lifts it out furred with black grains: crumbs of magnetite, with whole beds of iron-stone beneath, and any compass that comes here gets dragged off true. On a post at the cove mouth Bao Laozhen has left his mark, six cuts side by side: 'Six ships through the Black Sand together.'
column3: 海贼败了。龚墨斗拿一块吸铁石往沙里一探，提起来，毛茸茸裹了一层黑沙：这是磁铁矿的碎粒，沙底下还有成片的铁石，罗盘到这里就被拽偏了。湾口一根木桩上刻着鲍老针的记号，六道刻痕并排：「六船齐过黑沙。」

column2: Crab Racecourse
column3: 赛蟹场

column2: A flat patch outside the market marked with lines of white lime, where dozens of big mud crabs scuttle sideways and the first across the line wins. A squad of Fog Sea marines has taken over the course and bets the market traders' goods, and whenever a crab runs crooked they say, 'Doesn't count, run it again.' The old crab-keeper squats to one side, fanning his crabs in sorrow.
column3: 集市外一块平地，地上画着一道道白灰线，几十只大青蟹横着爬，哪只先过线哪只赢。一队雾海水兵把赛场占了，押的是集上商户的货，蟹爬歪了就说「蟹不算，重来」。养蟹的老汉蹲在旁边，心疼地给他的蟹扇风。

column2: The marines are driven off and the crabs go back in their baskets. Every year, the old man says, the flagship's bugler comes ashore and lays one bet, always on the same crab, which he calls Qianli, and it always loses, and he laughs. Last year, after placing his bet, he asked: 'Bao Laozhen's empty skiff. Have you ever seen it?'
column3: 水兵被赶走，蟹放回了篓里。老汉说旗舰上的号手每年上岸都来押一注，回回押同一只蟹，叫「千里」，回回输，输了就笑。去年他押完还问老汉：「鲍老针那条空舢板，你见没见过？」

column2: The Unfinished Game
column3: 残局廊

column2: Under the eaves of a fishing village stands a stone table with a game of xiangqi on it, half played, the pieces thick with ten years of dust, never touched. A squad of Fog Sea marines finds the table in their way and means to sweep the board off and smash the table for paving. The old fisherman who keeps it spreads his arms over the board: 'You can't! The game isn't finished!'
column3: 渔村的一条廊檐下摆着一张石桌，桌上一盘象棋，下到一半，棋子上落满了灰，十年没人动过。一队雾海水兵嫌石桌碍路，要把棋盘掀了，把桌子砸了垫路。守棋的老渔翁张开两只手护着棋盘：「掀不得！这盘棋还没下完！」

column2: The marines are driven off. His opponent, the old fisherman says, was the Qianli's pilot, a man named Xu. Halfway through the game the ship was ready to sail, and he said, 'Leave it. I'll finish it when I'm back.' Axi stares at the board a long time and recognises her father's style: sacrifice the chariot first, then check. She reaches out a hand and draws it back. 'He can make his own move.'
column3: 水兵被赶走。老渔翁说，对面那一方是千里号的领港，姓许，下到一半船要开了，他说：「留着，回来下完。」阿汐盯着棋盘看了很久，认出这是她爹的路数，先弃车，后将军。她伸出手，又缩了回来：「等他自己来走。」

column2: The Potato Still
column3: 番薯烧坊

column2: A distillery on the moor that makes spirit from sweet potatoes, strong enough to burn. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has taken it over and drunk itself silly; spent mash covers the yard, the chickens have eaten it and are drunk too, and staggering birds weave across the yard. The owner's wife chases the crossbowmen with a broom, and they're too drunk to hold their crossbows steady: a morning's shooting has hit three wine jars.
column3: 荒原上一座烧酒坊，拿番薯酿酒，酒烈得能点着。一伙雾海弩手占了酒坊，喝得东倒西歪，酒糟扔了一地，鸡啄了酒糟也醉，满院子鸡走着醉步。坊主的老婆拎着扫帚追着弩手打，弩手醉得连弩都端不稳，射了一上午，射中了三只酒坛。

column2: The crossbowmen are swept out the door and the still steams again. On the wall hangs a board scored with three hundred marks. The Qianli's sailors drank here three days, and when they left they said, 'Each of us owes a bowl. When we're back, the whole village drinks on us.' The owner seals one jar of old spirit every year. 'When they come back, not one bowl short.'
column3: 弩手被扫地出门，酒坊又冒起了蒸汽。墙上挂着一块木板，刻满了三百道道：千里号的水手在这儿喝过三天，临走说：「每人欠一碗，回来请全村喝。」坊主每年封一坛老酒，「等他们回来，一碗都不能少」。

column2: In the still you find the crossbowmen's hoard: twenty jars of spirit, a crock of mash-cured fish, two sacks of dried sweet potato, and an old hen too drunk to stand, stolen by the crossbowmen; the owner says take it for soup.
column3: 坊里抄出弩手囤的二十坛烧酒、一缸酒糟鱼、两袋番薯干，还有一只醉得站不起来的老母鸡，坊主说是弩手偷来的，就送你们炖汤。

column2: Every time you pass, the owner fills a flask of warm spirit for you and slips you a packet of roasted sweet-potato strips. 'Cold in the fog. One mouthful. No more.'
column3: 每次路过，坊主都灌一壶热酒给你们暖身子，又塞一包烤番薯干：「雾里冷，喝一口，不许多喝。」

column2: The Fritter Stall
column3: 油条摊

column2: A little stall frying dough sticks at the market crossroads, run by a hunchbacked old woman who dozes as she fries. A squad of Fog Sea marines eats a whole basket without paying, complains the oil is stale and kicks the pot over. The old woman doesn't even mind. She stoops, picks up the fritters, blows the dust off and sets them back in the basket. 'Safe travels, sirs.'
column3: 集市路口一个炸油条的小摊，摊主是个驼背老太太，一边炸一边打瞌睡。一队雾海水兵吃了一筐油条不给钱，还嫌油不新，把油锅踢翻了。老太太也不恼，弯腰捡起油条，吹吹灰，又摆回了筐里：「军爷慢走。」

column2: As the marines scatter, one grabs the cash box and bolts. Without looking, the old woman flicks a long chopstick and pins his sleeve to a post ten paces off. She is Auntie Bao's elder sister, and in her youth she ran boats through the fog in the dark; it was she who taught Old Needle to sail by night. 'The day he left he told me, I'll take them to the end of the fog and come back. That man never said a thing he didn't mean.'
column3: 水兵溃散时，有一个抢了钱匣就跑。老太太甩出一根长筷，隔着十步把他的袖子钉在了木柱上。她是鲍婶的大姐，年轻时在雾海上摸黑跑船，老针的夜航是她教的。「他走那天说，送到雾尽头就回来。他从不说空话。」

column2: Tug-of-War Green
column3: 拔河坪

column2: A wide green at the village gate, and hanging from the beam of the shrine beside it a hemp rope thicker than a bowl's mouth, tied with sixty knots, a little wooden tag on each. A large force of Fog Sea marines, crossbowmen and boarders has camped on the green to take the rope for an anchor cable, since the fleet's are nearly rotted through. The village's strong men have hold of the other end and won't let go.
column3: 村口一片大草坪，坪边的社庙梁上挂着一根粗麻绳，比碗口还粗，绳上打着六十个结，每个结上拴着一块小木牌。一大队雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手驻在坪上，要把这根绳子拿去当锚缆：舰队的缆绳烂得差不多了。村里的壮汉们抓着绳子另一头，不撒手。

column2: The navy is driven off and the rope goes back on its beam. Ten years ago, sixty of the Qianli's sailors had a tug-of-war against sixty of their men. The sailors were just about to win when Old Ding the cook banged a pot at the edge of the green and shouted 'Dinner!', and all sixty let go at once. Each tag carries one sailor's name. 'They said they'd come back for a rematch.'
column3: 水师被赶走，绳子挂回了梁上。十年前千里号的六十个水手跟村里六十条汉子拔过一场河，眼看要赢，大厨老鼎一敲锅喊「开饭」，六十人一齐撒了手。每个结上的木牌都刻着一个水手的名字，「说好回来再拔一场」。

column2: The Doctor's Shrine
column3: 女医龛

column2: A tiny stone shrine on the hillside behind the village, and in it no god but a medicine chest, with eggs, red dates and a child's tiger-head shoes laid before it. A squad of Fog Sea marines has come to smash it, saying the villagers 'worship the Qianli, contrary to military orders'. A crowd of women surrounds the shrine shoulder to shoulder, some with babies in their arms.
column3: 村后山坡上一座小小的石龛，龛里供的不是神，是一只药箱，箱前摆着鸡蛋、红枣、小孩的虎头鞋。一队雾海水兵上来要砸龛，说村里人「供奉千里号，有违军令」。一群妇人把龛围得严严实实，有人怀里还抱着孩子。

column2: The marines are driven off and the women set out fresh eggs. Ten years ago smallpox broke out in the village, and the Qianli's doctor, Madam Liu, came ashore and went three days without sleep and didn't let one child die. When she left she said of the chest: 'I'll be back in a year to restock it.' The children saved that year are around ten now, and each has left a pair of shoes at the shrine.
column3: 水兵被赶走，妇人们给龛前换了新鸡蛋。十年前村里闹痘，千里号上的柳医娘子上岸三天没合眼，一个孩子也没让死。走时她把药箱留下：「一年后回来补药。」那年救下的孩子，如今都十来岁了，每人往龛前放过一双鞋。

column2: The Impound Yard
column3: 扣船坞

column2: A stretch of waste ground crammed with small boats, sampans, fishing skiffs, bamboo rafts, all impounded by the Fog Sea navy, lying keel-up in rows like shoes set out to dry. Crossbowmen guard the yard and won't let a single boat be claimed. The local children turned it into a playground long ago, hopping from hull to hull; the crossbowmen chase one and ten run.
column3: 一片荒地上搁满了小船，舢板、渔舟、竹排，全是雾海水师扣下的，船底朝天，一排排像晒着的鞋。弩手们守着船坞，一条船都不许人领回。附近的孩子早拿这里当了游乐场，在船底上跳来跳去，弩手追一个，跑十个。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and owners come to claim their boats. In the impound book for the ninth month ten years ago: 'One small skiff, unmanned, drifted in from the fog. Forty taels of silver within, to the levy store. One bamboo tube, unopened, returned to the fisherfolk.' That empty skiff drifted back from the east. It was the one Bao Laozhen had left in.
column3: 弩手们被赶走，船主们来认船。扣船簿上十年前九月有一行：「无人小舢板一条，自雾中漂来。内有银四十两，入饷库；竹筒一个，未开，发还渔户。」那条空舢板是从东边漂回来的，鲍老针当年就坐着它走。

column2: Warm Water Rock
column3: 暖水矶

column2: A big rock on the shore, and every morning before dawn a white-haired old woman goes in for a swim, winter included, and comes out steaming. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has put a post on the rock and forbidden swimming, since deserters keep swimming out from here to pirate ships. The old woman swims anyway. When they aim at her she rolls onto her back, floats, and spits water at them.
column3: 海边一块大礁石，每天天不亮，就有个白发老太太下水游一圈，冬天也不例外，游完上岸还冒着热气。一伙雾海弩手在礁上设了哨，不许人下海：逃兵常从这里游去海贼船。老太太照游不误，弩手拿弩指着她，她就在水里翻个身，仰着漂，冲他们吐水。

column2: With the crossbowmen gone the old woman pulls on her clothes. All the water in the Sea of Fog cuts to the bone, she says, except one strip below this rock, which is warm. 'Water that comes up from the south. It's warm.' Xiaojiang puts his arm in and yelps in surprise. The warm strip runs north-east from here, round Freshwater Isle, then bends south-east, and along it the fog thins to a crack.
column3: 弩手被赶走，老太太披上衣裳说，满雾海的水都扎骨头，只有这块礁下面一线是温的：「从南边来的水，暖。」小桨把胳膊伸进去，惊得叫起来。那条暖水从这里往东北淌，绕过淡水岛，再折向东南，雾就顺着它薄了一线。

column2: Six-Stone Beach
column3: 六桩滩

column2: Six great stones in a row along the shore, each with a deep groove worn by a mooring line and carved with a number, one to six: ten years ago the Qianli's six boats were tied up here. A gang of Fog Sea boarders is hammering the numbers off, one stone after another, chips and sparks flying. At the sixth stone the hammer breaks its edge.
column3: 海边一溜六块大石头，每块上都有一道深深的缆槽，刻着「一」到「六」：十年前千里号的六条小艇就系在这里。一伙雾海跳帮手正拿铁锤凿石头上的字，凿一个，换一块，叮叮当当，火星乱溅。凿到第六块，锤子崩了个口。

column2: The boarders are driven off. Besides the 'six', the sixth stone bears a line of small characters the hammer couldn't touch, the stone is too hard: 'Number Six covers the rear. Shen.' So Number Six's ramming of the fleet that night was the owner's plan from the start. Axi runs her fingers over the words. 'She planned everything except whether her own ships would make it back.'
column3: 跳帮手被赶走。第六块石头上除了「六」，还刻着一行小字，凿不动，石头太硬：「六号断后。沈。」原来那一夜六号横撞舰队，是船主早就定下的。阿汐摸着那几个字说：「她什么都算好了，就是没算自己的船回不回得来。」

column2: The Fogwatch Light
column3: 望雾灯

column2: On the tip of the north cape stands a stone lighthouse, dark for ten years, its door rusted shut and its steps green with moss. At its foot waits the last company of the Lights-Out Camp, marines, crossbowmen and boarders, under the admiral's standing order: 'Not one lamp on the north cape.' They know the gaol has fallen and the prisoner is coming. They stand three ranks deep, every spearpoint aimed at the path up to the tower.
column3: 北岬尖上一座石砌的灯塔，黑了十年，塔门锈死，石阶上长满了青苔。塔下扎着灭灯营最后一支人马，雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手，奉的是提督的死令：「北岬一灯不许点。」他们也知道营狱破了、犯人来了，排成三列，枪尖都对着那条上塔的小路。

column2: The garrison scatters. Xiaoman opens the tower door with the copper key and Shouguang climbs step by step, Shouming carrying the oil, the Peat Village folk carrying dry peat. The scrubbed mirror goes back in its place, the whale oil catches, and a beam drives straight into the fog: three bright, one dark, three times over. For a long while nothing stirs. Then, far off to the south-east, three lamps light up side by side. Shouguang grips the rail and at last says, 'That's the boy. He remembers.'
column3: 守兵散了。小满拿铜钥匙捅开塔门，守光一级级爬上去，守明扛着油坛，泥炭村的人扛着干炭。灯镜擦亮了，装回原位，鲸油点着，一道光直直刺进雾里，三明一暗，打了三遍。雾里很久没有动静。然后，极远的东南方，亮起三盏灯，并排挂着。守光扶着栏杆，半天才说：「是那小子。他还记得。」

column2: The Shrine Beam
column3: 土地梁

column2: A little earth-god shrine at the edge of the village, its ridge beam replaced ten years ago and replaced so well that not a drop has leaked since. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has climbed the roof to pull the beam out: it's fine ironwood, and the fleet wants it for a mast. They've moved the earth god outside into the rain, and the old shrine keeper stands holding an umbrella over him.
column3: 村边一座小土地庙，屋脊上的大梁是十年前换的，换得极好，十年没漏过一滴雨。一伙雾海弩手爬上屋顶要拆梁：梁是上好的铁梨木，舰队要拿去做桅杆。土地公被他们挪到门外淋雨，老庙祝撑着伞，替土地公遮着。

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off the roof. Carved on the underside of the beam is a little boat and a line of words: 'Mended by Old Tenon, carpenter of the Qianli. If the roof doesn't leak, the ship won't.' Once the beam was in, says the old keeper, the carpenter slept a night in the shrine and woke saying it was the soundest sleep he'd had since he went to sea.
column3: 弩手被赶下屋顶。梁底下刻着一只小船，旁边一行字：「千里号木作老榫修。屋不漏，船不漏。」老庙祝说那木匠换完梁，在庙里睡了一觉，醒来说，这是他上船以来睡得最踏实的一回。

column2: The Humming Stage
column3: 哼歌台

column2: The village opera stage has been taken over as barracks by a large force of Fog Sea marines, crossbowmen and boarders, their uniforms drying on the boards, their horses tied to the pillars. One song is banned, and any family whose child sings it is fined in rice: the song came ashore from the Qianli ten years ago. So the children don't sing it. They hum it, until the whole village is full of the tune, and before long the marines are humming it too.
column3: 村里的戏台被一大队雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手占了当营房，台上晾着号衣，台柱上拴着马。村里不许唱一支歌，谁家孩子唱，就罚谁家交米：那支歌是十年前从千里号上传下来的。孩子们就不唱，改成哼，哼得满村都是调子，水兵们听着听着，自己也哼起来了。

column2: The marines are driven off and the children climb onto the stage and sing out loud: 'A stretch of water, a stretch of fog, three hundred lamps go on ahead; look back, you who come after, the lamps stay lit, the road's not lonely.' A pipa-playing sailor from the Qianli taught it to them. 'He said the owner wrote it, and we should sing it for whoever came after.'
column3: 水兵被赶走，孩子们爬上戏台，放开嗓子唱：「一程水，一程雾，三百盏灯走前路；回头看，后来人，灯不灭，路不孤。」教歌的是千里号上一个弹琵琶的水手，「他说是船主写的，要我们唱给后来的人听」。

column2: A Boy Called Qianli
column3: 名叫千里

column2: A nine-year-old boy races along the field banks with a gang of Fog Sea boarders behind him, yelling that they'll catch 'Qianli'. Qianli is the boy's name; he's the village blacksmith's son. The admiral won't have the Qianli spoken of, so the boarders mean to police names too and insist he be called Baili instead. The boy shouts back over his shoulder as he runs: 'My dad named me! It's none of your business!'
column3: 一个九岁的男孩在田埂上飞跑，后面追着一伙雾海跳帮手，嚷嚷着要抓「千里」。男孩就叫千里，是村里铁匠的儿子。提督不许人提千里号，跳帮手便连人名也要管，非要他改叫「百里」。男孩边跑边回头骂：「我爹起的名，你们管不着！」

column2: The boarders are chased off, and the boy's mother, A-Ling, comes out to thank you and blushes. Ten years ago she was sweet on a sailor from the Qianli named Zheng, who said he'd be back in a year. She waited a year and married the blacksmith, and it was the blacksmith who chose the name. 'He said if that young man ever comes back and hears it, it won't hurt him so much.'
column3: 跳帮手被赶跑，孩子他娘阿菱出来道谢，脸红了一下。十年前她和千里号上一个姓郑的水手好过，他说一年就回。她等了一年，嫁了铁匠，名字是铁匠起的：「他说那后生要是回来，看见这名字，也就不难过了。」

column2: The Deposit Store
column3: 寄存栈

column2: The floating market's oldest deposit store, stone walls and an iron door, keeping goods for ships on long voyages, a year or ten, released only against a receipt. Its door is now held by the fiercest company in the Fog Sea navy. The fleet is out of grain and the admiral wants the store opened for rice, but the old storekeeper said the goods have an owner and go only against a receipt, and swallowed the key. Marines, crossbowmen and boarders are watching him, waiting for the key to come out.
column3: 海上集最老的一座寄存栈，石墙铁门，替远行的船存货，存一年也行，存十年也行，凭条取货。如今栈门被雾海水师最凶的一支人马占着：舰上断了粮，提督要开栈取米，可老栈主说，栈里的东西有主，凭条才给，把钥匙吞进了肚子。水兵、弩手、跳帮手守着他，等钥匙出来。

column2: The guards are beaten and you take the door off its hinges. Inside stand three hundred crocks of pickled greens, mud seals intact, each labelled: 'For the Qianli's return voyage. One crock a head.' At the end sits one smaller crock marked 'Pilot'. The storekeeper, clutching his stomach, says: 'Owner Shen paid cash. She said people on the way home want something salty more than anything.'
column3: 守兵败了，你们把门卸了。栈里码着三百坛腌菜，坛口泥封完好，坛上贴着条子：「千里号回程用，一人一坛。」最边上还有一坛小的，写着「领港」。老栈主捂着肚子说：「沈船主付的现钱，说回程的人最想吃口咸的。」

column2: The Keepsake Store
column3: 遗物仓

column2: A great storehouse on the moor sealed with the admiral's own seal, guarded by a large force of Fog Sea marines, crossbowmen and boarders, more tightly than any granary. For ten years everything along the coast with any tie to the Qianli has been collected into it: a pot, a needle, a pair of straw sandals, a rattle drum. The villagers assume it was all burned long ago, and no one dares ask.
column3: 荒原上一座大仓，仓门贴着提督的封条，一大队雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手守在门口，比守粮仓还严。十年来，沿岸凡是跟千里号沾边的东西，都收进了这座仓：一只锅，一根针，一双草鞋，一面拨浪鼓。村里人都以为里头早烧光了，没人敢问。

column2: The guards are beaten and the doors opened. Everything inside is laid out in neat rows, each item tagged: 'Ladle of Old Ding, cook of the Qianli', 'Needle of Doctor Liu', 'Rattle drum given by the sailor Zheng'. On the wall hangs a handwritten order from the admiral: 'These are the Qianli's belongings. Keep them. Destroy nothing. Hold them until it returns.'
column3: 守兵败了，仓门打开，东西一件件摆得整整齐齐，每件都系着签：「千里号大厨老鼎之勺」「柳医之针」「水手郑某所赠拨浪鼓」。墙上贴着提督的手令：「此皆千里号遗物，存而勿毁，待其回。」

column2: Dark-Sailing Stockade
column3: 暗航寨

column2: A stockade on the shore that never lights a lamp. Its people walk without a sound, talk with their hands, and wrap their oars in cloth: a dark-sailing gang that runs boats through the fog unseen. The Fog Sea navy has camped two rings around it to take them all, but in fog the gang comes and goes like smoke, and in half a month of siege the marines, crossbowmen and boarders haven't laid a hand on one of them.
column3: 海边一座不点灯的寨子，寨里的人走路不出声，说话打手势，船桨裹着布，是专在雾里摸黑跑船的暗航帮。雾海水师的人马在寨外扎了两层营，要把他们一网打尽，可暗航帮在雾里来去无影，水兵、弩手、跳帮手围了半个月，连个人影都没摸着。

column2: The navy's camps are broken, and only then does the gang's leader show himself, saying in signs that they learned night sailing from the Bao family. Once they felt their way south-east along the warm water and came to a place where the fog glowed of itself, the sea lay flat as a mirror, and towers showed faintly in the distance. 'We didn't dare go further. We turned back. Old Needle dared.'
column3: 水师的营被打散，暗航帮的头领这才现身，比划着手势说：夜航是跟鲍家学的。他们顺着暖水往东南摸过一回，摸到一处地方，雾自己发着亮，海面平得像镜子，远处隐隐有楼台。「我们不敢再往前，就回来了。老针敢。」

column2: Placard Cliff
column3: 举牌崖

column2: A high cliff on the coast where Fog Sea crossbowmen watch Freshwater Isle across the strait day and night. It's the fleet's water source, and any boat that goes near gets shot at. The islanders aren't even allowed to shout across, so they hold up placards on the shore. Today's placard over there reads, in big characters: 'Water salty again.'
column3: 海边一处高崖，崖上的雾海弩手日夜盯着海对面的淡水岛。那是舰队的水源，谁的船靠近就射谁。岛上的人隔着海喊话也不许，只能在岸边举牌子。今天对岸举起的牌子上写着三个大字：「水又咸。」

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off the cliff, and across the water a new placard goes up: 'Cat still here.' There's an old cat on the island nobody can catch, says the old sentry; fleet men tried to carry it aboard and got their faces raked for it. 'The Qianli left it behind. The islanders treat it like treasure.'
column3: 弩手被赶下崖，对岸又换了一块牌子：「猫还在。」崖上的老哨兵说，岛上有只老猫谁也抓不住，舰上的人想抱它上船，被它挠了个满脸花。「它是千里号丢下的，岛上的人当它是宝。」

column2: The Sealed Qian Cave
column3: 封千洞

column2: A lonely cave on the shore, its mouth sealed with a great stone carved with the character Qian. The Fog Sea navy has kept a picked company on it for ten years, forbidden to open it or let anyone near. No one knows what's inside, and the admiral said, 'What we don't know, we guard.' The marines, crossbowmen and boarders before the cave have polished their weapons bright, and after ten years of waiting they finally have a fight.
column3: 海边一处荒僻的石洞，洞口用大石封着，石上刻着一个「千」字。雾海水师派了一支精兵守了十年，不许开，也不许人靠近：谁也不知道里头是什么，提督说「不知道的，就守着」。洞前的水兵、弩手、跳帮手兵器擦得锃亮，等了十年，总算等来了一场仗。

column2: The picked company is beaten and the stone rolled back. Inside are a spare anchor, two rolls of new sail and a coil of anchor cable, and on the anchor hangs a wooden tag in the owner Shen Du's hand: 'For the voyage home. If we don't come back, for whoever comes after.' Gong Modou runs a hand over the canvas and laughs. 'Houqianli was just short a sail.'
column3: 精兵败了，封石推开。洞里是一只备用大锚、两卷新帆、一盘锚缆，锚上挂着一块木牌，是船主沈渡的字：「回程用。若我们不回，给后来者用。」龚墨斗摸着帆布笑了：「后千里正缺一面帆。」

column2: The Singing Crocks
column3: 唱坛坊

column2: A pickling works with hundreds of great crocks in the yard, run by a big, cheerful woman who sings as she packs the greens, saying they only take the brine if they've heard a song. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has her pickling for the fleet and tells her to stop singing and work. When she doesn't sing, the greens won't pack tight, and when they won't pack tight, the crossbowmen shout. The yard is all salt smell and swearing.
column3: 一座腌菜坊，院里排着几百口大坛，坊主是个胖大嫂，腌菜时一边压菜一边唱歌，说菜听了歌才入味。一伙雾海弩手逼她给舰队腌菜，嫌她唱歌耽误工夫，要她闭嘴干活。她不唱，菜就压不实；压不实，弩手就骂。院子里一片咸味和骂声。

column2: With the crossbowmen gone, the woman sings again. The three hundred crocks in the deposit store are hers. When Owner Shen came to order them, she sang, and Shen hummed along. 'She said pickles for the way home should cure a long time, the longer the better.' The woman counts on her fingers. 'Ten years. They ought to be just right.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，大嫂又唱上了。寄存栈那三百坛就是她腌的：沈船主来订菜，她唱了一首，沈船主跟着哼。「她说回程的菜要腌得久一点，久了才香。」大嫂掰着手指算：「腌了十年，该香透了。」

column2: Cat-Watch Rock
column3: 望猫礁

column2: An old ferrywoman sits on the rocks by the sea; Fog Sea boarders have impounded her boat, so all she can do is sit and watch the water. Every eighth month, she says, an old cat on Freshwater Isle goes out to the westernmost rock and crouches there all day, looking this way.
