The boarders say she's mad and want her off the rocks before she 'calls up the Qianli's ghosts'.
column3: 海边礁石上坐着个摆渡的老婆婆，船被雾海跳帮手扣了，只好天天坐在礁上看海。她说每年八月，海对面淡水岛上有只老猫，会跑到岛子最西头的石头上，蹲一整天，朝这边望。跳帮手说她疯了，要把她从礁上撵走，省得她「替千里号招魂」。

column2: The boarders are driven off and her boat returned. Ten years ago, when the Qianli was taking on water at the island, she was ferrying people and saw a ginger cat leap off the ship while the whole crew shouted after it, 'Captain! Captain!' It never looked back. They called the cat Captain because it always slept in Owner Shen's chair.
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，老婆婆的船也领回来了。她说十年前千里号在岛上取水，她渡过人，看见一只黄猫从船上跳下来，满船的人在后头喊「船长！船长！」它头也不回。猫叫「船长」，是因为它总睡在沈船主的椅子上。

column2: Dinner Over the Rail
column3: 隔栏饭

column2: A wooden fence cuts the road in two. Inside is a squad of Fog Sea marines; outside, a crowd of old women with food baskets. The marines are sons of market families pressed into the navy and forbidden to leave camp; the mothers are forbidden to enter, so they pass meals over the rail. Today the marines have orders to stop that and seal the road for good, and the mothers hold their baskets over their heads and won't give an inch.
column3: 一道木栅栏把路拦腰截断，栏里是一队雾海水兵，栏外是一群提着饭篮的老太太。水兵都是集上人家的儿子，被拉进水师的，不许出营；娘们不许进营，只好隔着栏杆递饭。今天水兵接了令，不许再递，要把路彻底封死，娘们把饭篮举过头顶，谁也不肯退。

column2: The marines are beaten and the mothers rush in, hugging their sons and slapping them and weeping. A young marine holding his rice bowl tells you that since Old Needle left, no one in the fleet can find the warm strip, and they lose a ship on the rocks every year. A few days ago the admiral issued an order: 'Seek out the Bao family's heir and invite him to pilot the flagship.' It says 'invite'.
column3: 水兵败了，娘们一拥而上，抱着儿子又打又哭。一个年轻水兵捧着饭碗说：老针走后，舰上没人认得暖水那一线，船在雾里一年撞一条。提督前几天下了令：「访鲍家后人，请上旗舰领港。」说的是「请」。

column2: The Invitation Boat
column3: 请人艇

column2: A fast boat hung with red silk waits on the shore, an empty chair set in it with the word 'Pilot' pasted on its back. A squad of Fog Sea marines forms two lines on the beach and bows to Xiaojiang: 'Young Master Bao, the admiral invites you aboard.' The bowing done, and finding him unwilling, they reach out to drag him. Xiaojiang wraps his arms round Houqianli's bollard and won't let go.
column3: 海边停着一条挂红绸的快艇，艇上摆着一张空椅子，椅背上贴着「领港」两个字。一队雾海水兵在滩上排成两行，见了小桨就上来作揖：「小鲍爷，提督请您上船。」作完揖，见他不肯，就伸手来拽。小桨抱住后千里的缆桩不撒手。

column2: The marines are driven back into their boat, chair and all. 'Grandpa piloted the Qianli,' Xiaojiang pants. 'He doesn't pilot the ones who stop it.' The marines' leader isn't even angry. Over his shoulder he says, 'The admiral guessed you'd say that. He said ten years ago he should have invited the Bao family, not arrested them.'
column3: 水兵们被赶回了艇上，椅子也搬走了。小桨喘着气说：「爷爷领千里号，不领截千里号的。」领头的水兵倒也没生气，回头说了句：「提督也是这么猜的。他说，鲍家的人，十年前就该请，不该抓。」

column2: The Ferry Book Shed
column3: 渡簿棚

column2: There is only one ferry landing for Freshwater Isle, with a bamboo shed on it where the ferry book hangs and every crossing is logged. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has taken the landing, with every boat tied to their posts. A crossing costs three dou of rice, and after paying you wait for the admiral's permit, which comes once every three months.
column3: 去淡水岛的渡口只此一处，渡口上一座竹棚，棚里挂着渡簿，过海的人都要登记。一伙雾海跳帮手占了渡口，所有的船都拴在他们的桩上，过海一趟交三斗米，交了还得等提督的批文，批文三个月来一回。

column2: The boarders are driven off and the ferries cast loose. The old ferry book, at the eighth month ten years ago: 'Twenty-fourth day. Six boats of the Qianli to Freshwater Isle for water, three days there and back. Pilot Xu, owner Shen, sailors various, all paid the fare.' One line below: 'One cat. Unpaid.'
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，渡船解了缆。老渡簿翻到十年前八月：「廿四日，千里号小艇六条往淡水岛取水，往返三日。领船者许，船主沈，水手若干，皆付渡钱。」底下一行：「猫一只，未付。」

column2: Drum-Fishing Bay
column3: 敲罟湾

column2: Dozens of small boats ring the bay in a great circle, the fishermen hammering their gunwales with mallets, a rattle of wood driving the yellow croakers into the nets. A gang of Fog Sea boarders races into the ring in fast boats, grabs fish, slashes the nets and makes off. The head fisherman stamps on his deck in fury: 'The croakers only come these few days a year!'
column3: 海湾里几十条小船围成一个大圈，渔民拿木槌敲着船帮，梆梆梆响成一片，把黄鱼往网里赶。一伙雾海跳帮手驾着快艇冲进圈里，抢了鱼就跑，把网也划破了。领头的渔老大气得直跺船板：「黄鱼一年只来这几天！」

column2: The boarders are scattered, the nets mended and the fish driven in. In summer, the head fisherman says, the croakers come along the warm water, and at night they call, a croak-croak-croak you can hear with your ear to the planking. That year Bao Laozhen led the way with his ear on the boards. 'Wherever the fish are calling, that's where the warm water is.'
column3: 跳帮手被打散，网补上了，鱼也赶进去了。渔老大说，夏天黄鱼顺着暖水来，夜里会叫，咕咕咕地，贴着船板就听得见。鲍老针那年就是贴着船板听鱼叫领的路：「鱼往哪儿叫，暖水就在哪儿。」

column2: Lychee Slope
column3: 荔枝坡

column2: At the moor's end a lone lychee tree grows on the slope, conspicuous on this bare ground, a bamboo fence around it. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen guards it as the fleet's tree; every year, every fruit goes to the flagship. The village children circle the fence in longing, swallowing at every lap.
column3: 荒原尽头的坡上孤零零长着一棵荔枝树，在这片荒地上扎眼得很，树下围了一圈竹篱笆。一伙雾海弩手守着树，说这是舰队的树，每年结了果，一颗不少全送去旗舰。村里的孩子馋得在篱笆外头转，转一圈，咽一口口水。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the children finally get a taste. The tree was planted by the Qianli's sailors from a lychee stone brought from Quanzhou: 'When it fruits, we'll be back.' Seven years ago it fruited for the first time. The villagers picked the first lychee and put it down in salt in a jar, one each year since. There are seven in the jar now.
column3: 弩手被赶走，孩子们总算尝了一颗。树是千里号的水手种的，种的是泉州带来的荔枝核：「等它结果，我们就回来。」七年前它头一回结果，村里人摘下第一颗，拿盐腌着存在罐里，一年一颗，如今罐里有七颗。

column2: The Sky-Gun Fort
column3: 朝天炮城

column2: A small stone gun fort sits in a fold of the hills, and all its guns point at the sky, not at the sea, not at the road. The Fog Sea navy's finest are posted here: marines on the gate, crossbowmen on the walls, boarders patrolling the mouth of the fold. Everyone nearby says it guards something of the Qianli's, though nobody can say what of the Qianli's would need a gun fort to guard it.
column3: 一道山坳里修着一座石砌的小炮城，城里的炮口一律朝着天，不对海，也不对路。雾海水师最精的人马驻在这里，水兵守门，弩手上墙，跳帮手巡坳口。附近的人都说这里守的是千里号的东西，可千里号的什么东西要拿炮城来守，谁也说不上来。

column2: The fort falls. Its twelve bronze guns aren't the navy's; 'Qianli' is cast into their barrels. The Qianli unloaded them here: without the guns the ships drew less water and could clear the shallows. Stuffed in one muzzle is a sheet of oiled paper: 'The Qianli will not exchange fire with the emperor's ships. Shen Du.' The admiral took the guns, set them pointing at the sky, and in ten years never could bring himself to melt them down.
column3: 炮城被打下。城里十二门铜炮不是水师的，炮身上铸着「千里」，是千里号卸在岸上的：卸了炮，船吃水浅，过得了浅滩。炮口塞着一张油纸：「千里号不与官船交火。沈渡。」提督把炮收了，炮口朝天，十年没舍得熔。

column2: The Sailors' Gallery
column3: 水手画廊

column2: A portrait painter's stall at the village gate, a dozen likenesses on the wall, so true he's even put in the moles. A group of sailors had them painted ten years ago, says the painter, to send home to Quanzhou, but no ship could get out of the Sea of Fog, so here they've hung. Today a gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has come to collect them, 'Qianli belongings' for the admiral, and the painter clings to his easel.
column3: 村口一个画像的摊子，墙上挂着十几张人像，画得极像，连痣都点上了。画师说这些是十年前一群水手请他画的，要托人捎回泉州给家里，可船出不了雾海，画就一直挂着。一伙雾海弩手今天来收画像，说提督要「千里号遗物」，画师抱着画架不放。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the portraits come down one by one: a fat cook, a thin doctor, a pipa player, the youngest lad of all with Long Sihai's brows and eyes. The last is a dark-faced man squinting out to sea. Axi bursts into tears. 'That's my father.' The painter rolls it up and gives it to her.
column3: 弩手被赶走，画像一张张取下来：一个胖厨子，一个瘦郎中，一个弹琵琶的，一个最小的后生，眉眼像龙四海。最后一张是个黑脸汉子，眯着眼看海。阿汐一下子哭出了声：「是我爹。」画师把那张卷好，给了她。

column2: Wrecked Warship Beach
column3: 沉舰滩

column2: A dozen broken warships lie along a long beach, some dismasted, some nothing but keels, every bow still flying the Fog Sea navy's flag. These are the navy's own wrecks, ten years of ships run onto rocks in the fog and dragged ashore to be stripped for repairs. A large force of marines, crossbowmen and boarders is breaking them up, and at the sight of you they drop their hammers and take up blades.
column3: 一片长滩上躺着十几条破战船，有的断了桅，有的只剩龙骨，船头都还插着雾海水师的旗。这是水师自己的沉船，十年里在雾里撞礁撞沉的，拖上岸拆了补别的船。一大队水兵、弩手、跳帮手在滩上拆船，见了你们，放下锤子就抄起了刀。

column2: The wrecking crews scatter. On the stern of each wreck is nailed a board with the ship's name, the year it sank, and a line of names. The admiral wrote every board himself, ten years, not one missed. 'Every day the order stands, another ship goes down,' says the old soldier in charge. 'The admiral knows it. He still won't lift it.'
column3: 拆船的兵散了。每条破船的船尾都钉着一块木牌，写着船名和沉的那一年，还有一行人名。牌子是提督亲手写的，十年，一块不落。领头的老兵说：「令一天不撤，船就一条条地沉。提督知道，他就是不撤。」

column2: Echo Hollow
column3: 回声谷

column2: A shallow hollow on the moor between steep earth banks, where one shout comes back three or four times over. The old pilots of the blind school used to come here to train their ears. Now a squad of Fog Sea marines has taken it for a camp, reckoning the echoes will confuse any attacker. Xiaojiang stands at the mouth of the hollow, determined to go in and shout.
column3: 荒原上一道浅谷，谷两边是陡土坎，人在谷里喊一声，回声能折三四回。盲舟塾的老领港们常来这里练耳朵。如今一队雾海水兵把谷占了做营盘，说回声乱，敌人摸不进来。小桨站在谷口，非要进去喊一嗓子。

column2: The marines are driven out. Xiaojiang stands in the bottom of the hollow, shouts once, and counts with his eyes shut: one fast, two slow, one far. He opens his eyes grinning as if he'd found treasure. 'Close on the left, far on the right, and another bank behind!' At the mouth of the hollow the blind old master nods. 'The Bao ears are back.'
column3: 水兵被赶出了谷。小桨站在谷底喊了一声，闭着眼数：一声快，两声慢，一声远。他睁开眼，笑得像捡了宝：「左边近，右边远，后头还有一道坎！」盲老塾师在谷口点头：「鲍家的耳朵，回来了。」

column2: The Firework Hut
column3: 炮仗屋

column2: A little stone hut by the sea with a cartload of fireworks stacked inside, wrapped tight in oilcloth. The old fisherman who minds it has changed the oilcloth every rainy season for ten years. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has broken the door in; fireworks make good signal rockets, they say, and these are going to the fleet. The old man blocks the doorway with his body: 'Those were ordered! They're paid for!'
column3: 海边一座石头小屋，屋里码着一车烟花，拿油布裹得严严实实。看屋的老渔夫十年来每逢雨季都把油布换一层。一伙雾海弩手撬开了门，说烟花能做信号火箭，要运去舰上。老渔夫拿身子堵着门：「这是人家订的，钱都付了！」

column2: The crossbowmen are chased off and the old man wraps the oilcloth back on. The Qianli's sailors pooled their money for these fireworks: 'For the day we're back. Set them off on the shore.' Fireworks take two people, he says, one to light and one to watch. 'I'm minding this cartload for them. When they're back, I'll do the lighting.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，老渔夫把油布重新裹好。烟花是千里号的水手们凑钱买的：「回来那天，在岸上放。」他说放烟花得有两个人，一个点，一个看。「我替他们看着这车炮仗。他们回来，我替他们点。」

column2: The People Scale
column3: 称人秤

column2: A rice shop by the sea with a great steelyard hanging out front that can weigh three hundred jin. A squad of Fog Sea marines wants to carry it off for dividing rations aboard ship. The shopkeeper hugs the beam and won't let go; the counterweight drops on his foot and he hops about in pain, still shouting, 'Borrow the scale if you must, but not the book!'
column3: 海边一座米铺，铺前吊着一杆大秤，能称三百斤。一队雾海水兵要把秤扛走，说舰上分粮要用。米铺老板抱着秤杆不撒手，秤砣砸了自己的脚，疼得直蹦，嘴里还喊：「秤可以借，秤簿不能拿！」

column2: The marines are driven off and the shopkeeper opens the scale book. Before they left, every one of the Qianli's people got on the scale, saying they'd weigh again on the way back and see who'd got thin. Three hundred names, three hundred weights. Halfway down Axi finds one line: 'Pilot Xu Chaosheng, one hundred and twenty-eight jin.' She laughs and wipes her eyes. 'We'll have to feed him up when he's back.'
column3: 水兵被赶走，老板翻开秤簿：十年前千里号的人临走，一个个上秤称了一回，说回来再称，看谁瘦了。三百个名字，三百个斤两。阿汐在中间找到一行：「领港许潮生，一百二十八斤。」她笑着抹眼泪：「回来得给他多吃点。」

column2: The Flower Skiff
column3: 花舢板

column2: Outside a fisher family's door sits an old skiff, its hull filled with earth and planted with a boatload of balsam flowers, red and purple. A gang of Fog Sea boarders rushes up to haul it away: the admiral's new order says nothing of Bao Laozhen's may be left in other hands. The fisherwife shields her flowers and scolds: 'I claimed this ten years ago! These flowers have bloomed ten times!'
column3: 海边一户渔家门口摆着一条旧舢板，舱里填满了土，种着一船凤仙花，红红紫紫。一伙雾海跳帮手冲过来，要把舢板拖走：提督新下的令，凡是鲍老针的东西，一件不许落在外头。渔婆子护着花骂：「这是我十年前领回来的，花都开了十茬了！」

column2: The boarders are chased off. Xiaojiang parts the roots and, wedged between two planks, finds a bamboo tube that was never opened. Inside, in his grandfather's hand: 'Fee received in full; silver sent back in the boat. I'm going on with the ship and won't return. At the end of the fog there's a tower, and someone in it waiting for ships, and the ship needs a pilot. Tell the old woman not to wait.' Xiaojiang tucks the tube inside his coat and says nothing at all.
column3: 跳帮手跑了。小桨扒开花根，在船板缝里摸出一只竹筒，是爷爷的字：「工钱收齐，银子随船送回。我跟船走，不回了。雾尽头有座楼，有人在楼里等船，船上缺领港。告诉老婆子，别等。」小桨揣起竹筒，一句话没说。

column2: The Cat's Sandbar
column3: 猫引沙脊

column2: Freshwater Isle is in sight from the shore, a strait between, and only at the lowest tides does a thin ridge of sand show above the water. A gang of Fog Sea boarders holds this end of the ridge and chases everyone off, though they don't know how to walk it themselves; several who tried sank in quicksand. The tide is out, and through the fog a ginger cat is picking its way along the ridge toward you, step by step.
column3: 海边望得见淡水岛，岛和岸之间隔着一道海峡，只有大退潮时才露出一线沙脊。一伙雾海跳帮手守在沙脊这头，见人就赶，可他们自己也不知道沙脊怎么走，下去过的好几个都陷进了流沙。潮退了，雾里，一只黄猫正沿着沙脊一步一步朝这边走来。

column2: The boarders are driven off. The ginger cat comes right up, sniffs Houqianli's lanterns, turns and heads back, glancing over its shoulder every few steps. You cross the ridge in its pawprints and not one foot sinks. 'It knows this lantern,' says Xiaojiang. A piece is missing from its left ear. It's the cat they called Captain.
column3: 跳帮手被赶走。黄猫走到跟前，闻了闻后千里的灯笼，转身往回走，走几步回头看一眼。你们踩着它的脚印过了沙脊，一步没陷。小桨说：「它认得这盏灯。」猫的左耳缺了一块，正是那只叫「船长」的猫。

column2: Warm Gate Battery
column3: 暖水口炮台

column2: A battery at the far end of the coast, every gun aimed south-east, for it is here that the warm strip leaves the Sea of Fog. A large company of the Fog Sea navy holds it: marines on the guns, crossbowmen on the wall, boarders with the fast boats on the beach. For ten years they've polished the guns every day and never fired one. Today they see Houqianli's lanterns and the gunners scramble to load.
column3: 海岸尽头一座炮台，炮口一律对着东南：那一线暖水就是从这里出雾海的。炮台上驻着雾海水师的一大队人马，水兵守炮，弩手站墙，跳帮手守着滩上的快艇。十年来炮台天天擦炮，一炮没放，今天看见后千里的灯，炮手们手忙脚乱地装药。

column2: The battery falls and the gunners actually sigh with relief. The night log, twenty-eighth of the eighth month ten years ago: 'Five Qianli ships passed the Warm Gate. Ten shots, all missed. Number Six rammed broadside, captured. Five ships went south-east. Towers suddenly seen in the fog. They entered and vanished. Admiral's order: halt, no pursuit.' After that night the guns never spoke again.
column3: 炮台被打下，炮手们反倒松了口气。值夜簿十年前八月廿八写着：「千里号五船过暖水口，炮十发，皆不中。六号横撞，截获。五船东南去，雾中忽见楼台，入，不见。提督令：止，不追。」那一夜之后，炮就再没响过。

column2: Ghost Ship Hollow
column3: 鬼船坳

column2: A low hollow on the moor where, in thick fog, the fog pools like a pot of white porridge. A wrecked ship stands upright in the bottom, its hull daubed white, rotten sails on its mast, and when the fog thickens a green glow lights up aboard and someone drags a chain across the deck. Travellers drop their goods and run. The marines, crossbowmen and boarders round the hollow are deserters and thieves, waiting to pick up what's dropped.
column3: 荒原上一处低洼，每逢大雾，雾就积在坳里，像一锅白粥。坳底竖着一条破船，船身涂着白灰，桅上挂着烂帆，雾一浓，船上就亮起绿莹莹的光，有人拖着铁链在甲板上走。过路的人吓得扔下货就跑。坳边的雾海水兵、弩手、跳帮手都是逃兵和贼，正等着捡货。

column2: This lot of fake ghosts is driven out; the green glow turns out to be fungus shining on rotten wood, and the chain was stolen from the impound yard. But as long as the wreck stands here, every thick fog brings a new gang up its sides to whiten their faces, rattle chains and play the ghost. Before long you'll have to come and clear it again.
column3: 这一伙装鬼的被赶了出来，绿光原来是腐木上的荧光菌，铁链是从扣船坞偷的。可这条破船搁在这里一天，大雾一来，就总有新的一伙人爬上去，涂白脸，拖铁链，装神弄鬼。过一阵，你们还得再来赶一回。

column2: The Cooperage
column3: 箍桶铺

column2: A cooperage by the sea crammed with water casks, from ones big enough to hold a man to ones that hold a bowl. A gang of Fog Sea boarders is making the old cooper turn out casks for the fleet: there isn't enough water on the island to fill what they've got, they say, so more casks will mean more water. The cooper mutters as he hammers a hoop: 'More casks, more water? Shall I hoop you up a sea while I'm at it?'
column3: 海边一座箍桶铺，铺里堆满了水桶，大的能装下一个人，小的只装一碗。一伙雾海跳帮手逼着老桶匠给舰队赶桶，说岛上的水不够装，桶多了水就多了。老桶匠一边箍一边嘟囔：「桶多了水就多？那我箍个海出来给你们！」

column2: The boarders are chased off and only then does the cooper tell you: ten years ago the Qianli ordered three hundred and one casks from him, one per head and one over. He asked who the extra was for. 'For whoever comes after,' Owner Shen said. That cask was filled with water and left on the island.
column3: 跳帮手被赶跑，老桶匠才说起旧事：十年前千里号在他这儿订了三百零一只桶，一人一只，多一只。他问多的那只给谁，沈船主说：「给后来的人。」那只桶装满了水，留在了岛上。

column2: Pearl Divers' Bay
column3: 采珠湾

column2: A few pearling boats float in a clear bay, the women aboard tying stone weights round their waists and diving, staying down a long time before they surface. But these days it isn't oysters they bring up. It's cannon, the fleet's iron guns sunk in the bay, which Fog Sea crossbowmen make them haul up one by one to trade for rice. Not a single pearl has been brought up, and the pearl merchants have come and gone empty-handed.
column3: 一道清水湾里漂着几条采珠船，船上的女人腰系石坠，一头扎下去，半天才冒上来。可如今她们捞的不是蚌，是炮：舰队沉在湾里的铁炮，雾海弩手逼她们一门门捞上来，换米。珠子一颗也没捞，珠商来了好几趟，空着手走。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the divers go back to oysters, and in admiration they trade pearls with you. The fleet is so short of iron, says the old woman who leads them, that it fishes up its own sunken guns. Out among the islands, at the navy market, sailors trade anchor chain for rice. 'When the iron's all eaten, the ships will be nothing but wood.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，采珠女们又捞起了蚌，佩服你们，拿珠子跟你们换货。领头的阿嬷说，舰上缺铁缺得厉害，连沉炮都要捞，岛群那边的军市上，水兵拿锚链换米，「铁吃光了，船就只剩木头了」。

column2: Lantern-Send Beach
column3: 送灯滩

column2: A sandy beach where every Ghost Festival the fisher families used to float water lanterns, one lantern for each name, drifting away on the warm water. Since the lights went out, no lanterns are allowed here. A gang of Fog Sea boarders has taken the fishing huts at the head of the beach and sealed the families' boats, nets and rice jars, fining every household that ever floated a lantern. The families crouch on the sand clutching folded paper lanterns they don't dare light.
column3: 海边一片沙滩，从前每年中元，渔家都在这里放水灯，一盏灯一个名字，顺着暖水漂走。灭灯以后，滩上不许放灯，一伙雾海跳帮手占了滩头的渔寮，把渔家的船、网、米缸都封了，说放过灯的人家都要罚。渔家们蹲在滩上，手里攥着折好的纸灯，不敢点。

column2: The boarders are driven off and the huts unsealed. That night the families light ten years of held-back lanterns all at once and set them on the warm water, and a string of lights drifts south-east, still visible as it enters the fog. Xiaojiang floats one too. He doesn't write a name on it.
column3: 跳帮手被赶走，渔寮解了封。当夜渔家们把憋了十年的水灯一齐点着，放进暖水里，一串灯往东南漂，漂进雾里还看得见。小桨也放了一盏，没写名字。

column2: In the huts you find the boarders' hoard: fifty jin of dried fish, two jars of rice, a bundle of new nets, and a chest of confiscated paper lanterns, neatly folded, not one of which they had the heart to burn.
column3: 渔寮里抄出跳帮手囤的五十斤鱼干、两缸米、一捆新网，还有一箱收缴来的纸灯，折得整整齐齐，一盏都没舍得烧。

column2: Every time you pass, the fisher families give you a basket of fish fresh from the water and a folded paper lantern. 'If you don't need it on the road, float it, and say hello for us.'
column3: 每次路过，渔家都给你们一篓刚出水的鱼，再塞一盏折好的纸灯：「路上用不着就放了它，替我们问个好。」

column2: Qianli Dyke
column3: 千里堤

column2: Freshwater Isle is an island of white sand without a single stone on it, and its fishing village relies on one stone dyke to break the waves. The dyke was built ten years ago, and the surf has been tearing gaps in it ever since. The islanders used to trade dried fish to passing ships for ballast stones, but the fleet lets no ship land, and the stones stopped coming. A squad of Fog Sea crossbowmen holds the jetty and raises its crossbows at the sight of your ship. Behind them, the islanders hold up a placard: 'Got any stones?'
column3: 淡水岛是一座白沙岛，岛上没有一块石头，渔村全靠一道石堤挡浪。堤是十年前垒的，这些年被浪掏得七零八落。岛上的人从前拿鱼干跟过往的船换压舱石，可舰队不许船靠岛，石头断了来路。码头上守着一队雾海弩手，见了你们的船，弩都端了起来。岛上的人在后头举着牌子：「有石头吗？」

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off. Houqianli unloads her ballast stones, the islanders bring fish and taro in exchange, and the trade of stone for food is open again. Axi scoops up a handful of the island's sand: look closely and it's all broken shell and coral. This island was heaped up by living things in the sea, and its sand is white and soft and won't build a wall. The headman points at the old dyke. 'Those are the Qianli's stones. The year they came for water, they needed room for the casks, so they unloaded three hundred ballast stones to us and wouldn't take a copper.' Ever since, it's been called Qianli Dyke.
column3: 弩手被赶走，后千里卸下压舱石，岛上的人拿鱼和芋头来换，石头换粮食的买卖又开张了。阿汐抓起一把岛上的沙，细看全是碎贝壳和珊瑚屑：这岛是海里的活物堆起来的，沙子白，软，垒不成墙。村长指着那道旧堤：「这是千里号的石头。那年他们取水，要腾出地方装水桶，把三百块压舱石卸给了我们，一块没要钱。」从此这道堤就叫千里堤。

column2: The Old Zhenwu
column3: 镇雾旧舰

column2: In a sheltered fold behind the coast lies an old warship with her masts struck, a 'Zhenwu' nameboard still on her bow: the admiral's flagship ten years ago, her bow stove in, hauled ashore and made an armoury. The Fog Sea navy keeps its finest company on her, marines at the hatches, crossbowmen on the forecastle, boarders patrolling beneath her keel. The door of the stern cabin is locked, and no one may go up.
column3: 海岸背后一处避风的山坳里，搁着一条拆了桅的旧战船，船头还挂着「镇雾」的牌子，是提督十年前的旗舰，撞坏了船头，拖上岸做了军械库。雾海水师留了最精的一队人马守着它，水兵把舱口，弩手站船楼，跳帮手在船底下巡。船尾的舵楼门锁着，谁也不许上去。

column2: The picked company is beaten. In the stern cabin hangs the old log, and its last page reads: 'Twenty-eighth of the eighth month. Intercepted the Qianli at the Warm Gate. Number Six rammed broadside, our bow stove in; one empty ship taken. Five ships into the fog; towers appeared in it; gone. Orders forbid passing beyond the fog. Halted.' One line below, the ink pressed through the page: 'She called something back over her shoulder. I heard it.'
column3: 精兵败了。舵楼里挂着旧航海日志，最后一页：「八月廿八，暖水口截千里号。六号横撞，舰首破，截获空船一。五船入雾，雾中现楼台，不见。依令不得越雾，止。」底下一行，墨迹透了纸：「她回头喊了一句。我听见了。」

column2: The Sail Loft
column3: 补帆寮

column2: At the tip of the headland stands a great sail loft, torn sails hanging inside like huge birds set out to dry. The old sailmaker has hands of callus and a big needle that flies. He has an odd rule: if you want a sail mended or a trade made, first beat his apprentices. They are all retired Fog Sea marines, every one built like a door, and in ten years only one person has ever beaten them.
column3: 海角尽头一座补帆的大寮，寮里挂着一面面破帆，像一群晾着的大鸟。老帆匠满手老茧，一根大针使得飞快。他有个怪规矩：要他补帆、跟他换货，先打赢他寮里的徒弟。徒弟们都是退下来的雾海水兵，个个膀大腰圆，十年里只有一个人打赢过。

column2: The apprentices concede and the old sailmaker trades with you gladly. The one who beat them, ten years ago, was Owner Shen. He mends the Zhenwu's sails too, and every year when the admiral comes for them, he asks that they be sewn extra strong: 'The day the order's lifted, I'll have a long way to chase.' 'Whether it's lifted or not,' says the old sailmaker, 'go and ask the man himself.'
column3: 徒弟们服了，老帆匠痛快地跟你们换货。十年里打赢过的那一个，是沈船主。镇雾号的帆也是他补的，提督每年来取，都要他把帆缝结实点：「哪天令撤了，要追很远。」老帆匠说：「令撤不撤，你们去问问他本人吧。」

column2: The After-Comers' Spring
column3: 后来泉

column2: In the middle of Freshwater Isle is a spring, and beside it an old carved board: 'The Qianli drew water here. What is left is for those who come after.' The water is clear, but these last two years it has turned saltier and saltier. A gang of Fog Sea boarders holds the spring and ships it to the fleet by the barrel day and night, without pause. Beside the spring stands an old sealed cask nobody can move, because whenever someone tries, a ginger cat with a torn ear flies at him.
column3: 淡水岛中间一口泉，泉边立着一块旧木牌，字是刻的：「千里号取水于此，余水留后来者。」泉水清，可这两年越来越咸。一伙雾海跳帮手占着泉眼，日夜拿大桶往舰上运，一刻不停，泉边还摆着一只封着口的老水桶，谁也搬不动它，因为每回有人去搬，一只缺耳朵的黄猫就扑上来。

column2: The boarders are driven off. The fresh water under the island, the old people say, is rain gathered in the sand; it's lighter than seawater and floats on the salt like a layer of oil. Draw too hard and the salt pushes up from below. The Qianli took only what it needed; the fleet has pumped without stopping for ten years. The old cask is the Qianli's three hundred and first, marked 'For those who come after'. The cat jumps onto its lid, and stays.
column3: 跳帮手被赶走。老人说，岛下的淡水是雨水攒下的，比海水轻，像一层油浮在咸水上；舀狠了，咸水就顶上来。千里号只取够用的，舰队十年不停地抽。那只老桶是千里号的第三百零一只，写着「后来者」。猫跳上桶盖不走了。

column2: At the spring you find the boarders' hoard: eighty empty casks, two sacks of rice, a basket of salt fish, and the fleet's water order: 'One hundred casks a day, not one fewer.'
column3: 泉边抄出跳帮手囤的八十只空桶、两袋米、一筐咸鱼，还有一张舰队的取水令，上面写着「每日一百桶，不得少」。

column2: Every time you pass, the islanders draw you just enough water, by the Qianli's old rule, not a cask more, and bring a string of grilled fish: one for the cat, one for you.
column3: 每次路过，岛上的人都按千里号的老规矩，给你们打够用的水，一桶不多，再拿一串烤鱼，喂猫一条，给你们一条。

column2: Fast Boat Point
column3: 快艇岬

column2: A rocky point at the east end of Freshwater Isle with dozens of fast boats tied below it, iron hooks on their bows: the Fog Sea boarders' craft. As Houqianli rounds the island, a gong sounds on the point, and the boats dart out like a shoal of barracuda, hooks first, men right behind, all in one smooth rush. Ten years of drilling have not gone to waste.
column3: 淡水岛东头一道石岬，岬下拴着几十条快艇，艇头装着铁钩，是雾海跳帮手跳帮用的。望见后千里从岛后绕出来，岬上一声锣响，快艇像一群梭子鱼扑了过来，钩子先上，人随后到，一气呵成，十年的操练没白练。

column2: The fast boats are beaten off one by one and the boarders' chief is hauled up onto your deck. He's frank about it and shows you his orders: 'Any ship showing Qian lanterns is to be stopped. Take them alive. Harm no one.' In ten years, he says, not a word of it has changed. 'The admiral's as stubborn as they come. But it's not a bad stubbornness.'
column3: 快艇被一条条打退，跳帮头目被你们拎上了甲板。他倒也爽快，掏出军令给你们看：「凡挂千字灯者截之，生擒，不许伤一人。」他说十年来这条令一个字没改过，「提督是个死心眼，可他的心眼，不坏」。

column2: Welcome-and-Stop Isle
column3: 迎截岛

column2: A line of picket boats waits along the shore of the second island, and when the Fog Sea boarders aboard make out the three hundred Qian lanterns on Houqianli's masts, they fall into chaos. Some fire whistling arrows to raise the alarm, some throw lines into the sea to welcome the ship in, some raise their hooks to board, and one old sailor kneels in the bow weeping, 'It's back, the Qianli's back!' Three factions shove each other about in the same boat, and lines and hooks come flying at you together.
column3: 第二座岛的岸边排着一列哨船，哨船上的雾海跳帮手看清了后千里桅上那三百盏千字灯，一下子乱了套：有人往天上放响箭报警，有人往海里扔缆绳要迎船，有人举着钩子要跳帮，还有个老水兵跪在船头哭：「回来了，千里号回来了！」三拨人在一条船上推推搡搡，缆绳和钩子一齐朝你们飞了过来。

column2: The pickets are scattered, and the old sailor who knelt hangs over the rail until he can read the name on your stern. A long silence. 'Houqianli... It isn't her.' His cousin was a stoker on the Qianli. The picket captain sends a boat to the flagship: 'Not the Qianli. The Houqianli.' The reply comes quickly, and it is one line: 'Any ship showing Qian lanterns: stop it.'
column3: 哨船被打散，那个跪着的老水兵扒着船舷看清了船尾的字，愣了半天：「后千里……不是它。」他的表弟当年在千里号上烧火。哨长派快艇去报旗舰：「非千里号，乃后千里。」回令很快到了，只有一句：「挂千字灯者，截。」

column2: The Navy's Garden
column3: 水师菜园

column2: On the island's lee side lies a vegetable garden, sweet potatoes, mustard greens and spring onions in tidy rows, planted by old Fog Sea navy hands, and for ten years it has been the fleet's only source of anything green. But the man in charge is a quartermaster tight as a counting frame, who with a gang of boarders counts every plant and locks it in the store; an old gardener caught eating a single leaf gets the whip.
column3: 岛背风的一面开着一片菜园，番薯、芥菜、葱，一垄垄排得整整齐齐，是雾海水师的老兵种的，十年来全靠它给舰上添一口青。可管园子的是个铁算盘似的军需官，带着一伙跳帮手，把菜一棵棵点了数锁进仓里，种菜的老兵自己偷吃一片叶子都要挨鞭子。

column2: The quartermaster is tied up and the store thrown open, and the old gardeners eat what they've grown for the first time. One of them, cradling a bowl of mustard-green soup, says, 'Every time the admiral comes to the island he squats in the rows pulling weeds, and when he's done he says just one thing: plant more next year. If they come back, there'll be more mouths aboard.'
column3: 军需官被捆了，仓门打开，种菜的老兵们头一回吃上了自己种的菜。一个老兵捧着一碗芥菜汤说：「提督每回上岛，都蹲在地头拔草，拔完了只说一句：明年多种点，万一他们回来，船上人多。」

column2: In the store you find what the quartermaster had under lock: three hundred jin of sweet potatoes, twenty bundles of mustard greens, a crock of pickled onions, and a vegetable ledger that accounts for every single leaf.
column3: 仓里抄出军需官锁着的三百斤番薯、二十捆芥菜、一缸腌葱，还有一本菜账，记到了每一片叶子。

column2: Every time you pass, the old soldiers toss a few bundles of freshly pulled greens onto your deck, soil still on them. 'Eat your greens and your teeth won't loosen.'
column3: 每次路过，老兵们都往你们船上扔几捆刚拔的菜，带着泥：「吃青的，牙不松。」

column2: Anchor-Chain Market
column3: 锚链市

column2: In the bay of the third island the fleet's ships lie in a ring, gangplanks between them: the Fog Sea navy's market. What's for sale isn't goods but the ships themselves, anchors, anchor chain, nails, cannonballs, the iron bands off rudders, stripped piece by piece and traded to the islanders for rice. Today a gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen has sealed the market's entrance: the admiral's orders, the market closes when Houqianli arrives. Half-stripped chain lies on the gangplanks and nobody dares touch it.
column3: 第三座岛的海湾里，舰队的船围成一圈，船与船之间搭着跳板，就是雾海水师的军市。卖的不是货，是船本身：锚、锚链、铁钉、炮子、舵上的铁箍，一样样拆下来，跟岛上的渔户换米。今天一伙雾海弩手把市口封了，说提督有令，后千里一到，军市关门。拆了一半的锚链堆在跳板上，没人敢动。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the market reopens, iron from the ships for grain from the islands, and you put in a share of rice yourselves. The quartermaster sighs. The court hasn't paid in ten years, and the first thing the admiral stripped was his own: first he sold the guard off his sword, then the bronze bell from his ship. 'He said the order was given to him, so he'd be the first to go hungry.' The old hands point to the biggest ship in the ring, three lamps hanging side by side on her bow: the Zhenwu, and the admiral is aboard.
column3: 弩手被赶走，军市重开，舰上拆下的铁换岛上的粮，你们也添了一份米进去。军需官叹着气说，朝廷十年没发饷，提督第一个拆的是自己船上的东西：先卖了佩刀的刀镡，再卖了船上的铜钟，「他说，令是他接的，饿也得先饿他」。老兵们指着最大的那条船，船头三盏灯并排挂着：镇雾号，提督就在上面。

column2: Net Shed Village
column3: 网寮村

column2: A little fishing village at the north end of the second island, nets drying at every door, shells weighting the roofs. This year not one fish has gone into a village pot: the fleet levies nine-tenths of every boat's catch, and Fog Sea marines live in the village to watch, scraping off even the scales to take away. Rather than give it away for nothing, says the village's old fishwife, they'd sooner not fish at all, and they've dragged every boat up the beach.
column3: 第二座岛北头一个小渔村，家家门口晒着网，屋顶压着贝壳。可这一年的鱼一条都没进过自家锅：舰队按船抽鱼，一船抽九成，雾海水兵就住在村里看着，连鱼鳞都要刮下来带走。村里的老渔婆说，宁可不打鱼，也不白给，干脆把船都拖上了岸。

column2: The marines are driven off and the boats pushed back into the water, and the old fishwife, impressed, opens her drying yard to trade with you. Every twenty-eighth of the eighth month, she says, the admiral takes the Zhenwu out past the easternmost island and stops at the edge of the fog and sits there all night, and comes back at dawn. 'He goes to stand guard on that line,' she says. 'Ten years he's stood there.'
column3: 水兵被赶走，船推下了水，渔婆佩服你们，开了晒场跟你们换货。她说每年八月廿八，提督都把镇雾号开到最东头那座岛外面，停在雾跟前，一停一整夜，天亮再开回来。「他是去那条线上站岗，」她说，「站了十年。」

column2: Merrow Reef
column3: 鲛人礁

column2: South of the island lies a black reef where nothing grows. At night a song drifts out of the fog, a woman's voice, soft, like someone singing a child to sleep, in Quanzhou dialect. The fleet's men stop their ears with wax, and Fog Sea crossbowmen guard the reef and shoot anyone who rows toward the singing. You anchor off the reef and the song comes over line by line. Axi leans on the rail, her eyelids growing heavy. Xiaojiang cocks his head, listens a while, and goes white. 'She's calling a roll.' Each line of the song is a name. The last line is 'Axi'.
column3: 岛南一片黑礁，寸草不生。夜里雾中飘来歌声，女人的嗓子，软软的，像哄孩子睡觉，唱的是泉州话。舰上的人拿蜡封耳朵，雾海弩手守在礁前，谁往歌声那边划就射谁。你们泊在礁外，歌声一句句飘过来，阿汐靠着船舷，眼皮发沉。小桨侧耳听了一会儿，脸一下子白了：「她在点名。」歌里一句一个人名，最后一句是「阿汐」。

column2: The crossbowmen are beaten. There's no one on the reef at all, only rows of wave-worn holes that moan as the tide breathes in and out. Axi listens a long time. It's the song her father sang her to sleep with: every night the names of the people on the ship, and the last line was her. 'But nobody knows this song except my father.' Out in the fog, the singing stops.
column3: 弩手败了。礁上一个人也没有，只有一排排浪蚀的孔，潮一进一出，孔里就呜呜地响。阿汐听了很久：这是她爹哄她睡觉的歌，每晚唱一遍船上人的名字，最后一句是她。「可这首歌，除了我爹，没人会唱。」雾里的歌声停了。

column2: Shark Fin Lagoon
column3: 鲨鳍湾

column2: A reef lagoon at the west end of the third island, the water green, and on its surface a crowd of triangular fins circling. The sharks came with the fleet: ten years of fish bones and slops dumped overboard have drawn them here year after year. The fishers dare not cast a net, the marines dare not bathe, and even the boarders' fast boats go round. Today another little fishing boat has capsized at the lagoon's mouth, and the fisherman sits astride the upturned hull shouting for help.
column3: 第三座岛西头一道礁湖，水是绿的，湖面上却竖着一片三角背鳍，来回打转。鲨鱼跟着舰队来的：舰上倒下的鱼骨、剩饭，十年里把它们一年年引到这里。渔户不敢下网，水兵也不敢下水洗澡，连跳帮手的快艇都绕着走。今天又有一条小渔船翻在湖口，渔夫骑在船底上大喊救命。

column2: The fisherman is pulled out, this pack of sharks is driven from the lagoon, and the water is quiet for a few days. But the fleet is still anchored outside, and as long as the bones and slops keep coming, the sharks will be back season after season. The islanders say the lagoon will only truly be clear the day the fleet sails away; until then, someone has to come and drive them off every so often.
column3: 渔夫救上来了，这一回的鲨群被赶出了礁湖，湖面清净了几天。可舰队还泊在湖外，鱼骨剩饭一天不断，鲨鱼就一季一季地回来。岛上的人说，等舰队哪天开走了，这片湖才算真清净；在那之前，隔些日子就得来赶一回。

column2: The Order Stele
column3: 截令碑

column2: On the third island's high ground stands a stele of grey stone with a military order carved on it in characters as big as bowls. Before it stands a squad of Fog Sea marines in worn-out armour, ramrod straight, the admiral's honour guard, who have changed the watch before the stele every day for ten years. The back of the stone is covered in names, row upon row, newer the further down. As you climb toward them the marines bring up their spears as one.
column3: 第三座岛的高处立着一块青石碑，碑上刻着一道军令，字有碗口大。碑前站着一队雾海水兵，衣甲破旧却站得笔直，是提督的仪仗，十年来每天在碑前换一回岗。碑的背面刻满了人名，一排一排，越往下字越新。水兵们看见你们走上来，齐刷刷挺起了枪。

column2: The honour guard is scattered. The inscription is a Ministry of War order from ten years ago: 'If the Qianli enters the Sea of Fog, stop it. Let it not go east. Interception within the Sea of Fog. Do not pass beyond the fog.' Why, it doesn't say. The names on the back are ten years of sailors lost on the rocks. 'The admiral doesn't know why either,' says the leader of the guard. 'He only knows the order hasn't been lifted.'
column3: 仪仗被打散。碑文是十年前的兵部令：「千里号若入雾海，截之，勿令东去。截于雾海之内，不得越雾。」为什么要截，一个字没提。碑背是十年里撞礁死去的水兵。领头的水兵说：「提督也不知道为什么，只知道令没撤。」

column2: The Last Stake Line
column3: 最后一道桩

column2: A row of stakes is driven into the beach of the easternmost island, points sharpened, and behind them crouch the flagship's Fog Sea marines, cheekbones jutting with hunger, uniforms patched and patched again, spears polished bright. Beyond lies the Zhenwu's anchorage. They've heard how Houqianli fought its way here. Their sergeant grounds his spear in the sand. 'You beat the ones out there, that's to your credit. This line is the admiral's.'
column3: 最东头那座岛的海滩上打着一排木桩，桩顶削尖，桩后蹲着旗舰的雾海水兵，个个瘦得颧骨突出，号衣补了又补，可枪擦得发亮。再往东就是镇雾号的锚地。他们早听说后千里一路打过来，领头的什长把枪往沙里一顿：「你们打得过外头的，那是外头的本事。这一道，是提督的。」

column2: The stakes are torn down and the marines sit gasping on the sand. Not one runs. The sergeant passes you his water skin. His family is in Quanzhou, he says; he hasn't been home in ten years, and his son must be taller than him by now. 'Funny. Losing this fight's taken a weight off me.' He looks toward the anchorage. 'The admiral won't sleep tonight either.'
column3: 桩子被拔倒，水兵们坐在沙滩上喘气，没人逃。什长把水囊递给你们，说他家在泉州，十年没回去了，儿子该比他高了。「打了你们这一仗，心里倒松快了，」他望着锚地，「提督今晚也睡不着了。」

column2: The Speckled Hen-House
column3: 芦花鸡舍

column2: The easternmost island has a galley that cooks for the flagship, and beside it a hen-house, home to the loudest bird of all, the big speckled rooster the bugler carried aboard from the Fog Coast. A gang of Fog Sea crossbowmen holds the galley under orders: now Houqianli is here, not a grain of rice or a single egg is to fall into outsiders' hands. The rooster goes on crowing every day as usual, and the crossbowmen, sick of the noise, are discussing stewing it.
column3: 最东头那座岛上有座伙房，给旗舰做饭，伙房边搭着鸡舍，舍里那只最响的芦花大公鸡，就是号手当年从雾岸抱上船的。伙房被一伙雾海弩手把着，他们奉了令：后千里来了，一粒米、一个蛋都不许落进外人手里。公鸡天天照常打鸣，弩手嫌吵，正商量着炖了它。

column2: The crossbowmen are driven off and the rooster jumps onto the galley roof and crows long and loud toward the anchorage. Every morning, says the cook, the bugler comes to feed it, and then he stands in the bow looking west. 'Rooster's here, so's the man.' He ladles you a big bowl of rice. 'Whoever wins tomorrow, everyone's still got to eat.'
column3: 弩手被赶走，公鸡跳上伙房顶，冲着锚地打了一声长鸣。伙夫说，号手每天早上来喂它，喂完就站在船头，往西看。「鸡在，人就在。」他舀了一大碗米饭给你们：「明天打完仗，不管谁赢，都得吃饭。」

column2: In the galley you find what the crossbowmen were guarding: forty eggs, six sacks of rice, a crock of shrimp oil, and a stack of hardtack stamped 'Bugler's. No sesame.'
column3: 伙房里抄出弩手看着的四十只鸡蛋、六袋米、一坛虾油，还有一摞军饼，饼上刻着「号手的，不要芝麻」。

column2: Every time you pass, the cook gives you a basket of eggs still warm, and the rooster calls the hour for you from the roof.
column3: 每次路过，伙夫都塞给你们一篮热乎乎的鸡蛋，公鸡站在屋顶上替你们报时辰。

column2: Anchorage Lookout
column3: 望锚坡

column2: From a ridge on the island's summit you can look straight down on the Zhenwu: a great warship patched past counting, her sails old, half her anchor chain gone, three lamps hung side by side on her bow. A company of the flagship's Fog Sea boarders is camped on the ridge, sent by the admiral to keep an eye on you. That night you see a man standing in the Zhenwu's bow blowing a conch westward, a Quanzhou nanyin tune. Axi, Xiaojiang and Qi Xiaoman all come up to Houqianli's bow.
column3: 岛顶一道土坡，往下望就是镇雾号：一条打了无数补丁的大战船，帆是旧的，锚链少了一半，船头三盏灯并排挂着。坡上扎着旗舰的一队雾海跳帮手，是提督派来盯着你们的。夜里，你们看见镇雾号的船头站着一个吹海螺的人，往西吹着一支泉州的南音。阿汐、小桨、戚小满都站到了船头。

column2: The boarders are driven off the ridge. Before dawn the Zhenwu sends a boat with one line from the admiral: 'The hour of the dragon, before the Zhenwu. Any ship showing Qian lanterns will be stopped.' You carry up onto the deck everything you've brought this far: the Qi family's signal quilt, Azhou's letters, Bao Laozhen's bamboo tube, the oiled paper from the bronze gun. Axi lights the three hundred lanterns.
column3: 跳帮手被赶下坡。天亮前镇雾号放来一条小艇，传提督一句话：「辰时，镇雾号前。挂千字灯者，截。」你们把一路带来的东西摆上甲板：戚家的灯语被、阿舟的信、鲍老针的竹筒、铜炮里的那张油纸。阿汐点亮了三百盏灯。

column2: The Zhenwu
column3: 镇雾号

column2: At the hour of the dragon the fog thins by one layer. The Zhenwu lies broadside across the last line of the Sea of Fog, the navy's remaining warships drawn up on either wing, marines along the rails, crossbowmen in the tops, the boarders' fast boats slung at her sides. In her bow stands Cen Dingbo, Admiral of the Sea of Fog, fifty or so, his temples white, his uniform washed to grey, holding a bamboo tube with the order of ten years ago inside. He looks at Houqianli a long time, at the three hundred lanterns, at the people beneath them. 'You are not the Qianli. I know that. But the order says any ship showing Qian lanterns is to be stopped. I've waited ten years. The order has not been lifted, and I won't lift it first.' He raises his hand. 'Come. Beat me, and I'll count it as having tried to stop you.'
column3: 辰时，雾薄了一层。镇雾号横在雾海的最后一道线上，左右两翼排开水师仅剩的战船，水兵守舷，弩手上桅，跳帮手的快艇挂在船腹。船头站着雾海提督岑定波，五十来岁，两鬓全白，号衣洗得发灰，手里一只竹筒，装着十年前那道令。他看了后千里很久，看那三百盏灯，看灯下的人。「你们不是千里号，我知道。可令上写的是挂千字灯者截。我等了十年，令没撤，我不能先撤。」他举起手。「来吧。打过我，才算我截过了。」

column2: The Zhenwu's sails come down. Cen Dingbo sits on the deck with the bamboo tube on his knees, unopened. From the ranks of buglers steps a young man with a mooring bollard tattooed on his left forearm: Azhou. He takes his mother's letter, reads two lines and crouches down. Cen Dingbo speaks. 'That night Shen Du called back over her shoulder: “Tell whoever comes after, I'll wait in the Mirage.” I heard it. The order said not to pass beyond the fog, so I've stood on this line for ten years.' He points south-east, where the fog is parting in a crack and towers show faintly behind it. 'Houqianli isn't the Qianli. It was the Qianli I was ordered to stop. I never stopped you. Go.' Far behind on the Fog Coast, the north cape light flashes three bright, one dark, three times over.
column3: 镇雾号的帆落了。岑定波坐在甲板上，把竹筒放在膝头，没有打开。号手队里走出一个年轻人，左臂刺着一根系船柱：阿舟。他接过母亲的信，读了两行就蹲下了。岑定波说：「那夜沈渡回头喊了一句：『告诉后来的人，我在蜃楼等。』我听见了，令上说不得越雾，我就在这条线上站了十年。」他指向东南，雾正裂开一线，雾后隐约有楼台。「后千里不是千里号。我截的是千里号，没截过你们。去吧。」远处的雾岸上，北岬的灯三明一暗，打了三遍。

column2: The Mirage
column3: 蜃楼

column2: Upturned Tower Strand
column3: 倒楼滩

column2: The fog closes behind you. On Houqianli's first morning out of the Sea of Fog the water lies flat as a sheet of paper, and in the eastern sky floats a row of towers, tier on tier, eaves pointing down, hanging upside down in mid-air. The ship sails at them all day and they come no nearer and drift no farther. At dusk you put in at a white strand. On it stands a squad of mirage soldiers in old armour whose plates flicker in the sunset as if seen through water; behind their line are a few pirates, and their boots leave honest prints in the sand.
column3: 雾在身后合上了。后千里驶出雾海的头一个清早，海面平得像一张纸，东边天上浮着一排楼台，层层叠叠，檐角朝下，倒挂在半空。船朝它驶了一整天，它不近也不远。傍晚靠上一片白滩，滩上站着一队披旧甲的蜃兵，甲片在夕阳里一闪一闪，像隔着一层水；兵阵后头还有几个海盗，脚下踩出了实实在在的脚印。

column2: Blades go through the mirage soldiers and they scatter like heat haze; only the pirates end up tied in a row. They say the soldiers are breathed out by the Mirage King: scatter them and there'll be more tomorrow morning, and the pirates just follow along to pick up what falls. A Zhou looks up at the towers and says Shen Du's words once more: 'I'll be waiting in the Mirage.' Xiaojiang lies with an ear to the sand for a long while. 'Something under here is breathing. Very slow. Very big.'
column3: 刀砍上去，蜃兵像热气一样散了，只有海盗被捆成了一串。他们说蜃兵是蜃王吐出来的，打散了明早还有，他们只是跟在后头捡便宜。阿舟望着天上的楼，把沈渡那句话又念了一遍：「我在蜃楼等。」小桨趴在滩上听了半天：「地底下有东西在喘气，很慢，很大。」

column2: Price-Tag Beach
column3: 估货滩

column2: A beach on the coast where, every morning, a market floats up on the sea to the east, banners streaming, voices faint. When it fades a few fishermen row back from that direction, their boats loaded with cloth, iron pots, packets of tea. A pirate band holds the head of the beach and waylays these returning boats, taking the goods and shoving the people overboard.
column3: 海边一片滩，每天清早，东边海上浮出一座集市，旗幡招展，人声隐约。集市散了，就有几个渔户划着小船从那个方向回来，船上装着布匹、铁锅、茶包。一伙海盗守在滩头，专截这些回来的小船，货抢了，人推下水。

column2: The pirates are chased off and the fishermen haul their goods back aboard. Every item has a price tag tied to it, the ink gone yellow, dated 'Dingwei year, eighth month, twenty-fifth day', priced at ten-year-old prices. 'The sea market's goods are real,' a fisherman says. 'The sellers aren't. Whatever the tag says, that's what you pay.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，渔户们捞起了自己的货。每件货上都系着一张价签，墨色发黄，日子写着「丁未年八月廿五」，价钱是十年前的价钱。渔户说：「海市的货是真的，卖货的是假的。价签上写多少，就付多少。」

column2: Market-Board Rise
column3: 市牌岗

column2: On a rise above the shore stands an old board reading 'Sea Market, opens at the hour of the Dragon, closes at noon', and beneath it sits an old broker with a steelyard across his knees, known as Old Scale. Every morning when the market appears he calls its prices out over the water, and the people ashore trade by his word. A pirate band has come up the rise to make him call 'pirate prices', and he squints at them and won't change a figure.
column3: 岸边高岗上立着一块旧木牌，上书「海市，辰开午散」，木牌底下坐着一个老牙郎，膝上搁一杆秤，人称老秤。每天辰时海市一出，他就对着海上的集市报价，岸上的人照他的价买卖。一伙海盗上了岗，要他报个「海盗价」，他眯着眼，一个字不改。

column2: The pirates are thrown off the rise. Old Scale says he's seen the people of the sea market every day for ten years and not one has aged; every day they quote the same prices and buy the same things. 'That's the market of the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month, Dingwei year. The day the Qianli's people came to market.' He taps his steelyard. 'The people out there are living that one day. The people on shore are just living.'
column3: 海盗被打下了岗。老秤说，海市上的人他天天见，十年了，一个也没老，天天讲同样的价，买同样的东西：「那是丁未年八月廿五的集，那一天，千里号的人来赶过集。」他磕了磕秤杆：「海上的人在过那一天，岸上的人在过日子。」

column2: Cut-Cable Cove
column3: 断缆湾

column2: In a cove dozens of small boats are tied every which way, their cables half hacked through. This is a pirate band's main camp: over ten years who knows how many people have tried to row out to the sea market, and the pirates catch them at the cove's mouth, keep the people as labourers and tie up the boats. There are plenty of pirates here, with a squad of mirage soldiers among them, blades glinting in the morning light.
column3: 一道湾里横七竖八拴着几十条小船，缆绳都被砍断了一半。这是一伙海盗的大营：十年里不知多少人想划船去海市，海盗就在湾口截船，人扣下做苦力，船拴在湾里。营里海盗不少，还掺着一队蜃兵，刀枪在晨光里一闪一闪。

column2: The pirate camp is broken and the captives freed. The pirate chief says he rowed for the market himself once; a whole day of rowing and it stayed just as far. A Zhou stands at the cove's mouth watching the market all morning and suddenly points at a figure: a fat cook with two baskets of salt fish, haggling. 'That's Old Ding, the Qianli's head cook. I saw him when I was a boy.'
column3: 海盗营被打散，扣下的人放了。海盗头目说他自己也划去过海市，划了一整天，集市还在那么远。阿舟站在湾口看了一早上的海市，忽然指着一个人影：一个胖厨子，挑着两筐咸鱼讨价还价。「是老鼎，千里号的大厨。我小时候见过他。」

column2: Scale Family Inn
column3: 秤家栈

column2: A coaching inn on the coast road, run by Old Scale's wife, Granny Scale. Every morning at the hour of the Dragon the guests carry stools out to the door and watch the sea market like a play. A pirate band has taken the inn and now charges a mace of silver per stool, and the rice jars and wine jars have all gone up to the best rooms where they sleep. Granny Scale tends the stove and curses as she stokes.
column3: 海边大路上一座客栈，是老秤的老伴秤婆开的，每天辰时，客人都搬了凳子坐在门口看海市，像看戏。一伙海盗占了客栈，把看海市的凳子收了钱，一张凳子一钱银子，米缸、酒坛全搬进了他们住的上房。秤婆在灶下烧火，一边烧一边骂。

column2: The pirates are thrown out and the stools go back by the door, free of charge. Granny Scale says the Qianli's people stayed here that day ten years ago and left early next morning, and today's sea market shows them heading out that morning too. 'I watch them go every day. Never once in time to keep them breakfast.'
column3: 海盗被撵走，凳子又搬回了门口，不收钱。秤婆说十年前那一天千里号的人也住过这店，第二天一早走，今天的海市里也有他们早上出门的样子，「我天天看他们走，一回都没赶上留饭」。

column2: From the best rooms you seize the pirates' stores: twenty jars of aged wine, a crock of salt fish, four sacks of white flour, and a pile of silver scraps from the stool fees. Granny Scale counts it: exactly enough to replace every smashed window.
column3: 上房里抄出海盗囤的二十坛老酒、一缸咸鱼、四袋白面，还有一摞看凳子收的碎银，秤婆数了数，正好够把被砸的窗子都换新。

column2: Each time you pass, Granny Scale keeps a pot of hot congee and a steamer of buns for you. 'The ones out on the sea I can't keep. You I can. Eat your fill before you go.'
column3: 每次路过，秤婆都给你们留一锅热粥、一笼包子，说：「海上那些人我留不住，你们我留得住。吃饱了再走。」

column2: Knock-Salt Flat
column3: 敲盐坪

column2: The salt flat is white from edge to edge, and dozens of salt workers push brine into squares with wooden rakes to dry. A band of pirates has taken the flat, with a squad of mirage soldiers to drive the work, and every grain goes onto their boats. A girl of eight or nine walks among them with a wooden salt spoon, knocking on people. A salt worker: knock. A pirate: knock. A mirage soldier: the spoon goes straight through him. She nods and writes in a little book: 'Not real.'
column3: 盐滩上一片白，几十个盐工拿木耙把卤水推成方格，晒成盐。一伙海盗占了盐坪，夹着一队蜃兵督工，晒出的盐全装上他们的船。有个八九岁的丫头拎着一把木盐勺，挨个敲人：敲盐工，「咚」；敲海盗，「咚」；敲到一个蜃兵，勺子从他身上穿了过去。她点点头，在小本子上记了一笔：「假的。」

column2: The pirates run and the soldiers scatter. The girl is called Lumei, and the book is her Real-or-Not Book. Growing up under the Mirage, she can't tell what's real, so she knocks on everything and writes 'real' for what knocks back. She knocks on you too: 'Houqianli: real.' The first page is about her father, Luda: 'Went to the White City three years ago. Not back. Real.'
column3: 海盗跑了，蜃兵散了。丫头叫卤妹，小本子叫「真假簿」：在蜃楼底下长大，她分不清哪些是真的，就挨个敲，敲得响的记「真」。她也敲了敲你们，记下：「后千里，真。」簿子头一页写着她爹卤大：「三年前往白城去了，未回。真。」

column2: Same-Day Town
column3: 复日城

column2: At low tide a sand ridge rises from the sea and leads to a small walled town, its gate reading 'Mirage Harbour'. The streets bustle, but everyone says the same things: the fishmonger calls 'Twenty-fifth of the eighth month, fresh today!', an old man at his door says 'The Qianli's people have come to town.' A few town wardens stop you and hand you a sheet of paper: 'You're the Qianli's people. Read your lines.' On the gate tower stands a woman with a short blade at her waist, pointing at something out to sea.
column3: 退潮时，海边露出一道沙脊，通到一座小城，城门上写着「蜃港」。城里人来人往，热闹得很，可每个人说的话都一样：卖鱼的喊「八月廿五，新鲜的」，老头在门口说「千里号的人进城了」。几个镇丁拦住你们，递来一张纸：「你们是千里号的，照着念。」城楼上站着一个腰挂短刀的女人，正朝海上指着什么。

column2: The wardens are driven back. The townsfolk falter for a moment, then go on with their lines. The woman on the gate tower wavers and fades: Shen Du, cast up by the sea market as she was that day ten years ago. An old sweet seller whispers that the townsfolk are real. Mirage Harbour fell on hard times long ago, and everyone lives by that one day in the sky. 'On that day, everyone made money.'
column3: 镇丁被打退，城里人愣了一下，又接着念自己的词。城楼上那个女人的影子一晃就淡了：是海市里映出来的沈渡，十年前那一天的她。一个卖糖的老汉偷偷告诉你们：城里的人是真的，蜃港早就败了，大家照着天上那一天过日子，「那一天，人人都有钱赚」。

column2: Thirst Lake Flats
column3: 渴湖滩

column2: On the road east there is always a lake ahead, bright water mirroring the sky, and for every mile you walk it backs away a mile. A band of Mirage Mother believers in white hemp hold the crossroads, handing travellers empty waterskins: 'The Mother gives water. It's just ahead, no need to carry any.' Plenty believe them and walk toward the lake with empty skins until they drop with parched throats, and then the believers go and collect their bundles. Today they've stopped Lumei, and they tell her the Mother took her father too.
column3: 往东的路上，前头总有一片湖，水亮汪汪地映着天，可走一里，湖退一里。一伙披白麻的蜃母教徒守在路口，给过路人发空水囊：「蜃母赐水，前头就是，不必带。」不少人信了，空着水囊往湖走，走到口干舌燥倒在地上，教徒再去收他们的包袱。今天他们拦住了卤妹，说她爹也是蜃母收走的。

column2: The believers are beaten, and Lumei hugs an empty waterskin and grumbles. Axi points at the lake. 'The ground's baking, so the air right against it is hotter and thinner. Light coming slantwise from the sky gets bent back upward by it. That "water" is a patch of sky.' In the believers' register: 'Luda, given to the Mother.' Lumei strikes it out. 'He didn't believe in that. Not real.'
column3: 教徒们败了，卤妹抱着空水囊直哼哼。阿汐指着那片湖：「地面晒得滚烫，贴地那一层空气更热、更稀，天光斜照下来，被它往上一折。你看见的『水』，是一块天。」教徒的簿子上写着「卤大，献蜃母」。卤妹一笔划掉：「他不信这个。假的。」

column2: Skim Reef
column3: 抽水礁

column2: Beneath the sea market lies a reef that shows at low tide, and the few fishermen still trading ashore set up stalls on it, buying and selling by the prices in the sky. A pirate band has taken the head of the reef and skims three parts in ten from every sale, 'drawing water' they call it, with a squad of mirage archers posted on top so from afar it looks like a fort. The fishermen are crowded at the reef's foot, stalls lapped by waves.
column3: 海市底下有一片礁，退潮时露出来，岸上几个还在做买卖的渔户就在礁上摆摊，对着天上的集市照价收货。一伙海盗盘踞礁头，每卖一样抽三成，叫「抽水」，还拉着一队蜃弓手站在礁顶，远看像一座炮台。渔户们挤在礁脚，货摊挨着海浪。

column2: The pirates are driven off the reef and the fishermen's stalls move back to the good spots. An old fisherman looks up at the market in the sky and sighs. 'Five years ago you could count the pockmarks on those people's faces. Now their noses and eyes are a blur.' The market fades a little more every year, he says, like a painting left too long in the sun.
column3: 海盗被赶下了礁，渔户的摊子挪回了好地方。一个老渔户望着天上的集市叹气：「五年前，海市上的人脸上的麻子都数得清；现在鼻子眼睛都糊了。」他说海市一年比一年淡，像一幅晒久了的画。

column2: Empty Hoof Plain
column3: 空蹄原

column2: A troop of mirage riders charges at you across the plain, hooves flying, dust rolling, and after the time it takes to eat a meal they are still exactly as far away. What actually falls on you is a gang of horse-thieving salt bandits on scrawny mounts, hiding in the phantom dust and loosing arrows that come out of the image. Lumei crouches and feels the ground. 'The hoofbeats under my hand are far off. The close ones are those skinny horses.'
column3: 荒原上一队蜃骑朝你们冲过来，马蹄翻飞，尘土滚滚，冲了一顿饭的工夫，还在原地那么远。真正扑上来的是躲在蜃骑尘影里的一伙盗马盐寇，骑着瘦马，放冷箭，箭箭从幻影里钻出来。卤妹蹲下摸了摸地：「蹄声在脚底下，远着呢。近的是那几匹瘦的。」

column2: The bandits scatter. They say that troop charges every day and has never arrived; there's probably a real camp drilling somewhere a long way off. Lumei opens her book and, beside her father's page, copies out something he used to say: 'Everything you see is there. Just not where it looks.' For the first time she thinks he wasn't only saying it to soothe her.
column3: 盐寇被打散了。他们说那队骑兵天天冲，从没冲到过，大概真有一营人在很远的地方操练。卤妹翻开真假簿，在她爹那一页旁边抄上他常说的一句话：「看见的东西都在，只是不在那儿。」她头一回觉得，这句话不是哄她的。

column2: Ten-Year Ledger Loft
column3: 十年账楼

column2: A small timber loft on the plain, crammed with ledgers: Old Scale's ten years of sea-market accounts, every day's sales and prices written down. A pirate band has heard the books record 'where the sea market hides its goods' and surrounded the loft with a troop of mirage riders, piling firewood underneath and threatening to light it if he won't hand them over. Old Scale sits at the top of the stairs hugging a stack of ledgers and doesn't move.
column3: 荒原上一座小木楼，楼上堆满了账本，是老秤十年来的海市账：每天海市卖了什么、什么价，他都记一笔。一伙海盗听说账里记着「海市藏货的地方」，带着一队蜃骑围了木楼，在楼下堆柴，说再不交账就点火。老秤抱着一摞账本坐在楼梯口，一动不动。

column2: The pirates are run off and the firewood carried away. Old Scale shows you the ledgers: every day for ten years the same goods sold, but each day's total a little smaller than the last. Three hundred and twenty items the first year, a hundred and ten this year. 'The goods haven't run out. The stalls in the sky are going, one by one.' He shuts the book. 'Someone can't remember that day any more.'
column3: 海盗被赶走，柴堆搬开了。老秤翻账给你们看：十年里每天卖的都是同样的东西，可每天的总数都比前一天少一点，第一年三百二十样，今年只剩一百一十样。「不是货少了，是天上的摊子一个个没了。」他合上账：「有人记不住那一天了。」

column2: Memory-Swap Stall
column3: 换忆摊

column2: A half-collapsed goods shed on the shore, piled with real things: copper basins, satin, crates of needles and thread. But the stall keeper is an old merchant cast down from the Mirage, smiling at you through a sheen of water. He takes no money, only a memory you remember clearly: tell him one, and he hands you one item. Once you've told it, you can't quite remember it yourself. A pirate band guards the front of the shed and chases off everyone who comes to trade, meaning to keep the business for themselves.
column3: 海边一座半塌的货棚，棚里堆着真东西：铜盆、绸缎、成箱的针线。看摊的却是个蜃楼里映下来的老掌柜，隔着一层水光朝你们笑，不收钱，只收一段记得清清楚楚的事：你说一件，他递一件货。说完了，你自己就记不太清了。一伙海盗守在棚前，把来换货的人一个个撵走，要独吞这笔买卖。

column2: The pirates are routed and the old merchant opens for business as before, happy to trade with you. Xiaojiang swaps a memory of a dreadful dinner for an iron pot, then pats his stomach and says he can't recall what was dreadful about it. Axi thinks a moment and doesn't trade. 'Nothing about my father. Not one thing.' The old merchant smiles and nods, as if someone told him the same ten years ago.
column3: 海盗被打跑，老掌柜照旧开张，愿意跟你们换货。小桨拿一顿难吃的晚饭换了一口铁锅，换完拍着肚子说已经想不起来哪里难吃了。阿汐想了想，没换：「我爹的事，一件也不给。」老掌柜笑着点头，像十年前也有人这么跟他说过。

column2: The Rival House
column3: 对门行

column2: At a crossroads on the plain a big new trading house has opened, its sign reading 'The House Across the Way', and it exists to undercut Old Scale: whatever he calls for the sea market, they call ten per cent less. The owner has hired mirage riders and swordsmen to guard the door and sends clerks out daily to copy down every deal in the sea market, a whole room of copies by now. Today they mean to stop every one of Old Scale's customers on the road.
column3: 荒原路口新开了一家大商行，门匾上写着「对门行」，专跟老秤作对：老秤报海市的价，他们就压低一成。商行的东家雇了一伙蜃骑和刀客守门，又派伙计天天抄海市上的买卖，抄了满满一屋。今天他们要把老秤的客人全拦下，一个也不许过路。

column2: The swordsmen scatter and the owner spreads out his copies, begging for mercy. One page lists what the Qianli bought that day: three hundred straw hats, thirty casks of fresh water, a set of lute strings, and 'one pair of girl's shoes, embroidered with little fish'. Axi stares at that line a long time. 'When I was small, my shoes had little fish on them.'
column3: 刀客散了，东家把抄本摊开求饶。抄本里有一页是千里号那天买的东西：草帽三百顶，淡水三十桶，琵琶弦一副，还有「女童鞋一双，绣小鱼」。阿汐盯着那一行看了很久：「我小时候，鞋上就绣小鱼。」

column2: House of a Thousand Paintings
column3: 千画屋

column2: A mud house on the plain, its walls, beams and door panels covered in paintings, all of the White City in the sky. The painter is an old scholar who paints one every morning when the city appears; eleven years of it, and no two alike. A gang of salt smugglers barges in, calling the paintings treasure maps, and starts carrying them off in bundles. The old man throws himself across them. 'These are paintings of the sky! What treasure is there in the sky?'
column3: 荒原上一间土屋，墙上、梁上、门板上全是画，画的都是天上那座白城。画师是个老秀才，每天清早白城一出来，他就画一张，画了十一年，没有两张一样。一伙盐枭闯进屋，说这些画是「藏宝图」，要成捆搬走。老秀才扑在画上：「这画的是天！天上哪来的宝！」

column2: The smugglers are driven off. Lumei leafs through the paintings one by one and suddenly cries out: in the last two years' work, on top of the White City's tallest tower, there's a tiny figure with a salt rake on his shoulder, waving in every single picture. The old man has puzzled over it too. 'Towers don't move. People do. If a living man turns up in the picture, then somebody really is standing there.'
column3: 盐枭被赶走了。卤妹一张张翻画，忽然叫起来：近两年的画里，白城最高那座塔顶上多了个小人，扛着盐耙，每一张都在挥手。老秀才也纳闷过：「楼是死的，人是活的。活人上了画，那就是真有人站在那儿。」

column2: Script Street
column3: 念词街

column2: On Same-Day Town's long street everyone speaks from the script, not a word more, not a word less. But today the script is sticking: the fishmonger stalls halfway through his cry, the old man at the gate stands with his mouth open, unable to remember which way the Qianli's people came in. The keeper of the script is the night watchman Old Clapper, patrolling the street with town wardens and a few mirage soldiers, throwing out anyone who gets it wrong. They have hold of a little girl who said something that isn't in the script: 'See you tomorrow.'
column3: 复日城的长街上，人人照着词说话，一句不多，一句不少。可今天词卡住了：卖鱼的喊到一半，忘了下一句；城门口的老头张着嘴，想不起千里号的人从哪边进城。管词的是更夫老梆，带着一队镇丁和几个蜃兵沿街巡查，谁说错了就往城外撵。他们正揪着一个小丫头：她说了一句词里没有的话，「明天见」。

column2: The wardens are driven back and the little girl hides behind you. She's the sweet seller's granddaughter, born after that day, so the script has no part for her and she has to say things of her own. Old Clapper leafs through his worn script book muttering: several patches of the day in the sky have blurred, and he fills each one from his own memory. 'What I can't fill is gone.'
column3: 镇丁被打退，小丫头躲到你们身后。她是卖糖老汉的孙女，生在那一天之后，词里根本没有她，她只好自己说话。老梆翻着他那本磨破的词本，嘴里念念有词：天上那一天糊了好几块，他拿自己的记性一块块补，「补不上的，就是没了」。

column2: Salt Tax Barrier
column3: 盐课卡

column2: A tax barrier at the crossroads, where salt-tax men with ledgers collect from everyone: on the salt you carry, on the salt in your cart, and on the salt barns in the Mirage up in the sky, charged 'by sight', ten coppers a look. Salt workers walk past with hands over their eyes and still get caught: you saw it through your fingers. Behind the barrier crouches a squad of mirage archers to back the tax men up.
column3: 路口一座税卡，几个盐课税丁捧着簿子挨个收税：你挑的盐要收，你车上的盐要收，天上蜃楼里那几座盐仓，也按「过目」收，看一眼十文。过路的盐工捂着眼睛走，还是被逮住，说你从指头缝里看见了。卡后头蹲着一队蜃弓手，替税丁压阵。

column2: The tax men cover their heads and the barrier comes down. In their tax book, three years back, is a line: 'East Brine Works, Luda, salt tax paid, two dou.' Lumei taps the page with her spoon. 'A real tax means a real salt works.' A tax man mutters that the East Brine Works is three days off on the coast, in the very direction where the White City hangs in the sky.
column3: 税丁抱头，卡子拆了。翻他们的税簿，三年前有一行：「东卤场，卤大，缴盐税二斗。」卤妹拿勺子敲了敲那一页：「真的税，就有真的盐场。」税丁小声说，东卤场在三天路外的海边，天上的白城，就挂在那个方向。

column2: Passing Shadows
column3: 过街影

column2: Every morning at the Dragon hour the sea market's shadow falls across this street ashore, and a file of people walks from the inn to the harbour: men with carrying poles, men with casks, someone hugging a lute, laughing and chatting. The Qianli's people, ten years ago. The living on the street step aside for them. A pirate band mixes in among the shadows to rob, then ducks behind them, and whoever gives chase cuts at nothing but light.
column3: 每天辰时，海市的影子落到岸上这条大街，一队人从客栈走向码头：挑担的、扛桶的、抱琵琶的，有说有笑，正是十年前千里号的人。街上的真人都给影子让路。一伙海盗混在影子里抢东西，抢完往影子背后一躲，追的人一刀砍下去，砍的是一片光。

column2: The pirates are dragged out of the shadows one by one. The shadows walk on toward the harbour as before, and last of all comes a dark-faced man squinting out to sea, carrying a pair of little shoes embroidered with fish. Axi runs at him and passes straight through. She stands in the middle of the street, looking back at him. 'Dad, they're too small now.'
column3: 海盗被一个个从影子里揪出来。影子照旧往码头走，走在最后的是个黑脸汉子，眯着眼看海，手里提着一双绣小鱼的小鞋。阿汐冲上去，从他身上穿了过去。她站在街当中，回头望着那个背影：「爹，鞋小了。」

column2: Huo's Betting Tent
column3: 霍家赌棚

column2: In the middle of the salt flat stands a great roaring tent: the gambling house of the salt smuggler Huo Baimei, where the bets are on the Mirage. How many towers today, right way up or upside down, gone before the sun turns west or not. Losers have staked salt, boats, even daughters. Dozens of smugglers and mirage soldiers guard the tent, and no one who won't bet may pass.
column3: 盐滩当中搭着一座大棚，棚里人声鼎沸，是盐枭霍白眉开的赌场，赌的是蜃楼：今天天上出几座楼，楼是正是倒，日头偏西前散不散。押错的人把盐、船，甚至女儿都押了进去。棚外几十个盐枭夹着蜃兵守着，不赌的不许过路。

column2: The smugglers scatter and Huo Baimei has to own up. Three years ago Luda placed a big bet here: 'The White City is real, and I'll walk there to show you.' His stake was his salt rake. He went and never came back to report, so Huo hung the rake on the wall as his winnings. Lumei takes it down; her name is carved in the handle. Huo scratches his head. 'That one, I was hoping to lose.'
column3: 盐枭散了，霍白眉只好认账：三年前卤大在这儿押过一注大的，「白城是真的，我走过去给你们看」，押的是他的盐耙。他一走没回来报，霍就把耙挂在墙上当了赢头。卤妹摘下耙，耙柄上刻着她的名字。霍白眉挠挠头：「这一注，我倒是盼着输。」

column2: Market-Listening Slope
column3: 听市坡

column2: A gentle slope above the shore. On early mornings, cold sea below and warm air above, the sea market's sounds roll all the way up here: hawkers' cries, abacus beads, gongs, every one distinct. A pirate band has put up listening booths and charges five coppers for an incense stick's worth of listening, with a few mirage archers to keep out anyone who won't pay. 'Sound is goods too.'
column3: 岸边一道缓坡，清早海上冷、天上暖，海市的声音能一路滚到坡上来：吆喝、算盘、铜锣，听得清清楚楚。一伙海盗在坡上搭了几座听棚，一个人听一炷香收五文，还雇了几个蜃弓手守着，不交钱的人连坡都不许上，说「声音也是货」。

column2: The pirates are run off the slope, the booths come down, and everyone sits in the grass listening for free. Xiaojiang listens a long while with his eyes shut, then sits bolt upright: under all the clamour someone is humming, the song from Mermaid Reef. Axi's hands clench. 'That's my father. He hummed it every night aboard, and that day too.' So the sounds of that day were kept as well, and have been circling out at sea ever since.
column3: 海盗被撵下坡，听棚拆了，大家坐在草里白听。小桨闭着眼听了半天，忽然坐直：一片吵嚷底下，有人在哼歌，是鲛人礁上那支歌。阿汐的手攥紧了：「是我爹。他每晚在船上哼，十年前那一天也哼过。」原来那天的声音也被记了下来，一直在海上转。

column2: Reed Shed Post
column3: 苇棚哨

column2: A row of reed sheds at the edge of the salt marsh, tattered flags on the roofs. Mirage archers hold the place, and when their arrows come the bowmen look two li off, though they're lying in the reeds two hundred paces away: the shimmer has moved their shapes. Travellers shoot back at the shapes and never hit a thing. Lumei doesn't watch the men, she watches the reeds. 'Wherever the reeds shake, that's where they are.'
column3: 盐沼边一溜苇棚，棚顶插着破旗。一伙蜃弓手守在这里，箭射过来时，弓手看着像在两里外，其实就趴在两百步外的苇子里：热气把他们的影子挪远了。过路人照着影子还手，一箭也挨不着。卤妹不看人，盯着苇子：「哪片苇子晃，人就在哪儿。」

column2: The archers are dragged out of the reeds one by one. They had just robbed a salt pedlar from the east, and his basket holds salt cakes stamped with thumbprints. Lumei holds one up, sets her own hand against the print, and her eyes go red: salt is handed in with a thumbprint, and this thumb has a scar across it, just like her father's. 'This salt is new. He's still making salt.'
column3: 弓手一个个被揪出苇子。他们刚劫过一个东边来的盐贩，筐里是一块块按了手印的盐饼。卤妹捧起一块，把自己的手往印子上一比，眼圈红了：交盐要按手印，这个拇指上有道疤，她爹的拇指就有。「盐是新的，他还在晒盐。」

column2: Salt-Bone Ship
column3: 盐骨船

column2: A great ship sits on dry land a dozen li from the sea, crusted white with salt like sugar frosting, its mast still standing. A pirate band uses it as a den, the hold piled with loot, and at night they light fires on deck, so from afar it really looks like a ship sailing over land. Lumei knocks on the planking. 'Knock. Real. But how did a ship get here?'
column3: 平地上搁着一条大船，离海十几里，船身结满白盐，像裹了一层糖霜，桅杆还立着。一伙海盗拿它当窝，舱里堆着抢来的东西，夜里在甲板上点火，远远看去，真像一条船在陆地上航行。卤妹敲了敲船板：「咚，真的。可船怎么会在这儿？」

column2: The pirates are put off the ship. Gong Modou scrapes away the salt crust to look at the planks. 'Old. A hundred, two hundred years at least.' An old salt worker says this flat was once a bay; sand choked its mouth, the sun dried it year after year, the water left, the salt stayed, and so did the ship. On the hold wall, in fresh charcoal: 'East, three days. Lu.'
column3: 海盗被赶下了船。龚墨斗刮开盐壳看船板：「老船，少说一两百年。」老盐工说，这片盐滩从前是海湾，湾口被沙堵死，太阳一年年晒，水走了，盐留下了，船也搁下了。舱壁上有一行新划的炭字：「往东，三日。卤。」

column2: Brine Post
column3: 卤水驿

column2: The only post station on the salt flat: a few mud rooms around a brine pool, where travellers rest, change shoes and buy pickles. A gang of smugglers who carry themselves like soldiers has taken it, sent the postmistress to sleep in the stable, and sealed the grain jars, pickle crocks and straw sandals. To rest here you pay three dou of salt; no salt, and you work it off raking their brine pool.
column3: 盐滩上唯一的一座驿站，几间土房围着一口卤池，过路人在这儿歇脚、换鞋、买腌菜。一伙兵痞模样的盐枭占了驿站，把驿娘赶去马棚里住，粮缸、菜坛、草鞋全贴了封条。要歇脚，先交三斗盐；交不出盐，就去卤池里替他们捞盐抵账。

column2: The thugs are thrown out, the postmistress goes back to her stove and smoke rises again. She remembers Luda staying a night three years ago; he traded salt for new shoes and asked how far the White City was. A day, it looks like, she told him. He said he'd worked it out: three days. 'It only looks close because the light is fooling you.'
column3: 兵痞被撵走，驿娘回到灶前，炉子又冒了烟。她记得三年前卤大在这儿住过一夜，拿盐换了双新鞋，问她白城有多远。她说看着一天路。他说他算过，要三天：「看着近，是光哄人。」

column2: From the post you seize the thugs' hoard: twelve crocks of pickled radish, forty pairs of new straw sandals, three sacks of brown rice, and a small iron pot with the postmistress's name scratched on the bottom, the first thing they took from her.
column3: 驿里抄出兵痞囤的十二坛腌萝卜、四十双新草鞋、三袋糙米，还有一口小铁锅，锅底刻着驿娘的名字，是他们头一天就抢走的。

column2: Each time you pass, the postmistress gives each of you a pair of newly plaited sandals with double soles, because the salt flat burns your feet, and ladles out a bowl of pickled radish. 'Salt with salt. Walk the salt road and you'll never lack for flavour.'
column3: 每次路过，驿娘都给你们每人一双新编的草鞋，鞋底垫了两层，说盐滩烫脚；再舀一碗腌萝卜：「咸的配咸的，走盐路不口淡。」

column2: The Watch Tower
column3: 更楼

column2: At the top of Same-Day Town stands a watch tower, and every day before dawn Old Clapper beats the first watch there; hearing the clapper, the town rises and begins living the twenty-fifth of the eighth month again. Town wardens and a squad of mirage soldiers guard the foot of the tower in strength, and no one may touch the clapper. Seeing you come up, Old Clapper hugs it to his chest. 'This day can't be broken. If it breaks, she won't find the place when she comes back.'
column3: 复日城最高处是一座更楼，每天天不亮，老梆就在楼上敲第一更，城里人听见梆子声就起床，开始过八月廿五。楼下守着镇丁和一队蜃兵，人数不少，谁也不许碰那面梆子。今天老梆见你们上来，把梆子抱在怀里：「这一天不能断。断了，她回来就找不着地方了。」

column2: This time the wardens and mirage soldiers scatter. Old Clapper sits on the stairs and tells the day as it was. The Qianli's people came to town, and Captain Shen bought up the whole market's goods, paid in silver, and said, 'Keep them for those who come after.' At dusk she stood on the gate tower and said, 'Open the market tomorrow as usual.' Next day the ships left, the sea market went up into the sky, and there was never a day so good again. 'So we've gone on as usual ever since.' The sweet seller's granddaughter hands you a sweet and calls, 'Twenty-sixth of the eighth month! New sweets, five coppers!' It's the first new line in ten years. But half the town can't bear to let that day go; before long someone will climb the tower to beat the clapper for Old Clapper, and the wardens will gather again. You'll have to come back.
column3: 这一回镇丁和蜃兵都散了。老梆坐在楼梯上，说出了那一天：千里号的人进城，沈船主把满市的货都买了下来，付了现银，说「替后来的人留着」；傍晚她站在城楼上说，「明天照常开市」。第二天船走了，海市就挂上了天，再也没有那样的好日子。「我们就一直照常着。」卖糖老汉的孙女把一块糖递给你们，喊了一声：「八月廿六，新糖，五文！」那是十年来头一句新词。可城里还有一半人舍不得那一天，过不了几日，又会有人摸上更楼，替老梆敲梆子，镇丁又会聚起来。你们还得再来。

column2: Mirage Mother Cove
column3: 蜃母湾

column2: A band of old pirates lives by the cove, every beard gone white, too old for raiding, so they charge 'asking money' at the cove's mouth: one tael to ask the way to the sea market, two to ask what it is. Their leader is a gap-toothed old woman the pirates all call Mother. She sits on a rock cracking melon seeds, ringed by mirage soldiers, humming a little tune.
column3: 海湾边住着一伙老海盗，个个白了胡子，打不动劫，就在湾口收「问路钱」：问海市怎么去，一两；问海市是什么，二两。领头的是个缺牙的老婆婆，海盗们都喊她娘。她坐在礁上嗑瓜子，身边站着一圈蜃兵，嘴里还哼着小调。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter and the old pirates huddle together, but the old woman stays calm and gives you the two-tael answer for nothing. The old folk say there's a great shen in the sea, a clam, so big no one can see its edges, and when it breathes out, towers rise in the sky. 'It's not breath it breathes. It's what it remembers. It remembered that day, so it breathes it out every day.' She spits out a seed husk. 'An old thing like that. Its memory must be going too.'
column3: 蜃兵散了，老海盗们缩成一团，老婆婆倒不慌，二两的那句白送给你们：老辈人说，海里有一只大蜃，蛤蜊那样的，大得看不见边，它一吐气，天上就起楼。「它吐的不是气，是它记得的事。那天它记住了，就天天吐。」她吐出一片瓜子皮：「老东西，记性也该不好了。」

column2: Brine Shrimp Lake
column3: 卤虫湖

column2: On the shore of the little salt lake a blind old fisherman sweeps for brine shrimp with a fine gauze net: red creatures the size of a fingernail, dried to feed fish and hens. A few pirates have taken his net, sneered that shrimp are worthless, and are using it to scoop wild ducks, tearing it in several places. The old man feels his way along the shore after them. 'Give it back! I count my days by it!'
column3: 小咸水湖边，一个瞎眼的老渔翁拿细纱网捞卤虫：一种指甲大的红虫子，晒干了喂鱼喂鸡。几个海盗抢了他的纱网，嫌卤虫不值钱，拿网去兜湖边的野鸭，网兜破了好几处。老渔翁摸着湖岸一路追：「网还我！我靠它数日子呢！」

column2: The net is recovered. The old man says that three years ago Luda walked a day along the lake with him. 'He stuck a pole in the ground and sighted the towers' feet against it. The feet hang in the air, he said, so the light has turned a corner, and what comes round a corner is farther than it looks.' Then he turns his ear to the water. 'He hummed all the way when he left. A tune for putting a child to sleep.'
column3: 网要回来了。老渔翁说三年前卤大陪他在湖边走过一天，「他拿根竿子插在地上，比着天上的楼脚，说楼脚悬着不沾地，是光拐了弯，拐弯来的东西，比看着远」。说完他侧耳听了听湖面：「他走的时候一路哼歌，哼的是哄小孩睡觉的调子。」

column2: Runaways' Hollow
column3: 逃丁窝

column2: South of the salt flat lies sand, and in a sandy hollow hides a gang of runaway salt workers: fled from a salt works in the east, turned outlaw, robbing travellers of flatbread and water and losing most of the fights, so starved they've roped in a few mirage soldiers for show. They charge with clubs, and Lumei takes one look at their hands and shouts, 'Those are salt workers' hands! Don't hit too hard!'
column3: 盐滩往南是一片沙，沙窝里猫着一伙逃盐丁：从东边盐场逃出来的，在这儿落了草，拦路抢饼抢水，又抢不过谁，饿得前胸贴后背，只好拉了几个蜃兵充门面。他们挥着棍子冲上来，卤妹一眼看见他们的手，喊：「是晒盐的手！别打太狠！」

column2: The runaways drop their clubs and kneel in the sand begging food. They know Luda: an old hand at the East Brine Works who stepped in front when the foreman was beating someone and took three lashes on his back. He asked them to carry a little bird carved from salt to his daughter, and they've carried it a year without knowing where to take it. Lumei takes the bird and licks it. 'Salty. Real.'
column3: 逃盐丁扔了棍子，跪在沙里讨吃的。他们认得卤大：东卤场的老把式，管头打人，他挡在前头，背上挨了三鞭。他托他们给女儿捎一只盐雕的小鸟，他们揣了一年，不知道往哪儿送。卤妹接过小鸟，舔了一下：「咸的。真的。」

column2: Next-Morning Tea Shed
column3: 翌日茶棚

column2: A tea shed by the road, kept by a family who moved out of Same-Day Town; they won't live that day again and sell tea here to live their own. The town wardens hate them for breaking the rule and come every few days with mirage riders to smash the shed: 'Those who leave town don't speak of that day.' Today the teapot's been smashed again, and the owner's son blocks the door with a carrying pole.
column3: 路边一座茶棚，棚主是从复日城搬出来的一家人，不肯再过那一天，在这儿卖茶过自己的日子。城里的镇丁恨他们坏了规矩，带着几个蜃骑隔三岔五来砸棚，说「出城的人，不许提那一天」。今天茶壶又被砸了，棚主的儿子拿扁担堵在门口。

column2: The wardens and riders are run off and the shed boils water again. The owner says the town remembers only the twenty-fifth, but his family remembers the twenty-sixth. 'Early that morning the Qianli's five ships headed east through sea fog. The moment they left, the market went up into the sky, as if someone had written it down for us.' He pours you a bowl of tea. 'Living means going forward.'
column3: 镇丁和蜃骑被打跑了，茶棚又烧开了水。棚主说城里人只记得廿五，他家记得廿六：「那天一早，千里号五条船往东走，满海都是雾。船一走，海市就上了天，像是有谁替我们记下了。」他给你们倒了一碗茶：「过日子，得往后过。」

column2: Crate-Top Stand
column3: 站箱台

column2: Every day at noon, just before the sea market fades, one scene plays in the sky: a woman with a short blade at her waist steps up on a wooden crate and speaks to the whole market, and everyone stops what they're doing. This patch of ground ashore faces the scene squarely, and a pirate band sells 'show tickets' here, with mirage soldiers to block anyone who hasn't paid. Noon is close, the crowd is growing, and the pirates have doubled the price.
column3: 每天正午，海市散之前，天上会映出一幕：一个腰挂短刀的女人站上一只木箱，对满市的人说话，市上的人都停了手。岸上这块平地正对着那一幕，一伙海盗在这里卖「看戏票」，还雇了一队蜃兵挡住不买票的人。今天正午快到了，人越聚越多，海盗把票价翻了一倍。

column2: The pirates scatter and everyone watches the scene. The Shen Du in the sky speaks word by word, her voice carrying over the water: 'I've paid for these goods. Keep them for those who come after. We're going east. The road is long, and people's memories are short. Whoever keeps the road in mind for me, I'll keep their accounts for them.' Then she bows deeply toward the sea. Old Scale says, 'That bow, every single day, and I've never known who she was bowing to.'
column3: 海盗被打散，大家站着看那一幕。天上的沈渡一字一句，声音隔着海传过来：「货我付了，替后来的人留着。我们要往东去，路长，人的记性短。谁替我记着路，我就替谁记着账。」说完，她朝海里深深一揖。老秤说：「天天这一揖，我一直不知道她拜的是谁。」

column2: Snatching Gulls
column3: 叼货鸥

column2: Over a stretch of rocky shore hundreds of gulls wheel and scream. A pirate band has trained the flock to snatch from passers-by's baskets: purses, cloth, buns. The gull master stands on a rock and blows a whistle, and at the sound the flock dives, while a few mirage archers on the rocks loose arrows to clear their way.
column3: 海边一片礁滩上空，几百只海鸥盘旋，叫声刺耳。一伙海盗训了这群鸥，专从过路人筐里叼东西：叼钱袋、叼布头、叼包子。驯鸥的海盗站在礁上吹哨，哨一响，鸥群就扑下来，还有几个蜃弓手在礁顶放箭，替鸥群开路。

column2: The gull master is tied up, his whistle snapped, and after some aimless circling the flock settles back on the rocks. He says at first the gulls couldn't snatch anything: every day they flew into the sea market and came up empty, screaming with hunger, and that gave him the idea of training them on people. 'Birds are more honest than men. Ten years of empty dives, and they've long known it isn't real.'
column3: 驯鸥的海盗被捆了，哨子也折了，鸥群乱飞了一阵，飞回礁上去了。海盗说这群鸥最初是叼不着东西的：它们天天往海市里飞，扑个空，饿得直叫，他才想到驯它们抢人。「鸟比人老实，扑了十年空，它们早知道那是假的。」

column2: Mirror Cart Ring
column3: 镜车阵

column2: A string of big carts rolls in from the north, each with polished bronze mirrors standing upright, scattering light across the plain. The drivers are foreign smugglers who've hired a few mirage archers. They circle the carts on the salt flat so the mirrors throw up a fake city gate and lure travellers in for a night's lodging; whoever goes in won't come out with their bundles.
column3: 一队大车从北边过来，车上竖着一面面磨亮的铜镜，太阳一照，满荒原都是光斑。押车的是一伙番人走私客，雇了几个蜃弓手。他们把镜车在盐滩上摆成一圈，照出一座假城楼，骗过路人进「城」投宿；进去的人，就别想带着包袱出来。

column2: The smugglers scatter, the mirrors are laid flat, and the false city is gone. Their leader says they learned the trick from the sky. 'The city up there is a real city moved somewhere else. Ours is a heap of mirrors.' Lumei copies that into her book and adds beside it: 'The city Dad is in is not mirrors.'
column3: 走私客被打散，镜子一面面放倒，假城没了。头目说这手是跟天上学的：「天上的城，是真城挪了个地方；我们的城，是一堆镜子。」卤妹把这句话抄进簿子，又在旁边添了一句：「爹在的那座城，不是镜子。」

column2: Rope-Snip Marsh
column3: 剪绳沼

column2: In the salt marsh lies a pool of brine with soft, salty mud around it that salt workers always skirt: it's home to a horde of big blue crabs with claws larger than a man's hand, which swarm ashore at night and snip shoes, ropes and laundry on the line. Tonight they're up again, ringing a salt cart stuck in the mud and clacking through its harness ropes while the old woman driving it lays about with her carrying pole.
column3: 盐沼里有一片卤水塘，塘边的泥又软又咸，盐工都绕着走：塘里住着一群大青蟹，钳子比人手还大，夜里成群爬上岸，剪鞋子、剪绳子、剪晾着的衣裳。今晚蟹群又上来了，正围着一辆陷在泥里的盐车，咔嚓咔嚓地剪车绳，赶车的老妪拿扁担左扑右打。

column2: The crabs are driven back into the pool. The old woman carries meals out to the East Brine Works, and she says Luda is a good man there: every time food is handed out he gives the youngest an extra ladle and gnaws the pot scrapings himself. She points east. 'Follow the ruts. Three days. Go on, girl.' Lumei writes her name in the book, and after it: 'Real. Good person.'
column3: 蟹群被赶回了塘里。老妪是给东卤场送饭的，说卤大是场里的好人，每回发饭都多舀一勺给年纪小的，自己啃锅巴。她指了指东边：「顺着车辙走，三天。去吧，丫头。」卤妹把她的名字记进了簿子，后面写：「真，好人。」

column2: Latecomers' Warehouse
column3: 后来仓

column2: At the tip of the headland stands a great stone warehouse, its door carved: 'Paid in full by the Qianli. For those who come after to collect.' For ten years a pirate band has tried to get in and failed: the door has three iron bars and Old Scale holds the keys. So they've camped outside, their fiercest men on guard with a herd of mirage soldiers and riders, surrounding anyone who comes near, waiting for the day Old Scale gives in.
column3: 海岬尽头一座石砌的大仓，门上刻着「千里号付讫，后来者取」。十年来一伙海盗想进仓，进不去：仓门是三道铁闩，钥匙在老秤手里。他们干脆在仓外扎了营，海盗最凶的一批守着，还养了一群蜃兵蜃骑，谁靠近就围上来，等老秤哪天松口。

column2: The pirates are broken and Old Scale brings out three keys. Inside are three hundred straw hats, bolts of cloth, crate after crate of needles and thread, every item labelled 'Twenty-fifth day, eighth month, Dingwei year.' In a corner is a small wooden box holding a girl's shoes embroidered with little fish, and on its lid: 'For Axi, to wear when she's grown.' Axi holds them in her hands, crying and laughing at once. 'Dad, you got the sum wrong. I grew too fast.'
column3: 海盗被打散，老秤掏出三把钥匙。仓里码着三百顶草帽、成匹的布、一箱箱针线，每样都贴着「丁未年八月廿五」。角落里一只小木盒，装着一双绣小鱼的女童鞋，盒盖上写：「给阿汐，长大了穿。」阿汐把鞋捧在手里，又哭又笑：「爹，你算错了，我长得太快了。」

column2: Waiting-for-the-Fall Fleet
column3: 等落船

column2: On the sea beneath the market rides a crowd of pirate ships, hull against hull, masts like a forest. They believe a story: when the old shen dies, the market in the sky will drop into the sea all at once and the water will be full of goods. So they all anchor here and wait, and they've waited years, their hulls thick with barnacles. Mirage soldiers patrol their decks, and at the sight of your ship the gongs start beating.
column3: 海市底下的海面上泊着一大片海盗船，船挨着船，桅杆像一片林子。他们听信了一个说法：等那只老蜃死了，天上的集就会一下子掉进海里，满海都是货。于是全泊在这儿等，等了好几年，船底都长满了藤壶。蜃兵在他们的甲板上巡逻，看见你们的船就敲起了锣。

column2: The pirate fleet is broken and most of it weighs anchor and flees. A captured old helmsman says the market in the sky really is sinking: when he first came it hung three masts high above the water, and now it's a mast and a half. 'The shen is old, so the towers are low.' He glances east. 'Any lower and it'll drop into the sea, and then there'll be nothing.'
column3: 海盗船队被打散，起锚逃了一大半。被俘的老舵工说，天上的集真在往下沉：他刚来时，海市离海面有三根桅那么高，如今只剩一根半。「蜃老了，楼就低了。」他往东边看了一眼，「再低下去，就落进海里，什么也没有了。」

column2: Tower-Watch Stele
column3: 看楼碑

column2: A stone stele stands in the sand, a great character for 'wind' carved on it and a ring of notches around its foot like a clock face. Some salt smugglers are about to lever it over, saying old salt licences are buried under it. Its keeper, a mute old man, clings to the stone and keeps jabbing a finger at the sky, purple in the face.
