column3: 沙地上立着一块石碑，碑上一个大「风」字，碑脚下一圈刻痕，像一面钟。几个盐枭正要把碑撬倒，说碑底下埋着前朝的盐引。守碑的是个哑巴老汉，死死抱着碑身，手指一个劲地朝天上指，急得脸都紫了。

column2: The smugglers scatter. The mute draws it for you in the sand: on mornings when the sea is cold and the air above it warm, the White City comes early and high; when the wind turns rough, the towers break into pieces. The stele is a clock for watching towers, its ring of notches years of sightings. Lumei copies it down: 'The White City doesn't lie. It comes with the weather.'
column3: 盐枭散了。哑巴在沙上画给你们看：哪天早上海面冷、上头的风暖，白城就出得早、出得高；风一乱，楼就碎成一截一截。这块碑是看楼的钟，一圈刻痕记着多少年的楼。卤妹抄下：「白城不骗人，看天出。」

column2: Two-Invitation Stage
column3: 两请台

column2: A straw-roofed stage on the plain, and a small travelling troupe trapped on it between two crowds: salt smugglers on one side, salt-tax men on the other, each demanding the troupe sing at their feast tonight, and threatening to smash the trunks of whichever comes late. The troupe master bows left and right, the clown hides under the stage with his drum, and as the two sides shout, knives come out and a stage board gives way.
column3: 荒原上一座草台，一个走江湖的小戏班被两拨人堵在台上：一拨是盐枭，一拨是盐课税丁，都要戏班今晚到自家席上唱，谁家晚了就砸谁家的箱子。班主左右作揖，丑角抱着鼓躲在台底下。两拨人吵着吵着动了刀，台板都被踩塌了一块。

column2: Both crowds are driven off, and the troupe can choose its own play at last. The clown says that three years ago a salt worker rode a stretch with them and one night stood in as the Salt God, singing off key. Asked where he was going, he said: 'My girl can't tell real from not. I have to walk to something real, so I can show her.' Lumei bows her head and copies the sentence out, one character at a time.
column3: 两拨人都被打跑，戏班总算能自己定唱哪出。丑角说三年前一个晒盐的汉子搭他们的车走过一程，夜里帮着演了一回盐神，唱得跑调。问他去哪儿，他说：「我闺女分不清真假，我得走一趟真的，给她看。」卤妹低着头，把这句话一个字一个字抄下来。

column2: Old Market Footings
column3: 旧市基

column2: A waste of land by the shore, rows of stone plinths lying half buried in sand like a field of low gravestones. This is the real old market of Mirage Harbour, failed ten years ago when its harbour mouth silted up. A pirate band has been digging here for years, sure the merchants left in a hurry with silver buried underfoot, and they keep a big troop of mirage soldiers and riders on guard so no one else can cut in.
column3: 海边一片荒地，地上横着一排排石墩，半埋在沙里，像一片矮矮的墓碑。这是真的旧蜃港集市，十年前就败了，海口淤成了沙。一伙海盗在这里挖了好几年，说当年的商人走得急，地底下埋着银子，他们拉了一大队蜃兵蜃骑守着工地，不许别人插手。

column2: The pirates are chased off and their pits hold nothing but broken tiles. Old Scale counts the plinths one by one and stops at number nineteen. A line is cut deep into its face with a knife: 'The Qianli settled in full here. Shen.' The crate Shen Du stands on in the sky market sat on this very plinth. The stone is real, and so was the day.
column3: 海盗被赶跑，挖开的坑里只有碎瓦。老秤一墩一墩地数，在第十九号石墩前站住了：墩面上刻着一行字，刀刻的，很深，「千里号于此付清。沈」。天上海市里沈渡站的那只木箱，就摆在这一墩上。墩子是真的，那一天也是真的。

column2: Hard Crust Road
column3: 硬壳道

column2: There's only one way east that holds: a strip of hard salt crust with soft mud on either side that swallows a leg to the knee. A band of hired swordsmen guards its mouth and asks everyone, 'From the East Brine Works?' If yes, you're driven back; if not, you're searched. Their leader says they're paid by the foreman of the works: 'Not one of his people gets out.'
column3: 往东只有一条走得通的路：一线硬盐壳，两边是软泥，一脚下去拔不出来。路口守着一伙雇来的刀客，见人就问：「东卤场的？」是的，往回赶；不是的，搜身。刀客头目说他们拿的是东卤场管头的钱，「场里的人一个也不许出去」。

column2: The swordsmen sheathe their blades and talk straight: the foreman holds every salt worker's indenture, ten years each and renewed when it runs out, so no one ever leaves. Luda's is in the pile too. 'That fellow climbs the drying frame every noon and waves toward the west. The foreman calls it shirking. He says he's letting his girl know he's well.'
column3: 刀客收了刀，说实话：管头手里攥着全场盐工的卖身契，契上写十年，到期了再续，没人能走。卤大的契也在里头，「那汉子每天中午爬上晒盐的高架，冲西边挥手，管头骂他偷懒，他说他在给闺女报平安」。

column2: The Sea Market
column3: 海市

column2: At the Dragon hour the sea market appears, and this time not in the sky: the harbour mouth is at low tide, new stalls stand on the old market footings, and a dozen real merchants set out their goods, matching prices with that day overhead. A pirate band charges in with the last of its mirage soldiers and riders to tear the stalls down: once a real market opens, their skimming, listening booths and show tickets are finished. Old Scale sits on plinth number nineteen with his steelyard on his knees, waiting to open the scale.
column3: 辰时，海市出来了，这一回不在天上：海口退潮，旧市基上搭起了新棚，十几家真商户把货摆出来，跟天上那一天对着价。一伙海盗带着最后的蜃兵蜃骑扑上来，要把棚子掀了：真集开了，他们的抽水、听棚、看戏票就都没了。老秤坐在第十九号石墩上，膝上搁着秤，等着开秤。

column2: The pirates are driven into the sea. Old Scale lifts his steelyard and calls the first new price in ten years, and the trade of timber for metalwork starts up again, fifteen thousand a day. The market in the sky is still there, only faint, and today at noon no figure stepped up on the crate. Old Scale looks up. 'Her scene is gone.' He hands you one of his ten years of ledgers. 'The last day's total was a hundred and three items. Head east. If the shen can't remember any more, someone has to remember for it.'
column3: 海盗被打下了海，老秤提起秤杆，报了十年来头一个新价，木料换铁器的买卖重新做了起来，每天一万五千。天上的海市还在，只是淡了，正午那只木箱上的人影，今天没有出来。老秤看了看天：「她那一幕没了。」他把十年的账本交给你们一本：「最后一天的总数是一百零三样。往东去吧，蜃要是记不住了，总得有人替它记。」

column2: Fort of the Dry Banner
column3: 旱字堡

column2: Half buried in the sand stands an earthen fort, a banner faded to grey-white still flying from its wall, bearing the character for 'Dry'. A pirate band holds it with a squad of mirage soldiers and archers on the walls, trading the fort's old weapons to passing merchants for wine. They see your lanterns, stare for a moment, and then roar with laughter. 'Another Houqianli? The one last month paid in fake silver!'
column3: 沙里半埋着一座土堡，堡墙上还插着一面褪成灰白的旗，旗上一个「旱」字。一伙海盗占了土堡，夹着一队蜃兵蜃弓手守在墙头，拿堡里的旧刀枪跟过路的商人换酒。他们看见你们的灯笼先是一愣，接着大笑：「又来一个后千里？上个月那个给的是假银子！」

column2: The pirates are thrown out of the fort. A wooden board inside reads 'Dry Sea Army, Left Camp', and the muster roll still hangs on the wall: one thousand and one names, the last 'Commander Wei Changgeng'. A trussed-up pirate says a 'Houqianli' really did come through last month, three hundred lanterns and all, giving your names. 'They looked more like you than you do.' Gong Modou's face goes dark.
column3: 海盗被打出了堡。堡里的木牌刻着「旱海军左营」，兵册挂在墙上，一千零一个名字，最后一个是「军主卫长庚」。被捆的海盗说，上个月真来过一伙「后千里」，也挂三百盏灯，也报你们的名字，「比你们还像」。龚墨斗的脸黑了。

column2: Seven-Colour Salt Stall
column3: 七色盐摊

column2: At the end of a side track, a salt stall where the salt isn't only white: pink, red, yellow, grey, a bowl of each, like spilled paint. The seller is a fiery salt woman whose good, cheap salt has stolen the smugglers' trade. A gang of them smashed her stall and set mirage soldiers in front of it to drive buyers away, and she has stood with hands on hips cursing them all morning until her voice is gone.
column3: 岔路尽头一个盐摊，摊上的盐不止白的：粉的、红的、黄的、灰的，一碗一色，像打翻了颜料。卖盐的是个泼辣的盐婆，盐好价贱，抢了盐枭的生意。一伙盐枭砸了她的摊子，拿蜃兵守着摊前，见有人来买就赶，盐婆叉着腰骂了一早上，嗓子都哑了。

column2: The smugglers run, the salt woman sets her bowls out again and, impressed, opens for trade. The pinks and reds come from tiny living things in the brine pools, she says; the saltier the pool, the redder. Luda taught her to read them: 'One look at a pool's colour and he'd know which day to rake.' She tucks an extra handful of pink salt into Lumei's hands. 'Take that to your father. He loves it.'
column3: 盐枭被打跑，盐婆重新摆好碗，佩服你们，开张换货。她说粉的红的是卤池里长的小东西染的，池子越咸越红；她会认，是卤大教的：「那人看一眼池子的颜色，就知道哪天收盐。」她多抓了一把粉盐塞给卤妹：「给你爹带去，他爱吃这个。」

column2: Market Mouth Raid
column3: 截市口

column2: The new sea market has been open only a few days when a pirate band from the outer sea turns up at the harbour mouth in fast boats, preying on the ships bringing goods in. They know nothing of the day in the sky; they only know there's a real market here now, and a real market means real money. Their boats carry a few mirage soldiers too, crowded with heads from afar, half empty up close.
column3: 新海市开了没几天，海口就来了一伙外海的海盗，驾着快船，专劫往海市送货的船：他们不知道天上那一天，只知道这里有了真集，真集就有真钱。快船上还挂着几个蜃兵，远远看去船上人头攒动，近了才知道一半是空的。

column2: The fast boats are beaten off and the supply ships come into the harbour one after another. Their merchants say another piece of the sky market went this month: the Qianli's few stalls were there last month and gone this one. 'Whatever the sky forgets, the ground has to remember.' Old Scale has every item those stalls sold copied onto plinth number nineteen.
column3: 快船被打退了，送货的船一条条进了海口。船上的商户说，天上的海市这个月又少了一块：千里号那几个摊子，上个月还在，这个月不见了。「天上的忘一块，地上的就得记一块。」老秤叫人把那几个摊子卖的货，一样样抄在了第十九号石墩上。

column2: Duck-Pen Ferry
column3: 鸭栏渡

column2: Where the salt lake narrows there's a little ferry landing ringed with pens holding hundreds of ducks, quacking fit to deafen. A pirate band has taken it over to raise ducks, stuck two mirage soldiers by the pens as scarecrows, and makes anyone crossing first herd the ducks round once. The duck boy is run ragged and the ducks keep breaking for the lake.
column3: 咸水湖收窄的地方有个小渡口，渡口边圈着几百只鸭子，嘎嘎声震天。一伙海盗占了渡口养鸭，拿两个蜃兵插在栏边当稻草人，过渡的人要先替他们赶一圈鸭子。赶鸭的小哥被海盗支使得满头大汗，鸭子一群群往湖里跑。

column2: The pirates go into the lake and the ferry runs again. The duck boy says these ducks are ordered by the East Brine Works foreman, a delivery a month for his feasts. He's seen Luda on his runs. 'The foreman eats duck and the workers drink brine soup. Last month that fellow told the foreman his contract was up and he was leaving. The foreman said the contract was lost.'
column3: 海盗被打落水，渡船又能走了。赶鸭小哥说这些鸭子是东卤场管头订的，每月送一回给他办席。他去送鸭时见过卤大：「管头吃鸭，盐工喝卤汤。上个月那汉子跟管头说，契满了他要走，管头说契丢了。」

column2: Salt Pillar Wood
column3: 盐柱林

column2: A stand of salt pillars rises from the sand, taller than a man, bone white, like a wood with no leaves, moaning when the wind blows through. A pirate band has dug hollows in them to hide, leaping out from behind pillars at anyone passing. They've strung ropes hung with bells between the pillars; touch one and the whole wood rings, and the pirates close in on the sound.
column3: 沙地里立着一片盐柱，一人多高，白森森的，像一片没叶子的树林，风一吹，呜呜地响。一伙海盗在盐柱里挖了洞藏身，见人就从柱子后头扑出来。他们在柱子之间拴满了绳，绳上挂着铃铛，谁一碰，满林都响，海盗就顺着铃声围过去。

column2: The pirates are driven out of the pillar wood. At dusk you climb the tallest pillar and look east. There are no towers in the sky; far off on the ground lies a field of white heaps with a drying frame standing in the middle, small as a matchstick. Lumei looks for a long time. She doesn't knock and doesn't write. She only says, 'This time it isn't in the sky.'
column3: 海盗被赶出了盐柱林。傍晚爬到最高的一根盐柱上往东看，天上没有楼，地上远远一片白垛，一座晒盐的高架立在当中，小得像一根火柴。卤妹看了很久，没敲，也没记，只说：「这回不是天上的。」

column2: House of the Asked-Back Memory
column3: 讨忆屋

column2: A little house by the shore where an old widow lives. Ten years ago at the memory-swap stall she traded something for a bronze mirror: how her husband looked the morning before he went to sea. Once she had the mirror, she couldn't recall his face. Now she takes the mirror to the stall every day to trade the memory back, but a pirate band guards the stall and has shoved her, mirror and all, into the sand.
column3: 海边一间小屋，住着个老寡妇。十年前她在换忆摊上拿一段事换了一面铜镜：她男人出海前那天早上的样子。换完镜子，男人的脸就想不起来了。如今她天天拿着镜子去换忆摊，要把那段事换回来，可摊前守着一伙海盗，把她连人带镜子推倒在沙里。

column2: The pirates are driven off. The old merchant at the stall looks at the mirror and shakes his head: memories traded away aren't with him either, they went to 'the one who keeps things' in the sea. But that morning, in the market in the sky, a fisherman on the quay happened to look back and smile. The old widow holds her mirror up to the sky and looks a long time. 'It's him. I've got it now, and I'm not trading it again.'
column3: 海盗被赶走了。换忆摊的老掌柜看了看铜镜，摇摇头：换出去的事，他也没了，交给了海里那个「记事的」。可那天早上，天上的海市里正好有一个渔夫在码头上回头笑。老寡妇举着镜子对着天，看了很久：「是他。我记住了，这回不换了。」

column2: Pot for a Thousand
column3: 千人锅

column2: In a sandy hollow sits a huge iron pot, big enough for three men to sit in, camelthorn burning under it and congee bubbling inside. The cook is a one-armed old soldier everyone calls Uncle Ladle. Every day he boils enough congee for a thousand men, strikes the rim three times and calls 'Food's up!', and no one ever comes. A pirate band comes daily to eat for free, and today, done eating, they mean to carry the pot off and sell it for scrap.
column3: 沙窝里支着一口大铁锅，大得能坐进去三个人，锅下烧着骆驼刺，锅里咕嘟着一锅粥。烧锅的是个独臂老兵，人称瓢叔，每天熬一锅够一千人吃的粥，熬好了敲三下锅沿，喊「开饭」，可从来没人来。一伙海盗天天来白吃，今天吃完了，还要把锅抬走卖铁。

column2: The pirates are chased off and the pot is saved. Uncle Ladle says he was the Dry Sea Army's cook. Ten years ago Commander Wei Changgeng led the army along the coast escorting five ships, three days and nights, the men standing in the shallows with torches to mark the channel. Once the ships went into the Mirage the court's pay stopped and the camp broke up. 'When the Commander left, he said: keep serving food every day and the men will come back.' He strikes the rim three times again.
column3: 海盗被打跑，锅保住了。瓢叔说他是旱海军的伙头，十年前军主卫长庚领兵沿海岸护过五条船，三天三夜，兵举着火把站在浅滩上，替船标出水道。船进了蜃楼，朝廷的饷就断了，营散了。「军主走的时候说，天天开饭，人会回来。」他又敲了三下锅沿。

column2: Village of the Unpaid Bill
column3: 认账村

column2: A village on the high road. At the sight of your lanterns the people at its edge grab hoes and close in. 'Houqianli's back! Last time they took twenty pigs on credit and never paid a copper!' The village has hired swordsmen and mirage riders to hold its gate for the sole purpose of keeping 'Houqianli' out, and the moment they see you they charge without a word.
column3: 大路边一座村子，村口的人看见你们的灯笼，抄起锄头就围上来：「后千里又来了！上回赊了二十头猪，一文没给！」村里雇了一伙刀客和蜃骑守村口，就为了堵「后千里」，一见你们，二话不说就扑了过来。

column2: Only once the swordsmen are beaten will the headman bring out the credit slip. Gong Modou takes one look and stamps: it's signed 'Houqianli, Gong Mo-bean', in a scrawl like a crab's tracks. 'They can't even write my name and they dare pass off my ship!' You pay the pig money on the slip. Red-faced, the headman says that lot went south into the sands, and their ship was on wheels.
column3: 刀客败了，村长才肯拿出赊条。龚墨斗一看就跳脚：赊条上签的是「后千里龚墨豆」，字歪得像蟹爬。「我的名字都写不对，还敢冒我的船！」你们照赊条把猪钱垫上了。村长红着脸说，那伙人往南边沙地去了，船是装在车轮子上的。

column2: Salt Guard Camp
column3: 盐丁营

column2: Outside the East Brine Works sprawls a great camp, its walls built of salt bricks that glare white in the sun. The foreman's salt guards stand three deep inside and out, and he's paid for a troop of mirage soldiers and riders to pad out the walls, so from afar it's a sea of men and up close half of them are shadows. A board hangs on the gate: 'Salt workers whose contracts are not complete may not leave the camp.'
column3: 东卤场外头扎着一座大营，营墙是拿盐砖垒的，太阳一照白得刺眼。管头养的盐丁里外三层，又花钱请了一营蜃兵蜃骑站在墙头充数，远看人山人海，近看一半是影子。营门挂着一块牌子：「场内盐工，契未满者，不得出营。」

column2: The camp falls, the shadows scatter and the real men run. The salt workers crowd round and, hearing who Lumei is, all start grinning. 'So you're the girl who can't tell what's real?' They call Luda 'the Waver': every noon he waves from the drying frame and they all look west with him, and in three years they've all learned to miss home.
column3: 盐丁营被打破，影子散了，真人跑了。营里的盐工围上来，听说卤妹是谁，个个笑：「你就是那个分不清真假的丫头？」他们管卤大叫「挥手的」，每天中午他在高架上挥手，大家跟着他往西看，看了三年，也学会了想家。

column2: East-Gazing Strand
column3: 东望滩

column2: Where the coast turns east lies a long strand, and a pirate camp sits at its head, a few mirage soldiers still among them. But the soldiers fade as they stand, like paintings washed by water, some only half there. The pirates themselves are rattled: lately whoever breathes the soldiers out isn't quite right, they say, and the ones it breathes forget to bring their swords.
column3: 海岸往东拐的地方有一片长滩，滩头扎着一伙海盗的营，营里还剩些蜃兵，可这些蜃兵站着站着就淡了，像被水洗过的画，有的只剩半截身子。海盗们自己也慌了，说这阵子吐兵的那位不大灵光，吐出来的兵连刀都忘了拿。

column2: The pirate camp is broken. Old Scale has followed you this far, and he stands at the head of the strand looking east: the market in the sky grows fainter, and its last few towers all lean east. 'The towers lean that way, so that's where it is.' He points his steelyard east: at the foot of the eastern mountains stands a Mirage Customs House whose books record every trade you've made on the road. 'What it can't remember, someone there is writing down for it.'
column3: 海盗营被打散。老秤一路跟到这里，站在滩头往东看：天上的海市越来越淡，残下的几座楼都朝东歪。「楼往那边歪，那边就是它。」他把秤杆往东一指：东边山脚下有一座蜃楼市舶司，簿子上记着你们一路的买卖，「它记不住的，那里有人在替它记」。

column2: Drum-Roll Ground
column3: 点鼓场

column2: An old drill ground in the sand, a battered oxhide drum at its edge, and every day before dawn a lame old soldier comes to beat it and call the roll to an empty field, a thousand names, not one missed. A pirate band uses the ground as a depot heaped with stolen grain, and fed up with the noise they've set mirage soldiers around the drum to slash its skin. The old man clutches his drumsticks, hoarse from shouting.
column3: 沙地上一片旧校场，场边立着一面破牛皮鼓，一个瘸腿老兵每天天不亮就来擂鼓，冲着空场点名，点一千个名字，一个也不漏。一伙海盗把校场当了货场，堆满抢来的粮，嫌老兵吵，拉了一队蜃兵围着鼓，要把鼓皮划了。老兵抱着鼓槌，嗓子已经喊哑了。

column2: The pirates and soldiers are scattered and the drum is saved. The old man is called Old Drum, the Dry Sea Army's drummer. The last order the Commander gave before he left was 'Hold position and await orders', so he calls the roll every day. Halfway through, you look up: in the eastern sky a formation of troops has floated up, drilling to his beat, a thousand men, not one missing.
column3: 海盗和蜃兵被打散，鼓保住了。老兵叫老鼓，旱海军的鼓手。他说军主走前留的最后一道令是「原地待命」，他就天天点名。点到一半，你们抬头一看：东边天上浮出一片军阵，正跟着他的鼓点操练，一千个人，一个也不少。

column2: Mirror Sea
column3: 镜海

column2: After rain a thin film of water covers the salt flat, smooth as a mirror; clouds and far mountains lie in it upside down, and walking on it is like walking on the sky. But the figures in the mirror don't match you: you stand and your reflections walk; you go east and they go west. And among the reflections are rows of soldiers bearing banners, rising one by one up out of the water: mirage soldiers.
column3: 一场雨过后，盐滩上积了薄薄一层水，平得像一面镜子，天上的云、远处的山都倒映在里面，人走在上面像走在天上。可镜子里的人影跟你们不一样：你们站着，倒影在走；你们向东，倒影向西。倒影里还有一排排兵，扛着旗，从水面底下一个个站了起来，是蜃兵。

column2: The mirage soldiers shatter into scattered sparkles. The water smooths out and only now do your reflections line up with you. Axi crouches to look: the formation in the sky is mirrored in the Mirror Sea, the banners marked 'Dry', the soldiers' faces all young, not one aged. 'The Mirage King remembers them as they were ten years ago.' Far off Old Drum beats his drum, and the soldiers in the water lift their feet to the rhythm.
column3: 蜃兵碎成了一地水光。水面又平了，倒影这才跟你们对上。阿汐蹲下来看：天上的那片军阵倒映在镜海里，旗上是「旱」字，兵的脸都年轻，一个也没老。「蜃王记得他们十年前的样子。」老鼓在远处擂着鼓，水里的兵就跟着鼓点抬脚。

column2: Meeting of Two Ships
column3: 双船会

column2: Across the plain a 'ship' comes toward you: eight big cartwheels under the hull, dozens of donkeys hauling, three hundred lanterns on the mast and 'Houqianli' on the stern. The man at the bow is Gong Modou's height and has a pipe in his teeth too; beside him a girl holds a tide book; a gangly boy lies across the rail pretending to listen to waves like Xiaojiang. Their pirate crew gape at you for a long moment, then grab their weapons and pour down off the ship.
column3: 荒原上迎面驶来一条「船」：船底装着八只大车轮，几十头驴拉着，桅上挂着三百盏灯笼，船尾写着「后千里」。船头站着的人跟龚墨斗一般高，也叼着烟袋；旁边一个丫头也捧着潮信簿；还有个半大小子趴在船舷上，学小桨听浪。他们的海盗水手看见你们，愣了半天，随即抄起家伙冲下了船。

column2: The fake crew is beaten and the fake Gong Modou flings down his pipe and names himself: the pirate Ying Qi. A month ago he saw a ship in the sky, upside down, three hundred lanterns, every face aboard plain to see. 'You were still in the fog then.' He built this wheeled ship after the picture in the sky and has been eating free all along the way on your name. Gong Modou walks round the cart-ship once, so angry he laughs. 'The rudder's on backwards.'
column3: 假水手们败了，假龚墨斗把烟袋一扔，自报家门：海盗影七。一个月前他在天上看见一条船，倒挂着，三百盏灯，人脸都看得清，「那会儿你们还在雾里呢」。他照着天上的样子扎了这条车船，一路冒名吃白食。龚墨斗绕着车船看了一圈，气得直乐：「舵装反了。」

column2: Contract House
column3: 契房

column2: At the gate of the salt works stands a little brick house with iron doors and iron shutters: the foreman's contract house, where every worker's indenture is locked away. The foreman himself is cowering inside, his last salt guards and hired pirates outside the door. He shouts through the shutter: 'The contracts are lost! I can't find a single one!' A corner of yellowed paper is plainly sticking out through the crack.
column3: 盐场门口一座小砖房，铁门铁窗，是管头的契房，全场盐工的卖身契都锁在里头。管头本人缩在房里，门外剩下最后一伙盐丁和雇来的海盗守着。他隔着窗喊：「契丢了！一张也找不着！」可窗缝里分明露着一角发黄的纸。

column2: The guards and pirates are beaten, the iron door comes off, and the contracts lie in stacks on the table while the foreman squats in a corner with his head in his hands. Lumei finds her father's among them: it ran out two years ago, and someone has inked over the date. The salt workers carry every contract out into the yard and burn the lot, and in the firelight someone starts the salt rakers' work chant.
column3: 盐丁和海盗都败了，铁门卸下来，契纸一摞摞堆在桌上，管头抱着头蹲在墙角。卤妹在里头翻出她爹那一张，契早满了两年，被人拿墨改了日子。盐工们把契纸全抱到场院里，一把火烧了，火光里有人唱起了晒盐的号子。

column2: Flag-Raising Cliff
column3: 升旗崖

column2: A high cliff by the sea with a flagpole on top, and every sunrise a white-haired old soldier raises a banner marked 'Dry' and lowers it at sunset, never missing a day in ten years. A pirate band hates the banner for being so conspicuous, afraid it'll bring soldiers down on them, and shoots at it daily from below until it's more hole than cloth. Today they've climbed the cliff to cut the pole down.
column3: 海边一道高崖，崖顶立着一根旗杆，每天日出，一个白发老兵把一面「旱」字旗升上去，日落再降下来，十年没断过。一伙海盗嫌这面旗招眼，怕引来官兵，天天在崖下放箭射旗，旗上早已满是窟窿。今天他们爬上了崖，要把旗杆砍倒。

column2: The pirates are thrown off the cliff and the old flag-bearer runs the tattered banner up again. The year the camp broke up, he says, the Commander picked ten men and rowed a small boat to the smoking island out in the north-east sea, to fetch something the Qianli had left for the Dry Sea Army. 'Once I've fetched it, someone will come to relieve me,' he said. The boat went and didn't come back. He raises the flag every day for the people on that island to see.
column3: 海盗被赶下崖，老旗手把破旗又升了上去。他说营散那年，军主挑了十个人，划一条小船往东北海上那座冒烟的岛去了，说是去取千里号留给旱海军的一样东西，「取回来，就有人来接我的班了」。船去了，没回来。他每天升旗，是给岛上的人看的。

column2: Wheel-Trap Sands
column3: 陷轮沙

column2: Half of Ying Qi's cart-ship crew has run, and the rest drive it south and into a stretch of sand, where all eight wheels sink and dozens of donkeys can't shift it. So they turn the cart-ship into a fort and shoot from behind its rails, lighting its three hundred lanterns one by one until the glare makes it hard to see.
column3: 影七的车船跑了一半人，剩下的一伙海盗赶着车船往南逃，逃进一片沙地，八只轮子陷进沙里，几十头驴拉不动。他们干脆把车船当了堡垒，躲在船舷后头放箭，船上的三百盏灯笼一盏盏点起来，晃得人睁不开眼。

column2: The pirates on the cart-ship are dragged down one by one. Its hold is piled with everything they've taken on credit and never paid for: pork, rice, cloth, each tagged 'On Houqianli's account'. You load it onto carts to return item by item, and the pig money for the Village of the Unpaid Bill is settled too. Gong Modou takes down the stern board painted 'Houqianli' and shoulders it. 'They don't deserve this name.'
column3: 车船上的海盗被一个个拖了下来。舱里堆满了一路白吃白拿来的东西：猪肉、米、布，每样都贴着一张「后千里赊」。你们把东西装上车，一样样还回去，认账村的猪钱也有了着落。龚墨斗把那块写着「后千里」的船尾板卸了下来，扛在肩上：「这名字，他们不配。」

column2: Boot Mound
column3: 靴冢

column2: A field of boots stands planted in the sand, pair beside pair, mouths to the sky, in neat ranks like a little forest. Locals say the Dry Sea Army left them the day the camp broke up and no one may touch them. But a band of scavenging pirates has its eye on the oxhide and is pulling them up pair by pair and tossing them into baskets, with a few mirage soldiers keeping watch.
column3: 沙地上插着一片靴子，一双挨一双，靴口朝天，排得整整齐齐，像一片矮矮的树。附近的人说这是旱海军散营那天留下的，谁也不许动。可一伙拾荒的海盗看中了靴子的牛皮，一双双拔出来往筐里扔，还拉了几个蜃兵在旁边放哨。

column2: The scavengers are chased off and the boots are planted back one pair at a time. Old Drum arrives and counts row by row: nine hundred and ninety pairs, eleven short. 'The Commander and his ten went in theirs.' The day the camp broke up, he says, everyone took off their boots and planted them here, agreeing that when the Commander came back they'd return, put them on, and soldier on. The boots are full of sand, and not one pair has ever been reclaimed.
column3: 拾荒的海盗被打跑了，靴子一双双插了回去。老鼓赶来，一排排数：九百九十双，少十一双。「军主和那十个人穿着靴子走的。」他说散营那天，大家把靴子脱下来插在这儿，约好军主回来，就回来穿上，接着当兵。靴子里落满了沙，一双也没被人领走过。

column2: Pay Pavilion
column3: 军饷亭

column2: A little pavilion by the high road with a table inside and on it an empty cash box labelled 'Dry Sea Army pay, collect monthly'. On the first of every month an old pay clerk sits here awaiting the court's pay cart, and has done for ten years. A pirate band has taken the pavilion, posing as Dry Sea veterans to collect pay, and when there's no money they take it out on the clerk, with a squad of mirage soldiers circling the place.
column3: 大路边一座小亭子，亭里摆着一张桌子，桌上一只空钱箱，箱上贴着「旱海军饷，按月领取」。一个老书办每月初一坐在亭里，等朝廷的饷车，等了十年。一伙海盗占了亭子，冒充旱海军的老兵来领饷，拿不到钱，就拿老书办出气，还请了一队蜃兵把亭子围了。

column2: The pirates are run off and the old clerk straightens his hat. He opens the pay register: the last pay was ten years ago in the eighth month, with the Commander's note beneath. 'The Qianli to be escorted through the Mirage. This month's pay need not be reported to the Ministry of War.' So those three days and nights were the Commander's own decision; when the court learned of it, the pay stopped the next month. 'He traded a whole camp's pay for five ships through the Mirage.'
column3: 海盗被打跑，老书办扶正了帽子。他翻开饷册：最后一笔饷是十年前八月，底下有军主的批，「千里号过蜃，护之，此月饷不必报兵部」。原来那三天三夜，是军主自己做的主，朝廷知道了，第二个月就断了饷。「他拿一营人的饷，换了五条船过蜃。」

column2: Ying Qi's Den
column3: 影七寨

column2: On the lee side of the sands hides a stockade, the old lair of Ying Qi's crew, its walls also hung with three hundred lanterns, brighter than the ones on your ship, and a sign at the gate: 'Houqianli, Branch Office'. Hearing they've lost the cart-ship, the pirates inside have called up every man they have and hired a big troop of mirage soldiers and archers, and the walls are packed from top to bottom.
column3: 沙地背风的一面藏着一座寨子，是影七一伙的老窝，寨墙上也挂着三百盏灯，比你们船上的还亮，寨门口立着一块牌子：「后千里分号」。寨里的海盗听说车船丢了，把剩下的人马全调了上来，还雇了一大队蜃兵蜃弓手，寨墙上下站得满满的。

column2: The stockade falls and most of the pirates flee. Inside is a great bronze mirror facing the sky: this is how Ying Qi watched the pictures overhead and copied whatever he saw. Under it is a stack of drawings of things cast up in the sky: your ship, the Qianli's five ships, and a small boat rowed by ten men with an armoured figure standing in the bow.
column3: 寨子被打破，海盗跑了一大半。寨里有一面大铜镜，镜面朝天：影七就是拿它看天上的影子，看一样学一样。镜子底下压着一摞画，画的都是天上映出来的东西，有你们的船，有千里号的五条船，还有一条小船，十个人在划，船头站着一个披甲的人。

column2: Relief-Awaiting Terrace
column3: 候代台

column2: A stone terrace by the sea with a stele on it and a long spear planted before the stele, its tassel long rotted away. This is the Dry Sea Army's reviewing terrace. A pirate band has camped on it and uses the stele as a whetstone, while mirage soldiers form up below in ranks so neat someone must have drilled them. The inscription has been ground down to half.
column3: 海边一座石台，台上立着一块石碑，碑前插着一杆长枪，枪缨早烂光了。这是旱海军的点将台。一伙海盗在台上扎了营，把碑当了磨刀石，蜃兵在台下列阵，阵形整整齐齐，像是有人教过。碑上的字被刀磨得只剩半边。

column2: The pirates are driven off the terrace. The old flag-bearer wipes the broken stele with his sleeve and reads what's left: 'The Qianli to be escorted through the Mirage. Escort complete, await relief. Wei.' Guard the ships, then wait for someone to take over. 'That man won't leave until he's handed his command on.' The old flag-bearer gazes at the island out in the north-east sea. 'Ten years, and no one's come to relieve him.'
column3: 海盗被赶下了台。老旗手拿袖子擦着残碑，念出了剩下的字：「千里号过蜃，护之。护毕，候代。卫。」护完了船，等人来接替。「他这个人，令没交出去，就不肯走。」老旗手望着东北海上那座岛：「十年了，没人来替他。」

column2: Dry Sea Granary
column3: 旱海粮仓

column2: A mud granary in the sand, the Dry Sea Army's grain store, the seals on its door still those of ten years ago. A gang of deserters from somewhere else has torn the seals, moved in, traded the old grain for wine and blocked the road in front: travellers either hand over grain or turn their millstone. The old soldier who kept the store is locked in the mill room.
column3: 沙地里一座土仓，是旱海军当年的粮仓，仓门上的封条还是十年前的。一伙从别处逃来的兵痞撕了封条，住进仓里，把仓里的陈粮拿去换酒，又堵了仓前的路，过路的人要么交粮，要么替他们推磨。看仓的老兵被他们关在了磨房里。

column2: The deserters are chased off and the old soldier comes out of the mill room and goes first to touch the granary wall. Not much grain is left, but every sack still bears its company number, one sack per company, in neat rows. 'The Commander said a granary is a soldier's home. The men may scatter, but the home mustn't.' He seals the door again, and the date on the new seal is today.
column3: 兵痞被赶跑，老兵从磨房里出来，先去摸了摸仓墙。仓里剩的粮不多了，可每一袋都还写着营号，一营一袋，摆得整整齐齐。「军主说过，粮仓是兵的家，兵散了，家不能散。」他把仓门重新封上，封条上写的日子是今天。

column2: From the granary you seize what the deserters traded for: ten jars of spirits, thirty sacks of old rice, two cartloads of dry firewood, and a rolled-up old army banner they'd used as a mattress, its corner embroidered 'Dry Sea Army, Right Camp'.
column3: 仓里抄出兵痞换来的十坛烧酒、三十袋陈米、两车干柴，还有一面卷起来的旧军旗，兵痞拿它垫了床，旗角上绣着「旱海右营」。

column2: Each time you pass, the old storekeeper issues you rations by Dry Sea Army rules, one share each, no more, no less, and has you press a thumbprint in the ration book. 'Draw army rations and you're half a Dry Sea man.'
column3: 每次路过，看仓的老兵都按旱海军的规矩给你们发一份干粮，一人一份，不多不少，还要你们在粮册上按个手印：「领了军粮，就算半个旱海军的人了。」

column2: East Brine Works
column3: 东卤场

column2: In the middle of the works stands the drying frame, and beneath it heap after heap of white salt, like a white city. The works' kitchen and granary are still held by the foreman's last pack of bruisers, duck stewing in their pot while the salt workers stand outside holding bowls of brine soup. At noon a man climbs the frame with a salt rake on his shoulder and waves toward the west. Lumei lifts her spoon, lowers it again, and can't say a word.
column3: 盐场正中立着那座晒盐的高架，架下是一垛垛白盐，像一座白城。盐场的伙房和粮仓还被管头最后一拨打手占着，锅里炖着鸭子，盐工们端着卤汤站在外头。正午，高架上爬上去一个人，扛着盐耙，冲西边挥手。卤妹拿起勺子，又放下了，一句话也说不出来。

column2: Luda climbs down from the frame and wraps his daughter in his arms, and she knocks him once with her spoon. Knock. 'The sea's cold,' Luda says, 'so the air lying on it is cold and heavy, with warm air pressing on top. Light from far off gets bent between the two layers, and things behind the horizon get lifted into the sky. The White City was these salt heaps.' Then he points north-east. 'Ten years ago I saw five ships hanging upside down in the sky, heading north-east toward the cold water. All the Mirage's light is borrowed from over there.'
column3: 卤大爬下来抱住女儿，她拿勺子敲他，咚。他说：「海面冷，贴海的气又冷又重，上头压着暖气，远处的光在两层中间被压弯，天边背后的东西也被搬上了天。白城就是这片盐垛。」又指东北：「十年前我见过五条船倒挂在天上，往冷水去，蜃楼的光都是那儿借的。」

column2: From the kitchen and granary you seize the foreman's hoard: thirty salted ducks, fifty piculs of white rice, two jars of good wine, a chest of new padded jackets, and a basket of the workers' letters from home that he'd held back, seals still unbroken.
column3: 伙房和粮仓里抄出管头囤的三十只腌鸭、五十石白米、两坛好酒、一箱新棉袄，还有一筐盐工们被扣下的家信，封口都没拆。

column2: Each time you pass, the East Brine Works hands you a few sacks of fresh salt and Luda slips in a packet of pink salt, while Lumei stands on the drying frame waving. 'I've knocked on you already. You're real. Don't be afraid on the road.'
column3: 每次路过，东卤场的盐工都往车上搬几袋新盐，卤大再塞一包粉盐，卤妹站在高架上冲你们挥手，说：「我敲过了，你们是真的，路上别怕。」

column2: Shadow-Catching Camp
column3: 抓影营

column2: Ying Qi himself has hidden with his last pirates in an abandoned camp. Bonfires blaze inside, their light thrown by a ring of bronze mirrors up into the sky, where a far bigger camp appears above the real one, banners thick, horns sounding. From afar people take it for a garrison of thousands. Its real defenders are a few dozen pirates and a big troop of mirage soldiers and riders.
column3: 影七本人带着最后一伙海盗躲进了一座废营，营里点着火堆，火光照在一圈铜镜上，又照到天上，在营顶上映出一座更大的营，旗帜林立，号角声声。远处的人看了，都以为这里驻着千军万马。真守营的是几十个海盗和一大队蜃兵蜃骑。

column2: The mirrors are pushed over, the great camp in the sky vanishes, and Ying Qi is trussed up tight. Head hanging, he says he's copied so many things from the sky, but the little boat rowed by ten men he couldn't. 'It shows up in the sky once every morning, rowing for the island in the north-east, and halfway there it's gone. I built ten little boats and rowed over, and on the island there was nothing but smoke.'
column3: 镜子被推倒，天上的大营没了，影七被捆了个结实。他耷拉着脑袋说，他学过天上那么多东西，就那条十个人划的小船学不了：「那船天天早上在天上出现一回，往东北岛上划，划到一半就没了。我扎了十条小船，划过去，岛上只有烟。」

column2: Armour Redemption Shop
column3: 赎甲铺

column2: A smithy at the edge of the sands, its door hung with old armour, every plate branded 'Dry', all of it drifted out of the broken camp over the years. Pirates run the shop and sell the armour to passing swordsmen. Today a line of white-haired old men waits in front, clutching saved-up silver scraps to buy back their own armour, and the pirates insist: 'Price has gone up. Tenfold.' Behind the shop a squad of mirage soldiers backs them up.
column3: 沙地边一间铁匠铺，门口挂满了旧铠甲，甲片上都烙着「旱」字，是这些年从散了的营里流出来的。一伙海盗开着这铺子，把旧甲卖给过路的刀客。今天铺前排着一队白头发的老汉，捏着攒下的碎银，要把自己的甲赎回去，海盗一口咬定：「涨价了，十倍。」铺后还站着一队蜃兵替他们撑腰。

column2: The pirates are run off and the old men turn the armour over piece by piece; each breastplate has a name scratched on the back, and each man finds his own. Word has spread, they say, that a ship hung with lanterns is looking for the Commander, so the Dry Sea veterans are walking back from every direction. 'The Commander never handed over his command, so we're still soldiers.' One old man throws his armour on and can't fasten it. His belly has grown.
column3: 海盗被赶跑，老汉们一副副翻甲，每副甲的护心片背面都刻着名字，各人认各人的。他们说听人传，有一伙挂灯的船在找军主，旱海军的老兵就从四面八方往回走了。「军主没交令，我们就还是兵。」一个老汉把甲往身上一披，扣子扣不上了，肚子大了。

column2: The Wei Family House
column3: 卫家老屋

column2: An old blue-brick house on the plain, a cracked plaque over the door reading 'Residence of the Commander'. Inside lives the Commander's wife, Mistress Wei, who gets by mending clothes and armour. A troop of tax runners with a few mirage soldiers is blocking the door, waving a bill: when the Dry Sea Army broke up it owed the county three hundred piculs of grain. 'The Commander isn't here, so the Commander's house will cover it.' Mistress Wei holds a door bar across her chest.
column3: 荒原上一座青砖老屋，门楣上挂着一块「军主第」的匾，匾已经裂了。屋里住着军主的妻子卫嫂，靠给人缝补衣甲过日子。一伙税丁带着几个蜃兵堵在门口，拿着一张欠单：旱海军散营时欠了县里三百石粮，「军主不在，就拿军主的屋抵」。卫嫂把一根顶门杠横在胸前。

column2: The tax runners are driven off and the bill is torn up. From the bottom of a chest Mistress Wei takes a letter her husband left before he went to the island: 'The command is still in my hands; no relief has come. On the island is something the Qianli left for this army. I'll fetch it, make up the brothers' pay, and come home.' In the margin is a sketch of a smoking island. She says he never once got a date wrong in his life. This time he's ten years out.
column3: 税丁被赶走了，欠单撕了。卫嫂从箱底取出一封信，是丈夫上岛前留的：「令在我手，代者未至。岛上有千里号留给本军的一样东西，取回来，补上兄弟们的饷，便回。」信纸边上画着一座冒烟的岛。她说他这人说话从不算错日子，这一回算错了十年。

column2: Buried Jar Slope
column3: 埋罐坡

column2: On a sandy slope a gang of salt smugglers has dug a big pit, and at its bottom sits a large pottery jar sealed with wax. They've heard the Dry Sea Army buried pay silver around here years ago, and the moment the jar showed they started fighting over shares, calling up a troop of mirage riders to help. Their hired digger, an old salt guard, has been shoved to the pit's edge with his arms over his head. 'It's not silver! I saw them bury it!'
column3: 沙坡上一伙走私盐的挖了一个大坑，坑底露出一只封着蜡的大陶罐。他们听说旱海军当年在这一带埋过饷银，罐子一露头，就为分银子打了起来，又拉来一队蜃骑助阵。挖坑的雇工是个老盐丁，被他们推在坑边，抱着脑袋：「那不是银子！我看见他们埋的！」

column2: The smugglers are chased off. There's no silver in the jar, only a roll of oilcloth in Shen Du's hand: 'With thanks to the Dry Sea Army for three days' escort. This company cannot pay soldiers on the court's behalf; it can only settle its debts. On the island to the north-east, among the stone pillars: a year's grain and three thousand taels of silver, to cover your army's month of pay. Shen Du.' The old salt guard remembers the Commander reading the letter and going down to the coast to find a boat the very next day.
column3: 走私的被赶跑了。罐子里没有银子，只有一卷油布，布上是沈渡的字：「谢旱海军三日护送。本号不能替朝廷发饷，只能还账：东北岛上，石柱之间，存粮一年，银三千两，抵贵军一月之饷。沈渡。」老盐丁记得，军主读完信，第二天就去海边找船了。

column2: The Disbandment Order
column3: 裁撤令

column2: Officials come down the high road under the banner of the Ministry of War, led by a pale, plump clerk with swordsmen and mirage riders behind him. He's here to chase the Dry Sea Army's old accounts: the camp drew three hundred bows and sixty cooking pots and never returned them when it broke up. 'The men may scatter, but the books may not.' He arrests as he goes, tying anyone in old armour onto his cart.
column3: 大路上来了一支官差，打着兵部的旗，领头的是个白胖的书吏，身后跟着一队刀客和蜃骑。他是来追旱海军的旧账的：营里当年领了三百副弓、六十口锅，散营时没有交还，「人散了，账不能散」。他一路走一路抓人，见了穿旧甲的就往车上捆。

column2: The swordsmen are run off and the old soldiers on the cart are freed. With shaking hands the clerk brings out a document he calls his authority: 'Ninth month, Dingwei year: the Dry Sea Army is disbanded; Commander Wei Changgeng is to hand over his command and return to the capital forthwith.' It bears the great seal, and it was never delivered: the courier deserted halfway. The old soldiers read it and laugh until they cry. 'Disbanded ten years, and here we still are, standing guard.'
column3: 刀客被打跑，车上的老兵都放了。书吏抖着手拿出一张公文，说是他的本钱：「丁未年九月，旱海军裁撤，军主卫长庚即日交令回京。」公文盖着大印，却从没送到过：送公文的驿卒半路逃了。老兵们看着看着，笑出了眼泪：「裁了十年，我们还在这儿守着。」

column2: Smoke Island Ferry
column3: 烟岛渡

column2: A little ferry landing facing the island in the north-east sea, a wisp of white smoke on its summit day and night. A pirate band has impounded every boat here, saying the island holds Qianli treasure they mean to fetch themselves, but they've tried three times and three times been choked back by the smoke. The ferrywoman won't guide them, so they knocked a hole in her boat's bottom and left it tied at the quay to soak.
column3: 海边一座小渡口，正对着东北海上那座岛，岛顶一缕白烟，日夜不散。渡口的船全被一伙海盗扣着，说岛上有千里号的宝贝，要自己去取，可他们去了三回，三回都被烟呛回来。撑渡的渡娘不肯带路，海盗就把她的船底凿了个洞，拴在码头上泡着。

column2: The pirates are chased off and Gong Modou patches the ferry's hull. The ferrywoman says the smoke on the island is earth-fire that's been burning for centuries; it doesn't kill, it just chokes. 'Keep upwind and don't go poking into the smoke.' Ten years ago she ferried a small boat out there, eleven men, their leader in armour. 'He said he'd pay the fare on the way back. I've still got it on the books.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，龚墨斗把渡船的洞补上了。渡娘说岛上那缕烟是地火，烧了几百年，不吃人，只是呛：「顺着风走，别往烟里钻。」十年前她渡过一条小船去岛上，十一个人，领头的披着甲，「他说回来时给我付船钱。船钱我还记着账」。

column2: Mirage Grub Nest
column3: 蜃虫窝

column2: Deep in the salt flat lies a stretch of soft mud alive with tens of thousands of mirage grubs, fat and white and finger-thick, and each time one opens its mouth it breathes out a puff of heat with a little false scene floating on it: a tree, a pot, a beckoning figure. Travellers walk toward the scenes, sink into the mud, and the grubs swarm in to nibble. These past days the swarm has been crawling out of its nest toward the salt workers' drying yards.
column3: 盐滩深处有一片软泥，泥里钻着成千上万的蜃虫，白白胖胖，指头粗，一张嘴吐一口热气，热气上就浮出一小片假景：一棵树、一口锅、一个招手的人。过路的人朝假景走，一脚陷进泥里，蜃虫就围上来啃。这几天虫群爬出泥窝，往盐工的晒场去了。

column2: This time the swarm is driven back into its mud, and the false scenes by the drying yards wink out one by one. The salt workers say mirage grubs are the great shen's offspring, hatching brood after brood under the mud, three times a summer, impossible to clear for good. All you can do is come back every so often to drive them off before they reach the yards. As you leave, another little false scene floats up off the mud: a beckoning figure.
column3: 这一回的虫群被赶回了泥窝，晒场边的假景一个个灭了。盐工们说蜃虫是大蜃的子孙，泥底下一窝接一窝地孵，一个夏天能孵三回，怎么也清不干净。只能隔一阵来赶一回，别让它们爬上晒场。走的时候，泥面上又浮起了一小片假景：一个招手的人。

column2: Veterans' Muster
column3: 老兵集

column2: A lopsided wine shed on the salt flat, its front and back crowded with white-haired old men, some on crutches, some carrying rusty swords: Dry Sea veterans who've come on the news that someone's going to the island to find the Commander. A pirate band, annoyed that the old men are blocking the crossroads, comes with mirage soldiers to clear them, and the veterans stand and form a single rank, legs trembling, line still dead straight.
column3: 盐滩上一座歪歪斜斜的酒棚，棚前棚后坐满了白头发的老汉，有的拄拐，有的背着锈刀，都是旱海军的老兵，听说有人要去岛上找军主，一路赶来。一伙海盗嫌这群老头占了路口，带着蜃兵来撵，老兵们站起来，排成了一列，腿脚哆嗦，队形倒还是齐的。

column2: The pirates are run off and the veterans sit back down and give their names one by one, more than three hundred of them. Old Drum checks each against the roll. 'Zhang Er.' 'Here.' 'Li Mancang.' 'Here.' When he reads the name of a man who's dead, they all answer 'Here' together. He closes the roll. 'The men are all here. But without the command token, soldiers aren't an army.'
column3: 海盗被打跑，老兵们坐回棚里，一个一个报名，报了三百多个。老鼓拿着兵册一个个对：「张二，在。」「李满仓，在。」念到死了的，大家一齐说「在」。他合上兵册：「人是齐了，可没有令，兵不成军。」

column2: Phantom Host
column3: 幻军阵

column2: As the veterans head for the coast a whole army suddenly rises on the plain, banners marked 'Dry', soldiers with the young faces of ten years ago, mirage riders in front and mirage infantry behind, blocking the way. It's the formation from the sky come down to earth, and it doesn't know these old men; it takes them for strangers. A pirate band lurks behind it too, snatching the veterans' rations in the confusion.
column3: 老兵们往海边走，荒原上忽然起了一片军阵，旗是「旱」字旗，兵是十年前的年轻脸，蜃骑在前，蜃兵在后，挡住了去路。这是天上那片军阵落到了地上，它不认得这些老了的人，只当是外人。阵后还藏着一伙海盗，趁乱抢老兵的干粮。

column2: The phantom host dissolves and the pirates flee. The veterans stand where they are, silent a long while: the young flag-bearer across the field just now was the old flag-bearer himself, ten years ago. He thumps his own chest. 'It remembers us young. It doesn't remember us old.' He turns to you. 'The token is on the island. We'll wait for you to bring it back.'
column3: 幻阵散了，海盗也跑了。老兵们站在原地，半天没说话：方才对面那个年轻的旗手，就是老旗手自己十年前的样子。老旗手拍了拍自己的胸口：「它记得我们年轻的时候，不记得我们老了。」他转身对你们说：「令在岛上，我们等你们取回来。」

column2: Breathing Plain
column3: 喘气原

column2: The ground on this plain rises and falls once an hour, as though something beneath were slowly breathing in and out; each time it swells, salt water seeps up between the grass roots. A pirate band and a big troop of mirage soldiers have camped here, their tents rising and sinking, and the pirates are seasick but won't leave: each time the ground breathes, they say, the towers in the sky brighten, and when they do, pearls come up through the cracks.
column3: 荒原上的地，一个时辰起伏一回，像有什么在底下慢慢吸气、呼气；地一鼓，草根底下就渗出咸水。一伙海盗和一大队蜃兵在这片原上扎营，营帐一会儿高一会儿低，海盗们晕得直吐，却舍不得走：他们说地一喘，天上的楼就亮一回，楼亮的时候，地缝里会冒出珠子。

column2: The pirates are scattered. Xiaojiang lies listening with his ear to the ground for an hour. 'In, out. Slower than last time.' An old clam-digger with a basket on his back passes and tells him to get up. 'You're standing on the rim of its shell. It's old; it breathes slower every year.' He picks a pearl the size of a rice grain out of a crack, white going grey. 'When it drops pearls, it's dropping memories.'
column3: 海盗被打散了。小桨趴在地上听了一个时辰：「一呼一吸，比上一回慢了。」一个背筐的蛤户老汉路过，叫他别趴了：「你们脚底下踩的是它的壳边。它老了，喘得一年比一年慢。」老汉从地缝里抠出一粒米大的珠子，白里透灰：「掉珠子，是它在掉记性。」

column2: Pumice Cove
column3: 浮石湾

column2: A little cove where the water is covered with grey-white stones, some big as pillows, some small as buns, bobbing on the waves without sinking. A pirate band is fishing them out, calling them 'jade from the Dragon Palace' and hauling them off by the basket to sell. The children who used to collect them have been chased onto the rocks, and one still clutches a stone with a crooked character scratched into it.
column3: 海边一道小湾，湾里漂着一层灰白的石头，大的像枕头，小的像馒头，随着浪一起一伏，石头竟然不沉。一伙海盗在湾里捞石头，说是「龙宫的玉」，一筐筐运去卖。捡石头的小孩被他们撵到礁上，手里还攥着一块，石头上刻着歪歪扭扭的一个字。

column2: The pirates are chased off. The ferrywoman picks up a stone and weighs it in her hand. 'This is pumice. Molten rock the earth-fire throws out on the island; it cools full of bubbles, lighter than water, and can float at sea for months.' The child's stone is scratched 'Here'. Wedged in the cracks of the cove's rocks are dozens more, every one scratched 'Here', and the newest reads 'Nine'. For ten years the people on the island have been sending their count across.
column3: 海盗被赶跑了。渡娘拿起一块石头掂了掂：「这是浮石，岛上地火喷出来的石浆，一冷，里头全是气泡，比水还轻，能在海上漂好几个月。」孩子手里那块刻着「在」。礁缝里还塞着几十块，块块刻着「在」，最新的一块刻的是「九」。岛上的人一直在往这边报数。

column2: Mealtime Sands
column3: 开饭沙

column2: Uncle Ladle has hauled his pot for a thousand to the Boot Mound to boil congee for the returning veterans, Old Drum beating the drum, the old flag-bearer raising the banner. But a wind has got up, driving salt grit into the pot, and out of the grit rises a squad of mirage soldiers circling the pot, while a few half-starved pirates rush in under cover of the dust to grab the rice.
column3: 瓢叔把那口千人锅拉到了靴冢边上，要给回来的老兵们熬一锅粥，老鼓擂鼓，老旗手升旗。可起风了，风卷着盐沙往锅里灌，沙里又冒出一队蜃兵，围着锅转，还有几个饿疯了的海盗趁着风沙扑上来抢锅里的米。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter and the pirates squat trussed beside the pot, and Uncle Ladle still ladles them a bowl each. When the congee's done he strikes the rim three times. 'Food's up.' This time more than four hundred come. The veterans hold their bowls and no one starts; they all look toward the island in the north-east sea. 'We'll eat together when the Commander's back.'
column3: 蜃兵散了，海盗被捆着蹲在锅边，瓢叔还是给他们也盛了一碗。粥熬好，瓢叔敲了三下锅沿：「开饭。」这一回来了四百多人。老兵们捧着碗，没人先动筷子，都朝东北海上那座岛望着：「等军主回来，一起吃。」

column2: Smoke Island Customs Post
column3: 烟岛分卡

column2: On Smoke Island's south shore stands a tiny customs post, its sign reading 'Mirage Customs House, Smoke Island Post': a ledger room, a storeroom and a hot spring pool. A pirate band that came looking for Qianli treasure and didn't find it has taken over the post instead, soaking their feet in the spring and eating half the rice and salt fish in the store, and they've locked the old clerk in his ledger room to keep a tally of 'how much we've won'.
column3: 烟岛南岸有一座小小的税卡，门口挂着「蜃楼市舶司烟岛分卡」的牌子，卡里一间簿房、一间仓房、一口温泉池。一伙找千里号宝贝的海盗没找着宝，就占了分卡，在温泉里泡脚，把仓里的米和腌鱼吃得只剩一半，把看卡的老书办关在簿房里，让他替他们记「赢了多少」。

column2: The pirates are driven off the island and the old clerk comes out hugging his book, and the first thing he does is enter you: 'Houqianli, three hundred lamps, arrived in port.' He turns back a page and shows you an entry made a month ago: 'Houqianli sighted in the sky, three hundred lamps, not yet arrived.' 'Arriving in the sky first and on the ground later, both have to be recorded.' The head house is in the east, he says. 'Mo San is waiting to check accounts with you.'
column3: 海盗被赶下了岛，老书办抱着簿子出来，第一件事是给你们登记：「后千里，三百灯，到港。」他翻到前一页，指给你们看，一个月前他就记过一笔：「天上见后千里，三百灯，未到。」「天上先到，地上后到，都得记。」他说总卡在东边，「墨三在等你们对账」。

column2: From the storeroom you seize what the pirates hadn't eaten: ten sacks of rice, eight crocks of salt fish, two chests of silk robbed elsewhere, and a stack of the pirates' tallies of their winnings, which the old clerk glances at and says are wrong in three places.
column3: 仓房里抄出海盗吃剩的十袋米、八缸腌鱼、两箱从别处劫来的绸缎，还有一摞海盗记的赢账，老书办看了一眼，说加错了三处。

column2: Each time you pass, the old clerk lets you soak your feet in the hot spring and hands you a packet of eggs boiled in its water, the date written on each shell. 'Look before you eat. Know which day it was boiled.'
column3: 每次路过，老书办都让你们在温泉里泡一泡脚，再塞一包温泉水煮的鸡蛋，蛋壳上写着日子：「吃之前看一眼，是哪天煮的，记清楚。」

column2: Roll-Call Road
column3: 点卯道

column2: On the high road to the coast the pale, plump Ministry clerk is back, this time with more swordsmen and a troop of mirage riders, and notices are posted along the way: 'The Dry Sea Army is disbanded. Any who assemble will be charged with rebellion.' Hearing several hundred veterans have gathered, he panicked and fetched reinforcements overnight, meaning to call their names on the road and arrest them one by one.
column3: 去海边的大道上，兵部那个白胖书吏又回来了，这回带了更多的刀客和一队蜃骑，路上贴着告示：「旱海军已裁，聚众者以谋逆论。」他听说几百个老兵聚在一起，吓得连夜搬了救兵，要在大路上把他们一个个点名拿下。

column2: The swordsmen are scattered and the clerk hides under his cart and won't come out. Old Drum hauls him out and hands him the muster roll. 'Go on, call it.' In a shaking voice the clerk calls the roll, and one by one the veterans answer 'Here'. When he's done it's a while before he speaks. 'This roll is more complete than the Ministry's.' He takes down his notices, and doesn't leave either: he squats by the road, waiting to see the token.
column3: 刀客被打散，书吏缩在车底下不肯出来。老鼓把他拉出来，递给他那本兵册：「点吧。」书吏抖着嗓子点了一遍名，老兵们一个个答「在」。点完，他半天才说：「这本册子，比兵部的还齐。」他把告示揭了，自己也没走，蹲在路边等着看那只令。

column2: The Mirage Customs House
column3: 蜃楼市舶司

column2: A government compound on the plain, half brick and tile, half light: the gatehouse and spirit wall are real, but the courtyards behind float in mid-air, eaves pointing down. A pirate band with mirage soldiers and riders holds the gate, saying the ledgers here record every trade on the whole sea, and whoever gets hold of them can blackmail anyone for any deal they've ever done. In the gatehouse sits a thin scholar, head down, writing, and whatever happens outside, he never looks up.
column3: 荒原上一座衙门，一半是砖瓦，一半是光：门楼、照壁是真的，后面那几进院子浮在半空，檐角朝下。衙门口一伙海盗带着蜃兵蜃骑守着，说这里的簿子记着全海的买卖，抢到手，谁家做了什么生意都能拿来敲竹杠。门房里坐着一个瘦书生，埋头写字，外头打成什么样，他都不抬头。

column2: The pirates are thrown out of the compound and the trade of metalwork for gold opens again, ten thousand a day. Only now does the thin scholar look up: Mo San, clerk of the Mirage Customs House. He pushes a ledger across to you, and starting from Quanzhou harbour, through the Sea of Fog and the Sea Market, every trade you've made along the way is in it, not one missing. 'Whatever the sky shows, I write down.' Ten years ago Captain Shen hired him, he says: 'Write down every trade that crosses this sea, until someone who can keep accounts comes to check them.' He turns to the last page. It's blank. 'The one to check them hasn't come yet.'
column3: 海盗被打出了衙门，金银换铁器的买卖重新开了，每天一万。瘦书生这才抬头：墨三，蜃楼市舶司的书办。他把一本簿子推给你们，从泉州港开始，雾海、海上集，你们一路上的每一笔买卖都在上面，一笔不差。「天上照见的，我都记下。」他说十年前沈船主雇了他：「把从这片海过的每一笔买卖记下来，记到会算账的人来对。」他翻到最后一页，空着：「对账的人，还没来。」

column2: Pillar Camp
column3: 石柱营

column2: The north slope of Smoke Island is all black stone pillars, close-packed, six-sided in section, so regular they might have been laid by masons, with eleven huts built between them. A pirate band has just pried open a grain cache hidden in the cracks between the pillars and is hauling rice out, and ten white-haired old soldiers rush from the huts with fish spears to stop them. Day is just breaking, and on top of the tallest pillar a figure floats up: armoured, young, hand on his sword, the very man who stood in the bow of the little boat in the sky.
column3: 烟岛的北坡全是黑石柱，一根挨一根，截面六角，齐整得像有人砌过，柱间搭着十一座窝棚。一伙海盗刚撬开柱缝里藏的粮窖，正往外扛米，窝棚里冲出十个白发老兵，拿着鱼叉拦他们。天刚蒙蒙亮，最高那根石柱顶上浮出一个人影：披甲，年轻，按着刀，正是天上那条小船船头站着的人。

column2: The pirates are driven into the sea. The ten old soldiers say the Commander died last winter, and before he went he had them bury the token in the crack of the pillar where he stood each morning. 'When relief comes, hand it over here.' Gong Modou runs a hand over the stone: molten rock cooling and shrinking inward, he says, splits into six-sided columns like these. Then the figure on the pillar lifts a hand toward you and points to a crack at its feet. You reach in and touch a cold bronze tablet: the Commander's Token, 'Dry Sea' on its face and on the back, 'Borne by the one who relieves me.' The figure presses a hand to its chest and bows to you, and as the sun comes up it turns to a wisp of smoke. The ten old soldiers kneel. Of the silver the Qianli left, they never touched a tael.
column3: 海盗被打下了海。十个老兵说，军主去年冬天走了，临走让他们把令埋进他每天早上站的那根石柱缝里：「代者来了，就在这儿交。」龚墨斗摸着石柱说，这是岩浆冷下来往里缩，裂成的六角柱子。这时柱顶的人影朝你们抬手，指向脚下一道裂缝。你们伸手进去，摸到一块冰凉的铜牌：军主令，正面「旱海」，背面「代者持此」。人影把手按在胸口，朝你们一揖，日头一出，化成了一缕烟。十个老兵跪了下来。千里号留的银子，他们一两没动。

column2: Send-Off Slip
column3: 送船坞

column2: A half-collapsed boat shed by the sea holds a small boat half built, the shavings on its keel gone black. The owner is an old shipwright who built the Commander's boat for the island ten years ago. A pirate band has taken the shed and wants to break up the unfinished hull for firewood, and the old man circles the boat with a chalk line, snapping ink into the face of anyone who comes near.
column3: 海边一座塌了半边的船坞，坞里搁着一条造了一半的小船，龙骨上的刨花都发黑了。坞主是个老船匠，十年前给军主造过那条上岛的小船。一伙海盗占了船坞，要把半成品拆了当柴，老船匠拿着墨斗线，绕着船走，谁靠近就弹谁一脸墨。

column2: The pirates are chased off and Gong Modou and the old shipwright hit it off at once. The old man says the half-built boat was for the Commander's return. 'He said he'd fetch it and come back, and when he did he'd need a bigger boat, to hold eleven men and three thousand taels.' Halfway through, no one came back, so he stopped. Gong Modou rolls up his sleeves. 'The other half, I'll help you finish.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，龚墨斗跟老船匠一见如故。老船匠说这条半成品是给军主回程造的：「他说取了东西就回，回来要条大点的船，装得下十一个人和三千两银子。」船造到一半，人没回来，他就停了手。龚墨斗卷起袖子：「剩下一半，我帮你造完。」

column2: Boot-Donning Plain
column3: 穿靴原

column2: The veterans have all gathered at the Boot Mound, more than four hundred, each crouched before his own pair of boots and refusing to put them on: they're waiting for the token. A gang of salt smugglers has heard the veterans hold Qianli silver and closes in with mirage soldiers and archers, shouting that they'd like to 'borrow' a few bags. The veterans snatch up their boots as weapons, and the air fills with flying footwear.
column3: 老兵们都聚到了靴冢前，四百多人，各自蹲在自己那双靴子跟前，就是不肯穿：要等令。一伙盐枭听说老兵们手里有千里号的银子，带着一队蜃兵蜃弓手围了上来，喊着要「借」几袋。老兵们抓起靴子当武器，一时间满天都是飞靴。

column2: The smugglers are run off. You raise the Commander's Token, Old Drum beats three rolls, and four hundred men pull on their boots as one, shaking out ten years of sand. The old flag-bearer takes the token, looks it over, and hands it back. 'The Commander said that to go through the Mirage, the Qianli would have to get past the great shen last of all. It remembers the road, and it guards it too.' He points east. 'Take this token to a barracks and give a shout. We'll come.'
column3: 盐枭被打跑了。你们举起军主令，老鼓擂了三通鼓，四百多人齐刷刷穿上靴子，抖出十年的沙。老旗手接过令看了一遍，又还给你们：「军主说过，千里号进蜃，最后要过那只大蜃。它记着路，也守着路。」他朝东一指：「拿这块令去兵营喊一声，我们就来。」

column2: Shell-Touch Hamlet
column3: 摸壳屯

column2: A cluster of low houses roofed with big shells: a hamlet of clam-diggers. Pearl-poaching pirates have taken it and are pressing the diggers to lead them to the 'shen pearl', smashing shells when they refuse. A boy of ten or so walks barefoot back and forth, and every few steps he lies down to feel the ground; the pirates think he's hunting pearls and hold him by the collar, questioning him without pause.
column3: 一片矮屋，屋顶压着大贝壳，是蛤户住的屯子。一伙采珠海盗占了屯子，逼蛤户带路去找「蜃珠」，蛤户不肯，海盗就砸贝壳。屯里有个十来岁的男孩，光着脚在地上走来走去，走几步就趴下摸一摸地，海盗以为他在找珠子，揪着他的领子问个不停。

column2: The pirates are run off. The boy is Zhu'er, grandson of Granny Clam. Feeling the ground is how he 'asks the way': which patch is cool, which warm, where water runs underneath, he can tell them all. 'The warm place is its heart. Granny says never drive a stake there.' He takes you to see the iron stakes the pirates drove, and they're hammered into a patch of warm ground.
column3: 海盗被赶走了。男孩叫珠儿，蚌婆的孙子。他摸地是在「问路」：哪块凉，哪块温，哪块底下有水在走，他都摸得出来。「温的地方是它的心口，奶奶说千万别在那儿打桩。」他领你们去看海盗打的铁桩，桩子正钉在一块温热的地上。

column2: Silver-Sharing Ground
column3: 分银坪

column2: The veterans have brought the Qianli's three thousand taels back from the island and are sharing out pay by the muster roll on a patch of level ground, one share each. But a pirate band has had its eye on the silver all along and charges in with the last of its mirage riders, a few of the Ministry's swordsmen mixed in among them, saying the silver belongs 'in the treasury'. The pale, plump clerk stands in the middle, torn both ways.
column3: 老兵们从岛上运回了千里号留的三千两银子，在一块平地上按兵册分饷，一人一份。可一伙海盗早盯上了这批银子，带着最后的蜃骑冲了过来，还有几个兵部的刀客混在其中，说银子该「缴库」。白胖书吏站在中间，左右为难。

column2: The pirates and swordsmen are scattered. The clerk thinks for a while, then writes a line on the back of his own document: 'Dry Sea Army pay, eighth month of the Dingwei year, paid on its behalf by the Qianli. Settled.' And he stamps it with the Ministry's seal. When the veterans have their pay, each first puts in a mace of silver, and together they pay the ferrywoman her fare from ten years ago. 'The Commander's accounts are square at last,' says Uncle Ladle.
column3: 海盗和刀客被打散。书吏想了想，在自己的公文背面写了一行：「旱海军丁未年八月饷，千里号代付，已讫。」盖上了兵部的印。老兵们领了饷，每人先拿出一钱，凑给渡娘付了十年前的船钱。瓢叔说：「军主的账，总算平了。」

column2: Farewell Sands
column3: 送行沙

column2: The veterans escort you all the way to the eastern end of the salt flat; beyond it, the Mirage hangs low in the sky, so low it looks about to touch the ground. A band of pirates fleeing from the east blunders into the escort, a horde of mirage soldiers hard on their heels, cutting down anyone they meet, pirates included: they can no longer tell who's who.
column3: 老兵们一路把你们送到盐滩东头，再往东，天上的蜃楼就压得很低了，低得像要落到地上。一伙从东边逃过来的海盗慌慌张张撞上了送行的队伍，后头追着一大群蜃兵，蜃兵见人就砍，连海盗也砍：它们已经分不出谁是谁了。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter, and the fleeing pirates kneel and knock their heads on the ground, saying the mirage soldiers at the foot of the eastern mountains grow wilder by the day; even the people of the Mirage Customs House don't dare go out. Old Drum beats one last roll and the veterans form two lines on the sand. 'What the Commander didn't finish, you finish for him.' Looking back, you see four hundred men still standing there until they're out of sight.
column3: 蜃兵散了，逃来的海盗跪在地上直磕头，说东边山脚下的蜃兵越来越疯，连蜃楼市舶司的人都不敢出门了。老鼓擂了最后一通鼓，老兵们在沙上站成两行：「军主没走完的，你们替他走完。」你们回头望，四百多人一直站着，直到看不见了。

column2: Humming House
column3: 哼歌屋

column2: A little house built of shells in the middle of the sands, and before it a white-haired old woman who sits on the ground singing every night, then lays her ear to the earth to listen. This is Granny Clam, keeper of the great shen for fifty years. Pearl-poaching pirates with iron bars have surrounded her, demanding she tell them where the shen pearl is, and Granny Clam goes on singing with her eyes closed, not a note out of tune.
column3: 沙地中间一座贝壳垒的小屋，屋前一个白发老太太，每晚坐在地上唱歌，唱完了把耳朵贴在地上听。她就是蚌婆，守了这只大蜃五十年。一伙采珠海盗扛着铁钎围住她，要她说出蜃珠在哪儿，蚌婆闭着眼照旧唱，一个音也没走。

column2: The pirates scatter. When she sings, Granny Clam says, it hums back, and for fifty years it was always the same tune. Then ten years ago it suddenly learned a new song. 'A man on a passing ship sang it to it that year. A tune for putting a child to sleep.' Axi kneels and lays her ear to the ground: from far below comes a very slow, very low sound, humming her father's song.
column3: 海盗散了。蚌婆说她唱，它就哼，五十年都是一个调子；十年前它忽然学会了一支新歌，「是那年过路的船上一个汉子唱给它听的，哄孩子睡觉的调子」。阿汐跪下来，把耳朵贴在地上：地底下一个很慢、很低的声音，哼的正是她爹那支歌。

column2: Confiscation Store
column3: 罚没库

column2: A stone storehouse on the headland where the Customs House used to keep confiscated goods, seal pasted over seal on its door. A big smuggling ring has taken it, its best men and a big troop of mirage soldiers and archers guarding the door: inside they've turned up customs declarations from ten years ago and plan to dun the families who filed them for 'back taxes'. Hearing this, Mo San rolls up his sleeves to charge in.
column3: 海岬上一座石库，是市舶司当年存罚没货物的地方，库门上的封条一层压一层。一伙走私的大帮占了石库，最精的人手和一大队蜃兵蜃弓手守在门口：他们在库里翻出了十年前的报关单，要拿去找当年报关的人家要「补税」。墨三一听，袖子一挽就要冲。

column2: The smugglers are scattered and the declarations gathered back up one by one. Mo San draws one out: the declaration for the Qianli's five ships, cargo, crew and vessels all filled in clearly, only the 'destination' box left blank, and beside it a line in Shen Du's small hand: 'Destination to be filled in by those who come after.' Mo San slips it carefully into his ledger. 'She wrote everything. This one box she left for someone else.'
column3: 走私帮被打散，报关单一张张收了回来。墨三抽出其中一张：千里号五船的报关单，货、人、船都填得清清楚楚，只有「去处」一栏空着，旁边沈渡批了一行小字：「去处待后来者填。」墨三把单子小心夹进簿子：「她什么都写了，就这一栏，留给别人。」

column2: Evening Glow Tower
column3: 晚照楼

column2: Every evening a lamp lights in the tower floating above the Customs House's rear courtyard, and beneath it sits a woman with a short blade at her waist, head bent, writing. A pirate band says she's a ghost and there'll be trouble if she isn't laid, and they line up below to shoot fire arrows into the sky; the arrows go through the tower and land on the plain, setting a stretch of grass alight. Below, Mo San is hopping with anguish. 'Don't shoot! That's my employer!'
column3: 每天傍晚，市舶司后院浮在半空的那座楼上会亮起一盏灯，灯下坐着一个女人，腰挂短刀，低头写字。一伙海盗说那是女鬼，镇不住要出事，排在楼下朝天上放火箭，箭穿过楼，落在荒原上，烧着了一片草。墨三在楼下急得跳脚：「别射！那是东家！」

column2: The pirates are run off and the grass fire beaten out. The woman in the tower finishes a page, lifts her head and looks across the empty air at you, and her lips move. A Zhou can read her lips; he reads them twice. 'Accounts.' The lamp goes out and the tower fades. In ten years she has written every day, Mo San says, and he's never once seen her look up. 'She saw you.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，草火扑灭了。楼上的女人写完一页，抬起头，隔着半空朝你们看了一眼，嘴唇动了动。阿舟读得出她的口形，读了两遍：「账。」灯灭了，楼淡了。墨三说十年来她天天写，可他从没见她抬过头：「她看见你们了。」

column2: Pearl-Cutting Workshop
column3: 剖珠坊

column2: A little workshop on the plain run by a squinting old pearl-cutter called Old Che, who collects the broken pearls the great shen sheds and splits them open one by one to look inside. Pearl-poaching pirates burst in demanding every pearl he's saved, since split pearls are worthless and whole ones sell. Old Che hugs a box of half-opened pearls to his chest. 'Split, they're worth more! There are days in here!'
column3: 荒原上一间小作坊，坊主是个眯眼的老珠匠，叫老砗，专收大蜃掉下来的碎珠，一粒粒剖开看。一伙采珠海盗冲进坊里，要他把攒的珠子全交出来，说剖开了就不值钱了，留着卖。老砗把一盒半开的珠子护在怀里：「剖开才值钱！这里头是日子！」

column2: The pirates are chased off. Old Che lays the split pearls out for you: layer wrapped around layer, like a tree's rings. The old layers are thick, ring after ring perfectly clear; the last few years' are paper thin and broken in several places. 'It's forgetting.' He picks one out: wrapped in the layer from ten years ago is a fleck of red paint. 'Hull paint. That year ships passed over it.'
column3: 海盗被打跑。老砗把剖开的珠子摆给你们看：一层裹一层，像树的年轮。老的那几层厚，一圈一圈清清楚楚；最外头这几年的，薄得像纸，还断了好几处。「它在忘。」他挑出一粒，十年前那一层里裹着一星红漆：「船底的漆。那年有船从它身上过。」

column2: Shell-Drilling Ground
column3: 钻壳场

column2: A row of timber frames stands on the sand with iron drills hanging from them, and pearl-poaching pirates take turns cranking the winches to bore into the ground. Each time a drill rod comes out, salt water wells up from the hole, and after a while the ground shudders as if in pain. A few mirage soldiers guard the frames, but each shudder makes them fainter, and the pirates curse and keep drilling.
column3: 沙地上竖着一排木架，架上吊着铁钻，一伙采珠海盗轮班摇着绞盘，往地底下钻。钻杆一拔出来，钻眼里就往外冒咸水，冒一阵，地就疼似的抖一下。几个蜃兵守在木架旁，可地每抖一回，蜃兵就淡一层，海盗们骂骂咧咧，照钻不误。

column2: The pirates are chased off and the frames toppled. Zhu'er lies beside the bore holes and plugs them with mud one by one, and with each the ground seems to let out a breath. The drill bits are stamped with the character 'Hook'. The pirates' work book reads: 'Hook Seven's orders: three more zhang and you'll reach the pearl. Ten piculs of rice to whoever reaches it.' The reward isn't silver. It's rice.
column3: 海盗被赶跑，木架推倒了。珠儿趴在钻眼边，拿泥一个个堵上，堵一个，地就松一口气。钻头上錾着一个「钩」字。海盗的工簿上写着：「钩七令：再钻三丈，见珠。见珠者赏米十石。」赏的不是银子，是米。

column2: Shell-Drying Yard
column3: 晒贝场

column2: A great drying yard on the sand where the clam-diggers spread the clams and razor shells they dig on straw mats to dry, a year's food for them. A gang of shell dealers has seized the yard and forces prices down to a bowl of rice per basket, letting no one dry who won't sell, with a squad of mirage archers to guard it. The diggers have had to leave their wet catch heaped at their doors, where it's going bad.
column3: 沙地上一大片晒场，蛤户们把挖来的沙蛤、蛏子摊在草席上晒干，一年的口粮全靠它。一伙贝贩霸了晒场，压价收贝，一筐贝只给一碗米，不卖就不许晒，还雇了一队蜃弓手守着场子。蛤户们只好把湿贝堆在家门口，一堆堆臭了。

column2: The shell dealers are thrown out and the mats are spread across the yard again, the briny smell shot through with the smell of sunshine. Granny Clam says the diggers only take the little clams along the great shen's shell rim. 'Things that grow on it, it doesn't mind. What it minds is someone boring into its heart.' At the yard's edge stands a post hung with a string of shells: the diggers' calendar, one shell a day.
column3: 贝贩被撵走了，草席重新铺满了晒场，咸腥味里透着太阳味。蚌婆说，蛤户挖的是大蜃壳边上的小蛤，「它身上长的，它不心疼；它心疼的是有人往它心口钻」。晒场边立着一根木桩，桩上挂着一串贝壳，是蛤户记日子的，一天一枚。

column2: From the yard's storehouse you seize the dealers' hoard: eighty sacks of dried clams, thirty strings of dried razor shells, two vats of rice, and a rigged steelyard whose weight has been filled with lead.
column3: 晒场的库房里抄出贝贩囤的八十袋干蛤、三十串干蛏、两缸米，还有一杆做了手脚的秤，秤砣里灌了铅。

column2: Each time you pass, the clam-diggers fill a sack with perfectly dried clams for you, and Zhu'er lies down by the cart wheels to feel the ground. 'It's breathing evenly today. You'll travel well.'
column3: 每次路过，蛤户们都给你们装一袋晒得正好的干蛤，珠儿趴在车轮边摸一摸地，说：「今天它喘得匀，你们走得顺。」

column2: Tax-Farm Camp
column3: 包税营

column2: A stockade on the sand flying a banner reading 'Collecting under contract to the Customs House': a gang of tax farmers who claim they've bought the right to levy duties on this road from Mo San, taking three parts in ten of every load and impounding carts that won't pay. In fact Mo San has never sold anything. Their muscle is hired swordsmen plus a squad of mirage soldiers on sentry duty, all stony-faced like real bailiffs.
column3: 沙地上一座营寨，寨门口插着一面「奉市舶司包征」的旗，是一伙包税人：他们说从墨三手里买下了这一路的抽税权，凡是过往的货，十抽三，不交就扣车。其实墨三从没卖过什么。寨里的打手是雇来的刀客，还有一队蜃兵站岗，个个板着脸，像真的衙役。

column2: The tax farmers are scattered and the impounded carts released. Mo San opens his ledger and enters their extortions of these past years item by item, down to a single confiscated hen. Asked why he bothers, he says, 'Accounts don't sort good from bad. Leave one entry out and they won't balance.' The tax farmers' chief covers his face. 'You're writing that down too?' Mo San doesn't look up. 'That especially.'
column3: 包税人被打散，扣下的车都放了。墨三翻开簿子，一笔笔记下他们这几年的勒索，连扣下的一只鸡都记上了。有人问记这些做什么，他说：「账不分好坏，少一笔就对不上。」包税头目捂着脸：「连这个也记？」墨三头也不抬：「尤其是这个。」

column2: Telling Festival
column3: 报信祭

column2: Every autumn the clam-diggers hold a Telling Festival: the whole hamlet sits on the ground and each person tells the earth the year's news, whose son married, whose wife had a baby, which shoal brought new fish. That night the towers in the sky show the year as it was. This year the festival ground has been taken by the pearl poachers, who forbid any gathering: the worse the shen's memory, they say, the easier it is to drill.
column3: 蛤户每年秋天办一回「报信祭」：全屯的人围坐在地上，一个个对着地说这一年的事，谁家娶亲，谁家添丁，哪片滩来了新鱼。说完，晚上天上的楼里就会映出这一年的样子。今年祭场被采珠海盗占了，他们不许人聚，说蜃记性越差越好，好下钻。

column2: The pirates are chased off and the diggers sit down all over the ground; you join in and tell a little of your journey. That night towers do appear in the sky, but all in a jumble: last year's bride leading the year before's groom, the Zhangs' baby sitting on the Lis' roof. Granny Clam laughs as she watches, then sighs. 'It's kept it all. It's just put it back in the wrong places.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，蛤户们坐了一地，你们也跟着说了几句一路上的事。夜里天上果然映出了楼，可映得乱七八糟：去年的新娘牵着前年的新郎，张家的娃坐在李家的屋顶上。蚌婆看着看着笑了，又叹了口气：「它都收着呢，就是放乱了。」

column2: Three Roads Stele
column3: 三路碑

column2: At a crossroads on the plain stands a three-sided stele, a camel carved on one face, a horse on another, a ship on the third. A pirate band uses it as a mooring post, its shaft wound with cables, and they roast fish over a fire at its foot until the smoke has blackened the inscriptions. When Mo San comes to clean it they kick him aside. 'It's a lump of old stone. What's there to clean?'
column3: 荒原路口立着一块三面的石碑，一面刻驼，一面刻马，一面刻船。一伙海盗拿它当拴船桩，碑身上缠满了缆绳，还在碑脚下生火烤鱼，烟把碑字熏得漆黑。他们见墨三来擦碑，一脚把他踹开：「一块破石头，擦什么擦！」

column2: The pirates are chased off and the cables untied. Mo San and A Zhou clean the stele together and uncover a line: 'Silk, Tea and Sea, the three roads set out together, each keeping its own book. When they meet, the books are joined; when the books agree, the road is open. Raised by the Qianli.' Mo San stops scrubbing. 'Mine is the sea road's book. The silk road's is in that bookkeeper's hands. He's the one my employer is waiting for.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，缆绳解了。墨三和阿舟一起擦碑，擦出一行字：「丝、茶、海三路同发，各记一本账。会时合账，账合，路通。千里号立。」墨三擦着擦着停了手：「我这本是海路的。丝路那本，在那位账房先生手里。东家等的，就是他。」

column2: Mirage-Watching Platform
column3: 观蜃台

column2: A timber platform on high ground, set with bronze rules, bamboo poles and boards scored into grids: an old scholar's mirage observatory. He came from the capital and has recorded the Mirage for twenty years, which days it appears, for how long, showing what, all written in his volumes. A pirate band finds his poles in the way, suspects his volumes record hidden treasure, and is pulling the platform down.
column3: 荒原高处一座木台，台上架着铜尺、竹竿、刻着格子的木板，是一个老学究的观蜃台：他从京城来，记了二十年蜃楼，哪天出、出几刻、出什么，都记在册子上。一伙海盗嫌他的竹竿碍事，又疑心册子里记着藏宝的地方，正把台子往下拆。

column2: The pirates are run off and the old scholar climbs back onto the platform hugging his volumes. He shows you: after the twenty-eighth of the eighth month ten years ago, every morning the first thing in the sky was always a road of lights, a string of lamps running west to east above the sea, as if showing someone the way. 'Ten years, not one day missed.' But in the last two years' volumes the road is broken into pieces, and the latest page shows only seven lamps.
column3: 海盗被打跑，老学究抱着册子爬回台上。他翻给你们看：十年前八月廿八以后，每天清早，天上头一样东西总是一条灯路，一串灯从西往东，铺在海面上空，像在给谁指路。「十年，一天没断过。」可近两年的册子里，灯路断成了一截一截，最近一页只画了七盏。

column2: Pearl Lookout
column3: 瞭珠哨

column2: At the end of the sands stands an earthen lookout flying a banner painted with a hook: Hook Seven's watch post, set to spot where the ground breathes and where pearls surface, and signal with smoke when they do. There aren't many pearl poachers inside, but they're all Hook Seven's old hands, showing no light at night and lying on the roof by day wrapped in sand-coloured cloth, the same colour as the desert.
column3: 沙地尽头一座土哨，哨顶插着一面画着钩子的旗，是钩七的瞭望哨，专看哪里的地在喘、哪里冒珠子，看见了就放烟报信。哨里的采珠海盗不多，可都是钩七的老手，夜里不点灯，白天裹着沙色的布趴在哨顶，跟沙地一个颜色。

column2: The lookouts are knocked off the roof. The last pages of the post's log set out Hook Seven's plan: if the drills won't go through, go to the mountain foot in the south and pack gunpowder where the great shen's shell meets the rock. 'One blast and the pearl will come out by itself.' On the back is a crooked line: 'Two more starved on the island. Hurry.'
column3: 哨兵被打下了哨顶。哨簿最后几页记着钩七的打算：钻不下去，就去南边山脚，从大蜃壳和山石接缝的地方埋火药，「一炸，珠子自己就出来了」。簿子背面还有一行歪字：「岛上又饿死两个。快。」

column2: Borrowed-Dream Inn
column3: 借梦店

column2: A roadside inn on the plain with a banner reading 'Dreams to Borrow': sleep a night here and you'll dream a stretch of road, ships and lamps on it, and remember every bit when you wake. A pirate band has taken over the inn and sells the dreams by the night, a tael of silver each, with mirage soldiers guarding the door. Xiaojiang wants to go straight in and sleep, and gets kicked straight back out.
column3: 荒原路边一间客店，门口挂着「借梦」的幌子：在这儿睡一觉，就会梦见一段路，路上有船有灯，醒来记得清清楚楚。一伙海盗占了客店，把梦论夜卖，一夜一两银子，还拿蜃兵守着门。小桨一听就要进去睡，被海盗一脚踹了出来。

column2: The pirates are thrown out and Xiaojiang falls asleep the moment he lies down. In the middle of the night he dreams of a ship in fog with a wiry old man lying across its bow, ear turned to the water, listening and saying as he listens: 'Nearly there. Under that cold water ahead is something with no edges. It's memorising the road. Don't disturb it.' Xiaojiang wakes with his face wet. 'That was Grandad.' The innkeeper says the inn stands right on the great shen's shell, and the dreams are what leaks out of it.
column3: 海盗被撵走，小桨倒头就睡。半夜他梦见一条船，雾里，船头趴着一个干瘦的老头，侧着耳朵听水，嘴里念叨：「快到了，前头那片冷水底下有东西，大得没有边，它在记路，别吵它。」小桨醒来，满脸是泪：「是爷爷。」店主说，这店底下就是大蜃的壳，梦是它漏出来的。

column2: Lean Island Shacks
column3: 瘦岛棚

column2: A huddle of ramshackle shacks on the sand, home to a few dozen sallow, starving people, even the children down to skin and bone, digging sand clams to eat every day. The clam-diggers resent them for digging past the boundary, and the two sides have fought several times. Today the diggers have brought in a squad of mirage soldiers to drive them out, and the men in the shacks charge out with clam rakes while the women pull the children back.
column3: 沙地上搭着一片破棚子，住着几十个面黄肌瘦的人，连孩子都只剩一把骨头，天天在沙里刨沙蛤吃。蛤户嫌他们越界挖贝，两边打了好几回。今天蛤户请来一队蜃兵要撵人，棚里的男人们拿着蛤耙冲了出来，女人抱着孩子往后躲。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter and both sides lower their rakes. The shack people come from a little island out in the eastern sea called Lean Island; three years ago the fish stopped coming and its three hundred people were left with nothing to eat. 'Hook Seven is one of ours. He says a shen pearl would buy enough rice to feed the whole island for three years.' Granny Clam hears them out and says nothing for a long while, then has Zhu'er take two sacks of dried clams to the shacks.
column3: 蜃兵散了，两边都住了手。棚里的人是从东边海上一座小岛来的，岛叫瘦岛，三年前鱼群不来了，岛上三百口人没了吃的。「钩七是我们岛上的，他说挖出蜃珠，换的米够全岛吃三年。」蚌婆听完，半天没说话，让珠儿给棚里送了两袋干蛤。

column2: Knot-Cord Hut
column3: 结绳寮

column2: Beside the Customs House stands a straw hut where Mo San's little apprentice Xiaoyan lives. She's twelve, knows few characters, and keeps her records in knotted cord: one cord a day, big knots for big things, small knots for small. A pirate band has heard her cords record 'when the employer comes out' and wants them to sell to rich men eager to see a ghost, and failing to grab them they've set the hut alight. Xiaoyan has climbed onto the roof beam clutching a huge bundle of cord.
column3: 市舶司旁边一间草寮，住着墨三的小徒弟小砚，十二岁，不识几个字，记账靠结绳：一根绳一天，大结是大事，小结是小事。一伙海盗听说她的绳子记着「东家几时出来」，要拿去卖给想见鬼的阔人，抢不着就点火烧寮。小砚抱着一大捆绳子爬上了房梁。

column2: The pirates are run off, the fire put out, not a cord burned. Xiaoyan lays the cords out on the ground one by one. In the early years every cord has a big knot: the employer appeared every day. These past two years only three cords in ten are knotted, and this month only one, the day you arrived. 'She comes out less now,' Xiaoyan says. 'But she came out today. For you.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，火扑灭了，绳子一根没烧。小砚把绳子一根根摊在地上：头几年，每根绳上都有个大结，东家天天出来；这两年，十根里只有三根有结；这个月只有一根，就是你们来的那天。「她出来得少了，」小砚说，「可她今天又出来了，是为你们。」

column2: Tower Across the Air
column3: 隔空楼

column2: This evening the tower floats very low, almost touching the plain, and the woman on it is plain to see: Shen Du, her short blade, a strand of white at her temple, a ledger at her hand. Below it a pirate band out to get rich has put up ladders to climb in, and with every rung the tower backs away a step, so the pirates all shove the ladders forward together, a squad of mirage soldiers helping hold them steady.
column3: 这天傍晚，那座楼浮得很低，低得几乎挨着荒原，楼上的女人看得一清二楚：沈渡，短刀，鬓边一缕白发，手边一本账。楼下聚了一伙想发财的海盗，搭了梯子往楼上爬，爬一节，楼就往后退一步，海盗们一齐使劲推梯子，又拉来一队蜃兵帮着扶。

column2: The pirates topple with their ladders. On the tower Shen Du lays down her brush and speaks across the empty air, her voice far off, as if rising from very deep water: 'You've come. Where's the bookkeeper?' You hold up the ledger you brought from the Silk Road. She looks at it a long time, and smiles a little. 'He's always late. Accounts have to be checked face to face. Come east, to the great shen.' The tower fades, and Mo San writes it all down, word by word.
column3: 海盗和梯子一起倒了。楼上的沈渡放下笔，隔着半空说话，声音像从很深的水底传上来：「你们来了。账房先生呢？」你们举起丝路带来的那本账。她看了很久，笑了一下：「他向来晚。账要对，得当面对。往东来，到大蜃那儿。」楼淡了，墨三一个字一个字记下。

column2: Torn-Page Lane
column3: 撕页巷

column2: A little lane behind the Customs House lined with pawnshops that take not goods but ledger pages: a gang of ledger thieves tears pages from the Customs House's old books, and whoever's trade appears on a page gets a visit demanding money, or the page goes up on the city gate. Today they've torn out another stack and hired a few mirage riders to guard the lane's mouth while they wait for buyers.
column3: 市舶司后面一条小巷，巷里开着几家当铺，当的不是东西，是账页：一伙账贼专从市舶司的旧簿子里撕页，谁家的生意上了簿子，就拿那一页上门要钱，不给就把页子贴到城门口。今天账贼又撕了一摞，雇了几个蜃骑守着巷口，等买主上门。

column2: The thieves are run off and every torn page recovered. Mo San pastes them back one at a time and comes to an old roster, the crew list the Qianli registered with the Customs House. Under Ship Six is a line that's never been struck through: 'Helmsman A Zhou. Not arrived. Keep.' A Zhou looks at that line a long while before he speaks. 'She kept it all this time.'
column3: 账贼被打跑，撕下的页子全追了回来。墨三一页页对着补，补到一张旧名单，是千里号当年在市舶司登记的船员，六号船那一栏底下，有一行没划掉：「舵手阿舟，未到，留。」阿舟看着那一行，半天才说：「她一直留着。」

column2: Post to the Mirage
column3: 寄蜃驿

column2: A small post station on the plain where the Customs House receives mail, a sign at its door: 'Letters for Captain Shen in the Mirage, all accepted.' For ten years people all along the coast have sent letters here. These past days a squad of mirage soldiers gone mad has been hacking at anyone it meets, couriers included, and the courier is hiding in the horse trough clutching his mailbag, while a pirate band seizes the chance to grab the bag, thinking it full of banknotes.
column3: 荒原上一座小驿，是市舶司收信的地方，门口写着「寄蜃楼沈船主，概收」。十年来，沿海各处都有人往这儿寄信。一队发了疯的蜃兵这几天见人就砍，连送信的驿卒也砍，驿卒抱着信袋躲进了马槽，一伙海盗趁机来抢信袋，以为里头是银票。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter, the pirates flee, and the mailbag is saved. It's full of letters to Shen Du, not one opened: from Quanzhou, from the Sea of Fog, and one signed 'Long Sihai' with a single line: 'The berth is still kept. Whether you come back or not, it stays kept.' Mo San says his employer never answers letters. 'She says she'll answer them all at once, when the accounts are checked.'
column3: 蜃兵散了，海盗跑了，信袋保住了。袋里全是寄给沈渡的信，一封也没拆过：有泉州的，有雾海的，有一封署名「龙四海」，只有一句：「泊位还留着，你们回不回来，都留着。」墨三说东家从不回信，「她说等对完账，一次回」。

column2: Powder Hollow
column3: 火药坳

column2: A hollow at the foot of the southern mountains, wedged right on the seam where the great shen's shell meets the rock, heaped with powder kegs, their fuses buried crack by crack in the stone. Hook Seven has brought all his best pearl poachers here and hired a big troop of mirage soldiers and archers too, three ranks at the hollow's mouth and two along its rim. Hook Seven himself sits on a powder keg, a fire-starter clutched in his hand, his face worn down to skin.
column3: 南边山脚一道山坳，正卡在大蜃壳和山石的接缝上，坳里堆满了火药桶，引线一根根埋进石缝。钩七把手下最精的采珠海盗全调到了这里，又雇了一大队蜃兵蜃弓手，坳口三层，坳顶两层。钩七本人坐在火药桶上，手里攥着火折子，脸瘦得只剩一张皮。

column2: The elite are beaten and you wrest the fire-starter from his hand. Hook Seven doesn't run. He squats beside the kegs. 'I know it hurts. Three hundred people on the island hurt too.' He was Lean Island's head fisherman, he says; when the fish left, the court did nothing, and this was the only thing he knew how to do. You roll the kegs one by one into a ditch. He watches and doesn't stop you. 'If there were any other way, who'd want to bore holes in something alive?'
column3: 精锐败了，火折子被你们夺了下来。钩七没逃，蹲在火药桶边：「我知道它疼。岛上三百口人也疼。」他说他本是瘦岛的渔头，鱼走了，朝廷不管，他只会这一样。你们把火药桶一只只推进了水沟。他看着，没拦：「要是有别的路，谁愿意往活东西身上钻眼。」

column2: Black Ledger Tower
column3: 黑账楼

column2: A three-storey brick tower on the plain, lair of the smuggling 'Black Ledger Gang': they forge account books, fake IOUs and fake contracts for hire, and these past years their bestseller has been 'Qianli IOUs', used to dun coastal merchants for debts ten years old. Their fiercest bruisers, mirage soldiers and archers guard it floor by floor, and on the roof hang sheets of freshly aged fake ledger pages.
column3: 荒原上一座三层的砖楼，是走私的「黑账帮」的老巢：他们专门伪造账本，替人造假欠条、假契约，这几年造得最多的是「千里号欠条」，拿去找沿海的商户讨十年前的旧债。楼里最凶的打手、蜃兵、蜃弓手层层把守，楼顶上晾着一张张刚做旧的假账页。

column2: The Black Ledger Gang is scattered and their fake pages burn in the yard all afternoon. Mo San lays one fake IOU beside the Qianli's page in his own ledger and shakes his head. 'False. When the Qianli left, its accounts were square.' He points to a line in Shen Du's own hand: 'The Qianli owes: nothing.' Only the very last line is unfinished: 'Owed to those who come after: '.
column3: 黑账帮被打散，假账页堆在院子里烧了一下午。墨三拿着一张假欠条，和他簿子里千里号的那一页并排一比，摇头：「假的。千里号走的时候，账是平的。」他指着自己簿子上沈渡亲笔的那一行：「千里号，欠：无。」只有最后一行没写完：「欠后来者：」。

column2: Pearl Vault
column3: 珠库

column2: A stone cave at the foot of the mountains, its mouth closed by an iron grille: inside are the pearls Hook Seven has gathered these past years, picked from cracks, dug from bore holes, several hundred great and small, not yet shipped off to trade for rice. Guarding the vault are his toughest pearl poachers and a big troop of mirage riders, half transparent, looking ready to dissolve at any moment, yet refusing to give a step.
column3: 山脚一处石洞，洞口拿铁栅栏封着，里头是钩七这几年攒下的珠子：从地缝里抠的，从钻眼里掏的，大大小小几百粒，都还没来得及运去换米。守库的是他手下最狠的一伙采珠海盗，外加一大队蜃骑，洞前的蜃骑一个个半透明，像随时会散，却一步不退。

column2: The vault's guards are beaten and the grille is pried open. Zhu'er carries the pearls out and lays them one by one back into the breathing cracks in the ground, and with each one the earth grows a little warmer. That night the road of lights in the sky suddenly shines complete, west to east, not one lamp missing, as it was ten years ago. The old scholar counts them lamp by lamp on his platform, then sits down on the boards and weeps. 'It remembers. Just for tonight.'
