column3: 守库的败了，铁栅栏撬开了。珠儿捧着珠子，一粒粒放回地上喘气的缝里，放一粒，地就暖一下。那天夜里，天上的灯路忽然亮全了，从西到东，一盏不缺，像十年前那样。老学究在台上一盏盏数，数完了，坐在地上哭：「它想起来了，就这一夜。」

column2: Shell-Pecking Ridge
column3: 啄壳岭

column2: The slope at the foot of the mountains is covered in oystercatchers, black backs and red bills, tens of thousands of them, jabbing their long bills at the ground: the little clams growing along the great shen's shell rim have multiplied these past years and drawn birds from every hill. When the clams are pecked clean, the flocks go for travellers' ration bags and the diggers' drying mats, and they've even carried off Zhu'er's straw hat. The diggers have chased them again and again; the flocks rise all together and settle all together.
column3: 山脚的坡上落满了蛎鹬，黑背红嘴，成千上万，正拿长嘴啄着地面：大蜃壳边上长的小蛤这几年越来越多，引来了满山的鸟。鸟群啄空了蛤，就去啄过路人的干粮袋，啄蛤户的晒席，连珠儿的草帽都被叼走了。蛤户赶了好几回，鸟群一哄而起，又一哄而落。

column2: The flocks are driven up the mountain and the slope falls quiet. Granny Clam says the little clams have multiplied because the great shen's breath has run warm these last years, warming the water along its rim so the clams thrive. 'It's tired. Its body runs hot, like a person with a fever.' Zhu'er finds his straw hat in a nest with two eggs in it, and gently puts them back.
column3: 鸟群被赶上了山，坡上清净了。蚌婆说小蛤多，是因为大蜃这几年吐的气暖，壳边的水暖，小蛤就长得欢：「它累了，身子发热，像人发烧。」珠儿从鸟窝里找回了草帽，帽里还有两枚鸟蛋，他又轻轻放了回去。

column2: Abacus Reef
column3: 算盘礁

column2: On a rock by the sea sits a white-bearded old man with a gold-beaded abacus on his knees, clacking away for ten years now; they call him the Abacus Immortal. He's reckoning the Qianli's grand total across all three roads, and every time he's one copper out; reckon again, still one copper out. A pirate band covets the gold abacus and is swimming out to grab it, and the old man keeps clicking beads with one hand while kicking at them with his feet.
column3: 海边一块礁石上坐着个白胡子老头，膝上一把金珠算盘，噼里啪啦打了十年，人称算盘仙。他算的是千里号三路的总账，算一遍，差一文；再算一遍，还差一文。一伙海盗眼红那把金算盘，围着礁石泅水上来抢，老头一边打算盘一边拿脚踹。

column2: The pirates are driven back into the sea. The Abacus Immortal says the copper isn't his mistake; there's a book missing. 'The sea road's account is with Mo San, someone brought one page of the tea road's, and of the silk road's there's not a word. Without that book I'll always be a copper out.' You hand him the ledger of the Silk Road's bookkeeper. He leafs through a few pages. 'That's it, that's the copper. But it only counts in front of the employer.'
column3: 海盗被赶回了海里。算盘仙说那一文不是他算错了，是少了一本：「海路的账在墨三那儿，茶路的有人捎来过一页，丝路的一个字也没有。没有那本，永远差一文。」你们递上丝路账房的账，他翻了几页：「对了，就是这一文。可这得当着东家的面才算数。」

column2: Mo Family Noodle Stall
column3: 墨家面摊

column2: A noodle stall at the end of the Customs House's street, kept by Mo San's wife, Mistress Mo, who pulls her noodles long and fine. A gang of protection racketeers has come with a few mirage riders to make trouble: the stall's in their way, so pay up or move. Mistress Mo has a rolling pin in one hand and a ladle in the other. 'My husband hasn't been home from that office in a month, and now you come making trouble too!'
column3: 市舶司街口一个面摊，摊主是墨三的媳妇墨嫂，面条拉得又细又长。一伙收保护钱的地痞带着几个蜃骑来闹，嫌面摊挡了他们的道，要么交钱，要么搬走。墨嫂一手拿擀面杖，一手拿汤勺：「我男人在衙门里一个月没回家，你们还来添乱！」

column2: The racketeers are run off and Mistress Mo cooks each of you a bowl of noodles. Mo San hasn't been home in a month, she says, because his ledger is nearly full, all but the last page. 'He says he can't write that page himself. He has to wait for someone to come and write it in front of the employer.' She slips an extra egg into your bowls. 'You're that someone, aren't you? Once it's written, send him home to eat.'
column3: 地痞被打跑，墨嫂给你们一人下了一碗面。她说墨三一个月没回家，是因为簿子快满了，就差最后一页，「他说那一页不能他写，得等一个人来，当着东家的面写」。她往面里多卧了个蛋：「你们就是那个人吧？写完了，让他回家吃饭。」

column2: Ledger-Check Pass
column3: 验簿关

column2: A pass at the mountain foot, its gate tower half real, half not, and before it a row of old customs officers cast down from the Mirage, stopping everyone in turn with the same question: 'Is your name in the ledger?' Whoever can't answer has the mirage soldiers behind the officers fall on them. A pirate band is crowded outside the pass too, trying to slip through east for pickings and being cut about by the soldiers.
column3: 山脚下一道关口，关楼半真半假，关前站着一排蜃楼里映下来的老关吏，挨个拦人，问的都是同一句：「簿上有你的名字吗？」答不上的，关吏身后的蜃兵就扑上来。关口外头还挤着一伙海盗，想混过关去东边捞好处，被蜃兵砍得东倒西歪。

column2: The pirates are scattered and the mirage soldiers fall back. Mo San opens his ledger and reads out your trades along the road to the officers; with each entry they nod, and when he finishes they fade one by one and the gate opens of its own accord. 'Trades you've made are your pass,' Mo San says. 'The Mirage King only knows people who are written in the ledger.'
column3: 海盗被打散，蜃兵退了。墨三翻开簿子，把你们一路的买卖念给关吏听，念一笔，关吏点一下头，念完，关吏一个个淡了，关门自己开了。墨三说：「做过的买卖，就是过关的凭据。蜃王只认记在簿上的人。」

column2: Ledger-Buyer's Manor
column3: 买簿庄

column2: A great manor at the mountain foot whose master, a big merchant nicknamed Golden Abacus, has heard Mo San's ledger records every trade on the sea and offered ten thousand taels for it; refused, he means to take it. Who owes whom, who dodged their duties, it's all in there, and whoever holds it holds the whole sea by the throat. He's hired a big troop of swordsmen and mirage archers and blocked Mo San's road east tight.
column3: 山脚一座大庄子，庄主是个绰号「金算盘」的大商人，听说墨三的簿子记着全海的买卖，出了一万两要买，买不成就抢：谁家欠谁、谁家偷了税，都在里头，拿到手就能拿捏一海的人。他雇了一大队刀客和蜃弓手，把墨三去东边的路堵得严严实实。

column2: The swordsmen are scattered and Golden Abacus cowers in his counting house. Mo San turns to his page and reads out three dodged duties, and the merchant goes white. Mo San shuts the book. 'This ledger is for recording a road, not for squeezing people. The duties you dodged, go and pay them yourself.' Golden Abacus pays them the very next day, plus an extra tenth, for peace of mind, he says.
column3: 刀客被打散，金算盘缩在账房里。墨三翻到他那一页，念了三笔漏税，金算盘的脸一下子白了。墨三合上簿子：「簿子是记路的，不是拿人的。你漏的税，自己去补。」金算盘第二天就去补了，还多交了一成，说是买个安心。

column2: Shop Three Hundred and One
column3: 三百零一铺

column2: A general store by the sea, its signboard reading 'Kept by a hand of the Qianli', its owner a plump middle-aged man who tells everyone he's one of the Qianli's people. No one believes him, least of all the pirate band that comes to lean on him every day: 'A Qianli man, eh? Where's that ship's treasure hidden?' When he won't say they smash his shelves, and they've posted mirage soldiers at the door so no one can shop. The store hasn't opened in half a year.
column3: 海边一间杂货铺，招牌上写着「千里号伙计开」，铺主是个胖乎乎的中年人，逢人便说他是千里号的人。没人信，一伙海盗更是天天来敲他：「千里号的人？那船上的宝贝藏哪儿了？」不说就砸货架，还拿蜃兵守着铺门，不许人进去买东西，铺子半年没开张。

column2: The pirates are run off, and the moment A Zhou sees the owner he bursts out laughing. 'You're the one who overslept!' The owner is Hu Shiyi, signed onto the crew list on the very last day; next morning the ships sailed while he slept on, and by the time he'd chased down to the shore they'd gone into the fog. 'Number three hundred and one,' he says, scratching his head. 'The captain said my line isn't on the list, it comes after.' He opens up again, and every item he trades you is full weight.
column3: 海盗被打跑，阿舟一看见铺主就笑出了声：「你是那个睡过头的！」铺主叫胡十一，十年前最后一天才上名册，第二天开船他睡过了头，追到海边，船已进雾。「第三百零一个，」他挠着头，「船主说我这一行不在名单上，在后头。」他重新开张，换给你们的货件件足秤。

column2: Scramble-for-the-Scale Flat
column3: 抢秤坪

column2: The moment word goes out that the market at the mountain foot is opening, traders of every kind pour onto this flat and fall to squabbling over who goes on the scale first: Lean Islanders lugging dried clams, clam-diggers with shellfish on their backs, salt workers driving salt carts, and a pirate band posing as traders, charging about with mirage riders to seize the first place. Mo San is jammed in the middle and his ledger nearly gets squeezed out of his arms.
column3: 山脚互市要开张的消息一传出去，各路商贩全涌到了这片坪上，为了谁先上秤吵成一团：瘦岛的人扛着干蛤，蛤户背着贝，盐工赶着盐车，还有一伙海盗冒充商贩，带着蜃骑横冲直撞，要抢头一个位子。墨三被挤在当中，怀里的簿子差点被挤掉。

column2: The fake traders are run off, the rest form a queue, and Mo San has them draw lots. The first lot goes to a little girl from Lean Island, skin and bone, who sets a small sack of dried clams on the scale pan, eyes shining. Mo San writes in his ledger: 'Mountain Foot Market, first trade.'
column3: 冒充的海盗被打跑，剩下的商贩排起了队，墨三让大家抓阄。抓到头一个的，是瘦岛一个瘦得皮包骨的小姑娘，她扛着一小袋干蛤，往秤盘上一放，眼睛亮亮的。墨三在簿子上记了一笔：「山脚互市，第一笔。」

column2: Mountain Foot Market
column3: 山脚互市

column2: A stretch of level ground at the mountain foot facing the great shen's shell lip, once where the clam-diggers and hill folk traded, abandoned ten years ago. Now the market mouth is held by a last big pirate band and mirage soldiers: the pirates want the road to themselves, while the soldiers stop everyone, pirates included. Mo San has set his scale and ledger on a stone table at the market mouth, waiting for you to clear a way.
column3: 山脚下一片平地，正对着大蜃的壳唇，从前是蛤户和山民交换东西的地方，十年前就荒了。如今市口被最后一大伙海盗和蜃兵占着：海盗要独占这条路，蜃兵则什么人都拦，连海盗也拦。墨三把秤和簿子摆在市口的石台上，等你们打开一条路。

column2: The pirates and soldiers scatter and the trade of grain for stone opens for business, thirty thousand a day. The Lean Islanders shoulder their grain toward the shore, Hook Seven walking last, turning back to bow to the clam-diggers. Mo San enters every one of today's trades in his ledger and turns to the last page, still blank. He lays the Silk Road's book beside his own. 'Both books are here, and so are the people.' He looks toward the shell lip. 'Tomorrow at dawn it opens. The employer said accounts have to be checked face to face.'
column3: 海盗和蜃兵都散了，粮食换石料的买卖开了张，每天三万。瘦岛的人扛着粮往海边走，钩七走在最后，回头朝蛤户作了个揖。墨三把今天的每一笔都记进簿子，翻到最后一页，还是空着。他把丝路的那本账和自己这本并排摆好：「两本都在，人也到了。」他望着壳唇：「明天一早它张嘴。东家说过，账要当面对。」

column2: Blockaded Bay
column3: 封港湾

column2: The Customs House's little harbour is choked by a great crowd of pirate ships whose crews say they've 'come to check accounts': hearing the Customs House means to reconcile every account on the sea, and afraid their own old debts will come to light, they've simply blockaded the port, letting no ship in or out. Mirage archers stand in the bows and mirage soldiers hang along the rails, so from afar it looks like a navy, and only up close can you see half of it is shadow.
column3: 市舶司的小港被一大片海盗船堵住了，船上的人说是「来对账的」：他们听说市舶司要把全海的账对一遍，怕自家的旧账翻出来，干脆把港口封了，一条船也不许进出。船头站着蜃弓手，船舷挂着蜃兵，远看像一支水师，近了才看出一半是影子。

column2: The pirate fleet is broken and the harbour opens. The captured pirate chief hangs his head. 'Those old accounts of ours, are they all in the book?' Mo San says they are, every one. The chief sighs. 'Then keep them. Make what comes after look better.' Ships can come and go again, and one of them, loaded with grain, is bound for Lean Island.
column3: 海盗船队被打散，港口通了。被俘的海盗头子垂头丧气：「我们那些旧账，是不是都在簿子上？」墨三说在，一笔不少。海盗头子叹了口气：「那就记着吧，往后的，记好看点。」港里的船又能进出了，有一条装着粮，往瘦岛去。

column2: Sealed Account Pavilion
column3: 封账阁

column2: A small pavilion on a seaside cliff, its door pasted with a Customs House seal bearing Shen Du's stamp. Mo San hasn't dared open it in ten years: his employer said it was to be opened only when those who come after arrived. A pirate band is sure it holds the Qianli's treasure map, and with their best men and a big troop of mirage soldiers and riders they hold the cliff and are hacking at the door with axes. Mo San throws himself at them and is kicked to the cliff edge.
column3: 海边崖上一座小阁，阁门贴着市舶司的封条，封条上是沈渡的印。墨三十年没敢开过：东家吩咐，后来者来了才开。一伙海盗认定阁里是千里号的藏宝图，带着最精的手下和一大队蜃兵蜃骑守在崖上，正拿斧子劈门，墨三扑上去，被一脚踹到崖边。

column2: The pirates are driven off the cliff. Mo San peels off the seal. Inside there's only a small account book: Shen Du's own. 'Owed to Bao Laozhen: half his wages, payable on return. Owed to Qi Shouguang: ten jin of lamp oil, repaid by his granddaughter. Owed to the Dry Sea Army: one month's pay, stored on Smoke Island. Owed to Same-Day Town: one tomorrow. Owed to those who come after: a road.' Mo San sighs. 'Everything else is paid. This one she can't pay by herself.'
column3: 海盗被打下崖。墨三揭了封条，阁里只有一本小账，是沈渡自己的：「欠鲍老针工钱一半，回程付。欠戚守光灯油十斤，已由其孙女还。欠旱海军一月饷，已存烟岛。欠复日城一个明天。欠后来者：一条路。」墨三叹气：「别的都还上了，就这一笔，她自己还不了。」

column2: Road Before the Shell
column3: 壳前道

column2: The last stretch of road to the shell lip, low rocks on either side, the surface unnaturally flat and slightly soft underfoot. A band of pirates with nowhere left to go holds it, mirage soldiers behind them and you in front, trapped both ways, so they've steeled themselves, dug pit traps in the road and drawn up for battle. Beneath the ground the breathing comes heavier with every breath.
column3: 通往壳唇的最后一段路，两边是低矮的山石，路面平得反常，踩上去微微发软。一伙走投无路的海盗守在这里，后头是蜃兵，前头是你们，他们进退两难，干脆横下一条心，在路上挖了陷坑，摆好了阵。地底下的喘气，一下比一下重。

column2: The pirates are beaten, throw down their blades and sit by the road. These past nights, they say, the towers in the sky have sunk lower each night; two days ago their feet touched the sea, and yesterday the people in them walked east one by one and vanished into the shell lip. 'Like packing up a stall,' one says. 'It's taking back everything it's breathed out.'
column3: 海盗败了，扔了刀坐在路边。他们说这几天夜里，天上的楼一晚比一晚低，前天楼脚挨着了海面，昨天楼里的人一个个往东走，走进壳唇里就不见了。「像是在收摊，」一个海盗说，「它要把吐出去的东西都收回去。」

column2: Seaweed Paper Hut
column3: 海苔纸寮

column2: A papermaking hut by the sea whose owner, an old papermaker, pounds seaweed and worn-out nets into pulp. His paper smells of the sea but it's tough and won't fall apart even soaked, and every ledger at the Customs House is made of it. A pirate band has taken the hut, using the finished paper to caulk their hulls and steeping their reeking socks in the pulp vats, and the old man, driven outside, squats on the rocks wiping his eyes.
column3: 海边一间纸寮，寮主是个老纸匠，拿海苔和破网捣浆造纸，纸带着一股海腥味，可结实，泡了水也不烂，市舶司的簿子全用他的纸。一伙海盗占了纸寮，把造好的纸拿去糊船缝，纸浆缸里泡上了他们的臭袜子，老纸匠被赶到寮外，蹲在礁石上抹眼泪。

column2: The pirates are chased off and the pulp vats refilled with clean water. Ten years ago, the old papermaker says, Captain Shen ordered a quire of paper from him for 'the last page'. 'The toughest you've got. A hundred years without rotting.' No one has ever come to collect it. He wraps it and hands it to Mo San. 'Write the last page on this.'
column3: 海盗被赶跑，纸浆缸换了清水。老纸匠说十年前沈船主在他这儿订过一刀纸，说是给最后一页用的，「要最结实的，一百年不烂」。那刀纸一直没人来取。他把纸包好递给墨三：「最后一页，用这个写。」

column2: From the hut you seize the pirates' stores: forty bundles of dried seaweed, six sacks of rice, a cask of fish oil, and three hundred sheets of good paper they'd grabbed to caulk their boats, which the old papermaker smooths flat one by one, saying they'll still serve.
column3: 纸寮里抄出海盗囤的四十捆干海苔、六袋米、一桶鱼油，还有他们抢来糊船的三百张好纸，老纸匠一张张抚平，说还能用。

column2: Each time you pass, the old papermaker gives you a sheaf of seaweed paper and a packet of toasted seaweed. 'Paper for remembering, seaweed for filling up. Write down what happens on the road. Don't leave it all to your head.'
column3: 每次路过，老纸匠都给你们一叠海苔纸和一包烤海苔，说：「纸记事，海苔管饱。路上的事记下来，别全指望脑子。」

column2: Shen-Spawn Shallows
column3: 蜃子滩

column2: A stretch of shallows at the edge of the plain, and when the spring tide goes out it's thick with little clams the size of coins, opening and closing, and each time one opens it breathes out a small ball of light with a fingernail-sized tower floating in it. These are the great shen's spawn. A pirate band holds the shallows, gathering them by the basket to seal in glass jars and sell to rich men in the cities as 'towers in a bottle', and trampling whatever they can't carry.
column3: 荒原尽头一片浅滩，大潮一退，滩上密密麻麻趴满了小蛤，铜钱大，一张一合，每张一回嘴，就吐出一小团光，光里浮着一座指甲大的楼。这是大蜃的蜃子。一伙海盗守在滩上，一筐筐地捡，装进琉璃瓶里卖给城里的阔人当「瓶中楼」，捡不完的就拿脚踩。

column2: This time the pirates are driven off the shallows, and the remaining spawn slowly burrow back into the mud, their little towers going out one by one. Granny Clam says the great shen releases spawn at every spring tide, a dozen times a year, and while towers in a bottle are the fashion in the cities, the pirates will keep coming, crop after crop. 'Its children need someone watching over them.' When the next spring tide comes, you'll have to come and drive them off again.
column3: 这一回的海盗被赶下了滩，剩下的蜃子慢慢钻回了泥里，一滩小楼一盏盏熄了。蚌婆说大蜃每逢大潮就放一回蜃子，一年十几回，城里的瓶中楼一时兴，海盗就一茬接一茬地来。「它的孩子，总得有人看着。」过些日子大潮再来，你们还得再来赶一回。

column2: Reckoning Terrace
column3: 对账台

column2: Before the shell lip lies a flat white stone like a great desk. Mo San sets out two books on it, the sea road's and the silk road's, and spreads out the quire of seaweed paper. Dawn is near; a sheen of light rises along the shell lip, and out of it walks a figure: Shen Du, short blade, white hair, a ledger in her hand too. She lays it at the far end of the desk and looks at you. 'Where's the bookkeeper?' You answer for him: 'He's late.' Before the words are out, rank upon rank of mirage soldiers rise from the ground around the desk and close in on the stone.
column3: 壳唇前一块平平的白石，像一张大案。墨三把两本账摆上去，海路一本，丝路一本，铺开那刀海苔纸。天快亮了，壳唇边浮起一层光，光里走出一个人：沈渡，短刀，白发，手里也拿着一本账。她把账放在案的另一头，看着你们：「账房先生呢？」你们替他说：「他晚到了。」话音没落，案边的地里一排排站起了蜃兵，围住了石案。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter. Shen Du hasn't moved. She opens the silk road's book, sees the last words, 'Silk Road: accounts settled', and her eyes redden a moment. 'Still so fond of his sums.' Three books lie side by side, and one thing is missing. 'The road the great shen has been remembering for me. Ten years it's kept it, and it can hardly hold it any more. I need you to write it down.' She points at the shell lip. 'At first light it opens. It doesn't know anyone now. You'll have to wake it first.'
column3: 蜃兵散了，沈渡没有动。她翻开丝路的账，看到「丝路，对毕」，眼睛红了：「他还是那么爱算。」三本账并排摆着，只差一样：「大蜃替我记着的那条路。它记了十年，快记不住了，我要你们把它写下来。」她指着壳唇：「天一亮它张嘴。它谁也不认得了，得先打醒它。」

column2: Shell-Lip Hamlet
column3: 壳唇屯

column2: The easternmost clam-diggers' hamlet sits right on the great shen's shell lip, its houses strung along a curving white ridge like a string of beads. A gang of pirates who broke away from Hook Seven and answer to no one has taken it, opened the diggers' grain pits, drinks all day, and throws shells at the diggers' children for target practice. Beneath the ground the breathing comes faster and faster, and the hamlet's dogs bark all night.
column3: 最东头的蛤户屯就扎在大蜃的壳唇上，屋子沿着一道弯弯的白棱排开，像一串珠子。一伙从钩七手下散出来的海盗不服管，占了屯子，开了蛤户的粮窖，天天喝酒，还拿蛤户的孩子当靶子扔贝壳。地底下的喘气一阵比一阵急，屯里的狗整夜叫个不停。

column2: The pirates are thrown out and the hamlet's dogs fall silent. The diggers say the shell lip has been closing tighter these last days while the towers in the sky sink lower. 'It's saving up its last breath.' Granny Clam lays her ear to the white ridge and listens a long time, then lifts her head. 'It's waiting for someone. Tomorrow at dawn, it will open.'
column3: 海盗被撵走，屯里的狗不叫了。蛤户们说壳唇这几天合得越来越紧，天上的楼却越来越低，「它在攒最后一口气」。蚌婆把耳朵贴在白棱上，听了很久，抬起头：「它在等人。明天一早，它张嘴。」

column2: From the grain pits you seize what the pirates hadn't drunk: six jars of wine, fifty sacks of dried clams, twenty piculs of rice, and a basket of little copper bells taken from the diggers' houses, the ones children tie to their ankles so they don't get lost walking on the shell.
column3: 粮窖里抄出海盗喝剩的六坛酒、五十袋干蛤、二十石米，还有一筐他们从蛤户家抢来的铜铃，是孩子们挂在脚上、走在壳上不迷路用的。

column2: Each time you pass, the Shell-Lip diggers serve you a bowl of clam broth sprinkled with pink salt, and the children see you to the edge of the hamlet jingling the bells on their ankles. 'It's breathing well today. Say hello to it for us.'
column3: 每次路过，壳唇屯的蛤户都给你们端一碗蛤蜊汤，汤里撒一把粉盐，孩子们摇着脚上的铜铃送你们到屯口：「它今天喘得好，替我们问它好。」

column2: Plain of Wild Riders
column3: 乱骑原

column2: On the plain outside the shell lip troop after troop of mirage riders charges, but their directions have gone wrong: one troop east, one west, two collide and pass through each other and charge on. An old clam-digger leading an ox is being chased and hacked at by a troop of riders, and the terrified ox is bolting all over the plain. A few pirates trail along behind, picking up the baskets the diggers drop.
column3: 壳唇外头的荒原上，蜃骑一队接一队地冲，冲的方向却乱了：一队往东，一队往西，两队撞在一起，穿过去，又各自接着冲。有个蛤户老汉牵着牛走过，被一队蜃骑追着砍，牛吓得满原乱跑。几个趁乱打劫的海盗跟在后头，捡蛤户丢下的筐。

column2: The riders scatter, the pirates flee and the ox is found. Granny Clam says it's frightened: too many people have bored holes in it these past years, so it breathes out soldiers to stand guard, but its memory has gone and it can't tell anyone apart, so it takes everyone for a driller. 'It isn't fierce,' she says. 'It's muddled, and afraid.'
column3: 蜃骑散了，海盗跑了，牛也找回来了。蚌婆说它害怕了：这些年往它身上钻眼的人太多，它吐兵出来守着，可记性坏了，认不得谁是谁，见人就当是来钻眼的。「它不是凶，」蚌婆说，「它是糊涂了，又怕。」

column2: Shell-Hinge Cliff
column3: 壳枢崖

column2: Under the cliff at the mountain foot lies the great shen's hinge, where the two halves of its shell close together, a faint light seeping from the seam. Hook Seven's deputy Awl won't accept Hook Seven's calling it off and has led the remaining pearl poachers up the cliff with the powder they took, only to be muddle-headedly ringed in by a big troop of mirage soldiers, the two sides tangled in a brawl. Hook Seven stands below the cliff shouting up at Awl: 'Stop! There's another way to get rice!'
column3: 山脚崖下正是大蜃壳的枢口，两扇壳在这里合拢，缝里透出微微的光。钩七的副手「锥子」不服钩七罢手，带着剩下的采珠海盗和抢来的火药上了崖，又糊里糊涂地被一大队蜃兵围在当中，两边打成一锅粥。钩七站在崖下，冲锥子喊：「停手！米的事，有别的路！」

column2: Awl's gang is beaten and the powder soaked. Hook Seven helps Awl down from the cliff and tells him the market at the mountain foot is opening; trade dried clams and stone for grain, and Lean Island can live just the same. Granny Clam agrees on the spot: half the diggers' drying yard for the Lean Islanders. Awl sits on the ground and cries like a child. The light in the seam brightens a moment, as if letting out a breath.
column3: 锥子一伙败了，火药浇了水。钩七把锥子从崖上扶下来，说山脚的互市要开了，拿干蛤和石料换粮，瘦岛一样能活。蚌婆当场答应：蛤户的晒场，分一半给瘦岛的人。锥子坐在地上哭得像个孩子。崖缝里的光亮了一下，像是松了口气。

column2: Mirage Mother Temple
column3: 蜃母庙

column2: A little white stone temple at the mountain foot with no idol inside, only an old clam shell the size of a door on the altar. This is the head temple of the Mirage Mother faith, whose believers block the road below to collect 'incense oil', saying the Mother is hungry and must be fed with travellers' goods. Today a hundred white-robed believers have massed before the temple, with a squad of mirage soldiers at the door, and the temple keeper stands on the steps chanting faster and faster.
column3: 山脚一座白石小庙，庙里没有神像，只供着一片门板那么大的旧蛤壳。蜃母教的总坛就在这里，教徒们在山下拦路收「香油」，说蜃母饿了，要拿过路人的货喂她。今天庙前聚了上百个披白麻的教徒，拉着一队蜃兵守门，庙祝站在台阶上念经，越念越急。

column2: The mirage soldiers scatter and the believers kneel in rows. The old temple keeper hands over his scriptures: the earliest page isn't scripture at all but something a clam-digger saw with his own eyes ten years ago. 'Twenty-eighth of the eighth month: a woman ship's captain knelt before the hinge and begged the Mirage Mother to remember the road for her, until those who come after arrive.' Later people worshipped by that page until it became a faith, and the faith became a money-making business. The keeper reddens. 'The Mother doesn't eat goods. What she eats is memory.'
column3: 蜃兵散了，教徒们跪了一地。老庙祝交出经卷：最早那一页不是经，是一个蛤户十年前亲眼所见，「八月廿八，女船主跪在壳枢前，求蜃母替她记路，记到后来者来」。后来的人照着这一页拜，拜成了教，又成了买卖。庙祝红着脸：「蜃母不吃货。它吃的是记性。」

column2: Shell-Mirror Workshop
column3: 磨壳镜坊

column2: A mirror workshop at the mountain foot whose owner, an old mirror-maker, grinds mirrors from old shell the great shen has shed, their faces glazed with a rainbow sheen. Last year a pirate band bought a cartload of his mirrors and used them to throw up fake cities on the salt flat to trick people, and in his anger he shut up shop and swore never to sell another. Now those pirates are back with mirage archers, blocking his door and demanding ten cartloads more.
column3: 山脚一间镜坊，坊主是个老镜匠，拿大蜃掉下的旧壳磨镜子，磨出来的镜面带一层虹光。去年一伙海盗买走他一车镜子，在盐滩上照假城骗人，他气得封了坊门，发誓不再卖一面。如今那伙海盗又来了，带着蜃弓手堵在坊外，要他再磨十车。

column2: The pirates are run off and the old mirror-maker opens his doors and, impressed, is willing to trade, picking out the brightest mirror as a gift for Axi. He angles a big mirror toward the shell lip so you can see: in the moment before dawn, two giant shells slowly part in the glass, and inside lies a pearl as big as a house, layer wrapped in layer. 'That's the only moment it opens.'
column3: 海盗被打跑，老镜匠开了坊门，佩服你们，愿意换货，还挑了一面最亮的送给阿汐。他把一面大镜子斜着对准壳唇，让你们看：天亮前那一刻，镜子里映出两扇巨壳缓缓张开，壳里卧着一颗珠子，大得像一座屋，一层裹着一层。「它只在那一刻张嘴。」

column2: Shell-Asking Cave
column3: 问壳洞

column2: A stone cave in the deepest part of the mountain foot, its floor the back of the great shen's shell, cool to the touch and smooth as a wall. For fifty years Granny Clam has come here whenever something weighed on her, to talk to it. Now the cave mouth is jammed with mirage soldiers and riders, all half transparent, crowded together and letting no one in, Granny Clam included: it no longer knows even the woman who has kept it for fifty years.
column3: 山脚最深处一个石洞，洞底就是大蜃壳的背，凉凉的，摸上去像一面墙。蚌婆五十年来每有心事就来这里，跟它说话。如今洞口挤满了蜃兵蜃骑，一个个半透明，挤成一团，谁也不让进，连蚌婆也拦：它连守了它五十年的人都认不得了。

column2: The mirage soldiers and riders scatter, and Granny Clam goes to the back of the cave and lays her cheek against the shell, as if against the back of an old husband. For ten years, she says, it has breathed out that road again and again, so often that it's forgotten its own things. 'Tomorrow at dawn it opens, and it'll fight whoever it sees. Don't hurt it; just wake it. Once it's awake it'll hand the road over, and once it's handed over, it can rest.'
column3: 蜃兵蜃骑散了，蚌婆走到洞底，把脸贴在壳上，像贴着一个老伴的背。她说十年来它把那条路一遍一遍地吐出来，吐得太多，自己的事反倒忘了。「明天一早它张嘴，见了人就打。你们别伤它，打醒它就行。醒了，它会把路交出来，交出来，它就能歇了。」

column2: The Mirage King
column3: 蜃王

column2: Day breaks. The whole plain shifts underfoot, the shell lip parts, and two white shells slowly rise, so vast you can't see their ends, and only now do you realise you've been standing on its back all along. Light pours from the shell layer upon layer and the whole Mirage comes down to earth at once: the Sea Market, Same-Day Town, the Dry Sea Army's ranks, the Qianli's five ships, a road of lamps. Then come the soldiers, mirage infantry, archers and riders drawn up in three wings; it knows no one now, only that the road must be guarded. You lay out before the shell everything from the way: the Real-or-Not Book, Old Scale's ledger, the Commander's Token, the pearls Granny Clam returned, Mo San's book.
column3: 天亮了。脚下的荒原整个一动，壳唇裂开，两扇白壳缓缓张起，大得望不到头，你们才知道自己一直站在它背上。壳里的光一层层涌出来，蜃楼一齐落到地上：海市、复日城、旱海军的阵、千里号的五条船、一条灯路。接着是兵，蜃兵、蜃弓手、蜃骑三路排开，它谁也不认得，只认得要守住那条路。你们把一路的东西摆在壳前：真假簿、老秤的账、军主令、蚌婆送回的珠子、墨三的簿子。

column2: The soldiers scatter, and from the shell comes a song, very slow and very low, the one Axi's father used to sing her to sleep, and at the last line: 'Axi.' Axi kneels before the shell and sings it through with it. The road of lamps shines one last time, every lamp there, west to east, and Mo San writes them onto the seaweed paper one by one, and for each lamp A Zhou reads out, he marks 'Real' in Lumei's Real-or-Not Book. At the road's end, the sea lies still. Shen Du closes her ledger. 'The accounts agree. The people of all three roads have gone that way. I'll see you at the Return Ruins.' She walks into the road of lamps and goes farther and farther away. The two shells slowly close, and the breathing under the ground is even at last: it doesn't have to remember any more.
column3: 兵散了，壳里传出一支歌，很慢，很低，是阿汐她爹哄她睡觉的那支，唱到最后一句：「阿汐。」阿汐跪在壳前，跟着唱完。灯路最后亮了一回，一盏不缺，从西往东，墨三一盏一盏写上海苔纸，阿舟每念一盏，就在卤妹的真假簿上记一个「真」。路的尽头，海是静的。沈渡合上账：「账对上了。三路的人都往那儿去了，归墟见。」她走进灯路，越走越远。两扇壳慢慢合上，地下的喘气终于匀了：它不用再记了。

column2: The Return Ruins
column3: 归墟

column2: Still Water Gate
column3: 静水门

column2: Houqianli slips out of the last veil of mirage and the sea goes suddenly flat: no waves, no swell, and the wake behind the stern does not spread, like a plough furrow through bean curd that never closes. The three hundred lanterns hang in the water without a tremor, so there seem to be six hundred. Ahead a white reef runs like a low wall with grassland behind it, and on the shore stands a line of the Ruins' dead soldiers. Their faces are flat and blank, like stones the sea has worn for a hundred years. Xiaojiang lies in the bow listening for a long while. 'I can't hear any waves.'
column3: 后千里穿出最后一层蜃气，海忽然平了：没有浪，没有涌，船尾划开的水痕不往两边散，像犁过一块不会合拢的豆腐。三百盏灯笼倒映在水里，一盏不晃，看上去成了六百盏。前方一道白礁像矮墙，墙后是一片草地，岸上站着一排归墟亡兵，脸上平平的，什么都没有，像被海水磨了一百年的石头。小桨趴在船头听了半天：「听不见浪。」

column2: One by one the dead soldiers walk backwards into the water without raising a single ripple. An old stele stands on the shore in ancient seal script: 'The Return Ruins. Who comes, do not stay.' Lower down, a newer line, the cuts still pale: 'The Qianli passed here.' Gong Modou runs a thumb along the strokes. Whoever carved it had a steady hand, he says, and blew the dust away when they were done.
column3: 亡兵一个接一个倒退着走进水里，没起一圈涟漪。岸上立着一块老碑，字是古篆：「归墟。来者勿留。」碑脚下另有一行新些的刻字，刀口还发白：「千里号过此。」龚墨斗摸着刀口说，刻字的人手很稳，刻完还把石屑吹干净了。

column2: Field of Oars
column3: 千桨原

column2: Oars stand upright all over the grassland, hundreds of them, like a reed bed grown crooked. There is not a breath of wind, yet the shafts creak. Three columns of Ruin-keepers camp among them: dead soldiers guard the oars, dead archers crouch behind them, dead riders circle the edge. Touch an oar and they pull it out and plant it again somewhere else.
column3: 草原上插满了船桨，几百根，直挺挺地竖着，像一片长歪了的芦苇。没有一丝风，桨杆却吱吱地响。三路守墟人在桨林里扎营：亡兵守着桨，亡弓蹲在桨后，亡骑绕着外圈走。谁伸手碰一根桨，他们就把它拔出来，换个地方重新插好。

column2: The keepers fall back. Gong Modou goes from oar to oar: every one is carved with a ship's mark, some in styles a century old. This is where ships that reached the Ruins laid down their oars. Axi finds one with a tide notch cut into the blade and the character Xu beside it. She lays her palm on the notch. 'Father put down his oar.'
column3: 守墟人退了。龚墨斗挨根看过去：桨上刻着各式各样的船号，有的是百年前的样子，这里是到了归墟的船放下桨的地方。阿汐在里头找到一根，桨叶上一道潮刻，旁边一个「许」字。她把手按在刻痕上：「爹把桨放下了。」

column2: Lead Mule Bay
column3: 头骡湾

column2: On the northern beach a herd of mules stands in the still water eating seaweed, mouths stained green. They were born and raised here and have never seen a mountain. Only one old white mule does not eat. Every day it stands facing west with a worn-out pack saddle still on its back. A squad of dead archers on the dunes uses it for target practice, arrows landing beside its hooves, but it stands as if its four legs were nailed into the sand.
column3: 北边的海滩上，一群骡子站在静水里吃海草，吃得满嘴绿。它们是在这里生、在这里长的，没见过山。只有一头老白骡不吃，天天面朝西站着，背上还搭着一副磨烂的驮鞍。一队亡弓在沙丘上拿它当靶子，箭落在它蹄子边上，它四条腿像钉进了沙里，动也不动。

column2: The archers fall back and the old mule goes on facing west. A wooden tag is nailed under the saddle: 'Lu House, Lead Mule.' Xiaojiang asks what a lead mule is. The one at the head of the caravan, Gong Modou tells him, the one the chief rides himself. Axi follows the mule's gaze west, towards where the snow mountains lie. 'It's waiting for Lu Jiu.'
column3: 亡弓退了，老白骡还是朝西站着。驮鞍底下钉着一块木牌：「陆字号头骡」。小桨问头骡是什么，龚墨斗说是马帮里打头走的那一头，镖头自己骑。阿汐顺着骡子的眼睛往西望，那边是雪山的方向：「它在等陆九。」

column2: Tea Leaf Mound
column3: 茶渣岗

column2: A low mound rises in the open, its earth black and soft underfoot, and close up it smells of old tea. A squad of dead archers holds the top and shoots at anyone who climbs it, arrows sinking into the soil up to their fletching. The castaways say the mound grew a little at a time over ten years. Nobody knows what it is made of, only that the keepers forbid digging.
column3: 野地里一座小土岗，岗上的土是黑的，踩上去发软，走近了闻到一股陈茶味。一队亡弓守在岗顶，见人上岗就放箭，箭射进土里，一直没到箭羽。漂客们说这岗是十年里一点点堆起来的，没人知道是什么堆的，只知道守墟人不许人挖。

column2: The archers withdraw and you dig down a foot: still black, nothing but boiled tea leaves pressed layer on layer. Gong Modou squeezes a handful. 'A hundred-odd men drinking for years. That's what it takes to pile it this high.' Buried in the leaves is a great iron cauldron with a broken handle, cast on its base: 'Lu Family Caravan'. The caravan lived here, and for years.
column3: 亡弓退了，你们往下挖了一尺，还是黑的：全是煮过的茶叶，一层压一层。龚墨斗捏了一把：「百来号人，喝上好几年，才堆得起这么高。」茶渣里埋着一口缺了耳的大铁锅，锅底铸着四个字：「陆家马帮」。马帮在这里住过，而且住了好几年。

column2: Satchel Tree
column3: 挂袋树

column2: A dead tree stands alone in the open, white as bone, and from its highest branch hangs a canvas letter satchel, stuffed full. A few dead riders circle the trunk, round and round. Beneath it sits a thin old man in a broad straw hat, chewing a dry flatbread, in no hurry at all. His left sandal is caked with yellow sand, his right with red mud, and his trouser cuffs are crusted with salt. He brushes off the crumbs as you come up. 'No rush. I'm used to being late. Would you mind getting my bag down?'
column3: 野地里一棵枯树，白得像骨头，最高的枝上挂着一只帆布信袋，鼓鼓囊囊。几个亡骑绕着树一圈圈地走。树下坐着个瘦老头，戴一顶大斗笠，啃着一块干饼，一点也不急。他左脚的草鞋糊满黄沙，右脚的糊满红泥，裤脚上结着一圈盐霜。见你们过来，他拍拍饼渣：「不急，我晚惯了。劳驾，帮我把袋子够下来。」

column2: The riders scatter and the satchel comes down. The old man calls himself Old Yan, a letter carrier who delivers 'letters to people who don't come back'. He counts them one by one, none missing, then glances up at Axi. 'You'll be Pilot Xu's girl. Looks at the moon before she looks at the sea, just like her father.' Axi starts, but he is already tying the bag shut with a smile. 'A letter carrier knows a face or two from every house.'
column3: 亡骑散了，信袋取了下来。老头自称晏伯，是个信客，专送「寄给回不来的人」的信。他一封封数过，一封不少，抬头看了阿汐一眼：「许领港家的闺女吧？看海先看月亮，跟你爹一个样。」阿汐一愣，他已经笑着系好了袋口：「送信的嘛，谁家的脸都认得几张。」

column2: Parrot Crag
column3: 学舌岩

column2: A rock face on the coast is home to a flock of green parrots so loud the whole beach can hear them. They talk, and not in the Quanzhou tongue but in a hill-country accent; one starts and the whole cliff takes it up. A squad of dead archers below shoots up at them arrow after arrow, and the parrots fly up, settle again, and keep shouting. The keepers dislike noise. They have been fighting this cliff for years.
column3: 海边一面石崖，崖上住着一群绿鹦鹉，吵得整片海滩都听得见。它们会说人话，说的不是泉州话，是一口山里的腔调，一只起头，满崖跟着喊。一队亡弓守在崖下，一箭一箭往崖上射，鹦鹉飞起来，落下去，接着喊。守墟人不喜欢吵，这面崖他们打了好几年了。

column2: The archers withdraw and the parrots shout louder than ever. 'Drive the mules, hey!' 'Rest your feet, ho!' 'Has the chief come?' 'Not yet, wait a bit more.' Gong Modou recognises the muleteers' songs from the tea road. These birds grew up listening to the caravan men talk. The caravan left years ago, and still they ask, over and over: has the chief come yet?
column3: 亡弓退了，鹦鹉们喊得更响了：「赶马哟——」「歇脚啰——」「镖头来了没？」「没来，再等等。」龚墨斗听出来，是茶路上的赶马调。这些鹦鹉是听着马帮的人说话长大的。马帮走了好些年，它们还在一遍遍地问：镖头来了没。

column2: Flotsam Inn
column3: 拾遗栈

column2: An inn stands in the open, walls of ship's planking, roof of old sail, and half a rudder for a signboard. It is where those who drift into the Ruins come to rest, and a gang of salvagers has taken it. Whatever the sea brings, they fish out and sell: shoes, buttons, letters, even dead men's gold teeth. To frighten people they wear white masks with no nose or eyes and pass themselves off as Ruin-keepers. The archers upstairs are masked too, and their aim is real enough.
column3: 野地上一座客栈，墙是船板，顶是旧帆，门匾是半截舵。这是漂到归墟的人歇脚的地方，如今被一伙捞客占了：海上漂来什么，他们捞什么，鞋子、扣子、信，连死人的金牙都拿去卖。为了吓人，他们戴着没鼻子没眼的白面具，冒充守墟人；楼上的弓手一样戴着面具，射得倒是真准。

column2: The salvagers are thrown out, masks littering the floor, and the castaways move back in. Old Yan spreads his letters on the counter to sort them, picks out a yellowed one and hands it to Axi. 'To Xu Chaosheng, from his mother. Sent the winter of the Dingwei year. I've carried it ten years and never caught up with him. Your legs are quicker than mine. Take it the rest of the way.' Then he puts on his hat and sets off east alone. 'It's on my way. I'll go on ahead.'
column3: 捞客被赶了出去，面具扔了一地，漂客们回了栈。晏伯在柜台上把信摊开分拣，挑出一封发黄的，递给阿汐：「许潮生收，母字。丁未年冬天寄的，我揣了十年，没追上他。你们腿快，捎一程。」说完戴上斗笠，一个人往东去了：「顺路，我先走一步。」

column2: Upstairs you seize the salvagers' hoard: thirty-odd unmatched shoes, a bucket of brass buttons, forty jin of salt fish, two jars of fresh water, and a crate of prised-out ship's nails, every one polished bright to be sold by weight.
column3: 楼上抄出捞客囤的三十几双不配对的鞋、一桶铜扣子、四十斤咸鱼、两坛淡水，还有一箱撬下来的船钉，每根都擦得锃亮，准备论斤卖。

column2: Each time you pass, the castaways bring out a pot of fish soup and pick a few pairs from the shoe pile that fit your feet, scrubbed clean. 'Shoes are meant to keep walking.'
column3: 每次路过，漂客们都端出一锅鱼汤，再从那堆鞋里替你们挑几双合脚的，刷得干干净净：「鞋嘛，就该接着走路。」

column2: Bamboo Raft Bay
column3: 竹筏湾

column2: Dozens of rotting bamboo rafts lie beached in a bay. The bamboo is the big mountain kind; nothing like it grows in the Ruins. Ruin-keepers in three columns have camped here, taking the rafts apart one by one, stacking the poles, then throwing them into the sea one at a time and moving on to the next raft. The rafts drifted in from the west many years ago, the castaways say. The people on them came ashore, and the rafts have lain here ever since.
column3: 一道海湾里搁着几十张烂竹筏，竹子是山里的毛竹，归墟根本不长。三路守墟人在湾里扎了营，一张一张地拆筏子，拆下来的竹子码成一垛，又一根根扔进海里，扔完了再去拆下一张。漂客们说，这些筏子是很多年前从西边漂来的，筏上的人上了岸，筏子就一直搁在这儿。

column2: The keepers withdraw into the water. The rattan knots on the rafts are the knots muleteers use to lash their loads; Gong Modou knows them at a glance. On a crossbeam of the largest raft a line is carved: 'Where the river ends, the sea; where the sea ends, the Ruins. The chief stayed to guard the cliff road. He did not come.' The caravan came down the river on rafts. Lu Jiu did not come with them.
column3: 守墟人退进了水里。筏子上的藤结是马帮捆驮子的结法，龚墨斗一眼就认了出来。最大的一张筏子，横木上刻着一行字：「江尽处是海，海尽处是墟。镖头守着崖上的路，没有来。」马帮是扎了筏子顺江漂下来的，陆九没有跟来。

column2: Leafless Teahouse
column3: 无叶茶寮

column2: There is a teahouse at the crossroads. Every day at noon a squad of dead soldiers files in, each takes a bowl of tea, holds it a while, then pours the whole bowl on the floor and walks out. Uncle Wapan has poured for them for years and never dared refuse. Today the soldiers do not queue; they come straight in to carry off the stove, and Uncle Wapan cowers behind the counter clutching his teapot, wailing, 'Take the stove and what do I pour tomorrow?'
column3: 路口一间茶寮，每天正午，一队亡兵排着队进来，每人领一碗茶，端着站一会儿，再整碗倒在地上，转身出去。茶寮的瓦罐叔给他们倒了好些年，不敢不倒。今天亡兵不排队了，进门就来搬茶炉，瓦罐叔抱着茶壶缩在柜台后头，直喊「炉子搬走了，明天拿什么倒」。

column2: The soldiers are scattered and Uncle Wapan pours you each a bowl, clear and fragrant. When you ask what tea it is, he lifts the lid to show you: not a single leaf inside. 'It's water from the well to the east. Comes up tasting like this. The caravan men dug it.'
column3: 亡兵被打散，瓦罐叔给你们一人倒了一碗，茶汤清亮，香得很。你们问是什么茶，他揭开壶盖给你们看：里头一片叶子都没有。「是东边那口井的水，打上来就是这个味儿。马帮的人挖的井。」

column2: Wreck Stockade
column3: 破船寨

column2: A broken seagoing ship is wedged on the reef, bow to the sky, hull split in two. The pirates who came off it have built a stockade below the reef, drawn up in three columns: blades, bows, and riders on stolen mules. They came for 'the Qianli's holds full of Pu'er', a gold bar for every tea brick, they heard, and only once inside the Ruins did they find they couldn't get out. Now they dig everywhere ashore, three feet down.
column3: 海边礁上卡着一条破海船，船头朝天，船身裂成了两半。船上下来的海盗就在礁下扎了寨，三路排开，刀手、弓手，还有骑着抢来骡子的。他们是冲着「千里号满仓的普洱」来的，听说一块茶砖换一块金，进了归墟才发觉出不去，就在岸上到处挖，挖地三尺。

column2: This gang is broken, and some kneel and beg you to take them out with you. But this reef is the threshold of the Ruins: every few months another ship full of dreams of fortune runs onto it, the ship breaks, the men come ashore, and the stockade fills up again. Clear it once, the castaways say, and you get some peace for a while. All the pirates ever dug up was one tea brick stamped Lu, long since soaked to mud.
column3: 这一伙海盗被打散了，有的跪下来求你们带他们出去。可这道礁是归墟的门槛，每隔几个月就有一条做发财梦的船撞上来，船碎了，人上了岸，寨子又会满。漂客们说，清一回，能安生一阵子。他们挖出来的只有一块茶砖，砖上印着「陆」，早泡成了泥。

column2: Stopped Clock Hermitage
column3: 停漏庵

column2: Outside a little thatched hermitage rises a heap of smashed water clocks, hourglasses, sundials and tide rods. The Still Sea Society lives here. The sea of the Ruins does not move, they say, so time has stopped, and keeping anything that measures it is a sin. Draped in grey cloth, the faithful bar the gate with staves and, spotting the watch clock on your ship, cry out to 'set you free'. Their leader is an old clockmaker from Quanzhou, and he smashes hardest of all.
column3: 一座茅草小庵，门口堆着一座小山，全是砸碎的漏壶、沙漏、日晷和潮尺。庵里住着「静海会」的人，他们说归墟的海不动，时辰也就停了，留着计时的东西是罪过。会众披着灰布，拿木杖守住庵门，看见你们船上的更漏，嚷着要「替你们解脱」。会首是个泉州来的老钟匠，砸得最狠。

column2: The faithful scatter. Axi keeps watch on the reef for half a day and scratches two marks: the water rises a foot and more, then slowly falls back. 'There's a tide. Small, but it's there.' Turning, she sees an old line in charcoal on the hermitage wall: 'The tide is only a foot. Do not panic. Xu.' The old clockmaker stares at it a long time, then crouches and picks up a flattened water clock.
column3: 会众散了。阿汐在礁上守了半天，划下两道刻痕：水涨了一尺多，又慢慢退了下去。「有潮。小，可是有。」她一回头，看见庵墙上一行炭笔旧字：「潮小一尺，人勿慌。许。」老钟匠盯着那行字看了很久，蹲下去，捡起一只摔扁的漏壶。

column2: Swept Sand Path
column3: 扫沙道

column2: A little path of white sand winds north through the open land, swept so clean there is not a single leaf on it. A camp of Ruin-keepers holds its mouth, soldiers, archers and riders, turning back anyone who comes. When the fight is over the rest retreat into the water, all but one. He picks up a broom of palm fronds, turns his back, and goes on sweeping. A copper bell is tied at his wrist, green almost to black.
column3: 野地里一条白沙小路，扫得干干净净，一片落叶都没有，弯弯曲曲往北去。路口驻着一营守墟人，亡兵、亡弓、亡骑都有，见人就往回赶。打到最后，别的守墟人都退进了水里，只剩一个不走：他捡起一把椰叶扫帚，转过身，接着扫地。他手腕上拴着一只铜铃，绿得发黑。

column2: He ignores you and sweeps, stroke by stroke. Inside his bell is engraved 'Tea, Seventeen': a caravan mule's number. By the path Axi picks up a shell with a notch cut in it, the same as the one on the oar in the field. There is one every hundred paces, all the way north. Father walked this path. You fall in behind the sweeper.
column3: 他不理你们，一下一下地扫。铜铃里头刻着「茶·十七」，是马帮的牲口号。阿汐在路边捡起一枚贝壳，壳上一道刻痕，跟千桨原那根桨上的一模一样；每隔一百步就有一枚，一路往北。爹走过这条路。你们跟在扫地人后面走。

column2: Robber Crab Grove
column3: 椰蟹林

column2: A coconut grove, the ground beneath strewn with gnawed husks. A squad of dead soldiers stands motionless among the trees, and they have stood so long that the robber crabs take them for trunks and climb their legs. The crabs are the size of dogs, with claws that crack coconuts, and they steal anything that shines. Your ship's copper pots have barely touched the sand when one is dragged away.
column3: 一片椰林，树底下躺满了啃开的椰壳。林子里驻着一队亡兵，一动不动地站着，站久了，椰子蟹把他们当成了树，一只只顺着腿往上爬。那蟹有狗那么大，钳子夹得开椰子，专偷亮东西。你们船上的铜锅刚卸下岸，一转眼就被拖走了一只。

column2: The soldiers scatter and the pot turns up in a crab hole, along with spoons, buttons, half a pipe stem, and a brass sounding lead. Its base is hollowed out, the tallow packed in it long gone hard and stuck with pink grit. It's the old pilots' trick, Axi says: grease the bottom of the lead, let it touch the seabed, pull it up and you know whether the bottom is mud, sand or reef. 'Father sounded here. The bottom is coral.'
column3: 亡兵散了，铜锅在蟹洞里找着了，洞里还堆着勺子、扣子、半截烟杆，和一只铜测深锤。锤底凿着凹坑，坑里抹的牛油早已发硬，粘着一层粉红的碎屑。阿汐说这是领港的老法子：锤底抹油，落到海底，提上来一看，就知道底是泥、是沙还是礁。「爹在这儿量过，底下是珊瑚。」

column2: Mangrove Market
column3: 红树市

column2: In a mangrove forest in the marsh a dozen wooden huts hang in the branches, linked by plank walkways: the Mangrove Market. Its master is a one-legged foreign trader with a great beard. His ship sank; he didn't, and he opened shop up in the trees. But for days a troop of dead riders has been churning the mud beneath the walkways, overturning the planks under anyone who steps on them, and the trader has been cursing from his tree for three days until his voice is gone.
column3: 沼泽里一片红树林，林子当中十几座木屋吊在树杈上，一条条栈板连着，这就是红树市。市主是个独腿的番商，大胡子，船沉了，他没沉，就在树上开了铺。可这几天一队亡骑踩着烂泥在栈板底下转来转去，谁上栈板就把板子掀翻，番商在树上骂了三天，嗓子都骂哑了。

column2: The riders withdraw. The trader lowers a basket from his tree, impressed with you, and offers goods salvaged from wrecks in trade. The caravan men bought from him once, he says: every big clay jar in his shop, down to the last. 'They filled them with tea water from the well. Said east of here it's all sea, and you can't get tea at sea.'
column3: 亡骑退了，番商从树上吊下一只篮子，佩服你们，愿意拿沉船里捞来的货跟你们换。他说马帮的人在他这儿买过东西：铺子里所有的大陶罐，一只不剩。「他们拿罐子装井里的茶水，说往东全是海，海上喝不着茶。」

column2: Horseshoe Banyan
column3: 蹄铁榕

column2: An old banyan on the coast has its trunk studded with mule shoes, ring upon ring, rusted red-brown. A band of dead archers is prising them off one by one with knives to grind into arrowheads: the Ruins yield no iron, and iron is worth more than anything. An old castaway kneels at the foot of the tree begging them to leave a few. 'Those are somebody's markers!'
column3: 海边一棵老榕树，树干上钉满了骡蹄铁，一圈压一圈，锈成了红褐色。一伙亡弓拿刀把蹄铁一只只撬下来，磨成箭头：归墟不出铁，铁比什么都金贵。树下一个漂客老汉跪着求他们留几只：「这是人家的记号！」

column2: The archers are driven off and the shoes go back up one by one. Caravan custom, the old man says: when a mule dies on the road, you nail its shoes to a tree by the way. But most of these shoes were never worn; they are new. The day the caravan went east, they left all their mules behind, took off their shoes and nailed them here together. 'No use for mules at sea. Leave the mules for whoever comes after.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走，蹄铁一只只钉了回去。老汉说马帮的规矩，骡子死在路上，就把它的蹄铁钉在路边的树上。可这棵树上的蹄铁大半没磨过，是新掌。马帮往东走那天，把骡子全留下了，掌一齐卸下来钉在树上：「海上用不着骡子，骡子留给后来的人。」

column2: Mule Racecourse
column3: 赛骡场

column2: A racetrack laid out with pebbles in the open: the castaways' children race mules here every autumn, and the winner drinks a bowl of tea from the well. Halfway through this year's race a troop of dead riders burst onto the track and galloped along with the mules, faster than any of them. The children tumbled off in fright. The mules were not frightened at all, and set off after them.
column3: 野地里一圈跑道，是漂客家的孩子拿石子摆出来的，每年秋天在这儿赛骡子，赢了的喝一碗井里的茶。今年比到一半，一队亡骑闯进了跑道，跟着骡子一起跑，跑得比谁都快，孩子们吓得从骡背上滚了下来，骡子倒是不怕，撒开蹄子追了上去。

column2: The riders are chased off the track and the children climb back on. The race was started by the caravan, the eldest says: the year the caravan wanted to go east, the keepers wouldn't let them, so the caravan's leader raced the keepers' cavalry with the road as the stake, and the mules beat the horses. 'That's why the keepers come every year,' the boy says. 'They want to win it back.'
column3: 亡骑被赶出了跑道，孩子们又爬上骡背。领头的大孩子说，这场赛是马帮兴起来的：那年马帮要往东去，守墟人不放，马帮的头领就跟守墟人的骑兵赛了一场，拿路作注，骡子赢了马。「所以守墟人每年都来，」孩子说，「他们想赢回去。」

column2: Wet Hoof Strand
column3: 湿蹄滩

column2: At dusk hoofbeats sound along the beach. A troop of dead riders comes galloping on grey horses at the water's edge, each hoofprint filling with water the moment it is made, a glittering trail behind them. A fishing family has turned their boat upside down for a house, and all five of them huddle beneath it, peering through the cracks. The riders come every evening, they say, run the length of the beach, then ride into the sea. They have never missed a day.
column3: 黄昏，海滩上响起了马蹄声。一队亡骑骑着灰马沿着水边跑过来，马蹄印一踩下去就灌满了水，一路亮晶晶的。滩上一户渔家把船倒扣过来当屋子，一家五口缩在船底下，从板缝里往外看。他们说这队骑兵每天黄昏都来跑一趟，跑完就进海，一天也不落。

column2: The riders are beaten, and their hoofprints lead into the sea and stop before a gap between two white reefs. The South Reef Gate, the old fisherman calls it: ships from outside can only come in through there, and only on a spring tide. Ten years ago in autumn a string of big ships came through, one after another, and a man stood in the bow calling the depths in the Quanzhou tongue. 'That was my father,' Axi says.
column3: 亡骑败了，蹄印一路通进海里，停在两道白礁之间的一个豁口前。渔老汉说那是南礁门，外头的船只能从这儿进来，还得赶大潮。十年前的秋天，一溜大船就是从这里一条接一条进来的，船头站着一个人，拿泉州话一声一声地报水深。阿汐说：「是我爹。」

column2: Whalebone Village
column3: 鲸骨村

column2: A village stands in the open, every house framed with whale ribs bent into arches and roofed with grass mats. A few dozen castaway families live here, but for days now a large camp of Ruin-keepers has moved in: soldiers sleep in the bone houses, archers sit on the bone beams, riders tether their horses to a whale's jaw. They do nothing at all, they just live there, and the villagers sleep out on the grass with their children in their arms.
column3: 野地里一座村子，屋架全是鲸鱼的肋骨，一根根弯成拱，上面盖着草席。村里住着几十户漂客，可这几天一大营守墟人住了进来：亡兵睡在骨屋里，亡弓坐在骨梁上，亡骑把马拴在鲸鱼的下巴骨上。他们什么也不干，就是住着，村里人只好抱着孩子睡在外头的草地上。

column2: The keepers leave and the villagers move back into their bone houses. A crowd of children gathers to stare at you. Axi asks idly when the tide comes in today, and a barefoot girl rattles off: 'Moon overhead, water on the shore; moon in the west, water goes home; new moon and full, the tide is at its fullest.' Axi stops short. It is the song her father taught her, word for word. A dark-faced Teacher Xu taught them, the girl says. 'He said once you know it, you won't be afraid of the sea.'
column3: 守墟人走了，村里人搬回了骨屋。一群孩子围着你们看，阿汐随口问了一句今天几时涨潮，一个光脚丫头张嘴就背：「月上头，水上岸；月落西，水回家；初一十五潮最大。」阿汐愣住了：这是她爹教她的歌，一字不差。丫头说是黑脸的许先生教的：「学会了，就不怕海。」

column2: Waiting Stone
column3: 等茶石

column2: The swept path rounds a stand of scrub to a flat-topped stone by the wayside with a coarse bowl on it. Here the sweeper stops, unties a bamboo flask from his belt, fills the bowl with tea, stands a moment, then pours it out at the foot of the stone. A troop of dead riders charges out of the scrub to overturn the stone. The sweeper neither dodges nor blocks them; he only shields the bowl with his hand.
column3: 白沙路拐过一片矮林，路边一块平顶石，石上摆着一只粗碗。扫地的守墟人扫到这里停下，从腰间解下一只竹筒，往碗里倒满茶，站一会儿，再把茶泼在石头脚下。一队亡骑从林子里冲出来要掀了这块石头，扫地人不躲也不拦，只伸手护着那只碗。

column2: The riders are scattered. A crooked line is carved into the stone: 'Old Seventeen waits here to drink tea with Pilot Xu. Every day at the hour of the rooster.' Old Seventeen, the castaways say, drove the seventeenth mule in the caravan, a man with a big voice and the tide-watching pilot's best friend. The sweeper picks up his bowl and sweeps on. The path heads for the point.
column3: 亡骑被打散。石头上刻着一行歪歪扭扭的字：「老十七在此等许领港喝茶，每日酉时。」漂客们说老十七是马帮里赶第十七头骡子的，嗓门大，跟那个看潮的领港最要好。扫地人收起碗，接着往前扫，路朝岬角那边去了。

column2: Rope Twister's Rise
column3: 搓绳岗

column2: On a low rise sits a mountain of hemp rope, coil upon coil. The man twisting it is a white-bearded old fellow called the Sea Measurer. The Ruins have no bottom, he says, and he has spent ten years making rope to lower down and find out. A squad of dead archers has taken the rise and is shooting fire arrows into the pile. Every time a stretch catches, the old man throws himself on it to smother it, and half his beard is singed.
column3: 野地里一座小岗，岗上绕着一座小山似的麻绳，一圈压一圈。搓绳的是个白胡子老头，人称量海翁，他说归墟没有底，搓了十年绳，要放下去量一量。一队亡弓占了岗子，拿火箭射那堆绳，烧一截，老头就扑上去拿身子压灭一截，胡子都燎焦了半边。

column2: The archers fall back. The old man says he has let down more than two thousand zhang of line and never touched bottom. Axi opens the tide book: on one page her father wrote, 'A hundred li south, a trench in the seabed, deeper than mountains are high. Not bottomless.' A trench is a deep gash in the sea floor; at its deepest, you could drop the tallest mountain in the world into it and its peak would not break the surface. The Sea Measurer wipes his face. 'Then I'll twist another thousand.'
column3: 亡弓退了。老头说他放下去两千多丈，还没碰着底。阿汐翻开潮信簿，爹在一页上写着：「此去南百里，海底有沟，深过高山，非无底也。」海沟是海底裂开的一道深槽，最深处，把天下最高的山整座放进去，山顶也露不出水面。量海翁听完，抹了把脸：「那我再搓一千丈。」

column2: Leech Pond
column3: 蚂蟥塘

column2: A pond of dead water in the marsh, black and glossy, leeches stretching and bunching as they swim. A squad of dead soldiers stands in it waist-deep, motionless, leeches crawling all over their legs and never dropping off: there is no blood in them, so the leeches crawl for nothing. They guard a little mound in the middle with a bamboo pole stuck in it and a cloth bag hanging from the top.
column3: 沼泽里一片死水塘，水黑得发亮，蚂蟥一伸一缩地游。一队亡兵站在塘里，水没到腰，一动不动，蚂蟥爬满了他们的腿也不掉：他们身上没有血，蚂蟥白爬。他们守着塘中间一座小土墩，墩上插着一根竹竿，竿头挂着一只布袋。

column2: The soldiers are driven out of the pond, and you bind your trouser legs, rub salt on your shins and wade across. In the bag is a twist of tobacco and a note in caravan script: 'Crossing Leech Pond: salt on your legs, and a dab of tobacco juice makes them drop off. Left for the chief. He's scared of these.' Lu Jiu, the terror of the tea road, is afraid of leeches.
column3: 亡兵被赶出了塘，你们扎紧裤腿，腿上抹了盐蹚过去。布袋里是一包烟丝和一张字条，马帮的字：「过蚂蟥塘，腿上抹盐，烟油一点它就掉。给镖头留的，他怕这东西。」名震茶路的陆九，原来怕蚂蟥。

column2: Calling Reef
column3: 喊爹礁

column2: Every evening an eight- or nine-year-old boy stands at the end of a long reef on the coast and shouts 'Father!' eastwards, a hundred times, before he goes home. A troop of dead riders finds him too noisy and comes every day to chase him off the reef, his mother running after them, dragging her son with one hand and whacking the horses' legs with a broom in the other. The boy looks back as he runs. 'Thirty-seven more to go!'
column3: 海边一道长礁，每天傍晚，一个八九岁的男孩站在礁头，朝东喊「爹——」，喊满一百声才回家。一队亡骑嫌他吵，天天来把他从礁上赶下去，他娘追在后面，一手拉孩子，一手拿扫帚打马腿。男孩边跑边回头喊：「还差三十七声！」

column2: The riders are driven off and the boy finishes his last thirty-seven shouts. His father was a caravan man, his mother says, who made a home in the Ruins in those years. When he went east he said, 'When the chief gets here, I'll come back.' The boy has never seen a mountain, but everything he draws in the sand is mountains, each taller than the last. 'His father told him there's snow on mountains,' she says. 'He won't believe snow can be white.'
column3: 亡骑被打跑，男孩把剩下的三十七声喊完了。他娘说孩子他爹是马帮的人，那几年在归墟成了家，往东走的时候说：「等镖头到了，我就回来。」孩子长这么大没见过山，可沙滩上画的全是山，一座比一座高。「他爹说，山上有雪，」她说，「孩子不信，雪怎么会是白的。」

column2: Tea Well Market
column3: 茶井集

column2: A well in the middle of the open land, its curb a single slab of bluestone, ringed by stalls: the only market in the Ruins. Fish traders, coconut sellers, cobblers, all live off this well's water. But now a squad of dead archers stands on the curb, bows drawn, and shoots the bucket of anyone who lowers one. The keepers never used to care about the well, the castaways say. Only since Houqianli's lanterns lit up out at sea have they ringed it.
column3: 野地当中一口井，井台是整块的青石，井边围着一圈摊子，是归墟的漂客们唯一的集市：换鱼的、卖椰子的、修鞋的，都靠这口井的水过日子。可如今井台上站着一队亡弓，弓都拉满了，谁放下桶就射谁的桶。漂客们说，守墟人以前从不管这口井，自从海上亮起了后千里的灯，他们就把井围了起来。

column2: The archers withdraw and the first bucket comes up clear enough to see your face in. One mouthful tastes of tea, with a sweet finish. The castaways set their stalls up again, and grain-for-gold trade opens. On the curb the caravan carved: 'Three months digging. Each man dropped in a piece of tea. While the tea lasts, the road lasts. The chief has not come. One mouthful of tea is left for him.' A lidded bowl is weighted on the rim. Lift the lid: the tea in it has not dried in ten years, and it is still warm.
column3: 亡弓退了，第一桶水打上来，清得照得见人，喝一口，满嘴茶香，还回甘。漂客们把摊子重新支起来，粮食换金子的买卖开了张。井台上刻着马帮的字：「挖井三月，人人投茶一块。茶在，路在。镖头未至，留茶一口，候之。」井沿上压着一只扣着盖的碗，揭开一看，碗里的茶十年没干，还是温的。

column2: Lime Kiln Beach
column3: 烧灰滩

column2: A clay kiln smokes white on the beach. An old woman prises dead coral off the reef and carries it back to burn for lime, good for caulking seams and whitewashing walls. A squad of dead soldiers stands on the reef and will not let her, and whenever they see coral in her basket they tip the lot back into the sea. Furious, she bangs their greaves with her iron shovel until they ring. 'It's dead! I only take the dead stuff!'
column3: 海滩上一座土窑冒着白烟，一个老阿婆从礁上撬下死珊瑚，背回来烧石灰，抹船缝、刷墙都用得上。一队亡兵站在礁上，不许她撬，见她背篓里有珊瑚，就把整篓倒回海里。老阿婆气得拿铁铲敲他们的胫甲，敲得当当响：「死的！我撬的是死的！」

column2: The soldiers retreat. The old woman says she dived as a girl: in the shallows the coral is alive and every colour; deeper down it is all dead coral, layer on layer, and at the very bottom black rock. 'The mountain underneath is sinking, and the coral grows up and up, generation after generation. The mountain goes under, and only the ring of reef is left.' Axi opens the tide book. On one page her father drew a circle: 'The Ruins are a ring. In the middle, an old mountain.'
column3: 亡兵退了。老阿婆说她年轻时潜过水：浅水里的珊瑚是活的，五颜六色；越往深处越是死珊瑚，一层压一层，压到最底下是黑石头。「是底下的山在沉，珊瑚一辈一辈往上长，山沉没了，就剩这一圈礁。」阿汐翻开潮信簿，爹在一页上画了个圈：「归墟如环，中是旧山。」

column2: Bottle Bay
column3: 漂瓶湾

column2: A bay is heaped with bottles washed in from the sea, clay, porcelain, bamboo, every mouth stoppered. The currents swirl here, the castaways say, and whatever floats in from every quarter turns into the bay and never gets out. A band of dead archers guards the pile and shoots the hand of anyone who picks one up. A castaway who can read lives at the bay's edge and secretly reads the messages aloud for people, one arrow per letter.
column3: 一道海湾里堆满了漂来的瓶子，陶的、瓷的、竹筒的，瓶口都塞着东西。漂客说海上的流在这里打旋，四面八方漂来的东西都转进湾里，出不去。一伙亡弓守着瓶堆，谁捡一只就射谁的手。湾边住着个识字的漂客，偷偷替人念瓶里的字，念一封，挨一箭。

column2: The archers withdraw. In the pile Axi turns up a little wine bottle with a fat fish painted on it: she threw it into Quanzhou harbour when she was six. Inside is a slip of paper: 'Father, come home soon.' On the back is one more line, the ink faded: 'Got it. Father.' She sits holding the bottle for a long time. 'Of everything in this bay,' says the castaway who reads, 'that's the only one that ever got an answer.'
column3: 亡弓退了。阿汐在瓶堆里翻出一只小酒瓶，瓶身上画着一条胖鱼，是她六岁那年扔进泉州港的，里头一张纸：「爹快回来。」纸背面多了一行，墨色淡了：「收到了。爹。」她捧着瓶子坐了很久。识字的漂客说：「这湾里，只有这一封是回了信的。」

column2: Tide Bell Pavilion
column3: 潮钟亭

column2: A small pavilion stands in the open with a bronze bell hanging inside it, and beneath the bell a stone shaft with a hidden channel running to the sea. The bell used to ring by itself twice a day, the castaways say, and then it went dumb. For days a troop of dead riders has circled the pavilion, jabbing the bell with their spear butts until it swings, but it never rings. It won't ring, and still they won't leave.
column3: 野地里一座小亭，亭里吊着一口铜钟，钟下一口石井，井底有暗沟通着海。漂客们说这钟从前会自己响，一天两回，后来就哑了。这几天一队亡骑围着小亭打转，拿枪杆一下下捅那口钟，捅得钟身直晃，就是不响，捅不响，他们也不走。

column2: The riders scatter. Axi peers down the shaft: a wooden float inside is linked to the clapper, so when the tide rises the float lifts and the bell rings. The channel mouth is choked with weed, and she climbs down and digs for an hour. At dusk the tide comes in and the bell sounds once, clang, and every castaway across the fields looks up. Around its rim runs a line: 'For those who cannot read the moon. Xu.'
column3: 亡骑散了。阿汐趴在井口看了看：井里一只木浮子连着钟锤，潮一涨，浮子上来，钟就响。暗沟口被海草塞死了，她下去掏了半个时辰。傍晚潮来，钟「当」地响了一声，满野的漂客都抬起了头。钟沿上刻着一行字：「留给不会看月亮的人。许。」

column2: Tide Pole Point
column3: 潮杆岬

column2: The swept path ends at a stone point running out into the still water, with a tide pole at its tip and two flat stones beneath it like a pair of stools. A camp of picked Ruin-keepers holds the point, drawn up in three columns around the pole. At the neck of the point the sweeper stops his broom and, for the first time, turns to look at you. The bell at his wrist gives a soft ring.
column3: 白沙路扫到了尽头：一道石岬伸进静水，岬尖立着一根潮杆，杆下两块平石，像两张凳子。岬上驻着一营守墟的精兵，三路排开，把潮杆围在当中。扫地的守墟人走到岬口，扫帚停了，第一次回头看你们，手腕上的铜铃轻轻响了一下。

column2: The picked guards withdraw into the water. The pole is carved all over with tide times, and the last line reads: 'Eighth month, eighteenth day, spring tide. Deep water at the reef gate. A ship can leave.' Buried at its foot is a bamboo box holding two coarse tea bowls. Those years, say the fisherfolk below the point, a pilot and a caravan man sat on these stones every evening drinking tea and watching the tide. The day they left eastward, the caravan man tied his bell to the wrist of a keeper who stood on the point watching them every day. 'Keep the path swept for us. It'll be easier for whoever comes after.' The sweeper unties the bell and puts it in Axi's hand, leans his broom against the pole, and walks step by step into the water without a ripple. Axi closes her hand on the bell. 'They could have left. They knew they could, and they went east anyway.'
column3: 精兵退进了水里。潮杆上刻满了潮时，最后一行是：「八月十八大潮，礁门水深，可出。」杆底下埋着一只竹匣，匣里两只粗茶碗。岬下的渔家说，那几年每天傍晚，一个领港、一个马帮汉子坐在这两块石头上喝茶看潮；往东走那天，马帮汉子把铃拴在一个天天站在岬上看他们的守墟人手上：「替我们扫着路，后来的人好走。」扫地人把铃解下来，放进阿汐手里，扫帚靠在潮杆上，一步一步走进了水里，水面一圈涟漪都没有。阿汐握着铃：「能出去的。他们知道能出去，还是往东走了。」

column2: Night Stage
column3: 夜戏台

column2: A stage stands in the middle of the open land, and below it sits a great camp of Ruin-keepers: soldiers in the front rows, archers behind, riders on horseback at the very back. On stage is a troupe of a dozen castaway players who must perform every night until dawn. The troupe master's voice went long ago and he is still forcing it out; the young lead weeps as she sings. Below the stage there is not a single face, and not a single cheer.
column3: 野地中间搭着一座戏台，台下黑压压坐着一大营守墟人：亡兵坐前排，亡弓坐后排，亡骑骑着马站在最后头。台上是一个漂来的戏班，十几个人，每晚都得唱，唱到天亮才许歇。班主嗓子早哑了，还在硬撑，小旦一边唱一边掉眼泪，台下没有一张脸，也没有一声好。

column2: The keepers disperse and the troupe collapses on the boards. There is only one piece they will listen to, the master says, called Seeing Off the Tide, first sung on this stage by the Qianli's people ten years ago: a company walks east in a line, the pilot last of all, looking back three times and singing, 'The tide will bring them here.' 'The keepers listen to it again and again,' says the master, 'as if they're trying to learn it by heart.'
column3: 守墟人散了，戏班子瘫在台上。班主说他们只肯听一出，叫《送潮》，是十年前千里号的人在这台上唱的：一伙人排成一行往东走，领港走在最后，回了三次头，唱一句「潮会带他们来」。「守墟人一回回地听，」班主说，「像是想把这出戏记住。」

column2: Tea Tax Post
column3: 茶味税卡

column2: A wooden barrier crosses the road to the well with a sign: 'Tea Flavour Tax, one copper a bowl.' The collector is a castaway in a ragged official robe who calls himself the Court-Appointed Tea Commissioner of the Ruins, with a great seal in his hand; whoever he stamps must pay. He has a troop of dead riders guarding the post. They can't understand a word, but every time he speaks they stand there a moment, and it looks impressive enough.
column3: 去茶井的路上横着一道木卡，卡上挂着牌子：「茶味税，每碗一文」。收税的是个穿破官袍的漂客，自称朝廷委任的「归墟茶课大使」，手里一方大印，盖谁谁就得交钱。他雇了一队亡骑守卡，那些亡骑听不懂，他说一句，它们就站一会儿，倒也唬人。

column2: The riders scatter and the 'Tea Commissioner' hands over his seal. Gong Modou turns it over: no official seal at all, but a brick mould the caravan used for pressing tea, carved 'Pu'er. Tribute of the Qianli. Dingwei.' The bricks were tribute tea. But there is no court out here. Tribute to whom? The commissioner scratches his head. 'When I found it, I just fancied being an official.'
column3: 亡骑散了，「茶课大使」交出了大印。龚墨斗翻过来一看，哪是官印，是一块砖模：马帮压茶砖用的，刻着「普洱·千里号贡·丁未」。茶砖是贡茶，可这一路上没有朝廷，贡给谁？大使挠挠头：「我捡到的时候，就想当个官。」

column2: Hearth House
column3: 火塘屋

column2: A longhouse stands in the open where the caravan once lived. In the middle burns a hearth that has never gone out; a castaway widow feeds it coconut husks every day. A troop of dead riders circles the house, for the keepers cannot abide fire; with every lap they fling a handful of sand through the door. The widow shields the hearth with her body, sand all over her head and face, and keeps on feeding it.
column3: 野地里一座长屋，是马帮当年住的，屋当中一口火塘，火一直没灭，一个漂客寡妇天天往里添椰壳。一队亡骑围着长屋转，守墟人见不得火，转一圈，往门里扔一把沙。寡妇拿身子挡在火塘前，沙落了她一头一脸，她还在添。

column2: The riders are driven off and the widow shakes the sand from her hair. Carved on the great beam above the hearth is the caravan's roster, a tick beside each name, and a tick means 'gone east'. Only two lines have no tick. One reads 'Chief Lu Jiu'. The other has no name at all, only 'the runner', and beside it, as if someone added it in passing: 'Late again.'
column3: 亡骑被赶走，寡妇抖了抖头上的沙。火塘上方的大梁上刻着马帮的花名册，一个名字一道勾，勾的意思是「往东了」。只有两行没勾：一行是「镖头陆九」；一行没有名字，只写着「跑信的」，旁边一行小字，像是谁随手添的：「又晚了。」

column2: Tea Pack Warehouse
column3: 驮茶栈

column2: A long earthen warehouse beside the main road where the caravan once stored its tea, a row of pack frames still hanging on its walls. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it on hearing there is 'the Qianli's Pu'er' inside, digging several holes through the walls and piling the bricks they found at the door to swap with the castaways for wine. Their archers stand on the pack frames and shoot anyone who comes close.
column3: 大路边一座长长的土栈，是马帮当年存茶的地方，墙上还挂着一排驮架。一伙落难海盗占了土栈，听说里头有「千里号的普洱」，把墙挖了好几个洞，挖出来的茶砖一块块堆在门口，拿来跟漂客换酒。守门的弓手站在驮架上，谁靠近就放箭。

column2: The pirates are driven off and the bricks are stacked back inside. When the caravan left, says the old castaway who minds the warehouse, they left word: 'This tea is a consignment, not goods for sale. Wait for the chief to come and check it.' Ten years of waiting, and the bricks have aged into old tea, each more fragrant than the last. He pats the pile. 'If the chief doesn't come soon, this lot will be worth a fortune.'
column3: 海盗被赶走，茶砖码回了栈里。看栈的漂客老汉说，马帮走时留下话：「茶是镖，不是货，等镖头来了点验。」可等了十年，茶砖也陈成了老茶，一块比一块香。他拍拍茶堆：「镖头再不来，这茶就成了宝了。」

column2: At the door you seize what the pirates hadn't traded: forty tea bricks, six jars of wine, an iron pot, two pack frames, and a 'treasure map' they'd drawn, every X on it marked on the tea well.
column3: 门口抄出海盗换剩的四十块茶砖、六坛酒、一口铁锅、两副驮架，还有一张他们画的「藏宝图」，上面每一个叉都画在茶井上。

column2: Each time you pass, the old warehouseman draws you a jar of water from the tea well and breaks a corner off an old brick to tuck in its mouth. 'Old tea in well water. Drink it and your legs will carry you. I'm keeping the chief's share.'
column3: 每次路过，看栈的老汉都从茶井打一罐水给你们，再掰一角老茶砖塞进罐口：「井水泡老茶，喝了走得动路。镖头的那份我留着。」

column2: Gourd Ferry
column3: 葫芦渡

column2: A ferry landing on the coast, the South Islet just across the water. The ferry is a raft of hundreds of dried gourds lashed together, riding high and paddling slow. The ferryman is a mute old man who has worked this one crossing for ten years. A squad of dead soldiers squats at the landing, puncturing the gourds one by one with their spear points, and with each one the raft sinks a little lower while the old man crouches beside it patching them.
column3: 海边一处渡口，对面就是南屿。渡船是几百只干葫芦捆成的筏子，浮得高，划得慢。撑筏的是个哑巴老汉，十年来只摆这一条水。一队亡兵蹲在渡口，拿枪尖把葫芦一只只戳破，戳破一只，筏子就往下沉一点，老汉蹲在旁边一只只地补。

column2: The soldiers withdraw. The old man patches the last gourd and sketches in the sand for you: a dark-faced man crossed to the South Islet alone one night, a book held against his chest; at dawn he came back empty-handed. The old man holds up three fingers: that was three days before they all went east. He pats the raft and beckons you aboard.
column3: 亡兵退了，老汉补好最后一只葫芦，在沙上比画给你们看：一个黑脸汉子，夜里独自过渡去了南屿，怀里揣着一本簿子；天亮回来，手里空了。老汉竖起三根手指：那是他们往东走的前三天。他拍拍筏子，示意你们上来。

column2: Trench Pool
column3: 深沟潭

column2: A great pool in the reef on the coast, its mouth open to the outer sea, its bottom too black to see. At every spring tide the big fish from the trench come up with the cold water, each longer than a boat, mouths that could swallow a fish basket whole, and they smash the castaways' fish weirs round the pool one after another. A camp of Ruin-keepers holds the pool's edge in three columns, shoving into the water anyone who comes to mend a weir, as if feeding the fish.
column3: 海边礁上一个大潭，潭口通着外海，潭底黑得看不见。每逢大潮，海沟里的大鱼就顺着冷水涌上来，一条比船还长，嘴能吞下一只渔筐，把漂客们下在潭边的鱼簖一道道撞烂。一营守墟人守在潭边，三路排开，谁去修簖就把谁往水里推，像是给大鱼喂食。

column2: The keepers withdraw, you drive the great fish back to the depths with long tridents and torches, and the weirs go up again. But the pool's bottom opens onto the trench and has no end to it: at the next spring tide more great fish will rise with the cold water, and the keepers will return to the edge. Clear it once, the castaways say, and you get a month of fishing in peace. By the pool Axi finds one of her father's marks: 'Keep clear of this pool at spring tides.'
column3: 守墟人退了，大鱼被你们拿长叉和火把赶回了潭底，鱼簖修了起来。可潭底连着海沟，深不见底，下一回大潮，又会有大鱼顺着冷水上来，守墟人也会回到潭边。漂客们说，清一回，能吃上一个月的安生鱼。阿汐在潭边找到爹的一道刻痕：「大潮勿近此潭。」

column2: Pole-Passing Reef
column3: 接篙礁

column2: A dry reef at the edge of the open land, a little pilot boat tied up on it with a bamboo pole planted in its bow, the pole notched all over with measurements. A castaway lad of seventeen or eighteen sits in the boat surrounded by a troop of dead riders who won't let him push it into the water. He sticks out his neck and shouts, 'I'm a pilot! Ships coming through the reef gate need me to bring them in!' The riders don't understand; they just keep pulling out his pole and throwing it away.
column3: 野地边一道干礁，礁上拴着一条小领港船，船头插着一根竹篙，篙上刻满了尺寸。一个十七八岁的漂客后生坐在船里，被一队亡骑团团围着，不许他把船推下水。他梗着脖子喊：「我是领港！礁门进船要我领！」亡骑不懂，只管把他的篙一次次拔出来扔掉。

column2: The riders scatter and the lad plants his pole back in the bow. His name is A Jiao. Xu Chaosheng trained him, and in those years he followed him every day to sound the reef gate. The day they went east, Xu gave him this pole. 'More ships will come. You bring them in. If my daughter comes, you needn't guide her; she reads the tide better than I do.' A Jiao looks at Axi and holds out the pole. Axi doesn't take it. 'You keep guiding. Father said I wouldn't need to.'
column3: 亡骑散了，后生把篙插回船头。他叫阿礁，是许潮生教出来的，那几年天天跟着他量礁门。往东走那天，许潮生把这根篙交给他：「后头还会有船来，你领它们进来。我女儿要是来了，你不用领，她看潮比我准。」阿礁把篙递给阿汐，她没接：「你领吧，爹说我不用。」

column2: Swimming Lesson Bay
column3: 学水湾

column2: A shallow bay on the coast, its water clear to the bottom, where the castaways' children come every day to learn to swim. Today a squad of dead archers crouches on the reef at the bay's edge shooting arrows beside anyone who enters the water, and the children run for the shore bare-bottomed in fright. The old sailor who teaches them swears in fury. 'They can't swim themselves, so they won't let anyone else!'
column3: 海边一道浅湾，水清得见底，漂客家的孩子们天天在这儿学泅水。今天一队亡弓蹲在湾边的礁上，谁下水就往谁身边射箭，孩子们吓得光着屁股往岸上跑。教泅水的老水手气得直骂：「它们自己不会水，也不许别人会！」

column2: The archers are driven off and the children plunge back in. In those years, the old sailor says, the caravan men learned to swim in this bay too; mountain men sink the moment they're in the water, and the sailors spent a year teaching them. A wooden board on the shore keeps the record: 'Old Seventeen, sank.' 'Old Seventeen, sank again.' 'Old Seventeen, floated!' The last line: 'The chief can't swim either. We'll teach him when he comes.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走，孩子们又扑进了水里。老水手说，那几年马帮的汉子也在这湾里学水，山里人一下水就沉，船上的人教了一年。岸边木牌上记着：「老十七，沉。」「老十七，又沉。」「老十七，浮起来了！」最后一行：「镖头也不会水。等他来，再教。」

column2: Abacus Slope
column3: 拨珠坡

column2: On a gentle slope castaways queue to barter, and at the head of the line sits a girl of ten or so with an abacus wider than she is. Whoever trades what, however much, she clacks it out on the beads and writes it into a tattered ledger. A troop of dead riders hates the clatter and keeps coming to snatch the abacus, and she runs all over the slope hugging it, the ledger clamped in her teeth.
column3: 野地里一道缓坡，漂客们排着队换东西，队头坐着个十来岁的丫头，怀里抱着一架比她还宽的大算盘，谁换了什么、换了多少，她噼里啪啦一拨，就记进一本破账里。一队亡骑嫌算珠吵，三番五次来抢她的算盘，她抱着算盘满坡跑，账本咬在嘴里。

column2: The riders flee and the girl spits out her ledger. Her name is Zhuzhu and she was born in the Ruins. Carved on the abacus frame is 'Qianli. Silk Road. Bookkeeper's spare', left to her by the 'camel folk', which is what she calls the Silk Road people. 'They were fierce at sums.' She turns to the last pages of the ledger: she is recording the Qianli's people, a circle for each one, and she still has a long way to go.
column3: 亡骑跑了，丫头吐出账本，自报名叫珠珠，是在归墟生的。算盘框上刻着「千里号·丝路·账房备用」，是「驼客」留给她的。驼客是她对丝路那帮人的叫法：「他们算账可凶了。」她翻开账本最后几页：她在记千里号的人，记一个，画一个圈，还差得远。

column2: Old Ding's Stove
column3: 老鼎灶

column2: Beside the main road stands a great stone stove with a fire mouth a man could crawl into and a cauldron on top big enough to bathe in. It has been cold for years, yet a squad of dead archers sits around it every day, bows across their knees, as if waiting for dinner. The castaways would love to boil fish in it, but anyone who comes near gets shot, so they just gaze at the pot from a distance and swallow.
column3: 大路边一座石砌的大灶，灶口能钻进一个人，灶上坐着一口大锅，锅里能洗澡。灶冷了好些年，一队亡弓却天天围着它坐，弓搁在膝上，像在等开饭。漂客们想借锅煮鱼，一靠近就挨箭，只好远远看着那口锅咽口水。

column2: The archers scatter, the castaways light a fire, and the smell of fish soup carries half a li. Zhuzhu draws a circle in her ledger: 'Old Ding. Head cook. Fat.' His rule is carved on the stove: 'Cook for three hundred. The extra bowl is for whoever comes late.' In those years, the castaways say, there was a bowl left over in this pot every day. Next morning it was poured away, and another bowl was left.
column3: 亡弓散了，漂客们生了火，鱼汤的香味飘出半里。珠珠在账上画了一个圈：「老鼎，大厨，胖。」灶台上刻着他的规矩：「锅按三百人煮，多出来的一碗，给晚到的。」漂客们说，那几年这口锅里天天剩一碗，到第二天倒了，再剩一碗。

column2: South Islet Landing
column3: 南屿埠

column2: The gourd raft touches the South Islet, where a flight of stone steps climbs to the summit with a notched shell set every hundred paces, the same as on the Swept Sand Path. A squad of dead archers crouches at the foot of the steps, arrows already nocked. The mute ferryman gestures that he won't land, but Axi has already jumped into the waist-deep water.
column3: 葫芦筏靠上南屿，岸上一道石阶通上屿顶，阶边每隔一百步摆一枚刻了痕的贝壳，跟扫沙道上的一模一样。阶口蹲着一队亡弓，弓已经搭好了箭。哑巴渡夫比画着不肯靠岸，阿汐却已经跳进了齐腰的水里。

column2: The archers withdraw and Axi follows the shells up without stopping once. The last one lies on a flat stone at the top of the islet with a little dried sea salt in it, as if someone had set down a handful of seawater here to dry. Gong Modou, panting behind her, says, 'Your father did things more carefully than a bookkeeper.'
column3: 亡弓退了，阿汐顺着贝壳往上走，一步也不停。最后一枚贝壳摆在屿顶的一块平石上，里头盛着一点干了的海盐，像是谁把一捧海水放在这里晒干了。龚墨斗在后头喘着气说：「你爹做事，比账房还讲究。」

column2: Midwife's Shelter
column3: 接生棚

column2: A large grass shelter stands in the open, dried herbs hanging along its eaves and a stone mortar at the door still crusted with medicine. Ruin-keepers in three columns surround it: soldiers block the door, archers on the roof, riders circling outside. Inside lies a castaway woman about to give birth, and the midwife, kept outside, slaps her thighs in despair. 'Any longer and it's two lives!'
column3: 野地里一座大草棚，棚檐下挂着一排晒干的草药，门口的石臼还沾着药渣。三路守墟人把棚子团团围住，亡兵堵门，亡弓上了棚顶，亡骑绕着外圈。棚里躺着一个快临盆的漂客媳妇，接生婆被拦在外头，急得拍大腿：「再拖下去，两条命！」

column2: The keepers withdraw and before nightfall a loud wail rings out from the shelter. Wiping her hands, the midwife says she learned her craft from Doctor Liu, the woman on the Qianli. Every child born in the Ruins in those years was delivered by Doctor Liu. Zhuzhu blushes as she draws a circle: 'Doctor Liu. A woman. Cold hands.' She was one of those babies herself.
column3: 守墟人退了，天黑前棚里传出一声响亮的啼哭。接生婆擦着手说，她这手艺是千里号上的柳娘子教的，那几年归墟生的孩子，个个是柳娘子接的。珠珠红着脸画了个圈：「柳医，女的，手凉。」她自己就是柳娘子接生的。

column2: Broken String Pavilion
column3: 断弦亭

column2: A bamboo pavilion in the open, a pipa hanging from one of its posts, every string broken but one. The castaways' children come here to sing, the song about a stretch of water and a stretch of fog. A troop of dead riders, sick of the noise, snapped the strings with their spear butts and threw a fishing net over the whole pavilion. By the end of the fight one rider is tangled in his own net, horse and all, stuck in the mud.
column3: 野地里一座竹亭，亭柱上挂着一把琵琶，弦全断了，只剩一根。漂客家的孩子常来这儿唱歌，唱的是一程水一程雾。一队亡骑嫌吵，拿枪杆挑断了琴弦，又拿渔网把亭子罩了起来。打到最后，一个亡骑被自己的网缠住了，连人带马倒在泥里，挣不出来。

column2: The other riders retreat, but that one is still thrashing in the net. You don't finish him. You cut the net and haul him and his horse free. He stands, dips that featureless face towards you, and leads his horse into the water, a camel bell on his spearhead giving one small chime. Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'The pipa player. Surname unknown. He taught us the song.'
column3: 别的亡骑都退了，那一个还在网里挣。你们没补刀，割开网，把他和马拽了出来。他站起来，冲你们低了低那张没有五官的脸，牵着马走进了水里，枪头上挂着的一枚驼铃叮了一声。珠珠画了个圈：「弹琵琶的，姓什么不知道，歌是他教的。」

column2: Hidden Channel Field
column3: 暗渠田

column2: A taro field lies in the open with a hidden channel buried beneath it, bringing water from the foot of the hills, a shaft sunk every few dozen paces. A squad of dead archers stands by the shafts tipping in basket after basket of sand, and each time one fills, a patch of taro leaves yellows. The camel folk dug this channel, say the farmers, and among the diggers was a man named Zhou who sank shafts faster than anyone.
column3: 野地里一片芋头田，地底下埋着一条暗渠，从山脚引水过来，每隔几十步有一口竖井。一队亡弓守在竖井边，往井里一筐筐地填沙，填满一口，田里的芋头叶就黄一片。种田的漂客说，这渠是驼客挖的，挖渠的人里有个姓周的，挖井挖得最快。

column2: The archers are driven off, the shafts dug out one by one, and the water runs again. On the curb of the last shaft is carved 'Old Zhou', and beside it in small characters: 'Dug two hundred and ninety-nine at the royal city. Digging the three hundredth here.' The craft of the desert's underground channels had come all the way to the sea. Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'Old Zhou. Well digger. Loved humming tunes.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走，竖井一口口掏开，水又流了起来。最后一口井的井沿上刻着「老周」，旁边一行小字：「在王城挖了二百九十九口，到这儿挖第三百口。」坎儿井的手艺从沙漠一路带到了海边。珠珠画了个圈：「老周，挖井的，爱哼小调。」

column2: Pennant Reef
column3: 三角旗礁

column2: A tall reef on the coast with a black pennant planted on its crest, its point to the east. The Ruins have no wind, yet the pennant stands spread: strips of bamboo are sewn along its edges to hold it out. A squad of dead archers below shoots at it arrow after arrow until it is nothing but arrow holes, and still it does not fall.
column3: 海边一块高礁，礁顶插着一面黑色的三角旗，旗角朝东，归墟没有风，旗却是展开的：旗边缝着竹篾撑着。一队亡弓守在礁下，一箭一箭往旗上射，旗上早已是一片箭孔，就是不倒。

column2: The archers withdraw. It is the black pennant of the Lu family escort, and sewn to its back is an oilcloth slip, a consignment note: 'Lu Family Escort of the tea road, carrying the Qianli's tribute tea from the Tea Mountains to the Ruins.' Below it: 'Consignment delivered, received and checked by the lamp keeper.' Where the receipt should be signed there is no name, only a little drawing of a straw hat. Gong Modou clicks his tongue. 'Whoever took delivery couldn't be bothered to write.'
column3: 亡弓退了。是陆家镖的黑三角旗，旗背面缝着一张油布单子，是镖单：「茶路陆家镖，承运千里号贡茶，自茶山至归墟。」底下一行：「镖已送到，交守灯人点收。」收讫的地方没有签名，只画了一顶小小的斗笠。龚墨斗咂咂嘴：「这收镖的，倒是懒得写字。」

column2: Joining Stone
column3: 合砖石

column2: A square stone in the open with half a tea brick set into its face, pressed so tight that in ten years not a corner has crumbled. Where the other half should be there is an empty socket exactly half a brick in size. The old white mule that stood facing west at Lead Mule Bay has somehow walked here on its own and lies down beside the stone. A troop of dead riders surrounds it, trying to drive it off, and it does not even raise its head.
column3: 野地里一块方石，石面上嵌着半块茶砖，茶砖压得紧，十年了一角没缺，另一半的位置空着，正好一个半块的凹槽。头一天还在头骡湾朝西站着的那头老白骡，不知什么时候自己走到了这里，卧在方石边上。一队亡骑围着它，要把它赶走，它头也不抬。

column2: The riders withdraw; the old mule stays lying there. On the side of the stone the caravan carved: 'Two hundred-odd of the tea road. Half our brick is here; the other half is in the chief's casket. Only the day the halves are joined will the tea road have arrived.' The rim of the socket is worn glossy by ten years of one mule's chin. Xiaojiang crouches and strokes its head. 'It's stopped looking west. It knows the chief's half is coming this way.'
column3: 亡骑退了，老白骡还卧着。方石侧面刻着马帮的字：「茶路二百余人，半砖在此；另一半在镖头匣里。两半合上那天，茶路才算到了。」凹槽边磨得发亮，是十年里一只骡子的下巴磨的。小桨蹲下摸了摸骡头：「它不朝西看了。它知道镖头的那一半，要往这边来。」

column2: Three Bowl Pavilion
column3: 三碗亭

column2: A stone pavilion stands squarely in the main road with a stone table inside and three bowls set into its top: one celadon, one coarse clay, one copper. Each holds a dried stain, one red, one brown, one white. A squad of dead archers guards the pavilion and will pin to the table the hand of anyone who tries to pour something in.
column3: 大路正中一座石亭，亭里一张石桌，桌面上嵌着三只碗：一只青瓷，一只粗陶，一只铜的。碗里各有一层干了的渍，一碗红，一碗褐，一碗白。一队亡弓守着石亭，谁想往碗里倒东西，就把谁的手射穿在桌上。

column2: The archers withdraw. Gong Modou licks a fingertip and tastes each in turn: the red is grape wine, the brown is tea, the white is salt, dried seawater. The three roads met here, each poured a bowl, and they drank one another's. Carved on the table's edge is a line: 'The three roads have come. Three are missing. We wait one year.' Zhuzhu says she heard the grown-ups talk about that day: everyone cried, then laughed, then went on waiting.
column3: 亡弓退了。龚墨斗舔了舔指头，挨个尝过：红的是葡萄酒，褐的是茶，白的是盐，是海水干了。三路的人在这里会了面，各倒一碗，换着喝了。桌沿刻着一行字：「三路至。缺者三，候之一年。」珠珠说她听大人讲过那天，人人都哭了，哭完又笑，笑完接着等。

column2: Seeing-Off Stone
column3: 送船石

column2: On the summit of the South Islet lies a great flat rock with a little hut below it, nets drying out front: the store of the few castaway families on the islet. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it, driving the fisherfolk to live under the rock, eating the grain and stringing the nets across the bay to charge passing boats a toll. Words are carved into the flat rock, and the pirates, finding them in the way, have scraped half of them off with knives.
column3: 南屿顶上一块大平石，石下一座小屋，屋前晾着网，是屿上几户漂客的仓。一伙落难海盗占了仓，把渔家撵到了石头底下住，仓里的粮他们吃，渔网他们拿去拦海湾收过路钱。平石上刻着字，海盗嫌碍事，拿刀刮去了一半。

column2: The pirates are driven off the islet and the fisherfolk move back into their store. Axi kneels before the flat rock and traces the surviving words one by one: 'Pilot Xu Chaosheng saw the ships this far. Inside the reef gate, the tide was mine to read; east of the reef gate, there is no need of a pilot. Xi, Father has gone on ahead.' She lays her grandmother's letter beneath the words and weighs it down with a stone. As she rises she sees a line of fresh footprints in the soft mud beside the rock, yellow sand in the left prints, red mud in the right, heading east.
column3: 海盗被赶下了屿，渔家搬回了仓。阿汐跪在平石前，把没刮掉的字一个个摸出来：「领港许潮生，送船到此。礁门以内，潮由我领；礁门以东，不用领了。汐，爹往前去了。」她把奶奶那封信压在字底下，压了块石头。起身时，她看见石边的软泥里有一行新脚印，左脚印里带着黄沙，右脚印里带着红泥，往东去了。

column2: In the store you seize the pirates' hoard: two vats of dried sweet potato, a basket of eggs, eight big nets for blocking the bay, a bucket of toll money, and a packet of stone dust scraped off the flat rock, which they meant to sell to the castaways 'to drink as a charm'.
