column3: 仓里抄出海盗囤的两缸番薯干、一筐鸡蛋、八张拦海的大网、一桶收来的过路钱，还有一包从平石上刮下来的石粉，他们留着说要卖给漂客「当符水喝」。

column2: Each time you pass, the islet's fisherfolk carry a basket of fish to your boat and sweep the leaves from before the flat rock for Axi. 'We'll look after Teacher Xu's words for him. You go on ahead and don't worry.'
column3: 每次路过，屿上的渔家都往你们船上搬一篓鱼，再替阿汐在平石前扫一遍落叶：「许先生的字，我们替他看着，你们放心往前走。」

column2: Half-Built Slip
column3: 半船坞

column2: A small slipway on the coast cradles half a boat: keel and ribs complete, planking on one side only, like a fish split open. A squad of dead soldiers has taken the slip and is prising off the fitted planks one by one and throwing them into the sea. The old castaway who keeps the slip says the man who was building it left years ago. He has looked after the half-boat for him all this time. He can't let it rot.
column3: 海边一座小船坞，坞里架着半条小船，龙骨、肋骨都齐了，船板只钉了一边，像一条被剖开的鱼。一队亡兵占着船坞，把钉好的船板一块块撬下来扔进海里。看坞的漂客老汉说，造船的人走了好些年，这半条船他替人家看着，不能叫它烂了。

column2: The soldiers retreat and most of the planks are fished back out. Two characters are carved on the bow: 'A Ling'. The builder was a sailor named Zheng, the old man says, who wanted to build a little boat and sail back to Quanzhou. He was halfway done when everyone made ready to go east, and he put down his axe and went with them. 'He said somebody had already walked the road home. The road ahead, nobody had.' Zhuzhu draws a circle, thinks, then asks: 'Who's A Ling?'
column3: 亡兵退了，船板捞回来大半。船头刻着两个字：「阿菱」。老汉说造船的是个姓郑的水手，想造条小船回泉州，造了一半，大伙要往东走了，他放下斧头跟着走了：「他说，回去的路有人走过了，往前的路还没有。」珠珠画了个圈，想了想又问：「阿菱是谁？」

column2: Counting School
column3: 算学棚

column2: A low shelter in the open with dozens of little stools and a great slate on the wall covered in sums. It is the arithmetic school the camel folk opened for the castaways' children, teaching the abacus. A squad of dead soldiers has taken it over and sits in rows on the little stools. Several stools have collapsed beneath them and still they sit, motionless, like a class too dim ever to learn.
column3: 野地里一座矮棚，棚里摆着几十只小板凳，墙上一块大石板，石板上写着算式。这是驼客给漂客家孩子开的算学，教打算盘。一队亡兵占了棚子，排排坐在小板凳上，板凳压塌了好几张，他们还坐着，一动不动，像一班学不会的笨学生。

column2: The soldiers get up and leave, and Zhuzhu is first through the door, stroking the slate with tears running down: this was her school. The teacher's last question is still on it: 'Three hundred minus two hundred and ninety-nine makes what?' Beneath it the children's answer: 'One.' The teacher circled the 'one' in red clay and wrote beside it: 'Makes one who comes after.'
column3: 亡兵起身走了，珠珠第一个冲进去，摸着石板直掉眼泪：这是她的学堂。石板上还留着先生出的最后一道题：「三百减二百九十九，得几？」底下是孩子们的答案：「一」。先生拿红土把「一」圈了，旁边改了一行：「得一个后来的。」

column2: Anchor Barrow Beach
column3: 锚冢滩

column2: Twenty or thirty paces above the waterline, four great iron anchors are planted in a row on the beach, flukes skyward, shanks driven into the sand like four headstones. A troop of dead riders gallops round and round them, striking a fluke with a spear butt on every lap, clang. They have been striking them for years, the castaways say, always the same number: four a day.
column3: 海滩上离水二三十步，一字排开埋着四只大铁锚，锚爪朝天，锚杆插进沙里，像四块墓碑。一队亡骑绕着铁锚来回地跑，跑一圈，拿枪杆敲一下锚爪，当的一声。漂客们说，他们敲了好些年，敲的次数都一样，一天四下。

column2: The riders scatter. Cast into the shanks are the words 'Qianli Two', 'Qianli Three', 'Qianli Four', 'Qianli Five'. Xiaojiang feels a knot tied on every anchor ring, tied the way his grandfather Bao Laozhen tied them. Gong Modou frowns. Bring your anchors ashore and you don't mean to sail again. But where are the ships? Four ships, and not one in sight.
column3: 亡骑散了。锚杆上铸着字：「千里·二」「千里·三」「千里·四」「千里·五」。小桨摸到每只锚环上都打着一个结，正是爷爷鲍老针的结法。龚墨斗皱起眉头：锚上了岸，船就不打算走了。可船呢？四条船，一条也没看见。

column2: Barber's Stool
column3: 剃头凳

column2: A tall stool stands in the open with a brass basin beside it and a yellowed towel over the rim. Every morning one dead archer comes, sits on the stool, tips his head back and waits. Nobody shaves him, so he sits there till dark. Today a whole squad has come, jostling over the stool in a heap, and they have chased away every castaway who came for a shave.
column3: 野地里一张高脚凳，凳边一只铜盆，盆沿挂着一条发黄的手巾。每天清早，一个亡弓过来，在凳子上坐下，仰起头，等着。没人给他剃，他就一直坐到天黑。今天来了一队，争着坐那张凳子，挤成一团，把来剃头的漂客全赶跑了。

column2: The archers scatter. The stool belonged to Liu One-Stroke, the Qianli's barber, the castaways say. On the first of every month he shaved two hundred-odd people one after another, and even the keepers liked to come and sit for a turn. 'He shaved them too,' an old man laughs. 'Nothing on their faces, so he'd scrape them with the back of the razor and say it freshened them up.' Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'Liu One-Stroke. Barber. Talked a lot.'
column3: 亡弓散了。漂客们说，凳子是千里号上的剃头匠刘一刀的，每月初一，他给二百多号人挨个剃一遍，连守墟人都爱凑过来坐一坐。「他也给它们剃，」一个老汉笑，「脸上没东西，他就拿刀背刮一刮，说精神。」珠珠画了个圈：「刘一刀，剃头的，话多。」

column2: Ship Rib Bridge
column3: 船肋桥

column2: The main road crosses a dry gully on a bridge whose arches are curved timbers, plainly a ship's ribs, and whose deck is ship's planking still pocked with nail holes. A squad of dead soldiers guards it and lets people cross westward only, never east. A castaway with a carrying pole tries to cross east to trade and is flicked back with a spear shaft, tries again, and is flicked back again.
column3: 大路过一道干沟，沟上架着一座桥，桥拱是一根根弯木，一看就是船的肋骨，桥面是船板，还留着钉眼。一队亡兵守着桥，只许往西走，不许往东过。漂客挑着担子要过桥去东边换东西，被一枪杆拨回来，再上，再拨回来。

column2: The soldiers fall back and the castaway crosses with his load. Gong Modou lies under the bridge studying it a long while: 'Qianli Three' is branded on the ribs, but several are scorched black. Fire has been at them. His face darkens. 'They burned a ship, then pulled it apart for a bridge?' The ship was burned, the castaway says, he has heard as much. Who burned it, he couldn't say.
column3: 亡兵退了，挑担的漂客过了桥。龚墨斗趴在桥底下看了半天：肋骨上烙着「千里·三」，可好几根上有一层焦黑，是火烧过的。他脸色不好看：「烧过的船，拆下来架桥？」漂客说，船是烧了的，他听人讲过，至于谁烧的，他就说不清了。

column2: Vine Islet
column3: 葡萄屿

column2: On the lee side of the South Islet, grapevines creep through every crack in the rock, bunches so purple they are almost black. Grapes on a sea island: the castaways call it a wonder. A squad of dead soldiers guards the trellises, tearing off the ripe bunches one by one and hurling them into the sea until the beach runs purple, and they will not let anyone pick a single grape.
column3: 南屿背风的一面，石缝里爬满了葡萄藤，一串串紫得发黑。海岛上长葡萄，漂客们都说是个怪事。一队亡兵守在藤架底下，把熟了的葡萄一串串揪下来扔进海里，扔得满滩紫汁，就是不许人摘一颗。

column2: The soldiers fall back and the castaways climb the islet with baskets. The camel folk brought the vines from the royal city, cuttings wrapped in wet felt, across desert and over snow mountains, and not one died on the way. The man who planted them was called Grape Zhang, and he used to say, 'A vine knows its planter. It keeps count of the years for him.' Zhuzhu tries one, screws up her eyes at the sourness, and draws a circle: 'Grape Zhang. Grows vines. Bad teeth.'
column3: 亡兵退了，漂客们挎着篮子上了屿。藤是驼客从王城带来的，插枝裹在湿毡里，过了沙漠、过了雪山，一路没死。种藤的人叫葡萄张，他说过：「葡萄认人，谁种的，它就替谁记着年头。」珠珠尝了一颗，酸得眯眼，画了个圈：「葡萄张，种藤的，牙不好。」

column2: Silk Sail Cove
column3: 丝帆湾

column2: A small cove on the coast shelters a dozen castaway fishing boats, and their sails shimmer: they are made of silk, red and blue, woven with roundel patterns. A troop of dead riders charges into the cove and slashes the sails one by one with their spear points, the torn silk drooping from the masts like faded banners.
column3: 海边一道小湾，湾里泊着十几条漂客的渔船，船上挂的帆一张张流光溢彩，是绸子做的，红的、青的、织着团花。一队亡骑冲进湾里，拿枪尖把帆一张张挑破，挑破的绸子挂在桅上，耷拉下来，像一面面褪了色的旗。

column2: The riders retreat and the fishing families take down the silk to mend it. Every selvedge is stamped with the caravan's mark: 'Silk Road, load number such-and-such.' One year a great storm soaked the Silk Road's goods, the silk was ruined with salt and couldn't be sold, so the camel folk cut it up for the fishermen's sails. 'Goods just sit there. Sails go places.' Zhuzhu draws a circle: 'The one who cut the sails. A woman. Quick hands, quick temper.'
column3: 亡骑退了，渔家把绸子收下来缝补。绸边上都印着驼队的记号：「丝路·第几驮」。那年一场大雨淋了丝路的货，绸子泡了盐水卖不出去，驼客就裁了给渔家做帆：「货是死的，帆是活的。」珠珠画了个圈：「裁帆的，女的，手快，脾气大。」

column2: Prow House
column3: 船头屋

column2: A ship's prow is wedged beneath a cliff on the North Islet, pointing skyward, carved as a sea beast with gaping jaws big enough to crawl into. An old woman lives inside the beast's mouth with a brood of chickens. A squad of dead archers crouches on the clifftop shooting at the prow until the beast's face bristles with arrows, the old woman shielding herself inside with a pot lid while chickens flap all over the cliff.
column3: 北屿的崖下卡着一截船头，船头朝天，雕着一只张嘴的海兽，嘴里能钻进人。一个老阿婆住在海兽嘴里，养着一窝鸡。一队亡弓蹲在崖上，冲船头射箭，射得海兽一脸的箭，老阿婆在嘴里拿锅盖挡着，鸡飞了一崖。

column2: The archers are driven off. This is the prow of Qianli Four, the old woman says. She saw with her own eyes the keepers hack the ship apart with axes. 'They split them, one night, all four ships.' Gong Modou looks at the break: it was sawn, not hacked, a neat clean cut. The old woman waves a hand. 'I'm old, my eyes are poor. But I heard axes.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走了。阿婆说这是「千里·四」的船头，那年她亲眼看见守墟人拿斧头把船劈开的，「船是它们劈的，一夜之间，四条船」。龚墨斗看了看船头断口：是锯的，不是劈的，锯口整整齐齐。阿婆一摆手：「我老了，眼神不好，可我听得见斧子响。」

column2: Three Roads Sand Table
column3: 三路沙盘

column2: On a broad flat stretch of open ground, the whole world has been laid out in sand, pebbles and shells: yellow sand in the north-west for the great desert, a strip of red earth in the south-west for the tea mountains, a spread of crushed shell in the south for the sea, and three pebble roads winding in from three directions to meet at one point. A squad of dead archers is tramping all over it; one step and a mountain collapses.
column3: 野地里一大片平地上，用沙子、石子和贝壳堆出了一幅天下：西北一片黄沙是大漠，西南一溜红土是茶山，南边一摊碎贝壳是海，三条石子路从三头弯弯绕绕，最后汇到一个地方。一队亡弓正在沙盘上踩来踩去，一脚下去，一座山就塌了。

column2: The archers withdraw and Gong Modou squats to stand the trampled mountains back up one by one. Where the three roads meet a little bamboo slip is planted, labelled 'the Ruins'. But from the Ruins a fourth pebble road runs on east, all the way to the edge of the table and off it, into nothing at all. The camel folk came every day to add to that road, Zhuzhu says. They'd add a little, measure it, and shake their heads.
column3: 亡弓退了，龚墨斗蹲下来把踩塌的山一座座扶起来。三条路汇合的地方插着一根小竹签，签上写「归墟」。可从归墟往东，还有第四条石子路，一直铺到沙盘边上，铺出去了，沙盘外头什么也没有。珠珠说，驼客天天来添这条路，添一点，量一量，摇摇头。

column2: Signpost Mast
column3: 指路桅

column2: Where six roads meet stands a thick mast taller than any tree, four signboards nailed to it. A squad of dead soldiers stands guard round it, and anyone who walks up and looks at the boards gets spun round three times until they're too dizzy to know which road to take. Several dizzy castaways already sit at the crossroads, clutching their heads and retching.
column3: 六条路交会的地方立着一根粗桅杆，高过所有的树，杆上钉着四块指路牌。一队亡兵围着桅杆站岗，谁走到跟前抬头看牌子，就被他们推着转三圈，转晕了，往哪条路走都不知道。路口已经坐了好几个转晕的漂客，扶着脑袋干呕。

column2: The soldiers scatter. The four boards read 'Quanzhou, twelve thousand li', 'Tea Mountains, eight thousand li', 'Royal City, nine thousand li', and the fourth, pointing east, a single word: 'Onward.' No distance. A cord tied at the foot of the mast carries a string of knots, and Xiaojiang feels along them one by one. 'Grandpa's knots. He's saying the road east can't be measured.'
column3: 亡兵散了。四块牌子分别写着：「泉州，一万二千里」「茶山，八千里」「王城，九千里」，第四块朝东，只写了一个字：「前」。没有里数。桅杆脚下系着一根绳，绳上一串结，小桨一个个摸过去：「是爷爷的结。他说，往东的路量不出来。」

column2: Borrowed Names Village
column3: 借名村

column2: A little village in the open with twenty or thirty children who hide as soon as they see you. For days a troop of dead riders has ridden in every day, pausing at each door as if calling a roll, then leaving, then coming back the next day. The grown-ups lock their children indoors and say the keepers have come to 'collect names'.
column3: 野地里一座小村，村里二三十个孩子，见了你们就躲。一队亡骑这几天天天进村，在每户门口停一停，像在点名，点完了就走，走了明天又来。村里的大人把孩子锁在屋里，说守墟人是来「收名字」的。

column2: Once the riders are driven off the children dare come out and give their names one by one: Little Ding, A Liu, Pipa, One-Stroke, Zhou Zhou... every one a name from the Qianli. Children born in those years were all named after the Qianli's people, the adults say, and when those people left they said, 'Leave the names, and we're still here.' Zhuzhu ticks them off against her ledger one by one, and at the end she looks up. 'What about me? Whose name is mine?'
column3: 亡骑被赶走，孩子们才敢出来，一个个报名字：小鼎、阿柳、琶琶、一刀、周周……全是千里号的人名。大人说那几年生的孩子，都拿千里号的人起名，那些人走的时候说：「名字留下，人就还在。」珠珠一个一个对着账本打勾，对到最后，抬头问：「我呢？我的名字是谁的？」

column2: Hillfoot Timber Market
column3: 山脚木市

column2: An open yard at the foot of the hills is stacked with timber: ship's planks, masts, rudder stocks, ribs, all fine wood, and every castaway in the Ruins builds houses and mends boats from it. But now a troop of dead riders stands on top of the stacks, hooves on the timber, and rams off anyone who comes to shoulder a beam. The carpenters squat at the edge of the yard, axes in hand, and just watch.
column3: 山脚下一片空场，堆着一垛垛木料：船板、桅杆、舵杆、肋骨，全是好木头，归墟的漂客盖屋、修船都靠这里。可如今木垛顶上站着一队亡骑，马蹄踩着木料，谁来扛木头就把谁撞下去。木匠们蹲在场边，手里攥着斧子，干看着。

column2: The riders withdraw and the carpenters surge in. Their leader, an old carpenter, recognises Houqianli at once. 'Quanzhou docks, Mother Long's stall! The day you chased off those thugs, us porters finally got a bowl of noodle soup.' Later he signed on with a timber boat, which ran into the reef ring last month and drifted into the Ruins. At his shout every carpenter in the yard takes your side, and timber-for-gold trade opens. All the wood is branded Qianli Two to Qianli Five. 'They took the ships apart themselves and gave us the timber for houses. The one that burned, that's another story.'
column3: 亡骑退了，木匠们一拥而上。领头的老木匠一眼认出了后千里：「泉州码头，龙母摊！那天你们赶跑了刀手，我们这帮扛包的才吃上一碗面线糊。」后来他上了一条贩木船，上个月撞进礁圈，漂到了归墟。他一招呼，满场的木匠都认了你们，木料换金子的买卖开了张。木料上都烙着「千里·二」到「千里·五」：「船是他们自己拆的，拆了给我们盖屋。烧的那条，是另一回事。」

column2: Rope Walk Lane
column3: 缆绳巷

column2: A long lane runs through the open land, wooden frames on either side strung with ropes from end to end, some thicker than a man's leg. It was once a rope walk. A squad of dead archers has taken it and is cutting the ropes one by one, and every time one parts, the lane rings with a twang that sets the frames shaking.
column3: 野地里一条长长的巷子，两边立着木架，架上拉着一根根缆绳，从巷头拉到巷尾，有的粗过人腿。这是从前打缆的地方。一队亡弓占着巷子，把缆绳一根根割断，断一根，巷子里就嘣的一声响，震得架子直晃。

column2: The archers are driven off. The cuts are clean, but the ropes are newly laid, and the knots are Xiaojiang's grandfather's. These past years the keepers have come every day to cut them, the castaways say, and every night someone splices them again: spliced and cut, cut and spliced. Xiaojiang joins a severed rope and ties it off with a knot exactly like the old one. 'The first knot Grandpa ever taught me. It's called Wait.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走了。断口是割的，割得整齐，可缆绳是新打的，结是小桨爷爷的结。漂客们说，这几年守墟人天天来割，割完了，夜里不知谁又给接上，接了割，割了接。小桨把一根断缆接上，打了个结，跟原来那个一模一样：「爷爷教的第一个结，叫『等着』。」

column2: Lamp Keeper's Shop
column3: 守灯铺

column2: A squat stone tower on the coast with a lamp on top and a shop below selling lamp oil, wicks and flints. The keeper is a tall, thin old man who lights the lamp every night to guide ships that blunder into the reef ring. But for a month a troop of dead riders has circled the tower daily, pouncing on any flame. Every time he lights the lamp it goes out again, and he isn't allowed to open the shop either. He sits on the doorstep turning a wick between his fingers.
column3: 海边一座矮石塔，塔顶一盏灯，塔下一间铺子，卖灯油、灯芯、火石。守灯的是个瘦高的老汉，夜夜点灯，给撞进礁圈的船指路。可这一个月一队亡骑天天在塔下转，见火就扑，灯点一回灭一回，铺子也不许开门，老汉坐在门槛上，捏着一截灯芯发呆。

column2: The riders are driven away, the lamp burns again, the shop opens, and the old man, impressed, trades you lamp oil and flints for your goods. When the Qianli's people came, he says, his oil had long run out, and they gave him a barrel of whale oil with one instruction: 'Don't let the lamp go out. There are more coming.' He looks up at the lanterns on your masts. 'The ones coming after. So it was you.'
column3: 亡骑被赶走，灯又亮了，铺门也开了，老汉佩服你们，拿灯油、火石跟你们换货。他说千里号的人来时，他的灯油早用光了，是他们分了他一桶鲸油，叮嘱一句：「灯别灭，后头还有人。」「后头的人，」他看看你们桅上的灯笼，「原来是你们。」

column2: Upturned Hull Camp
column3: 覆舟营

column2: On the high ground of the North Islet lies a great ship's hull, keel to the sky, like a long black hall. Ruin-keepers in three columns have made it their camp: soldiers resting beneath it, archers lying along the keel, riders patrolling the islet. No castaway on the North Islet dares look this way at night. The keepers' chief lives in that ship, they say.
column3: 北屿的高处扣着一条大船的船底，船底朝天，像一座黑色的长屋。三路守墟人以它为营：亡兵在船底下歇着，亡弓趴在龙骨上，亡骑在屿上来回巡。整座北屿上的漂客，夜里都不敢往这边看，说那条船里住着「守墟人的头儿」。

column2: The keepers withdraw into the sea. There is no chief beneath the hull, only row on row of bunks, tally marks scratched into every plank. The timber is Qianli Five. On the bulkhead, in charcoal blurred by sea damp, is a line in large characters: 'Do not burn the ships. Do not sink them. Leave them for those who come after.' Below it, in a crooked hand, as if someone were arguing back: 'No use leaving them. Ships can't go east.'
column3: 守墟人退进了海里，船底下没有什么头儿，只有一排排睡铺，铺板上刻着一道道「正」字。船底的木料是「千里·五」。舱壁上用炭写着一行大字，墨迹被海雾洇过：「船不烧，不沉，留给后来的人。」底下另有一行歪字，像是有人反驳：「留也没用，东边去不了船。」

column2: Sober-Up Slope
column3: 醒酒坡

column2: A sunny slope in the open has several hundred wine jars buried in it, their mouths sealed with clay and a handprint pressed into each seal. A troop of dead riders is prising them open with spear points, and having opened them, they don't drink, they pour them out. The whole slope reeks of wine, the castaways herding goats below are reeling, and several goats have passed out too, lying in the grass kicking their legs.
column3: 野地里一面向阳的土坡，坡上埋着几百只酒坛，坛口封着泥，泥上按着手印。一队亡骑正拿枪尖一只只撬坛口，撬开了也不喝，倒在地上，满坡酒气，熏得坡下放羊的漂客直打晃，羊也醉倒了好几只，躺在草里蹬腿。

column2: The riders are driven off and the surviving jars are sealed again. Each carries a label: grape wine, rice wine, highland barley wine, something from every road. The three roads buried them together in those years, says the goatherd, and agreed to open them once the missing ones arrived. 'The day we open them, three days drunk.' They have lain buried till today and not one has been opened. Zhuzhu writes in her ledger: 'Wine. Not drunk.'
column3: 亡骑被赶走，剩下的坛子又封了回去。坛上贴着签：葡萄酒、米酒、青稞酒，三路各有。放羊的说，这是那几年三路的人一起埋的，说好等缺的那几个都到了再开，「开坛那天，一醉三天」。坛子埋到今天，一只都没开过。珠珠在账上写：「酒，没喝。」

column2: Listening Stone
column3: 听海石

column2: A great rock at the eastern end of the North Islet has a hollow worn into it by someone's sitting, and beside the hollow is chiselled a little ear-shaped pit, just right for pressing your ear to. A squad of dead soldiers holds the rock and keeps the castaways well away, though they don't sit on it either, only stand around it. The moment Xiaojiang reaches the islet he runs for the rock, and a spear shaft comes across his chest.
column3: 北屿东头一块大石，石面上被人坐出了一个窝，窝边凿着一个耳朵形的小坑，贴耳朵正好。一队亡兵占着石头，把漂客赶得远远的，自己却也不坐，只围着站。小桨一上屿就往石头那边跑，被亡兵一枪杆横在胸前。

column2: The soldiers withdraw and Xiaojiang sits in the hollow, presses his ear into the pit and listens a long time. 'There's a sound down there. Very low, like an ox lowing under the ground.' Bao Laozhen sat here every day in those years, the old islanders say, listening. One day he leapt up and ran across the whole island shouting, 'Up the mountain! Everyone up the mountain!' They all ran uphill, and that afternoon the sea came pouncing ashore.
column3: 亡兵退了，小桨坐进那个窝，把耳朵贴进小坑，听了很久：「底下有声音，很低，像牛在地底下叫。」岛上的老人说，鲍老针当年天天坐这儿听，有一天他忽然跳起来，满岛地喊：「上山！都上山！」大伙跑上了山，那天下午，海就扑上来了。

column2: Driftwood Bay
column3: 碎木湾

column2: A bay on the coast is carpeted with broken wood, planks, barrel staves, hatch covers, packed so tight you can't see the water. A squad of dead archers holds the mouth and shoots the hull of any castaway boat that paddles in to gather wood. Everything in this bay was smashed by the great wave that year, the castaways say. Ten years and it still hasn't drifted away; in still water, nothing ever drifts away.
column3: 海边一道湾，湾里漂着一层碎木头，船板、桶板、舱门，挤得看不见水。一队亡弓守着湾口，见有漂客划小船进来捞木头，就射船底。漂客们说，这湾里的木头都是那年大浪打碎的东西，十年了还没漂干净，静水里，什么都漂不走。

column2: The archers are driven off and the castaways paddle in to gather wood. Gong Modou fishes out a hatch cover, half charred, the other half carved 'Qianli Three'. So the burned ship was never set alight: the great wave smashed the cookhouse ashore and tipped its live coals onto the ship. He lets out a breath. 'Nobody burned it.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走，漂客们划着小船进湾捞木头。龚墨斗捞起一块舱门，门上烧焦了一半，另一半刻着「千里·三」。原来那条烧过的船不是火烧的：大浪打碎了岸上的灶屋，炭火扣在了船上。他松了口气：「不是人烧的。」

column2: Wave Refuge Terrace
column3: 避浪坪

column2: A level terrace on the lower slopes is crowded with dozens of low shelters, built by castaways who fled up here the year of the great wave; when the water went down, some never came back down. For days a troop of dead riders has charged onto the terrace, flipping shelters over with their spear shafts as though trying to drive the people downhill. The old folk refuse to budge. 'Down there it flooded once. Up here it won't.'
column3: 山脚上一片平坪，坪上搭着几十间矮棚，是那年大浪时漂客们逃上来住的，浪退了，有人就再没下山。一队亡骑这几天天天往坪上冲，拿枪杆把棚子一间间挑翻，像是要把人往山下赶。坪上的老人们不肯走：「下面淹过一回，上面不会淹。」

column2: The riders withdraw. A wooden post at the terrace's edge is marked with the height the wave reached that day, a man's height and more below the terrace rim. Pinned beneath it is a board in Bao Laozhen's hand: 'If the sea pulls back half a li and the fish are flapping on the sand, the wave is coming. Do not go after the fish. Run for high ground.' That board saved the whole island that day, the old folk say. Every child who ran out for the fish was dragged back.
column3: 亡骑退了。坪边立着一根木杆，杆上刻着那天浪到的高度，比坪沿低了一人多。杆下压着一块木牌，是鲍老针的字：「海先退了半里，鱼都蹦在滩上，那就是浪要来了，不许去捡鱼，往高处跑。」老人们说，那天正是这块牌子救了一岛人，捡鱼的孩子全被拽了回来。

column2: Three Elders' Tale
column3: 三老说

column2: Under a great banyan beside the main road three castaway elders sit and argue every day, always about the same thing: how the Qianli's ships came to be gone. Today the row is at its worst. A squad of dead soldiers stands round them under the tree as if listening too. None of the three pays the keepers any mind; each slaps his own thigh. 'I saw it with my own eyes!'
column3: 大路边一棵大榕树下，三个漂客老人天天坐着吵架，吵的是同一件事：千里号的船是怎么没的。今天吵得最凶，一队亡兵站在树下，围着他们，像是也在听。三个老人谁也不理守墟人，各拍各的大腿：「我亲眼看见的！」

column2: The soldiers withdraw and the three elders each give their version. The first: the ship's master ordered the ships burned to cut off any way back. The second: the keepers split the ships in a single night so the living couldn't leave. The third: the great wave smashed them, nobody's fault at all. Having spoken, they glare at one another, then all turn to you. 'Well, which of us is right?' Gong Modou rubs his chin. 'Each of you saw a piece. None of you saw the whole.'
column3: 亡兵退了，三个老人一人一个说法。头一个说：船主下令烧了船，断了回头路。第二个说：守墟人一夜劈了船，不让活人走。第三个说：是大浪打碎的，跟谁都没关系。三个人说完，互相瞪着，又一齐看你们：「你们说，谁对？」龚墨斗摸着下巴：「都看见了一点，都没看全。」

column2: Fish-Drying Flats
column3: 晒鲞场

column2: A wide drying ground on the coast where the bamboo racks ought to be hung with split fish. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it: their ship struck the reef and sank, they came ashore, and they seized the fishing families' flats. They eat the dried fish, and the half-dried fish too. The guards ride scrawny stolen mules so hungry they gnaw the racks, which collapse row after row.
column3: 海边一大片晒场，竹架上本该挂满剖开的鱼，如今被一伙落难海盗占了：他们的船撞在礁上沉了，上了岸，就抢渔家的晒场，晒好的鱼他们吃，没晒好的他们也吃。守场的是几个骑着抢来的瘦骡子的，骡子饿得啃竹架，架子塌了一排又一排。

column2: The pirates are driven off the flats, the racks go back up, and row after row of split fish hang there again. There is no sea breeze, but the sun dries them just the same. Old Ding from the Qianli taught them how, the fishing families say: rub in seven parts salt, dry for three days, turn twice. Zhuzhu adds a stroke in her ledger, a little fish beside Old Ding's circle.
column3: 海盗被赶下了场，竹架重新立起来，一排排鱼鲞又挂满了，海风不吹，太阳照样晒。渔家说，晒鲞的法子是千里号的老鼎教的：盐抹七分，晒三日，翻两回。珠珠在账上添了一笔，老鼎的圈旁边多了一条小鱼。

column2: In the pirates' shacks you seize three hundred jin of dried fish, half a hold of hard biscuit, two barrels of fresh water, a big stolen iron pot, and a chest of gold and silver jewellery looted along the way. With nowhere to spend it in the Ruins, they had been using it to weigh down the salt fish.
column3: 海盗的窝棚里抄出三百斤鱼鲞、半船舱的硬饼、两桶淡水、一口抢来的大铁锅，还有一箱他们一路抢来的金银首饰，到了归墟，没地方花，拿来压咸鱼。

column2: Each time you pass, the fishing families stack a bundle of dried fish on your carts, made Old Ding's way, and tuck in a little packet of salt besides. 'If you can dry your own fish on the road, you'll never go hungry.'
column3: 每次路过，渔家都往你们车上码一捆鱼鲞，按老鼎的法子晒的，再塞一小包盐：「路上自己会晒鱼，就饿不着。」

column2: North Islet Coop
column3: 北屿鸡寮

column2: On the shady side of the North Islet a row of coops backs onto the cliff, home to the countless descendants of the prow-house granny's chickens, which run all over the islet. A squad of dead archers has taken the coops and is throwing the eggs into the sea nest by nest. They drive the hens out too, not to eat, just to throw. The granny's granddaughter squats outside, cradling the last few eggs in her skirt and sniffling.
column3: 北屿背阴的一面，一排鸡寮靠着崖壁，寮里是船头屋阿婆的鸡生下的一大群鸡，满屿乱跑。一队亡弓占着鸡寮，把鸡蛋一窝窝扔进海里，鸡赶出来又不吃，就那么扔着。阿婆的孙女蹲在寮外，拿裙子兜着最后几个蛋，抽抽搭搭。

column2: The archers are driven off and the hens go back in. The granddaughter says the first of this flock came off the Qianli. 'A ship needs a hen to count the days,' the sailors said, and when they came ashore they left the hens with Granny. Gong Modou remembers the speckled rooster aboard the Zhenwu in the Sea of Fog. 'Same temper as that one.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走，鸡又回了寮。阿婆的孙女说，这群鸡的老祖宗是千里号上带下来的，船上的人说「船上要有鸡，替人数日子」，下船的时候把鸡留给了阿婆。龚墨斗想起了雾海镇雾号上那只芦花鸡：「镇雾号上那只，跟这一窝是一个脾气。」

column2: Behind the coops you find six baskets of eggs the archers didn't get to, a brood of newly hatched chicks, and a dozen bales of dried seaweed the keepers dragged from who knows where, stacked neatly as if to make someone a bed.
column3: 鸡寮背后抄出亡弓扔剩下的六篮鸡蛋、一窝刚出壳的小鸡，还有守墟人不知从哪儿拖来的十几捆干海草，码得整整齐齐，像要给谁铺床。

column2: Each time you pass, the granny's granddaughter comes running down the cliff with a skirt full of eggs and picks out the biggest for you. 'Granny says people who count the days should eat eggs from the hens that count them.'
column3: 每次路过，阿婆的孙女都兜着一裙子鸡蛋跑下崖来，挑最大的给你们：「奶奶说，给数日子的人，吃数日子的鸡下的蛋。」

column2: Nameless Mound
column3: 无名坟

column2: A small earth mound in the open, no headstone in front of it, only a bamboo pole with a baby's silver lock hanging from the top. Zhuzhu stops dead when she sees it. A squad of dead soldiers stands in a ring around the mound, facing outward as if guarding something, and will let no one near. Zhuzhu's hands shake on her abacus. 'Mother told me she found me here.'
column3: 野地里一个小土包，包前没立碑，插着一根竹竿，竿头挂着一只婴儿的银锁。珠珠一看见它就站住了。一队亡兵围着土包站成一圈，背朝外，像在守着什么，谁也不许走近。珠珠攥着算盘的手直发抖：「我娘说过，我是从这里捡回去的。」

column2: The soldiers withdraw. The mound is not a grave but a tiny cellar, lined with dry straw, with a cradle in it carved 'Qianli. Carpentry'. Engraved on the back of the silver lock are two characters: 'Abacus Count'. Zhuzhu's mother tells the truth at last: that year a camel man's wife gave birth to her here. The couple were going east, the road was too long to carry a baby, so they left her with the castaways. 'They said they'd come back for her when the accounts were settled.'
column3: 亡兵退了。土包不是坟，是一座小小的地窖，窖里铺着干草，摆着一只摇篮，摇篮上刻着「千里号·木作」。银锁背面刻着两个字：「珠算」。珠珠的娘说了实话：那年一个驼客的媳妇在这里生了她，夫妻俩要往东走，路太远，就把孩子托给了漂客。「他们说，等回来，账算清了，再接她。」

column2: Camel Bell Pit
column3: 驼铃坑

column2: A sand pit in the open, its mouth weighed down with boulders, the strap of a camel saddle showing through a crack. A squad of dead archers guards it, fiercer than anywhere else, shooting on sight. Halfway through the fight a dead rider steps out from among the archers leading his horse, a camel bell hanging from his spearhead. He stands between you and the archers and presses one of their bows down with his hand.
column3: 野地里一片沙坑，坑口压着几块大石，石缝里露出一截驼鞍的皮带。一队亡弓守在坑边，比别处的都凶，见人就射。打到一半，弓手堆里走出一个亡骑，牵着马，枪头上挂着一枚驼铃。它站到你们和弓手中间，伸手把一张弓按了下去。

column2: It is the one you freed from the net at the Broken String Pavilion. The archers withdraw and he rolls the boulders from the pit's mouth and steps back. Buried inside are several camel saddles, and in a saddlebag a thick ledger the camel folk left behind, a ledger of people: two hundred and ninety-nine of them, one line each, where they were born, what they could do, what they liked to eat. Zhuzhu hugs it with shaking hands. 'All the people I was missing, they're all here.' The camel bell chimes once; the rider is already far away.
column3: 是断弦亭网里救出来的那一个。弓手们退了，它搬开坑口的大石，退后一步。坑里埋着几副驼鞍，鞍袋里一本厚账，是驼客留下的「人账」：二百九十九个人，一人一行，生在哪儿、会什么、爱吃什么，都记着。珠珠抱着账本直抖：「我差的人，全在这儿了。」驼铃叮了一声，那个亡骑已经走远了。

column2: Rudder Stock Strand
column3: 舵杆滩

column2: A massive rudder stock stands upright on the beach, ironwood, gleaming black, half buried in the sand and the other half taller than a man. A troop of dead riders gallops round it and bowls over anyone who tries to pull it up. Gong Modou's eyes go wide at the sight; he drops his pipe and charges in. 'Ironwood! A stock like that won't rot in ten years!'
column3: 海边沙滩上竖着一根粗大的舵杆，铁力木的，黑得发亮，半截埋进沙里，另半截比人还高。一队亡骑绕着舵杆跑，谁要拔它，就被马撞开。龚墨斗一看就直了眼，扔下烟袋冲了上去：「铁力木！这一根，十年不烂！」

column2: The riders withdraw and Gong Modou runs his hands over the stock for a long while. It is carved 'Qianli Two'. Shipwrights have a rule, he says: break up a ship, but never break its rudder. 'The rudder is a ship's life. Take the rudder apart and the ship's truly dead.' Yet this one was carefully unshipped and stood here like a post, as if to say: the ship is going no further, but remember, it could have.
column3: 亡骑退了，龚墨斗抱着舵杆摩挲了半天，杆上刻着「千里·二」。他说造船的规矩，拆船不拆舵：「舵是船的命，拆了舵，船就真死了。」可这根舵却是被好好地卸下来，竖在这儿的，像插一根桩，像在说：船不走了，可要记着，它是能走的。

column2: Sawpit Ridge
column3: 锯木岭

column2: On an earth ridge at the foot of the hills are dug long pits with logs laid across them: sawpits, one man standing above and one below, push and pull. A squad of dead soldiers crouches in them, one above, one below, miming the sawing with nothing in their hands, push and pull, push and pull, for who knows how many years.
column3: 山脚下一道土岭，岭上挖着几个长坑，坑上横着木头，是锯木头用的锯坑，一人站在上头，一人站在坑底，一推一拉。一队亡兵蹲在坑里，一个上一个下，学着锯木头的样子，手里却什么都没有，一推一拉，一推一拉，锯了不知多少年。

column2: The soldiers withdraw. The pit floors are deep in sawdust, and beneath it lies a great saw, its blade stamped 'Qianli. Carpentry'. Gong Modou holds its teeth against the cut he saw on the North Islet prow: this is the one. 'Sawn,' he says. 'One man above, one below, for days on end. The keepers stood by and watched, and learned it.'
column3: 亡兵退了，坑底还堆着厚厚的锯末，翻开来，底下压着一把大锯，锯条上刻着「千里号·木作」。龚墨斗拿锯齿比了比北屿船头的断口：就是这一把。「是锯的，」他说，「一个人在上，一个人在下，锯了好些天。守墟人在旁边看着，看会了。」

column2: Nail Smithy
column3: 钉子铺

column2: A smithy stands in the open, its forge cold, a row of ship's nails laid on the anvil, long and short, every one hammered straight. A squad of dead archers holds the shop, and the smith, a castaway, is made to bend the nails one by one. Once bent, the archers take them and straighten them, then hand them back to him. The smith's palms are covered in blood blisters.
column3: 野地里一间打铁铺，炉子冷着，铁砧上摆着一排船钉，有长有短，一律掰直了。一队亡弓守着铺子，铺里的铁匠是个漂客，被他们逼着把钉子一根根掰弯，掰弯了，他们又拿去掰直，掰直了，再递给他。铁匠的手上全是血泡。

column2: The archers withdraw and the smith slumps against his anvil. These are nails from the Qianli's ships, he says. In those years he straightened them every day so the castaways could build houses with them, one by one, tens of thousands. 'The keepers watched for years and learned to straighten them,' he says, rubbing his hands. 'But they never learned what nails are for.'
column3: 亡弓退了，铁匠瘫在砧子边。他说这些钉子是千里号拆船拆下来的，那几年他天天替他们掰直，好让漂客们盖屋用，一根一根，掰了上万根。「守墟人看了几年，学会了掰直，」他搓着手，「可它们不知道钉子拿来干什么。」

column2: Flagpole Lane
column3: 旗杆坊

column2: A narrow street off the main road, a flagpole at its mouth with no flag, only an empty birdcage hanging from the top. Every house along it is built of ship's planking, with hatch covers for doors and portholes for windows. A squad of dead soldiers paces the street closing the portholes one by one, house by house; the castaways open one, the keepers close it.
column3: 大路边一条小街，街口立着一根旗杆，杆头没有旗，挂着一只空了的鸟笼。街两边的屋子都是船板盖的，门是舱门，窗是舷窗。一队亡兵在街上来回走，挨家挨户把舷窗一扇扇关上，漂客们开一扇，它们关一扇。

column2: The soldiers withdraw and the portholes open one by one. The whole street is four ships: the door plates read 'Qianli Two', 'Qianli Three'... At the end stands a little house with 'Pilots' Lodge' over the door, an empty bunk inside, and at its head a bamboo tube stoppered with wax. Xiaojiang holds the tube without opening it, his hands shaking. 'It's Grandpa's.'
column3: 亡兵退了，舷窗一扇扇打开。整条街就是四条船：门牌上写着「千里·二」「千里·三」……街尾一座小屋，门楣上写着「领港寮」，屋里一张空铺，铺头一只竹筒，筒口塞着蜡。小桨拿着竹筒没拆，手一直在抖：「是爷爷的。」

column2: Kneeling Camel Flat
column3: 跪驼坪

column2: On a level flat in the open lies an old camel, half its hair gone, both humps sagging soft: the last camel left of the Silk Road caravan. A troop of dead riders surrounds it, prodding it with spear shafts to make it stand. It won't; each prod gets a grunt. Zhuzhu runs at it the moment she sees it and is blocked halfway by a grey horse.
column3: 野地里一片平坪，坪上卧着一峰老骆驼，毛掉了大半，两个驼峰软软地塌着，是丝路驼队剩下的最后一峰。一队亡骑围着它，用枪杆捅它起来，它不起，捅一下，哼一声。珠珠一看见它就冲了过去，被一匹灰马挡在了半路。

column2: The riders withdraw. The old camel raises its head and looks at Zhuzhu a long while, then slowly folds its forelegs and kneels to her: a camel kneels only to its own household. A brass tag is tied to its saddle: 'Camel master Li Ersuan, and wife, née Liu.' Zhuzhu finds the line in the ledger of people. Beside it is written: 'One daughter, named Abacus Count, left in a castaway family's care. Will return when the accounts are settled.' She draws circles round both names, then draws a small one beside them.
column3: 亡骑退了。老骆驼抬起头，看了珠珠很久，慢慢屈下前腿，朝她跪了下来：骆驼只给主家的人跪。驼鞍上拴着一块铜牌：「驼主李二算，妻柳氏。」珠珠在人账里翻到这一行，旁边写着：「女一，名珠算，寄养漂客家。账清即回。」她在两个名字上画了圈，又画了一个小的。

column2: Breaking Ledger
column3: 拆船簿

column2: A little wooden hut in the open, its door nailed shut and a yellowed notice pasted on it bearing the Qianli's seal. A troop of dead riders circles outside and charges anyone who tries to tear the notice down. A book is locked inside, the castaways say. No one has seen it in ten years, but those who once did say it records 'how the ships came to be gone'.
column3: 野地里一座小木屋，屋门钉死了，门上贴着一张发黄的告示，盖着千里号的船印。一队亡骑守在屋外，绕着屋子转，谁要撕告示，它们就冲过来。漂客们说屋里锁着一本簿子，十年了没人见过，见过的人都说里头记的是「船是怎么没的」。

column2: The riders scatter, you prise the door open, and the book lies on the table. The first page is in Xu Chaosheng's hand: 'The master stays in the Mirage and has not come. By the pilot's order in her stead: break up Two, Three, Four and Five. Timber to be shared among the castaways; nails, cables and sails all left here. Number One not to be broken; she waits for her master.' The last page holds only half a sentence: 'Fire in Three's hold, the great wave...' The rest is torn out, the tear still fresh, and on the road towards the hills there are hoofprints.
column3: 亡骑散了，你们撬开门，簿子摆在桌上。头一页是许潮生的字：「船主在蜃楼未至，领港代令：拆二、三、四、五号，木料分与漂客，钉、缆、帆尽留。一号不拆，候船主。」最后一页只有半句：「三号舱失火，大浪……」后面撕掉了，撕口还新，往山那边去的路上，有马蹄印。

column2: Hold Number Two
column3: 二号货舱

column2: A great cargo hold half buried in the sand on the coast: the lower hold of Qianli Two, all that was left when she was broken up, its hatch covered with oilcloth. Its keeper is a one-eyed old sailor who says he stayed behind to mind the goods, and for ten years he has asked anyone who wants cargo, 'What will you trade for it?' For days now a squad of dead archers has held the hatch, and even he can't get in. He sits on a sand heap cursing. 'My hold! Ten years I've minded it!'
column3: 海边一座半埋在沙里的大货舱，是「千里·二」拆剩下的底舱，舱口盖着油布。看舱的是个独眼老水手，自称当年留下看货的，十年来谁来要货，他都要先问一句「拿什么换」。可这几天一队亡弓守在舱口，连他自己都进不去，他坐在沙堆上骂：「我的舱！我看了十年！」

column2: The archers are driven off and the one-eyed sailor climbs back into his hold and pulls back the oilcloth: bale after bale of ten-year-old cargo, porcelain, brass gongs, crates of needles. He sizes you up with his one eye, impressed by how you fight, and agrees to trade his decade-old goods for your new ones. 'The master said cargo's not to be given away, it's to be traded,' he says. 'Keep trading and the road stays open.'
column3: 亡弓被赶走，独眼老水手爬回舱里，掀开油布：一捆捆十年前的货，瓷器、铜锣、成箱的针。他眯着独眼打量你们，佩服你们的身手，肯拿十年前的货换你们的新货。「船主说了，货不能白给，得换，」他说，「换着换着，路就通了。」

column2: Hillside Water Stop
column3: 半山汲站

column2: A spring halfway up the hillside with a stone hut beside it, where the castaways drank when they fled uphill the year of the great wave. Now a band of shipwrecked pirates has seized it, hoarding water in the hut and selling it at a copper a ladle. The castaways below can't afford it and drink brackish water until their mouths blister. The pirates' archers stand on the hut roof and shoot anyone who comes near.
column3: 半山腰一处泉眼，泉边一座石屋，是大浪那年漂客们逃上山时喝水的地方。如今一伙落难海盗占了泉眼，在屋里囤水卖水，一瓢一钱，山下的漂客挑不起这个价，只好喝咸水，喝得满嘴起泡。守泉的海盗弓手站在石屋顶上，谁靠近就放箭。

column2: The pirates are driven down the hill and the spring water runs down to the lowlands through bamboo pipes again. A line is carved on the hut wall: 'Third day after the wave receded. Bao Laozhen found this spring.' If Old Needle hadn't heard this spring gurgling under the rock that year, say the castaways, half the people on the mountain would have died of thirst.
column3: 海盗被赶下了山，泉水又顺着竹管流到了山下。石屋墙上刻着一行字：「浪退后第三日，鲍老针寻得此泉。」漂客们说，那年要不是老针听出了这口泉在石头底下响，山上的人要渴死一半。

column2: In the hut you seize the pirates' hoard: twenty vats of spring water, a basket of coconuts, a bundle of bows and arrows, and their water-selling ledger, a copper a ladle, kept for three full years. The largest entry: 'Sold to the old woman below, one ladle, on credit.'
column3: 石屋里抄出海盗囤的二十缸泉水、一筐椰子、一捆弓箭，还有一本卖水的账，一瓢一钱，记了整整三年，最大的一笔是「卖给山下老阿婆，一瓢，赊」。

column2: Each time you pass, the hill folk fill your water skins and cut you a length of bamboo pipe. 'Old Needle used to say, water runs downhill and people climb up. Carry a pipe and you can tap water anywhere.'
column3: 每次路过，山上的漂客都替你们把水囊灌满，再折一根竹管给你们：「老针说过，水往低处走，人往高处走，竹管带着，哪儿都能接上水。」

column2: Yellow Silk Shrine
column3: 黄绢祠

column2: A little stone shrine at the foot of the hills, with no idol inside, only a bundle of yellow silk embroidered with a faded dragon. The castaways have worshipped it for ten years, setting coconuts before it on the first and fifteenth of each month. A squad of dead archers guards the door. They don't mind who kneels and kowtows, but reach for the bundle and an arrow lands beside your hand.
column3: 山脚下一座小石祠，祠里没有神像，供着一只黄绸包袱，绣着一条褪了色的龙。漂客们拜了它十年，逢初一十五往前头摆椰子。一队亡弓守着祠门，谁跪下磕头都不管，可谁伸手去碰包袱，箭就钉在谁的手边。

column2: The archers withdraw. Mo San holds his breath and unties the bundle: inside is an empty edict cover, its wax seal long since slit, and on its face a line: 'Secret. To Shen Du, master of the Qianli. To be opened at the Ruins.' The edict itself is gone. Hearing that they have been worshipping an empty envelope for ten years, the castaways look at one another, then all kneel and kowtow once more. 'Empty or not, it's still the Emperor's.'
column3: 亡弓退了。墨三屏着气解开包袱：里头是一只空了的诏封，封口的火漆早已剖开，封面一行字：「密。付千里号船主沈渡，至归墟启。」诏书不在。漂客们听说拜了十年的是个空信封，面面相觑，又一齐跪下磕了个头：「空的也是皇上的。」

column2: Empty Berth One
column3: 一号空泊

column2: The main road ends at a little creek where a stone quay is carved with a great character 'One'. The berth is empty, its bollard worn shiny. A squad of dead soldiers stands on the quay in a row as though waiting for a ship to come in. After the great wave went back that year, the castaways say, this berth was empty. Ship Number One was gone, and no one knows where.
column3: 大路尽头一道小河汊，汊口一座石砌的码头，码头上刻着一个大大的「一」字，泊位却是空的，系船柱磨得发亮。一队亡兵守在码头上，排成一排，像在等船靠岸。漂客们说，那年大浪退了以后，这个泊位就空了，一号船不见了，没人知道去了哪儿。

column2: The soldiers withdraw. Azhou runs a hand over the rope groove in the bollard and smiles slightly. 'My brother kept Berth One for me back in Quanzhou too.' Gong Modou sounds the creek's depth, then looks up at the open country to the east, muttering, 'A wave that big. If the ship's not in the sea, where would it be...' Xiaojiang holds his grandfather's bamboo tube to his ear as if listening for something.
column3: 亡兵退了。阿舟摸着系船柱上那道绳痕，笑了一下：「我哥在泉州也给我留了一号泊。」龚墨斗量了量河汊的水深，又抬头看了看东边的野地，喃喃道：「这么大的浪，船不在海里，会在哪儿……」小桨把爷爷的竹筒贴在耳朵上，像在听什么。

column2: Torn Page Camp
column3: 藏页营

column2: The hoofprints lead from the hut of the Breaking Ledger to the foot of the hills and into a dead-end stone gorge. At its far end stands a camp of picked Ruin-keepers in three columns, better ordered than any outside. In its centre is a stone platform with a rock weighing something down, a corner of paper showing beneath it, and the keepers are packed so tight around it not a drop could leak through.
column3: 马蹄印从拆船簿那间木屋一路往山脚去，钻进一道死胡同似的石峡，峡底扎着一营守墟的精兵，三路排开，比外头的都齐整。营当中一座石台，台上压着一块石头，石头底下露出一角纸，被守墟人围得水泄不通。

column2: The picked guards withdraw, and beneath the rock is the torn-out half page in Xu Chaosheng's hand: 'Fire in Three's hold. A great wave coming. Bao Laozhen ordered everyone up the mountain. After the wave, Two to Five all damaged beyond sailing; the cookhouse fire burned half of Three's hold; Number One carried off by the wave, whereabouts unknown. The keepers stood watching us saw up the ships for ten days, and learned to saw too. Agreed by all: since the ships cannot sail, break them and share the timber with the castaways; we go east, and need no ships.' The keepers couldn't read the page, but they knew it mattered, so they tore it out and guarded it. Each of the three elders had a piece of the truth: the wave broke the ships, the fire came from the stove, people held the saws, and the keepers only watched.
column3: 精兵退了，石头底下就是撕掉的那半页，许潮生的字：「三号舱失火，大浪将至，鲍老针令众上山。浪后，二至五号尽伤，不能再航；三号灶火烧了半舱；一号随浪而去，不知所终。守墟人在旁看我们锯船，看了十天，也学着锯。众议：船既不能走，拆木分与漂客；人往东行，不用船。」守墟人不懂这页纸，可它们知道这是要紧的东西，就撕下来守着。三个老人的话，各对了一截：船是浪打坏的，火是灶里的，锯子是人拿的，守墟人只是在旁边看。

column2: Headcount Strand
column3: 点数滩

column2: A long strand on the coast with a great clay vat buried at its head, its mouth capped with a stone slab carved with one large character: 'Count'. A troop of dead riders gallops back and forth along the beach, leaning down to flick away with a spear shaft anyone who goes near the vat. The camel folk buried it the day they left, the castaways say. No one knows what's inside.
column3: 海边一片长滩，滩头埋着一口大陶缸，缸口用石板盖着，石板上刻着一个大大的「数」字。一队亡骑沿着滩来回跑，谁走近陶缸，就从马上俯身一枪杆把人挑开。漂客们说，那缸是驼客临走那天埋的，谁也不知道里头装的是什么。

column2: The riders withdraw and you lift the slab: the vat is full of small pebbles. Before they left, the camel folk counted heads one last time, each dropping a pebble in. Zhuzhu leans over the rim and counts them one by one all afternoon: there are not two hundred and ninety-nine. At the bottom of the vat three small hollows have been left empty, each carved with the word 'Awaiting'. And at the end of the ledger of people, three lines carry only a name and no 'gone east'.
column3: 亡骑退了，你们掀开石板，缸里是满满一缸小石子。驼客走之前点了最后一回人，一人往缸里扔一颗。珠珠趴在缸边一颗颗数，数了一下午：石子没有二百九十九颗，缸底留着三个空着的小坑，坑边刻着「待」。人账翻到最后，也有三行只有名字，没有「已往东」。

column2: Parted Camp
column3: 让路营

column2: A great camp in the open, Ruin-keepers drawn up tight in three columns: soldiers in front, archers on the wings, riders behind. Yet straight through the middle runs a lane one person wide, the grass trodden flat towards the east. The moment the keepers see you, the lane snaps shut and every spear point swings your way.
column3: 野地里一座大营，三路守墟人扎得严严实实，亡兵在前，亡弓在两翼，亡骑在后。可营当中让开了一条笔直的道，宽一人，草被踩得倒向东边。营里的守墟人一见你们，那条道一下子合上了，枪尖齐齐转了过来。

column2: The keepers withdraw. Yesterday at dusk, says a castaway herding goats at the camp's edge, a woman came from the west, white-haired, a short knife at her belt and a ledger in her hands. The keepers stepped aside one by one, and she walked straight through the middle of the camp without a glance at them. She asked him only one thing: 'Where is my ship?' Azhou looks along the flattened grass. 'It's her.'
column3: 守墟人退了。营边放羊的漂客说，昨天傍晚有个女人从西边来，白头发，腰上挂一把短刀，手里捧着一本账。守墟人一个个往两边让，她看都没看它们，从营当中走了过去，只问了他一句：「我的船呢？」阿舟望着那条倒伏的草：「是她。」

column2: Untied Knot Point
column3: 解结岬

column2: A stone point on the coast with a mooring bollard at its tip, wound with turn after turn of rope, each turn knotted, from the foot of the bollard to the top. A troop of dead riders guards the neck of the point, galloping round the bollard, their horses' tails sweeping the rope on every lap until the knots pull tighter and tighter. Xiaojiang goes white the moment he sees them.
column3: 海边一道石岬，岬尖一根系船柱，柱上缠着一圈圈缆绳，每一圈都打着结，从柱脚一直打到柱顶。一队亡骑守着岬口，绕着石柱跑，跑一圈，马尾巴扫一下缆绳，结越扫越紧。小桨一看见那些结，脸就白了。

column2: The riders withdraw and Xiaojiang feels the knots one by one. Every one below is a Wait, tied daily through the years Grandpa was here. The topmost is different, a slip knot that opens with a single pull. Xiaojiang pulls it and the rope's end drops loose, pointing east. 'Grandpa taught me,' he says quietly. 'When you're done tying Waits, the last knot you tie is a slip knot. It's called Gone.'
column3: 亡骑退了，小桨一个个摸那些结：底下全是「等着」，是爷爷来的那几年天天打的。最顶上一个不一样，是活结，一拉就开。小桨拉开它，绳头垂下来，指着东边。「爷爷教过，」他小声说，「『等着』打完了，最后打一个活结，叫『走了』。」

column2: Rowing Chant Camp
column3: 号子营

column2: A great camp of Ruin-keepers in the open, three columns of them sitting on the ground row after row as though seated at the oars of a boat. They hold no oars, yet together they reach forward and pull back in perfect unison. The camp is silent but for one dead soldier standing at the very front, that mouthless face lifted as if calling the stroke.
column3: 野地里一大营守墟人，三路排开，都坐在地上，一排一排，像坐在船上划桨：手里没有桨，可一齐往前一探，往后一拉，动作整得一丝不差。营里没有声音，只有一个亡兵站在最前头，张着那张没有嘴的脸，像在喊号子。

column2: The keepers withdraw. Xiaojiang takes the caller's place at the front, thinks a moment, and bellows out his grandfather's rowing chant: 'First stroke, hear the waves, oh! Second stroke, hear the wind! Third stroke, hear nothing, and drive on through!' The castaways at the camp's edge stand stunned. Ten years ago, to that very chant, they watched the Qianli's people learn to row on this ground: muleteers and camel men practising for a whole year on dry land.
column3: 守墟人退了。小桨站到那个领号子的位置上，想了想，扯开嗓子喊起了爷爷的号子：「一桨听浪呦——二桨听风——三桨不听，往前冲——」营边的漂客们愣了：十年前，他们就是听着这支号子，看千里号的人在这片地上学划桨的。马帮和驼客在这片旱地上学划了一整年。

column2: Echo Mimic Pass
column3: 学声垭

column2: A narrow pass at the foot of the hills where the echo never repeats what you said. Shout 'Anyone there?' and back comes 'No.' Shout 'Let us through' and back comes 'Won't.' A squad of dead soldiers guards the pass, cringing back under the echo's abuse but refusing to leave. Lu Mei yells, 'Are you real or fake?' and the pass answers: 'Guess.'
column3: 山脚下一道窄垭口，冲里头喊一声，回声不是你的话：喊「有人吗」，回来的是「没有」；喊「借过」，回来的是「不借」。一队亡兵守在垭口，被回声骂得直往后缩，又不肯走。卤妹扯着嗓子喊了声「你是真的还是假的」，垭口里回了一句：「你猜。」

column2: The soldiers fall back and a skinny old man squeezes out of a crack in the rock. It was him mimicking the echo, to frighten the keepers. That year, he says, the Qianli's people opened the edict at the Yellow Silk Shrine and came into this pass to read it aloud. He hid in the crack and listened. He couldn't follow every word, but he remembers the last line: 'Three hundred lines in all. The last left blank, for whoever comes after.' Ten years he's mimicked echoes, and that one line he has never dared repeat. 'That's not an answer I can give for anyone.'
column3: 亡兵退了，石缝里钻出个瘦老头，是他在学回声，专吓守墟人。他说那年千里号的人在黄绢祠开了诏，到这垭口里大声念了一遍，他躲在缝里听，字认不全，只记住最后一句：「凡三百行，末一行空，候后来者。」他学了十年回声，就这一句不敢学：「那不是我能替人答的。」

column2: Palm-Tapping House
column3: 叩掌屋

column2: A little house in the open where an old woman lives who is deaf and mute, unable to hear the waves or speak. A squad of dead soldiers blocks her door and lets no one in or out, so she pokes one hand out through a crack in the window and taps and dabs at her palm in a way no one can follow. Xiaojiang watches her hand a moment, then shoves his way to the front. 'She's talking to me.'
column3: 野地里一间小屋，屋里住着个又聋又哑的老阿婆，听不见浪，也说不了话。一队亡兵堵在她门口，不许人进出，她就隔着窗缝伸出一只手，在掌心里拍拍点点，没人看得懂。小桨盯着她的手看了一会儿，忽然挤到最前头：「她在跟我说话。」

column2: The soldiers are driven off and the old woman takes Xiaojiang's hand and taps on his palm. He reads it aloud as she goes: in those years Bao Laozhen came every day and tapped the sea into her palm so she could hear it: light taps for waves, heavy for wind, long slow strokes for the tide. The last time, what he tapped was 'I'm going east. I'm leaving you my ears.' She taps it into Xiaojiang's palm three times, then pats him on the head.
column3: 亡兵被赶走，老阿婆拉着小桨的手，在他掌心里拍。小桨一边看一边念：那几年鲍老针天天来，在她手心里拍给她听海：轻点是浪，重点是风，一下下长的是潮。最后一回，他拍的是「我往东了，耳朵留给你」。她把这几下拍在小桨手心里，拍了三遍，然后拍拍他的头。

column2: Dry Ship Plain
column3: 旱舟原

column2: A dozen li from the sea, a great ship sits squarely upright in open country, hull whole, three masts still standing, grass grown thick over her deck, and two great characters on her stern: 'Qianli'. A troop of dead riders gallops round her and lets no one climb aboard. At the foot of the rope ladder by the bow stands a white-haired woman with a short knife at her belt, gazing up a long while: Shen Du. She doesn't turn. 'Ten years I kept her road in the Mirage, and she came ashore before me.'
column3: 离海十几里的野地上，端端正正坐着一条大船，船身完好，三根桅还立着，甲板上长满了草，船尾两个大字：「千里」。一队亡骑绕着船跑，不许人上去。船头的绳梯下站着一个白发女人，腰挂短刀，仰着头看了很久：沈渡。她没回头：「十年，我在蜃楼替它记路，它倒先上了岸。」

column2: The riders scatter. That year, an old castaway says, the seabed quaked somewhere far out. In the deep sea the wave stood barely a foot high and nobody aboard any ship even woke; but in the shallow bay, where the bottom rose, it reared up several zhang and lifted Ship Number One off her moorings, carrying her overland and setting her down here. Shen Du opens the hold: silk, tea, porcelain, bound tight and labelled 'Homeward cargo', not a rope touched in ten years. The castaways set up stalls around the ship, and stone-for-metal trade opens. She goes into the master's cabin and opens the edict box. It is empty. 'The list isn't aboard,' she says. 'They took it east and gave it to whoever was waiting there.'
column3: 亡骑散了。老漂客说，那年远海底下地动，浪在深海里只有一尺来高，船上的人连觉都没惊醒；到了浅湾，水底一浅，浪就立起来几丈高，把泊着的一号船端上了岸，一路送到这里放下。沈渡掀开货舱：丝、茶、瓷，捆得好好的，贴着「回程货」，十年没人动过一根绳。漂客们围着船摆开了摊，石料换金属的买卖开了张。她走进船长舱，打开诏匣，匣里是空的。「名单不在船上，」她说，「他们带着往东去了，交给了等在那边的人。」

column2: Returning Tide Strand
column3: 回潮滩

column2: At the far end of the southern beach, every time the tide comes in, Ruin-keepers stand up out of the still water rank on rank: soldiers walking up the sand from the seabed, seaweed hanging from the archers' bows, water streaming from under the riders' hooves. With each tide a new batch comes up to contest the beach with the castaways, and wherever they take, the houses empty. Zhuzhu stands behind you hugging her ledger of people and does not shrink back at all.
column3: 南边海滩尽头，每回涨潮，静水里就一排排站起守墟人来：亡兵从水底走上滩，亡弓的弓背上挂着海草，亡骑的马蹄底下淌着水。潮涨一回，上来一批，跟漂客们抢滩，抢到哪儿，哪儿的屋子就空了。珠珠抱着人账站在你们身后，一点也不躲。

column2: This tide's keepers sink back into the water and the castaways put their houses to rights. But the Ruins have two tides a day, and every one brings new keepers up; before long the beach will need clearing again. Zhuzhu sits on the sand and lays the ledger of people beside her own tattered one, checking circle by circle, and when she is done there are exactly two hundred and ninety-nine. At the end she adds one more box and leaves it empty, chewing her pen a long while. 'I can't work this one out. The man who lights the lamps over east can probably do it.'
column3: 这一潮的守墟人退回了水里，滩上的漂客把屋子收拾了回来。可归墟的潮一天两回，每回都带上来新的，过些日子还得再来清一遍。珠珠坐在滩上，把人账和自己的破账并在一起，一个圈一个圈地对，对完了，账上整整二百九十九个圈。她在最后添了一格，空着，咬着笔头想了半天：「这一格，我算不出来。东边那个点灯的人，大概会算。」

column2: Carved Shell Beach
column3: 刻甲滩

column2: On a white beach on the coast, sea turtles crawl ashore one by one at night to lay. A band of shipwrecked pirates holds the beach, waiting for each turtle to finish so they can dig out the nest, then flipping the mother onto her back to carry off for soup. The castaways can't stop them and crouch behind the dunes watching, the overturned turtles slowly paddling their flippers at nothing.
column3: 海边一片白沙滩，夜里海龟一只只爬上来下蛋。一伙落难海盗守着沙滩，等龟下完蛋就扒窝，还要把母龟翻过来，背朝下，抬回去熬汤。漂客们拦不住，蹲在沙丘后面看，海龟翻在沙上，四只鳍慢慢地划，划不着地。

column2: The pirates are driven off the beach and you turn the overturned turtles back one by one. One old turtle has a few faint characters carved into her shell: 'Dingwei. Qianli.' A mother turtle knows the beach she hatched on, the castaways say, and however far she swims she comes back there to lay. In those years the Qianli's people carved hatchlings' shells and let them into the sea. 'They'll come back, and so will we.' This year, one has come back.
column3: 海盗被赶下了滩，你们把翻倒的海龟一只只翻了回去。有一只老龟背甲上刻着几个浅浅的字：「丁未·千里」。漂客们说，母龟认生它的那片滩，游得再远也回来下蛋。那几年千里号的人在小龟背上刻了字放进海里：「它们会回来，我们也会。」今年，回来了一只。

column2: New Moon Market
column3: 朔夜市

column2: On the night of the new moon, with no moon at all, a row of stalls suddenly appears in the open, and every stallkeeper is a Ruin-keeper: soldiers squatting, riders holding their horses, each with one small thing set out in front of them: a comb, a thimble, half a pipe stem. They trade among themselves, then trade back, without a word. As you come near every stall packs up at once and the riders vault into the saddle and charge.
column3: 初一的夜里，没有月亮，野地上忽然摆开了一溜摊子，摊主全是守墟人：亡兵蹲着，亡骑牵着马，面前各摆一样小东西，一把梳子、一只顶针、半截烟杆。它们互相换，换了又换回来，一句话也没有。你们一走近，所有的摊子一齐收了，亡骑翻身上马冲了过来。

column2: The keepers scatter, leaving a few things on the ground. Mo San picks up the thimble: 'Liu' is engraved inside the rim; the comb's spine reads 'Liu One-Stroke'. The night before the Qianli's people went east, the castaways say, they gave each keeper something they carried. 'You watched us all these years. Something to remember us by.' Every new moon the keepers bring them out and trade them round, as if counting those people over and over.
column3: 守墟人散了，地上落下几样东西。墨三捡起那只顶针，内圈刻着「柳」；梳子背上刻着「刘一刀」。漂客们说，千里号的人往东走的前一夜，挨个给守墟人送了一样随身的东西：「看了我们这么多年，留个念想。」守墟人每到初一就拿出来换着看，像在一遍遍地数那些人。

column2: No-Answer Cliff
column3: 不应崖

column2: A high cliff on the coast with the eastern sea directly below. A squad of dead soldiers holds the top and pushes anyone who climbs up back down. Xiaojiang is determined to go up; there is a trick of Grandpa's he has to try here: shout into the fog, and a quick echo means a cliff, a slow one an island, and no echo at all, open sea. Fists clenched, lip bitten, he waits for you to clear the way.
column3: 海边一道高崖，崖下就是东边的海。一队亡兵守着崖顶，谁上来就推谁下去。小桨要上崖，说爷爷教的法子得在这儿试一试：冲雾里喊一声，回声快是崖，慢是岛，没有回声，是开阔海。他攥着拳头，咬着嘴唇，等你们把路打开。

column2: The soldiers withdraw. Xiaojiang stands at the cliff's edge and shouts east with all his strength: 'Grandpa!' You all wait. You wait a long time, and nothing comes back. He turns round, eyes shining. 'No echo. It's open sea ahead.' Then, more quietly: 'Grandpa didn't lie to me. There really is a way east. It's just too far for a voice to reach.'
column3: 亡兵退了，小桨站在崖边，冲东边使尽力气喊了一声「爷爷——」。你们一起等着。等了很久，什么也没回来。他回过头，眼睛亮亮的：「没有回声，前头是开阔海。」又低声补了一句：「爷爷没骗我，东边真有路，就是太远了，声音够不着。」

column2: Clay Face Hollow
column3: 塑面坳

column2: In a hollow where five roads meet, the ground is covered with faces modelled in clay, some half done, some with the nose slid round by the ear. A squad of dead soldiers squats by a clay pit, digging, moulding, holding each face up before their own flat ones to compare, shaking their heads, smashing it and starting again. As you enter they drop the clay, snatch up their spears and close in.
column3: 五条路交会的山坳里，地上摆满了泥捏的人脸，有的捏了一半，有的鼻子歪到耳朵边。一队亡兵蹲在泥塘边，挖泥，捏，举到自己平平的脸前比一比，摇摇头，拍碎了重捏。你们一进坳，它们扔下泥巴，抄起枪围了上来。

column2: The soldiers withdraw, leaving a hollow full of clay faces. You pick out a few of the best: a fat face, a squinting dark face, a small face with dimpled cheeks. Axi picks up the dark one and stands staring: the features are crude, but that squint out to sea is her father's. The keepers were not trying to make their own faces. They were making the faces of the people who left.
column3: 亡兵退了，坳里只剩一地泥脸。你们挑出几张捏得最好的：一张胖脸，一张眯眼的黑脸，一张笑出酒窝的小脸。阿汐拿起那张黑脸，愣了半天：眉眼粗得很，可那副眯着眼看海的神气，是她爹。守墟人捏的不是自己的脸，是那些走了的人的脸。

column2: The Captain's Chair
column3: 船长椅

column2: A little castaway village in the open, and in the middle of its threshing floor stands a high-backed chair, its back carved with waves, its arms worn glossy. The headman sits in it every day to settle disputes. For days now dead soldiers have taken turns sitting in it and refusing to get up, so the headman has had to squat beside it to do his judging. Shen Du stands at the edge of the floor looking at the chair a long while, and the corner of her mouth twitches.
column3: 野地里一座漂客的小村，村口晒谷场当中摆着一把高背椅，椅背雕着浪花，扶手磨得发亮，村长每天坐在上头断事。一队亡兵这几天轮着来坐那把椅子，坐下就不起来，村长只好蹲在旁边断事。沈渡站在场边看着那把椅子，看了很久，嘴角动了一下。

column2: The soldiers are coaxed out of the chair and the headman explains: it came off Ship Number One, dug out of the mud after the great wave. Shen Du sits down and leans back with a sigh. 'I could never sit in this chair half an hour before a yellow cat squeezed me out of it. Where's the cat?' On Freshwater Island, Axi tells her, sitting on a barrel marked 'For whoever comes after'. Shen Du laughs. 'Trust it to understand before I did.'
column3: 亡兵被请下了椅子，村长才说，这是从一号船上搬下来的，大浪之后在泥里捡的。沈渡坐上去，往后一靠，靠出一声叹气：「我在这把椅子上坐不了半个时辰，就被一只黄猫挤下去。」她问：「猫呢？」阿汐说猫在淡水岛，蹲在「后来者」的水桶上。沈渡笑了：「它倒比我先懂。」

column2: Tide-Listening Stop
column3: 听潮栈

column2: A small rest stop on the coast with a row of bamboo tubes hanging under its eaves, stuffed with dry grass; press your ear to one and you can hear the sea. Pilots used to rest here. A band of shipwrecked pirates has taken it, using the tubes for wine and driving the castaways off the beach. The archers on the door are reeling drunk but hit whatever they aim at. Xiaojiang, his grandfather's bamboo tube tucked in his shirt, stops outside.
column3: 海边一座小栈，屋檐下挂着一排竹筒，竹筒里塞着干草，耳朵贴上去能听见海。这是领港们当年歇脚的地方。一伙落难海盗占了栈，拿竹筒装酒，把漂客赶下了海滩。守门的弓手醉醺醺的，射箭倒是一射一个准。小桨揣着爷爷的竹筒，在栈外站住了。

column2: The pirates are driven off and the tubes go back under the eaves. Xiaojiang sits on the threshold and at last peels the wax from his grandfather's tube. 'Xiaojiang: if you're hearing these words, you've made it. Grandpa has gone on ahead. The road in front needs no ears, only nerve. I'm lending you mine; listen out for the ships that come after. Over east there's a man who lights lamps. He says he'll wait for the last one. Go and thank him for me.' Xiaojiang folds the paper, tucks it back in his shirt, and gazes a long time at the lights to the east.
column3: 海盗被赶走，竹筒挂回了屋檐。小桨坐在门槛上，终于剥开了爷爷竹筒上的蜡：「小桨：你听得见这几个字，就是到了。爷爷先走一步，前头那条路用不着耳朵，用的是胆子。耳朵借给你，替我听着后来的船。东边有个点灯的，说他会等最后一个人，你去替我谢谢他。」小桨把纸折好，揣回怀里，冲东边的光望了很久。

column2: In the stop you seize the pirates' hoard: twelve jars of wine, a basket of dried fish, a bundle of bamboo tubes, half a sack of coarse rice, and a brass gong engraved 'Qianli Four' on the back, which they had been using as a wine bowl.
column3: 栈里抄出海盗囤的十二坛酒、一筐干鱼、一捆竹筒、半袋糙米，还有一只铜锣，锣背刻着「千里·四」，被他们拿来当了酒盆。

column2: Each time you pass, the castaways at the stop take down a bamboo tube for Xiaojiang to listen to and load a basket of fish onto your carts. 'The pilot's grandson is here. Even the sea keeps quieter.'
column3: 每次路过，栈里的漂客都摘一只竹筒给小桨听一听，再往你们车上搬一筐鱼：「领港的孙子来了，海都安静点。」

column2: East Gaze Gap
column3: 东望口

column2: Here the main road narrows to a gap between low walls of piled reef stone, a line of dead archers on top with their bows at full draw. Beyond the gap the open land swells gently to the east, and on the swell there is light, point after point, as though someone has lit a great field of lamps over there, still and unflickering. Shen Du stops before the gap. 'That's the place.'
column3: 大路到这里收成一道窄口，两边是礁石垒的矮墙，墙头一排守墟的亡弓，弓弦拉得满满的。窄口外头，野地往东微微隆起，隆起的地方有光，一点一点，像有人在那边点了一大片灯，静静的，不晃。沈渡在窄口前停下了脚：「就是那儿。」

column2: The archers withdraw and the gap opens. Pinned under the wall is a wooden board in Xu Chaosheng's hand: 'The master has not come. The list is given to the lamp keeper.' Shen Du turns it over twice in her hands and says nothing. Axi tries to count the distant lights and loses count halfway. Xiaojiang lies with his ear to the ground a while. 'No voices over there. But someone's walking. One person, walking very slowly.'
column3: 亡弓退了，窄口开了。墙脚下压着一块木牌，是许潮生的字：「船主未至。名单交守灯人。」沈渡把木牌拿在手里翻了两遍，没说话。阿汐数着远处的灯，数到一半就数乱了。小桨趴在地上听了一会儿：「那边没有人声，可是有人在走，一个人，走得很慢。」

column2: Homecoming Bet House
column3: 押归坊

column2: A great shed in the open, a gambling house run by shipwrecked pirates, and only one thing is bet on: the day the Qianli's people come back. The walls are papered with betting slips, on the first of the month, the fifteenth, next year; in ten years not one has won. A large crowd of pirates guards the place in three columns, and when they see your lanterns the banker slaps the table. 'Here to bet, or here to smash the place?'
column3: 野地里一座大棚，是落难海盗开的赌坊，赌的只有一样：千里号的人哪天回来。墙上贴满了押条，押初一的、押十五的、押明年的，十年里没有一张赢过。一大伙海盗守着赌坊，三路排开，见了你们的灯笼，庄家一拍桌子：「来押的还是来砸的？」

column2: The pirates are scattered and the banker clutches his cash box, begging for mercy. In the heap of slips only one names no day at all. It reads 'They won't come back, they'll go on ahead', the stake is a single copper, and it is signed by a castaway child. The banker smiles wryly. 'Ten years, and that's the only slip that's never lost.' Mo San peels it off the wall and tucks it into his book.
column3: 海盗被打散，庄家抱着钱匣子求饶。押条堆里只有一张没押日子，写着「不回来，往前走」，押的是一文钱，落款是漂客家的一个孩子。庄家苦笑：「十年了，就这一张一直没输。」墨三把那张押条揭下来，夹进了自己的簿子。

column2: Eye of the Ruins
column3: 归墟眼

column2: A small cove on the coast where the still water steams, strings of bubbles rolling up from the bottom, the rocks crusted yellow, and a smell of rotten eggs. The castaways call it the Eye of the Ruins: all the world's water drains away down here, they say, and whoever falls in arrives in another world beneath the sea. A squad of dead soldiers stands chest-deep in the steaming water, barring the cove.
column3: 海边一道小湾，湾里的静水冒着白汽，一串串气泡从水底往上翻，礁石结着一层黄壳，一股臭鸡蛋味。漂客们管这里叫归墟眼，说天下的水都从这儿漏下去，掉进去的人就到了海底下的另一个世界。一队亡兵站在冒汽的水里，水没到胸口，守着湾口不许人靠近。

column2: The soldiers withdraw and Lu Mei crouches to touch the water: hot enough to scald. She knocks off a flake of the yellow crust, licks it and spits. 'Sulphur. The water isn't draining down, it's coming up.' Seawater seeps down into the hot rock of the old volcano below, heats up, and wells back out carrying sulphur. Everyone says the Ruins are where all the world's water returns to; in truth it is where hot water pours out from under the earth. Gong Modou scratches his head. 'Then calling it the Return Ruins has it backwards.'
column3: 亡兵退了，卤妹蹲下摸了摸水，烫手。她敲下一块黄壳舔了舔，呸了一口：「是硫黄。水不是往下漏，是往上冒的。」海水渗进底下旧火山的热石头里，烧热了，带着硫黄又翻上来。归墟不是天下的水归去的地方，是地底下冒热水的地方。龚墨斗挠头：「那叫『归墟』，岂不是叫反了？」

column2: Star Board Platform
column3: 牵星台

column2: A stone platform in the open, its top scored with line after line like a giant ruler. Beside it stands a wooden post hung with a dozen ebony boards of different sizes. A squad of dead archers has taken the platform and shoots at the sky every night, loosing an arrow, then gazing upward for a while, as if shooting at the stars. They have been at it for who knows how many years.
column3: 野地里一座石台，台面上刻满了横道，一道挨一道，像一把大尺子。台边立着一根木柱，柱上挂着十几块大小不一的乌木板。一队亡弓占着石台，夜夜朝天放箭，射一箭，抬头看一会儿，像在射星星，射了不知多少年。

column2: The archers withdraw and Axi takes down an ebony board, holds it at arm's length against the northern sky. 'Star boards.' Line the bottom edge with the sea and the top with the Pole Star; whichever board fits tells you how many fingers high the Pole Star stands, and that tells you which line north or south your ship is on. The marks on the platform were measured night after night by her father and Bao Laozhen. The last line reads: 'Pole Star three fingers and a quarter. Going east, hold this line.' Wherever they went east, they kept the Pole Star at that one height.
column3: 亡弓退了，阿汐取下一块乌木板，伸直胳膊对着北边的天一比：「是牵星板。」下沿齐海面，上沿齐北辰，量出北辰几指高，就知道船在南北哪一线上。台上的刻道是爹和鲍老针一夜夜量下来的，最后一行：「北辰高三指一角。往东，守此线。」他们往东走，一直守着这一指的高低。

column2: Eastward Bow Flat
column3: 拜东坪

column2: A level flat in the open. Every sunrise a great camp of Ruin-keepers lines up on it rank on rank, soldiers, archers and riders, and bows to the east together, staying bent until the sun is a pole's height up. The castaways on the flat bow with them; they have done it for ten years and no one knows what they are bowing to. As you step onto the flat the keepers straighten and turn round.
column3: 野地里一片平坪，每天日出，一大营守墟人在坪上排成一行行，亡兵、亡弓、亡骑，一齐朝东弯腰，弯下去就不起来，直到太阳升过一竿高。坪上的漂客也跟着拜，拜了十年，没人知道拜的是什么。你们一上坪，守墟人直起腰，转过身来。

column2: The keepers withdraw, and only then does an old castaway tell how it began. Early one morning the Qianli's people lined up on this flat and bowed to the keepers, thanking them for watching over them all those years, then turned and walked east. The keepers stood without moving, and only when the people were far away did they bend down in imitation. 'They're not bowing to the east,' the old man says. 'They're returning that bow. Ten years they've been returning it and they're not done yet.'
column3: 守墟人退了，坪上的老漂客才说起头一回：那天清早，千里号的人在这坪上排成行，朝守墟人鞠了一躬，谢它们看了这么多年，然后转身往东走了。守墟人站着没动，等人走远了，才学着弯下腰。「它们不是拜东边，」老人说，「是在回那个礼，回了十年，还没回完。」

column2: Porters' Track
column3: 搬货道

column2: A track trodden shiny across the open land, and a great column of Ruin-keepers files along it carrying wooden crates east, soldiers shouldering them, archers with them on their backs, riders with them slung across their horses. The crates are branded 'Qianli': cargo off Ship Number One. At the track's end they set the crates down, walk back empty-handed, and fetch the next.
column3: 野地里一条踩得发亮的土道，一大队守墟人排成长串，一个接一个地扛着木箱往东走，亡兵扛，亡弓背，亡骑驮在马上。箱子上烙着「千里」两个字，是从一号船上搬下来的。走到道尽头，它们放下箱子，又空着手往回走，再扛下一箱。

column2: The keepers withdraw, leaving dozens of crates stacked square at the track's end. Shen Du opens one: lamp oil, jar after jar, sealed with wax. She counts, looks at the lights to the east, and something crosses her face. 'There was enough lamp oil on Number One to keep two hundred and ninety-nine lamps burning ten years. Someone has been taking it all this time.' She closes the lid. 'The keepers didn't want it. Someone taught them to carry it.'
column3: 守墟人退了，道尽头码着几十只木箱，码得方方正正。沈渡打开一只：是灯油，一罐一罐，封着蜡。她数了数，又看了看东边的光，脸色变了一下：「一号船上的灯油，够点二百九十九盏灯点十年。有人一直在拿。」她把箱子盖上：「不是守墟人要的，是有人教它们搬的。」

column2: Kite Slope
column3: 放鸢坡

column2: A long slope in the open, a row of bamboo poles along its crest wound with broken kite strings. Every year on the eighteenth of the eighth month, the castaways say, they fly kites here, towards the east, with the Qianli's names written on them. But the Ruins have no wind and the kites won't rise, so they hold them up and run east with them. This year a band of Ruin-keepers has taken the crest and is tearing the kites to pieces one by one.
column3: 野地里一道长坡，坡顶插着一排竹竿，竿上缠着断了的风筝线。漂客们说，每年八月十八，他们都在这儿放风筝，往东放，风筝上写着千里号的人名。可归墟没有风，风筝飞不起来，他们就举着风筝往东跑。今年一队守墟人占了坡顶，把风筝一只只扯碎。

column2: The keepers are driven off the slope and the children gather the kites still whole and run east holding them up. They reach the bottom with the kites still skimming the ground. Mo San checks the names on them one by one: Xu Chaosheng, Bao Laozhen, Old Ding, Doctor Liu... The last kite has nothing written on it at all. 'That one's for the one whose name nobody knows,' a child says.
column3: 守墟人被赶下坡，孩子们捡起没扯碎的风筝，举着往东跑，跑到坡底，风筝还是贴着地。墨三看着那些风筝上的名字，一个个对过：许潮生、鲍老针、老鼎、柳娘子……对到最后一只，风筝上什么也没写。孩子说：「这只是给不知道名字的那个人的。」

column2: Stone Boat Shore
column3: 石舫岸

column2: A boat lies on the shore of the coast, built entirely of stone, prow and stern, bulwarks and mast step, nothing missing, except that it can never touch water. A troop of dead riders has made it their stable, horses tied to the stone mast and the hold heaped with hay. A few old castaways who wanted to go in and sit were kicked out by the horses. It's 'the most peaceful boat to sit in', they say.
column3: 海边岸上搁着一条船，是石头砌的，船头船尾、舷墙桅座，一样不缺，就是不能下水。一队亡骑把石船当了马厩，马拴在石桅上，船舱里堆满了干草。几个漂客的老人想进去坐坐，被马踢了出来，他们说这条船「坐着最安心」。

column2: The riders withdraw and the old folk settle into the stone boat with contented sighs. Carved on the prow: 'Built by the camel folk.' The Silk Road people had never been on a boat in their lives, they say; they reached the sea and got sick at the sight of a wave, yet they would have a boat no matter what. So they built one of stone after the pattern of Number One. 'Build it on land and it'll never sink.' When they left they bowed in the stone boat as if it were a temple.
column3: 亡骑退了，老人们坐进石船，舒舒服服地叹了口气。船头刻着「驼客造」。他们说丝路的人一辈子没坐过船，到了海边，见浪就晕，可又说什么也要有条船，就照着一号船的样子拿石头砌了一条：「造在岸上，就不会沉。」他们走的时候，在石船上拜了一拜，像拜一座庙。

column2: Circling Bay
column3: 转圈湾

column2: A reef-bound bay on the coast holds a great school of silver fish, thousands of them, swimming round and round in a circle from dawn to dusk without the ring ever breaking. A squad of dead soldiers walks the shore with them, round and round as well, until they have worn a deep groove in the ground. Whenever the castaways try to cast a net, the soldiers tear it away and throw it among the fish.
column3: 海边一道礁湾，湾里一大群银鱼，几千条，绕着一个圈游，从早游到晚，圈子一丝不乱。一队亡兵站在湾边，跟着鱼群绕着湾走，也是一圈一圈，脚下踩出了一道深沟。漂客们想下网，一靠近，亡兵就把网扯了扔进鱼群里。

column2: The soldiers withdraw; the fish keep circling. Xiaojiang lies on the reef listening. 'They're not going round aimlessly. They're waiting for a gap.' There is a crack in the reef at the bay's mouth, too shallow most days for the fish to get out. Axi counts the days: three more and the spring tide will deepen it. The Qianli's people watched the fish here too that year, the castaways say, watched them a long time, and said: 'When the tide comes, they'll go. So will we.'
column3: 亡兵退了，鱼群还在转。小桨趴在礁上听了一会儿：「它们不是乱转，是在等一个口子。」湾口有一道礁缝，平日太浅，鱼出不去。阿汐算了算日子：再过三天大潮，缝里的水就深了。漂客们说，那年千里号的人也在这儿看过鱼，看了很久，说：「等潮来，它们就走了。我们也是。」

column2: Faceless Barracks
column3: 无面营

column2: At the edge of the open land stands a great camp, row on row of stone huts with row on row of helmets hung before them, some rusted to a skin, some in styles centuries old. The keepers' finest camp is stationed here in three columns, neater than anywhere else. A black stone tablet stands at the gate with only four words on it: 'The living must not stay.'
column3: 野地尽头一座大营，营里一排排石屋，石屋前一排排挂着头盔，有的锈得只剩一层皮，有的样式是几百年前的。守墟人最精的一营驻在这里，三路排开，比哪一处都齐整。营门口立着一块黑石碑，碑上只有四个字：「生人勿留」。

column2: The picked guards withdraw and you look at the back of the tablet. An ancient inscription is carved there and Mo San reads it word by word: 'Who comes to the Ruins and stays too long forgets their face. Who forgets their face keeps the Ruins. The keepers drive the living out, that no more may forget.' Inside every helmet a name is scratched, half worn away. They were people too, who stayed in the Ruins too long and forgot what they looked like. They drive people off so no one else will forget.
column3: 精兵退了，你们翻过石碑，背面刻着一段古字，墨三一字一字念：「来归墟者，留久则忘其面，忘面者守墟。守墟者驱生人，勿使再忘。」每只头盔里都刻着一个名字，刮得只剩一半：它们也是人，在归墟留得太久，忘了自己长什么样。它们赶人，是不想再有人忘。

column2: Silent Child Stockade
column3: 哑童寨

column2: A wooden stockade stands in the open land near the coast, guarded tight by Ruin-keepers in three columns. On top of its wall sits a barefoot child of eight or nine who does not speak. Seeing you come, the child bows to you deeply, exactly the way the keepers bow on the Eastward Bow Flat. The keepers step in front of the child, every spear point turned outward.
column3: 海边野地里一座木寨，三路守墟人守得严严实实。寨墙上坐着个八九岁的孩子，光着脚，不说话，看见你们来，朝你们深深弯了个腰，跟拜东坪上守墟人的腰弯得一模一样。守墟人把孩子往身后一挡，枪尖齐齐朝外。

column2: The keepers withdraw; the child stays on the wall. He was washed ashore the year of the great wave, the castaways say, and no one ever found his parents. The keepers took him in and raised him in the stockade. Having no faces, they couldn't teach him to speak; all they could teach him was to bow. Azhou climbs the wall, sits down beside him and plays a Quanzhou nanyin tune on his conch. The child listens, and listens, then opens his mouth and says, 'Ah.'
column3: 守墟人退了，孩子还坐在墙上。漂客们说，他是大浪那年被冲上岸的，爹娘没找着，守墟人把他捡了回去，养在寨里。它们没有脸，教不了他说话，只教会了他弯腰。阿舟爬上墙，在他旁边坐下，掏出海螺吹了一支泉州的南音。孩子听着听着，张开嘴，「啊」了一声。

column2: Walling Slope
column3: 封东坡

column2: An earth slope in the open, its road running down to the sea. A squad of dead soldiers is laying stones across the road one by one, building a wall that already stands chest-high. Each time they finish a course they step back, look at it, and lay another. Castaways on the far side want to come through and shout over the wall, but the soldiers pay no heed and keep building.
column3: 野地里一道土坡，坡上的路通往海边。一队亡兵正一块块往路上垒石头，垒成一道墙，墙已经齐胸高了。垒好一层，它们退后看一看，再垒一层。墙那边的漂客要过来，隔着墙喊，亡兵也不理，只管垒。

column2: The soldiers withdraw and you open a gap. The stones at the base are the oldest, mossy, laid ten years ago: after the Qianli's people went east along this road, the keepers began walling it, building by day while the night tide knocked a little down, and building again the next morning. 'They're not trying to stop people leaving,' the castaways say. 'They just don't want anyone else to go this way and never come back.'
column3: 亡兵退了，你们拆开一个豁口。墙根底下的石头最旧，长了青苔，是十年前垒的：千里号的人从这条路往东去了以后，守墟人就开始垒，白天垒，夜里潮来冲塌一点，第二天接着垒。漂客们说：「它们不是不让人走，是不想再有人从这儿走了回不来。」

column2: Borrowed Fire Pavilion
column3: 借火亭

column2: A little pavilion in the open with a single lamp inside, its chimney smoked black, its flame small, and it has not gone out in ten years. When castaways nearby need to light a fire, they come here to borrow, kindling a stalk of grass to carry home. A troop of dead riders circles the pavilion, for the keepers cannot abide fire, kicking sand at the lamp with their hooves, and each time the borrowers throw themselves in the way.
column3: 野地里一座小亭，亭里一盏灯，灯罩熏得发黑，火苗不大，十年没灭过。附近的漂客要生火，都来这儿借，点一根草棍带回去。一队亡骑围着小亭打转，守墟人见不得火，拿马蹄刨沙往灯上扬，扬一回，借火的人就扑上去用身子挡一回。

column2: The riders scatter, and the lamp still burns. A line is cut into its base: 'This lamp is not counted.' The lights to the east were lit one at a time, the castaways say, and when the last of them was done, this one was lit too but never carried over; it was set down here instead. 'The lamplighter said this one is for the road. Whoever passes can borrow a light.'
column3: 亡骑散了，灯还亮着。灯座上刻着一行小字：「此灯不在数内。」漂客们说，东边那片灯是一盏一盏点起来的，点到最后，这一盏点好了，却没有搬过去，就放在了这儿。「点灯的人说，这一盏是给路上的，谁路过，谁借个火。」

column2: Lamp Front Slope
column3: 灯前坂

column2: The last slope on the way east, and from its crest you can see the lamps at last: set out one by one across a level field in row after row, as still as if the stars had fallen to the ground. A camp of Ruin-keepers holds the slope in three columns, spears pointing west, backs to the lamps, standing ramrod straight like the guard of a city gate kept for many years. Shen Du stands among you, holding her ledger tight.
column3: 往东最后一道坡，坡顶就能看见那片灯了：一盏一盏摆在一片平地上，排成一行行，静得像星星落了一地。坡上驻着一营守墟人，三路排开，枪尖朝西，背对着灯。它们站得笔直，像守了很多年的城门。沈渡站在你们中间，把那本账抱紧了。

column2: The keepers withdraw down the slope, form ranks on either side, and bend low as they do on the Eastward Bow Flat. Mo San holds up a lantern and counts three times: two hundred and ninety-nine lamps, not one more, not one fewer. In the middle of them stands a low table, and behind it sits a figure in a straw hat with his back to you, trimming the wicks one by one with a thin bamboo pick.
column3: 守墟人退下坡去，在两边排成行，弯下了腰，像拜东坪上那样。墨三举着灯笼数了三遍：二百九十九盏，一盏不多，一盏不少。灯阵当中有一张矮桌，桌后坐着一个人，戴着斗笠，背对着你们，正拿一根细竹签，一盏一盏地挑灯芯。

column2: Glowing Strand
column3: 夜光滩

column2: A reef flat on the coast where at low tide the water only reaches your ankles. At night, every step you take lights the water with a blue glow, one shining footprint after another that only slowly fades. A troop of dead riders gallops across the flat every night, their hooves striking trails of blue fire, chasing off the castaways who come to see the light. At its far end the flat runs on into the darkness of the east.
column3: 海边一片礁坪，退潮后水只没到脚踝。夜里一脚踩下去，水里就亮起一片蓝光，一步一个亮脚印，一会儿才暗下去。一队亡骑每夜在礁坪上跑，马蹄踏出一溜溜蓝火，把来看光的漂客赶得远远的。礁坪的尽头，一直伸向东边的黑暗。

column2: The riders scatter. The light comes from tiny living things in the water that glow when touched, Mo San says; it is no ghost fire. The Qianli's people left from here, says the old castaway who comes to watch: that night the tide went far out, and a few hundred people walked barefoot east across the reef flat, a trail of blue footprints behind each of them, hundreds of trails, glowing all night and only going out at dawn. 'In all my life,' he says, 'I never saw a road so beautiful.'
column3: 亡骑散了。墨三说，这光是水里极小的活物，碰一下就亮一下，不是鬼火。看光的老漂客说，千里号的人就是从这里走的：那夜大退潮，几百个人赤着脚踩着礁坪往东走，一人身后一串蓝脚印，几百串，亮了一整夜，天亮才灭。「我活了这么大，」他说，「没见过那么好看的路。」

column2: East Reef Gate
column3: 东礁门

column2: At the end of the reef flat two black reefs stand like a pair of gates, and beyond them the sea is moving at last: wave after wave rolls in from the east and breaks on the reef in white foam, the first sound of surf you have heard since entering the Ruins. Inside the gate stands the keepers' finest camp in three columns, backs to the waves, faces to you, not yielding a step.
column3: 礁坪的尽头，两道黑礁像两扇门，门外的海终于在动：一道道浪从东边涌过来，拍在礁上，碎成白沫，是你们进归墟以来头一回听见浪声。门里扎着守墟人最精的一营，三路排开，背对着浪，面朝着你们，一步也不让。

column2: The picked guards withdraw, but not into the water: they form up on either side of the reef gate like two rows of gateposts. An ancient line is carved into the rock: 'Who passes this gate is on no chart.' Below it is a newer one, the cut still pale: 'The Qianli, going east.' Shen Du unrolls her chart on the reef. It stops at this gate; east of it is blank paper. She looks at it a long time, then rolls it up. 'Later. First we finish settling the accounts.'
column3: 精兵退了，却没有退进水里，而是排在礁门两边，像两排门柱。礁上刻着一行古字：「出此门者，不在海图。」底下有一行新的，刀口还白：「千里号，往东。」沈渡把海图摊在礁上，她的图画到这道门就断了，往东是一片白纸。她把图卷了起来：「以后再说，先把账对完。」

column2: Long Table Slope
column3: 长席坡

column2: A gentle slope in the open with a long feast laid out down it, stones for tables and coconut shells for bowls, from the top of the slope to the bottom, several hundred places. A squad of dead soldiers sits along it shoulder to shoulder, an empty bowl before each, sitting very properly, and pushes back down anyone who comes to clear the bowls. This feast was laid to see the Qianli off, says an old castaway at the slope's edge. In ten years nobody has dared clear it.
column3: 野地里一道缓坡，坡上摆着一条长长的席，石头当桌，椰壳当碗，从坡顶一直摆到坡脚，几百个座。一队亡兵一个挨一个坐在席上，面前摆着空碗，坐得端端正正，谁来收碗就把谁按回去。坡边一个老漂客说，这席是给千里号送行摆的，十年没人敢收。

column2: The soldiers rise and leave and the feast stands empty. The old man leads you to the first place at the top of the slope. Every other bowl lies upside down, to show it was finished; this one alone sits upright, a pair of chopsticks laid neatly across it and beside it a flatbread ten years dry. 'Old Ding's idea,' the old man says. 'Whoever comes late ought to find something hot when he gets here.'
column3: 亡兵起身走了，席上空了下来。老人领你们走到坡顶的头一个座：别的碗都倒扣着，表示吃完了；只有这一只是正放着的，碗里一双筷子，搁得整整齐齐，旁边摆着一块干了十年的饼。「老鼎说的，」老人说，「晚到的那个人，回来总得有口热的。」

column2: Left Grain Cellar
column3: 留粮窖

column2: A cellar in the open, its door carved 'Left by the Qianli, for those who come after.' A band of shipwrecked pirates has prised it open and is hauling out the grain sack by sack, carrying it to the shore to pile into a heap and 'buy passage' out of the Ruins from the keepers. The cellar's guardians, a few castaways, are tied to posts at its mouth, watching the grain disappear sack after sack.
column3: 野地里一座地窖，窖门上刻着「千里号留，后来者取」。一伙落难海盗撬开了窖门，把窖里的粮一袋袋往外搬，搬到海边，要堆成一座小山跟守墟人「买路」出归墟。守窖的是几个漂客，被捆在窖口的木桩上，眼看着粮一袋袋没了。

column2: The pirates are driven off and the grain is carried back down sack by sack. The cellar's guardians untie themselves and rub their wrists, laughing: the keepers neither take grain nor sell passage, and for three days the pirates piled it up with no one paying them any heed. Every sack stacked at the cellar's bottom has a name on it; each of the Qianli's people left one. 'We're going on ahead. We won't need to eat it.'
column3: 海盗被赶走，粮一袋袋扛回了窖里。守窖的漂客解开绳子，揉着手腕笑：守墟人不收粮，也不卖路，海盗堆了三天，没一个人理他们。窖底码着的粮袋上，每一袋都写着一个名字，是千里号的人一人留了一袋：「我们往前走，吃不着了。」

column2: From the shore you recover the pirates' pile: sixty sacks of grain, two pots, a winnowing fan stolen from somewhere, and a white flag reading 'Buying Passage' whose staff is an oar.
column3: 海边抄回海盗堆的六十袋粮、两口锅、一架从别处抢来的风车，还有一面写着「买路」的白旗，旗杆是一根船桨。

column2: Each time you pass, the cellar's guardians follow the Qianli's rule and scoop you a handful from each named sack. 'This handful's Old Ding's, this one's Doctor Liu's. They said it was for whoever came after.'
column3: 每次路过，守窖的漂客都按千里号的规矩，从写着名字的粮袋里各舀一捧给你们：「这一捧是老鼎的，这一捧是柳娘子的，他们说了，给后来的人。」

column2: The Latecomer Store
column3: 后来者号

column2: On the last beach on the coast a bamboo stall flies a great banner reading 'The Latecomer'. Its owner, a castaway merchant with oiled hair and a powdered face, tells everyone he meets that he is the three hundredth name on the list: 'That last line, it's me.' He sells 'Latecomer certificates' at ten coppers each, which supposedly get you into the lamps over east when you die. A troop of dead riders stands before the stall. His bodyguards, he says; in fact the riders just can't stand how the banner glares.
column3: 海边最后一片滩上，一座竹棚挑着一面大旗，旗上三个字：「后来者」。棚主是个油头粉面的漂客商人，逢人就说自己就是名单上的第三百个，「最后一行写的就是我」，一张「后来者凭据」卖十文，买了的人死后能进东边的灯里。一队亡骑守在棚前，他说那是他的护卫，其实亡骑只是嫌那面旗晃眼。

column2: The riders withdraw, and when the stallholder sees the three hundred lanterns on your masts his legs give way and he plumps down on his pile of certificates and owns up: he's never seen the list, only heard the castaways talk of it. Impressed with you, he brings out his best goods from the bottom of his chests to trade, and when the trading is done he rolls up the great banner himself and hands it to you with both hands. 'Three years I've flown this and not one person believed me. If you fly it, maybe someone will.'
column3: 亡骑退了，棚主见你们桅上的三百盏灯笼，腿先软了，扑通坐在凭据堆上，老实招了：名单他没见过，是听漂客们传的。他佩服你们，把压箱底的好货拿出来跟你们换，换完了，自己动手把那面大旗卷了起来，双手递给你们：「这旗我挂了三年，没一个人信。你们挂，大概有人信。」

column2: Two Hundred and Ninety-Nine Lamps
column3: 二百九十九灯

column2: In the middle of the lamps, the figure in the straw hat lays down his pick, turns, and lifts his hat: a thin face, a grizzled beard, yellow sand on the left sandal and red mud on the right. It is Old Yan, who sat under the Satchel Tree waiting for you to fetch down his bag. He smiles. 'No rush. I'm used to being late.' Behind him all two hundred and ninety-nine lamps brighten a shade, and out of the still water stand rank on rank of dead soldiers, archers and riders. 'Ten years ago the three roads parted, and I ran their letters back and forth between them. Whichever road counted heads, they came up one short: me. By the time I caught up at the Ruins they had gone east, and left the list with the lamp keeper. That's me.' He draws half a name list from his shirt. 'The last line on the list needs someone to fill it. Beat me, and it's your turn.'
column3: 灯阵当中，戴斗笠的人放下竹签，转过身，掀开斗笠：瘦脸，花白胡子，左脚草鞋糊着黄沙，右脚糊着红泥，是挂袋树下等你们够信袋的晏伯。他笑了笑：「不急，我晚惯了。」身后二百九十九盏灯一齐亮了一分，静水里一排排站起亡兵、亡弓、亡骑。「十年前三路分手，我替他们来回送信，哪一路点人都差我一个。等我追到归墟，他们已经往东去了，名单留给了守灯的人，就是我。」他从怀里掏出半张名单：「名单上最后一行，要有人填。打得过我，才轮得到你们。」

column2: The keepers sink back into the still water. Old Yan sits down at his low table again and lays his half of the list beside the half from Lu Jiu's casket: two hundred and ninety-nine handprints, and the last line blank, two small words beside it: 'Whoever comes after'. 'That line was kept for me. I never caught up, so I've no right to write in it.' You take up the brush and write your company's name. Shen Du opens the Qianli's log and writes on its last page: 'The Qianli has arrived.' Among the lamps, two wicks have never burned down: one stands on a base carved with an abacus, one on a base carved with a lock. Old Yan points to them. 'Those two are still on the road.' He puts his hat back on and walks off towards the East Reef Gate. 'It's on my way. I'll go on ahead.'
column3: 守墟人退回了静水。晏伯坐回矮桌，把他的半张和陆九匣里的半张并在一起：二百九十九个手印，最后一行空着，旁边两个小字：「后来者」。「那一行本来留给我，我没赶上，不配写。」你们提笔写下了开拓队的名号。沈渡翻开千里号的日志，在最后一页写：「千里号，到了。」灯里有两盏的灯芯一直没烧短，一盏座上刻着算盘，一盏刻着锁。晏伯指指它们：「这两位，还在路上。」他戴上斗笠，往东礁门走去：「顺路，我先走一步。」
